descriptions.1: This book deals with the subject of Islamic jurisprudence, its characteristics, and its sources in an integrated manner. It begins by providing a detailed definition of jurisprudence and discusses its origins and importance in Islamic law. It focuses on clarifying the concept of jurisprudence and distinguishing it from beliefs and morals, and explains the nature of jurisprudential rulings and their classification into mandatory and positivistic. The book also addresses the main sources of jurisprudence, such as the Qur’an, Sunnah, consensus, and analogy, and reviews the most important characteristics that distinguish Islamic jurisprudence from other legal sciences.
descriptions.2: This book is an explanation of jurisprudential rules that include fundamental issues related to the provisions of worship and transactions. It focuses on interpreting jurisprudential rules and explaining their applications in Sharia rulings. In his explanation, the author addresses issues such as the ruling on doubt in acts of worship, the conditions for the obligation of actions, the priority of legal evidence, the controls of legal assignment, and other rules that form the basis of Islamic jurisprudence. The book is numbered automatically and contains indexes that help in accessing the jurisprudential rules easily.
descriptions.3: This book deals with the topic of analogy in the principles of jurisprudence, and reviews its importance as a main jurisprudential guide, with a discussion of fiqh evidence supporting the validity of analogy, and evidence opposing it. The author begins by defining analogy linguistically and terminologically, and discusses its types and the first to quote its denial. Then he presents the evidence of the negation of analogy from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the reasonable, and responds to it, and in turn infers the validity of analogy from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and consensus. The book aims to prove the validity of analogy and explain its importance in deriving jurisprudential rulings, while responding to those who deny it.
descriptions.4: This book is an explanation of a system in the principles of jurisprudence organized and explained by Dr. Muhammad Al-Habash. The book deals with the definition of the science of jurisprudence, its topics, benefits, history, and methods of writing about it. It also studies the main and specific Islamic legislative sources, with a focus on the Qur’an, Sunnah, consensus, and analogy. The book also contains an introduction that discusses the systems education curriculum and its importance in transmitting Sharia sciences.
descriptions.5: This book is an explanation of the book “Al-Waraqat” on the principles of jurisprudence by Imam Al-Juwayni, written by Muhammad Al-Hasan Al-Dado Al-Shanqeeti. The explanation addresses the definition of the principles of jurisprudence and its terminology, the sections of legal rulings, and the types of positive discourse, relying on precise scientific divisions and rules. The book aims to clarify how to draw deductions from legal texts and understand the meanings of rulings. It is suitable for science students who are beginners in this art.
descriptions.6: A book on the principles of jurisprudence that examines the concept of the objectives of Islamic law and its general and specific objectives, and explains the levels of human interests, including necessities, needs, and improvements, with a breakdown of the five universals that include preserving religion, soul, mind, lineage, and money, through a systematic presentation of the principles of this science.
descriptions.7: This book is a memorandum on the principles of jurisprudence that includes basic definitions and concepts in this science. The book deals with the definition of the principles of jurisprudence as an additional component and as an independent science, and explains the meanings of the word “usul” and “jurisprudence” in language and terminology. It also studies the general rules on which jurisprudence is built, Sharia rulings, and methods of jurisprudential reasoning. The book also includes topics such as dividing speech into fact and metaphor, commands and prohibitions, abrogation, consensus, narration, analogy, ijtihad, and imitation.
descriptions.8: This book by Al-Nawawi deals with the subject of the etiquette of fatwa, mufti, and questioner, and emphasizes the importance of this topic and its great danger and virtue in Islamic law. The author focuses on the conditions, sections, and etiquette of the mufti, mentioning the etiquette and rulings of the mufti. The book aims to provide practical advice to those practicing fatwa and advises investigation and scrutiny before answering jurisprudential questions.
descriptions.9: The Etiquette of the Mufti and the Mufti is a book written by Imam Abu Amr Othman bin Abdul Rahman, known as Ibn al-Salah al-Shahrazuri, in which he mentioned the conditions, descriptions and rulings of the mufti, the description and rulings of the mufti, how to issue a fatwa and referendum, and its etiquette. Published by the Library of Science and Wisdom in Medina and printed in 1423 AH - 2002 AD, edited by Dr. Muwaffaq Abdullah Abdul Qadir.
descriptions.10: In his book “Four Rules upon which Rulings Revolve, followed by a Brief,” Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab presents a presentation of four basic jurisprudential rules, aiming to clarify the principles of Sharia rulings. He begins with the rule of prohibiting speaking against God without knowledge, citing Qur’anic verses as evidence. Then he moves to the second rule, which relates to what the street was silent about, considering this an amnesty that no one has the right to prohibit or require. The third rule relates to leaving out evidence, focusing on the importance that the author attaches to understanding these rules in the context of jurisprudential principles.
descriptions.11: This book, “Usul al-Sarkhasi,” is written by Imam al-Sarkhasi in the field of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules. The book deals with multiple topics in the principles of jurisprudence, including the obligation and requirement of a command, the rule of duty and command, the quality of goodness in rulings, intention and licence, the specific and the general, truth and metaphor, in addition to research into the linguistic meanings used in jurisprudence and the controls for reasoning with legal evidence. The book aims to explain the rules and principles from which jurisprudential rulings can be used and to separate what is permissible from what is forbidden.
descriptions.12: Usul al-Shashi is a book on the principles of jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. The book is taught as an essential part of the student curriculum in many Islamic seminaries, especially in South Asia. There is controversy over the identity of the author of the work, whether it was Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Shashi Nizam al-Din Abu Ali or Muhammad Fayd al-Hasan al-Kankuhi.
descriptions.13: This book is an explanation of a system in the principles of jurisprudence, covering various topics, including legal rulings, evidence, commands and prohibitions, and abrogation. The author aims to provide a brief and useful explanation of the Gihat al-Amal system, focusing on the strongest evidence and the most important jurisprudential rules. The book is directed to science students who wish to understand the principles of jurisprudence and its basic rules.
descriptions.14: This book on the principles of jurisprudence deals with the definition of this science, its origin, and its main topics, with a focus on the most important issues that a jurist cannot do without in the practice of his work. The author deals with issues of legal ruling, its evidence, the meaning of words, contradiction, ways to defend it, ijtihad, and imitation, with an interest in clarifying the truth of the disagreement and correcting any misunderstanding that occurs in writing issues of fundamentals. The book is directed to students of science and beneficiaries of the faculties of Sharia and Islamic studies, and aims to provide clear and comprehensive scientific material in this field.
descriptions.15: This book, “Ijmal al-Isaba fi Sayings of the Companions” by the scholar Salah al-Din al-Ala’i, deals with the subject of silent consensus and the status of the sayings of the Companions in Islamic jurisprudence. The author focuses on studying the individual sayings of the Companions and how to infer them, relying on subdivisions related to the extent of the spread of these sayings among the Companions and their reactions to them. The book aims to explain the ways of inferring the sayings of the Companions and to separate what can be relied upon from others, while providing an answer to the suspicions surrounding this topic.
descriptions.16: Guiding stallions to achieve the truth from the science of jurisprudence is one of the books on the fundamentals of jurisprudence, written by Imam Muhammad Al-Shawkani (1173 AH, 1250 AH - 1759, 1834). In his book, the author intended to clarify what is more correct in jurisprudence from what is more likely, and in it he clarified what is wrong from what is correct in matters of the science of jurisprudence, so that the fundamentalist scholar would have insight into his knowledge. Imam Muhammad Al-Shawkani arranged his book according to an introduction and seven objectives. And a conclusion. Imam Muhammad Al-Shawkani says in the introduction to his book:
descriptions.17: This book, “Guiding Critics to Facilitate Ijtihad,” by Al-San’ani, deals with the subject of ijtihad from the perspective of the principles of jurisprudence. The author focuses on the definition of ijtihad in the language and in the terminology of the fundamentalists, and points out its conditions and importance, considering it a continuous divine gift. The book also addresses discussions about freedom of thought and ijtihad among scholars, and reviews some controversial ideas in the field of terminology, with a focus on scholars’ responses to prohibiting ijtihad and ways to facilitate it.
descriptions.18: The book “Strutting Fairness in the Effects of Disagreement” by the scholar Sibt Ibn al-Jawzi deals with the subject of fabricated and weak hadiths in Islamic jurisprudence, pointing out their weaknesses and revealing the mysteries about them. The author aims to provide an objective criticism of jurisprudential narrations, distinguishing between authentic and weak ones, without bias toward a particular doctrine. The book is a work on the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, and in it Ibn al-Jawzi reviews a collection of hadiths related to jurisprudential rulings, referring them to major scholars and well-known scholars.
descriptions.19: The book “Awakening the Spirits of Those with Vision to Imitate the Master of the Emigrants” deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence, focusing on the opinions of the scholars of the four imams and their followers. The author, Al-Fulani, provides a comprehensive overview of the principles of jurisprudence from the perspective of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and other scholars of schools of jurisprudence, with a focus on the principles that these scholars adopted in their fatwas. The book aims to motivate the reader to imitate the traditions of the Companions and Followers, and calls for working according to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet, while emphasizing the importance of verifying the authenticity of hadiths and staying away from heresies and plagiarism.
descriptions.20: The book “Al-Ashbah wa Al-Naza’ir” written by Taj Al-Din Al-Subki is a book on the principles of jurisprudence that deals with jurisprudential rules and legal concepts. It focuses on clarifying the general and specific rules in Islamic jurisprudence and explaining how to derive rulings from them. The book is concerned with explaining the concept of similarities and analogues and how they are used in jurisprudence, while providing examples and practical applications of these rules. In his introduction, Al-Subki discusses the importance of jurisprudence and its sections, and mentions important books in this field, such as the book Al-Qa’id by Ibn Abd al-Salam and the book Al-Ashbah wa Al-Naza’ir by Ibn Al-Marhil, explaining the motivation behind writing his book.
descriptions.21: This book, “Al-Usul Al-Jami’ ila Il-Durar Al-Manzoumah in the field of collecting mosques,” is written by Hassan Al-Sinauni, and is related to the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence. In this work, the author deals with basic concepts in the science of jurisprudence, such as defining jurisprudence and its principles, ruling and obligation, good and bad, duties and prohibitions, conditions and prohibitions, severance and invalidity, and other important jurisprudential rules. The book aims to explain and detail the contents of the book “Collecting Mosques” in a simplified and useful way, while adding new information and additions to what was mentioned in previous sources.
descriptions.22: This book, “The Principles of Ilm al-Usul,” by Ibn Uthaymeen, deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence and its rules. He defines the principles of jurisprudence by considering its two terms “usul” and “jurisprudence,” and explains the meaning of each of them. The book deals with the definition of the principles of jurisprudence as the science of knowing practical legal rulings with their detailed evidence, indicating the differences between legal, scientific, and ordinary rulings. It also indicates that knowledge of jurisprudential rulings may be certain or speculative, and reviews the sections of legal and mandatory rulings, and discusses important concepts in the science of principles such as knowledge and its sections, speech and its sections, truth and metaphor, command and prohibition and their formulas.
descriptions.23: Assets and controls. A book written by Imam Abu Zakaria Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH), in which he mentioned nine issues related to the most important needs of the student of legal sciences of jurisprudential rules, important principles, required objectives, and similar issues, with a representation of them with the branches that follow from them, or similarities and analogues that join them. He said in the introduction to the book:
descriptions.24: This book, “Al-Anjum Al-Zahirat Ala Hal Al-Afazat Al-Waraqat” is an explanation of the principles of jurisprudence by its author, Shams Al-Din Al-Maridini. The book addresses definitions of the main concepts of jurisprudence and discusses the types of rulings and jurisprudential rules, providing examples and illustrative evidence. The author aims to provide a moderate explanation between simplification and detail, while ensuring clarity of meaning and ease of understanding for beginners in this scientific field.
descriptions.25: This book is an explanation of the book "Minhaj al-Wusool", which deals with the principles and rules of jurisprudence, where the author Taqi al-Din al-Subki focuses on defining the principles of jurisprudence, the divisions of jurisprudential rule, and the conditions of the mujtahid. The book begins with an introductory introduction that includes praise and praise to God, then prayers upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, indicating the importance of the science of principles in building Islamic law and branching out its rulings.
descriptions.26: The book “Consensus in Islamic Sharia” by Muhammad Rushdi Alyan deals with the topic of consensus as one of the evidences of the principles of jurisprudence, indicating its importance after the texts in legal argument. The book focuses on the definition of consensus in language and terminology, the support for consensus, its authority, and its types, relying in doing so on dividing its discussions into two parts, the first deals with the consensus on it, and the second deals with the people of consensus.
descriptions.27: This book may be one of the following: Al-Ihkam fi Usul Al-Ahkam (Ibn Hazm), a book on the principles of jurisprudence written by Ibn Hazm Al-Andalusi. Al-Ahkam fi Usul Al-Ahkam (Al-Amdi), a book on the principles of jurisprudence written by Al-Amdi.
descriptions.28: This book deals with the fundamentalist opinions of Imam Abu Abbas Ahmad bin Omar bin Surayj in Shafi’i jurisprudence, and reviews his scientific standing among the scholars of his time and his influence on the Shafi’i doctrine. The author focuses on studying the fundamentalist sayings of Ibn Surayj by collecting them from multiple books on the principles of jurisprudence, and explains the reasons that prompted him to study the opinions of this eminent scholar and present them in a separate book. The book aims to show the importance of Ibn Surayj in the science of principles and his role in renewing the Shafi’i doctrine in the third century AH.
descriptions.29: This is a book on the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, explaining the evidence of the legal rulings related to angels, messengers, and the rest of the worlds. The author divides the rulings into two parts: obligatory rulings related to request, and positive rulings that do not require demand, such as permissibility and setting reasons, conditions, and prohibitions. The book shows the methods of inferring rulings based on formulas and reports, and the good or evil that results from them in the immediate and future.
descriptions.30: يتناول كتاب "الإنصاف في التنبيه على الأسباب التي أوجبت الاختلاف بين المسلمين" للبطليوسي موضوعات الفقه وأصوله، مستعرضاً أسباب الخلاف الفقهي بين العلماء والمذاهب الإسلامية. The book is divided into several sections that address different aspects of the causes of disagreement, including the commonality of words, metaphor and truth, generality and specificity, abrogation, analogy, and other jurisprudential rules. The book aims to achieve fairness in understanding the reasons for this difference and to explain its wisdom from a divine point of view, using the Holy Qur’an and the Prophet’s hadiths as evidence.
descriptions.31: This book, “Al-Insaaf fi Bayan Bayan al-`Aziz al-Difference,” by Shah Waliullah Dehlawi, deals with the topic of the reasons for differences between scholars and schools of jurisprudence in Islam. The book focuses on analyzing the reasons for the differences between the Companions and their followers in the branches of jurisprudence, as well as the differences in the doctrines of the jurists, and the reasons for the disagreement between the scholars of hadith and the people of opinion. The author aims to provide a balance that helps determine the right to these jurisprudential differences.
descriptions.32: This book is written by Al-Juwayni, Abu Al-Maali, and it deals with the subject of ijtihad in Islamic jurisprudence and its principles. The author focuses on discussing the opinion of the scholars regarding the correction of the jurisprudence and mentioning the areas of disagreement on this subject, while reviewing the opinions of the jurists on the issues of principles and sub-issues in diligence. The book also deals with the jurisprudential rules related to imitation and details the characteristics of the scholar and the person who asks the question.
descriptions.33: The book “Al-Bahr Al-Muhit fi Usul al-Fiqh” by its author, Al-Zarkashi Badr al-Din, deals with the subject of jurisprudential jurisprudence and its rules, focusing on the concept of evidence and consideration in Islamic jurisprudence, and dealing with multiple issues related to the principles of jurisprudential deduction and its sections. The book aims to establish the science of principles and explain its importance in understanding and applying the provisions of Islamic Sharia.
descriptions.34: Al-Burhan fi Usul al-Fiqh is a twelfth-century treatise written by Abu al-Ma’ali al-Juwayni, the imam of the fundamentals of jurisprudence in his time. It is a highly regarded work by Al-Juwayni on the principles of jurisprudence. It is considered one of the four pillars in the field of legal theory. The other three are: 1. Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali, who wrote Al-Mustasfa from Ilm Al-Usul; 2. Judge Abdul Jabbar, who wrote “Al-Amad”; 3. Abu Al-Hussein Al-Basri, who wrote “Al-Mu’tamid” (Explanation of the Book of Al-Amad).
descriptions.35: This book, “Insight into the Principles of Jurisprudence,” by Al-Shirazi Abu Ishaq, deals with issues of jurisprudential principles related to commands and prohibitions, generalities and specifics. It focuses on analyzing the forms of commands and prohibitions and their conditions, and studies issues such as the obligation of action when the imperative form is abstract, and the inclusion of slaves in the absolute legal command. It also studies the forms of generality and the conditions for specifying it. The book aims to clarify the fundamental rules related to these jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.36: This book, “Al-Tahrir Sharh Al-Tahrir fi Usul Al-Fiqh,” is an explanation by the author Al-Mardawi of his previous book, “Tahrir Al-Manqul,” in the field of Usul Al-Fiqh. The commentator deals with the doctrines of well-known fundamentalist scholars and their followers, with reference to the opinions of the Mu'tazilites, the Rafidites, and the Ash'aris, and reviews the opinions of the scholars of the Hanbali school. It aims to provide sufficient explanations to solve jurisprudential problems and explain issues of fundamentals from a comprehensive and diverse perspective.
descriptions.37: The book deals with the subject of Islamic legislation and argues for the validity of this legislation for application in various times and environments. The author focuses on the wisdom of the emergence of Islam from the Arabian Peninsula and its treatment of various aspects of life, expressing the advantages of Islamic legislation and its suitability to all environments. It also points to the importance of the Sunnah in clarifying the Qur’an and its role in interpreting Sharia rulings. The book aims to show the compatibility of Islamic legislation with all the needs of individuals and groups throughout the ages.
descriptions.38: This book, “Report and Inscription,” by Ibn Amir Haj, deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence. It focuses on liberating the concept of the science of jurisprudence and its topics, while reviewing the logical premises and theoretical theories that establish this science. The book also addresses the linguistic and terminological aspects of jurisprudence terminology, relying on the analysis of vocabulary and sentences and their linguistic and terminological connotations.
descriptions.39: The book “The Introduction to Graduation of Branches on Usul” by Al-Isnawi is a book on the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules. It aims to explain how to graduate the subsidiary jurisprudential rulings and link them to the general principles and jurisprudential rules. The book deals with basic topics in the science of jurisprudence, such as division of words, derivation, synonymy, association, truth and metaphor, generality and specificity, prohibitions, and how to infer using words, with a focus on applying these principles to jurisprudential issues. The author begins with an introduction in which he explains the importance of the science of jurisprudence as a basis for ijtihad and a condition for the validity of the fatwa, pointing out what the diligent person needs in terms of knowledge of the Qur’an, the Sunnah, consensus, language, and analogy.
descriptions.40: The book “The Complete Questions of the Principles of Jurisprudence and Their Applications” by author Abdul Karim Al-Namlah provides a brief introduction to the science of the principles of jurisprudence, focusing on the basics of this science without diving into the controversial details. The book deals with the definition of the principles of jurisprudence, the differences between it and jurisprudence, the topics of this science, and its importance in learning. It also studies the types and divisions of Sharia ruling, with a focus on the Sharia evidence used to prove rulings, and reviews the sources from which the science of jurisprudence was derived.
descriptions.41: This book deals with the issue of disagreement among scholars regarding jurisprudential rulings, and reviews the reasons for this disagreement from the perspective of the principles of jurisprudence. The author focuses on clarifying the factors that may lead to disagreement among jurists in understanding legal texts or deriving rulings from them, noting that this disagreement does not affect the basic unity of Muslims, but rather relates to subsidiary matters. The book aims to clarify the sources of jurisprudential disagreement and how to deal with it in a scientific and systematic manner.
descriptions.42: The book Al-Risala by Imam Al-Shafi’i is the first book written on the science of the principles of jurisprudence. By writing this book, Al-Shafi’i wanted to set the controls that a jurist or jurist would adhere to in order to clarify the legal rulings for every hadith and innovation in every era. It is one of the books that Al-Rabi’ narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i. The book Al-Risalah is located in one volume in which Al-Shafi’i dealt with fundamental issues such as the hadith of Al-Wahid and the evidence for it, the conditions for the authenticity of the hadith and the justice of the narrators, the refutation of mursal and interrupted reports, and other issues of fundamentals and weighting. The introduction to the long letter (one hundred pages) constitutes a large part of its material. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi says about al-Shafi’i’s leadership in establishing the science of jurisprudence
descriptions.43: This book is “The Necessary in the Principles of Jurisprudence or Mukhtasar al-Mustasfa” by Ibn Rushd al-Hafid, and it is a summary of the book “Al-Mustasfa” by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali in the Principles of Jurisprudence. The book deals with the rules and principles upon which the jurisprudential branches of the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus are built, with a focus on analogy and linguistic and textual significance. The author aims to provide a useful and accurate summary of these basic principles of jurisprudence, while providing an introductory introduction that explains the nature of jurisprudential sciences and the methods in deriving legal rulings.
descriptions.44: This book, “The Toolkit in the Fundamentals of Jurisprudence,” by Imam Abu Ya’la Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Farra, deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence through an integrated scientific approach, based on authentic sources in the principles, branches, language, and grammar. The author aims to collect and compile the principles of the Hanbali school of thought and detail its jurisprudential issues, presenting an independent vision of the Hanbali jurisprudence. The book is rich in scientific material and well organized and tabulated. It is considered one of the important works in the field of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.45: This book, “Al-Aqd Al-Talid fi Ikhtisar Al-Durr Al-Nadhid,” or also known as “Al-Mu’aid” by Al-Ulamwi, deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence, focusing on the etiquette of the teacher and the learner in the field of legal science. The book deals with the virtues of engaging in science and its classification, and discusses the sections and levels of forensic science, with a focus on the etiquette of teachers and learners in the field of teaching and learning, including their etiquette within themselves and in the lesson council.
descriptions.46: This is a book on the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, written by Imam Al-Qarafi, entitled “Al-Furuq” or “Anwar Al-Buruq fi Anwa Al-Furuq”. The author aims to explain the subtle differences between similar legal rules and rulings, relying on the comparison and detail approach in matters of jurisprudence and fundamentalism. The book begins with an introductory sermon, then covers multiple chapters and sections, such as the difference between testimony and narration, the difference between the rules of construction and predicate, and the difference between linguistic conditions and others, while listing various applied issues.
descriptions.47: The Book of Distinctions by Al-Karabisi is a book on the science of jurisprudence that deals with various jurisprudential issues from the perspective of differentiating between sayings and jurisprudential rules, relying on the famous disagreements among jurisprudential scholars and recalling the subtle differences between legal rulings. The book includes various chapters that address issues of purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, and other sections of jurisprudence, with a focus on distinguishing between the various jurisprudential rulings and explaining the subtle differences between them.
descriptions.48: This book, “The Sublime Thought in the History of Islamic Jurisprudence,” by Al-Hajwi, deals with the emergence and development of Islamic sciences with a focus on Islamic jurisprudence. The author studies the stages of development of jurisprudence from before Islam until the era of the Prophet, reviewing the most important legislative sources and methods of jurisprudential deduction. The book aims to open new horizons for researchers in the field of Islamic jurisprudence and shed light on important aspects of the emergence of Islamic sciences and their development throughout the ages.
descriptions.49: Al-Fawaid fi Ikhtasar Al-Maqasid is a book on the principles of jurisprudence that deals with the topics of legal objectives, interests, and evils. The author focuses on explaining interests and harms and their varying ranks, and how to bring about interests and ward off harms in various aspects of life in this world and the hereafter. The book also addresses the concept of charity and moral considerations in Islamic law.
descriptions.50: A book on the principles of jurisprudence that examines the concept of finality in the four legal proofs (the Qur’an, the Sunnah, consensus, and analogy), and divides it into two parts: The first deals with the finality of the evidence in terms of its aspects (provenance and significance), what benefits or prevents it, and its effect on terminology, ijtihad, and conflict. The second concerns the rulings of definiteness in the Qur’an and Sunnah from the standpoints of proof and significance, such as the definiteness of a recurring and single report and the definiteness of a text, its generality and its meaning.
descriptions.51: This book deals with the subject of jurisprudential rules and their applications in the four schools of thought, presenting their definition, benefits, and sources, and reviewing a number of basic jurisprudential rules with their benefits. The author aims to clarify the importance of jurisprudential rules in applying Sharia rulings and organizing Islamic jurisprudence, relying on the Qur’an, Sunnah, and jurisprudential jurisprudence throughout history.
descriptions.52: This book deals with the jurisprudential rules and controls that express the principle of facilitation in Islamic law, reviewing a set of jurisprudential rules formulated by scholars based on extrapolation of the various branches of jurisprudence. The author aims to clarify the jurisprudential rules that carry the meaning of facilitation in acts of worship and transactions, relying on a specific scientific approach in studying them. The book focuses on highlighting the facilitative aspect of Sharia law without neglecting the other aspects, considering that even though jurisprudential obligations carry within them a degree of hardship, the principle of facilitation remains present in many jurisprudential rulings.
descriptions.53: This book is by the scholar Ibn al-Laham, and it is one of the works on the science of jurisprudence that deals with the fundamental rules and their subsidiary rulings. The author focuses on explaining multiple fundamental rules, providing examples and issues related to each of the sub-rules. The book aims to provide a deep understanding of fundamentalist rules and how to derive legal rulings from them, with an interest in defining the concept of jurisprudence and its scientific limits.
descriptions.54: This book deals with the issues of ijtihad and imitation in Islamic jurisprudence, and the author, Ibn Mulla Farroukh, reviews different opinions on these issues and provides his personal guidance. It focuses on the importance of correctly understanding the meaning of imitation and ijtihad, and discusses ways to reach the truth in Islamic jurisprudence, indicating that there is something that is necessarily clear from religion that does not depend on following a particular doctrine. The book is a type of jurisprudential book that is concerned with the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence.
descriptions.55: The book “The Useful Saying in the Evidence of Ijtihad and Taqlid” by Muhammad Al-Shawkani discusses the topic of taqlid in Islamic jurisprudence and establishing the right to whether it is permissible or not. Al-Shawkani begins by presenting the evidence of those who say that imitation is permissible, then he moves on to explain the opinions of scholars prohibiting it, and reviews the opinions of the four imams in this regard. The book also addresses the issue of the blockage of the door to ijtihad, discusses its evidence, and provides advice to those who take the lead in issuing fatwas and judging from among the imitators.
descriptions.56: Al-Kawkab Al-Dari, while graduating on grammatical principles from the branches of jurisprudence, is a book on jurisprudential principles that deals with the applications of grammatical rules in jurisprudential issues. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as nouns, implicits, connectives, derivatives, infinitives, adverbs, duality and plurals, prepositions, conjunctions, conditional letters, feminine ta’s, and exceptions. The book aims to link grammatical rules to the branches of jurisprudence and understand their Arabic evidence.
descriptions.57: Al-Lam’ fi Usul al-Fiqh is a book on the science of the fundamentals of jurisprudence based on the Shafi’i school of thought. Its author is Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi. Some of his brothers asked him to compile for them a summary of the fundamentals of the school of thought. He responded to their request and wrote this book, in which the compiler summarized his book “Al-Tabisrah fi Usul al-Fiqh.” Its author said: “Some of my brothers asked me to compile a summary of the doctrine, on the principles of jurisprudence, so that this would be in addition to the insight I had done on the dispute, so I responded to him in response to asking him and fulfilling his right, and I pointed out in it a mention of the dispute and the necessary evidence, so perhaps this would come to someone who did not have what I had done on the dispute.” He began compiling it in the year 455 AH and finished it in the year 469 AH. The book contains a lot of evidence. …
descriptions.58: This book, “Al-Mahsool fi Usul al-Fiqh” by Ibn al-Arabi, is a work in the field of the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules. The author deals with the definition of jurisprudence and its principles, and studies the legal evidence and classification of legal acts into obligatory, prohibited, recommended, disliked, and permissible, with a discussion of jurisprudential limits and legal ruling.
descriptions.59: The book “Al-Mahsool” written by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi is considered one of the important works in the field of the principles of jurisprudence. The book deals with the definition of the principles of jurisprudence and its introductions, and includes multiple chapters that address the definition of knowledge and suspicion, consideration and evidence, the legal ruling, the division of the legal rulings, and other issues related to the principles of jurisprudence. The book aims to provide a scientific methodology for understanding jurisprudential rules and their applications.
descriptions.60: Al-Mukhtasar fi Usul al-Fiqh is a brief book on the fundamentals of the jurisprudence of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, written by al-Hafiz Ibn al-Lahham (752-803). He wrote it explaining its symbols and mysteries, but without delving into the reasoning and evidence, noting what had occurred in it of disagreement or consensus on some issues. He arranged the book in the order of books on the science of jurisprudence, and answered some of the questions he received about this science. Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Laham said in the introduction to the book:
descriptions.61: This book deals with the study of Islamic jurisprudential schools in the form of an introductory introduction, as it focuses on documenting and understanding the Islamic heritage and the principles of the main schools of jurisprudence, such as the Shafi’i and Hanafi doctrines. The author aims to provide a correct understanding tool for the jurisprudential heritage and the rules of schools of thought, while emphasizing the importance of benefiting from it without absolute acceptance, absolute rejection, or random selection.
descriptions.62: The Introduction to the Doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, one of the books of the late scholars of Hanbali jurisprudence, written by Abd al-Qadir ibn Badran al-Dimashqi (1280 AH - 1864 AD / 1346 AH - 1927 AD). The book is considered one of the most comprehensive books on Hanbali jurisprudence, as the book includes an introduction and eight contracts. In its introduction, the author explains his doctrine of beliefs and the reason for his choosing the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal regarding the branches, the reason for the departure of many people from the Hanbali doctrine, and the decline of his influence in Syria, and the reasons for writing the book and his method.
descriptions.63: This book deals with the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and explains its concepts and jurisprudential principles. The author, Bakr Abu Zaid, focuses on defining doctrine and jurisprudence from a linguistic, legal, and terminological perspective, then explains the types of jurisprudence recorded in Islamic jurisprudential schools. It also discusses the history of the doctrine, the conditions for transmitting the doctrine, and the causes of errors in it. The book aims to understand the principles of jurisprudence and its rules in the Hanbali school in detail.
descriptions.64: Al-Mustasfa min Ilm al-Usul is a 12th-century book written by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali. It is an abbreviation of his book Tahdheeb Al-Usul, which tends to be comprehensive, and is superior to the book Al-Mankhul, which tends to be short.
descriptions.65: This book, “The Draft on the Principles of Jurisprudence,” by Majd al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah, deals with issues of orders in the principles of jurisprudence, reviewing their formulas, rulings, and objectives. The author discusses various issues about the validity of considering the imperative form and considering the will of the speaker in it. He also studies the ruling on the absolute imperative, repetition and time, and also studies the ruling on those who enter into legal discourse such as the Prophet, believers, slaves, the coerced, and others. The book focuses on discussing the different viewpoints between the Mu'tazilites, Ash'aris, and jurists on these issues.
descriptions.66: The book “Al-Musalih Al-Mursalah” by Muhammad Al-Amin Al-Shanqeeti deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence, reviewing how Islamic law perfected the religion and completed the blessing upon Muslims, and how the first generation of the nation relied on the texts of the Qur’an and its explicit expressions, and then jurisprudential practices developed with the development of life and the emergence of new needs. The book focuses on the importance of the Qur’an and the Sunnah as primary sources of legislation, and refers to the efforts made by scholars in establishing the principles of jurisprudence to derive rulings from their evidence, including the topics of the Qur’an related to the general, the specific, the absolute, the restricted, the abrogated, and the abrogated.
descriptions.67: The book “Fundamentalist Terminology and the Problem of Concepts” by author Ali Jumaa deals with a scientific study of the importance of terminology in Islamic jurisprudence and the impact of its manipulation on Islamic identity and thought. The book focuses on reconsidering the issue of fundamentalist terminology and terminology, and points out the challenges faced by Sharia sciences in the modern era due to changes in the use of concepts and terminology. The book also deals with a practical application of fundamentalist thought through analysis of the term analogy, and aims to clarify the scientific importance of understanding fundamentalist terminology correctly.
descriptions.68: This book deals with the topic of Islamic jurisprudence in Islamic jurisprudence, which is one of the most important jurisprudential rules that scholars of fundamentals have paid attention to. The author focuses on defining the transmitted interest and explaining its authority, conditions, and conditions for deducing it, relying on an objective scientific approach. The book also presents the position of scholars on the matter of mission and what they differed about regarding it, and reviews some practical examples of its application. The book is part of studies on the principles of jurisprudence that aim to gain a deeper understanding of the origins of Islamic legislation and its applications.
descriptions.69: This book deals with the subject of the absolute and the restricted in the science of jurisprudence. It reviews the definitions of these two concepts in language and terminology, and studies their connotations and their difference with the indefinite and the general. It also examines the rule of the absolute and the restricted, cases of assigning the absolute to the restricted, its conditions, and the reasons for disagreement among scholars on this subject. The book focuses on the applications of this concept in jurisprudential issues related to prayer, purity, punishments, expiations, and other jurisprudential topics.
descriptions.70: This book, “Al-Mu’tamid fi Usul al-Fiqh,” by Abu al-Husayn al-Basri al-Mu’tazili, deals with the topics of the foundations of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence in an organized and organized manner. The author focuses on addressing the main issues of jurisprudence, such as commands and prohibitions, general and clear, abrogated and abrogated, consensus, news, analogy, prohibition and permissibility, and other basic rules related to the principles of jurisprudence. The book aims to provide useful and organized content that is compatible with the nature of the principles of jurisprudence without going into details that are not related to its direct topic.
descriptions.71: This book, “Al-Manthur fi Al-Qawaa’ al-Fiqhiyyah,” by Al-Zarkashi Badr al-Din, deals with the rules and principles of Shafi’i jurisprudence, explaining the general rules of jurisprudence and their details. It aims to control the various jurisprudential rulings within unified laws, and reviews jurisprudential rules that regulate the principles of the Shafi’i school of thought and clarify the basis of jurisprudence over its prohibitions. The book combines brevity and clarification, and reviews the differences and agreements in the jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.72: Al-Ghazali’s book “Al-Mankhool Min Commentaries on Usul” deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence, as it focuses on preparing the scientific principles necessary to understand the branches of jurisprudence and their applications. In this book, Al-Ghazali explains the nature of the three legal sciences: theology, principles, and jurisprudence, clarifying the sources and purpose of each. The book also addresses multiple issues in the principles of jurisprudence and the logical rules that help in deriving legal rulings, noting the importance of distinguishing between definitive evidence and assumptions in the science of principles.
descriptions.73: The Book of Confirmations in Explaining the Objectives of the Qur’an, Sunnah, Ruling, and the Overall Interests Underlying the Individual Evidences and Vocabulary of Legislation and Defining the Secrets of Obligations in Sharia, written by Al-Hafiz Ibrahim bin Musa Al-Shatibi (d. 790 AH 1388). Ibrahim bin Musa Al-Shatibi chose a name for the book other than the name of Al-Mu’awafaqat, which is an introduction to the secrets of assignments, but he changed it to Al-Muwafaqat, and that was because of a vision by one of his sheikhs when the Sheikh said to Imam Al-Shatibi, “I saw you in my sleep yesterday with your hand in it.” A book I wrote, so I asked you about it, and you told me that it was Al-Muwafaqat. I asked you about the meaning of this cute name, and you told me that with it you reconciled the doctrines of Ibn al-Qasim and Abu Hanifa.
descriptions.74: This book, “Al-Nidha Al-Kafiya fi Ahkam Usul Al-Din” by Ibn Hazm, deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, focusing on issues such as consensus, analogy, opinion, frequent transmission, and single narrations. The author aims to provide a simplified summary of the issues of the principles of jurisprudence, based on proof and evidence, and aims to facilitate access to the legal facts and guide the reader to the stages of jurisprudence in religion.
descriptions.75: This book deals with the issue of the deficiency in the text in the Prophetic hadiths and its impact on their argument and strength, with a focus on the monotheist Sunnah. The author studies its reality and ruling, discusses the various jurisprudential schools of thought around it, and reviews its types and impact in invoking the Sunnah. The book is a work on the principles of jurisprudence and aims to examine the rule of “deletion from the text is abrogated” and its impact on working with the single Sunnah.
descriptions.76: The book “Al-Wajeez fi Clarifying the General Rules of Jurisprudence” by Muhammad Sidqi Al-Borno provides a comprehensive overview of the general rules of jurisprudence and their origins, defining the rules of jurisprudence and explaining their place in Islamic law and their benefits. The author focuses on the differences between jurisprudential rules and jurisprudential rules, and discusses the types, ranks, and sources of jurisprudential rules, while reviewing the ruling on using them as evidence for jurisprudential rulings. The book also deals with the development of jurisprudential rules throughout history and includes detailed chapters on the objectives of jurisprudence and the most important jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.77: Al-Waraqat fi Usul al-Fiqh is a text written by Abu al-Ma’ali al-Juwayni. Al-Hattab said about it in Qart al-Ain: “A book whose size is small, its knowledge is abundant, its benefit is great, and its blessing is evident.”
descriptions.78: This book deals with the topic of the appropriate description of the law of governance from a fundamentalist jurisprudential perspective, focusing on studying the methods of identifying the reason for the legal rulings. The author focuses on the importance of analogy as a tool for deducing new rulings, and discusses methods for extrapolating the cause through appropriate description, reviewing its divisions and types. The book aims to clarify how to use these rules in understanding and interpreting legal rulings, with a focus on the fundamental and jurisprudential aspects related to reason and analogy.
descriptions.79: This book, “Al-Ashbah wa Al-Naza’ir” by Ibn Najim is one of the jurisprudential books that deals with the general rules and principles of jurisprudence. It focuses on clarifying the concept of intention and its terms and conditions, while dealing with multiple topics related to intention and legal intention in acts of worship and transactions. The book aims to explain how to distinguish similarities and counterparts in jurisprudential rulings, and includes general jurisprudential rules and details on various issues of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.80: The book “Al-Ashbah wa Al-Naza’ir” by Ibn Najim is one of the jurisprudential books that deals with the general rules and principles of jurisprudence. It focuses on analyzing the intention and objectives in acts of worship, and reviews multiple topics about the reality of the intention and its conditions and provisions, while providing examples and analogues for the application of these jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.81: This book, “Al-Muhaddhab fi Ilm Usul al-Fiqh Comparative,” by Dr. Abdul Karim al-Namlah, deals with the subject of fundamentals of jurisprudence in a comparative manner, providing a definition of the concept of principles, jurisprudence, and the principles of jurisprudence, reviewing the differences between fundamental and jurisprudential rules, and explaining the importance and foundations of this science. It also studies the terminology and methods used in studying the principles of jurisprudence, and reviews the sources from which this science was derived and the methods of its composition.
descriptions.82: This book, “Al-Muhadhdhab fi Ilm Usul al-Fiqh Comparative,” by Dr. Abdul Karim al-Namlah, deals with the topics of the science of jurisprudence in a comparative manner, focusing on the definitions of principles, jurisprudence, and principles of jurisprudence, the differences in fundamentalist and jurisprudential rules, the importance and origins of this science, and the sources and methods of its composition. It also focuses on the terms and logical foundations that the researcher needs in this science, such as limit and proof, with an explanation of their divisions and conditions.
descriptions.83: This book is an explanation of Ibn al-Hajib’s book Mukhtasar fi Usul al-Fiqh, written by Abu al-Thana’ al-Asbahani to clarify the meanings of Mukhtasar and explain its rulings. The book deals with basic concepts in the principles of jurisprudence, such as the limits of the principles of jurisprudence, its benefits, and the sections of knowledge, limit, and issue. It also focuses on the relationship between reason and Sharia in deriving legal rulings, and aims to clarify the jurisprudential rules and theological principles on which these principles depend.
descriptions.84: This book, “The History of Islamic Legislation” by Dr. Manna Al-Qattan, deals with the history of jurisprudential legislation in Islam from a historical and methodological perspective. The author focuses on the era of legislation from the beginning of the prophetic mission until the death of the Messenger, showing the state of the Arabs and the world at that time and the legislative mission of Islam. It also studies the main sources of legislation, which are the Qur’an and the Sunnah, and discusses the place of the Sunnah in Islamic legislation and the development of hadith science. The book aims to understand the origins of Islamic jurisprudence and its development throughout the ages, and its role in providing solutions to life’s problems in every era.
descriptions.85: This book is by the scholar Salah al-Din al-Ala’i, and it concerns an important topic in the principles of jurisprudence, which is the requirement of prohibiting corruption. In this research, the author addresses the issue of the ruling on prohibition in Islamic law, and studies the aspects of using the formula “no” in the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet, reviewing the opinions of imam scholars in this field. The book contains detailed discussions on this topic based on Qur’anic and Hadith evidence, and aims to provide a deeper understanding of the jurisprudential rules related to prohibitions and prohibitions.
descriptions.86: This book, “Graduation of Branches on Principles,” by Zanjani Abu al-Manaqib, deals with multiple jurisprudential topics related to the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules. It focuses on clarifying how to derive the branches of jurisprudence from the principles, relying on various jurisprudential issues that include acts of worship, transactions, punishments, and retaliation. The author aims to provide a clear methodology for understanding the connection between principles and branches in Islamic jurisprudence, trying to bridge the gap between scholars of principles and scholars of branches.
descriptions.87: The book “Tazim al-Fatwa” by Ibn al-Jawzi deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, explaining the conditions for fatwas and the importance of caution in expressing a legal opinion. The author points out that the scholars of the predecessors were investigating the necessary conditions before issuing fatwas, and warns against the recklessness of some caliphs in this area. The book focuses on the necessity of memorizing the Qur’an and Sunnah and understanding them correctly before being able to issue a fatwa, and mentions a severe threat to those who issue fatwas without possessing the necessary competence.
descriptions.88: The book “Report on Istihad fi Tafsir Ijtihad” by Al-Suyuti deals with the topic of Ijtihad in Islamic jurisprudence, reviewing its conditions and importance, and reviewing the opinions of scholars in this field. The book begins with a discussion of diligence as a sufficient obligation, then moves on to explain the conditions for diligence according to the views of various scholars, and concludes with a response to those who oppose the idea of ​​the existence of a diligent person in the present era.
descriptions.89: The book “Evaluating Consideration of Commonly Controversial Issues” by Ibn al-Dahan deals with disputed jurisprudential issues, and aims to evaluate consideration of them and bring the facts closer together. The book deals with issues of worship, transactions, marriage, and crimes, relying on the four schools of jurisprudence while introducing the Shafi’i doctrine. The book focuses on presenting controversial jurisprudential issues in a systematic manner, and aims to guide the reader to the correct consideration of these issues.
descriptions.90: This book, “Summary of Fundamental Principles,” by Hafez Thana Allah Al-Zahidi, deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence and its rules, as it focuses on the analysis of fundamental terminology and methods of inference from legal texts. The book begins by providing a definition of the principles of jurisprudence, its subject matter, and its benefits. Then it moves on to explaining the methods of deduction from texts according to the different schools of jurisprudence, with a focus on the jurisprudential statements deduced from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book is part of a scientific project to consolidate the correct fundamentalist awareness among students of science, while alerting to deviant opinions in jurisprudence and the importance of freedom from jurisprudential rigidity.
descriptions.91: This book, “Taysir al-Tahrir” by Amir Bad Shah, deals with topics in the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence. The author focuses on simplifying the concepts of jurisprudence and dividing jurisprudential vocabulary and formulas, while presenting his own investigations in the field of jurisprudential and jurisprudential sayings. The book aims to provide comprehensive and accessible scientific material in the field of jurisprudence, reviewing the sources and research of famous scholars in this field.
descriptions.92: This book, “Taysir Ilm Usul al-Fiqh,” by Dr. Abdullah Al-Jada’i, deals with the definitions and principles of the science of jurisprudence, and reviews the differences between fundamental and jurisprudential rules. It also studies the issues of jurisprudential rulings and discusses their types and categories, while addressing the concept of positive ruling and mandatory ruling. The book focuses on simplifying the concepts of this complex science and bringing them closer to the reader, while pointing out the importance of sincerity in seeking knowledge and its role in achieving the goals of Sharia.
descriptions.93: This book is part of a master’s thesis covering the explanation of “Revision of Chapters in Ilm al-Usul” by Shihab al-Din Ahmad bin Idris al-Qarafi. The research focuses on studying and investigating this explanation within a specific scientific method, based on an examination of the historical and scientific circumstances in which Al-Qarafi’s works emerged. The book deals with the author's life and era, and discusses the political, social and scientific situation at that time, and how it affected Al-Qarafi's intellectual production.
descriptions.94: The book “Jamaa’ al-Ilm” by Al-Shafi’i deals with topics in the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, focusing on the validity of prophetic news and the controls for accepting it. In this book, Al-Shafi’i presents the opinions of the various groups in confirming the news about the Prophet ﷺ, and explains the violations of some of them to the controls of legal reasoning, relying on the Qur’an and Sunnah as the basis of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.95: This book is a footnote by the scholar Hassan Al-Attar on the explanation of Al-Jalal Al-Mawlili for the book Collection of Al-Jami', and it is related to the topics of the principles of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence. In his footnote, Al-Attar discusses detailed definitions of fundamental terms such as jurisprudence, fundamentalism, obligation, obligation, recommended, recommended, evidence, knowledge, and ignorance. He also studies topics on sayings, what is spoken, what is understood, issues of obligation, the legal condition, and the legal ruling.
descriptions.96: This book deals with the Hadith of Misra from two main perspectives: narration and knowledge. Author Theeb Al-Qahtani focuses on studying the hadith in terms of its transmission and study, reviewing the sources and references of the hadith. The book aims to clarify the importance of following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in various aspects of life, whether worship or transactions, relying on the Prophet’s hadiths and verses from the Holy Qur’an to support its position.
descriptions.97: This is a book on the principles of jurisprudence that examines the issue of a single report and its validity. It deals in two chapters with what the single report is useful in terms of suspicion or knowledge, and the ruling on acting on it in fatwas, testimony, punishments, etc., with a discussion of the evidence of the prohibitors and a response to them.
descriptions.98: The book “Studies in the Principles of Jurisprudence” by Dr. Ali Ahmed Muhammad Babiker provides a comprehensive overview of the science of jurisprudence, addressing its definition, limits, and main topics. The book focuses on discussing the multiple definitions provided by scholars for the science of origins, and analyzing the reasons for this diversity in formulation and understanding. The book also addresses the main jurisprudential sources such as the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus, in addition to other jurisprudential and fundamental rules.
descriptions.99: A treatise on the principles of jurisprudence by Ibn Shihab al-Akbari, which dealt with defining the main concepts of the principles of jurisprudence, such as the obligatory, the permissible, the forbidden, the recommended, the valid Sunnahs, and the Sunnah, clarifying the differences between them and determining their meanings and controls in Islamic law. The book focuses on explaining these concepts and explaining their provisions and limits, relying on Sharia evidence and jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.100: Latifa’s treatise on the principles of jurisprudence provides a comprehensive overview of the science of jurisprudence, explaining its comprehensive and partial evidence and how to use it in deriving legal rulings. The author focuses on defining the principles of jurisprudence and explaining their importance in diligence and legal consideration, with an explanation of the concept of the five main jurisprudential rulings and their classifications. The book aims to provide clear and easy-to-understand scientific material for those who wish to study the principles of jurisprudence.
descriptions.101: This book deals with the topic of caring for interest and wisdom in Islamic legislation, reviewing the definition of interest, its types, and its importance in understanding Sharia rulings. The author focuses on the necessity of studying purposes and interests when interpreting legal texts, and discusses the views of jurists on justifying rulings by interests, while emphasizing the importance of understanding the goals and objectives for which God has enacted rulings. The book aims to show the importance of studying stated and deduced interests and explaining them to people to renew jurisprudence and activate it.
descriptions.102: This book is an explanation of Ibn al-Hajib’s summary of the principles of jurisprudence, written by Taj al-Din al-Subki to study the legislative principles of jurisprudential rules. The book deals with the definition of jurisprudence and the mechanisms of reasoning, and reviews important concepts such as analogy, exception, and verbal participation, with a focus on clarifying the principles of jurisprudential principles and their applications.
descriptions.103: Rawdat al-Nazir and Jannat al-Mandahir fi Usul al-Fiqh is a book in the field of fundamentals of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, in which its author, al-Maqdisi Muwaffaq al-Din, deals with multiple topics related to the foundations of reasoning and proof in Islamic law, with a focus on the arguments of evidence, its rules, and the sections of legal ruling. The book aims to clarify the correct approach in understanding and applying jurisprudential rulings, reviewing important concepts such as proof, analogy, limitation, and legal ruling.
descriptions.104: This book deals with seven important issues in the science of jurisprudential disagreement, showing the differences between fixed definite matters in which there is no room for opinion and speculative matters that require diligence and disagreement. The author focuses on the importance of understanding these issues for those who wish to study the provisions of Sharia, and points out the necessity of accepting certainties and not delving into what is related to them, while encouraging the use of reason and understanding in understanding speculative matters. The book is a classification of the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.105: This book, “Explanation of Waving on Clarification,” by its author Al-Taftazani, deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence and its rules. It reviews the definitions of the principles of jurisprudence from various aspects, discusses the Sharia evidence and its classifications, with a focus on interpreting the words of the Qur’an and the Hadith and explaining their meanings and rules. It includes a detailed analysis of the metaphorical uses of words and how to understand them in the context of the Sharia evidence.
descriptions.106: The book “Explanation of Jurisprudential Rules” by the scholar Ahmed Al-Zarqa provides a detailed explanation of the main jurisprudential rules, reviewing each rule from two perspectives: explanation and application. The book deals with the interpretation of the meanings of the rules and their objectives, then shows their applications in various fields of jurisprudence, noting the necessary exceptions and caveats. The book focuses on the importance of understanding the objectives of actions and words in applying Sharia rulings, and reviews the applications of rules in sections of jurisprudence, such as financial transactions, contracts, guarantees, penalties, and others.
descriptions.107: Explanation of the enlightening planet by the Hanbali jurist Taqi al-Din Ibn al-Najjar is an interpretation of the summary of the liberation of the principles of jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought. The book deals with scientific definitions of the word and its meaning, types of metaphor, and legal rulings, relying on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah in its treatment of jurisprudential and fundamentalist topics.
descriptions.108: The book “The Characteristics of the Fatwa, the Mufti, and the Questioner” by Imam Ibn Hamdan deals with the topics of jurisprudence and its principles related to the fatwa, explaining the conditions for the mufti and the questioner and how to obtain a fatwa, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the legal controls in giving fatwas and warning against the spread of wrong fatwas among the ignorant and foolish.
descriptions.109: This book, “Aqd al-Jayid fi Ahkam al-Ijtihad wal-Taqlid,” by Dehlawi Shah Waliullah, deals with the topics of the principles of jurisprudence related to ijtihad and taqlid. The author focuses on clarifying the reality of ijtihad, its conditions, and its divisions, and discusses the differences between the absolute diligent, the diligent scholar of the doctrine, the memorizer of the books of the doctrine, and the layman. The book aims to explain the concept of ijtihad, its conditions, and how to achieve it, while discussing some important jurisprudential issues related to this topic.
descriptions.110: In his book, “The Science of the Fundamentals of Jurisprudence and the Summary of the History of Legislation,” Abdul-Wahhab Khalaf presents a detailed study of the foundations of Islamic jurisprudence and its rules. In the book, he deals with legal evidence such as the Qur’an, the Sunnah, consensus, and others, and discusses the fundamental linguistic rules and their applications in jurisprudence. The book also presents a glimpse into the author's life and his scientific and practical career, indicating his contributions in the fields of Islamic law and Arab culture.
descriptions.111: This book, “The Science of the Fundamentals of Jurisprudence” by Abdul-Wahhab Khlaf, covers the topics of the science of the foundations of jurisprudence in a comprehensive manner, as it explains the types of legal evidence such as the Qur’an, the Sunnah, consensus, analogy, and others. It also details the legal rulings and their classifications. The book aims to clarify the difference between jurisprudence and the science of jurisprudence, and provides an in-depth analysis of the foundations of deduction in Islamic law.
descriptions.112: This book deals with the subject of legal objectives in Islam, and it is one of the fundamentalist works that relate to the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules. The author, Nour al-Din al-Khademi, focuses on defining objectives and explaining their relationship to other fundamental terms, and points out their importance in diligence and jurisprudential deduction. The book also deals with the history of research into objectives and their development throughout the ages, and reviews their benefits in achieving legitimate interests and warding off evil. The book aims to clarify how to use Maqasid correctly in accordance with Sharia controls, while emphasizing its importance in understanding Sharia evidence and applying it in practice.
descriptions.113: This book is an explanation of the brief book “Lubb Al-Usul” by Zakaria Al-Ansari, and aims to clarify the concepts of jurisprudential principles and the rules of deduction. The book deals with multiple topics in the principles of jurisprudence, such as duties, prohibitions, absolutes, and restrictions, relying in its explanation on the expressions of his sheikh, the scholar Al-Mahli, for their clarity and good writing. The author seeks to simplify the meanings and explain the difficult pronunciation to facilitate understanding the jurisprudential rules and their application in the life of a Muslim.
descriptions.114: This book, “Winking the Eyes of Insight in Sharh al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir,” is an interpretation of the rules and principles of jurisprudence, focusing on explaining important concepts such as intention, certainty, and doubt. The author, Ahmed bin Muhammad Makki Al-Hamwi, deals with the general rules in jurisprudence and points out the importance of intention in acts of worship and its conditions. He also explains important rules in the principles of jurisprudence, such as the rule of certainty that is not removed by doubt and the rule of origin regarding things that are permissible. The book aims to clarify these rules and explain their meanings and applications in Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.115: “Fath al-Qadeer” may mean the following: Fath al-Qadeer, a book by Al-Shawkani. Fath Al-Qadeer for the Helpless and Poor, a book by Ibn Al-Hammam Al-Hanafi.
descriptions.116: Qawati’ al-Ilwal is a book on the fundamentals of Islamic jurisprudence, written by Al-Hafiz Abu al-Muzaffar al-Sam’ani (426 AH - 489 AH). In his book, the author spoke about the introductions to the fundamentals of jurisprudence, and the sections of speech, commands, general and specific, general and clear, narrations, abrogated and abrogated, consensus, analogy, ijtihad, and other fundamentalist chapters. The book al-Qawat’ al-Usul by Abu al-Muzaffar al-Sama’ani is considered one of the most important books written in the fundamentals of jurisprudence. The author wrote it in a unique and wonderful style, in which he benefited greatly and was brilliant, because even though he classified it in the manner of theologians, he mixed it with some jurisprudence, as jurists do. Al-Hafiz Al-Subki said in the Shafi’i Tabaqat:
descriptions.117: Qawi’ al-Ahkam fi Masalih al-Anam, or Qawi’ al-Ahkam fi Islah al-Anam, is a book by Imam al-Izz ibn Abd al-Salam on jurisprudence and the principles of jurisprudence. It is considered his greatest book, the pinnacle of his production, and the deepest of his research. It is the conclusive evidence of the imamate of al-‘Izz in ijtihad and principles. Therefore, Taj al-Din al-Subki said: “Among the works of Sheikh Izz al-Din are “Al-Qa’id al-Kubra” and the book “The Metaphor of the Qur’an,” and these two books bear witness to his imamate and his great status in the sciences. Sharia law, and the major rules are reduced to minor rules and the metaphor is in another.” …
descriptions.118: This book, “Rules of Jurisprudence” by Al-Barakati, deals with the origins of controversial issues in Hanafi jurisprudence and the general rules of jurisprudence. The author focuses on discussing the jurisprudential disagreements between ancient scholars, while presenting rules and principles that help in understanding and clarifying these disagreements. The book also includes a study of Arabic vowel words and how to employ them in Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.119: The book Al-Talkhis fi Usul al-Fiqh by al-Juwayni Abu al-Ma’ali deals with the definitions and principles of jurisprudence from a linguistic and terminological perspective, explaining the truth of jurisprudence and its evidence, and addressing the concept of knowledge, definition, and adjective. The book focuses on clarifying the terms of the principles of jurisprudence and the conditions for their validity, relying on the distinction between reason, knowledge, and consideration, and explaining the meanings of assignment, duty, recommended, and disliked.
descriptions.120: This book, “Kashf al-Asrar Sharh Usul al-Bazdawi,” is an interpretation and explanation of the principles of jurisprudence written by Alaa al-Din al-Bukhari. The book deals with various definitions and sections of jurisprudence, such as the specific, the general, the common, and the interpreted, as well as the differences between interpretation and interpretation, and reviews other sections of jurisprudential principles such as truth, metaphor, explicit, and metaphor. The book aims to clarify the methods of Sharia law, the rules of religion, and its teachings in a detailed and comprehensive manner.
descriptions.121: This book deals with issues of the matter in the principles of jurisprudence, reviewing Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah’s criticism of these issues in a collection of his fatwas. Al-Ruhaili focuses on Ibn Taymiyyah’s approach in criticizing fundamentalist rules, relying on an analysis of the issue of will to command and rule with a single action that is commanded and forbidden. The book aims to understand the foundations of jurisprudence through Ibn Taymiyyah’s critical methodology, while providing an overview of his scientific and practical biography.
descriptions.122: Principles of assets. A book dictated by the Algerian Imam Abdel Hamid Ibn Badis, known as Ibn Badis, on the principles of jurisprudence. Published by the National Publishing and Distribution Company, investigated by Dr. Ammar Al-Talbi. The investigator Ammar Al-Talbi said in defining the book: “An important treatise from Imam Ibn Badis on the science of principles, in which his scientific activity was connected to the activity of his ancient predecessors, and with it he revived scientific research and consideration of the principles and the method. He was not satisfied with the branches, as was the custom of later jurists who limited themselves to particulars, and paid little attention to the universals on which they are based.”
descriptions.123: This book is written by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and deals with the topic of ijtihad and disagreement in Islamic jurisprudence. It focuses on discussing the rules and principles that govern ijtihad and the emergence of disagreement among jurists, reviewing the opinions of scholars about the validity of the words of the Companions and Rightly Guided Caliphs in the face of the opinions of others. The book is part of the works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and constitutes a contribution to the field of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.124: This book is a collection of benefits and explanations on a system of jurisprudential rules, written by Saleh Al-Asmari to explain the meanings of the rules, their divisions, and their applications. The book deals with the definition of the jurisprudential rule, discusses the differences between it and the jurisprudential rule, reviews the sections of the various jurisprudential rules, and mentions the importance of codifying them. The book also explains the main jurisprudential rules, such as the rule of matters according to their objectives, the rule of religion based on bringing interests and warding off harm, and the rule of hardship brings ease, while clarifying its meanings, rulings, and jurisprudential applications.
descriptions.125: The book, “The Advantages of Sharia and the Disadvantages of Man-made Laws,” provides a comprehensive overview of the advantages of Islamic Sharia and its perfection in achieving goodness in various aspects of life, comparing that to what the author considers to be the negatives of man-made laws. Sheikh Attiya Salem focuses on the fact that benevolence includes all aspects of life, from verbal speech to daily transactions, through morals and judiciary, explaining how Islamic law calls for benevolence in everything, even in matters whose meaning people may ignore, such as slaughter and killing. The book also deals with the practical application of Sharia in judiciary and transactions, relying on jurisprudential principles and jurisprudential rules.
descriptions.126: This is a summary of the book Al-Mu'amil fi Al-Radd ila Al-Amr Al-Awwal, compiled by the scholar Imam Shihab Al-Din Abu Shamah. The book deals with the foundations of jurisprudence and the rules of jurisprudence, reviews the virtues of Imam Al-Shafi'i and his virtue in spreading science, and mentions the importance of referring to the books of the Sunnah and the texts of the imams in following the Quran and the Sunnah, while warning against blind imitation and stating the virtue of scholars who were interested in verifying legal evidence.
descriptions.127: This book, “A Memorandum on the Principles of Jurisprudence” by Al-Shanqeeti Muhammad Al-Amin, deals with various scientific topics in the field of the principles of jurisprudence, including the reality of the ruling and its parts, the conditions for assignment, what is recommended and what is disliked, and the need for rules and principles that regulate jurisprudence. It aims to provide a methodology for understanding legal texts and applying them to new facts, while emphasizing the importance of deduction and correct understanding of religious texts. The book focuses on developing understandings of legal rulings and organizing their topics into specific sections and chapters, taking into account the historical development of the science of principles and its applications in Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.128: This book by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi deals with the topic of invoking Al-Shafi’i in jurisprudence and its principles, and reviews the views of scholars on Al-Shafi’i’s narration of the hadith and the acceptance of his hadiths by Al-Bukhari and others. The author focuses on discussing the objections of some scholars to Al-Shafi’i and answers them, indicating his scientific and jurisprudential status among the imams. The book falls within the scope of the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules and aims to clarify the authority of Al-Shafi’i’s statements and correct any doubts that may arise around them.
descriptions.129: This book deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence from the perspective of the Sunnis and the community, and reviews the definition of this science, its subject, sources, and benefits. It also deals with the history of the development of the science of jurisprudence through the ages, focusing on the contributions of prominent Sunni scholars such as Imam Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Taymiyyah, and Ibn Al-Qayyim. The book aims to explain the importance of this science in understanding and applying Islamic law.
descriptions.130: Knowledge of Hadith sciences and the quantity of its types. The second book classified in the science of hadith after the book Al-Ramhurmuzi (The Hadith Separator between the Narrator and the Conscious One), it was classified by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hakim Al-Naysaburi.
descriptions.131: This book deals with the topic of the principles of jurisprudence, as it focuses on the position of guidance between tradition and ijtihad. The author, Sheikh Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Mubarak, aims to explore the concept of guidance in Islamic jurisprudence and the issues related to it in the field of tradition and ijtihad. The book falls within the category of scientific books specialized in the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, and aims to provide a comprehensive overview of its subject, relying on the approach of the Salaf in understanding and applying Islamic law.
descriptions.132: This book, written by Zakaria bin Ghulam Qadir al-Pakistani, deals with the subject of the principles of jurisprudence from the perspective of the scholars of hadith. The author focuses on clarifying the rules and principles upon which the jurisprudence of Ahl al-Hadith is based, relying on the literal interpretation of texts and the understanding of the righteous predecessors.
