It also refers to the praise of previous scholars for the jurisprudence of Ahl al-Hadith and their role in preserving Islamic law from heresies and distortions.
descriptions.133: This book deals with the approach and wisdom of Islamic legislation, focusing on the meaning of the approach and Islam in legal language and terminology. The author focuses on explaining the concept of submission and submission to God Almighty through belief, affirmation, and action, and discusses the differences between faith and Islam from a legal perspective. The book is a classification of the principles of jurisprudence and jurisprudential rules, and aims to clarify the principles of Islamic legislation and the wisdom of Sharia in organizing the lives of Muslims.
descriptions.134: This book, “Nuzhat al-Ain al-Nawazir fi the Science of Faces and Analogies” by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, deals with the subject of the science of faces and counterparts in the Holy Qur’an, which is a branch of the science of jurisprudence. The book aims to clarify the different meanings intended for a single word mentioned in different places in the Qur’an, while preserving its pronunciation and vowels, while its interpretations and connotations differ. The book also addresses the efforts made by previous scholars in this field, and points out the importance of understanding these aspects and counterparts to derive the correct meanings from the Qur’anic texts.
descriptions.135: This book deals with the theory of the objectives of jurisprudence according to Imam Al-Shatibi, reviewing its historical origins and its development throughout the ages. Author Ahmed Al-Raisuni focuses on the importance of the Maqasid theory in understanding the goals and objectives of Sharia law, and points out the necessity of moving the Muslim mind from focusing on particulars to paying attention to generalities and general objectives. The book aims to clarify ways to achieve Sharia objectives and understand them more deeply, while pointing out the importance of this theory in rebuilding contemporary Islamic thought.
descriptions.136: Nihayat al-Sul Sharh Minhaj al-Wusool is a book on the principles of jurisprudence in which al-Isnawi explains the book “Minhaj al-Wusool ila Ilm al-Usul” by Ibn al-Baydawi. The book deals with the definitions of jurisprudential principles and their divisions, discusses the legal ruling and its elements, and reviews the ruler, the ruled, and the ruled. The book aims to clarify the principles of fundamentals and its applications, based on classic sources in this field.
descriptions.137: This book, written by Sheikh Ibn Baz, deals with the topic of the obligation to follow the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the disbelief of those who deny it. It focuses on the principles considered in proving legal rulings, indicating the importance of the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Prophet in Islamic legislation. It also refers to the evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah on the necessity of following and adhering to the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.138: This book deals with authentic hadiths from Sahih Muslim, where Al-Maqdisi Diya al-Din focuses on narrating the hadiths in their original form, while mentioning their transmission chains. The book begins with a hadith by Abdullah bin Masoud, and continues by presenting other hadiths by prominent Islamic figures, pointing out the authenticity of those hadiths and the methods of narrating them. The book aims to number the hadiths automatically and present them in a systematic way to facilitate study and research.
descriptions.139: This book includes hadiths collected and narrated by Affan bin Muslim Al-Saffar, and it is one of the hadith books that are numbered automatically. The book deals with the series of hadith narrations through a series of narrators, starting from Affan bin Muslim and ending with the oldest narrators, with a focus on transmitting hadiths and documenting them accurately.
descriptions.140: This book contains hadiths transmitted by Yazid bin Abi Habib Al-Masry, and it is one of the hadith books that includes a series of hadith narrations in the form of chain of transmission and text. The book deals with a group of hadiths attributed to the Companions and followers, relying on multiple methods of transmitting and narrating them.
descriptions.141: This book, written by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, is related to the topic of the Tasbih prayer and its virtues, based on multiple hadiths and narrations. The book discusses several councils and methods in discussing this topic, citing the sayings of the Companions and scholars regarding the Tasbih prayer and how to perform it.
descriptions.142: This book is a collection of Prophetic hadiths numbered consecutively. It begins with the first hadith and continues until hadith thirty. In each hadith, the author Ibn Jama`ah deals with a chain of narrators connected to the other, providing an authentic chain of transmission for each hadith that ends with one of the companions (may Allah be pleased with him). The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and presenting the chains of their narrations.
descriptions.143: This book is a collection of Prophetic hadiths extracted from the six well-known books in the science of hadith, and it was arranged and divided by Al-Nabulsi Abu Al-Muzaffar. The book deals with multiple topics from the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, his sayings, and his actions, relying on the automatic digitizer to organize the hadiths.
descriptions.144: Al-Akhbar Al-Muwafiqiyat by Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar is a hadith book that contains hadiths and narrations that are numbered automatically. It appears from its first excerpt that it deals with dialogues and historical events related to rulers and princes, with a focus on some social and political issues of that time.
descriptions.145: This book includes forty numbered hadiths, and falls within the framework of the hadith parts that are numbered automatically. In this work, the author Musafer Haji deals with a group of noble Prophetic hadiths, presenting them in a numbered manner that helps in arrangement and organization, while preserving the original meaning and content of the narrations.
descriptions.146: This book contains forty mechanically numbered hadiths of the Prophet, covering the speeches of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The first hadith of the book deals with a sermon by the Prophet on his beautiful camel, where he talks about death and the facts associated with it, and brings up the idea of ​​returning to the dead who are considered to be on a short journey to return to them. The book aims to transfer and preserve the Prophet’s hadiths, understand them, and apply them in daily life.
descriptions.147: The book “The Forty Narrations of Malik on the authority of Nafi’” by Al-Suyuti consists of forty hadiths, all of which were narrated on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar (may Allah be pleased with them both). The book deals with a group of prophetic hadiths narrated with this chain of transmission. It begins with a hadith explaining the virtue of the afternoon prayer, followed by another hadith urging not to be careful about prayer times, and then mentions a hadith related to the intention of the early Muslims to perform ablution from a single vessel.
descriptions.148: The Book of Forty on the Virtue of Supplication and the Callers is a collection of selected prophetic hadiths that relate to the virtue of supplication and its importance in the life of a Muslim, and also includes recommended supplications in specific situations and times of the day. The book covers various topics, from supplication after eating to recommended supplications when leaving the house or entering the cemetery, through to ruqyah and recommended supplications at specific times.
descriptions.149: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by the sheikhs of Hijaz, where the author, Ali bin Omar Al-Harbi, quotes hadiths from multiple sources and presents them in a selected and concise manner. The book deals with various topics from Muslim life and worship, with a focus on hadiths related to Hajj, Umrah, prayer, and other Islamic worship. The book is distinguished by presenting the hadiths in an automatically numbered manner, which makes it easier for the reader to access the information he wants to search for.
descriptions.150: This book deals with the series of hadiths and hadiths, which are the hadiths about which the preservation of the hadith is doubtful because the appearance of the wording or content is a clear indication that they are not authentic. It was written by Abu Al-Rabi’ Al-Kala’i, a preacher and scholar of hadith, based on what he heard from his sheikhs, and the jurist Al-Tajibi took from him on this subject. The book aims to warn against fabricated hadiths and pay attention to what indicates the authenticity of communication, while following the doctrine of preservation in this regard.
descriptions.151: Al-Mu'jam Al-Latif is one of Al-Dhahabi's works. It is a collection of hadiths and narrations compiled in a dictionary, which deals with various topics related to morals, worship, and Islamic jurisprudence. The book is distinguished by its presentation of narrations in various hadith frameworks, while pointing out the validity or weakness of some of them, which makes it a useful reference for researchers of the Prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.152: This book is part of the selections of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim al-Maqdisi, and it was collected and digitized by Ibn al-Kamal al-Hanbali. The book covers multiple prophetic hadiths, and each hadith begins with a sequential chain of narrators, then the hadith text follows. The book focuses on religious and spiritual topics, reviewing two promises of Paradise and what God has prepared for righteous believers.
descriptions.153: The book “Al-Mawfiyyat Al-Tasnaiyat” by Al-Damiyati Abd al-Mu’min ibn Khalaf is a collection of the Prophet’s hadiths, numbered automatically, and deals with various topics from good morals to the provisions of Islamic law. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths in a sequential and organized manner, relying on an authentic chain of transmission in its transmission of narrations.
descriptions.154: This book, written by Ibn Wahb, is related to judicial issues in sales, as it addresses multiple issues related to the sale of slaves, inheritance, debts, and conditions in contracts. It focuses on the legal rulings related to financial and commercial transactions, relying on the Prophet’s hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas.
descriptions.155: This book by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani deals with the grading of the hadiths mentioned in the beautiful names of God Almighty, which is the designation that includes positive divine expressions that reflect the great attributes of God. Al-Asqalani focuses on the hadith, “Allah has ninety-nine names. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise,” and details the hadiths related to these names, showing the authenticity and accuracy of each hadith.
descriptions.156: This book is written by Al-Dhahabi, and it is a detailed translation of Imam Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj Al-Qushayri (may Allah have mercy on him), with mentioning of authentic narrators. The book deals with his biography and the lives of his hadith narrators, and mentions the names of the scholars from whom Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan, one of the narrators of Sahih Muslim, narrated. It also indicates his scientific and spiritual status among his peers.
descriptions.157: This book is part of the hadith of Abu Orouba al-Harrani. It contains a group of prophetic hadiths that are numbered automatically. These hadiths were narrated through a series of narrators starting from Abu Orouba to Antioch. The part deals with various topics related to practical and religious life, including those related to marriage, purity, charity, and fasting, in addition to hadiths related to morals and transactions.
descriptions.158: This part of the Hadith Graduation by Sheikh Al-Abdiyya Abu Al-Hasan Al-Abdi contains the narration of prophetic hadiths through their connected chains, relying on the narrations of his sheikhs and scholars. The book addresses multiple topics from good manners and mercy, to faith and good deeds, through the provisions of prayer and zakat, thus providing a comprehensive reference for the automatically numbered hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.159: The book “Part of the Hadith of Those Who Sell Allegiance with Option” was written by Abd al-Azim al-Mundhiri, and it is part of the hadith parts that are numbered automatically. The book deals with a hadith related to the right of option in sales, and reviews the chain of transmission of the hadith, mentioning the narrators and hadith scholars who narrated it.
descriptions.160: This book is written by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, and it is related to a jurisprudential research on a hadith related to the prohibition of cursing the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The author focuses on the issue of determining its chain of transmission: whether it is from the chain of transmission of Abu Hurairah, Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, or both, reviewing different narrations of the hadith and discussing the opinions of scholars about it. The book is part of a collection of hadith parts that are numbered automatically, and aims to clarify an important issue in the science of hadith and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.161: This book is a collection of mechanically numbered hadiths of the Prophet, dealing with the hadith related to Ibn Abi al-Makarim. The author presents a series of hadith narrations, starting with Sheikh Imam Ibn Abi al-Makarim, passing through multiple hadiths from sources, and its content is dominated by authentic hadiths reported by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj and other scholars.
descriptions.162: This book includes a hadith about a Bedouin who presented a lizard to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and challenged him to believe in him. The Prophet responded to his supplication and spoke to the lizard, speaking in a clear Arabic language. It is one of the many hadiths that are narrated in hadith books and carries meanings of affirmation of the power of God and His Messenger. The book is classified by Al-Tabarani as one of the hadith parts that are numbered automatically.
descriptions.163: This book deals with a discussion of the poetry of Al-Nabigha Al-Jaadi and his tribute to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, focusing on Abu Al-Yaman Al-Kindi’s narration of a poetic story and the story of his ode through a series of connected narratives. The book is concerned with presenting hadiths related to this topic in a machine-numbered manner, which facilitates access to and analysis of information.
descriptions.164: This book deals with five serial hadiths, which are hadiths connected to a single chain of transmission that goes back to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author, Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi, focuses on presenting these hadiths, relying on their serial chain of transmission, and mentions each hadith with its narrator and chains of transmission, indicating its importance in the hadith heritage.
descriptions.165: This book deals with the topic of the handshake by narrating several prophetic hadiths about it. The author begins by narrating hadiths about shaking hands through various documents, reviewing narrations from the texts of hadiths on the authority of the companions Jundub ibn Abi Buraida and Anas ibn Malik. The book aims to collect hadiths related to handshakes and document them, relying on trustworthy narrators for their chain of transmission.
descriptions.166: The book “Awali Abu Bakr bin Abdul-Daim” deals with a collection of automatically numbered prophetic hadiths. It focuses on transmitting the hadith chains and their narrators in the form of serial chain of transmission, while preserving the original modernization formula. The book addresses multiple topics from the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, including jihad, martyrdom, and financial and ethical dealings.
descriptions.167: The book “The Benefits of Al-Faryabi” is a collection of automatically numbered prophetic hadiths. It deals with various topics of legal rulings and provisions, including the Prophet’s prohibition against killing women and children, and his prohibition against swearing by the names of fathers, with a focus on the chain of transmission of the hadiths and their narrators. The book combines practical benefits with religious teachings, providing a useful reference for researchers of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.168: This book includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, which deals with multiple topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, relying on connected and disparate documents in their sources. It focuses on transmitting the hadiths in their original form with attribution, without interpretation or commentary, which makes it an important reference for researchers of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.169: This book, “Qudwa Al-Ghazi,” by Ibn Abi Zaminin, deals with the topic of jihad and traveling for the sake of God from a legal and jurisprudential perspective. It focuses on the encouragement of conquest and the virtues of the invaders, and discusses the good morals that the invader should follow, and what is permissible and what is not permissible for him to do in terms of actions and words. The book includes hadiths and Quranic verses related to invasion and jihad, and organizes them into multiple sections that address various aspects of this topic.
descriptions.170: This book covers forty hadiths on the virtues of remembering God Almighty, accompanied by a legal chain of transmission. The author Musafir Haji focuses on presenting the noble Prophetic hadiths that show the virtue of contemplating God and constant remembrance of Him, relying on the narration of the hadiths in their chain of transmission. The book targets those who are interested in the Prophetic hadiths and students of knowledge who wish to learn about the virtues and benefits of dhikr.
descriptions.171: This book from Muwatta Ibn Wahb deals with the topic of warfare and discusses the legal rulings related to it, reviewing hadiths and narrations attributed to the Companions and followers. He focuses on the rulings related to fighting and battles, relying on the narration of Yunus bin Abdul-Ala al-Sadfi on the authority of his father. The book also includes a hadith related to the story of a man whose hands and feet were cut off for carrying weapons against Muslims, linked to a verse from the Holy Qur’an that talks about warriors.
descriptions.172: This book is a collection of scholarly councils held over several years. It contains various prophetic narrations and hadiths narrated by Ibn Mandah on the authority of his sheikhs. Each council begins with a narration or hadith that begins with “tell us,” followed by a continuous narration series. The book deals with multiple topics from the Prophet’s hadiths, varying in content between news, directives, and stories, arranged in a sequential documentary manner according to the dates of the councils in which they were held.
descriptions.173: Musnad Uqba bin Aamir is a book that collects the hadiths of the great companion Uqba bin Aamir al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him), and it was collected and arranged by the Sheikh Imam, the scholar Zain al-Din Qasim al-Hanafi. The book contains biographies and hadiths of some scholars such as Dhul-Nun al-Misri, Bakr bin Qutaybah al-Qadi, and Abu Jaafar al-Tahawi, in addition to the hadiths of Uqba bin Amer on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.174: This book, “The Sheikhs of Ibn Jama’ah,” deals with the hadith narrators and the sheikhs of the hadith scholars, arranging their names according to the alphabet. The author Badr al-Din Ibn Jama`ah focuses on mentioning his sheikhs and teachers, indicating their scholarly standing and their advantages in transmitting and preserving hadith. The book aims to provide a summary for those who wish to belong to the scholars of hadith and get to know their sheikhs, taking into account the organized arrangement according to the letters of the dictionary.
descriptions.175: This book contains a collection of automatically numbered Prophetic hadiths, which deals with various topics related to morals, transactions, and worship. The book begins with a hadith about the returnee of his gift, and contains other hadiths about justice in distributing money among children, a warning against controversy in the Qur’an, and the story of the Prophet Muhammad dyeing his beard with yellow.
descriptions.176: This book includes a collection of automatically numbered Prophetic hadiths, with a variety of topics, including morals, acts of worship, and sermons. The first hadith deals with the ruling on taking something out of the mosque and throwing it, while the second hadith focuses on warning the worshiper not to spit while facing the qiblah. As for the third hadith, it mentions Abu Darda’’s advice regarding the importance of piety and performing prayers on time. The fourth hadith reviews the Prophet’s warning against turning around during prayer, along with his permissibility of voluntary prayer.
descriptions.177: This book is a compilation of the narrations of the sheikhs of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal from the Book of Confirmations, compiled and compiled by al-Maqdisi Diya al-Din Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahid. The book deals with the narrations of a number of sheikhs, such as Muhammad ibn Bishr and Muhammad ibn Saqiq, and reviews the series of chains of narrations with precision and care, relying on graduation and verification of the authenticity of the hadiths.
descriptions.178: This book is the ultimate desire of the listeners in the realms of the hadiths of the Successors. It is a compilation of the hadiths of the Successors and their followers. It focuses on the chains of transmission that end with five narrators between the author and the hadith. The book covers a group of narrators and chains of transmission, and aims to present hadiths of high scientific value and connected to a strong narrative chain. The book is an important reference in the field of Prophetic Hadith and Hadith studies.
descriptions.179: This book is a collection of poems written by the ascetic Sheikh Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Fanjuwih Al-Thaqafi, and it contains a narration of the virtues of the month of Ramadan. In it, the conversation about the virtue of this blessed month is narrated through serial narrations from eminent scholars and imams, in which Ibn Fanjuwayh is mentioned as he narrates what he learned from other scholars. The book is one of the hadith parts that are numbered automatically, and it aims to spread science and religious knowledge related to the month of Ramadan.
descriptions.180: This book is a collection of the hadiths and hopes of the ascetic Sheikh Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Fanjuwih Al-Thaqafi on the virtues of the month of Ramadan. The volume covers a hadith narrated by the author through a series of narrators, and is classified among the automatically numbered hadith parts.
descriptions.181: Al-Sari bin Sahl’s copy is a collection of the Prophet’s hadiths, numbered automatically, dealing with various topics, including legal rulings and fatwas on matters of jurisprudence and acts of worship. The book contains supported hadiths that begin with hadiths about performing ablution with wine in the absence of water, and moves on to discussing the ruling on cursing the dead, then deals with a description of the condition of some people at the end of time, and finally mentions a ruling regarding vows of silence and seclusion.
descriptions.182: This book, “Wasl Balaghat al-Muwatta” by Ibn al-Salah, deals with investigating the chains of transmission of hadiths that were not transmitted in Imam Malik’s Muwatta, which are known as reports and correspondences. The author was interested in verifying the four hadiths for which Ibn Abd al-Barr did not find a connected chain of transmission, and he presented them in a special message. The book aims to correct some misconceptions about the authenticity of the hadiths of Al-Muwatta, and provides valuable investigations for those working in hadith science.
descriptions.183: This book deals with the reason for the serial hadith on the two Eids, and combines the hadiths related to the two Eids, with chain of transmission and chain of transmission. The author, Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, focuses on documenting the narration of the hadith on the day of Eid between the prayer and the sermon, and carefully reviews the chain of transmission. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with studying and documenting the chains of transmission of the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.184: This book, “Etiquette of Companionship” by Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, deals with the subject of etiquette and ethics of companionship among people, addressing various types of social relationships such as friendship, clan, and the company of parents and children, with an emphasis on the importance of choosing wise, scholarly, and pious friends, and avoiding the company of ignorant people. The book focuses on the guidance of the Qur’an and Sunnah in dealing with others, and emphasizes forgiveness, tolerance, and cooperation in meeting the needs of others.
descriptions.185: This book includes hadiths by Abu Orouba al-Harrani, narrated by al-Hakim Abu Ahmad, and it contains a collection of prophetic hadiths related to marriage, divorce, waiting period, and other jurisprudential issues related to marriage. The book also covers some hadiths related to other social and legal matters, presenting multiple narrations on similar topics to ensure the authenticity and strength of the hadiths.
descriptions.186: This book is part of the Prophet’s hadiths and is concerned with the narration of Abu Al-Zubayr Muhammad bin Muslim on the authority of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The book covers narrations about Abdullah bin Omar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Usayd, Abdullah bin Amr, Abu Hurairah and other companions, and focuses on narrations that were not mentioned in the narration of Jabir bin Zaid. The book is classified by Abu Al-Sheikh Al-Asbahani and is included in the hadith parts.
descriptions.187: The book “Hadiths of Al-Shamukhi” is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It deals with multiple topics related to morals, worship, and transactions, focusing on warning against lying, cheating, and deception, while highlighting the importance of knowledge and spreading it among people. The book is distinguished by the sequential chain of transmission in the narration of hadiths, which reflects the method of hadith scholars in collecting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.188: This book deals with a collection of Prophetic hadiths related to six different meanings, and it has been arranged in a way that focuses on understanding and interpreting those meanings through the hadiths associated with them. The author relies on a series of narrations connected to different hadiths to explain and clarify these meanings, which makes him an important reference in understanding hadiths and their rulings.
descriptions.189: This book contains prophetic hadiths with chain of narrations from nineteen of Ibn Tabarzad’s companions. The hadith mainly deals with the biographies of the Companions, their sayings, and their actions, relying on multiple methods of transmitting hadiths. It focuses on presenting historical narratives according to well-known modern terminology.
descriptions.190: This book deals with prophetic hadiths that disparage theologians and its people, as they were selected by Imam Abu al-Fadl al-Muqri from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami’s response to the people of theology. The book focuses on hadiths that highlight the importance of avoiding exaggeration in speech and preferring contemplation of God’s creation over contemplation of God’s essence, relying on a series of hadith chains of transmission related to scholars and narrators.
descriptions.191: This book includes prophetic hadiths narrated from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, classified into sevens, which are sequential hadiths with connected names of narrators. The hadith addresses many topics, such as dyeing hair, the call to prayer for Hajj and Umrah, and the importance of giving one’s real name and not a nickname, based on the narration of Maroun bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari on the authority of Hamid Al-Tawil. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and classifying prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.192: This book contains hadiths from the authentic Musnad, compiled and narrated by Abu Hamid Ibn al-Sharqi. In his narration of hadiths, the author relies on a series of narrators, and presents multiple texts of hadith narrations from companions and ancestors. The hadiths revolve around religious and devotional topics, relying on reliable sources to support the hadith.
descriptions.193: This book contains hadiths from the battles of Musa bin Uqba, and it is one of the hadith parts that deals with the biography of the Prophet Muhammad and the events of his conquests. The book is based on a series of connected narratives that begin with Musa bin Uqba and end with hadiths of the Prophet, presented with a strong chain of transmission from well-known narrators.
descriptions.194: The book “Rules of the Two Eids” by Al-Faryabi is a book that deals with the Prophet’s hadiths related to the rulings and recommendations of the two Eid prayers and their rituals. The book focuses on dealing with the hadiths contained in the names of the two Eids, the etiquette of going out to them, the takbeers, and the recitations, relying on multiple narrations from the Companions and followers. The book aims to provide an accurate understanding of the rituals of the two Eids according to the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.195: The book “Akhbar Al-Thakala” is written by Al-Hasan Al-Khallal. It includes a collection of hadiths and narrations related to the heavy-weights, whether in meaning, determination, or worship, explaining how to deal with them and mentioning some stories and sermons on this subject. The book was compiled from various hadiths and multiple narrators, making it an important reference in the field of Prophetic hadith and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.196: The book “The News of the Sheikhs and Their Morals” by Abu Bakr Al-Marwadhi is considered one of the important sources in the field of hadiths and morals. The book deals with the conduct of scholars, their morals, and their opinions in dealing with rulers and officials, relying on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and proven sayings from the righteous predecessors. The book focuses on the importance of honesty and advice in confronting leaders and officials, and also includes advice and news about the behavior of scholars in various situations.
descriptions.197: The book narrates the news, stories, and conversations of grammarians, dealing with topics related to scholars’ warnings against melody in the Arabic language, the emergence of the science of grammar, and the virtues of learning Arabic and parsing. It includes various types of stories and anecdotes related to prominent grammarians and linguists, with a focus on the importance of a healthy tongue and good pronunciation in the Islamic linguistic heritage.
descriptions.198: This book deals with news and poems by Abu Abdullah Al-Humaidi, where Al-Humaidi narrates hadiths and stories about his sheikhs, with a focus on the Prophet’s hadiths and religious sermons. The book begins with a narration of a hadith on the authority of Shu’bah ibn al-Hajjaj in which he urges giving alms, even half a date. In it, al-Humaidi mentions several similar narrations about burning fire and asking for alms, even with a kind word.
descriptions.199: This book deals with news and stories attributed to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ghassani, and contains historical and scientific novels and stories. The book is concerned with documenting the chain of narrations in the narration of stories, which makes it fall within the hadith parts. The text includes excerpts from a hadith by Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) about the pillars of faith and their sections, with a focus on patience, certainty, justice, jihad and its different branches.
descriptions.200: This book, “Women’s Literature, Marked as the Book of Care and Ending,” by Abd al-Malik ibn Habib, deals with multiple topics related to women’s literature and etiquette in Islam. The book focuses on the virtues of a righteous woman and how to deal with her. It also talks about the qualities that a woman should have, and also discusses the virtues of a virgin, the etiquette of a marital relationship, and what is desirable and undesirable in it. The book also includes advice on women's adornment and men's adornment, in addition to menstruation and isolation etiquette and other topics related to Muslim women.
descriptions.201: This book, “Forty Hadiths by Forty Sheikhs from Forty Towns,” written by Ibn Asakir, includes forty selected hadiths from different countries, aiming to strengthen Sharia knowledge and establish it in the souls of Muslims, away from suspicion and speculation. The hadiths deal with various religious topics, and the author aims through them to guide the reader to important hadiths related to matters of religion, expressing the importance of memorizing them and understanding their correct meanings.
descriptions.202: This book, “Names of the Sheikhs of Imam Al-Bukhari,” by Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Mandah Al-Asbahani, deals with a narration of the names of the sheikhs of Imam Al-Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him) according to the letters of the dictionary. The book begins with the letter Alif and then gradually moves to the rest of the letters. Under each letter, it mentions the names of the sheikhs about whom Al-Bukhari narrated, along with some details about their lives and deaths.
descriptions.203: This book deals with the topic of the signs of the Hour and the signs of its approach, with a focus on the departure of the good people and the survival of the bad ones. It contains a variety of hadiths about the events that will occur before the Hour comes, including the emergence of the Antichrist and the descent of Jesus, peace be upon them both. Author Abdul Malik bin Habib focuses on describing the social and moral conditions that would characterize that period, including the spread of lying, betrayal, and dishonesty.
descriptions.204: This book deals with hadiths attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, selected from the book “Indications of Prophecy,” Part Six. He focuses on narrating the hadiths in a sequential manner, relying on multiple narration chains starting from Al-Jawzjani up to Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Qasim. The book includes various topics from the life of the Prophet and his attributes, relying on the narration of hadiths in an accurate scientific manner.
descriptions.205: The book “Amali al-Mahamli, the novel of Ibn Yahya al-Bai’” consists of a series of dictation sessions, in which al-Mahamli records hadiths and legal narrations, listening to them from his sheikhs. The book deals with various jurisprudential and hadith topics, including the legal rulings related to theft and divorce, relying on narrations connected to an authentic chain of transmission from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.206: Amali Al-Mahamli is a narration of hadith masters by Ibn Mahdi Al-Farsi, and it includes a collection of hadiths and narrations that he recorded in various sessions during the year three hundred and twenty-nine. The book is divided into several parts, each part containing one or more narration sessions, where the hadith is narrated by sheikhs such as Abu Othman, Jarir, Layth, Nafi’ and others. The book deals with various topics from the Prophet’s hadiths, including those related to purity, morals, and acts of worship.
descriptions.207: A book that collects the Prophetic hadiths that were presented in the form of proverbs. The author explains in his introduction that these prophetic proverbs differ from the previous Arab proverbs, as they are an explanation, explanation, and representation that agree with the proverbs of revelation regarding the promise and threat, analysis and prohibition. The book includes various chapters, such as the chapter on metonymy and simile, and epithets of heaven, hell, the world, women, tribes, and horses, in addition to the chapter on the dual, rare expressions, and anecdotes.
descriptions.208: This book deals with the chain of mothers of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from grandmothers to mothers, traced back to their origins and mothers, and focuses on their lineage and lineage. In this work, author Muhammad bin Habib al-Baghdadi follows a scholarly tradition in the field of genealogies and histories, and provides detailed information on the lineage of the ancient women of Quraysh, including the maternal mothers of the Prophet ﷺ. The book is a type of hadith and genealogical book that is concerned with the history of genealogies and genealogies in Islam.
descriptions.209: The book “Invalidation of Interpretations of Narrations of the Prophet’s Attributes” by Abu Ya’la Ibn al-Farra aims to criticize and clarify the interpretations adopted by some scholars in interpreting the hadiths on the Prophet’s attributes, which may lead to likening people to creation. The book focuses on proving the attributes of God Almighty and denying any interpretation that might give the illusion of resemblance, relying on authentic hadiths and their chains of transmission.
descriptions.210: Ibn Battah’s book “Anti-Tricks” deals with the topic of tricks and devious methods that some people use to evade the provisions of Sharia law or break the oath, indicating that these practices are contrary to the teachings of the Islamic religion. The author focuses on the importance of adhering to the legal limits and rejecting tricks and illegal methods, stressing that the true jurist is the one who fears God and fears Him in his words and actions.
descriptions.211: This book, Ithaf al-Zahir wa Itharaf al-Muqimin, for those who walk in the visit of the Prophet ﷺ, by its author, Abu al-Yaman Abd al-Samad bin Asakir, deals with the subject of visiting the grave of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and its etiquette, and mentions in it what the visitor should do and avoid, relying on the authentic hadiths contained in this regard. The book includes directions on how to enter the Prophet’s Mosque, and important places inside it that are recommended to be visited, while providing general advice on preparing for the visit and etiquette for traveling there.
descriptions.212: This book, “The Threat of Benefits” by Saladin Al-Ala’i, deals with a collection of hadiths and hadith benefits from various sources, including Awali Malik by Al-Razi and Al-Khatib, Ziyadat Awali Malik by Al-Shahami, and Musnads of Al-Shafi’i and the Companions, in addition to other books on literature, reading, and morals. The author aims to collect and document the Prophet’s hadiths and the sayings of scholars in multiple fields, while providing scientific and practical benefits from them.
descriptions.213: The book “Proof of Intercession” is written by Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Ahmed bin Othman al-Dhahabi, and it falls within the scope of hadith parts. The book deals with hadiths and narrations related to the topic of intercession in Islam, relying on narrations from the Companions and the sayings of scholars. Al-Dhahabi focuses on proving the validity of the concept of intercession and denying the claims of heresy, emphasizing the intercession of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for those who commit major sins from his nation, and that it is accepted, God willing.
descriptions.214: Proving the Attribute of Sublimeness by Muwaffaq al-Din Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi, who wrote the hadith parts. He talks about proving the attribute of the Sublimeness of God, which was denied by some sects such as: the Jahmites, the Mu’tazilites, the Maturidis, and the Ash’aris. He cited a number of the aforementioned evidence. He cited some Qur’anic verses indicating this issue, hadith texts, the sayings of the Companions, the sayings of the imams, the jurists, and some of what was reported from the stories of the prophets in this regard.
descriptions.215: This book deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths related to matters of religion and life, with diverse topics ranging from jurisprudence, ethics, and monotheism. The author focuses on narrating hadiths in their original form, mentioning the chain of narrators, which gives the book a scientific character in the field of hadith. The book includes a detailed hadith about Zaid bin Haritha (may Allah be pleased with him)’s conversion to Islam, mentioning details of his biography and incidents.
descriptions.216: The book “Honoring the Guest” by Imam Ibrahim Al-Harbi deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths that urge generosity and good treatment of the guest, emphasizing that belief in God and the Last Day requires honoring and being kind to the guest. The book focuses on Islamic literature related to hospitality of the guest and explaining his status in Islam, relying on multiple hadith narrations about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.217: This book deals with hadiths and sayings related to various types of foods and drinks, classifying them according to their type, from honey and bread to beans and eggplant. Ibn Bashkwal focuses on conveying the traces and narrations related to each type of food, including the chains of transmission and hadiths related to them without going into other details.
descriptions.218: This book by Al-Daraqutni deals with the hadiths narrated by Malik bin Anas on the authority of Egyptian scholars such as Al-Zuhri, Nafi’, Yahya bin Saeed and others, in which the companions of these scholars disagreed with him. He focuses on contradictions in Malik's narrations and discusses them by presenting the hadiths in which his narrations differed from the narrations of other scholars and scholars.
descriptions.219: This book deals with the Prophetic hadiths that are authentically transmitted and accurately documented, focusing on individual hadiths that are uniquely narrated by important figures in Islamic history. The author aims to provide accurate scientific criticism of hadiths, relying on strict standards in correcting the methods of transmitting and documenting them. The book is of the type of hadith parts that are concerned with collecting and correcting the Prophet’s hadiths, and it is distinguished by its precise scientific style in dealing with the subject.
descriptions.220: In his book “Long Hadiths,” Al-Tabarani presents a collection of long and detailed narratives about important events in the Prophet’s biography and Islamic history, dealing with the Islam of the Companions and their hadiths, with a focus on detailed narratives about important historical events such as the Prophet’s migration to Medina and his conquests. The book focuses on narrating important events in precise detail, which makes it an important reference for the study of Islamic history and the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.221: This book is a collection of selected prophetic hadiths presented by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, in which he collected ten of the hadiths that he selected from his hearing and narrations, and explained their reasons after each hadith. The book discusses multiple attributions for the narrations, noting that they fall short of the rank of authentic books, despite serious attempts to document them and explain their reasons.
descriptions.222: This book deals with a group of prophetic hadiths based on the part of Ibn Arafa al-Abdi, where Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah focuses on transmitting the hadiths with their chain of transmission, relying on the selection of Imam al-Dhahabi. The book includes various topics of jurisprudence, morals, and acts of worship, such as dhikr after prayer and sleep, the virtues of reciting the Qur’an loudly and silently, and the rulings on menstruating women and those in a state of ritual impurity, in addition to other topics related to supplications, remembrances, and signs of the Hour. The book is one of the hadith parts concerned with transmitting and analyzing hadiths.
descriptions.223: This book deals with the Prophetic hadiths related to the days of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, presenting them in their historical and narrative context. The author, Abu Taher Al-Salafi, focuses on the narration of the hadiths that were mentioned during the days of Eid, relying on continuous and related chains of transmission from the narrators, which enhances the authenticity and authenticity of their transmission. The book is an important reference in the field of Prophetic hadiths related to the days of Eid.
descriptions.224: This book covers one hundred hadiths, each of which contains a reference to one of the crafts, arranged according to the letters of the alphabet. The author aims to collect hadiths in a systematic way that relies on linking artifacts with the Prophet’s hadith, drawing inspiration from a previous hadith scholar, his sheikh, Jamal al-Din Abu al-Muhsin Yubin al-Mubarrad al-Salihi. The book focuses on presenting the hadiths in an organized and orderly manner, while pointing out some of the errors that occurred in previous attempts at such an arrangement.
descriptions.225: The Forty Countries by Abu Taher al-Salafi is a hadith book that deals with selected prophetic hadiths from different countries, focusing on forty hadiths in each of the twenty countries mentioned in the index. The book aims to disseminate and preserve the Prophet’s hadiths by distributing them to cities of historical and religious importance in the Islamic world at that time.
descriptions.226: The book “The Forty Taymiyyah” is a collection of selected prophetic hadiths. In this book, Ibn Taymiyyah discusses forty important hadiths, examining each hadith while documenting its narration and explaining its content. The book falls within the hadith sections, and aims to spread Islamic jurisprudence and enhance knowledge of the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.227: The book The Forty Minors by Imam Al-Bayhaqi deals with a collection of selected Prophetic hadiths that focus on a Muslim’s practical and moral obligations, addressing topics such as monotheism, repentance, sincerity, and trust, with an emphasis on good behavior in dealing with others such as parents and those under the Muslim’s control. The book aims to teach the reader how to live according to Islamic values ​​and apply the teachings of the religion in daily life.
descriptions.228: This book deals with forty hadiths with chain of transmission, where the author focuses on narrating hadiths with highly proven chains of transmission that are related to their transmission. Through this work, Al-Iraqi aims to evoke the era of scholarly councils that witnessed an intense presence of narrators and inquirers. In his text, he deals with authentic and good hadiths, while including some oddities from narrators who are not known for presenting falsehood, while refraining from narrating what is attributed to those who are famous for lying.
descriptions.229: The Forty of Kilani by Sheikh Abd al-Razzaq al-Kilani includes forty hadiths attributed to forty noble sheikhs. These hadiths were chosen for those students who pass by us and are affiliated with us, and they address multiple topics related to morals, acts of worship, and virtues, relying on hadith documents connected to the golden chain.
descriptions.230: This book covers forty hadiths extracted from approved hadith books, and is distinguished by the consistency of their chain of transmission in terms of reliability and authenticity. Ibn Asakir focuses on talking about equality in the narration, as he chose hadiths with the same chain of transmission from trustworthy narrators, which adds additional credibility to its content. The book deals with various topics of Islamic jurisprudence and etiquette, providing a comprehensive overview of the teachings of the Islamic religion through these selected hadiths.
descriptions.231: This book deals with the conditions of achieved Sufis and their spiritual and moral qualities, citing hadiths and narrations that show their high ranks and high status in Sufism. The author, Abu Naeem Al-Isbahani, focuses on explaining their origins and conditions, showing how they achieve comprehensive faith and beneficial knowledge, and how they avoid the deceitfulness of the world and its desires, relying in this on a group of hadiths and stories that reflect their spiritual reality and their level of worship.
descriptions.232: This book, “The Forty in Sufism” by Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, deals with the topics of Islamic Sufism and the attributes of Sufism, deriving its evidence from the Prophet’s hadiths and authentic sayings. It focuses on the characteristics of the poor and righteous scholars, and calls for effort, chastity, and contentment, while noting the status of Sufis in Islam and their closeness to the Messenger ﷺ. The book includes forty chapters that address various aspects of the life of Sufis, their morals, and their attributes, providing a comprehensive picture of the concept of Sufism in Islam.
descriptions.233: This book, “Forty Fi Dala’il al-Tawhid,” is a collection of selected hadiths of the Prophet that deal with the doctrine of monotheism and the foundations of faith. The author, Abu Ismail Al-Harawi, focuses on affirming the attributes and monotheism of God Almighty, while responding to those who disagree with these issues. The book also addresses the importance of sincere intention and advice for Muslims, in addition to other topics related to Islamic worship and morals.
descriptions.234: This book is a collection of forty selected hadiths of the Prophet, collected and arranged by Ibn al-Muqri. It deals with hadiths on various topics related to worship, morals, and Islamic jurisprudence, relying on authentic and reliable narrations.
descriptions.235: The Book of Forty of Awali al-Mujayzin by Al-Maraghi Abu Bakr is a collection of selected prophetic hadiths. It contains forty hadiths narrated with authentic chains of transmission, and aims to provide examples of hadiths of high scientific and legal value. The book focuses on presenting hadiths in a sequential manner, relying on their connected and solid chains of transmission.
descriptions.236: This book deals with forty hadiths from the Musnads of the twenty sheikhs, as it focuses on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths through a continuous chain of narrators, starting with Imam Al-Qushayri and his grandfather, passing through other imams, all the way to the honorable companions. The first hadith in the book deals with a story that happened with Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), where he led the people in prayer while the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was in detention, and then the Prophet ﷺ returned to lead them in prayer after the prayer ended.
descriptions.237: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths related to the virtue of mercy and the reward of the merciful. It contains forty hadiths that address the topic of mercy and its importance in the life of a Muslim. Through this work, the author Ibn Tulun aims to encourage the reader to practice mercy and explain its virtue before God Almighty.
descriptions.238: Al-Amali Al-Halabiyya by Imam Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani is a collection of hadiths, fatwas, and sermons that he dictated orally to his students. The book deals with multiple religious and scientific topics, and reviews a series of Prophetic chains of transmission and hadiths, with a focus on the authenticity and veracity of their chain of transmission. The book represents part of the works of Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani in the field of Hadith and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.239: The book “Al-Amali Al-Safiriyat Al-Halabiyyah” by Imam Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani is a collection of hadiths and traces narrated by the author during his travels and visits, as it relies on a continuous chain of narrations that begins with his contemporary sheikhs and ends with the Companions. The book deals with religious and devotional topics, with a focus on the authenticity of hadiths and their chains of transmission, which makes it an important reference in hadith science.
descriptions.240: The book “Al-Amali Al-Mutlaqa” by Imam Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani is one of the hadith books that includes narrations of the Prophet’s hadiths with their chains of transmission. The author presents a group of hadiths, mentioning their narrators and the methods of arriving at them, indicating the authenticity or weakness of each hadith. The book consists of hundreds of hadiths attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, relying on multiple and diverse references to ensure the accuracy of the information.
descriptions.241: The book “Al-Amali and Al-Qira’a” consists of a collection of hadiths, prophetic fatwas, and the effects of the Companions, with a variety of topics, including acts of worship, transactions, and morals. The book deals with many issues of rulings and rulings in the form of hadiths and narrations, relying on multiple sources of hadith and interpretation books.
descriptions.242: The book “The Firsts” by Ibn Abi Asim deals with topics related to the first thing that happened in creation and monotheism, covering stories and hadiths about the first thing God created, the first to perform important actions in religious history and the last, relying on the Prophetic hadiths in dealing with its topics. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting Prophetic hadiths and classifying them according to topics.
descriptions.243: The book “The Firsts” by Al-Tabarani is a collection of hadiths that deal with the first things that happened in creation and existence, dealing with topics related to the first things that God Almighty created, and the first people to perform important actions in religious and moral history, with a focus on the events and personalities that preceded others in important events in Islam and the Qur’an. The book deals with various topics related to the first to deny, the first for whom the grave will open in Resurrection, the first to enter Paradise, and other topics related to those who preceded them in their actions and religious truths.
descriptions.244: This book deals with investigating errors and errors in the introduction of Abu Abdullah al-Hakim Nisaburi, where the author, Abdul-Ghani al-Azdi, points out errors and omissions that appeared in the original book, and cites the opinions of scholars to correct them and show what is correct in them. Al-Azdi focuses on the details of the chain of transmission and narration in the Prophet’s hadith, and aims to correct the erroneous implications that copies of the original book may have included.
descriptions.245: This book, “Enjoying the Forty Different Hearings,” written by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, contains forty diverse hadiths, which the author selected from his personal narrations, committing to direct hearing without authorizations or communions. The book begins with a hadith from the narration of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), then continues with narrations from other companions, arranging hadith after hadith according to the letters of the dictionary. The book aims to clarify the reasons for the hadiths and criticize them, while preserving the contrast and continuity in their origins.
descriptions.246: This book is a dictation in the translation of Issaas, and it includes a series of narrations and reports that were dictated in the voice of a Musnad sheikh, and were written down by Ibn Nasir al-Din al-Dimashqi. The book deals with hadith narrations or specific Qur’anic verses, and reviews the chain of transmission of dictated narrations, making it part of hadith literature.
descriptions.247: The book “Faith by Al-Adni” is a book on Islamic jurisprudence and doctrine, dealing with multiple topics related to faith and its conditions and requirements, through the presentation of hadiths and prophetic narrations. The book focuses on the importance of the five pillars of Islam and their impact on faith. It also talks about the characteristics of hypocrites and the conditions for perfect faith. It also reviews the obligations of Islam and its Sunnah, noting the importance of prayer, zakat, and Hajj in building faith.
descriptions.248: This book, “Differences in Pronunciation and the Response to the Jahmiyyah” by Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinouri, deals with the response to the Jahmiyyah and the Mushabbah in matters of monotheism and attributes, and discusses the views of the deviant sects on the Qur’an, destiny, angels, and other Islamic beliefs. The author focuses on clarifying religious facts and pointing out the errors of innovators, and aims to guide Muslims to the correct belief according to what the righteous predecessors did.
descriptions.249: This book deals with the topic of using Surat Al-Fatihah to achieve success in matters and meet needs, reviewing hadiths and narrations that emphasize the virtue of reciting Al-Fatihah and its positive impact on the life of a Muslim. The author relies on a series of chains of narrations and narrations to support his claim about the importance of seeking help from Al-Fatihah in various situations and demands. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and presenting their effects on the lives of Muslims.
descriptions.250: This book, “Victory for the Companions of Hadith,” by Al-Samani Abu Al-Muzaffar, deals with defending the Companions of Hadith and criticizing those who disparage them, explaining their virtue and the place of the science of hadith in the Islamic religion. The book focuses on urging Muslims to follow the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the community, and to reject innovation and division, relying in this on the Prophetic hadiths and Sharia evidence. It also points out the importance of acting on the hadith and transmitting it, and discusses the concept of reason and its role in religion among the Sunnis.
descriptions.251: The book “The Misers” by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi deals with the topic of miserliness from a religious and social perspective, reviewing the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in denouncing stinginess and warning against it, and also reviewing what was stated in the Prophet’s hadiths about the consequences and shame of miserliness. The book also mentions the sayings of scholars and poets in satirizing and vilifying misers, and presents situations and events related to miserliness and its negative effects on the individual and society.
descriptions.252: This book, “The Resurrection” by Ibn Abi Dawud, deals with the subject of the Resurrection, the grave, Paradise, and Hell, reviewing hadiths and narrations about the torment of the grave and the bliss of Paradise, with a focus on the events of the Day of Resurrection and people’s entry into Paradise and Hell. The book also includes a detailed description of Paradise, including its gates, trees, and rivers, with hadiths about the fate of the prophets and their nations in the afterlife.
descriptions.253: The book “Al-Baldaniyat” by Al-Sakhawi is a modern volume that collects hadiths and narrations related to a number of countries, arranged in chapters according to the names of those countries. The book begins by mentioning the country of Jeddah, covering its virtues, news, and antiquities contained therein. Then it moves on to list the rest of the countries, such as Medina, Jerusalem, Aleppo, and others, to form a small geographical modern encyclopedia.
descriptions.254: The book “Al-Baytuta” by Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Khorasani is a collection of selected hadiths of the Prophet, which dealt with various topics related to worship, morals, and daily transactions. The book focuses on transmitting the hadiths in their original form while preserving their historical context, and contains texts related to the times of the call to prayer, night prayer, emancipation, and special provisions regarding fasting and marriage.
descriptions.255: Al-Tabseer fi Ma’alim al-Din or Tibseer Uli al-Nah wa Ma’alim al-Guidance is a book by Muhammad bin Jarir bin Yazid bin Katheer bin Ghalib, known as Imam Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Jarir al-Tabari, (224 AH-310 AH / 839-923 AD). It is a book on the Islamic faith and an explanation of some of its origins, and it is a message to the people of the town of Amal Tabaristan. A response to the people of the town to him, in which he explains what he has imitated regarding the fundamentals of religion. It is one of the two books that Al-Tabari wrote in order to explain his belief, his method and his approach, which are: Al-Tabseer and Sareh Al-Sunnah, and Abdul Aziz bin Baz explained it in his lessons.
descriptions.256: Determination in Perfection and Tajweed is a book by Abu Amr Al-Dani, one of the books on the science of Tajweed.
descriptions.257: This book is part of the series of grading of Sahih Hadith, where its author Al-Ateeqi deals with grading hadiths from the books of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, based on trustworthy principles. The book focuses on presenting authentic hadiths by quoting them from trustworthy sheikhs, taking into account the conditions of graduation approved in the main hadith books.
descriptions.258: The book “The Ticket” by Al-Humaidi covers a collection of news and poems collected and narrated by the author, Sheikh Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abi Nasr Al-Humaidi. Al-Humaidi mentions in the introduction to his book that he wrote this reminder out of respect and affection for one of his sheikhs, and he also mentions the series of narrations of the book from his sheikhs and teachers. The book falls within the hadith sections and contains narrations and hadiths that Al-Hamidi transmitted from his sheikhs through narration and hearing.
descriptions.259: The book “Encouraging Supplication” by Abdul-Ghani Al-Maqdisi deals with the virtues of supplication and its importance in the life of a Muslim, and urges adherence to it and making it a daily approach. The book contains multiple sections that talk about the appropriate times for supplication, the Most Beautiful Names of God, and special supplications for specific situations such as travel and illness, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and Qur’anic verses.
descriptions.260: This book deals with the virtues of patience in the face of calamities, especially the loss of children, citing Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths that emphasize the reward and dignity of the patient with God. The author focuses on the directives of the Messenger ﷺ and the sayings of the Companions on this subject, providing practical advice to the bereaved to overcome their affliction with wisdom and righteousness. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and classifying prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.261: This book is compiled by Al-Tahawi, and is related to the subject of the Prophet’s hadiths and the forms of performing them. It focuses on the reconciliation between the forms of “we spoke” and “tell us” in the narration of hadiths, and studies how these forms can lead to a different understanding of the meaning of a single hadith. The book also deals with the ruling on transmitted hadiths and the relationship of the Companions to the revelation that came down to them.
descriptions.262: The book “Condolences” by Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madaini is a collection of hadiths and narrations related to consolation for the afflicted and consolation for the dead. In writing it, the author relied on the narrations of a number of famous narrators, as he quotes them directly or through them. The book begins with a narration that talks about the greatness of consolation in God after the death of the Messenger ﷺ, indicating that true consolation lies in the reward and good deeds that the believer reaps in his life, and that disappointment comes from the one who feels safe. Punishment.
descriptions.263: This book is a graceful commentary written by Al-Naji, which deals with the subject of sealing with agate and other stones, reviewing the opinions of scholars on the ruling on sealing with these stones and their narrations in the hadith. The author relies on reviewing and evaluating prophetic hadiths on this subject, and reviews the opinions of scholars such as Al-Nawawi and Ibn Al-Jawzi regarding the authenticity of these narrations. The book focuses on sealing with agate in particular, and aims to provide an accurate understanding of its ruling and its narration in hadith sources.
descriptions.264: The Book of Tawheed by author Abdul Ghani al-Maqdisi is a hadith book that deals with the subject of monotheism for God Almighty, and it contains prophetic hadiths with chain of transmissions of chain of transmission that begin with talking about God Almighty and His teachings to people. The book opens with the words “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful” and “In the Name of God the Helper,” and then moves directly to the series of Prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.265: This book is part of Al-Daraqutni's collection Al-Fawa'id Al-Fa'idin, and it is one of the hadith books that includes narrations of independent hadiths. The eighty-third part of the collection deals with the narration and education of the Prophet’s hadiths, mentioning the chain of narrators starting with al-Daraqutni and ending with some of his contemporary hadith scholars. The text includes an introduction that includes a supplication to God Almighty and a request for help and facilitation, followed by a series of hadiths narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and other prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.266: This book is the second part of “The Slogan of the Righteous in Supplications and Remembrances” by Ibn al-Sheikha, and it contains hadiths and prophetic supplications attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book focuses on documenting hadiths and narrating them through a series of narrators, relying on hadith extraction techniques to ensure the authenticity and accuracy of what is contained therein. The book aims to publish supplications and remembrances learned from authentic Prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.267: The first part of Amali Abi Ishaq contains a collection of prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas, covering various topics related to worship, morals, and daily transactions. The book focuses on conveying the words and actions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, while presenting some jurisprudential fatwas related to those hadiths.
descriptions.268: This book is the first part of “Al-Fawa’id al-Sihah wal-Gharāib wa al-Infrad” by its author, Abu al-Qasim al-Harfi, in which he presents Al-Ansari’s narration of its benefits in the field of Prophetic hadith. The book deals with the benefits and hadiths of Sihah, Ghariba and Mufradah, relying on Sheikh al-Tabari’s grading of them. The book aims to transmit and document the Prophet’s hadiths in an accurate, scientific manner, while presenting their sources and chains of narration.
descriptions.269: The first and second parts of Fawa'id Ibn Bishran include a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the Companions, dealing with multiple topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, relying on documents varying in strength and nature.
descriptions.270: This book is the second part of the hadith of Yahya bin Moin Al-Fawaid, and it includes Abu Bakr Al-Maruzi’s narration of fatwas and scholarly quotes from Yahya bin Moin. The book covers interpretations of some Qur’anic verses and hadith narrations, with a brief explanation of legal vocabulary and rulings, focusing on topics related to worship, morals, and transactions.
descriptions.271: Musnad Abu Hurairah by Abu Ishaq Al-Askari is part of a Musnad containing hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him). The book is one of the hadith parts that follows the Musnad method in collecting hadiths according to chronological or thematic order, and its narration is based on a series of connected narrators.
descriptions.272: This book is the fifth part of the collection of individual hadiths collected and narrated by Sheikh Abu Hafs Omar bin Ahmed bin Othman, and it contains strange and individual hadiths that are not mentioned in other hadith books. The book deals with multiple topics from the life and year of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, relying on trustworthy documents in the narration.
descriptions.273: This book is the fifth part of the Musnad of the Hadith of Malik ibn Anas, written by Al-Jahdhami, and contains hadiths transmitted to the Prophet ﷺ via Malik ibn Anas. The book includes hadiths attributed to Hisham bin Urwa bin Al-Zubayr and other narrations that dealt with various topics such as legal rulings and prophetic stories.
descriptions.274: This book deals with selected hadiths from the parts of Abu Mansur al-Khawjani, narrated by the author Abu Taher al-Salafi. It contains multiple narrations from different sources, including what Al-Salafi narrated directly on the authority of Al-Khawjani, and some of which Al-Khawjani narrated on the authority of others. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths in their original form without interpretation or comment, and aims to preserve and document these prophetic narrations.
descriptions.275: This book is part of a larger collection that deals with the narration of the elders on the authority of the younger ones in the Prophet’s hadith, and it is written by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Suleiman Al-Baghandi. The first part of this collection deals with the narrations of famous memorizers about younger memorizers, and presents a series of narrators starting from Al-Baghandi up to the younger narrators, showing how they transmitted and documented the hadith. The book falls within the classification of hadith parts, and it is part of a larger collection that dealt with the narration of the elders on the authority of the younger ones in the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.276: This book is part of the news of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, and it is written by Al-Hafiz Abu Sulayman Al-Rab’i, known as Ibn Zubr. The book deals with the narration of the news of Ibn Abi Dhi’b through a series of connected narrations, which the author collected from various sources and documented meticulously. The book falls within the hadith sections concerned with documenting and narrating hadiths and historical news.
descriptions.277: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, containing a hadith narration by Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad bin Humaid al-Hourani al-Dimashqi on the authority of his sheikhs. The book mentions the narration of the hadith through a series of narrators starting from Abu al-Tayyib to the six sheikhs who narrated from him. The book also discusses the attribution and chronological history of the hadith narration, relying on the traditional hadith classification.
descriptions.278: This book deals with Al-Attar’s hadiths about his sheikhs, and presents the chain of narration by mentioning the names of the sheikhs from whom he narrated, starting with Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hasan bin Yaqoub bin Muqasim Al-Attar and finally ending with Sheikh Al-Islam Abu Al-Fadl Ahmed bin Ali Al-Asqalani. The book focuses on describing how hadiths were transmitted through a chain of narrators, relying on authorizations and hearing aids between them.
descriptions.279: This book deals with the hadith of Abu Amr Othman bin Omar al-Draj, as the author narrates it through a series of prophetic hadiths related to it. The book is based on the narration attributed to Umm al-Fadl Hajar bint al-Sharaf, which was read to him in Rajab in the year 865 AH. The book contains several hadiths supported by a series of narrators, starting with the hadith of Al-Mu’mil ibn Ihab and ending with the hadith of Tha’labah ibn Abd al-Rahman. The book falls within the hadith parts that follow a method in collecting hadiths and their narrators.
descriptions.280: This book is part of the benefits of the hadith of Abu Dhar al-Harawi, and it contains hadiths and narrations transmitted by the author from his sheikhs, relying on dictation and reading. It addresses religious and moral topics through the Prophet’s hadiths, and aims to spread the benefits learned from these hadiths and enhance commitment to Islamic teachings.
descriptions.281: This book deals with the virtues and rulings of Friday by presenting hadiths and narrations related to this topic. The author, Abu Bakr Al-Umawi Al-Maruzi, focuses on various aspects of Friday prayer, starting with its virtue and the virtue of Friday prayer, and even special provisions for it, such as washing the Friday prayer and dressing well during it. The book also mentions the benefits of walking to the mosque and attending Friday prayers early, indicating its times and the rulings on abandoning it.
descriptions.282: The book “Jihad by Ibn Al-Mubarak” is a collection of hadiths and narrations related to jihad for the sake of God, as it focuses on the virtues of jihad and its reward in this world and the hereafter, and also includes instructions and rulings related to this topic. The book deals with the sayings of the Companions and followers regarding the virtue of jihad and its explanation, relying on reliable hadith narrations.
descriptions.283: This book deals with the encouragement of trade, industry, and work, and is based on hadiths and narrations from Islamic sources. The author, Abu Bakr Al-Khallal, focuses on the wise directives of the street that encourage lawful earning and trust in work, refuting the claims of those who claim trust and abandon work. The book also addresses aspects of trust, zakat, and how to distribute credit to relatives and mahrams.
descriptions.284: This book, “Al-Hujja fi Bayan al-Hujjah wa Sharh al-Aqeedah of the Sunnis,” is written by Ismail al-Isbahani. It deals with the subject of the Islamic faith according to the method of the Sunnis, and aims to explain the belief of the imams of the predecessors and competent scholars in different countries. The author focuses on the importance of following the Sunnah of the Prophet and rejecting heresies, and bases his explanation on hadiths and sayings contained in approved Islamic sources. The book aims to guide the reader towards adhering to the teachings of the Sunnis and the community and avoiding innovation in religion.
descriptions.285: Al-Hanaiyat is a collection of benefits and narrations by Sheikh Abu Al-Qasim Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Hana’i, classified into eleven parts. This collection deals with hadiths and narrations of the Prophet, with documentation and evaluation of the authenticity of the hadiths, making it an important reference in the field of hadiths of the Prophet and hadith studies.
descriptions.286: This book, “Al-Kharaj,” by Yahya bin Adam Al-Qurashi, deals with various topics in Islamic jurisprudence related to tribute, tax, raids, and spoils, relying on the Prophet’s hadiths in dealing with these topics. The book focuses on explaining the issues of zakat, charity, and inheritance, and discusses issues of agriculture, trade, and how to divide spoils and spoils among Muslims.
descriptions.287: This book, “The Precious Pearl in the News of Medina” by Imam Al-Hafiz Muhib al-Din Ibn al-Najjar, deals with the history and importance of the city of Medina through its various eras. The author focuses on mentioning the names of the city and its first inhabitants, its conquest, its virtues, the virtue of dying in it, its prohibition, its wells and its springs. It also mentions hadiths and narrations related to the city and its residents, and aims to spread the virtues of Dar al-Hijrah, the source of revelation, and encourage people and residents to visit it.
descriptions.288: This book deals with the topic of supplication in various daily situations and occasions, such as riding an animal, traveling, entering or leaving the house, or at sunset or dawn. It contains prophetic hadiths and legal supplications related to these situations, directing the Muslim to conjure the appropriate supplication in each case. The book is a type of hadith book that collects hadiths related to a specific topic.
descriptions.289: This book is part of Al-Dhahabi’s works in the field of Prophetic hadiths, in which he deals with a series of hadiths and narrations related to the dinar and other topics, reviewing their chain of transmission and strength. The author relies on the narration of hadiths through major sheikhs and their careful documentation, which indicates his interest in the hadith and documentation aspects of hadith science.
descriptions.290: This book is an appendix to part of the Hadiths of the Basin narrated by Baqi bin Mukhlid, which Ibn Bashkwal expanded and added new narrations from the Companions about the Hadith of the Basin. The book covers multiple narrations from different sources, and aims to strengthen and clarify the Hadiths of the Basin with their correct chains of transmission.
descriptions.291: This book, “The Quartet in Hadith” by Abd al-Ghani al-Azdi, is a classification of hadith parts that deals with hadiths in which the narrations of four companions or followers were combined, with each of them narrating directly on the authority of his companion. The author focuses on studying these rare hadiths that are united by a chain of transmission in the chain of transmission, reviewing examples of them and reviewing hadiths that were not mentioned by his predecessors in this field.
descriptions.292: This book, “The Journey in Pursuing Hadith,” by Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, deals with the subject of scholars’ journeys in seeking hadith and transmitting knowledge, explaining their virtues and importance in spreading religious knowledge. It mentions the journeys of the Companions, followers, and others in pursuit of knowledge, and refers to those who traveled to seek a single hadith or to gain more knowledge from a particular sheikh. The book focuses on urging the pursuit of knowledge and its journey, and mentions prophetic hadiths that emphasize the importance of seeking knowledge wherever it is found.
descriptions.293: This book deals with the topic of kissing the hand from a legal and behavioral perspective, reviewing hadiths and narrations related to this act through various contexts in the lives of the Companions and righteous predecessors. The author focuses on the legal permission to kiss the hand and the meanings of respect and appreciation that these practices carry, noting some of the limits and controls followed in this regard.
descriptions.294: The book “The Response to the Jahmiya” by its author, Ibn Mandah Muhammad bin Ishaq, deals in its content with responses to the opinions of the Jahmiya on religious and philosophical issues, relying on the Prophet’s hadiths and authentic sayings. The book focuses on clarifying the meanings of the Qur’anic verses related to seeing God on the Day of Resurrection, and also includes discussing the differences of the Companions and followers in interpreting some verses and hadiths.
