descriptions.295: This book is a response from Abu Bakr Al-Najjad to those who claim that the Qur’an is created, as the author addresses his arguments and evidence to demonstrate the invalidity of this claim and confirm the doctrine of the divinity of the Qur’an. The book relies on the hadiths of the Prophet and the hadiths mentioned on this subject, and cites the sayings of scholars and hadith scholars to support its position.
descriptions.296: This book is a response from Imam al-Hafiz Abd al-Rahman ibn Mandah to those who deny the alif, lam, and mem from the words of God Almighty, and it is classified among the hadith parts. In his book, the author addresses the issue of the literalism of Qur’anic words, citing the Prophet’s hadiths and linguistic rules to confirm that the alif, lam, and meem are among the letters written in the Holy Qur’an, and denies that they have any characteristic that other sects deny.
descriptions.297: The rich message about silence and staying at home addresses topics related to the wisdom of remaining silent and keeping one’s tongue, and what a person must do when temptations spread, namely staying at home and seeking safety, while emphasizing the importance of working with what is beneficial and refraining from interfering in matters that do not concern him. The book focuses on the hadith aspect, reviewing hadiths and narratives that support his ideas and views on these topics.
descriptions.298: Al-Risala Al-Wafiyya by Abu Amr Al-Dani is a book on Islamic beliefs that deals with the Sunni doctrine of beliefs and the foundations of religion. The author focuses on explaining Sunni beliefs in divine attributes, destiny, angels, and other doctrinal issues, relying on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book aims to explain the basic beliefs that Muslims must believe and adhere to, while emphasizing the necessity of adhering to the legal texts and understanding them in the correct way.
descriptions.299: The book “Tenderness and Weeping” by Ibn Qudamah Al-Maqdisi deals with the topic of piety and modesty in the life of a Muslim, reviewing the impact of the prophetic directives in shaping the believer’s behavior and controlling his whims. The book focuses on the commandments of the Prophet ﷺ to Muadh bin Jabal about the necessity of adhering to the Qur’an and adhering to it, and how a Muslim can protect himself from destruction in his desires. It also points out the importance of prayer, fasting and charity in a Muslim’s life and how to face death and the afterlife.
descriptions.300: This book, “Asceticism and the Description of the Ascetics,” written by Ibn al-A’rabi Ahmad ibn Bishr, deals with the subject of asceticism by presenting the opinions and sayings of scholars and imams of Islam on this subject. The book focuses on defining asceticism and explaining its meaning and characteristics, reviewing multiple statements by prominent Islamic figures about the concept and nature of asceticism, with a focus on the spiritual aspects and humility as part of true asceticism.
descriptions.301: The book “Asceticism” by Abu Hatem Al-Razi deals with a collection of prophetic hadiths and heritage stories that focus on promoting spiritual and moral values, relying on the transmission of words and actions that urge asceticism in this world, humility, and sincere worship. The book deals with various topics related to asceticism and piety, and through its conversations, it reviews how a person can live a rich and upright spiritual life, with a focus on warning against the deceitfulness of this world and encouraging the afterlife.
descriptions.302: The book “Additions to the Book of Major Sins by Al-Burdiji” by Al-Diya’ Al-Maqdisi presents an examination of the Prophet’s hadith about major sins forbidden in Islam, with the addition of new and diverse narrations on this subject. The book focuses on identifying the types of major sins criminalized by Islamic law, relying on multiple narrations from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.303: This book is a continuation of Al-Muzani’s book on the Prophetic Hadiths, in which Ibn Ziyad Al-Naysaburi deals with many sections of Islamic jurisprudence through the narration of hadiths related to them. The book focuses on various topics related to purity, prayer, and funerals, relying on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths to clarify the legal rulings on these topics.
descriptions.304: This book deals with the discussion of the divine attributes, heaven, and hell, reviewing hadiths and narrations about the description of torment in Hell and how its people enter it. The author focuses on conveying hadiths related to these topics without going into details of their methods or interpretation, while emphasizing their acceptance as they were presented without addition or distortion.
descriptions.305: This book, “Prayer” by Abu Naim al-Fadl bin Dakin, deals with topics related to the rulings on purity and prayer, and reviews legal rulings on multiple aspects of worship, including the prohibition of prayer and its analysis, cases of tayammum and ritual impurity, and the etiquette of sleeping with a menstruating wife. The author relies on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths to clarify the jurisprudential rulings related to these topics.
descriptions.306: The book “Fasting” by Al-Faryabi deals with the rulings on fasting in the month of Sha’ban and its virtues, while mentioning prophetic hadiths about the desirability of fasting during it and connecting it to Ramadan. The book also reviews hadiths on other rulings on Muslim fasts, such as the prohibition of intercourse during fasting, the recommendations for breaking the fast, and what it is recommended for a fasting person to break his fast with, with reference to the ruling on fasting while traveling.
descriptions.307: This book, “Al-Ajalah fi Al-Musiliyya Hadiths,” is written by the religious scholar Muhammad Yassin Al-Fadani, in which it deals with the Prophetic hadiths that follow in a serial manner, that is, in a series of chains of transmission. The author focuses on presenting these hadiths according to different classifications, including those related to worship and morals, and those related to jurists, grammarians, and hadith scholars from various Islamic regions. The book aims to present these hadiths in a serial manner, while adhering to the principles and conditions of this type of hadith.
descriptions.308: This book, “Preparing for Distress and Distress,” by Dia al-Din al-Maqdisi, deals with the recommended supplications and remembrances when distress and adversity occur, explaining how to seek help from God Almighty in adversity and adversity. The author focuses on presenting the Prophetic hadiths and the supplications that were mentioned regarding the virtue of seeking refuge in God and relying on Him in times of adversity.
descriptions.309: The Book of the Throne and what was narrated in it is a book about the exaltation of God Almighty and His Throne, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Jaafar bin Abi Shaybah (210 AH - 297 AH). In his book, the author discusses one of the important issues of belief among Muslims, specifically in an issue of attributes in which there are many schools of thought and sayings, and this issue is the issue of the exaltation of God and His equality on His Throne, Glory be to Him. …
descriptions.310: This book deals with a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, with a focus on what was narrated by Salih bin Ahmed and his additions. It contains multiple hadith texts, both chained and suspended, that dealt with various topics from the life of the Prophet and his teachings, relying on multiple chains of transmission and narrations connected to a chain of narrators. The book aims to document and expand the circle of hadith narrations by presenting new or rare narrations in the field of Prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.311: This book deals with the marriages of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in which Ibn al-Mubarrad mentions whom the Prophet married and explains their names and conditions. The author relied on multiple accounts from different sources in his information, which enhances the reliability of the information contained therein. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the prophetic hadiths related to the life of the Prophet and his personal circumstances.
descriptions.312: This book, “Science” by Zuhair bin Harb, deals with a collection of Prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential sayings about the value of science and its importance in the life of a Muslim. The author focuses on strengthening the concept of seeking knowledge and disseminating it as a religious obligation, mentioning the virtues of scholars and urging Muslims to learn and understand religion. The book contains hadiths and narrations that confirm that God grants success to those who wish to learn and understand religion, and that the angels bless the seeker of knowledge.
descriptions.313: This book, “Al-Umdah min al-Fawa’id wa al-Athar al-Sihah fi the Mashaykhah of Shahada,” deals with the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ and its transmission, with a focus on the sheikhdom, which includes what the hadith scholar Shahada narrated on the authority of her sheikhs. The book aims to document the connection between the chains of transmission in the Prophet’s hadith across the ages, which represents an important aspect of hadith sciences. The book falls within the hadith sections and is distinguished by the fact that it is rare among modern women sheikhs, which makes it a valuable reference in this field.
descriptions.314: Al-Awali by Ibn Al-Isbahani is a hadith book that contains a collection of Prophetic hadiths narrated from the Companions and their chains of transmission. It focuses on transmitting the chains of transmission and narrations in detail. The book includes multiple topics related to morals, worship, and daily behavior, relying on multiple narratives and transmission chains.
descriptions.315: The book “Al-Ghurabaa” by Al-Ajri deals with the description of strangers among the believers and their conditions in this world, mentioning their characteristics and status in Islam. The book focuses on urging people to reach the levels of exile and explaining the characteristics of an honest stranger in dealing with and adhering to good morals, while pointing out their great status in the eyes of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.316: This book is an index of the sheikhs of Judge Iyad, in which he mentions the names of his scholars from whom he learned, giving an idea about each one of them. The book covers different sheikhs in various scientific fields, briefly describing each of them in a way that gives an idea of ​​their academic and personal status. The book is a type of hadith and scientific book that is concerned with documenting chains of scientific chains of narration.
descriptions.317: This book, “The Mysteries and Ambiguities in the Prophetic Hadith,” by Abdul-Ghani Al-Azdi, deals with ambiguous and ambiguous topics in the Prophetic Hadiths, reviewing Prophetic hadiths and stories that need clarification and detail. It focuses on interpreting the ambiguous and unknown in Islamic narratives, relying on their hadith chains and supports.
descriptions.318: Al-Fanid fi Halawat al-Asanid by Al-Suyuti is a book that deals with the subject of chains of transmission in the Prophet’s hadith, as it focuses on studying the methods of documenting hadiths and their narrators. The book contains multiple studies of different chains of narration, some of which are shared by companions, and some of which include narrators from the Successors or later scholars. The book aims to analyze and evaluate the validity and strength of chains of narrations, while providing various examples of different forms of chains of narrations in hadith.
descriptions.319: This book deals with the topic of temptations and tribulations that will occur at the end of time, with a focus on the Antichrist, his appearance, and the events that will result from it. The author, Hanbal bin Ishaq, relies on the Prophetic hadiths in his treatment of this topic, explaining details about the personality of the Antichrist, his actions, and how to protect oneself from his evil. The book falls within the framework of hadith books that are concerned with documenting and analyzing the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.320: The Book of Fatwa by Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Sulami is a book in the field of Prophetic hadiths, in which the author discusses the good morals and virtues of actions based on the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book focuses on presenting the behavior of the prophets and righteous people in following the fatwa method, which indicates the virtues and good morals that a Muslim must follow.
descriptions.321: The Book of Obligations by Imam Sufyan al-Thawri is a work on the science of obligations and inheritance, dealing with the rules of inheritance distribution according to Islamic law. The book contains detailed chapters that address various cases of inheritance, including those related to ascendants, children, and spouses, relying on authentic Prophetic hadiths in this field.
descriptions.322: This book deals with the serials of the Noble Prophet’s Hadith, which are methods of transmission connected by a single chain of transmission. The author focuses on presenting a series of interconnected narratives across time, showing how they were transmitted between scholars and preservationists across various historical periods and geographical regions. The book includes series related to jurists, historians, grammarians, and poets, as well as series related to historical events and prominent religious figures.
descriptions.323: This book, “Al-Fawa’id Al-Hassan from the Trustworthy Sheikhs” or “Masheykha” by Abu Bakr bin Al-Naqour, is a book in the science of hadith that deals with the series of hadith narrations and their grading. The author focuses on mentioning the scientific and narrative benefits that he benefited from his sheikhs, demonstrating the depth of his connection to the chain of transmission of hadith and the interest of scholars of previous generations in this science. The book falls within the classification of hadith parts, and it was written by the trustworthy hadith scholar Ibn al-Naqur, who died in the year 565 AH.
descriptions.324: This book, “Al-Fawa’id Al-Awali Al-Mukhtarikh min Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” by its author, Muhammad bin Ali Al-Souri, deals with a group of agreed-upon and strange prophetic hadiths, presenting the benefits learned from them. Al-Souri relies in its content on the narration of hadiths from the books of al-Sihah and strange hadiths, while presenting a jurisprudential and scientific vision about them.
descriptions.325: This book is a collection of hadiths, prophetic benefits, and curiosities derived from Kufan ​​narrators, and it was collected and narrated by Muhammad bin Ali al-Suri. The book covers multiple narrations from companions and ancestors, and reviews letters from the science of hadith and its arts, presenting the reader with a rich material of chains of transmission and hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.326: The book “Al-Fawaid, News, and Tales from Al-Shafi’i and Hatim” by Sheikh Abu Ali Al-Hassan bin Al-Hussein bin Hamкан Al-Hamdhani covers a series of novels, stories, and hadiths related to the lives of Imam Al-Shafi’i, Al-Hatim Al-Asam, Marouf Al-Karkhi, and other scholars. The author relies on the narrations of his sheikhs and scholars to document this information, thus providing a rich cultural and historical view of the lives, words, and actions of these scholars.
descriptions.327: The book “Al-Fawa’id wal-Akhbar” by Ibn Duraid is one of the hadith parts that includes narrations and hadiths transmitted by the author from his sheikhs, and it contains scientific benefits and historical news. The book presents a connected chain of narrations between Ibn Duraid and his teachers, showing how he conveyed this information through a series of narrators.
descriptions.328: This book deals with topics related to kissing various body parts and objects, reviewing kissing etiquette and its rulings in light of the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author focuses on his talk about kissing the cheek, mouth, stomach, navel, etc., while mentioning prophetic hadiths related to these topics. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting hadiths and classifying them according to specific topics.
descriptions.329: This book deals with the topic of fate and includes a group of works and narrations related to it. It contains a chapter that talks about the pilgrims of Adam and Moses, peace be upon them, and also deals with other topics such as the Prophet ﷺ’s information about two books, the wisdom of appreciating the paths of creatures before their creation, and it discusses the nature of divine management and human work. The book is a hadith book and is based on prophetic narrations and hadiths.
descriptions.330: This book deals with the topic of reading in cemeteries and the stories and hadiths related to that. In it, Abu Bakr al-Khallal mentions narrations from scholars such as Ahmad ibn Hanbal and al-Shafi’i, and tells about the Ansar’s custom of reciting the Qur’an on graves after the death of their loved ones. The book combines prophetic hadiths and historical narratives on this topic, and aims to show the different practices and attitudes towards reading the Qur’an in cemeteries.
descriptions.331: This book, “Contentment” by Ibn al-Sunni, deals with the topic of contentment and its virtues, and defines contentment as contentment with what God has divided for man. It contains hadiths and poetic poems that show the virtue of contentment and encourage following it, mentioning the reasons that help achieve it in daily life. The book aims to encourage the reader to follow the path of contentment and to clarify its place in Islamic law.
descriptions.332: This book is a collection of benefits and narrations by Abu al-Qasim al-Harfi, selected and produced by al-Tabari from al-Rais al-Thaqafi’s narration about him. The book deals with hadiths and prophetic narrations, relying on multiple chains of transmission connected to authentic and strange chains of narration, and aims to collect scientific and hadith benefits through Al-Thaqafi’s narration by Abu Al-Qasim Al-Harfi.
descriptions.333: This book deals with the benefits and hadiths of the Prophet collected and cited by Abu Bakr al-Abhari. It mentions the hadiths in the form of information about the chain of narrators of each hadith. The subject of the hadiths varies between virtues, sermons, and legal rulings. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and classifying prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.334: The book deals with generosity, generosity, and good manners from an Islamic perspective, reviewing Prophetic hadiths and Qur’anic verses that emphasize the importance of these qualities in a Muslim’s life. The author, Al-Barjalani, focuses on promoting good morals and rejecting obscenity and indecency, presenting a picture of Islam’s tolerance in dealing with others and imbuing oneself with the qualities of generosity and generosity.
descriptions.335: This book, “Discourse on Reciting the Recitation of the Qur’an to the Dead,” was written by Ibn Abi Al-Surur Al-Maqdisi, and it is one of the Hadith parts that dealt with the subject of the reward of reciting the Qur’an reaching the dead. In it, the author presents the opinions of scholars on the ruling on giving the reward for reading to the dead, reviewing various opinions of eminent scholars, and in his discussions, he relies on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths to support his views.
descriptions.336: This book deals with the talk about love for God and His Messenger and love for God, reviewing prophetic hadiths that show the status of love in God and the Messenger and its impact on faith. The author focuses on emphasizing the importance of love being in God alone and no one else, and that a Muslim’s love for his brother in God is the love that pleases God. The book is of the hadith genre, as it relies on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and an analysis of their meanings.
descriptions.337: This book deals with the subject of those who disappeared or fled from Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf, and mentions stories about the escape of prominent religious and scientific figures from the oppression of Al-Hajjaj. It focuses on the details of their disappearance and escape to different places to avoid being pursued, while mentioning some incidents and stories related to that historical period. The book is a type of hadith book that narrates historical events and stories about the companions and followers.
descriptions.338: The Five Councils of Al-Sulaifi is a group of hadith councils that includes five councils that shed light on hadiths and prophetic narrations. The book addresses multiple topics by narrating hadiths in dictation, making it an important reference in the field of hadiths. The book focuses on transmitting and documenting hadiths through a series of narrators, which enhances their credibility and value in hadith studies.
descriptions.339: Al-Majalis Al-Asharah Al-Amali by Al-Hasan Al-Khallal is a book that deals with hadith about fasting and its rulings. It contains hadiths and sermons about the virtues and etiquette of fasting, with a focus on the virtues of the month of Ramadan and its rulings. The book also presents some hadiths of the Prophet related to other acts of worship and Islamic ethics, providing a comprehensive overview of the principles of the Islamic religion through hadiths and sermons.
descriptions.340: This book is compiled by Ibn Abi Asim, and deals with the topic of reminders and reminders in the Qur’an and Sunnah, with a focus on the Prophetic hadiths related to this topic. The author mentions Quranic verses related to remembrance and warning, and reviews prophetic hadiths that emphasize the importance of remembrance and insight in the life of a Muslim. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to clarify the meanings of remembrance and its importance in the Islamic religion.
descriptions.341: The book “Al-Mustakhraj Ali Al-Mustadrak by Al-Hakim = Amali Al-Iraqi” is one of the hadith works that deals with the virtues of hadith science and its people, with an emphasis on the importance of petition in transmitting and documenting hadith. The book includes an introduction that explains the virtue of hadith science, and a translation by the hadith scholars Al-Lubadi and Al-Iraqi, in addition to the benefits of petition in transmitting and preserving hadith. The book covers multiple chapters that address various topics related to hadith and its sciences, relying on approved hadith sources and principles.
descriptions.342: This book deals with a group of chained or serial hadiths, which are hadiths that begin with similar phrases and then branch out into several narrations. The book contains twelve serial hadiths, each of which begins with a different phrase, and the narrators of each hadith and its chains of transmission are reviewed. The book is a classification of hadith parts, and it aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the subject of serial hadiths and their chains of transmission, with a focus on the hadiths that were widespread among scholars and hadith scholars in scholarly councils.
descriptions.343: The Baghdadi Sheikhs of the Umayyads is a book that deals with the series of hadith narrators in Baghdad, where the author, Ibn Maslama Al-Umayyad, mentions his sheikhs and narrators in an organized manner, and emphasizes the value of this scholarly version by mentioning successive reputations. The book documents the narration and transmission from its sheikhs in a way that confirms the authenticity and accuracy of what is contained in it.
descriptions.344: The Baghdadi Sheikhs of Ibn Maslamah Al-Umayyad is a collection of hadith books that include a series of hadith narrations from the sheikhs of Baghdad, where the author mentions the names of the scholars of Baghdad and his professors from whom he took knowledge. The book deals with the narration of the hadith and its chain of transmission in detail, and aims to show its credibility and narration of the noble Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.345: This book, “Al-Mushaykhah” by Ibn al-Abnusi, deals with the narration of the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ about his sheikhs, and contains selected scientific benefits from their hadiths. It focuses on the series of hadith narrations and discusses eminent hadith scholars such as Al-Daraqutni, Al-Muqri’ Al-Kattani, and Al-Bazzar. The book is part of a scientific study that aims to document the hadith chain of transmission in an accurate and documented manner.
descriptions.346: This book is a collection of rare and unique Prophetic hadiths collected by Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili. It deals with hadiths from a number of companions and includes hadiths that are not famous or rare, which adds scientific value to the hadith content. The book aims to present diverse hadith material that is different from the famous hadiths, while maintaining accuracy in transmitting and documenting hadiths.
descriptions.347: This book is “The Selected Min Gharābīth of the Hadiths of Malik ibn Anas,” written by Abu Bakr ibn al-Muqri al-Asbahani, and it contains rare hadiths from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas. The book is a hadith book, as it focuses on narrating the Prophet’s hadiths in a selected and strange way, which adds scientific value to the hadith content.
descriptions.348: This book deals with the lives of the wives of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, focusing on telling the stories of their marriage and the details of their life with him. The author, Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar, deals with the life of each of the Prophet’s wives separately, reviewing important events in their lives with him and their personal characteristics. The book is a type of hadith book that relies on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and historical stories.
descriptions.349: This book is a collection of hadiths and hadiths related to asceticism and gentleness. In this work, Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi deals with selections from the Prophet’s hadiths and righteous sayings of prominent religious figures. The book focuses on promoting spiritual and moral values, and includes topics such as asceticism in this world, certainty in God, sincere love, and correcting the method in seeking knowledge. The book is distinguished by the diversity of its sources, as it combines sacred hadiths, antiquities, and stories told about the righteous.
descriptions.350: This book is a collection of selected hadiths of the Prophet, where Imam Al-Mizzi Jamal al-Din selected fifty-five hadiths from among what his sheikhs narrated. The book deals with a group of benefits and wisdom learned from hadiths, presenting them in an organized and organized manner, while maintaining the correct chain of narration for each hadith.
descriptions.351: This book is a collection of the virtues and news of Umm Sunbula Al-Aslamiya and other personalities. It deals with her biography and virtues, while mentioning her narrations and hadiths. Author Abu Orouba Al-Harrani focuses on conveying the chains of transmission and narrations related to these figures, relying on multiple sources in the field of Prophetic hadith. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the chains of transmission and transmitting historical and religious news.
descriptions.352: Al-Muntaqa min Musnad al-Muqaleen by Daalaj al-Sijzi is a book that deals with prophetic hadiths attributed to the Companions and followers, as it focuses on narrating the hadith in multiple and different forms from different methods, which enhances the authenticity and veracity of the transmission of those hadiths. The book contains a collection of hadiths that dealt with religious and devotional topics, relying on trustworthy narrators in a series of narrations of each hadith.
descriptions.353: The book “Al-Manthur Min Anecdotes and Questions” was written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Tahir Al-Maqdisi, and it is one of the hadith books that includes various anecdotes and hadiths. The book addresses various topics by narrating tales, legends, and prophetic hadiths, while providing comments and analyzes of the wisdom learned from them. The book combines historical fiction and philosophical reflection, making it a rich source of religious and moral information and teachings.
descriptions.354: This book, “Al-Mahrawaniyyat” or “Al-Fawaid Al-Mukhtabah Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” is a heritage study that deals with the lives and works of Abu Al-Qasim Al-Mahrawani and Abu Bakr Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi, with a focus on their scientific upbringing, their travels, their sheikhs, their students, and their impact on science. The book also deals with the benefits and strange things of the Prophet’s hadiths, relying on a careful selection of correct and important narrations.
descriptions.355: Al-Nisa’i’s book “The Names and Attributes” deals with the names and attributes of God, reviewing a group of Prophetic hadiths that mention these names and attributes, with a focus on their importance and the virtue of preserving them and using them in daily life. The book contains hadiths about mentioning God by His Most Beautiful Names, mentioning God’s name when eating and slaughtering, and other topics related to God’s names and attributes.
descriptions.356: This book is a collection of hadiths and fatwas related to piety and the morals of the jurist, where Ahmed bin Hanbal, in Al-Maruzi’s narration, addresses the definition of piety, its characteristics, and its importance in the life of a Muslim. The book focuses on warnings and rulings related to not diving into wells that Muslims hate, abstaining from dealing with those they hate, and avoiding buying from specific places, with reference to what is desirable and what is disliked in earning and working.
descriptions.357: This book, written by Al-Nasa’i, deals with the death of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and several chapters talk about the symptoms of his illness, his condition in his last days, his death, and his burial. The book mentions hadiths and narrations about what the Prophet indicated as evidence that his death was approaching, the pain he was suffering from, what he was doing during his illness, and the details of his burial, health, and shroud.
descriptions.358: This book deals with the indexes of the science of the Noble Hadith, focusing on selecting the Awali and important prophetic hadiths from the indexes of the author Sheikh Imam Al-Attar. It includes a scientific authorization from Sheikh Al-Attar to his student Sheikh Shaker Al-Aqqad, and it also includes serial hadiths and Shafi’i jurisprudential Sunnahs. The book was compiled by Al-Kuzbari from the books of his sheikhs and teachers, and it is considered a useful reference for students of knowledge in the field of the Prophet’s hadith and the chain of transmission of the narration.
descriptions.359: This book is a selection of biographies of hadith scholars whose surnames corresponded to the name of their father, selected by Alaa al-Din Moghalatai from the book of al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Khatib al-Baghdadi. The book deals with biographies according to the letters of the alphabet, and reviews the biographies of scholars and their chains of transmission without length or bias, relying on a careful investigation of an important scientific heritage in the field of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.360: This book, written by Al-Bayhaqi, is one of the hadith parts. It aims to correct the sayings of those who made a mistake in transmitting the sayings of Imam Al-Shafi’i. It contains hadiths on various topics related to worship and obligations, including those related to ablution, prayer, and Hajj. It reviews the hadiths in their correct form according to their original sources.
descriptions.361: The book, “Bughayat al-Multims fi Sevens of the Hadith of Imam Malik ibn Anas,” by the scholar Salah al-Din al-Ala’i, deals with a detailed study of the sevens of the hadith of Imam Malik ibn Anas. The book is divided into multiple parts, each part containing seven hadiths, and provides an accurate analysis and interpretation of each of these seven hadiths. The book aims to enrich jurisprudential and hadith knowledge by presenting the texts of the hadiths of Malik bin Anas in an organized and comprehensive manner.
descriptions.362: Baghyat al-Multams fi Sevenes of the Hadith of Imam Malik ibn Anas is a book that deals with the noble Prophet’s hadith by presenting its seven, i.e. the hadith narrated by Imam Malik ibn Anas in his book al-Muwatta’. The book consists of multiple parts, each part containing several hadiths, and aims to provide a comprehensive and detailed overview of these hadiths, relying on correct attribution and connected narration.
descriptions.363: The book “The History of Raqqa and Those Who Came to It Among the Companions of the Messenger of God” by Al-Qushayri Abu Ali deals with the history of the city of Raqqa and its people, including the Companions, Successors, jurists, and hadith scholars. The book mentions the biographies of a number of historical figures who lived in Raqqa, starting with the Companions such as Wabisa bin Ma’bad, all the way to the later Tabi’een and scholars. The book is part of the modern sections, and is concerned with documenting historical events and personalities associated with the city of Raqqa in early Islamic times.
descriptions.364: The book “The History of Denisar” by Dr. Omar bin Al-Khader deals with the biographies of the scholars and imams of Denisar in the fields of hadith, jurisprudence, and asceticism. The book focuses on presenting the biographies of the famous scholars for whom Denisar was famous, whether they lived there or passed through it, mentioning their scientific contributions and the importance of their role in spreading Sharia and Quranic sciences in the region.
descriptions.365: This book is a history of the death of the sheikhs who were taught by Al-Baghawi, and it is one of the hadith parts that includes a record of the deaths of scholars and memorizers who were contemporary to its author, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi. The book mentions the names of these sheikhs along with the dates of their deaths, and presents some details about his relationship with them and writing about him or not.
descriptions.366: The book “The Prohibition and Glorification of Murder” by Imam al-Maqdisi Abdul Ghani deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths that warn against killing a Muslim and are of great importance in Islamic law. The book focuses on the consequences and danger of killing a Muslim, considering it one of the major sins that destroy Islamic brotherhood and expose the perpetrator to torment in this world and the hereafter. The book also clarifies the protection of Muslim blood and the sanctity of violating it, and stresses the need to avoid strife and disagreement that lead to killing and destruction.
descriptions.367: This book by Al-Ajri deals with the prohibition of games and hobbies that are considered gambling or immorality, such as dice, chess, and music that carry inappropriate meanings. The author focuses on proving the prohibition of these activities through Sharia evidence, and states that listening to or practicing them is forbidden and invalid. The book aims to educate Muslims about the provisions of Sharia law regarding these forbidden activities.
descriptions.368: This book, written by Ibn Abi Hafez al-Maqdisi, deals with the issue of the prohibition of temporary marriage by reviewing the Prophetic hadiths and the legal evidence that confirms its invalidity and corruption, while clarifying the issue of abrogation in the legal rulings and how to establish the abrogated ruling and expire the abrogated ruling. The book also explains the difference between temporary marriage and adultery, and also includes a mention of the opponents’ arguments and their responses on this subject.
descriptions.369: This book, written by Al-Hafiz Jamal Al-Din Al-Mazzi, deals with the translation of the companion Maslama bin Mukhlid and an explanation of his companionship with the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Mizzi focuses on proving the companions of Maslama bin Mukhlid and transmitting his hadiths, while touching on some historical facts related to his life, especially the period of his rule over Egypt under Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan. The book falls within the framework of the hadith sections and aims to provide accurate information about the personality of Maslama bin Mukhlid and his role in Islamic history.
descriptions.370: This book deals with the legacy of the Prophet ﷺ and his sayings and deeds. It focuses on the Prophet's will regarding his various legacies, showing how they were distributed and organized after his death. The book includes talk about horses, animals, weapons, clothing, beds, comforters, pollen, and the service of the Messenger, thus providing a comprehensive picture of the Prophet’s material legacy and its rulings.
descriptions.371: This book is a classification by Abu Naim Al-Asbahani that deals with the narration of the Prophet’s hadith, focusing on mentioning the narrators and documenting their chains.
descriptions.372: This book, written by Abu Naeem Al-Asbahani, deals with the narrators from whom Saeed bin Mansour narrated, and mentions one hadith for each of them to determine their number and names. The author aims to highlight the status of Saeed bin Mansour as a trustworthy and honest hafiz. He refers to the death of Saeed bin Mansour in the year 227 AH, and mentions some of the great memorizers who narrated from him, such as Harun al-Hammal and Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Hanbal.
descriptions.373: This book, written by Ibn Asakir, deals with the topic of condolence in death, relying on the Prophet’s hadiths and sayings from the righteous. It focuses on the tragedy of a brother's death and the pain and grief it causes, and also mentions the virtues of good condolences and how to comfort those affected by loss. The book also covers some poems and hadiths related to death and patience with fate.
descriptions.374: This book deals with a famous hadith by Bahz bin Hakim (may Allah be pleased with him), as the author Ibn Nasir al-Din al-Dimashqi narrates it through a series of connected narrations, and in it he reviews hadiths and prophetic fatwas related to Islamic etiquette and morals, relying on Bahz bin Hakim’s narration and the sayings of scholars in documenting and correcting it. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with presenting and evaluating the Prophet’s hadiths and their narrations.
descriptions.375: The book “Three Councils of Amali Ibn Mardawayh” includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths and Islamic narrations, as it focuses on transmitting religious hadiths and sermons in a sequential and organized manner. The book deals with various topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, reviewing the sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and correcting prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.376: This book deals with the reward of fulfilling the needs of Muslim brothers through narrating prophetic hadiths about the virtue of those who seek to help their brothers in their needs. The author focuses on mentioning the reward that the helper receives from God Almighty, relying on authentic documents in the hadith narrations. The book is a hadith book that aims to strengthen the bonds of brotherhood between Muslims and encourage them to help each other.
descriptions.377: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, containing hadiths narrated on the authority of Al-Alaa bin Musa Al-Bahili by several narrators. The book covers a group of prophetic hadiths, including a hadith about the planting of Umm Mubashir al-Ansariyya, and another related to the hadith of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Omar, in addition to the hadith of Siwar bin Musab. The book is considered a source of hadith and aims to transmit and educate the Prophet’s hadiths through a continuous chain of narrations.
descriptions.378: Juz’ Abu al-Abbas al-Asmi is a collection of the Prophet’s hadiths narrated with serial chains of transmission, dealing with multiple topics of Islamic legislation and rulings. The book falls within the hadith parts that collect hadiths in an organized and orderly manner, relying on a connected narrative between narrators.
descriptions.379: The book “Part of Hadiths on Poetry” by Muhammad al-Maqdisi deals with the Prophetic hadiths related to poetry and its rulings, explaining what was reported from the Prophet ﷺ in praising and criticizing him. The book contains indexes to various topics related to poetry, including those related to the condemnation of poetry and what is mentioned regarding its virtue, with an appendix that includes hadiths about poetry that are not mentioned in the main part.
descriptions.380: This book is part of the hadith parts, containing hadith narrations transmitted by Ahmed bin Issam Al-Thaqafi. The part begins with a narration on the authority of Abu Hurairah in which a man asks the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ about a man’s prayer in one garment, and the hadith mentions in multiple details about the recommended dress for prayer. It also contains other narrations from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ related to the timings of bowing and prostrating in prayer and the virtues of the advanced rows in the mosque.
descriptions.381: This book is a hadith part in which Ibn Tharthal narrates a group of Prophetic hadiths with connected chains of transmission, and begins with the hadiths of the companion Ka’b ibn Ujrah. The book includes hadiths in various sections of jurisprudence, etiquette, and subtleties, such as the rulings on ablution, prayer, sales, farming, and Friday prayers, in addition to prophetic commandments regarding nudity, quarrels, and temptations.
descriptions.382: The book “Juz Ibn Amshliq” is a part of the hadith parts. It contains a collection of prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission. It begins with a narration on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Hussein bin Abi Al-Thabit, and mentions in it a hadith with a weak chain of transmission in an authentic text on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Abbas. It also contains other traceable and suspended hadiths, mentioning the weakness of some of their chains of narration.
descriptions.383: Juz’ Ibn al-Ghatrif by al-Jurjani is a part of selected Prophetic hadiths. It deals with a group of hadiths and fatwas related to purity, prayer, and other obligations, with a focus on some important jurisprudential rulings. The book contains hadiths related to ablution, washing, wiping over the socks, Hajj, Umrah, and other jurisprudential topics, accompanied by documents transmitted by Ibn al-Ghatrif from his sheikhs.
descriptions.384: The book “Juz’ Ibn Fayl” is a hadith fragment attributed to Abu Tahir al-Hasan bin Ahmad bin Fayl al-Balsi. It deals with a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The book is distinguished by its transmission of narrations through a series of narrators, and begins with a narration on the authority of Anas bin Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) about the Prophet ﷺ’s shortening of his prayers during the Farewell Hajj.
descriptions.385: The book Juz al-Karda by al-Kinani is a hadith fragment that contains selected hadiths of the Prophet, narrated with continuous chains of transmission. The book deals with multiple topics from the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his sayings, relying on connected narratives and authentic chains of transmission.
descriptions.386: The book “Juz’ al-Jirkani” is a collection of hadiths narrated from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, including multiple narrations through a series of authentic chains of transmission. The book deals with various religious and scientific topics, from ethics and worship to social and political issues, reviewing important hadith texts based on trustworthy narrators.
descriptions.387: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, containing the narration of Al-Hasan bin Rashiq Al-Askari on the authority of his sheikhs from Al-Amali. The book deals with the narration of the hadith through a series of narrators, starting from Al-Hasan bin Rashiq to Yusuf bin Khalil bin Abdullah Al-Dimashqi. The book focuses on transmitting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and their narration through a series of sheikhs.
descriptions.388: Juz' al-Hasan ibn Arafa al-Baghdadi is a collection of hadiths, fatwas, and prophetic rulings, dealing with various topics related to worship, morals, and Islamic jurisprudence. The book is distinguished by its part format, which includes separate hadiths that are not arranged within specific sections, which makes it a reference for researchers of prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas.
descriptions.389: Juz' al-Mu'mil ibn Ihab is a hadith juz that contains a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, relying on continuous chains of transmission. The book addresses multiple topics related to morals, worship, and sermons, presenting valuable texts in Islamic jurisprudence and the daily behavior of a Muslim.
descriptions.390: Juz’ Bakr ibn Bakkar is a collection of the Prophet’s hadiths in serial numbers. It includes issues of jurisprudence and Islamic etiquette, including those related to worship, transactions, etiquette, and fatwas on various jurisprudential topics. The book is based on the narrations of Jabir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), and is concerned with presenting the legal rulings in a direct and clear manner, relying on questions directed to the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them).
descriptions.391: This book is a part of the Prophet’s hadiths known as Juz Bibi, and it is part of the heritage of Muslim jurists and scholars. The book deals with a collection of Islamic hadiths and narrations, dealing with various topics from the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his teachings, relying on a series of narrators related to Al-Hurra Bibi bint Abd al-Samad al-Harawiyah al-Harthamiyya.
descriptions.392: This book is part of the Prophet’s hadiths, in which Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated his hadiths according to the narration of Zakaria bin Yahya Al-Maruzi. The book deals with an analytical study of the hadiths of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, along with providing information about its narrator and the chain of transmission for its narration. It is considered one of the important hadith parts in the Islamic heritage due to its high quality and containing important methods for correcting or improving hadiths, in addition to its many benefits that are not found in other sources.
descriptions.393: This book is part of the Fawa’id Ibn al-Sammak. It includes hadiths and fatwas by Hanbal bin Ishaq, and is classified as Hadith parts. It deals with various topics related to morals, legal rulings, and Islamic behaviors, deriving most of its content from the hadith of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the actions of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them).
descriptions.394: The book “Part of Ali bin Muhammad Al-Himyari” is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Messenger ﷺ. It deals with multiple topics related to morals, worship, and transactions, following the chain of transmission in their transmission. The book focuses on transmitting the hadiths in their original form while preserving their historical context, without addition or comment from its author.
descriptions.395: This book, “The Virtues of Rajab,” is part of the hadith volumes. It deals with the virtues of the month of Rajab, and in it Ibn Asakir transmits narrations and hadiths about the virtues of this month through a series of connected narrations. The book relies on the author's dictates and narrations from famous scholars and imams, and aims to document hadiths related to the month of Rajab and explain its virtues.
descriptions.396: This book is part of the Prophetic hadiths, containing narrations by Abu Hamid Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Yahya bin Bilal Al-Naysaburi, narrated by the imam Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah bin Mandah, then narrated by his son Abu Umair Abdul Wahhab. The section deals with a group of hadiths that were narrated in the context of the travels of students of knowledge, and the book mentions the names of the sheikhs who narrated these hadiths.
descriptions.397: This book is part of the Prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan Al-Ghadhairi on the authority of his sheikhs, and it was narrated in turn by the president, Abu Abdullah Al-Qasim bin Al-Fadl bin Ahmed bin Mahmoud Al-Thaqafi. The book deals with a group of hadiths circulating in Islamic heritage, with a variety of topics and stories, relying on narration links linked to a series of well-known narrators.
descriptions.398: This book is part of the Prophet’s hadiths. It contains a group of hadiths that he collected and narrated. It begins with a hadith related to the etiquette of sleeping and being awake, then moves to a hadith related to praising men and applauding women. It also includes hadiths related to various aspects of Islamic life such as hunting and prostitution, with a focus on legal rulings and Islamic etiquette.
descriptions.399: This book is part of the hadith sections, containing hadiths narrated by Al-Hasan bin Musa Al-Asheb on the authority of his sheikhs. It begins by narrating a hadith about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in which he mentions gratitude to God for His blessings, then deals with a group of miscellaneous hadiths on religious, scientific, and social topics. Hadiths are transmitted in the form of chain of transmission and narration, and include topics such as virtues, legal rulings, morals, and historical stories.
descriptions.400: This book is part of the hadith sections, containing the hadiths of Awwal from the audio recordings of Muhammad bin Abdul Moneim bin Ammar bin Hamel. The book deals with a series of hadiths and poetic poems that were heard from famous scholars and imams, and presents them in a sequential manner that begins with the author’s narration on the authority of his sheikh, then on the authority of his sheikh’s sheikh, and so on.
descriptions.401: This book is part of the Prophetic hadiths narrated with a continuous chain of transmission, as it contains hadiths that Sheikh Al-Hafiz Abu Dharr Al-Harawi heard from his sheikhs, and narrated from him by his children and grandchildren. The book deals with a series of narrations and hadiths attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, thus addressing the field of prophetic hadiths and their chains of transmission.
descriptions.402: This book is part of the selected hadiths of the Prophet from the part of Abu Masoud Ahmad ibn al-Furat, selected by the Hafiz Saladin al-Ala’i. It contains thirteen hadiths, including twelve hadiths from Al-Abdal and Al-Awali, in addition to another hadith narrated by Ibn Al-Furat through several narrators. The book deals with various topics from the life and year of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, presenting multiple accounts of important prophetic events and sayings.
descriptions.403: This part contains hadiths narrated by Yahya bin Ma'in on the authority of Abu Mansur Al-Shaybani, and includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential and doctrinal issues, in addition to the narrators' modifications and modifications. The book provides valuable benefits in the field of hadith and jurisprudence, especially with regard to jurisprudential issues that are not mentioned in other books by Ibn Moin. It also contains rare hadiths and chains of transmission.
descriptions.404: This book is part of Amali Abd al-Ghafir al-Farsi, containing dictations from Imam Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Ghafir ibn Ismail al-Farsi. The book covers a hadith agreed upon as authentic, from the hadith of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, and other hadiths transmitted by the author through a series of narrators. The book focuses on the Prophetic hadiths and their transmission with a connected chain of transmission, which makes it part of the hadith sections.
descriptions.405: This book deals with the noble Prophetic hadith by combining the prose and the composed ones, as it combines the hadiths in their original prose form and them after they have been set in poetry. The author aims to present hadiths in a diverse way that facilitates memorization and understanding, while preserving their accuracy and correct attribution to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book is one of the Hadith volumes that is concerned with collecting and classifying the Prophet’s hadiths in an innovative, artistic way.
descriptions.406: This book is part of the selected hadiths of the Prophet, containing thirty-three hadiths, collected by Al-Baghawi Abu Al-Qasim. The first hadith deals with the ruling on lying when swearing an oath related to someone other than the religion of Islam, while the second hadith talks about the virtue of praying for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book covers multiple topics of ethics and worship, and aims to spread the teachings of Islam and promote the concepts of faith and good deeds among Muslims.
descriptions.407: This book is part of the hadith parts containing a collection of prophetic hadiths with varying topics, ranging from legal rulings, sermons, and historical stories related to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. The book is characterized by a sequential chain of transmission that reflects the nature of the traditional hadith parts, with a focus on narrating the hadiths in their original form without interpretation or lengthy commentary.
descriptions.408: This book deals with two hadiths, one of which relates to the virtue of the month of Rajab, and it is one of the prophetic hadiths that talk about the virtues of the sacred months and their importance in Islam. The author Abu Muasher al-Tabari narrates it through a series of connected narrations, and aims to convey and document this hadith in an accurate and documented manner. The book falls within the hadith sections that are concerned with collecting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.409: This book is part of the hadith parts containing five graduation hadiths about the five imams, which are hadiths narrated by Al-Hafiz Alaa Al-Din Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Balban from his audiobooks. The book deals with only five hadiths, each hadith related to a male narrator. In his introduction, Ibn Balban reviews the importance of the prophetic hadiths and the virtue of transmitting them from the imams of hadith.
descriptions.410: This book deals with seven sessions of Hadiths and Amali by Abu Taher Al-Mukhlis, where in each session it presents a group of narratives, stories, and prophetic hadiths. The book is based on a series of connected narrations that begin with the sheikh and jurist Bahaa al-Din al-Qasim bin Imam Thiqa al-Din, passing through several other narrators until it reaches Abu Taher al-Mukhlis. The book falls within the hadith sections that are concerned with documenting and transmitting the Prophet’s hadiths and the narrations of scholars.
descriptions.411: This book deals with the terms and conditions of Caliph Omar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) with the Christians, explaining the treaties and conditions he agreed upon in his dealings with them. The book includes a narration of the hadith of Wasil al-Dimashqi and his debate with the Christians, relying on a series of continuous narrations from hadith scholars. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and the jurisprudential decisions of the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
descriptions.412: This book is part of the works of Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi. It deals with the hadith of Ibn Omar (may Allah be pleased with them both) on how to check the sighting of the crescent at the beginning and end of the month of Ramadan. It focuses on the Prophetic hadiths related to the rulings on fasting during Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr, relying on multiple methods of narrating the hadith, and aims to show confirmation of the sighting of the crescent moon or estimate the number of days in the month in case of ambiguity.
descriptions.413: This book is part of my hadith dealing with the narration of the hadith “On the authority of Ka’b bin Ujrah in praying upon the Prophet ﷺ”, written by Ali bin Al-Mufaddal Al-Maqdisi. The book deals with the study of the author's life and his writings, with a focus on this part devoted to the aforementioned hadith. The book also includes a scientific investigation of the hadith, where the author studied and documented the methods of its chain of transmission, while providing a textual attribution service for the hadiths contained therein. The book falls within the hadith sections that hadith scholars followed in previous centuries to serve the Sunnah of the Prophet in an objective and concise manner.
descriptions.414: This book is part of the hadith parts that deals with the readings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakr and Omar in the Holy Qur’an. It contains multiple hadiths about Malik’s reading of Surat Al Imran and other surahs, narrated on the authority of the Companions and Followers. It aims to show the diversity of frequent readings from the predecessors in the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.415: This book is part of a collection of Prophetic hadiths. It begins with a narration of a hadith about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in which he urges us to convey the hadiths as he heard them without distortion. The book contains multiple narrations of various prophetic hadiths, narrated by noble companions, and is distinguished by its transmission of chains of transmission and hadiths in an accurate documentary manner.
descriptions.416: This book is part of Ibn al-Ghazi's collection of Amāl, containing one majlis that was dictated in the Vizier's House in Isfahan. The council deals with a hadith about seeing God in a dream, where the author reviewed the narrations of hadith scholars on this subject, relying on what was narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ and the famous narrations mentioned by some imams in this context. The book is one of the hadith parts concerned with documenting hadiths and transmitting them from their sheikhs.
descriptions.417: This book is part of the hadith parts, containing one session of the hadith of Imam Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Ibrahim bin Daoud bin Al-Attar Al-Shafi’i. The book deals with the narration of the hadith through a continuous chain of chain of transmission, as it begins with the narration of the author’s sheikh and the approval of his hadith scholars, and then moves to the narration of the hadith through a series of well-known narrators. The book aims to show the high level of chain of transmission and the accuracy of interpretation in the narration of the Noble Prophet’s Hadith.
descriptions.418: This book is part of a collection of hadiths and benefits by Imam Al-Layth bin Saad, which deals with the hadith of Thumama bin Uthal Al-Hanafi and his story with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book focuses on the Prophetic hadiths and their benefits, and reviews the methods of documenting the hadiths and their narrators.
descriptions.419: This book includes two parts of the hadiths and narrations of Imam Abu Al-Hussein Ali bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bishran, narrated from him by other scholars. The book deals with the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and traces through a continuous narration series, which makes it part of the hadith parts. It includes historical and literary texts related to the narration of the hadith and its transmission among scholars.
descriptions.420: This book is part of the Hadith volumes containing dictations by Al-Nasa’i, in which he narrates hadith after hadith using dictation. The text begins with a sequence in the narration through a series of narrators, and contains a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by the companions and followers. The book also includes another council that follows the first part, which indicates that it is part of a larger series or group of hadith parts.
descriptions.421: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, dealing with the handshakes of Imam Muslim and Imam al-Nasa’i. It contains a hadith about a handshake by Imam Muslim and hadiths about a handshake by Imam al-Nasa’i, with some other hadiths related to a handshake included. It aims to document and evaluate these hadiths through graduation and investigation.
descriptions.422: This book is part of a collection of hadiths by Imam Abu Naim Al-Asbahani. It deals with hadiths about Abu Ali Al-Sawaf and contains multiple narrations from the Companions and followers. It focuses on transmitting hadiths in a sequential manner, relying on authentic documents in its transmission of narrations, and contains various topics related to morals, worship, and transactions.
descriptions.423: This book deals with the hadiths of Imam Ayoub Al-Sakhtiani, narrated by Al-Jahdhami, and contains a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, arranged in a part-and-page manner. The book focuses on transmitting the hadiths in their original form, while mentioning the chain of transmission for their narration, and reviews multiple topics from the lives of Muslims, their worship, and morals, relying on an authentic chain of transmission in the narration of the hadiths.
descriptions.424: This book is part of the Prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the sheikhs of Abu Al-Hussein Abdul-Wahhab bin Al-Hasan Al-Kilabi, known as the brother of Tabuk. It contains serial narrations by Al-Kilabi and his teachers, and begins with Judge Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Abdul Baqi Al-Ansari’s narration from him. The book deals with a group of hadiths that dealt with various topics from the life and Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, including those related to historical events such as the conquest of Mecca, and some related to legal rulings and Islamic etiquette.
descriptions.425: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, dealing with the narration of hadiths about major sins on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ by eleven companions. The author Al-Bardiji begins by narrating a hadith by Abdullah bin Masoud about major sins, in which the Prophet ﷺ was asked about them and he replied that among the major sins are associating others with God, killing one’s father for fear that he will eat with him, and adultery with his neighbor’s partner. The book continues to mention the narrations of other companions on this subject.
descriptions.426: This book is part of “Awali Hisham bin Urwa and others” written by Ibn Khalil, and is related to the field of prophetic hadiths and historical narratives. It contains multiple narrations about the companion Hisham bin Urwa and other hadiths, taken from many different sources, which indicates the importance of this part as a source of hadith and narration.
descriptions.427: This book is a selected part of the biography of Ibn Hisham, containing a collection of hadiths related to the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the biography of the Companions. The author Muhammad Al-Muzaffari relies on a continuous chain of transmission to transmit the hadiths, and the book begins with a long narration that narrates Juwayri bin Mut’im’s observations of the Prophet before the revelation came to him. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to present a selected overview of the Prophet’s biography through a group of related narratives.
descriptions.428: This book is a part that deals with the deaths of a group of hadith scholars, written by Imam Al-Hafiz Abdul Rahim bin Abi Al-Wafa Al-Asbahani, known as Ibn Abi Masoud. The book mentions the death of a number of scholars and hadith scholars, along with some details about them. It is one of the hadith parts concerned with documenting chains of transmission and translations.
descriptions.429: Juz Lulu’ is a hadith book that deals with the rulings on playing backgammon, and it was written by Lulu’ bin Ahmad. The book is concerned with the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and their grading. In it, the author mentions the series of hadith narrations by mentioning the names of the narrators and hadith scholars who heard from him or authorized him. The book includes approvals and endorsements from eminent scholars, which indicates its scientific status in the world of hadith.
descriptions.430: This book is part of the hadith parts, containing a hadith narration attributed to Muhammad bin Asim Al-Thaqafi Al-Asbahani. The book relies on a series of narrators starting from Al-Hussein bin Ali Al-Jaafi to Muhammad bin Asim, and includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the companions and followers. The book also includes biographies of some narrators and their narrations of hadiths, with a focus on the chain of transmission in transmitting hadiths.
descriptions.431: This book is part of the hadiths of Abu Bakr al-Souli. It contains a collection of prophetic hadiths that he narrated on the authority of his sheikhs. The hadith initially deals with the phenomenon of a solar eclipse and how the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ dealt with it, then it moves on to talking about how to identify hypocrites through their hatred of Ali bin Abi Talib (peace be upon him). The book is of the type of hadith parts that collect hadiths in a specific order without dividing them into sections or chapters.
descriptions.432: This book is part of the hadiths of Abu Omar Al-Sulami, containing his narrations from his sheikhs, and it contains a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the companions and followers. It deals with various topics related to worship, morals, and sermons, with a focus on hadiths that urge submission to God’s command and staying away from pre-Islamic customs such as ritual punishment and infection. The book is one of the hadith parts concerned with documenting hadiths and transmitting them with a continuous chain of transmission.
descriptions.433: This book is part of the hadiths of Abu Amr Al-Sulami, containing a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, dealing with various topics of worship, morals, and transactions. The book is distinguished by its sequence in the chain of transmission, as it begins with hadiths attributed directly to the Prophet, passing through generations of narrators until it reaches Abu Amr Al-Sulami.
descriptions.434: This book is a part of a hadith in which Ibn al-Muqayr narrates hadiths on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission. It includes a collection of diverse prophetic hadiths on topics of beliefs, acts of worship, etiquette, and rulings, such as the virtue of conquest for the sake of God, the signs of the Hour, the prohibition of tattoos, the urge to learn the Qur’an, the rulings on prayer, charity, sacrifices, and others included in his index.
descriptions.435: This book is part of Al-Qazzaz’s hadiths from his sheikhs. It contains a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, transmitted through a series of narrators. The hadith mentioned at the beginning of the book deals with the ruling on Friday prayer being obligatory for men, with the exceptions of women, slaves, travelers, and the sick. The book falls within the hadith sections, which include transmitting hadiths in their original form with mentioning of their narrators.
descriptions.436: This book is part of the hadith of Ibn Shaheen, and it includes a series of hadiths of the Prophet and narrations of hadith scholars, dealing with various topics of morals and acts of worship. The book is based on Ibn Shaheen’s narration of his sheikhs and scholars, and presents a continuous narration chain starting from Ibn Shaheen up to the most ancient imams and scholars. The book falls within the hadith sections that are concerned with collecting and documenting hadiths.
descriptions.437: This book is part of the hadith of Ibn Shaheen, which Ibn al-Muhtadi collected from the narration of Sheikh Abu Hafs Omar bin Ahmed bin Shaheen. The book deals with the narration of Ibn Shaheen’s hadith through a series of narrators, starting from Ibn Shaheen until the last reader, with a focus on narrating and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths. The book falls within the hadith sections that are concerned with collecting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.438: This book is part of the hadith of Al-Awza’i, narrated by Ahmed bin Hudhalam, and contains a collection of prophetic hadiths and historical narrations, with diverse topics ranging from jurisprudence, ethics, and Islamic history. The talk addresses various topics related to worship, transactions, and morals, with a focus on historical events and facts related to Islamic society in early times.
descriptions.439: This book is part of the version of Ibrahim bin Saad, and it includes a chain of transmission of hadith. The index mentions a number of Prophetic hadiths on various topics related to worship, morals, and transactions. The book relies on a continuous chain of narrations from hadith scholars, which indicates its importance in the field of hadith chains of transmission and hadith narrations.
descriptions.440: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, containing fifty-eight hadiths, and it was narrated by Sheikh Al-Musnad Al-Muammar Abi Ali Al-Hasan bin Omar Al-Kurdi. The book deals with hadith after hadith in the chain method, reviewing selected benefits from the narrations of the two sheikhs Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn al-Salt and Abu Ahmad Ubayd Allah al-Fardhi, relying on the graduation of Uthman ibn Balban al-Muqatali.
descriptions.441: Juz’ Ya’la bin Abbad is a hadith juz that contains a copy of the hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, narrated from his sheikhs, and is distinguished by its style in narrating the hadiths and their chains of transmission. The book covers multiple topics from the Prophet's life and morals, providing a comprehensive overview of his teachings and rulings.
descriptions.442: This book is part of the Hadith volumes, dealing with the conditions of the Christians according to what was narrated by Judge Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Zubr al-Rab’i. It contains hadiths related to the opinions of jurists about dealing with Christians, accompanied by hadiths attached to it by Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahhab bin Ahmad al-Kalabi. It focuses on conveying hadiths and narrations related to the topic through a connected narration chain.
descriptions.443: This book is part of the hadith sections. It deals with the conditions for Christians set by Judge Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Zubr al-Rab’i, and it contains prophetic hadiths in this context. In its formulation, it follows the well-known hadith tradition, as it begins with the chain of transmission of the hadith, then its text, and mentions at its end other hadiths by Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahhab bin Ahmad al-Kalabi.
descriptions.444: The book Jamharat al-Juza’ al-Hadith is a collection of rare hadith parts. It contains nineteen different parts, each of which deals with a group of hadiths and narrations. The book includes narrations from various hadith scholars and scholars, and aims to collect and document rare and important hadith parts of Islamic heritage. The book provides a comprehensive overview of hadiths and narrations that have been narrated over time by well-known hadith scholars.
descriptions.445: This book by Ibn al-Mubarrad deals with a hadith mentioned in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad about the cupping of the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque, and presents the point of view that the hadith is a Qur’an and that it was “he cupped” instead of “he cupped.” The author deals with the narrations of the hadith and the sayings of the scholars regarding it, and infers the authenticity of the narration “He was cupped” despite what is being raised about the authenticity of the authentication. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to clarify the correct understanding of the hadith and indicate whether it is a Qur’an or not.
descriptions.446: The book “Jiyad Al-Musilasalat” by Al-Suyuti is a book that deals with a group of serial hadiths, where each hadith is classified based on a specific series related to a topic or a specific category of scholars or practices. The book covers various topics ranging from hadiths related to Shafi’i and Sufi jurists, through hadiths on the day of the two Eids and answering prayers, all the way to hadiths related to the fathers and Egyptians. The book focuses on methods of sequencing hadiths and transmitting them from one narrator to another, which makes it a useful reference in studying methods of transmitting and documenting hadiths.
descriptions.447: This book is a collection of hadiths and narrations on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam (may Allah be pleased with him), narrated by Al-Juybari and collected by Al-Bayhaqi on various issues. The book addresses multiple topics related to the life and fatwas of Abdullah bin Salam, reviewing his narrations and analyzing them from the perspective of hadith science.
descriptions.448: This book deals with the hadith of Al-Ifk, which is a well-known hadith in the biography of the Prophet related to the incident of Aisha’s accusation (may Allah be pleased with her), where the author Abdul-Ghani Al-Maqdisi explains the narration of the hadith and its chain of transmission through a series of narrators. The book focuses on documenting the chains of transmission and narrations related to this famous hadith, while providing information about the virtues of female companions.
descriptions.449: This book includes a hadith by Imam Taqi al-Din al-Baalbaki, which is one of the authentic hadiths of the Prophet circulated in hadith books. The book deals with a collection of hadiths and narrations about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, dealing with various topics of morals, worship, and transactions. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and classifying the Prophet’s hadiths and documenting their narration.
descriptions.450: This book by the writer Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi deals with a specific hadith narrated by six followers, and mentions in it the ways of narrating the hadith and the differences in it. The author focuses on researching and analyzing this hadith from a critical scientific perspective, reviewing the opinions of scholars and their criticism of it. The book falls within the hadith sections that are concerned with studying and analyzing the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.451: This book is a study and investigation of the narrations and hadiths of Imam Al-Sakan bin Jumah, as it deals with a group of prophetic hadiths that were narrated and circulated across generations, relying on a series of narrations connected to the main hadith books. The book focuses on transmitting and analyzing hadiths from a historical and scientific perspective, while preserving their context and narrators.
descriptions.452: This book deals with a hadith by a Salafi about the ruler of Kufa, and it contains multiple prophetic hadiths narrated from companions and imams among the followers. It focuses on describing the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ’s prayer and his actions during prayer, while presenting a narration series of chains of transmission that the author found. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and correcting prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.453: This book includes a hadith by Al-Dibaji Al-Uthmani, which is one of the Prophet’s hadiths and monuments that deal with the commandments and sayings of important Islamic figures. The talk focuses on the importance of good deeds and asceticism in this world, based on the context of a dialogue between Salman Al Farsi and others, in addition to a dialogue between two monks. The talk also covers advice on how to deal with life and death, with an emphasis on humility and asceticism.
descriptions.454: This book deals with the hadith of shaking hands through a series of connected narrations starting from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ until the author of the book, Abu Taher Al-Salafi. The book focuses on describing the moment of the handshake with the Prophet and the feelings and attributes that accompanied it, then moves on to document the chain of handshakes over time with each narrator until it reaches the Salafi. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.455: This book deals with the story of an incident that occurred in Mecca about the search for missing money called “Al-Himyan,” which is a thousand dinars that was mentioned in a hadith of the Prophet. The author, Mu'alla bin Saeed Al-Tanukhi, tells the story of the poor sheikh who found it and refused to take it for himself, but rather recommended that it be returned to its owner. The book falls within the framework of the modern parts and contains a dialogue between the main characters about how to deal with this lost money, with an emphasis on religious and moral values ​​in such situations.
descriptions.456: This book is part of the hadith of Shu'bah bin Al-Hajjaj Al-Ataki, as it deals with the narration of his hadiths and their grading by Ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Bazzaz. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths and their chains of transmission through a series of narrators, starting from the author’s sheikhs and ending with Shu’bah ibn al-Hajjaj. The book aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the Prophetic hadiths narrated by Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj and document them.
descriptions.457: This book deals with the hadith of Muhammad bin Bashar Bandar on the authority of his sheikhs, and is concerned with narrating the Prophetic hadiths in their sequential form from the narrators to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author, Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili, focuses on transmitting hadiths in an accurate documentary manner, relying on a solid narrative chain of transmission that shows the path of transmission of hadiths across generations.
descriptions.458: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the great companion Anas bin Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), and it was narrated by Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari on the authority of Suleiman Al-Taymi and other narrators. The book deals with hadith after hadith, showing the chain of narration of each hadith from the beginning of the chain of transmission to the end, with a focus on the hadiths that relate to the words and actions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.459: This book deals with the hadith of Musab bin Abdullah Al-Zubayri, and is considered part of the hadith works. Al-Baghawi’s author, Abu al-Qasim, presents a collection of the Prophet’s hadiths with a chain of transmission, and the text begins by narrating the hadith from its first sources through a series of narrators. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths accurately while preserving the chain of transmission, which makes it an important reference in the field of hadiths.
descriptions.460: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in which Hisham bin Ammar deals with various hadiths from their primary sources, showing the chain of their narrations and chains of transmission.
