The book focuses on transmitting hadiths in their original form while preserving their historical and narrative context, which makes it an important reference in the field of Prophetic hadith.
descriptions.461: This book was written by Al-Bayhaqi, and it deals with the lives of the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them after their death, reviewing hadiths and narrations indicating that the prophets are alive in their graves praying, relying on multiple sources, including what was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Qutaybah. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to document these meanings by conveying the hadiths and sayings contained on this subject.
descriptions.462: Characteristics of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, is a book written by Ahmed bin Shuaib Al-Nasa’i, one of the imams of the Prophet’s hadith, in which he collects the virtues and virtues of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib.
descriptions.463: This book includes five hadiths from the hadiths of Al-Hafiz Al-Iraqi, dealing with topics related to the importance of answering the call, Bilal’s command to intercede in the call to prayer and frequency in the iqama, and teaching prayer to boys, relying on a chain of continuous and reliable narrations. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and transmitting them with correct chains of transmission.
descriptions.464: Evidence of Prophethood by Al-Faryabi is a book that deals with hadiths and narrations that confirm the prophecy of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book focuses on proving the miracles and evidence that confirm the truth of his prophecy, by narrating events and stories that happened with him and his companions. The book is a type of hadith book that relies on the narration and documentation of the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.465: This book deals with the hadith of Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, who is Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Ubaid bin Sufyan Al-Qurashi, known as the author of the book Al-Shiqat. In this work, the author Al-Madani mentions what he encountered from the hadith of Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, and provides information about his biography and knowledge, with a focus on his role as a teacher of noble sons during the era of the caliphs. The book contains stories and hadiths related to Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and his influence on those around him.
descriptions.466: A book on hadith parts, in which the author, Abu Musa al-Madini, mentions the names of those he heard from among the companions of the imam al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah bin Mandah, arranging them according to the letters of the dictionary, with allocating chapters to the worshipers, the family of Ibn Mandah, their women, and their dependents.
descriptions.467: This book, written by Abu Naeem Al-Isbahani, deals with mentioning those who bear the name of a group of follower narrators, explaining their biography and narrations about the Companions. It focuses on several people with the same name, each of whom has his place in the world of hadith and Islamic history, and mentions the stories that were told about them. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting hadith narrators and their biographies.
descriptions.468: This book by Al-Hasan Al-Khallal is one of the hadith parts. It addresses those who only had one hadith and those who did not narrate from their sheikh except one hadith. In this work, Al-Khalal shows the hadiths of some narrators who only narrated one hadith, or only narrated one hadith on the authority of their sheikh, which indicates the importance of those hadiths in documenting the chain of transmission of the hadith and the authenticity of its transmission.
descriptions.469: This book, “The Condemnation of Interpretation” by Sheikh al-Maqdisi Muwaffaq al-Din, deals with the subject of interpretation of the attributes of God Almighty, and mentions the doctrine of the Salaf in this regard. The author focuses on clarifying the names and attributes of God that the righteous predecessors followed, and calls for following them and imitating them in the afterlife. The book is a hadith book and aims to demonstrate the danger of wrong interpretation of the attributes of God Almighty.
descriptions.470: This book, “Investigation of Heavy People,” by Ibn al-Marzban al-Muhawili, deals with the subject of censure and censure of heavy people, that is, those who tend to be slow, lazy, and lethargic in their actions and behavior. The book relies on Prophetic hadiths and Qur’anic verses to explain the consequences and harms of heaviness in religion and the world. It aims to warn the reader against following these qualities and encourage him to acquire light qualities that mean speed and activity in worship and good deeds.
descriptions.471: The book “The Condemnation of Sodomy” by Al-Ajri deals with the topic of adultery between men, reviewing the provisions of Islamic law regarding this forbidden sexual intercourse, and citing the story of the people of Lot and the torment that befell them, to alert Muslims and warn them against committing such immorality. The book also reviews the opinions of scholars and jurists on the ruling and punishment of sodomy, with a focus on warning against falling into this sin and explaining its severe punishment.
descriptions.472: This book is a collection of hadiths about repentance and the virtues of the month of Ramadan, in addition to a hadith about the virtues of the Day of Arafah. It also includes a chapter on condemning those with two faces and two tongues. In this work, the author Ibn Asakir deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths, explaining in them the virtues of some religious deeds and condemning those who show a different face and speak a different language. The book is one of the hadith parts and aims to publish authentic hadiths and explain the virtues of some Islamic acts of worship.
descriptions.473: This book is part of Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir’s gatherings in the Damascus Mosque, in which he discusses censuring those who do not act according to his knowledge. The author focuses on reminding people of the importance of applying the knowledge and jurisprudence they know, and cites prophetic hadiths and narrations to strengthen his arguments. The book is part of a series of hadiths and sermons aimed at guiding Muslims towards the right path in their religious and worldly lives.
descriptions.474: This book deals with the topic of seeing God Almighty in the afterlife, reviewing the Prophetic hadiths related to this topic. The author focuses on clarifying that seeing God will not harm any of His servants, and that it will be similar to seeing the moon in its brilliance, with the promise of Paradise and an increased view of the face of God Almighty. The book relies on a series of hadiths related to this topic, and presents them in the form of chain of transmission and narration.
descriptions.475: Imam Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi’s letter to Imam Abu Muhammad al-Juwayni deals with issues in the science of hadith and others. In his letter, al-Bayhaqi discusses issues related to the narration and authentication of hadith, commenting on al-Juwayni’s classification in the science of hadith. The letter also touched on Al-Bayhaqi’s methodology in distinguishing what is valid and what is not valid as evidence as evidence, with references to some hadiths and jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.476: Risala Al-Musilasilat by Al-Kattani Muhammad ibn Jaafar is a study in the science of hadith that deals with different types of serial hadiths, which are hadiths connected to each other by certain links such as the day of Eid, reading Surat Al-Saff, the jurists, shaking hands, and others. The book focuses on the series of chains of transmission and how to link and document them, relying on transferring hadiths from multiple sheikhs and documenting them in a serial manner.
descriptions.477: This book is an interpretation of God Almighty’s saying, “Indeed, Abraham was a nation,” attributed to its author, Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Ali bin Tulun. The book deals with the interpretation of the Holy Verse and the analysis of its various meanings, reviewing the life of Abraham (peace be upon him), his attributes, and his role in spreading the correct doctrine. It also focuses on the concept of the nation in Islam and how people imitate Abraham in worship and piety.
descriptions.478: This thesis deals with research into the claim of some people that they are descendants of Hamzah al-Khalaf ibn al-Abbas, and investigates whether there is any historical or proven origin for the existence of a person with this name within the descendants of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him). The author, Burhan al-Din al-Naji, relies in his criticism on available historical and scientific sources, and confirms that there is no mention of a person named Hamza al-Khalaf in the approved genealogy books. It also stresses the need for the plaintiff to prove with conclusive evidence the validity of his claim, and notes the danger of claiming paternity without strong evidence. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to verify the authenticity of the claimed lineages and criticize unconfirmed historical claims.
descriptions.479: The book “Sports of the Body” by Abu Naim Al-Asbahani deals with sports and physical games in Islam, reviewing prophetic hadiths related to wrestling, archery, and other sports. The book focuses on the virtue of exercising and its benefits in purifying the soul and cleansing sins, basing its content on authentic prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.480: Silsilat al-Dhahab by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani is an investigation of al-Shafi’i’s narrations on the authority of Malik, and follows the chain of chains of transmission of the hadith from Malik to al-Shafi’i. The book deals with the narration of the Prophet’s hadith through a series of narrators, with a focus on what was narrated on the authority of Malik bin Anas through Al-Shafi’i.
descriptions.481: Sunan Abu Bakr Al-Athram is a book in Islamic jurisprudence that deals with the hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ related to ablution and bathing, with a focus on the details of wiping the head and how to do it. The book also includes hadiths about the rulings on ablution and washing on various topics such as wiping the turban, wiping the ears, impurities, and other issues related to purity in Islamic law.
descriptions.482: This book, “The Slogan of the Companions of Hadith,” by Abu Ahmad Al-Hakim, deals with multiple topics in Islamic jurisprudence and the Prophet’s hadith, including faith and work, an explanation of the Qur’an, the uncreated word of God, and the obligatory conditions for prayer and purity, with a focus on hadiths and evidence related to these topics. The book also includes details on how to perform prayers and greetings, etiquette of entering the mosque, etiquette of prostration, and other topics related to Islamic worship.
descriptions.483: Hammam bin Munabbih's newspaper is one of the oldest hadith newspapers compiled by the Islamic scholar Hammam bin Munabbih (born in 19 AH, died in 101 AH/719 AD).
descriptions.484: The clear Sunnah or the interpretation of the people of prohibition and the landmarks of guidance is a book by Muhammad bin Jarir bin Yazid bin Katheer bin Ghalib, known as Imam Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Jarir al-Tabari, (224 AH-310 AH / 839-923 AD) and it is a book on the Islamic faith and an explanation of some of its origins. This book is considered one of the brief texts that express Al-Tabari’s position on some doctrinal issues of his time, and it reflects the approach of the Sunnis and the community on issues of attributes, faith, the Qur’an, the Companions, seeing God in the afterlife, the actions of His servants, and so on. Then warn against saying to someone what he did not say. Thus he concluded the book.
descriptions.485: This book, “The Description of Paradise,” by Hafiz Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi, deals with the description of Paradise and its details by talking about its doors, rivers, rooms, trees, food, and drink. The author mentions prophetic hadiths related to the description of Paradise and what brings its people into it, with the writer and reader constantly praying that God will admit everyone to Paradise. The book is a type of hadith book that relies on the Prophet’s hadiths to describe Paradise.
descriptions.486: This book describes the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in multiple aspects of his life, including his physical attributes, morals, biography, and etiquette. The author relies on historical narratives and hadiths to present a comprehensive picture of the Prophet, focusing on his physical description and good qualities. The book consists of hadith sections and aims to introduce the reader to the life of the Prophet and his attributes in a detailed and accurate manner.
descriptions.487: The book, “The Characteristics of Hypocrisy and Condemnation of Hypocrites,” by Al-Farabi, deals with the interpretation of the characteristics and morals of a hypocrite, reviewing prophetic hadiths that show that whoever lies when he speaks, breaks a promise when he promises, and betrays when he is trusted is a true hypocrite. The book focuses on three characteristics that indicate an individual's hypocrisy, mentioning cases of those who have lost one or two of these characteristics and the consequences that result from that.
descriptions.488: The book “The Characteristics of Hypocrisy and the Characteristics of the Hypocrites” by Abu Naim Al-Asbahani deals with the topic of hypocrisy and its symptoms, reviewing verses from the Holy Qur’an and the hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that talk about condemning hypocrisy and explaining the characteristics of hypocrites. The book focuses on describing the morals of the hypocrite and how to warn against them, relying on hadith sources to provide a comprehensive picture of this important topic in Islamic law.
descriptions.489: This book deals with a hadith about the Most Beautiful Names of God, focusing on the narration of the hadith: “Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. It is Witr and loves Witr.” The author Abu Naeem Al-Isbahani presents multiple versions of this hadith through a series of chains of narrations, relying on different methods of transmitting and documenting it. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to collect and analyze narratives related to this important hadith in Islamic literature.
descriptions.490: This book deals with the description of the Prophet’s pulpit and clearly defines the pulpit in its context, highlighting the news and hadiths related to the construction and finishing of the pulpit taken by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author Ibn Nasir al-Din al-Dimashqi relies on a series of narrators to convey this news, making it part of Hadith literature.
descriptions.491: This book contains ten hadiths from the first and second parts of the hadith of Al-Layth bin Saad, and the content relates to the narration of prophetic hadiths through a connected narration series, with a focus on hadiths related to purity and acts of worship.
descriptions.492: This book deals with topics from hadiths and anecdotes related to rational people who appear to be mad or obsessed. It contains various narratives and hadiths narrated in the form of Prophetic hadiths, dealing with special cases of people whose intelligence appears at specific times despite their mental illness. It focuses on characters such as Ulayan the Majnun, and presents dialogues and stories that show the intelligence and wisdom of these people at certain moments.
descriptions.493: This book deals with the topic of hadiths related to the two days of Eid, arranged in a sequential manner in narration and transmission. It focuses on a hadith told by Yahya bin Abi Mansur Al-Sayrafi on the authority of his sheikhs, and presents a sequence in the narration that begins with Sheikh Thabit bin Mishrif Al-Khabaz and ends with Imam Ibn Qadamasa. The book aims to clarify the reason for the serial hadith on the day of the two Eids, and it includes a narration of the series of narrations of hadiths related to the two Eids.
descriptions.494: Awali Al-Harith bin Abi Usama is a book that deals with the noble Prophetic hadith, as it contains a collection of hadiths and narrations about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths in their original form without lengthy commentary or interpretation, which makes it an important reference in hadith science. The book includes multiple topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, based on the narration of Al-Harith bin Abi Usama, which is considered one of the reliable narrations in Islamic heritage.
descriptions.495: This book is an investigation by Awali Al-Layth bin Saad, and it is a collection of Prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Companions and Followers. The book deals with a group of separate and diverse hadiths in their topics, presented by one narrator to another through a series of connected narratives. The book aims to collect and document what was reported from the people of his journey from Egypt, and begins by narrating the transmission chain of hadiths starting from Al-Layth bin Saad to the earlier narrators.
descriptions.496: The book “Awali Muslim” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani covers forty hadiths selected from Sahih Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj. The workbook focuses on the difference in the narrations of these hadiths between Sahih Muslim and Sahih al-Bukhari, either in the chain of transmission or in the third or fourth part of it. The book aims to collect and analyze these intersecting narratives among the treasures of the Prophet’s hadith, providing the reader with an opportunity for further study and analysis in this field.
descriptions.497: This book deals with the virtues of naming the names Ahmed and Muhammad, using legal narrations and hadiths as evidence. The author aims to show the blessings associated with these names and the virtue of naming them, reviewing the traces mentioned in the command to name children Ahmed or Muhammad, hoping for the blessings of the honorable name. The book is a hadith book, as it relies on the narration and documentation of the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.498: This book, “The Virtues of Archery for the sake of God,” by its author, Ishaq Al-Qarrab, deals with the virtues of archery in Islam by presenting prophetic hadiths that show its reward and the virtue of those who practice it for the sake of God. The book focuses on emphasizing the importance of learning archery and teaching it to children as it is a force commanded by God. It mentions the virtues of those who throw arrows for the sake of God and calls for not abandoning this art after learning it.
descriptions.499: This book deals with the virtues of the Levant and Damascus by collecting prophetic hadiths and sayings that indicate the status of these cities in Islam. The author focuses on mentioning the virtues of mosques, buildings, and historical monuments in Damascus, relying on modern narratives that emphasize their religious and spiritual importance. The book also includes a mention of some of the stories and events associated with Damascus throughout Islamic history, emphasizing its role as a city with a special place in the Islamic faith.
descriptions.500: This book deals with the virtues of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), focusing in particular on the praise of our master Omar bin Al-Khattab and Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq. The author Al-Daraqutni mentions the sayings and actions of the Companions that reflect their great position in Islam, focusing on their wisdom, advice, and care for religion and the world. The book aims to enhance love for the Companions and enlighten people about their virtues and their high place in the history of Islam.
descriptions.501: The Virtues of Medina for the Soldier is a book that deals with the virtues of Medina and the virtue of inhabiting it, mentioning prophetic hadiths related to Medina, its mosque, the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, and the prohibition of hunting and cutting down its trees. The book focuses on the prophetic calls for Medina and its benefits to its people, while addressing some of the legal rulings related to it.
descriptions.502: This book, “The Virtues of Bayt al-Maqdis,” by Judge Diaa al-Din al-Maqdisi, deals with the virtues of Al-Aqsa Mosque and Bayt al-Maqdis through the narration of prophetic hadiths and Qur’anic verses related to it. The book focuses on mentioning the merit and special status of Al-Aqsa Mosque in Islam, and reviews prophetic hadiths that emphasize the importance of visiting this mosque and praying in it. The book also mentions the shrines of the Companions and historical events related to Jerusalem, and also reviews some hadiths related to the Night Journey and Mi’raj.
descriptions.503: This book deals with the virtues of the blessed month of Ramadan, and reviews its etiquette and rulings through an honorable hadith, with a focus on the virtues of Suhoor and Laylat al-Qadr. The author Abdul-Ghani Al-Maqdisi relies on a series of chains of narrations in transmitting hadiths related to the month of Ramadan, explaining its virtues and the reward of deeds during it.
descriptions.504: This book deals with the virtues of the great companion Othman bin Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), reviewing hadiths and narrations that show his high status with God and His Messenger. The author, Abdullah bin Ahmed, relies on a series of connected chains of transmission to convey these virtues, thus demonstrating the importance of Othman bin Affan in Islamic history and in the heart of Muslims. The book also contains additions and additions from other sources, which increases the richness and diversity of its content.
descriptions.505: This book deals with the virtues and rulings of the month of Ramadan, and mentions the blessings, mercy, and forgiveness it contains. It also explains the virtue of fasting and performing prayers in this month, and reviews the Prophetic hadiths related to that. The author focuses on encouraging Ramadan fasting and being harsh on those who break the fast without an excuse, while presenting multiple accounts of its virtue and status among other months.
descriptions.506: This book deals with the virtues of Mecca and calls for living there, reviewing its spiritual and religious effects. The author, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, focuses on mentioning hadiths and sayings that show the virtue and honor of Mecca, and urges staying there and being attached to it. The book is a type of hadith book that relies on transmitting hadiths and prophetic and hadith sayings on a specific topic.
descriptions.507: This book, “The Virtues of Jihad and the Mujahideen,” by Ahmed bin Abdul Wahid al-Maqdisi, deals with the virtues of jihad for the sake of God and the status of the mujahideen in Islam. The author focuses on encouraging jihad and explaining its reward and reward, showing the virtue of martyrdom, conquest, and bonding for the sake of God. It also mentions the qualities that God grants to the mujahideen upon their martyrdom, and their ranks in Paradise. The book includes prophetic hadiths that emphasize the importance of jihad and the virtue of those who participate in it.
descriptions.508: This book, by Al-Tabarani, deals with the virtues of archery and its importance in Islam, explaining its rulings and benefits through a group of Prophetic hadiths related to this art. It focuses on confirming its position in Islamic law and explaining its virtue and reward, while mentioning some jurisprudential rulings related to archers for the sake of God.
descriptions.509: This book deals with the virtues of praying upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, reviewing hadiths and narrations that emphasize the great reward and great reward for those who pray frequently upon him. The author focuses on the Prophet’s affirmations and comments on the virtue of this worship, while mentioning some of the Prophet’s hadiths that urge frequent prayers for him, especially on Friday.
descriptions.510: This book deals with the topic of the virtue of giving thanks to God for His blessings and studies the duties that a person must have in giving thanks to the one whom he has bestowed. The author focuses on clarifying the importance of gratitude and its reward, citing examples from the Prophet’s hadiths that stress the necessity of thanking God for His many blessings. The book is a type of hadith book that relies on the Prophet’s hadiths to emphasize the importance of gratitude.
descriptions.511: This book deals with the issue of justice in administrative and state positions, and reviews prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential opinions about the importance of justice in the rule of governors and their responsibility for their subjects. The author focuses on emphasizing the necessity of taking matters into their own hands and rejecting undeserving appointments, citing examples from the lives of the Companions and their sayings on this subject. The book is a type of hadith book that relies on the Prophet’s hadiths in dealing with topics.
descriptions.512: This book, “The Arts of Wonders in the News of the Past of the Children of Israel,” by Abu Saeed Al-Naqqash, deals with a group of strange stories and events related to the stories of the prophets and the Children of Israel. The book focuses on narrating strange and amazing events, relying on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and the stories of the predecessors, with the aim of showing the greatness and wisdom of God in His creation.
descriptions.513: This book deals with the benefits and hopes of Abu Bakr Al-Qasim Al-Mutraz, and contains a collection of prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas, relying on multiple narrations from his sheikhs, and covers various topics related to worship, morals, and daily transactions.
descriptions.514: This book deals with a group of prophetic hadiths and the benefits learned from them, with diverse topics ranging from encouragement and intimidation, legal rulings, sermons and wisdom. It relies on a solid chain of transmission in the narration of hadiths, and reviews topics such as what is said in the grave, the virtues of reading the Qur’an, and images of the torment of the grave. It aims to teach the reader through narrated hadiths and their deduced benefits.
descriptions.515: The book “The Benefits of Abu Ya’la Al-Khalili” is a collection of Prophetic hadiths and historical narrations, where the author relies on the Riyad Al-Hadith series to transmit and document them. The book deals with various topics related to hadith and Islamic jurisprudence, relying on reliable sources in its chain of transmission.
descriptions.516: This book includes benefits and hadiths transmitted by Ahmed bin Nasr bin Bujayr from his sheikhs, and contains a series of abrogated hadith parts. The book deals with the narration of hadiths attributed to famous scholars and sheikhs, with a focus on the interpretation of hadiths and their chains of transmission. The book is part of a series of hadith parts aimed at transmitting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and the narrations of scholars.
descriptions.517: The book Benefits of Ibn al-Baghban is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with a continuous chain of transmission. It deals with multiple religious and scientific topics, and reviews narrations about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The book relies on multiple methods of transmitting hadiths, and begins with an extensive supplication narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.518: This book deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths and the benefits learned from them, focusing on legal and ethical issues related to worship, transactions, and Islamic etiquette. It contains supported hadiths that touch on many topics, such as the funeral prayer, the permissibility of the cupper and the person undergoing breakfast, the virtue of fasting, the obligation of praying for the Prophet Muhammad, and other jurisprudential and spiritual issues.
descriptions.519: This book, “The Benefits of Ibn Nasr on the authority of his sheikhs,” is a collection of scientific narratives and benefits collected and presented by Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman bin Omar bin Nasr al-Dimashqi on the authority of his sheikhs. The book covers hadiths and historical narratives about the Prophet Muhammad and his companions, and contains scientific benefits and various prophetic hadiths. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting and narrating the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.520: The book “Benefits of the Iraqis” by Abu Saeed Al-Naqqash deals with a collection of hadiths, prophetic sayings, wisdom and legal rulings, with diverse topics ranging from virtues, etiquette, worship and morals. The book focuses on explaining and clarifying jurisprudential and ethical issues in a direct and useful way, relying on the narration of authentic hadiths and reliable hadiths.
descriptions.521: This book is a collection of hadiths and hadith benefits derived from the scholars of Kufa, and it was collected and narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Ghanaim Al-Narsi. The book covers narrations from famous Kufan ​​sheikhs, and reviews interpretations and chains of transmission for many of the Prophet’s hadiths, thus providing a valuable reference in hadith science and Islamic studies.
descriptions.522: This book deals with the hadith of Abu Umair and the benefits and wisdom related to it, focusing on telling the story and analyzing the lessons it contains in jurisprudence, Sunnahs, and wisdom. The author aims to show the value of hadith scholars and narrators, and to show that they deserve praise and praise for the knowledge and wisdom they transmit.
descriptions.523: This book deals with the benefits of hadith that Al-Hafiz Abdul-Ghani bin Saeed Al-Azdi worked hard on the authority of his sheikhs, as it presents a series of hadiths and narrations, mentioning their chain of transmission and analysis. The author focuses on conveying what his sheikhs learned from him, while citing the scientific and hadith benefits that he derived from those narrations. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the chains of transmission and analyzing the content of hadiths.
descriptions.524: This book deals with selected benefits from the narrations of Sheikhs Abu Al-Hasan Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Salt and Abu Ahmad Al-Fardi. It includes fifty-eight hadiths that were extracted by Othman bin Balban Al-Muqatali. The book focuses on transmitting the Prophet’s hadiths narrated by their sheikhs, relying on a chain of connected narrations through several scholars.
descriptions.525: The Salafi poem is one of the religious chants that dealt with intellectual and doctrinal topics. It criticized the Mu’tazilites, the Jahmiyyah, and the Kharijites on the issue of monotheism, and denounced their attempts to distort the meaning of monotheism and deem the Sunnis as infidels. The poem also criticized those who are full of simile and Jahmism who invalidated the beautiful names and attributes of God, warning against deviation from the path of truth. It was recited by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi Al-Asbahani, and it was narrated and recorded by the scholars of his time.
descriptions.526: The book of Forty Hadiths by Al-Ajri is a collection of Prophetic hadiths that the author chose to summarize the rulings of religion and its etiquette, focusing on what benefits the Muslim in his practical life in terms of worship, dealings, and morals. The book deals with various topics of Islamic law, presenting examples of the Sunnahs of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in various aspects of life, with the aim of teaching the reader how to follow and memorize the correct Sunnahs.
descriptions.527: The Book of Forty Arranged on the Forty Layers by Imam Ali bin al-Mufaddal al-Maqdisi is a book that deals with forty hadiths attributed to forty hadith memorizers, imams of hadith, arranged into ten chronological layers. The book aims to present an elite group of Islamic memorizers throughout the ages, focusing on their historical sequence and scholarly connections.
descriptions.528: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths selected by Al-Sadr Al-Bakri, in which he collected forty hadiths from forty different sources, each hadith from the hadiths of the sheikhs and elders of the ascetics. The book deals with various topics related to asceticism, gentleness, and encouragement to good deeds, relying on hadiths with separate and varied meanings.
descriptions.529: This book is a collection of forty hadiths transmitted from forty male and female companions, selected by Al-Muayyad bin Muhammad al-Tusi from the noble hadiths of the Prophet. The book deals with a group of important hadiths that carry virtues in their narration, reviewing the biographies of its sheikhs, prominent memorizers of the sixth century AH. Through this work, the author aims to imitate the imams of the predecessors in selecting useful and purposeful hadiths, while pointing out the virtues mentioned in the narration of the forty hadiths from the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.530: The Book of Forty in Guiding Those Who Walk to the Homes of the Pious by Abu al-Futuh al-Ta’i covers forty hadiths from the Sunnah of the Prophet, each hadith from a different narrator, and aims to guide the reader to the levels of faith and piety. The author explains the benefits of each hadith, and provides explanations of some complex linguistic aspects, adding appropriate anecdotes and poems to clarify the meanings.
descriptions.531: This book is a collection of hadiths on the subject of jihad and the mujahideen, collected and cited by Abu Al-Faraj Al-Muqri in forty hadiths. The hadith book deals with topics related to jihad from a legal and jurisprudential perspective, reviewing the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his actions in this field. The author is Afif al-Din Abu al-Faraj al-Wasiti, a well-known hadith scholar famous for his narration and investigation, and he narrated hadiths on the authority of a number of famous hadith scholars of his time.
descriptions.532: The Book of Forty in the Sufi Sheikhs by Al-Malini is a collection of hadiths and narrations that deal with the biographies and sayings of famous Sufi sheikhs. It focuses on conveying a series of chains of transmission to important figures in Islamic Sufism. The book aims to document the historical and spiritual foundations of Sufism and the most prominent people who contributed to its dissemination and development, relying on the technique of mentioning hadith chains of transmission.
descriptions.533: This book, by Al-Dhahabi Shams Al-Din, deals with forty hadiths about the attributes of God Almighty, explaining in them what was reported from the predecessors regarding these attributes. The author focuses on clarifying the attributes of God Almighty and confirming His transcendence and transcendence above the resemblance of created beings, relying on the Prophetic hadiths and Salafi sayings in this field.
descriptions.534: This book deals with the virtues and morals of the Mothers of the Believers, as it contains forty hadiths that explain their virtues and the characteristics of their Prophet Muhammad ﷺ towards them. The author, Ibn Asakir, focuses on narrating the Prophetic hadiths that talk about the Prophet’s wives, explaining the virtue and characteristics of each one of them. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and classifying prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.535: The Book of Forty by Al-Hasan bin Sufyan Al-Nasawi is a collection of selected prophetic hadiths, dealing with multiple topics of Islamic law, including faith, acts of worship, morals, and jurisprudential rulings, distributed into forty-four chapters, each chapter focusing on a specific topic of a Muslim’s life and religion.
descriptions.536: The Book of Firsts by Abu Orouba Al-Harrani is a translation that dealt with multiple topics related to the firsts of creation and events, covering topics such as the first creation, the first mountain placed in the earth, the first water, the first tree, the first prophets, the first messengers, the first to enact killing, the first mosque placed on earth, and other topics related to the firsts of events and things in Islamic and religious history. The book relies on multiple narrations from different sheikhs and begins by mentioning the oneness of God and His being first before all else.
descriptions.537: The Book of Faith by Ibn Abi Shaybah is a book that deals with a definition and detail of the concept of faith in Islam, reviewing its various dimensions, conditions and pillars, relying on the Prophetic hadiths mentioned on this topic. The book focuses on the close relationship between faith and good morals, considering that the most complete believers in faith are those with the best morals. It also emphasizes the importance of honesty as one of the strong pillars of faith.
descriptions.538: Al-Nasa’i’s Book of Friday is part of his hadith works specialized in Friday prayer and its rulings. The book deals with hadiths and narrations related to the principles of the obligation of Friday prayer, its virtues, rulings, and etiquette, with a focus on encouraging its attendance and warning against missing it. The book also includes hadiths related to special rulings on Friday, such as washing, sermon, and arriving early for prayer.
descriptions.539: This book deals with the jurisprudence of Hajj and its rituals, extracting its issues from well-known books, and reviews the rulings on obligatory and voluntary Hajj, mentioning the differences between Hajj and Umrah. It also includes hadiths and fatwas by scholars such as Malik bin Anas and Isa bin Dinar about the ability to perform Hajj and the obligations related to it. It also addresses various issues related to Hajj, such as prohibited acts of ihram, ihram rituals, circumambulation, stoning, and slaughter.
descriptions.540: The Book of Hajj by Al-Majshun is one of the hadith books that includes hadiths and fatwas about the rituals and rulings of Hajj, extracted from multiple sources other than the written ones. The book deals with the instructions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Hajj, and discusses the provisions of Ihram and the clothes of the Muhrim, with a focus on what is permissible and what is forbidden in this season.
descriptions.541: The Book of Attributes by Al-Daraqutni is an investigation of a book on the Prophetic hadiths related to the attributes of God Almighty, as it deals with hadiths related to different images of God’s attributes, such as the foot, hand, face, and laughter. The book aims to show the legal evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah on this subject, with the translation of the narrators and the hadiths. It is part of two twin investigations, one of which is the Book of Revelation. The book falls within the important Islamic heritage in the field of monotheism and Islamic belief.
descriptions.542: The book “Reciting Behind the Imam” by Imam Al-Bayhaqi addresses the issue of the obligation of reciting the Qur’an in prayer for the imam, the person being led in prayer, and the one praying alone in each rak’ah, while extending evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah on the necessity of reciting Al-Fatihah and other verses of the Qur’an in prayer. The book reviews numerous narrations from the hadiths of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) to support the position of the obligation of reading behind the imam, thus demonstrating the legal importance of this aspect of worship.
descriptions.543: The Book of Judiciary by Siraj Ibn Yunus is a book on Islamic jurisprudence and jurisprudence, dealing with various issues and rulings related to responsibility and compensation in various cases, such as the insanity of an insane person, the injury of a virgin, or the death of the person in charge. The book relies on Prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential narratives to present legal rulings in civil and criminal cases, and aims to provide practical judicial guidance to the court and judge.
descriptions.544: This book, by Al-Bardiji, who is one of the imams and scholars, deals with the topic of major sins in Islam through the narration of the hadiths of the Companions about the Prophet ﷺ in this field. This book is considered the first work on the subject of major sins, and is distinguished by its large content despite its small size, as it contains important texts and hadiths on this subject. It is also one of the rare books by an author whose works have only reached us in two books.
descriptions.545: The Book of Descent by Al-Daraqutni is a book that deals with the narration of the Hadith of Descent, as it mentions the various narrations from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ about the descent of God Almighty to the lowest heaven on the Night of Destiny and other nights, relying on the narrations of the Companions and their followers. The book contains a collection of hadiths and narrations revolving around this topic, with notes on the authenticity and strength of some narrations.
descriptions.546: This book is a series mentioning the sheikhs of Sheikh Abdul Haq bin Khalaf, dealing with their biographies, hadiths, and knowledge. The author focuses on presenting the chain of transmission and narration in an accurate documentary manner, reviewing the hadith imams and hadith scholars from whom Sheikh Abdul Haq bin Khalaf learned. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting the chains of transmission and presenting the narrators of the hadith, and it aims to transfer the scientific and spiritual experiences of the nation’s predecessors to subsequent generations.
descriptions.547: This book, by Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi, deals with the virtues of the Holy Qur’an and the reward for learning and teaching it, explaining the reward of reciting it and its importance in raising people up and status others. It also mentions the virtues of some surahs and verses, and reviews the etiquette of reading and memorizing the Qur’an, noting the rewards and virtues that result from its recitation. The book relies on authentic Prophetic hadiths to confirm the importance of the Qur’an and the virtue of learning and teaching it.
descriptions.548: This book is written by Al-Daraqutni, and it includes forty hadiths from Musnad Burayd bin Abdullah bin Abi Burda, where Burayd bin Abdullah narrates on the authority of his grandfather Abu Burda bin Abi Musa Al-Ash’ari. The book deals with a group of important prophetic hadiths, serialized in a systematic manner, starting from the first hadith and ending with the fortieth hadith, relying on the techniques of collecting hadiths.
descriptions.549: This book, “Maqtab al-Ilm” by Ibn Faris, deals with topics related to the principles of preserving and transmitting hadith. It focuses on how knowledge is carried out by modernization, discusses the differences between the terminology of hadith scholars, and reviews the issue of approval and handling. The author aims to clarify the foundations and rules of hadith science, and the book includes a special section discussing melody in the novel.
descriptions.550: This book is part of the benefits of Abu Ahmed Al-Hakim, and it includes narrations and hadiths transmitted by Al-Hakim from his sheikhs. The book deals with a series of chains of narrations and narrations that were connected to the author from his sheikhs, and reviews the methods of transmitting the hadith and the methods of verifying the authenticity of the hadiths. The book is one of the hadith parts that is concerned with documenting the chains of transmission and tracking the methods of transmitting the hadith.
descriptions.551: This book deals with the narration of the greats on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, as it contains hadiths and narrations transmitted by Muhammad ibn Makhlid from famous scholars and memorizers. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths in their original form without comment or interpretation, relying on continuous and reliable documents. The book also includes memories and notes about the circles of knowledge and narration in Malik's era, providing a cultural insight into the hadith publishing environment at that time.
descriptions.552: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths related to the basin and Al-Kawthar, as narrated by Baqi bin Mukhlid on the authority of honorable companions such as Abu Umamah, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, and Abdullah bin Omar. The book covers multiple hadiths about the description of the basin, its drink, and related matters, relying on narrations related to the Companions and followers.
descriptions.553: This book is part of the prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, as it contains a group of hadiths whose chain of transmission is close and authenticated by Imam Abu al-Qasim Ismail bin Ahmad al-Samarqandi. The book deals with the narration of hadiths through their chains of transmission related to the narrators and their chains of transmission, with a focus on the accuracy in transmitting the hadith and the validity of its chain of transmission. The book is one of the important heritage works in the field of the Noble Prophet’s Hadith.
descriptions.554: This book deals with the virtues of the month of Shaban and its rulings, explaining what was stated in the derivation of the month’s name and what has been proven regarding the virtue of fasting. It also mentions the introduction of the obligation of fasting in Ramadan and turning the qiblah, reviewing the historical events and legal benefits related to this month. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting prophetic hadiths related to a specific topic.
descriptions.555: In his book “Councils of Scholars,” Al-Zajjaji presents a series of scholarly councils in which he collected the conversations of famous scholars and linguists, narrating their dialogues and conversations on issues of language and literature. The book deals with many councils between prominent scholars such as Issa bin Omar Al-Thaqafi and Abu Amr bin Al-Ala, and documents the linguistic and scientific discussions that took place between them, thus providing a window into the world of language and literature in the Abbasid era.
descriptions.556: This book deals with the names of the narrators on the authority of Imam Malik bin Anas, as the author Al-Rashid Al-Attar mentions the names of those who narrated the hadith on the authority of Imam Malik, arranged according to the alphabetical letters. The book begins with Chapter Alif and ends with Chapter Ya, and contains brief information about some of the narrators, along with a brief mention of hadith from some of them. The book is part of its author’s works related to the narration of hadiths on the authority of Imam Malik, and it comes after the book Al-Mustadrak by Al-Khatib and Al-Attar.
descriptions.557: This book deals with a hadith about seeing God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection, reviewing the opinions of scholars and hadith scholars on this subject. It contains a narration of narrations and hadiths related to seeing God, relying on accurate scientific documents in transmitting hadiths. In it, the author Muhammad bin Abdul Wahed Al-Daqqaq mentions a hadith on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ in which he describes what happened between the people and their vision of their Lord. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting and correcting prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.558: This book is A Council on Humility by Amali Al-Jawhari, and it includes novels and hadiths on the subject of humility. The book covers prophetic hadiths and narrations from the Companions and followers related to humility and its virtue, introducing some of the narrators who narrated about it. The book is classified as Hadith parts, and aims to enhance the value of humility in Islamic behavior and the daily life of a Muslim.
descriptions.559: This book deals with a famous hadith by the companion Jabir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), and reviews the chain of narration of this hadith through a series of connected narrators. The author focuses on documenting the chain of transmission of the hadith and presenting it in a way that shows the path of its transmission over time, which makes it a useful reference for students of hadith and narration.
descriptions.560: This book is a council at the end of the book Al-Shifa, defining the rights of the Chosen One, written by Ibn Nasir al-Din al-Dimashqi. The book deals with the conclusion of the book Al-Shifa, written by Ibn Nasser Al-Din, in which it reviews the definition of the rights of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and an explanation of his great destiny and noble qualities. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with documenting and explaining the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.561: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Naim Al-Isbahani in a dictation session. Its narrations mostly focus on the virtue of fasting six days of Shawwal following Ramadan, while following the different methods of narration and its chains of transmission. The book falls within the hadith sections that are concerned with collecting hadiths related to a specific topic or the narration of a single sheikh.
descriptions.562: This book is a collection of hopes and anecdotes that were narrated on the authority of Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Qasim Al-Anbari, who died in the year 328 AH. The book deals with a hadith narration that follows a series of chains of transmission, mentioning the authors and narrators from whom Ibn al-Anbari narrated. The book focuses on accurately transmitting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths and their narrations, which makes it an important reference in the field of Islamic hadiths and narrations.
descriptions.563: A Majlis from Amali Al-Asbahani is a collection of hadiths and prophetic narrations narrated in the Amali method, in which the hadith narrator records what he hears from his sheikhs without being restricted by extra frameworks. The book deals with the narration of hadiths through a series of narrators, with a focus on acquiring knowledge and transmitting it accurately. It is one of the hadith works concerned with collecting and documenting prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.564: The book “Two Majlis Min Amali Nizam al-Mulk” consists of narrations and hadiths with chain of transmission from the Prophet, as it begins by narrating the chain of transmission of the narrations in the form of “he told us,” “he told us,” and “he told us,” thus following the Hadith tradition in transmitting hadiths. The book deals with various topics of Islamic jurisprudence and etiquette, relying on the narration of authentic Prophetic hadiths that have been dealt with by hadith scholars over time.
descriptions.565: This book is a collection of hopes collected by Imam Ahmed bin Musa bin Mardawayh, and it contains two collected hadiths, one of which deals with the attributes of God Almighty. The book begins with Sheikh Al-Maqdisi’s narration about a series of narrators who the book did not mention by their full names. It contains a group of prophetic hadiths, including a hadith about the Prophet’s love for his sons Hassan and Hussein, another hadith about the will, and a third about a tired body.
descriptions.566: This book is a sum of three hadith parts, containing benefits and hadiths of three specific scholars, namely Abu Ali Al-Raffa’, Khaldi, and Makram Al-Bazzaz. The book deals with the biographies of these scholars, including their hadith benefits, and it is part of the Endowment Publishing Series, which aims to spread knowledge and facilitate access to it. The book also points out the importance of publishing modern books online in the modern era, while preserving their intellectual property rights.
descriptions.567: The book “Literature of Souls” by Al-Ajri provides an in-depth perspective on the self’s caution against whims and desires, reviewing Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths calling for self-control and good morals. The author focuses on the importance of warning against being led by desires and the necessity of awakening oneself from forbidden pleasures, stressing that whoever succeeds in this will find his refuge in Paradise. The book also addresses how a person can thank God for his mercy, which is manifested in protecting the soul from deviation.
descriptions.568: This book is part of a group of hadith parts that deal with various prophetic hadiths on various topics, including what relates to the Antichrist and his entry into Mecca and Medina, including what urges one to wash for Friday prayers, the etiquette of walking at funerals, and the means of spending in the path of God. The book is based on narrations from companions and followers, and shows a diversity of topics and sermons aimed at guiding Muslims in their daily and spiritual lives.
descriptions.569: This book deals with the issue of “Glory be to God” through a careful hadith study, reviewing the opinions of scholars and commentators on its meanings and rulings. The author Naftawayh focuses on interpreting and clarifying the purposes of this praise through the use of prophetic narrations and hadiths, trying to provide a comprehensive and deep understanding of this religious worship. The book is of the type of hadith parts, and aims to enhance the correct understanding of the religion of Islam by relying on reliable hadith sources.
descriptions.570: The book “The Question of Names” by Ibn al-Qaysrani deals with the ruling on reciting “In the Name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful” out loud at the beginning of Al-Fatihah and other surahs of the Qur’an in congregational and private prayer. The author explains his evidence from authentic hadiths and narrations that indicate the necessity of concealing this naming during prayer, basing this on the principles of jurisprudence and agreed-upon hadiths. The book aims to clarify the jurists’ point of view on this subject and explain the evidence on which they relied, while discussing the opinions of the hadith scholars who used this naming in prayer.
descriptions.571: This book is the Musnads of Abu Yahya Firas bin Yahya al-Maktab al-Kufi, containing his narrations on the authority of al-Sha’bi and other companions. The book deals with the series of chains of transmission and narrations that were transmitted from Firas bin Yahya to other hadith scholars, with a focus on his narrations on the authority of al-Shabi and his request for hadith from the Companions.
descriptions.572: Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq by Ahmad ibn Ali al-Marwazi is a book that collects various narrations and hadiths about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) by other companions, as it contains narrations of Omar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, ibn Umar, ibn Abbas, Aisha, Zaid ibn Thabit, Rifa`ah ibn Rafi`, Ka`b ibn Malik and others. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths and narrations related to Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq through a connected narration chain, which makes it a reliable source for studying the life and sayings of the first Rightly Guided Caliph.
descriptions.573: Musnad Amatullah Maryam bint Abd al-Rahman al-Hanbaliya is a book that deals with the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths, relying on multiple chains of narration, and contains issues of jurisprudence and Islamic etiquette. The book focuses on various topics of wisdom, etiquette, and hadiths, including those related to cursing and fighting a Muslim, the heaviest thing to be placed on the scale, the virtue of patience, and the etiquette of reading the Qur’an, in addition to hadiths related to the virtues of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.574: Musnad of the Commander of the Faithful Omar bin Abdul Aziz by Al-Baghandi Al-Saghir is a book that collects hadiths and narrations transmitted by Omar bin Abdul Aziz on the authority of the companions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book contains multiple chains of narrations for different narrations, divided into chapters that begin with the names of the companions who narrated hadiths from them. The book includes narrations about Uqba bin Amer, Yusuf bin Abdullah, Tamim al-Dari, and other companions, relying on chains of transmission related to Omar bin Abdul Aziz.
descriptions.575: This book is one of the hadith parts collected by Ibn Zaydan, and it includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics in worship, etiquette, and sermons, such as the rulings on prayer, Hajj, and charity, the virtue of controlling the tongue, and explaining the characteristics of believers. The book begins with a chain of transmission of a hadith on the authority of Aws ibn Aws in which he describes the appearance of the Prophet ﷺ in prayer, then the narration of the chained hadiths continues with continuous chains of transmission.
descriptions.576: Musnad Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak is a book that contains hadiths and narrations transmitted by Imam Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, who is one of the imams of scholars and scholars. The book deals with multiple topics of Islamic jurisprudence, meanings, and ethics, relying on the narrations of the noble Prophet’s hadiths and the narrations of the Companions and followers.
descriptions.577: Musnad al-Hub bin al-Hab Usama bin Zaid by al-Baghawi is a book that deals with the narration of hadiths on the authority of Usama bin Zaid (may Allah be pleased with him), as it combines the hadiths that were narrated from him and the virtues that were narrated about him. The book contains narrations attributed to the companions to whom Osama narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, such as Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, and Jabir bin Abdullah.
descriptions.578: Musnad al-Muqalilun min al-Amir al-Sultan by Tamam bin Muhammad al-Dimashqi is a book that deals with hadiths and narrations about princes and sultans from different eras, focusing on the situations of scarcity and distress that rulers may go through. The book is based on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and traces through a series of narrators, and aims to show lessons and lessons learned through the experiences of these rulers.
descriptions.579: Musnad Bilal bin Rabah is a book that deals with the hadith of Abu Abdullah Bilal bin Rabah (may Allah be pleased with him), and contains hadiths and narrations from him on various topics, including wiping over the socks and the rulings on the call to prayer. The book was written by Ibn al-Sabah al-Zaafarani, and falls within the classification of hadith parts, as it focuses on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths through the connected chain of transmission.
descriptions.580: Musnad Khalifa bin Khayyat is a book containing prophetic hadiths narrated by the great companions. It focuses on narrating hadiths in the “Musnad” format, in which the narrations are followed by the names of the narrators sequentially. The book includes hadiths attributed to more than thirty companions, including Anas bin Malik, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurairah, and other prominent figures who were contemporary with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.581: Musnad Saad bin Abi Waqqas al-Durqi is a book that deals with the narration of the hadiths of Saad bin Abi Waqqas through his offspring and grandchildren, as it mentions what was narrated on the authority of Saad by his son Jabir bin Samra and his other son Musab bin Saad and others. The book focuses on transmitting the prophetic hadiths narrated by these generations on the authority of Saad bin Abi Waqqas, relying on multiple documents and reliable narrators.
descriptions.582: Musnad Aisha by Ibn Abi Dawud is a book containing prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Mrs. Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), as it relies on multiple chains of transmission that often begin with Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha. The book deals with various topics from the life of the Prophet ﷺ with Lady Aisha, including their daily customs and legal rulings.
descriptions.583: Musnad Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf by al-Barti is a book that deals with narrations and hadiths related to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with him) through different narrators, as it contains the hadiths of Abdullah ibn Abbas, Anas ibn Malik, al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, Jubayr ibn Mut’im, and others on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. The book focuses on collecting hadiths and narrations related to this great companion through a series of multiple narrators, providing a comprehensive view of the life and teachings of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.
descriptions.584: This book is a Musnad that includes hadiths and narrations about the companion Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, where the author Yahya bin Muhammad bin Sa’id mentions multiple narrations about him through a series of different chains of narrations. The book deals with one hadith repeated across several narrations, which is a hadith related to the prayer of the Awwabin when breastfeeding the faction, relying on famous narrators such as Al-Qasim bin Awf and Al-Sha’bi. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to collect and document hadiths related to this companion in particular.
descriptions.585: Musnad Abdullah bin Omar by Al-Tarsusi is a book that contains hadiths and narrations about the great companion Abdullah bin Omar (may Allah be pleased with them both). The book deals with various aspects of Ibn Omar’s life, his sayings and his actions, with a focus on the prophetic hadiths that he narrated about him. The book also includes some of the legal rulings and fatwas for which Ibn Umar is famous, providing a comprehensive overview of his Sunnah and knowledge.
descriptions.586: This book is a Musnad for Uthman bin Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) written by Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi, and it contains hadiths and narrations from the great companion Uthman bin Affan (may Allah be pleased with him). The book deals with multiple topics from Uthman’s life, fatwas, and sayings, relying on a series of narrators connected to the companion. The book is one of the hadith parts that aims to collect hadiths related to the personality of Uthman ibn Affan and classify them in a systematic way.
descriptions.587: Musnad Omar bin Al-Khattab by Yaqoob bin Shaybah is a book that collects the hadiths of the great companion Omar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), where it deals with different narrations through their multiple chains of narration, indicating their sources and the chains of transmission of their narrators. The book focuses on presenting the hadiths in their original form, while touching on some details related to the narrators of the hadith, their strength, and the validity of their chain of transmission.
descriptions.588: This book is a collection of books on hadith sheikhs. It deals with a series of narrations and graduations of the hadiths of the sheikhdom of Imam Abu Al-Munji Abdullah bin Omar bin Ali bin Zaid bin Al-Lati Al-Baghdadi, who died in the year 635 AH. The book contains three books from the Hadith series and books, and reviews Ibn al-Lati’s narration of the Prophet’s hadith through a series of sheikhs, with a graduation from Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Barzali.
descriptions.589: This book deals with the sheikhdom of Imam Abu Bakr bin Al-Hussein bin Omar Al-Qurashi, known as Al-Maraghi, and reviews his scientific biography and his narrations in hadith. It focuses on his contributions to the transmission and graduation of hadiths, indicating his high status in the sciences of hadith and its narrators. The book is part of the series of works of the Islamic Heritage Revival Center at Umm Al-Qura University, and aims to revive and document the scientific contributions of Muslim scholars in the field of the Prophet’s Hadith.
descriptions.590: This book deals with the sheikhdom of Abu Bakr bin Abdul-Daim al-Maqdisi, and it is a series of narrations and chains of transmission that begin with the first sheikh and extend until the end of the sheikhdom. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths and historical information through a series of narrators, as it mentions the names of the sheikhs and their chains of transmission in detail. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to document the series of narrations of the Prophet’s hadiths and document the reliable narrators in transmitting them.
descriptions.591: This book deals with the sheikhdom of Abu Taher Ibn Abi Al-Saqr, as the author mentions the names of the sheikhs from whom he took knowledge and hadith. The book focuses on presenting the series of scholars’ narrations and documenting the authenticity of their transmission, which makes it an important reference in the field of chains of transmission and scientific documentation. The book includes the names of famous sheikhs who specialize in hadith memorization and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.592: This book is part of the sheikhdom of Imam Ibn al-Bukhari, in which Ibn al-Dhahiri discusses hadith after hadith in the biographies and narrations of scholars, with a focus on the Prophet’s hadiths and their chains of transmission. The book aims to provide a service to hadith scholars and researchers in the sciences of hadith by documenting the narration of hadiths and presenting them in a scientific, systematic manner.
descriptions.593: This book deals with the narration of the sheikhs of Ibn al-Jawzi, a group of scholars from whom the hadith was taken. In it, Ibn al-Jawzi mentions seventy sheikhs, and describes his experience in seeking knowledge and hearing hadith from these sheikhs, expressing his interest in the quality of the scholarly quantity more than the large number. The book focuses on listing information related to each of these sheikhs, while mentioning some details about their scholarly lives and narratives.
descriptions.594: This book is part of Ibn Shazan's minor Mashaykh, and it includes a series of Prophetic hadiths narrated through multiple chains of transmission. The book begins by narrating a hadith about the Prophet ﷺ, narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik, and continues to present other hadiths through different chains of transmission, which indicates his interest in presenting hadiths and their narration chains.
descriptions.595: This book deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas, focusing on issues related to worship, morals, and transactions. The author deals with various topics, from rulings on breastfeeding and purity to rulings on marriage and divorce, through prophetic hadiths about the afterlife and future events. The book is distinguished by its transmission of narrations through a series of narrators, with a focus on hadiths related to the destruction and destruction of the Prophet’s household.
descriptions.596: This book is the sheikhs of Imam Abu Hafs Omar bin Al-Hasan bin Mazyad Al-Maraghi, and it includes a series of sheikhs from whom he took knowledge and hadith. The book presents the sheikhs in chronological order or the order chosen by the author, starting from the first sheikh to the seventeenth sheikh, with details about how he heard the hadith from them. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to accurately record, trace and document the chain of transmission of hadith.
descriptions.597: This book, “Mashaykhat al-Bayan” by Ibn Rafi’ al-Salami, deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths and Islamic narrations, and reviews the ways of documenting and transmitting them over time. It focuses on presenting hadiths in a Sheikh way, that is, by tracing and analyzing the chain of transmission of the narration, which helps in determining the authenticity and reliability of the hadith. The book includes various hadiths related to ethics, jurisprudence, and Islamic etiquette, relying on multiple narration methods and different sources.
descriptions.598: The book of the Sheikhs of Al-Suhrawardi is a series of hadith books that include a series of hadith narrations through the Sheikhs of Imam Shihab Al-Din Abi Hafs Omar bin Muhammad Al-Suhrawardi. The book deals with the narration of hadiths through a series of scholars and sheikhs, and aims to document the chain of transmission of the Prophet’s hadiths and their authentication. The book is part of a collection of three books on modern sheikhs, and it includes the names of the sheikhs from whom Al-Suhrawardi narrated, mentioning the date of death of some of them.
descriptions.599: This book deals with the sheikh of the eminent Sheikh Abu Abdullah Muhammad al-Razi, in which its author, Abu Taher al-Salafi, mentions his hearings from his sheikhs in Egypt and neighboring regions, and describes his efforts to memorize and control the hadiths he heard from them. The book focuses on narrating the chain of transmission and speakers, while highlighting the importance of these practices in hadith science.
descriptions.600: This book deals with the sheikhdom of Muhammad bin Ibrahim al-Bayan, known as Ibn Imam al-Sakhra, in which he mentions the chains of transmission and narrations that he read in the mosques of Damascus, relying on his ten sheikhs and attached sheikhs. The book focuses on grading the hadiths and presenting the narration series by listing the names of the sheikhs and their hadiths, which makes it a useful reference in the field of prophetic hadiths and Islamic narrations.
descriptions.601: This book deals with the sheikhs of Al-Na'al, and it is a narration of the translations of the sheikhs of its author, with the graduation of one hadith for each sheikh. The text focuses on mentioning the cases and deaths of sheikhs, beginning with the author’s maternal grandfather’s translation. The book is a classification of hadith parts, and it aims to present narration testimony for each of the mentioned sheikhs, while being careful to be brief and not lengthy.
descriptions.602: The book “Masheykhat Sharaf al-Din al-Yunini” is one of the hadith works that includes a series of narrations of prophetic news and hadiths. The book deals with the accounts of the sheikhs whom the author met and read about, and reviews their scientific and religious biography. The book focuses on grading hadiths and presenting their chains of transmission, which makes it an important reference in the field of hadith and hadith studies. The book consists of several parts, and each part contains narrations attributed to different sheikhs, which reflects the depth of the author’s historical and scientific research in the field of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.603: This book is the sheikh of Imam Muhyiddin al-Yunini, and it includes hadiths and narrations from his twenty-six sheikhs, with their graduation by another sheikh, Shams al-Din al-Maqdisi. The book deals with the narration of the Noble Prophet’s Hadith, relying on the continuous chain of narrations from the sheikhs of Al-Yunini. The book clearly mentions Al-Yunini’s care in documenting his scientific travels and hearing the hadith from his sheikhs.
descriptions.604: This book is a dictionary that deals with the sheikhs of Muhammad bin Abdul Wahed Al-Daqqaq, and mentions the narrators of the hadith and its chains of transmission, linked to the letters of the dictionary from A to Z. Each chapter begins with an Arabic letter, and under each letter the names of the sheikhs associated with it are mentioned, along with their narrations and chains of transmission in Hadith sciences.
descriptions.605: This book is a modern part that deals with a collection of Prophetic hadiths and historical stories related to the Hijaz journey and Hajj. The author, Ibn Rashid al-Sabti, focuses on transmitting hadiths and events related to visiting the Prophet’s Mosque and the Grand Mosque, while mentioning some stories about the Companions and righteous predecessors. The book also includes a description of some traditions and... After that, there is no need to worry about it.
descriptions.606: This book, by Al-Tabarani, deals with the narrators of the hadith called Ata’, and reviews their lives and narrations, focusing on the importance of their role in transmitting and documenting the Prophet’s hadiths. The book includes a number of narrators, such as Ataa Al-Shaibi and Ataa bin Yasar, and provides information about their words and actions, indicating the methods of documenting them and the authenticity of their narrations.
descriptions.607: The book “From the Selected Benefits of Al-Hasan Al-Awali” by Al-Samarqandi includes a collection of hadiths and prophetic and scientific benefits, taken from hadith books and narrations. The book addresses multiple topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, relying on sound and solid documents in its transmission of narrations. The book is characterized by a sequential reference format that reflects the author’s care in documenting the sources of what is transmitted.
descriptions.608: This book is part of a hadith by Abu Al-Tahir, which deals with a group of noble Prophetic hadiths, with a variety of topics, including worship, morals, and sermons. It focuses on transmitting hadiths in their original form with attribution, without interpretation or comment, preserving their authenticity and elegance in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.609: This book is part of a series of Hadith volumes and books. It deals with the narration of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in the Musnad, in which Abu Abdul Rahman al-Muqri Abdullah ibn Yazid agreed with him. It contains hadiths transmitted by the reciter Abdullah bin Yazid, in which he agreed with the narration of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, and presented and concluded by Imam Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi al-Hanbali. The book focuses on the Prophetic hadiths agreed between these two prominent narrators in the world of hadith.
descriptions.610: This book deals with a collection of prophetic hadiths sequentially transmitted by Ibn al-Askari on the authority of his sheikhs. It begins with the narration of the hadith from Muhammad bin Khalaf Waki` al-Qadi all the way to Anas bin Malik. The book contains multiple narrations through a series of reliable narrators, and reviews various topics related to this life and the afterlife, with a focus on morals and worship. The book is one of the hadith parts and aims to convey and educate the reader with the authentic hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.611: This book contains a collection of prophetic hadiths attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, narrated through Ibn al-Muqri. It includes hadiths about battles, fasting, and travel, the etiquette of ablution, the virtues of Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), and other etiquettes in worship and transactions. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths sequentially, mentioning the chain of narrators, without interpretation or comment on their content.
descriptions.612: This book contains hadiths narrated by Imam Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of his sheikhs, and focuses on the narration of al-Sari bin Yahya on the authority of al-Thawri, in addition to the narration of Muhammad bin Yusuf al-Faryabi on the authority of him. It deals with hadiths on various topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, relying on solid documents in the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.613: This book is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the companions and followers, in which Ibn Zanbour al-Warraq collects hadiths from the books of al-Baghawi, Ibn Sa`id, and al-Hashimi. The book deals with multiple topics in the lives and morals of Muslims, including modesty, faith, the Aqeeqah, and reading Surat Al-Tur in Morocco, relying on authentic chains of transmission of hadiths.
descriptions.614: This book deals with the journey of Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi to the city of Abhar, where he narrates what he heard and learned from its people. Contains a detailed discussion of some of the aorticists, with comments by Dr. Jamal Azoun. The book addresses multiple topics from literature, jurisprudence, and preaching, indicating the importance of intention in worship and its impact on acceptance.
descriptions.615: This book deals with a collection of hadiths narrated from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, focusing on the narrations of Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Muqri.
descriptions.616: This book deals with an account of the lives of a group of companions who lived one hundred and twenty years or more, focusing on their biographies, works, and stories. The book begins with the story of Hakim bin Hizam, and then the book mentions the lives of other characters from the Companions, relying on narrations and hadiths of the Prophet in dealing with their lives.
descriptions.617: This book deals with the virtues of Surat Al-Ikhlas and the merit of reciting it, reviewing hadiths and narrations that emphasize its importance and the reward of reciting it. The author, Al-Hassan Al-Khalal, focuses on mentioning the Prophetic hadiths that indicate that reading Surat Al-Ikhlas is equivalent to reading a third of the Qur’an, while mentioning other benefits for those who regularly read it. The book is a type of hadith book that is concerned with collecting hadiths and explaining the virtues of religious actions.
descriptions.618: The book “From the Benefits of Abu Bakr Al-Shashi” includes prophetic narrations and hadiths transmitted from Imam Abu Bakr Al-Shashi, where Al-Shashi presents scientific and hadith benefits in detail, narrating the chains of transmission in a continuous form. The book is one of the Hadith volumes concerned with transmitting the Prophet’s hadiths and documenting their sources, which makes it an important reference in the field of Hadith studies and Islamic law.
descriptions.619: This book deals with a group of companions and their spouses whose names match, and reviews different situations among them in terms of the companionship of the Messenger ﷺ and his quality, in addition to cases of marriage, divorce, and their successors. The author focuses on describing and documenting these relationships through narratives and hadiths related to them.
descriptions.620: This book is a masterpiece of the Commander of the Faithful Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) by Ibn Al-Maghazili. It is one of the hadith books that deals with the biography of Ali bin Abi Talib and includes hadiths and narrations related to his virtue and status. The book covers Ali's lineage, mother, birth, and nickname, in addition to prophetic hadiths about him and stories from his biography. Despite the importance of the topic, Ibn Taymiyyah criticized this book for collecting fabricated narrations that do not agree with the science of hadith.
descriptions.621: This book is a study of the virtues of Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), as its author, Ibn Al-Jazari, deals with the hadiths and serials reported from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, through multiple methods, including what was narrated on the authority of the Companions and Ahl al-Bayt. The book focuses on demonstrating the virtues and virtues that distinguished the character of Ali bin Abi Talib, using the modern classification method in presenting hadiths and narrations.
descriptions.622: This book, “The Virtues of Imam Al-Shafi’i,” by Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Abri, deals with the biography of Imam Al-Shafi’i, his virtues, morals, and wisdom.
