It contains sayings, hadiths of the Prophet, and poetry that shows its scientific and moral standing, and is based on manuscripts and parts published in other books. The book aims to document the virtues of Imam Al-Shafi’i and explain his status in the world of scholars and jurists.
descriptions.623: This book is “Selected from the Book of Poets” by Abu Naim Al-Asbahani, and it includes poems by prominent poets from different eras, from Hassan bin Thabit to Abu Nawas and Abu Al-Atahiya. The book deals with examples of ancient Arabic poetry, relying on oral narration of poetic texts, and aims to present aspects of the lives of poets and their poems in a selected and concise manner.
descriptions.624: This book is a selection of the hadiths of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Abdawi, which is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated through Abu Al-Hasan Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Abdawi. In this book, the author Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi relies on a continuous chain of narrations, as he mentions a chain of chains of transmission from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdawi to the hadith scholars from whom he narrated. The book falls within the hadith sections, and it aims to collect and document the Prophet’s hadiths in a systematic and scientific manner.
descriptions.625: The book “Selected News from Al-Asma’i” by Judge Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Rab’i deals with a group of news and hadiths related to the life and sayings of Al-Asma’i. The book is based on the author's sheikhs' narration of Al-Asma'i's news, and contains examples of wisdom and sayings of a literary and religious nature. The book also deals with some historical stories related to some Islamic figures such as Khalid bin Al-Walid and Omar bin Al-Khattab, which reflects the nature of the book as a modern work that combines scientific interest and wisdom.
descriptions.626: This book is a collection of Prophetic hadiths drawn from the first and third parts of the hadith of Al-Maruzi. It deals with multiple topics related to worship, morals, and transactions, relying on various documents in the narration of the hadiths. The book focuses on transmitting hadiths in their original form without commentary or detailed explanation, which makes it an important reference for researchers in the field of Prophetic hadith.
descriptions.627: This book is the Muwatta of Abdullah bin Wahb, and it is a collection of reliable and frequently transmitted hadiths of the Prophet, classified according to jurisprudential topics. The book deals with various topics of Islamic law, such as acts of worship and transactions, and reviews rulings on drinks, rituals, zakat, marriage, blood money, and others. The book is distinguished by the authenticity of its chains of transmission and principles, as it relies on established narrations from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.628: Nuzhat al-Huffaz by Ibn al-Madini is a book on hadith science that deals with chain of transmission and narrators, as it focuses on examining and evaluating the chain of transmission of the Prophet’s hadiths. The book covers various chapters related to the narration of hadiths through different narrators, and aims to classify and analyze hadiths through multiple narration chains. The book is concerned with collecting hadiths that have never been classified and collected before, and it is considered a useful reference in the field of prophetic hadiths and their chains of transmission.
descriptions.629: This book, “Nuzhat al-Nazir fi Dhikr Min al-Nadha narrated on the authority of Abu al-Qasim,” by al-Rashid al-Attar, deals with a narration of the life and conditions of the memorizers and scholars from whom Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi narrated. Al-Attar focuses on mentioning those who narrated on the authority of Al-Baghawi, including the Hafiz and the greats, arranging their names according to the letters of the dictionary. The book aims to bring together Al-Baghawi’s sheikhs and narrators, with a focus on mentioning those who narrated from him or heard from him from hadith memorizers and notable narrators, and provides a comprehensive overview of the narration network that extended over time to Al-Baghawi.
descriptions.630: This book is a hadith part that includes the narrations of Abu Musahar Al-Ghassani, and it contains supported prophetic hadiths that he narrated on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission, including a holy hadith that he narrated on the authority of Gabriel on the authority of God Almighty that includes commandments and sermons to His servants. The book also includes another copy of the hadiths narrated by Yahya bin Saleh Al-Wahazi, making it a collection of small hadith parts concerned with transmitting the Sunnah of the Prophet with its chains of transmission.
descriptions.631: The version by Taloot bin Abbad is a collection of hadiths transmitted and transcribed by Taloot bin Abbad Al-Sayrafi. The book includes narrations of prophetic hadiths through a series of narrators. It begins with the narration of Fadal bin Jubayr on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, and mentions hadiths related to Islamic morals and virtues, such as a hadith related to the pillars of faith and Muslim etiquette in talking, lying, and betrayal. It also deals with hadiths that talk about strange or future events such as the rising of the sun from the west.
descriptions.632: This book is a copy of the hadiths and fatwas attributed to Abdullah bin Saleh, the writer of Al-Layth, and it contains a collection of prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas related to buying and selling, animals, prayers, Ramadan fasting, zakat al-Fitr, and other jurisprudential and social topics. The book also deals with some legal rulings related to daily transactions and acts of worship, relying on multiple references from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.633: This book is a copy of the hadith narrated on the authority of Nabeet bin Barat Al-Ashja’i, a hadith narrator with companions. It contains the narration of Abu Al-Hasan Ahmed bin Al-Qasim bin Al-Rayyan Al-Masry on the authority of Nabeet bin Barat, and includes a series of prophetic hadiths that were transmitted through a series of narrators. The book falls within the hadith sections and aims to preserve and document the Prophetic hadiths and their narrators.
descriptions.634: Waki`'s version on the authority of al-A'mash is a collection of hadiths and prophetic narrations, in which Waki` ibn al-Jarrah records what he narrated on the authority of Imam Sulaiman al-A`mash on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The book deals with multiple topics, including prophetic sayings and sayings, focusing on hadiths related to worship, morals, and sermons, relying on a solid chain of narration based on a series of reliable narrators.
descriptions.635: The book “Nazm al-Laali Bi’la al-Awali” by Imam Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani is an edited account of one hundred hadiths that the author heard in one sitting from his sheikh al-Burhan al-Din al-Shami. The book deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths that have been transmitted, indicating the importance and honor of the authentic chain of transmission in transmitting hadith, and the Islamic sciences included under it.
descriptions.636: This book, “Nafhat al-Nasamat Fi Wasool Giving Rewards to the Dead,” written by Imam al-Suruji, is one of the hadith books that dealt with the topic of giving rewards to the dead. The book contains letters from eminent scholars that dealt with the ruling on giving the reward for reading the Qur’an and good deeds to the dead, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and jurisprudential sayings. The book aims to prove the validity of the dead benefiting from the reward received by the living, citing prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential opinions.
descriptions.637: This book, “The Gift of the Living to the Dead and the Benefits That Reach Them,” by Abu Al-Hasan Al-Hakari, deals with topics related to the receipt of reward to the dead through the actions of the living, such as charity, supplication, reading the Qur’an, and prayer. The book focuses on proving that these actions benefit the dead in their graves, relying on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book also includes the benefits of asking forgiveness for parents and the benefits of a special prayer for parents, in addition to the etiquette of dealing with graves.
descriptions.638: This book, “Hawatif al-Jinan” by Al-Kharaiti, deals with hadith topics related to the jinn, as it tells about their types and descriptions, and mentions conversations and conversations between them and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. The book is based on the narration of hadiths and stories that indicate the existence of communication between humans and jinn, with a focus on the spiritual and educational aspect of these communications.
descriptions.639: This book deals with the commandments of the prophets and companions upon the arrival of death, explaining what each of them recommended to the following generations. The author focuses on conveying the commandments and prophetic sayings related to death and commandments, relying on modern and historical sources in his treatment of his topic.
descriptions.640: This book deals with the biography and news of Abu Tammam Habib bin Aws Al-Tai, the pre-Islamic poet and ancient Arabic poetry. It contains letters, stories, and hadiths related to Abu Tammam’s life and poetry, with a focus on his relationships with some prominent figures of his time. The book also presents different opinions about his merit in poetry and his place among the poets of his time, while providing an overview of his lineage and personal character.
descriptions.641: The book “Abu Nawas News” by its author, Abu Hafan, provides a closer look into the life and works of the famous poet Abu Nawas, reviewing events and sayings from various historical and literary sources. The book deals with his biography and his famous stories with princes and poets, presenting a picture of his era and its literature, with a focus on aspects of his personal, social and cultural life. The book is distinguished by its literary style and its reliance on reliable sources to document facts and sayings, which makes it a useful reference for learning about the personality of Abu Nawas and his influence on Arabic literature.
descriptions.642: The book deals with the poems of the six pre-Islamic poets, and provides detailed translations of each poet with an analysis of their selected poems. Al-Alam Al-Shantamari focuses on Imru' Al-Qais, Alqamah Al-Fahl, Zuhair bin Abi Salma, Tarfa bin Al-Ablaj, and Antara bin Shaddad, showing their social and cultural backgrounds and their influence on their poetry. It also presents the opinions of critics on their poetry and conducts rhetorical analyzes of specific verses, focusing on the characteristics of each poet and his artistic styles.
descriptions.643: The book “Anwar Al-Rabi’ fi Types of Badi’” by Muhammad Masoum Al-Hassani deals with the art of Badi’ and its foundations by studying its various types such as eloquence, metaphor, alliteration, metaphor, and others. In its content, the author reviews the concepts of Al-Badi and its applications in poetry and prose, indicating its importance in improving the style of speech and increasing its beauty and influence. The book aims to provide a detailed explanation of the art of Badi and its techniques, with a focus on its artistic applications in Arabic literature.
descriptions.644: The book “Illusions of Arab Poets about Meanings” by Muhammad Taymur Pasha addresses the issue of the mistakes that poets can make when describing meanings and facts that they have not seen themselves. The author divides the book into several sections to examine the reasons for these illusions, including the poet’s ignorance of what he mentions due to his distance from it, or his inability to describe what he did not see or witness personally. The book cites examples from ancient Arabic poetry to demonstrate this phenomenon, and emphasizes that even though poets are people of tongue who do not make mistakes in pronunciation, they may fall into exaggeration or neglect in describing meanings.
descriptions.645: The book “Hope and Expected” by researcher Ibn al-Marzban deals with topics related to methods and etiquette in seeking help, praise, and blame in this context. The book focuses on how to deal with the different circumstances that a writer or questioner may face, from humiliation and confusion to the comfort and glory of despair, condemning eagerness and haste and urging diligent contemplation and gentleness in seeking. The book aims to provide practical advice to writers and students on how to manage their relationships and requests in an ethical and effective manner, with an emphasis on the importance of patience and wisdom in dealing with difficult circumstances and sensitive situations.
descriptions.646: The book “The Preferences” by the scholar Ali bin Munjib deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric, including letters and treatises on forgiveness, intercession, praise, and extolling the virtues of important figures. The book focuses on praising moral virtues and good qualities, and its talk revolves around benevolence in literary systems and poetry, with an emphasis on poetic rhymes and rhetorical methods. The book also includes various topics related to the legal, philosophical, medical and other sciences, which indicates the breadth of its author’s vision and the comprehensiveness of its content in the fields of knowledge and literature.
descriptions.647: The book “Al-Amali” by Al-Marzouqi is one of the literary and rhetorical works that deals with the grammar and grammar of the Arabic language. The book focuses on studying grammatical and morphological structures and rules, relying on examples from poetry and antiquities to clarify its issues. The book includes multiple chapters that address a variety of topics from parsing and weakness to strange and anecdotes, making it a useful reference for students of the Arabic language and its grammar.
descriptions.648: In his book "Proverbs", Maraj Al-Sadoosi presents an encyclopedic study of Arabic proverbs, reviewing a collection of popular proverbs and sayings that reflect the wisdom and intelligence of the Arabs in expressing various life issues. The book deals with proverbs through a sequential narrative, explaining their origins and the poets’ sayings about them, with an explanation of their meanings and aspects of metaphor. It also refers to the uses of proverbs in poetry and prose, and how to use them to persuade and express thoughts and feelings.
descriptions.649: This book deals with the topic of weapons and their importance in ancient Arab culture, covering different types of weapons such as swords, spears, and shields, and mentioning sayings and hadiths related to these weapons. The author focuses on the virtue of weapons and their qualities, and reviews what has been said on this subject in poetry and proverbs, with reference to some historical facts related to weapons in the days of the Arabs.
descriptions.650: A book by Abu Ishaq, Ibrahim al-Shatibi al-Gharnati, and it is classified as a book that restricts the sources of issues, controls them, and collects the narrated benefits, whatever the knowledge to which they are related.
descriptions.651: This book, “The Prosperity in the Hadiths and Athars of Poets” by Al-Suyuti, deals with the collection of poetry that contained famous hadiths and sayings, classifying it in the art of literature and rhetoric. The book aims to benefit from these poems in various fields, such as proving the authenticity of the hadiths, documenting their fame in the early ages, including them in dictation councils, and using them as examples in the arts of rhetoric and creativity.
descriptions.652: This book, “The Wonderful Description of Spring,” written by Al-Himyari Abu Al-Walid, is one of the literary works that deals with describing the spring season and its beauty. The author focuses on describing spring flowers, their colors, and types, providing a wonderful literary description of ornamental trees and their roses in this beautiful season. The book aims to document what the authors overlooked in describing the descriptions of spring and its flowers, relying on the Andalusians’ description of these flowers in particular, while pointing out the differences between the people of Andalusia and the Levant’s approach to this topic.
descriptions.653: This book is a literary and rhetorical criticism of the poetry of Abu Al-Ala Al-Maarri, in which Al-Suyuti addresses Al-Maarri’s famous criticisms, known as Ma’aratha, and provides a response to them by tracing the names of dogs in language books and organizing them into poetic narratives. The book aims to disavow Al-Ma'arri's accusations and demonstrate the extent of his knowledge and knowledge in the field of names and the Arabic language.
descriptions.654: The book “Al-Tahf wa Al-Zarf” by Al-Darimi Muhammad bin Ahmed Al-Tamimi is a book on literature and rhetoric that combines poetry, sermons, wisdom, hadiths, and proverbs. The book deals with various topics, such as the Qur’an, Hadith, sermons, and medicine, and includes poetry distributed over different chapters related to the topics of the book. The author aims to provide useful and diverse literary content that combines art and scientific originality.
descriptions.655: This book, “Antiques and Gifts” by Abu al-Bakr Muhammad and Abu Uthman Saeed al-Khalidien, deals with the subject of gifts and antiques from a literary and rhetorical perspective, classifying poetry and sayings on this subject into several sections, including those who were given a gift with poetry, those who were given a gift and thanked them for it with poetry, those who requested the gift with or without poetry, those who disparaged what was given to them, and those who did not accept the gift out of respect and rejected it out of respect. The book also includes news about gifts from kings and anecdotes in this field, thus presenting a literary encyclopedia on the subject of precious gifts and antiques.
descriptions.656: This book, “The Saadian Remembrance in Arabic Poetry,” by the scholar Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Obaidi, deals with the art of Arabic poetry in its various fields, from enthusiasm and pride to literature, wisdom, and proverbs, passing through lineage. The author focuses on selecting poems with noble meaning and beautiful pronunciation, classifying them into multiple chapters that reflect the diversity of Arabic poetry throughout the ages. The book aims to present a selection of the most wonderful works written in Arabic poetry, achieving excellence in style and meaning alike.
descriptions.657: The book “The Honorary Ticket” by Mawlana Bahaa al-Din al-Irbli deals with the subject of literature and rhetoric, focusing on several elements of poetry, spinning, wine, singing, spring, nature, stars, and praise. The author focuses on describing the aesthetic and expressive meanings of these elements, reviewing their effects in Arabic poetry and their influence on Arabic literature and culture. The book is machine-numbered and contains an introduction that begins with praise of God and prayers upon the Prophet Muhammad, relying on poetry as one of the most important forms of literature in the Arab heritage.
descriptions.658: The book “Similes” by Ibn Abi Aoun is a work of literature and rhetoric. It collects a selection of poets’ similes and their masterpieces, divided into thematic sections, such as the simile of the Pleiades, the morning, the horse, lightning, and crying. The author aims to present examples of rare realistic simile, strange metaphor, and common proverb, limiting himself to rare funny verses, with the book beginning by mentioning similes from the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.659: The book consists of a collection of poems, proverbs, prophetic hadiths, and literary anecdotes, with a variety of topics and styles, distributed into different chapters, some of which are related to poetry and wisdom, and some of which deal with genealogies and geographical and social knowledge. Author Abu Ali Al-Hijri relies on telling stories and proverbs through his tales of poets and sages, relying on the Arab literary and cultural heritage.
descriptions.660: The book “Al-Tamam fi Tafsir Hudhayl ​​Poetry” by Ibn Jinni deals with a detailed interpretation of verses of pre-Islamic poetry by poets from the origins of Hudhayl, with a focus on poets whose poetry was not interpreted by Abu Ubaidah Musafa bin Sulaym. The book focuses on analyzing words, meanings, and parsing, relying on Ibn Jinni's extensive knowledge of linguistics and literature. The book deals with prominent poets from Hudhail, and explains their poetry in detail, noting the differences between linguistic schools in interpreting some words and grammatical rules.
descriptions.661: This book, “Alerts on Narrators’ Mistakes,” by Ali bin Hamza Al-Basri, deals with correcting the mistakes and mistakes that occurred in prophetic and poetic narratives and hadiths. The author focuses on reviewing the anecdotes of some famous narrators, such as Abu Ziyad Al-Kalabi, and points out the linguistic and grammatical errors found in their interpretations and poems, correcting them according to the correct rules of the Arabic language. The book aims to clarify and correct misconceptions, and addresses topics related to literature and rhetoric, relying on reliable linguistic and poetic references.
descriptions.662: The book “Horses” by Abu Ubaida Muammar bin Al-Muthanna deals with a detailed study of the importance of horses in Arab culture, covering aspects including the names of horses, the names of horses, their faults, and their aesthetic and moral descriptions. The book focuses on documenting the elements that distinguish the quality and character of the horse, noting the differences between male and female horses, and the different colors of horses. The author also points out the changes that occurred in Arabs’ dealings with horses from pre-Islamic times to Islam, showing how horses transformed from a symbol of power and pride in Arab societies into a tool of war in Islam.
descriptions.663: The dissertation explaining the thefts of Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi and his fallen poetry deals with a literary book that focuses on discussing al-Mutanabbi’s quotations from other poets and analyzing his verses, some of which are considered unsuccessful. The author Ibn al-Muzaffar al-Hatimi addresses this issue in the context of a literary dispute that occurred with him in a scholarly council, where he invited him to write a letter explaining these accusations. The book falls within the category of literature and rhetoric, and aims to provide objective literary criticism of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry, focusing on certain aspects of his poetic production.
descriptions.664: The book “Al-Zahra” by Ibn Dawud Al-Zahiri is a book on literature and rhetoric, dealing with topics related to love, passion, reason, and wisdom. It consists of several chapters, each of which deals with different aspects of these topics, showing the relationship between sight and passion, reason and longing, and psychological treatment through description and misdescription of the condition. Through proverbs, proverbs, and poetic verses, the book reviews the concepts of love, love, and the human mind in dealing with feelings of love and passion.
descriptions.665: Leg on Leg is a novel by Ahmed Fares Al-Shidyaq, one of the founders of modern Arabic literature. The novel talks in detail about the life of Al-Fariq, as an expression of the author’s ego, and provides an explanation of intellectual and social issues. It is described as always dazzling and often funny. It is also considered the most wonderful, funniest, and most surprising Arabic novel. The novel is an unclassifiable book. The novel was originally published in 1855 in Arabic in Paris. The novel was translated into English by Humphrey T. Davies in 2014, and published by New York University Press.
descriptions.666: This book, “The Detailed Contract in the Majd Tribe,” by Al-Haidar Al-Hilli, deals with a moral and literary study of the Majd tribe, explaining its lineage, origins, and good qualities. The author focuses on examining the characteristics of the tribe through multiple chapters that address the virtues of its members in the areas of morals, intelligence, and eloquence, while including samples of their prose and poetic compositions. The book is divided into parts organized according to rhyme. Each section contains chapters that deal with different topics such as praise, lamentation, ghazal, and satire.
descriptions.667: This book is by Al-Badr Al-Damamini, and it is one of the works of literature and rhetoric that are numbered automatically. The book deals with a detailed prosodic study of Arabic poetry, focusing on the analysis of meter and rhyme in various poetic meters, while providing examples and evidence from classical poetry. The author aims to clarify the rules of prosody and their applications in poetry, while providing literary criticism of some specific poetic forms.
descriptions.668: The Book of Chapters and Objectives, also known as Paragraphs and Periods, is one of the works of Abu Al-Ala’ Al-Ma’arri (who died in the year 449 AH/1058 AD), the author of the Treatise of Al-Sahil and Al-Shahj and the Epistle of Al-Ghufran. He wrote it, as Ibn Al-Adim says, after his return from Baghdad: “The first thing he wrote after his interruption in his home, after his return from Baghdad, was the book known as “The Chapters and Objectives in the Glorification of God Almighty.” And the Sermons” is the book for which he was slandered, and it was said that he contradicted the surahs and verses with it, as a transgression against him, injustice, and falsehood and sin. The book is not in opposition to anything. Its value is one hundred booklets. …
descriptions.669: This book, “The Earring on Al-Kamil” by Imam Ibn Saad Al-Khair, deals with the study of the era of the Taifa kings in Andalusia and the arts and literature that resulted from it. The author focuses on examining aspects of political, social, and cultural life in that era, with an emphasis on the lives and works of prominent literary figures such as Abu al-Walid al-Waqshi and Abu Muhammad Ibn al-Sayyid al-Batalyusi. The book aims to shed light on the literary and scientific contributions of Andalusia during the period of the Taifa Kings, and to analyze the environment in which these contributions arose.
descriptions.670: In his book "Al-Qawafi", Al-Akhfash Al-Awsat provides an explanation of the science of rhymes, addressing their definition and the number of their types, relying in this on what was approved by the eloquent Arabs. The book focuses on clarifying the concept of rhyme and the letters and vowels it contains, while discussing the rules for forming rhymes and their controls. It also discusses differences in understanding the concept of rhyme between poets and Arabs, reviewing opinions and examples from Arabic poetry to clarify its issues.
descriptions.671: This book deals with poetry in praise of beautiful slave girls, trying to present a sophisticated literary image of their beauty and good morals. In this work, Al-Shehab Al-Hijazi deals with aspects of the lives of female slaves through elegiac and descriptive poems, reviewing their physical and spiritual qualities. The book aims to raise the value of women in society and appreciate their beauty and intelligence, relying on poetry as a literary means to express these meanings.
descriptions.672: This book, “Al-Latif and Al-Latif” by Al-Thaalabi Abu Mansour, deals with a collection of anecdotes and anecdotes related to the figures of various arts and classes in Islamic history. It contains hadiths and sayings of prominent figures from the Companions and Followers, kings and ministers, writers and poets, jurists and scholars, philosophers and doctors, singers and singers, and other groups. He focuses on highlighting the wit, generosity, and intelligence in the words and actions of these individuals, relying on eloquent words and brevity of expression. Through this book, the author aims to draw closer with his literary works to Sheikh Brigadier General Abi Sahl Al-Hamdouni, and to introduce him to interesting groups of virtuous people in various arts and classes.
descriptions.673: The book “Advantages and Disadvantages” written by Al-Bayhaqi Ibrahim is one of the books that deals with the fields of literature and rhetoric. The book focuses on presenting the advantages and disadvantages associated with historical figures, stories, and events, relying on famous hadiths and sayings of important figures in Islamic history. The book deals with various topics, including the virtues and exemplary actions of some of the Companions and followers, and the disadvantages and mistakes of those who abandoned the religion or returned to the Prophet’s family (may Allah be pleased with them). The book also includes poems and boasts related to these figures, providing a comprehensive overview of some of the positive and negative aspects of Islamic history and Arabic literature.
descriptions.674: In his book “Lectures on Language and Literature,” Al-Hasan Al-Yusi presents a diverse literary and rhetorical content, in which he addresses multiple intellectual and cultural topics, from the benefits of naming and the rules of literature to wisdom, sermons, and proverbs. The author combines intellectual depth with literary expression, reviewing the types of people and geographical environments, and also reviewing his personal positions and experiences with scholars and writers. The book is rich in wisdom and sayings that reflect the author's wisdom and philosophical vision of life and science.
descriptions.675: This book is by Al-Sari Al-Rafaa, and it is one of the works of literature and rhetoric that is concerned with describing the descriptions of hair and parts of the human body and beauty. In its various chapters, the book deals with descriptions of hair, temples, virgins, horses, cheeks, cheeks, eyebrows, eyes, noses, teeth, good breath, good speech and tone. It focuses on describing beauty and poetic qualities in a sophisticated literary style, using sublime rhetorical language and perfect aesthetics, relying on the provisions of truth and skill in rhetoric and oratory.
descriptions.676: This book, written by Ibn Khordadhabh, deals with topics of literature and rhetoric related to singing, music, and singers. The book mentions the virtues of singing and its effect on the soul, and reviews wisdom and sayings by scholars and jurists about the ruling on singing. It also mentions names and news about famous singers in Islamic history. The book also deals with musical philosophy and the impact of music on the minds and senses, and mentions sayings by wise philosophers on this subject.
descriptions.677: This book, by the scholar Ibn Saeed al-Maghribi, is related to the field of literature and rhetoric, as it deals with the history of Arabic poetry throughout the different eras, focusing on the poets of the East and Morocco. The book deals with the biographies of poets and their poems, with a focus on some stories and news related to them, including some love stories and famous tales about famous poets. The book aims to collect and document lyric poetry and dance, and it includes the names of poets from various Arab eras and countries.
descriptions.678: The Book of the Poor is a book of prose by Mustafa Sadiq Al-Rafi’i, which he presented with an eloquent introduction to the meaning of poverty, charity, and human compassion. It consists of various chapters, with no unified unit that links them except that they are images of many-colored, multi-shaded human suffering. …
descriptions.679: This book, “Al-Mujaddid Min Fa’alat Al-Ajawad” by Al-Tanukhi Al-Muhsin Bin Ali, deals with the stories and actions of generous and generous people. The author focuses on telling inspiring stories about generosity and generosity, reviewing the heroic actions of great figures such as Ali bin Abi Talib and Hassan bin Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both). The book aims to inspire and motivate the reader to practice goodness and generosity, relying on examples from Islamic history to enhance the values ​​of giving and giving.
descriptions.680: The book “Long Livers and Wills” by Al-Sijistani Abu Hatim Sahl bin Othman presents texts and hadiths about the longest-lived people in Islamic history and circulating myths, with a focus on the stories of Adam, Noah, and Al-Khidr, and narrations about their ages and wills. The book also deals with the life of Luqman bin Adia Al-Kabir and the story of his life for a long time, mentioning some discrepancies in the ages mentioned. The book falls into the category of literature and rhetoric, and contains automatically numbered texts, making it easy to access specific information.
descriptions.681: The book “Al-Maqamat Al-Zayniyyah” by Ibn Al-Saqil Al-Jazari is a collection of literary Maqamat that is based on the classical Maqamat style in Arabic literature. The book addresses multiple topics through its various shrines that move between many cities, presenting a picture of the social and cultural life in those cities. The book is automatically edited, making the content easy to access and analyze. The text is characterized by a sophisticated literary style that combines humor and wisdom, relying on the dialogue of the characters and their stories to convey its literary and moral message.
descriptions.682: This book, “Houses and Homes” by Ahmed bin Murshid bin Ali bin Muqallid bin Nasr bin Munqidh Al-Kanani, deals with various topics related to homes, homes, and homelands, explaining their conditions and descriptions through various chapters. The author focuses on describing homes, homes, ruins, and dwellings, expressing his sadness at the devastation and destruction that befell his homelands, and expressing his acceptance of God’s will and destiny. The book combines literature and eloquence in its description of homes and homes, expressing the author's sad feelings over the calamities and destruction that befell his homeland.
descriptions.683: This book deals with the history of Christianity and its spread among Arab tribes in the pre-Islamic era, with a focus on the miscellaneous information contained in Arab books, the works of Orientalists, and the writings of Eastern Christians. The author divides the research into two parts: the first deals with the history of Christianity in the Arabian Peninsula and its Christianized tribes, and the second focuses on Christian literature in that era, reviewing its effects on the Arabic language and proverbs.
descriptions.684: This book is one of the types of literature and rhetoric. It deals with the linguistic and literary lapses and mistakes that respectable and educated speakers make, with the addition of news about lucky fools. The author focuses on collecting rare and surprising examples of these lapses and omissions, and presents them in an awareness-raising way to alert his readers to the importance of caution in using language.
descriptions.685: This book is an interpretation of some of Al-Mutanabbi's difficult and ambiguous verses of poetry. The author, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Isbahani, deals with the problems of meanings and wording in the poet's poetry, reviewing the aspects of interpretation and explanation available for these verses. The book aims to simplify understanding of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry and remove confusion about it, relying on his deep literary and rhetorical knowledge.
descriptions.686: This book deals with topics of Arabic literature and poetry, focusing on mentioning poets and figures from different eras and places. It contains overviews of the lives of poets and selected poems from them, with a focus on sayings and hadiths related to them. The book deals with personalities such as Ward bin Saad Al-Ammi and Abu Al-Adhafer, and mentions poems and poems by other poets, while providing historical and literary information about them. The book aims to provide a comprehensive picture of Arab poetry and its figures throughout the ages.
descriptions.687: The book “Attainment of Hope in the Art of Zajal” is a book by Ibn Hajjat ​​al-Hamawi in which he collected what was said about the art of zajal and its origins, and was the first to write about it.
descriptions.688: This book is an explanation of the poems of Mawla Ishaq, in which Al-Siyaghi deals with philosophical and religious research on the concept of the soul. The author focuses on discussing the differences between scholars and thinkers about the permissibility of speaking about the essence of the soul, the reality of its existence, and its independence after death, relying in this on Qur’anic verses, prophetic hadiths, and the opinions of interpretive scholars. The book aims to explore the meaning and nature of the soul, while pointing out the cognitive limits that humans must respect in this context.
descriptions.689: This book, “Decorating the Markets in the News of Lovers,” by Dr. Daoud Al-Antaki, deals with the subject of love and passion from a literary and religious perspective, trying to reconcile the good contemplation of beauty and disciplining oneself from vices. It contains hadiths and sayings of the wise about love, and also includes famous stories about lovers in the Arab heritage, with a focus on the spiritual and moral consequences of different cases of love. The book aims to soften hearts and develop literary taste by presenting inspiring and inspiring stories.
descriptions.690: This book, “Relief of Anguish in the Knowledge of Arab Illiteracy,” by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Qasim bin Abdul Wahed bin Zakour Al-Farsi, deals with a detailed explanation of Arab Illiteracy, which is a famous poem in Arabic literature. The author aims to clarify the meanings of poetic verses and explain their strange words, thus providing an important means of learning Arabic eloquence and understanding ancient literature. The book is distinguished by its attractive style and precise explanation, which makes it a useful reference for students of Arabic literature and language.
descriptions.691: This book is an interpretation of some verses of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry, written by Abu Murshid Al-Maarri. The book deals with the interpretation of the linguistic and rhetorical meanings of Al-Mutanabbi’s poems, indicating the noble words and gentle meanings in them. In this book, the author deals with the interpretation of the linguistic and rhetorical meanings of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry, indicating the honorable words and gentle meanings in them, and reviews the opinions of previous interpreters of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry, relying on brevity and brevity in his treatment.
descriptions.692: The book “Tawshi’ al-Tawshih” by Al-Safadi deals with the subject of literary muwashahs, and reviews their origins, divisions, and types, with a focus on the muwashshah art as one of the literary arts for which the people of Morocco are famous. The book aims to collect poetry collections in one collection, noting that this type of poetry is not easy to collect or compose, but it remains an object of admiration for those who master its art. The book also deals with the history of the emergence of stanzas and their development over time, mentioning some of the names that contributed to the development of this literary art.
descriptions.693: This book, “Collecting Jewels in Salt and Anecdotes,” by Al-Husri Al-Qayrawani, deals with the art of joking, anecdotes, and humor in Arabic literature. The author focuses on the importance of joking in social communication and its impact on human relations, explaining the conditions and origins of good joking, and how it can be used as a means of optimism and self-entertainment. The book contains examples, funny stories, and amusing situations, relying on a gradual methodology in presenting topics to facilitate the reader’s understanding and enjoyment of the content.
descriptions.694: This book deals with the topic of poems that talk about beautiful boys, focusing on the poetry of Al-Shihab Al-Hijazi in particular, away from the popular poetry. The author aims to provide an artistic and literary view to describe the beauty of boys, while acknowledging the difficulty of this topic in his time. The book combines poetic verses with critical comments, providing a deep artistic reading of the boys’ poetry, while acknowledging the limits of his creativity and the lack of his production in this field compared to previous poets.
descriptions.695: This book, “Hadayek al-Azhar fi Mustahsan al-Ajuba wa-l-Farqa’,” by Ibn Asim al-Andalusi, deals with topics of literature and rhetoric through a diverse presentation of clever answers and light jokes. The book is divided into several gardens, each garden includes various sections dealing with surprising anecdotes, poetic jokes and lengthy ones, news of the Bedouins and forecasters, and common proverbs and their wisdom. The book aims to entertain the souls and provide diverse and enjoyable literary content.
descriptions.696: This book, “The Ornament of the Knights and the Slogan of the Brave,” by Ibn Hudhail, deals with the subject of horses from a literary and scientific perspective. The book includes multiple sections dealing with the creation and spread of horses, their virtues and hadiths, their preservation and preservation, the names of their members, their praiseworthy qualities, and their colors and types. The book aims to provide comprehensive knowledge about purebred Arabian horses and their appreciation in Islamic culture.
descriptions.697: This book, “The Ornament of the Lecture,” by Ibn al-Muzaffar al-Hatimi, deals with the making of poetry and its types, focusing on the types of eloquence and creativity in Arabic poetry. Through its various chapters, the author presents examples of good poetry in metaphor, matching, naturalization, division, and other rhetorical techniques, reviewing the most creative aspects of these types of Arabic poetry. The book aims to highlight the secrets of eloquence and eloquence in poetry, and to present distinct examples of good poetry in various techniques of poetic art.
descriptions.698: The book “The Enthusiasm of the Gentle” by Abdulkani Al-Zozni is a collection of poems that reflect various themes of Arabic literature, such as old age, gray hair, satire, and praise. Through verses of poetry, the book addresses topics related to age, youth, and old age, expressing wisdom and sermons through poetic sayings and proverbs. The book is classified within the arts of literature and rhetoric, and contains texts from ancient and modern poets, making it a rich literary reference that addresses topics relevant to life and society.
descriptions.699: Khorida Al-Qasr and Al-Asr Newspaper is a literary book in 21 volumes, in which its author, Imad Al-Din Al-Isfahani, translated several poets in the fifth and sixth centuries AH.
descriptions.700: Diwan al-Sababa by Ibn Abi Hajleh is a literary composition that deals with the topic of love and affection from a literary and artistic perspective, examining its causes, signs, levels, and names, relying on poems, proverbs, and historical events related to this topic. The book focuses on describing the state of lovers and their feelings, and includes multiple chapters dealing with beauty and beauty, kings and caliphs in love, lovers who fell in love with hearing, and different cases of love and passion.
descriptions.701: Al-Tha'alibi's letters are a collection of literary and rhetorical letters that include multiple chapters dealing with topics such as the virtues of writers, the morals of writers, sermons, congratulations, condolences, visits, and worship. The book also addresses social and political topics such as estrangement, time, and livelihood, with a focus on the etiquette of speech and writing in the context of social and political relations. The book aims to enhance the skills of writers in expressing various topics in a polite and intelligent manner, with a focus on the importance that kings and rulers attach to literature and knowledge in managing the affairs of the state and society.
descriptions.702: The Treatise of Al-Sahil and Al-Shajah by Ibn Sulaiman Al-Maarri deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric in the form of a dialogue between two shepherds, where the writer expresses the concepts of literature and wisdom in a symbolic manner through a dialogue between two shepherds in the pastures. The book also addresses themes of weakness and strength, powerlessness and power, relying on rich literary metaphors and similes.
descriptions.703: The Epistle of the Spectrum by Bahaa al-Din al-Irbli is a literary book that deals with the fields of literature and rhetoric. It presents, through verses of poetry and its likes, the concepts of morality and wisdom, with an emphasis on the importance of deliberation in directing one’s gaze and lowering one’s gaze, considering this a piece of wisdom in life and advice to a person to avoid falling into problems and worries. The book contains poetic texts of various poetic meter that address topics of love, beauty, wisdom, and contemplation of life.
descriptions.704: This book, “The Expansion of Salt and the Exodus of Joy,” by Ibn al-Dajji, deals with various topics of literature and rhetoric, mixed with famous tales, proverbs, and sayings. It combines news of prophets and sages and stories of caliphs and ministers, with a focus on the literary and poetic arts. It aims to make the reader laugh and benefit him by providing a mixture of useful information and interesting stories, taking into account a sophisticated and beautiful literary style.
descriptions.705: In this book, Ibn Sayyidah provides a detailed explanation of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry, focusing on interpreting the meanings and rhetorical and linguistic connotations of the complex poems. The author deals with an in-depth interpretation of some verses of poetry, reviewing the rhetorical aspects and implicit meanings, relying on his linguistic and critical skills in analyzing Al-Mutanabbi’s complex texts.
descriptions.706: This book is an explanation of the poetry collection of the poet Abu Al-Tayeb Al-Mutanabbi, written by Al-Wahidi. The explanation deals with Al-Mutanabbi’s poems and explains their meanings and rhetorical secrets, showing the beauty of poetry and its importance in Arabic literature. The book focuses on analyzing poetic verses and detailing their vocabulary and meanings, with reference to the poetic arts and rhetorical rules used by the poet.
descriptions.707: The book “The Dove’s Tawq” by Al-Suyuti deals with a literary and rhetorical study of pigeons, covering the language of pronunciation and its terminology, and the distinction between pigeons and doves, along with a description of the character and characteristics of pigeons. The book relies on texts and sayings by linguists and literary scholars, such as Al-Jawhari, Al-Asma’i, and Al-Rafi’i, to explore its topic through a linguistic and literary perspective, focusing on the different types of pigeons and their individual and collective characteristics.
descriptions.708: This book is a response by Al-Aswad Al-Ghandjani to Ibn Al-Sirafi, in which he criticizes Ibn Al-Sirafi’s interpretations of verses from the book of Sibawayh. In his response, Al-Aswad addresses the errors of Ibn Al-Sirafi in his attribution of some verses to poets other than their authors, and his distortion of their meanings and wording. In his responses, Al-Aswad relies on evidence from authentic Arabic poetry, and provides corrections to some verses in which Ibn Al-Sirafi admitted there were flaws. The book is classified as literature and rhetoric, and contains explanations and analyzes of various poems, relying on poetic and grammatical sources.
descriptions.709: This book, “Fasus al-Khawatim, regarding what was said about banquets,” deals with the topic of banquets and weddings from a literary and legal perspective, examining different types of banquets, such as the wedding banquet, the aqeeqah, mourning, and others. The author explains the meaning of the feast and its definition in language and Sharia, and mentions its rulings and etiquette, relying on linguistic and Sharia sources. The book combines jurisprudence and literature in its treatment of the subject of banquets, and aims to explain its origins, legal controls, and general etiquette.
descriptions.710: The book “The Pole of Pleasure in the Descriptions of Wines and Wines” by Al-Raqiq Al-Qayrawani, deals with the topics of wines and wines from a literary and cultural perspective, reviewing the sayings of poets and madmen in this field, and reviewing the opinions of philosophers about the benefits and harms, mentioning various hadiths and stories about wine and sugar, and evidence from poetry arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. The book combines interest and enjoyment, and provides a comprehensive picture of the place of wine in ancient Arab culture.
descriptions.711: This book, “Kashf al-Hawl fi Description al-Khal” by Al-Safadi, deals with the description of the maternal uncle from a linguistic and physiognomic perspective, and reviews the opinions of scholars and thinkers on this subject. The author focuses on the analysis of the uncle as a knightly trait and the meanings it denotes, and mentions examples from Islamic and Arab history of characters known for their uncle. The book falls within the field of literature and rhetoric, and aims to provide a comprehensive vision of the meaning of the uncle and its influence on physiognomy and personality.
descriptions.712: This book deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric through the study of humans and animals. The first chapter focuses on explaining the characteristics of humans and their honor, while the second chapter moves on to discuss the natures of animals with fangs and nails. The author aims to provide general information about the morals and character of various animals without going into medical or anatomical details that are considered topics for other specialized books.
descriptions.713: Thalab’s Councils is a book on literature and rhetoric that deals with scholarly councils, literary stories, and conversations. It consists of several parts, and contains a talk about a story between a man and a woman related to a poem, in addition to mentioning another story about a priest and a woman related to a Qur’anic verse. The book relies mainly on storytelling and literary conversations.
descriptions.714: This book is a collection of proverbs and proverbs contained in Arabic poetry throughout the ages, starting from the era of Ya'rab bin Qahtan until the twentieth century.
descriptions.715: The book “Mas’a’il al-Niqdat” by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Sharaf al-Qayrawani is a book on literature and rhetoric, in which the author deals with various hadiths and literary genres, some of which are eloquent and wonderful in their organization, and some of which are strange in their translations and hadith chains. In some of his hadiths, Al-Qayrawani quoted famous tales, such as the story of Kalila and Dimna, and wrote them in a twisted literary way, as Sahl ibn Harun did in his book “The Tiger and the Fox.” The book aims to provide different and diverse meanings for the benefit of the readers and lecturers. It includes twenty hadiths with diverse topics and meanings, expressing the difficulty of achieving it in light of the difficult circumstances that the writer went through.
descriptions.716: This book deals with comparing the proverbs of Kalila and Dimna with similar proverbs from Arabic poetry, trying to link the sayings and proverbs drawn from the famous story with the proverbs and sayings of Arab poets and writers. The author focuses on conveying wisdom and sermons through poetic proverbs and quotations, reviewing multiple topics related to morals, behavior, and dealing with others. The book aims to provide a deep insight into the values ​​and ethics of Arab society through these proverbs and sayings.
descriptions.717: This book, “The Rise of Bedours and Houses of Pleasure” by Al-Ghazouli, deals with topics of literature and rhetoric through studying the art of construction and interior decoration, based on the analysis of buildings, their parts, and interior elements, and includes advice and ideas about choosing the appropriate place for construction, arranging rooms and interior decorations, neighborly etiquette, good reception, organizing food and drinks, and other topics related to social and cultural life at that time.
descriptions.718: The book, “The Miracle of Ahmad Explanation of the Diwan of Al-Mutanabbi,” provides an interpretation and analysis of verses from the poetry collection of the poet Al-Mutanabbi, covering several poetry collections, including Iraqiyyat, Shamiyyat, Al-Sayfiyyat, Al-Misriyyat, and others. Author Abu Al-Ala Al-Maarri focuses on clarifying the rhetorical meanings and linguistic connotations of the poems, reviewing Al-Mutanabbi’s artistic style and the characteristics of his poetry. The book is numbered automatically and provides a detailed explanation of many poems and verses, with a focus on the linguistic and moral dimensions of the poetic text.
descriptions.719: This book, “Muntaha al-Talab min al-Arab Poetry,” is an automatically numbered poetry collection that includes one hundred poems for each of ten parts. In it, the author Ibn Maimon collected four hundred poems from the poems of pre-Islamic and Islamic poets. He selected the most beautiful and eloquent things they said. The book deals with prominent poets such as Ka'b bin Zuhair, Amr bin Kulthum and Antara, and includes poems from the selections of Al-Mufadliyat and Al-Asma'iyat, in addition to the anthologies of Jarir and Al-Farazdaq and poems from the book "Al-Shawarid" by Ibn Duraid. Ibn Maimonides wrote an explanation of some strange words on the sides of the leaves. He compiled this book after spending sixty years studying poetry, memorizing it, and transcribing its collections.
descriptions.720: This book, “Minhaj al-Bulagha and Siraj al-Adabā’” by Al-Qurtajani, deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric through multiple approaches to studying meanings and methods of employing them in poetry and rhetoric. The author focuses on ways to understand meanings and how to quote and organize them, emphasizing the importance of the fit between meanings and the human psyche. The book includes a first curriculum that explains the nature of meanings and their types, and a second curriculum that deals with methods of obtaining meanings and how to compose them, in addition to other approaches that study the conditions of meanings and their characteristics in their various locations.
descriptions.721: This book, “Nukhbat Aqd al-Ajyad fi al-Safnat al-Jiyad,” by the Algerian Muhammad ibn Abd al-Qadir, deals with the subject of horses from a literary and religious perspective, explaining their virtue and honor in Islam and the love of the Arabs for them, describing their types, colors, and descriptions, mentioning the wonderful similes and metaphors in describing them, and detailing the forelock, the turban, the circles, and the names of the joints, natures, and neighing.
descriptions.722: A Journey of Insights with Stories of News and Poetry by Abdul Rahman bin Dirham, a book that deals with poetry and literature, focusing on presenting various poems and poetic praises for prominent figures in Islamic history, with a focus on Abu Tammam as one of the most prominent poets. The book combines poetry, stories, and conversations in an automatically numbered manner, making it easy to access the rich poetic and critical content that accompanies it.
descriptions.723: This book, “Supporting the Rebel against the Walking Proverb” by Al-Safadi, deals with criticism of the book “The Walking Proverb” by Ibn Al-Atheer, trying to refute Ibn Al-Atheer’s claims regarding his literary merit and superiority over other writers. Al-Safadi focuses on discussing the concepts of rhetoric and eloquence, and criticizes Ibn al-Atheer’s style of writing, presenting examples from his original book. The book also addresses linguistic and literary issues such as the color of metaphor and metonymy, and discusses the issue of matching pronunciation with meaning in literary composition.
descriptions.724: This book, “Nadhrat al-Ighrid fi Nusrat al-Qarid” by the scholar al-Muzaffar ibn al-Fadl al-Alawi, deals with the subject of poetry, its rulings and qualities, and reviews its various sections and conditions. The author focuses on analyzing poetic techniques such as allusion, metonymy, balancing, alliteration, and other rhetorical techniques, indicating their strengths and weaknesses and how to use them effectively. The book aims to support Arabic poetry and explain its virtue and purity, while discussing its benefits and harms in the context of literature and rhetoric.
descriptions.725: This book deals with proverbs and proverbs in an organized and numbered manner, as it contains a collection of proverbs and proverbs arranged according to alphabetical letters. Author Abdullah Fikri focuses on providing wise advice and sayings related to morals and human behavior, relying on alphabetical order to organize his content. The book addresses various topics related to personal reform, dealing with others, good morals, and wisdom in life.
descriptions.726: This book was produced by Al-Husri Al-Qayrawani, and it includes verses and prose describing light and blossom, with various chapters dealing with literary and rhetorical topics. The book is distinguished by its poetic and critical style, as the author deals with literary topics in a sophisticated poetic style, mixed with philosophical reflections and deep meanings. The book is classified within the arts of literature and rhetoric, and is distinguished by its beautiful prose and elegant poetry, with an emphasis on the concept of light as a source of inspiration and radiance.
descriptions.727: This book deals with the wills of kings and the sons of kings from the lineage of Qahtan bin Hood, as the author Dabal Al-Khuzai narrates the wills of kings and presidents from the descendants of Qahtan throughout history. The book begins by narrating Qahtan’s lineage and the story of Hud (peace be upon him), then moves on to mentioning the wills attributed to the kings and chiefs of Qahtan’s sons, thus addressing topics of ancient Arab literature, rhetoric, and history.
descriptions.728: This book by Ibn Duraid deals with the description of rain and clouds and what the Arabs called them from different regions, reviewing what the Arabs mentioned in the pre-Islamic and Islamic era of literary descriptions of these natural phenomena. The author focuses on collecting Arabic sayings and proverbs that reflect the splendor of the Arab language in describing nature, relying on wisdom, prophetic proverbs, and stories from Arab heritage.
descriptions.729: This book combines poetry and literature in providing advice, sermons, wisdom, and proverbs with a spiritual and religious dimension. It is divided into two parts: the first deals with the Islamic faith from the perspective of the Sunnis and the community, and the second contains various poetic verses that focus on virtuous morals and urging useful knowledge and good use of time. The author aims to present these verses to readers to increase their knowledge and culture and strengthen their faith, relying on his careful selection of their contents from multiple sources.
descriptions.730: The book covers a poem by Dr. Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali, which talks about his struggle with leaders from the people of Morocco who fought against the monotheism of God and following the Sunnah of the Messenger. The poem refers to the attempts of these people to weaken his advocacy activity and their plots against him, expressing his steadfastness in the face of the threats and challenges he faced in order to spread the Salafist doctrine. The poem also includes a reference to the attempts of the enemies of the Sunnah to extinguish the light of God, expressing hope for victory and divine support for the campaign of monotheism and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.731: The book “The Best I Have Heard” by Al-Thaalabi Abu Mansour covers selections of poetry and eloquent verses in various fields of literature and religion, dividing them into sections dealing with divinities, prophets, kings, brotherhood, literature, wine, seasons, places, food, women, flirtation, morals, illnesses, congratulations, and elegies. The author focuses on verses that carry meanings of praise to God, thanks for His blessings, and trust in Him, while presenting a scathing criticism of the time and its conditions.
descriptions.732: News of Fools and Fools is a book about the news and positions of fools and fools, written by the Hanbali scholar, jurist, hadith scholar, and historian Abu Al-Faraj Ibn Al-Jawzi (508 AH - 597 AH). The author divided his book into twenty-four chapters, in which he mentions poems, eloquence, and the natures, characteristics, and types of fools in people, with a mention of some of their witticisms. The author also mentions proverbs that were used about fools.
descriptions.733: News of the Circumstances and the Immoralists is a book about the situations of the adventurous and the imaginative people, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Jawzi (508 AH - 597 AH). The author combines in the book two types of news: the news of the adventurous and the immoral people, and the news of the immoral and immoral people. There is an overlap of some kind between the adverb and the immorality, due to the proximity of their topics. Immorality in language books is that a person does not care about what he has done, and as for the adverb, it is a pun on what is necessary. Shyness, intonation and eloquence of speech. Ibn al-Jawzi divided his book into three main sections, the first section: What is narrated on the authority of men, and he mentioned five sections in it: What is narrated on the authority of the prophets (peace be upon them), What is narrated on the authority of the Companions, What is narrated on the authority of the scholars, What is narrated on the authority of the Arabs, and What is narrated on the authority of the common people. …
descriptions.734: Akhbar al-Nisa’ is a book published for the first time in Egypt in the year 1319 AH, attributed to Ibn al-Qayyim. The correct view is that it was written by Ibn al-Jawzi. He summarized it and stripped its chains of transmission from Kitab al-Nisa’ by Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani, and Dr. did not point out that. Nizar Reda, in his publication of the book, attributed it to Ibn al-Qayyim, and the material of the book indicates that it is far from being written by Ibn al-Qayyim, whose scientific and literary personality is evident in all his writings. The book is based on nine chapters, without an introduction. It is about descriptions of women and their morals, and it contains the eighth chapter: (From the hadiths of the authors), which is an arbitrary title, and may have been one of the copyists’ additions. …
descriptions.735: This book deals with news and biographies of famous Andalusian figures, extracted from Al-Salafi’s Dictionary of Travel, and provides information about the author Ahmed bin Muhammad Al-Salafi and his academic and travel life. It focuses on his biography and his scientific travels between Islamic cities, while mentioning details about his birth, death, marriage, and seeking knowledge from the scholars of his time in Isfahan and Baghdad.
descriptions.736: The Ethics of the Two Ministers is a book in which Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi collected the faults of the two ministers, al-Sahib ibn Abbad and Abu al-Fadl ibn al-Amid, and in it he mentioned what happened to him in the presence of al-Sahib and what Abu Hayyan encountered due to his miserliness and his prevention of giving and prayers from him. Like most of Abu Hayyan’s books, it is dominated by a literary character, and the author filled the book with anecdotes, poetry, and news.
descriptions.737: The book “Adab Al-Khawas fi Al-Mukhtar Min Rhetoric of the Arab Tribes” by the Moroccan minister provides a close look at the literature and rhetoric of the Arabs, with a focus on the individual and subjective peculiarities of this literature. The book deals with multiple topics related to the history of the Arabic language and its development, and includes chapters on the derivation of the word “Arabs” and the development of the Arabic language, in addition to a study of the poets of the Arabic language. The author focuses on the importance of contemplation and a deep understanding of literature, and notes the necessity of freedom from tradition and intellectual stagnation. The book is characterized by deep self-criticism about the importance of self-control and wisdom in expression and action.
descriptions.738: The book “Adab Al-Kitab” or “Adab Al-Kitab” by Ibn Qutaybah Al-Dinawari deals with the topic of literature and rhetoric, showing the importance of literature and the increasing number of people regressing from it in his time. The author focuses on addressing multiple linguistic and literary issues, including the interpretation of words and definitions, the origins of people's names, plant types, and the defects and descriptions of horses. He also points out people's misunderstanding of literature and their disdain for it, considering that scholars have been submerged and the goods of people of literature have dried up. The book aims to clarify the value of literature and its sciences and to explain the skills and principles that a writer must have in writing and expression.
descriptions.739: The literature of the book: Some people say: “The literature of the writer.” It was written by Al-Suly at the time of Al-Radi Billah, as can be understood from what he wrote in the chapter “What People Write About Today.” He said in the introduction: “We have written this book according to what is needed by the highest-ranking writers and the lowest-ranking among them. He made it comprehensive of everything the writer needed, so that he could rely on no one but him for all of it.
descriptions.740: Secrets of rhetoric in the science of rhetoric. A book on rhetoric compiled by Imam Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani.
descriptions.741: The book “Names of Arab Horses and Their Riders” by Ibn al-Arabi Abu Abdullah deals with the topic of Arabian horses and their importance in Arab-Islamic culture. The book focuses on mentioning the names of the horses of the main Arab tribes and their stories, with reference to the horses of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and individual companions. The book also discusses the origin of Arabian horses and their development over time, mentioning some stories and hadiths related to horses in Islam.
descriptions.742: The book "The Gold Markets" consists of prose chapters that are diverse in their topics and purposes, dealing with social, philosophical, and religious issues, drawn from the writer's experiences and his judgment of events, relying in their formulation on the methods and rules of Arabic literature. The book deals with topics such as homeland, freedom, religion, and morals, reviewing the conditions of society and human conditions, expressing its philosophical and social visions in a sophisticated literary style.
descriptions.743: This book deals with the poems of the children of the caliphs and their news, following an approach similar to a previous book by the author on the poems of the caliphs themselves. The work deals with poems and events related to the sons of the caliphs, with a focus on poetry and stories related to them. The book begins with the poems of Muhammad bin Abi al-Abbas al-Saffah, and continues to review the poems and stories of the sons of other caliphs, while providing historical information and personal stories related to them.
descriptions.744: The book “Women’s Poems” by Al-Marzbani deals with a literary presentation of poems and poems written by women from various Arab tribes, with a focus on stories of poetic courtship between them and high-ranking poets such as Al-Nabigha Al-Jaadi. The book also covers stories and poems by women from Bani Rabi’a, Bakr, Tamim and other tribes, providing a comprehensive picture of women’s contributions to ancient Arabic poetry.
descriptions.745: This book is a collection of articles, sermons, and sermons on ethical and behavioral topics, in which Al-Zamakhshari addresses issues such as humility, honor, asceticism, and good morals. The author focuses on guidance and religious sermons to enhance good qualities and avoid vices, using rhetorical and literary methods to present his ideas. The book aims to guide the reader towards a high moral life and sound Islamic behavior.
descriptions.746: The book of Arab proverbs by its favorite author, Al-Dhabi, whose full name is Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mufaddal bin Muhammad bin Ya’la bin Amer Al-Dhabi, 168 AH. It is worth noting that most of the proverbs stories mentioned by Al-Mufaddal Al-Dhabi, although not in all their details, were transferred to the works of ancient linguists, from the Kufans and the Basrans. To these were added the stories narrated by Ibn al-Kalbi.
descriptions.747: This book by Ibn al-Kalbi deals with the lineage of horse stallions in pre-Islamic times and Islam, and mentions hadiths and narrations related to the importance of horses in ancient Arab society. The author shows how the Arabs used to tether horses, honor them, and take pride in them. Then he mentions the orders of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to take horses and tether them, and his preference for the two arrows over their owners. It also cites prophetic hadiths that emphasize the importance of horses in Islam and the virtue of tying them for the sake of God.
descriptions.748: The book “The Most Guided Path to My Knowledge of Hebron” by the scholar Mahmoud Mustafa provides a detailed study of the knowledge of Hebron, which is one of the branches of Arabic linguistics. The book deals with the letters of taqtāqī, zāfāf, and illāl, while providing practical exercises to apply these concepts. The book is distinguished by its analytical and detailed style of explaining these linguistic sciences, which makes it a valuable reference for students and professors of the Arabic language and literary studies.
descriptions.749: The book “Rebuke the Book” by Ibn al-Abar deals with a literary and rhetorical study of a group of famous writers in Islamic history, showing their virtues and importance in serving princes and caliphs. The book focuses on describing the skills of these writers in eloquence and public speaking, and how they influenced the formulation of decisions and documentation of events, noting their prestigious status and appreciation by the rulers. The book also mentions examples of poetry and novels that reflect the position of writers and their role in the political and cultural community.
descriptions.750: The book “Trends of Contemporary Arabic Poetry” by Dr. Ihsan Abbas deals with a simplified study of the overall artistic and intellectual developments in modern Arabic poetry, trying to avoid political or nationalist analyzes that might diminish the psychological and intellectual depth of poetry. The author focuses on exploring general trends in contemporary poetry through his analysis of artistic and intellectual phenomena, relying on poetic models of high artistic value to support his ideas and viewpoints.
descriptions.751: This book deals with studies of pre-Islamic literature from a critical perspective, as author Afif Abdel Rahman presents all the research and studies that dealt with pre-Islamic literature throughout the ages, starting from the efforts of the ancients and ending with modern studies of Arab and Orientalist authors. The book focuses on the methods of literary studies and their applications to pre-Islamic poetry, relying on thematic divisions covering various aspects of pre-Islamic literature and research related to it.
descriptions.752: The book provides a comprehensive study of contemporary Arabic literature in Egypt, examining the development of poetry and prose during a specific period. The author focuses on presenting the effects of historical events and different cultures on literature, with an emphasis on the development of poetry and analyzing the effects of a number of prominent poets. The book also deals with the development of prose arts and discusses prominent figures in this field, noting their role in the development of modern Egyptian literature.
descriptions.753: The book “Literature and its Arts - Study and Criticism” by literary thinker Ezz al-Din Ismail deals with theoretical topics in literature and literary criticism, and discusses the main literary arts such as poetry and stories. The book focuses on defining literature and the nature of criticism, and discusses the elements of different literary genres and their characteristics, while providing practical applications to literary arts such as biography, memoirs, and essays. The book aims to present the basic elements of literary thought in an understandable way for those who need to understand them, while maintaining intellectual unity between its various chapters.
descriptions.754: The book “Times and Places” by Al-Marzouqi is a book in the field of literature and rhetoric that deals with the topics of time and place from a linguistic and grammatical perspective, reviewing Qur’anic verses and sayings of grammarians, and dealing with the names of time and place and their relationship to astronomical phenomena. The book focuses on the interconnectedness of time and space, explains their terms, and discusses the sayings of scholars in this regard, relying on Qur’anic, hadith, and scientific texts.
descriptions.755: The book “Style” by Ahmed Al-Shayeb deals with an integrated scientific study of the science of Arabic rhetoric, trying to introduce it into a new curriculum that keeps pace with modern literary developments. The book focuses on analyzing literary style through studying letters, words, sentences, and images, relying on the sciences of sound, psychology, and music. The book also deals with the sciences of meanings, rhetoric, and badi’ within the section on style, considering them as chapters within it rather than independent sciences, with the aim of developing a deeper understanding of Arabic rhetoric and making it more suitable for expressing modern literary arts.
descriptions.756: This book deals with Al-Asma'i, which are sayings, proverbs, and poetic verses collected and chronicled by Al-Asma'i. It contains texts attributed to various personalities, such as Suhaim bin Watheel and Khafaf bin Nadba, and reviews topics related to poetry, wisdom, and popular proverbs. The book focuses on aspects of ancient Arab culture and documents the popular and linguistic heritage of the Arabs at that time.
descriptions.757: This book, “Al-Amali” by the writer Abu Ali Al-Qali, deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric, focusing on interpreting strange hadiths and poetic verses, explaining the meanings of rare words and obscure vocabulary, while providing information in areas such as names, tongues, and colors. The book is distinguished by its collection of various scientific and literary contents, and aims to spread useful knowledge to those who deserve it and appreciate its value.
descriptions.758: The book “Al-Amali” by Al-Azizi Al-Yazidi presents various literary and scholarly selections, including elegies, poems, stories, and news, in addition to linguistic studies. The book deals with various literary topics through poetic texts and historical novels, with a focus on ancient Arabic literature and its arts. The book is distinguished by its collection of a group of poems and stories that reflect the splendor of ancient Arabic literature and the depth of its linguistic and cultural heritage.
descriptions.759: A book on literature and rhetoric, in which its author collected a group of proverbs formulated by the Messengers and Islamists, and divided them into sections that include sermons and wisdom, praise and condemnation, humor and immorality, and simile and metaphor. The book includes proverbs in verse and prose, and specializes in a comprehensive chapter on the people of Baghdad for their proverbs, with attention paid to what is mentioned in the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.760: This book deals with the topic of proverbs in Islam through the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet, showing their importance in conveying meanings and wisdom to people. The author focuses on the fact that God Almighty set parables to help people understand what may be mysterious or far away from them, and that they are a mirror that reflects the truth of the human soul and its condition. The book deals with proverbs as a tool for wisdom and understanding, explaining how they help guide souls and clarify cloudy truths.
descriptions.761: The book “The Firsts” by Abu Hilal Al-Askari deals with an account of those who established or carried out the first works in various fields between the Quraysh and the common people of pre-Islamic times. The book focuses on highlighting the first events and practices in pre-Islamic Arab societies, providing a rich cultural and historical view of the customs and traditions that prevailed in that era. The book combines literature and history, and provides valuable scientific material for those who wish to study the origin and beginnings of ancient Arab culture.
descriptions.762: Al-Souli’s book “The Papers, Department of Poets’ News” provides a close look at the history of Arabic literature in the Abbasid era, mixing poetry and political events. The book deals with the biographies of Abbasid poets contemporary with the caliphs, with a focus on the relationships between poets and rulers and their political events. The book constitutes an important document of Arab literature and history, as it combines poetic material with historical stories of prominent Arab figures in the Abbasid era.
descriptions.763: The book “Camels” written by Al-Asma’i is one of the books of literature and rhetoric that dealt with the subject of camels from its various aspects. Its content dealt with sayings, proverbs, and names related to camels, as well as their medicines, behavior, colors, and sounds, in addition to his mention of breeding seasons and methods of fertilization, thus providing a comprehensive view of the world of camels in ancient Arab culture.
descriptions.764: The Miracle and the Brief is one of the most important works of Abu Mansur Al-Thaalabi. This work, like all of Al-Tha'alabi's works, is written in Arabic. It includes a collection of Arabic proverbs. Al-Tha'alibi says in the introduction to this book: Perhaps this work is one of the most creative works that have been written in the book, as it is characterized by the beauty and elegance of the prose. It is unique in its language that overflows with magic, and caresses the mind with kindness and deep artistic taste. Every word in it is vibrant, and every sentence arouses in the soul a feeling of rhythmic harmony, so that verbal beauty blends with the brilliance of meaning, so that the reader almost dissolves in the secret of this prose that quenches the conscience and stimulates the imagination. …
descriptions.765: Poetic slave girls.
