A book by Abu Al-Faraj Al-Isbahani shows the prowess of women poets as they stand with the poets of the Abbasid era and attests to their exceptional poeticism, presenting rare pictures of magic councils in Baghdad: during its golden age. The book includes anecdotes from thirty-three Abbasid poets.
descriptions.766: Enjoyment and Sociability is a book that narrates what happened during the thirty-seven nights that Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi spent in courting with Vizier Abu Abdullah al-Arid, the vizier of Samsam al-Dawla al-Buwayhi. Al-Tawhidi collected it and gave it to the engineer Abu Al-Wafa Al-Buzjani, who connected him with Minister Abu Abdullah. It is three parts. The book includes discussions on issues such as the mind and soul, language, and science, in addition to criticism of some aspects of society and scholars of his time.
descriptions.767: Clarification in the sciences of rhetoric. It is a book on the science of rhetoric compiled by the preacher Al-Qazwini, and it is an explanation of his book “Summary of the Key,” which is an abbreviation of the book “Miftah al-Ulum” by al-Sakaki.
descriptions.768: The book "The Two Choices" is one of the literary and rhetorical works that dealt with the poetry of classical Arabs in the pre-Islamic and Islamic eras. The book collects the selections of Al-Mufaddal Al-Dhabi and Al-Asmai from classical Arabic poetry, deriving these poems from the narrations of trusted sheikhs of the language. The book includes poems and verses by prominent poets, with explanations of some of the words and phrases used, making it a useful reference for scholars and those interested in classical Arabic poetry and the Arabic language.
descriptions.769: This book deals with the topic of literary research and discusses its pillars, foundations, and nature, while addressing the differences between types of academic writings such as letters, articles, and investigations. The author focuses on the importance of research in the development and growth of human thought, and provides practical guidance for choosing a research topic, collecting its material, and formulating it. The book targets science students and researchers in various sciences and literature, with a focus on the close connection between literary research and other linguistic and literary sciences.
descriptions.770: The Book of Misers is a book in which Abu Othman Amr bin Bahr Al-Jahiz recorded some images of miserliness among those he met and got to know in his own environment, especially in the town of Marv, the capital of Khorasan. Al-Jahiz depicted misers in a realistic, sensual, psychological, and humorous way. He documented their movements, their anxious or reassuring looks, and their psychological whims. He exposed their secrets and the secrets of their homes and informed the readers of their various conversations, revealing all of their psyches and conditions. The first person to study the text of misers was the orientalist Van Vleuten in 1900 AD. …
descriptions.771: This book presents a study of Al-Badi’ according to Al-Hariri, reviewing his literary works, with a focus on the famous Book of Maqamat. The book deals with the definition of Maqamat and its literary nature, showing how Hariri became famous for his innovation of these literary arts that were mixed with wisdom and eloquence. The book focuses on the rhetorical and aesthetic dimension of Hariri’s Maqamat, highlighting his skills in using badi’, proverbs, and metaphor, which made them widely known in Arabic literature.
descriptions.772: The book “Al-Badi’ fi Al-Badi’” by Ibn Al-Mu’tazz deals with an in-depth scientific study of the styles of rhetoric and badi’ in Arabic poetry and literature, examining its origins, history, and development throughout the ages. The author focuses on explaining and analyzing different types of badi' such as metaphor, simile, and metonymy, relying on his own standards in understanding these rhetorical tools. The book aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the Arabic statement and its development, with a focus on Ibn al-Mu'tazz's personal contributions in this field.
descriptions.773: This book, “The Wonderful Criticism of Poetry” by Ahmed bin Munqidh, deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric, focusing on the types of naturalization and its various sections. The author explains the types of naturalization such as heterogeneous, similar, and misrepresentation, and explains the differences between them through examples from the Holy Quran and Arabic literature. The book aims to analyze and criticize poetry by studying its rhetorical techniques and artistic divisions, relying on terms and examples from religious and literary sources.
descriptions.774: Al-Barasan, the Lame, the Blind, and the Cross-eyed is a book written by Al-Jahiz in which he talks about people with disabilities, such as the lepers, the lame, the blind, and the cross-eyed, among the notables, nobles, celebrities, and poets in Arab society at that time. The book is one of the rare books of Al-Jahiz, in which he spoke exclusively about the nobles and famous people with disabilities, and it is a response to Al-Haytham bin Adi because he wrote a book about the faults of the nobles with disabilities.
descriptions.775: This book, “Insights and Ammunition” by Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi, is a work in the field of literature and rhetoric, in which the author deals with conveying what was mentioned in the Diwan al-Sama’ and drawing what was covered in the novel since the year three hundred and fifty, with a focus on the most prominent things that are wonderful and sublime in the field of literature, rhetoric, and eloquence. The book covers various topics, including prose and poetry, oppositions and answers, sermons and arguments, articles and literature, trying to present what is selected from ancient Arabic literature.
descriptions.776: The book “Mules” by Al-Jahiz is one of the literary books that deals with the subject of mules from a diverse scientific and literary perspective, as it combines scientific information, stories, and proverbs, reviewing their nature, benefits, and anecdotes. The book is part of the Animal Book series, and Al-Jahiz intended to include it in order to enhance its content, but his personal circumstances prevented him from achieving this goal. The book deals with various topics related to mules, including character, riding, praise and blame, which reflects Al-Jahiz’s encyclopedic culture and the diversity of his intellectual walks.
descriptions.777: The book “Arabic Rhetoric” by Muhammad Abd al-Rahman Habankah al-Maidani deals with the topics of rhetoric and literature by discussing the purpose of studying the sciences of rhetoric, analyzing the goals of speech, and explaining the foundations of high rhetoric and high literature in three independent chapters. The book focuses on the technical aspects of rhetoric, such as eloquence and beauty in speech, and studies semantics by dividing the Arabic sentence and analyzing its elements, while exploring rhetorical phenomena such as shortening and the system of harmony in speech.
descriptions.778: Al-Bayan wal-Tabyen or Al-Bayan wal-Tabyen is one of Al-Jahiz’s greatest works. It follows the book Al-Hay’awal in terms of size and is superior to all of his other books. If the book “Animal” deals with a scientific topic, then the book “Al-Bayan wal-Tabyin” focuses on treating a literary topic. But Al-Jahiz in these two books, like in all his books, takes a philosophical approach. In the Book of Animals, he does not limit himself to news about animals, their characteristics, and their nature, but rather touches on philosophical topics such as latency and generation, essences and symptoms, the indivisible part, magicianism, eternity, etc. In the book Al-Bayan wa Al-Tabin, he does not content himself with presenting literary selections, including sermons, letters, hadiths, and poems, but rather attempts to lay the foundations of the science of rhetoric and the philosophy of language. …
descriptions.779: This book, “Al-Bizra,” written by Baziar Al-Aziz Al-Fatimi, deals with topics related to hunting and goshawks, covering the arts of caring for and training goshawks, and treating the diseases that afflict them. It also mentions the types of birds of prey and their characteristics, and reviews the virtues of hunting and its psychological and physical advantages. The book falls within the scope of literature and rhetoric, focusing on the practical and scientific aspect in the field of hunting and hunting.
descriptions.780: The Crown in the Ethics of Kings is a book on literature and rhetoric by Al-Jahiz that talks about entering upon kings, feeding them, and admonishing them, and about the qualities of remorse and the good manners that kings must have among the subjects, in both situations of humor and seriousness. During this, Al-Jahiz does not fail to mention types of hadiths and colors of anecdotes, which he derives from Arab history at times, and from Persian history at times, speaking about the morals of kings and peoples, regardless of their lands. After each talk, he tries to lay out the general outlines, indirectly, of high social literature.
descriptions.781: This book, “Literary Editing,” by Hussein Ali Muhammad, deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric through theoretical studies and applied models. It focuses on modern editing arts and encourages proper writing, while providing practical linguistic rules that help the student remember and apply them in their writing and creative practices. The book combines theory and practice to facilitate university students’ understanding of literary editing and developing their skills in it.
descriptions.782: The book “The Hamdunian Remembrance” by Abu Al-Ma’ali Muhammad bin Hamdun is a book in the field of literature and rhetoric, dealing with various topics related to religious and worldly sermons and etiquette, the biography of the righteous predecessors, the etiquette of government and politics, honor and leadership. The book focuses on conveying the sayings and news of the wise, scholars, and companions, while providing advice and sermons in various aspects of life, trying to establish lofty moral and political values.
descriptions.783: This book by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi deals with the topic of parasites and the stories of parasites and their news. It introduces the concept of parasites and discusses its ruling and the opinions of scholars about it. It also mentions the news of parasites, their poems and anecdotes in various fields. The book combines seriousness and humor in a literary context that aims to please the heart and soothe the mind, noting that the practice of parasitism has been a subject of controversy between those who condemn it and forbid it and those who praise it and protest to its people.
descriptions.784: This book deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric through a collection of condolences, elegies, sermons, and testaments. It contains sayings and hadiths from various sources about death and sermons, relying on quotes from poets and scholars. The book includes the wills of important historical figures such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Omar ibn al-Khattab, in addition to other sayings about death and patience. The book aims to provide advice and consolation to readers through these sayings and hadiths.
descriptions.785: This book, “Acting and Lecture,” by Al-Thaalabi Abu Mansour, is a work of literature and rhetoric. It deals with the art of acting and lecturing in various fields, reviewing examples from the heavenly books, the Holy Qur’an, the sayings of the prophets, wisdom, and Arabic and Persian proverbs. It focuses on how to use representation to communicate meanings and ideas in artistic and aesthetic ways, relying on multiple and diverse sources to explore this literary art.
descriptions.786: This book is “Al-Tanbih Ala Abu Ali’s Delusions in his Amaliyah” by its author, Abu Ubaid al-Bakri, and it is a work of literature and rhetoric that deals with correcting some of the errors and illusions that appeared in Abu Ali’s writings. The book aims to alert the reader to these errors in a fair manner, citing appropriate evidence and evidence. In this book, Al-Bakri deals with poems sung by personalities such as Buriya bin Al-Numan, and reviews Abu Ali’s interpretations of them, stating his point of view on them.
descriptions.787: This book, “The Righteous and Sufficient Savior and the Anis, the Healer and Adviser,” by the worshiper, the jurist, and the healer, Ibn Zakaria, deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric, reviewing wisdom and sayings by scholars and Bedouins, relying on hadith and poetic verses to explore their linguistic and grammatical meanings. Through it, the author aims to provide a spiritual companion who comforts and guides the reader, including news anecdotes and stories of ascetics, with scientific comments on their content.
descriptions.788: This book deals with the famous names of horses in pre-Islamic times, and reviews Arab news, poetry, and feats related to horses. The author focuses on the importance of horses in the lives of Arabs and their role in jihad and military power, showing the Arabs’ interest in the value of horses and their pride in them. The book combines literature and rhetoric, reviewing the names of famous horses according to the letters of the dictionary, while pointing out the historical and cultural importance of these names in the context of pre-Islamic Arab civilization.
descriptions.789: This book, “Visual Enthusiasm,” by Sadr al-Din al-Basri, deals with multiple fields of Arabic literature and poetry, focusing on different types of poetry such as enthusiasm, praise, lamentation, literature, poetry, and satire. The author divides the book into multiple sections to present these types of poetry, relying on selections from ancient and modern poets, and aims to present literary content rich in creativity and punctuation, while avoiding prolongation and excessive detail.
descriptions.790: This book, “Moroccan Enthusiasm, Summary of the Book of the Elite of Adab,” written by Al-Jarrawi, deals with the praise of the Prophet Muhammad and other companions, relying on Arabic poetry to describe heroism, pride, and asceticism. The book also includes various topics from elegies, descriptions, proverbs, and aphorisms, providing a comprehensive picture of Arabic literature and rhetoric.
descriptions.791: This book, “Al-Hoor Al-Ain” by Al-Humayri Nashwan, deals with the subject of literature and rhetoric through his interpretation of the meters and rhymes of poetry. The author focuses on explaining the different types of poetry and its rulings, expressing his concern about the deterioration of the value of literature in his time and the decline of people’s morals. The book aims to educate young people and increase the knowledge of writers, while providing a brief explanation of his message of the same name.
descriptions.792: Book of Animals is the first comprehensive book written in Arabic on zoology. In it, his writer Al-Jahiz spoke about the Arabs, their conditions, customs, claims, and sciences, and some issues of jurisprudence and religion, the selected elite of Arab poetry, proverbs, rhetoric, and the criticism of speech. All those who wrote before Al-Jahiz in this field, such as Al-Asma’i, Abu Ubaidah, Ibn Al-Kalbi, Ibn Al-Arabi, and Al-Sijistani, dealt with one animal, and their interest was linguistic and not scientific, but Al-Jahiz was interested, in addition to language and poetry, in researching the nature of animals, their instincts, conditions, and habits. …
descriptions.793: The Book of Letters is a collection of rare letters by Al-Jahiz, and each of these letters discusses one topic, with an in-depth and extensive study that arouses admiration and appreciation. Al-Jahiz wrote many treatises on literature, religion, and politics, which were completed by a group of Arab and Orientalist researchers, but the largest and most accurate series was written by Dr. Abdel Salam Haroun.
descriptions.794: The book “Political Letters” by Al-Jahiz consists of ten letters that dealt with various political and literary topics. Al-Jahiz was interested in explaining the concept of politics and its principles, and discussed issues such as patriotism and party conflict. The messages focus on how to manage people's affairs and achieve public interests, relying on the principles of enticement and intimidation in state administration. The letters also dealt with other topics, such as the virtues and morals of rulers, and the etiquette of government, and the writings are distinguished by their rhetorical style and deep political ideas.
descriptions.795: This book covers a collection of various proverbs and proverbs, classified according to the letters of the alphabet. Author Ahmed Al Hashemi focuses on collecting wise and honorable sayings that are characterized by eloquence and eloquence, presenting them in an organized and organized form. The book aims to provide educational and social advice and wisdom through proverbs and aphorisms, thus providing a rich cultural and literary reference.
descriptions.796: This book deals with the study of Arabic poetry in Khorasan from the era of the Islamic conquest until the end of the Umayyad era.
descriptions.797: This book deals with the topic of poetry from the perspective of Islamic law. The author, Muhammad Abd al-Rahman Shumaila al-Ahdal, examines the status and importance of Arabic poetry, and studies Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths related to poetry. It focuses on understanding the miracle of the Qur’an and its explanation, while providing an overview of Muslim poets and their role in spreading the Islamic call. The book also addresses some of the legal rulings related to poetry, such as the dislike of poetry for those who master it. The book aims to present a comprehensive, legal vision of poetry and its impact on Muslim society.
descriptions.798: Poetry and poets are among the oldest books compiled in biographies of poets. It was written by Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Muslim bin Qutaybah Al-Dinouri (d. 276 AH, 889 AD), one of the imams of the third century AH. He was from the Al-Jahiz class among the Mu'tazilites, a skilled imam with many aspects of his writings. The Book of Poetry and Poets is one of the most important books translated by poets. It is considered an authentic source and an important reference in its field. It is very similar to the book Tabaqat Fahl al-Shu'ara' by Ibn Salam al-Jumahi. In this book, Ibn Qutaybah was not only keen to interview the poets, list them, and investigate their biographies, but he also limited himself to the famous ones. …
descriptions.799: The book “The Vampire Poets of the Pre-Islamic Era” by Youssef Khalif deals with an in-depth study of the vagabond poets of the pre-Islamic era from linguistic, geographical, social and economic perspectives. The author focuses on interpreting the phenomenon of tramps and analyzing their poetry, reviewing the sources and artistic manifestations of their poetry and their social and economic influences on pre-Islamic society. Khalif emphasizes the idea of ​​“tramp socialism,” which he believes reflects a social and economic revolution in that era, despite reservations about describing it as contemporary socialism.
descriptions.800: This book, “Feeling One-eyed” by Al-Safadi, deals with the topic of one-eyedness from different perspectives, including linguistic, rhetorical, and jurisprudential, and reviews hadiths, proverbs, and poems related to one-eyed people. The author aims to explain the strange hadiths, explain their meanings, and interpret the ambiguous ones, and also mentions those who were one-eyed throughout history. The book combines depth of research and comprehensiveness in topics related to its subject, and targets the reader interested in literature, jurisprudence, and the Arabic language.
descriptions.801: This book is written by Abu Mansour Al-Thaalabi in the field of literature and rhetoric. It deals with the topics of complaint, reproach, defamation, broadcasting, and sympathy. It contains stories and hadiths related to complaints, reproaches, and what happened to friends and companions, based on texts and examples from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the Companions. The book is divided into several sections that address various topics related to complaints and reproach, while presenting poetic and literary texts that reinforce the main idea of ​​each section.
descriptions.802: This book, “Al-Subh Al-Mutanabbi Anan Al-Mutanabbi, by the writer Youssef Al-Bada’i, deals with a literary study of the poems and news of Al-Mutanabbi, one of the most famous Arab poets. The author focuses on Al-Mutanabbi's virtues and poetic methods, showing his high status in the world of literature and poetry. The book combines an introduction that explains the author’s vision of poetry and the poet, a summary of Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry and its analysis, while providing historical information about his life and circumstances.
descriptions.803: The book “Friendship and the Friend” by Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi is one of the literary works that dealt with the subject of friendship and human relations, reviewing their various aspects and forms, and deducing from them rules and principles that establish a true friendship relationship based on chivalry, loyalty, and cooperation. The book also deals with the concept of familiarity and brotherhood and the moral and behavioral principles related to it, citing the sayings of wise men, thinkers, and people of religion and chivalry.
descriptions.804: The book “The Two Crafts” by Abu Hilal Al-Askari deals with the arts of writing and poetry, reviews the concepts of rhetoric and eloquence, and discusses the differences between them. The author relies on the works of his predecessors in this field to provide a comprehensive and integrated overview of the industry of rhetoric and literature, trying to present the essence of what has been written on this subject before. The book covers various topics related to statement, redundancy, and brevity, and provides in-depth literary criticism of the art of writing and poetry.
descriptions.805: The book “The Literary Image, History and Criticism” by Muhammad Ali Subh deals with the topic of the literary image from a linguistic, grammatical, and critical perspective, examining its development through the ages, from ancient to modern criticism. The book focuses on defining the concept of literary image and analyzing its nature and function in literature, relying on the study of words and phrases that symbolize meanings and embody ideas. The book also discusses the types of literary images in various genres of literature, and their role in shaping meaning and achieving artistic effect.
descriptions.806: The book presents an analytical artistic study of the most important purposes of poetry according to the poet, critic, and writer Abu Bakr Al-Souli, examining aspects of his poetic art and his literary visions. Author Ahmed Jamal Al-Omari focuses on praise as one of the most important topics addressed by Al-Souli in his poetry, while pointing out other areas of the purposes of his poetry. The book shows how Al-Souli’s poetry was colored by the spirit of the era in which he lived, reviewing the impact of personal experiences and social relationships on his poetic creativity.
descriptions.807: The book “Al-Taraz for the Secrets of Rhetoric and the Sciences of Miraculous Facts” is one of the rhetorical works that dealt with the sciences of literature and rhetoric in a literary analytical manner, trying to depart from the dry logical method followed by Al-Sakaki and his followers. The author, Yahya bin Hamzah Al-Alawi Al-Yamini, deals with the sciences of rhetoric, relying on the Holy Qur’an and its evidence, and reviews the arts of Al-Badi’ and rhetoric while presenting various literary analyses, trying to imitate Ibn Al-Atheer’s method in the literary approach to rhetoric. Despite Al-Alawi's serious attempts to depart from the Sakaki tradition, he could not completely break free from the divisions and branches of the Sakaki school in the structure of his book.
descriptions.808: Lessons is a book written by the Egyptian author and writer Mustafa Lutfi Al-Manfaluti, published in 1915 AD. The book’s stories revolve around many topics that preoccupied society at that time, and it combines two forms of short stories: The first form consists of four short stories that Al-Manfaluti wrote in response to his desire to work in narratives, and they are, respectively: The Orphan, The Veil, The Abyss, and The Punishment. It is noteworthy that the last story is in an intermediate position between setting and wording, meaning that he adapted it from an American story entitled “The Screaming of the Graves.” As for the second form of the stories in this book, it consists of four, which are, respectively: Martyrs, Memory, Punishment, Victim, and in a recent edition of the book, revenge was included. …
descriptions.809: Al-Iqd Al-Farid is a book written by Ibn Abd Rabbuh Al-Andalusi (d. 328 AH), considered one of the forefathers of Arabic literature. The book includes a number of news, proverbs, proverbs, sermons, poems, and more. It was called “The Contract” because Ibn Abd Rabbo divided it into chapters or books, each of which bore the name of a precious stone, such as the peridot, the coral, the ruby, the gem, the pearl, and other things that dealt with the true contracts of Al-Hassan.
descriptions.810: This book, “Al-Umdah fi Al-Mahasin Al-Sha’ar wa Al-Adabah” by Ibn Rashiq Al-Qayrawani, deals with the subject of Arabic poetry, its virtues, and its etiquette. The author focuses on discussing the virtues of poetry and comparing it to prose. He also discusses the impact of poetry in Arab societies and its role in preserving heritage and values. The book also deals with technical aspects of poetry, such as poetry structure, rhymes, and meters, in addition to the poet’s etiquette and methods of writing poetry.
descriptions.811: The book Al-Fakher by Abu Talib Al-Mufaddal bin Salamah deals with the interpretation of the meanings of expressions and words that are common among the common people in their speech and proverbs, showing their different aspects according to the differences of scholars in their interpretation. The book aims to introduce the reader to the pronunciations and expressions that people say, and to reveal their mysterious meanings to the average reader.
descriptions.812: The book “Al-Fadil” written by Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad is a literary book that deals with various fields of literature and rhetoric. It deals with the virtues of poetry and poets, discusses news and poems of the Arabs, and reviews anecdotes from a foreign language. It also deals with other topics such as generosity and generosity, blame for sin, forbearance, gratitude, and personal virtues such as secrecy and envy, with a focus on eloquence and beauty. The book combines hadiths, anecdotes, and poetic verses, and aims to promote virtues, appreciate knowledge, and work with it.
descriptions.813: Relief after Distress is a book written by Judge Al-Tanukhi, in which he included a lot of news and stories and divided it into 14 chapters. Al-Tanukhi’s book is not the only book that bears this name, as its author indicated in the introduction, where he mentioned that the first person to name a book with this title was Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madaini, then Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, then Al-Qadi Abu Hussein. He said: “I found that Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and the judge Abu Al-Hussein did not mention that Al-Madaini had a book with this meaning. If they did not know this, then it is funny, and if they deliberately left out mentioning it out of misuse of their books and covering up the man’s book, then it is funnier...”
descriptions.814: The book “The Astronomy Revolving on the Walking Proverb” by Ibn Abi Al-Hadid presents a literary and scientific criticism of the book “The Walking Proverb” by examining its topics and analyzing its methods, thus presenting an opposing point of view that complements the scientific interest of the original work. The book falls within the framework of literature and rhetoric, and the author displays his multiple literary and scientific skills, relying on his broad scientific and cultural background.
descriptions.815: This book deals with a detailed study of the doctrines of Arabic poetry throughout the ages, focusing on three main doctrines: craftsmanship, fabrication, and artificiality. The author studies the development of Arabic poetry from the pre-Islamic era until the Abbasid era, reviewing the various influences that influenced its poetic doctrines, including political, cultural, and linguistic changes. It also focuses on the importance of craftsmanship in Arabic poetry and its development over time, noting the influences of singing and music on lyrical poetry.
descriptions.816: This book deals with a detailed study of the doctrines of Arabic prose throughout the ages, focusing on the doctrine of craftsmanship and the doctrine of manufacturing. The author, Shawqi Dhaif, begins with an analysis of the craftsmanship of pre-Islamic prose and Islamic rhetoric, then moves to the Abbasid era and their influence on the development of Arabic prose. The book focuses on the development of linguistic and artistic styles in prose, from the soothsayers’ rhyme to the speeches of the Umayyad era, passing through the unique style of Ibn al-Muqaffa. The book aims to understand how Arabic prose developed and was influenced by religious and cultural influences, while preserving the magnificence and elegance of the Arabic language.
descriptions.817: Al-Kamil fi al-Lughah wa al-Adab is a book on the art of literature written by al-Mubarrad. The book is divided into four parts and has been printed many times. It was explained by Sayyed Al-Marsafi in eight large parts entitled “The Desire of Hope to Explanate Al-Kamil.”
descriptions.818: Al-Kashkul is a book on literature and rhetoric written by Al-Baha Al-Amili. It deals with various topics, including interpretation, news, wisdom, proverbs, linguistic conventions, and grammatical rules, drawing on a rich Arab, Islamic, and philosophical heritage. The book is distinguished by the diversity of its content and its richness with wisdom, poetic verses, and sermons, trying to present integrated cultural and scientific material in a diverse literary form.
descriptions.819: Al-Latif wa Al-Zaraif is a book written by Al-Tha’alabi for Abu Al-Abbas Ma’mun bin Ma’mun Khwarazm Shah in Al-Jurjaniya, where he resided from the year 403 AH until the year 407 AH.
descriptions.820: The prevailing example in the literature of the writer and poet is a book on literature and rhetoric by Abu al-Fath Diya al-Din ibn al-Atheer, who died in the year 637 AH. He is one of the most famous books in the two industries (literature and poetry). Haji Khalifa said: “Al-Jazari collected and comprehended it, and left nothing related to the art of writing without mentioning it.”
descriptions.821: Al-Majmu’ Al-Lafif by Ibn Hibatullah is a comprehensive literary composition that deals with the benefits and anecdotes of poetry and prose in various literary, religious, scientific and historical fields. The book combines sermons, letters, sermons, hadiths, stories, and anecdotes, and is distinguished by the diversity of its content, which includes religious sciences, language, literature, genealogy, travel, and natural and social sciences. Taking its material from traditional books, it includes poetry rich in selections from well-known and unknown poets, making it a rich and useful cultural and literary reference.
descriptions.822: Advantages and Opposites is a literary book compiled by the writer Abu Othman Al-Jahiz and formulated in a sober style in which he talks about the advantages and disadvantages of things, in their various forms, including habits, actions, characteristics, facts, and matters that are opposites of good and bad. He opened it by complaining about his envious writers and scholars who enumerated the shortcomings of his books. If he attributed them to other early writers, such as Ibn al-Muqaffa and al-Khalil, they praised them and studied them in admiration for what was in them, so he says:
descriptions.823: The book “Lectures and Dialogues” by Al-Suyuti is a comprehensive literary encyclopedia, which includes sayings and quotations from precious heritage books, investigating the art of literature and rhetoric, and delving extensively into various fields of Islamic sciences and knowledge, including literary, religious, and historical news, in addition to poetry, prophetic hadiths, and the etiquette of science and ethics.
descriptions.824: In his book “The Selected Poetry of the Andalusian Poets,” Ali bin Munjib presents examples of Andalusian poetry, demonstrating its virtue and splendor, and reviewing the works of prominent poets from this literary school. The book deals with poetry as part of the study of rhetoric, and aims to show that literary virtues are not limited to a specific place or time, but rather can be found in different eras and places. Through the examples of poetry he chooses, he mentions how Andalusian poetry in the era of Al-Mu'tamid and other eras was not devoid of creativity and beauty.
descriptions.825: This book, “Introduction to the Art of Journalistic Editing,” by Abdul Latif Mahmoud Hamza, deals with topics related to the art of journalistic editing and its role in shaping public opinion. It includes a definition of news, its importance, and how to formulate it, as well as a discussion of issues of press censorship and journalistic taste. The book focuses on establishing the art of journalistic editing and presenting its basic principles, relying on the heritage of modern and ancient Arabic literature.
descriptions.826: The book “Literary Schools of Modern Poetry of the South of the Kingdom” by Muhammad Ali Subh deals with a detailed study of the schools of modern poetry in the southern region of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The book focuses on analyzing the main poetic doctrines such as the conservative school, the conservative renewal school, and the liberal school of renewal, while reviewing their artistic characteristics and their most prominent poets. This research comes in the context of efforts to understand originality and tradition in modern Saudi poetry, and constitutes a valuable contribution to the field of studies of modern Arabic literature, especially in the field of Saudi poetry.
descriptions.827: The book “The Extremist in Every Fann is Extremist” is considered one of the important literary works that dealt with collecting anecdotes, proverbs, and wisdom in various sections of literature and science. It included a diverse content of news, sayings, and proverbs, distributed into chapters and sections that dealt with multiple topics from belief and worship to reason, science, and literature, relying on multiple sources from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, Arabic proverbs, and poetry. The book is distinguished by its unique flavor and new materials that are not mentioned in other works of its kind.
descriptions.828: Al-Muqtasas fi Proverbs of the Arabs is one of the most famous proverbs books, but it does not reach the level of the book of his field contemporary (The Collection of Proverbs). It is well-known that when Al-Zamakhshari contemplated Al-Maidani’s book, he regretted that he had written a comprehensive book of proverbs. He thought that he had collected in it something that had not been prepared for anything else, and he boasted by calling it “Al-Mustaqasa.” Then it became clear to him that it was less useful and easier to collect than Al-Maidani’s book. Al-Zamakhshari began writing Al-Mustaqsa after his return from Mecca and completed it in the year 499 AH.
descriptions.829: The book “Al-Masoun fi Al-Adab” was written by Al-Askari Abu Ahmad, and it is one of the works that dealt with topics of literature and rhetoric in a variety of ways. The book deals with poetry criticism and analysis, with a focus on the forms and types of simile and description in Arabic poetry. It also includes selections of poetry and news, and discusses news of grammarians and scholars, thus providing a comprehensive picture of the world of literature and poetry in the era in which it was written.
descriptions.830: The book “Literary Battles” by a prominent Egyptian thinker and writer, Anwar El-Gendy, presents intense discussions and theses between Arab thinkers and intellectuals on issues of literature, language, culture, and Arab nationalism. The book deals with an intellectual debate between conservatives and modernists over the concepts of Arabic literature, culture, and language, and discusses intellectual battles between figures such as Al-Akkad, Zaki Mubarak, and Taha Hussein over issues such as Arab nationalism, the Arabic language, translation, and open literature. The book also addresses various intellectual currents, such as Westernization and the return to originality, and highlights the importance of these discussions in understanding the history of modern Arab thought and literature.
descriptions.831: This book, written by Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinouri, is concerned with studying poetic verses that include descriptions of horses and other animals. In this book, the author deals with describing horses and comparing them with different types of animals and things, reviewing the sayings of poets in this field. The book is a work of literature and rhetoric, and contains analyzes of some poetic verses with a detailed explanation of their meanings and connotations.
descriptions.832: Al-Mufadaliat is a book by Al-Mufaddal Al-Dhabi. It is a collection of poetry, containing 130 poems, and it is the oldest collection of Arabic poetry. Other books appeared after it, including Al-Asma'iyat by Abu Sa'id Abd al-Malik bin Quraib Al-Asma'i, The Collection of Arab Poetry by Abu Zaid Muhammad bin Abi Al-Khattab Al-Qurashi, Selections of Arab Poets by Abu Al-Sa'adat bin Al-Shajri, and others. …
descriptions.833: Al-Muqabasat is one of the books of Abu Hayyan Al-Tawhidi. It is considered one of the most important and distinguished books written by Al-Tawhidi, as it is closer to being a specialized philosophical book that dates a fertile period in the history of Arab-Islamic philosophy in the fourth century AH.
descriptions.834: This book deals with the study of the essay and its development throughout the ages, showing its features in ancient Arabic literature and its stages in modern literature. The author focuses on the diversity of essay forms and their impact on reviving thought, while reviewing the efforts of prominent writers in various fields. The book also addresses the role of the article in addressing the intellectual issues that preoccupied Arab public opinion, especially in Egypt before and after the 1919 revolution, while highlighting the new colors that emerged under it, such as thought, idea, and caricature.
descriptions.835: This book, “The Excerpt from Azhar al-Tarf,” by Ibn Saeed al-Maghribi, deals with the fields of literature and rhetoric in a diverse artistic form, as it combines the prose and the rhyming, the eloquent and the precise. The book contains collections of short lyrics, medium and long texts, distributed across multiple vignettes, each vignette containing different layers of prose and poetry. Through this work, the author aims to strengthen unity and cohesion between various parts of the Islamic world, by highlighting the cultural and artistic diversity in Arabic literature.
descriptions.836: The Imposter by the Thalabi writer Abu Mansour is a book in the field of literature and rhetoric, dealing with various topics related to calligraphy, writing, congratulations, condolences, good morals, satire, wisdom, supplications, and other literary topics. The book contains quotations from famous poets such as Al-Buhturi, Kashajim, and Ibn Abi Al-Baghl, which indicates his interest in the Arabic language and its literary arts.
descriptions.837: The book “The Fair to the Thief and the Stolen from Him” deals with the topic of literary criticism and Arabic poetry, focusing on the poetry of Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi and discussions about imitating his poets and stealing meanings. The author Ibn Waki` al-Tanisi explains his point of view on the appreciation of al-Mutanabbi and his poetry, and compares him with other poets, reviewing the opinions of those who praised and criticized him. The book aims to reconcile praise and criticism, and presents some poetic verses as examples of the literary debates taking place in his time.
descriptions.838: The book, “The Clear Curriculum for Rhetoric,” by Hamid Awni, deals with the three arts of rhetoric: meanings, statement, and goodness, with a focus on explaining the concepts and clarifying them for secondary school students. The book deals with the definition of rhetoric, semantics, simile and its sections, truth and metaphor, metonymy, and the wonderful. It aims to provide clear and easy-to-understand scientific material for students new to rhetoric, while providing applied exercises to enhance understanding and independent thinking.
descriptions.839: The Balance between Abu Tammam and Al-Buhturi, or The Balance between the Ta’iyyin, is a book written by Abu Al-Qasim Al-Hasan bin Bishr Al-Amdi, who died in the year 371 AH, in which he presents a comparison between the two mentioned poets.
descriptions.840: This book, “Al-Muwashah fi Ma’akat al-Ulama’ on Poets,” by Al-Marzbani, deals with literary scholars’ criticisms of ancient and modern poets, pointing out their shortcomings in poetry from a linguistic, grammatical, and stylistic perspective. The author focuses on analyzing common errors in meter, meaning, and structure, relying on the opinions of scholars in this field. The book aims to warn poets against falling into these mistakes and provide constructive criticism for the development of Arabic literature.
descriptions.841: The book “Al-Moushi = Circumstance and Gentleness” by Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yahya Al-Washa deals with the topic of literature and morals, focusing on the concept of circumstance, the limits of politeness, and the laws of chivalry. The author urges the importance of examination and inquiry before addressing new topics, and emphasizes the necessity of choosing brothers and sisters carefully, with an emphasis on keeping the company of righteous people and keeping secrets. The book also presents the laws of circumstance and argues about the virtue of honesty and the ugliness of lying, while pointing out the importance of keeping secrets and preserving what is within the conscience.
descriptions.842: Looks is a book of literary short stories by the Egyptian writer Mustafa Lutfi Al-Manfaluti. He is a brilliant writer and author in writing and Arabic literature. He was unique in his pure style in his articles. His book, Looks, consists of three parts. It includes a collection of articles on social literature, criticism, politics, and Islam, as well as a collection of written or transmitted short stories, all of which were published in newspapers, and began being written in 1907 in some local newspapers. Mustafa Lutfi Al-Manfaluti was known for his easy and simple style, as he tells us stories with words that are easy to understand and also meaningful, such as the story of the orphan from the Book of Lessons.
descriptions.843: Literary criticism and its modern schools Author: Stanley Hayman Translated by: Ihsan Abbas Edition: 1 Publisher: Dar Al-Thaqafa - Beirut - Lebanon Part: 1, 1958 AD Part: 2, 1960 AD Published in association with the Franklin Printing and Publishing Corporation, Beirut - Cairo - New York 1958
descriptions.844: This book deals with literary criticism and its standards during the era of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphate. The author focuses on the influence of Islam on Arabic literature and the development of literary criticism during that period, while reviewing the Prophet’s position on poetry and literary criticism and his position on it. The book also addresses the role of the Rightly Guided Caliphs in literary criticism and their applications of its principles.
descriptions.845: The book “Modern Jokes in the News of Egyptian Ministers” by the judge and jurist, Najm al-Din Amara bin Abi al-Hasan al-Hakami and then al-Yamani, deals with a narration of the events and news of Egyptian ministers in his time, relying on his personal vision and reliable narrations. The author mixes poetry and prose in presenting a summary of news and history, pointing out the wonders and deeds that the era witnessed, without mentioning personal or undocumented details.
descriptions.846: This book was written by Al-Jurjani, Abu Al-Hasan, and deals with mediation between Al-Mutanabbi and his opponents and criticism of his poetry. The author focuses on his defense of Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi and his poetry, stating his views on literary criticism and reviewing the opinions of scholars about al-Mutanabbi and his poetry. The book also deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric, such as poets’ errors, poetic thefts, and fillers in poetry, relying on an approach that aims to clarify the facts and correct misconceptions about Al-Mutanabbi’s poetry and his personality.
descriptions.847: The book “Bada’i’ al-Badayah” by the scholar Ibn Dhafer al-Azdi covers selections of poetic verses and linguistic innovations, demonstrating the art of responding and answering among poets. The book brings together poems and proverbs from different eras, explaining how poetry and rhetoric skills have developed over time. The book also includes novels and hadiths about prominent poets such as Imru’ al-Qais and Ubaid ibn al-Abras, with a focus on the art of poetic response and the exchange of linguistic ideas between them.
descriptions.848: In his book “Badr Shaker Al-Sayyab, a Study of His Life and Poetry,” Ihsan Abbas provides a comprehensive overview of the life of the poet Badr Shaker Al-Sayyab and the development of his poetry over time. The book deals with multiple aspects of Al-Sayyab's personal, social, and political life, and how each of them influenced his poetic creativity. The author focuses on presenting an integrated picture of Al-Sayyab as a human being and a poet, relying on a method that combines chronology and psychological and artistic changes, with the aim of presenting a comprehensive vision to the reader. Abbas also seeks to avoid generalizations and metaphors in his analysis, preferring to present clear facts based on the historical and psychological facts that influenced Al-Sayyab.
descriptions.849: The book “For the purpose of clarification to summarize the key to the sciences of rhetoric” by Muhammad Abd al-Mu’tal al-Saidi deals with the fields of semantics by dividing it into chapters that begin with an introductory introduction and then applied exercises, focusing on the sections of truth, metaphor, and the relationship between the verb, the object, and the subject. The book aims to summarize and explain the book “The Key to the Sciences of Rhetoric” by Al-Khatib Al-Qazwini within an educational methodology that combines theoretical foundation and practical application, relying on precise scientific divisions of the sciences of rhetoric according to the school of Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani.
descriptions.850: Reports of Women is a book that forms the eleventh volume of the now fragmented book Al-Manzum wal-Manthur by Ibn Abi Tahir Tayfur (d. 280/893). It is noted as one of the major surviving collections of women's literature in medieval Arabic, and has been described as the first surviving book devoted entirely to women in Arabic literature.
descriptions.851: The History of Arab Literature is a book by the writer, thinker, and poet Mustafa Sadiq al-Rafi’i. It covers the history of Arabic literature in the early ages (the pre-Islamic era and the Islamic era), up to the period of Muslim rule in Andalusia. The book provides a critical study of the Arabic language, poetry, the linguistic miracle of the Holy Qur’an, prophetic eloquence, the history of oratory, Arabic poetry, and commentaries, and the history of writing and its methods. The first edition of this book was published in 1911 AD, and it was the first book of its kind to cover this topic, and it is divided into three main parts.
descriptions.852: The book “The History of Arabic Literature in the Nineteenth Century” by Dr. Louis Sheikho deals with a detailed study of the development of Arabic literature during the nineteenth century and the first quarter of the twentieth century, indicating the developments of poetry and literature in the East and Europe, and reviewing the works of famous Muslim, Christian, and Orientalist writers in that era. The book aims to fill a gaping gap in the history of Arabic literature, providing a scientific criticism of the works of writers and their writings, and reviewing the reasons that led to the development or decline of Arabic literature in that period.
descriptions.853: This book is the second part of a literary historical series dealing with Andalusian literature, as it focuses on the era of the Taifas and Almoravids. In this part, Ihsan Abbas deals with the literary phenomenon during this historical period, reviewing the social and political conditions that affected literary life, with a focus on scientific, philosophical, and critical studies. This book differs from the first part in its methodology and details, as it focuses on specific developments in this era without singling out special translations of famous poets, as was done in the previous book. The author faces difficulties in accessing reliable sources, especially since many of them are still manuscripts, which increases the value of this literary and historical work.
descriptions.854: This book deals with the study of the era of Cordoba’s sovereignty in the history of Andalusian literature, trying to present an organized picture of an important period of Andalusian literature by relying on available sources and reliable texts. The author focuses on analyzing the circumstances of the emergence of Andalusian poetry in the context of literary and cultural councils, and its development over time between the influences of the authentic Arabic style and new innovations, with reference to the influences of the cultural and artistic environment on the development of literature in that period.
descriptions.855: The book “The History of Arabic Literature in the Pre-Islamic Era” by Shawqi Dhaif deals with a detailed study of the history of Arabic literature in the pre-Islamic era, examining the various social, cultural and religious aspects that contributed to the formation of literature in that period. The book focuses on the Arab environment, the development of the Arabic language, and the emergence of pre-Islamic poetry, while providing a comprehensive overview of the pre-Islamic era and its main literary figures. The author aims to provide detailed critical historical research that reveals the depth and diversity of Arabic literature in the pre-Islamic era.
descriptions.856: In his book “The History of Literary Criticism among the Arabs,” Ihsan Abbas presents an extensive study of the development of literary criticism in the Islamic world from the late second century AH until the eighth century, focusing on the Levant and the Maghreb. The author followed a gradual, chronological approach to represent criticism as an evolving movement across the ages, and focused on the main issues without partial details that might distract from the intellectual aspects of criticism. He investigated a number of critics from various schools, whether applied or theoretical critics, to understand the intellectual foundations that guided their critical works.
descriptions.857: This book, “Tahrir Al-Tabriyah in the Making of Poetry and Prose,” by Ibn Abi Al-Asbaa, deals with the arts of rhetoric and literature in the making of poetry and prose. The author focuses on analyzing and explaining the principles and origins of Al-Badi by studying elements such as metaphor, alliteration, counterpoint, and others. The book aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the arts and techniques of literary discourse, noting the development of these arts over time and the influences of previous rhetoric scholars on them.
descriptions.858: This book, “Improvement of the Ugly and Ugly of the Good,” by Abu Mansour al-Thaalabi, deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric, trying to improve the image of what is considered ugly and make what is considered good ugly through metaphors and rhetorical methods. The author addresses topics such as improving the learner and education, improving poverty, improving religion, improving imprisonment, and improving other social and personal matters, using his skills in literature and rhetoric to transform a negative outlook into a positive one and vice versa.
descriptions.859: In his book “The Development of Modern Literature in Egypt,” Ahmed Heikal presents a comprehensive study of the development of Egyptian literature during modern times, covering periods of awakening, awareness, and struggle. The book focuses on the development of poetry and prose, and discusses how the scientific movement of the French campaign and the revival of Arab heritage influenced Egyptian literature, while reviewing the most important cultural and political institutions that contributed to the development of literature during those periods.
descriptions.860: Ibn Duraid's comments on his Amaliyah include poems, hadiths, and literary and historical events, dealing with various topics of poetry, genealogy, and wisdom. The book combines literary art and historical tributaries, relying on narrating events and stories in a way that combines literary and spiritual documentation.
descriptions.861: This study deals with the treatise “Coloring the Discourse” by Ibn Kamal Pasha, which is one of the literary and rhetorical works concerned with analyzing the discourse and detailing its diversification aspects. The dissertation falls within the category of precious literary manuscripts, and is distinguished by its small size and high scientific value, as it provides an in-depth study on the techniques of literary and rhetorical discourse. In this thesis, the author deals with topics related to the arts of language and its secrets, reviewing the opinions and sayings of rhetoric scholars, relying on previous sources and research.
descriptions.862: The Book of Fruits of Hearts in the Mafad and Mansoub is one of the pioneering books in Arabic literature, written by the linguist and grammatical imam Abu Mansour al-Tha’alabi, who is considered one of the most prominent scholars of the fourth century AH. This book is distinguished by its unique style in dealing with the topic of “genitive and attributive,” as it shows readers the linguistic and semantic dimensions this topic contains, from which references emerge to various aspects of human and mental life.
descriptions.863: The book “The Fruits of Papers in Lectures” written by Ibn Hajjat ​​al-Hamawi is one of the literary books that deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric. It contains stories, proverbs, and anecdotes related to intelligent and wise Arabs, in addition to examples of composition and rhetoric. The book focuses on highlighting the skills of intelligence and mental alertness in various situations, relying on the transfer and analysis of examples from Arabic history and literature.
descriptions.864: The Collection of Poetry of the Arabs is a book by Abu Zaid al-Qurashi. It is a collection of selections of pre-Islamic, ancient, and Islamic Arabic poetry. He divided the book into seven sections, each section having seven poems, and he made all the sections graduated from the pre-Islamic era until the Umayyad era.
descriptions.865: The Collection of Proverbs is a scientific and literary encyclopedia written by Abu Hilal Al-Askari. It contains a large collection of Arabic proverbs. The compiler has compiled his book on the letters of the alphabet. He presents a proverb, explains its origin, its saying if known, and what it is true for, and explains its meanings.
descriptions.866: A Collection of Arab Speeches in the Prosperous Arab Ages is a book in which Ahmed Zaki Safwat collected everything he wrote about the Arabs, including speeches, commandments, and the dialogues, debates, and debates that took place in the councils of kings, caliphs, and presidents. It contains four sections in three parts: The first part, which contains: On the sermons of pre-Islamic times, in the sermons of early Islam, the second part, and It contains the sermons of the Umayyad era, the third part, and it contains: The sermons of the first Abbasid era, the tail of the crowd, in separate sermons.
descriptions.867: This book deals with the subject of the science of composition in literature and rhetoric, and reviews its origins, rules, and the importance of eloquence in writing. The author focuses on how to structure and organize speech, while providing advice on how to open and close composition topics. The book also deals with various writing arts, such as correspondence and correspondence, and includes studies of famous writings in this field. The book aims to teach the reader how to compose texts in an eloquent and beautiful manner, taking into account clarity and ease of expression.
descriptions.868: The book “Jawahir Al-Balagha fi Al-Ma’ani, Al-Bayan, and Al-Badi’” is one of the works of Mr. Ahmed Al-Hashemi, and it is one of the books that deals with the science of rhetoric in its three fields: Al-Ma’ani, Al-Bayan, and Al-Badi’. The book deals with the basic rules of Arabic eloquence and rhetoric, and reviews the cases of the predicate and the predicate, with a focus on dividing speech into predicates and constructions, and analyzing the different types of constructions such as command, prohibition, interrogative, wishful thinking, and appeal. The book is directed to those who wish to learn the arts of the Arabic language and the rules of rhetoric, and it is one of the works concerned with developing linguistic expression and analysis skills.
descriptions.869: This book deals with the poetry of the ancients, pre-Islamic people, and veterans, trying to show the similarities and similarities between it and the poetry of the modernists. The authors focus on analyzing meanings, similes, and metaphors in ancient and modern poetry, while acknowledging the quality of creativity of the early poets and their influence on those who came after them. The book combines ancient and modern poetry to compare their vocabulary and meanings, focusing on what distinguishes each time period in Arabic poetry.
descriptions.870: The book “Al-Qurashi’s Enthusiasm” by Abbas Al-Qurashi is an anthology of poetry in literature and rhetoric, in which the author collects poems and verses by different poets, arranged in thematic sections that begin with pride and enthusiasm, include elegies, eulogies, praise, and satire, and end with wine. The book aims to present examples of Arabic poetry in its various purposes, with a focus on the meanings of courage, pride, and dignity that emerge in the first chapter.
descriptions.871: The book “The Great Life of the Animal” is Kamal al-Din al-Damiri’s most famous book. There are two versions: minor and major. The printed version is the major one, and is distinguished from the smaller one by adding historical materials and interpreting the dreams in which these animals occur. It includes (1069) articles arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, but this number does not mean the number of animals for which it was translated, as many of these articles are synonymous. It is translated for many animals in various places, according to the multiplicity of their names, or the specialty of their children and females with other names. These translations vary in their explanations, as some reach (11) pages, such as the lion, and some: a few words. Birds and mammals occupy an excellent place in the book. …
descriptions.872: This book, “Khas al-Khas,” written by Al-Thaalabi Abu Mansour, deals with multiple fields of literature and rhetoric, focusing on brevity in speech and its magic, while providing examples from the words of kings and presidents and the opinions of writers, grammarians, readers, and hadith scholars. The book is also concerned with the cuteness and curiosities that express the wisdom of witty people and the genius of craftsmen, presenting various models of literary and intellectual discourse.
descriptions.873: This book, “The Palace Scrap and Al-Asr Newspaper,” written by Imad Al-Isfahani, deals with the field of literature and rhetoric, and reviews Iraqi poets and scholars of his time. The author aims to document and preserve the works of the people of his time, given the loss of the custom of credit and the decline of people’s interest in it. The book is likened to a collection of literary and scientific treasures, as it contains benefits and new ideas in the field of literature and poetry, trying to imitate what Al-Tha'labi and Al-Bakhrazi presented in this field.
descriptions.874: Khorida Al-Qasr and Al-Asr Newspaper is a literary book in 21 volumes, in which its author, Imad Al-Din Al-Isfahani, translated several poets in the fifth and sixth centuries AH.
descriptions.875: Khorida Al-Qasr and Al-Asr Newspaper is a literary book in 21 volumes, in which its author, Imad Al-Din Al-Isfahani, translated several poets in the fifth and sixth centuries AH.
descriptions.876: “The Treasury of Literature” originally, and as its author states in his introduction to it, is an explanation of his aforementioned innovation, which he created, as he states, “with a drawing from Muhammad bin al-Barazi al-Juhani al-Shafi’i,” the author of the Diwan al-Insha’ in the Islamic Kingdoms. In it, he followed the example of “Tarz al-Burda” after Muhammad bin al-Barazi stopped at the innovation of Sheikh Izz al-Din al-Mawsili, in which he adhered to naming the original genre, and misinterpreted it from the genre of ghazal, in order to distinguish it from Sheikh Safi al-Din al-Hilli, who did not He adheres to this in his originality. …
descriptions.877: This book, “The Treasury of Literature and Lub Lubab Lisan al-Arab,” by Abdul Qadir al-Baghdadi, deals with the topics of literature, rhetoric, grammar, and morphology. In it, Al-Baghdadi explains the evidence of Al-Kafiya’s book by Al-Radi Al-Astarabadi, and provides precise interpretations and critical analyzes of the verses of poetry in question, relying on his extensive knowledge of poetry and the Arabic language. The book aims to clarify the ambiguous meanings and complex explanations of Arabic literary texts. It includes indexes and an introductory introduction that explains the book’s objectives and the organization of its content.
descriptions.878: The book “Characteristics of Structures: An Analytical Study of Issues of Semantics” deals with the subject of semantics and rhetoric through an analytical study of Arabic methods of explaining meanings. The author, Muhammad Muhammad Abu Musa, focuses on extrapolating the speech of the Arabs and tracing the characteristics of their linguistic structures, stressing the importance of preserving the character of Arabic sciences from hybridization and mixing with other sciences. The book covers several chapters that study the conditions of attribution, the subject and the predicate, relying on a careful analysis of the methods of Arabic constructions and their traditions in expressing meanings.
descriptions.879: The book “Dar al-Taraz fi Mushahat Work” by Ibn Sana al-Malik provides a detailed study of the art of poetic stanzas, as the author deals with the different types of stanzas, their rules, and their origins. The book contains introductory introductions and examples of manuscripts, in addition to analyzes of the forms of stanzas and details of their poetic structure. This book is considered one of the important works in the field of Arabic literature and rhetoric, especially in the field of studying Mawshahi poetry and its development.
descriptions.880: The book “Studies in Journalistic Art” by Muhammad Ibrahim Imam deals with the subject of journalistic art as a media art, reviewing its definition, characteristics and stages of development in various countries, with a focus on the different forms of journalistic editing and directing and how to simplify information and embody it for the public. The book also addresses the relationship between journalistic art and society, and its functions in media, guidance, and entertainment, with an explanation of the role of visual and linguistic elements in achieving these goals.
descriptions.881: In his book “A Study of Pre-Islamic Era Texts, Analysis and Appreciation,” Mr. Ahmed Emara presents an in-depth study of poems from the pre-Islamic era, focusing on analyzing the artistic and aesthetic aspects of poetic texts, and exploring the psychological and social meanings they carry for their writer. The book deals with characters and events from the pre-Islamic era, reviewing examples of pre-Islamic poetry in which various images of Arab life at that time appear, from departure and immigration to warnings against invasion and adherence to tribal affiliation.
descriptions.882: This book, “The Puppet of the Palace and the Squeeze of the People of the Age” by Al-Bakhrazi, is a type of literary book that includes studies on poetry and poets. The book covers biographies of poets from various Arab regions, focusing on Bedouin and Hijaz poets. The book begins with an introduction that addresses the author's journey in the world of literature and poetry, and refers to his father's efforts in educating him and his literary upbringing. The book aims to provide a comprehensive overview of prominent Arab poets and analyze their literary works.
descriptions.883: Diwan al-Ma'ani by Ibn al-Askari is a book on literature and rhetoric that deals with the most eloquent works of poetry and rhetoric, choosing what is well-arranged and tightly arranged, far from what is flimsy, loose, or wrinkled and crude. The book deals with various topics such as praise, pride, satire, and reproach, relying on the most prominent, notable, and anomalous meanings, and aims to determine the extent of the writer’s knowledge and the extent of his memorization.
descriptions.884: The collection of Imru’ al-Qais, one of the most prominent poets of pre-Islamic times, includes poems and verses that reflect the depth of the poet’s human and psychological experience. The collection deals with various topics from love and flirtation to invasions and battles, presenting a sophisticated artistic image of ancient Arabic poetry. It is characterized by a high linguistic and literary aesthetic, as it contains a famous commentator and various poetic verses in their themes and meters, which makes it one of the most important poetic works in Arabic literature.
descriptions.885: The collection of Tarfa bin Al-Abd is a collection of pre-Islamic poetry that includes verses that reflect the poet’s life and personal experience, in which he expresses the injustice he faced at the hands of his relatives and his reactions towards it. It also addresses other topics such as friendship, social isolation, and the search for recognition and social status. Tarfa's poetry is distinguished by its sweet style and rich poetic images that reflect the reality of life in pre-Islamic times.
descriptions.886: The poetry collection of Labid bin Rabia Al-Amiri is a collection of ancient Arabic poetry, dealing with various topics of sadness and joy, condemnation and enthusiasm, expressing the poet’s life experience through its various stages. This collection is distinguished by its diversity in poetic purposes, as it includes poems of lamentation, enthusiasm, and poetry, expressing the depth of the poet’s poetic and historical experience.
descriptions.887: Rubaiyat is a well-known type of poetry in Persian poetry, and Omar Khayyam was known for it. He is Ghiyath al-Din Abu al-Futuh Omar ibn Ibrahim al-Khayyam, known as Omar Khayyam (1048 - 1131 AD), a Persian poet, astronomer and mathematician. It was probably written in the early twelfth century AD/568 AH, and the title comes from the plural form of the Arabic word quatrain, which refers to a form of Persian poetry. The quatrain is a poetic piece of four verses that revolves around a specific topic and forms a complete idea. Either the rhyme of the first and second parts agrees with the fourth, or all four parts of the rhyme agree.
descriptions.888: The Spring of the Righteous is a book by the Islamic scholar Al-Mu'tazil al-Zamakhshari about Islam.
descriptions.889: The Book of Letters is a collection of rare letters by Al-Jahiz, and each of these letters discusses one topic, with an in-depth and extensive study that arouses admiration and appreciation. Al-Jahiz wrote many treatises on literature, religion, and politics, which were completed by a group of Arab and Orientalist researchers, but the largest and most accurate series was written by Dr. Abdel Salam Haroun.
descriptions.890: Al-Maqrizi's letters to Cairo by Abu Al-Abbas Al-Maqrizi include an introductory introduction to the author and a detail of his numerous works in the fields of literature, history, and jurisprudence. The book deals with various topics, including the conflict between the Banu Umayyad and Banu Hashim, a chapter on the specialty of the Banu Hashim in prophethood and advocacy, and a discussion of the major and minor types of polytheism, with a focus on the monotheism of God and an explanation of the types of polytheism and disruption. The book reflects the richness of Al-Maqrizi’s scientific production and the diversity of its topics.
descriptions.891: The Treatise of Disciples and Whirlwinds by Ibn Shahid Al-Andalusi deals with the fields of literature and rhetoric by studying the influences of poets and writers on their works, with a focus on literary criticism and analysis of literary and fairy figures. The book includes a rich literary dialogue between its author and Zuhair bin Numayr, one of the bravest jinn, in which they discuss the concept of influence and being influenced in literary creativity, while providing examples from the lives of poets and writers and their works.
descriptions.892: The Epistle of Forgiveness is a literary work by Abu Al-Ala Al-Maarri, a poet and philosopher from the Abbasid era (363 AH - 449 AH) (973 - 1057 AD). It is considered one of the most beautiful things Al-Maarri wrote in prose. It is a letter that describes the conditions in heaven and hell and the characters there. It was said that Dante Alighieri, the author of the poetic epic The Divine Comedy, took the idea and content of the epic from Abu Al-Ala. Abdel Fattah Kilto wrote that the Epistle of Forgiveness was not popular during his reign and that Abu Al-Ala’s contemporaries did not pay much attention to it, and did not consider it distinct from the rest of his epistles, such as the Epistle of Angels, or the Epistle of Jinn. …
descriptions.893: This thesis deals with an overview of the theory of systems and formulation in literature from the perspective of Ibn Kamal Pasha, as he calls for renewing the rhetorical direction of Abdul Qaher al-Jurjani and discusses aspects of the theory of systems and the value of artistic formulation away from artificial embellishment. It is a study that falls within the framework of literature and rhetoric, and aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the meanings of grammar and emotional experience.
descriptions.894: Rawd al-Akhyr al-Mukhtab from Rabi` al-Abrar is a book of literature and rhetoric that deals with wide areas of science and knowledge, from worship and morals to jurisprudence and jurisprudence, passing through medicine and nature, wisdom and proverbs, crafts and crafts, strange things and miracles, morals and etiquette, and legal and worldly sciences. The book consists of multiple chapters covering various areas of life, providing a comprehensive overview of the sciences and ideas of his time, relying on a combination of wisdom, science, and literary taste.
descriptions.895: This book, “The Rihanna of the Book and the Nagah of the Mantab,” by the writer Lisan al-Din ibn al-Khatib, deals with various areas of literature and rhetoric, including praises, congratulations, condolences, and intercessions, in addition to political and personal correspondence with princes and ministers. The author focuses on the arts of formal and personal speech and writing, relying on his skills in literature and eloquence to present letters and literature of a highly diplomatic and personal nature.
descriptions.896: The Flower of Manners and the Fruit of Minds is a literary book compiled by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Ali Al-Husri Al-Qayrawani (d. 413 AH, 1061 AD), a writer from Kairouan, an eloquent author and publisher. He is a contemporary of the famous poet Abu al-Hasan al-Husri al-Qayrawani, and they are related. According to Al-Husri, Abu Al-Hassan is the author of the famous poem “Yaleel Al-Sab”. Zahr al-Adab is a purely literary book in which the author did not deal with anything of grammar, morphology, or language. Rather, he restricted it to the arts of speech, such as poetry and prose, and the forms of eloquence related to that, the beauty of wording, the correctness of the simile, the good construction, and the quality of rhetoric. The book is based on collection and narration, and its author did not bother to scrutinize, discuss, and comment on the news and poems. …
descriptions.897: Zahr al-Akma fi Proverbs and Wisdom is a book on Arabic literature and the art of proverbs, written by the Moroccan scholar al-Hasan bin Masoud bin Muhammad al-Yusi (1040–1102 AH/1630–1691 AD), known as “Abu al-Mawahib al-Yusi.” It is considered one of the most prominent Moroccan works of the eleventh century AH. It combines heritage documentation, linguistic analysis, and literary explanation of proverbs and aphorisms.
descriptions.898: This book by Al-Thaalabi Abu Mansour deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric through its description of nature and human life. It focuses on describing times and places, and includes a detailed description of spring, summer, and winter, in addition to describing the psychological state of a person in the various stages of his life. The book is distinguished by its beautiful rhetorical style and the aesthetics of its language in describing nature and man.
descriptions.899: The Secret of Eloquence by Ibn Sinan Al-Khafaji is a book on literature and rhetoric that deals with defining eloquence, its secret, and explaining its truth, while addressing the rulings on sounds, letters, speech, and language. The book aims to clarify the difference between eloquence and other literary forms, and to demonstrate its importance in the literary and legal sciences, with a focus on understanding the meanings and words composed. The book seeks to bring the concept of eloquence closer to the reader and present it in the clearest possible way without prejudice to brevity or excessive redundancy.
descriptions.900: The book “The Pleasure of the Soul through the Perceptions of the Five Senses” is one of the literary works that deals with describing times and natural conditions, focusing on night and day and their different conditions. In this book, the author Ahmed bin Youssef Al-Tifashi deals with various topics related to the phenomena of nature and daily life, reviewing literary descriptions of the most famous nights, their lengths and shortness, and also reviewing descriptions of dawn, dawn, the song of birds, and the crow of the rooster. The book is distinguished by the fact that it combines the Arab, Islamic and Greek cultures, and is considered a middle link between scientific knowledge and literary entertainment, presenting literary images to bring nature closer to the souls.
descriptions.901: This book is an explanation and detail of the writer’s literature by Ibn Qutaybah. It was explained and detailed by Ibn al-Jawaliqi in the field of literature and rhetoric. The book provides a detailed explanation of the verses and parts of the book The Writer’s Literature, clarifying the linguistic and rhetorical problems contained therein, and presenting various interpretations and opinions about them. It focuses on analyzing nouns and words used, and discusses Arabic grammar and its applications in writing and literature.
descriptions.902: Explanation of the Nine Mu’allaqat by Ibn al-Shaybani is a literary interpretation of the most famous poems of pre-Islamic times. It deals with each of the nine Mu’allaqat, mentioning its successor, and analyzing its vocabulary and rhetorical methods. The book focuses on clarifying the ambiguous meanings and linguistic linguistics in the poems, with reference to the historical and social stories they dealt with.
descriptions.903: In his book, “Explanation of the Seven Mu’allaqat,” Al-Zawzni provides a comprehensive explanation of the Mu’allaqat of Bashar ibn Burd and Abu Tammam, in addition to the seven Mu’allaqat by Abu al-Atahiya, Tarfa ibn al-Abbad, Jarir, and al-Akhtal. The book deals with the emergence and development of pre-Islamic poetry, with a focus on the lives and poems of poets. Al-Zouzani also presents the artistic and technical methods used in pre-Islamic poetry, and discusses the artistic tradition of the Arabic poem in the pre-Islamic era.
descriptions.904: This book is an explanation of the book “Diwan of Enthusiasm,” a selection of pre-Islamic poetry, in which Al-Tabrizi discusses poets and poems from the collection, explaining their meanings and rhetorical secrets. The explanation covers prominent poets from various Arab tribes, and aims to provide a deeper understanding of poetic texts and explain their artistic and literary goals. The book falls within the arts of literature and rhetoric, and reviews important aspects of ancient Arabic poetry.
descriptions.905: Explanation of the Diwan of Enthusiasm by its author Al-Marzouqi Al-Isfahani deals with a literary and rhetorical interpretation of the Arabic poems of Enthusiasm, focusing on an analysis of the meanings and poetic methods used in this famous collection. The book focuses on explaining and clarifying the sayings of poets from various Arab tribes, while providing linguistic and terminological information related to some of the terms and names mentioned in the original text.
descriptions.906: The book “Poetry of the Kharijites” by Dr. Ihsan Abbas provides a comprehensive literary overview of the poetry of the Kharijites, attempting to collect what was contained in the manuscript and printed sources, including poems and poems, and organize them chronologically to trace their development with the passage of historical events. The book deals with the poetry of the Kharijites during a period of time extending from the Battle of Nahrawan until the Battle of Qudayd, relying on historical sources such as the history of al-Tabari and the genealogies of al-Baladhuri. The book also includes historical notes, summaries of poems, and definitions of notable figures, which provides the reader with a deeper understanding of the historical and literary context of Kharijite poetry.
