descriptions.907: This book deals with the study of poetic literature in the period of the first Islamic conquests, focusing on the influences of Islam and jihad on Arab poetry. The author examines how religious and political transformation gave rise to new themes and styles in poetry, challenging notions of the time that pre-Islamic poetry continued fundamentally unchanged. The book also studies the lives and poems of prominent poets who participated in the conquests, such as Amr ibn Ma'di Yakrib al-Zubaidi and al-Qaqa ibn Amr al-Tamimi.
descriptions.908: The book “Shawqi’s Poetry in the Balance of Criticism” by Muhammad Al-Majzoub reflects on Hafez Shawqi’s literary works from a comprehensive critical perspective, addressing the various poetic purposes addressed by the poet. Al-Majzoub addresses the political, social, descriptive, and representational aspects of Shawqi’s poetry, highlighting the intellectual development and artistic expressions that the poet went through through the various stages of his life. It sheds light on the nature of Shawqi's political ideas and how they were affected by changing personal and social circumstances. It also analyzes his style of descriptive and representative poetry and his relationship with Arab and Frankish poets.
descriptions.909: Subh al-A’sha fi Sina’ al-Insha’a is a book consisting of 14 parts written by Abu al-Abbas al-Qalqashandi, who died in the year 821 AH 1418 AD, who held the position of the Diwan al-Insha’ during the reign of Sultan al-Zahir Barquq. The book is considered a comprehensive encyclopedia of all legal, literary, geographical and historical sciences.
descriptions.910: This book by Al-Suyuti deals with the topic of good taste and its qualities in various groups of society, from kings and princes to poets and writers. The author describes the characteristics of a person with good taste in each category, and compares them with the characteristics of someone who lacks this taste. The book focuses on the importance of intelligence and reason in shaping good taste, considering that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the most perfect of people in these qualities. The book aims to explain the characteristics of people of understanding and the opposite of them who deviate from the truth.
descriptions.911: This book deals with the topics of literature, ethics, wisdom, and proverbs, as it focuses on promoting virtues and spreading noble values ​​through words and deeds. The author, Judge Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Mahdi, deals with concepts such as science and reason and their relationship to morality and religion, reviewing the importance of knowledge in raising motivation and honoring the teacher, and reason in contemplation and guidance. It also points out the importance of wisdom and proverbs in guiding behavior and consolidating positive values ​​in society. The book aims to inspire the reader and motivate him to think and act in a way that pleases God and benefits people.
descriptions.912: The book “The Natures of Women and the Wonders, News, and Secrets Contained therein” by Ibn Abd Rabbuh Al-Andalusi deals with the topic of women from a literary and rhetorical perspective, covering their characteristics, news, and what scholars say about them. The book focuses on choosing a good wife and good qualities, relying on wisdom, proverbs, and prophetic hadiths to clarify the concept of chastity and beauty in women. It also points out the importance of a good wife in building a happy home, and reviews famous sayings and proverbs about women and their natures.
descriptions.913: This book deals with the life and literature of Taha Hussein from an Islamic perspective, as the author Ibrahim Muhammad Sarsik criticizes Taha Hussein’s positions on Islam and Arabic literature. The book focuses on analyzing Taha Hussein's ideas and opinions in various fields, and discusses his influence on thought and literature in Egypt and the Arab world. The book is divided into three sections covering the stages of Taha Hussein’s formation and literary maturity, in addition to his opinions and conflicts with his peers.
descriptions.914: The book “The Wise Men of the Crazy” by Ibn Habib al-Naysaburi is one of the books that deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric, as the author focuses on studying the cases of the insane and analyzing their behavior and characteristics. The book deals with the causes and types of madness, and also includes a study of famous mad personalities in Arab heritage, trying to understand whether they are truly mad or whether they pretend to be mad to achieve a specific goal. The book combines lesson and wisdom, drawing lessons for life and thinking from cases of madmen.
descriptions.915: This book deals with the science of prosody and rhyme, and provides a simplified definition of this science and its origins, with a focus on explaining the different meters of poetry and exercises on them. The author begins by defining the performances and the role of Khalil bin Ahmed in establishing it, then moves on to explaining the long sea and the rest of the poetic seas, while providing examples and evidence from poetry to enhance the reader’s theoretical and applied understanding.
descriptions.916: This book, written by Ahmed bin Mustafa Al-Maraghi, deals with the three sciences of rhetoric: statement, meanings, and badi’. The author focuses on analyzing the concepts of eloquence and rhetoric linguistically and idiomatically. The book includes studies in semantics based on detailed divisions of predicates and constructions, and aims to provide exercises and models for developing rhetorical skills. The book aims to understand the secrets of Arabic rhetoric and its characteristics, and how to apply it in speech, with reference to its role in the miracle of the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.917: The Caliber of Poetry is a book on criticism of Arabic poetry written by Ibn Tabataba Al-Alawi. It is classified among the books of literary criticism in the fourth century AH, and deals with issues related to the definition of poetry, its standards, and tools for making it. The book The Standard of Poetry comes in the context of the development of criticism in the fourth century AH, as this stage witnessed a transition from the impressionistic form to setting rational standards to control poetic quality.
descriptions.918: This is the book “Uyun al-Akhbar” by Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Muslim bin Qutaybah al-Dinouri, and it is one of the works of literature and rhetoric. The book deals with various topics related to politics, ethics, and literature, providing advice and etiquette to writers, kings, and common people. The author focuses on straightening the tongue and hand and explaining the origins of literature, while presenting funny anecdotes and funny words to relieve the reader from seriousness. In his material, Ibn Qutaybah relies on various sources, including Arabic and Indian literature books and the sayings of scholars and jurists.
descriptions.919: This book, “Gharaibat Al-Nahibihat Ala-Gharaibat Al-Aja’ibahat Al-Aja’ibahat” by Ibn Dhafer Al-Azdi, deals with topics of literature and rhetoric, focusing on the art of similes in Arabic poetry. The book discusses various analogies for natural phenomena, such as celestial bodies, the moon, and stars, and also studies other analogies for things such as wine, rainbows, snow, and lightning. The book aims to review the strangeness and wonders of poetic similes and how to use them in Arabic literature.
descriptions.920: This book, “The Deceptions of Clear Characteristics, and the Deceptions of Obvious Contradictions,” written by Al-Bat, deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric through the study of morals and human qualities. The book is divided into sixteen chapters. Each chapter deals with a specific moral quality or personal trait, such as generosity, meanness, intelligence, and cowardice. Each chapter is divided into three chapters detailing the meanings and examples of these qualities. In this book, the author reviews the advantages of good qualities and the disadvantages of vice qualities, presenting examples of literature and wisdom to clarify its content.
descriptions.921: The book “The Virility of Poets” by Imam Al-Asma’i deals with the study of pre-Islamic poetry and its most famous poets, focusing on the concept of virility in poetry and its standards. Al-Asma'i compares prominent poets such as Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani, Zuhair bin Abi Salma, and Imru' Al-Qais, reviewing their characteristics and poetic styles, and cites some poetic verses to support his opinions on the question of who is the most poetic and the best of poets.
descriptions.922: This book is an explanation of the book “Proverbs” by Ibn al-Bakri, and aims to interpret and analyze Arabic proverbs in terms of language, parsing, stories, and reasons. In this work, the author deals with multiple sources of proverbs, and reviews the opinions of previous scholars and imams in this field, indicating the importance of sayings and narrations related to proverbs and their synonyms. The book is divided into several sections or sections, each of which deals with a topic or category of proverbs, which helps the reader understand and follow the content of the book easily.
descriptions.923: The superiority of dogs over many of those who wear clothes, or The superiority of dogs over many of those who wear clothes, is a book written by Abu Bakr bin Al-Marzban, who died in the year 309 AH. The book mentions what was said about the dog, including Qur’anic verses, hadiths, and sayings of poets, sages, and narrators. The book also reflects an attitude toward people who are disloyal, appreciating the value of loyalty in a dog that accompanies people to be their guardian and companion. The sources mention that there is doubt about the authorship of the book being attributed to Abu Bakr ibn al-Marzban. …
descriptions.924: The book “The Art of Elocution” by Muhammad Taha Abdel Fattah Muqallad deals with the study of the art of elocution from the perspective of linguistic sounds and pronunciation rules, with a focus on the history of the emergence of this art and its development throughout the ages. The author begins by discussing the efforts of early Muslim scholars to preserve the purity of the Arabic language and its grammatical and morphological correctness, then moves on to analyzing linguistic sounds and their characteristics and their relationship to the rules of diction. The book also addresses pronunciation defects and hearing errors and how to avoid them.
descriptions.925: This book deals with the art of Arabic editing, its controls and patterns, showing the foundations on which the art of good writing is based. The author focuses on the importance of mastering the linguistic tool and practicing fine literary styles, while emphasizing the necessity of familiarity with serious modern culture and forming an intellectual base for the subject written about. The book also includes a study of the sources of classical and modern Arabic culture, while presenting practical applications in the field of dictation, expression, and composition in the stages of general education.
descriptions.926: The book “The Art of Biography” by Dr. Ihsan Abbas deals with the study of autobiographical narrative literature in Arabic literature, trying to link it to the history of Arab civilization and the current of Arab thought and psychology. The author focuses on the importance of autobiography as an image of lived experience in literature, considering that it illuminates the past and future and provides a deeper understanding of the mission of literature. Abbas presents examples of Arab and Western autobiographies, trying to highlight the differences and similarities between them, focusing on artistic biography as an independent literary art.
descriptions.927: The book “The Art of Journalistic Writing” by Farouk Abu Zaid deals with the various arts of journalistic writing from a theoretical and practical perspective, reviewing the basics and applications of speech, investigation, reporting, and journalistic articles. The book is divided into four chapters, each of which deals with a specific journalistic art and divides it into several detailed sections, with the aim of presenting a comprehensive picture of the art of journalistic writing and its continuous developments with the development of the journalism profession.
descriptions.928: The book deals with the art of the journalistic article in the literature of Taha Hussein, reviewing the environment in which this art arose in Egypt and the influences that contributed to its formation, with a focus on Taha Hussein’s style of journalistic writing and his eloquence in communicating with the masses. The book also discusses the methods followed by Taha Hussein in editing his articles, relying on simplification, journalistic modeling, and realistic, investigative, and inductive methods in conveying events and expressing his ideas.
descriptions.929: The book “The Art of the Essay” by Muhammad Youssef Negm deals with a critical historical study of the concept of the literary essay across the ages, surveying its development from ancient times until the modern era. The author focuses on the difference between the subjective essay and the objective essay, and discusses the development of the art of the essay in Western and Arab literature, noting the decline in interest in it in Arab criticism compared to the West. The book also addresses the transformation in the nature of the article from a literary art to a tool for scientific research in the modern era.
descriptions.930: The book “The Arts of Journalistic Editing between Theory and Practice” by author Mahmoud Adham deals with the art of the journalistic article as a basic axis in the field of journalistic editing. The book focuses on defining the article and its historical development, and discusses its different types and their importance in Arab journalism, analyzing the characteristics of each type and its editing mechanisms. The book also addresses the role of the article in shaping public opinion and its impact on the reader, considering it an art that is more professional and has a deeper impact than other arts in the field of journalistic editing.
descriptions.931: The book “On Modern Literature” by Muhammad Omar Al-Desouki deals with the history of Arabic literature in the modern era, focusing on the developments that occurred in Egypt and the Arab countries during the nineteenth century and beyond. The book examines how contacts with the West and the educational renaissance influenced the formation of Arab literature and art, and how Eastern and Western cultures blended to form a new literary language and style. The book covers different periods of the modern era, starting from the era of Muhammad Ali until the era of Ismail, through the renaissance of poetry and prose, and the influence of translations and educational missions on Arabic literature.
descriptions.932: The book “On the New Balance” by Mohamed Mandour deals with the topics of literature and rhetoric by studying contemporary Egyptian literature and comparing it with Western literature, with a focus on the methods of literary criticism and their applications. The book addresses various topics such as myth in literature, realistic literature, whispered poetry, and rhetorical poetry, while providing objective criticism of selected literary texts.
descriptions.933: This book deals with the topic of Arab literary criticism and its development throughout the ages, focusing on critical issues related to poetry and the literary arts. In the book, the author deals with the stages of literary criticism from oral criticism in the pre-Islamic era to its codification in later eras, with a review of the most important critical letters and newspapers and their impact on the development of the critical movement. The book also focuses on the issue of the poetry column and the opinions of critics about it, and discusses critical issues related to meaning, pronunciation, style, rhythm, image, and music in Arabic literature.
descriptions.934: This is a book on the history of pre-Islamic literature. It aims to provide a comprehensive study of the pre-Islamic era from its various aspects, going beyond being limited to studying examples of poets. The book begins with an introduction about the pre-Islamic people and the meaning of pre-Islamic times, then deals in detail with the genealogies of the Arab tribes, their homes, and their political, social, and religious life, touching on their customs such as divination, divination, and idol worship, to be a comprehensive reference for everything the researcher needs in this field.
descriptions.935: The book “The Story of Literature in Hijaz” by Dr. Abdullah Abdul Jabbar deals with an in-depth study of literary life in Hijaz during the pre-Islamic era and the Prophethood, with a focus on the social, political and religious factors that contributed to the formation of Hijazi literature. The book deals with the Hijaz environment from its political, social, and religious perspective, and reviews important figures and literary works in Hijaz before Islam, to understand the cultural background in which the Islamic call arose. The book also studies the impact that the Qur’an had on Hijaz literature, and the role of Hijaz as a center for Arab culture and literature.
descriptions.936: A book on literature and rhetoric that studies and analyzes the issues of free poetry in the Arab world. Its author divides it into three main sections: the first examines free poetry as a literary and social movement, the second studies its performances, rules, and formations, and the third examines its impact on the public. The book is based on an examination of published free poems and the laws of Arabic prosody, with the author noting in her introduction the development of her views on some rules with the passage of time and the intensity of poetic production.
descriptions.937: This book, “The Rules of Poetry” by Fox, deals with the art of poetry and its origins by analyzing its main types and basic pillars. It begins by explaining the four basic types of poetry, which are command, prohibition, news, and intelligence. Then it expands on its sub-branches such as praise, satire, elegy, simile, and others.
descriptions.938: This book deals with the similes used in Andalusian poetry during the Umayyad and Amirid eras, and presents examples of poetry that contain these similes. The author focuses on presenting new facts about Andalusian poetry and analyzing it through specific poetic models, while making important modifications in the second edition based on his previous studies. The book falls within the framework of literature and rhetoric, and presents the challenges of scientific investigation of ancient poetic texts.
descriptions.939: The Book of Prosody by Ibn Jinni is a book on the science of prosody, one of the arts of literature and rhetoric, in which it deals with the definition of prosody and its function in Arabic poetry. It shows how to divide poetic verses and classify them into different types, with an explanation of the lines and circles of poetry. It reviews the basic concepts of prosody such as reason, chord, and comma, and explains the rules for activating poetic verses and classifying them into different types of poetry.
descriptions.940: This book, “Revealing Secrets in the Ruling on Birds and Flowers,” written by Izz al-Din al-Maqdisi, deals with literary and rhetorical topics by interpreting the meanings of signs and symbols in birds and flowers. The author focuses on understanding the hidden wisdom behind the existence of these creatures, reviewing the signals and tones of flowers and birds and how they express their states and circumstances. The book reviews a group of flowers and birds, and attempts to explain the wisdom and secret that each of them expresses, trying to link that to human reality and its understanding of existence and life.
descriptions.941: Kalila and Dimna is a book that includes a collection of stories. It was translated by Abdullah bin Al-Muqaffa from Fahlawi into Arabic in the Abbasid era, specifically in the second century AH, corresponding to the eighth century AD, and he formulated it in his own literary style, adapting it from the original book. Many researchers agree that the book has Indian origins: the Five Chapters (Sanskrit: पञ्चतन्त्र; Panchatantra) were written in Sanskrit in the fourth century AD, and then translated into the Pahlavi language in the early sixth century AD by order of Khosrow I. …
descriptions.942: In the book “Kanasha Al-Nawader,” Abdul Salam Haroun presents various anecdotes and events related to Arab life and Islamic culture, covering topics that include literature, language, traditions, and customs, with a focus on protecting Arab heritage from distortion and Westernization. In his introduction, the author criticizes the attempts to distort the Arabic language and the Arab identity, in defense of Arabism and the authentic Islamic identity against extremist and Orientalist trends.
descriptions.943: The book “Lubab Al-Adab” by Al-Tha’alabi Abu Zaid is a book on the art of praising and praising kings and rulers, in which the author deals with the origins and methods of writing poems and praising sultans and ministers, with a focus on praising God, His Messenger, and his family. The book also addresses multiple topics related to politics, government, and soldiering, providing examples of sophisticated literary language in this field.
descriptions.944: The book “Unpublished Amāli al-Shajri” deals with the sayings of grammarians, linguists, and writers, as Ibn al-Shajri dictated it in eighty-four sessions. It includes topics in grammar, language, and literature, with a focus on specific courses such as explaining verses from the poetry of Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi and mentioning the mistakes of Makki ibn Abi Talib in parsing the Qur’an. The book includes notes on the importance of attributing sayings to their original sources.
descriptions.945: The book “Free Literature in the Gardens of the Arabs” by Father Louis Sheikho deals with various topics in literature and rhetoric, including wisdom, walking proverbs, and animal proverbs, with a focus on the religious and pious aspects of Arab life. The book combines intellectual depth and literary style, presenting rich cultural and scientific content that reflects its author’s broad vision in the field of Arabic literature.
descriptions.946: Collection of Proverbs is a book written by Abu al-Fadl Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Naysaburi, known as al-Maydani. This book is considered a reference in ancient Arabic proverbs. Its number of pages is no less than two thousand pages divided into thirty sections, full of narratives, poetry, and proverbs of Arabs in pre-Islamic times and in Islam. It is said that after Al-Zamakhshari wrote Al-Muqtassa in Proverbs of the Arabs, he came across this book and looked at it for a long time and liked it very much. It is said that he regretted writing Al-Muqtasas because he He recorded a collection of proverbs in good composition, placement, simplicity of expression, and abundance of benefits.
descriptions.947: The Bahrain Al-Yaziji Complex is a collection of literary maqams that reflect the flavor of different Arabic dialects. The book consists of many maqamat, each of which represents a specific Arabic dialect, such as Bedouin, Levantine, Aleppo, and others. Maqamat usually revolves around exciting stories and events, starting with the story of Suhail bin Abbad, who travels through the desert and meets various characters, which opens the door to interesting adventures and stories that reflect the culture and customs of those regions.
descriptions.948: The book “Lectures of Writers and Dialogues of Poets and Rhetorics” by Al-Ragheb Al-Isfahani deals with topics related to literature and rhetoric, as it focuses on the concept of reason, knowledge, ignorance, and what is related to them. The book also deals with dialogues between writers, poets, and rhetoricians, reviewing the virtues of reason and its necessity in achieving other virtues, and also reviewing the disadvantages of ignorance and foolishness. The book also points out the importance of piety in preserving the mind, discusses the difficulty of combining reason and seriousness, and warns against following whims.
descriptions.949: The book “Selections of Arab Poets” by Ibn Al-Shajari deals with selections of poems by famous Arab poets, combining poetic poems with critical definitions of them. The book covers poems by prominent poets such as Laqit bin Yamar, Hatem Al-Tai, Tarfa bin Al-Abd, Zuhair, and other well-known poets. The book focuses on presenting examples of the best written in ancient Arabic poetry, while providing historical and critical information about the poets and their poems.
descriptions.950: The Book of Marzban-Nama is a rhetorical literary work that contains tales and anecdotes of an educational nature, taken from the tongues of animals, birds, and jinn, similar to the Book of Kalila and Dimna in its style and pattern. The author narrates different stories through multiple verses, including proverbs and proverbs, designed to enlighten the reader about the principles and ethics of life. The book has been translated several times over the centuries from Tiberius to Persian and Arabic, with poetry and proverbs added in each new version.
descriptions.951: The book “Sources of Pre-Islamic Poetry” by critic Nasser al-Din al-Assad deals with an in-depth study of writing topics and tools in the pre-Islamic era, with a focus on the origins, development, and codification of poetry. The book also deals with the methods of transmitting pre-Islamic poetry through narration and listening, and discusses the problem of setting and style in pre-Islamic poetry, trying to understand its role in shaping Arabic literature throughout the ages.
descriptions.952: The book “The Wrestler of Lovers” by Al-Sarraj Al-Reader deals with the topic of love and passion from a literary and philosophical perspective, reviewing different opinions and sayings about the nature of love and its effects on humans. The book deals with multiple aspects of love as a disease and illness that afflicts people of circumstances, and as the first play and the last spoilage, with a review of cases of pious lovers and witnesses. He also points out that the sins of lovers are often forced as a result of their emotional states, and reviews the cases of famous crazy poets in the Arab heritage.
descriptions.953: The book “The Aspiration of Souls and the Theater of Humanization in the Salt of the People of Andalusia” by the minister and writer Abu Nasr al-Fath ibn Khaqan deals with literary expositions of prominent figures in Andalusia, including ministers, scholars, and writers. The book is divided into three sections: the first deals with ministers and state clerks, the second focuses on scholars and notable judges, and the third section deals with the distinguished writers of Andalusia. The book aims to show the exploits of these figures and revive them after they were unknown, and provides a comprehensive picture of the nobility of the Andalusians and their superiority in various literary, scientific and political fields.
descriptions.954: This book, “Institutes of Textualization of the Evidences of Summary,” by Abu al-Fath al-Abbasi, deals with topics from the sciences of literature and rhetoric, focusing on the evidence of the science of meanings, rhetoric, and al-Badi’. The book deals with evidence of the various literary sciences, relying on poetry as a tool to explain and clarify the concepts of these sciences, and it reviews the works of various ancient and modern poets. The book aims to provide interpretations and analyzes of evidence of literature, with a focus on clarifying the meanings and rhetorical and creative methods in poetry.
descriptions.955: The key to science. A book on the sciences of the Arabic language compiled by Yusuf bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Ali Al-Sakaki Al-Khwarizmi Al-Hanafi Abu Yaqoub.
descriptions.956: The book “Ufid of Sciences and Exterminator of Concerns” by Al-Khwarizmi deals with various topics in Islamic literature and sciences, including monotheism, the rulings of prophecy, and the miracles of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book also presents the wonders of the creation of man and the universe, and reviews a diverse Islamic history, with a focus on the biography of the Prophet and the conquests. It also deals with psychology and the treatment of psychological disorders, and contains chapters on Arabic language and etiquette, making it a comprehensive scientific masterpiece that combines the literary and scientific arts.
descriptions.957: Al-Hariri’s Maqamat are literary maqamat written by Muhammad Al-Hariri Al-Basri (446 AH/1054 AD - 6 Rajab 516 AH/September 11, 1122 AD). They are among the most famous maqamats that belong to an art of Arabic writing that was invented by Badi’ al-Zaman al-Hamdhani. They are a type of short stories full of representational movement, in which the dialogue takes place between two people, and whose author is committed to craftsmanship. Literary literature that relies on assonance and badi’. Maqamat Al-Hariri, organized by Muhammad Al-Hariri and its story drawn by Yahya bin Mahmoud Al-Wasiti, revolves around extorting money through trickery through the adventures of its hero, Abu Zaid Al-Sarouji, narrated by Al-Harith bin Hammam. …
descriptions.958: Al-Zamakhshari’s Maqamat are fifty maqamat written by Abu Al-Qasim Al-Zamakhshari. Their goals are divided into wisdom, commandments, literature, and history. The author drank in them and scooped up from the sea of ​​literature what he exuded with his clarification, and mastered the pearls of speech. He also sought to explain the eloquence of the language and the beauty of its words. In the introduction, he gave advice to those who read the book carefully to read it, pay attention to every word, and understand the meanings contained. He also advised that the book should only be presented to a scholar, religious person, or writer. He also asked those who wanted to copy the book to copy it in good handwriting and put the author’s name on it. He also asked to pray for his mercy and satisfaction.
descriptions.959: This book, “Maqamat Al-Suyuti,” written by Al-Suyuti, deals with types of spices, medicinal herbs, and flowers, providing a literary description of their properties and benefits. The book focuses on certain types of perfumes, such as musk, amber, saffron, and civet, and presents them in the form of literary maqamat, relying on aesthetic description and rhetoric in dealing with its topics. The book falls within the category of literature and rhetoric, and aims to provide cultural and literary information about the mentioned spices and plants in a distinct manner from a literary standpoint.
descriptions.960: The Maqamat of Badi al-Zaman al-Hamdhani, the first book written on the art of Maqamat. However, it did not receive the care given to the Maqamat al-Hariri in explaining it and interpreting its strangeness, for reasons known to those who looked at the Maqamat of Badi al-Zaman and his letters, such as letter No. 167. The largest part of it was lost, and only 52 remained of the 400 Maqamat, which is the total of the book, and the copyists destroyed them, as Professor Imam Muhammad Abduh says: It harms the principles and takes the mind away from the intelligible, and a deficiency shakes the methods and destroys the structure of the structures, so if the one looking into it is weak, he is lost and confused, and if he is a knowledgeable person, he is not safe from stumbling. …
descriptions.961: The one who missed the singer is a book written by Al-Thaalabi Al-Nisaburi. A book on poetic selections, which is considered the appendix to Al-Tha’alabi’s book (The Best I Have Heard) due to the agreement of the two books in approach, material and style, and because it opens most of its chapters by saying: (The best I have heard in this) and it is likely that Al-Tha’alabi wrote it after finishing the orphanage. Abu Al-Ala did not seem to have become famous during Al-Tha’alabi’s writing of his book (The Best I Have Heard) so he did not mention Abu Al-Ala in it, while we find him interested in Abu Al-Ala’s poetry in his book (Who Was Absent from Him). Al-Mutrib) which indicates that it is one of his later books. …
descriptions.962: The book “Prose of Durr in Lectures” is a literary and rhetorical work that deals with a range of religious and moral topics, as the author focuses on Qur’anic verses and important Islamic topics such as prayer, justice, trust, jihad, and monotheism. The book opens with an introduction that begins with praise and praise to God, then calls on the author to seek help and guidance from God, emphasizing the importance of gratitude, trust, and adherence to Islamic law. The book aims to remind the reader of the importance of religious and moral values ​​in the life of a Muslim.
descriptions.963: The book “Naja’ al-Ra’id wa Shar’at al-Wād fi al-Mutādāf wa al-Mutawadir,” by Ibrahim al-Yāzīji, deals with multiple topics related to human creation, instincts, and faculties, as well as the natural conditions of man. The book focuses on describing the physical and psychological characteristics of humans, and discusses various topics from good looks and ugliness, to moral qualities such as generosity and cowardice, through to human instincts and their effects. The book also deals with human natural conditions, such as sleep and satiety, providing a comprehensive study of human nature and its various manifestations.
descriptions.964: The book “Nuzhat al-Jalasa fi Women’s Poetry” by al-Suyuti deals with a group of poems by modern women poets, avoiding mentioning earlier Arab women in previous eras, such as pre-Islamic women and female companions. The book focuses on presenting the poetry of women from the late eras, while providing brief information about their lives and their most important poetic productions. The book deals with various poetic topics that reflect the emotional and social experiences of women at that time, while preserving literature and poetic eloquence.
descriptions.965: The book deals with the emergence of modern prose and its development in Arabic literature, showing how it got rid of the harms of the past and rose from sluggishness and dross to strength, health, and artistic beauty. The author focuses on other prose arts, such as the letter, the book, and the article, and traces their development over a century and a half, reviewing the contributions of prominent figures in Egypt, Iraq, and the Levant, and the influence of the press on the development of style.
descriptions.966: The book “Nashwār al-Muḥāḍara wal-Akhbar al-Muḍaratah” by Judge al-Muhsin bin Ali al-Tanukhi is a literary work that deals with tales and news from gatherings of sages and thinkers, and combines humor and wisdom, providing readers with examples of various wisdom and sayings from prominent figures in Islamic history. The book focuses on topics related to political wisdom, ethics, and commercial savvy, relying on what the author heard from the mouths of men and discussed among them in councils, without transferring any material from other books, which makes it a unique source in its field.
descriptions.967: The Ecstasy of the Drunk from the Redhead of Thithkar Al-Ghazal is a book written by Abu Al-Tayeb Muhammad Siddiq Khan bin Hassan bin Ali bin Lutfullah Al-Husseini Al-Bukhari Al-Qanuji (1248 - 1307 AH / 1832 - 1890 AD). It is a book that is included in the books written on love, love, love, and infatuation. It is a statement of love, lovers, and beloved women, and the related developments of boyhood. And Al-Hayman, and he mentioned the opinions of the ancients and the wise about love, including Pythagoras, Plato, Aristotle, Ibn Sina and others, and mentioned the opinions of the Sufis, including Al-Junaid Al-Baghdadi. Then he touched on the afflictions of the heart and its attachment to beloved women, and narrated stories well-known in the Arab heritage about passion and platonic love, and what lovers have become in their behavior and conditions, and the types of women, and a statement of…
descriptions.968: The book “The Flow of Flowers in Selected Poems” by Shaker Shuqair Al-Batlouni includes a collection of poems, sayings, and poetic verses selected from various literary topics. The book deals with various poetic topics such as flirtation, praise, wisdom, enthusiasm, pride, reproach, flowers, wine, and lamentation, based on the poems of famous poets from different eras. The book focuses on presenting examples of the finest writings on these topics, while preserving the beauty and elegance of poetic language.
descriptions.969: Nafh al-Tayyib min al-Ghusn al-Andalus is a book of literature and rhetoric that deals with the history of Andalusia and its Islamic civilization. The author Al-Maqri Al-Tilmisani focuses on describing the beauty of Andalusia and its geographical and historical characteristics, pointing out important events such as its conquest and its contributions to the spread of Islam. The book also mentions the travels of scholars and writers between Andalusia and the Levant, and devotes a part to the life of the minister Lisan al-Din, who had a prominent role in Andalusian history.
descriptions.970: The book Criticism of Poetry by Qudama bin Jaafar falls within the framework of Arab criticism. It came in the context of a cultural movement influenced by logic, philosophy, and the Greek heritage, especially Aristotle.
descriptions.971: Nihayat al-Arb fi Funun al-Adab is a literary encyclopedia completed by the Egyptian historian Shihab al-Din al-Nuwairi before the year 721 AH. In it, Al-Nuwairi collected a summary of the Arab heritage in its two parts, literature and history. The book consists of thirty-three volumes containing more than four thousand and four hundred pages. As Ibn Katheer mentioned, he used to copy it with his own hand and sell the copy for a thousand dirhams. …
descriptions.972: The Book of Inspiration of the Pen is a literary work by Mustafa Sadiq Al-Rafi’i, one of his best works. The book consists of three parts, which is a collection of his critical and constructive articles inspired by contemporary social life, stories, and Islamic history scattered in many famous Egyptian newspapers and magazines at the beginning of the last century, such as: Al-Risalah, Al-Muayyad newspaper, Al-Balagh, Al-Muqtafat, Al-Siyasa, and others. …
descriptions.973: This book deals with the lineage and events of the Al-Jarbaa family, and reviews their journey from the south of the Arabian Peninsula to the north, and their move to Iraq, with a focus on prominent members of the family and its various branches. In his research, the author relies on oral narration and colloquial poetry to enhance the available historical information, and aims to present a comprehensive picture of the role of the Al-Jarba family in building national identity in Iraq and Syria, while pointing out some of the negatives that were associated with their presence in those regions.
descriptions.974: This book deals with the study of genealogy in Oman, where its author, Salem Al-Siyabi, collected as much information as he could about the lineage of different Omani tribes. The book focuses on dealing with the lineages of many Omani clans and families, relying on an unorganized method of arrangement and division, which makes it a useful reference for reviewing information related to the origins of the people of Oman when needed.
descriptions.975: This book, “Genealogies of the Arabs,” by Al-Sahari, deals with the history of the Arabs’ lineage from the beginning of creation until Qahtan ibn Hud, passing through the story of Adam (peace be upon him) and his descendants, all the way to Noah (peace be upon him) and his children. The book also mentions the lineage of the Arab tribes and their branches, while presenting some news and poems related to important historical events, trying to be brief and concise in its narration so that the information is clearer and easier for the reader.
descriptions.976: The Book of the Wreath is a book written by the geographer and historian Lisan al-Yemen Abi Muhammad al-Hasan bin Ahmed al-Hamdani. It is his most important book, and its full title is The Wreath - From the News of Yemen and the Genealogy of Himyar. It consists of ten parts that combine the sciences of news, archeology, genealogy, and language. It is considered one of the most famous historical books in Yemen and the region. Researchers consider it an encyclopedia of Yemeni civilization for the pre-Islamic period. The Book of the Wreath by al-Hamdani is in addition to being a book. History, genealogies, monuments, and antiquities. It is also considered a book of historical and cultural identity for Yemen, with the enormous cultural and historical heritage Yemen has, most of which remains unknown to this day. …
descriptions.977: This book, “Al-Inas bi-lām al-‘ālīm,” deals with the subject of Arab genealogies, and aims to clarify the similarities and differences between famous names and surnames in Arab tribes. The author focuses on clarifying the subtle differences between similar names to avoid confusion, and the book includes the names of individuals and tribes from Adnan, Qahtan, and other Arab dynasties. It also aims to help the average reader in literature avoid distortions in Arabic genealogies, and contains poetic verses and comments related to the names mentioned. The book is organized according to the letters of the dictionary, making it easy to access the required information.
descriptions.978: This book deals with the subject of Arab genealogies, focusing on the lineage of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his families, then moving on to review the lineage of the main Arab tribes such as Kinana, Asad, Hudhayl, Rabia, and Thaqif. The author aims to clarify lineages, explain their origins in relation to family ties, and know the legal rulings related to them, reviewing sayings of the Prophet and his companions about the importance of knowing lineages.
descriptions.979: Muhammad bin Hamad Al-Bassam, in his book “Al-Durar Al-Mafakhir fi Akhbar Al-Arabi Al-Akhir”, presents a detailed study of the conditions of the Arab tribes in various regions of the Arabian Peninsula, focusing on describing the tribes of Yemen, Tihama, Hijaz, Najd, Oman, Iraq, and Aleppo. The book comprehensively covers the history of the tribes and their social, cultural and military characteristics, with a focus on their knights, heroes and fighting forces, providing a comprehensive picture of the customs and traditions of these tribes and their importance in the Arab arena.
descriptions.980: This book deals with the topic of Arab genealogies, focusing on the lineage of Arab tribes and their classes. In his various chapters, the author Al-Mughiri discusses the origins of the Arab Arab and Mozarab tribes, relying on reliable historical and literary sources. The book aims to compile a brief overview of genealogy, including the origins of the Arabs and their lineage, while pointing out the importance of this science in introducing people to their ancestry and family ties.
descriptions.981: Ibn al-Kalbi's Collection of Genealogies of the Arabs is a detailed study of the origins and history of the Arab tribes, focusing on their lineage and branches. The book deals with the genealogies of the main Arab tribes, starting with Maad bin Adnan, and reviews their development over the generations, relying on historical sources and popular narratives at that time. The book also includes mentions of prominent members of the tribes and their families, with reference to some historical events related to them.
descriptions.982: This book deals with the lineage of Quraysh, focusing on omitting some individuals or families from this lineage. The author begins by mentioning the lineage of Abd Manaf bin Qusayy and his families, then moves on to discuss other members of the Quraysh, such as the sons of Abu Lahab and the allies of Banu Hashim. The book also includes lineages of other members of the Quraish tribes, such as Banu Abd bin Qusayy and Banu Makhzum. The book aims to provide a comprehensive picture of the lineage of Quraysh, with a focus on some specific personalities and lineages.
descriptions.983: This book, “The Haste of the Beginner and the Virtue of the End in Lineage” by Al-Hazmi is a book on genealogy, in which the author studies and traces the lineage of Arab and Persian tribes. The book is divided according to the letters of the alphabet, and in each section it reviews the genealogies of the tribes that are attributed to the aforementioned letter, with a focus on the importance of knowing genealogies in the science of hadith and building the foundations of Islam. The book aims to provide a brief introduction to each type of Hadith science, highlighting the importance of knowledge of genealogy as one of the foundations of this science.
descriptions.984: The Encyclopedia of Iraqi Tribes is a huge four-volume book, written in the first half of the twentieth century AD, by the professor, historian, writer, and lawyer Abbas Al-Azzawi, about the history and genealogy of the Iraqi Arab Bedouin and rural (Shawiyya) tribes, and the Kurdish tribes. Its natural extension is in Syria, and the book is considered one of the strongest references in this regard.
descriptions.985: This book is by Ibn al-Bayhaqi, and it deals with the subject of genealogy and surnames in Islam, explaining the virtue of this science and its importance in investigating Arab lineages, detailing the groups of people, and linking them to their origins. The book also mentions the virtues of the Quraish and Banu Hashim and refers to the names of some prominent people who were interested in this science in the past. The book focuses on the historical and social aspect of genealogy, relying on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths to clarify the importance and virtue of this science.
descriptions.986: This book is by Imam Ibn al-Qaysrani, and it is one of the books that deals with lineages, as it focuses on dealing with lineages that agree in a line that is symmetrical in dots and precision. The book deals with different lineages arranged according to the letters of the alphabet, starting from Alif to Z, while providing information about the personalities associated with those lineages, and mentioning some of the scholars and jurists who were attributed to them.
descriptions.987: The book “Genealogies” by Abd al-Karim al-Sam’ani is a genealogical work that deals with the lineage of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the Quraish tribe and many Arab tribes, relying on previous sources and his sheikhs. The book focuses on studying the lineage of the Arabs and their origins, reviews the history of some tribes and their journeys, and mentions the praise of scholars of previous generations for its author.
descriptions.988: Al-Inbahit Ali Tribes of Narrators is a book on genealogies, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Abd al-Barr (368 AH - 463 AH). The author mentioned in his book the genealogies of the tribes that narrated hadiths on the authority of the Messenger of God. This comes out of knowing the genealogy of everyone who narrated a hadith about the Prophet Muhammad in order to demonstrate the extent of their truthfulness.
descriptions.989: The Jewel in the Lineage of the Prophet and His Ten Companions is a book on the genealogies of the Arab tribes written by Muhammad bin Abi Bakr al-Bari, who lived in the seventh century AH between the years (605 AH - 665 AH), and who completed writing the book in the year 644 AH. The book is divided into two parts and is more than a thousand pages long.
descriptions.990: This book, “Al-Lubab fi Tahdheeb Al-Ansab” by Ibn Al-Atheer, is one of the historical works that dealt with genealogies and accounts. The book deals with the lineage of families and families through the letters of the dictionary, indicating their origins and the history of their emergence and spread. The book begins with the letter Alif and gradually moves to the rest of the letters. In each chapter, it reviews the names of the families associated with those letters, mentioning their origins and places of origin.
descriptions.991: This book deals with the genealogy of civilian families, focusing on the families that attribute to themselves the relative authenticity of the supporters who supported the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book deals with a number of famous houses in Medina and attributes them to the Ansar, mentioning their history and main families. The book aims to provide information about the noble lineages of Medina and reveal the pride and dignity associated with them.
descriptions.992: The book “Sentences of Noble Lineages” by Al-Baladhuri is a genealogical heritage that deals with the lineage of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his family from Noah to Adnan, and reviews the genealogies of the Arab tribes branching out from Adnan and Mudar. The book focuses on tracing lineages through ancient times, and provides historical and mythical information about the origins of the Arabs and their ancestors, relying on ancient sources and narratives circulating at that time.
descriptions.993: The collection of Quraysh lineages and their information by Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar is a detailed study of the Quraysh lineage and its members, focusing on specific branches of Al-Alat, Zaban bin Sayyar and others. The book deals with the genealogy and discusses the sayings of poets and verses of poetry related to tribal members, relying on popular narratives and legends. The book combines history, genealogy, and poetry, presenting a comprehensive picture of the Quraish tribe and its branches.
descriptions.994: Qala’id al-Juman fi Introducing the Tribes of the Arabs of Time is a book by Ahmed bin Ali bin Ahmed al-Fazari al-Qalqashandi, which he completed in the year 819 AH. Haji Khalifa mentioned it as Qala’id al-Juman in his introduction to the tribes of the Arabs of the Age, and said that it was written by the father of the author of Nihayat al-Arb, but he deviated from the truth in his statement, as Qala’id al-Juman and Nihayat al-Arb are two books by the same author. The book was edited by Ibrahim Al-Ebiary and published by the Egyptian Book House and the Lebanese Book House.
descriptions.995: The book “Lub al-Lubab fi Tahrir al-Ansab” by al-Suyuti is an encyclopedia of genealogy that follows the letters of the dictionary to trace the lineage of people and tribes. The book deals with Arab and Islamic genealogies, mentioning the geographical locations associated with them, and reviews the names of places and people starting with the letter Alif, relying on previous sources with the addition of comments and corrections from its author. The book is brief but comprehensive in its content, directed to skilled hadith scholars who need a reliable source in the field of genealogy.
descriptions.996: This book is a summary of genealogy, covering the names of Arab and Islamic cities, villages, and towns, along with some information about them. It is classified according to the letters of the alphabet, starting from the letter hamza to yaa, and provides a brief definition of each name mentioned, indicating its geographical location and relatives, if any. The book is written by Abbas Al-Madani, and aims to highlight the importance of genealogy and preserve it from loss.
descriptions.997: This book, “The Various Tribes and Their Compounds,” by Muhammad bin Habib Al-Baghdadi, deals with the study and tracing of the lineages and origins of the Arab tribes, indicating their various lineages and branches. The book includes a number of major Arab tribes, such as the Azd, Tamim, Rabi'ah, Asad bin Khuzaymah, Hamdan, Tai, Muzainah, Khuza'a, Quraish, and Awud, while providing information about their origins and branches.
descriptions.998: This dictionary deals with Arab tribes throughout various eras, from before Islam until the modern era, in various Arab and Islamic countries. It focuses on studying the origins, branches, history, geography and other aspects related to the Arab tribes, mentioning the sources on which the author relied in his research.
descriptions.999: This book is a dictionary that deals with the tribes of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, arranged alphabetically, and aims to provide brief information about the tribes and their branches, focusing on the tribes that have a current presence in the country, and avoiding addressing the ancient tribes or those from which their branches have been completely displaced. It has been prepared in a succinct manner, avoiding going into the historical details of genealogies or dwelling on the various sayings about the branching of large tribes.
descriptions.1000: This book deals with the study of the lineage of the Adnan and Qahtan tribes, and reviews the history and origins of many of the main Arab tribes, such as the Mudar, Qays, Khandaf, and Quraysh tribes. The book also mentions the lineage of the Hudhail, Hawazin, and Azd tribes, and provides information about the lineages of the Banu Umayyad and Banu Abd Manaf. The book relies on historical sources and ancient genealogies in dealing with its subject.
descriptions.1001: This book, “The Lineage of Quraysh,” by Al-Zubairi Musab bin Abdullah, deals with the study of the lineage of Quraysh from Ma’ad bin Adnan until the era in which the book was written. The book focuses on tracing the lineage of individuals and lineages within the Quraish tribe, with attention to the lineage of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his relatives from the Banu Hashim and Banu Abd Shams. The book relies on historical and genealogical sources in its treatment of this topic, and provides a comprehensive vision of the lineage of Quraysh across various branches and dynasties.
descriptions.1002: This book, “The Lineage of Ma`ad and the Great Yemen,” by Ibn al-Kalbi, deals with the study of genealogy in Yemen and the northern Arabian Peninsula, focusing on the lineage of the Adnan and Qahtan tribes. The book studies the lineage of Adnanite tribes such as Bani Asad, Bani Taim Allah, Bani Rabi’a, and Bani Iyad, in addition to other Qahtan tribes. He aims to document the lineage of these tribes and their relationship to their historical and genealogical origins, relying on the historical and literary sources available in his time.
descriptions.1003: The Book of Nihayat al-Arb fi Ma’rifat al-Arab Genealogies: A book on genealogies written by Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ahmad al-Qalqashandi, who died in the year 821 AH. He was a researcher in knowledge of Arab tribes and their genealogies. His work divided it into: an introduction, a purpose, and a conclusion. The introduction was to mention matters needed in genealogy and knowledge of tribes. The purpose is to know the details of the genealogies of the Arab tribes, and it contains two chapters: the first is to mention the pillar of the Prophet’s lineage and the lineages that branch out from it, and the second is to mention the details of the tribes arranged in alphabetical order, in addition to mentioning what was known of their homes in that era. The conclusion is to mention matters related to the conditions of the Arabs. Of religions, boasts, wars, fires, and markets.
descriptions.1004: This book, “The Dangerous Relationships in Mention of the Emirs of the Levant and the Peninsula,” by the scholar Izz al-Din Ibn Shaddad, deals with a historical and cultural description of the city of Aleppo, the Levant, and the Peninsula. The author focuses on mentioning the princes and rulers who ruled the region, while providing historical and geographical information about the cities, castles, mosques, and monuments. The book also deals with the virtues of the Levant and the hadiths and stories mentioned about its virtues, with a detailed description of its architecture, buildings, and geographical borders.
descriptions.1005: In his book "Geography", Ibn Sa'id al-Maghribi provides a detailed description of the world from a geographical and travel perspective, dividing the globe into nine main sections, including what is behind the equator to the south, and the first to seventh regions, with a detail of the first part of the southern region, which includes Sudanese cities, deserts, and the springs of the Nile River. The book describes the Earth as a sphere surrounded by water, and divides the globe into sections based on width and length, focusing on the details of the natural and human geography in those regions.
descriptions.1006: This book, written by Yaqut al-Hamawi, deals with topics related to geography and history, focusing on the study of sites, buildings, and places known as houses, houses, and deira in various regions. The book is divided into multiple sections, each section deals with detailed research on a specific house, house, or monastery, mentioning its historical, geographical, and cultural details. The book aims to provide comprehensive information about these sites and their importance in the historical and geographical context of the region.
descriptions.1007: The book “Al-Diyarat” was written by Abu Al-Faraj Al-Asbahani, and it includes news and biographies about different monasteries located in different parts of the Levant and Iraq. The book deals with the history of these monasteries and the most important events and stories associated with them, with a focus on Deir Ablaq, Deir al-Ala, and other famous monasteries. The book also covers a description of the monasteries, their geographical location, and historical stories related to them, with reference to some of the prominent figures who lived or visited these monasteries.
descriptions.1008: A book on travel literature and biographies, written by the author Khaled Al-Balawi to set the course of his Hijaz journey and describe the landmarks of the eastern destination, following the mention of the virtuous sheikhs and scholars he met on his way. The book combines geographical descriptions of countries and homes, and an introduction to prominent scholars and writers, with examples of their speech and eloquence.
descriptions.1009: The History of the Clairvoyant is a geographical book written by the historian Ibn al-Mujawar (601 AH - 690 AH). In his book, the author talked about describing the countries of Yemen, Mecca, and the Hijaz. He began by talking about Mecca and then ended with Bahrain. In it, he reviewed the famous navigational guides and learned about the ancient sciences of navigation that describe navigation lines and their lengths between southern Arabia and the island of Java. He devoted part of his book to describing the cities of Aden and Jeddah. It is believed that Ibn al-Mujawar wrote his book Al-Mustabsir before 1233 AD.
descriptions.1010: This book is an introduction to the places mentioned in Ibn Katheer’s book, The Beginning and the End, as it deals with the cities, towns, castles, and historical sites mentioned in the original book. The book focuses on clarifying and interpreting the geographical and historical sites mentioned at the beginning and end, while providing brief information about each site, including its geographical location and the most important historical events related to it.
descriptions.1011: This book deals with its author's trip to Egypt, as he details his companionship with Judge Joy Zadeh on their trip from Damascus to Cairo. The text focuses on describing the adventures and experiences that the author went through during his journey, and also refers to visiting the citadel in Jerusalem and inspecting the church there based on government orders. The book falls within the category of geographical and descriptive travelogues, and provides a glimpse into the historical and cultural events in the region during the period of the author's writing.
descriptions.1012: The Danger of the Spectrum in the Journey of Winter and Summer: It is one of the Arabic books written by the writer Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Saeed Al-Salmani Al-Lushi, originally from the Andalusian Granati, “Abu Abdullah,” famous for the tongue of religion Ibn Al-Khatib (who died in 776 AH). It is a book in which the writer described an official trip he made to Granada with the Prince of Muslims, Abu Al-Hajjaj Yusuf bin Nasr. The goal of this trip was to inspect the conditions of the eastern borders of the Kingdom of Granada, and the departure of the Sultan’s cavalcade from Granada was on Sunday, Muharram 17, 747 AH. …
descriptions.1013: This book, “The Oddities of Expatriation and the Excursion of Minds in Going,” by Shihab al-Din al-Alusi, deals with its author’s travels and experiences in the countries he visited, with a focus on the oddities and wonders he saw and important events he encountered during his travels. In his various chapters, Al-Alusi discusses matters subject to Istikhara, hadiths, and stories related to his travels, expressing his feelings and personal impressions regarding the places and events he saw. The book combines descriptions of geography, history, and local culture in the areas visited by its author, while adding his personal observations and opinions about what he saw and heard.
descriptions.1014: This book deals with Egypt's virtues and distinctive characteristics, compared to other countries, reviewing its historical, scientific, and religious effects. The author, Abu Omar Al-Kindi, mentions Egypt’s virtue in religion and the world, and cites Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths that indicate Egypt’s great status. The book also lists the names of scholars, sages, jurists, and ascetics who lived there throughout the ages, showing what made it a preferred country in the eyes of God and His Messenger.
descriptions.1015: The book “Nafadat al-Jarab fi Alaalat al-Igharaba,” written by Lisan al-Din Ibn al-Khatib, is one of the books that deals with various topics related to history, geography, and politics in Morocco and Andalusia. The book deals with different periods of the rule of the Marinid and Barmekh sultanates, and mentions important political and social events, in addition to some of the works and poems written by Ibn al-Khatib during that period. The book also refers to the author's travels and visits to some cities and mountains, with a focus on political and social relations in those places.
descriptions.1016: Antiquities of the Country and News of the People is a book on history and geography written by Abu Abdullah bin Zakaria Al-Qazwini. The book contains three introductions about the need to establish cities and villages, the characteristics of the country, and the impact of the environment on the population, plants and animals. It also presented the regions of the Earth known at that time, dividing them into seven regions and presenting the characteristics of each of them and its cities. This book also includes news of nations, biographies of scholars, writers, and sultans, and descriptions of whirlwinds, a flying dragon, a water fountain, and more.
descriptions.1017: The book “Akam Al-Murjan fi Mention of Famous Cities Everywhere” by author Ishaq bin Al-Hussein Al-Munajjim provides a comprehensive overview of important cities and places in the Islamic world, covering their history, geography, and characteristics. The book includes cities of religious and cultural importance such as Mecca, Medina, and Jerusalem, in addition to other cities of historical importance such as Baghdad, Sanaa, and Damascus. The book deals with various topics related to these cities, without addressing recent details or specific facts.
descriptions.1018: The best analysis of the knowledge of the regions is a geographical book, written by Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Maqdisi, known as al-Maqdisi al-Bashari (336 AH - 380 AH). The book is one of the most famous geographical encyclopedias that appeared in the fourth century AH - the tenth century AD. Its author, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ahmad al-Maqdisi, singled out the mention of the Islamic regions and the seas, lakes, and rivers in them, and described their famous cities, their mentioned cities, their inhabited houses, and their used roads. And the elements of drugs and machines, and the metals of carrying and trade, and the differences between the people of countries in their words, voices, tongues, and colors, and their sects, and their measures and weights, and their money and exchange, and the description of their food and drink and their food and their fruits and their water, and knowledge...
descriptions.1019: This book is about places that have the same pronunciation and different names, and it is a classification of countries, geography, and travel. In this book, the author discusses places and countries that share the same pronunciation but differ in meaning and name, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. It mentions what is related to the places mentioned in the battles of the Prophet and the stories of the Companions, with reference to some of the places mentioned in the days of the Arabs, trying to link them with historical and modern news.
descriptions.1020: The book “References to the Knowledge of Visits” by the traveler Al-Harawi Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abi Bakr bin Ali presents a scientific journey through various cities and towns in the Islamic world, focusing on visiting historical and religious monuments and shrines. The book covers the itineraries of visits to cities such as Aleppo, Antioch, Qinnasrin, and Damascus, with a brief description of their locations and their historical and religious importance. The author aims to provide brief references to familiarize the reader with the landmarks of these cities and their tributaries, thus providing a useful historical and touristic reference.
descriptions.1021: Al-Istibsar fi Aja’ib al-Amsar, a book that combines the style of paths and kingdoms and travel literature. Its author is an unknown Marrakesh. He began writing it in the year 587 AH and finished it in the year 591 AH. Parts of it were printed for the first time in Vienna and then translated into French. Then the entire book was reprinted in Alexandria, with a French translation of the missing parts in the previous translation.
descriptions.1022: The book “Countries” by Al-Yaqoubi is a historical geographical work that describes the countries of the Islamic world at that time, explaining the emergence of countries and cities, the reasons for naming them, and the customs of their people. Al-Yaqoubi relies in its content on his personal observations and asking the people of the countries about their history, and comments on the stories he hears about the customs and traditions of their people, trying to distinguish between what is logical and what is pure myth. The book also mentions the conquest of the country by the caliphs and princes and the amount of its tax, which makes it an important and accurate geographical source for its era.
descriptions.1023: Insight into Trade in Describing the Exquisite Bags, Precious Jewels, and Precious Jewels Exported in Countries is a book written by Al-Jahiz in which he lists the types of stones and jewelry, their names, and how to distinguish between the real ones and the fake ones. It is transferred from it to clothes and apparel. He also mentioned the countries from which he brought fabrics and jewelry, what distinguished each country in its production and exported it, and what each country imported.
descriptions.1024: Mountains, Places, and Water is a famous book, written by Al-Zamakhshari. It was printed for the first time in 1857 AD, with the care of Salver Daddy Gharafa. Then it was printed in Najaf in 1968 based on another manuscript containing additions to the first edition. Then it was printed in 1968 AD with the verification of Dr. Ibrahim Al-Samarrai, relying on what the owners of the two editions had not seen. It is different from the book by Nasr al-Iskandarī (d. 561 AH): which was published by Fuad Sezgin in 1990 AD, illustrated with the title: (Places, Waters, and Mountains) and includes (2938) translations, of which (2317) are translations that fall within the subject of his book (The Compound and the Different).
descriptions.1025: The book "Climate and Vegetation Geography" provides a comprehensive overview of climate science and its applications, covering the theoretical and practical aspects of knowing weather phenomena and how to measure and analyze them. The author focuses on the close relationship between climate, agriculture, industry, and urbanization, relying on the latest scientific theories in the fields of morphology, hydrology, and agriculture. The book also includes specialized chapters on the climate of Africa and the climate of the Arab world, providing rich scientific material for geography students and specialized researchers, while ensuring ease of understanding and sufficient clarification for non-specialized students.
descriptions.1026: Al-Rawd al-Muttar fi Khabar al-Aqtar is a book written by the scholar of countries Muhammad bin Abd al-Moneim al-Himyari (d. 900 AH / 1495 AD). There is a slight disagreement in its name between the indefiniteness of the word “rawd” or its definition, as well as between “Khabar al-Aqtar” or “Akhbar al-Aqtar” or “Zikr al-Aqtar.” The manuscripts adopted by Ihsan Abbas and Lévy Provençal agree on this. It is “al-Rawd al-Mu’tar fi Khabar al-Aqtar.” Al-Himyari was keen to make his book a geographical-historical dictionary, limiting his attention, mostly to famous places related to a funny story or wisdom, sometimes even to surprising news. …
descriptions.1027: The book “Paths and Kingdoms” or “Al-Aziziya” by its author Al-Muhallabi is one of the important geographical and historical sources that dealt with describing the regions of the Fatimid state, its roads and paths. The book deals with the main trade routes and roads in the empire, with a detailed description of some cities and regions such as the Arabian Peninsula, Hadhramaut, Yemen, and Egypt. The book is distinguished by its descriptions of sites that no other travelers have ever visited, and it also reflects a Shiite point of view in some of its historical and political comments.
descriptions.1028: The book “Introduction to Geography and the Environment” by Muhammad Mahmoud Muhammadin provides a comprehensive overview of the topics of geography and the environment, examining geographical thought throughout the ages and its development from ancient civilizations to the modern era. The book focuses on the relationship between geography and the environment, and includes an introduction to the concepts of astrogeography, surface geography, water, climate, soil, and biogeography. The book also addresses the role of humans in the environment and pollution, as well as the importance of maps in geography.
descriptions.1029: Tracts and Kingdoms: A Genre of Medieval Arabic Geographical Literature. Paths and Kingdoms (Ibn Khurdadhba): A book written by Ibn Khurdadhbah. Paths and Kingdoms (Al-Bakri): The book of Abu Ubaid Al-Bakri. Paths of Kingdoms: A book by Al-Istakhri on geography. Paths and Kingdoms (Al-Muhallabi): A book written by Al-Muhallabi. Image of the Earth (Book): A book on geography and travel, written by Ibn Hawqal around the year 977 AD. Paths of Vision in the Kingdoms of the Lands: A book written by Ibn Fadlallah Al-Omari.
descriptions.1030: This book deals with the study of archaeological and historical monuments in Islamic countries, focusing on estimating ancient distances by modern standards and ancient regional divisions. In this work, author Muhammad Hassan Sharrab deals with geography and Islamic history, focusing on sites and landmarks of historical and cultural importance in the Islamic world. The book aims to clarify the cultural importance of studying archaeological monuments and explain the efforts that have been made to collect information about them, while pointing out the political and cultural motives behind the West’s interest in these studies.
descriptions.1031: The book provides basic introductions to the field of physical geography, focusing on the astronomical and physical aspects of natural phenomena. In this work, author Abdulaziz Tareeh Sharaf deals with multiple branches of physical geography, including astronomical geography, physiology, marine geology, climate, and life, with a focus on celestial bodies and the solar system. The book aims to present basic concepts in these fields to geographers from various disciplines, while recognizing the limits of human knowledge about the vast universe and the secrets it still contains.
descriptions.1032: Sermons and Consideration by Mentioning the Plans and Effects Known as the Maqrizi Plans, a book written by Ahmed bin Ali bin Abdul Qadir, Abu Abbas al-Husseini al-Ubaidi, Taqi al-Din al-Maqrizi (deceased: 845 AH), and it was investigated and published by Ayman Fouad Sayyed.
descriptions.1033: The book “The Musky Whip in the Meccan Journey” by Al-Suwaidi is an encyclopedic work in the field of countries, geography and travel. The book covers the details of the author's trip to Mecca, during which he reviews many aspects of his biography, his sheikhs, and his various writings in various sciences, in addition to his scientific personality and his poetry.
descriptions.1034: An Investigation into the Acceptable or Reprehensible Saying of India by Abu al-Rayhan al-Biruni. It is the most important and extensive book we have ever come across in describing the beliefs of the Hindus. He spent 40 years in India studying their laws, their customs regarding marriage, their food, their holidays, their systems of life, and the characteristics of their language. Brockelmann saw in it (the most important thing produced by Islamic scholars in the field of knowledge of nations).
descriptions.1035: The book “Geography of Climate and Plants” by Youssef Abdel Majeed Fayed is concerned with studying the natural climate and its relationship with plants, based on the methodology of distributing continents as geographical units. It includes detailed chapters on temperature, atmospheric pressure and wind, humidity and precipitation, air masses, climate classifications, detailed climate, and the impact of climate on humans, in addition to a review of the climate of the continents and the distribution of plants there. The book is aimed at students of geography to provide them with a comprehensive scientific foundation in physical geography.
descriptions.1036: The Boundaries of the World from the East to the West is a Persian-language geography book, published in the 10th century by an anonymous author from Cossacks, now located in northern Afghanistan. It was written in the year 372 AH by an unknown author in the Persian language, but with contact with Arabic scholarship. The book did not reach us except through a single manuscript found by the Russian orientalist Tumansky. We do not know about the writer except that he had a relationship with the court of Abu al-Harith Muhammad ibn Ahmad Farijun, the ruler of Jawzjan. The Persian text was published with an introduction by the orientalist Vasily Barthold in 1930 AD. It was translated into English by Minorsky in 1937 AD. Titled Regions of the World, as translated from Persian to Arabic by Yusuf Al-Hadi, the first edition was published in 1419 AH / 1999 AD. …
descriptions.1037: The book Kharida al-Ajaib wa Farida al-Gharaib by Siraj al-Din Ibn al-Wardi is a geographical author that falls under the classification of countries, geography, and travel. The book deals with the distances and division of the Earth, and reviews the details of the various seas, rivers, springs, and wells, in addition to describing mountains, monuments, and stones. It also includes chapters devoted to plants, fruits, legumes, grasses, and animal species, making it a comprehensive reference for the natural and geographical knowledge of its time.
descriptions.1038: The book “My Memories in Africa” by Sheikh Muhammad Al-Aboudi, Secretary-General of the League, presents a set of personal observations that he made during his trips to several African countries, with a special focus on the Islamic scene and the situation of Muslims. The content is organized into chapters on countries such as Eritrea, Abyssinia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, Congo, Zambia, Rhodesia and Malawi, allowing the reader a diverse geographical and cultural overview. The book combines travel narrative and religious reflection without going into extensive research details, making it a reference for those interested in travel and African countries from an Islamic perspective.
descriptions.1039: The book “The Journey of Ibn Battuta,” called “The Masterpiece of the Species of the Oddities of the Lands and the Wonders of Travel,” presents its author Ibn Battuta’s travels and visits to various cities and countries throughout the Islamic world in the Middle Ages. The book provides a detailed description of mosques and historical and cultural monuments, mentioning stories and events related to those places. The book focuses on the geographical, historical and religious aspects of cities such as Cairo, Jerusalem, Damascus and Baghdad, providing the reader with a comprehensive picture of Islamic civilization in that period.
descriptions.1040: The book “The Journey of Ibn Battuta, The Masterpiece of the Watchers in the Curiosities of the Lands” is a critical copy of the famous journey of the Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta. It is classified under geography and travel. It includes an introduction that explains the motives for publication and reviews issues of the text’s authenticity and summary. The text is accompanied by a detailed account of the sources of the thirty manuscripts upon which the copy was prepared, highlighting the research effort to document the original text. The content focuses on describing the countries and routes taken by travelers, with reference to some disputed points in traditional narratives.
descriptions.1041: The Journey of Ibn Jubayr or a reminder of the news about travel agreements is a book on travel literature by Muhammad Ibn Jubayr Al-Andalusi.
descriptions.1042: The book “Ibn Fadlan’s Journey to the Lands of the Turks, Russians, and Saqlabis” is a geographical travel text that presents the message of Ibn Fadlan, who was loyal to the Abbasid conquest, in which he describes his diplomatic mission to the Slavic lands on the banks of the Volga. The book includes an introduction, beginning, and itinerary of the trip, and covers his observations about the Persians, Turks, Russians, and Saqlabis, in addition to indexes and appendices documenting the details of the route and the mission. It is classified as the literature of countries, geography, and travel, and is considered a historical source that sheds light on Arab relations with the Slavic peoples in the fourth century AH.
descriptions.1043: The book “The Journey of the Serafi” by Abu Zaid Hasan bin Yazid al-Serafi is a literary text that combines geographical and economic narration of the experience of a merchant from the port of Seraph to China. It includes a description of the seas that separate India and Indus and islands such as Muljan Island, and reviews the customs and peoples of India and China in terms of kings, commercial rituals, and burials.
