The book also highlights the details of the mountains, rivers, and animals that the traveler passed through, with reference to the maritime trade routes between the Arabian Gulf and the countries of the East. This work is considered a reference in the classification of countries, geography, and travel, as it combines field observation with narrated stories about Arab and Persian merchants.
descriptions.1044: The book “The Journey of Benjamin of Tudila” is a record of the travels and writings of the Spanish Jewish traveler Benjamin ibn Rabi Yuna of Tudila. It includes a detailed description of his paths through the Byzantine Empire, the Abbasid Caliphate, India, East Asia, South Yemen and Egypt, with his analyzes of the political and religious conditions in those regions. The text also includes comments and observations on merchants and economics, as well as religious discussions dealing with relations between Jews, Christians, and Muslims. The book is classified within the literature of countries, geography, and travel, and shows an interest in historical documents and doctrinal views of the twelfth century.
descriptions.1045: Safar Nama by Nasir Khusraw is a travel book in which the author describes his journey through the Levant, Egypt, and Hijaz, providing a detailed description of the cities and religious and cultural monuments he visited, with a focus on mosques, churches, and holy graves. The book also covers a political and social description of the regions through which its author passed, adding his personal observations about the customs and traditions prevailing in those places.
descriptions.1046: This book is an excerpt from the encyclopedia "Al-Rawd Al-Ma'tar" by Al-Himyari, and it specializes in describing the country of Andalusia and its geography. The author aims to mention famous places and places of interest or interesting news, arranging them according to the letters of the dictionary to facilitate research. The book combines descriptions of countries and regions, and narration of news and facts related to them, to be a reference in countries, geography, and history.
descriptions.1047: The Characteristics of the Arabian Peninsula is a book written by the traveler and geographer Abu Muhammad al-Hamdani in the fourth century AH (tenth century AD). It describes the geography of the Arabian Peninsula and its plant life and enumerates its villages and tribes. It also evaluates the “eloquence” of the different regions. It contains a famous mention of a tribe in Yemen that still spoke a southern Arabic language, which the author called “Himyariya.” It is Al-Hamdani’s most famous book after Al-Iklil, and it is one of Al-Hamdani’s last written books, in which he mentioned “Al-Iklil,” “The Dragonfly,” and “The Secrets of Wisdom” in astronomy. …
descriptions.1048: The Picture of the Earth, also known as Paths and Kingdoms, is a book on geography and travel written by the traveler and merchant Abu al-Qasim Muhammad bin Hawqal following his travels that began in the year 331 AH. He was influenced by Al-Istakhri, who asked him to complete the book Paths and Kingdoms, which he initially agreed to, but later he chose to write a new book, relying on the book of Al-Istakhri and other geographers, in addition to his observations and the information he gleaned from his travels, so the material of the book was presented in an accurate and detailed presentation. In addition to geographical information, the book also contained a group of sciences, such as history and biography, and some chapters were presented in the form of a tourist guide. …
descriptions.1049: This book deals with the virtues of Andalusia and its people through letters and dissertations by a number of authors, focusing on praising its scholars, kings, and writers. The book expresses the historical and cultural importance of Andalusia by presenting the exploits of its people and their biography in various fields, while pointing out the shortcomings in recording and documenting these virtues over time.
descriptions.1050: The book “The Virtues of Jerusalem” by Ibn al-Jawzi, classified as a country, geography, and travel book, is a review of the importance and status of the city of Jerusalem. The book deals with the virtue of the Holy Land, and mentions the mountain on which it stands, in addition to the beginnings of the Order of Jerusalem.
descriptions.1051: This book, “General Geography Rules,” deals with the natural and human aspects of geography, and reviews natural phenomena and human factors affecting the environment. The author, Jawda Hassanein, studies the quality of the Earth as part of the solar system and discusses changes in the lithosphere and atmosphere. He also focuses on the interactions between humans and their environment, and includes population distribution, urbanization patterns, and manifestations of human activity in different environments.
descriptions.1052: The Motaker of Reluctant Determination to the Most Honorable Places by Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Al-Jawzi falls within the classification of countries, geography, and travels, and is concerned with a detailed explanation of the rituals of Hajj and the etiquette of traveling to Mecca, with a description of the environments, distances, and famous houses on the pilgrims’ routes. The book deals with the provisions of Ihram, the limits of the Sanctuary, and the virtues of charitable deeds on the road, with practical instructions for the traveler. He integrates spiritual and graphic narrative to provide a comprehensive guide to the spiritual and geographical journey.
descriptions.1053: This book, written by Ibn al-Jawzi, deals with the topic of Hajj and its context, explaining its obligations, rulings, and etiquette, and reviewing the etiquette of traveling to Mecca and how to prepare for the trip, mentioning some famous houses on the way and realistic stories that happened there. It also refers to the virtue of Hajj and the reason for the soul’s longing for Mecca, and mentions some hadiths and sayings related to Hajj.
descriptions.1054: Observatories to See the Names of Places and Spots is a historical geographical book written by Abd al-Mu’min bin Abd al-Haqq al-Quta’i al-Baghdadi (d. 739 AH) as an abbreviation of the book Dictionary of Countries, written by Yaqut al-Hamawi. It has been reposted numerous times.
descriptions.1055: The Visitors' Guide to the Graves of the Righteous by Sheikh Zain al-Din Ibn al-Muwaffaq is considered a reference in the field of countries, geography, and travel, focusing on Mount Mokattam, the tombs of the righteous, and the mosques that surround it. The book includes chapters describing the mountain, the names of the pioneers who visited it, and the virtues associated with it, in addition to details about the mosques and surrounding valleys. The author combines geographical and spiritual narratives to provide a comprehensive guide for visitors and those interested in the religious heritage of the region.
descriptions.1056: Masalik al-Absar fi Mamlik al-Amsar is a book by the historian Shihab al-Din Ahmad bin Fadlallah al-Omari.
descriptions.1057: The book Mu'jam al-Buldan is a famous encyclopedia by the writer and poet Sheikh Imam Shihab al-Din Abu Abdullah Yaqut bin Abdullah al-Hamawi al-Rumi al-Baghdadi, famous for Yaqut al-Hamawi. He wrote it between the years 1220 and 1224 AD. The Dictionary of Countries is an important historical source for describing that era, and it has been printed several times and translated into various languages. The book also contains descriptions of many towns, cities, and countries during that period in an eloquent Arabic style. He mentions the following topics in his book: mentioning the image of the Earth and what the early and late scholars said about it. News of countries that are mentioned in one place or another. A definition of the units of measurement used in his time, such as the farsakh, the post, the ball, and the mile. …
descriptions.1058: A dictionary of the names of countries and places that have been anagrammatically written is a geographical linguistic dictionary written by Abu Ubaid Al-Bakri, in which he mentioned a number of things mentioned in hadiths, news, histories, and poems, such as homes, homes, villages, and cities. It mentions its landmarks and scenes, mountains and monuments, water and wells, circuits and heats, with specific attributes and classified according to the letters of the dictionary. It is considered beneficial to the geographical field and Arab culture.
descriptions.1059: The book “The Criterion of Selection in Mentioning Institutes and Homes” by Al-Lasan al-Din Ibn al-Khatib is concerned with determining the criteria for mentioning places and institutions in geography and travel. It includes chapters dealing with the biography of the author and his evaluation by some orientalists, in addition to a review of his intellectual heritage, including works on the history of Granada, medicine, and literature. The text highlights through its excerpt that Lisan al-Din was an Andalusian minister, doctor, writer, historian, and jurist. He grew up in Granada and received his education from its sheikhs. The book concludes with a series of articles that range between medical, literary, and veterinary topics, reflecting the comprehensiveness of his interests and areas of contributions.
descriptions.1060: The book “Mandamat al-Atlal wa Samarat al-Ikhayal” by Ibn Badran falls within the literature of countries, geography, and travel. It is divided into two parts that deal with the role of the Holy Qur’an and the Noble Hadith by listing what is known as the House of the Qur’an and the House of Hadith in different cities and regions, with introductory philosophical and spiritual reflections that reflect the author’s view of existence and divine wisdom.
descriptions.1061: Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi Penetrating the Horizons, or Kitab Roger, is a travel book written by al-Idrisi. This book is considered a geographical encyclopedia of the world in the twelfth century. Al-Idrisi wrote this book for King Roger II at his request. The work is also known in Arabic as the Book of Roger and in Latin as the Tapiola Rogeriana. It contained all the sound information that the ancients knew, and added to it what he had acquired and what he had seen and observed in his travels and tests. This book remained a reference for European scholars for more than 300 years, and it contains about one thousand and seventy maps, and was verified by the orientalist Umberto Ristano.
descriptions.1062: The book “The River of Gold in the History of Aleppo,” written by Kamel Al-Ghazi, provides a comprehensive historical and geographical study of the city of Aleppo and its surroundings, with a special focus on the River of Gold and its associated other rivers and natural environments. In his chapters, the author discusses the city's geography, its borders, coasts, mountains, climate, and changes in weather conditions, in addition to its dates, names, and political developments. The book is classified under the category of countries, geography, and travel, which makes it an important reference for those searching for the history and civilization of Aleppo from a documented and encyclopedic perspective.
descriptions.1063: This book, “Wafaa al-Wafa Akhbar Dar al-Mustafa” by Al-Samhudi, is a historical heritage that deals with the history of Medina and its exploits. The author focuses on narrating the historical facts and events related to the city of the Prophet ﷺ, relying on reliable historical sources. The book covers various topics related to the city’s history, culture, and personalities, providing a comprehensive picture of this sacred town throughout the ages.
descriptions.1064: The book “The Ayyubids after Saladin” by Ali Muhammad al-Salabi is concerned with studying the stage of the Ayyubid state after the death of Saladin, focusing on the division of regions, the disputes between his successors, and the shifts of power between the just, the best, and the mighty king. The author details the alliances, victories, and loyalty that affected the course of the Ayyubid state, based on a comprehensive index that includes topics on virtuous judges, wars with the Franks, and Ayyubid homes. The book is classified as historical literature, and is considered an important link in the series of Crusades in which the political and military events of that period are reviewed.
descriptions.1065: The book “The Comprehensive Incidents and Beneficial Experiments in the Seventh Hundred” by Ibn al-Futi is classified as an automatically numbered historical work. It includes a group of diverse events that took place in the seventh century AH, from the dismissal of ministers, the conquests of cities, educational institutions, and administrative and religious details. The text focuses on a sequential narration of events with reference to their dates and personalities, based on reliable sources of that era.
descriptions.1066: Al-Dibaj by Abu Ubaidah Muammar bin Al-Muthanna is a historical work that provides an evaluation of Arab poets in pre-Islamic times and Islam, based on the opinions of their contemporaries and literary comparisons. The book includes multiple chapters dealing with the classification of poets, and sections on Arab tribes and their social and political manifestations in different periods. The text is highlighted by discussing the details of pre-Islamic poets, such as Imru’ al-Qais, al-Nabigha, and Zuhair, and projecting them onto Islamic poets to determine their preferences and comparisons.
descriptions.1067: The book “The Nisrin Whisper and the Marinid Glance” written by Ibn al-Ahmar is a historical work that specializes in narrating the events of the Marinid state, and relies on a style that combines poetic verses with detailed explanation. The index includes three main sections: the basmala, the verses, and the explanation, which indicates the integration of poetic texts with historical comments. Its classification under “History - Machine Numbered” indicates that it is a reference work concerned with documenting and interpreting the historical facts of the mentioned era.
descriptions.1068: The book “Al-Yawaqit and Al-Darb in the History of Aleppo,” written by Ismail Abu Al-Fida, is a history that deals with the history of the city of Aleppo and its rulers throughout the ages. The book focuses on mentioning the kings, princes, and governors who ruled Aleppo, while providing some information about the ministers and judges. In his historical material, the author relies on the book “The Butter of the Milk” by Mawla, the author of the exploits, Kamal al-Din Abi Hafs, Omar bin Ahmed al-Uqaili, and adds to it the additional information he found. The book also deals with the naming of Aleppo and the emergence of its citadel hill, reviewing historical accounts about the origin of the name.
descriptions.1069: This book deals with the history of Damascus in the Levant during the period of Ottoman rule, focusing on the events and challenges that the city faced during a painful period full of strife. The author, Suleiman Al-Mahasni, expresses his gratitude to God and thanks him for his blessings, and mentions the virtue of the Ottoman Empire in supporting the Islamic religion and suppressing injustice and disbelief. The book contains praise for the Sultan of the era at the time, Sultan Mustafa Khan, and points out the importance of the Ottoman rule as a continuation and inheritor of God’s commandment in the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.1070: This book deals with a daily record of the events of Damascus in the sixth century AH, documenting important political, social, economic, and religious events. The author, Al-Badiri Al-Hallaq, deals with various events during the reign of the Banu Al-Azm ministers, including earthquakes, eclipses, natural phenomena, cases of high prices and high prices, appointments to public jobs, and the entry of pilgrims into the Levant, relying in this on his daily information and the narratives of the public without accurate documentation.
descriptions.1071: The book “Aqd al-Juman fi Tarikh Ahl al-Zaman” by Badr al-Din al-Aini is a historical work that records events and events that took place in a specific period of time. The book covers important details related to countries and sultanates, such as the Sultanate of Shajar al-Durr, the Turkmen Sultanate of Aybak, and the Sultanate of King Al-Ashraf Muzaffar al-Din Musa, in addition to mentioning the deaths of notables. The book also includes an account of prominent battles and incidents, such as the defeat of the Franks and the capture of Red Avrans, and what happened after that.
descriptions.1072: Mukhtasar Sana al-Barq al-Shami is a historical work that deals with the biography of the state of Nur ad-Din Zengi and important events in the Levant and Egypt. The book includes chapters on the author's arrival in the Levant, his entry into the service of Nur al-Din, and events related to Asad al-Din and Turnshah, in addition to mentioning the death of Nur al-Din Mahmud. It also addresses the conquest of Ja'bar Castle, the Franks' march to Egypt, and the death of Asad al-Din.
descriptions.1073: The book “The Position of the Companions on Violent Incidents in the Era of the Caliphs” by Hessa Bint Abdul Karim falls within the classification of automatically numbered history. The research deals with the definition of violence, its ruling, and its effects, and reviews the position of the Companions in understanding Islamic legislation by studying the violent incidents that occurred during the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. The content is divided into chapters that address the position of the Companions on violence during the reigns of Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman, with a conclusion and references.
descriptions.1074: The book “Sham Diaries” by the author Muhammad bin Issa bin Mahmoud bin Kinan presents a series of diaries and daily reports of incidents and events that occurred in the Levant during the eleventh century AH. The book addresses various topics, including political, social and cultural events, with an emphasis on the importance of the art of history in transmitting experiences and stories across generations. The author also points out the importance of historical news in learning the lessons of the past and emulating the noble morals of the ancients.
descriptions.1075: The book “The Impact of the Salafist Call on the Unification of the Kingdom of Arabia” by Hamoud Al-Ruhaili is a historical book that studies the role of the Salafist Call in the process of unifying the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with a focus on its impact on the first and second Saudi states and the formation of the third Saudi state at the hands of King Abdulaziz. In its chapters, the author discusses the factors for the establishment of the Third State, the personality of King Abdulaziz, and an analysis of the impact of the Salafist call in unifying the country, based on linguistic and Islamic definitions of the call as stated in the opening excerpt. The book aims to show the relationship between the Salafist call and the historical process of unifying the kingdom.
descriptions.1076: This book deals with the history of the Wahhabi call in the Arabian Peninsula and the religious and urban reforms that resulted from it, and aims to correct misconceptions about it and reveal their truth. The author focuses on the personality of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and the role of Al Saud in spreading this call. He also talks about its impact on the Hijaz and the Arabian Peninsula in general. The book aims to remove the illusions and lies about this religious movement and present a clear and objective picture of it.
descriptions.1077: The book “The Impact of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s call on the reform movement of Othman bin Foudi in West Africa” by author Mustafa Massad presents a historical study of the impact of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s call, which began in the twelfth century to migrate, on the reform movement led by Othman bin Foudi in the West African continent. In his chapters, the author discusses the emergence and spread of the call, its relationship with Islam in West Africa, in addition to the role of Othman bin Foudi in implementing the principles of reform. The work focuses on clarifying how to reproduce the method of preaching wisdom, good preaching, and argumentation in a way that is best, in the context of Muslims’ quest to renew the religion in accordance with the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the righteous predecessors.
descriptions.1078: News of the Abbasid State, which includes news of Al-Abbas and his son, is a historical book that deals with the biography of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib and his sons from Abdullah bin Al-Abbas to Ali bin Abdullah, with a focus on their positions on the imamate and their role in the Abbasid call. The book includes detailed chapters on the lives of Abdullah bin Al-Abbas and Ali bin Abdullah, in addition to their news with the caliphs and governors, and ends before the establishment of the actual Abbasid Caliphate. The manuscript shows good cursive layout and dates back to the fourteenth century AH, and concludes with two lists of dates for the Umayyad and Abbasid caliphs.
descriptions.1079: The book “Akhbar Al-Radi Al-Allah wa Al-Fatihu Al-Allah” by Al-Suli is considered a historical work that focuses on the events of the Abbasid state, as it combines the historical narrative with the news of the characters Al-Radi Al-Allah and Al-Lilah Al-Fatiha. The index includes detailed dates for the years twenty-three to twenty-nine of the third century, in addition to poetic sections arranged according to different rhymes. The text begins by mentioning details of the caliphate and literary activities, which demonstrates its combination of history and poetry.
descriptions.1080: The book “Akhbar al-Zaman” by Al-Masoudi is one of the important historical sources that deals with the events and wonders of time. In this book, the author deals with various topics related to the history of nations, ancient civilizations, geography, humankind, and jinn. He also mentions news of kings and states throughout the ages. The book is distinguished by the diversity of its content and its richness with historical, geographical and cultural information, which makes it a valuable reference in the field of history and genealogy.
descriptions.1081: The book “News and Biography of the Banu Ubaid Kings” by Al-Sinhaji is a historical work that narrates the biography of the Banu Ubaid kings based on various manuscripts and sources. It includes chapters devoted to Ubayd Allah, Muhammad al-Qaim, al-Mansur, al-Mu'izz, al-Aziz, al-Hakim, al-Zahir, al-Mustansir, al-Mustali, al-Amir, al-Hafiz Abd al-Majid, al-Dhafir, al-Faiz and al-Adid, allowing the reader a comprehensive overview of the path of rule in this dynasty. The text highlights the author's method of collecting and recording news, with an indication of the differences in the lineage of some characters. The work aims to document the history of Bani Ubaid and present it as a reference for researchers in Islamic history.
descriptions.1082: The book “Asmaa al-Muttalib fi Biography of the Commander of the Faithful Ali” is considered one of the important historical books that deals with the biography of the Commander of the Faithful Ali bin Abi Talib. The book provides a comprehensive study of the life of Ali bin Abi Talib, from his birth until his martyrdom. It includes information about his name, lineage, nickname, his conversion to Islam, his most important deeds in Mecca, and his exposure to the Holy Qur’an and its impact on him in his life. The book shows the importance of Ali bin Abi Talib in Islamic history, and provides a comprehensive vision of his personality and era. The book is considered a valuable source of information about the biography of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, and provides a deep understanding of the transformations of life in the Rashidun era.
descriptions.1083: The book “Arab Markets in Pre-Islam and Islam” by Saeed Al-Afghani is a historical work that sheds light on Arab trade activities between the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods, addressing Arab commercial affairs and the stages of their development. It includes chapters devoted to Quraish commercial events, in addition to a detailed study of a number of traditional markets such as Dumat Al-Jandal Market, Al-Mashgar Market, Hajar Market, Amman Market, and others. The book aims to fill a gap in the history of Arab trade by collecting and analyzing economic, social and political information related to the markets in those eras.
descriptions.1084: Anbaa al-Ghamr bi Ibn al-Umar is a huge book containing about a thousand large pages, written by Shihab al-Din Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahmoud ibn Ahmad ibn Hajar al-Asqalani. It follows the system of yearbooks, months, and days in recording events, then follows the events of each year with notable deaths. He has mentioned in detail what is related to Egypt of these events, and it deals with the events that occurred between the years (773-850). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said, speaking about his book:
descriptions.1085: The Hanafi preaching about the news of the Fatimid imams, the caliphs, or The Hanafi preaching about the news of the successor Fatimid imams, is a historical book written by the Egyptian historian Taqi al-Din al-Maqrizi about the history of the Fatimids. This book is considered the most complete source on Fatimid history. Al-Maqrizi began by chronicling the origin of the Fatimids, the problem of their lineage, the establishment of their state in Morocco, and its four caliphs there. After that, he talked about the entry of the Fatimids into Egypt and their struggle with the Qarmatians, then he chronicled each of their caliphs, one by one, until the end of their state. In this book, Al-Maqrizi summarized what historians mentioned about the Fatimids in his era and the era that preceded it. …
descriptions.1086: Al-Akhbar Al-Tawwal is a book by the author Abu Hanifa Al-Dinauri. He is the scholar and master of arts, Ahmad bin Dawud bin Watand Al-Dinauri, the grammarian. He was a linguist, computer engineer. The book is a rich source for collecting a lot of knowledge about the history of Alexander and the Sassanian state, the conquests of Iraq, what happened between Ali and Muawiyah, the news of the Kharijites, the killing of Hussein and the strife of the Azariqs, the strife of Mukhtar, the fall of the Umayyads, and the machinations of the Alawites, especially in Khorasan while dealing with the history of the caliphs.
descriptions.1087: The book presents a historical study on the role of Al-Azhar University in the emergence of the modern literary renaissance, based on a comprehensive analysis of the stages of its founding and the development of its educational system. The author examines Al-Azhar’s cultural influence across multiple periods, including the French campaign and the era of Muhammad Ali, and reviews its role in providing schools with knowledge and scientific missions. The book also highlights Al-Azhar’s contributions to the literary and scientific heritage, highlighting its connection with mosques, mosques, and various educational institutions.
descriptions.1088: Al-Ans Al-Jalil in the History of Jerusalem and Hebron is a manuscript by the Arab historian Abu Al-Yaman Al-Qadi Mujir Al-Din Al-Hanbali. He is an Arab Hanbali judge, scholar, jurist, and historian. He was born in Ramla in 1456 (860 AH) and then moved to live in Jerusalem. Sources indicate that the book is the most comprehensive and detailed about Jerusalem and Hebron at that time. …
descriptions.1089: In his book “Islam in Africa Throughout History,” Muhammad Aman Al-Jami provides a comprehensive overview of the history of Islamic advocacy on the African continent throughout the ages. The book deals with the different roles that Islamic work went through in Africa from the time of the Negus until the present era, with a focus on the importance of the first Muslim migration to Abyssinia and how Islam spread on the continent. The book divides history into main phases to analyze the development of the Islamic call and its challenges over time, with a review of the role of preachers and the historical circumstances that contributed to the spread of Islam in the region.
descriptions.1090: The book “Al-Inbaa fi Tarikh Al-Khalifa” by Ibn Al-Omrani deals with the history of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and the Imams of the Umayyad state, presenting a unique vision in style and historical sequence that was not similar to traditional history books. The book begins with the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his family, then moves to the rule of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and the Umayyad crown princes, reviewing the period of their rule and its characteristics.
descriptions.1091: The Investigation of the News of the Countries of the Far Maghreb is a history book written by the Moroccan historian Ahmed bin Khaled Al-Nasiri, published in four parts in Cairo in 1894, and it is considered one of the most famous books on the history of the Far Maghreb from the period of the Islamic conquest to the author’s era (1835 - 1897). This book is considered an essential reference in writing Moroccan history, as Al-Nasiri combined news narration with accurate documentation of the course of political, military, and social events. …
descriptions.1092: The book “Consideration” by Osama bin Munqidh narrates his autobiography during the period of his military and political rule, speaking about his participation in the wars against the Franks, his travels between Egypt and Damascus, and his conflicts with the rulers and ministers. The book also deals with important historical events such as army revolts and assassinations of princes, with a focus on Osama's role in those events and his positions on them. It is considered an important document for learning about the political and military conditions in the Umayyad era in the Levant and Egypt.
descriptions.1093: This book, “The Beginning and History” by the Jerusalemite author, Al-Mutahhar bin Taher, is classified under the category of history. This book is considered one of the most important historical sources of the period in which it was written, as it covers multiple topics such as the history of creation, the attributes of God, prophecy, and the history of Islam. The book begins with chapters related to the mind, the intelligible, the senses, and the sensed, then moves to the chapters related to the Creator, the monotheism of the Creator, his attributes and names, confirming the message and affirming prophecy, and mentioning the beginning of creation. The book shows great interest in debate and controversy, as it warns against corrupting the doctrine of fools and distorting the truth for the weak. This book is a valuable source for historical and philosophical understanding of the period in which it was written.
descriptions.1094: The Beginning and the End is a huge historical encyclopedic work, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir Ismail bin Omar Al-Dimashqi, who died in the year 774 AH. It is a presentation of history from the beginning of creation to its end. It begins with the beginning of the creation of the heavens, the earth, and the angels until the creation of Adam, then it briefly addresses the stories of the prophets, then details the historical events since the sending of the Prophet Muhammad until the year 768 AH, using a tabulation method based on years. The Sunnah begins with his saying, “Then a year entered...” Then he lists the historical events in it and then mentions the most prominent people who died in this year. As for the end part, it contains the signs of the Hour until the Day of Judgment in detail. …
descriptions.1095: Al-Barq Al-Shami is one of the history books, written by Imad Al-Din Al-Isfahani (519 AH - 597 AH). The book dates the period of time between the years 562 AH - 589 AH in several parts. The writer began his book by mentioning himself and the picture of his move from Iraq to the Levant, and what happened in his service to Sultan Nour Al-Din Mahmoud and his service to Sultan Saladin Al-Ayyubi. He mentioned in the book something of the conquests of the Levant. The author named his book “The Levantine Lightning” because he likened his times in those days to lightning flashes due to their goodness and the piety of their passing.
descriptions.1096: The book Al-Bayan Al-Mughrib fi Brief News of the Kings of Andalusia and Morocco, written by Ibn Adhari Al-Marrakshi, was printed in three volumes, and the entire book was translated into French. It was translated by Fanian in the year 1332 AH, 1914 AD. He said in his introduction that in the third part he reached the news of the year 667 AH, but the printed version stops at the year 460 AH. In the first part of it, he referred to a book he wrote on the history of the East, the fate of which was unknown. It is the only book that we have received from Ibn Adhari’s legacy, and from it historians derived the translation of Ibn Adhari, about whom all biographies were silent. Lisan al-Din referred to it several times in his book (Al-Ihātah). Al-Zirakli said: (It is one of the greatest and most reliable references on its subject). …
descriptions.1097: This book, by Judge Al-Maqrizi, deals with the history of the Arab tribes in Egypt through different eras. It focuses on mentioning the Bedouins who migrated to Egypt from the Islamic conquest until modern times, indicating their origins, history, and whereabouts in the country. The book also deals with the Arab tribes in Egypt during the pre-Islamic era and subsequent eras, with a focus on their political and social role in various historical periods.
descriptions.1098: This book is a history of Mansuri, also known as “Summary of Kashf and Bayan fi Hadiths of Time,” written by Ibn Nazif al-Hamawi. The book provides a detailed account of the historical events that occurred in various years, starting from the year 895 AH and ending in the year 621 AH. The author focuses on describing the political, military, and social events that Islamic countries witnessed during that period, relying on the historical sources available to him.
descriptions.1099: Blogging in Qazvin News” is a historical book that sheds light on the city of Qazvin by reviewing its virtues and characteristics, and detailing its name, construction, areas, cemeteries, and mosques. The book includes a collection of narrations from the Companions and Followers related to Medina, in addition to classification sections for the fathers according to letters. The author aims to document what he has learned about the history of his country and to benefit researchers about the conditions of scholars and leaders in that region.
descriptions.1100: The book “The Supplement to the Book of Connection” by Ibn al-Abar is a historical work that completes what his predecessor began in the Book of Connection. It is concerned with listing information about historical figures according to an alphabetical order that includes Bab Ahmad, Bab Bakr, and other letters, in addition to a section that mentions names such as Musa, Muawiyah, Marwan, and others. The work includes two parts that include chapters dealing with individuals, surnames, and strangers, which shows its prospographical character in documenting names and lineages. The book opens with a religious and literary introduction that highlights the author’s goal of completing what his predecessor began and providing what contributes to preserving the historical heritage.
descriptions.1101: Al-Tanbih wa al-Ashraf is one of the books written by the Abbasid historian Abu al-Hasan al-Masoudi in the tenth century. It is considered, along with the book Muruj al-Dhahab, one of the most important books he wrote in which he spoke about the history of the world and nations since the emergence of the world according to the ideas of that time until the era of the Abbasid caliphs. He also spoke about astronomy, planets, and the seas. He referred to the history of several peoples, such as the Chaldeans, Persians, Greeks, Copts, Romans, and Franks. The Dutch orientalist De Goe translated it into English and Dutch.
descriptions.1102: The book “The Pure Fruits of the Sanusi Movement in Libya” by Ali Muhammad al-Salabi is a historical work that sheds light on the biography of Imam Muhammad bin Ali al-Senussi and his approach to establishing the Sanusi movement from its educational, organizational, advocacy, and political aspects, and reviews the organizational, educational, and political dimension of Sanusiism. It also includes chapters that analyze his preaching style and intellectual wealth, and present the biography of the two leaders Muhammad al-Mahdi al-Senussi and Ahmed al-Sharif, their positions, and the development of the movement in light of regional challenges and international relations. The book falls within the series “Pages of Islamic History in North Africa” and relies on multiple references and sources to document the research.
descriptions.1103: Al-Hillah Al-Siraa - It is a work by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abi Bakr Al-Qada’i Al-Balansi, known as Ibn Al-Abar. Achieved by Dr. Hussein Munis in 1985 AD. It is considered one of the best books written by Ibn al-Abar, and the most useful. Indeed, it is a valuable treasure that no researcher of Andalusian heritage can do without. It was said that its title was “The High Court in the Poetry of Princes,” but Dr. Hussein Mu’nis - the investigator of this book - did not find anything to support this statement.
descriptions.1104: The book deals with the last Umayyad campaign against Constantinople during the reign of Caliph Suleiman bin Abdul Malik, highlighting the efforts and plans that were made for this campaign and the reasons for its failure. The author relies on reviewing and analyzing historical narratives related to the campaign, relying on new narratives from Arab sources and sometimes Western references to provide an accurate and documented view of the events. The book aims to clarify some of the ambiguities and confusions in the historical accounts around this campaign, and to provide a more accurate picture of the events.
descriptions.1105: The book “The Student in the History of Schools” by Al-Naimi is classified as a history book, and deals with the path of development of religious schools through chapters devoted to the role of the Holy Qur’an and the Noble Hadith, in addition to a chapter specializing in Shafi’i schools. It highlights multiple educational institutions known as “Dar al-Qur’an” and “Dar al-Hadith,” explaining their names, locations, and contributions to the transmission of religious sciences. The narrative is limited to a historical presentation of the schools without going into details about the biography of individuals or specific facts.
descriptions.1106: The book “The Ottoman Empire - Factors of Rise and Causes of its Fall” by Ali Muhammad Al-Sallabi is a historical book that deals with the path of the Ottoman Empire from the roots of the Turks and their origins to its founding and conquests, focusing on the factors that led to its rise and the factors of its fall. It includes chapters that review the origin of the Turks, the role of the Seljuk state, and the stages of establishing the Ottoman Empire through the biography of its first sultans such as Osman I, Orhan, and Murad I, with reference to their internal and foreign policies. The book aims to provide a comprehensive picture of the historical approach followed in studying this era, with a focus on the religious and humanitarian values ​​that supported the state’s journey.
descriptions.1107: A historical book that sheds light on the Fatimid state in North Africa, with a focus on the Shiite aspects, its definition terminologically, and the history of its establishment. The author deals with the various Shiite sects, from the Nusayris to the Twelvers and the Ismailis, and reviews the conflicts between the Fatimids and the inhabitants of the region, including the revolts of the Hawara and Burqa tribes and the departure of Abu Yazid. It also discusses the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community about the Mahdi and their position on the hadiths related to him.
descriptions.1108: The book “Apostasy” by Al-Waqidi is one of the important historical sources that dealt with the period of the apostasy wars that followed the death of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book focuses on describing the events and facts that occurred during that period, relying on historical news and reports. The book also contains a lot of poetry, exceeding nine hundred lines, representing horsemanship and Arab heroism. It is poetry by unknown poets who were not known for writing poetry. Most of them originated from fighters who improvised their poetry in the context of wars and battles, which gives a vivid picture of that historical period.
descriptions.1109: The book deals with war letters in the era of the Ayyubid state, focusing on collections related to the Ayyubid army and their importance in the military administration of the state. The author divides the research into three sections that deal with the main offices and their heads, then the war letters exchanged between the leaders during the period of Saladin Al-Ayyubi and his successors, with a comparison between these letters and contemporary poetry in expressing the feelings of Muslims after their victory in the wars against the usurpers.
descriptions.1110: This book deals with the Battle of Zallaqah, which took place in Andalusia in the year 479 AH, and the author classifies it as one of the most important and decisive battles in Islamic history. Al-Masry focuses on the strategic importance of this battle in preserving the presence of Muslims in Andalusia after the fall of the Umayyad Caliphate and the Amiriyya state, and the role of the Almoravids in supporting Muslims there. The book also discusses the political and military developments that preceded the battle, and the circumstances that led to its historical results in stopping the Crusader advance in the region.
descriptions.1111: This book deals with the biography of Sultan Imad al-Din Zengi and his era, focusing on the origins and roots of his family, his political and military status, his internal and foreign policy, and his relationship with the Seljuk authority and the Abbasid Caliphate. It also talks about its expansion into the northern Levant and the Jazira region, and its role in resisting the Crusader threats and unifying the Islamic Front against the occupation.
descriptions.1112: The biography of the Prophet means the biography of the Prophet Muhammad, ﷺ, and it is the science specialized in collecting what was reported from the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his moral and moral attributes, in addition to his conquests and missions.
descriptions.1113: A book on history by Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti.
descriptions.1114: This book, by the scholar Ibn Bashkwal, is a history that deals with the imams of Andalusia. It is classified according to the alphabet and deals with each personality in detail about their scientific and cultural biography, mentioning their narratives, professors, and works. The book covers prominent figures from the people of Andalusia and their scholars, and mentions some historical facts related to them, such as the ordeal of Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Faraj and his imprisonment in Jaén. The book aims to record the biographies of Andalusian scholars, their narratives, and their cultural and religious influence on Andalusian society.
descriptions.1115: Lessons in the story of those who passed and in some sources the lessons in the news of the book by Imam Al-Dhahabi in which he summarized his book The History of Islam and the Deaths of Celebrities and Notables, and it began in the first year of the Hijra and ended in the year 700 AH.
descriptions.1116: The book "Arabs in Ancient Times" by Lutfi Abdel Wahhab deals with a comprehensive historical study of the region of the emergence of civilizations and the Arabian Peninsula, with a focus on the role of the Semites and Arabs in this region. The book deals with a cultural comparison between this region and other regions, and discusses the reasons for the emergence of the first civilizations there, in addition to discussing the issue of the Semitic origin of the Arabs and the Arabian Peninsula. The book aims to provide a comprehensive vision of the ancient history of the Arabs and the region, while benefiting from modern studies and archaeological sources.
descriptions.1117: The book Arabs in Sicily by Ihsan Abbas is a historical study that addresses the presence of Arabs in Sicily from a political, social, and cultural perspective, as it sheds light on the Islamic conquest, transformations in governance, financial systems, and the agricultural and industrial renaissance. The research includes chapters detailing political, social, and mental life, with a focus on cultural connections, schools, jurisprudence, science, asceticism, and Sufism. The author relies on multiple historical sources to form a comprehensive picture before delving into an analysis of Sicilian Arabic literature and poetry. The book aims to show the interaction between history and literature in shaping the identity of Arab Sicilians.
descriptions.1118: The Pearly Necklaces in the History of the Rasulid State by Sheikh Ali bin al-Hasan al-Khazraji is a historical book that sheds light on the affiliation of the kings of the Prophet’s sons to Yemen and their distribution of power between the right and the left. Then, he traces the emergence and development of the dynasties of multiple states such as the Mansuriyyah, al-Muzaffariya, al-Ashrafiyya, al-Mawaidah, al-Mujahidiyah, and al-Awdiyah, reviewing their times and conquests. The book combines factual narration and jurisprudential analysis of kings, based on Harith Al-Raish’s poems and testimonies to explain their role in preserving the kingdom and filling its gaps. It concludes with details of the establishment of the Great Ashrafi Empire and its events.
descriptions.1119: The book “The Omari Conquest of Jerusalem is a Model for Calling for Action and Example” by the writer Shafiq Jasser Ahmed Mahmoud is concerned with studying the history of the conquest of Jerusalem at the hands of the Caliph Omar bin Al-Khattab, based on Islamic and Christian sources to document the events and the behavior of the Caliph and his companions. It sheds light on the moral values ​​on which the behavior of Muslims in that era was based, explaining how these values ​​contributed to attracting Christians to Islam and strengthening confidence in the justice of Islamic rule. The work concludes with an analysis of the religious and social implications of the conquest, with reference to the construction of the mosque in Al-Aqsa Square and the provision of source references.
descriptions.1120: The book “Sedition and the Battle of the Camel” by Saif bin Omar is a historical work that deals with the details of the strife that followed the killing of Uthman bin Affan, starting with the exile of the violators from Kufa and Basra, through the revolutionary meetings and negotiations between Uthman and his commoners, all the way to the pledge of allegiance to Ali bin Abi Talib and his succession, and ending with the Battle of the Camel and the mobilization of the people of Medina. The author focuses on narrating the political events, dialogues, and speeches that took place between the leaders, while adding various opinions on the analysis of the strife. The book aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the course of the internal conflict in early Islam by reviewing the successive stages of strife.
descriptions.1121: The book “The Mujahid Leader Nour al-Din Mahmoud al-Zenki, His Personality and Era,” by the author Ali Muhammad al-Salabi, is considered a historical book that sheds light on the biography of Nour al-Din Mahmoud al-Zenki, reviewing his internal policy and personal traits, from seriousness and intelligence to asceticism and courage. The book deals with his lineage and family relationships, and details the role of Saif al-Din Ghazi in unifying the word. It also highlights his efforts in applying Sharia law and rebuilding the Zengid state on the foundations of the Sunnis. The book also highlights the features of his judicial and judicial reforms, highlighting his justice and reforms in judicial institutions. The work concludes with an analysis of his concept of monotheism, love of jihad, and worship that characterized his character.
descriptions.1122: Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh is a book written by Izz al-Din Abi al-Hasan Ali bin Abi al-Karam Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Abdul Karim bin Abdul Wahid al-Shaybani, known as Ibn al-Atheer al-Jazari. Its originals were corrected by Abdul Wahab Al-Najjar in Cairo, Al-Muniriya Printing Department, in 1357 AH / 1938 AD.
descriptions.1123: Al-Mukhbar is one of the Arabic books written by Muhammad bin Habib bin Umayyah bin Amr Al-Hashemi Al-Baghdadi. It was edited by Dr. Else Lichten-Stetter, and published by the Ottoman Encyclopedia. This book contains 502 pages, excluding appendices.
descriptions.1124: The book “Al-Muhann” by author Abu Al-Arab Al-Tamimi deals with a historical account of the events of the killing of a number of prominent companions and scholars, with a focus on the bloody events that the Islamic State witnessed in its early eras, such as the killing of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, the events of Al-Jamal, Al-Nahrawan, Al-Harra, and other painful events. The book presents a series of bloody incidents that shook the Islamic scene, highlighting leaders and individuals from various groups, relying on chains of narration to narrate these events.
descriptions.1125: The book Al-Mukhtasar fi Akhbar al-Bashar by Ismail Abi Al-Fida is a work on the history of the world from the beginning of creation until the year 732 AH (1331 AD), which is the year in which the author died. Abu Al-Fida was a statesman, historian, geographer, and patron of intellectual life in the Syrian city of Hama. Nowadays, the work acquires special value due to its description of the city in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. The first volume of this four-volume edition is devoted to the history of the prophets of the heavenly religions and the life of the Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and his first honorable companions. The subsequent volumes narrate the history of Islamic kingdoms, rulers, and prominent intellectual figures. …
descriptions.1126: Al-Ma’arif by Ibn Qutaybah Al-Dinuri is a historical work that combines the writer’s biography and details about his lineage and writings, with a comprehensive presentation of the scholars, writers, and jurists who were active in the era of the Abbasid caliphs. The book also deals with aspects of scientific and literary life in Baghdad, and reviews the approaches to comprehensive writing that prevailed at that time, with reference to the political and social circumstances that surrounded the era. It also contains sections dedicated to studies of the Qur’an in terms of the strange, the problematic, meanings, readings, and their parsing.
descriptions.1127: The admirer in summarizing the news of Morocco is considered one of the most important historical works that dealt with the history of Morocco and Andalusia during the Islamic era. It was written by Abdel Wahed al-Marrakshi in response to the request of one of the major notables. The book deals with the events of the conquest of Andalusia and the biographies of the kings who ruled the region, with a focus on the rule of the Umayyads, Almoravids, and Almohads. It also mentions the figures of virtue and literature who were contemporary with the author. Although Al-Marrakshi admits to some of his flaws in writing, the book is an important reference for the political and cultural history of Morocco and Andalusia in the Islamic era.
descriptions.1128: This book is a comprehensive Islamic history that deals with the lives of the prophets, the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and the events of the Umayyad era. The author, Yaqoub bin Sufyan Al-Faswi, deals with the life of the Prophet Muhammad, his wives, and his children, then moves to the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, governors, and scholars, showing important events in Islamic history. The author wrote after long trips in the East and West to seek knowledge and hear hadith from his sheikhs.
descriptions.1129: Morocco in the Jewels of Morocco is a book written by Ibn Saeed Al-Maghribi Al-Andalusi, and it is considered one of the important sources that contributed greatly to preserving the Andalusian heritage. The manuscript in our hands, which was completed by the distinguished scholar Dr. Shawqi Dhaif, written in the handwriting of Ibn Saeed, who was the last of the six authors who passed down the book over a period of one hundred and fifteen years. They continued to work on it day and night, refining and refining it until only the purest jewels of poetry and the eye-catching stanzas and songs came out. The value of this book lies in that it is considered one of the most important Andalusian works that depicted Andalusian poetry in various eras. …
descriptions.1130: This book deals with the history of the Mongols and Tatars and their invasion of Muslim countries, shedding light on the Mongol project and the factors of its spread and defeat. The author begins by studying the historical roots of the Mongols, their definition, and their original homeland, then moves on to studying the conditions of the Islamic world prior to the Mongol invasion. It also focuses on the emergence of Genghis Khan and his role in unifying the Mongol tribes and establishing the Mongol Empire, relying on an analysis of the power factors that enabled the Mongols to achieve their wide spread in the Islamic world.
descriptions.1131: Al-Mufassal fi Tarikh al-Arab before Islam is a book on the history of the Arabs before Islam written by the Iraqi historian Jawad Ali. It consists of ten parts, one of which is devoted to the index. It is considered the largest academic work on the history of the Arabs and the Arabian Peninsula in the period before the emergence of Islam. It has been issued in several editions.
descriptions.1132: The quote from Al-Andalus News is a history by the historian Ibn Hayyan Al-Qurtubi, in which he discusses the history of Andalusia from the beginnings of the Islamic conquest of Andalusia in the year 91 AH to the year 363 AH during the rule of Al-Hakam Al-Mustansir Billah. The reason for calling it “the quote” is that the author relied on “quoting” from previous books. The quote is a huge book of ten volumes, but only a few pieces have survived from it. …
descriptions.1133: This historical book deals with the biography of the Bahri Mamluks and their role in confronting the Crusaders in the Levant. The book reviews the emergence of the Mamluks and their training methods, then moves to the establishment of the Bahri Mamluk state, passing through important events such as the accession of the Sultanate to prominent figures such as Qutuz, al-Zahir Baybars, and al-Nasir Qalawun. It also highlights the jihad of these sultans against the Crusaders, including the fall of Antioch.
descriptions.1134: This book deals with a historical narrative of events that occurred in different eras, focusing on Persian and Arab kings and rulers. It begins with the story of Al-Dahhak and Afridoon, then moves to the era of the Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him), and mentions some details about the kings of Egypt and Pharaoh. The book also deals with the lives of Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf Al-Thaqafi and the Azd kings, while providing historical and anecdotal information about important figures and events in Islamic and Arab history.
descriptions.1135: The book “Al-Muntazim in the History of Kings and Nations” by Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Jawzi is a comprehensive historical encyclopedia in which the great historian dealt with an important period of Islamic history, and was distinguished by his broad outlook on the political, social and intellectual events of his time. The book deals with the author's approach and style in writing history, and also includes the sources of information that Ibn al-Jawzi relied on, in addition to the importance of this historical work and its impact on subsequent generations.
descriptions.1136: Al-Munami fi Akhbar Quraysh” by Muhammad bin Habib Al-Baghdadi is a historical book that specializes in narrating the news of the Quraysh tribe, as it includes chapters on their lineage, fathers, virtues, and alliance, in addition to stories about their battles and rivalries between the Quraysh branches. The book includes a collection of hadiths and stories that show details of lineages, heroics, and rivalries within the Quraish tribe. This work is a valuable source of historical knowledge related to the Quraish tribe in the Arab heritage.
descriptions.1137: The Bright Stars in the Kings of Egypt and Cairo is a book of biographies and biographies, written by the historian Ibn Taghri Bardi (813 AH - 874 AH). The author began his book by mentioning the conquest of Egypt at the hands of the Muslim army led by the companion Amr ibn al-Aas, then he began by mentioning the kings of Egypt before Islam, then followed by those who assumed the caliphate of Egypt after Islam, mentioning the most important events that occurred during his caliphate. The author collected in his book those who assumed the emirate of Egypt before and after Islam until the end of the year 871 AH, which is a huge book by the Egyptian historian Ibn Taghri Bardi, in which he chronicled the history of Egypt from the beginning of history until the year 1467 AD. …
descriptions.1138: Al-Nawadir al-Sultaniyya wa al-Mahasin al-Yusufiyah is a book written by Abu al-Mahasin Bahaa al-Din ibn Shaddad al-Asadi al-Mawsili (d. 632 AH), which talks about the biography of Saladin al-Ayyubi. It is located in an introduction that prepares the subject of the book, followed by the first section: in which it is concerned with mentioning the birth of Saladin al-Ayyubi and its characteristics, and the second section was: in explaining the fluctuations in his circumstances and his conquests in their dates. Then the book ended with the illness and death of Saladin. Al-Ayyubi.
descriptions.1139: The book “Intentious Attacks on Islamic History” by Muhammad Mazhar Siddiqi is concerned with analyzing and clarifying the opposing positions targeting Islam as a faith, civilization, and history, based on criticism of new trends in writing biography and history. The author deals with multiple periods from the prophetic mission to the formation of the Islamic state, reviewing topics such as invasions, caliphate, conquests, and Ottoman politics, in addition to issues of strife and criticisms directed at Islam. The work aims to expose attempts to distort and provide a defense of Islamic heritage by reviewing the available historical evidence.
descriptions.1140: The book presents a historical study of the spread of Islam through the conquests during the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, based on an analysis of the preaching plans drawn up by the Messenger ﷺ. The author discusses the factors of psychological power and legitimacy that facilitated the conquest, reviewing the role of soldiers and preachers and the application of the principles of Islamic warfare. It also highlights the treatment of the people of open lands in accordance with the provisions of Islam and freedom of religion for minorities, based on Islamic sources.
descriptions.1141: The book The History of Abu Zara’ah al-Dimashqi is a historical book that deals with the biography of the Prophet Muhammad from his birth until his death, and reviews his raids and battles such as Badr, then addresses the periods of the Rightly Guided Caliphate and its sayings from Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman, in addition to mentioning the judges and the events of the Levant in those eras. The book includes organized chapters that list facts, lineages, and monuments related to guardianship, death, and classes, based on documented attributional narratives. This work is considered a reference for researchers in the early history of Islam.
descriptions.1142: Ibn al-Wardi’s History Book is a historical book that summarizes human history from ancient times until the Islamic conquests, and adopts a chronological order for kings and prophets. It includes chapters dealing with the prophets of God from Adam to Jesus, the Persian kings, and the kingdoms of Egypt, Greece, and Rome, in addition to the Arab kings before Islam. It aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the histories of peoples and kings according to a brief and codified methodology.
descriptions.1143: The History of Islam and Deaths of Celebrities and Notables by Imam al-Dhahabi is one of the most prominent encyclopedic works in Islamic heritage, and it is considered one of the most important historical sources that combined general history and individual biographies. This book differs from his other encyclopedia, Biographies of Noble Figures, in that it focuses on monitoring Islamic history from the Prophet’s migration until the year 700 AH/1300 AD, relying on a chronological classification consisting of seventy classes, which is equivalent to seven hundred years in the Hijri calendar. This period represents the time frame for the emergence of an Islamic civilization that extended geographically between the East and the West, and was affected and affected by them in various fields. …
descriptions.1144: Al-Basrawi’s History Book is a historical book that provides an annual account of events according to Hijri dates, detailing each year with its events and interviews with administrative and religious figures. The text includes mention of local incidents, such as the fire of the Public Prosecution House in Damascus, and jurisprudential discussions among scholars, reflecting the details of public and authoritarian life in those periods. The index shows a chronology extending over several centuries, making it a reference for documenting local history in the Levant.
descriptions.1145: The book The History of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, Conquests and Achievements, by Muhammad Suhail Taqoush, is a historical work that sheds light on the stage of the Rightly Guided Caliphate, reviewing the political situation in the Arabian Peninsula after the death of the Prophet and its development during the reigns of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Omar ibn al-Khattab. The book details the wars of apostasy and the conquests that included Iraq, the Levant, Egypt, and Persia, with a focus on the internal and external factors that influenced the formation of the early Islamic state. It also links religious, social, and political aspects to provide a comprehensive analysis of the achievements that paved the way for the nation's transition from a tribal alliance to a central state.
descriptions.1146: The History of the Caliphs is a book on the history of the Muslim caliphs, written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849 AH - 911 AH). The book specializes in a specific class, namely the caliphs, from the beginning of the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs to the end of the era of the Abbasid Caliphate. It gives an extensive translation of the caliphs and mentions the beginning of the caliphate of each of them, its deeds and effects during the days of his caliphate, his workers in the country, and the most important figures who died in his time and the Islamic states. Then he mentions the date of his death and his burial place, and he expanded on the details. The Rightly Guided Caliphs.
descriptions.1147: The History of the Ottoman Empire is a historical book in which the author, Muhammad Farid Bey, discusses the history of the Ottoman Empire from its founding until its fall at the beginning of the twentieth century, and he paved the way for that with an introduction in which he talked about the caliphs before the Ottoman Caliphate.
descriptions.1148: The History of Nations and Kings, or the History of Messengers and Kings, known as The History of al-Tabari, is a book on history written by Muhammad bin Jarir al-Tabari, who died in 310 AH. The book dates from the beginning of creation to the end of the year 302 AH, and it was said that the year 309 AH.
descriptions.1149: The book “The History of the Ancient Arabs” by Tawfiq Berro provides a comprehensive study of the history of the Arabian Peninsula and its pre-Islamic civilizations. The book focuses on discussing the historical sources available for its subject, and points out the difficulty of simplifying ancient Arab history due to the lack of established sources and the spread of scientific hypotheses. The book also addresses the geographical and topographic aspects of the Arabian Peninsula, and explains its strategic importance as a crossroads between the continents of Asia, Africa and Europe.
descriptions.1150: This book deals with the history of the Arabs and their civilization in Andalusia through different eras, starting from the conquest of Spain and their settlement there until the fall of Granada. The book covers the eras of the emirate, the caliphate, and the era of the taifa states, with a focus on the political, military, and cultural aspects of Arab society in Andalusia. The book consists of five chapters, all written by specialized authors, and its content includes information about the Arab conquests, political systems, Arab civilization, and cultural influences on Europe.
descriptions.1151: The book "History of the Philippines" provides a comprehensive overview of the geographical and historical aspects of the country, starting with a description of the geographical location of the islands, their number, area, and population, through to their historical developments from the Islamic era to the Spanish colonization and other colonies. The book also examines the political and religious system in the Philippines, focusing on the situation of Muslims in the country and their challenges throughout the ages. The book also includes a description of the most important tourist cities and natural landmarks in the Philippines.
descriptions.1152: The book “The History of Endowment Schools in Medina” by Muhammad Tariq bin Abdullah Hajjar deals with a descriptive historical study of the extinct endowment schools in Medina from the sixth century AH until before the year 1340 AH. The book aims to shed light on the role of the endowment in the field of education and upbringing in accordance with Islamic legislation, and to demonstrate the importance of continuing such development projects in strengthening ties between Muslims. The book also discusses the social impact of the endowment in Muslim society and its role in the reconstruction of mosques and the building of endowment schools, which played a pivotal role in spreading science and knowledge in the Islamic world.
descriptions.1153: The book “The History of Yemen during the Eleventh Century AH” by Minister Al-San’ani is a historical work that sheds light on the course of events in Yemen during that period. The author combines narratives of political, military, and social facts, based on various sources and presenting them in a narrative style that combines facts and stories. The book includes chapters dealing with the conquest of Baghdad, the arrival of Ottoman soldiers in Mecca and Yemen, and local incidents such as the siege of Dhi Al-Marmar and internal conflicts, which provides a comprehensive picture of the history of Yemen in the aforementioned century.
descriptions.1154: The History of Jerusalem is a historical book about the history of Jerusalem, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Jawzi (508 AH - 597 AH). The book talks about the history of Jerusalem through the following points: at the beginning of the construction of Jerusalem and the Al-Aqsa Mosque, and at the beginning of the journey to Jerusalem. The virtue of praying in Jerusalem, and the virtue of entering ihram from Jerusalem. And talking about the rock and that it is from heaven.
descriptions.1155: The book of history by Khalifa bin Khayyat is considered one of the oldest books written in the annals, and the sources indicate that the original copy of it has been lost and has not reached us today except from the narration of the Andalusian imam Baqi bin Makhlid, which is the only copy in circulation at the present time. The author began it by saying: “This is the book of history, and through history people knew the matter of their Hajj and fasting, the expiration of the number of their women, and the settlement of their debts...”
descriptions.1156: Ibn al-Qalanisi's History of Damascus is a historical work that sheds light on the city's path from the Islamic conquest until the Abbasid eras, documenting the details of the states and rulers who took over its affairs over the centuries with reference to specific dates such as sixty-three hundred years AH and what followed. The book deals with the urban, social, and economic transformations that Damascus witnessed in light of the conflicts between different dynasties, based on the investigator’s introduction and an introduction that explains the impact of the conquest on the Arab structure of the region.
descriptions.1157: The book The History of the Wonders of Antiquities in Biographies and News by Al-Jabriti is considered a historical book that reviews the events of Egypt and the biographies of its notables and rulers through chapters organized by year, starting from the year 1143 and continuing until the early thirteenth century. The author combines in its content a narration of events with personal records of the most prominent figures, shedding light on the developments of Egyptian society and its exploits throughout the mentioned periods. The introduction shows an emphasis on the importance of justice and fairness in organizing human affairs, which gives the book a philosophical character in addition to its historical presentation.
descriptions.1158: The book “Mukhtasar al-Dawl” by Ibn al-Abri is a historical work that summarizes the path of states and lineages starting from Adam to Umram, and combines historical narrative and genealogy in a concise and rhetorical style. It contains content that includes a detailed index mentioning proper names and places according to lexical order, with reference to the differences in Syriac and Arabic narratives. The author demonstrates a breadth of knowledge of science and languages, drawing on multiple sources to provide a comprehensive picture of historical facts.
descriptions.1159: The book The History of Mecca, the Grand Mosque, and Medina by Sheikh Imam Allama Ibn al-Diya is considered a historical book that sheds light on the path of Mecca and its religious status throughout the ages. It deals with the details of the creation of the Kaaba before the heavens, and its construction by the angels, Adam, and Abraham, and reviews the stages of its establishment and change from pre-Islamic times to Islam, in addition to mentioning events related to Medina and the Holy Grave. It includes chapters dealing with the roles of Bani Ishmael, elephant stories, and the development of rituals and pilgrimage, making the text a comprehensive reference for the history of the holy places.
descriptions.1160: Experiences of Nations and Succession of Determinations is a historical book written by Ahmed bin Muhammad Miskawayh that deals with the events of the period from 295 AH to 369 AH. Since Miskawayh himself was treasurer and vizier of the Buyid state in western Iran, his book is of special value. The first volume of this six-volume work focuses on general history, drawing in particular on the writings of the ancients, such as al-Tabari. His use of government documents, especially in later volumes, reinforces the value of Miskawayh's work as historically important.
descriptions.1161: The Masterpiece of Princes in the History of Ministers is a historical work that narrates the course of the Arab ministries through a detailed account of records and correspondence showing their tasks and administrations, with a focus on figures such as Ali bin Muhammad bin Al-Furat, Abu Al-Hasan, and Abu Al-Abbas. The book includes chapters detailing financial and judicial positions and administrative departments, and is based on graphic descriptions of the events and decisions taken by these ministers. This provides a reference that shows the development of administration and authority in the periods covered by the text.
descriptions.1162: This book deals with correcting misconceptions about Wahhabism and the call of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, explaining the reason for the historical error that led to the attack on the call and its founder. The author focuses on removing confusion about the call to monotheism and confronting the suspicions and false ideas that the enemies of Islam have exploited to undermine the unity of Muslims. The book aims to clarify the historical truth and correct misconceptions about this Islamic call.
descriptions.1163: The book provides a comprehensive historical study of the development of journalism in Egypt from 1798 to 1981, based on accurate documents and evidence. The author deals with the official and popular press across multiple periods, including the Urabi Revolution, the occupation, and after the friendly agreement, in addition to the press between the two world wars and the period after 1940. It also includes an analysis of legislation related to the press and a list of Arab and French newspapers published in Egypt, with research references and documentary appendices.
descriptions.1164: This book is a continuation of the history of al-Tabari, written by al-Maqdisi Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik and related to the field of history. The book deals with historical events related to the period of the Abbasid Caliphate, focusing on the reigns of the caliphs and their ministers and the events of the years mentioned in the index. The author aims to record the virtues of the Abbasid family and document its historical events to benefit from them in the future.
descriptions.1165: This book by Ibn al-Jawzi deals with multiple topics in history and biography, as it combines the arts of biography with the eyes of hadith sciences. It aims to provide useful information for beginners and a reminder for the elite, and covers topics such as the creation of the universe, the order of the prophets, the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, his lineage, wives, and followers.
descriptions.1166: This book deals with the biography of Othman bin Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) by studying his personality and era, covering his lineage, upbringing, conversion to Islam, marriage, and his role in the Islamic conquests. It also focuses on his social and economic contributions to building the Islamic state, mentioning the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ about his virtues. The author aims to draw lessons and lessons from the life and times of Uthman in order to benefit from them in building societies and spreading Islam.
descriptions.1167: The book “The Renewal and Reform Movement in Najd” by Dr. Abdullah Al-Ajlan deals with the history of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s reform movement in Najd, explaining the reasons for its emergence and its social, political and religious circumstances. The author focuses on the basic idea of ​​the call and the principles upon which it was based, relying on the historical context to clarify the circumstances that paved the way for this movement and depict the environment in which it arose, with the aim of clarifying its educational approach in preparing the individual and society.
descriptions.1168: Hassan Al-Mudathah fi the History of Egypt and Cairo is a book written by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (Cairo 849 AH/1445 AD - Cairo 911 AH/1505 AD), describing what was reported about Egypt in ancient times, the era of the Pharaohs and the pyramid builders, and more recently what was reported in his era, describing the Islamic conquests and the facts and events that accompanied them, and the mixing of Egyptians with Arabs when it was conquered. Egypt by the companion Amr ibn al-Aas in the year 20 AH, in which he mentioned the immigrants to Egypt, historians, storytellers, poets, and others, and mentioned the customs of the Egyptians, their seasons, their holidays, and the events that took place between them, and the literature clubs and poetry and evening gatherings that existed therein. The book is considered a historical document about the life of the scholar Al-Suyuti because he devoted an entire chapter to his biography...
descriptions.1169: A historical book that sheds light on the biography of Imam Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his call to pure monotheism, based on chapters dealing with his lineage, birth, his scientific trips outside the peninsula, the implementation of the call and its stages, in addition to its maneuvers and opposition. It also deals with the Imam’s relationship with the Al Saud family, which embraced and supported him, and reviews his sermons and letters and his influence on the scientific and literary renaissance and the spread of the call outside the Arabian Peninsula. The author, Abdullah bin Saad Al-Ruwaished, provides an analysis of the two letters that explain the Sheikh’s doctrine, and reviews the opinions of thinkers and scholars about his Salafist call.
descriptions.1170: Incidents of Eons over the Days and Months” is a historical work written by Ibn Taghri Bardi. It specializes in recording the events of each year and month according to a chronological order that begins with the year one hundred and forty-five and ends with the year one hundred and eighty-fifty, with biographies of the deaths attached. In his book, the author relies on reviewing and expanding what was stated in the book “Conduct in Knowing the Countries of Kings” and adds his own analyzes to bring benefit to the reader. It aims to collect incidents and biographies at the same time to provide a comprehensive reference for the aforementioned era.
descriptions.1171: The Life of the Companions is a book in Arabic written by Yusuf Al-Kandahlawi. He finished writing it around 1959 and later expanded it into four volumes with additional commentaries and introductions by Abu al-Hasan Ali al-Hasani al-Nadawi and Abd al-Fattah Abu Ghadda. The book was first published by the Tablighi Jamaat. It relies on sources such as hadith, history, and biography, with a particular focus on the lives of the Companions. The book consists of nineteen chapters, each of which deals with specific topics related to the Companions.
descriptions.1172: The book A Compendium of the Complete Biography of the Wonders of the News of Kings by Al-Himyari Nashwan is a historical author that deals with the biography of the Himyar kings and the sayings of Yemen, with a detailed explanation of their events and lineage. It includes a narration of the sayings of prophets such as Hud, and their commandments, in addition to mentioning conquests, building cities, and distributing kingdoms between generations. It aims to collect wonders and facts related to the vassal kings while providing moral advice to readers. It is considered a reference linking history and the Prophet’s biography in an ancient Arab context.
