descriptions.1173: The book “Khulasa al-Wafa Bi Akhbar Dar al-Mustafa” by Al-Samhudi deals with the history and virtues of Medina, explaining its names and conditions throughout the ages, and reviewing its religious and scientific virtues, with a focus on the Prophet’s Mosque, its architecture, and the events and landmarks related to it. The book is divided into sections that deal with the virtue of the city and its belongings, the virtue of visiting the Prophet’s Mosque, the news of its inhabitants from the earliest times until the arrival of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the architecture of the Prophet’s Mosque and its expansions over time.
descriptions.1174: A historical book that sheds light on the succession of the Commander of the Faithful, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, based on a detailed record of his lineage, characteristics, and stages of his activity during the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and then during the era of the Umayyads, including his sale to Yusuf bin Muawiyah and his movement against them. The author, Ali Muhammad al-Sallabi, provides an analysis of the facts through chapters that address his participation in the battles of Yarmouk, the writing of the Qur’an, his jihad in North Africa, and his role in the Battle of the Camel, in addition to the details of his sale to the caliphate after Yazid’s death. This work is considered a reference for studying the Umayyad state and the factors of its prosperity and collapse through the biography of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr.
descriptions.1175: The book “Studies in the History of the Ancient Arabs” by Muhammad Bayoumi Mahran is a historical book that deals with the sources of Arab history before Islam, starting with archaeological sources and passing through Jewish, Christian, and Arab writings. It also reviews modern scientific research in various regions of the Arabian Peninsula. The book focuses on criticizing the methodology of Islamic historians in treating pre-Islamic times, while showing the gaps and confusion in relying on oral narratives. It also adds chapters on the geography of the Arabian Peninsula and its historical division according to Greek and Roman sources.
descriptions.1176: The book “The Seljuk State and the Emergence of an Islamic Resistance Project” by Ali Muhammad Al-Sallabi is considered a historical study that deals with the emergence of the Seljuk state, the origins of its sultans, and its political path in the Levant and other regions. It sheds light on the attempts at Islamic resistance that emerged in response to the internal penetration and Crusader invasion, based on detailed analyzes of topics that include the origins of the Seljuks, their policies, and their relations with the Abbasid caliphs. The author combines historical narrative and religious objectivity to show the role of the Seljuk state in shaping the path of Islamic resistance.
descriptions.1177: The book provides a comprehensive historical study of the Almohad state in North Africa, highlighting its founder Muhammad ibn Tumart and his intellectual and ideological biography. It deals with the career of Abdel Moumen Ben Ali and his sons, with an analysis of the military and legal policies he adopted in unifying Morocco and managing relations with Christians and Jews. It also provides a description of the decisive battles, such as the Battle of Arak in 591 AH, and reviews the intellectual and ideological foundations that shaped the call of the Almohads, with an indication of the need for the nation to adhere to the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community.
descriptions.1178: Diwan al-Mubtada wa al-Khabar fi Tarikh al-Arab and Berber is a historical work written by the scholar Ibn Khaldun, in which it presents a comprehensive study of the development of Arab and Berber societies through chapters dealing with human urbanization, geography, tribal fanaticism, and the impact of the environment on human behavior. The book includes analyzes of the nature of Bedouin and urban generations, comparisons between the characteristics of souls, in addition to a discussion of the origins of nervousness and the intersection of lineages. The work aims to show the historical and social relationships that shaped the path of peoples in the region.
descriptions.1179: This book is a sequel to the book “Mirror of Time” by Ibn al-Jawzi, and the Greek author Abu al-Fath deals with the historical events that occurred after the end of the original book, covering a time period that begins in the year 654 AH and includes important events in Islamic history, especially in the Mamluk and Tatar era. The book focuses on important political and military facts, including the spread of the Tatars and their influence on the rule of Islamic countries, the disputes of kings and ministers, and detailed histories of events in the main Islamic capitals.
descriptions.1180: Buttermilk in the History of Aleppo by Ibn al-Adim, is a summary of another work by this author with the aim of requesting the history of Aleppo. Although this book is a local history, it contains valuable information about the Frankish attacks on the Levant, especially the cities of Aleppo and Antioch. It was published by Dar Al-Kutub Al-Ilmiyyah, in Beirut, Lebanon.
descriptions.1181: This book, “The Scaling of the Awali Stars in the News of the First and the Successive,” by Al-Isami, is a work on history that deals with the biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his circumstances, and also includes a mention of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and their events. The author divides the book into sections and chapters detailing the lineage and circumstances of the Prophet, then moves on to mention the four caliphs and their events, while addressing some historical issues and important figures of their time. The book aims to present a comprehensive Islamic history that deals with events and facts in an organized and detailed manner.
descriptions.1182: “Souss the Scientist” by Mokhtar Soussi presents a historical study of the sciences that flourished in the Moroccan Souss region. The author relies on his personal biography and education in traditional corners and schools, and moves on to a detailed review of the sciences, from the art of readings to jurisprudence, medicine, logic, and others. The book sheds light on the stages of the scientific renaissance in Souss after the eighth century and its causes, concluding with a conclusion that explains the importance of the Soussian scientific heritage in the broader historical context.
descriptions.1183: Nuggets of Gold in News from Gold is a history book, written by the jurist and historian Ibn al-Imad al-Hanbali (1032 AH - 1089 AH). In his book, Ibn al-Imad chronicled the first thousand years of Islam, beginning with the first year of the Hijra, then the second, then the third, and so on, indicating in each year its most important events, noting who among the notables and hadith scholars who died in this year, especially with mentioning a part of its translation. The book Nuggets of Gold in The reality of the matter is a summary of the history of Islam by Al-Dhahabi, a summary of the book “The Pearls Hidden in the Notables of the Eighth Hundred” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, “The Shining Light of the People of the Ninth Century” by Al-Hafiz Al-Sakhawi, “The Planets Traveling with the Virtues of Notables of the Tenth Hundred” by Al-Najm Al-Ghazzi, and a summary and appendix of what has been written over the years...
descriptions.1184: The book Fragments from Lost Books in History by Ihsan Abbas is a historical author who collects excerpts from rare and lost historical sources, and presents them in multiple chapters that deal with genealogies, biographies of personalities, and histories of different cities and regions. In his presentation, the author relies on reviewing and analyzing ancient texts such as the history of Damascus and the history of Aleppo, highlighting the accuracy of the landmarks and the richness of the sources. The work aims to show the diversity of historical content and enrich historical research with scattered evidence.
descriptions.1185: The book “Healing Love with News of the Sacred Land” by Sheikh Al-Taqi Al-Fassi is a historical work that sheds light on the honorable Mecca, reviewing its rulings, limits, and virtues through the hadiths and monuments reported. It includes chapters that address the mention of Mecca, its prohibition, defining its borders from different directions, and demonstrating its superiority in worship compared to other cities. It aims to provide documented historical information about the sanctity of the city and its place in Islamic heritage.
descriptions.1186: The book “Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi and his efforts to eliminate the Fatimid state and liberate Jerusalem” by Ali Muhammad al-Salabi is a historical book that deals with the biography of Saladin and his role in ending the rule of the Fatimid state and restoring Jerusalem, based on a comprehensive study of the causes and incentives of the Crusades and their political, religious, social and economic context. The content includes detailed chapters on the previous Crusades, the roots of the conflicts, and the stages of the conflict between Muslims and the Crusaders, with a dedication and an introductory introduction based on Qur’anic texts. The book aims to present an integrated historical vision of the era that witnessed the rise of the Ayyubid state and the liberation of Jerusalem.
descriptions.1187: The book “Layers of the Righteous People of Yemen” by Abdul Wahab Al-Burahi is classified as a history book, and provides a historical summary that includes the biography of scholars and virtuous people in Yemen, arranged according to cities and regions such as Sana’a, Haraz, Malhan, Ibb, Zabid, Lahj and Aden. In his presentation, the author relies on mentioning those he knew and their condition, and those he verified from the people of those regions, with reference to the information found about them. The book concludes by listing the names of scholars and notables from Taiz and Mawza, giving the reader a comprehensive overview of the intellectual and religious heritage in Yemen.
descriptions.1188: This book deals with the history of the city of Tarsus in Asia Minor during the Islamic era, highlighting its role in jihad and protecting Islamic borders. The author focuses on the city's development stage through the Umayyad and Abbasid eras, and points out its contribution to spreading the Islamic call and its role as an important jihadi center. The book also deals with jihad and ribat in Islamic borders and its role in protecting Islamic borders.
descriptions.1189: The Wonders of the Destined in the News of Timur by Ibn Arabshah is a historical author that narrates the biography of Timur and the path of his seizure of kingdoms, reviewing his lineage and his transformation from ruler to sultan through a series of conquests and agreements. The book details his military and political movements in Khorasan, Khiva, Balkhshan and others, mentioning his meetings with prominent figures such as Ali Sher, Shah Mansour, and the Persian sultans of Iraq. The text focuses on narrating historical events and clarifying the political dimensions of Timur's conquests.
descriptions.1190: The book “The Age of the Rightly Guided Caliphate - An Attempt to Criticize the Novel” by Akram Al-Omari is a historical book that presents a criticism of the historical novel of the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphate based on the approach of the hadith scholars. It includes an analysis of historical and hadith sources and the science of men, and is divided into sections dealing with the system of caliphate and politics under the caliphates of Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman. It aims to show the influence of Islamic values ​​on administration, economics and society in that period.
descriptions.1191: This book deals with the era of the Zengid state and its role in resisting internal penetration and the Crusader invasion, focusing on the rule of Imad al-Din Zengi and his son Nur al-Din Mahmoud. The book studies the origins of the Zengid dynasty and the development of Imad al-Din Zengi's political and military personality, as well as his relations with the Abbasid Caliphate and the Seljuk authority. It also addresses the expansion of the Zengid state in the northern Levant and the Jazira region, and highlights the role it played in preserving the Islamic project during that historical period.
descriptions.1192: The book “Omar bin Abdulaziz, Milestones of Renewal and Reform” by Ali Muhammad Al-Sallabi is a historical book that deals with the biography of the Rightly Guided Caliph Omar bin Abdulaziz from his birth until his caliphate, based on chapters detailing the stages of his life, and the influence of family, social and scientific factors on the formation of his personality. The author focuses on his role during the reigns of Al-Walid and Suleiman, explaining his reform positions from Shura and justice to redressing injustices and reforming administration, and reviews the features of his renewal that were based on the approach of prophecy.
descriptions.1193: The book “Uyun al-Rawdhatain fi Akhbar al-Dawlat al-Nuriya wa al-Salihiyya” by Abu Shamah al-Maqdisi is a historical work that narrates the details of the political and military events in the Zangi country, especially in Mosul, Homs, and Syria during the middle of the thirteenth century. It includes chapters dealing with the conquest of cities, the sultans' shares, their funerals, and details of the conflicts with the Persians and Franks, in addition to the biography of some of the leaders. The author concludes by narrating the annual events from the years forty-two to fifty of the fifth century, which provides an important reference for understanding the history of the region in that period.
descriptions.1194: The book “The Conqueror of Constantinople, Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror,” by Ali Mohamed Al-Sallabi, is a historical book that sheds light on the emergence of the Ottoman Empire and its development through its first sultans, up to the conquest of Constantinople by Mehmed the Conqueror. The book includes chapters dealing with the biography of Osman, the founder of the state, Orhan’s work in building the army and its policies, the career of Murad I and Bayezid I, in addition to studying the features of the biography of Mehmed the Conqueror and his achievements. In his presentation, the author relies on a review of the leadership qualities and norms adopted by leaders in building and developing the state. The book aims to provide a comprehensive vision of the factors that contributed to the rise and fall of the Ottoman Empire and to determine the role of scholars, jurists, and soldiers in achieving conquest.
descriptions.1195: The book “The Sedition of the Killing of Othman Ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)” by the writer Muhammad Ibn Abdullah Ghaban Al-Subhi is concerned with a historical study of the sedition that led to the killing of Caliph Othman, as it details the justifications for rebelling against him, the events of the siege in a house, and the details of his murder and funeral, with the attribution of relevant authentic hadiths. The content is divided into chapters that deal with the alleged justifications, the instigators of sedition, a description of the siege house, and Uthman’s negotiations with his besiegers, in addition to criticizing some of the writings of contemporaries. The book concludes with appendices that include authentic hadiths, making it a historical reference for analyzing the facts and differing opinions about this strife.
descriptions.1196: Conquests of Countries: The most comprehensive and authentic book of conquests. This book is considered one of the first Arabic history books. Al-Baladhuri summarized it from his huge book, “Al-Buldan Al-Kabir,” written by Al-Baladhuri Ahmed bin Yahya bin Jaber bin Daoud, who died in the year 278 AH. The book talks about the conquests of Muslims from the time of the Prophet Muhammad until the time of its writing. Al-Baladhuri collected in it the details of the conquest and the subsequent administrative organization of all the countries conquered by the Arabs.
descriptions.1197: The book “Conquests of the Levant” by Al-Waqidi is a historical work that narrates the details of the Islamic conquests in the Levant from the era of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq until the conquests of Khalid bin Al-Walid and Omar bin Al-Aas, based on multiple narrations from the Companions and followers. The catalog includes multiple battles, testaments, and tales of women’s heroism, in addition to texts from speeches and letters, reflecting the focus on the military and jurisprudential narrative of the conquest. The first volume opens with a religious introduction in which Imam Al-Waqidi mentions the narratives he heard about the beginning of the conquests, citing Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.1198: The book “Conquests of Egypt and Morocco” by Ibn Abd al-Hakam is a historical work that collects multiple narratives about the history of Egypt before Islam, its Islamic conquests, and the details of the administration under Amr ibn al-Aas, in addition to the biography of the conquests in Morocco and Andalusia. The author relies on sources from the school of Yazid ibn Abi Habib and others, and divides his book into parts that deal with the virtues of Egypt, conquest, plans, land administration, and the conquests of Africa. This book is considered one of the oldest written references about the Islamic era in Egypt, and reflects the influence of the scholarly family to which the author belongs in the field of jurisprudence and hadith.
descriptions.1199: The book The Jurisprudence of Empowerment among the Almoravid State by the writer Ali Muhammad Al-Salabi is a detailed historical study on the emergence and state of the Almoravid, as it deals with the historical roots, the political and religious roles of the leaders Yahya bin Ibrahim and Abdullah bin Yassin, and the development of the broad outlines of the state. The book also analyzes the Almoravids' defense of Muslims in Andalusia and the factors of their weakness before the Christian forces, and reviews their internal and external policies, from the rights of the subjects to their relations with the Abbasid Caliphate and European kings. The researcher concludes by detailing the systems of governance, administration, judiciary, and army in the Almoravid state, highlighting the dimensions of jurisprudence and empowerment in their historical context.
descriptions.1200: The book “How did the Tatars enter Muslim countries” by Suleiman bin Hamad Al-Awda is a historical book that deals with the entry of the Tatars into the lands of the Islamic world, based on a deeper analysis of the events and a review of the narratives to clarify the causes and consequences. It is divided into chapters that deal with the origin of the Tatars and their belief, the first motives, their invasions and tragedies in Bukhara and Samarkand, the events of Baghdad and the fall of the Abbasid Caliphate, in addition to a review of the fateful, political and economic factors that contributed to that ordeal. The author aims to show how contemplating history can draw lessons for the present and the future.
descriptions.1201: The book “Mirror of Heaven and the Lesson of Al-Yaqzan in Knowing What is Considered” by Sheikh Al-Yafi’i is classified as historical literature. It reviews the biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the sequence of the Hijri years, mentioning his humility, character, worship, miracles, and material and spiritual attributes, in addition to what relates to his companions, successors, and kings of their time. In his compilation, the author relies on historical sources from the books of shamail and histories, with abbreviations of knowledge to facilitate access to the most important facts and anecdotes.
descriptions.1202: “The Course of Truths and the Secret of Creatures” by King Al-Mansour is a historical book that narrates the details of the year that the author mentions in its title, highlighting the political and economic conditions in the countries of the Caliphate. The narrative includes multiple events, such as the conflicts of the sultans, the invasions in the Levant, Egypt, and Yemen, and the tragedies of prominent figures such as Zahir al-Din ibn al-Attar and Sharaf al-Din Qaraqush. The book concludes with a mention of the conquests and regional transitions, with an indication of their impact on the Ayyubid House and the management of public affairs.
descriptions.1203: The book “Landmarks of the History of the Ancient Near East” by author Muhammad Abu Al-Mahasin Asfour provides a comprehensive overview of the history of the region from prehistoric times until the late periods, with a focus on the various stone phases and the civilizations that arose in the Upper and Lower Egypt. The author deals with the methodology of history and the development of civilizations in the Near East, and devotes chapters to detailing the stages of ancient Egypt and its successive phases. The book aims to provide a simplified reference for non-specialist readers who wish to learn about the course of the ancient history of the region.
descriptions.1204: The book "Landmarks of the Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations" deals with the study of ancient civilizations in the Middle Eastern region, focusing on Egypt and other civilizations that arose in the region. The author aims to provide a comprehensive overview of these civilizations by reviewing their basic components and their development over time, noting that this book does not replace other specialized sources in the field of historical and civilizational studies.
descriptions.1205: The Fruit of Khalan fi Aḥāqīt al-Zaman is a book written by Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Ali Ibn Tulun al-Salhi (880-953 AH / 1475-1546 AD) on history, travels, and travels. In it, he spoke in detail and accurately about the history of Egypt and the Levant. He talked about the causes of events, their factors, and the way they occurred and took place, and he did not neglect any of their elements.
descriptions.1206: Muqatil al-Talibi, or Muqatil al-Abi Talib, is a book written by Ali bin al-Hussein bin Muhammad, known as Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani (who died in 356 AH). This book is considered one of the most important historical sources that dealt with the biographies and struggles of the Abi Talib family. In it, the author reported news of approximately 500 martyrs from the sons of Jaafar bin Abi Talib, Ali bin Abi Talib, and Aqeel bin Abi Talib, who died in defense of the oppressed or in the revolutions against the Umayyad state and the Abbasid state, especially the revolution of Hussein bin Ali against Yazid bin Muawiyah.
descriptions.1207: The book “A Summary of the Islamic Conquests” by the writer Taha Abd al-Maqsoud Abd al-Hamid Abu Ubayya is a historical book that deals with the path of the spread of the Islamic State from the time of the Prophet ﷺ until the conquests in Morocco and Andalusia, reviewing the campaigns in the East, the Byzantine regions, and the stages of conquest in North Africa and Western Europe. The work focuses on the military and political aspects of the conquests, explaining the stages of exploration, settlement, and establishment of Islamic rule in the conquered areas. It provides the reader with a comprehensive overview of conquest strategies and their development throughout different eras.
descriptions.1208: The book “The Battle of Yarmouk, Study and Analysis” by the writer Muhammad Al-Sayyid Al-Wakil deals with a detailed historical analysis of the Battle of Yarmouk, based on a geographical description of the site and detailing the steps of the military leaders from Khalid bin Al-Walid to the Caliph. It highlights leadership strategies and attack and defense tactics, and is based on the table of contents, which deals with the stages of preparation, planning, and execution of the battle, and the Muslim victory over the Romans. This work is considered a reference in studying the military and political dimensions of the battle within a comprehensive historical framework.
descriptions.1209: This book deals with historical events that occurred in Andalusia during the rule of the Nasrid kings, focusing on the reign of Prince Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Saad. The author mentions the news of the kings and their political and military events, focusing on the stages of the fall of their state and their victories and defeats in the face of enemies. The book is limited to brevity and conciseness in describing events without expanding into details.
descriptions.1210: The book “The Rapture in the History of the Pre-Islamic Arabs” by the scholar Ibn Sa’id al-Maghribi provides a detailed history of some ancient Arab tribes in the Arabian Peninsula and neighboring regions. The book deals with historical events and legends related to the tribes of Ad, Thamud, Tasm, the Giants, and others, with a focus on their origins, locations, and religious and mythological stories. The book combines history and mythology, and also reviews some of the kings and rulers who ruled these tribes in ancient times.
descriptions.1211: A historical book that studies the systems of government and political fees in the Umayyad state in Andalusia, from its inception in 138 AH until its fall in 422 AH. In two volumes, the book deals with the political, administrative, and financial system, in addition to political, war, and religious plans such as the hijab, the ministry, the army, the judiciary, the hisbah, and the police. The research aims to explain how the presidency of the state and the Crown Prince are organized, while linking these systems to the general political situation of the state.
descriptions.1212: This book deals with anecdotes and events that occurred during the eras of the Umayyad and Abbasid caliphs, focusing on the interesting facts and inspiring situations that took place during the era of these caliphs. In this historical work, author Muhammad al-Atlidi deals with stories and wisdom from the lives of the caliphs and ministers, relying on events that happened to the Baramkehs with the Abbasids. The book begins with a story of Omar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) with an old woman from Medina, thus presenting a picture of the caliph’s sensitivity and understanding of the circumstances of his subjects.
descriptions.1213: The book “The Martyrdom of Al-Hussein, may God be pleased with him, among the facts” by Ali Muhammad Al-Sallabi is concerned with studying the biography of Imam Al-Hussein bin Ali in terms of his lineage and virtues, and opens the door to investigating the facts that led to his martyrdom in Karbala, with a distinction between what is proven and what is delusional. It is based on the classification of biographies and classes, and reviews the details of Hussein’s departure to Kufa, the positions of the companions and followers, and the stages of the conflict with Yazid and Ubayd Allah bin Ziyad, up to the battle of Karbala and the fate of its people. It concludes by highlighting the positions of Hussein's companions after his martyrdom and identifying the disputed responsibilities in those events.
descriptions.1214: The Dangerous Durra fi Poets of the Peninsula by Ibn al-Qattaa al-Siqilli is a reference of biographies and classes that specializes in the biography and poetry of a group of poets of the Peninsula, as it includes all of the jurists, judges, writers, and princes, with examples of their poems. The content is arranged according to the names of poets, and each personality is presented with a brief overview that highlights their literary and jurisprudential characteristics, along with poetic excerpts that demonstrate their style. The book is an important source for researchers in ancient Arabic literature and the history of the island.
descriptions.1215: Al-Rawd al-Aneeq fi Fadl al-Siddiq is a book mentioning the virtue of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911). In it, the author collected forty hadiths about the Prophet, which show the degree and status of the Rightly Guided Caliph regarding the Greatest Messenger. Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti said in the introduction to his book:
descriptions.1216: Al-Rawdah Al-Fayhaa fi Alam Al-Nisa by Yassin Al-Khatib is a collection of biographies and classes that sheds light on righteous women in Islamic history, starting from Eve and her wife Sarah to the women of the Companions and followers such as Khadija, Aisha, and Fatima Al-Zahra. The book includes detailed articles on various personalities, including the wives of the prophets, women mentioned in the Prophet’s biography, and mothers of the believers, relying on Qur’anic texts and noble hadiths to explain their virtues and positions. This work is a reference that organizes information about the lives and achievements of women within the framework of biographies organized according to the classification of biographies and classes.
descriptions.1217: The book, which is of the type of biographies and classes, presents the biography of the venerable Sheikh Omar Al-Mukhtar, from his birth and lineage to his activity in the Libyan jihad. The author covers the details of his upbringing, his education at the Jaghbub Institute, his qualities and courage, in addition to his battles with the Italian occupation and his travels to Egypt. The work also concludes with an account of his last days, his captivity, trial and execution, with reference to his correspondence and his role in the negotiations.
descriptions.1218: The book “Sheikh Izz al-Din bin Abdul Salam - Sultan of Scholars” by Ali Muhammad al-Salabi is a type of biographies and classes. It sheds light on the biography of the jurisprudential and military scholar in the era of the Crusades and the confrontation with the Mongols, reviewing his lineage, upbringing, and perseverance in seeking knowledge. The book discusses his sheikhs, students, and his works in teaching, fatwas, judiciary, and public speaking, in addition to his qualities and principles in innovation, education, etiquette, and Sufism. The author aims to show the role of Sheikh Izz al-Din as a prominent jurist leader who contributed to the victories of the Islamic nation.
descriptions.1219: This book, “Sunni Classes in Hanafi Biographies,” by Taqi al-Din al-Ghazi, deals with the biographies and conditions of famous Hanafi scholars, presenting selected biographies of prominent figures in the Hanafi school of thought throughout history. The book aims to introduce the reader to the imams of this school of thought and their followers, with a focus on the greatest scholars who followed the example of Ibn Thabit al-Numan Abu Hanifa, the founder of the Hanafi school of thought, and followed his words and actions. The book is a type of traditional book that is concerned with biographies and classes. It provides a comprehensive overview of the development of the Hanafi school of thought over the ages, noting the importance of Hanafi scholars in spreading and activating their jurisprudence.
descriptions.1220: Al-Ghurar fi the Virtues of Omar is a book mentioning the virtues of Omar ibn al-Khattab, written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849 AH - 911 AH), in which the author mentioned forty hadiths on the authority of the Messenger in mentioning Omar ibn al-Khattab.
descriptions.1221: Study of the Titles of Poets by Al-Nashabi Al-Erbli is an author of biographies and classes who specializes in studying the titles of Arab poets, dividing them into chapters according to the reason for the title, such as what is derived from his poetry, or from his mark, or from his color, or from a verb that dominates his name. The book includes a narration of many poets, explaining their lineage and the sayings that gave them their titles. It relies on a precise classification methodology without length.
descriptions.1222: The comprehensive dictionary of biographies of contemporary scholars and students of science is a dictionary that includes biographies of contemporary scholars and students of science, collected by members of the Ahl al-Hadith Forum from electronic sources and arranged alphabetically to facilitate access to information. It is classified into biographies and classes, and is presented in a comprehensive manner that contributes to documenting the biography of scientific figures in various arts.
descriptions.1223: This is a book of biographies related to Imam Muhyiddin al-Nawawi, in which the author al-Sakhawi collected his biography and his stories, relying on what his student Alaa al-Din Ibn al-Attar included, with additions that he distinguished by saying, “I said.” The book begins by mentioning al-Nawawi’s lineage, birth, and upbringing, then addresses his sheikhs, classifications, jobs, and disciples, arriving at his qualities, virtues, asceticism, piety, and dignity, singling out the words of the scholars in his books and those who translated him.
descriptions.1224: The book presents a brief file of events and deaths throughout history, covering political, religious, and scientific figures from ancient civilizations and Islamic figures, mentioning important historical events such as the building of the pyramids in Egypt, the establishment of the unified Jewish kingdom in Palestine, the Battle of Kadesh, and others. The book is incomplete and includes events before Islamic history and characters from the ancient Pharaohs and kings, in addition to Islamic events and people. The author expressed his desire to complete and develop it in the future.
descriptions.1225: Tuhfat al-Talibin in the Translation of Imam al-Nawawi is a book of biography and biographies presented by Ibn al-Attar. It specializes in the biography of Imam Abu Zakaria Yahya bin Sharaf al-Khuzami al-Nawawi, and reviews his lineage and ancestry, his birth and death, the principles of his work, his vision, his sheikhs in jurisprudence, language, and hadith, his books, his dignities, and his positions with scholars and kings, according to his classification in biographies and classes. It aims to collect his virtues and exploits and document his scientific and spiritual journey for readers.
descriptions.1226: Brief biographies of prominent figures is an encyclopedia of brief biographies of prominent figures of Islam, classified into biographies and classes and automatically arranged according to letters. The book includes brief biographies of scholars, narrators, and historical figures, mentioning their names, times of their death, and their writings or positions. It aims to provide a quick reference for those looking for basic information about these figures.
descriptions.1227: The book “Men of the Ten Pendants” by Al-Ghalayini covers a wide range of historical, geographical and cultural information about the Arabs before Islam, as it focuses on describing their land, country, locations, lineage, customs and morals. The book also includes information about the Arab kingdoms of that period and their linguistic and literary developments, while providing an overview of the pre-Islamic era, its literature and sciences. The book is a machine-numbered book, which facilitates access to the required information easily and quickly.
descriptions.1228: “The Predecessors of the Age in the Virtues of Poets in All Egypt” written by Ibn Masum al-Hasani is a tragic work that specializes in mentioning the virtues and sayings of Egyptian poets, as it includes a collection of biographies and classes of many of the poets and scholars mentioned in the index. The content of the book is limited to providing overviews of these writers while highlighting aspects of their eloquence and virtues. The author has arranged them in an automatic order that facilitates access to each character. The book opens with a poetic sermon that glorifies the value of poetry and eloquence. It begins with a glorification of the Prophet Muhammad, which reflects the literary and spiritual character of the book.
descriptions.1229: The book “Correct Your Copy of Tahdheeb al-Kamal” by the writer Eid Fahmy is a work of the type of translations and classes concerned with correcting the printed text of the book “Tahdheeb al-Kamal” regarding the names of men. It provides rules of spelling and care for adjusting the text, in addition to instructions on adjusting genealogies and restricting the names of countries. The book also includes scientific notes on the footnotes, with an analysis of typographical corrections and attribution to sources, and is considered a reference that contributes to improving the quality of heritage texts.
descriptions.1230: The book “The Tales of Dhakhira and the Tales of the Island” by the writer Al-Asaad bin Mamati is a book of the type of biographies and classes, in which it collects the biographies of poets, authors, and visitors of Andalusia, mentioning their titles and positions. It includes chapters on birds and pigeons, in addition to biographies of a number of ministers and poets. The book also deals with topics related to literature and rhetoric and is based on a narrative style that links historical events and literary stories. The work highlights the diversity of content between autobiography, natural and linguistic themes.
descriptions.1231: The book “Masmarat Al-Darif bi Hasan Definition” by Sheikh Muhammad Al-Senussi is the author of biographies and classes, which includes sequences from the biographies of Mawla Hussein Pasha Bey and other Tunisian pashas, ​​with reference to the dates of their mandates and positions. The first part includes an introduction to the imams of the Zaytouna Mosque, which adds a scientific dimension to the work alongside the historical narrative of the authorities. The content is arranged in a mechanical order that links the characters and the time periods, and shows their efforts in building palaces, schools, and mosques. The book aims to document the paths of these leaders and scholars in the history of Tunisia.
descriptions.1232: This book deals with the biographies of the Hanbali author’s sheikhs and scholars, mentioning their names and the most important information about them. It focuses on the series of sheikhs and scholars from whom he learned, while providing an overview of their lineage and works. The book is a type of traditional book dealing with translations and classes, and is automatically numbered to facilitate use.
descriptions.1233: The Dictionary of the Companions of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah is a biographical dictionary specializing in the companions and scholars of Imam Ibn Taymiyyah, collecting brief information about them. It was prepared by the author Walid Al-Amawi, based on classic biographical sources such as the books of Al-Dhahabi, Ibn Kathir, and others, and based on what they heard of his knowledge and their praise of him. The dictionary is arranged according to the letters of the Arabic alphabet, and includes the names of several personalities from different sects and countries, with an indication of their works, if any.
descriptions.1234: This is a dictionary that includes biographies of Arab poets throughout the ages from pre-Islamic times until the middle of the twentieth century, arranged alphabetically. The book deals with the lives of poets and their most important poetic contributions, with a focus on notables from different eras and generations, who have at least one or two verses. The dictionary includes brief information about the upbringing of poets, their lives, and their literary works, while providing an overview of some of their poetic and scientific works.
descriptions.1235: This book is biographies of poets bearing the name “Amr” from various eras, starting from pre-Islamic times until the days of the Abbasids. The author, Muhammad bin Daoud bin Al-Jarrah, deals with the lives of these poets and their poems in a brief manner, relying on the news, lineages, and poems reported about them, and aims to give a comprehensive picture of the famous and little-known poets who bear this name.
descriptions.1236: A book that translates two of the most prominent innovators in Islam, Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and it introduces their lineage, upbringing, sheikhs, and scholarly and advocacy efforts. The author aims to explain the truth about their Salafist call and doctrine, and to respond to the suspicions that have been raised about them, while clarifying the origins of their call based on monotheism and following the approach of the Salaf.
descriptions.1237: The book “The Whiff of Rihanna and the Splatter of Paint from the Bar” by the author Al-Muhibbi is a tragic and practical reference that specializes in mentioning the virtues and personalities of the poets of Damascus and its environs, and arranges them according to lineages and famous families in literature. The book includes chapters in which the names of poets and authors from prominent houses are listed, with references to their peers and relatives, which shows the network of literary relations in that region. The text begins with a rhetorical introduction that expresses the glorification of God and eloquence, paving the reader to the educational and declarative narration style followed in the biography.
descriptions.1238: Nour Al-Qabas by Al-Ghamwari is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in the biography of grammarians, scholars, and narrators, especially those from Basra. It includes an introduction urging the pursuit of knowledge and mastery of the Arabic language. The author relies on previous sources, such as Al-Shihab Al-Qabas, and presents information about several personalities, including jurists and linguists, with reference to their role in grammar and reading. It aims to provide a documented reference for researchers in the sciences of the Arabic language and its history.
descriptions.1239: The book “Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, the First of the Rightly Guided Caliphs” by the writer Muhammad Reda is classified among biographies and classes, and presents the biography of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) with a focus on his role as the first caliph after the death of the Prophet ﷺ. In its chapters, the author deals with the details of the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr, his management of the events of apostasy, and sending armies to various regions, in addition to his battles and positions that contributed to establishing the Islamic State. The book aims to clarify the biography of the Caliph and highlight his wisdom and courage in facing the challenges that faced the Islamic community in that period.
descriptions.1240: The Conditions of Men It is also called the Book of Knowledge of Men, and some of them call it: Al-Jarh wal-Ta'deel or Al-Du'afa'in. The book specializes in criticizing wounded narrators, liars, or innovators. It was written by Ibrahim bin Yaqoub bin Ishaq Al-Saadi Al-Jawzjani.
descriptions.1241: The book “News of Abu Hafs Omar bin Abdul Aziz (may Allah have mercy on him) and his biography” by Al-Ajri falls within the biographies and classes, and collects the news and biography of Omar bin Abdul Aziz among the Muslims until his death. The text quotes from multiple narratives transmitted through a series of narrators, and relies on stories and situations recorded in various sources. It aims to document the life and details of the Caliph Al-Rashid according to the traditional biographical approach.
descriptions.1242: The book “Akhbar Abu Hanifa and His Companions” by Sheikh Al-Saymari is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in the biography of Abu Hanifa Al-Numan bin Thabit and the details of his personal and scientific life. It covers his lineage, description, moral features, the beginnings of his jurisprudence, and his positions with the Companions and Followers, in addition to what was narrated about him of piety, asceticism, honesty, and generosity. It also includes news of his contemporaries, including caliphs and scholars, and mentions of what was mentioned in his praise and poetry praising him, as well as details of his death. The book aims to collect narratives and hadiths about Abu Hanifa to provide a comprehensive picture of his personality and his place in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.1243: The book “News of the Scholars of the Best of the Wise” by Jamal al-Din al-Qifti is a book of the type of biographies and classes that aims to collect the biography and works of the wise and scholars from different eras and nations. The content is arranged according to the letters of the alphabet, with each letter devoted to a list of names, mentioning their books and their details, with a special focus on the works of Galen and other philosophical and natural sources. In the introduction to the book, the author provides an indication of the differences between scholars in determining who was the first to speak in the field of wisdom, and relies on historical and literary sources to document the information. This book is a reference that makes it easy for the reader to learn about the lives and thoughts of the sages and the history of their writings.
descriptions.1244: This book, “The News of Judges” by Imam Muhammad bin Khalaf al-Dhabi, known as “Waki’,” deals with the biography of judges and their news throughout the ages, discussing the sayings of scholars in the judiciary and its virtue, and reviewing some of the Prophet’s hadiths and jurisprudential orders related to this field. The author focuses on the importance of the judiciary and the conditions of the judge, and deals with the lives of a number of prominent judges throughout Islamic history, with reference to their experiences and the sayings of their scholars. The book is of the type of biographies and classes, and it aims to present a comprehensive picture of the judicial profession in Islam and its development over time.
descriptions.1245: This book, “Akhbar al-Makkiyyin,” written by Ibn Abi Khaythamah, is classified under the category of biographies and classes. The book contains a table of contents that explains the content of the book, which appears to deal with the history of the city of Mecca and its antiquities, while mentioning some hadiths of the Prophet related to the subject. Excerpts from the beginning of the book indicate the presence of a Syriac book in the pillar or shrine in Mecca, and some prophetic hadiths related to Mecca are mentioned, such as hadiths about the Messenger of God ﷺ. The book seems to aim to document Meccan history and antiquities, while mentioning some information about the origin of the name Mecca and its antiquities.
descriptions.1246: This book, by Al-Serafi Abu Saeed, deals with the news of the Basra grammarians and documents their scientific ties, mentioning details of their lives and sayings. The book begins with a discussion of who was the first to draw up grammar, then deals with the life of Abu Al-Aswad Al-Du'ali and his role in spreading the science of grammar. The book then reviews the lives of a number of prominent visual grammar scholars.
descriptions.1247: This book deals with the news of women who came to Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan, focusing on their conversations and stories with him. The book includes dialogues and stories of women from different tribes, presenting their interactions with the Commander of the Faithful, Muawiyah, in different situations, showing aspects of these women’s lives, thoughts, and political and social opinions. The book is of the type of biographies and classes, and it reviews the biographies of prominent women in the era of Muawiyah.
descriptions.1248: This book deals with the news of the men arriving to Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan, focusing on the delegations of the people of Kufa to him. The book mentions stories and events related to these delegations, and reviews prominent figures among them, focusing on their dialogue and discussions with Muawiyah. The book is of the type of biographies and classes, and aims to record and trace the words and actions of these men at that time.
descriptions.1249: This book is a translation of Judge Ayyad, written by Al-Maqri Al-Tilmisani, and it falls in the category of biographies and classes. The book deals with the biography of Judge Ayyad, his life, works, and writings, with mention of some of his sheikhs and professors. It also contains an overview of Judge Ayyad's academic and personal condition, in addition to some poetry written in praise of him. The book aims to shed light on Judge Ayyad’s contributions in the field of science and literature, and to provide a comprehensive picture of his personality and role in Islamic history.
descriptions.1250: The book “Names of those Narrated by Muhammad bin Ismail al-Bukhari” by the writer Ibn Adi falls within the category of biographies and classes. It aims to collect the names of the sheikhs who were narrated by Imam al-Bukhari in his Sahih, along with an explanation of their origins, lineages, and geographical locations. The content is arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, and each letter is separated with data about each name in terms of its birth, attribute, virtues, knowledge, and the news known about it. The author relies on contemporary accounts and testimonies to provide a glimpse into the personality of each sheikh, his level of knowledge, and his asceticism. The book concludes by providing additional details about some names according to the order of the letters.
descriptions.1251: The Lion of the Jungle in Knowledge of the Companions, also known as the Lion of the Jungle for short, is a book written by Ibn al-Atheer in which he attempted to survey all the Companions (i.e. those who accompanied the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) and their biographies. The author states in the introduction to the book his intention to comprehend four basic works from the books of the “Companions” that were written before him, which are the works of Abu Abdullah bin Mandah and Abu Naim Ahmad bin Abdullah (whom he described as memorizers) and Abu Omar bin Abdul-Barr Al-Qurtubi (who described them as Imam), and Abu Musa Muhammad bin Abi Bakr bin Abi Issa Al-Isfahani, complementing the work of Ibn Mandah, in addition to others, including Abu Ali Al-Ghassani. …
descriptions.1252: The book “The Names of the Mudallisin” by Al-Suyuti is considered a reference in the classification of biographies and classes. It specializes in collecting the names of the Mudallisin from the scholars of hadith according to alphabetical order to facilitate identifying them. The book includes nice letters that list the names according to the letters of the dictionary, along with the authors’ documentation of the allegations related to the falsification of the hadith. The text shows an interest in clarifying the differences between Al-Suyuti’s words and the investigators’ comments in order to clarify what is attributed to each of them.
descriptions.1253: Names of Those Known by His Kunya by Ibn al-Fath al-Azdi is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in collecting the names of the Companions and Followers who were known by their nicknames. Its content is arranged according to the order of the letters of the Arabic alphabet from Alif to L, with each chapter containing a group of names and nicknames associated with it. In each entry, the author provides brief information about each character, based on what was mentioned in the Sunnah and narrations, as is evident from the index and the beginning excerpt, which lists examples from Chapter Alif and Chapter Ba. The book is a useful reference for researchers in the sciences of biography and hadith who wish to identify individuals through their surnames.
descriptions.1254: The book deals with the originality of the approach in the biography of King Abdulaziz bin Saud and its impact on the stability of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with a focus on the Wahhabi doctrine and Islamic law as the main foundations of the original approach followed by King Abdulaziz. The author also discusses the characteristics of this approach and the characteristics of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, noting the importance of adhering to the true guidance of Islam in achieving security, stability, and cultural renaissance.
descriptions.1255: The book “Images of the Prophet’s Biography in the Second Century of the Hijra” by Farouk Hamada falls within the category of biographies and classes, and reviews the figures of the Prophet’s biography that emerged in the second century of the Hijra. The author divides the content of the work into four main parts that conclude with a summary, sources, and references, which shows an organized scientific methodology in presenting the biography. The book aims to provide an objective study that contributes to understanding the developments of the Prophet’s biography in that historical period.
descriptions.1256: Notables of the Age and Helpers of Victory by Al-Safadi is a book of biographies and classes that sheds light on prominent figures from his time, mentioning their names, lineages, and positions, with a focus on those who had a role in victory or support. The index includes a wide range of names, especially those bearing the name Abraham, and adopts a traditional style of introduction that opens with the mention of God and the Messenger. The author aims to document their lives and provide references for researchers in Islamic history.
descriptions.1257: A book on biographies and classes that specializes in the titles of the Companions and Followers as mentioned in the two Sahih Musnads, and clarifies what is permissible to mention names without adding an insult or omission. The author divides the content of the book into alphabetical chapters dealing with the Companions and Followers according to the letters, and attaches an introduction that explains the rulings on mentioning surnames in the science of hadith. It aims to acquaint the reader with the names of famous people in Sindh and explain the purposes of their use in accordance with the directives of jurists and hadith scholars.
descriptions.1258: The book “Irshad Al-Qasi and Near to the Biographies of the Sheikhs of Al-Tabarani” is considered one of the important books in the field of biographies and classes, as it presents a translation of the sheikhs of Imam Abi Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani. The book shows the importance of this work in facilitating students of knowledge in finding translations of the sheikhs of Al-Tabarani and the people of that class, which contributes to understanding the conditions of men and judging hadiths. The book provides translations of a large number of sheikhs, and is a valuable resource for those interested in studying translations and classes. The book shows a blessed effort in facilitating difficulties for students of science, and is considered a tremendous scientific wealth in the field of translations.
descriptions.1259: Is’af al-Mutta’ bi Rijal al-Muwatta is one of the books of hadith and one of the books of al-Jarh wal-Ta’deel, written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911). The book specialized in biographies of the narrators mentioned in Muwatta’ of Imam Malik. Al-Hafiz al-Suyuti began his book with an introduction in which he collected the sayings of some scholars of al-Jarh wal-Ta’dil that clarified Imam Malik’s approach and approach in narrating and narrating on trustworthy narrators. After that, al-Suyuti mentioned the names of the narrators from whom Malik narrated in Al-Muwatta’, where he arranged them according to the letters of the dictionary, and Al-Suyuti’s method in translating the narrator is as follows: He mentions the narrator’s name, lineage, nickname, and his references if he was a companion, then he mentions his sheikhs from whom he narrated, and his students who narrated from him, then he mentions some of the sayings of the scholars of jarh and hadith in it,...
descriptions.1260: This book, “Ikmal al-Ikmal” by Ibn Nuqtah, is a continuation of the book “Al-Ikmal” by Ibn Makula, in which the author deals with the biographies of the hadith scholars whose books Ibn Makula collected, and adds to it what he overlooked or what was mentioned after his death. The book focuses on clarifying the translations and the necessary corrections, relying on trustworthy and reliable sources, and aims to remove doubts and clarify the facts in the field of translations and classes.
descriptions.1261: The book “Intention of Narrators on Intention of Grammarians” written by Jamal al-Din al-Qifti is one of the books that deals with biographies and classes. The book covers biographies of grammarians and imams of the language, providing an overview of their lives, sciences, and writings, with a focus on grammar narrators and their transmission of knowledge. The book is part of a series of Arabic books concerned with documenting scholars and imams of various sciences, which provides researchers and scholars with a reliable source for knowing the facts about these scholars and their works.
descriptions.1262: Al-Manawi’s book “Ithāf al-ṣīl bima Fatimah al-Mākim al-Mākim al-Mākim al-Māqīl and Virtues” by Al-Mānawi deals with the biography of Fatima al-Zahra (may Allah be pleased with her), as it focuses on her virtues and virtues by reviewing the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with her, starting with her birth and naming, through her marriage to Ali bin Abi Talib, and reaching her high position in Islam. The book discusses her virtues through a group of hadiths that show her status and the Prophet’s love for her, with a focus on her protection, care, and concern for her.
descriptions.1263: This book deals with the life of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab (may Allah have mercy on him) through a detailed study of his social, political and scientific environment, his journeys in seeking knowledge, his students and his writings, and also discusses his thought about hisbah, sincerity and wisdom. The author aims to present a comprehensive picture of the personality of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his intellectual and religious influence on his society.
descriptions.1264: The book presents the dependence of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s call on the Qur’an and Sunnah through an analysis of the environment in which he grew up and the circumstances that contributed to the formation of his personality and call. The author Manaa Al-Qattan focuses on understanding the social and cultural factors that influenced Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, how he interacted with his environment and society, and his role in spreading the Wahhabi call based on the principles of the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book also discusses how the social environment and traditions influenced the formation of the preacher’s personality and his success in spreading his message.
descriptions.1265: The book “Adopting the Jurisprudence of the Call of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab” by the writer Saleh bin Abdul Rahman Al-Atram falls within the classification of biographies and classes, and systematically reviews the extent to which the Sheikh’s call is based on the Qur’an and Sunnah through studying his biography, his sayings, and his doctrinal foundations. In three substantive sections, the author discusses the rules that the Sheikh established for unifying worship, his evidence for that in his writings, and what his predecessor scholars said about his approach. The work aims to show the link between the call of the Sheikh and the righteous predecessors and its impact on the individual and society.
descriptions.1266: The High Notables in the Virtues of Ibn Taymiyyah is a book written by Abu Hafs Al-Bazzar in which he explains the biography of Ibn Taymiyyah and the praise and praise of Ibn Taymiyyah by the Sunni scholars.
descriptions.1267: Al-A'lam is a dictionary of biographies of prominent Arab, Arab, and Orientalist men and women prepared by Khair al-Din al-Zirkali. The book includes multiple introductions explaining the classification of encyclopedias and the history of the preparation of the work, which was launched in 1912 and was published in three editions until 1969. The index includes chapters arranged alphabetically and details such as Hijri, Gregorian, death of pre-Islamic people, and sources of information, making it a comprehensive reference in the field of biographies and classes.
descriptions.1268: Briefing on the News of Granada is a book by the Andalusian writer San al-Din Ibn al-Khatib. It is considered one of the most important Andalusian history books on which researchers have relied. The subject of the book is to talk about the history of Granada, the last Islamic stronghold that fell in Andalusia. It is an encyclopedia that chronicles everything related to this city in terms of news, descriptions, and historical landmarks, perhaps the first of which is the Alhambra Palace. The writer has taken care to cover all the geographical aspects of sites and topography, and the intellectual and social aspects (the history of those who visited it since the era of the first Arabs, the writers, poets, writers, ministers, and conquerors who passed through it, a translation of more than 500 important figures in the city’s history,...) but what is noted is that Ali Ibn al-Khatib in his book Count...
descriptions.1269: The Guidance in the Knowledge of Hadith Scholars by Sheikh Abu Ya’la Al-Khalili is a reference of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in documenting the biography and academic degree of a number of hadith narrators, with a focus on the students and followers of Imam Malik. The book includes detailed indexes of the names of scholars, explaining the areas of trust and weakness in their narrations and the sources of their chain of transmission. It aims to guide the reader to know the authenticity of hadiths by evaluating their authors according to the traditional standards of hadith.
descriptions.1270: Al-Isaabah fi Tamiyez al-Sahabah is a book written by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in which he sought to survey all the Companions (i.e. those who accompanied the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) and their biographies. It is considered one of the most important and extensive books ever written in the history of Islam, and its subject is distinguishing between the Companions: those whose companionship was authentic and those who were not, and whose existence was authentic or not. The total number of his translations is (12,446) translations. It took forty years to write.
descriptions.1271: The book “Information by Notable Men in the History of India” by Abd al-Hay al-Hasani is a book in the category of biographies and classes. It includes a collection of biographies of prominent figures and scholars of India from the first to the seventh century, with reference to their origins and roles in society. The content is organized into layers according to time periods, and is based on a traditional method that aims to collect and document news of writers, sheikhs, and kings who wrote the Islamic history of India.
descriptions.1272: The completion of mentioning those who have a narration in the Musnad of the Imam by Ibn al-Husseini is a tragic reference that specializes in the names of the narrators from whom hadiths were mentioned in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad. The author arranges the names according to the order of the letters of the Arabic alphabet, and adds a special section for nicknames, allowing the reader to view biographical and trustworthy information for each narrator. The book falls within the literature concerned with documenting and evaluating hadith narrators.
descriptions.1273: This book, “Al-Ikmaal fi Rafi’ al-Doubt A’n Al-Mu’alif and Al-Different in Names, Surnames, and Genealogies” by Imam Ibn Makula, is one of the biographical books that dealt with names, surnames, and genealogies, in which the author provided detailed information about Arabic names and their classifications, reviewing the letters of the dictionary one by one. The book aims to clarify definitions and differences between names, nicknames, and lineages, relying on reliable scientific and literary sources.
descriptions.1274: A book of the type of biographies and classes written by Abdullah bin Abdul Mohsen Al Turki, which presents the biography of Imam Muhammad bin Saud as a leader who founded the first Saudi state and contributed to spreading the Salafist call, based on the political, religious and social conditions in Najd before its emergence. The author deals with the lineage of the Imam, his character, and his support for the call, in addition to the historical meeting with Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and the positions of contemporary figures from the Saudi state. It also includes Arab and foreign sources and references that document the path of the call and its development.
descriptions.1275: This book is a translation of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, covering his biography and mission, delivered as a lecture by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz. The book focuses on the Sheikh’s upbringing, his journeys in seeking knowledge, the circumstances of Najd before his appearance and call, the various reactions towards him, and the details of the call he began and the events that resulted from it. The book aims to shed light on the role played by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab in spreading the Wahhabi call and fighting polytheism and heresies in Najd.
descriptions.1276: This book, written by Mahmoud Sheet Khattab, deals with the study of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab in the city of Mosul. In his research, the author relies on information from the book “Gharib Al-Athar” by the historian Yassin bin Khairallah Al-Khatib Al-Omari Al-Mawsili, who mentioned that the Imam came to Mosul and read to the scholar Mulla Hamad Al-Jumaili. The book also reviews some historical details about the Imam’s visit to Mosul and his death, relying on accurate historical sources.
descriptions.1277: This book is by the scholar Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, and it is an encyclopedia of biographies and classes in which the narrators of the book Al-Athar by Imam Al-Shaybani dealt with it. In this work, the author deals with the biographies of narrators arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, then he details the nicknames and unknown persons, and mentions the information that can be reached about each narrator, whether he is a scholar of refinement or others. The author limited himself to being brief and concise in mentioning what indicates praise or slander, while including everyone mentioned in the Book of Antiquities, whether named or unnamed.
descriptions.1278: Al-Isti’ab fi Ma’rifat al-Ashaba is a book about translating the Companions, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Omar Yusuf bin Abdullah al-Nimri, known as Ibn Abd al-Barr (368-463). The book is considered one of the first books written about the Companions. The author’s approach in his book was to mention the Companion and those who narrated from him, and something from those who narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and some matters related to him, his death, and his age. Ibn Abd al-Barr collected in it what he was able to collect from the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned the following in the introduction to his book Al-Isti’abah: Ibn Hazm Al-Andalusi praised the collection of the works of his sheikh Ibn Abd al-Barr in general, in his talk about the virtues of Al-Andalus, and specifically praised his book Al-Isti’abah, saying:
descriptions.1279: Ibn Duraid’s book “Al-Ishtiqāq” deals with a detailed study of the origins of Arabic names and their derivations, focusing on the names of prominent Arab tribes and personalities. The author explains the Arabs' doctrines of naming during pre-Islamic times, and discusses some people's criticism of Arabic naming methods, defending the validity of names and their derivatives. In his book, Ibn Duraid goes beyond the scope of tribes and personalities to also include the names of plants and inanimate objects, focusing on names that may be ambiguous or controversial. The book aims to correct misconceptions about Arabic names and show the beauty and depth of their language.
descriptions.1280: This book, “Rejoicing at the One Who Was Accused of Mixing,” by the writer Burhan al-Din, the son of Ibn al-Ajami, deals with the subject of narrators who were accused of mixing at the end of their lives, and classifies them according to the letters of the dictionary. The author aims to determine the validity of accepting the narrations of these trustworthy people before and after the period of their mixing, while presenting a jurisprudential ruling on accepting or rejecting their narrations based on these determinations. The book falls within the category of biographies and classes, and reviews the lives and narratives of a group of well-known scholars and historians.
descriptions.1281: The book “Selection on the Virtues of the Three Imams of Jurists” by Sheikh Ibn Abd al-Barr is a work of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in narrating the news and sayings of the followers of the imams Malik bin Anas, al-Shafi’i, and al-Hanafi, while highlighting their virtues and positions in religion and science. It includes detailed content that mentions several names of their companions and followers, divided into two parts that deal with each imam separately, documenting their lineage, locations, and sayings. The author aims to summarize the virtues and instructions reported about these imams to facilitate their memorization and teaching to readers.
descriptions.1282: The book Al-Badr Rising with Virtues from After the Seventh Century by its author, Muhammad Al-Shawkani, in the history of Muslim figures from the eighth century AH to his time - and he died in the year 1250 AH - mentioning those who he considered to be among the diligent scholars and people of knowledge, and he included servants, caliphs, kings, and scholars among them if they were of great majesty, and he did not stipulate that those who were contemporary with them, if he included them in his book, be that they had reached their peak. He paid attention to stating the year of birth and death if he read it, and arranged his book according to the letters of the dictionary, so his biographies amounted to 596 translations.
descriptions.1283: Al-Lughah in the Biographies of the Imams of Grammar and Language is one of the works of Majd al-Din al-Fayrouzabadi, who died in the year 1414 AD. It deals with the biographies of the imams of grammar and language up to the author’s era. The work includes more than four hundred translations by poets, writers, jurists, grammarians, and linguists.
descriptions.1284: The book “The Middle History is erroneously printed under the name The Small History” written by Al-Bukhari, and is classified among biographies and classes, as it combines the biography of the Prophet ﷺ and the hadiths of the Companions and Followers, mentioning their origins and deaths. It includes diverse content from the stories of prominent figures such as Zainab, daughter of the Messenger of God, Khadija bint Khuwaylid, Hafsa, and Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman, in addition to records of deaths during the reigns of the caliphs from Abu Bakr to Ali and then subsequent periods. It also contains narratives about historical events and situations from the lives of immigrants, supporters, and followers, with reference to some unconventional stories such as “Al-Majishun.” The book aims to provide a comprehensive and brief overview of the nation’s history through what was mentioned in hadiths and narrations.
descriptions.1285: The Great History” by Ibn Abi Khaythamah is a book from the category of biographies and classes. It includes the second book of the author’s history and is divided into sections according to the letters of the Arabic alphabet, which shows a systematic organization of biographical and genealogical data. The text includes chains of chain of transmission that present historical hadiths and reports, and it also includes a narration of facts and opinions transmitted by narrators from generation to generation. This work is an important reference for researchers in the history of Arabs and Islam in the early periods.
descriptions.1286: Al-Tarikh Al-Kabir is one of the most prominent books of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama`ah in al-Jarh, al-Ta'deel, and Ilm al-Rijal. It was written by Imam Muhammad bin Ismail al-Bukhari and published it in Medina al-Nabawiyyah when he was eighteen years old. Al-Bukhari said: “When I had passed for eighteen years, I began to compile the cases and sayings of the Companions and Followers, and that was in the days of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, and I compiled the book of history at that time at the grave of the Prophet ﷺ on the moonlit nights. There is not a single name in history except that I have a story with it.” This book is considered one of the most important sources for biographies of narrators of the Prophet’s Hadith.
descriptions.1287: This book, “Al-Tabyin li Asma’ al-Mudallisin,” was written by Burhan al-Din, the son of Ibn al-Ajami, and falls within the scope of biographies and classes. The book deals with the topic of fraud in hadith and includes biographies of narrators based on dictionary letters and nicknames, along with an introduction that shows the importance of the science of chains of transmission in preserving the Islamic religion and scrutinizing the news. The author aims to document the men and scrutinize their hadiths to distinguish the correct from the incorrect in transmitting hadith.
descriptions.1288: The inscription in the great dictionary by Ibn Abd al-Karim al-Sam’ani is a book of classes and biographies that specializes in the names of scholars and jurists whose names begin with the letter alif. It gives each person a brief biography that includes their lineage, geographical locations, and their writings or imams, with an indication of their knowledge and sources. The index includes a wide range of names such as Abu Ishaq Al-Ansari, Abu Al-Futuh Al-Zainabi, and Ismail Al-Musaybi, which reflects the comprehensiveness of the work in documenting the layers of Islamic heritage. This book is an important reference for researchers in the field of biography and classes, and it falls within the series known as “The Great Dictionary.”
descriptions.1289: The Gentle Masterpiece in the History of the Noble City” by Sayyid Shams al-Din al-Sakhawi is a tragic and practical work that specializes in narrating the biographies and news of virtuous people in the city, and its content is arranged according to the order of the letters of the Arabic alphabet over two volumes. The book opens with a sermon that glorifies morals and virtues and highlights the importance of following the footsteps of the righteous. This is then followed by a group of chapters devoted to each letter of the language, concerned with documenting their information and histories within the context of the history of the honorable city.
descriptions.1290: The book “Al-Ta’deel wal-Jarih for those who Al-Bukhari narrated from him in Al-Jami’ Al-Sahih” by Suleiman bin Khalaf Al-Baji is concerned with studying the narrators of the hadith of Imam Al-Bukhari according to the methodology of Al-Jarh and Ta’deel, as it details the knowledge of the rules of criticism and consideration and presents chains of narration agreed upon as to their authenticity and presentation. It includes chapters that introduce the wounded and justice, and show ways to avoid mistakes, in addition to the biography of Al-Bukhari, his lineage, and the history of his writing of the mosque. The book is classified under biographies and classes, which makes it a reference for researchers in the sciences of hadith and the sciences of the novel.
descriptions.1291: This book deals with the ordeal of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and the torture and abuse he endured in order to defend the Sunnah of the Prophet. It presents his life, his writings, and his disciples, and discusses his role in the victory of the Sunnis over the heretics. The book also shows the virtue of Imam Ahmed and his efforts to spread knowledge and protect religion from heresies, with a focus on his patience and strength in the face of harm. The book also mentions the upbringing of Imam Ahmed and how it affected his personality and behavior.
descriptions.1292: This book, “The Limitation to Knowing the Narrators of Sunan and Musnad,” by Ibn Nuqtah, is a classification in the science of men that deals with knowledge of the narrators of the six major hadith books and other books of Sunan and Musnad. The book aims to provide information about the distortion and modification of these narrators and their status among scholars, with a focus on the most famous and popular among them. These works came at the request of Sheikh Al-Qurtubi, who wanted to know the news of the narrators and their level of investigation and editing.
descriptions.1293: This book deals with the biography of the Rightly Guided Caliph Othman bin Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), explaining his conditions and death in an objective manner that avoids bias or fanaticism. The author relies on reliable historical sources to narrate the events of the Caliphate of Uthman, and divides the book into twelve chapters that deal with various aspects of the Caliph’s life and death, with a focus on the political and social events that led to his calamity.
descriptions.1294: The book “Alert and Awakening to What is in the Footnotes of the Preservation Memorandum” by the scholar Ahmed Al-Tahtawi deals with a review and correction of some of the information contained in the footnotes of the Preservation Memorandum. It is a scholarly summary that aims to clarify the facts and correct what the author considered to be contradictory or inaccurate in the original sources. The book deals with topics related to the preservation classes and discusses the commentaries of the scholars of men, with an emphasis on providing new information and a careful review of the dates and events associated with the lives and writings of the scholars.
descriptions.1295: The Trustworthy People The book is considered one of the important scientific references in the science of wounds, modification, and knowing the conditions of men. Imams of hadith and diligent scholars refer to it in revealing the conditions of men and knowing the trustworthy ones from those who are wounded. The book was written by Ibn Hibban.
descriptions.1296: The book deals with the religious aspect in the life of King Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud, reviewing his words, actions, and religious positions, his interest in science and scholars, his foreign policy, and how this affected the unification of the country. The author, Dr. Khaled Muhammad Al-Saadi, focuses on the role of King Abdulaziz in building the third Saudi state and unifying it through his religious and moral perspective, indicating the importance of this aspect in the country’s renaissance and development.
descriptions.1297: Wound and modification. A book compiled by Al-Hafiz Ibn Abi Hatim, in which he spoke about the class of narrators, their classes, the degrees of their circumstances, and the varying degrees of their degrees, so that he would know who among them was in the position of criticizing, criticizing, criticizing, searching for men, and knowing them - and these are the people of acclamation, modification, and wounding. The great critics - this also supports his hadith. …
