descriptions.1298: This book, “The Luminous Jewels in the Hanafi Classes” by Judge Abdul Qadir al-Qurashi, deals with the biographies and conditions of scholars and hadith scholars of the Hanafi school of thought, arranging their names according to the alphabet. It focuses on providing brief information about their scientific and professional lives, with reference to the most important works they left behind. The book aims to highlight the role of Hanafi scholars in spreading and developing the jurisprudence of the school of thought throughout the ages.
descriptions.1299: Al-Durr al-Manthun fi Tabaqat Rabbat al-Khadur by Zainab Fawaz is a tragic and applied work that specializes in the biographies of different women from multiple eras and cultures. Its content is arranged alphabetically, starting with the letter Alif, and includes Arab characters such as Amna bint Abd al-Muttalib and non-Arab characters such as Arsinoe, daughter of Ptolemy I, and Artemisia, Queen of Halicarnassus. The book combines historical and graphic narration, relying on heritage sources to provide glimpses into the lives of these women and their place in their societies, relying on a narrative style that shows the aspects of wisdom, eloquence, and virtues for which they were known. The book remains a reference for researchers of women's history in Islamic and global heritage.
descriptions.1300: The Pearls Hidden in Notables of the Eighth Hundred is a book examining the science of translations, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani (773 AH - 852 AH). In it, the author collected the biographies of those who were in the eighth hundred of the Prophet’s Hijra from the beginning of the year 701 to the end of the year 800, from notables, scholars, kings, princes, writers, ministers, writers, and poets. He focused on the narrators of the Prophet’s hadith, so he mentioned those who were familiar with its condition and referred to some of its narrations. The author wrote the book in six parts. The author followed his book with a special volume called the tail of the pearls hidden in the notables of the ninth century, in which he translated the notables of the ninth century to the year 832 in the same manner as the notables of the eighth century, but he arranged them according to the years.
descriptions.1301: The book “Religion, Honor, and Chivalry in the Sense of King Abdulaziz” by Awad bin Ahmed Al-Shehri is considered one of the biographies and classes, as it sheds light on the biography of King Abdulaziz from an Islamic perspective in which it highlights conscious strength, innate intelligence, faith in God, and detachment from the temptations of prestige and power. In his chapters, the author discusses a group of elements that link religious values ​​and national responsibility, such as establishing the state on Islamic foundations, enjoining good and forbidding evil, and patience and wisdom in managing state affairs. The book aims to show how faith and professional values ​​were embodied in the king’s behavior, and the resulting impact on uniting the nation and preserving the security of Muslims.
descriptions.1302: A book of ammunition on the virtues of the people of the Peninsula, written by Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Bassam Al-Shantarini, one of the most prominent Andalusian writers and critics, in the fifth and sixth centuries AH. He was born on the island of Sintrin, where he has lineage, in a well-to-do family that took care of raising him, educating him, and preparing him for a prosperous future. Ibn Bassam showed some literary talent from a young age, and began writing poetry and prose, which attracted attention. The book “Al-Dhakhira fi Al-Mahasin Al-Jazira” is a source of great importance for the researcher in the history and literature of Andalusia during the period of the Taifa kings, which followed the end of the Umayyad Caliphate of Cordoba, the fifth century AH / eleventh century AD. …
descriptions.1303: This book, “The Pure Prophetic Offspring” by Al-Dulabi, deals with the series of genealogies and biographies related to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his descendants, focusing on the lineage and family of Khadija bint Khuwaylid (may Allah be pleased with her), the Prophet’s wife, and mentioning her children and their grandchildren. The book also includes hadiths and narrations about Al-Hasan, Al-Hussein, and the sons of Ali (may Allah be pleased with them), providing a comprehensive overview of the Prophet’s family and its descendants.
descriptions.1304: Al-Radd Al-Wafir is a book written by Ibn Nasir al-Din al-Dimashqi, in which he clarifies the names of the scholars from the Sunnis and the community who gave Ibn Taymiyyah the title of Sheikh of Islam, and he mentions something in it and mentions more than 80 scholars who praised him. The reason for writing the book is to respond to those who claim that whoever calls Ibn Taymiyyah the Sheikh of Islam is an infidel.
descriptions.1305: The book was written by Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi and falls within the category of biographies and classes, as it specializes in mentioning trustworthy narrators and what necessitates or does not necessitate their rejection based on what he recorded in his work “Al-Mizan.” The author explains the issue of trust in the Companions, followers, and some imams, clarifying the differences between approved wounds and rejected wounds, and presents this within a chapter framework dealing with credited wounds and rejected wounds.
descriptions.1306: Al-Riyadh al-Nadhra fi the Virtues of the Ten by al-Tabari Muhib al-Din is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in mentioning the virtues of the ten honorable companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and presents in detail their exploits and virtues according to multiple sections that include what was mentioned about their virtue, the warning against delving into their trees, and what concerns the four caliphs, Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman. The second section of the book also adds the virtues of individuals, as it devotes detailed chapters to each of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Hafs Omar ibn al-Khattab, dealing with their lineage, the conversion of their parents to Islam, their names, characteristics, migrations, characteristics, virtues, differences, and other topics related to their lives. The book is divided into two volumes, each of which includes organized chapters that shed light on the biography and history of these companions and caliphs.
descriptions.1307: The fifth book of the book “Al-Dhayl” and the sequel to “My Book” by Al-Ansari Al-Marrakshi is part of a collection of biographies and classes dealing with the biographies of historical figures, as it includes a group of entries detailing the lives of individuals from the Abd al-Malik dynasty in alphabetical order. The preparation of this book relied on three main manuscripts, while preserving the marginal comments that were documented in the first version. The book aims to document the information available about these notables and present it systematically to researchers in the field of biography and genealogy.
descriptions.1308: “Behaviour in the Classes of Scholars and Kings” by the soldier writer Bahaa al-Din is a work of the type of biographies and classes that sheds light on the behavior of scholars and kings throughout the ages, based on what was reported from genealogies and historical news. The book is divided into two parts, each of which is concerned with mentioning and evaluating different Islamic figures, with a focus on distinguishing the good from the bad and explaining their impact in religion and the world. The author combines historical narrative and moral statement based on Qur’anic texts and references to Salafi scholars and interpreters.
descriptions.1309: The behavior to know the states of the kings is one of the most important historical books by the scholar Al-Maqrizi. The book is the fourth part of Al-Maqrizi’s books on the history of Egypt. The first of them is the statement and parsing of those who entered Egypt among the Bedouins. The second is the contract of the Jawaher Al-Asfat in the news of the city of Fustat. The third is the preaching of the Hanafi with the news of the Fatimid imams, the caliphs. The fourth is the book in our hands, which dates to the period of rule of the Ayyubid state and the Mamluk state of Egypt, which is an important period of Islamic history, especially since it accompanied the emergence of personalities. And Important Events, which is a historical book considered one of the most prominent works of the Egyptian historian Taqi al-Din al-Maqrizi and the most important books written about the history of medieval Egypt, in which al-Maqrizi collected and recorded a lot of information about…
descriptions.1310: Tashkubarizadeh (901 - 968 AH / 1495 - 1561 AD) was an Ottoman historian. He is Ahmed bin Mustafa bin Khalil: Abu Al-Khair, Essam Al-Din Tashakbarizadeh. He was born in Brusa and grew up in Ankara. He became the judge in Istanbul in the year 958 AH.
descriptions.1311: The book “The Pure Testimony in the Imams’ Praise of Ibn Taymiyyah” by Al-Mar’i Al-Karmi falls within the category of biographies and classes, and is concerned with praising Imam Ibn Taymiyyah and documenting what the imams and scholars said about him. It includes a chapter on the death of Sheikh al-Islam, a nice conclusion, and a warning, and is based on an introductory style that highlights expressions of praise and remembrance.
descriptions.1312: This book deals with the life and thought of Sheikh Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his approach to matters of faith. The author, Amna Muhammad Naseer, focuses on studying the Sheikh’s approach in purifying the concept of monotheism from polytheism, and analyzing his thought and its influence on Islamic thought and politics. The book covers various aspects of the Sheikh’s life and times, and discusses his positions on doctrinal and practical issues, with a focus on the role of faith in building the individual and society.
descriptions.1313: In his book “The Slandered Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab Al-Mujaddid,” Sheikh Ahmed bin Hajar Al Butami presents a translation of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab (may Allah have mercy on him), explaining his role in reforming society and rejecting polytheism and heresies. The book focuses on responding to the suspicions and lies that were attached to Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his followers, and shows the efforts he made in spreading the correct doctrine and achieving monotheism. The book is of the type of biographies and classes, and aims to correct misconceptions about the Wahhabi call and explain its reality and goals.
descriptions.1314: This book presents a critical study of the Orientalist vision on the life of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his mission, shedding light on the foreign sources on which Orientalist studies relied, and criticizing the perceptions woven by Orientalists about his birth, travels, and scientific formation, as well as addressing the legislative and behavioral aspects of his mission through criticism of the Orientalist vision of it.
descriptions.1315: The book “Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab in the Mirror of Scholars” by author Mahmoud Mahdi Al-Istanbouli falls within the category of biographies and classes, and collects the opinions and evaluations of a number of Eastern and Western scholars about the biography of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his religious status. It includes texts transmitted by authors such as Ibn Bishr, Al-Jabarti and others, in which they highlight the Sheikh’s virtues of thanking God and directing him to reform beliefs and combat temptations. The work focuses on presenting a comprehensive picture of the Sheikh through the testimonies of writers and historians, with reference to his role in uniting Najdi society and eliminating injustice.
descriptions.1316: Al-Du’afa’ al-Saghir is a small book on al-jarh, ta’deel, and biographies, written by Muhammad bin Ismail al-Bukhari. He specializes in translating weak narrators, and has translated four hundred and eighteen narrators.
descriptions.1317: The Book of Weak and Abandoned by Ibn al-Jawzi is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in classifying weak and abandoned names in the science of hadith. It includes an introduction and sermon to the book and the classification method. It then contains several names beginning with the letter Alif, with an explanation of the weakness or omission of each name. The author aims to document and clarify the situation of narrators who were subjected to criticism, based on Salafi sources. He is considered a reference in the field of criticizing weak hadiths and determining the credibility of narrators.
descriptions.1318: The book “The Weak” by Abu Naim Al-Isbahani is a book of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in narrating the biographies and details of people who are considered weak in the science of hadith, and its content is arranged according to an alphabetical order that begins with the alif and ends with the yaa. The book includes chapters consisting of names placed under each Arabic letter, in which what is known about each weak person in terms of lineage, readings, and traces is mentioned. In his presentation, the author relies on narrations and references to document their information, which makes him a reference for researchers in the sciences of hadith and classes.
descriptions.1319: The Shining Light of the People of the Ninth Century is a book on history written by Shams al-Din al-Sakhawi. It is the most extensive source in the history of the Islamic Middle Ages. The number of translations in it reached (11,699). In it, he translated for scholars, judges, narrators, writers, poets, caliphs, kings, and ministers, from the people of Egypt, the Levant, the Hijaz, Yemen, the Romans, and India, east and west, men and women, who died in this era, or who delayed until the tenth century. He listed - in translating each one - his archives, his sheikhs, his works, his circumstances, his birth, and his death, and the eleventh part of it was devoted to nicknames. The twelfth is for women. …
descriptions.1320: This book, “Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra” or “Lawafih Al-Anwar fi Tabaqat Al-Akhyar” by Al-Shaarani Abdul-Wahhab, is biographies of prominent Islamic figures throughout history, covering the biographies of the Companions, followers, and notable scholars and scholars. The author focuses on presenting the biographies of these figures, pointing out their achievements and the importance of their role in Islamic history, with an emphasis on the spiritual and moral aspects of their lives.
descriptions.1321: The Great Book of Classes by Muhammad bin Saad bin Muni’ al-Basri al-Zuhri, known as Ibn Saad, is one of the most important books written on classes and biographies of men. It was only preceded in this subject by “The Book of Classes” by his sheikh al-Waqidi. However, al-Waqidi’s book has not reached us, and it is said that Ibn Saad benefited greatly from it. The Great Book of Classes is considered a reference in the Prophet’s biography, biographies, and histories. In it, his work dealt with the purified Prophet’s biography, presenting those who issued fatwas in Medina, and compiling the Holy Qur’an. Then he presented biographies of the Companions and those who came after them among the followers and some jurists and scholars. …
descriptions.1322: The major classes, the complementary section for the followers of the people, is part of the work of Imam Muhammad bin Saad, the writer of Al-Waqidi, which specializes in compiling and documenting the biography of the followers of the people of Medina. The content is arranged in multiple layers starting from the third layer and ending with the sixth layer, with references to sources and references. The book relies on the style of biographies and classes with attribution of narrations to provide a comprehensive picture of the personalities of the next generation of companions.
descriptions.1323: Al-Aqwad Al-Durriyya is one of the virtues of Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, a book written by the scholar Ibn Abdul-Hadi in which he talks about Ibn Taymiyyah, his virtues, and the scholars’ praise of him.
descriptions.1324: The book “The Young Branches in the Beauties of the Poets of the Seventh Century” by Ibn Saeed al-Maghribi is a biographical dictionary of poets of the seventh century, including their biographies and works, with reference to the years of their birth and death. The content is divided into chapters dealing with each year, and under each year selected translations of the poets’ poems are included with explanatory comments. This work falls within the classification of biographies and classes, and is concerned with documenting the lives of writers and evaluating their poetic creativity.
descriptions.1325: The book “Educational Thought in the Letters of King Abdul Aziz” by the writer Tariq bin Abdullah Hajjar falls within the category of biographies and classes, and reviews and analyzes the educational texts contained in the letters of King Abdul Aziz that dealt with education and upbringing affairs. The author presents a classification of the letters, highlighting their general characteristics, then extracts the educational directives contained in them and reviews their characteristics in terms of doctrine and commitment to the Qur’an and Sunnah. The work concludes with a statement of the benefits derived and recommendations for researchers in the field of Saudi educational thought.
descriptions.1326: This book, “Al-Kashef fi Ma’rifat al-Ma’rifah fi Ma’rifat al-Muhna’ fi Ma’rifat al-Sijah al-Books” by al-Dhahabi, is biographies and sayings in the science of hadith, in which al-Dhahabi addresses the mention of those who have a narration in the six books of the Prophet’s hadith, and mentions the sayings of scholars about it. Researchers describe it as an important tool for studying men in hadith. As for the “Hawtiya” of the tribe of Ibn al-Ajami, they are comments and corrections on the original book, and provide additional explanations and data for its contents. The two books together constitute a comprehensive and reliable source in the field of translations and classes.
descriptions.1327: Al-Kamil fi Difa’a al-Rijal is one of the most important books of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah on al-Jarh wal-Ta’deel and Ilm al-Rijal. It was written by Al-Hafiz Abu Ahmad Ibn Adi al-Jurjani, known as Ibn Adi. It is a huge book in which the author tried to trace and understand the names of all the hadith narrators about whom the imams of al-Jarh and Ta’deel spoke of weakness, and he mentioned in each narrator’s translation what hadiths the scholars denounced or what he considered strange or objectionable. Al-Kamil’s book by Ibn Adi is considered one of the most extensive books classified on weak subjects, and one of the most complete books he has written in this field. As it has surpassed other books on this subject, such as the book Al-Majrouhin by Ibn Hibban, and the book Al-Dhufa’ Al-Kabir by Al-Uqaili.
descriptions.1328: This book deals with the biographies of the poets of the eighth century AH in Andalusia, and it is part of the “Andalusian Library” series, whose author, Lisan al-Din Ibn al-Khatib, is concerned with documenting the literary and historical heritage of Andalusia. The book focuses on providing information about these poets and their works, based on ancient Andalusian manuscripts, and aims to serve the heritage of the Arab nation, encouraging cooperation between scholars in Morocco and the East.
descriptions.1329: This book, “The Intensive Revealing of Those Who Accused of Fabricating the Hadith,” by Burhan al-Din, the son of Ibn al-Ajami, deals with the accusations leveled against some narrators of falsifying the Prophet’s hadiths. The book classifies the names of the narrators who were accused of fabricating the hadith alphabetically, and relies in its biographies on reliable sources such as “Mizan al-Itidal” by al-Dhahabi and other traditional books. The aim of this work is to verify the validity of the accusations of Hadith status and provide an objective criticism of the characters of the Islamic novel.
descriptions.1330: The book “Al-Kunya and Names” by Imam Muslim is a book from the category of biographies and classes. It specializes in studying the “Kunya” and its categories and clarifying their meanings in the context of Hadith science. It clarifies the definition of “Kunya” according to Arabic, fundamentalist, and rhetorical opinions. The content is arranged alphabetically according to Arabic letters, which makes it easy for students and researchers to refer to the information of the narrators according to a systematic order. The book aims to document and clarify the names and surnames of the narrators in order to strengthen the correct understanding of the hadith and preserve its chain of transmission from confusion.
descriptions.1331: The Planets Walking with Notables of the Tenth Hundred by Ghazi Najm al-Din is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in narrating the biographies of scholars and distinguished personalities. The author organizes the content of the book into alphabetical layers, starting with the first layer, which includes the Muhammadans, and continuing through the letters of the alphabet, with details about their origins, knowledge, and positions. The text provides historical information about the lives of these notables through a documented and detailed narration. This work is an important reference for researchers in the history of Islamic jurisprudence and science.
descriptions.1332: Al-Kawakib Al-Nairat fi Ma’rifa from the Trustworthy Narrators by Ibn Al-Kayyal is the author of biographies and classes that aims to clarify trustworthiness and narrators who were mixed in their age, and collects seventy narrators from the origins of the hadith with their order according to the letters of the dictionary, based on sources such as Mukhtasar Al-Tahtheeb by Al-Andarashi and the book of Ibn Makula. The book includes chapters arranged in alphabetical order. Each chapter includes biographies of a number of narrators, such as Ahmed bin Abdul Rahman bin Wahb bin Muslim Al-Qurashi, Aban bin Samaa, and others. It reviews whether the narrators were mixed before or after their death to evaluate the authenticity of the hadiths.
descriptions.1333: The book “The Compound and the Different in the Names and Nicknames of Poets” by Abu al-Qasim al-Amidi is a book from the category of biographies and classes that specializes in clarifying the differences and similarities in the names of poets, their surnames, and the names of their fathers, while clarifying the differences between form and point in writing. The content is arranged according to the letters of the alphabet, with a section devoted to each letter with which the name begins, and it deals with names that are clever, strange, or less famous. It aims to facilitate identifying poets and avoid confusion between similar names.
descriptions.1334: Ibn al-Qaysrani's Al-Mu'talif wal-Mu'mutafir is a work in the field of biographies and classes that specializes in studying genealogies and clarifying the differences and matches in names and genealogies between various sources. The author arranges the content of the book according to the letters of the Arabic alphabet, where each chapter opens with a letter from A to Z, and what is agreed upon and disagreed about in terms of wording and meanings is presented. The book aims to guide genealogists and provide a reliable reference for correcting and clarifying problems related to names and genealogies.
descriptions.1335: Al-Mubhij fi Interpretation of the Names of the Poets of the Diwan al-Hamsa by Ibn Jinni is a book of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in explaining the origins and meanings of the names of the poets mentioned in the Diwan al-Hamsa. The author proposes a method for classifying nouns into intransitive and improvised, and presents a linguistic analysis that includes indefinite types, verbs, adjectives, and others, while illustrating examples from the poets mentioned in the index.
descriptions.1336: Al-Muttafiq and Al-Muftaraq by Al-Khubayt Al-Baghdadi is a book in the field of biographies and classes that specializes in clarifying the names and lineages mentioned in the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ, showing what matches and what differs. The author relies on multiple narratives and presents them in chapters arranged according to letters, relying on different chains of chain of transmission to show agreement and difference between individuals. It aims to clarify points of confusion that may arise from the similarity of names or the closeness of lineages between companions and followers.
descriptions.1337: Al-Majrouhin is a book that includes biographies of wounded and weak narrators, and it is written by Abu Hatim bin Hibban Al-Basti.
descriptions.1338: Al-Majmu’ in the translation of the scholar and hadith scholar Sheikh Hammad is a book of biographies and classes that presents the biography of Sheikh Hammad bin Muhammad Al-Ansari, the hadith narrator of the Prophet’s city, highlighting his migration from Africa to the Two Holy Mosques and his role in seeking and disseminating knowledge. It includes a brief translation of his life, an overview of his upbringing, his writings, and the appreciation of his colleagues, as well as an account of pages from his diaries and his interviews with scholars. The book aims to document a distinguished scientific career and show its impact in the field of Hadith and its sciences.
descriptions.1339: The Mixed People by Sahih al-Din al-Ala’i is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in narrators who became mixed up at the end of their lives, and classifies them into three categories according to the effect this had on their weakness or lack of effect on their speech. The book includes alphabetical dictionaries that include multiple names from different eras, with reference to the jurists’ observations and sources. It aims to clarify the authenticity of the hadiths narrated by these narrators after the mixing occurred.
descriptions.1340: What is different about them by Ibn Shaheen is a book of biographies and classes that summarizes the opinions of Imam Al-Hafiz regarding sixty-seven narrators mentioned in his books “The Trustworthy” and “The Weak and the Liars,” and it highlights his leniency in judgment based on the statements of some scholars, with an explanation of the reasons for that. The commentator also adds notes on the version used in terms of omissions, distortions, and overlap in translations. The content of the book is limited to an introduction that explains the method and sources and references on which it is based.
descriptions.1341: Al-Mudallasin by Wali al-Din bin al-Iraqi is a book of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in collecting the names of those accused of fraud in the science of hadith, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary for easy reference. The book includes chapters that begin with the letter of each name, and mentions what hadith scholars mentioned in terms of chain of transmission or criticism of this person, with reference to their sources. The author aims to document what was reported about these commentators according to an approved scientific method in classifying and evaluating hadith narrators.
descriptions.1342: The book deals with the role of women in the life of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab by reviewing legal documents and letters related to him and his family, shedding light on a neglected aspect of his biography. It is presented by Hamad Al-Jasser within the framework of the classification of biographies and classes, based on what was stated in the research of the Sheikh’s Call Symposium.
descriptions.1343: The Small Dictionary of the Narrators of Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari by Akram Ziadeh al-Faluji is a dictionary of biographies and tabulations that specializes in collecting the names of narrators from whom Imam al-Tabari quoted his hadiths and narrations in his interpretation of “Jami` al-Bayan” and his other works, and it is based on descriptions of relevant manuscripts and publications. The book includes a translation approach that explains tabulation, numbering, and definition of each narrator, and the arrangement of the translations according to the indexes, in addition to detailed chapters on the sources of interpretation, history, antiquities, and authenticity on which the researcher relied. The dictionary aims to facilitate the work of researchers in the sciences of Hadith and the Qur’an by providing a concise and comprehensive reference for narrators associated with the writings of Al-Tabari.
descriptions.1344: The dictionary of hadith scholars by Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi is a dictionary of biographies and classes that specializes in the names of hadith scholars. It provides brief overviews of each hadith scholar, mentioning their titles and basic information about them. The book's content is arranged in alphabetical order, beginning with the letter Alif and ending with the letter Ya, with nicknames included to facilitate identification of the characters. It aims to document the students of hadith who sat with the hadith scholars or approved their narrations, while highlighting what distinguishes each of them in this field.
descriptions.1345: This book, “The Dictionary of the Suspect Names of Hadith Scholars,” by Al-Harawi Abu al-Fadl, deals with the subject of translations and classes, and aims to clarify the similarity in the names of narrators and hadith scholars, and to clarify the differences between them to avoid confusion in transmitting the hadith. The book deals with the names of suspected hadith scholars and separates them according to the alphabet, highlighting the differences between people whose names or surnames are similar.
descriptions.1346: This book, “Al-Ma'in fi Latakat al-Muhaddin” by Al-Dhahabi, deals with the biographies and sayings of hadith scholars throughout the ages, distributing its notables into specific time periods, starting with the Companions and their followers until the era in which its author lived. It focuses on mentioning the names of the bearers of the prophetic monuments and documenting their scientific and religious status, while providing brief information about their lives and works without diving into the fine details. The book aims to give a general idea about the history of hadith science and its pioneers over the centuries.
descriptions.1347: Al-Mughni’s book on the weak, written by Imam Abu Abdullah Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman, known as al-Dhahabi, who died in the year 745 AH. It is a small, brief book that contains the weak, the liars, and the lowly. Among them are the abandoned and perishing, and among them are the weak among the hadith scholars and transmitters. Then he mentions the many who are delusional among the truthful ones, then he mentions the trustworthy ones who have some softness or stubbornness in them, then it contains the unknown ones as well, and they are many. Al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi mentioned some of them who stated: His ignorance is Abu Hatim Al-Razi, and he said: This is unknown, and he mentioned some of them whose condition is unknown, and from whom only one man narrated, it was denied. This book was limited to mentioning those who are less than weak, and it did not mention the trustworthy ones, and whoever it was said that his place is truthfulness or there is nothing wrong with him...
descriptions.1348: Al-Maqamat by Abdul Rahman bin Hassan Al-Sheikh is a book of the type of biographies and classes that includes an introduction and nine numbered Maqamat. It sheds light on the writer’s biography, his scientific career, and his family lineage, in addition to his responses to the criticisms directed at him, aiming to benefit the reader and direct him to a deeper understanding of religion.
descriptions.1349: Al-Muqtana fi Narrat al-Kunya by al-Dhahabi Shams al-Din is a tragic and applied work that specializes in explaining the nicknames of the narrators and clarifying their identity between the name and the nickname, and it relies on reviewing manuscripts and checking translations. The book is divided into two parts, which include an introduction, a chapter that explains the hadith scholars’ interest in nicknames, and a chapter that explains the works on nicknames, in addition to a description of the manuscript versions and the investigation process, and the content is arranged according to the letters of the alphabet. The author aims to revive this important science to serve researchers in the field of Sunnah and Hadith.
descriptions.1350: The most reasonable purpose in mentioning the companions of Imam Ahmad is a book of biographies and classes in which Ibn Muflih Burhan al-Din collects the biographies of the companions of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, arranging them according to the letters of the dictionary to facilitate navigation between them. The content includes a detailed index that begins with the letter Alif and continues until the letter Ain, mentioning the names of multiple figures such as Abraham, Isaac, Ismail, Al-Hussein, Ubayd Allah, and others. The author aims to benefit the reader in knowing the lineage, sayings, and details of the Imam’s companions through a narrative style that takes into account accuracy and reliability.
descriptions.1351: The book “King Abdulaziz Al Saud, A Nation in a Man” by the writer Abdullah bin Abdul Mohsen Al Turki falls within the category of biographies and classes, and reviews the biography of King Abdulaziz from his upbringing and unification of the Arabian Peninsula to his internal and foreign policies. The author deals with the stages of unifying the kingdom, its religious principles, its administration of Sharia law, security, Shura, and development, in addition to its relations with the Turks, Britain, and the Palestinian issue, based on the testimonies of its Arab and non-Arab contemporaries. The book concludes with the death of the king and his heirs and includes a list of the most important sources and references.
descriptions.1352: This book is “The Selected Min Dhayl Al-Mudhayl” by Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Jarir Al-Tabari, and it is one of the biographies and classes. The book includes selections from the book “Dhayl al-Mudhayl,” which the author wrote about the Companions and Followers, where he mentions events and information about some important figures in the history of Islam, such as the death of Khadija bint Khuwaylid, Zainab bint the Prophet Muhammad, and Jaafar bin Abi Talib.
descriptions.1353: Selected from the Book of Context for the History of Nishapur is a book written by Abu Ishaq al-Sarfini. It falls within the classification of biographies and classes. It specializes in collecting the biography and knowledge of sheikhs, scholars, and hadith imams from Nishapur and those who passed through it. It includes multiple layers that list multiple names from Muhammad bin… to others, explaining their roles as imams, jurists, preachers, and reciters. The book aims to document the history of the emergence and scientific activity of the region through a brief narration of the general features of the aforementioned classes.
descriptions.1354: The book “The Selected Min Dictionary of Sheikhs of Al-Sam’ani” by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Sam’ani is considered a reference in the field of biographies and classes, as it specializes in narrating the biographies of sheikhs of scholars who have names that begin with the letter Alif. The book includes a group of lineages and genealogies related to the sheikh, mentioning chain of transmission and narrations that show the connection of each sheikh to others. The opening excerpt of the book shows a traditional style of providing attribution and introduction to the hadith, which reflects its documentary and declarative character.
descriptions.1355: This book, “Individuals and Onenesses,” was written by Muslim, and is related to the subject of translations and classes. The book deals with naming those from whom only one man narrated, mentioning those from whom only one man narrated, and reviews various cases of hadith narrators from whom only one person narrated.
descriptions.1356: This book is biographies and chronicles of many personalities of scholars and princes in the Mamluk era. It deals with their biographies, works, and the facts of their lives, providing a comprehensive overview of their time and culture. The author, Ibn Taghri Bardi, presents these characters in a sober literary style, reviewing important historical events in the context of the lives of these men, relying in this on his extensive information from the history books and historical sources available to him.
descriptions.1357: هذا الكتاب "النور السافر عن أخبار القرن العاشر" للعيدروس، يتناول سردًا لوفيات العلماء والصالحين والأدباء والملوك والأعيان من مختلف الأقطار خلال القرن العاشر الهجري. The book also includes some strange incidents, tales, and strange salt, providing a comprehensive overview of the many figures and events of the era. The book combines history, jurisprudence, and literature, presenting a comprehensive picture of the tenth century AH.
descriptions.1358: This book is guidance and guidance in knowing the people of trust and trustworthiness, by its author, Abu Nasr al-Kalabadhi, and it falls under the classification of biographies and classes.
descriptions.1359: Al-Wafi bi al-Wafiyat is the largest of Al-Safadi’s works, and the most comprehensive of the books written in Islam regarding biographies of men. Al-Safadi compiled it in thirty volumes, and it comes in second place in terms of size after his book: Al-Tazkira Al-Safadi or Al-Tazkira Al-Saliha, which is still in manuscript and is a major book on history, language, and literature. Al-Safadi referred to the notables of the era and the helpers of victory to the forty-sixth volume of it, and referred to it. The translations of the book were chronologically extended, starting with pre-Islamic times and ending with some of those who lived in the eighth century AH, that is, those who were contemporary with Al-Safadi. The biographies also covered wide spatial areas, from the far east to the far west. …
descriptions.1360: Al-Wajeez fi Dhikr al-Majjaz wa al-Mujaz by Abu Taher al-Salafi is a book of biographies and classes that summarizes the biography of scholars, narrators, and poets, explaining their degrees, confidence, and weakness according to what was reported about them in terms of hadiths, sayings, or poetry. The author presents a dated dictionary that collects the necessary statements and positions without going into great detail. This work falls within the literature that aims to document the scientific and jurisprudential biography of Sufis and jurists in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.1361: Deaths: A Chronological Dictionary of the Companions and Notable Hadiths by Ibn Qunfuth is a biographical dictionary that specializes in documenting the dates of the deaths of the Companions, scholars, and hadith scholars, arranging them according to Hijri hundreds. The book includes chapters dedicated to the first ten Companions, the Mothers of the Believers, and the seven Tabi’in jurists, in addition to detailed sections for every hundred years. The author aims to provide a reference that contributes to verifying the authenticity of the narratives by knowing whether the narrator lived at the time of the reported event.
descriptions.1362: The book “Names and Nicknames” written by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal falls within the classification of biographies and classes, and is specialized in collecting and clarifying the names and nicknames of people from the Companions, followers, and others. The book opens with a remembrance of the name of God and then follows with a series of hadiths and narrations that explain the origins of the names and their details, based on well-known methods of attribution. The text shows an interest in documenting names through the transmission of hadiths and traces, which makes it a reference for researchers in Islamic genealogy and lineages.
descriptions.1363: The book “The Names” written by Ahmed bin Hanbal falls within the category of biographies and classes, and is specialized in collecting and clarifying the names and nicknames of the people mentioned in the biography and hadith. The author presents the names through chains of attribution that show multiple narrations about figures such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and other Banu Hashim and the Successors. The content of the book focuses on documenting names and detailing their origins within the framework of stratigraphy.
descriptions.1364: The book “Bahr al-Dam regarding those about whom Imam Ahmad spoke in praise or blame” by the writer Ibn al-Mubarrad is considered one of the biographies and classes, as it collects and details what Imam Ahmad mentioned in terms of praise or condemnation of his companions and personalities, arranging the names according to the letters of the Arabic alphabet. It includes an introduction that introduces the author and his biography, followed by chapters divided according to each letter, allowing the reader a systematic review of the layers associated with the Imam’s hadith.
descriptions.1365: A book written by the historian Omar bin Ahmad bin Hibatullah bin Abi Jarada, known as Sahib Kamal al-Din Ibn al-Adim, who is an Arab historian. This book is considered one of the most important history books that dealt with the history of Aleppo from the beginning of creation until the era of Ibn al-Adim. It was written about everyone who set foot on the land of Aleppo. Ibn al-Adim wrote a summary of the work on Zabadat al-Halab in the History of Aleppo
descriptions.1366: Baghiyat al-Multamim fi Tarikh al-Rijal al-Andalus, one of the works of Ibn Amira al-Dhabi, who died in the year 1202 AD. It deals with the biographies of the men of Andalusia and also mentions the women of Andalusia, mentioning in it an introduction to the history of Andalusia from its conquest to the year 92 AH and the rule of Hisham al-Mu`tadid Allah. It included biographies of prominent hadith narrators, jurists, and scholars of literature and poetry from the beginning of the conquest to the year of the author’s death or shortly before.
descriptions.1367: In order to be aware of the classes of linguists and grammarians, it is a book written by Abd al-Rahman Abi Bakr al-Suyuti (849 AH / 1445 AD - 911 AH / 1505 AD), in which he collected biographies of linguists and grammarians from all the books that preceded him in this regard, and added to them what he selected from books of literature, history, biographies, dictionaries of sheikhs, introductions to books, and other things.
descriptions.1368: The book “Statement of Al-Bukhari’s Error” by Al-Razi Ibn Abi Hatim is concerned with correcting the errors contained in the history of Imam Al-Bukhari, and it is considered one of the works of biographies and classes that is concerned with explaining the differences between the correct and the incorrect in the biography. The book includes the editor's introduction, the method of verifying the text, in addition to a detailed presentation of the errors in Bukhari's history, based on the only preserved ancient copy. It aims to clarify the mistakes that occurred in the historical texts of Sheikh Al-Bukhari to avoid relying on them without review.
descriptions.1369: The book The History of Trustworthy Names by Ibn Shaheen is a book of biographies and classes that specializes in compiling the names of trustworthy narrators in the science of hadith. The content is arranged in alphabetical order, starting with Alif, then Baa, Taa, and others. Brief information is provided for each name that shows the extent of its truthfulness and reputation according to what was narrated about it in the chain of transmission. The author relies on multiple narrations from hadith sheikhs to demonstrate the reliability of each person mentioned. The book aims to facilitate reference to trustworthy names for researchers and those interested in verifying the authenticity of hadiths.
descriptions.1370: This book, “The History of the Names of the Weak and Liars,” by Ibn Shaheen, deals with the study of the conditions of narrators in terms of justice and precision, and reviews the sayings of the imams in their evaluation, showing who deserves weakness and lying according to the opinions of the critical scholars of his time. The author relies on the approach he followed in his book “Al-Thiqat” without comment, where he mentions every narrator who was weak by critics, noting that some of the narrators he mentioned in this book even though he touched on them in his previous book due to a difference in their assessment. The book is part of the art of distortion and modification, which is one of the arts that distinguished the Islamic nation in order to preserve the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from distortion and maliciousness.
descriptions.1371: This book, “The History of Isfahan” by Abu Naim Al-Isfahani, deals with the biographies of the scholars and imams of Isfahan and its hadith narrators, arranging their names according to the order of the alphabetical letters. The author begins by mentioning the conquest of Isfahan and its characteristics, then moves on to mention the narrators and hadith scholars from the people of the city and those coming to it, while providing historical and scientific information about each of them. The book is a type of biographies and classes, and it is an important reference for studying the history of the scholars of Isfahan and its hadith narrators.
descriptions.1372: The book “The History of Erbil” by Ibn Al-Mustafi Al-Erbali deals with the biography of the notables and notables of the city of Erbil throughout the ages, shedding light on its prominent figures of scholars and virtuous people. The author focuses on the biographies of important historical figures, relying on a documented approach based on investigation and review, noting some of the challenges that the investigators faced in the original manuscript version.
descriptions.1373: This book is the history of Ibn Ma'in, narrated by Al-Darimi. It contains biographies of the imams of hadith and the companions of the narrators, dealing with the sayings of Yahya ibn Ma'in regarding the reliability of the narrators and their strength in the hadith, relying on questions addressed to him by Al-Darimi. The book deals with various topics about hadith narrators and imams of knowledge, and divides the biographies according to the first letters of their names. It begins by narrating Ibn Ma’in’s evaluation of some famous narrators such as Malik, Aqil, Muammar, and Sufyan bin Uyaynah.
descriptions.1374: The History of Ibn Yunus al-Masry” is a historical book of the type of biographies and classes, specializing in narrating the biographies and names of Egyptian figures according to alphabetical order beginning with Arabic letters, as is evident from the index, which includes multiple chapters for each name. The book provides a comprehensive overview of the lives of notables and lineages in Egypt, based on multiple historical sources and relying on the documentation method that was prevalent among Ibn Yunus al-Sadfi. This work is part of a group of lost historical books that have been revived and rearranged to bring the text closer to its original state.
descriptions.1375: The book “The History of Trustworthy Persons” by Al-Ijli is concerned with compiling and documenting the biography of trustworthy people in the science of hadith, based on the rules of chain of transmission, narration, and modification that he explains in the introduction to the book. The author arranges the trustworthy documents according to a detailed Arabic alphabetical order by letter, providing an explanation of the degrees of authentication and a comparison between the different sources. The work aims to guide researchers to what is desirable in narrations from trustworthy people and to avoid weak ones, with reference to books specialized in narration, modification, and classes.
descriptions.1376: This book, by Judge Abi al-Mahasin al-Tanukhi, is a history that deals with the lives of grammar scholars from the Basra and Kufic schools, showing their scholarly ranks, lineages, and history. Through it, the author aims to correct misconceptions about these scholars and show the differences between them. He also aims to offer consolation to readers suffering from the loss of loved ones among grammar scholars.
descriptions.1377: The book “The History of Baghdad and Its Aftermaths” by the expert Al-Baghdadi is a book of the type of biographies and classes that sheds light on the history of Baghdad and its society through its eras, documenting the lives of scholars, hadith scholars, jurists, and writers who lived there or visited it. It includes the biography of Al-Khatib himself, from his upbringing and scholarly journeys to details of his contributions to various Islamic branches such as hadith, jurisprudence, doctrines, literature, and asceticism. The book highlights the activity of the hadith scholars in Baghdad and the impact of libraries and public schools on the prosperity of the intellectual movement, with reference to a large number of translations collected by the author.
descriptions.1378: The History of Baghdad is a book written by the scholar Ahmed bin Ali bin Thabit, known as Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi (392 AH - 462 AH), an Arab Muslim historian, and many historians after him wrote books similar to this book. Such as the History of Damascus by Ibn Asakir.
descriptions.1379: “The History of Bayhaq” is a work translated into Arabic that falls within the classification of biographies and classes. It presents the biography of Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Zaid bin Muhammad bin al-Hussein bin Faql, known as Dhahir al-Din al-Bayhaqi, with details about his lineage, upbringing, education, teachers, doctrine of jurisprudence, and his numerous writings on history, jurisprudence, and astrology. The book includes chapters dealing with countries, famous histories, histories of cities and their authors, as well as a chapter on the virtues of Bayhaq, based on comprehensive content covering his life and scholarly contributions.
descriptions.1380: The History of Gorgan or Knowledge of the Scholars of the People of Gorgan is one of the history books that specializes in mentioning the news of Gorgan, written by Al-Hafiz Hamza Al-Sahmi.
descriptions.1381: The book on the history of Damascus, whose full name is “A History of the City of Damascus - May God Protect It - and Mention of Its Virtue, and the Name of Those Who Solved It from the Examples, or Passed Through Its Areas from Its Residents and People” written by Imam Al-Hafiz, the Muhaddith of the Levant, Ibn Asakir. It is a huge book containing about eighty volumes. It is considered one of the largest, most voluminous and most important works in the history of Islam. In it, the author dealt with the history of the city of Damascus, and spoke about the biographies and narrations of notables and narrators from everyone who lived, lived in, or passed through the city of Damascus. He translated a huge number of notables in the history of Islam from its appearance until before the author’s death. It is compiled in the style of the book The History of Baghdad, which was written by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi. …
descriptions.1382: The book The History of Andalusian Scholars by the writer Ibn al-Fardi falls within the classification of biographies and classes, and is concerned with collecting the biography and names of scholars and jurists in Andalusia with their lineages and scholarly positions. The content is arranged according to the letters of the alphabet, and chapters such as “The Letter Alif” and “The Letter Ba” appear, with detailed sections for each name. The author aims to provide a brief reference that makes it easier for researchers to access the news of scholars and their contributions to jurisprudence and science in Andalusia.
descriptions.1383: The book “The History of the Judges of Andalusia, Al-Muraqba Al-Ulia Fimen” by Al-Nabahi falls within the classification of biographies and classes, as it presents the concept of judges and girls in Islam and reviews the characteristics that deserve a judge and a fatwa. It includes two main doors; The first discusses the principles and purposes of the judiciary, and the second narrates the biography of a group of Andalusian judges with reference to some hadiths and jurisprudential opinions related to them. The author aims to clarify the criteria for selection, following the example of a righteous judge, and clarifying the limits of fatwa in Sharia law.
descriptions.1384: The book “The History of the Births and Deaths of Scholars” by Al-Rab’i Abu Suleiman falls within the category of biographies and classes, and is specialized in documenting the births and events of scholars according to a chronological order detailing each year separately from “Year One” to “Year Thirty-Three.” In his narration, the author relies on the multiple chain of narrators, where travelers mention each world through a series of narrators, as appears in the opening excerpt. The book aims to provide a comprehensive reference for the history of scientific figures in the Islamic heritage, focusing on the dates of their birth and death.
descriptions.1385: Book of the History of Wasit. Author: Aslam bin Sahl bin Aslam bin Habib al-Razzaz al-Wasiti, Abu al-Hasan, Bahshal. (deceased: 292 AH) Hadith (Wasit) in his time. He was one of the trustworthy memorizers.
descriptions.1386: This book is written by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi, which summarizes the names of narrators whose names contain extra letters, such as Alif, Ba, Ta, Ta, and others. The book is concerned with dividing names according to the extra letter in them, and provides brief information about each narrator mentioned in each chapter, with reference to their hadiths and chains of transmission. The book is a type of traditional book that is concerned with translations and classes.
descriptions.1387: The book “Tabseer al-Muntahab bi Tahrir al-Suspect” by the scholar Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, one of his biographical and taxonomic works, aims to clarify and clarify the genealogies and names of suspects in biographies, bypassing the problems faced by a previous author in this field. The book deals with the names of the suspects, arranged according to the alphabet, and reviews their biographies in more detail than Al-Dhahabi did in his similar book, relying on multiple sources, including a manuscript copy by his author.
descriptions.1388: This book is “The Masterpiece of Collection in the Mention of the Narrators of Murasil” by Wali al-Din bin al-Iraqi, and it is related to the subject of biographies and classes. The book deals with mentioning the narrators of the Murasil, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, while adding new and distinctive information about each narrator, benefiting from previous works in this field. The author aims to provide a useful and comprehensive classification of narrators of correspondence, distinguishing between information he took from other sources and information he added himself.
descriptions.1389: Tuhfat al-Siddiq fi the virtues of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, written by Ibn Balban Ala al-Din, falls within the category of biographies and classes. It sheds light on the biography and morals of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq through a group of hadiths attached to the author’s introduction. The book includes a series of hadiths that deal with the virtues of the great companion and highlight his status among the Muhajireen and Ansar. Its content is limited to presenting these hadiths without going into other historical or analytical details.
descriptions.1390: Tuhfat al-Muqadil by Ibn al-Abar is a biographies and classes book that specializes in a brief biography and classes of poets and writers from Andalusia and Morocco, with reference to their literary style and excerpts from their poetry. The index includes names such as Ibn Khalsa, Ibn Abi Salt, Ibn al-Baraa al-Tajibi and others, which indicates the comprehensive coverage of different literary schools. In his presentation, the author relies on literary comments and poetic passages, contributing to the revival of the Arab literary heritage.
descriptions.1391: The book Tadhkirat al-Huffaz by Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Qaymaz al-Dhahabi is a book of biographies and biographies for the preservation of the Prophet’s knowledge.
descriptions.1392: An appendix to the predecessors of the era by Abdullah Al-Jazairi is a book of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in narrating the biographies and circumstances of a number of Shiite writers and poets. The book includes figures such as Ismail bin Saad al-Musawi al-Huwaizi, Maatouq bin Shihab al-Din al-Musawi al-Huwaizi, Sheikh Fathallah bin Alwan al-Kaabi al-Dawrqi, Qawam al-Din al-Hasani al-Saifi al-Qazwini, al-Nur al-Din bin Nimat Allah al-Jazairi, the scholar Ali Balil al-Musawi al-Durqi, and Ibrahim bin Ali Balil al-Durqi. It aims to collect information about these writers and document their contributions to the Shiite literary heritage. It relies on historical literary sources to provide a comprehensive picture of the era’s poets and writers.
descriptions.1393: The book “Biographies of the Men of al-Daraqutni in his Sunan who have not been translated” by Muqbil bin Hadi al-Wada’i specializes in compiling the biography of the men of al-Daraqutni mentioned in his Sunan, focusing on the names bearing the name Abdullah and detailing their origins and lineage. The author relies on the sayings of al-Daraqutni and other translation sources to document their positions on hadith science, and classifies it among biographies and classes.
descriptions.1394: It is a book of several parts by Judge Ayyad and is considered the largest encyclopedia dealing with the translation of the men of the Maliki school of thought, the narrators of “Al-Muwatta” and its scholars.
descriptions.1395: The book is a translation of the biography of Sheikh Abdul Rahman Al-Afriqi prepared by Omar Fallata, and it falls within the classification of biographies and classes. It includes chapters dealing with his birth and upbringing, his arrival in the Two Holy Mosques, his sheikhs and students, his qualities and morals, his works, and his death. It aims to show the distinguished personality of a scientist by narrating his career and achievements.
descriptions.1396: The book “Name the Jurists of the Provinces from the Companions of the Messenger of God” by Al-Nasa’i is a tragic reference that specializes in recording the names of the jurists from the Companions and the Successors and those after them, distributed according to the cities and regions to which they belonged, such as Medina, Mecca, Kufa, the Levant, Khorasan, and Egypt, in addition to mentioning the owners of the different schools of thought such as Malik and Al-Shafi’i. The content includes detailed lists of the names of jurists in chronological and geographical order, based on the hadith narrations in which their names are mentioned. The book aims to document the classes of jurists and determine their connection to the different schools of jurisprudence.
descriptions.1397: The naming of the sheikhs of Abu Abd al-Rahman Ahmad bin Shuaib is part of the book “Al-Nasa’i’s Sheikhs,” which is concerned with naming the sheikhs and documenting their chains of transmission according to the classifications of trustworthiness and trustworthiness. Al-Nasa'i combines hadiths and opinions about a number of scholars, with an indication of the validity of their chain of transmission, and includes an appendix explaining those who were mentioned in Al-Nasa'i's sheikhs as a matter of delusion or misrepresentation.
descriptions.1398: This book, written by Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, deals with naming the Companions and their followers as mentioned by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs. The book divides the names of the Companions according to the letters of the dictionary, and begins with names from the alphabet Alif to D, passing through a list of famous and well-known Companions, while mentioning some additional information about some of them. The book aims to provide a useful reference for studying the hadiths of the Companions and their sayings contained in the main hadith books.
descriptions.1399: This book by Ali bin Al-Madini, which is one of the works of Biographies and Classes, deals with naming those from whom it was narrated among the ten children mentioned in the title. It focuses on mentioning their names and biographies, with reference to some famous lineages and narrators. The book combines Islamic history and the Prophet’s hadith, providing valuable information about the first generations of companions and followers.
descriptions.1400: The book was written by Al-Nasa’i and falls within the classification of biographies and classes, as it specializes in naming those from whom the hadith or saying was narrated by only one man, and lists them according to jurisprudential and geographical classes, such as the people of Medina, the people of Egypt, and the jurists from Kufa, Basra, the Levant, and others, with a reference to their chains of transmission and notes about the absence of other narrators. It aims to document these names and determine their place in the science of hadith and jurisprudence.
descriptions.1401: The book “Accelerating Benefit with the Additions of the Men of the Four Imams” by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani falls within the category of biographies and classes, as it summarizes the biography and sayings of the men of the Four Imams, with additions that contribute to clarifying the benefits. Its content is arranged according to the letters of the Arabic alphabet from A to Z. Each letter includes a mention of the names of scholars and their classification according to what was stated in the six books of hadith. The author aims to make it easier to benefit from information about translations and classes by condensing it and adding something that refines and highlights it.
descriptions.1402: The book “Introducing the People of Sanctification to the Ranks of Those Described as Counterfeiters” was written by the scholar Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, and it falls within the classification of biographies and classes. It introduces the reader to the ranks of deceivers and classifies them according to their level of deception. The book includes an introduction by the investigator and an introduction by the writer, then chapters detailing each of the five ranks mentioned in the index. It is considered a reference for researchers in the science of men and classes, aiming to clarify the evidence of the mudalis and clarify their degrees for those interested in the people of sanctification.
descriptions.1403: This book is Al-Daraqutni’s Commentaries on Al-Majrouhin by Ibn Hibban. In this work, Al-Daraqutni deals with biographies of a number of narrators who are famous for being weak or wounded, stating the sayings of scholars about them and their documents, while providing criticism and analysis of their narrations and hadiths. The book aims to warn against suspicious narrators and clarify their status in the eyes of scholars.
descriptions.1404: Tahdheeb al-Tahdheeb is one of the books of al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (773-852). The author wrote his book Tahdheeb al-Tahdheeb, which is an abbreviation of Tahdheeb al-Kamal by al-Hafiz al-Mizzi. Then Ibn Hajar summarized his Tahdheeb with this book, Tahdheeb al-Tahdheeb. The importance of the book is that it is a comprehensive guide with the names of the narrators of the six noble books of the Prophet’s hadiths. Ibn Hajar restricted it to the name of its translator briefly, and the degree of its authentication. And his job, and the signs that Al-Mizzi mentioned to him. The book is distinguished in that it mentioned the works of the authors of the six books, and summarized the talk about the narrator in a short, comprehensive, edited phrase.
descriptions.1405: A tribute to Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani on Al-Rad Al-Wafir is a work of the type of biographies and classes presented by Imam Al-Safi Al-Din Al-Bukhari. It aims to review and comment on the book Al-Rad Al-Wafir by the scholar Ibn Hajar. The book contains the text of the message, a question and answer by the scholar, and a picture of the answer, in addition to a reference to its author, Saleh bin Omar Al-Balqini. It falls within the literature that documents the biography of scholars and evaluates their writings in jurisprudence and hadith.
descriptions.1406: The book “Restricting the Neglected and Distinguishing the Problem, the Neglected Sheikhs of Al-Bukhari” by Abu Ali Al-Ghassani falls within the category of biographies and classes, and specializes in compiling a definition of the sheikhs of Al-Bukhari whom he mentioned in his book, along with documenting their lineages and regions. It aims to clarify who is neglected in terms of lineage, and to point out the differences between similar or different names that may cause confusion in identifying them. It includes an index that divides the content according to the first letters of the names of the sheikhs, which facilitates access to each personality and reviewing the information provided about them.
descriptions.1407: Completion of completion of completion in lineages, names and titles. A book written by Ibn al-Sabouni, Muhammad bin Ali bin Mahmoud, Abu Hamid, Jamal al-Din al-Mahmoudi (deceased: 680 AH). Ibn al-Sabouni mentions in the introduction to his book the reason that prompted him to write it, and that is that he found that “Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ghani ibn Nuqtah” had neglected to mention a group in a section of the biographies in his book “Iktilam al-Ikmal.” He was free to mention them, but he overlooked a group whose mention had not occurred to him or crossed his mind, so he wanted to draw attention to them, so he wrote his book “Ikmel al-Ikmal,” which is considered one of the most famous books in the world of historical culture, as it contains the biographies of men from different classes and classes, such as jurists and teachers. The hadith scholars, ministers, commentators, and poets...
descriptions.1408: The book “Summary of the History of Nishapur” by the writer Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah is a work of biographies and classes that specializes in the biography of scholars and narrators associated with the city of Nishapur, and collects documents, names, genealogies, dates of birth and death that are not available in other biographies. It includes the translation of Persian words into Arabic and the correction of errors based on Tehran versions, noting that the electronic version contains special numbering for the translations. The book is notable for the presence of hundreds of rare biographies documenting the ruler’s sheikhs and their details, making it an important reference in the history of the Naysaburi.
descriptions.1409: Tahdheeb al-Asma wa al-Lughat is a book in language, translations, and the language of jurisprudence. Its author is Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi (631 AH-676 AH). He discusses words, linguistic investigations, and biographies of prominent figures in the Mukhtasar of Abu Ibrahim al-Muzani, al-Muhadhdhab, al-Tanbih, al-Waseet, al-Wajeez, and al-Rawdah, the summary of Sharh al-Wajeez. The names translated for them are mentioned: males, which has eight chapters, females, which has seven chapters, and they are all arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. Languages: Arrange them according to the letters of the dictionary. When translating a person, he mentions his place in the six books, the number of his narrations if he has a narration, the number of his narrations in the two Sahihs, and the oddities of the issues narrated about him, especially in the field of jurisprudence.
descriptions.1410: Tahdheeb al-Tahdheeb is a book that specializes in the knowledge of the narrators of the Prophet’s hadith, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. This book is considered a summary of a large book on the names of the men of the six books of hadith and their conditions, written by Al-Hafiz Abdul-Ghani Al-Maqdisi Al-Hanbali and called it (Al-Kamal fi Asma Al-Rijal). In it he deposited the sayings of the imams regarding the men of the Two Sahihs and the Four Sunan, relying on the histories of Al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim’s book (Al-Jarh wal-Ta’deel). Then Al-Hafiz Al-Mizzi came and summarized the book. Al-Hafiz Al-Maqdisi wrote in a new book called (Tahdheeb Al-Kamal), then Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani came after that, and he shortened it and added to it things that they had missed, which were many, and he commented on them, and called his summary: (Tahdheeb Al-Tahdheeb), then he summarized it in the book (Taqrib Al-Tahdheeb). …
descriptions.1411: Tahtheeb Al-Kamal fi Asma Al-Rijal is a book on the science of men written by Al-Hafiz Jamal Al-Din Abu Al-Hajjaj Al-Mizzi. In it, he revised, revised, and added to the book Al-Kamal fi Asma Al-Rijal by Al-Hafiz Abdul-Ghani Al-Maqdisi.
descriptions.1412: This book, “A Continuing Refinement of Illusions for Those with Knowledge and Those with Understandings,” by Ibn Makula is one of the works of Biographies and Classes, in which the author deals with the refinement and clarification of some names and expressions, correcting previous scholars in this field, and pointing out the facts and rulings they overlooked regarding names, and aims to provide a deeper and more accurate knowledge of the meanings of names and their classifications.
descriptions.1413: This book, “Clarification of Suspects in Seizing the Names and Lineages of Narrators” by Ibn Nasir al-Din al-Dimashqi, deals with the subject of investigating the names and lineages of narrators, and aims to clarify the suspected names and lineages in the chains of transmission and narrations. The book is based on dividing names according to alphabetical letters, and provides useful information in the field of science of men and the control of chains of transmission.
descriptions.1414: This book deals with three detailed biographies of prominent scholars, which are precious biographies of Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Barzali, and al-Mazi. In this book, author Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi focuses on presenting the biographies of these scholars, their works, and their achievements, relying on classification within the art of biographies and classes. The book sheds light on the life of Ibn Taymiyyah in particular, showing the stages of his scientific life, his jurisprudential and hadith positions, and how his knowledge spread and influence.
descriptions.1415: The book Jami’ al-Tahseel fi Ahkam al-Marsail, by the scholar Salah al-Din al-Ala’i, deals with the subject of the Mursal hadith and discusses its rulings and the doctrines of the scholars regarding it. The book is divided into several sections that begin with defining the mursal hadith and distinguishing it from other types of hadiths. Then it moves on to discussing the opinions of scholars regarding its acceptance and the validity of inferring it. It reviews the evidence indicating those opinions, and concludes by detailing the hidden messages sent according to the letters of the alphabet.
descriptions.1416: He is Abu Abdullah bin Abi Nasr Muhammad bin Futuh bin Abdullah bin Futuh bin Humaid al-Azdi al-Maywarqi al-Humaydi (420 AH - 488 AH), the imam al-Hafiz, the jurist al-Zahiri, a student of Imam Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi. He was described as intelligent, knowledgeable, proficient, religious, and pious. He had a good tone in reciting hadiths, and he wrote many works. The most important of them is the strange interpretation of what is in the Sahihs of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and the source of the quote in the mention of the governors of Andalusia. While he was in Andalusia, Hamidi was a student of Ibn Abd al-Barr. He was also a student and friend of Ibn Hazm, from whom Hamidi took his apparent opinions in Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.1417: The book “Part of Illusions in the Noble Sheikhs” by the scholar Diya al-Din Abu Abdullah al-Maqdisi, is a translation of the book “The Noble Sheikhs” by Abu al-Qasim Ali bin al-Hasan bin Habti Allah al-Dimashqi, with the correction of some errors and hints that the author found in it. The book deals with biographies of famous scholars and imams, reviewing what the previous author mentioned about them and correcting what may have been an oversight on his part. The biographies are divided according to first names, and the book begins with the chapter on Ahmed, then moves to the rest of the names in succession.
descriptions.1418: A book written by Ibn Mandah Yahya bin Abdul Wahhab that falls under the classification of biographies and classes. It specializes in mentioning Abu al-Qasim Sulayman bin Ahmed bin Ayyub al-Tabarani, explaining his birth, death, excavation, and the number of his classifications. The part includes a brief narration of the virtues of Al-Tabarani and his biography, with reference to narrations transmitted by sheikhs of the memorizers. The text provides basic information about Al-Tabarani’s life and his contributions to the transmission of hadiths, within a framework of narrative documentation.
descriptions.1419: The book “King Abdul Aziz’s Efforts in Spreading Public Education” by Saleh Al-Ghamdi is classified under biographies and classes, and presents a historical study focusing on King Abdul Aziz’s contributions to developing the public education system in the Prophet’s City, based on a historical overview of the emergence and development of the Directorate of Knowledge. The author deals with the achievements of the City's Knowledge Directorate, and reviews the period from the city's entry into the prosperous Saudi era until the king's death, highlighting the foundations he laid for the educational renaissance. The work concludes with a conclusion that summarizes the sources and references on which the research was based.
descriptions.1420: The book “The History of Humans in the History of the Thirteenth Century” by Sheikh Abdul Razzaq Al-Bitar is a collection of biographies and classes that record the biography of a number of prominent figures, especially scholars and sages who bore the name Ibrahim, across various regions in the thirteenth century. The author relies on a traditional method in biographies, where he provides an introductory religious introduction and then moves between chapters detailing their scientific, jurisprudential, and social paths. The work is considered a reference that shows the diversity of lineages and jobs in that period, and highlights the importance of biography in preserving the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.1421: The book “The Life of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and His Scientific Implications” by Sheikh Ismail Al Ansari deals with the biography of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, reviewing his birth and upbringing, his sheikhs and students, and his works, in addition to his call to what the righteous predecessors did and its effects. It is classified under Biographies and Classes, as it highlights his role as a mujaddid in the twelfth century and his contributions to the renewal of religion according to the Salafi approach. The author combines historical narrative and scientific analysis to present a comprehensive picture of the life and legacy of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab.
descriptions.1422: The book “The Life of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and the Truth of His Call” by Suleiman Al-Hogail falls within the biographies of classes, as it sheds light on the biography of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and reviews the essence of his call. The book includes chapters that address his life, an explanation of the truth about his calling, and an analysis of the suspicions that were raised about it with responses based on sources and references. The author aims to provide a balanced presentation that combines historical narrative and doctrinal analysis.
descriptions.1423: The book “The Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Fahd bin Abdulaziz” by Abdul Rab Nawab Al-Din is classified among biographies and classes, and deals with the biography of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz with a focus on his efforts in establishing the foundations of education in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The content includes chapters dealing with his birth and upbringing, the stages of development of education before the establishment of the Ministry of Education, his contributions to education inside and outside the Kingdom, in addition to the characteristics of the Saudi educational system. The book shows how King Fahd sought to expand the scope of science and develop it as a basic basis for the nation's progress.
descriptions.1424: The book deals with the characteristics of the jurisprudential thinking of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, reviewing the jurisprudential situation in the Islamic world and Najd in particular, and the intellectual tributaries that influenced his scientific personality. The book explores the jurisprudential characteristics of the Sheikh through analyzing the jurisprudential legacy he left behind, relying on inductive and deductive studies to understand the nature of his jurisprudential thinking and his contributions to the field of Islamic legislation and jurisprudence.
descriptions.1425: “Summary of the Impact on Notables of the Eleventh Century” by Al-Muhibbi is a book of the type of biographies and classes that specializes in collecting the biography and works of prominent figures in the eleventh century. Its arrangement is based on the sequence of letters of the Arabic alphabet, as is evident from the table of contents divided into parts according to letters. The author begins his book by praising the Prophet Muhammad and explaining his goal in collecting news and sayings of prominent figures, adopting a rhetorical method that aims to show their exploits and enrich historical references. This work falls within the literature concerned with documenting the lives of scholars, jurists, and religious and social figures, and is considered a reference for researchers of the history of figures in that period.
descriptions.1426: This book is a summary of the jurisprudence of Tahdheeb al-Kamal fi Asma al-Rijal by Safi al-Din al-Khazraji, and it is a summary of the books that the author adopted in the field of biographies and classes. The book contains information selected from many books, such as Tahhab al-Dhahabi, Taqrib Ibn Hajar, and others, with the addition of notes and corrections from its author. The book is distinguished by its division into categories according to names, and includes the letter Alif in the excerpted part from the beginning of the book.
descriptions.1427: The book provides a translation of the life of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, the founder of the Wahhabi call, covering the stages of his upbringing, his calling, and its impact on society and the state. The author focuses on the context of the call in the eighteenth century and the intellectual and political currents that preceded it, showing how Ibn Abdul Wahhab’s call came as a response to the deviations that afflicted the Islamic nation in its beliefs and traditions.
