The book focuses on providing linguistic, rhetorical, and jurisprudential interpretations of the verses, relying on traditional interpretive sources and hadith narrations. The book is distinguished by its precise scientific style and its deep analysis of the Qur’anic text, which makes it a valuable reference for researchers and interpreters in the field of interpretation.
descriptions.1559: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an written by Ibn Ashour, focusing on liberating the correct meaning and enlightening understanding. The commentator uses an integrated scientific approach in his interpretation, combining interpretation with the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the predecessors, taking into account occasions, history, and invasions. Through his interpretation, Ibn Ashour aims to reform understanding and renew consideration of religious texts, trying to reconcile the Islamic faith with contemporary life.
descriptions.1560: Al-Tashil li Ulum al-Tanzeel is one of the books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Ibn Jazi al-Kalbi.
descriptions.1561: The graphic interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Aisha Abdul Rahman bint Al-Shati, is an interpretation that focuses on explaining the Arabic language and its rhetorical characteristics in the text of the Qur’an, and is concerned with showing the linguistic and graphic aspects of the verses. The book includes a detailed introduction and then deals with a selection of surahs such as Al-Duha, Al-Sharh, Al-Zalzalah, Al-Adiyat, Al-Nazi’at, Al-Balad, and At-Takabir in the first part, and this is complemented by the surahs of Al-Alaq, Al-Qalam, Al-Asr, Al-Layl, Al-Fajr, Al-Hamza, and Al-Ma’un in the second part. The work targets students of the Arabic language and those interested in studying the Qur’an from a literary and graphic perspective, relying on a methodology that links traditional interpretation and analysis of the Qur’anic text as the highest example of Arabic statement.
descriptions.1562: The modern interpretation of Muhammad Azzat Darwaza is a Qur’anic interpretation that arranges the surahs according to the order of revelation, and provides a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through chapters that address the nature of the text and its revelation, its rhetorical style and its spiritual and social impact, in addition to discussing its collection, codification, and formation of the Qur’an. The book combines objective analysis of the Qur’an with an interview with contemporary issues faced by young people, seeking to demonstrate the wisdom and principles of revelation in a way that brings the reader closer to the sacred text. It is classified as a book of interpretations, and targets the reader seeking a modern and renewed understanding of the Qur’an that keeps pace with the needs of the times.
descriptions.1563: The book “The Qur’anic Interpretation of the Qur’an” by Abdul Karim Younis Al-Khatib falls within the classification of interpretations, and provides a comprehensive study of the Qur’an, starting with an introductory introduction and then moving on to a discussion of Mecca and Medina, with statistics of the number of verses, words, and letters. This is followed by a detailed explanation of the verses, starting with Surah Al-Fatihah and then Surah Al-Baqarah in verse-by-verse order. The author aims to link the Qur’anic text with spiritual and jurisprudential meanings, as is evident from the introduction, which begins with a mention of “In the Name of God” and calls for adherence to the Qur’an.
descriptions.1564: The Tafsir al-Mazhari by Muhammad Thana Allah al-Mazhari is an interpretive work that specializes in clarifying the meanings and effects of Surat al-Fatihah and Surat al-Baqarah at the verse level, with parsing and linguistic detail of the Qur’anic phrases. The author provides a detailed explanation of the verses starting with In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, drawing on previous narrations and interpretations to clarify the aspects of merit and healing attributed to the surahs. The book is classified within the category of interpretations, and it adopts a phenomenological approach that focuses on the linguistic and graphic phenomena of the Qur’anic text.
descriptions.1565: The book “The Enlightening Interpretation of Doctrine, Sharia, and Method” by Dr. Wahba Al-Zuhaili provides a comprehensive interpretation of the Holy Qur’an that addresses multiple aspects of it, including doctrine, law, and method. The author focuses on providing a simplified scientific explanation away from boring prolongation and obtrusive brevity, while maintaining originality in interpretation, avoiding Israeli narratives, and linking it with contemporary reality and the requirements of the era. The book aims to bring the Qur’an closer to its readers by treating it with a comprehensive scientific analysis and focusing on the goals and objectives of its revelation, while paying attention to linking the Muslim to the Book of God in a close scientific way.
descriptions.1566: The easy interpretation is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an prepared by a group of scholars under the supervision of His Excellency Sheikh Saleh bin Abdulaziz bin Muhammad Al-Sheikh. It is based on a methodology that explains the controls of interpretation and addresses the lack of correct translations of the meanings of the Qur’an, while providing an introduction that explains the origins and development of the science of interpretation. It includes an explanation of the verses from Surat Al-Fatihah to Surat Al-Mu’minun, divided according to the surahs, with simplified parsing and interpretation aimed at facilitating understanding for the reader.
descriptions.1567: The Clear Interpretation by Muhammad Mahmoud Hijazi is a book in the field of interpretations that aims to clarify the meanings of the Holy Qur’an in a clear and accessible manner. The book begins with an introduction and dedication, then deals with Surat Al-Fatihah and Surat Al-Baqarah, divided into paragraphs that explain the vocabulary, meanings, reasons for the revelation, and legal and linguistic topics related to the verses. It includes detailed analyzes of the verses in terms of describing the righteous, unbelievers, and hypocrites, and highlighting proverbs and verses that deal with the history of the Children of Israel. The author aims to enable the reader to understand the Qur’anic text without the need for extensive knowledge of linguistic and legal sciences.
descriptions.1568: Al-Zuhayli’s Interpretation is a Qur’anic interpretation written by Wahba Al-Zuhayli. It falls within the classification of interpretations and targets the reader with an average culture, as it combines clarification and approximation of meanings. It includes an introduction and the opening of the Qur’an, then begins with Surat Al-Fatiha and Surat Al-Baqarah, covering multiple topics from demonstrating the divinity of God to descriptions of hypocrites and the goals of the Children of Israel. The author explains the interpretation methodology across three levels—enlightening, brief, and intermediate—based on previous radio experiences to facilitate understanding and bring the text closer to the reader.
descriptions.1569: The Intermediate Interpretation of the Holy Qur’an by its author, Muhammad Sayyid Tantawi, deals with an intermediate interpretation in detail between the brief and comprehensive interpretations, covering verses from Surat Al-Fatihah and Surat Al-Baqarah. The book focuses on providing clear explanations of the meanings and purposes of the verses, with reference to the beliefs, acts of worship, and rulings contained therein, with the aim of guiding the reader to the straight path and enhancing his understanding of the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.1570: This book deals with the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an through the narration of Abu Jaafar al-Tirmidhi, as it contains interpretations by a group of scholars such as Yahya ibn Yaman and Nafi’ ibn Abi Na’im, in addition to interpretations by Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji and Ata al-Khorasani. The book focuses on transmitting and interpreting verses of the Holy Qur’an, relying on a continuous narrative from well-known interpretation scholars.
descriptions.1571: Al-Tha’alabi’s interpretation, called Al-Jawahir Al-Hasan fi Interpretation of the Qur’an, by Imam Abd al-Rahman al-Tha’alabi al-Maliki (786 AH - 875 AH). It is brief in interpretation and is considered an important reference in its section because it is considered the sap of the interpretation of Ibn Attiya, which Ibn Khaldun considers the sap of the interpretations that preceded it. In general, it is considered an archaeological interpretation with a Sufi and preaching tendency that is concerned with social issues. It is also concerned with comparing the various interpretations, and giving preference to some of them over others. The other, in many places in his interpretation.
descriptions.1572: Al-Durr al-Masun fi Ulum al-Kitab al-Maknoon, a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, and at the same time it is considered an interpretation of the Qur’an. It includes the parsing of Qur’anic verses, the science of readings, grammar and language, poetry, rhetoric, and other sciences. Written by Al-Samin Al-Halabi.
descriptions.1573: Al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi al-Ma’thur is a book of interpretation, written by al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911).
descriptions.1574: This book deals with the study of the exegetical narratives in the book Fath al-Bari by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. The author focuses on Ibn Hajar’s approach in interpreting Qur’anic verses, and the research includes his treatment of issues of abrogation, the reasons for revelation, mentioning readings, and explaining the strange parts of the Qur’an. The book also includes a study of the life of Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar and his book Fath Al-Bari, and deals with his approach in the context of narratives, criticizing them, and judging them.
descriptions.1575: Al-Siraj Al-Munir fi Helping to Know Some is a Qur’anic interpretation written by Al-Khatib Al-Sherbini that aims to clarify the meanings of God’s words in the selected surahs. It includes an introduction and then an explanation of the Surahs of Al-Fatihah to the stories according to their traditional order, relying on the method of the Salaf in parsing and explaining. The work focuses on showing the rulings and linguistic synonyms of the verses with reference to their legal context.
descriptions.1576: The Divine Openings and the Unseen Keys Explained by Al-Nakhjawani is a Qur’anic interpretation that focuses on the surahs of Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah, reviewing the Divine Openings and the Unseen Keys that clarify the meanings of the verses. In his explanations, the author combines the spiritual and metaphysical aspects of the Qur’an, based on a comprehensive introduction to the secrets of knowledge and facts. The work aims to guide the reader to a deeper understanding of the verses and direct the heart to piety and remembrance.
descriptions.1577: “Revealing the Mysterious Realities of Revelation” is a Qur’anic interpretation written by the scholar Al-Zamakhshari. It falls within the classification of interpretations, and aims to show the meanings of the verses and clarify the secrets of the sacred texts. The interpretation is divided into detailed sections starting with Surat Al-Fatihah and then Surat Al-Baqarah, with each verse explained separately according to its order in the Qur’an. In his introduction, the author relies on glorifying the Qur’an and demonstrating its ability to guide the reader to religious and worldly benefits.
descriptions.1578: Revelation and Explanation of the Interpretation of the Qur’an is one of the books on the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abu Ishaq Ahmad Al-Thaalabi (d. 427 AH - 1035).
descriptions.1579: Al-Lubab fi Ulum al-Kitab is one of the books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Ibn Adel al-Hanbali (775 AH - 880 AH). The Syrian historian Omar Reda Kahhala says in his book Dictionary of Authors: “Omar bin Ali bin Adel, an interpreter, and among his works is Al-Lubab fi Ulum al-Kitab fi Tafsir al-Qur’an. He completed his work in 879 AH.”
descriptions.1580: Al-Muharrāt Al-Wajīz fi Tafsir Al-Kitāb Al-Aziz is one of the books on the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Atiya Al-Andalusi.
descriptions.1581: This book, written by Dr. Abdel Fattah Ibrahim Salama, deals with the topic of interpretation and denial of the miracles and unseen things mentioned in the Holy Qur’an. The author studies the opinions of various scholars and commentators regarding the interpretation of these miracles, and analyzes attempts to deny and question them. It focuses on how miracles and the unseen have been interpreted throughout Islamic history, and discusses the views of scholars such as Al-Tabari, Al-Zamakhshari, and Al-Razi on this topic. The book aims to examine the issue of interpretation and denial from a scientific and philosophical perspective, and to explain the truth about the miracles and unseen things mentioned in the Qur’an.
descriptions.1582: The book “The Selected Fi Interpretation of the Holy Qur’an” is a collection of interpretations prepared by a group of authors, and is classified within the literature of interpretation. The text covers surahs from Al-Fatihah to Al-Rum, and begins with an explanation of the glorification of God and His attributes before entering into an explanation of the verses. It aims to provide a selected interpretation that takes into account the comprehensiveness of the surahs and guide the reader to understanding the spiritual and legal meanings.
descriptions.1583: The Qur’anic Encyclopedia by Ibrahim Al-Ibiary is a detailed work classified as interpretation, combining the interpretation of Qur’anic texts with the historical context of the life of the Prophet ﷺ. The first part includes a chapter that sheds light on the Arabian Peninsula before the Prophet was sent, and the details of his birth, lineage, marriage, the beginning of the revelation, and the development of the call to Islam, in addition to the opposition and conspiracy of the Quraysh. The book provides a systematic account of the eras that preceded Islam and those that followed with the emergence of the first companions and the establishment of rituals. It aims to show the relationship between historical events and the interpretation of the Qur’an in a comprehensive framework.
descriptions.1584: Guidance to the End is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abu Muhammad Makki bin Abi Talib (d. 437 AH). The book is a precious interpretation, one of the pearls of the Andalusian interpretive heritage, in which various types of sciences were collected.
descriptions.1585: Al-Wajeez fi Tafsir al-Kitab al-Aziz is one of the books of abbreviations of interpretation, written by Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Ahmad al-Wahidi al-Naysaburi.
descriptions.1586: The Interpretation of the Holy Qur’an by Imam Ali bin Ahmad Al-Wahidi Al-Naysaburi is one of the important books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an among the Sunnis and the community. It is a comprehensive interpretation of the verses of the Holy Qur’an, combining an explanation of linguistic meanings and legal rulings, with special attention to the reasons for the revelation. “Al-Wasit” is part of a series of interpretations written by Al-Wahidi, which also includes “Al-Basit” and “Al-Wajeez.” Each serves a different audience, but Intermediate stands out for those looking for a medium-depth explanation that combines scholarship with precision.
descriptions.1587: Bahr al-Ulum or Tafsir al-Samarqandi is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi. There was a difference of opinion in calling the book “Bahr al-Ulum,” as those who translated Abu al-Layth did not mention the name “Bahr al-Ulum” among his books. Rather, they called it an interpretation of the Qur’an.
descriptions.1588: A book in the field of interpretations that focuses on the reflections and effects of the verse that urges not to have intercourse while secluding in mosques, and reviews the definition of seclusion and its rulings, in addition to the definition of intercourse and its rulings with and without intercourse, and the mosques in which seclusion is permissible. The author, Abdul Aziz bin Saleh Al-Ubaid, provides a detailed analysis based on sources of jurisprudence and hadith to clarify the legal rulings related to this issue. The work concludes with a conclusion that summarizes the conclusions reached and includes sources and references that support the research.
descriptions.1589: The book “Coping for the Rest of Life in the Management of Surat Al-Nasr” by Suleiman Al-Lahim is an interpretation of Surat Al-Nasr and links its meanings to the Muslim’s preparation for the afterlife. The author focuses on the reality of death and life as a test, drawing on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths to guide the reader to increasing worship and seeking forgiveness with age. The book includes an introduction that explains its objectives, sources, and references.
descriptions.1590: Tadhkirat al-Areeb fi Tafsir al-Gharib is one of the books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by the Hanbali jurist Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi.
descriptions.1591: A book that studies the places in which God Almighty glorifies Himself in the Holy Qur’an. The author collected it from twenty-five verses, then classified them according to their basic topics. The book is divided into three chapters, the first of which deals with praising God for associating others with Him, the second for praising Him for taking a child, and the third for praising Him for various other matters. The author aims to explain the wisdom behind the occurrence of praise in every place, and to explain the connection between it and the verses before and after it, while seeking help from the words of commentators and mentioning rhetorical and linguistic subtleties.
descriptions.1592: Interpretation of verses from the Holy Qur’an by its author, Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, is a work of interpretations that includes an explanation of verses from Surat Al-Fatihah to Surah Al-Qassar, with the inclusion of stories of the prophets and passages from short surahs. It is based on two complete manuscripts that were compiled and provided with footnotes explaining the texts of the verses, the graduation of hadiths, and the definition of the notable figures mentioned. The book includes an introduction that explains the interpretation methodology and shows the author’s interest in explaining the linguistic and legal meanings of the verses, with reference to the sources and references he used in preparing the text. This is the fifth part of the works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and is presented as a comprehensive reference for researchers and readers interested in understanding the Qur’an according to the traditional interpretation approach.
descriptions.1593: Tafsir Abu Al-Saud is a Qur’anic commentary written by Abu Al-Saud that aims to guide the sound mind to the merits of the Holy Book. The interpretation covers surah after surah, starting from Al-Fatihah to Al-Ankabut, highlighting the meanings and statements that clarify the truth and directing the reader to the straight path. This work falls within the classification of interpretations, and its style relies on inferring verses and clarifying their connotations to strengthen mental and spiritual understanding.
descriptions.1594: The book Tafsir Ibn Abi Al-Izz is a Qur’anic interpretation that combines the collection and explanations of the texts of Imam Ibn Abi Al-Izz and their commentary. It includes an introductory introduction to the author and his scientific method. It includes a comprehensive study of the surahs from Al-Fatihah to Saba according to the traditional order of the Qur’an, with an explanation of the reasons for choosing the topic and the research plan. It aims to provide an integrated interpretation based on correct doctrine and addresses the philosophical differences that have influenced some interpretations.
descriptions.1595: Tafsir Ibn Badis is one of the modern books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abd al-Hamid Ibn Badis.
descriptions.1596: Tafsir Ibn Fourk from the beginning of Surah Al-Mu’minun to the end is a detailed explanation of the Holy Qur’an written by Imam Ibn Fourk, and falls within the classification of interpretations. The text deals with the verses of Surat Al-Mu'minun, clarifying the meanings of words and phrases and their purposes, and continues to other surahs such as Al-Nour, Al-Furqan, Al-Shu'ara', Al-Naml, and Al-Qasas according to the order of the verses mentioned in the index. The explanation relies on a question-and-answer method to clarify linguistic and jurisprudential concepts related to worship and morals. It aims to clarify the correct understanding of the verses for the Muslim reader.
descriptions.1597: The book “Interpretation of Imam Ibn Arafa” is a book in the science of interpretation that presents a definition of the truth of the Qur’an, its subject and its meaning, based on the Arabic language and rhetoric and based on evidence from poetry and parsing. The author explains the conditions for the interpreter to memorize the entire Qur’an and the tools of ijtihad, and reviews the usefulness of interpretation in deriving rulings and meanings from the principles of religion and jurisprudence. The book includes Surahs Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah as samples of annotated Qur’anic texts.
descriptions.1598: Tafsir Imam al-Shafi’i is a collection of interpretations that collects what was narrated by Imam al-Shafi’i in explaining the verses of the Holy Qur’an, arranged according to the order of the surahs in the Qur’an. It includes his sayings about various parts of the surahs, such as Al-Fatihah, Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran and Al-Nisa, and deals with the rulings on seeking refuge before reading and the description of prayer, and what Al-Shafi’i influences regarding interpretation and meanings regarding purifications and prayers. It aims to clarify matters related to recitation and worship according to the Shafi’i approach.
descriptions.1599: Tafsir al-Iji, written by Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Hasani al-Husseini al-Iji al-Shafi’i, who died in the year 905 AH. He wanted, in writing the book, to compile a brief book full of scientific benefits due to what he saw as people’s disengagement from lengthy scholarly treatises, and his desire to participate in writing in the science of interpretation, and he called it: “Jami’ al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur’an.”
descriptions.1600: Tafsir al-Tustari is one of the books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by the eminent Sunni Sufis in the third century AH, Sahl al-Tustari. The book consists of sayings by Sahl, collected by Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ahmed al-Baladi, mentioned at the beginning of the book, who used to say a lot. Abu Bakr said, Sahl was asked about the meaning of such-and-such, and he said: such-and-such. Then he included it in this book and attributed it to him. The interpretation is distinguished by its small size, as it does not include a complete interpretation of all the verses of the Holy Qur’an. Rather, it is an interpretation of some verses of the Holy Qur’an, and comments that were a response to the questions of some of al-Tastari’s students. It was therefore a brief interpretation, as is the method of the Sufis.
descriptions.1601: Tafsir Sufyan al-Thawri is a Qur’anic commentary written by Imam Sufyan bin Saeed bin Masruq al-Thawri al-Kufi. It includes an introduction that addresses the biography of the author and his position in jurisprudence and interpretation, in addition to details about his sheikhs, students, and the characteristics of his version. This is followed by a presentation of the surahs of the Qur’an from Al-Baqarah to Al-Hijr, with an indication of the drawbacks of translation and the characteristics of writing. This work is considered one of the classic books of interpretation that combine interpretation and historical statement by scholars.
descriptions.1602: Tafsir al-Jalalayn is a summary of an interpretation of the Qur’an, written by Jalal al-Din al-Muhalla, and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. Saad bin Taher Al Ansari
descriptions.1603: Tafsir Al-Hujurat - Al-Hadid is a brief interpretation of the Holy Qur’an prepared by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen. It includes an explanation of Surahs Al-Hujurat, Al-Hadid and other surahs such as Al-Qaq, Al-Dhariyat, Al-Tur, Al-Najm, Al-Qamar, Al-Rahman, and Al-Waqi’ah. The interpretation focuses on the etiquette of faith and worship, based on the methodology of jurisprudence and doctrine followed by the author. It includes an introductory introduction to give readers pause before going into the explanation of the surahs.
descriptions.1604: Tafsir al-Raghib al-Isfahani is a book on the science of interpretations presented by Sheikh Abu al-Qasim al-Raghib al-Isfahani. It focuses on clarifying the linguistic and rhetorical rules that are used in understanding the Qur’an, and addresses topics such as the commonality of pronunciation, the difference between truth and metaphor, and the distinction between interpretation and interpretation. It also includes chapters on the wisdom of similarity in verses, the miracle of the Qur’an, and the tools needed by the interpreter. The book concludes with a detailed explanation of Surat Al-Fatihah according to a scientific methodology.
descriptions.1605: Al-Shaarawi’s interpretation or Al-Shaarawi’s thoughts is Sheikh Muhammad Metwally Al-Shaarawi’s interpretation or his thoughts about the Holy Qur’an. It is the most famous book of modern interpretations, and some place it in the position of books renewing the matter of religion, about which the Messenger ﷺ said in the authentic hadith, “God sends at the beginning of every hundred years someone who will renew the matter of its religion for this nation.” …
descriptions.1606: Jami’ al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur’an or Jami’ al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur’an or Jami’ al-Bayan fi Interpretation of the Qur’an, known as “Tafsir al-Tabari” by Imam Muhammad bin Jarir bin Yazid bin Katheer bin Ghalib, known as Imam Abu Jaafar al-Tabari, (224 AH-310 AH / 839-923 AD), is one of the most famous Islamic books specialized in the science of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an among the Sunnis and the community, and some consider it the first reference. To interpret the sayings, Where he mentions a verse from the Qur’an, then lists the sayings of the Companions and Followers in interpreting it with their chains of transmission, and pays attention to the different readings in each verse and considers one of them more likely, and lists the Prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, and jurisprudential rulings. He is famous for his many Israeli stories, or what are called Israelites, and...
descriptions.1607: Interpretation of Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah by Ibn Uthaymeen is a work within the classification of interpretations that focuses on explaining Surahs Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah, while providing an introductory introduction that explains the importance of the principles of the science of interpretation. The book deals with the topics of the revelation of the Qur’an, its distinction between Meccan and Medinan, its compilation and writing, in addition to discussing the meaning of interpretation and its rulings and the duties required of a Muslim in interpreting the Qur’an. It also reviews the opinions of the Companions and Followers in interpretation and relies on the Qur’an and Sunnah as a basic reference.
descriptions.1608: Interpretation of the Holy Qur’an (Tafsir Al-Manar) written by Muhammad Rashid Reda is a detailed work in the field of interpretations that aims to explain the meanings of the Holy Qur’an and clarify its purposes. The book includes an introductory introduction and then deals with the surahs from Al-Fatihah to Yusuf in a traditional order, with reference to the verses and their interpretation in a scientific manner. The author focuses on highlighting the differences between clear and similar verses, based on an interpretive methodology that relies on linguistic and legal understanding.
descriptions.1609: Interpretation of the Mighty Qur’an by Ibn Abi Zamanin is a detailed work in the field of interpretations that explains the verses of the surahs from Al-Fatihah to Al-Ankabut according to the order of the Qur’an. In his explanation, the author relies on attributing hadiths and narrations to the Companions and Followers, and relies on the sciences of language, grammar, and jurisprudence to clarify the meanings of the Qur’anic text. The book includes an introductory introduction that explains his approach in combining what was stated in previous interpretations and adding what has not been explained before, while directing the reader to understand the verses comprehensively.
descriptions.1610: Tafsir al-Qur’an al-Grazim by Ibn Kathir is one of the books of interpretations that combines the science of the text and translation with a detailed explanation of the Qur’anic passages. The author begins with an introduction in which he mentions his biography and a review of his sheikhs, then he discusses Surah Al-Fatihah, explaining its virtues and the hadiths mentioned in it. The book also includes an index explaining Ibn Kathir's various works in historical and modern sciences. This interpretation is considered an essential reference for anyone who desires an in-depth understanding of the Qur’an according to a scientific approach.
descriptions.1611: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an written by Al-Razi Ibn Abi Hatim. It aims to provide a brief interpretation of the verses with the most correct chains of narrations, while omitting other evidence and narrations. The author focuses on providing correct interpretations of the verses without elaborating on other details, basing this on the sayings of the Messenger ﷺ and the Companions and followers.
descriptions.1612: The interpretation of the great Qur’an, known as “Tafsir Ibn Kathir,” by Imam Imad al-Din Abi al-Fuda Ismail bin Kathir al-Qurashi al-Dimashqi, known as Ibn Kathir (who died in 774 AH), is one of the most famous Islamic books specialized in the science of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, and it is considered one of the most famous things written on the subject of interpretation by tradition or interpretation of the Qur’an by the Qur’an. It relies on the interpretation of the Qur’an by the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet, and it also mentions the hadiths and traces attributed to its authors. And the sayings of the Companions and Followers. He also paid attention to the Arabic language and its sciences. He paid attention to the chains of transmission and its criticism. He paid attention to mentioning the different readings and the reasons for the revelation of the verses. It also includes jurisprudential rulings, pays attention to the Prophetic hadiths, and is famous for being devoid of...
descriptions.1613: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Quran by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, one of the prominent scholars of Islam. The interpretation deals with verses from multiple surahs of the Qur’an, with a focus on providing deep explanations and interpretations of the Qur’anic text through an integrated scientific and religious perspective. The book aims to better understand the meanings and connotations of the Qur’an, and provides various interpretations of various verses from different surahs, including Surat Al-Fatihah and Surat Al-Baqarah.
descriptions.1614: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an written by Al-Izz bin Abdul Salam, and it is an abbreviation of Al-Mawardi’s interpretation. The book deals with the interpretation of Meccan and Medinan surahs in detail, with a focus on the linguistic and terminological meanings and connotations of Quranic verses and names. The author begins with an interpretation of Surat Al-Fatihah and then moves successively to the rest of the surahs. In his introduction, he reviews definitions of the names of the Holy Qur’an and details of some important surahs such as the Seven Long, Al-Mathani, and Al-Mufassal, along with providing explanations of some verses and narrations related to these names.
descriptions.1615: Tafsir Al-Samani is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an that deals with the interpretation of the Meccan and Medinan surahs, and begins with detailing the meanings and connotations of Surat Al-Fatihah, reviewing its names and aspects of its virtues, with reference to the opinions of scholars regarding its revelation and chronological order. The book focuses on providing linguistic and spiritual interpretations of Qur’anic verses, relying on interpretation of the hadiths and other interpretations.
descriptions.1616: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an with the parsing of its verses, written by Abu Al-Hussein Ubaidullah bin Abi Jaafar bin Ahmed bin Abi Al-Rabi’ Al-Andalusi. In his interpretation, the author deals with the interpretation of Qur’anic meanings with a focus on the grammatical and morphological aspects. He reviews issues of parsing and their impact in directing meaning. He also refers to multiple scientific sources in his treatment of Qur’anic texts. The book represents a scientific effort that combines linguistic and jurisprudential interpretation with attention to grammatical and morphological rules. It was produced by a well-known Andalusian scholar, famous for his Arabic sciences and the sciences of the Qur’an.
descriptions.1617: The book Tafsir al-Kahf by Ibn Uthaymeen is an interpretation of Surat al-Kahf within the classification of interpretations. It includes an introduction and detail of the verses based on a scientific course held in the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal of the year 1419 AH at the Grand Mosque in Unayzah. The text was compiled from recordings of Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Othaimeen’s lectures, which were reviewed and completed by Dr. Saleh Al-Saleh, to be presented in the form of a unified interpretation aimed at benefiting the reader.
descriptions.1618: Tafsir Al-Mawardi is one of the books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Al-Mawardi.
descriptions.1619: Interpretation of Al-Maraghi. One of the contemporary books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by the Al-Azhar scholar Ahmed Mustafa Al-Maraghi, is dominated by linguistic interpretation.
descriptions.1620: The Meanings of Revelation and the Facts of Interpretation, it is a brief interpretation, which its author, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Mahmoud Al-Nasafi, summarized from Tafsir Al-Baydawi, and from Al-Kashshaf by Al-Zamakhshari, so it came, as the author said: “A moderate book in interpretations, bringing together the aspects of parsing and readings, containing the details of my wonderful knowledge and current references to the sayings of the Sunnis and the community, devoid of the falsehoods of the people of innovation and misguidance, not “By long and boring, and not by short and boring.” …
descriptions.1621: The book “Tafsir Juz Amma” by Sheikh Musaed Al-Tayyar is a book in the field of interpretations that specializes in interpreting the last surahs of the Qur’an. It follows an approach that combines the text and the footnote, with a focus on clarifying linguistic vocabulary, showing the differences between the commentators and the predecessors, and highlighting the weightings. It includes chapters for specific surahs from Surat An-Naba to Surat At-Takhab, and is based on the interpretation of Imam al-Tabari with reference to the opinions of Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim without delving into the sciences of grammar, rhetoric, and jurisprudence in an extensive way. The author aims to provide a clear and easy-to-phrase interpretation limited to the Qur’anic text and its explanatory notes.
descriptions.1622: Tafsir Juz Amma by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen is a work of interpretations that specializes in Juz Amma of the Holy Qur’an. It includes an introductory introduction and then an interpretation of Surat Al-Fatihah, Surat Al-Naba’, Al-Nazi’at, Al-Abs, and other short surahs up to Surat Al-Humza. The book aims to explain the meanings of the verses and extract rulings and benefits from them according to what God has made available to him in terms of knowledge, faith, and contemplation. It is considered a brief reference for those who wish to understand the texts of the last part of the Qur’an in an easy and readable manner.
descriptions.1623: Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq al-San’ani is one of the oldest books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by the hadith scholar of Yemen, Abd al-Razzaq al-San’ani.
descriptions.1624: Tafsir Mujahid is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by the Tabi’i Mujahid bin Jabr.
descriptions.1625: Muqatil’s interpretation is the title of the interpretation written by Muqatil bin Sulaiman (150 AH). Researchers, ancient and modern, have differed in determining the time of the appearance of the first complete interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, but some consider Muqatil’s interpretation to be the first complete interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, and what is certain is that this interpretation is one of the advanced interpretations. The book Tafsir Muqatil was printed, edited by Abdullah Shehata, in Dar Ihya’ al-Turath al-Islami, 1423 AH, and edited by Ahmed Farid al-Mazidi, in Dar al-Kutub al-Ilmiyyah, 1424 AH.
descriptions.1626: Tafsir Yahya bin Salam is a book written by Yahya bin Salam al-Taymi al-Basri al-Qayrawani (d. 200 AH), and the time of its writing dates back to the second half of the second century AH. It is a comprehensive interpretation of all the surahs of the Holy Qur’an, with all their verses, based on famous sayings that were narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, or on the authority of the Companions and Followers (may Allah be pleased with them).
descriptions.1627: Tawfiq Al-Rahman in the Lessons of the Qur’an by Faisal Al-Mubarak is an author in the field of interpretations that aims to simplify the meanings of the Qur’an in the language of the reader. The author relies on the sayings of great commentators such as Ibn Jarir, Ibn Kathir and Al-Baghawi, and presents the lessons according to the order of the surahs, starting from Al-Fatihah to An-Nisa. The book includes an introduction that explains the importance of interpretation and directs the reader to understand the texts according to his ability, while clarifying concepts such as abrogation and abrogation.
descriptions.1628: The book Tafsir al-Saadi or Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir Kalam al-Mannan, one of the interpretations of the Holy Qur’an in the modern era.
descriptions.1629: The book by Taysir al-Latif al-Mannan fi Khalasa Tafsir al-Qur’an by Sheikh Abd al-Rahman al-Saadi is a brief interpretation that focuses on extracting rulings and sciences from the texts of the Qur’an, based on selecting selected verses that cover the topics of monotheism, doctrine, and principles. The book provides an explanation of basic acts of worship such as prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj, in addition to chapters on purity, jihad, financial transactions, inheritance, and rights between God and people. The author aims to provide a simple explanation that makes it easier for the reader to understand the legal and jurisprudential purposes of the Qur’an without prolonging the narrative.
descriptions.1630: Jami’ al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur’an or Jami’ al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur’an or Jami’ al-Bayan fi Interpretation of the Qur’an, known as “Tafsir al-Tabari” by Imam Muhammad bin Jarir bin Yazid bin Katheer bin Ghalib, known as Imam Abu Jaafar al-Tabari, (224 AH-310 AH / 839-923 AD), is one of the most famous Islamic books specialized in the science of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an among the Sunnis and the community, and some consider it the first reference. To interpret the sayings, Where he mentions a verse from the Qur’an, then lists the sayings of the Companions and Followers in interpreting it with their chains of transmission, and pays attention to the different readings in each verse and considers one of them more likely, and lists the Prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, and jurisprudential rulings. He is famous for his many Israeli stories, or what are called Israelites, and...
descriptions.1631: A book that studies the Qur’anic places in which God praised His Noble Self, reviewing fifteen places in different surahs such as Al-Fatihah, Al-An’am, and Al-Kahf. The author aims to explain the wisdom behind the occurrence of praise in every place, and to reveal the connection between the verse and what comes before and after it, relying on the sayings of the commentators. The work falls within the interpretive studies that focus on the connotations of Qur’anic words and their rhetorical secrets.
descriptions.1632: Al-Shihab’s footnote to Tafsir al-Baydawi is a detailed explanation of Imam al-Baydawi’s interpretation, prepared by al-Shihab al-Khafaji from the Hanafi school of thought, and it is concerned with clarifying parsing, meanings, explanation, wisdom, derivation, and other sciences of language and jurisprudence. The book includes comments on multiple surahs, starting from Al-Fatihah to Al-Qasas, and is intended to provide the judge with the care and sufficiency of Al-Radi in understanding the Qur’anic text. The author aims to clarify the verses and make them easier for readers to understand through a clear and organized manner.
descriptions.1633: Al-Shihab Al-Khafaji’s footnote to Tafsir Al-Baydawi is a detailed explanation concerned with clarifying the meanings of the Qur’an and clarifying the evidence for parsing and clarification in Imam Al-Baydawi’s interpretation. It is considered one of the most important jurisprudential and linguistic footnotes in the field of interpretation. The book includes notes and introductions covering the surahs from Al-Fatihah to the stories, with parsing and linguistic connotations that contribute to understanding the Qur’anic text. In it, the author shows extensive knowledge of legal and linguistic sciences, providing an explanation that makes it easier for the reader to understand jurisprudence and rhetoric in Al-Baydawi’s interpretation.
descriptions.1634: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an written by Imam Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali. It deals with multiple verses from different surahs and explains their meanings and secrets. It focuses on the virtues of the Qur’an and its profound impact on hearts and lives, and reviews verses such as Surat Al-Fatihah, Al-Mu’awwidhatain, and Surat Al-Baqarah, while providing detailed explanations of some other verses from the Qur’an. The book aims to enhance the reader’s understanding of the Qur’an and encourage him to think and ponder its meanings.
descriptions.1635: Ruh al-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur’an is one of the books of interpretation, written by Abu al-Fidaa Ismail Haqqi bin al-Sheikh Mustafa al-Istanbouli al-Idosi al-Hanafi al-Jalouti.
descriptions.1636: Zad al-Masir fi Ilm al-Tafsir is one of the books of interpretation, written by al-Hafiz Ibn al-Jawzi (510 AH - 592 AH). The book is considered an average book on interpretation in which the author collects the sayings of the early commentators and others. Sometimes he does not mention the author of the statement, but rather says, and in the Almighty’s saying (then he mentions the verse) there are two or three opinions and then lists them. Sometimes he gives preference and sometimes he does not give preference. He is also exposed to readings, and he is also exposed to jurisprudential and linguistic issues.
descriptions.1637: Safwat al-Tafsir is a book on the science of interpretation, authored by Muhammad Ali al-Sabouni. It is an interpretation of Qur’anic verses, an explanation of their meanings and connotations, and what is taken from them. Its author relied on the most important sources for interpreting the Holy Qur’an taken from the most reliable books of interpretation of the ancient imams. He also mentions the sayings of later scholars. The book Safwat al-Tafsir includes a summary of the sayings of the imams of interpretation, in a simple style that is easy for the learner and reader to understand, and in clear and useful phrases. By interpreting linguistic meanings, rhetorical methods, and the meanings and rulings contained in the verses.
descriptions.1638: This book, “The Path of Guidance, Principles and Introductions to the Science of Monotheism according to the Sunnis and the Community,” deals with defining the term “Ahl al-Sunnah wal Jama’ah” and explaining their characteristics, with a focus on the science of Monotheism and its principles according to this school of jurisprudence. The author begins by explaining the term "Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah" from a linguistic and terminological standpoint, then moves on to clarify the legitimacy of this term and compare other similar terms. In the second part of the book, he focuses on the principles of monotheism and its importance in the Islamic religion, stressing the necessity of singling out God for worship and His monotheism as the first priority in the heavenly calling.
descriptions.1639: Oddities of Interpretation and Wonders of Interpretation. Its author is Abu al-Qasim Mahmoud bin Hamza bin Nasr al-Kirmani, the grammarian. This book contains abundant knowledge in the various sciences of the Qur’an. Its author has included in it meanings that cannot be relied upon, some of which are far from the intent of the verse. He only mentioned that to warn against it, and not to rely on it. The reason for the presence of strangeness in interpretation is that there are people who have a passion for strangeness in speech, even if they deviate from the path and ride a bumpy road.
descriptions.1640: The Oddities of the Qur’an and the Oddities of the Furqan is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by the commentator Nizam al-Din al-Naysaburi.
descriptions.1641: Tafsir Fath al-Qadeer by Al-Shawkani (1173 - 1250 AH) is considered one of the foundations of interpretation, and a reference among its references, because it combined interpretation by narration and interpretation by knowledge, as its author excelled in it in the chapter of narration, and expanded upon the chapter of knowledge. He began writing it in the month of Rabi` al-Akhir in the year 1223 AH.
descriptions.1642: In the Shadows of the Qur’an, known as The Shadows, is a book of interpretation of the Qur’an written by Sayyid Qutb Ibrahim Hussein al-Shazly, known as Sayyid Qutb (October 9, 1906 AD - August 29, 1966 AD) and divided it into thirty parts according to the division of the parts of the Qur’an and in the same order. It was printed several times in volumes. The book of interpretation, “In the Shadows of the Qur’an,” is classified among the interpretations based on aphorisms. It combines the analytical, rhetorical, and social literary aspects. It is also classified among the objective interpretations, as it is concerned with the objective unity of the surah. “This is done by talking about the surah as a whole, in terms of its general and specific purposes, while linking its topics to each other, until the surah, which is in the utmost harmony and precision, appears as if it were a string of pearls arranged with the utmost creativity.” …
descriptions.1643: The book “Interpretation of the Qur’an” by Sheikh Ibn al-Mundhir al-Naysaburi is an interpretation from the class of interpretations. It adheres to the approach of the predecessors in explaining the Qur’an with the Qur’an, then with the Sunnah of the Prophet, then with the sayings of the Companions and Followers, and it relies on ijtihad in deducing meanings. The book includes detailed introductions to the author’s biography, his sheikhs and students, and his scholarly standing, in addition to a systematic explanation of the book in terms of documenting its attribution to the author, the work’s methodology, and comparing copies. It aims to clarify the meanings of the verses and contemplate them for readers according to the principles of accurate and sound interpretation.
descriptions.1644: The chapter on interpretation in the meanings of revelation is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Ali bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Shehi, known as Al-Khazen.
descriptions.1645: Lata’if al-Isharat” is a Qur’anic interpretation prepared by Abd al-Karim al-Qushayri. It specializes in dealing with the Qur’anic text on the approach of the Sufis and the Mujahideen. It is a rare approach in the Arab library that differs from the interpretations that focus on language, jurisprudence, or the reasons for revelation. The book includes an introduction that explains its importance and reviews the author’s approach in writing the book, then follows in detail the verses in Surat Al-Fatihah and Surat Al-Baqarah according to their order. The work aims to collect the sayings of the sheikhs of the people of truth and present them in a sequential Syrian context that enriches the reader with a Sufi understanding of the Qur’an.
descriptions.1646: Investigations of Interpretation by Ibn al-Muzaffar al-Razi is a book in the field of interpretations that specializes in explaining the Holy Qur’an in a critical and analytical manner. It opens with the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, then moves to Surat al-Fatihah, in which it deals with linguistic and syntactic issues related to the basmalah and the name. This is followed by detailed chapters for both Meccan and Medinan surahs from Al-Baqarah to Al-Anfal, including passages based on Qur’anic verses and discussing the meanings of words and their interpretations according to the opinions of jurists and linguists. The book stands out through its observations on the origins of names and the origins of words and its comparison between different sects, which makes it an important reference for researchers in the sciences of the Qur’an and the Arabic language.
descriptions.1647: The virtues of interpretation, known as Tafsir Al-Qasimi, is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Jamal Al-Din Al-Qasimi (1283 - 1332 AH / 1866 - 1914 AD). His interpretation is considered a modern encyclopedia in interpretation, because he was one of the latecomers, so he looked at the interpretations of the predecessors, and knew what was in them of riches and precious things, so he included the interpretation of many anecdotes of benefits and unique things, and chose the most correct and accurate opinions. It was presented in the language and style of the era.
descriptions.1648: Brief Tafsir Ibn Kathir is a summary of the interpretation of the venerable Imam Ismail bin Kathir al-Dimashqi, prepared by Professor Muhammad Ali al-Sabouni within the framework of the classification of interpretations. It aims to provide a brief explanation of the Holy Qur’an that combines narration and knowledge. The book covers surahs from Al-Fatihah to Al-Rum, based on the approach of clarifying meanings and extracting rulings and masterpieces from the Qur’anic text.
descriptions.1649: Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Baghawi is one of the brief books on interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Ali al-Zaid. The book is an abbreviation of Tafsir al-Baghawi.
descriptions.1650: Brief Interpretation of Surat Al-Anfal” is a work written by Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab that falls within the classification of interpretations. It is limited to providing a brief explanation of Surat Al-Anfal with reference to its sources and references. The book includes an introductory introduction explaining the context of the revelation and the facts related to Surah Anfal, which is then followed by a brief explanatory text. The section concludes with a statement of the sources on which the author relied in preparing this interpretation.
descriptions.1651: Marah Labid to Reveal the Meaning of the Glorious Qur’an” is a Qur’anic interpretation written by Nawawi al-Jawwi that aims to clarify the meanings of the holy text. The book includes an introduction, a sermon, and a translation by the author. It then begins with Surat Al-Fatihah and follows it with Surat Al-Baqarah, divided into sections according to its verses. This work falls within the classification of interpretations and relies on a detailed explanation methodology for the verses.
descriptions.1652: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an written by Imam Al-Baghawi. It deals with the verses of the Holy Qur’an, explaining their meanings and showing the aspects of interpretation in the light of texts and hadiths. In his interpretation, Al-Baghawi focuses on understanding the verses of the Holy Book and explaining its secrets and rulings, relying on the interpretive methodology prevailing in his time. The book begins with an introductory introduction that addresses the virtues of the Qur’an and its recitation, then moves on to interpreting the Meccan and Medinan surahs in turn, presenting the reader with an integrated interpretation of the Qur’an that combines knowledge and a deep understanding of the Qur’anic text.
descriptions.1653: Meanings of the Qur’an is one of the books of interpretation that focuses on the meanings of the Holy Qur’an. It was written by the grammarian Al-Akhfash Al-Awsat.
descriptions.1654: The meanings of the Qur’an and its parsing, called The Brief on the Parsing of the Qur’an and Its Meanings, is a book whose subject is parsing the Holy Qur’an and explaining its meanings. In it, the author expressed many sentences of the words of the Holy Qur’an and also clarified the meanings contained in the Holy Qur’an through his explanation of the Qur’anic verses and words. Al-Zajjaj classified this book, “The Meanings of the Qur’an,” and stated that he wanted it to explain its meanings and parsing with the first intention and to know its interpretation with the second intention. Therefore, you will find most of what is in the book related to grammar, language, and morphology, while benefiting from what was reported from the predecessors in interpretation in giving preference to this or that statement.
descriptions.1655: Keys to the Unseen or Al-Tafsir Al-Kabir by Al-Razi is an expanded interpretation of the Qur’an that focuses in the first part on Surah Al-Fatihah, and includes an introduction and chapters that deal with the sciences of the Surah in terms of alerting to its meanings and purposes. The book provides a detailed explanation of the Basmala and the Isti'adah, and presents linguistic and grammatical analyzes of the verses, in addition to discussions of the origins of the faith and the afterlife. It also includes sections that address the rules related to nouns, verbs, and letters, with their parsing and detail. The author aims to clarify the sciences deduced from the Qur’anic text and guide the reader to a deep understanding of the meanings.
descriptions.1656: This book is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an that focuses on directing verses that are similar in wording and refuting attempts at atheism and obstruction. The author, Abu Jaafar Ahmad bin Al-Zubair Al-Gharnati, discusses verses from several Qur’anic surahs, reviewing the opinions of those who disagree and citing evidence of the validity of the correct interpretation of the text. The book is a type of interpretation that aims to show the meanings of the Qur’an and explain its facts to readers, with a focus on responding to the Mu’tazila, Rafidites, Jahmiyya, and Ash’aris.
descriptions.1657: This book is an encyclopedia of interpretation based on the hadiths. It focuses on collecting and compiling authentic hadiths related to the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an. The author, Hikmat Bashir Yassin, discusses the most famous methods and chains of transmission in interpretation, relying on a scientific approach to criticism and brevity. The book aims to distinguish authentic hadiths from others, and to provide reliable interpretations of Quranic verses based on the sayings of the Companions, the Successors, and their followers. The book also addresses the importance of the science of interpretation of the hadiths in understanding the meanings and objectives of the Qur’an.
descriptions.1658: Nazm al-Durar fi Proportionality of Verses and Surahs is a book of interpretations of the Holy Qur’an, written by Imam Burhan al-Din al-Baqa’i (809 AH - 885 AH). The book is considered one of the venerable books. In it, his compiler placed knowledge that no one had preceded him. In it, he mentioned the occasions for arranging surahs and verses. He extended contemplation and indulged in contemplating the verses of the Book. He included in his book one of the aspects of the linguistic miracle in the Holy Qur’an, and demonstrated the connection between all parts of the Qur’an. The systems are detailed between each verse and verse in each surah of the Holy Quran.
descriptions.1659: This book is a footnote by Imam Al-Suyuti on Tafsir Al-Baydawi, in which Al-Suyuti discusses his explanation and interpretation of the verses of the Holy Qur’an, reviewing the opinions of previous scholars in interpreting Qur’anic texts. The book focuses on providing different interpretations of some verses, relying on previous hadiths, traces, and sayings, and aims to enrich the reader’s understanding of the Qur’anic text by presenting multiple points of view.
descriptions.1660: The Journal of the Islamic University of Medina is a scientific and cultural publication that combines academic research, jurisprudential and cultural studies, as it addresses various topics related to Islamic ethics, jurisprudence, the call to God, and Islamic culture. The magazine includes articles by prominent scholars and jurists on various topics aimed at disseminating Sharia sciences, strengthening Islamic jurisprudence, and highlighting issues relevant to the Muslim community.
descriptions.1661: The Damascene Truths magazine, issued by Abd al-Qadir al-Iskandarani, deals with Islamic religious issues, from monotheism and education to jurisprudence and jurists, to the Arabic language and its scholars, in addition to ethics, criticism, history, and other diverse topics. The magazine includes articles that explain the principles of religion and show its impact in improving morals and guiding souls in a deductive and analytical manner. The indexes show a diversity of content among a number of sections, such as jurisprudence, language, and social sciences, which reflects the comprehensive nature of the magazine as a cultural and religious newspaper in Damascus.
descriptions.1662: Umm Al-Qura University Journal is a scientific periodical that brings together a collection of articles that address multiple Islamic topics such as interpretation of the Qur’an, rulings on worship, jurisprudential issues, linguistic studies, and historical and cultural topics related to Islam and the Arab world. The issue features articles on the science of David and Solomon, the rulings on the siwak, the concept of political authority in the Islamic system, human rights in Western philosophy, and the influence of Islamic culture in Malay countries, in addition to linguistic studies on Arabic forms and the intersection of languages. The publication aims to provide objective research that analyzes religious texts and reviews contemporary issues from an Islamic perspective.
descriptions.1663: The Journal of the Islamic Jurisprudence Academy is a periodical issued by the Islamic Jurisprudence Academy of the Organization of the Islamic Conference. It includes a collection of official speeches, decisions, and reports related to the establishment and activation of the Jurisprudence Academy. The volumes include speeches by senior officials, resolutions of summits and conferences, reports of studies, research and fatwa divisions, in addition to detailed lists of members of the council and representatives of countries. The book aims to document the collective efforts of jurists and scholars in addressing contemporary issues in accordance with the Sharia approach and its objectives.
descriptions.1664: Athar Ibn Badis is a comprehensive collection of the works of Sheikh Abdel Hamid Ibn Badis, combining interpretation of the Qur’an and explanation of the Hadith on the one hand, and his social, educational and reform articles on the other hand, and reviewing his intellectual and cultural career in the Islamic Maghreb and his role in the modern renaissance of Algeria. The first volume includes an introduction to mental life and the renaissance, and chapters dealing with reform trends, the role of the Arab press, and the factors that shaped his personality, in addition to his views on education and student organization. The book also shows his criticism of the educational curricula of his era and his vision of educational institutions. This work is an important reference for understanding the Islamic reform movement in North Africa.
descriptions.1665: This book deals with various jurisprudential researches issued by the Council of Senior Scholars in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The first volume includes research on topics such as the ruling on sa’y above the Mas’a ceiling and banknotes, relying on jurisprudential opinions and documented scientific decisions. The book is part of a series that brings together multiple research papers by different authors in the fields of Sharia and Fatwa.
descriptions.1666: The book is a documentary collection that records the activities of the World Conference to direct the call and prepare preachers. It includes the speeches of senior scholars and officials, in addition to the conference’s program, research, and work councils. It includes an opening speech by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz, speeches by the Minister of Higher Education, Sheikh Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad, and Sheikh Abi Al-Hassan Al-Nadawi, in addition to committee reports and daily programs. It also includes the conference guide, its content, general objectives, and the main topics discussed in it. It is classified as mosques, magazines, and the like, which makes it an important reference for those interested in preaching Islam and preparing preachers.
descriptions.1667: The book “Al-Hawamil wa Al-Shamil, Questions of Abu Hayyan Al-Tawhid” by Ibn Miskawayh is a collection of various issues that address linguistic, moral, natural, psychological and medical issues, by asking questions and analyzing them. The book falls within the classification of mosques and magazines, which reflects its nature as a periodical or a collection of scientific and philosophical articles. The author aims to explore the differences between concepts and explain the causes and results in the various fields he presents.
descriptions.1668: Al-Sharia newspaper of the Prophet Muhammadiyah is a newspaper issued by the Association of Algerian Muslim Scholars under the supervision of Professor Abdelhamid Ben Badis. The newspaper dealt with important religious and social issues, and focused on defending the Sunnah of the Prophet and resisting Christian evangelism in Algeria. The newspaper also included statements and messages from the association about its activities and initiatives, and recorded the nation’s reactions to important administrative decisions such as disabling “Al-Sunna” newspaper.
descriptions.1669: Al-Ustad Magazine is a humorous, scientific newspaper published every week. It deals with various topics, including science, literature, morals, and customs, with a focus on scientific and spiritual benefits without delving into sensitive political issues. The magazine combines intellectual sophistication with an entertaining nature, as it presents scientific articles and intellectual research along with humorous paragraphs and anecdotes, relying in its content on the articles and research of its authors and their friends among scholars and thinkers.
descriptions.1670: The Journal of Islamic Research is a periodical magazine issued by the General Presidency of the Departments of Scientific Research, Fatwa, Call and Guidance. It includes scientific and research articles in the fields of Islamic law, call and fatwa. It covers religious topics and religious people, and contains research on the arbitration of Islamic law and its impact on the life of the individual and society, in addition to discussing the concepts of religion and religiosity. The magazine is published every three months and brings together articles from different authors on important Islamic issues.
descriptions.1671: Al-Bayan Magazine is an international Islamic magazine issued by the Islamic Forum. It aims to spread Sharia knowledge, consolidate the approach of the Sunnis and the community, and unify the efforts of Muslims away from fanaticism and partisanship. The magazine covers various topics related to jurisprudence, belief, history, and literature. It uses an elite group of scholars and researchers to provide solid scientific content, and works to publish it through modern technical means. The first issue was published in 1406 AH, and it went through developmental stages in style, drafting, and artistic direction.
descriptions.1672: Abdullah Al-Nadim’s magazine “Al-Tankit wa Al-Nadeem” is a collection of humorous and sarcastic articles and studies aimed at social and political reform. The magazine covers topics ranging from history and literature to politics and society, relying on sharp criticism and clever satire to shed light on contemporary issues in Egypt and the Arab world. The magazine combines literature and social analysis, using literary and narrative methods to convey political and reform messages.
descriptions.1673: Al-Manar magazine, written by Muhammad Rashid Reda, constitutes one of the most important Islamic magazines in the world, as it was distinguished by its reformist and awareness-raising role in spreading contemporary Islamic thought. The magazine dealt with various topics related to beliefs, morals, sciences and arts, aiming to develop and modernize Islamic societies while preserving their religious and cultural identity. It continued to be issued for forty-three years, greatly influenced Islamic thought and public opinion, and left a deep mark on the history of Arab and Islamic journalism.
descriptions.1674: Dialogue Etiquette and Rules of Disagreement by Omar bin Abdullah Kamel is a reference that specializes in directing Muslims to paths of sound dialogue and defining the controls for disagreement within the framework of the call and the conditions of Muslims. It includes chapters that address the psychological, scientific, and verbal etiquette of dialogue, with a focus on sincerity, fairness, humility, good listening, and respect, in addition to the rules of disagreement between the reprehensible and the praiseworthy. The book aims to establish a scientific and ethical methodology for debate that enhances mutual understanding and prevents deviation into extremism or fanaticism, based on what is stated in the Sharia texts.
descriptions.1675: The book “The Impact of Sharia Science in Confronting Violence and Aggression” by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Fawzan bin Saleh Al-Fawzan deals with the role of Islamic law in addressing the phenomenon of violence and aggression by focusing on the preventive, educational and punitive aspects that Islam presents to ensure security and achieve happiness and stability for societies. It includes chapters that analyze the prohibition of attacking oneself and others and demonstrate the necessity of denying evil, and concludes with a conclusion that explains the conclusions drawn.
descriptions.1676: I Want to Talk to the Brotherhood” is a preaching book that sheds light on the characteristics of the Muslim Brotherhood’s call and its spiritual and practical stages, based on the biography of the prophets as role models in calling to God. The author focuses on perseverance and patience in calling, and urges detachment and devoting one's heart, time, and effort to it. It also shows the importance of determination in religion apart from permission, with an indication of the effect this has on their morals and worship.
descriptions.1677: The book Youth Crises: Causes and Solutions by Sheikh Muhammad Ahmed Kanaan deals with youth problems from an Islamic perspective, based on the concepts of faith and good deeds. It includes chapters dealing with the stages of human life, human nature from the animal and mental aspects, and individual and emergency responsibility, in addition to sections dealing with heavenly and acquired emergencies. It aims to clarify the causes of crises and provide solutions based on religious teachings.
descriptions.1678: This is a book that studies the advocacy and educational methods derived from Surat Ibrahim, as it relies on induction and contemplation of its verses. It begins with a general definition of the surah and its thematic unity, then addresses the features of its da’wah approach by stating its message, the characteristics of the messengers, the obstacles to da’wah and its methods, and concludes with the approach to guidance and education learned from the surah.
descriptions.1679: The book presents a legal study on the concept of terrorism directed at those who are safe, and the position of Islamic law on it. It defines terrorism and prohibits it in Islam, and reviews the definition of security, its pillars, and its formulas, based on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It also explains the duties that a Muslim has towards those who trust him, such as justice, non-transgression, and benevolence, and reviews what is required of those who trust him in Muslim countries, concluding with his recommendations.
descriptions.1680: The book “The Family” sheds light on the Islamic view of the family system and the status of marriage, reviewing the legislation that governs marital relations and determines the mutual rights between husband and wife and those shared for children. The author explains the original differences between men and women according to Sharia texts, emphasizing the balance between duties and rights within the Islamic family.
descriptions.1681: A book that collects the answers of a number of sheikhs and scholars to questions and inquiries received from Muslims as a result of the events and trials they are experiencing, with the aim of directing feelings and energies towards constructive work. The book is divided into two main axes, the first of which deals with the state of youth between enthusiasm and apathy in terms of causes, effects and treatment, and the second of which focuses on the concept of the nation between the years of trial and work. The content addresses topics such as vitality and strength, will and challenge, work and production, and also addresses ills such as apathy, frustration and weakness in education, concluding with instructions on how to support Islam and carry out the missionary duty.
descriptions.1682: This book deals with the comprehensive strategy for supporting the Messenger ﷺ by studying the experiences of Islamic scholars in confronting the challenges that the Islamic nation faced in the era of the Crusades. The author focuses on how to deal with the intellectual, cultural, and religious issues raised by the Christians, and includes a discussion of the Christians’ beliefs and rituals, as well as responding to the suspicions they raised about Islam. The book also addresses the role of leaders and scholars in calling non-Muslims to Islam and adopting a comprehensive strategy to support the Messenger ﷺ.
descriptions.1683: The book deals with Islam as a moderate religion that encourages virtues and eternal values, showing how it calls for goodness, justice, benevolence, and kindness. The author focuses on explaining the meaning of moderation in Islam and explaining its dimensions through Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths, reviewing the Islamic values ​​called for by Islamic law, such as honesty, trustworthiness, mercy, and responsible freedom. The book aims to present a comprehensive picture of Islam as a religion that calls for moderation and moderation in behavior and morals, with an emphasis on the importance of applying Islamic values ​​in the daily lives of Muslims.
descriptions.1684: The book “Difference in Islamic Action, Causes and Effects,” by Sheikh Nasser bin Suleiman Al-Omar, falls within the classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and deals with the phenomenon of disagreement and division in the Islamic nation. The book begins with fundamental introductions to the concept of difference and an explanation of its different types and categories. Then it moves on to detailing the reasons that lead to reprehensible division, such as ignorance of religion, oppression, and fanaticism, and concludes by explaining the negative effects resulting from that, such as weakness, impotence, and the destruction of the nation.
descriptions.1685: The book “Moderation in Dawah” by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen presents the concept of balance between extremism and negligence in the call to Islam, based on the fact that calling to God is one of the pillars of good deeds. The author explains that the call intersects between two parties; One is the side of excess and the other is the side of negligence, and it is based on the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions as a standard for the middle. The book aims to guide Muslims to a moderate approach that combines severity and leniency in advocacy, with a focus on knowing God, His attributes, His law, and the reward of the obedient.
descriptions.1686: The book “Introducing Islam,” written by a group of authors, is concerned with providing a comprehensive explanation of the Holy Qur’an in terms of its definition, names, preserving it from distortion, the etiquette of its recitation, its virtue and status, in addition to reviewing the stages of its revelation and its division into Meccan and Medinan and the characteristics of each of them. It also deals with its collection and arrangement in the Qur’an. The book falls within the category of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and is based on the content of the Qatar Center for Introducing Islam project, targeting the reader interested in understanding the Qur’an and its teachings. The book includes chapters that explain the merits of reciting the Qur’an, the purposes of the revelation, and the stages of its collection, with an indication of the number of surahs and verses and their sections.
descriptions.1687: The book “Social Solidarity” presents the concept of solidarity in Islam as a collective obligation to preserve public and private interests and prevent damages, while clarifying that this duty extends to all members of society, from the individual to the family and the group. The book deals with the scope of solidarity and its various fields, including sponsoring the elderly, the young, and the poor, and caring for the rights of the neighbor and the guest, and reviews the means of Islam to achieve this on the individual and collective levels. The text links these principles with the teachings of the Qur’an and Sunnah, stressing that solidarity is not limited to material benefit but rather includes all the spiritual and intellectual needs of the nation.
descriptions.1688: The book presents a historical study of fanaticism, extremism, terrorism, and violence from an Islamic perspective. The author defines the meanings of the terms associated with them, reviews their roots in other religions, and then focuses on their origin and development in Islamic thought, with reference to the Kharijites, the Mu’tazilites, and others. It also discusses the effect of exaggeration in the chapter on names and rulings and suggests inductive responses based on the approach of the middle Sunnah.
descriptions.1689: The book “The Generation Promised Victory and Empowerment” by Magdy Al-Hilali presents the idea of ​​a generation that fulfills God’s promise of expansion and empowerment by fulfilling specific Islamic conditions and qualities. The author relies on Qur’anic texts and examples from the Companions to demonstrate the importance of sincerity, heartfelt love for God, intense fear of Him, humility, asceticism in this world, and jihad. It aims to guide the reader on how to embody these qualities in contemporary reality and guide the nation towards victory and empowerment.
descriptions.1690: The book “The Hijab is God’s Law in Islam, Judaism, and Christianity” by Sami Amiri deals with the hijab as a religious and social issue from an Islamic, Jewish, and Christian perspective, based on the texts of Sharia, jurisprudence, and the history of dress in the three religions. In his chapters, the author explains the definition of the hijab in Islam, the obligation to cover the head, and responds to contemporary suspicions. Then he moves on to study the origins of the hijab in Judaism from the Old Testament to Jewish jurisprudence, and finally reviews the positions of Christianity from the New Testament to the traditions of the churches. The work concludes with a concluding speech that summarizes the comparative views and emphasizes the importance of the hijab as a spiritual and cultural value.
descriptions.1691: The book “Al-Hikma” by Sheikh Nasser bin Sulaiman Al-Omar deals with the topic of wisdom from an Islamic perspective, examining its linguistic and honorable meanings, its divisions, and examples from the Qur’an and Sunnah, while addressing the reasons for its absence and contraindications. The author aims to direct the efforts of preachers and scholars towards enhancing wisdom in the Islamic nation, and to show the correct path to sustaining the religious and scientific renaissance that the nation has recently witnessed.
descriptions.1692: The book “Dialogue with People of Religions: Its Legitimacy, Conditions, and Etiquette” by Dr. Ahmed bin Saif al-Din Turkestani deals with the topic of dialogue between Muslims and people of other religions. The author focuses on the legitimacy of this dialogue in Islam, its conditions and etiquette, reviewing the opinions of religious scholars in this field. It also sheds light on the importance of dialogue in our current era and the opportunities it provides for understanding and peaceful coexistence between different cultures, while emphasizing the necessity of respecting freedom of opinion and thought away from coercion and coercion.
descriptions.1693: A book that deals with one of the methods of calling to God Almighty, which is the individual call directed to individuals, and shows its importance in raising generations in a sound upbringing with follow-up. The author explains the virtue of calling to God, distinguishes between collective and individual calling, mentions the benefits and cases of individual calling, then details its practical stages, starting with establishing an acquaintance with the called person and ending with his enthusiasm for seeking knowledge. The author also devotes a section to the reasons that help the success of this call, such as sincerity, knowledge, planning, progression, and a good example.
