descriptions.1694: The book deals with the concept of religion in Islamic terminology, explaining its four pillars as stated in the Qur’an, and reviews the rational evidence that proves the authenticity of the innate religiosity in humans and its generality to all humans. It also links religion and science through approaches to knowledge based on divine texts, common sense, and reason, and presents Islamic visions about common sense and the approach to belief. This work falls within the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims.
descriptions.1695: The book “The Race to the Minds” by the writer Abdullah Qadri Al-Ahdal is concerned with calling Muslims to adhere to the truth and convincing the minds of it, based on legal inferences about God’s creation of the universe with truth and its distinction between the people of truth and the people of falsehood. Through its chapters, the author addresses topics such as the status of reason with God, the goals of the people of truth in conveying messages and establishing proof, and establishing loyalty to God and His Messenger, with reference to examples of the behavior of civilized people. The book aims to motivate the reader to believe in the unity of God, instill faith in the unseen, and apply God’s law in people’s lives.
descriptions.1696: The book “Science Calls for Faith” provides the average reader with a variety of scientific content covering the fields of astronomy, geology, chemistry, biology, and others, presenting new scientific information in a simple and attractive way that brings it closer to the mind of the average reader. The author aims to show the relationship between science and faith by presenting amazing scientific facts that call for contemplation about the creation of the universe.
descriptions.1697: The book “Scholars are Preachers” by the writer Nasser Al-Aql, a book in the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, deals with the definition of scholars and their role as callers to God based on legal texts, and reviews the problems of the separation between knowledge and preaching and its effects on Islamic behavior and concepts. He explains the reasons for the spread of this separation through an analysis of social phenomena and group unions, then presents solutions that call for the attention of scholars and students of knowledge, abolishing illegitimate loyalties, and activating direct advice as a useful means.
descriptions.1698: Extremism: Causes and Treatment by the writer Nasser Al-Aql is a scientific work that sheds light on the roots of extremism in religion from a historical and scientific perspective, and reviews the most important factors that led to its emergence within Saudi society and on the general level at all times and places. The book deals with the manifestations of fanaticism in the modern era and suggests ways to treat and prevent it, based on extensive analyzes of religious and social phenomena. This book falls within the classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and relies on religious and historical backgrounds to explain extremist phenomena and provide practical proposals to address them.
descriptions.1699: This book, by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al-Rajhi, deals with the subject of calling to God, enjoining good and forbidding evil, and reviews the origins of this duty and its importance in Islam. The author focuses on explaining the meanings of good and evil linguistically and legally, and points to the legal evidence that urges this duty and threatens those who neglect it. The book also addresses the conditions for the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil, and discusses the effects of violating this duty on the individual and society.
descriptions.1700: The book “Women Before and After Islam” sheds light on the status of women before the emergence of religion, then shows how Islam established the principle of equality between men and women in origin and destiny, eligibility for legal discourse, and rights within the family and the judiciary. The text addresses topics such as equality in upbringing, destiny, intellectual and religious rights, and is based on Qur’anic verses to illustrate the concept of divine justice. This work falls within the classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and aims to clarify the social and legal transformation that Islam has brought about in women’s lives.
descriptions.1701: Al-Mustabat fi Reasons for the Success of the Call of Imam Muhammad is the work of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yusuf al-Rahma. It sheds light on the factors that made the call of Imam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab continue and spread. In his chapters, the author presents a group of reasons, ranging from monotheism and adherence to the Sunnah to interest in Sharia knowledge and commitment to enjoining good and forbidding evil, while clarifying the role of the group and the state in supporting the call. The book falls within the classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and aims to show the advantages of the Najdi Salafi call and prove its success in its objectives.
descriptions.1702: This book deals with topics related to the teaching profession and teacher ethics, drawing its origins from the biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his words and actions in the field of teaching and upbringing. The author, Fouad Al-Shalhoub, focuses on the ideal qualities and duties of a teacher, relying on authentic hadiths of the Prophet and the teachings of the Holy Qur’an. The book also addresses effective teaching methods and techniques, reviewing how to apply them in daily educational practice.
descriptions.1703: The book deals with the concept of moderation and its reality in light of the Holy Qur’an, indicating that this approach needs clarification and detail because it is not properly understood by many. The author aims to clarify the meaning of moderation by definition, rooting, specification and application, citing the verse of Al-Baqarah: “And thus We made you a moderate nation.” The book also addresses the errors in understanding moderation by different groups, and reviews the concept of fanaticism and extremism versus moderation, relying on Qur’anic and prophetic interpretation.
descriptions.1704: The book “Easiness and Easement in Islam” by Sheikh Faleh bin Muhammad Al-Sagheer deals with the concept of ease and grace in Islamic law, based on the texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah, and presents the foundations of the approach of ease from permission to prohibition of extremism. It highlights the applications of ease in various areas of religion, from belief and worship to transactions and punishments, and extracts legal rules based on texts. It also discusses the effects of moving away from the facilitation approach and concludes with a conclusion of the research. He is considered a reference in the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims.
descriptions.1705: The book “Cooperation of Preachers and its Impact on Society” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen deals with the importance of cooperation between preachers and its impact on Islamic society, based on the religious duty it requires in Sharia. The author explains the characteristics and skills of the preacher, such as insight and patience, and reviews the etiquette of preachers and their questions related to the message. The book is classified within the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and provides practical guidance for activating cooperation within the framework of calling to God.
descriptions.1706: The book “Globalization Culture as an Extremist Discourse” by Abdullah Al-Ashi addresses the phenomenon of globalization from a critical perspective that compares it to post-modernist discourse, highlighting the dismantling of values ​​and systems and the transformation of identity in light of this discourse. The author combines ideological, cultural, and violent analyzes of globalization, and reviews its effects on Arab and Islamic societies, while proposing ways of confrontation from both theoretical and practical perspectives. The book is classified within the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, which highlights its tendency to link global issues with Islamic reality.
descriptions.1707: The book “The Efforts of the Imams of the Salafist Call in Najd to Confront” by researcher Saleh bin Abdullah Al-Furaih highlights how to confront violence and terrorism by applying the jurisprudence of denying evil among Salafist preachers in Najd. In his chapters, the author discusses the principles before and after denial, with an analysis of the perpetrator’s reasons, methods of denial, and its impact on those in charge. The work aims to show the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil as a means of advocacy in light of contemporary challenges.
descriptions.1708: This book deals with the topic of public speaking and the importance of calling to God, focusing on the qualities and skills of a successful orator. In this work, the author Amir bin Muhammad Al-Madri discusses the fifty commandments that a preacher must follow in order to be influential to his audience, indicating the importance of the sermon as an effective tool for advocacy and guidance. The book focuses on multiple aspects of the speaker's personality, culture, and skills, while providing practical advice for developing public speaking skills and achieving the desired effect.
descriptions.1709: The book “Guide to Da’wah Opportunities and Means” by Khalid bin Muhammad Al-Dubaikhi is a practical reference that explains da’wah opportunities in various places such as mosques, cemeteries, hospitals, schools, prisons, and modern means. It also reviews a variety of da’wah means, from gifts to guidance materials. It aims to enable preachers to exploit diverse circumstances and environments to achieve the goals of calling to God.
descriptions.1710: The Guide to Dawa Methods of the Cooperative Office for Call and Guidance in Jeddah is a practical reference that explains a set of advocacy activities and materials proposed for application in various locations such as hospitals, cemeteries, camps, Hajj season, and residential environments. The book includes a description of methods such as distributing multilingual guidebooks, placing illuminated signboards, preparing a booklet on forensic procedures in cases of death, organizing telephone lectures, and issuing messages via mobile phone and e-mail, in addition to field tools such as mobile prayer halls and delegations in neighborhoods and villages. The guide aims to direct advocacy efforts and enhance religious and social awareness by investing in waiting times and providing comprehensive information to beneficiaries. The book is classified under the category of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims.
descriptions.1711: The book “A Sharia View in Debate and Dialogue with the People of the Book” by Sheikh Sharif Muhammad bin Hussein Al-Samadani is concerned with clarifying the provisions of the call to Islam through discussion with the People of the Book, based on the texts of the Qur’an and the Sunnah and based on Sharia evidence that shows the legitimacy of debate and controversy. The author divides his topic into chapters that address the definition of dialogue and debate, the types of debaters from among the People of the Book, the conditions for dialogue such as knowledge, justice, and knowledge of what is contradicted by their opponent, in addition to a review of the trends calling for rapprochement and modernism. The book aims to guide preachers to a legal approach that contributes to jihad with the tongue for the truth, according to its classification in the field of preaching and the conditions of Muslims.
descriptions.1712: An urgent message to preachers addresses the topic of the call to God and the conditions that Muslims are going through in the present era. The author focuses on the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil, and discusses the challenges of the Islamic nation in confronting intellectual alienation and the danger that threatens it from within and without. It also calls for advising rulers and warning them against deviation, and reviews ways to achieve unity and solidarity among Muslims to restore their glory and power.
descriptions.1713: The "Muslims in the World" book series aims to present general facts about the conditions of Muslims in various countries of the world, whether in Islamic countries or in countries where Muslim minorities or communities live. The series is distinguished by dedicating a book to each country, and the small size of the book, which makes it easy to benefit from, with a focus on providing accurate and documented information that contributes to strengthening cooperation and brotherhood among Muslims in various parts of the world.
descriptions.1714: The book “The Preachers’ Society Series” by Dr. Abdul Rahman Al-Harfi addresses the topic of calling to God and its various mechanisms, focusing on the role of the teacher in this field. The book provides an analysis of the necessity of dawah from multiple legal perspectives, and then moves on to discuss self-dawah through good example and good scientific material. The book also presents practical advocacy by providing practical advice to teachers on how to deal with their students and motivate them to believe and do good deeds, while addressing the challenges and obstacles of advocacy and how to overcome them.
descriptions.1715: The book deals with Islam’s tolerance in dealing with non-Muslims through three main axes: trade and justice, warding off borders, and cases of necessity. The author focuses on clarifying that Islam is a religion that calls for tolerance and gentleness with others, refuting the misconceptions that promote an image of the Islamic religion as a violent religion. The book cites hadiths and Quranic verses to support its position on the importance of forgiveness and pardon in dealing with non-Muslims, stressing that forgiveness is an essential part of the teachings of Islam.
descriptions.1716: The book “Islam’s Tolerance in Treating Non-Muslims” by Dr. Abdullah bin Ibrahim Al-Luhaidan deals with the topic of tolerance and ease in dealing with people of other religions from an Islamic perspective. The book focuses on explaining the wisdom of Islam in its dealings with non-Muslims and its tolerance in this field, reviewing the sayings and opinions of scholars on this matter throughout the ages. The book also addresses the legal controls that were established to regulate relations between Muslims and other human beings, showing how Islamic legislation has received the attention of jurisprudence scholars throughout history to discuss this important issue.
descriptions.1717: The book “Doubts of the Skeptics” is a collective work that falls within the category of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims. It aims to respond to the doubts raised by skeptics about the sources of the Qur’an and the teachings of Islam, based on a discussion of topics such as the compilation of the Qur’an, the multiplicity of the Qur’an and readings, and a group of linguistic and legal issues that are used to distort the correct understanding of the texts. The content includes chapters that separate various types of disputed speech and point out grammatical and rhetorical errors exploited by critics. The book presents scientific and religious arguments to demonstrate the authenticity of the Qur’an and promote a sound understanding of the teachings of Islam.
descriptions.1718: The book “Doubts About the Qur’an” by Dr. Muhammad Amara addresses ten doubts raised by opponents of Islam about the Holy Qur’an, based on a preaching approach that strengthens the Muslim’s faith and removes false doubts. The work is divided into introductory and concluding chapters, where each suspicion is discussed separately in chapters called the first to the tenth suspicion, citing sources and references. The author aims to stimulate Muslim mental thinking and confront criticism through intellectual dialogue based on Qur’anic texts and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.1719: The book “Tall al-Rabwa, Raising the Preaching Professor and His Student” by the writer Abdullah Qadri al-Ahdal, is concerned with guiding the preaching teacher towards the foundations of effective Islamic education, as it links strengthening the connection with God, the principles of sincerity, the practice of worship, and adherence to Sharia, and the methods of teaching and dealing with students. It includes chapters detailing the factors that strengthen the relationship between the professor and his students, the steps of the lesson, and the skills of organizing trips, with a focus on developing individual responsibility and seriousness in seeking knowledge. It is classified within the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and provides comprehensive guidance for forming good behaviors and establishing Islamic values ​​in an educational environment.
descriptions.1720: The book “The Justice of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, in the light of the Qur’an” by the writer Imad Al-Sayyid Muhammad Ismail Al-Sherbini presents a scientific approach that responds to the suspicions of criticism directed at the Companions by reviewing the Qur’anic evidence, the Sunnah, and the consensus of scholars. The work includes chapters that define the Companions and justice linguistically and terminologically, review evidence of their justice, and discuss suspicions based on Qur’anic texts and Sunnah. The author aims to highlight the status of the Companions as a basis for building the nation and to confirm that criticizing them threatens the foundations of Sharia. The book is classified among the works on advocacy and the conditions of Muslims.
descriptions.1721: This book addresses the response to the enemies of the Prophetic Sunnah and the advocates of Westernization through several important issues, including clarifying the mission of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in his message, refuting the suspicions of the enemies of the Sunnah about the nature of his explanatory mission, the necessity of obeying him in both the Qur’an and the Sunnah, and repelling suspicions about the punishments for adultery and apostasy mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah. The author aims to clarify the truth of the Prophet’s call and explain the importance of the Prophet’s Sunnah in Islam.
descriptions.1722: The book “Factors of Victory and Empowerment in the Calls of Messengers” by Ahmed bin Hamdan Al-Shehri is concerned with analyzing the connotations of empowerment in the language and the Qur’an, and reviews the promise of empowerment for messengers and believers and its advantages, while clarifying the levels of victory and authority from safety to caliphate. The author focuses on deducing the factors of victory from the Qur’anic texts, and presents a study on the role of patience and community in achieving empowerment, based on examples of the prophets’ calls and positions. The book is classified within the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and is considered a systematic Qur’anic study that highlights the factors that provide victory and empowerment in the path of messengers.
descriptions.1723: The book addresses the issue of the return of glory to the Islamic nation in the current era, based on Qur’anic and Prophetic glad tidings and asking whether these glad tidings are an illusion or a realistic reality. The author combines advocacy and historical analysis, reviewing topics such as the caliphate on the path of prophecy, victory over the Jews, and the reasons for punishment, and proposes faith-based solutions that include prayer and prohibitions. It aims to guide the reader to a deeper understanding of current circumstances and the possibility of realizing the good news in our time.
descriptions.1724: This book deals with the issue of denial by hand from a jurisprudential perspective and includes a study of the legal evidence for the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil, while clarifying the conditions and aspects of legal denial. The author focuses on discussing the two main opinions about the necessity of the Sultan’s permission to deny by hand, and also reviews the legal degrees of denial and its rulings. The book is part of an excerpt from a larger study on the rulings on those who commit major sins, and aims to clarify the importance of denial in preserving the rulings of religion and warding off temptations.
descriptions.1725: The book Jurisprudence of Disagreement and its Impact on Eliminating Terrorism by Dr. Youssef Al-Shubaili deals with the subject of Jurisprudence of Disagreement and its importance in avoiding intellectual deviation and extremism, reviewing the rules of disagreement deduced from the texts of the slide and the sayings of scholars, and aims to clarify how to deal with jurisprudential differences with wisdom and moderation, with a focus on how to confront the phenomenon of terrorism through a correct understanding of Islamic jurisprudence and its etiquette.
descriptions.1726: The book deals with the jurisprudence of Islamic advocacy in the West and the necessity of renewing it on the basis of wisdom and moderation, relying on the model of advocacy in Andalusia as a historical experience. The author focuses on the importance of renewing religious discourse in the West in line with the moderation of Islam and its wise approach, in contrast to the practices of terrorism that claim to belong to Islam. The book aims to provide a practical vision on how to practice Islamic preaching in the West in a way that contributes to spreading peace and understanding between cultures, away from violence and extremism.
descriptions.1727: This book deals with the jurisprudence of changing evil from a legal and practical perspective, explaining the necessity of change, its importance, and its conditions, circumstances, and levels. The author focuses on explaining the truth about change and its means, while explaining the etiquette of those who change evil and how to deal with it. The book aims to clarify the role of the Muslim in spreading goodness and fighting evil in accordance with Sharia controls, considering this to be at the core of charity that must characterize the Islamic nation.
descriptions.1728: The book “On the Terms of Terrorism and its Rule: A Critical Reading of the Concept” by the writer Qutb Mustafa Sano presents a critical legal study of the concept of terrorism and its provisions according to Islamic jurisprudence. The author discusses the definition of terrorism and its forms, then analyzes the issue of security and purpose in light of Sharia texts, and classifies the different types of terrorism according to the legitimacy of the purpose and the safety of the home. The work concludes by stating the legality of terrorism to the ruler and confirming its categorical prohibition, based on the methods and principles of jurisprudence.
descriptions.1729: The book “The Story of Humanity” by Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad is a preaching book that presents the path of creation and humanity from an Islamic perspective, and reviews the biography of the Prophet Muhammad and the principles of religion from faith and worship to good morals. It links true happiness with faith in God, presents the pillars of Islam and the components of the faith, and compares the call of the prophets and the concept of happiness. It aims to introduce non-Muslims to Islam and convince them of its importance as a path to spiritual tranquility and righteous living.
descriptions.1730: A scientific book that addresses the subject of enjoining good and forbidding evil from a legal and systematic perspective, as it presents seven basic rules that show the originality of Sharia law, the role of knowledge and insight, and the conditions and procedures for denying evil in the stages of hand, tongue, and heart. The research combines Qur’anic evidence and the Sunnah of the Prophet with a clear methodology that includes a summary, introduction, and research plan. It is concerned with prioritizing the most important over the important and considering the benefits and harms in applying these rules. The book is classified under the category of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and targets researchers and those interested in understanding the mechanisms of calling to goodness and applying them in reality.
descriptions.1731: The book “The Writings of the Enemies of Islam and Their Discussion” by Imad El-Sherbini is a work of advocacy concerned with analyzing and discussing what opponents of religion write in terms of linguistic and terminological concepts related to the Sunnah and Hadith, and reviews the definitions of these terms and their sources. The book also deals with the study of the enemies of the Sunnah, the people of whims and heresies, with a special focus on the Kharijites and their positions on the purified Sunnah. This research is considered a reference in the field of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, as it combines scientific methodology with introduction to multiple branches of Islamic jurisprudence and history.
descriptions.1732: This book deals with the topic of advocacy discourse and its impact on the Islamic nation, focusing on the problems that the call suffers from in the present era. The author shows the shortcomings of the current preaching discourse, especially when discussing the nation's tragedies and confusions, and calls for the need to focus on reminding Muslims of the return of Muslims to God and achieving sincere repentance. It also calls for clarifying effective and practical solutions to the nation's problems instead of focusing on the problems themselves or lamenting the current situation. The book targets preachers and reformers to guide them towards a more effective and influential advocacy discourse in directing the nation towards the right path.
descriptions.1733: This book, “How to Win People,” by Mazen Al-Fraih, deals with the topic of winning people’s hearts and rooting them for the truth and the Islamic call through prophetic means. The author focuses on ways to enhance positive relationships with others through good behavior and virtuous morals, indicating the importance of this aspect in the success of preachers and their influence on the public. The book contains practical means to improve dealing with people and achieve intellectual and spiritual rapprochement, drawing its ideas from the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.1734: The book, “What’s Next for True Support for Palestine,” deals with the issue of Palestine and the situation of the Islamic nation from a preaching and intellectual perspective. Author Majdi Al-Hilali focuses on analyzing the root causes of the suffering of Muslims in Palestine and the world, and calls for a comprehensive vision to solve the problem that is not limited to limited emotional and political reactions. He calls for the necessity of changing the nation's internal conditions first through jihad, education, and reform, to enable it to confront external challenges effectively and sustainably.
descriptions.1735: This book deals with the topic of teachers, their responsibilities and roles in society, emphasizing the importance and virtue of science and education in Islam. It focuses on guidance and sayings to enhance teachers' morals and behavior with their colleagues and students, while noting the religious and social importance of the teaching profession. The book aims to motivate teachers to perform their duties honestly and sincerely, with an emphasis on piety and good morals in the practice of their profession.
descriptions.1736: The book “From the Ethics of the Preacher” by Dr. Salman Al-Awda deals with the topic of ethics in the context of Islamic advocacy, indicating the importance of the moral virtues of the preacher and their role in his success. The book focuses on qualities such as honesty, patience, humility, justice, and lively emotion, considering them essential for a preacher to adhere to the teachings of Islam and spread them effectively. The book also deals with justice in dealing with Sharia texts, reality, and disputes, relying on the purposes and spirit of Sharia law in directing advocacy behavior.
descriptions.1737: The book “Among the Means of Da’wah” by Dr. Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Thuwaini Topics related to methods and tools of calling to Islam. The book focuses on the importance of using appropriate and legitimate means to spread advocacy, reviewing multiple types of advocacy methods such as writing, radio, the Internet, and public speaking. He also points out the importance of going to the places of those invited and offering them assistance to build confidence and enhance the effectiveness of the call. The book is the product of a lecture on preparing preachers, and aims to provide the reader with comprehensive knowledge about best practices in the field of Islamic preaching.
descriptions.1738: The Encyclopedia of Jews, Judaism, and Zionism is a huge encyclopedic work prepared and presented by Dr. Abdul Wahab Al-Mesiri in eight large volumes. Abdul Wahab Al-Mesiri began his journey of writing this encyclopedia in the mid-seventies of the last century, and continued to do so until the end of the nineties, using volunteers and researchers to collect the various materials.
descriptions.1739: The book “This is How Let Us Call to Islam” by Muhammad Ramadan Al-Bouti deals with the subject of the call to Islam and its mechanisms, explaining the conditions for the preacher and the importance of establishing the correct doctrine among Muslims first before turning to others. The book also addresses problems facing preachers in their fields, including the issue of takfir and the Muslim’s policy with his family, reviewing the starting points of the call and its impact on society. The book aims to provide a clear methodology for the preacher to convey the message of Islam in a correct and effective manner, taking into account the intellectual and political challenges that Islam faces in the modern era.
descriptions.1740: The book “The Moderation of Islam and its Call to Dialogue” by Muhammad Abd al-Rab Nawab al-Din deals with the topics of terrorism, extremism, and violence from an Islamic perspective, reviewing the definitions of these concepts and explaining their prohibition in Islam. The book also focuses on the moderation of Islam in doctrine, law, morals, and advocacy, showing how Islam calls for dialogue as an effective means of confronting extremism and suspicions, and emphasizing the importance of dialogue in dispelling misunderstandings of religion and spreading moderation and tolerance.
descriptions.1741: The book deals with the moderation of Islam, its tolerance, and its call for dialogue between nations and cultures, reviewing the principles of the Islamic religion of moderation, tolerance, and peaceful coexistence. The author focuses on the importance of spreading ideal Islamic values ​​in humanitarian cooperation and dealing with non-Muslims on the basis of human brotherhood, while emphasizing the rejection of terrorism and extremism in any form. The book aims to clarify the true image of Islam and its lofty principles in the face of the biased accusations directed against it, and to explain its true position on global issues and international conflicts.
descriptions.1742: The book “The Moderation and Tolerance of Islam” by Dr. Wahba Al-Zuhaili deals with the topic of moderation and tolerance in Islam from a jurisprudential and rational perspective. The author focuses on explaining the concept of moderation and tolerance in Islamic law and the mechanisms for applying it in various aspects of life, from worship to transactions and morals. The book also addresses Islam's call for constructive dialogue and an explanation of the aspects of ease and tolerance in the principles of Sharia, citing Qur’anic and prophetic texts to confirm these principles. The book aims to correct misconceptions about Islam and explain its sublime truth away from false interpretations and extremism.
descriptions.1743: The book “The Moderation of Islam” by Saleh Habibullah Al-Sini deals with the concept of moderation in Islam and its implications, reviewing how this moderation calls for staying away from excess and negligence. The book focuses on the nature of moderation as a social approach and examines the manifestations of religious extremism in comparison. In his treatment of the topic of moderation, Al-Sinni relies on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths, explaining their meanings and applications in the daily and social life of Muslims.
descriptions.1744: The book “A Quiet Pause with Those Who Attack the Dawa Groups” by Dr. Abu Abdullah Al-Masry deals with the topic of criticism and accusations directed at Islamic Dawa groups, especially the Muslim Brotherhood and the Salafist Dawa. The author focuses on responding to the accusations of some muftis and scholars against advocacy groups, and refers to fatwas from respected scholars confirming the efforts of these groups to spread Islamic advocacy. The book aims to clarify the facts and point out the legal violations that may exist while advising them with wisdom and kindness. It comes in the context of protecting the Islamic nation from the negative effects of intellectual invasion and military operations targeting Muslims.
descriptions.1745: This book deals with the life of the great companion Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) and his role in spreading the Sunnah of the Prophet, and reviews his status among hadith scholars and the importance of his narrations. The author focuses on showing Abu Hurairah's justice and his preservation of hadith, while responding to those who criticized him or questioned his narration. The book falls within the scope of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and aims to defend the Companions and respond to those who doubt them, while highlighting their role in spreading Islam and preserving its rulings.
descriptions.1746: This book deals with the topic of unity and solidarity in the Islamic nation from the perspective of the Islamic faith. The author focuses on analyzing the reality of the Islamic nation and identifying the reasons that led to its division, then presents the foundations for achieving unity through doctrine, purpose, leadership, and method. It also suggests practical means to achieve these foundations, including education, media, and the independent economy. The book aims to present a comprehensive vision for solving the problem of dispersion in the Islamic world and achieving solidarity among Muslims.
descriptions.1747: This book deals with the role of scholars in achieving the mission of the mosque and its role in Islamic society. The author focuses on the importance of scholars and their characteristics, and how they can activate the role of the mosque in education, advocacy and guidance. The book includes a discussion of the different roles of scholars within the mosque such as imamate, preaching, fatwa, and lessons, while providing general suggestions on how to enhance the role of scholars in achieving the mission of the mosque.
descriptions.1748: This book deals with the topic of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, focusing on the means and methods of deception and intellectual invasion that Islam and Muslims face. The author, Abd al-Rahman Habankah al-Maidani, begins with a translation of his life and the life of his father, then moves on to an analysis of the intellectual invasion and its mechanisms, defining the three wings of deception and their means, and reviewing the main tasks of the enemies of Islam and ways to confront them. The book aims to understand opponents' strategies and enhance Islamic awareness of their methods of indirect influence.
descriptions.1749: This book deals with the attacks and criticisms that the Sunnah of the Prophet was subjected to by Orientalists and Christians, and then by some Muslims in the modern era. The author focuses on a massive, arbitrary project by an unnamed person aimed at isolating Sunnis from the practical reality of Muslim life and removing the Prophet Muhammad from any practical role in the message. The book also addresses attempts to cast doubt on hadith scholars and imams of jurisprudence and reveals the falsity of the suspicions raised against them.
descriptions.1750: This is a book that studies the methods of calling to God as mentioned in the Holy Qur’an. The author divides them into doctrinal, religious, and legislative methods, with a focus on the Qur’an’s approach to determining belief and inferring it. The book deals with the characteristics of these methods in terms of clarity, wisdom, and good advice, and reviews various models of them, such as informative, constructive, dialogue, and story methods.
descriptions.1751: A book that studies and analyzes the methods of intellectual invasion to which the Islamic world is being exposed by two main forces: the Western trend and the Marxist trend. In the introductory chapter, the author reviews the reality of the Islamic nation and the backwardness and division it suffers from. Then, in the first chapter, he details the stages of the Western intellectual invasion, starting with the Crusades, Orientalism, and proselytization, all the way to the overthrow of the Caliphate, and discusses the mechanisms of political and social change such as secularism and nationalism. The second chapter is devoted to the Marxist invasion, its foundations and principles, to reveal the nature of the intellectual and ideological conflict facing the nation.
descriptions.1752: This book deals with the topic of methods of calling to God and methods of dealing with sins and afflictions among Muslims. The author focuses on how to call upon disobedient people and correct their conditions, indicating that this issue is very important for the true preacher. In his book, Abd al-Rab Nawab al-Din presents the types of sins and their causes, then details the various methods of advocacy that can be used to return the disobedient to the path of truth, from education and reminders to changing the environment and finding alternatives. The book is part of the Salaf’s approach to advocacy, and aims to provide practical guidance to those who wish to spread the truth and correct deviant thoughts and actions in Muslim society.
descriptions.1753: This book deals with the topic of Friday sermon style from a legal perspective in accordance with the Qur’anic and Prophetic texts. The author, Abdullah Al-Ruhaili, focuses on deducing the legal foundations of the Friday sermon from the Qur’an and Sunnah, analyzing the prophetic methods of public speaking, and extracting the characteristics and methods of the sermon through studying and analyzing the legal texts. The book aims to provide practical guidance to mosque preachers on how to prepare an effective and influential sermon that complies with Sharia principles, while pointing out the importance of adhering to the foundations of Islamic preaching in this context.
descriptions.1754: The book, “The Most Correct Religion for Humanity in Doctrine and Sharia,” deals with a comparison between various religions and social sects from an Islamic perspective, reviewing religions such as communism, Brahimism, Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, and others. The author, Ahmed bin Abdul Ghafour Attar, aims to show the validity of Islam for humanity in terms of belief and Sharia, considering it the seal of religions and calling on the sound mind to choose the correct religion that combines belief, Sharia, and virtuous morals. In its context, the book reviews the prevailing sects and religions in the world, trying to evaluate them through the criteria of reason and conscience.
descriptions.1755: This book, “Origins of Dawah,” by Abdul Karim Zaidan, deals with the subject of the call to Islam from its general perspective and basic principles. The book focuses on four main principles of advocacy: its subject, the caller, the invited person, and the means and methods used in advocacy. The book begins by presenting a definition of the call to God, then deals with the definition of Islam, its pillars and characteristics, and reviews the various systems of Islam from morals to the social system, fatwas and hisbah. The book is divided into four chapters, each chapter dealing with one of the principles of the aforementioned call.
descriptions.1756: The book, “Highlights on Our Political Situation,” deals with Muslims’ political and social issues from an Islamic perspective, trying to decipher the challenges facing the Islamic nation in today’s world. The author focuses on the importance of returning to the principles of Islam in guiding politics and public life, and calls for comprehensive reform that begins at the leadership level and is rooted in society as a whole. The book also discusses the role of Muslim leaders and the importance of honesty in word and deed, with an emphasis on the necessity of rejecting any agreements that contradict Islamic principles, especially with regard to the conflict with Israel.
descriptions.1757: The book, “Highlights on Islamic Culture,” by Nadia Sharif Al-Omari, deals with the topic of Islamic culture, its characteristics, and its importance, reviewing the definition of culture and its relationship with civilization and science, then focusing on the divine characteristics, comprehensiveness, and balance that distinguish Islamic culture, and its role in cultural prosperity and scientific progress. The book also studies the pillars of Islamic culture, including faith, doctrine, and legislation, and stresses the importance of adhering to religious teachings and contemplating God’s verses to strengthen the Islamic personality and enable it to perform its role in reform and guidance.
descriptions.1758: The book deals with the goals of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s call, indicating its intellectual, social and religious dimensions. The author focuses on clarifying the Wahhabi doctrine and its goals in achieving human servitude to God and rejecting polytheism and heresies, with reference to the Sheikh’s efforts to reform Islamic society and establish God’s law. The book aims to clarify the truth of this call to those who do not know it, and to enhance its correct understanding among Muslims.
descriptions.1759: The book “The Importance of Da’wah” deals with the subject of Islamic da’wah and its role in spreading the message of Islam and promoting scientific religiosity in societies, reviewing the da’wah approach and its various frameworks. It was produced by a conference held at the Islamic University of Medina, and includes studies aimed at guiding preachers and providing effective approaches and methods for Islamic advocacy in various fields.
descriptions.1760: The book “The Confusion of the Jews, the Story of Al-Samaw’al’s Islam, and His Vision” by Al-Samaw’al ibn Yahya Al-Maghribi deals with multiple topics related to the religious debate between Muslims and Jews. The author tells the story of his conversion to Islam and his vision of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and presents a book dedicated to convincing the Jews and Christians with rational argument and explaining the abrogation of the Torah and the prophecy of Muhammad and Jesus, peace be upon them. The book also addresses some Jewish slanders and attempts to invalidate them, while at the same time reviewing some false Jewish beliefs and practices.
descriptions.1761: This book deals with the topic of the relationship between modern science and religious knowledge, reviewing the opinions of some thinkers who try to reconcile them or ambiguity in their understanding. Sheikh Abdel Fattah Ashmawi focuses on interpreting Qur’anic verses related to the concept of the unseen and how to understand it through an Islamic perspective. The book also addresses how Muslim scholars can understand scientific knowledge through a religious perspective, relying on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths to clarify the concept of the unseen and how to understand it.
descriptions.1762: This book deals with a critical study of the Christian slanders against the Holy Qur’an, claiming that it supports the claim of the divinity of Jesus (peace be upon him). The author, Ali bin Atiq Al-Harbi, focuses on responding to these allegations through Islamic interpretations of the Qur’an and the books of the Two Testaments, relying on divine oneness and denying divinity about Jesus (peace be upon him), his humanity, and his prophecy. The book aims to defend the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet against attempts at misinterpretation by missionaries, and reviews the topics from two perspectives: Islamic through the Qur’an, and Christian through the Torah and the Gospels.
descriptions.1763: The book “The Educational Impact of the Mosque” by Dr. Saleh Al-Sadlan addresses the topic of the educational role of mosques in Islamic society, indicating the position of the mosque in Islam and the comprehensiveness of its functions. The book focuses on the importance of the mosque in strengthening community and faith education, and its role in spreading science and knowledge and instilling good morals among Muslims. The book also addresses the role of the mosque in promoting community unity and spreading justice and mercy among its members.
descriptions.1764: This book deals with the study of the Holy Scriptures among the Jews and their impact on their deviation from the truth, relying on the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet to criticize the areas of distortion and alteration in their books. The author focuses on analyzing the content of the Torah, the Talmud, and the subsequent books, and discusses how the Jews’ reliance on these distorted books led to their deviation in their beliefs, ideas, and rituals, warning Muslims of the dangers of being influenced by these distorted Jewish ideas.
descriptions.1765: The book “The Principles of Sharia When Suspicions Resolve” by Sheikh Saleh Al-Sheikh deals with topics related to faith and Islamic doctrine, and includes chapters on predestination, trials, martyrdom, loyalty and disavowal, with a focus on the importance of adhering to the approach of the Salaf in confronting suspicions and falsehoods. The book also addresses the ruling on taking lives, being vigilant against rumours, and being wary of stirring up strife within the nation, and calls for moderation and adherence to the guidance of the predecessors when strife appears.
descriptions.1766: This book deals with the scientific foundations of the Salafi call, discusses the concept of imitation in Islamic jurisprudence, and explains the Salafi approach to understanding Islam and acting upon it. It also presents the aim and objectives of the Salafi call, and mentions its advantages and characteristics. In the book, the author reviews suspicions and responses about the Salafist call, and provides a general vision about its origins, goals, and characteristics.
descriptions.1767: This book deals with the topic of moderation in Islam and its importance in doctrine, legislation, and advocacy, reviewing verses in the Holy Qur’an and the hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that confirm this moderation. The author focuses on the importance of adhering to the Prophetic method in calling to God and staying away from extremism and extremism, while emphasizing the necessity of adhering to Islamic principles and adopting useful modern sciences. The book aims to explain the truth of the middle nation and demonstrate the importance of uprightness on its middle path in various religious and social fields.
descriptions.1768: This book deals with the topic of enjoining good and forbidding evil from an Islamic perspective, based on the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author, Suleiman Al-Hogail, discusses the history of this topic throughout the ages, and explains its importance in Islam and its obligation according to his understanding. It also studies the difference between the specific obligation and the sufficiency in this duty, and points out the conditions that must be met by those who enjoin good and forbid evil. The book focuses on the practical importance of this topic in the daily lives of Muslims, while providing practical advice on how to implement it correctly.
descriptions.1769: The book “Security in People’s Lives and Its Importance in Islam” by Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Mohsen Al Turki deals with the topic of security from an Islamic perspective and its role in the life of the individual and society. The author focuses on security from the perspective of Islamic law and its applications in contemporary Islamic history, indicating the importance of security in achieving stability and well-being for Islamic societies. The book also addresses how the concept of security can be applied in the Islamic state and how it can be achieved for the individual, society, and state alike, with a focus on the application of these principles in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
descriptions.1770: The book, “Orientalism, Its Efforts, and Its Objectives in Combating Islam,” deals with the subject of Orientalism as a scientific movement whose apparent meaning is the study of Eastern heritage, while its essence is fighting Islam and distorting its mission. The author, Abdel Moneim Muhammad Hassanein, shows how Orientalists use the study of Eastern languages, especially Arabic, as a means to distort the image of Islam and sabotage its culture, by spreading misguided concepts and slanders on the sources of Islamic legislation. It also presents the ongoing efforts of Orientalism to spread misleading intellectual currents among Muslims and to fight the Arabic language, and suggests ways to confront these attempts and protect Islam from distortion.
descriptions.1771: The book “Islam in Sierra Leone” by Muhammad Saleh Mahairi provides a comprehensive overview of the presence of Islam in this African country, covering various aspects of its history, geography, and spread among the population. The book begins by providing information about the geographical location of Sierra Leone and its historical development, then moves on to address the history of the entry of Islam into the country and its spread among the population, with a focus on the level of Islamic culture and the role of religious institutions in it. The book also deals with the Salafist Dawa movement and its influence, as well as the missionary efforts made by Christian missions in the country.
descriptions.1772: The book deals with Islam and contemporary subversive movements, written by Sheikh Abdul Qadir Shaybah Al-Hamad, as it focuses on analyzing the influence of the Freemasonry, Zionism, communist, and socialist movements on Islamic societies. The author believes that these movements represent a great danger to humanity and work to destroy identity and moral and religious values, trying to expose their methods and hidden goals that aim to dismantle societies and spread chaos and moral dissolution.
descriptions.1773: This book deals with Islam and socialist doctrines in the context of a profound intellectual debate, focusing on the nature of Islam as a comprehensive and timeless religion, and arguing that its teachings are valid for all times and places. The author compares Islam and modern socialist doctrines, reviewing different types of socialism and reviewing how Islam differs from them in its principles and provisions. The book aims to clarify the fundamental differences between Islam and socialist doctrines by interpreting the provisions and principles of the Islamic religion.
descriptions.1774: This book deals with the topic of human rights in Islam and their relationship to global changes, reviewing the Islamic principles and values ​​that guarantee these rights. The author focuses on the importance of this topic in the current global context, showing how Islam has preceded in affirming and guaranteeing human rights since its inception. The book addresses multiple aspects of human rights in Islam, including the right to life, freedom, equality, social rights, and the rights of women and children, in addition to the right to a healthy natural environment. The book aims to correct common concepts about human rights, and to clarify whether they are the fruit of contemporary civilization or new principles, while monitoring skepticism and slander against Islam in this context.
descriptions.1775: The book deals with the media and Islamic advocacy in the modern era, indicating the importance of the media in spreading ideas and changing beliefs, and its effective role in calling to Islam. The author focuses on the impact of the media on Islamic societies and the necessity of using it as an effective tool in spreading Islamic advocacy, especially in light of the challenges these societies face in terms of intellectual and cultural deviations. It also emphasizes the necessity of using radio and other media to achieve unity among people by spreading wise Islamic ideas and good sermons.
descriptions.1776: This book deals with the topic of Orientalism and proselytization in the Islamic world, and reviews their goals and methods in influencing Islamic culture and thought. The author focuses on analyzing the hidden motives and goals behind the emergence and spread of Orientalism, and how it is used as a tool to serve Western colonialism. The book also addresses the position of Orientalists and missionaries on Islam and Muslims, and discusses the intellectual and cultural issues that resulted from this phenomenon, highlighting the fundamental differences between Christianity as a religion and Crusading as a cultural and political trend.
descriptions.1777: The book deals with the topic of Orientalism and its relationship with the Sunnah of the Prophet, explaining the goals of the Orientalists and their methods in questioning the Islamic religion. The author focuses on analyzing the motives behind the emergence and development of Orientalism, while reviewing the suspicions of Orientalists about the Sunnah of the Prophet and its personalities, and how they use culture and knowledge as tools to colonize minds. The book also studies the relationship between Orientalism and various Islamic sects, trying to expose the attempts of Orientalists to question the origins of the Islamic religion and distort its image.
descriptions.1778: This book, “Insight in the Call to God,” by the preacher Aziz bin Farhan Al-Anazi, deals with the topic of calling to God Almighty according to the approach of the prophets and messengers, with a focus on the importance of insight in this context. The author addresses the concept of insight and discusses how to achieve it in the field of advocacy, noting the necessity of knowledge and certainty in calling to God. It also focuses on the importance of wisdom in dealing with invitees and how to reach them in the best way. The book aims to provide practical guidance to those who wish to call people to God with insight and in accordance with the correct legal approach.
descriptions.1779: The book “The Happy Home and Spousal Disagreement” deals with the topic of building the Muslim family and protecting it from disintegration, emphasizing the importance of faith in God and getting close to Him as a basis for a happy home and the elimination of marital disputes. The author focuses on the role of spouses in maintaining affection and compassion between them, while providing practical advice for resolving any differences that may arise between them, reviewing the causes of disagreement and means of addressing it.
descriptions.1780: This book deals with the topic of warning against the means and methods of Christianization adopted by the enemies of Islam, and presents various practices and activities that target Muslims with the aim of distorting their religion or keeping them away from Islam. The book focuses on the duty of Muslims to confront these dangers and protect their religion from misinformation, while pointing out the modern threats that have emerged in the modern era.
descriptions.1781: This book deals with the subject of gradation in the call of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, reviewing the aspects of gradation in the call in terms of subject, method, style, and invitee. It focuses on the importance of following the Messenger’s approach in calling to Islam, emphasizing the necessity of gradual dissemination of doctrine, law, and morals, and explaining how to deal with the various target groups of the call. The book aims to correct the understanding of some of those involved in Islamic advocacy who are ignorant or ignore the importance of following the Prophet’s guidance in the advocacy process.
descriptions.1782: The book “Islamic Education for Youth” by Dr. Abdul Rahman Bullah Ali deals with the topic of youth from an Islamic perspective, focusing on its linguistic, social and cultural dimensions. The author focuses on the importance of paying attention to youth as they are the driving force of the nation and its beating heart, reviewing the responsibilities of parents and scholars towards them. The book also addresses multiple aspects of the lives of young people and their role in building society, relying on linguistic terms and detailing their meanings in the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.1783: The book “Education in Muslim Countries” by Mohamed Abdel Fattah Ashmawy addresses multiple topics related to education policies and goals in the Islamic world. The book focuses on the importance of science and scholars in Islam, and examines the necessity of learning and teaching from a religious and social perspective. The book also addresses education curricula, materials, and goals, reviewing how education in the Islamic world can be Islamic in policy and content.
descriptions.1784: The book “Progress and Reaction” by Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali deals with the topic of cultural and intellectual development in the Islamic world and Europe, reviewing the concepts of progress and reaction and how to employ them in the cultural and social context. The author focuses on the difference between progressives who strive towards the future in search of truth and prosperity, and reactionaries who tend to return to previous eras and adhere to superstitions and traditional customs. Al-Hilali also analyzes the beginning of the Renaissance era in Europe and the decisive developments it caused, comparing this to the situation of the Arab peoples who suffered from reactionism in recent times.
descriptions.1785: This book deals with the topic of Christianization by defining it and explaining its goals and means, with a focus on the regrets of the Christian missionaries. The author discusses the stages of conflict between Christianity and Islam throughout history, and points out that Christianization is an extension of the Crusades. The book also studies the various means of Christianization and how to confront them, with reference to the effects of Christianization on Muslims and their societies.
descriptions.1786: The book “Christianization, its concept, goals, means, and ways to confront it” by Muhammad Ali bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad Al-Namlah deals with the phenomenon of Christianization from an Islamic perspective, reviewing the definitions of Christianization, its goals, and various means throughout history. The author focuses on the developments that occurred in Christianization from its early beginnings until the modern era, while reviewing the mechanisms for confronting this phenomenon by Muslims. The book also addresses the cultural and social effects of Christianization, how it adapted to the times and followed modern methods to achieve its goals, with reference to the scientific and intellectual efforts made by Muslims to confront this phenomenon throughout the ages.
descriptions.1787: The book “The Culture We Need” deals with the topic of the culture necessary for the happiness and advancement of the nation, focusing on the role of religion in building personality and consolidating spiritual and moral values. The author compares the situation of the Arabs before and after Islam, showing how religion influenced society to change and improve its conditions, especially for women and boys. It also refers to the social and legal transformations introduced by Islam, which raised the status of women and gave them rights equal to men in inheritance and choice in marriage.
descriptions.1788: The book deals with jihad from the perspective of the Islamic faith and discusses the suspicions of orientalists about this subject. The author focuses on the continuation of the Islamic call from its beginnings in Mecca until its spread in Medina, indicating the stages of the emergence and development of Islamic society. He also points out the importance of strength and armament in achieving victory, and compares the position of the early Muslims towards the call to the reservation that some Quraysh sheikhs met with.
descriptions.1789: This book deals with the media aspects of the Prophet’s sermons ﷺ, reviewing the media connotations and meanings in his various sermons, and also reviewing the components of the media discourse approach and the principles of persuasion in them. Through this study, the author aims to highlight the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in communicating with people and conveying the media message effectively and competently, and to consolidate Islamic media through studying the Prophet’s speech.
descriptions.1790: The book “The Salafist Movement and its Role in Reviving the Sunnah” by Dr. Abdul Rahman Al-Fariwai deals with a historical study of a scientific and reform renaissance that spread in India during the thirteenth century AH. The author reviewed the Sunnah Revival movement led by Imam Al-Nawab Siddiq Hassan Al-Bufali and Mr. Nazir Hussein Al-Dahlawi, and their role in spreading the sciences of hadith and promoting adherence to the Sunnah of the Prophet on the method of the Salaf. The book focuses on the impact of this movement in stimulating interest in the sciences of hadith and publishing Sunnah books, and its role in saving these sciences from extinction in the era of the weakness of the Islamic state.
descriptions.1791: The book “Islamic Civilization, Its Foundations and Means and Images of Muslim Applications of It” by Dr. Abdul Rahman Habankah Al-Maidani deals with a deep intellectual study on the origins and principles of Islamic civilization and its impact on the development of humanity. The author focuses on analyzing the meaning of civilization from an Islamic perspective and explaining Islam’s position on civilizational progress. He also studies the intellectual and psychological foundations that founded civilizations, with a focus on Islamic civilization, its universality, and its openness to various cultures. The book is part of a series of works that aim to provide a comprehensive overview of Islamic civilization and its applications in the world.
descriptions.1792: The book deals with Islamic civilization in its comprehensive context, reviewing its components and the reasons for its growth and prosperity. The author discusses how Islamic civilization derived its elements and features from the Islamic religion itself, considering it the religion of human civilization. The book focuses on the nature of Islamic civilization as a unique global civilization, and denies the concept of Arab civilization, considering that it did not exist without Islam. The book also discusses the features of Islamic civilization from its spiritual, intellectual, and social perspective, reviewing how elements of the Islamic religion contributed to spreading its civilizational character on a large scale.
descriptions.1793: This book deals with the topic of wisdom in calling to God Almighty, reviewing its definition, controls, types and pillars. The author focuses on the importance of calling for wisdom according to the Sharia approach, indicating the relationship between the linguistic and terminological definition of wisdom. It also includes a study of the main pillars of wisdom, which are knowledge, forbearance, and patience, with an explanation of the sections of knowledge, the reasons for attaining it, and how to achieve forbearance and patience in calling.
descriptions.1794: The book “Islamic Rhetoric” by Muhammad Abdel Ati Shalabi deals with the subject of rhetoric from an Islamic advocacy perspective, emphasizing the importance of qualified preacher cadres scientifically, morally, and socially. The author focuses on the qualities of the ideal orator and the etiquette of public speaking, reviewing examples of sermons throughout the ages, starting with the sermons of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ until the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. The book aims to provide a guide for those who wish to develop their oratorical skills, drawing inspiration from the eloquent and eloquent speeches selected by the author.
descriptions.1795: This book by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz deals with the topic of calling to God and the morals of preachers. It focuses on the virtue and wisdom of the call, how to perform it and its methods, and the matter to which one should be called. It aims to clarify the importance of preaching in Islam and explain its origins and rulings, with a focus on the morals that preachers must have in practicing their message.
descriptions.1796: This book deals with the reform call in Najd at the hands of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his followers, explaining its goals and importance in reviving the correct faith and rejecting heresies. The author focuses on the biography of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his scientific upbringing, and explains his approach in calling for monotheism and rejecting polytheism and heresies, while reviewing the opinions of scholars about him. The book aims to clarify the reformist role of Sheikh bin Abdul Wahhab in spreading sound doctrine and correcting religious practices in the Arabian Peninsula.
descriptions.1797: This book deals with the topic of public opinion in Islamic society by defining it and clarifying its elements and composition, with a focus on the influences that contribute to its formulation in accordance with Islamic principles. The author focuses on the importance of public opinion being compatible with the Islamic faith and Sharia values, considering that an Islamic society that adheres to the Qur’an and Sunnah is capable of producing correct public opinion guided by their guidance. It also talks about the functions that public opinion can perform in preserving Islamic principles and achieving the legitimate interests of the nation.
descriptions.1798: This book deals with responding to the suspicions and questions raised by skeptics of Islam, using verses from the Holy Qur’an, prophetic hadiths, and evidence from reason and logic. The author focuses on the importance of dialogue and debate within legal controls, discusses the issue of the crucifixion of Christ and contradictions in the Gospels, and also reviews some punishments in Islam. The book aims to clarify the facts and explain what he believes is right by discussing these issues in both a scientific and religious manner.
descriptions.1799: The book deals with the Salafists and the Four Imams (may Allah be pleased with them), as it focuses on the importance of ijtihad in Islamic jurisprudence and its relationship to the four Imams. The author aims to clarify the truth of the Salafi call in jurisprudence and legislation, and to explain the position of the Salafists regarding the four imams, while responding to the accusations of the imitators who believe that calling to the Qur’an and Sunnah negates their status. The book is a classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims. It reviews the concept of ijtihad and its conditions, and discusses the challenges facing Muslims in order to follow the Qur’an and Sunnah in every time and place.
descriptions.1800: The book deals with the suspicions that were raised about the call of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and reviews responses to those suspicions with the aim of clarifying the facts related to this call. Author Abdul Karim Al-Khatib focuses on discussing issues related to the call and the conditions of Muslims, by analyzing the conflicts and challenges faced, with an emphasis on jihad and loyalty to the believers.
descriptions.1801: The book presents the suspicions raised to deny the Sunnah of the Prophet and refutes them, as it deals with thirty suspicions that contradict the Prophet’s hadith, including doubts related to the history of the hadith and its narration, doubts related to the nature of the Sunnah and the status of its hadiths, and doubts related to the credibility of the narrators. The author aims to clarify the facts and refute suspicions that seek to cast doubt on the value and validity of the Sunnah, by presenting evidence and proofs that confirm the validity of the Sunnah and its necessity in understanding Islam.
descriptions.1802: This book deals with the topic of communism from a religious and intellectual perspective, reviewing the contradictions between it and divine religious doctrines. The author focuses on the nature of man, which is naturally oriented towards religiosity, and discusses how communism seeks to change and distort this nature. The book also addresses discussions and debates about communism, discusses the intolerance that surrounds it, and attempts to invalidate some misconceptions about it. The book falls within the category of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and aims to clarify the facts and concepts related to communism from an Islamic point of view.
descriptions.1803: The book “The Path to Islam” by Dr. Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad deals with the topic of the call to Islam and the conditions of Muslims, providing a comprehensive explanation of the teachings of the Islamic religion and its basic principles. The book begins with an introduction that focuses on the importance of faith in God in achieving true happiness, then moves on to explain the pillars of Islam and the principles of the Islamic faith, with a focus on the characteristics and virtues of the Islamic religion. The book also addresses the status of women in Islam and responds to suspicions about it, and aims to introduce non-Muslims to Islam and its principles in an easy and clear way.
descriptions.1804: Dr. Ali Abdul Latif Mansour, in his book “Worships in Islam and Their Impact on Muslim Solidarity,” presents a jurisprudential study of the meaning of worship in language and Sharia, examining the impact of Islamic worship in strengthening unity and solidarity among Muslims. The book focuses on the most important major Islamic acts of worship, namely prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj, indicating their role in developing Islamic spirituality and strengthening relationships between members of the Muslim community.
descriptions.1805: The book “Secularism and Islam’s Position on It” by Dr. Hamoud Al-Ruhaili deals with the topic of secularism from an Islamic perspective, reviewing its definition, concept, and development in the West, the reasons for its transmission to the Islamic world, and its negative effects. The book also explains Islam's rule for secularism and discusses the principles and rules of secularism and denies it based on the Islamic approach. The book is a type of scientific and intellectual book that aims to clarify concepts and state facts from an Islamic perspective.
descriptions.1806: Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz defines intellectual invasion in his book “Intellectual Invasion and Its Means” as concentrated efforts undertaken by one nation to exploit or influence another, considering that this type of invasion is more dangerous than military invasion due to the secrecy of its nature and the difficulty of discovering it. The book focuses on analyzing the phenomenon of intellectual invasion and its effects on the Islamic nation in general and the Arabs and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in particular, with a focus on the means used by the West to promote its ideas, especially the Christian, Crusader, Jewish and communist intellectual invasion.
descriptions.1807: The book “Intellectual Invasion” by Mamdouh Fakhry deals with topics related to the challenges facing the Islamic nation in the intellectual and cultural fields, focusing on the mechanisms and reasons for the dismantling of the Islamic social and political fabric after the fall of the Ottoman Caliphate. The book deals with the manifestations of intellectual invasion through various means and programs, and discusses ideas and slogans that aim to undermine Islamic identity and the cohesion of the nation.
descriptions.1808: The book “Modern Islamic Thought and its Connection to Western Colonialism” by Muhammad Al-Bahi deals with confronting the intellectual trends that attempt to separate Muslims from their religion and make them subservient to colonial powers. The author focuses on combating trends such as Marxism and Qadianis, and points out the role of Islam in solving the problems of modern material societies. The book presents his ongoing struggle with the forces that support these trends, both inside and outside Islamic societies, and emphasizes the importance of Islamic values ​​in guiding societies towards the right path.
descriptions.1809: This book deals with the topic of role models and their importance in the lives of Muslims, defining their types, purposes, and origins. The author focuses on good role models and the qualities of those who practice them, such as righteousness, good morals, honesty, patience, compassion, and humility. It also urges the importance of agreement in word and deed, and provides living examples of exemplary positions in the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. The book is a preaching book that aims to consolidate Islamic principles in society.
descriptions.1810: The book deals with satellite channels from an Islamic perspective, trying to evaluate their impact on Muslim societies. The author discusses the advantages and disadvantages associated with these channels, and reviews the opinions of thinkers and reformers on their use. The book aims to provide a scientific vision about the reality of satellite media and the extent of its benefit or harm, with a focus on how to deal with it in accordance with Islamic values.
descriptions.1811: The book “Society and Family in Islam” by author Muhammad Taher Al-Jawabi deals with the topics of society and family from an Islamic perspective, explaining the foundations of building a Muslim society, the importance of Islamic ethics in social relations, and the role of science and work in educating individuals and consolidating Islamic values. The book also addresses issues related to the family in Islam, such as marriage, polygamy, divorce, and family problems, while providing legal solutions to them, within the framework of protecting society and the family from disintegration and deviation.
descriptions.1812: The book entitled “Drugs are the Most Dangerous Obstacles to Development” by Dr. Ibrahim Imam, deals with the issue of drugs and their negative effects on human and social development in the Islamic world. The author focuses on Islam's position on drugs compared to alcohol, discusses their dangers to the individual and society, and links the spread of drugs to backwardness and crime. It also refers to religious and media efforts to combat this phenomenon, and reviews the impact of drugs on different groups in society, especially young people.
descriptions.1813: The book “Orientalists in the Balance” by Abdel Aziz Al-Qari deals with the history of the Orientalist movement and its impact on Islamic and Arabic studies. The book focuses on discussing the goals and methods of Orientalists in studying Islamic civilization, while providing a critique of some of the research mechanisms used by them. The book also deals with the period of the spread of Islamic civilization in Andalusia and the impact it had on the European peoples in the Middle Ages.
descriptions.1814: The book “Orientalists and Christianization” by Dr. Ali bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad Al-Namlah deals with the relationship between Orientalism and Christianization, reviewing the categories of Christianized Orientalists and the extent of their influence in this field. The book aims to study this relationship with an objective, scientific methodology, far from whims and excess emotion, while emphasizing that there is an Orientalism that did not depend on Christianization, just as there is a Christianization that did not benefit from Orientalism. The book focuses on analyzing the multiple connections to the phenomenon of Orientalism, while providing a comprehensive and balanced view of this complex relationship.
descriptions.1815: This book deals with the topic of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims in the Arab and Islamic world, with a focus on the role of orientalists and missionaries in this context. Author Ibrahim Khalil Ahmed presents his vision of his upbringing in a Christian environment and his conversion to Islam, and how his personal and cultural experiences influenced his understanding of the Islamic and Christian religions. The book also addresses missionary and Orientalist policies and their impact on Islamic societies, with a review of some of the educational institutions and missionary initiatives in the region.
descriptions.1816: The book deals with the jurisprudence of preaching and preaching according to King Abdulaziz Al Saud from an Islamic perspective, explaining the higher purposes of Islam in its speech and approach. The author focuses on the religious and moral role of King Abdulaziz in building the modern Saudi state, and how he confronts the political and cultural challenges of the modern era, while preserving the identity and principles of the Islamic state. The book also discusses the efforts made by King Abdul Aziz to achieve political unity in the Arabian Peninsula and protect the Two Holy Mosques.
descriptions.1817: This book deals with the topic of calling to God Almighty according to the correct approach, indicating the importance of correct belief and monotheism in this context. The author focuses on the necessity of starting with the call to monotheism as a basis for all advocacy efforts, and points out the pillars upon which the correct approach to advocacy is based. He also addresses the reasons for the nation’s deviation from this approach and its effects on the effectiveness of the call. The book aims to clarify how to follow the approach of the Messenger ﷺ in calling to God with wisdom and good preaching, and to demonstrate the importance of returning to the fundamentals of religion and correcting beliefs as a basis for effective advocacy work.
descriptions.1818: The book “The Curriculum between Past and Present” by Muhammad Abdullah Qadri, Dean of the College of Arabic Language, deals with the topic of education and curricula from an Islamic perspective. The author focuses on the importance of education in guiding society and achieving worship of God Almighty, indicating what the education curriculum should be in Islam and its implications for the lives of Muslims and their relationship with God. The book also discusses the reality of education and curricula in the present compared to the past, and criticizes some educational practices that contradict the correct Islamic curriculum.
