descriptions.1819: This book deals with the topic of Islamic unity from its doctrinal, religious, and Sharia perspective, explaining the reality of the Islamic nation and the deviations and conflicts it suffers from. It then explains the reasons for this reality, and then moves on to clarify the foundations of unity upon which the nation should agree, and the means of achieving these foundations. The book is divided into four sections and a conclusion. The first deals with the nation’s reality in belief, worship, and Sharia, while the second focuses on the reasons for this reality. The third section talks about the foundations of unity, and the fourth section talks about the means of achieving it.
descriptions.1820: The book deals with Islamic unity from a historical and civilizational perspective, reviewing how the Islamic nation in the first centuries was one unified nation and then how it split into states over time, followed by religious and national minorities. The author seeks to explore the ways in which Islamic unity can be achieved again, based on the common doctrinal, ritual and legislative balance of Islam among Muslims, taking into account the current changes in conditions and circumstances.
descriptions.1821: This book, “The Clear Commandments for Benefiting from Scientific Lessons” by Sheikh Saleh Al-Sheikh, deals with the topic of making the most of scientific lessons and training courses. The author focuses on the importance of good organization, having a competent teacher, and serious students to ensure the success of scientific lessons. The book includes practical advice for science students on how to prepare well for lessons, and how to make the most of them, with an emphasis on sincerity and seriousness in learning.
descriptions.1822: This book is the result of a symposium on the impact of the Qur’an in achieving moderation and repelling extremism, and it contains various researches from different authors. The book deals with the topic of moderation and moderation in Islam through the Qur’an and Sunnah, and reviews the concepts of moderation and moderation and their evidence. It also focuses on Islam’s tolerance and ease in dealing with violators and addressing the phenomena of fanaticism and deviation. The book aims to establish the concept of moderation in Islamic individuals and societies by relying on Qur’anic and Prophetic texts.
descriptions.1823: This book presents various research on Islamic preaching during the reign of King Abdul Aziz (may Allah have mercy on him), covering multiple aspects of the history of preaching in the Arabian Peninsula from the era of Imam Muhammad bin Saud until the era of the founding king. The book focuses on the development of the call during the era of the first and second Saudi states, and includes studies on the call before the era of King Abdul Aziz, and an analysis of the characteristics of the call in the personality of King Abdul Aziz and his role in qualifying preachers and developing the means of preaching.
descriptions.1824: An Effort to Conquer the Jews is a book written by Al-Samawāl ibn Yahya Al-Maghribi (Rev. Shmuel ibn Judah ibn Abuwan), a Jewish cleric from a family known for knowledge, religious standing, and knowledge of worldly sciences such as medicine and mathematics. Ibn Abi Usaibah, the author of “Uyun al-Anba,” mentioned him among the ranks of doctors with the famous doctors of his time. It is one of the most important books written in response to the Jews. He stated that his motivation for writing it was to consider the steps he went through to leave Judaism and enter Islam. He wrote: I mention the reason for what God has given me in terms of guidance and how my situation led me from the time I grew up to my transition from the Jewish doctrine so that it would be an example and a warning to those who encounter it. …
descriptions.1825: The book “Building an Islamic Society” by critic Nabil Al-Samalouti deals with the subject of sociology from an Islamic perspective, reviewing the foundations of building an Islamic society in accordance with Islamic law. The book focuses on analyzing Islamic social and ethical concepts, and showing how they can be applied in building a just and integrated society. The author also discusses the importance of reconsidering Western scientific currents of sociology from an Islamic perspective, based on the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.1826: The book “The Children of Israel in the Light of Islam” by Sheikh Muhammad Amin Salim deals with an objective study of the Children of Israel from an Islamic perspective, showing their conditions and morals throughout history. The author focuses on their negative behavior such as immorality, envy, and selfishness, while pointing out their positive contributions to ancient civilizations, especially in the artistic and professional fields. The book aims to present a comprehensive picture of the Children of Israel, based on Qur’anic texts and Islamic history.
descriptions.1827: The book Islamic Educational Environments by Dr. Abbas Mahjoub deals with the study of educational environments in Islam, focusing on the family, the mosque, the school, and society. The book deals with the role of each of these environments in the process of upbringing and guidance, with a focus on the family as the oldest social institution for education, and then the development of the role of other institutions in the educational process with the progress of human life and the increase in types of knowledge and professions.
descriptions.1828: This book deals with various topics related to the conditions of Muslims and the challenges they face in the fields of politics, economics, and society. In his articles, Malek Bennabi focuses on issues of independence and revolution, and also discusses the conflict in Palestine and the obstacles to economic development in the Arab world. The book aims to provide a comprehensive vision of the political and social situation in the Islamic world, with a focus on how to emerge from a state of wandering towards guidance and civilizational advancement.
descriptions.1829: The book deals with the influence of reform movements in Indonesia on the call of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, showing how this call influenced the spread of monotheism and the rejection of polytheism and heresies in Indonesian society. The author focuses on the influence of the book “Kitab al-Tawhid” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and the impact it achieved in spreading the correct doctrine among the people of Indonesia. The book is part of the research of a symposium held on the preaching of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab at Imam Muhammad bin Saud Islamic University.
descriptions.1830: The book presents reflections on the call of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, examining its goals, method, and circumstances of its emergence. It focuses on the soundness of the approach and the clarity of the goals in the Sheikh’s call, and the role of the House of Saud in spreading it, noting that the Sheikh was influenced by the nation’s predecessors and scholars, especially Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. The book also addresses how this call restored the status of Muslims in the Arabian Peninsula and their hope of building strong Islamic societies.
descriptions.1831: The book Reflections by the Algerian writer and thinker Malek Bennabi, published in 1961, is mostly lectures given in various Arab capitals and deals with the problem of civilization and culture and the place of the Arab-Islamic world and the African and Asian peoples thereof in that history. In his lectures, the writer makes many realistic comparisons, identifies the elements that he sees as the cause of the birth or death of a civilization, and analyzes the cultural components that make up the culture of a particular society and distinguish it from others. The author formulates culture as a concept in his book as follows: Culture is the general atmosphere that characterizes the way of life in a certain society and the behavior of the individual in it with a special character, different from the character that we find in the life of another society. (p. 152)
descriptions.1832: This book deals with the jurisprudence of victory and empowerment in the Holy Qur’an, reviewing its types, conditions, causes, stages, and goals. The author focuses on studying cases of empowerment in Quranic history, including conveying the message, destroying the infidels and saving the believers, participating in governance, and establishing the state. The book also studies recent historical events to draw lessons learned from them in the context of empowerment jurisprudence. The book aims to understand the origins of the jurisprudence of empowerment through a detailed analysis of the Holy Qur’an, and to demonstrate its importance in the life of the contemporary Islamic nation.
descriptions.1833: The book “Fortifying Muslim Society Against Intellectual Invasion” by Dr. Hamoud Al-Ruhaili deals with the topic of intellectual invasion and its impact on Islamic societies, reviewing its definition, goals and methods, then showing ways to prevent it by adhering to the correct doctrine and spreading it, and explaining the impact of faith and piety in protecting Muslim society from this phenomenon.
descriptions.1834: This book deals with the topic of preparing preachers and training them in public speaking methods, seminars, radio, and visual speech. The author focuses on the importance of training and its characteristics, and points out multiple paths to developing preachers' skills in effective communication. The book aims to qualify preachers scientifically, morally, and psychologically so that they can spread the Islamic call correctly in accordance with Islamic law.
descriptions.1835: The book “Aspirations to the Future at the Beginning of the New Hijri Century” by Muhammad Qutb deals with the topic of change and development in the lives of Muslims, reviewing the idea of ​​entering the new Hijri century and whether this event is merely wishful thinking or does it carry a balance of reality that can lead to real change. The author discusses how real change in people's lives does not occur based on numbers of years or centuries, but rather requires self-change from the people themselves. Qutb calls for reflection on whether Muslims have begun to change themselves enough to welcome this new century with a new reality.
descriptions.1836: The book “Polygamy: Between the Realities of Revelation and Misleading Fabrications” by its author, Mahmoud Muhammad Gharib, deals with the topic of polygamy from an Islamic perspective, reviewing different opinions about it and citing legal and scientific evidence. The book focuses on discussing the accusations against this topic and trying to correct the misunderstanding about it, trying to reconcile the teachings of Islam with the reality of Muslims in the modern era. The book also addresses social and psychological aspects related to polygamy, reviewing the opinions of scholars and writers on this matter.
descriptions.1837: This book deals with the subject of the polygamy of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, comparing this to the polygamy in the lives of previous prophets. The author begins by discussing polygamy in the lives of prophets such as Abraham, Jacob, Moses, David, and Solomon, then moves on to analyze the wisdom of the Prophet’s marriage ﷺ to his wives, and reviews the lives of each of them. The book also addresses the claims of the enemies of Islam on this subject, and attempts to refute them by providing scientific and logical justifications for the Prophet’s multiple wives.
descriptions.1838: The book “The Present of the Islamic World” by Ali Jarisha deals with the reality of the Islamic nation in various intellectual, political, social and economic fields. The author focuses on the challenges facing the Islamic world locally and globally, and discusses contemporary issues such as Palestine, Andalusia, and the Soviet Union, relying on information from reliable sources and testimonies from certain parties. The book aims to provide an objective and in-depth study of current Islamic issues, while maintaining personal neutrality and focusing on the roots of the problem to achieve effective solutions.
descriptions.1839: The book “Human Rights in Islam” by Tahir Ahmad Maulana Jamal al-Layl deals with the topic of human rights from an Islamic perspective, reviewing the principles and values ​​on which these rights are based in Islamic law. The book addresses various aspects of human rights such as cultural, social, political, civil and economic rights, with a focus on equality between people and the embodiment of these rights in practice. It also sheds light on the development of the idea of ​​human rights throughout history and compares it to what is stated in Islam, considering it the final religion that carries these rights in its texts and rulings.
descriptions.1840: The book deals with human rights and major issues from an Islamic perspective, and reviews the basic concepts of human rights in accordance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, with a focus on the shortcomings in its application and ways to enhance it. The author addresses various topics related to human rights, including women's rights, minorities, fundamental freedoms, dialogue among civilizations, workers' rights, international cooperation, and the laws of war. The book also addresses important Islamic issues such as Palestine, Chechnya, and the Muslims of the Balkans, reviewing the role of Islam in promoting human rights and spreading lofty human values.
descriptions.1841: This book deals with the topic of Friday sermons, their importance in Islam, and the responsibilities of preachers in performing this sermon in an optimal manner. The book focuses on the first axis, which talks about the purpose of the sermon, its description, and the controls for its preparation, and the second axis, which deals with the characteristics of the preacher, his responsibilities, and his mistakes. The book aims to develop religious rhetoric and enhance its role in spreading the Islamic call and consolidating the correct doctrine among Muslims.
descriptions.1842: This book deals with the subject of takfir and bombing and the negative effects that result from them. It emphasizes that the ruling on takfir is legitimate and belongs to God and His Messenger, and that it is not permissible to issue a ruling on takfir except with an explicit text from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It also warns of the danger of rushing to issue takfir rulings and carrying out bombings, and the resulting bloodshed and destruction of facilities. The book aims to remove confusion in understanding the concept of atonement and explain its correct legal ruling.
descriptions.1843: This book deals with the subject of atonement from a legal perspective and the jurisprudence of the rules of prohibition and analysis in Islam. It focuses on the seriousness of the takfir ruling, its consequent legal rulings, and its impact on Muslim society. He warns against rushing to issue a ruling on takfir without conclusive evidence, and explains that takfir is a legal ruling attributed to God and His Messenger, so clear evidence of disbelief must be available before issuing a ruling on takfir. The book seeks to remove confusion in understanding the concept of atonement and explain its correct legal ruling.
descriptions.1844: The book, “Christian Claims regarding the Coming of Christ (peace be upon him),” by Saud bin Abdulaziz Al-Khalaf, deals with a comparative study of Christians’ claims about the coming of Christ at the end of time. The author explains the Christians' turmoil on this issue and discusses the sources they rely on, indicating that they are not fixed and their meaning is not clear. The book also addresses the response to these claims by analyzing the texts on which they rely, and aims to clarify the correct understanding of the religion of Islam on this subject.
descriptions.1845: This book deals with a defense of the call of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab by responding to the accusations and suspicions attached to it. The author, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad Al Abdul Latif, focuses on denying the allegations of distortion or extremism directed at the sheikh, and points out that the call is based on pure monotheism and following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book is divided into multiple sections to discuss the various accusations and suspicions about the call, while providing scientific and jurisprudential responses to them.
descriptions.1846: This book, “The Preacher’s Guide,” by Naji bin Dayel Al-Sultan, deals with the subject of preaching to Islam and the etiquette of preachers, providing advice and guidance for those who wish to spread the Islamic faith and communicate it in the best way. The book focuses on the personal qualities and etiquette of the preacher, how to deal with people and protect oneself from faults, in addition to effective preaching methods and choosing appropriate topics for the audience of listeners. The book is a useful reference for novice and veteran preachers alike, as it collects the author's long experiences in the field of advocacy and presents them in an integrated, methodological form.
descriptions.1847: This book addresses the role of the media in promoting Islamic solidarity, indicating the importance of unity among Muslims in accordance with the principles of the Islamic faith. The author focuses on how to use the media as an effective tool to unite ranks and spread the spirit of brotherhood among the members of the Islamic nation, reviewing different media methods and how to employ them to achieve Islamic advocacy goals.
descriptions.1848: The book deals with the role of the Muslim and his message in the last third of the twentieth century, reviewing intellectual and advocacy ideas about the responsibility of the Muslim in this era. It contains two lectures given by the author in Damascus, the first entitled (The Role of the Muslim in the Last Third of the Twentieth Century), and the second (The Muslim’s Message in the Last Third of the Twentieth Century).
descriptions.1849: The book deals with the role of the Muslim and his message in the last third of the twentieth century, reviewing intellectual and advocacy ideas related to the conditions of Muslims in this era. It contains two lectures given by Malek Bennabi in Damascus in 1972, the first entitled “The Role of the Muslim in the Last Third of the Twentieth Century” and the second “The Muslim’s Message in the Last Third of the Twentieth Century.”
descriptions.1850: This book is a response to the fallacies and suspicions contained in the Hebrew Encyclopedia about Islam and its Messenger ﷺ. The author Musa Al-Basit addresses the claims of the Orientalists and denies the false allegations, based on legal and scientific evidence. It focuses on clarifying Islamic truths and demonstrating the greatness of the Prophet’s message, relying on an objective scientific approach far from emotional reaction.
descriptions.1851: The letter “A Message to Male and Female Teachers” by its author, Abu Bakr Ahmed Al-Sayyid, deals with the topic of Islamic advocacy and its importance in the field of education. The message focuses on how male and female teachers guide their students towards faith and piety by teaching them various sciences and knowledge, while emphasizing the importance of the intention of calling to God in all the education they provide. It also emphasizes the role of the teacher as a caretaker of his students and responsible for them, warning of the importance of holding oneself accountable for the words and actions that affect them. The message aims to explain how to transform classrooms into platforms for sound advocacy, while maintaining the credibility of science and knowledge.
descriptions.1852: The book “Zad the Caller to God” deals with the topic of calling to God and the mechanisms for spreading the correct doctrine among people. The author focuses on providing the preacher with the education and knowledge necessary to convey the message, while emphasizing the importance of wisdom and good morals in dealing with the addressees. It also stresses the necessity of breaking the psychological and social barriers that may stand in the way of advocacy, and rejecting hatred and harshness in dealing with those who disagree with one’s opinion. The book was written by Ibn Uthaymeen, and falls within the classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims.
descriptions.1853: This book deals with the characteristics of believers in the face of temptations and fluctuations in circumstances, and reviews ten important characteristics related to morals and dealing with leadership, scholars, and temptations, with an emphasis on the importance of returning to the people of knowledge and adhering to the fundamentals of religion. The author begins with a call to praise and thank God for His blessings, then moves to an introduction in which he calls for referring to the people of knowledge when in doubt or change, and stresses the importance of sound knowledge and the sound approach in confronting doubts and suspects.
descriptions.1854: This book aims to deny the accusations directed against Islam that it is a violent and terrorist religion, and refutes those claims promoted by some anti-Islamic parties in Europe and elsewhere. The author, Abdul-Azim Al-Mutani, focuses on the tolerance of Islam in calling to God and relationships with others, reviewing verses from the Holy Qur’an and events from the Prophet’s biography to show that Islam is a tolerant religion that calls for peaceful coexistence with the People of the Book and the polytheists. The book also addresses the positions of peaceful Islamic advocacy in the civil era and defends the image of Islam as a religion that respects freedoms and calls for tolerance and harmony among people.
descriptions.1855: The book “The Ladder of Ethics of Prophecy” by Dr. Mahmoud Muhammad Gharib deals with an in-depth study of the morals of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his praiseworthy qualities, deriving its material from the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book aims to present an integrated model of the morals of the Islamic message and how to acquire and apply them in a Muslim’s daily life. He also focuses on the importance of raising generations on these morals, considering this one of the greatest prophetic miracles.
descriptions.1856: This book deals with the subject of the Sunnah of the Prophet and its importance in Islamic legislation, and presents the position of the Qur’anists on the Sunnah and their doubts about it. The author explains the position of the Sunnah in legislation and its evidence, and reviews the historical roots of the deniers of the Sunnah and their most famous sects, with a focus on the Quranist sect, their suspicions, and reactions to them. The book is a type of religious scientific book that aims to clarify the concept of the Sunnah and explain its importance in Islam.
descriptions.1857: The book “Doubts of the Qur’anists” by Othman bin Sheikh Ali addresses the topic of the relationship between the Qur’an and the Sunnah in the correct understanding of the religion of Islam. The author focuses on the necessity of adopting the Sunnah of the Prophet for a sound understanding of the Qur’an, reviews the efforts of predecessors in defending the authority of the Sunnah, and discusses the ruling on those who deny its authority. The book also presents a series of doubts raised by methodologists regarding the Qur’an only, and provides a response to them with the aim of clarifying the validity of following the Sunnah with the Qur’an.
descriptions.1858: Conditions of the Renaissance is a book by the Islamic thinker Malek Bennabi, published in French in 1949 AD under the title (in French: les Conditions de la Renaissance). It was translated into Arabic by Abdel Sabour Shaheen and Omar Kamel Misqawi under the supervision of the author, and it was published in Arabic in 1957 AD. The second edition was published in 1960 with some additions and modifications by the author in response to comments and questions from readers of the first edition. It is a book that stems from the Islamic intellectual dimension, through which the author attempts to provide basic foundations and concepts that will help rebuild (colonized) Asian and African societies and get them out of the pitfalls of backwardness and dependency. …
descriptions.1859: This book is from the “My Son” series by Mahmoud Muhammad Gharib, and aims to clarify aspects of Islamic law, especially those related to punishments. In a simplified scientific dialogue with different personalities, the author addresses topics such as the divine aspect and the diligent aspect of Sharia law, and points out the importance of distinguishing between them. It also emphasizes the Islamic principles of justice and transparency in the application of punishments, while emphasizing the importance of repentance and mercy in the penal system. The book aims to simplify the understanding of Islamic law and its principles for readers through an enjoyable and simplified dialogue.
descriptions.1860: This book deals with the conflicts of religious thought with materialism and atheists in the modern era, and reviews the challenges of belief in God and the Last Day in light of contemporary scientific and philosophical claims. The author focuses on discussing the ideas of prominent thinkers such as Bertrand Russell and Freud, and also discusses the issue of what Al-Azm called the tragedy of Satan. The book aims to refute the claims of atheists and refute their theses about the conflict between Islam and science, and emphasizes that scientific facts ultimately move towards compatibility with religious concepts.
descriptions.1861: This book deals with the issue of the punishment for apostasy from Islam by discussing the legal evidence and confronting the suspicions raised against it. The author focuses on refuting the fallacies promoted by those who deny the punishment of apostasy, reviewing various suspicions and the evidence to respond to them based on the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book also discusses the jurisprudential dispute over some details of apostasy and denies allegations of distorting the events of the era of the Prophet related to it.
descriptions.1862: The book deals with the relationship of the Christian Crusader camp with Muslims throughout history, reviewing its basic starting points and causes, whether original or accidental. It also examines the present of this relationship and the extent to which it has been influenced by its past, as well as the Christian Crusader camp’s view of Muslims today and whether it is unified or disparate between its countries, peoples and institutions.
descriptions.1863: This book, “Ghayat Al-Maqsood fi Al-Ra’d Al-Tari’a Al-Maqsud fi Al-Ra’id Al-Tari’a Al-Maqsood Al-Maghribi” by Al-Sawwal bin Yahya Al-Maghribi, deals with responding to the falsehoods of Christians and Jews and refuting their statements that contradict religious truths. The author focuses on proving the validity of Islam and abrogating its previous laws, drawing inferences from the same biblical texts on which they rely, and aims to support them with rational and textual argument. The book also dissects some of their mistaken beliefs and their changes in religious texts, highlighting the virtues of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.1864: This book deals with the jurisprudence of advocacy through the hadiths contained in Sahih Al-Bukhari, as it focuses on analyzing the hadiths related to the most important advocacy and social issues in Islam. The author deals with topics such as commandments and their rulings, relying on a scientific methodology to study and analyze hadiths, with the aim of extracting lessons and lessons that can benefit preachers and Muslims in their daily lives.
descriptions.1865: The book “Shells of Truth” by Dr. Muhammad Al-Ghazali deals with various topics related to intellectual and religious conflict in Islamic societies. The book focuses on discussing the challenges facing Islam by thinkers and groups that attempt to question its foundations and teachings, and defends the Islamic message and its law. The book also addresses specific intellectual and scientific issues that some slanderers try to use to distort the image of Islam, and presents an integrated religious vision that includes belief, law, and social life. The book aims to strengthen the status of Islam and its teachings in Islamic societies and protect them from distortion and distortion.
descriptions.1866: This book addresses the issue of violence in contemporary Islamic work through a scientific dialogue between a group of authors. The book focuses on analyzing the causes of the phenomenon of violence in Islamic societies, and ways to address it in accordance with Islamic law, while preserving the unity of the Muslim ranks. The book is divided into several sections that discuss the origins and causes, the mechanisms of sound denial, parties and groups, the sedition of takfir, the application of Sharia law in Islamic countries, and finally the effects and consequences of violence.
descriptions.1867: This book deals with the subject of the perfection of the Islamic religion, its truth and its advantages, indicating that Islam is the religion accepted by God and reviewing its pillars and teachings. The author focuses on the tolerance of Islam and the ease of its teachings, considering it a complete religion that includes everything people need in their religious and material lives. It also points out the importance of calling to Islam and explaining its purposes and virtues, while emphasizing the necessity of acting according to its apparent and hidden laws.
descriptions.1868: This book, “Detectors of Deceptions,” by Abd al-Rahman Habankah al-Maidani, is a scientific, critical, and analytical study of contemporary intellectual schools of thought from an Islamic perspective. The book discusses false opinions and ideas coming to the Islamic nation, reviewing the means of deception used to promote them, and also reviewing slanders that are promoted against religion and morals. The book also studies imams and partial schools of thought in various sciences, and analyzes dialectical fallacies and slanders that aim to destroy the foundations of religion and morals in society.
descriptions.1869: The book “How to Call People” by Muhammad Qutb deals with the topic of the call to God and the responsibility of the Islamic nation in spreading the message of Islam. The author focuses on the importance of advocacy in our current era, considering that it is a task of building more than just a reminder, given the collapse of the foundations of Islamic understanding and practice in the nation. The book also addresses the challenges facing preachers in the face of ignorance of religion and the spread of temptations, relying on Qur’anic texts and Prophetic hadiths to support its ideas.
descriptions.1870: The book “Glimpses into Islamic Culture” by Muhammad Omar Odeh Al-Khatib deals with the topic of Islamic culture and its characteristics, reviewing the concept of culture in general and its importance in the lives of nations, then moving on to detailing the pillars of Islamic culture and its unique characteristics that distinguish it from other cultures. The author focuses on the importance of this culture in protecting Muslims from the negative influences of other cultures, and enhancing their Islamic identity and social cohesion. The book also addresses the relationship between culture and civilization in the Islamic context, and calls for the resumption of an Islamic life based on the principles of religion and its law.
descriptions.1871: What did the world lose with the decline of Muslims? It is a book written by the Islamic thinker and preacher Abu al-Hasan al-Nadawi. It revolves around an important idea, which is the role of Islam in leading humanity, and the impact of the decline in the role of Muslims on the world. The author spoke about the state of the world before Islam, its East and its West, its Arabs and its non-Arabs, and explained that it was living in complete darkness, until the message of Islam came, which transformed the pagan Arabs, who were divided and quarreling among themselves, into a nation, in fact, the best nation ever brought forth for mankind. {You were the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right And you forbid evil and believe in God...} (110) Surah Al Imran.
descriptions.1872: The book “Lectures on Christianity” by Dr. Muhammad Abu Zahra deals with an objective study of Christianity from an Islamic perspective, reviewing its history, origins, and development throughout the ages. The author focuses on Christianity as it appeared in the Holy Qur’an, then moves on to discuss Christianity after Jesus (peace be upon him), comparing the Islamic vision with the current Christian vision. The book also deals with the philosophy and thought that influenced Christianity, relying in its research on Christian and Islamic sources, and aims to present scientific facts far from religious attacks or harassment.
descriptions.1873: This book deals with the topic of Muhammad ﷺ from the perspective of the Torah, the Bible, and the Qur’an, reviewing the prophecies of the previous prophets and their explanations about the coming of the Noble Messenger. The author focuses on clarifying the divine truths related to Muhammad and explaining them to Christians and Jews, using verses from the three heavenly books. The book aims to show the deservingness of Ishmael's descendants to the final prophetic message, and calls on the People of the Book to follow the straight path mentioned in the Holy Quran.
descriptions.1874: The book “The School of Da’wah” by Muhammad al-Sayyid al-Wakil deals with the topic of the first Islamic call to Mecca, focusing on Dar al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam as the first school of da’wah, where the Messenger ﷺ taught the first generation the correct doctrine and removed traces of paganism from their hearts. The book focuses on the characteristics of the Dawa school, which was characterized by a complete divine curriculum, concerned with correcting the doctrine and awakening the meaning of resurrection in souls, and focused on the worship of God and sincere obedience to Him.
descriptions.1875: Contemporary Intellectual Doctrines, a book written by Muhammad Qutb. The book, which came in 654 pages, dealt with criticism and analysis of seven basic doctrines and ideologies, namely: communism, democracy, secularism, rationalism, nationalism, patriotism, humanism, and atheism, and the reasons for their spread among Muslims, and their dangers to their identity, with their applications in politics, ethics, economics, art, and ethics, while mentioning Islam’s position on each of them. In the introduction to the book, he presents the reasons that led to the spread of doctrines, ideas, beliefs, and superstitions.
descriptions.1876: This book addresses the topic of the responsibility of Islamic countries in spreading the Islamic call and conveying the message of Islam, with a focus on the experience of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as a model. The author, Abdullah bin Abdul Mohsen Al Turki, deals with the dimensions of the call in Islam and its relationship with the state and the nation. He discusses the development of this topic throughout Islamic history and the challenges the call has faced in the modern era, especially the influence of Western thought on Islamic societies. It also refers to the efforts made by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in this field.
descriptions.1877: This book addresses the issue of the imam's responsibility in the mosque from a religious and social perspective. The author focuses on the definition of the Imamate and its virtues, discusses the ideal qualities of the Imam and his choice, then moves on to detail the various responsibilities of the Imam according to his position and knowledge, with an emphasis on the importance of adhering to the Prophet’s guidance and wisdom in rhetoric and guidance. The book aims to explain the multiple roles of the imam in Muslim society and how to perform these roles efficiently and responsibly.
descriptions.1878: The book deals with the problems of preaching and the conditions of preachers in the modern era, reviewing the experiences of prophets and messengers in confronting injustice and ignorance. The author focuses on the reality of preaching in different eras, comparing the problems faced by preachers in the past and present, and reviewing the challenges that Islamic preaching has faced throughout the ages, with a focus on the role of the preacher and his means in facing challenges and difficulties.
descriptions.1879: The book “The Term of Educational Philosophy in Light of the Islamic Curriculum” by Dr. Khalid bin Hamid Al-Hazmi deals with a critical study of the term “educational philosophy” in the Islamic context, reviewing Western influences on educational thought in the Islamic world and their negative effects on Islamic principles. The book focuses on the contradictions of Western educational philosophy with the Islamic faith, and discusses attempts to reconcile Islamic and Western values, highlighting the fundamental errors that may result from blind imitation of Western curricula in the field of education.
descriptions.1880: This book deals with the concept of wisdom in the context of the call to God, defining wisdom and explaining its components and importance in the call. The author focuses on how to apply wisdom in dealing with invitees, by understanding their nature and classes, and taking into account the appropriate circumstances for presenting the invitation, while providing practical advice on effective methods of guidance and counselling. The book aims to enhance hope and certainty among preachers, and motivate them to awaken a sense of responsibility among those called to correct their paths and refine their morals.
descriptions.1881: The book “The Friday Pulpit is a Trust and a Responsibility” by Dr. Abdullah bin Muhammad Al Hamid deals with the topic of preaching in mosques, focusing on the importance of the Friday pulpit and the preacher’s responsibility towards it. The book covers the etiquette of standing on the pulpit, mistakes to avoid, and suggestions regarding preparing and drafting the sermon. The author emphasizes that a successful preacher is one who is careful and careful in his sermons, avoids previous mistakes, and seeks innovation and diversity in the methods and styles of his sermons. The book aims to provide a comprehensive overview of how to deliver a sermon effectively and effectively.
descriptions.1882: This book is a method for preparing the Friday sermon. It deals with the topics of public speaking and the importance of the preacher in society. It reviews the definition, purposes, and types of the sermon, with a focus on how to prepare the sermon, its structure, and its elements. It also addresses the qualities and etiquette of the preacher and how to influence the listeners. The author aims to provide a comprehensive contribution in this field, taking into account the importance of innovation and innovation in rhetoric without compromising the established principles of Islamic preaching.
descriptions.1883: This book deals with the topics of the Friday sermon and their importance in guiding the Islamic nation and achieving its interests. It reviews the rules and controls necessary for choosing sermon topics and delivering them effectively. The author focuses on establishing the rules of what is said in the Friday sermon and organizing its parts, while providing practical advice to mosque preachers on how to choose topics, prepare them, and present them in a useful and influential way to worshipers.
descriptions.1884: The book, “A Call to the Vatican: Review Your Holy Books,” deals with an objective discussion of the Islamic religious doctrine in relation to other heavenly religions, focusing on the Torah and the Gospel. Author Mustafa Abdel Latif Darwish emphasizes that all heavenly books call for the worship of God alone, with sub-differences in religious rites and rituals. The book also addresses the issue of distortion attributed to the heavenly books that preceded the Qur’an, and calls for a reconsideration of the original texts of those books by believers in other religions.
descriptions.1885: The book, “A Look at the Concept of Terrorism and the Position on It in Islam,” by Abdul Rahman Al-Matroudi, deals with a scientific study of the concept of terrorism and its multiple definitions, relying on an Islamic perspective in analyzing its causes, roots, and ways to combat it. The book studies terrorism from different perspectives, including linguistic and terminological, and compares Western definitions with the Islamic definition of the concept of terrorism. The book also addresses Islam's position on terrorism and its principles in combating it, and reviews international efforts to combat terrorism and the role of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in this context.
descriptions.1886: This book, “This is your Prophet, my son,” by the writer Mahmoud Muhammad Gharib, deals with a study in the Islamic faith by analyzing some of the events that occurred in the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author aims to clarify the Islamic faith and remove suspicions about it, focusing on the great contribution that the Prophet made to the Islamic call and his application of the provisions of Sharia even in his private life. The book falls within the classification of advocacy and the conditions of Muslims, and reviews the need for messengers in the world and their role in transforming morals into practical behavior.
descriptions.1887: The book “Etiquette of Scholars and Learners” by Al-Hussein bin Al-Mansur Al-Yamani deals with etiquette and rules of conduct for scholars and learners in their scientific and educational fields. The book focuses on clarifying how the scholar deals with his knowledge and with his students, and how the learner should deal with his sheikh and his books. The author divides the book into chapters that address various topics related to the etiquette of science and learning, with a focus on the scholar’s ​​intention in teaching and preserving knowledge, and the necessity of humility and serenity in transmitting knowledge.
descriptions.1888: The book “Asbab al-Mughafir” by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali deals with the virtues of supplication, seeking forgiveness, and monotheism as one of the most important reasons for the forgiveness of sins before God Almighty. The author focuses on the conditions for successful supplication and the benefits of complete seeking forgiveness, while emphasizing the importance of monotheism in purity of the heart and forgiveness of sins. Ibn Rajab cites prophetic hadiths to support his thesis on these spiritual and worship topics.
descriptions.1889: This book deals with the topic of benefiting from the month of Ramadan to strengthen faith and morals, showing how to revive the heart and maintain integrity throughout the year. The author focuses on the importance of taking advantage of spiritual opportunities during this holy month, and provides practical advice on acts of worship and morals that can be practiced to achieve this goal. The book is divided into sections that talk about fasting, reading the Qur’an, prayers, seclusion, supplication, charity and other acts of worship, with a focus on how to self-account and spiritual growth during the holy month.
descriptions.1890: The book, “Where is the way out, for the rock has closed the cave” addresses the challenges facing the Islamic nation in today’s world, and calls for a return to the Qur’an as a source of guidance and guidance. Author Magdi Al-Hilali focuses on the necessity of strengthening faith and understanding the true value of the Qur’an in the life of a Muslim, considering that the real cure for the nation’s problems lies in returning to the teachings of the true religion. The author uses the example of the people of the cave to encourage the reader to hold on to hope and trust in God in the face of difficulties.
descriptions.1891: This book deals with the topic of the hijab and the legal controls that protect the mind and religion from the whispers of Satan and the delusions of love and passion. The author focuses on three main doors through which temptations enter: sight, hearing, and singing. He cites hadiths, Quranic verses, and stories from biography and history to demonstrate the danger of opening these doors to the individual and society. The book is a type of religious educational book that aims to develop morals and consolidate Islamic values ​​in the hearts of Muslims.
descriptions.1892: The book “The Qur’an is the Secret of Our Renaissance” by Dr. Magdy Al-Hilali deals with the topic of the relationship between the Holy Qur’an and the renaissance of the Islamic nation, reviewing how the Qur’an can be an incentive for progress and advancement. The author focuses on the uniqueness of the Nation of Islam and its specificity before God Almighty, considering that the path to its renaissance must differ from the paths of renaissance of other nations. Al-Hilali emphasizes the importance of returning to the Qur’an as a main source of spiritual and intellectual strength, stressing the need to rearrange priorities and link material progress with spiritual and faith commitment.
descriptions.1893: The book deals with Islamic etiquette related to the daily behavior of a Muslim in various aspects of his life, covering aspects including entering and leaving the house, eating and drinking etiquette, supplications for sneezing and yawning, toilet etiquette, sleeping and waking up, dress and adornment, and road and mosque etiquette. It aims to strengthen the Muslim’s spiritual and doctrinal connection through guidance and supplications related to personal activities, emphasizing the importance of these supplications in achieving psychological reassurance and spiritual comfort.
descriptions.1894: This book, “Useful Etiquette with Selected and Comprehensive Words,” by Ibn Shams Al-Khilafah, deals with the topics of etiquette, morals, wisdom, and proverbs, deriving its content from legal texts and the sayings of the wise and imams. The book focuses on providing advice and ideas on how to behave and deal with life and others, using famous phrases and sayings of important historical figures. The book aims to educate the reader through wisdom and advice, relying on a mixture of religious and philosophical guidance.
descriptions.1895: The book deals with the topic of ethics in Islam and discusses its philosophical and practical dimensions, indicating that it is a divine-human system that aims to direct human behavior towards goodness and virtue. It focuses on the importance of ethics in Islam as the essence of the message and the spirit of the religion, linking it to faith, worship, and transactions. It also addresses the types of innate and acquired morality and the effects of their stability in the life of the individual and society, and reviews important Islamic moral values ​​such as justice, modesty, and forbearance.
descriptions.1896: This book by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim deals with philosophical and spiritual topics related to the study of the internal organs of man and the soul, with a focus on the characteristics of the heart, chest, soul, and Satan. The book also deals with spiritual interpretations of some names and religious matters, such as the interpretation of the names of Abraham, Satan, and the olive tree. The author focuses on describing knowledge, light, and the creation of Adam (peace be upon him), while providing a deep insight into the structure of the human soul and its relationship with the spiritual world.
descriptions.1897: This book deals with the topic of night prayer and dawn prayer, and reviews the reasons for assistance in performing them. The author, Ruqayyah Al-Muhareb, focuses on the importance of these two acts of worship in the life of a Muslim, and discusses the spiritual and material benefits of them. He also mentions the reasons that encourage night prayers and urges people to attend the dawn prayer in congregation, and reviews the effects of abandoning them. The book contains an introduction and a conclusion, and is divided into chapters that address various topics related to the night prayer and the dawn prayer, including encouragement and intimidation in performing them, and hadiths and sayings contained in the virtue of the night prayer.
descriptions.1898: This book deals with the topic of affliction and how supplications can benefit from it, reviewing the causes of affliction and its various forms. The author emphasizes that affliction is a fixed year in the life of vocations, and that it is an opportunity to benefit and grow, indicating the importance of a deep and integrated analysis of affliction cases to understand their dimensions and implications. The book focuses on providing a comprehensive and integrated view of the phenomenon of affliction, while clarifying the benefits that advocacy can reap through it.
descriptions.1899: This is scientific research that deals with the topic of crying in the light of the Qur’an and Sunnah, and is classified among the books of gentleness, etiquette, and remembrance. The research aims to extrapolate the types of crying mentioned in the legal texts, dividing them into three categories: praiseworthy crying, such as crying out of fear of God and when reading the Qur’an, reprehensible crying, such as wailing and pretending, and permissible crying, such as crying of sadness, pain, and longing. The research relies on the inductive approach to the verses and hadiths of the Prophet, limited to examples from the six books for each meaning.
descriptions.1900: The book deals with the topic of Bluetooth technology and its various effects on daily life, reviewing the history of the name Bluetooth and the development of its use. The book also raises fundamental questions about the benefits and risks of this technology, and reviews its applications in various fields from communication to games and entertainment. The book aims to encourage serious dialogue about modern technology and its effects on society.
descriptions.1901: The book “Educational Balance and Its Importance for Every Muslim” by Majdi Al-Hilali deals with the topic of education from an Islamic perspective, defining its importance and its various dimensions in the life of the individual and society. The author focuses on understanding the meaning and goals of education, and how to achieve educational integration in various fields, while pointing out the challenges that may stand in the way of positive soil results. The book also addresses the religious and educational importance of reflection and useful knowledge, stressing the necessity of educating individuals and societies on a sound moral and ethical basis.
descriptions.1902: This book deals with daily lessons from the Sunnah and Sharia rulings, focusing on educating people and disseminating the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in an easy-to-understand manner, with a constant link to the Qur’an and Sunnah. It deals with multiple topics from sincerity and intention to monotheism and trust, as well as the importance of preserving times and warning against hypocrisy and polytheism. The author aims to educate Muslims to relate to the Qur’an and Sunnah and to refer to them as the only legal source.
descriptions.1903: This book, “The Precious Dhikr” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen, deals with the supplications that a Muslim should recite in the morning and evening. The author focuses on detailing these supplications, mentioning their benefits and fruits, and investigates the authenticity of the hadiths contained in them, taking into account the conditions he mentioned in the term hadith. The book is directed to all Muslims to urge them to adhere to these remembrances and make them a daily habit in their lives.
descriptions.1904: The book presents legal ruqyah through Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths, categorizing them into three sections: brief, medium, and long. It aims to treat incurable spiritual diseases such as witchcraft, the evil eye, and epilepsy, reviewing the opinions of scholars such as Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim in this field.
descriptions.1905: This book deals with the topic of happiness from an Islamic perspective, showing that happiness is not limited to the material aspect only, but extends beyond it to the spiritual and moral aspect. The book deals with the reasons for achieving happiness in this world and the hereafter, relying on the legal texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah, and stresses the importance of faith, good deeds, and virtuous morals in achieving true happiness.
descriptions.1906: This book deals with the topic of worship in Islam and includes its definition and inclusion of all of life, its goals and its impact on the individual and society. It shows that worship goes beyond religious obligations to purify the heart and soul, achieve human freedom, and build a good society. It also addresses the principles of Islamic reform related to worship, and mentions the effects of worship in the life of a Muslim.
descriptions.1907: The book “Reason and Passion” by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim is a literary-spiritual work that sets an analytical framework for the mind and its counterparts to passion, based on a list of fifty assistants to the mind. The book deals with detailed explanations of the concepts of understanding, sight, knowledge, certainty, jurisprudence, endowment, dream, inspiration, sincerity, humility, generosity, and correctness, with an explanation of their opposition to passion. The work falls within the classification of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances, and adopts a systematic approach in presenting the differences between reason and passion.
descriptions.1908: The book “Returning to the Qur’an Why and How” by the writer Majdi Al-Hilali is concerned with explaining the reasons for the revelation of the Qur’an and its role in guiding man, based on chapters dealing with the creation of Adam, Satan, heavenly messages, the concept of guidance, and introducing man to the mind, soul, and heart, in addition to directing the reader to how to restore the relationship with the Qur’an. It is classified under Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, which highlights its literary and spiritual character that links moral jurisprudence and dhikr. The book aims to guide the reader to a deeper understanding of the Qur’an as a way of life that offers happiness in this world and the hereafter.
descriptions.1909: The book “The Qur’an and the Return of Glory” by Magdy Al-Hilali is concerned with religious and literary reflections on the state of the Islamic nation, based on existential questions that address the reason for abandoning God, God’s punishment, and what He wants from His servants, while directing the reader to the Qur’an as a solution and a source of influence. It includes content that includes motivational messages, fictional historical passages, and discussions about people’s negligence and love of the world, and falls under the classification of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances.
descriptions.1910: This book, “Islamic Values,” is concerned with analyzing and interpreting the concept of value in Islam, with a focus on the necessary and basic value in Islam, which is justice. The author shows that justice is the straight scale that distributes rights and shares, and provides an example of the importance of justice in Islam, as he points out that justice is the foundation of the world and religion, and the reason for the well-being of the people and the country. It also highlights that justice is one of the most important pillars of happiness in people’s lives, and that people seek it in their lives, and that justice is necessary in Islam, and Islam works to prove and establish it among people.
descriptions.1911: The book “Al-Laali” by Imam Ibn Al-Jawzi is a collection of sermons and sermons arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, in which the author deals with religious and literary topics in a sophisticated form of rhetoric and statement. The book focuses on reminding us of God and His blessings, and calling for contemplation about the creation of the heavens and the earth, relying on Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths in its emphasis on the importance of faith and good deeds.
descriptions.1912: The book “Al-Latif” by the scholar Ibn al-Jawzi deals with multiple topics related to morals, etiquette, and remembrance, focusing on contemplating God’s signs, working for the afterlife, and warning against heedlessness of the Day of Resurrection. The book deals with topics such as sincerity, fear of God, and warning against the filth of the world, relying on Qur’anic texts and prophetic hadiths. The book is distinguished by its delicate style and subtle references that aim to apply the preaching to the heart before hearing it.
descriptions.1913: This book is a collection of selected prophetic sermons and sermons, aiming to strengthen a Muslim’s commitment to the teachings of the Islamic religion and their application in his daily life. The author focuses on the importance of the Noble Prophet’s Hadith as a primary source of jurisprudential legislation, and points out the close connection between the science of Hadith and Islamic jurisprudence. The book is designed as a curriculum for the first stage in the College of Islamic Sciences, and contains fifty authentic hadiths that deal with various aspects of life and worship.
descriptions.1914: Al-Manthur by Ibn al-Jawzi is a book that deals with refined topics in literature and remembrance, mixed with an aesthetic description of nature and its elements. The author focuses on glorifying the Creator through his precise description of the magnificence of creation in plants and animals, expressing God's greatness in reviving the dead and detailing nature in a sophisticated literary style. The book is rich in philosophical and spiritual reflections on creation and predestination, relying on beautiful descriptions of nature as a means of understanding the greatness of the Creator.
descriptions.1915: This book deals with the subject of advice in Islam from a comprehensive perspective, addressing advice to God Almighty, His Messenger ﷺ, His Book, and the general Muslims and their special ones. The author focuses on the importance of advice as part of faith, and points out that the greatest ignorance is a person's ignorance of himself. The book addresses various topics, such as following God’s commands, supporting religion, honoring the relatives of the Prophet, improving the recitation of the Qur’an, and defending the honor of Muslims. It also points out some of the diseases that may affect those who practice worship, along with providing advice to avoid and treat them.
descriptions.1916: The book “The Ruby” is a collection of Islamic sermons by Sheikh Ibn al-Jawzi, concerned with warning against sins and reminding the reader of the necessity of repentance and piety through contemplation of death, fear of God, and attention to good deeds. Its classification under Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance highlights its literary and devotional character, as it combines spiritual advice and moral etiquette. The author relies in his style on Qur’anic and Prophetic references to guide the reader to righteous behavior and self-purification.
descriptions.1917: The book “Dearing Parents” by Ibn al-Jawzi is concerned with explaining the concept of righteousness and respect for parents and linking that to family ties, based on legal texts and reason, and reviews the virtues of righteousness and its effects on lifespan and how to apply it. The book also addresses a warning against disobedience and its punishments, and provides practical instructions for righteousness after the death of parents and visiting their graves.
descriptions.1918: The book The Crescent Crescent on the Characteristics That Cause Shadows by Sheikh Al-Suyuti is a book of the type of Al-Riqaq, Al-Adab, and Remembrances. It collects and explains the hadiths of prophecy related to the qualities that God shades, along with their chain of transmission and an explanation of their state of health and weakness. The content is divided into sections that deal with seven famous qualities and then seven others, and is completed to seventy qualities with reference to the stated methods of shade. The work focuses on clarifying texts and reviewing their chains of transmission based on multiple hadith sources.
descriptions.1919: The joy of gatherings, the comfort of gatherings, and the sharpening of the obsessive mind (full title) is an encyclopedic literary book written by Imam Abu Omar Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Barr al-Nimri al-Qurtubi (d. 463 AH), one of the Andalusian scholars in the fifth century AH, and one of the Maliki hadith scholars and jurists.
descriptions.1920: The book “Achieving Connection between the Heart and the Qur’an” by Dr. Magdy Al-Hilali deals with the topic of the relationship between the heart, the human being, and the Qur’an, reviewing the importance of the Qur’an in correcting behavior and building faith. The author focuses on how to truly benefit from the Qur’an to build a strong individual and a cohesive nation, drawing his insights from the historical experiences of the first generation of Muslims. The book aims to alert the reader to the forgotten aspects of the Qur’an that many of those dealing with it may not pay attention to, expressing his hope that the Qur’an will become the main project for the renaissance of the Islamic nation.
descriptions.1921: The book “Soothing the Souls of Women and Men When They Lose Children” by Sheikh Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali is a book from the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrances. It aims to guide Muslims to patience and seeking reward when afflicted with loss, based on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths that show the value of patience in alleviating grief. The book includes an introduction that explains its purpose and approach, and includes a text linking faith and the ability to overcome psychological pain through trust in God. It is considered a literary and spiritual reference that entertains hearts and enhances confidence in God in times of distress.
descriptions.1922: The book “Tamheed Al-Farsh fi Al-Qualātīb al-Mābibībah Ḥaḥ al-Arsh” by Al-Suyuti is a book in the field of Al-Riqāq, etiquette, and dhikr. It focuses on collecting and organizing hadiths related to the seven whom God shades under the shadow of His throne, with reference to seven other hadiths and seventy weak hadiths. The text includes explanations and evidence of these qualities, and presents them in poetic verses according to the classification of Sheikh Abu Shama and Sheikh Ibn Hajar. The author aims to clarify the rules and foundations on which these hadiths are based and to show the shadowy evidence of each hadith.
descriptions.1923: The book “Islamic Instructions by Abdullah bin Hamid” is a book that includes a group of religious texts that focus on calling to God with wisdom and beautiful preaching, and reviews the virtues of Islam and the importance of adhering to the unity of the nation, in addition to the instructions it contains about the provisions of Hajj. It is classified under the category of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances. The book aims to guide scholars and guardians of religion to perform their duty of guidance and advocacy, based on what is stated in the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.1924: The book, “So We Don’t Lose Ramadan,” by Magdy Al-Hilali, aims to remind the reader of the importance of achieving the true purpose of religious worship, comparing this to a patient visiting the doctor and taking medications. Al-Hilali emphasizes that living the heart with faith is the primary goal, and that worship is merely a means to achieving this goal, warning against turning the means into goals in themselves. It invites the reader to contemplate the spiritual depth of worship and understand the purpose behind it, so that this is reflected in his behavior and daily dealings during the month of Ramadan and other days of the year.
descriptions.1925: This book deals with the issue of the inviolability of a Muslim to another Muslim and discusses many of the moral and religious violations that may occur between people, such as backbiting, gossiping, lying, hatred, envy, and other sins. The author focuses on the importance of keeping one's tongue, practicing Islamic morals, and avoiding offending others, recalling the seriousness of violating a Muslim's sanctity and how it contradicts the tolerant teachings of Islam. The book aims to remind the reader of the importance of respecting the rights of others and achieving justice and compassion in dealing with them.
descriptions.1926: The book “The Truth about Slavery” by Majdi Al-Hilali deals with the topic of servitude to God Almighty and discusses its meanings and importance in the life of a Muslim. The book focuses on the difference between worship and slavery, and calls for the importance of adhering to form and content in worship, focusing on the true meanings of slavery in the heart. The book aims to clarify the reality of slavery and how to achieve it in our daily lives, while highlighting the danger of rebellion against this slavery and the danger of paying attention to form rather than content in worship.
descriptions.1927: This book tells the stories of people from various religious and cultural backgrounds who have converted to Islam from their previous beliefs, whether ecclesiastical, theological, or scientific. Author Abdul Rahman Mahmoud examines the lives of religious figures and former missionaries from Egypt, Africa, America and Asia, and refers to their spiritual journey towards Islam, providing an in-depth look at their personal experiences and religious transformations.
descriptions.1928: A letter to my brother in God by Dr. Magdy Al-Hilali deals with the topic of brotherhood in God, its nature, and its importance in the life of a Muslim. The author focuses on clarifying what helps to strengthen and purify this relationship, and what may disturb its peace, relying on the thoughts that came to his mind about this topic. The book aims to provide practical advice to strengthen brotherhood in God and protect it from breakage or deterioration, while at the same time reviewing the importance of this relationship in Islam.
descriptions.1929: This book deals with topics related to marital happiness and the good treatment of each other by spouses. The author focuses on providing practical advice to couples to strengthen their relationship and improve their morals. The book includes topics such as choosing a husband and wife, the qualities of a good husband, ways to improve morals, and the common rights of spouses. The book aims to guide couples towards building a happy marital life based on the teachings of Islam.
descriptions.1930: The book Salwat al-Ahzan, to avoid sitting with juveniles and women, by the writer Al-Mashtouli, falls within the category of gentleness, etiquette, and remembrance, and relies on the topics of monotheism, ethics of speech, and behavior to guide the reader towards staying away from illicit mixing and promoting spiritual integrity. His book includes chapters dealing with the prohibition of sitting with juveniles and women, the principles of monotheism, etiquette of the tongue, and practical advice for staying away from sin, making it a reference for those seeking moral and religious guidance.
descriptions.1931: Explanation of the memetic system in legal literature by the scholar Hafez Hakami. It is a work presented by Abd al-Karim al-Khudair in which he explains the memetic verses that deal with the commandments and scientific etiquette in religion. It deals with the topics of the commandment according to the Book of God, the commandment according to the Sunnah, the religious duties and instruments, and the warning against innovated sciences, with a conclusion that seeks to obtain the beneficial fruits of knowledge. The book falls under the category of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, and is automatically numbered according to the lesson system.
descriptions.1932: Explanation of the Book of Knowledge by Abu Khaythamah by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudair is an interpretation and commentary on the work of Abu Khaythamah Zuhair bin Harb al-Nasa’i, known as the Book of Knowledge, in which the commentator focuses on the importance of seeking legal knowledge as a beacon that urges the learner to fear and religious commitment. This work falls within the category of Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrance, and is presented in the form of sequential lessons that highlight the etiquette of seeking knowledge and the sayings of the predecessors in this field. The text aims to motivate the reader to gain more knowledge and avoid complacency, while highlighting the value of science as an essential part of a person’s spiritual capital.
descriptions.1933: The book “Sabra Al Yasser” by Dr. Magdi Al-Hilali deals with the topic of trials and tribulations in the lives of preachers, reviewing their positive and negative effects and how to benefit from them. The book focuses on the importance of self-analysis of afflictions and linking them to individual responsibility, with an emphasis on servitude to God and supplication to Him as a response to affliction. The book aims to direct preachers towards greater attachment to God and freeing themselves from attachment to anything other than Him, while presenting a positive outlook for benefiting from crises and tribulations in strengthening the call.
descriptions.1934: The book “Ten Characteristics for Women in Search of Beauty” by the writer Muhammad Al-Amari falls within the category of Al-Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrance, and provides detailed instructions on ten qualities that those seeking beauty should embrace, starting from cleanliness and washing to taking care of hair, clothes, kohl, perfume, and jewelry. Then he moves on to direct female readers to good manners and chastity, relying on Qur’anic quotations and Prophetic hadiths to show the importance of these behaviors in achieving complete beauty. The book aims to guide female readers to practices that combine external appearance and internal virtue.
descriptions.1935: The book “The Return of the Spirit and the Awakening of Faith” by the author Magdy Al-Hilali, which is one of the books of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, deals with the subject of the psychological defeat that befalls the individual and the Islamic nation, and examines its causes and dangerous effects on the present and the future. The book aims to instill hope in souls by emphasizing that everything is in God’s hands, and that renaissance is possible with sincere determination and trust in Him, reviewing concepts such as the law of causality, trust, and divine supply.
descriptions.1936: This book, “Fasl Al-Khattab fi Asceticism, Softness, and Etiquette,” by Sheikh Muhammad Nasr al-Din Muhammad Uwaydah, deals with the subject of asceticism, gentleness, and Islamic manners. The author focuses on defining asceticism and explaining its truth and divisions, mentioning its virtues and wisdom. He also presents the topic of death and the benefits of mentioning it, and warns against loving the world and the danger of being infatuated with it. The book aims to remind the reader of the importance of asceticism in the life of a Muslim and its role in achieving the pleasure of God Almighty.
descriptions.1937: The book “The Preference of the Knowledge of the Salaf over the Successor” by Sheikh Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali is concerned with clarifying the value of the knowledge that the predecessors had compared to the knowledge that was transmitted to subsequent generations, based on Qur’anic texts and religious sayings to classify knowledge into useful and useless. In his chapters, the author reviews the meanings of knowledge, and opens a door to clarify the difference between useful knowledge that pleases God and knowledge that does not bring benefit, with reference to examples from the stories of the prophets. The book is classified under the literature of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, and is arranged automatically to facilitate benefiting from it.
descriptions.1938: The book “Treasures of the Prophetic Sunnah” by writer Bari Irfan Tawfiq is a selection of authentic and good hadiths dealing with the virtues of remembrance, blessings upon the Prophet, the Qur’an, and various acts of worship such as fasting, night prayers, and supplication. The content is arranged according to chapters that deal with the morning and evening remembrances, the times of praise, the virtues of silence, Hajj and Umrah, and other literary and spiritual topics. The author aims to revive the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and guide the reader to apply it in his daily life. The book is a reference for those interested in Islamic etiquette and dhikr.
descriptions.1939: The book “Be Helpers in Goodness” by the writer Muhammad Saleh Al-Munajjid is concerned with clarifying the concept of assistance and cooperation in Islam from a linguistic and legal perspective, explaining the difference between righteousness and piety on the one hand and sin and aggression on the other hand, and based on Qur’anic verses and jurisprudential sayings. It sheds light on the principles and controls of cooperation and reviews its various fields such as advocacy, establishing worship, building mosques, seeking knowledge, and charitable activities, while warning against cooperation in sin and heresies. It aims to revive the spirit of cooperation in righteousness and goodness in light of the spread of evil and the lack of helpers, calling for unifying efforts to achieve the common good.
descriptions.1940: This book deals with the topic of humility in prayer, directed specifically to Muslim women. Author Ruqaya Al-Muhareb focuses on explaining the virtue and importance of humility, while providing practical advice on how to achieve it in the various parts of prayer. The book includes specialized chapters on reverence in bowing, prostration, and tashahhud, in addition to preparing for prayer. The book is based on the Prophet's hadiths and examples of the behavior of the righteous predecessors to enhance the reader's understanding of true humility in worship.
descriptions.1941: This book deals with the topic of the love of God and the servant’s longing for Him, trying to clarify how to develop this love in hearts and its effects on Muslim behavior. The author focuses on the importance of sincere love for God and discusses its fruits in the life of the servant. He also talks about the reasons for God’s love for His servants and his pride in them. The book aims to guide the reader towards the path of developing and strengthening his love for God in his daily life.
descriptions.1942: This book deals with the topic of reviving the heart in the month of Ramadan by meditating on the verses of the Qur’an and maximizing the reward for good deeds in this holy month. Author Magdy Al-Hilali focuses on the importance of setting goals and following the appropriate means to achieve them during the days of Ramadan, while emphasizing the importance of continuing to give and do good after the end of the holy month. The book aims to motivate the reader to benefit from the virtues of Ramadan and maximize the rewards of worship during it.
descriptions.1943: This book deals with the topic of anger and its negative effects on the individual and society, and provides practical advice for avoiding and treating it. The author divides the book into chapters that address the definition of anger, its causes, and the motivations for its continuation, mentioning painkillers and inhibitors for anger, as well as the difference between anger and sadness, and explaining praiseworthy and reprehensible types of anger. The book is an educational and behavioral book that aims to develop good morals and avoid bad traits.
descriptions.1944: The book “What Do We Want from Ramadan” by Majdi Al-Hilali is concerned with directing the reader to the goals of the month of fasting through a comprehensive review of individual acts of worship such as fasting, night prayers, the Qur’an, supplication and charity, in addition to social behaviors such as being kind to the family, maintaining family ties, and being generous. The author combines spirituality and ethics in chapters that highlight the importance of acquiring piety and spiritual preparation to welcome this blessed month. The work concludes with a call to adhere to covenants and achieve a balance between worship and good deeds.
descriptions.1945: Educational landmarks for seekers of the legal states of Islamic law by Sheikh Muhammad Al-Mukhtar Al-Shanqeeti. It is concerned with setting moral and moral landmarks for students of legal science, divided into chapters that deal with the etiquette of dealing with scholars, the virtues of piety and sincerity, and the elements of seeking such as patience, saving time, and choosing companionship. It also includes instructions on the method of seeking and controlling knowledge, and a chapter on the rulings of fatwas in terms of intention, piety, and knowledge of interests, and ends with answers to insightful questions. The book aims to guide students to correct behavior and to assume the responsibility entrusted to them in conveying the prophetic message.
descriptions.1946: Considerations on Faith Education by Majdi Al-Hilali addresses the necessity of educational integration for Muslims and the status of faith education by reviewing the four components of the controls of education and the benefits of starting with it. Then, he highlights the fruits of faith and ten of them, from the initiative to a feeling of tranquility. It also explains the stages and goals of faith growth, linking them to the topics of dealing with the world, money, people, and life events, thus providing a reference that integrates spiritual values ​​with daily behavior.
descriptions.1947: Let's Believe One Hour” by the writer Magdy Al-Hilali is a work that belongs to the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrances, in which its author presents an effort to strengthen faith by reviewing the fruits of faith in the generation of companions and showing ways of heartfelt awakening and spiritual advancement. The book addresses topics such as taking the initiative to do good, asceticism in this world, awakening hidden powers, and the desire for God. It also sheds light on a person’s relationship with his Lord and his dealings with money, people, and life events. It aims to motivate the reader to develop spiritual awareness and achieve peace and tranquility in the heart.
descriptions.1948: The book “Wards of the Day and the Night” by Sheikh Khaled Al-Jarisi is a collection of supplications and supplications that accompany the Muslim in his daily prayers and actions from morning until evening.
