The content is arranged according to chapters dealing with supplications for waking up, ablution, entering and leaving the house and the mosque, riding the car, and the various positions of prayer from the opening prayer to the tashahhud and prostration. This book is considered a reference for spiritual enlightenment and etiquette, and is based on what has been proven from the Sunnah of the Prophet in formulating the selected supplications.
descriptions.1949: Eating Etiquette is a book by Ibn al-Imad al-Aqfahsi in which its author explains a poetic system on the etiquette of banquets and inviting them and responding to them. The system consists of (328) lines of poetry that begin with this line: and end with: The book was published by Dar al-Kutub al-Ilmiyyah in Beirut in 1986 AD. It was printed without introduction or definition of its subject, except for a translation of the author, which included a narrative list of his works, which are: (33) works, between a book and a treatise, including (The Clear Secret of the Properties God Has Deposited in the Parts of Animals) and (The Reporting Statement on the Error of Al-Kamal Al-Dumiri). Among his anecdotes: Research on the hadith: Dipping flies, and those who said: What is meant by flies: bees.
descriptions.1950: The book “Al-Shafi’i Etiquette and Virtues” by Al-Razi Ibn Abi Hatem falls within the category of Al-Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrances, and collects what was reported about the biography of Imam Al-Shafi’i, his knowledge, humility, piety, generosity, erudition, and knowledge of languages, in addition to his debates and his jurisprudential and doctrinal positions. It also includes texts on his personal etiquette and his sayings regarding worship and transactions such as ablution, prayer, fasting, zakat, sales, and others. The book quotes from multiple narrations to explain the characteristics and purposes of the Imam, and aims to show the biography of Imam Al-Shafi’i and his moral and scientific principles.
descriptions.1951: The etiquette of companionship and the mention of companionship and brotherhood is a small booklet written by (Badr al-Din al-Ghazi - 904 AH - 984 AH), in which the author summarized a set of etiquette and morals that companions and brothers must have, and the rights and duties of each of them. He cited various sayings and poems for this. …
descriptions.1952: This book, “Etiquette of Mutuality,” by the Gazan author, Abu Al-Barakat, is classified under the category of parchment, etiquette, and remembrance. The book contains a list of defects that the author considers to be part of the etiquette of eating, and he divides them into several categories such as itching, crawling, majū’, mishna, and others. The book begins by defining these defects and explains how to deal with them in financial support. The book aims to teach readers how to behave correctly in dining, and to introduce them to the importance of etiquette and dealing with others.
descriptions.1953: Etiquette of Souls, a book by Imam Al-Harith Al-Muhasibi, who died in the year 243 AH, in the chapter on Sunni Sufism, and he is one of the first to write about Sufism.
descriptions.1954: This book deals with the topic of the impact of worship on the life of a Muslim, as it focuses on the importance of worship in the life of an individual Muslim and discusses the different types of worship and the five pillars of Islam. The author defines worship as everything that God loves and is pleased with in terms of words and actions, and states that God created creation, sent messengers, and revealed books to call people to worship Him alone. The book is a type of religious book that aims to clarify the concept of worship and explain its virtues and importance in the life of a Muslim.
descriptions.1955: The book “Ethics of Muslim Youth” by Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali deals with the topic of Islamic morals and etiquette related to youth, reviewing the importance of divine honor for man and his superiority over all other creatures, and citing Qur’anic verses and sayings of interpretive scholars to confirm the importance of good morals in the progress and prosperity of nations. The book focuses on psychological literature and its role in shaping an individual’s personality and place in society, considering that reason and literature are the two basic characteristics that God has given to man.
descriptions.1956: The book “The Ethics of Scholars” by Al-Ajri falls within the category of Al-Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrances, and is concerned with describing the behavior of scholars and their moral qualities in seeking knowledge, meeting scholars, and sitting with them, in addition to reviewing their virtue in this world and the hereafter. The book includes chapters that address descriptions of the scholars who benefit from God’s knowledge, their characteristics in seeking knowledge, their encounters with scholars, as well as their behavior with other people. It concludes by mentioning God’s question to the people of knowledge about their work with knowledge. The text aims to show the status of scholars and the impact of their morals in guiding people and promoting religious understanding.
descriptions.1957: The book presents a comprehensive study of the literature of disagreement in Islam, based on a historical and comparative analysis between the various stages from the era of prophecy until contemporary jurisprudence. In its chapters, the author addresses the truth about disagreement, its types, etiquette, and benefits, with a review of the experiences of the Companions and Followers and the positions of scholars in doctrinal and jurisprudential disputes. It also sheds light on the imams’ approaches to deduction and the reasons for disagreement throughout the ages, seeking to revive the faith dimension and direct discussions to constructive paths.
descriptions.1958: The Literature of the World and Religion is a book written by Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mawardi, in which he collected a lot of etiquette and morals, from verses of the Holy Qur’an and the Prophet’s hadith, then the proverbs of the wise, the etiquette of rhetoricians, and the sayings of poets. He originally called it the Book of the Supreme Pursuit of the Literature of Religion and the World, but the name that became popular among the people was the Book of the Literature of the World and Religion.
descriptions.1959: The book “Childhood Literature between the Holy Qur’an and the Noble Sunnah” by Ali Ali Sobh sheds light on the Islamic approach to raising and disciplining children based on Qur’anic and Prophetic texts, reviewing Islamic literature for children as nature and worship. It covers chapters on recitation of the Qur’an for children, Qur’anic and Prophetic stories, and Prophetic and Luqmani commandments, in addition to the stages of childhood in Sharia literature and their impact on disciplining the child in poetry and prose. The author concludes with a reference to the sources and references he relied on in his presentation.
descriptions.1960: The book “The Etiquette of Seeking and Utmost Literature” by Sheikh Al-Shawkani is classified under Al-Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrance, and it deals with the controls of the behavior of the seeker of knowledge in terms of devotion to God, staying away from bias and race, and commitment to fairness and diligence. The author presents the causes of fanaticism and the ills that may affect sheikhs and students, and suggests ways to address these problems and achieve the pursuit of knowledge with purity of intention and objectivity of presentation.
descriptions.1961: The etiquette of sitting together, praising the tongue, and the virtue of speech and condemning Ibn Abd al-Barr belongs to the category of Al-Riqaq, etiquette, and remembrances, and focuses on the etiquette of sitting among the Companions and directions in praising the tongue and the virtue of speech while condemning empty speech. It includes chapters on teaching parsing and moderation in dialogue, based on the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ and the sayings of the Companions, and addresses the topics of eloquence, silence, and moderation in speech.
descriptions.1962: The book “Sermon Literature” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad introduces the concept of the sermon and reviews its occurrence in the Holy Qur’an, while clarifying its purposes and rulings, within a framework that aims to guide the preacher to wise methods and beautiful etiquette in calling to goodness. The author focuses on the necessity of employing appropriate argument and language to bring hearts closer to virtue, while highlighting the importance of knowledge and intelligence in guiding souls. This work falls within the category of letters, etiquettes, and remembrances, and is considered a reference for those interested in the arts and literature of preaching.
descriptions.1963: The Book of Remembrances for Purity and Prayer is a book concerned with collecting remembrances and etiquette related to purity and prayer, and provides an explanation of the meanings of those remembrances, their connotations, rulings, and purposes. The book covers topics such as toilet etiquette and supplications, ablution supplications, prayer supplications, and supplications after saying salaam, and provides details on how to relieve oneself and when entering and exiting the toilet. The book shows the importance of etiquette in Islam and the perfection of the blessed law of purification, cleanliness, purification, and purification.
descriptions.1964: This book deals with the morning and evening remembrances and their etiquette according to Islamic law, and reviews the Prophetic hadiths related to these remembrances and their virtues. It also contains guidance on how to practice these acts of worship correctly and continuously, with an emphasis on their importance in a Muslim’s daily life. The book aims to remind the reader of the importance of mentioning God at specific times of the day and to point out their virtue to the servant in this world and the hereafter.
descriptions.1965: The book “Types of Arrogant People” is a book that is classified within the field of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances, and it provides a comprehensive study on the types of vanity in humans. The author, Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali, divides people into different categories, and points out that arrogance accompanies all believers, accountable people, and unbelievers, except for those whom God protects. The book provides an analysis of the infidel’s arrogance, and its treatment, and indicates that arrogant people, with the exception of infidels, are divided into four types: scholars, servants, lords of money, and Sufis. The book aims to expose the arrogance of these groups, and to clarify the argument therein, in a clear and concise manner.
descriptions.1966: The book deals with the origins of Islamic education and its methods at home, school, and society, reviewing the concepts of education, religion, and Islam and their relationship, and the sources of Islamic education from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It discusses the educational foundations in Islam from the view on man, the universe, and life, as well as the devotional and legislative foundations and their impact on educating thought and character. It also focuses on the purpose and objectives of Islamic education, reviewing the importance of the goal and its definition in the educational process. The author begins his book by warning of the necessity of paying attention to Islamic education in light of what he sees as the loss in raising children as a result of excessive care and pampering of them.
descriptions.1967: The book “Goals of Islamic Education” by Majid Arsan Al-Kilani provides a comprehensive study of the importance of goals in the educational process, reviewing the crises of modern education and the demands of educational systems and institutions in the Arab and Islamic world. The first part is devoted to raising the Muslim individual, focusing on the concept of good deeds, reason, ideals, religious and social experiences, will and harnessed ability. It then moves on to analyze the role of education in bringing out the Muslim nation by reviewing its components of believing individuals, migration, jihad, mission, and shelter, to provide a theoretical framework that contributes to directing educational policies.
descriptions.1968: The book “The Importance of Paying Attention to Interpretation, Hadith, and Jurisprudence” by the writer Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad highlights the value of adhering to the three legal sciences by citing Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths that confirm the virtue of knowledge. It focuses on the role of interpretation, hadith, and jurisprudence in building a sound understanding of religion, and reviews the methodology of relying on evidence and comparing the four schools of thought. The book falls under the category of Al-Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrance, which reflects his interest in Islamic etiquette and directing the reader to proficient scientific behavior.
descriptions.1969: The book, The Horrors of the Graves by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali, falls within the category of Al-Riqaq, Manners, and Remembrances, and deals in a legal manner with the topics of the isthmus and the torment and bliss of the grave, reviewing the conditions of the dead from their encounters in the graves to the visits of the living to them, while clarifying what is stated in the Qur’an and Sunnah about these issues.
descriptions.1970: Reviving the Sciences of Religion is one of the works of Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali and one of his most important works. He wrote it in Arabic between the years 489 - 495 AH / 1096 - 1102 AD after he left the Nizamiyya pulpit in Baghdad in the year 1095 AD / 488 AH and decided to leave it for Mecca as a pilgrimage. He retired in deep seclusion and devoted himself to studying, and he wrote it during that period. He is famous for his distinguished efforts in Ash'ari thought, Shafi'i jurisprudence, and Sufi spiritual trends. His book Al-Ihya is considered a “Sunni Sufi encyclopedia.” It is divided into four quarters, each containing ten books. The first quarter deals with acts of worship and duties, focusing on the five pillars of Islam. …
descriptions.1971: The book “The Hour Has Approached, So Repent, O Sinners” by Sheikh Abu Bakr Al-Jazairi, is concerned with explaining the imminence of the Hour and comparing the hour of death with the Hour of Resurrection, based on Qur’anic texts and prophetic hadiths. It includes chapters that explain the signs of the Hour, such as the Prophet’s mission, his death, the conquest of Jerusalem, and the temptations that will appear. It aims to remind the reader of the necessity of faith, piety, and returning to God to avoid the torment of the Two Hours. It is classified under the literature of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance.
descriptions.1972: Legal Etiquette and Granted Grants is one of the books of the Hanbali jurist Muhammad bin Mufleh bin Muhammad al-Maqdisi, and it is a book of great value and great benefits. It has a share in its name; It is a book of etiquette, morals, wisdom, and rulings, and scholars, ancient and modern, still quote it and find in it what they seek. The book included most of the issues that were mentioned in the books of its predecessors in the field of Islamic rituals, traditions, and morals. Imam Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Muflih says in the introduction to his book:
descriptions.1973: The book “Virtuous Ethics: Rules and Starting Points for Acquiring It” by the writer Abdullah Al-Ruhaili is concerned with studying good morals from a comprehensive Islamic perspective, based on the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and passages from the sayings of the predecessors. It reviews the definition of good morals, ways to acquire it, and the educational foundations for evaluating it. The book includes chapters detailing the moral rules derived from Sharia texts, and dividing morality into origins and branches according to their relationship to God or people, with a presentation of the facts that the author arrived at during his journey. The author aims to show the importance of ethics in the life of the individual and society and provide a practical theoretical approach to its development.
descriptions.1974: The book “Ethics and the Path to Healing Souls” by Sheikh Ibn Hazm is concerned with showing ways to reform morals and manage human behavior in his quest to heal the soul. It falls under the category of gentleness, etiquette, and remembrance, and in his sermon he presents an introduction that highlights the importance of balance between worldly and otherworldly work, with a focus on educating the soul and repairing what is corrupted. The text aims to guide the reader to what is beneficial in terms of righteous behavior and sincere remembrance that raises the spirit and strengthens faith.
descriptions.1975: Little Literature and Great Literature is a book by Abdullah Ibn al-Muqaffa, Great Literature: Ibn al-Muqaffa admits that he took this book from the sayings of the ancients, and he presented it with a preface: “On the virtue of the ancients in knowledge, the conditions for studying it, and the purpose of this book.” He divided it into two sections: the first is about the Sultan and his companion and the beautiful qualities of each of them. In this topic, there are two sections: the first is about the Sultan and the second about the company of the Sultan. The second section dealt with friends, choosing a friend well, treating him well, and everything related to friends. Small literature: Ibn al-Muqaffa was also a transmitter of small literature. He said: “I have put in this book some of the people’s words that have been preserved in letters,” but he acted on what he transmitted. …
descriptions.1976: This is the book “Al-Adhkar” by Al-Nawawi, and it is one of the traditional Islamic and Arab books, classified under the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Azkar. The book contains several chapters that address topics related to dhikr and worship, such as the virtue of dhikr, the etiquette of dhikr, the characteristics of places of dhikr, and the ruling on dhikr in several situations. The book is considered one of the most important and widely used books in the field of dhikr, and it competes with the book “Riyadh al-Salehin” for fame. The book contains an introduction by the author, an introduction to the book, identification of the book’s topics, and an explanation of the importance of the book in the field of dhikr.
descriptions.1977: This book, “Al-Adhkaar” by Al-Nawawi, deals with the virtues of dhikr and its importance in the life of a Muslim, and reviews the dhikr mentioned by the Prophet ﷺ in his various daily situations. It focuses on reminding us of the importance of sincerity in actions, and includes multiple chapters that show what should be said in various situations, from wearing clothes to entering and leaving the mosque, while neglecting the brevity of the chains of transmission and focusing on the authenticity of the hadiths and their controls.
descriptions.1978: The Forty in the Buildings of Islam and the Rules of Rulings, known as The Forty of An-Nawawi, a text that included forty-two hadiths compiled by Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi, who died in 676 AH.
descriptions.1979: The book “Useful Reasons for Acquiring Good Manners” is considered one of the books concerned with rituals, etiquette, and remembrances, as the author, Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad, presents a comprehensive vision about the importance of acquiring good morals and ways to achieve this. The book stresses the importance of sound faith and its role in improving morals. It also highlights the role of supplication in changing for the better. The book provides a separate chapter on the reasons for acquiring good character, making it easier for the reader to understand and apply these principles in his daily life.
descriptions.1980: The book “Righteousness and Connection” by Ibn al-Jawzi deals with the topic of honoring parents and maintaining family ties from a religious and moral perspective, showing the importance of these meanings in Islam and their favor with God Almighty. The book covers hadiths and sayings that show the virtues of honoring parents and maintaining family ties, and calls for adhering to these values ​​and strengthening them in society, while mentioning the bad consequences for those who neglect these rights or disobey their parents.
descriptions.1981: This book deals with the topic of blessing in livelihood and the reasons for attracting it through an approach derived from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The author, Abdullah Al-Sawalma, focuses on explaining the meanings of some of the terms mentioned in the title, then goes on to review a group of reasons that lead to increased blessings in livelihood, such as piety, trust, praise, supplication, gratitude, and repentance. The book aims to provide a comprehensive overview of how to enhance blessings in livelihood through a Muslim’s commitment to good deeds and obedience.
descriptions.1982: The book “The Statement on Satan’s Entrances” by Abdul Hamid Al-Bilali deals with the topic of warning against Satan’s entrances and his methods of temptation and temptation, based on the authentic Qur’anic texts and the reliable Sunnah of the Prophet. The book focuses on interpreting Qur’anic verses related to Satan and his plans, relying on the interpretations of Salaf scholars and hadith scholars, thus examining the unseen facts related to Satan and his plans, and providing a comprehensive overview of how to protect yourself from his entrances.
descriptions.1983: The book “Al-Tabisrah” by Ibn Al-Jawzi is a collection of sessions in which the biography of the prophets and Qur’anic figures is mentioned, based on narrative narration, sajj on Qur’anic verses, and reflections on the meanings of monotheism and worship. This work falls within the classification of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, as it combines literary eloquence and pure remembrance, and relies on a rhetorical style that combines narration and statement to direct the reader to the morals and virtues drawn from the stories of the prophets.
descriptions.1984: The book “Al-Tabyin for the Supplications of the Sick and Injured” is considered one of the books that specializes in supplications, etiquette, and supplications, as it deals with topics of interest to the sick and injured, such as what is said to them, supplications of distress, and supplications for grief, anxiety, and sadness. The book presents some supplications and supplications that can be used to promote sick people, such as the opening of the book, and shows how these supplications can be a reason for healing and well-being. The book shows the importance of ruqyah in treating patients, and provides examples from the Sunnah on this subject. The book is considered a useful resource for those looking for supplications and supplications that can help them in difficult life situations.
descriptions.1985: Fear of Hell and Definition of the Condition of Dar al-Bawar is a book written by Imam Abu al-Faraj Abd al-Rahman bin Ahmad bin Rajab al-Hanbali. The book deals with the subject of the fire of Hell as mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah. In it, he talks about the fire of Hell, its people, its stones, its bottom, and its torment. Ibn Rajab said in the introduction to the book:
descriptions.1986: A reminder of the conditions of the dead and matters of the afterlife. A book written by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ahmed bin Abi Bakr bin Farah Al-Ansari Al-Khazraji Shams al-Din al-Qurtubi (died: 671 AH). The subject of the book revolves around the conditions of the dead and related matters of the afterlife. The author arranged his subject in an order that took into account the sequence of topics and divided it into four units: The first unit: death and its introductions, then the grave, its torment, its bliss, and what emerges from it until the breath of resurrection. The second unit: It begins with the resurrection, the resurrection, the blowing of images, the gathering, the situation and its horrors, and what one will be saved from. The third unit: On the people of Paradise entering Paradise and what God has prepared for its people of lasting bliss, and on the people of Hell entering Hell and the painful punishment He has prepared for its people. …
descriptions.1987: Al-Tadhkirah fi Preaching is one of the books of Imam Abu Al-Faraj Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad Ibn Al-Jawzi Al-Baghdadi. It contains various advice and sermons that deal with various aspects of life, and useful Islamic advice for commitment to worship in Islam.
descriptions.1988: The book “Creative Education in the Perspective of Islamic Education” by Dr. Khalid bin Hamid Al-Hazmi deals with the topic of creativity through its Islamic rooting, reviewing the concept of creativity, its limits, obstacles and benefits, with a focus on the role of the mind in the creative process. The author emphasizes the necessity of directing creativity towards righteousness and guidance, warning against deviating towards destructive paths. The book also deals with aspects of mental education and the means of preserving and developing it, indicating the importance of caring for the mind and protecting it from deviation, while emphasizing the necessity of balancing reason and Islamic law in the process of educational upbringing.
descriptions.1989: The book “Islamic Education, Its Origins and Development in the Arab Countries,” by Muhammad Munir Morsi, is concerned with studying the roots of Islamic education and the stages of its development in the Arab world, based on a historical and intellectual analysis of the educational curriculum before and after Islam. The book addresses basic concepts such as the virtue of the pen and books and the status of knowledge in Islam, and reviews the goals of Islamic education from an integrative and behavioral perspective that links the individual and society. It also provides a critical review of the methodological problems in writing in this field and is based on the recommendations of international conferences to modernize Islamic education.
descriptions.1990: The book “Islamic Education: Its Principles, Method, and Teacher” by Atef Al-Sayyed defines the concepts and foundations on which education is based in the Islamic framework, and reviews its curriculum and characteristics through chapters that address the principles, curriculum, methods, and teaching methods. It also explains the appropriate teaching and evaluation methods for teaching various branches of Islamic education, such as the Qur’an, Hadith, doctrine, and acts of worship. It aims to provide a comprehensive guide for teachers and those interested in developing the educational process in accordance with Islamic values.
descriptions.1991: The book “Islamic Education and the Stages of Development” by Abbas Mahjoub deals with the concept of education in Islam according to the stages of human development, starting from before birth, through the stages of childhood and adulthood, all the way to adulthood, with special attention paid to sexual education. The work is considered within the classification of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Azkar, and is based on a systematic review of the developmental stages and linking them to the principles of the Islamic religion in choosing a partner and directing moral behavior.
descriptions.1992: The book “Education in the Ages Before and After Islam” by Abbas Mahjoub is concerned with studying the concept of education and its development from pre-Islamic times to the Islamic method, based on what historians mention of traditional and automatic learning methods, and based on Qur’anic texts that highlight the role of man as a caliph on earth. The content is divided into an introduction that explains the general foundations, then a chapter on education in the pre-Islamic era, and another that highlights the methodological development of education in Islam, making it a reference in the field of literature, etiquette, and remembrance.
descriptions.1993: Encouragement and intimidation from the Noble Hadith, one of the hadith books that collected the Prophetic hadiths related to enticement and intimidation, collected by Al-Hafiz Abdul-Azim Al-Mundhiri from the books of Hadith and included in four volumes.
descriptions.1994: This book, “Seeking Happiness in Fulfilling a Promise” by Al-Sakhawi Shams Al-Din, deals with the topic of fulfilling a promise from a religious and cultural perspective. The author combines hadiths and hadiths related to this topic, with an explanation of a Qur’anic verse related to loyalty, and also reviews some poems that deal with the same meaning. The book aims to show the importance of fulfilling covenants and appointments by integrating the texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah, while highlighting the strength of the evidence on the necessity of fulfillment.
descriptions.1995: The book introduces the Holy Qur’an and reviews the evidence of its virtue in the first section, then deals with adherence to the Qur’an and its manifestations in the second section, and examines the impact of adherence to the lives of Muslims through what has been seen of its good application in the nation’s past and currently in the third section, concluding with a conclusion based on sources and references that support what has been mentioned.
descriptions.1996: The book “Rebuke and Warning” by Abu Sheikh Al-Asbahani deals with the topic of advice and compassion among Muslims, explaining the qualities and etiquette that every Muslim must have towards his brother, with a focus on urging them to cover up and not reveal the private parts of others, and explaining the punishment for whoever backbites or slanders a Muslim. The book's content is based on Prophetic hadiths and Quranic verses that emphasize the importance of having good morals and avoiding slander and backbiting.
descriptions.1997: Dr. Hamid Abdel Salam Zahran, in his book “Psychological Guidance and Counseling,” provides an integrated presentation of the concept of psychological guidance and counselling, its goals and applications, relying on scientific methods and philosophical, psychological and educational foundations. The book deals with the fields of psychological guidance and counseling and its relationship with related sciences. It reviews the theories of this field and the similarities and differences between them. It also focuses on the need for psychological guidance and counseling in modern societies.
descriptions.1998: The book “The Illusion in the Description of the Conditions of the Hereafter” by Al-Harith Al-Muhasibi deals with his detailed description of the conditions of the people of Hell and the people of Paradise in the afterlife. The book aims to remind Muslims of the importance of faith and patience in the face of material temptations and temptations, stressing the necessity of constant remembrance to strengthen faith and commitment to obedience. The author cites the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet to reinforce his message about the importance of remembering and turning to God Almighty.
descriptions.1999: This book, by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, deals with topics related to patience, contentment with destiny, and God’s destiny, with a focus on steadfastness at the time of death. It contains news and stories about the prophets, righteous companions and others, explaining the virtues of patience and its reward, and reviewing how the patient and contented faced death and adversity. The book aims to promote the values ​​of patience and contentment in the face of trials and adversity.
descriptions.2000: The book “Encouragement to memorize knowledge and mention of great memorizers” by Ibn al-Jawzi is concerned with the importance of memorizing the Qur’an and knowledge and explaining ways to consolidate it. It details the characteristics of memorizers, methods of raising a boy to memorize, and medical and temporary means that enhance memory. It also includes an explanation of the provisions of archives and guidance on the preservation that should be provided, and it concludes by mentioning the names of senior memorizers from different generations. The book is classified under Al-Riqaq, Al-Adab, and Al-Adhkaar, which shows its literary and edifying nature in addition to its scientific guidance.
descriptions.2001: Encouraging the pursuit of knowledge and diligence in collecting it” by Ibn Al-Askari Abu Hilal is an author who belongs to the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance. The text focuses on motivating the reader to pursue knowledge and diligence, based on sayings and literary passages that stress the value of diligence and moderation in understanding. The book includes letters and notes from the Companions and an introduction that includes an Islamic greeting, which reflects its moral and spiritual character.
descriptions.2002: The Hijab by Al-Manfaluti is a literary work that belongs to the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Azkar. It deals with philosophical reflections on the concept of the Hijab as an internal veil that covers the soul and identity by narrating the experience of a person returning from Europe with changes in his appearance and feelings. The text highlights the human struggle between tradition and the West, presenting a symbolic dialogue between the narrator and the character whom he describes as “the mighty rock.”
descriptions.2003: The book “Humility in Prayer” by Muhammad bin Lutfi Al-Sabbagh deals with the topic of humility in prayer and its relationship to faith and obedience, reviewing its definition, place and importance, reviewing the obstacles that prevent it from being achieved, while providing practical advice to strengthen it in hearts and bodies. The book is a type of religious book that aims to guide Muslims towards improving their prayer and worship, based on Qur’anic texts and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.2004: The pulpit sermons by its author, Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, are a collection of religious speeches that he delivered on various occasions such as Ramadan, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Sacrifice, and the days of Hajj, and fall within the category of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances. The series includes introductory and guiding sermons calling for piety and returning to God, and is based on a rhetorical style that highlights the meanings and morals of religion.
descriptions.2005: Al-Durari fi Zikr al-Dharari by Ibn al-Adim belongs to the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, and in its many chapters it presents topics of raising children, urging parents to acquire them, praising and disparaging them, and directing them to care for and teach them, in addition to discussing feelings of fear, compassion, and the altruism of parents toward them. The book combines the sayings of the Prophet and religious scholars to demonstrate the value of offspring and its impact in this world and the afterlife.
descriptions.2006: The book “Supplication followed by treatment with ruqyah from the Qur’an and Sunnah” by Saeed bin Wahf Al-Qahtani combines an explanation of the virtue of supplication and its etiquette according to the Qur’an and Sunnah, and presents the Most Beautiful Names of God as a reference for dhikr. It includes detailed chapters on methods of ruqyah treatment based on Sharia texts, including treating witchcraft, the evil eye, and mental and physical illness with means such as the Qur’an, honey, and Zamzam water. The author aims to provide a practical guide for the pious who seeks to benefit from supplications and spiritual treatments in his daily life.
descriptions.2007: The pretext to the good deeds of Sharia is a book written by Abu Al-Qasim Al-Hussein bin Muhammad, known as Al-Raghib Al-Isfahani (died: 502 AH), from the people of Isfahan who resided in Baghdad, and became famous, to the point that he was associated with Al-Ghazali. It is concerned with establishing the ethical theory of Muslims, in which it answers the question: “How does a person reach the status of servitude that God made an honor for the pious, and how does he rise from it if he reaches the status of the caliphate that God made it?” May God give honor to the righteous and martyrs?
descriptions.2008: Al-Risala Al-Qushayriyya is a work by Imam Abu Al-Qasim Abdul Karim bin Hawazin Al-Qushayri Al-Shafi’i, who died in the year 465 AH. It consists of fifty-four chapters and three chapters. It is two volumes. The first volume, from page 61 to the end, was devoted to biographies of the sheikhs of Sufism. He began it with this title: “A chapter mentioning the sheikhs of this order and what their biographies and sayings indicate regarding the veneration of the Sharia.” Then he mentioned biographies of eighty-three of the major leaders of Sufism.
descriptions.2009: This book, “Ruqyah Sharia from the Qur’an and Sunnah,” written by Ali bin Muhammad Nasser Al-Faqihi, is considered an important book in the field of ruqyah, etiquette, and dhikr. The book aims to clarify the concept of legal ruqyah and determine what is legitimate from ruqyah and what is rejected, focusing on the importance of preserving the Muslim faith and avoiding doubts and illusions. The book shows that the legitimate ruqyah is the ruqyah that is performed using the Holy Qur’an, especially with the Fatihah of the Book and the Mu’awwidha, and this is based on the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author stresses the importance of preserving the Muslim faith and avoiding doubts and illusions, and warns that opening clinics in the name of legal ruqyah has led to the spread of false propaganda about jinn possessing humans. This book is an important resource for Muslims looking for a precise understanding of the concept of ruqyah.
descriptions.2010: The book Asceticism by Al-Maafi bin Imran Al-Mawsili deals with topics related to asceticism and piety, speaking about the virtue of lack of money and children and the hatred of ostentation and pride. The book focuses on humility, subsistence, and rejecting luxury and desires, relying on the Prophetic hadiths mentioned in this field.
descriptions.2011: The book of Asceticism by Luki` ibn al-Jarrah deals with the topic of asceticism and austerity in this world and their virtue over the servant in the afterlife, reviewing the sayings of the predecessors and hadiths of the Prophet in this field. The book focuses on the importance of asceticism as a means of understanding religion and preparing for the afterlife, while addressing various topics such as preparing for death, crying, laughing, humility, poverty, and wealth.
descriptions.2012: This book, “Asceticism,” by Asad ibn Musa deals with topics related to the afterlife, reckoning, and recompense, focusing on describing the torment of hellfire and the bliss of heaven. The author talks about the valleys of Hell, its mountains, its life, and the drink of the people of Hell. He also mentions the path, the position before God, intercession, the scales, and retribution. The book aims to remind the reader of the Last Day and explain the consequences of actions in this life.
descriptions.2013: This book by the scholar Ibn al-Jazari deals with topics related to etiquette, morals, and remembrance, focusing on warnings against sins and transgressions and the etiquette of dealing with others. The author encourages repentance and getting closer to God Almighty, and explains the importance of contemplating death and the afterlife, while providing practical advice to avoid sins and protect oneself from temptations. The book aims to develop good morals and consolidate the Muslim faith in his words and actions.
descriptions.2014: Al-Zawajar on committing major sins by Imam Ibn Hajar Al-Haytami (d. 974 AH), a book on recommendation and admonition, in which his author explains the major sins and the rulings, rebukes, promises, and threats related to them.
descriptions.2015: The book, “Educational Advancement: Its Concept, Methodology, and Features in Light of the Islamic Approach,” by Dr. Khalid bin Hamid Al-Hazmi, deals with a comprehensive study on the concept of educational advancement and its methodological foundations in Islam, comparing it to other educational approaches. The author focuses on the importance of Islamic educational studies and their effectiveness in applying lofty values ​​and principles, refuting common fallacies about the superiority of Western curricula in the educational field. The book aims to clarify the concept of educational precedence and explain the fundamental differences between it and other educational curricula, relying on authentic Islamic references.
descriptions.2016: The book provides an overview of the biography of Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz (may Allah have mercy on him), focusing on various aspects of his scientific and practical life, highlighting the depth of his knowledge, the breadth of his knowledge, and his benefit to Islam and Muslims. Author Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad discusses a lecture he gave about this venerable scholar, reviewing aspects of his lineage and upbringing, his disciples, his knowledge, his worship, his writings, and other aspects that reflect his scientific and spiritual status.
descriptions.2017: The book is a lecture given by Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad at the Islamic University, in which he discusses the biography of Sheikh Omar bin Muhammad Fallatah (may Allah have mercy on him), reviewing his name, lineage, belief, call, approach, teaching in the Prophet’s Mosque, and his management of Dar Al-Hadith, in addition to his works, supervision, number of proofs, his qualities, and comparison with his sheikh. The book falls within the category of letters, etiquette, and remembrances, which makes it a literary and religious reference that aims to introduce the Sheikh and shed light on his scientific and spiritual path.
descriptions.2018: The book “Sheikh Muhammad bin Uthaymeen is one of the divine scholars” by Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad is a lecture given by Abdul Mohsen bin Hamad Al-Abadi Al-Badr at the Islamic University in Medina, dealing with the biography of Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh bin Uthaymeen and his scientific and advocacy contributions. The text includes a presentation of his lineage, upbringing, sheikhs and disciples, his writings and his status among the people, in addition to his commandments and proposals. The book is classified under the category of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, which highlights its literary and spiritual character.
descriptions.2019: The book “Sahih Al-Musnad Min Al-Hadith Al-Qudsi” by Sheikh Mustafa Al-Adawi is a collection of the sacred hadiths that the author of the book considered authentic, and he presents them without chains of chain of transmission, with a brief parsing of the meanings and an explanation of the ruling related to each hadith. The author focuses on the topics of slavery, etiquette, and remembrance, discussing the virtues of monotheism, remembrance, repentance, and love among Muslims, in addition to warnings against polytheism and sins. The book aims to benefit the public by extracting moral and spiritual lessons from these hadiths.
descriptions.2020: Patience, the Ride of Success, is a poem about wisdom, composed by Ibn al-Dhahir al-Irbali, and it falls within the classification of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance. The poem includes a group of verses that deal with various topics such as the short duration of life, the virtue of piety, destiny and destiny, and the effect of reason and deliberation in decision-making. The poem shows the character of traditional Arabic literature in directing the reader to proper behavior based on patience and spiritual awareness.
descriptions.2021: The brilliant light of the mosque sermons is a collection of sermons delivered by Ibn Uthaymeen, classified under Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, and it deals with topics of knowledge and its importance, details of God’s names and attributes, and references to verses of the Qur’an. It also includes the biography of the Prophet ﷺ from his mission to his conquests, making it a reference for public religious rhetoric.
descriptions.2022: The book “The Path to Excellence” by Muhammad Al-Faqi addresses topics related to Islamic ethics and etiquette, with a focus on how to achieve excellence and success in life through connection with God and good deeds. The author focuses on the importance of faith, trust, tolerance, and sincerity as a basis for achieving desired goals and objectives, while providing practical advice on how to use time and energy efficiently to achieve success.
descriptions.2023: The book “Worships in Islam and Their Impact on Reforming Society” by the writer Mahmoud Al-Sayyid Shaykhun is concerned with clarifying the relationship of monotheism with worship and explaining how prayers, zakat, fasting and Hajj contribute to refining souls and reforming hearts, which is reflected in the improvement of society. It is classified under Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, and is based on its table of contents, which includes chapters on the unification of divinity and the virtues of various acts of worship, with reference to its role among the predecessors and successors as a medicine for spiritual and social pain.
descriptions.2024: The Book of Solitude by Al-Khattabi is a book that falls under the classification of Al-Riqaq, Manners, and Remembrances, and it contains a group of chapters that deal with topics related to isolation and introversion, such as reasons that make isolation easier for a person, abandoning a large number of friends, warning against bad companions, and the corruption of time and its people. The book seems to aim to provide advice and guidance on how to deal with people and the surrounding environment, with an emphasis on the importance of isolation and introversion at times. The book contains a comprehensive table of contents covering multiple topics, and the author seems to have been interested in providing practical advice and guidance on how to deal with various situations and circumstances.
descriptions.2025: This book deals with the topic of treatment and ruqyah by reviewing the legitimate ruqyahs from the Qur’an and Sunnah, and the three principles of healing, which are cupping, honey, and cauterization, in addition to mentioning types of prophetic medicines and the treatment of spiritual diseases such as magic and the evil eye, with an emphasis on the importance of the psychological aspect of treatment and its effect on the patient. The book combines supplications and sayings from the Qur’an, the Prophet’s Hadith, and medical treatments mentioned in the Sunnah of the Prophet, and aims to provide a practical guide for treating various types of physical and spiritual diseases.
descriptions.2026: In his book “The Counseling Process,” Muhammad Mahrous El-Shenawy provides a comprehensive overview of counseling and psychotherapy methods, covering the definition of the counseling process, the characteristics of the counselor, the counseling relationship and its skills, and starting the relationship in the first interview. The book aims to fill a gap in the field of counseling and psychotherapy by presenting the steps and skills necessary to carry out counseling work, with a focus on professional ethics and methods of recording and writing reports.
descriptions.2027: This book deals with the subject of the action of the people of Lot from a religious and moral perspective, explaining its ruling and prohibition in Islamic law, and reviewing its negative effects on the individual and society in the religious, moral, social, economic, psychological and health fields. The book also discusses the causes of this abnormal act and methods of preventing it and treating its effects, citing the texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah and the fatwas of Salaf scholars on this subject.
descriptions.2028: This book by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali deals with the topic of the difference between advice and reproach, reviewing the types of advice and how to provide it, with an explanation of the punishment for those who misuse it. He also explains the difference between advice and reproach, explaining that each of them includes reminding a person of what he hates, but they differ in purpose and outcome. The book focuses on the religious importance of correctly understanding the concepts of advice and reproach, and also discusses literature related to providing constructive criticism within the framework of Islamic law.
descriptions.2029: The Book of Benefits, Asceticism, Softenings, and Elegies by Jaafar Al-Khalidi is a collection of short articles that combine religious benefits, Islamic etiquette, and dhikr, and deals with multiple topics such as predestination, well-being, love for Ali bin Abi Talib, jurisprudence, fasting of close associates, the virtues of the Shahada, angels, asceticism, hospitality, and lamentation. The book falls within the classification of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances, and targets the reader seeking moral and spiritual guidance based on prophetic texts and monuments.
descriptions.2030: Delicious Fruits in Pulpit Sermons and Sermons by Abd al-Rahman al-Saadi is a collection of pulpit sermons addressed to different occasions, combining preaching, education, and directing the reader to religious and moral values. The book addresses multiple topics such as piety, charity, trust, remembrance, and etiquette in a rhetorical manner that aims to motivate souls to do good deeds and avoid harmful behaviors. The work falls within the classification of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, which reflects its literary and spiritual character.
descriptions.2031: The book “Contentment, its concept, its benefits, and the path to it” by Ibrahim Al-Hogail is concerned with defining contentment and explaining its spiritual and social benefits, based on its linguistic meanings and its relationship to asceticism and contentment. The book includes chapters that review examples of the conviction of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, explain the reasons for the obstacles to contentment, and provide ways to reach self-satisfaction. It is classified under Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Azkar, which makes it a reference in Muslim moral and spiritual literature.
descriptions.2032: The book “The Good Rules in the Secrets of Obedience and Preparation for Ramadan” by the writer Reda Ahmed Samadi is concerned with preparing the soul for worship during the month of fasting through a set of rules and exercises that alert the heart’s longing for God and strengthen determination and resolve. The book includes chapters concerned with knowing the virtues of the seasons, preparing oneself for obedience, reviewing the provisions of fasting, and achieving the pleasure of remembrance and prayer, with practical directions for attaining the sweetness of obedience and worship. It is classified within the literature of the soul, etiquette, and remembrance, and targets the reader seeking to renew his spirituality and revive the worship of fasting with awareness and sincerity.
descriptions.2033: The Book of Major Sins is a book written by Imam Muhammad bin Othman al-Dhahabi. It includes a number of major sins and sins that a Muslim must avoid. It was first published by Muhammad Abd al-Razzaq Hamzah in 1955 AD, relying on three manuscripts and a manuscript that he stated was from the version of the Minor Sins [and it is most likely the authenticated version]. Muhammad Abd al-Razzaq Hamzah apologized for the presence of the weak ones in this copy and spoke about the hadiths in the manner of the people of his time. The book has collected 70 major sins to alert heedless hearts and worn-out souls and to remind them of the dire consequences resulting from these major sins. …
descriptions.2034: The Good Speech is a book in which Ibn Taymiyyah collected several prophetic hadiths about the supplications that a Muslim says on his day in various matters. The book began with an introduction about the encouragement to remember and its importance.
descriptions.2035: Al-Kalam Al-Nawabigh by Al-Zamakhshari is a book in the field of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances. It deals with wisdom, proverbs, and sayings that encourage thought and reflection on life, with a focus on religious and moral values. The book contains words of sermon and wise advice, directed to those who wish to improve their morals and behavior in accordance with the Sunnah of the Prophet, with references to the importance of listening and contemplating lessons and sermons.
descriptions.2036: In his book “Politeness and its Impact on Public Relations between People,” Muhammad bin Saad Al Saud reviews the concept of politeness from a terminological linguistic perspective, and is based on what is mentioned about it in the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The writer then analyzes the impact of this behavior on society and public relations between individuals, based on detailed studies that include the definition of politeness, its legal connotations, and its social applications. The work concludes with a conclusion and references that support the legal and social study.
descriptions.2037: The book “The Amazing” by Ibn al-Jawzi is considered one of the important books in the field of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances, as the book presents a variety of topics that form part of the Islamic heritage. The book covers several sections, including the sciences of the Qur’an, the inflection of the language and the Qur’an’s agreement with it, the sciences of hadith, and the sources of history, in addition to mentioning our Prophet ﷺ and the genealogies of the Companions and Followers. The book shows the author's interest in Quranic and linguistic studies, in addition to his interest in recording Islamic history and writing down the biographies of the Companions and Followers. The book is a valuable source of information on these topics, and shows the importance of Islamic heritage in understanding Islamic history and culture.
descriptions.2038: The book “Chivalry” by Ibn al-Marzban al-Muhawili deals with the concept of generosity and chivalry from an Islamic perspective, reviewing prophetic hadiths that explain these concepts and link them to religion and morals. The author focuses on defining chivalry and explaining its connection to piety, reason, and character, citing the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions to clarify its meanings and applications in daily life.
descriptions.2039: This book deals with a group of stories and supplications related to seeking help from God Almighty in times of adversity and need. Author Ibn Bashkwal focuses on telling stories of famous Islamic figures, showing the virtue of seeking God’s help and trusting in Him in adversity. It also mentions the virtues of some days and deeds, and presents lessons from the stories of those who underestimated supplication and continued to sin. The book is a type of recitations and remembrances, directed to those who are looking for religious consolation and encouragement to trust in God in various situations.
descriptions.2040: The book “Intoxicants from a Psychological Point of View” by Malak Ghulam Murtada deals with a scientific study of the effect of intoxicants on the mind and human behavior. The author focuses on the reality of drunkenness from a psychological perspective and discusses the causes of addiction and its harms, reviewing the opinions of scholars and commentators on the ruling on drinking alcohol and its negative effects on the individual and society. The book also discusses possible treatments for eliminating addiction and conveys the opinions of religious scholars on the ruling on alcohol and its effect on common sense.
descriptions.2041: Interesting in reading and seeking knowledge by Ali Al-Omran is a literary treatise concerned with urging the reader to seek knowledge and reading. It reviews the honor of knowledge and its place in the Islamic heritage and shows the reasons for students’ retreat from reading and the impact of reality on that. The book covers examples from the biographies of scholars and science enthusiasts, and is based on the sayings of the predecessors and Qur’anic references to emphasize the importance of increasing knowledge. It is classified as rituals, etiquette, and remembrance, which highlights its moral and linguistic character in directing people toward cognitive expansion.
descriptions.2042: Disturbing. A book compiled by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, in which he collected frightening hadiths, warnings against evil deeds, descriptions of punishments, and disturbing stories that worry the reassured, unsettle the tranquil, soften the hard heart, stream tears, and lift up the lazy and retiring person.
descriptions.2043: The book “The Two Obstacles Poetry of Ibn al-Nahwi and al-Ghazali” by Al-Ansari Zakaria is a work that falls under the classification of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrances. It combines poetic texts of the Manfarajah that were created by both Ibn al-Nahwi and al-Ghazali with a comprehensive introduction by the commentator. The book includes an explanation of the obtuse verse, a poem of faith, and an Islamic argument, in addition to sections dealing with descriptions of adversity, supplication and supplication, advice for the soul, a call to imitate the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, and then the conclusion of the poem. The text aims to seek relief and salvation from God and direct the reader to seek help from spiritual and remembrance etiquette.
descriptions.2044: The Savior from Misguidance and the Explainer of Conditions, a book by Imam Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali in which he wrote about his spiritual and intellectual experience with philosophers, mystics, theologians, and Sufis.
descriptions.2045: Al-Munhiyyat by Al-Tirmidhi is a book that collects what the Prophet ﷺ forbade in terms of behavior and etiquette in various aspects of daily life, including dress, purity, sexual behavior, and public morals. The book falls under the category of rituals, etiquette, and remembrances, and is based on multiple narrations from the Prophet’s companions. It aims to clarify the actions that are desirable to avoid in order to ensure adherence to legal controls and Islamic etiquette.
descriptions.2046: This book, “Deliverance, Deliverance, O Servants of God,” by Abu Bakr Al-Jazairi, deals with the topic of faith and its importance in the life of a Muslim. He defines faith as believing in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and destiny, indicating that true faith is like the spirit that gives a person true life, while he describes the infidel as spiritual death for losing this spirit. The book focuses on the difference between a true believer and a false believer by analyzing what a believer must do and what he must avoid in order to gain the satisfaction of God and His Messenger.
descriptions.2047: Sonal Advice is a book written by Suleiman bin Khalaf Al-Baji in which his father provides comprehensive advice to his two sons. It includes topics of faith in God, the pillars of religion, memorizing the Qur’an and acting upon it, establishing prayer, paying zakat, fasting in Ramadan, Hajj to the House and Umrah, jihad for the sake of God, seeking knowledge, the virtues of knowledge, understanding religion, and following the example of the Qur’an and Sunnah, the Messenger, the Companions, and the scholars. In the introduction to the book, the author places emphasis on the necessity of obeying the father’s advice and directing the children to the behavior of the righteous ancestors in accordance with the approach of Al-Riqaq, etiquette, and remembrance.
descriptions.2048: The Book of the End in Trials and Epics by Sheikh Ibn Katheer falls within the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrances, and specializes in collecting and clarifying the Prophetic hadiths that deal with temptations, signs of the Hour, and future events mentioned in the Sunnah. The first volume includes an introductory introduction and then a series of prophetic references to the fates of the caliphs, the conquests, and the temptations that will occur at the end of time, with an explanation of the keys to the unseen that only God knows. The text aims to convince the reader of the necessity of believing in the unseen things and indications of the Hour, based on reliable narrations.
descriptions.2049: Useful Means for a Happy Life by Sheikh Abdul Rahman Al-Saadi is a book within the classification of Al-Riqaq, Manners, and Remembrances, which outlines true happiness based on Qur’anic evidence and Prophetic guidance. The book includes chapters dealing with the causes of anxiety and nervous tension, ways to ease the chest and reassure the heart, the causes of happiness and the removal of anxiety, in addition to treatments for heart and nervous diseases. The author links faith and good deeds with achieving happiness and reassurance in the life of a Muslim.
descriptions.2050: Research into Answering the Invitation by Ibrahim Al-Ubaid is a jurisprudential study that deals with the ruling on answering invitations and their purposes from the perspective of Islamic literature, based on documented prophetic hadiths from the books of the Sunnah. The book is divided into an introduction and two sections: The first explains the rulings on the answer, the second discusses the issue of eating for the guest when he arrives, and then a conclusion summarizing the results. The work falls within the classification of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, and is based on Islamic sources and references.
descriptions.2051: The Sea of ​​Tears is a book written by Ibn al-Jawzi, and it is one of the books of enlightenment and preaching. Its author was distinguished by an interesting style that touches the heart. In it, he presented stories that make the eyes cry and move the hearts, and he classified it into chapters. He spoke about forbidden matters, disparaged them, and insulted those who did them. It is a book that encourages the remembrance of God through repentance and remorse, and makes them a means of removing grief, warding off affliction, and bringing happiness. The author enriched it with verses from the Holy Qur’an, the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ, and excerpts from poetry. He also included many sayings of the predecessors, including ascetics and worshippers, and the book is of great benefit to preachers and preachers.
descriptions.2052: The Beginning of Guidance is a book by Imam Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali, on Sufism, and is considered an introduction to the book The Revival of Religious Sciences. Al-Ghazali divided it into two parts: The first section: It dealt with obedience, and it included the etiquette of sleeping, waking up from it, entering the toilet, ablution, washing, tayammum, leaving and entering the mosque, and what follows sunrise until noon, and the etiquette of preparing for the rest of the prayers, which is the foundation of the religion, and one of the pillars of Islam, and mentioned in it what is related to the imamate, following the example, Friday prayers, and fasting. The second section talked about avoiding sins, and explained the sins of the heart, and that they are more dangerous than sins of the limbs, and the etiquette of companionship and intercourse with the Creator, Glory be to Him, and with creation.
descriptions.2053: This book, with a Mahmoudian brilliance in explaining the Muhammadan method and prophetic law, deals with multiple topics in Islamic law and morals, including adherence to the Qur’an and Sunnah, explaining heresies and their rulings, economy in worship, correcting belief, the importance of legal sciences, and the virtues of piety. The author focuses on clarifying the methods of legal behavior and explaining the actions that a Muslim must do and avoid forbidden matters, while highlighting the virtue of following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in various aspects of life.
descriptions.2054: Bustan al-Arifin, a book by Imam Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi on Sufism, the subtleties and ascetics, in which its author mentions sentences from the verses of the Qur’an, the Prophet’s hadiths, and the sayings of scholars from ascetic tales and poetry. He often clarifies the authenticity and goodness of the hadiths and the condition of their narrators, and clarifies what may be hidden or distorted in their meanings, and controls what needs to be restricted. …
descriptions.2055: The Garden of Preachers and the Garden of the Listeners is a book on preaching, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Jawzi (508 AH - 597 AH). The book consists of gatherings that the author held to remind and preach of God Almighty. It consists of eighteen sessions, including: a session on seeking refuge, a session on mentioning the Day of Resurrection and its horrors, a session on mentioning Paradise and its descriptions, and a session on the virtue of fasting. Ibn al-Jawzi supported his book with verses. The Holy Qur’an, the hadiths of the Prophet, and many effects.
descriptions.2056: This book, “The Beloved’s Good News of Atonement for Sins,” written by Al-Qabouni, deals with topics related to forgiveness and forgiveness in Islam. The author focuses on the Prophetic hadiths, sayings, and actions that bring forgiveness from God Almighty, and mentions the virtues of good deeds that bring the servant closer to his Lord and raise his status with God. The book includes various topics such as the virtue of knowledge and scholars, the virtue of praying in the first row, the virtue of trusting behind the imam, the virtue of seeking forgiveness, and the importance of forgiveness and tolerance among Muslims. The book aims to motivate the reader to get closer to God and work in a way that brings forgiveness and mercy.
descriptions.2057: This book is “Gloomy Good News of the Meeting of the Beloved” by the writer Al-Suyuti. It deals with the subject of death and its effects on believers, explaining its grace upon them and its being a release from this world to the abode of eternity. It mentions the conditions of the dead in their graves and the welcome and dignity they receive. It points out that death for believers is a masterpiece, a spoil, and an atonement, and describes it as a release from the prison of this world to another, better world.
descriptions.2058: The book “Reflections on the Believer’s Likeness to the Palm Tree” by the writer Abdul Razzaq bin Abdul Mohsen Al Badr is a book in the field of prayers, etiquette, and remembrances, in which he presents spiritual reflections on the believer’s likeness to the palm tree in order to clarify the virtue of faith and its lofty purposes. The text focuses on highlighting the importance of faith as the greatest of demands and the most lofty of goals, based on Qur’anic examples and literary passages to illustrate the fruits of faith and its benefits in this world and the hereafter. The book also includes an index limited to sources and references that support the evidence and guidance presented by the author.
descriptions.2059: This book by the scholar Ibn Baz deals with the recommended remembrances and supplications in various daily situations of a Muslim, from entering and leaving the house, entering the mosque, starting to eat and drink, and other situations. It focuses on the supplications mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah, and mentions their virtues and importance in the spiritual and worldly life of a Muslim. The book is directed to help the reader establish the habit of remembrance and supplication in his daily life, relying on the correct legal sources.
descriptions.2060: Tuhfat al-Dhakirin Bi’dat al-Husn al-Husayn from the words of al-Shawkani is a book that falls under the classification of al-Riqaq, etiquette, and adhkaar. It focuses on the virtue of remembrance, supplication, and blessings upon the Prophet, with an explanation of their etiquette, times of response, and their blessed locations. The book includes detailed chapters on the virtue of the Most Beautiful Names of God, and the preference of remembrance over charity and jihad, in addition to the doubts of some scholars about certain hadiths and their answers. It also includes chains of transmission, translations, sermons, and discussions about the Greatest Name of God and a comparison between the scholars’ sayings about it.
descriptions.2061: The book “Teaching the Holy Qur’an in Prisons and Observation Institutions” by the writer Muhammad Habib Ahmed Mukhtar is concerned with studying the royal efforts in memorizing the Qur’an inside prisons and observation institutions, based on the definition of the prison, its reformative role, and its history, in addition to analyzing the role of charitable societies and memorization circles in prisons. The research also addresses the role of observation and care for delinquent juveniles by defining observation institutions and procedures for reforming them, while highlighting the importance of the Qur’an in the lives of Muslims, as cited in the introduction. The book is classified under the category of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, which places it within the framework of religious literature concerned with the social and humanitarian effects of teaching the Qur’an.
descriptions.2062: The book Purification of Souls by Ahmed Farid falls within the category of purification, etiquette, and remembrance, and is concerned with purifying and purifying the soul by clarifying the concepts of sincerity, following the Sunnah, and the virtue of knowledge and scholars. The book deals with the types and divisions of hearts, the four poisons of the heart, the causes of its illness, and ways to nourish it with remembrance, seeking forgiveness, supplication, and blessings upon the Prophet. It aims to guide the reader to ways to improve the heart and achieve success in this world and the hereafter.
descriptions.2063: The book “Entertaining People of Misfortune” by Al-Manbaji falls within the category of Al-Riqaq, Manners, and Remembrances, and deals with the concept of misfortune from an Islamic perspective, explaining its reality and what God has prepared for the one who recovers, relying on the Qur’an and Sunnah in directing the reader to seek God’s help and replace complaint with remembrance. It sheds light on the prohibition of crying, lamenting, and wailing, and shows that misfortunes are a cure for arrogance and a key to contentment and seeking reward, while providing practical advice for steadfastness in faith and reliance on God.
descriptions.2064: Entertaining a blind person about the affliction of blindness to the public by Ali Al-Qari falls within the category of rituals, etiquette, and dhikr, and is concerned with clarifying the status of the blind in Islam and the hadiths reported about the reward of affliction, especially loss of sight. The book includes an introduction, a study of the author’s life, and an analysis of the book itself, in addition to an edited text based on sources from the Qur’an and Sunnah, with reference to scientific references. It aims to stimulate patience and gratitude for the affliction that is faced, and to show God’s promise of Paradise to the righteous.
descriptions.2065: This book is by the writer Ragheb Al-Isfahani, and it deals with topics related to tortillas, etiquette, and dhikr. The author focuses on detailing the types of beings and the human being’s place among them, reviewing the creation of the universe from a divine point of view, starting from the pen and tablet to the mind and spirituality, passing through inanimate objects and animals, and concluding with the human image. The book consists of several sections that address various topics related to existence and creation, with a focus on the differences between creative entities and complex categories, and how man was created and taught about names.
descriptions.2066: The Devil’s Dressing is a book written by Imam Abu Al-Faraj Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad Ibn Al-Jawzi Al-Qurashi Al-Taymi Al-Bakri, who was born in Baghdad in the year 510 AH and died there in the year 592 AH. Ibn Al-Jawzi divided the book into thirteen chapters, warning in it of the temptation of Satan Satan and fearing his tricks. He reveals the hidden actions of his deeds in misleading people from the straight path, and exposes his arrogance and the arrogance of those who follow him. Perished among the sons of Adam.
descriptions.2067: Alert to the heedless about the hadiths of the Master of the Prophets and Messengers, or (Attention to the Heedless) is a work by Abu Al-Layth Nasr bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Samarqandi, who died in the year 375 AH. It is a book of preaching, sermons, and etiquette. Al-Zirkli said in the translation of Al-Samarqandi: “He has valuable works, including Al-Tahbeer Al-Jafilin,” printed. It is a folder. The beginning: (Praise be to God who guided us to His Book... etc.). Arranged into: ninety-four chapters.
descriptions.2068: Alert the Sleeper Al-Ghamr on the Seasons of Life is a book about seasons, the division of ages, and their obedience, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Jawzi (508 AH - 597 AH). In his book, the author mentioned the divisions of a person’s life and made them four seasons. Then he mentioned the age of each season and detailed it, and alerted the heedless about missing out on the seasons of life and acts of worship. Topics of the book Alert the Sleeper: Immersion on the seasons of life: The first season: from the time of birth to the time of puberty, which is fifteen years. Season Two: From the time of puberty to the utmost youth. Season Three: Adulthood. Season 4: Aging.
descriptions.2069: The book “Raising a Child and Parents’ Ways to Treat and Confront Him” by Zakaria El-Sherbiny deals with the process of socialization of the child and the role of parents in directing his behavior and nurturing his moral values ​​and loyalty to society. It is based on concepts and theories in psychology and sociology, and reviews the stages of upbringing and the variables affecting them, such as aggression, imitation, and the family environment. It also discusses the goals of upbringing and its content in terms of morals, language, and the formation of the child’s identity in light of cultural transformations. It aims to provide guidance to parents and educational institutions to prepare children for effective integration into society.
descriptions.2070: This book, “Refining Morals and Purifying Races” by Ibn Miskawayh, deals with the subject of morals and human ethics from a philosophical and religious perspective. The author focuses on developing virtuous character and refining the human soul, reviewing virtues such as chastity, courage, generosity, and justice. The book also addresses various topics related to juvenile discipline and social and political etiquette, trying to present a comprehensive theory on how to achieve human perfection and true happiness.
descriptions.2071: In his book “Islamic Directives for Reforming the Individual and Society,” Muhammad Jamil Zaino presents various legal directives and rulings related to Islamic acts of worship, remembrance, and morals, trying to present them in an easy-to-understand and deep-meaning way. The book covers multiple topics from the pillars of Islam and the pillars of faith to hadiths and rulings on prayers, fasting and Hajj, with a focus on the main characteristics of Islam and its benefits in the life of the individual and society.
descriptions.2072: The book “A Collection of Arafat Speeches” by Abdulaziz bin Abdullah Al Sheikh contains a collection of sermons delivered by the author on the day of Arafat over continuous decades. The sermons address religious and educational topics, and aim to teach pilgrims and remind them of the importance of Hajj and the virtues of the Day of Arafat. The sermon is distinguished by the fact that it was delivered directly to the pilgrims in Nimra Square, and was broadcast through the media to reach Muslims in various parts of the world.
descriptions.2073: This book, "Mosques of Supplication", is written by Dr. Khaled Al-Jarisi addresses the topic of supplication from a comprehensive Islamic perspective, explaining its virtue and importance in a Muslim’s life and how to perform it in the correct way. The book focuses on the conditions and etiquette of supplication, and combines Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths related to this topic, while providing a general overview of response times and special cases that increase the effectiveness of supplication. The book is from the “Zad Al-Mu’min” series and falls into the category of Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance.
descriptions.2074: The Muslim Fortress from the Remembrances of the Qur’an and Sunnah is a book of supplications written by Saeed bin Ali bin Wahf Al-Qahtani, edited in the month of Safar 1409 AH. The book contains the remembrances of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in various situations of daily life. It is one of the most widespread Islamic books due to its easy style and its commitment to authentic hadiths. The book contains 160 pages, measuring 8.5*12 cm, and is classified under supplications and prayers according to the indexing of the King Fahd National Library in Saudi Arabia.
descriptions.2075: The book “Smash Your Idol and Be Small with Yourself” by the writer Magdy Al-Hilali presents an Islamic study on the danger of self-admiration and hidden polytheism, based on what was stated in the introduction and the chapters that address the causes of self-aggrandizement, from ignorance of God and the self to neglecting self-purification and multiple praise and authority. It highlights examples from reality to illustrate the disease of self-conceit and how it leads to the corruption of good deeds, targeting preachers, scholars, worshipers, writers, and people with talent. It aims to guide the reader to avoid self-aggrandizement and enhance devotion to God through deep awareness of the effects of hidden polytheism on behavior and good deeds.
descriptions.2076: Preserving Life by Ibn al-Jawzi is a book that belongs to the classification of Al-Riqaq, Adab, and Remembrance, highlighting the value of life and the necessity of using it for good. In three chapters, the book deals with explaining the honor of life and urging the reader to take advantage of it, mentioning those who rush to save their moments, and explaining the reasons for wasting time. In his preaching style, he links credit for work with legal obligation, calling for seriousness and certainty in striving for the afterlife.
descriptions.2077: The Knowledge Student’s Ornament” written by Bakr Abu Zaid is a book that falls under the classification of Al-Riqaq, Etiquette, and Remembrance. It specializes in the student’s etiquette in seeking legal knowledge, and in its chapters it presents the student’s etiquette with himself, with his sheikh, and with his colleagues, in addition to ways of seeking and receiving. The text focuses on attaining virtuous morals, kindness, and adhering to the etiquette of the ancestors, while directing the reader to avoid the behaviors of the tyrants, idle talk, and hesitations. The book aims to guide students of science to a balanced behavior that combines piety and seriousness in the pursuit of knowledge.
descriptions.2078: This is a message that we send out to the people to encourage the women of the believers to be virtuous, and to reveal the claims of foreigners to immorality. The book aims to protect the Islamic virtues of the women of the believers from the advocates of sedition who sought paths of sedition and to spread and spread immorality.
