descriptions.2433: This book, “People’s Confusion over the Issue of Speech with the Statement of the Truth,” by author Abdul Karim Murad, is classified under the classification of faith. The book provides a brief explanation of people's statements and their confusion regarding the issue of speech, along with an explanation of the truth indicated by evidence and attested by good nature. The author analyzes the various opinions about the meaning and name of speech, and explains that speech is both the word and the meaning. He also discusses the various opinions on this subject, including the opinions of the predecessors and the later generations.
descriptions.2434: This book, “The Belief of the Imams of Hadith,” by Abu Bakr al-Ismaili, deals with the beliefs of the scholars of hadith in the Islamic faith, explaining the principles of belief upon which the scholars of hadith and their imams agree. The author focuses on clarifying the names and attributes of God mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah, while emphasizing the necessity of accepting authentic narrations about them without opposition or modification. The book also shows the positions of the scholars of hadith on important doctrinal issues such as faith and disbelief, heaven and hell, destiny, and other doctrinal issues about which scholars differed.
descriptions.2435: This book, “The Belief of the Imams of the Salaf, Ahl al-Hadith,” by the author Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman al-Khamis, is considered a book on belief that aims to explain the belief of the Salaf, Ahl al-Hadith, and Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah. The author points out the importance of explaining this doctrine and challenging those who oppose it, and is based on the works of Salaf scholars such as Imam Al-Ash’ari and Imam Al-Hakim. The book is divided into four sections: the first is concerned with the belief of the Salaf in general, the second is concerned with the belief of the hadith scholars, the third is concerned with explaining the belief of the hadith scholars which was stated by Imam Al-Ash’ari in his articles, and the fourth is concerned with the sources and references of the book. This book is an important source for learning about the doctrine of the Salaf and Ahl al-Hadith, and it forms part of the efforts made by the author to clarify the correct doctrine and challenge those who oppose it.
descriptions.2436: The book “The Belief of the Sunnis, Explanation of the People of Hadith” by the writer Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khamis is concerned with explaining the Sunni doctrine according to the approach of the People of Hadith, as it deals with the origins of belief, the attributes of God, the stations of faith and Islam, the concepts of predestination, destiny, resurrection, reckoning, and other doctrinal issues, as appears in the table of contents. The author opens his work with an introductory introduction based on Qur’anic texts and calling for the commitment of the predecessors to steadfastness in the doctrine.
descriptions.2437: The book “The Belief of the Four Imams” by the writer Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khamis is concerned with studying the belief of the four imams in Sunni schools of thought, focusing on the monotheism of God, destiny, faith, and their position on the Companions and theology. The author shows through his chapters that the four imams of the doctrine agree on the fundamentals of religion in terms of the attributes of God, affirming the Qur’an as uncreated words, and obliging the heart and tongue to believe. The work is considered a reference in the field of doctrine that highlights the doctrinal compatibility between the four imams of jurisprudence.
descriptions.2438: The Book of Beliefs of Muslim and Polytheist Sects by Al-Razi Fakhr al-Din is a book in the field of belief that sheds light on the positions and doctrines of various Islamic and Eastern sects. The author provides a detailed explanation of the sects such as the Mu'tazilites, Kharijites, Karramites, Jabriyahs and others, explaining their positions on the attributes of God, the Qur'an, and doctrinal issues. The work aims to clarify the differences between these teams and show what they have in common and what distinguishes them.
descriptions.2439: The book “The Division of the Ummah into Seventy-One Sects” by the writer Al-San’ani is classified among the works of the faith, as it collects and reviews prophetic hadiths dealing with the division of the nation into seventy-three sects, with reference to the division of the Jews and Christians into a similar number of branches. The author focuses on analyzing texts and comparing their narratives, relying on sources such as Ibn al-Atheer, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi, to clarify the consequences of this division in terms of fate in hell or heaven. The book aims to clarify the concept of unity and difference within the nation from a legal perspective.
descriptions.2440: The book “Al-Athār al-Marwīyah fi Sifat al-Ma‘iyya” by its author, Muhammad bin Khalifa al-Tamimi, deals with the subject of faith, as it collects texts narrated on the attribute of al-Ma‘iyya and is based on the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the traditions of the predecessors. It is divided into four topics dealing with the verses of Al-Ma’iyah, the scholars’ sayings regarding their interpretation, the combination of the attributes of transcendence and Al-Ma’iyah, and people’s sayings about this attribute. The author aims to clarify issues related to association and respond to the suspicions that arise about it.
descriptions.2441: A book that collects the narratives narrated on the authority of Caliph Omar bin Abdul Aziz in the chapters of faith, and studies them scientifically. Its content is limited to what was mentioned about the unification of divinity and divinity, and the most beautiful names of God and His highest attributes, with details in the topics of supplication, trust, fear, hope, and prohibition of polytheism and its means.
descriptions.2442: The clear verses about the dead not hearing, written by Ibn al-Alusi, a book in the field of faith that presents Qur’anic and jurisprudential evidence that the dead do not hear the words of the living, based on the sayings of the Hanafi imams and the sources of jurists. The book includes chapters dealing with indoctrination after burial, the lives of the prophets in the isthmus, and bliss and torment in the grave for the soul and body, in addition to discussing the torment of the grave and visits to graves. The author aims to clarify what the public is ignorant of regarding the sayings of scholars and to show what is correct regarding the issue of not hearing the dead according to the Hanafi approach.
descriptions.2443: The book presents an analytical study of the famous hadith narrated by Imam Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) on the description of istiwa, based on a brief translation of the Imam and a discussion of the belief of the Sunnis and the community. The author addresses the importance of rules in knowing the attributes of God, and presents documentation of the hadith by grading it and proving its authenticity with the Qur’an, Sunnah, and the analogues of the righteous predecessors. It also includes invalidating the distortions of innovations related to this work and mentioning general benefits derived from it, with a conclusion and reference sources.
descriptions.2444: This book, “Useful Answers to the Tasks of Doctrine,” by author Abdul Rahman Al-Dosari, is classified under the category of doctrine. The book contains a table of contents covering a range of questions and answers related to monotheism, slavery, religion, and Islam. The book begins with an introduction from the publisher, followed by an introduction from the author, in which he emphasizes the importance of religion and monotheism in human life. The book shows the author's interest in presenting information in a simplified question-and-answer format, making it easy to understand and study.
descriptions.2445: This book is a lecture by Sheikh Muhammad Al-Amin Al-Shanqeeti in which he discusses the topic of the names and attributes of God Almighty from two perspectives: transmission and reason. The author focuses on clarifying the belief of the Salaf on this subject and showing the correct path towards understanding the verses about attributes in the Qur’an. Al-Shanqeeti emphasizes the necessity of moderation in the search for attributes and warns of the three foundations upon which believers in this field must rely, which are God’s dissociation from similarity to created beings in attributes, and belief in what God and His Messenger have described, while emphasizing the impermissibility of likening God’s attributes to the attributes of created beings or denying His attributes without legal evidence.
descriptions.2446: This is a brief introductory overview of the book “Terms and Terms Concerning the Oneness of Godhood” by the author Amal bint Abdul Aziz Al-Amr: The book is a classification of the doctrine, and aims to study the terms and terminology of the doctrine, determine their meanings according to the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community, and explain what the sects mean by them. The book begins by defining the need to know these limits, and defining the sources of the Sunnis and their rules in the words of the doctrine and its terminology, then it moves on to studying the sources of the opponents and their rules in the words of the doctrine and its terminology. The book also discusses the meaning of the limit according to logicians and its criticism according to the Sunnis. The book is an important source for learning about the meanings of the doctrine’s words and terminology, and explaining what the sects mean by them. It helps student scholars to refute their falsehood and clarify the truth to them.
descriptions.2447: A book on doctrine, written by Abd al-Rahman bin Yusuf al-Ifriqi in response to a request from some of the Brotherhood for a scientific study on the issue of heresy and the Sunnis’ denial of the Tijaniya method. The author aims to show that what was not a religion in the early days cannot be a religion today, relying on the statements of Sunni scholars in interpreting the verses and hadiths that condemn heresy and its people.
descriptions.2448: This book is a brief treatise on faith, in which the author examines the truth of the Ibadi sect and the extent of its affiliation to the Kharijite sect. The author begins by clarifying the motives for writing about this sect, including its notable activity in publishing its books. Then he moves on to defining Ibadis and explaining the sources of their reception, to then answer the central question: Are Ibadis Kharijites? The book concludes with advice addressed to the Ibadi community.
descriptions.2449: Explaining the Fundamentals of Religion is a book on the science of Islamic belief, written by Abu al-Hasan al-Ash’ari, in which he talked about the disputed doctrinal principles, such as the vision of God, his speech, his ascendance to the throne, destiny, and what is similar to the Qur’an, with rational and transmissional evidence and a response to the opposing sects on those issues and other principles. The Lebanese hadith scholar and researcher, Gabriel Fouad Haddad, states that the current version of Al-Ibanah attributed today to Imam Al-Ash’ari is an unsupported, anonymous, and forged copy by Al-Mujasimah, and clearly carries an anti-Ash’ari and anti-Hanafi tendency. He also confirms that the original, unaltered copy was in the possession of Ash'ari scholars such as Ibn Asakir, Abu Uthman al-Sabouni, and others.
descriptions.2450: This book, “Creativity in Explaining the Perfection of Sharia and the Danger of Innovation,” by author Ibn Uthaymeen, falls within the classification of doctrine. The book contains a table of contents covering multiple topics, including an explanation of the perfection of Islamic law, the danger of innovation, heresy, the Sunnah, and the interpretation of Qur’anic verses. The book begins by mentioning praise be to God, then moves on to explaining the foundations of religion and the branches of religion, and points out that the Great Qur’an in which God Almighty has explained the foundations of religion and branches of religion, including monotheism, etiquette of gatherings, and seeking permission. The book contains excerpts from the Holy Qur’an, such as the verse “O you who have believed, when it is said to you: Make space in the gatherings, then make space, and God will make space for you” (Al-Mujadila 11). It appears that the book aims to demonstrate the perfection of Islamic law, educate people about the danger of innovation, and explain the importance of adhering to the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.2451: This book deals with a detailed criticism of the theory of mixing the religion of Islam with other religions, such as Judaism and Christianity, and aims to invalidate attempts at rapprochement between these religions and refute their dangers to Islam and Muslims. The author discusses the history of this theory throughout the ages and its negative effects, relying on legal and scientific evidence to confirm its invalidity. The book falls within the field of Islamic faith and aims to warn against attempts at Westernization and external influences on the Islamic religion.
descriptions.2452: The book “Al-Ithaf in Response to Al-Sahhaf” by the scholar Abdul Latif Al Al-Sheikh deals with topics of the Islamic faith by responding to the ideas of Abdul Latif Al-Sahhaf who opposes the Salafist call. The author focuses on clarifying the meaning of monotheism and explaining the types of atonement and their ruling, citing legal evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It also clarifies the difference between takfir based on legal evidence and that of one who issues it merely because of enmity or whims. The book aims to correct misconceptions about matters of faith and promote a correct understanding of monotheism and atonement.
descriptions.2453: This book, “Guidance to True Belief and the Response to People of Polytheism and Atheism,” by Sheikh Saleh Al-Fawzan, is a book on the Islamic faith that aims to clarify the correct belief and direct people towards monotheism and reform of the belief. The book covers the most important matters in the Islamic faith, such as the monotheism of divinity, the monotheism of divinity, and belief in angels, books, and messengers, and it also addresses the people of polytheism and atheism. The book is based on the sayings of Muslim scholars, such as Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim, and also addresses some modern practices that contradict the Islamic faith. This book is a valuable resource for learning about the correct Islamic faith and correcting misconceptions.
descriptions.2454: This book, “Islam, Its Origins and Principles,” by Dr. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Saleh Al-Suhaim, deals with the Islamic faith in a comprehensive and integrated manner. The author focuses on clarifying the origins of the Islamic religion and its basic principles, relying on the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet as main sources. The book aims to highlight the truth of Islam and the calling of the Messengers, and to explain the difference between it and other religions, while presenting a deep doctrinal vision that aims to invite non-Muslims to Islam.
descriptions.2455: The book is a book in the field of doctrine that aims to expose what the author sees as corruption and illusions in Christian teachings, especially with regard to the concept of hypostases, the Trinity of Oneness, and the doctrines of union and solutions. The author relies on reviewing their ideological positions and then presenting responses and arguments to refute them, based on Sharia and declarative evidence. The text includes detailed chapters dealing with invalidating their statement regarding the hypostases and showing the weakness of their arguments regarding the union, along with a review of the responses to the questioners’ questions. The book shows a critical methodology aimed at demonstrating the correctness of Islamic monotheism against what it describes as heresies.
descriptions.2456: The book “Information of Violations of Approvals and Settlements” by the writer Nasser Al-Fahd deals with a critical analysis of the positions of Imam Abu Ishaq Al-Shatibi on the doctrine, focusing on what the author sees as violations in the unification of divinity and the unification of names and attributes, as well as in issues of faith and destiny. This is based on a detailed index that includes chapters and topics dealing with the attributes of God, the interpretation of injustice, issues of mental improvement and ugliness, and the concept of causes and causes. The book aims to clarify the gap between Al-Shatibi’s doctrine and the components of the Sunni faith according to the Ash’ari approach.
descriptions.2457: This book, “The Imamate and the Response to the Rafidah,” by the author Abu Naim Al-Asbahani, is classified under the classification of doctrine. The book is considered one of the most important historical and jurisprudential sources in understanding and interpreting the doctrine of imamate and caliphate in Islam, and it contains an index of contents that shows the author’s orientation towards the topics of the book. The book begins by mentioning the Caliphate and the Commander of the Faithful, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, then talks about the Shiites and presents different opinions about the Imamate, and the author tries to prove the correctness of these opinions. The book is considered one of the important sources in understanding the Islamic faith, especially with regard to the caliphate and imamate.
descriptions.2458: Fairness in what was said about the Mawlid regarding the exaggeration and unfairness by the writer Abu Bakr Al-Jazairi. He is a doctrinal author who deals with the issue of the Prophet’s Mawlid from a critical perspective. He clarifies what he sees as exaggerations and transgressions in celebrating it and sets boundaries between heresy and legitimate innovations. The book includes chapters that explain the Islamic rulings on birthdays in general and in detail about the Prophet’s birthday, and presents arguments to respond to mutual accusations between the conflicting groups, with guidance on acceptable alternatives. It aims to calm the strife surrounding this topic and guide the reader to a balanced understanding.
descriptions.2459: This book deals with the topic of faith from two main perspectives: the doctrine of the Salaf and the theologian doctrines. The author focuses on explaining the doctrine of the Salaf regarding the truth of faith, its increase, and its deficiency. Then he moves on to present the opinions of the various theological schools of thought, such as the Kharijites, Murji’ahs, Ash’aris, and others, on the issue of faith. The book aims to explain the Salaf’s point of view regarding the opinions of theologians in this field and to refute those opinions according to the Salaf’s approach.
descriptions.2460: The book “Faith: Its Reality, Its Laws, and Its Nullifiers According to the Sunnis and the Community” by Sheikh Abdullah bin Abdul Hamid Al-Athari is concerned with clarifying the concept of faith in language and legal terminology, while relying on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book deals with the definition of faith, its conditions, the factors of its increase and decrease, and its stages, in addition to a review of the pillars of faith, such as the unification of divinity, divinity, and attributes, and belief in angels, books, and messengers. It also highlights the exceptions in faith and Islam and compares them, with reference to the opinions of the imams of the Sunnis and the community, making it a brief reference supported by evidence for students and those interested in the faith.
descriptions.2461: The book “Faith and the Response to People of Heresy” by Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Hassan Al Sheikh deals with the subject of faith, as it explains the concept of faith in Islam and answers questions about heresies through inferences from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It includes chapters called Al-Fawa'id that deal with explaining the meaning of there is no god but God, the difference between absolute faith and absolute faith, and the rulings on acts of worship and transactions, in addition to answers to jurisprudential questions related to heresies. It aims to clarify the principles of faith and link them to apparent and hidden actions, with a focus on responding to practices that contradict the faith.
descriptions.2462: The book “The Qadiri Belief” by Abu Taher Al-Karaji is concerned with studying the biography of the Abbasid Caliph Al-Qadir Billah and highlighting his efforts in manifesting Islam and establishing the Sunnah. It also deals with an analysis of the text of the Qadiri Belief in terms of its author, the occasion of its composition, its advantages and its effects. The work falls within the classification of doctrine, and is based on a research methodology that includes an introduction, introduction, and detailed chapters that address the topics of legal manifestation and response to esotericism. This book is considered a reference that sheds light on the role of the Abbasid leader in promoting the doctrine of the Sunnis and documenting the impact of the doctrinal text.
descriptions.2463: This book, “Belief” by Ibn Abi Ya’la, is a work on the Islamic faith that deals with the concepts of faith and monotheism according to the approach of the Sunnis and the community. The author explains the doctrine of the Salaf in matters of faith, attributes, destiny, and others, and reviews the efforts made to defend this doctrine against the innovators and the individualists.
descriptions.2464: A book on the Islamic faith, aiming to explain the doctrine of the righteous predecessors, which is characterized by moderation between excess and negligence. The author deals with a number of basic doctrinal issues, such as the attributes of God Almighty, belief in destiny, the Last Day, and other topics, relying on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.2465: Victory in the Response to the Wicked Qadari Mu'tazilites is a book of faith by the author Yahya bin Al-Khair Al-Omrani. The origin of this book is a doctoral dissertation from the Islamic University under the supervision of Dr. Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad. The name of the book was mentioned in the manuscript as follows: (The Victory in the Response to the Wicked Qadari Mu’tazila), and it was written above the word Mu’tazila (Sahih), which indicates that it was added in the case of an interview or something similar. Al-Jaadi mentioned it as: (Victory in responding to the evil Qadariyya). …
descriptions.2466: This book deals with the reactions to Hassan al-Maliki’s views on the Islamic faith, where the author Abdul Mohsen al-Abbad explains al-Maliki’s falsehoods and exposes the falsity of his claims that it is a Sunni Hanbali approach. Al-Abbad focuses on Al-Maliki's criticism of Sunni books and his false accusations against the followers of the Hanbali school of thought, refuting his claims one by one. The book aims to defend the correct Sunni doctrine and state the facts by responding to Al-Maliki’s slanders and denying his suspicions.
descriptions.2467: This book, “The Victory for the Unitarian Party of God and the Response to the Controversies,” written by Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abdul Aziz Ababtain, is considered a book in the field of Islamic doctrine. The book deals with topics related to monotheism and faith, and includes responses to debates about polytheism and heresies. The book seems to aim to defend the Islamic faith and respond to those who argue against it. The book contains multiple chapters, including an introduction and difference between major polytheism and heresies, and includes an excerpt from the beginning of the book that explains the importance of defending the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2468: This book, “Victory for the Good Companions in Refuting Hasan al-Maliki’s Falsehoods,” written by Abdul Mohsen al-Abbad, deals with defending the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) and refuting the suspicions raised by those who doubt them. The author focuses on refuting Hassan al-Maliki's claims and criticizing his views regarding the Companions, citing evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book emphasizes the Sunni belief in loving the Companions and being loyal to them, and emphasizes the danger of attacking or disparaging them.
descriptions.2469: The book “Victory for the Companions and Family from the Fabrications of the Misguided Heavenly Ones” by Ibrahim bin Aamer Al-Ruhaili is a doctrinal work that specializes in discussing and refuting the claims of the Rafidah towards the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt. It includes the definition of the Shiites, their upbringing, and beliefs, and then presents responses to their arguments through inferences from hadiths and narrations, based on the positions of the Sunnis and Ahl al-Bayt. The work aims to establish the Sunni doctrine and show the validity of the Companions’ position on these claims.
descriptions.2470: The motivation to deny heresies. A book written by Imam Shihab al-Din Abu Shama al-Maqdisi.
descriptions.2471: This book deals with the issue of the Islamic faith by responding to the suspicions raised by followers of other religions, especially Christians, about their beliefs and divine books. The author focuses on proving the validity of Islam and explaining its proofs, reviewing verses from the Torah and the Gospel that indicate the prophecy of Muhammad ﷺ, and also reviewing the contradictions that indicate the distortion of these books. The book aims to show religious facts in an elaborate scientific and research manner, relying on investigation and scrutiny of other religious texts.
descriptions.2472: This is the book “The Annual Heresies” by Sheikh Abdullah Al-Tuwaijri. It is a book on faith that focuses on the subject of heresies and defining them, and includes chapters on the causes of the emergence of heresies, their impact on society, and means of preventing them. The book begins by defining heresy, then addresses the reasons for its emergence, its effects, and means of preventing it, while addressing some similarities that may arise in relation to heresy. The book is considered an important source for understanding the concept of heresies in Islam and putting an end to them.
descriptions.2473: This book, “Innovations and Their Bad Effects,” by Sheikh Abd al-Karim Murad, is considered a book in the field of faith. It aims to define the concept of heresy in Islamic law and condemn it, while shedding light on jurisprudential approval and the mursal reasoning called maslahah mursalah. The book begins with an introduction that explains the importance of the subject of heresy and its bad effects. Then it moves on to defining and explaining heresy, where it is defined as an invented method in religion that is similar to the legal method. It is explained that heresy is an act carried out in this manner, and behavior based on it is considered worship of God Almighty. This book is an important source for learning about the concept of heresy in Islam, and is considered a reference for jurists and commentators in the field of faith.
descriptions.2474: This book deals with the topic of heresies in Islam and their impact on the deviation of religious perceptions. The author, Sheikh Saleh Al-Suhaimi, reviews the concept of heresies and its ruling in Islamic law, relying on the Qur’an and Sunnah. It also explains the difference between heresy and the correct guidance brought by the message of Muhammad, and urges adherence to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet and to stay away from everything that contradicts them. The book is classified as a doctrine and aims to clarify the dangers of innovation in the Islamic religion and explain the reasons that lead to division and disagreement among Muslims.
descriptions.2475: The book “Islamic Proofs in Refuting Persian Suspicions” by Sheikh Abdul Latif Al Sheikh is a doctrinal work that aims to present Islamic arguments to respond to Persian suspicions, and is based on the approach of investigating the message and documenting evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book includes chapters explaining the investigation method, the author’s translation, his biography, his students and sheikhs, in addition to a conclusion and reference sources.
descriptions.2476: The book “Baha’ism is one of the backbones of colonialism and Zionism” by Sheikh Abdul Qadir Shaybah Al-Hamad falls within the classification of faith, and it deals with a critical analysis of Baha’ism as an atheistic conspiracy planned by Zionist Freemasonry to change and weaken the Islamic religion. In his presentation, the author relies on a historical review that includes the stages of the group’s emergence, the Badasht Conference, and its transformations from Babism to Baha’ism, with reference to personalities and institutions that he describes as an organization. The text aims to clarify what the writer sees as the threats this movement poses to the identity and faith of the Islamic community.
descriptions.2477: The book “Al-Bayan Al-Mubadi of the Heinousness of Meaningful Speech” by Suleiman bin Sahman is a doctrinal work that sheds light on the monotheism of God and the manifestation of truth over falsehood, based on the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the predecessors. It includes an introduction that praises God and confirms the testimony of monotheism, then deals with responses to contemporary jurisprudential and sectarian opinions, based on legal inferences. It aims to strengthen the Islamic faith and refute what it sees as heresies and concepts that are contrary to the Sunni approach.
descriptions.2478: This is the book “Al-Bayan wal-Ishhar” written by Sheikh Fawzan Al-Sabir, and it is a book on belief that aims to refute the suspicions of the atheist Hajj Mukhtar and correct the correct belief. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as the atheist’s distortion of the word of God, his behavior in it, a response to his claim that ijtihad is an innovation, an explanation of the doctrine of the Salaf, evidence from his words in his fight against the doctrine of the Salaf, his fabrication of lies, the atheist’s declaring the scholars of the Salaf to be infidels, and rebutting what the atheist claimed about the tyranny of the Wahhabis and their oppression of the Hijaz. The book is considered useful in its subject matter, and the author has dealt with it to refute the suspicions of polytheists and hypocrites who mix truth with falsehood.
descriptions.2479: The book “Al-Bayhaqi and His Position on Divinity” by Ahmed bin Attiya bin Ali Al-Ghamdi is concerned with studying the biography of Imam Al-Bayhaqi and his doctrinal approach, with a focus on his views on proving the existence of God, His names, and His attributes. It includes detailed chapters on his life, his sheikhs, his writings, and his method of reasoning, and then deals with a systematic analysis of his positions on the divine, including rational and experiential attributes and the vision of God. It is classified among the works of faith and is based on selected sources and references.
descriptions.2480: Insight into religion and distinguishing the saved sect from the perished sect is a book written by Imam Abu al-Muzaffar Shahfur bin Tahir al-Isfarayini (d. 471 AH), nicknamed Hujjat al-Muttaqallimun. Imam Muhammad Zahid al-Kawthari edited the book, translated the author’s hadiths, and annotated his hadiths.
descriptions.2481: The book “Warning against Heresies” by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz deals with the issue of legal rulings related to religious celebrations that are considered heresies, based on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It is divided into messages detailing the ruling on celebrating the Prophet’s birthday, the night of the Isra’ and Mi’raj, and the night of the middle of Sha’ban, and responding to an alleged vision related to the Prophet’s maid. This work falls within the classification of faith, as it focuses on clarifying what is desirable and what it is desirable to avoid in terms of illegal practices in religion.
descriptions.2482: This book is an explanation of the poetic collections written by Imam Ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani in the field of the Islamic faith. The explanation addresses important topics in the Sunni faith, such as the vision of God Almighty, the attribute of descent, the doctrine of the Sunnis regarding the Companions, belief in destiny, and belief in the Last Day, while warning against heresies and deviant sects such as the Kharijites and the Murji’ah. The book was prepared and written by Abd al-Razzaq bin Abd al-Muhsin al-Badr, and it is a detailed explanation of the famous Sunni poem known as “Al-Ha’iya.”
descriptions.2483: The Madani Masterpiece in the Salafi Doctrine is a book by Sheikh Hamad bin Nasser Al Muammar, which specializes in the subject of the Salafist doctrine, in which it presents the concept of divine names and attributes from the perspective of the Qur’anic and Hadith texts, with an explanation of the proof of the attribute of transcendence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book includes chapters based on the sayings of the four imams and other Salaf scholars, and in its inferences it relies on what was reported from God Himself and His Messenger without adaptation or representation. It aims to provide a comprehensive explanation of the views related to the divine attributes according to the approach of the righteous predecessors.
descriptions.2484: The Mahdi Masterpiece Explanation of the Tadmurian Creed by Sheikh Faleh bin Mahdi Al Mahdi is an educational work in the field of belief that clarifies the articles of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah on the issue of monotheism from the perspective of divinity and Sharia. It reviews the implications of the two Surahs of Ikhlas on the types of monotheism and addresses the subject of names and attributes. The explanation includes detailed discussions about various sects such as the Qarmatians, Mu’tazila, and Jahmiya, with evidence from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, the biography of the predecessors, and the sayings of scholars. The book aims to clarify the correct doctrine and invalidate false beliefs that have spread throughout the ages.
descriptions.2485: Declaring what has been repeatedly mentioned in the Descent of Christ is a book written by Anwar Shah Al-Kashmiri, d. 1353 AH. The book was printed several times and verified. The book conveys the news of the descent of Christ as part of the signs of the end times mentioned in the Prophetic hadiths and the narrations of the Companions and Followers, and this news is part of the signs of the Day of Resurrection, and the author does not touch in his book on Christian or Jewish sources. Christian narratives regarding the so-called second coming of Christ differ from Islamic narratives, even though they agree with them in some aspects. The writing of the book coincided with the spread of the new Qadiani religion, which denies the true descent of Christ and makes it symbolic. So they say that what is meant by his revelation is the coming of someone similar to him from the Islamic nation.
descriptions.2486: Getting to know the doctrine of the people of Sufism, a book on the science of Sufism, written by Abu Bakr al-Kalabadi, who died in the year 380 AH, where he says in his introduction to the book: “This led me to write in this book a description of their method - that is, Sufism - and an explanation of their approach and path of saying about monotheism and attributes and everything related to it, which was suspected by those who did not know their doctrines and did not serve their sheikhs. It revealed with the tongue of knowledge what could be revealed, and described with apparent clarity what was appropriate to describe, to be understood by those who understood their signs, and to be understood by those who did not understand their expressions. …
descriptions.2487: The book “Sunni Commentaries on the Wasitiyyah Creed” is an explanation and commentary on the text of the Wasitiyyah Creed, and falls within the classification of the Islamic faith. The book deals in detail with the issues of the fundamentals of religion related to the names and attributes of God, proving them in the manner of the Sunnis and the community, while denying representation and disruption. This includes topics such as proving hearing, sight, will, will, face, hands, leveling, height, accompaniment, and speech to God Almighty, in addition to the interpretation of some verses, such as the sura of sincerity and the verse of the Throne. It also presents the position of the Sunnis regarding the hadiths mentioned in the attributes and distinguishes them from other sects.
descriptions.2488: This book, “The Brief Commentaries on the Text of the Tahawi Doctrine” by Sheikh Saleh Al-Fawzan, is considered a book on the classification of doctrine, aiming to explain the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community according to the doctrine of the jurists of the religion, and to explain the principles of religion by which they adhere to the Lord of the Worlds. The book is based on the text of the Tahawi doctrine by the scholar Hujjat al-Islam Abu Jaafar al-Warraq al-Tahawi, and it deals with topics about the monotheism of God, His attributes, His power, the oneness of God, His lack of a partner, His lack of resemblance to creatures, His existence does not end, He does not die, He does not sleep, He does not need anything, He does not fear anything, and He does not experience difficulty in anything. The book is considered an important source for learning about the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community, explaining the fundamentals of the religion, explaining what is wrong with it, and helping to understand the correct doctrine, paying attention to it, and paying attention to what is wrong with it.
descriptions.2489: This book, “Comments on the Board of the Shine of Belief,” by Ibn Jibreen, is classified under the category of belief. This book is a commentary on the book “Lum’at al-Iqidan” by Ibn Qudamah al-Hanbali, in which Ibn Jibreen provides an interpretation and explanation of the doctrinal concepts and rulings in the original book. The excerpt provided shows that the book aims to facilitate understanding of the Islamic faith for scholarly students, with an emphasis on stating simple meanings and interpretations of hadiths and verses. This book is a useful resource for learning and benefiting from Islamic doctrinal concepts.
descriptions.2490: This book, “The Talmud, Its History and Teachings,” by author Zafarul Islam Khan, falls within the category of doctrine. The book contains a comprehensive table of contents covering various topics of the book, including the origins of the Talmud and its impact on the Jews, the Talmud of Jerusalem and the Talmud of Babylon, the Pharisees and other Jewish sects, Talmud and Karaite beliefs and the impact of Islam, women in the Talmud, the Talmud and the question of Christ, the rules of Talmudic logic, Talmudic superstitions, Talmudic religion and Hinduism, and many other topics. The book begins with an introduction by the author, where he explains the reason for his interest in the Talmud and its history, and talks about the lack of serious studies in the Arab library that address Arab and Zionist issues objectively. The book is considered an important resource for anyone who wishes to study the Talmud, its history, and its teachings.
descriptions.2491: This book, “Adhering to the Sunnahs and Warning Against Heresies,” by the scholar Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi, is considered one of the most important sources in the Islamic faith, as it focuses on the importance of adhering to the Sunnahs and warning against heresies and misguidance. The author begins by mentioning the importance of following and innovation in the validity or corruption of one’s faith, and presents the Qur’anic verses in which God commanded followers of His Messenger ﷺ. He also mentions the sayings of the righteous predecessors in this regard, and presents their own writings in this field. This book is considered an important source for learning about the correct Islamic faith, and helps understand the importance of adhering to the Sunnahs and warning against heresies and misguidance.
descriptions.2492: The introduction to the explanation of the Book of Tawheed is a detailed explanation of the Book of Tawheed by Ibn Abdul Wahhab. It explains the principles of monotheism and refutes forms of polytheism, magic, and other practices that contradict the monotheism of worship. It is presented by Saleh Al-Sheikh as part of recorded lectures at the Sheikh Al-Islam Mosque in Riyadh, and includes content divided into sections dealing with the virtue of monotheism, the call to the testimony of there is no god but God, and an analysis of the various manifestations of polytheism and heresies. It aims to clarify the meanings of monotheism according to the Qur’an and Sunnah, with evidence from verses and hadiths.
descriptions.2493: The book “Al-Nahibat Al-Latifah regarding what Al-Wasitiyyah Contains” by Sheikh Abdul Rahman Al-Saadi is concerned with explaining the Al-Wasitiyya doctrine through subtle warnings detailing the topics of monotheism, the names and attributes of God, belief in God, the Qur’an as uncreated speech, and other doctrinal issues. The book includes chapters that discuss the establishment of the Most Gracious on His throne, the closeness of God, the intercessions of the Prophet, belief in destiny, and commitment to enjoining good and forbidding evil, while directing the reader to an integrated understanding of the Sunni approach to belief. Through an introductory introduction, the author provides an explanation of the importance of the science of monotheism as the most noble of sciences, calling for the monotheism of God in His divinity, names, and attributes in accordance with the prophetic approach.
descriptions.2494: The book “Brief Warnings Explanation of Inevitable Obligations” by Ibrahim Al-Khuraisi falls within the classification of faith, and is concerned with explaining the concept of monotheism and the conditions for affirming there is no god but God in terms of knowledge, certainty, sincerity, honesty, love, submission and acceptance, based on legal evidence. The book includes detailed chapters on the Basmalah, the three daily prayers, and the origins of religion, and then deals in depth with each of the conditions of monotheism, clarifying their meanings and their impact on faith. The author opens the text with a preface that highlights the importance of knowing God and realizing His monotheism as the first duty of the servant to achieve happiness and salvation in this world and the hereafter.
descriptions.2495: The book “Tawhid for Youth and Beginners” by the writer Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad Al Abdul Latif is concerned with simplifying the concepts of the Islamic faith and clarifying the basics of monotheism in a way that suits the category of youth and beginners. The book includes general directions and guiding questions that address the topics of belief in God, the pillars of the two testimonies, the foundations of belief, and the types of monotheism, in addition to discussing the polytheism it contradicts and the effect of faith on behavior. The content is formulated in a concise and clear manner that aims to teach monotheism and enhance the reader’s doctrinal understanding.
descriptions.2496: This book, “Monotheism and the Explanation of the Pure Salafi Doctrine,” by the author Abdullah bin Humaid, is considered a book on the classification of doctrine. The book includes chapters on the unification of divinity, the unification of divinity, and the unification of names and attributes, in addition to an introduction that presents the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book is concerned with explaining the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community, and bears witness to the monotheism of God and His attributes. They believe that God is the Creator, the Creator, the Formator, the Sustainer, the Provider, the Provider, the Ruler. They believe that God is the Wise, the Most Merciful, the Forgiving, the Forgiving, and they describe Him as He described Himself.
descriptions.2497: Kitab al-Tawhid by al-Mutridi is concerned with the doctrine of monotheism in Islam, as it rejects blind imitation and affirms the necessity of knowing the religion with evidence based on hearing and reason. In its chapters, the author deals with issues related to the attributes of God, existence and creation, and the concept of the throne and vision, in addition to discussing the opinions of different jurists and thinkers. The work highlights a rational approach to reasoning about belief, based on eyes, news, and theory as ways to reach knowledge. The book concludes by explaining the differences in sects in the world and the methods of monotheism.
descriptions.2498: A book on faith that sheds light on the concept of disbelief in terms of speech, action, and belief, based on the statements of scholars from various sects and schools of jurisprudence. The author, Alawi Al-Saqqaf, presents a moderate and economical approach in dealing with issues related to verbal and practical expiations, based on historical references and detailed explanations. The book includes a comprehensive understanding of the subject through a group of fatwas and opinions that have been scrutinized and reviewed by a number of scholars.
descriptions.2499: The book “Tawassul in the Book of God Almighty” by the writer Talal bin Mustafa Arqsus provides an objective study in the doctrine of the concept of tawassul and its rulings. The author relies on the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, and in his chapters he reviews the meanings of supplication, examples from Surah Al-Fatihah, the prophets, the Companions, and those of understanding, and explains the legitimate ways of supplication in faith, good deeds, remembrance, and righteousness. It aims to clarify the correct understanding of tawassul and remove disputes related to it by collecting evidence and explaining the etiquette of tawassul to God Almighty.
descriptions.2500: This is the book “The Useful Clarification of the Issues of the Book of Tawheed” by the author Abdullah Al-Dawish. It is a book on faith that aims to clarify and explain some issues related to monotheism and polytheism. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as the virtue of monotheism, fear of polytheism, supplication to the testimony that there is no god but God, interpretation of monotheism, polytheism, the ring and the thread, incantations and amulets, sacrifices to other than God, vows to other than God, seeking refuge in other than God, seeking help from other than God, intercession, guidance, exaggeration in the righteous, protection of the Chosen One ﷺ, magic, soothsaying, astrology, and astrology. The book is considered a useful source for learning about some doctrinal and jurisprudential issues in Islam, and reflects the influence of Sheikh Abdullah Al-Dawish in the field of doctrine and jurisprudence.
descriptions.2501: The book “The Clarification of the Oneness of Creation in the Answer of the People of Iraq” by Suleiman bin Abdullah Al Sheikh is a doctrinal work that responds to the positions of the people of Iraq towards Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s approach to the Oneness of the Creator, and is based on the letters and criticisms received from the Sheikh. The book addresses basic definitions such as apostate, consensus, salaf, and intercession, and presents arguments on issues of monotheism, righteous means, Salafi doctrine, and the positions of the Kharijites and Mu’tazilites. It concludes by clarifying the importance of reviving the doctrinal heritage according to the approach of the Sunnis and the community as a basis for building the Islamic society.
descriptions.2502: The book “Clarification and Explanation of the Tree of Faith” by the scholar Abd al-Rahman al-Saadi is a book in the field of faith that explains the concept of faith in terms of its limits and interpretation, based on Qur’anic texts and prophetic hadiths to clarify its origins and components. It also discusses the sources of faith and what is derived from it, reviewing the benefits and fruits of faith through a group of hadiths that clarify the impact of faith on the believer’s behavior and spiritual state. The book is divided into chapters that deal with the definition of faith, mentioning matters of deriving faith, and the benefits of faith, with a conclusion that summarizes what has been stated.
descriptions.2503: This book is an explanation of the Book of Tawheed by Sheikh al-Islam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, written by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz al-Qaraawi. The explanation addresses the topics of monotheism and its importance in Islam, addressing issues of polytheism and its various forms, and reviewing verses and hadiths related to the monotheistic faith. The book aims to clarify the meanings of monotheism and explain the forms of polytheism, and studies the concepts of extremism regarding the righteous and the worship of graves, with a focus on protecting monotheism from heresies and superstitions.
descriptions.2504: This book, “The Brilliant Collections of the Salafi Doctrine,” by the author Abu al-Mundhir al-Minyawi, is classified under the category of doctrine. The book is a collection of teachings and words that I collected from the interpretation of “Adwaa al-Bayan” by Al-Shanqeeti, with the addition of some words from his student, Sheikh Attiya Muhammad Salem.
descriptions.2505: The Book of Paradise and Hell is a book describing Paradise and Hell in Islam and shows the condition of the people of Paradise and Hell according to the Muslims’ belief about them in the Qur’an and Sunnah. It was prepared by Sheikh Omar bin Suleiman Al-Ashqar in 1998, as part of the series The Creed in Light of the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.2506: The Lurid Jewels by Sheikh al-Islam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab is a doctrinal book that explains the concept of monotheism in Islam and presents messages that address the five basic issues, hypocrisy with its parts and attributes, the two testimonies, and the word monotheism and its details, in addition to explaining the truth of Islam from the Qur’an and Sunnah and comparing that with the statements of those who claim knowledge and knowledge. The book focuses on the unification of divinity and the lordship of God, explaining the morals and practices that entail clear and hidden polytheism. The author aims to guide the reader to sincerity in worship and to avoid heresies and forbidden pleasures.
descriptions.2507: Al-Habayik fi Akhbar al-Malaika is a book about the news of angels and their conditions, written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911). Al-Suyuti mentioned in the introduction to the book that he collected it on the news of angels, and the hadiths and narrations contained therein, then he concluded it with benefits that are scattered issues. The total number of hadiths and narrations in this book reached 813 hadiths and narrations. …
descriptions.2508: A book in the field of faith that highlights the importance of adhering to the Sunnah and warns the reader against heresies and their dangers, based on verses, hadiths, and hadiths that support this trend. The author discusses the definition of heresy in language and law, and explains the difference between misguided innovations and innovations that are not considered good, while clarifying that their danger is more severe than sins. The book also discusses that following the Sunnah is not limited to the fundamentals, but rather extends to the branches, and warns against the temptation of defamation and innovation in our time.
descriptions.2509: The book “The Limit Between Faith and Disbelief” by Sheikh Abd al-Rahman bin Abd al-Khaleq is concerned with explaining the concept of faith and the truth it entails. He reviews in depth the reasons for the collapse of faith through what he calls the nullifiers of faith. Then he defines disbelief and differentiates between the infidel and the true infidel. The author relies on a simplified scientific approach in his successive chapters, relying on legal texts and comparisons between rulings, and concludes by pointing out errors in interpreting the word of God. This work is considered one of the works of faith that aims to clarify the nuances between faith and disbelief for Muslim readers.
descriptions.2510: Gardens in the High and Difficult Philosophical Demands of Al-Batalyusi is a doctrinal work that deals with a detailed explanation of the various characteristics of souls, from plant to animal, human, wise, prophetic, and universal. This is accompanied by a presentation of a series of philosophical proofs based on the concept of the first cause and the cycles of existence. The book aims to clarify the purposes of the faith and remove doubts through rational inferences based on texts.
descriptions.2511: The book “The Wahhabi Movement: A Response to an Article by Muhammad al-Bahi” by the writer Muhammad Khalil Haras presents a study of the doctrine that deals with the origins, emergence, and principles of the Wahhabi movement, based on a comprehensive index that covers its foundations, the emphasis on monotheism, and its relationship to the Islamic heritage and the righteous predecessors. The author responds to Muhammad Al-Bahi’s criticism, stressing that the critics’ claims lack scientific evidence, and highlighting that the movement is not about demolition, but rather construction and reform aimed at reviving religion according to the approach of the predecessors. It also reviews the movement's applications in the Saudi reality and its interaction with contemporary thought, highlighting its theoretical and practical aspects. The work concludes with a call for an upright, truth-based approach.
descriptions.2512: This book deals with topics of the Islamic faith and discusses important jurisprudential and doctrinal issues. The author focuses on clarifying the understanding of the concept of polytheism and explaining its forms, and also discusses the issue of imitation in Islamic jurisprudence and its rule. The book also addresses the concept of heresy and denies what deniers of the Sunnah consider it to be. The book also includes discussions of some jurisprudential practices and an analysis of some Prophetic hadiths related to worship and supplication.
descriptions.2513: This book, “Judging a thing is a branch of its perception,” by author Muhammad Aman al-Jami, falls within the classification of belief. The book covers multiple topics, including judging a thing based on its perception, the study of names and attributes, and Khomeini’s Islam. The book is considered a discussion of the opinions and ideas of some journalists who were exposed to facts they could not imagine. The book aims to correct these errors in light of the Qur’an and Sunnah, while providing special advice to lecturers and general advice to preachers to God. The book also covers other topics, such as extremism and dispersion, the Hijra and Takfir groups, and imitation.
descriptions.2514: Incidents and Heresies by Abu Bakr al-Tartushi is a book in the field of belief that aims to clarify the concept of heresy in religion and show its harms, based on what was stated in the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the teachings of the Companions. The book deals with the definition of heresy and methods of denying it, and devotes chapters to detailing issues of prayer in Ramadan, reading the Qur’an, and mosque etiquette, in addition to discussing other matters of temptation and innovation. The author focuses on reviewing the corruption that innovation has caused in the behavior of Muslims and presents an approach to preventing it.
descriptions.2515: This is a book on the Islamic faith, which studies the mention of “Al-Hawqalah,” which is the saying “There is no power nor strength except in God.” The book explains the concept of this word and its linguistic and grammatical meaning, then reviews its virtues mentioned in the Sunnah of the Prophet, and finally explains its doctrinal connotations and the meanings it contains of monotheism and lack of God.
descriptions.2516: Neutrality and apology in responding to those who say that the Qur’an was created is a book that tells the story of the famous debate that took place between Abd al-Aziz bin Yahya bin Muslim al-Kinani al-Makki, who died in the year 240 AH, representing the Sunnis and the community, and Bishr al-Marisi, one of the leaders of the Mu’tazila who believed in the creation of the Qur’an. In this debate, Bishr presents the thought of his group, and Abd al-Aziz al-Kinani refutes his arguments, breaks down his opinions, and shows the difference in his approach and sayings, through The Qur’an and the Sunnah, and through logic, as well as through theology.
descriptions.2517: The book “Al-Durrah Al-Bahiyyah Explanation of the Ta’i Poem in Solving the Qadariyah Problem” by Abd al-Rahman al-Saadi deals with the topic of fate and predestination from an Islamic doctrinal perspective, explaining the doctrines of fatalism, refuting their arguments, and refuting their falsehoods. The book focuses on responding to heresies and misguidance related to the concept of destiny, and emphasizes the unity of God in creation and management, while proving His wisdom and comprehensive will. The book aims to clarify the correct understanding of destiny and show that everything that happens in the universe is by God’s will and will, and that He has no partner in His sovereignty.
descriptions.2518: Evidence in the Ruling on Loyalty to the People of Polytheism is a book on loyalty and disavowal in the Islamic faith, written by Sheikh Suleiman bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab (deceased: 1233 AH).
descriptions.2519: This book, “Religion and Universal Sunnahs,” by Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali, is considered a book in the field of belief, as it addresses pagan Indian Sufi thought and explains how this thought is incompatible with true religion. The book begins with an introduction explaining that true religion does not contradict universal laws, because their source is the same, which is the will and rule of God. The book is used as evidence that pagan Indian Sufi thought is wrong, and shows how some Indian philosophers claimed that leaving the world and asceticism in it was the only path to self-realization and purity, which led to negative results. The book also refers to the idea of ​​the reincarnation of souls, which considers that souls are limited and neither increase nor decrease, and it shows how some Indian philosophers claimed that the reward for each of the lives a person lives is raised or descended to different levels according to his work.
descriptions.2520: This book deals with the topic of collective dhikr in Islam, and reviews the opinions of jurists and thinkers about its ruling and legitimacy. The author, Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khamis, deals with the definition of collective dhikr and its origins, then presents the arguments and evidence adopted by the scholars and his opponents. It also mentions the fatwas of Islamic scholars and their opinions on this subject, and reviews the suspicions raised by some believers about collective dhikr and answers them. The book falls within the framework of discussing heresies and innovations in Islamic worship and their ruling.
descriptions.2521: This book, “The Response to Burdah,” by Abdullah Aba Butin, is part of the classification of doctrine. The book begins with an introduction to the author, as he is known as the Mufti of the Najdi lands, and talks about the importance of the word monotheism in Islam. The author points out that people have been divided into two groups: a group that has been guided to the correct belief in monotheism, and a group that has gone astray into polytheism and heresies. It indicates that Al-Busiri, the author of the Burdah, was a poet and not a scholar of Islamic law, and thus he went astray in the concepts. The author points out that Al-Busiri has woven misguidance and suspicions into his apostasy, and speaks about the importance of jihad with the sword of words and statement in repelling the plots of enemies.
descriptions.2522: This book, “The Response to the Jahmiyyah and the Heretics,” by its author, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, deals in its pages with the response to the falsehoods of the Jahmiyyah and the heretics in the doctrine of monotheism and predestination. In this work, the author details the positions of the heretics on several Qur’anic verses, and explains their mistakes in interpreting religious texts, citing legal evidence to refute their suspicions and correct the correct doctrine.
descriptions.2523: This book, from the Doctrine Classification, deals with the response to the writers Yousef Hashim Al-Rifai and Dr. Muhammad Saeed Ramadan Al-Bouti, who were accused of lying to the Sunnis and calling them to heresies and misguidance. The author, Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad, focuses on discussing Al-Rifai and Al-Bouti’s accusations against the Sunnis, denies the charges against them, and shows the danger of their call to the correct Islamic faith.
descriptions.2524: The Response to Those Who Advocate the Unity of Existence is a book written by Mullah Ali Al-Qari, in which the author responds to those who believe in the unity of existence, mentions their doctrine, responds to the scholars, and mentions their most prominent figures, including Ibn Arabi, Al-Hallaj, Ibn Seventy, and others.
descriptions.2525: This book, “The Response to the Suspicions of Those Who Seek Help from Other than God,” by Sheikh Ahmed bin Issa, is part of the classification of doctrine, and aims to respond to the suspicions raised by those who oppose the call of the Messengers and their followers. The book begins by mentioning the Quranic verses that indicate that glory, invincibility, statehood, and victory belong to those who achieve monotheism and are patient in the face of harm. Then he moves on to mention the call for reform and renewal in Najd carried out by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, which faced bitter enemies and witnessed steadfastness before them. The book aims to respond to the suspicions raised by opponents of this call, and is considered part of the efforts made by the author in defending the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2526: This book is by the great scholar Ibn Rushd, and it is one of the works of the Islamic faith. The book deals with the subject of the unseen and the related hadiths and Qur’anic verses, and reviews different points of view on the validity of what is narrated in this field. The author focuses on discussing the wisdom of the sayings attributed to the prophets regarding the knowledge of the unseen, and answers specific questions on this topic, citing legal and scientific evidence.
descriptions.2527: The book “The Response to Those Who Lied with the Authentic Hadiths Contained” by Sheikh Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad is a doctrinal work that focuses on refuting claims that contradict the Prophet’s hadith related to the Awaited Mahdi. It includes chapters that address four main suspicions raised against authentic hadiths, based on legal texts and logical analysis. It aims to clarify the authenticity of what was reported about the Mahdi in the Sunnah of the Prophet and refute what the author describes as distortions or misunderstandings. Through his introduction, the author shows his keenness to defend the Islamic faith from temptations and false claims.
descriptions.2528: The book of personal letters by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab includes a collection of letters addressed to individuals and groups, in which he explains his faith and defends his call from false accusations. The author divided the letters into five sections that deal with the Sheikh’s doctrine, the types of monotheism, the meaning of there is no god but God, and an explanation of the polytheism that contradicts it, as well as general guidance for Muslims in belief, enjoining good, and forbidding evil.
descriptions.2529: Al-Risala al-Mufidah by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab is a doctrinal work that focuses on the monotheism of God. He explains three parts of it: the monotheism of divinity, the monotheism of divinity, and the monotheism of names and attributes, based on Qur’anic verses. The book also discusses the different types of polytheism, and its major, minor, and hidden types, in addition to classifying disbelief and hypocrisy from a doctrinal and practical standpoint. The author aims to clarify that worship is purely for God alone, and that sincerity in worship is the basis of the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2530: The book “Messengers and Messages” by Suleiman Al-Ashqar deals with the subject of faith through a definitional study of the Prophet and Messenger and an explanation of the differences between them, based on Qur’anic and linguistic texts. It is divided into two main sections: The first focuses on the prophets and messengers, and the second deals with heavenly messages and their purposes. The author aims to clarify the doctrinal concepts related to prophecy and the message and to clarify their dimensions in Islamic understanding.
descriptions.2531: The book “The Spirit in Discourse on the Souls of the Dead and the Living” by Sheikh Ibn al-Qayyim is a doctrinal work that deals with issues of the soul in Islam. It raises a group of issues about knowing the dead to visit the living, the meeting of souls, the fate of the soul after separation, and the torment of the grave. The author relies on texts from the authentic Sunnah to clarify the doctrine of the nation’s predecessors and remove false concepts related to the soul and the afterlife. It aims to clarify the Islamic doctrine about the life of the soul between this world and the afterlife.
descriptions.2532: Al-Rawdah Al-Smiling in the Defense of the Sunnah of Abu Al-Qasim is an author in the field of doctrine that aims to defend the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and clarify its position on the disputed sects, with a focus on refuting the Zaidiyyah and demonstrating the Sunni preferences. The book includes an introduction that explains the author’s goal and approach, and includes chapters that address defining the book, proving its attribution to the author, the reasons for its writing, and reviewing manuscripts and editions with reference to scholars’ comments. It also contains an edited text explaining the status of the Sunnah and citing sayings and poetry in praise of the hadith and its people. The text shows a scientific style that combines doctrinal analysis with a historical statement of the methodology followed.
descriptions.2533: This book, “Al-Rawd Al-Basim fi Al-Dhib on the Sunnah of Abu Al-Qasim - ﷺ -” is a doctrinal book that is considered one of the most important books by the author, the diligent Imam Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Wazir. The book is considered one of the most important sources in defending the Sunnah of the Prophet and responding to the Ash’ari and Zaydi. The book contains an extensive table of contents covering various topics of the Islamic faith. The book is considered one of the most important sources for understanding the Islamic faith and responding to the Ash’ari and Zaydi.
descriptions.2534: A book on belief that aims to distinguish established Sunnahs from newly invented innovations with regard to remembrances, prayers, and purity, following what is authentic in the hadiths and what is not authentic in these acts of worship. The author criticizes what he sees as superstitions and innovative practices, especially among women in some acts of worship, calling for returning to the Qur’an and Sunnah and judging them without the opinions of men.
descriptions.2535: A book that sheds light on the biography of Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Saadi and reviews his efforts in clarifying the components of the Islamic faith, detailing the unification of divinity, the names and attributes, and the unification of divinity, in addition to explaining belief in prophecies and the Last Day and their purposes. The author, Abdul Razzaq bin Abdul Mohsen Al Badr, presents a systematic analysis of doctrinal topics through chapters dealing with the sheikh’s scholarly and personal life, and then moves on to discuss the definition of faith and the issues related to it. The work is considered a reference concerned with clarifying the foundations of faith and clarifying issues related to monotheism and the afterlife within a documented scientific framework.
descriptions.2536: This book, “Divine Attributes, Their Definition, and Their Sections,” by the author Muhammad bin Khalifa Al-Tamimi, is classified under the category of belief. The book provides an introduction that emphasizes the importance of knowledge of God, His names, and His attributes. The first chapter deals with the definition of the attributes and the relationship between them and the chapter on names and the chapter on information, while the second chapter is devoted to the sections on the attributes, as the author divides them into sections according to the Sunnis and the community and sections according to the opponents. The book shows interest in achieving a correct understanding of the divine attributes and defining their divisions, making it a useful resource for specialists in Islamic doctrine and jurisprudence.
descriptions.2537: This book, “Divine Attributes in the Qur’an and the Prophetic Sunnah,” by Muhammad Aman al-Jami, is considered one of the most important books in the field of Islamic belief, as it deals with the subject of the divine attributes in the Qur’an and the Prophetic Sunnah. The book aims to present the thought of the righteous predecessors in this field, and to analyze the Qur’anic and Sunnah texts related to the divine attributes, while addressing the relationship between the attributes and the divine essence, and the nature of the relationship of the attributes to each other. The book is an important source for learning about Islamic thought in the field of faith, and helps readers understand the correct meanings of the divine attributes in the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.2538: Al-Sawarim Al-Haddad, the Breaker of the Relations of the Lords of the Union, written by Muhammad Al-Shawkani.
descriptions.2539: The book The Burning Thunderbolts Against the People of Rejection, Misguidance, and Heretics is a book criticizing the Twelver Shiite belief, written by the Shafi’i Sunni jurist and theologian Ibn Hajar al-Haytami.
descriptions.2540: The book “Al-Sawai’iq Al-Mursalah Al-Shihabiyya Ala Al-Shubah Al-Dahhih Al-Shamiya” is a book in the field of doctrine, written by Suleiman bin Sahman. The book contains a group of chapters that respond to suspicions and fabrications about the Salafi doctrine, and answers various questions and criticisms. The book seems to be interested in discussing issues such as seeking help from the prophets and the righteous, and the lives of the prophets in their graves, and it also deals with other topics related to monotheism and responding to slander. It appears that the author relies on Prophetic hadiths and Quranic verses to support his arguments and echo his ideas. In general, it can be said that the book aims to defend the Salafi doctrine and respond to the suspicions raised around it.
descriptions.2541: A book on belief, a response to the suspicions of one of the critics of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s reformist call. It includes chapters explaining the truth of this call and repelling accusations about it, such as accusing it of departing from or diminishing the prophets, with a discussion of doctrinal issues such as proving attributes and responding to the interpretation of opponents. It includes historical investigations about the state of Najd before the call and the position of the Ottoman and Egyptian countries towards it.
descriptions.2542: The book "The Throne", written by Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi, is a book on faith that focuses on studying the names and attributes of God, introducing the Sunni doctrine, studying ambiguous and doubtful sayings about God's names and attributes, studying the attributes of height and leveling, and studying the throne and everything related to it. The book begins with a definition of the Throne, then moves on to studying the Qur’anic evidence proving the Throne, and ends with a study of issues related to height and leveling. The book is considered one of the important sources in the study of the Islamic faith, and is considered a source of Islamic thought in the field of faith.
descriptions.2543: This book, “The Precious Contract in Explanation of the Hadiths of the Fundamentals of Religion,” by Sheikh Hussein bin Ghannam, is one of the heritage works in the field of the Islamic faith. The book explains hadiths related to the origins of religion, focusing on proving that Islam is the only religion of God. The author aims to spread correct knowledge and enhance adherence to Prophetic guidance, while warning against heresies and innovations in religion.
descriptions.2544: This is an introductory summary of the book “Reason and Transmission according to Ibn Rushd” by the author Muhammad Aman Al-Jami: This book is considered one of the most important sources that dealt with Ibn Rushd’s philosophy and his ideas about reason and transmission. The author begins by defining Ibn Rushd and explaining his life, then moves on to address his position on reason and transmission, where he explains the definition of reason and transmission, and presents Ibn Rushd’s philosophy on these issues. The author sheds light on the existence of God and oneness according to Ibn Rushd, and how they are united with science, and also addresses destiny and destiny and their causes. The author concludes the book by defining the conclusion that brings together the main ideas discussed in the book. This book is an important source for learning about Ibn Rushd's ideas about reason and transmission, and is a good starting point for philosophical and religious study.
descriptions.2545: The Safarini Creed, called Al-Durra Al-Madi fi Aqdat Ahl Al-Murdiyya, is a system of Islamic doctrine written by Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Safarini (1114 - 1188 AH / 1702 - 1774 AD).
descriptions.2546: This book by the scholar Ibn Baz deals with the topic of the correct Islamic faith and discusses the ideas and sayings that contradict it. It focuses on the importance of believing in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and destiny, indicating that this correct doctrine is the foundation and origin of the Islamic religion. The book also mentions the types of deviants from this doctrine and their suspicions, and points out the nullifiers of Islam that invalidate faith.
descriptions.2547: This book deals with the topic of the correct belief in Islam and what contradicts it, stressing the importance of the correct belief as a basis for the Islamic religion and the acceptance of deeds. The author focuses on the origins of the correct doctrine of belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and destiny, relying on evidence from the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.2548: This is the book “The Doctrine Narrated by Abu Bakr al-Khallal” by Sheikh Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It is a book on the Islamic faith that focuses on the monotheism of God, his attributes, and his characteristics. The book begins by explaining Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal’s belief in God and describing him as having power, vitality, and knowledge. Then he moves on to explaining God’s attributes, such as the All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and points out that God is one, indivisible and indivisible. He talks about the existence of God and describing him as having power, vitality, and knowledge. The book contains multiple chapters that address various aspects of the Islamic faith, including the monotheism of God, his attributes, and characteristics, an explanation of faith, obedience, and disobedience, as well as an explanation of the virtues of Islam and the balance.
descriptions.2549: The book “The Belief in God,” written by Suleiman Al-Ashqar and Omar, deals with the topic of belief in God and His monotheism, showing its importance as a main principle in the Islamic faith. The book focuses on the evidence of the existence of the Creator and repelling doubts about this subject. It deals with introducing God through studying His signs and creation, and calls for the monotheism of God and the rejection of polytheism. It also studies the history of the divine belief and its development over time.
descriptions.2550: The Sublime is for the Most High, the Great, and the clarification of Sahih Al-Akhbar from Suqiha, or Al-Al-Al-Al-‘Al-Ulwah is for the Most High, the Forgiving, is a book by Shams Al-Din Al-Dhahabi (d. 748 AH), compiled by Al-Dhahabi in the year 691 AH, and summarized by Al-Albani in his summary of the attribute of Sublimeness. It talks about proving the attribute of the sublimeness of God, which was given by some sects such as: the Jahmiyyah, the Mu’tazilites, the Maturidites, and the Ash’aris, and the refutation of them. He also presented a number of pieces of evidence, including the verses of istiwaa and sublimeness, and the hadiths contained in Al-Alwa, and a number of traces of the ancestors on Al-Alwal, arranged according to the layers.
descriptions.2551: Al-Awasim Min Al-Qawasim fi Anhqah The Positions of the Companions After the Death of the Prophet is a book written by the Hafiz and Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi. The writer discusses the issue of infallibility, according to Ibn al-Arabi, and from the point of view of the Sunnis and the community, infallibility is only for the prophets, but that does not mean that he should criticize the companions of the Prophet, because attacking the companions of the Prophet is attacking the Prophet himself. Because of the ongoing dispute between Sunnis and Shiites, the author defends the Companions and mentions their virtues and dignity. He called the lawsuit “conclusive” and the response to it “capital,” until he reached his responses to the Abbasid era.
descriptions.2552: The book Al-Awaasim wa Al-Qawasim fi Al-Dhab on the Sunnah of Abu Al-Qasim is one of the comprehensive books of a number of arts. It was written by Muhammad bin Al-Wazir Al-Yamani (died: 840 AH) after one of his sheikhs wrote a treatise in response to it. Ibn Al-Wazir discussed it in this book, and he focused in it on the issue of ijtihad and imitation, then discussed several doctrinal and jurisprudential issues, such as: seeing God in the afterlife, the great imamate, and creating the actions of the servants. The advantage of the book lies in its author’s expansion in discussing the issues raised and explaining their evidence in detail, and in relying in his book on original sources in the Islamic religion. …
descriptions.2553: The book “Al-Ayn and Al-Athar fi the Beliefs of the People of Athar” by Sheikh Ibn Faqi Suffah deals with the sciences of the Islamic faith, as it details the knowledge of God, His attributes, and His words, then moves to His actions and to the rulings of Sharia law and prophecy, according to what the table of contents shows.
