This book is considered one of the most important books in the field of Islamic belief, as it aims to unify worship and single out God for all types of worship, and seeks to block all pretexts that could lead to major or minor polytheism. The book deals with various chapters that concern the Islamic faith, from the unification of knowledge and proof to the unification of names and attributes, and it also deals with topics such as prophecy, the message, the imamate, and rebellion against the ruler. The book relies on the Qur’an and the authentic Sunnah to clarify and expand understanding of the Islamic faith, and aims to provide a barrier to the pretexts that can lead to polytheism or a breach of monotheism.
descriptions.2676: This is the book “Explanation of the Palmyra Message” by the author Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khamis, and it falls within the classification of doctrine. The book contains an introduction and three sections, and the chapters and sections include an analysis of the main topics in the Islamic faith, such as monotheism, attributes, law, and destiny. The book begins with an introduction to the author and an explanation of the book, then moves on to an explanation of the Tadmurian treatise by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, which is considered one of the most important treatises in the Islamic faith. This book is an important source for learning about the Islamic faith and responding to heresies and misguidance.
descriptions.2677: This is a book on the Islamic faith by Imam Al-Muzani, in which he explains the principles of the Sunnah that the predecessors of the nation followed. The book deals with major topics such as faith, the Qur’an, attributes, predestination, angels, heaven and hell, vision, obedience to imams and companions, and other issues of belief. The book was written in response to an inquiry received from the author asking him to explain the Sunnah on these issues. Its explanation comprehensively included the principles of the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community.
descriptions.2678: “Explanation of the Sunnah” may mean: Explanation of the Sunnah by Al-Barbahari: a book written by Al-Barbahari. Explanation of the Sunnah by Al-Baghawi: A book written by Al-Baghawi. Explanation of the Sunnah by Al-Muzani: A book written by Ismail bin Yahya Al-Muzani.
descriptions.2679: This book, “Explanation of the Issues with the Prohibition of Raising Graves” by Al-Shawkani, deals with the issue of the prohibition of raising graves and addresses the disagreements among Muslims on this matter. The author calls for referring to the Qur’an and Sunnah in determining the ruling on removing graves, and defends the necessity of adhering to the legal controls in dealing with the graves of the dead. The book is a doctrinal book that focuses on legal rules and their applications in controversial issues.
descriptions.2680: This book, “Explanation of the Breasts Bi Explanation of the Condition of the Dead and the Graves” by the author Al-Suyuti, is classified under the category of doctrine. This book is considered one of the most important sources in understanding the topics of death, the isthmus, and graves, as Al-Suyuti explains these topics through quotations from marfoo’ hadiths and suspended and mutuqat reports. The book begins by defining death, its virtues, and how, then it moves on to describing the Angel of Death and his helpers, and then explains the state of the soul after leaving the body, its ascension to God Almighty, and its meeting with the spirits and its abode after that. Al-Suyuti also explains the state of the grave, its affliction, its temptation, its torment, its vastness, and its narrowness, and the book ends with an index of the topics that will be covered in the book.
descriptions.2681: This book is an explanation of the Safarini doctrine by its author, Safarini, and it was explained by the scholar Ibn Uthaymeen. The book deals with the topics of the Islamic faith through its explanation of the system that deals with the origins of the religion and its pillars, and details the belief of the Sunnis and the community in monotheism, prophethood, imamate, and the signs of the Hour. The book is divided into several sections that address different aspects of the Islamic faith, and it is one of the works concerned with explaining and clarifying Islamic doctrines.
descriptions.2682: The book provides a detailed explanation of the Wasitiyya doctrine by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, which is a famous doctrine in explaining the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community. The explanation is based on what is stated in the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the predecessors, and aims to clarify the meanings of the doctrine with its evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus. The book deals with most issues of belief and the foundations of faith, while highlighting the practical moral aspect of the Salaf’s doctrine, and it is considered one of the important books in the field of Islamic faith.
descriptions.2683: This is an explanation of the Wasitiyya doctrine by the scholar Muhammad Khalil Haras. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the field of Islamic belief, as the author explains the Wasitiyya doctrine, which is considered one of the most important Salafist doctrines, and provides a detailed explanation of it. The book contains a special appendix that includes issues of faith that were not mentioned by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in the Wasitiyya doctrine. This appendix provides an important addition to researchers and teachers in this field. This book is an important source for study and teaching in the field of the Islamic faith, and contributes to providing information and a correct understanding of the Wasitiyya doctrine.
descriptions.2684: This book is an explanation of the four rules written by Sheikh al-Islam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, presented by the scholar Saleh al-Fawzan to fill the need for an explanation of these important rules in the Islamic faith. The book deals with the definition of monotheism and polytheism and details their meanings according to the Qur’an and Sunnah, while explaining the importance of understanding these rules in building the correct belief that establishes the rest of the religious acts of worship and rituals.
descriptions.2685: This is the book “Explanation of the Three Principles” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab. It is a book on faith that explains the three principles that a person must know, which are the servant’s knowledge of his Lord, his religion, and the Messenger of God. The book explains these principles in detail and interpretation, and also addresses other topics such as monotheism, polytheism, the Islamic religion, the ranks of religion, and the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. The book is considered one of the most important works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and it is one of the books that is considered the basis of the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2686: This book is an explanation of the doctrine of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab by the scholar Saleh Al-Fawzan. The book deals with the origins of the Islamic faith and discusses the concepts of belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and destiny, with a focus on the moderation of the Sunnis in matters of faith and the rejection of extremism and extremism. The book also shows the difference between the doctrine of the Saved Sect and the sayings of the Mu’tazila, Jahmiyyah, and Kharijites, and stresses the importance of adhering to the Qur’an and Sunnah in building the correct doctrine.
descriptions.2687: This is the book “Explanation of Revealing Suspicions, followed by Explanation of the Six Principles” by Ibn Uthaymeen, and it falls within the classification of doctrine. The book contains the author's translation, an explanation to uncover suspicions, and an explanation of the six principles. The book begins with a translation by the author, Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, who was born into a house of knowledge, honor, and religion, and was raised to memorize the Qur’an and study jurisprudence. The author's translation is distinguished by details about his scientific life, and his travels in pursuit of knowledge in the suburbs of Najd, Mecca, and the Prophet's city, and scholars know him for his intense goal of research and writing. This is followed by a translation by the commentator, Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen, who is considered one of the prominent scholars of his time. The book shows interest in the Islamic faith, and focuses on an explanation of Revealing Doubts, which is considered one of the most important works of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab. The book also contains an explanation of the six principles, which are among the most important principles of the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2688: This book is an explanation of a group of pre-Islamic issues mentioned by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, which were explained and detailed by the scholar Saleh Al-Fawzan. The book deals with a number of wrong practices and beliefs that were prevalent in pre-Islamic times, some of whose effects are still present in Islamic societies. The explanation focuses on the importance of understanding these issues to avoid falling into them, and includes an analysis of several points, including the supplications of saints, blind imitation, and exaggeration among scholars. The book is classified as doctrine and falls under the category of Islamic jurisprudence. It is directed to alert Muslims to the danger of these practices and to urge them to follow what the Messenger came ﷺ.
descriptions.2689: This book, “Conditions of There Is No God but God,” by Awad Al-Mu’tak, is considered one of the important books in the field of the Islamic faith. In this book, the author provides a detailed explanation of the conditions that must be met by a person to be an honest Muslim. These conditions include knowledge, certainty, sincerity, honesty, love, submission, and acceptance. The author begins by defining the meaning of “there is no god but God” and achieving it, then moves on to explain its conditions, addresses the importance of martyrdom in Islam, and explains that martyrdom is the key to Islam, and by achieving it one will be saved from Hell. This book is an important source for learning about the Islamic faith and explaining the conditions of faith.
descriptions.2690: This book, written by Sheikh Suleiman Al-Kharashi, addresses the response to those who accused Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah of fraud, and aims to show the truth of Ibn Taymiyyah’s position on Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and his companions. Al-Kharashi explains, through passages from Ibn Taymiyyah’s words, that the latter was not a Nasibi as some slanderers claimed, but rather he was defending the Companions and defending their truth, and confirming that his love for Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was not at the expense of his hatred for the rest of the Companions. The book also deals with Ibn Taymiyyah’s approach in responding to the Shiites and responding to their slander, and reviews his statements regarding the virtue of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him).
descriptions.2691: The book “Pouring Punishment on Whoever Cursed the Companions” by the author Mahmoud Shukri Al-Alusi is a book on faith that deals with the subject of the Shiites’ rejection of the Companions of the Messenger -(peace be upon him)-. The author attempts to criticize the opinions of the Shiites and determine his position on them. The book begins by introducing the author and explaining the importance of the book, then it deals with the position of the Shiites on the Companions of the Messenger -(peace be upon him)-, and talks about the Arjuza organized by the Shiites in response to the book. The author deals with their position on the Ahl al-Bayt -(peace be upon them)-, and talks about their beliefs in the Companions, and deals with the hadith about “the separation of the nation” and explaining its meaning, and talks about the beliefs of the Shiites in the saved sect, and deals with their position on the Ahl al-Bayt -(peace be upon them)-. The book is one of the books that reflects the author's position on the Shiites and their views on doctrine.
descriptions.2692: This book deals with the signs and signs of the Hour by collecting authentic hadiths on this topic. The author, Issam Musa Hadi, focuses on recording authentic hadiths related to the minor, middle, and major signs of the Hour, while being careful to distinguish between authentic and false hadiths in circulated hadiths. The book aims to provide accurate information about the signs of the Hour in a simplified manner that makes it easy for the general reader to understand, with a focus on the hadiths authenticated by the hadith scholar Nasser al-Din al-Albani.
descriptions.2693: This book, “The Attributes of God Almighty Contained in the Qur’an and Sunnah,” by Alawi Al-Saqqaf, falls within the classification of faith. The book contains a table of contents that includes topics related to the attributes of God, such as the meaning of the name and attribute, general rules regarding attributes, types of attributes, and the fruits of belief in the attributes of God. The book begins with the introduction to the second edition, which explains some of the modifications made to the first edition, including the addition of some new features. It appears from the excerpt at the beginning of the book that the book aims to clarify the attributes of God and define their limits, while directing attention to the importance of monotheism and purity in understanding these attributes.
descriptions.2694: The book “Preserving Man from the Whispers of Sheikh Dahlan,” written by Muhammad Bashir Al-Sahswani, is a book on faith that aims to introduce the reader to the Sunnah and the community and heresies, and to explain the importance of preserving the Sunnah and the community in the Islamic religion. The book begins by defining the Sunnah and the group and heresies, then moves on to explaining the importance of preserving the Sunnah and the group, explaining what innovations are occurring in the nation, and explaining the importance of adhering to the Sunnah and the group at all times and places. The book is considered one of the important sources in understanding the Islamic faith and introducing the Sunnah and the community.
descriptions.2695: This book deals with the phenomenon of postponement in Islamic thought and discusses the relationship between faith and work, reviewing the origins of this phenomenon and the doctrines of postponement and its effects. The author focuses on the truth of faith and its connection to work, and discusses the Islamic sects that spread throughout history that followed the beliefs of the Murji’ah, reviewing the opinions of the predecessors on this subject. The book also deals with the emergence of postponement and its development throughout the ages, and discusses the relationship between the faith of the heart and the faith of the limbs.
descriptions.2696: The book “The World of Jinns and Demons” by Suleiman Al-Ashqar, Omar, deals with the topic of jinn and demons from an Islamic doctrinal perspective. The book focuses on defining the jinn and explaining their characteristics, showing that they are an independent world other than the world of humans and angels, with a common destiny between them in reason and moral choice. The book also deals with the wisdom of the creation of the jinn, their hostility towards humans, and the believer’s weapons in confronting them, reviewing the opinions of scholars regarding their origin, creation, and attributes.
descriptions.2697: This book deals with the topic of angels in Islam by reviewing their characteristics and abilities, their role in the worship of God, and their relationship with humans and other creatures. The author focuses on clarifying belief in angels as one of the foundations of the Islamic faith, citing texts from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book also addresses the differences between angels and human beings, relying on what is stated in the legal texts about angels and their various functions.
descriptions.2698: This is a critical and guiding study of the book “A Study on the Differences in the History of the Kharijite and Shiite Muslims,” written by Dr. Ahmed Muhammad Ahmad Jalli, by Dr. Ali bin Muhammad Nasser Al-Faqihi. The author provides a presentation and criticism of the book, focusing on the fourth chapter, which deals with the Twelver Imami Shiites and their most important teachings. The author admires the first edition of the book, but notes some errors in the second edition. The author aims to give the author his due and point out the errors that occurred in the book, focusing on the topics of the book as a whole.
descriptions.2699: This book, “Aqd al-Durar fi Akhbar al-Muntazer,” by Sheikh Yusuf bin Yahya al-Sulami, deals with the topic of the Awaited Mahdi from a doctrinal perspective and modern jurisprudence. The author focuses on the Mahdi’s descendants and characteristics, discusses the Prophetic hadiths related to him, and reviews the temptations that will occur before his appearance and how to prepare for his appearance. He also talks about the blessings that will happen to him during his caliphate, and ends by mentioning the temptations that will occur after the end of his term. The book aims to clarify the characteristics of the Mahdi, his appearance, and how to prepare for his appearance according to the hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.2700: This book, “The Doctrine of the Sunnis and the Impact on the Awaited Mahdi,” by author Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad, falls within the classification of doctrine. The book deals with the topic of the Awaited Mahdi, as it contains chapters related to this topic, including mentioning the scholars who wrote about the Mahdi, the frequency of hadiths about the Mahdi, mentioning some authentic hadiths related to him, as well as answering some of the conflicts that may appear in relation to this topic. The book begins by mentioning the significance of the many hadiths that the nation received with acceptance about the emergence of the Mahdi, whose name corresponds to the name of the Messenger ﷺ, and after whom Jesus bin Maryam, peace and blessings be upon him, will pray. The book aims to clarify the indigenous doctrine on this subject, and is based on authentic and frequent hadiths.
descriptions.2701: The Doctrine of the Sunnis and the Community is a book by Sheikh Ali Jumah in which he addresses a number of issues of the science of belief from the perspective of the Sunnis and the Community. The book was written in an easy and simplified way for the average, non-specialized reader.
descriptions.2702: This book, written by Ibn Uthaymeen, deals with the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community in the fundamentals of faith, explaining its basic components, which are belief in God, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day, and destiny. The author focuses on explaining these main beliefs and explaining what a Muslim should believe in them, while pointing out the fruits of adhering to this correct belief. The book aims to clarify the Salafist doctrine and explain what a Muslim must believe regarding the truths of religion, with an emphasis on the importance of following the example of the righteous predecessors in this field.
descriptions.2703: This is an introductory summary of the book “The Doctrine of Monotheism in the Holy Qur’an” by author Muhammad Khalil Malkawi: This book is considered one of the most important books in the field of Islamic belief, as it focuses on the doctrine of monotheism with which God sent His messengers and revealed it in His books. The author begins by defining the doctrine linguistically and legally, then moves on to define the source of the Islamic faith, which is based on the Qur’an and Sunnah. It also highlights the features of the Islamic faith, such as its compatibility with nature, clarity, and suitability for people. The author shows that the doctrine of monotheism is the doctrine that is characterized by clarity and ease, that it is an innate, fixed and specific doctrine, and that it is the origin of messages. It also highlights the impact of faith on the behavior of the individual and society, and presents examples of the effects of faith. The author also shows that the doctrine of monotheism is a doctrine that is characterized by stability and clarity, and that it does not need complexity or sterile controversy.
descriptions.2704: This book on the science of Islamic belief deals with the subject of monotheism and an explanation of the polytheism and heresies that oppose it. It aims to clarify the concept of belief and its importance as a basis for religion, while explaining its correct sources and ways to protect it from deviation. The author focuses on the unification of divinity, divinity, names, and attributes, and reviews the types of polytheism and doctrinal deviations, based on classic sources from the books of the imams of Salafism. The book is written in easy and simple language, and aims to educate Muslims about the necessity of taking care of their correct faith in a time of spread of deviant trends.
descriptions.2705: This is an introductory summary of the book: “The Doctrine of Al-Hafiz Taqi Al-Din Abdul Ghani bin Abdul Wahid Al-Maqdisi” is a doctrinal book that is considered one of the most important sources in understanding the Islamic faith. The book deals with issues of the Islamic faith through the approach of the righteous predecessors. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as the attributes of God, descent, vision, the word of God, destiny, and other topics. The book is an important source for learning about the Islamic faith, and contributes to disseminating and promoting the approach of the Salaf al-Salih.
descriptions.2706: This book deals with the Salafi doctrine of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and its impact on the Islamic world. The author focuses on Dr. Saleh bin Abdullah Al-Abboud discusses the Sheikh’s approach to his belief and his call, and points out the characteristics of his belief in monotheism. He also studies the impact of this belief on various eras and events in the Islamic world, from the Sheikh’s era until the present. The book aims to gain a deeper understanding of the doctrine of the righteous predecessors and how it spread throughout history.
descriptions.2707: The book “Ghayat Al-Amani fi Al-Rad Al-Nabhani” is a work on doctrine, which falls within the framework of debate and response to opponents, in which its author responds to the opinions and objections of Yusuf Al-Nabhani. The book deals with doctrinal issues such as ijtihad, seeing the Prophet ﷺ after death, seeking help, and defining heresy, and defends Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, citing the scholars’ sayings and their praise of them.
descriptions.2708: Ghayat al-Maram fi Ilm al-Kalam is a book on theology and the principles of religion, written by Imam Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Salem al-Taghlibi, known as Saif al-Din al-Amidi.
descriptions.2709: The book “Important Fatwas for the Whole Ummah” by Ibn Baz is a work in the field of doctrine that deals with the subject of monotheism and its types, detailing the characteristics of the surviving sect and the reasons for the strength of the Muslims. The book also addresses the types of polytheism, the definition of heresy, and the ruling on new religious celebrations, in addition to issues related to major and minor polytheism, such as swearing by other than God, supplicating to shrines, supplicating to the people of graves, slaughtering for other than God, and seeking help from other than God. The book also deals with rulings related to images, magic, the evil eye, ruqyah, allegiance to infidels, residing in their countries, the ruling of one who rules by other than what God has revealed, and mocking those who are committed.
descriptions.2710: This book deals with the topic of faith, as it examines the science of monotheism with its definition, sections, and different types. It also addresses issues related to proving the existence and oneness of God, the difference between a prophet and a messenger, the possibility of revelation and the world’s need for it. The book reviews the approach of the Messengers in calling to God and proving His monotheism, while responding to doubts related to the origin of the world.
descriptions.2711: This book, “Fath Allah, the Praiseworthy and Glorious in Explanation of the Book of Tawheed,” by the author Hamid bin Mohsen, is considered one of the most important and famous explanations of the book called “The Book of Tawheed,” written by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab Al-Tamimi. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics related to monotheism, such as polytheism, blessing, slaughter, vows, seeking refuge, intercession, exaggeration of the righteous, magic, soothsaying, divination, and divination. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the field of the Islamic faith, and it forms part of the important Islamic heritage.
descriptions.2712: Fath al-Majid Sharh Kitab al-Tawhid is one of the books of faith, written by Abdul Rahman bin Hassan bin Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab bin Suleiman al-Tamimi (d. 1285 AH). The author explains the Book of Tawheed by Muhammad ibn Abdul Wahhab, in which he explained monotheism and its virtue, and the major polytheism that contradicts it, or its obligatory perfection, the minor polytheism and heresies. A number of investigators investigated the book: Abdul Qadir Al Arnaout, Al Walid bin Abdul Rahman Al Faryan, and Ashraf bin Abdul Maqsoud. In the edition of the Cordoba Foundation, Abdul Aziz bin Baz added comments and warnings to the body of the book.
descriptions.2713: This book, “Fath Rab al-Bariyah Bi Tkhalis al-Hamwiyya,” by the scholar Ibn Uthaymeen, deals with the subject of the Islamic faith and the mechanisms for understanding the verses about the attributes and their hadiths in the Qur’an and Sunnah. The author focuses on clarifying the doctrine of the Sunnis in this field, and discusses the innovations and deviations that occurred in the understanding of these texts by some of the later generations, trying to clarify the doctrinal truths in accordance with the understanding of the righteous predecessors. The book aims to clarify precise concepts in the Islamic faith and protect them from distortion and wrong interpretation.
descriptions.2714: This book, which is classified into doctrine, deals with the issue of belief through a fatwa and its answer. The book includes chapters that address differences in interpretation, discord in hearts, and condemnation of evil desires and seductive opinions, in addition to a chapter on equality.
descriptions.2715: This book deals with the issue of atonement of the Jahmiyas, and reviews the opinions of Sunni imams on that. It also addresses the issue of prayer, and discusses the opinions of some Islamic sects, such as the Ibadi. The book falls within the science of belief, and in it the author presents a presentation of controversial issues related to declaring some sects as infidels.
descriptions.2716: This book deals with contemporary sects that are affiliated with Islam, and explains Islam's position on them. The book begins with introductions about the study of sects and their importance, then addresses the prohibition of disunity, restricting the sects mentioned in the Prophet’s hadith, and how disagreement arises among Muslims. The second chapter also deals with the Ahl al-Sunnah wal Jama`ah sect, their belief, and their efforts in serving Islam, with important warnings on matters of belief.
descriptions.2717: This is a book about the Islamic faith, and it is an explanation of the treatise “Issues of Pre-Islamic Time” which examines the characteristics and conditions of pre-Islamic times that Islam contradicted. The book includes a study of the concept of pre-Islamic language and terminology, its types, and the ruling on disobeying its people, with an investigation of the original text and an explanation of its issues.
descriptions.2718: The book “Fasl Al-Khattab fi Explaining Pre-Islamic Issues” by Al-Alusi Mahmoud Shukri presents an intellectual and social criticism of phenomena that represent a return to pre-Islamic customs among some Muslim circles. The author discusses issues that the Messenger of God ﷺ considered to be contrary to Islamic guidance, reviewing forms of blind imitation and exaggeration in estimating some personalities, diverting texts from their true meanings, and accusing those who call for the truth with false accusations. The book aims to warn against the return of these harmful customs that contradict the spirit and complexity of Islam.
descriptions.2719: This is a book on the Islamic faith, explaining the issues of pre-Islamic times in which the Prophet ﷺ disagreed with the people of pre-Islamic times, and shows their deviations in monotheism, worship, and following. The author presents a number of issues, such as worship by involving the righteous, imitation, fanaticism, distortion of books, and atheism in names and attributes, explaining them in the light of the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.2720: The Scandals of the Batiniya and the Virtues of the Mustazhiriyya is a book written by Imam al-Ghazali al-Tusi (d. 505 AH), in response to the Batiniya.
descriptions.2721: This book, which falls under the category of doctrine, deals with the dangers of Sufi thought and reviews aspects of its beliefs and the methods of argumentation of its followers. The author shows that Sufi thought represents a danger to the Islamic nation, and points out that among its dangers are distracting people from the Qur’an and the Hadith, opening the door to esoteric interpretation, destroying the Islamic faith, and calling for immorality and immorality. The book also addresses how to argue with a Sufi and explains the difference between Islam and Sufism.
descriptions.2722: This book deals with the topic of the virtue of the Ahl al-Bayt and their high status among the Sunnis and the community, and reviews the difference between the Sunni belief in the Ahl al-Bayt and the belief of others. The author focuses on clarifying the status of the Prophet’s family ﷺ by reviewing their virtues mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah, and the scholars’ praise of them, while emphasizing the prohibition of unjustified affiliation with the Ahl al-Bayt. The book is divided into ten chapters covering various aspects of this topic.
descriptions.2723: This book, “The Virtue of Islam,” written by the revered Imam Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, is considered one of his works. It is classified under the category of faith, and covers topics related to the virtue of Islam, the obligation of Islam, interpretation of Islam, deviating from the claim of Islam, heresy, and warning against heresy. The book begins by defining the virtue of Islam, and includes sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Qur’anic verses, and comments on the importance of Hanifism, the path, and the Sunnah in worship. This book is considered one of the most important works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and it reflects his interest in introducing people to the virtues of Islam, and explaining the importance of preserving the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.2724: This book is a collection of benefits extracted from the explanation of the Book of Tawheed, written by Abdul Aziz Al-Sadhan. The book deals with the subject of faith, and reviews sections related to the virtue of monotheism, fear of polytheism, calling for it, and its interpretation, in addition to issues related to ruqyah and amulets, seeking blessings from other than God, slaughtering, vows, seeking refuge and seeking help from other than God. It also addresses intercession, exaggeration of the righteous, idolatry, magic, divination, divination, divination, astrology, rain showers, and other issues related to polytheism.
descriptions.2725: This book deals with the issue of the ancient world and the sequence of events, and reviews the opinions of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in contrast to the opinions of philosophers. The book includes discussions on the basic terms related to the subject, the sayings of theologians and hadith scholars, in addition to a review of the opinions of those who disagree with Ibn Taymiyyah. The book falls within the category of doctrine.
descriptions.2726: The book “Harvesting the Fruit in Explaining the Doctrine of Ahl al-Athar” by Allama Siddiq Hassan Khan deals with the subject of the Islamic faith from the perspective of the Sunnis and the community. The book focuses on clarifying Sunni beliefs on major doctrinal issues, relying on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book addresses topics such as the attributes of God Almighty, faith and work, predestination, the intercession of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and other aspects of the Sunni faith. The book aims to enlighten Muslims about the principles of the true religion and warn them against heresies and deviations.
descriptions.2727: The book Qatf al-Jinna al-Dani is one of the books specialized in explaining the introduction to the treatise of Ibn Abi Zaid al-Qayrawani. It was written by Sheikh Abd al-Muhsin al-Abbad al-Badr, in which the sheikh explains the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community. Its author, Sheikh Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad, said: “Sunni scholars, ancient and modern, have written works that clarify the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community, some of which are brief, and some of which are lengthy. Among these abbreviations was Imam Ibn Abi Zaid al-Qayrawani al-Maliki’s introduction to his message, and the introduction to his message in the manner of the predecessors is brief and useful, and a combination of the principles. The branches are in one book, which is rare in the work of the authors, and it is good. It makes those who work in the jurisprudence of worship and transactions aware of...
descriptions.2728: This book, which is classified on doctrine, addresses the response to those who challenge the belief of the imams of Islam, especially the Hanbalis. The author reviews introductions related to the rulings on atonement and innovation, the importance of legal evidence, and the invalidity of some claims and affiliations. He also criticizes certain opinions about contemporary Hanbalis, and refutes what he sees as deviant ideas or atheistic opinions.
descriptions.2729: Al-Risala Al-Qudsi fi Rules of Beliefs is a book written by Imam Al-Ghazali Al-Tusi (d. 505 AH). This book is part of the book “Al-Ihya”, but it was separated separately a long time ago, perhaps dating back to the time of Al-Ghazali himself and with a reference from him, as evidenced by the fact that Al-Ghazali refers to it individually.
descriptions.2730: This book, “The Sayings of the Pagan Greek Philosophers Concerning the Unification of Godhead,” by the author Saud bin Abdulaziz Al-Khalaf, is classified under the category of belief. The book provides a brief definition of the Salaf’s doctrine of monotheism, then moves to an introduction that introduces the content of the book. The book analyzes the sayings of the pagan Greek philosophers regarding monotheism, and is divided into different sections, including the sayings of atheist philosophers and writings. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book is concerned with analyzing the statements of the pagan Greek philosophers about God, and explains that these statements are considered among the most corrupt articles and the most far from sound reason.
descriptions.2731: The book “The Fundamentals of Faith in the Light of the Qur’an and Sunnah” is a work in the field of faith, dealing with the foundations of faith based on the Holy Qur’an and the Noble Prophet’s Sunnah. The book includes discussions on the monotheism of divinity, divinity, names, and attributes, with an explanation of their evidence and importance, in addition to addressing topics such as polytheism, disbelief, and fanaticism.
descriptions.2732: The book “Usul al-Din” by Jamal al-Din al-Ghazni deals with the topics of the Islamic faith in detail, focusing on the fundamentals of religion and the attributes of God Almighty and how to know the Creator. The book also deals with topics related to the prophets, angels, the dignity of saints, and the actions of servants, relying on doctrinal roots and contemplation of God’s signs in the universe.
descriptions.2733: The Book of Idols The origin of the book is a manuscript that contained a hadith by the author Abu Al-Mundhir Hisham bin Muhammad Abi Al-Nadr Ibn Al-Sa’ib Ibn Bishr Al-Kalbi, who died in the year 204 AH, in which he narrated a hadith he heard from his father and others about the story of idols since the time of Ismail bin Ibrahim when he lived in Mecca.
descriptions.2734: The Book of Tawheed, which is God’s right over slaves and is known for short as the Book of Tawheed, is one of the works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, in which he explained the individuals of monotheism, and it is based on a verse and a hadith, and sometimes the saying of one of the predecessors.
descriptions.2735: The Book of Tawheed, which is God’s right over slaves and is known for short as the Book of Tawheed, is one of the works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, in which he explained the individuals of monotheism, and it is based on a verse and a hadith, and sometimes the saying of one of the predecessors.
descriptions.2736: Tawhid is a book by Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah Al-Shafi’i Al-Naysaburi (223 AH - 311 AH) on the Islamic faith according to the archaeological approach. Its author explained the reason for his classification of this book, as he stated that at the beginning of his career he was busy writing books on jurisprudence, content with the debates taking place with opponents in the councils of knowledge. However, when he was prevented from appearing and teaching, and he feared that some students of knowledge would be influenced by what they heard from heretics such as the Qadariyya, the Mu’tazilites, and the Mu’tazilites, he decided to classify this book. In it, he collected texts from the Holy Qur’an and authentic hadiths, in order to clarify the doctrine of the scholars of hadith. …
descriptions.2737: The book “Al-Qadr” by Al-Faryabi is a work on theology that deals with the issue of fate. The book includes traceable and suspended texts, in addition to works responding to people of whims and innovations. The book aims to clarify the issue of fate and remove suspicions related to it.
descriptions.2738: This book, “Exposing Illusions and Confusion About the Likeness of Some Idiots,” by Suleiman bin Sahman, is classified under the category of belief. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the field of Islamic doctrine, as it deals with topics such as atonement and similarity between people. The book begins by mentioning the story of a question from Hussein bin Sheikh Hassan bin Hussein to Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Latif, where he poses a question about atonement for the Jahmiyah. The author addresses this topic through multiple inferences and statements, including the statements of scholars from the Sunnis and the community. The book shows the author's interest in dialogue and discussion on doctrinal topics, and is characterized by analysis and reasoning in dealing with these topics.
descriptions.2739: Revealing Suspicions is a treatise on the unification of divinity, written by the Sunni Salafist scholar Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, in stating the importance of distinguishing between the unification of divinity and divinity and responding to the arguments and suspicions that were spreading in his time to justify supplication to graves, the dead, saints, and others. Today, the book is considered to be of great value to students of knowledge, and it is one of the first texts to be taught about the science of belief during their studies.
descriptions.2740: The book “Kashf al-Shubahtain” by Suleiman bin Sahman is a work on theology that deals with important issues related to the belief of the Sunnis and the community. The book includes discussions on the issue of takfir, the loyalty of believers, and disavowal of unbelievers, in addition to editing some jurisprudential issues and providing guidance to preachers.
descriptions.2741: This book, written by Suleiman bin Sahman, deals with the call of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, contradicts the slanders of its enemies, and reviews his debates with the scholars of Mecca and the translation of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab. The book also addresses various topics related to the Salafist doctrine, denies the accusations against it, and reviews important issues in Islamic doctrine and history.
descriptions.2742: This book, which was classified in the Doctrine, deals with the topic of revealing what Satan threw into the heart of Daoud bin Girgis. The book includes an introduction and discussions on verifying the proportion of the book and its subject, in addition to examples of omissions, distortions, and additions, and a description of the written copies and the investigation methodology. It also discusses a brief translation of the author and the position of the scholars of the Salafi Call on Ibn Jarjis.
descriptions.2743: The book “The Word of Sincerity and Realization of its Meaning” by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali, a book on doctrine, deals with the topic of monotheism and its importance. Through its index and excerpts, the book initially reviews the virtue of achieving monotheism, and cites noble prophetic hadiths from the Two Sahihs and others to demonstrate the greatness of this word and its impact on salvation from Hell and entering Paradise.
descriptions.2744: This book, “How to Understand Monotheism,” written by Muhammad bin Ahmed Bashmil, is considered a book in the field of Islamic belief, aiming to clarify the concept of monotheism and warn Muslims against major polytheism. The author begins by affirming that God created creation and His messengers to worship Him alone, and talks about worship and polytheism among the masses in directions other than God. The author criticizes scholars who conceal the truth and encourage disbelief, and describes them as misguided and misguided. The book aims to bring Muslims out of the darkness of polytheism into the light of monotheism, and is considered a humble attempt by the author to present this message to the servants of God.
descriptions.2745: The most important evidence in the foundations of the beliefs of the Sunnis and the community is a book by Imam Al-Juwayni, which is a treatise on the Islamic faith, or just a brief book on the doctrine that the Sunnis and the community of Muslims believe in. He wrote it to explain the truth of the Sunni doctrine in the doctrine, supported by brief evidence and rational proofs. He wrote this treatise mostly at the beginning of his life in response to the invitation of his companions, disciples and students who surrounded him and sat with him, and he limited the message to the issues of doctrine and theology that He saw it as more worthy of mention than others, and the disagreement over it became intense between the theologians, the Mu’tazilites, and other followers of theological schools of thought.
descriptions.2746: The Shine of Belief, by its author, Al-Maqdisi Muwaffaq Al-Din, dealt with the subject of the Islamic faith by reviewing the opinions of Salaf scholars and religious imams regarding the divine attributes, relying on Qur’anic and prophetic texts. The book focuses on the necessity of believing in everything that is stated in the Qur’an or authenticated by the Prophet Muhammad, while warning against interpretation or analogy to incomprehensible divine attributes, and stresses the necessity of submitting and accepting them as they come.
descriptions.2747: The book “Lawam’ Al-Anwar Al-Bahiyya wa Sawa’ Al-Asrar Al-Athari” by Al-Safarini, a book on belief, is an explanation of the issues of belief among the people of Athar. In its introduction, the book deals with important definitions related to the division of the Muhammadan religion, issues of attributes, opinion and interpretation, types of reports, mutawatir and ahad, the doctrine of the Salaf, and the emergence of heresies. It also includes an explanation of the Basmala, the meaning of praise and thanks, and the attributes of God Almighty such as eternity, survival, life, knowledge, and power, in addition to evidence of the existence of the Creator, blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ and the ranks of the Companions.
descriptions.2748: The book “What a Muslim Should Know About His Religion” by Abdullah Al-Khayyat, which is in the field of faith, deals with basic topics related to Islam. The book begins with an introduction that includes verses from Surat Al-Asr, then moves on to a detailed explanation of the pillars of Islam, focusing on practical aspects such as the conditions and characteristics of prayer, the virtue of Friday, and voluntary prayers. The book also addresses the details of the third pillar, which is zakat, the fourth pillar, which is Ramadan fasting, and the fifth pillar, which is Hajj, including the provisions of Tawaf and the Day of Arafat.
descriptions.2749: This book deals with the study of the Islamic faith through the verses of Surat Al-Zumar, as it focuses on the monotheism of God Almighty in His names and attributes, and His monotheism in worship. In its various chapters, the author discusses the Surah’s evidence of God’s transcendence of doubts and proof of His perfect attributes, clarifying the concept of unification of worship and its importance, and stating that Islam is the religion of all prophets and messengers. The book aims to reveal the sciences and facts contained in the Holy Qur’an, demonstrate its miraculous nature, and strengthen faith in God and His monotheism.
descriptions.2750: This book, “Avoiding the People of the Dead, Praying in the Landscapes and at the Graves,” by the author Abdul Aziz bin Faisal Al-Rajhi, is classified under the category of faith. The book is a response to those who permitted prayer in cemeteries and at the graves, and aims to correct the suspicions of the grave people and eliminate one of the means of shameful polytheism. The book contains multiple chapters that address various topics, such as the prohibition of prayer in cemeteries and at graves, an explanation of the status of the narrated hadiths regarding the virtue of visiting the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, and refuting the suspicions of those who object to the absolute prohibition of prayer in cemeteries and at graves. The book is considered a useful resource for understanding the Islamic faith and correcting doubts.
descriptions.2751: The book “The Outline of the Belief of the Imams of the Salaf” deals with the subject of the Islamic faith, as the author presents the agreement of the imams of the ancestors on most issues of the fundamentals of religion and their interest in issues of belief. The book reviews excerpts from the opinions of respected imams such as Abu Hanifa, Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Taymiyyah, and others, with a focus on the importance of God’s monotheism and the Qur’an and Sunnah’s clarification of Him.
descriptions.2752: This is a collection of letters by Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab on faith, dealing with basic topics in monotheism and faith. The messages include issues related to pre-Islamic times, an explanation of some of the biography, an interpretation of the word monotheism, the origins of the faith, the nullifiers of Islam, and the unification of worship.
descriptions.2753: A book on the Islamic faith, which deals with the subject of love for the Prophet ﷺ according to the method of following the Sharia, and warns against the deviations that occur in this love, such as extremism and innovation. The book explains the concept of obligatory love for the Messenger and its manifestations, and details the statement on the obligation of obeying and following him. Then it moves on to explain the danger of extremism regarding him and the heresies that have emerged under the pretext of love for him, reviewing examples of extremism among some sects such as the Shiites and Sufis.
descriptions.2754: This is a summary of Izhar al-Haqq, a doctrinal book written by Rahmatullah al-Hindi, which aims to explain the names of the books of the Old and New Testaments and prove their distortion and abrogation. The book begins with an introduction and an explanation of the matters that must be taken into account, then it moves on to an explanation of the names of the books of the Old and New Testaments and their enumeration. It deals with the state of the Torah, the state of the book of Joshua ibn Nun, and the state of the Gospels. The book shows the differences, errors, and distortions in these books, and provides examples of this through the first and second sections, where it presents some differences and errors in the books of the Old and New Testament. The book aims to reveal the truth, prove the authenticity of Islam, and distort the books of the Old and New Testaments.
descriptions.2755: The book “Summary of Fundamentalist Questions and Answers on the Doctrine” is a book that specializes in the Islamic faith, and provides concise and simplified answers to basic questions about important religious concepts. The book covers topics such as the meaning of praise, the concept of the Messenger and Prophet, guidance, religion, the testimony that there is no god but God, the monotheism of divinity, the names and attributes, and the pillars of faith. The book aims to provide a clear and simple understanding of basic Islamic concepts, making it a useful reference for those seeking a deeper understanding of the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2756: This book deals with the subject of the Islamic faith by presenting a brief introduction to the Salafi rules regarding the divine attributes. The author focuses on simplifying ideas and presenting them in clear, unambiguous words, drawing inspiration from the legacy of the Salaf al-Salih and Ibn Taymiyyah. The book divides the topic into four basic axes. Each axis represents a specific Salafist rule that includes its prohibitions, with the aim of clarifying the correct belief in divine attributes and avoiding heresies and deviations.
descriptions.2757: This book is a brief introduction to the Islamic faith, aiming to present its basic issues in an accessible manner for students and non-specialists. It begins by defining doctrinal terms such as doctrine and Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah, then explains the characteristics of the Islamic faith and the moderation of Ahlus-Sunnah among the sects. The book deals with the origins of the faith through the chapters of worship, the names and attributes of God, predestination and destiny, promise and threat, and the virtue of the Companions, and details the three types of monotheism: divinity, divinity, and names and attributes.
descriptions.2758: This book is a summary of the book “Al-I’tisam” by Imam Al-Shatibi, and it deals with the topic of heresy in terms of its definition, its condemnation, the bad consequences of its people, its types, its rulings, and the difference between it and other legal issues. This summary aims to present the original material of the book in a concise and accessible manner for the seeker of knowledge and the author of the Sunnah, while preserving its original meanings.
descriptions.2759: This book is a summary of the book “Maaraj al-Qabul” in doctrine, aiming to bring closer the issues of monotheism and the principles of correct doctrine according to the approach of the righteous predecessors. It begins by defining worship and the covenants that God has imposed on the children of Adam, then addresses in detail the sections of monotheism, beginning with the predicate-creative monotheism, which includes proving the essence of God, His names, and His attributes, with an explanation of their meanings and atheism in them.
descriptions.2760: This is the book “Introduction to the Sciences of Recitations” by the author, Mr. Rizk Al-Taweel, and is classified under the category of doctrine. This book is an introduction to the sciences of recitations, as it covers topics such as recitations and reciters, acceptable and abnormal recitations, and reciters, and relies on its chains of transmission, methods of performing it, aspects of its reading, and its drawing system. The author shows his interest in the Qur’an, its history and its roots, and believes that the sciences of readings give people more knowledge of the Qur’an and preserve it. The book aims to facilitate knowledge of the Qur’an and provide lessons and investigation of some issues that require study and investigation.
descriptions.2761: A book on the science of Islamic belief, examining the origins of belief, the emergence of the science of belief, and its historical development, with an explanation of the link between belief and Sharia, and the importance of belief and its impact. The book deals with basic definitions such as faith, Sunnah, and monotheism, and presents the issues in a manner that aims to simplify and bring them closer to students of knowledge.
descriptions.2762: This book, “Memorandum of Tawheed,” by Abd al-Razzaq Afifi, deals with the topics of the Islamic faith in a systematic manner, focusing on the concept of monotheism and its various branches. The author explains the sections of monotheism and its importance, and reviews the main issues of the Islamic faith, such as proving the existence and oneness of God, the types of monotheism, the difference between the prophet and the messenger, and the human need for the message and miracles. The book also addresses the main Islamic sects and their branches, while providing an overview of the basic issues of Islamic doctrine within a specific educational curriculum.
descriptions.2763: This is a book on the Islamic faith, written by Al-Yafi’i to respond to the suspicions of the Mu’tazilites and their controversial issues related to the fundamentals of religion. The book begins with a question from one of the Zaidi jurists, then the author discusses issues such as knowledge of God Almighty, the relationship between reason and hearing, and the issue of the actions and character of people, defending the doctrine of the Sunnis and supporting the book “The Revival of Religious Sciences.”
descriptions.2764: This is a book on the Islamic faith, and it was originally a scientific thesis that was discussed to obtain a master's degree. It deals with the topic of rapprochement between the sects of the Sunnis and the Shiites, and in its first section, it presents an introduction to the Sunnis and the community and their sources in receiving the doctrine, with a general statement of their most important doctrines in which the Shiites differed from them. The second section deals with the definition of the Shiites, their origin, and their groups, in the context of a scientific study that aims to evaluate the foundations of this approximation in light of the doctrinal origins of each group.
descriptions.2765: This is a book on faith by Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, enumerating the issues in which the Prophet ﷺ disagreed with the people of pre-Islamic times, both the writers and the illiterate. The author begins by explaining the importance of knowing these issues to distinguish truth from falsehood, then lists a number of principles that the people of pre-Islamic times followed, such as associating others with God, division in religion, disobeying the rulers, imitation, being deceived by the majority, and other issues that are presented in order to demonstrate their misguidance and contradiction to what Islam brought.
descriptions.2766: This book, “The Lamp of Darkness in Response to Those Who Lied Sheikh the Imam,” is a defensive response from Abdul Latif Al Sheikh to accusations directed at the Sheikh Imam of declaring Muslims to be infidels and accusing him of ignorance and infidelity. The book deals with responding to the allegations of the objectors and discusses the issue of faith and disbelief according to the principles of Islamic law, and aims to clarify the correct position on these thorny doctrinal issues.
descriptions.2767: The book “The Death of Sufism” or “The Idiot’s Attention to the Infidelity of Ibn Arabi” by the scholar Burhan al-Din al-Buqa’i deals with the subject of the Islamic faith through his criticism of some Sufi practices and beliefs that the author believes conflict with the fundamentals of the religion. The book focuses on criticizing the thought of Ibn Arabi and other Sufis, considering some of their ideas contrary to Islamic law and basing this on Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths. The book aims to warn against the doctrinal deviations that he believes have spread among some followers of Sufism, and calls for a return to the authentic principles of Islam.
descriptions.2768: This book, “Terms in Books of Doctrine,” by the author Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Hamad, is part of the classification of doctrine. The book contains a broad content index that covers a range of topics related to the Islamic faith, including atheism, disruption, representation, simile and conditioning, delegation, interpretation, esoteric interpretation, solutions and union, affirmative and negative attributes, subjective, actual and mental attributes, negative attributes, additional attributes, compound attributes, the self, thing, essence and truth, issues created by theologians, and a brief study of some general words, pronunciations and pronouns. And the name and the named, and the statement that faith is created or uncreated, and the essence, and the form, and the body, and individual essences, and theology and theologians, and heresy, and philosophy and philosophers.
descriptions.2769: This is a book on the Islamic faith, which studies the Twelver Shiite doctrine in its origins and branches, with a focus on the issue of imamate, which the author sees as a fundamental doctrine that prevents rapprochement between sects. The book reviews the evidence of the Imamate from the Qur’an and the Sunnah, and discusses it from the perspective of the Sunnis and the community, showing the impact of this doctrine on jurisprudence and its principles.
descriptions.2770: This book, “The Means of Acceptance with an Explanation of the Ladder of Access to the Science of Principles” is an explanation of a system in the science of principles and Islamic doctrine, written by Hafez bin Ahmed Hakami. The book addresses multiple doctrinal topics, including the monotheism of God, His attributes, and His beautiful names, relying on the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the understanding of the righteous predecessors. The author aims to explain the concept of monotheism and its necessity in the life of a Muslim, while emphasizing the importance of following the teachings of the Qur’an and Sunnah without relying on philosophical or logical analogies.
descriptions.2771: This is a book on the Islamic faith, written by Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali, and it deals with the subject of the human soul in terms of its reality and its synonymous names (soul, heart, spirit, mind), and proves that it is an independent essence with rational and textual evidence. The book examines the animal and perceptual powers, the levels of the mind, and the relationship between the mind and the law, and ends with an explanation of the truth of perception, the origin of virtues and vices, and the issue of the emergence and survival of the soul, with a conclusion on the basis of prophecy and the message.
descriptions.2772: Ma’alim fi Usul al-Din or Ma’alim fi Usul al-Din is a book on the fundamentals of religion and theology by Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (d. 606 AH).
descriptions.2773: This is the second study in the series “Studies on the Discussion of the Unification of Names and Attributes,” and it is entitled “The Belief of the Sunnis and the Community in the Most Beautiful Names of God.” The author, Muhammad bin Khalifa Al-Tamimi, aims to address the issue of the names of God in detail, after dealing with it in general in the first study. The author focuses on important topics related to this issue, and seeks to collect, arrange and formulate what has been scattered in the books. The author begins with an introduction that monitors the positions of the sects regarding the Most Beautiful Names of God, then moves to the first chapter, which deals with the confirmation and designation of the names. This chapter includes four sections, in each of which the author focuses on specific topics, such as knowing the criteria for the beautiful names, people’s approaches to enumerating the beautiful names, people’s approaches to specifying the beautiful names, and the efforts of scholars in collecting the beautiful names. The author aims to clarify the belief of the Sunnis and the community in the Most Beautiful Names of God, and to explain the evidence that supports this belief.
descriptions.2774: This book deals with the topic of unifying names and attributes from the perspective of the Sunnis and the community, and aims to explain their beliefs in this matter in a comprehensive and precise manner. The author focuses on clarifying the differences between the types of monotheism and explaining the foundations of the Sunnis’ belief in the names and attributes of God, while pointing out the corruption in the articles of the people of innovation and misguidance in this field. The book is part of a series of studies specialized in the topics of unifying names and attributes, and aims to provide a comprehensive and in-depth view of this doctrinal subject.
descriptions.2775: This is a dictionary of verbal prohibitions and benefits of words. It is a book that collects a large collection of words and sayings that are forbidden from being uttered in Islam, and it includes various aspects of belief, jurisprudence, literature, and language. The book contains a dictionary of verbal prohibitions, in addition to benefits of words, and deals with topics such as the monotheism of God, His names and attributes, the Prophet ﷺ, the two noble revelations, the Companions, the rulings on the actions of slaves, supplications and remembrances, blessings and etiquette, peace and congratulations, times and places, names, nicknames and titles, terminology, foreign languages, dialects and contemporary generating methods, behavior and heresies. The book is a useful source for learning about the words and sayings that are forbidden from being uttered in Islam, improving the meanings that corrupt them, and promoting good etiquette, monotheism, and honor.
descriptions.2776: A book on faith that deals with the meaning of the testimony “There is no god but God,” its requirements, and its impact on the life of the individual and society. The author explains the status and virtue of this word, clarifies its pillars and conditions, and differentiates between cases of its benefit to humans and its lack of benefit, while explaining its practical effects.
descriptions.2777: This book, by Al-Zarkashi, deals with an important philosophical and religious topic, which is the meaning of the testimony, “There is no god but God.” The author focuses on analyzing and interpreting the dimensions of this important word in Islam, reviewing the profound and rare benefits associated with it. The book reflects on the doctrinal and linguistic meaning of the testimony, using linguistic and philosophical concepts to explain its dimensions and importance in the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2778: This book, “The Concept of Names and Attributes,” by Saad bin Abdul Rahman Nada, is classified under the category of faith. The book is considered one of the main topics in the Islamic faith, as it deals with the concept of the names and attributes of God Almighty. The book begins with an introduction that explains the importance of belief in Islam and the necessity of fearing God, then moves to an explanation of the Most Beautiful Names mentioned in the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows the author's interest in issues of the Islamic faith and the necessity of distinguishing between truth and falsehood, and the fear of God in the hearts of believers.
descriptions.2779: This book was written by Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and it deals with topics of the Islamic faith and discusses the issue of the blasphemy of those who abandon monotheism. The book focuses on the necessity of enmity against the enemies of God, such as infidels, apostates, and hypocrites, and cites prophetic hadiths to support his doctrine of monotheism and the rejection of polytheism.
descriptions.2780: This book deals with the topic of the topic of disruption, which is an intellectual and doctrinal issue that appeared in Islamic history, and reviews its various types, degrees, and phases over time. The book also studies the personality of Al-Jaad bin Dirham and his role in publishing this article, and provides an overview of his lineage, upbringing, and the story of his murder. The book is a classification of faith and aims to understand the dimensions of this intellectual conflict between the people of truth and its enemies on the issue of belief in God.
descriptions.2781: This book, “Introductions to the Science of Maqalat Al-Furq,” written by Muhammad bin Khalifa Al-Tamimi, falls within the category of doctrine. The book aims to provide a general study on the science of difference essays, specifically in the general aspects of this science. The book begins with an introduction that emphasizes the importance of praise be to God, and indicates that the science of the articles of difference is an important science that needs introductions that clarify its aspects related to its definition and importance. The book is divided into three sections, where it analyzes the article in language and terminology, and highlights the importance of the science of articles in the Qur’an and Sunnah. This book is an important source for understanding the science of sects of difference, and helps readers become familiar with the basics of this science.
descriptions.2782: This book is a collection of critical notes written by Abd al-Qadir bin Habibullah al-Sindhi as a comment on another book entitled “The Doctrine of the Predecessors and the Successors.” These notes included a warning against the author of the original book mixing and confusing the doctrine of the predecessors and the doctrine of the successors, while directing criticism for not achieving it and distinguishing between them. At the beginning of his book, the author reviews an opinion issued by the Dean of the Faculty of Hadith at the Islamic University advising against reading the aforementioned book to young students. Then he begins to detail the reasons for this ruling and discuss the methodological and scientific errors contained in the book.
descriptions.2783: This book, from the doctrines of the predecessors, the response to the Jahmiya, by Ibn Mandah, deals with the response to the Jahmiya doctrines in the Islamic faith, citing authentic hadiths of the Prophet and verses of the Holy Qur’an. The author focuses on clarifying the meanings of some divine names and attributes, such as mentioning the hand, the palm, and the face, using prophetic hadiths and historical events to confirm the validity of the Salafi interpretation of them.
descriptions.2784: This book, “Advising Imam Wahb bin Munabbih to a Man Influenced by the Kharijite Doctrine,” by the author Abdul Salam bin Barjas Al Abdul Karim, is classified under the category of doctrine. The book tells the story of a man influenced by the Kharijite doctrine and confronted by Imam Wahb bin Munabbih. The book shows the importance of guidance and education in the Islamic religion. The book begins by telling the story of a man from the people of Sana'a who found an sealed book containing a text from Imam Wahb bin Munabbih, advising this man to be pious and obedient to God and His Messenger. The book also shows the importance of adhering to the Sunnah of the Prophet and legitimate succession.
descriptions.2785: A book that collects the debates of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah with different sects of religious scholars and scholars, such as the Christians, the people of unity, pantheism, the Qaburis, the Rifa’is, the Rafidites, and the negation of attributes, relying on what Ibn Taymiyyah broadcast in his books and letters. The author aims to highlight Ibn Taymiyyah’s skill in arguing and determining the legitimacy of debates, while explaining the diversity of their circumstances and issues.
descriptions.2786: This book deals with an intellectual debate between Islamic scholars and Christian priests that was held in Khartoum, where the participants discussed the basic doctrines and concepts of the two religions, reviewing the contradictions of the Christian faith according to the Holy Books. The book aims to reveal forgotten or unknown facts about Christianity and expose its contradictions, focusing on the beliefs of the Trinity, crucifixion, and redemption. The book also presents discussions about the Gospels and their analysis from an Islamic perspective, making it an important source for understanding both the Islamic and Christian religions.
descriptions.2787: This book, “Granting the Answering Relative in Response to the Worshipers of the Cross,” by author Abdul Aziz bin Hamad Al Muammar, is classified under the category of faith. This book is considered one of the most important sources used to understand and clarify the doctrine of Islam and challenge Christian claims. The book contains an extensive table of contents covering various topics, including the differences between Christians in the matter of their religion and their distortion of their religion, their councils, the claim of killing and crucifying Christ, rejecting the claim of Christians to kill and crucify Christ, the descent of Jesus at the end of time, the doubts of Christians about their books, the mastery of Muslim scholars in narrating hadiths about the Messenger ﷺ, and examples of the differences in Christian books, and the assertion of the authenticity of the Qur’an and that it came from God. The book begins with a greeting to God Almighty and glorification of Him, then it comes with a greeting to the Messenger ﷺ, then it begins to explain the doctrine of Islam and challenge the claims of Christians.
descriptions.2788: This is a book on doctrine, written by Sheikh Suleiman bin Sahman to respond to the ideas of fanaticism and extremism that appeared in his time, which were the nucleus for the behavior of the Kharijites in declaring Muslims to be infidels, attacking scholars, and rebelling against those in power. The book addresses important issues such as takfir and its controls according to the Sunnis, and issues of abandonment and emigration, and clarifies the correct understanding of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab’s statements in this section, in response to the suspicions raised by the extremists.
descriptions.2789: This book deals with defining the Sunnis and the community and explaining their path in belief and work, and reviews the method of followers of this approach in worshiping God, the truth of the Messenger ﷺ, the Companions, the saints and imams, and reform in society. The author focuses on the importance of adhering to the Prophetic Sunnah and adhering to the truth, while clarifying the difference between them and the innovators who deviated from this approach.
descriptions.2790: This book, “The Methodology of Establishment and Sanctification in Revealing the Suspicions of Daoud Ibn Jarjis” by author Abdul Latif Al Sheikh, is classified under the category of doctrine. The book is the third part of the series “The Reformist Heritage in Doctrine and Sharia.” It was preceded by the two parts “The Lamp of Darkness” and “The Precious Final Say.” The book aims to reveal the suspicions of Daoud bin Jarjis in his book “Reconciliation of the Brotherhood,” in which he claims that some books testify to the desirability of praying to the righteous and seeking help from them. The author shows his defense of the two sheikhs Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim, whom Ibn Jarjis slandered by falsifying their words. The book is considered a response to the suspicions of the slanderer David, and it forms part of the reformist heritage in doctrine and law.
descriptions.2791: This book deals with the approach of the Sunnis and the community in listening and obedience to rulers, reviewing the decision of the Council of Senior Scholars regarding the incident at the Grand Mosque in 1400 AH, and a fatwa by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz regarding the prohibition of rebellion against the Muslim ruler. The book is based on the legal texts from the Qur’an and Sunnah that urge obedience to rulers and avoiding disobedience to them, while mentioning some prophetic hadiths that emphasize the necessity of listening and obeying what is right.
descriptions.2792: This book, “The Ash’ari Approach to Doctrine,” by Safar al-Hawali, is considered a book on the classification of doctrine, examining the thought and ideas related to the Ash’ari sect in Islam. The book contains a table of contents that includes various parts, including a commentary on Al-Sabuni’s articles, the methodological principles in the Ash’ari doctrine, and Is There Any Doubt Remaining? Which of them is the surviving group? The book begins with a commentary on Al-Sabuni's articles, in which the author presents his opinions on Ash'arite thought and presents some of the criticisms he directed at Al-Sabuni. It appears from the book excerpt that the author aims to make some observations about Ash'arite thought and intends to conduct broader research on this topic.
descriptions.2793: This book deals with Sheikh Muhammad Rashid Reda’s approach to the Islamic faith, reviewing the environment in which he grew up and in which his ideas developed. The author focuses on studying the political, scientific, and religious factors that influenced Rashid Rida. He also analyzes his position on doctrinal issues and his method of reasoning. The book aims to understand the impact of Rashid Rida in spreading and strengthening the doctrine of Salafism in the Islamic world during the thirteenth century AH.
descriptions.2794: This is a book on the Islamic faith, which studies the approach followed by the Holy Qur’an in calling the polytheists to monotheism and Islam. The book is divided into two volumes. It initially deals with the issue of monotheism and polytheism in human history, then moves on to detail the features of the Qur’anic approach to advocacy. This includes establishing arguments and proofs, refuting the suspicions of the polytheists about the unseen and the message, and finally explaining how to convey the polytheists in worship and behavior and the position of Islam towards them.
descriptions.2795: This book, from the classification of doctrine, deals with the subject of predestination and destiny from the perspective of the Holy Qur’an. Author Mahmoud Muhammad Gharib focuses on the interpretation of Qur’anic verses related to this topic, and discusses the concepts of divine justice and appreciation in human life. It aims to clarify that everything that happens in the universe, including the events of human life, is according to God’s judgment and destiny, which provides man with reassurance and solace in the face of traumatic events, and urges him to work and take courage in facing the future.
descriptions.2796: This book, “The Methodology of Hadith and Sunnah Scholars in the Fundamentals of Religion,” by Mustafa Helmy, is considered a book on the classification of belief. The book provides a comprehensive overview of the approach of the scholars of Hadith and Sunnah to the fundamentals of religion, with a focus on the method of the scholars of Hadith and Sunnah in considering and contemplating, and an explanation of their positions on the fundamentals of religion and their method in discussing and responding to their opponents. The book shows that the scholars of Hadith and Sunnah were relying on rational evidence and logical proofs based on the interpretation of Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths, and were guided by the understanding of the early ones who were more knowledgeable and familiar with the secrets of the Arabic language, the reasons for the revelation, and the subtleties of the beliefs related to the fundamentals of religion. The book aims to give the scholars of Hadith and Sunnah their due explanation and clarification, and to appreciate the method of the people of Hadith and Sunnah in the fundamentals of religion.
descriptions.2797: This book, “A Method and Studies of the Verses of Names and Attributes” by Al-Shanqeeti, Muhammad Al-Amin, is classified under the category of doctrine. The book is an extensive study on the verses on names and attributes in the Holy Qur’an, highlighting the importance of understanding these verses and their impact on the Islamic faith. The book begins by discussing the importance of dealing with the verses about attributes, specifically three basic foundations: God’s transcendence of doubt, belief in what God described himself, and belief in what His Messenger described himself. The author highlights the importance of understanding these foundations correctly, and warns of the danger of delving into research on the verses about attributes without a proper understanding of them.
descriptions.2798: A book on the Islamic faith that examines the positions of the various sects regarding the unification of names and attributes. It first presents the position of the Sunnis and the community, which is based on proof with exaltation, then it deals with the positions of the disruptive sects such as the philosophers and theologians who denied the attributes or interpreted them, and concludes by explaining the position of the doubters and those to whom simile and anthropomorphism are attributed, all within the framework of a comparative study aimed at distinguishing the approach of truth from others.
descriptions.2799: This book deals with the history of the Jews and their origins throughout the ages, shedding light on their various historical stages from the time of Moses until the modern era. The author also focuses on exposing the allegations and falsehoods they promote, especially those related to their chosen people, their pure race, and their historical right to Palestine. The book aims to show the corruption of their religion and state historical facts instead of the false narratives they promote.
descriptions.2800: This book, “The Position of People of Desires and Sects on the Prophetic Sunnah” by the writer Muhammad bin Matar Al-Zahrani, is considered a book in the field of doctrine. It addresses the roots and origins of the heresy and its historical development. It deals with the position of the sects and sects on the Prophetic Sunnah and its narrators. It provides examples of the plots of ancient and modern enemies. It deals with how to make an alliance between these two plans in the present era.
