It deals with the most important features of the policy of the new Crusader-Zionist plan, its trends and foundations, and provides sources and references. The book focuses on the origins of heretics, sects, and deviant sects in the history of our Islamic nation, and deals with their roots, means, and goals, ancient and modern.
descriptions.2801: This book deals with Imam Ibn Taymiyyah’s position on the Mu’tazilites and Ash’aris in the field of Islamic doctrine. The author focuses on the approach of the Salaf and the Sunnis, and discusses the life of Ibn Taymiyyah and his jurisprudential and scientific opinions in confronting other trends. The book aims to better understand the development of doctrinal schools of thought in Islamic history and to determine their place in the modern scientific arena.
descriptions.2802: This book, “A Brief Introduction to the Islamic Faith,” by Ibn Uthaymeen, is classified under the classification of faith. The book covers topics of the Islamic faith, including the Islamic religion, its pillars and foundations, belief in God, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and destiny, and the goals of the Islamic faith. The book begins by defining the Islamic religion and its status among religions, then moves on to explaining the pillars and foundations of Islam, and belief in God Almighty, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day, and destiny. The book aims to teach Muslims about the Islamic faith and enhance their understanding of it, to build his religion on a sound and sound foundation.
descriptions.2803: This book, “The Blessing of the Defeat in Supporting the Sharia” by Al-Halabi, deals with topics related to the Islamic faith, and aims to support the Sharia and expose the error and ignorance of the existentialist sect. The author focuses on discussing ideas and opinions that are contrary to Islamic law, and reviews some of the points that appeared in the book Al-Fusus to discuss and refute them. The book aims to clarify religious truths and explain heresies and misguidance in some philosophical and existential doctrines.
descriptions.2804: This book, “Imam Abu Saeed Othman bin Saeed’s refutation of Al-Muraisi,” by the author Al-Darimi, is considered a book in the field of doctrine, as it aims to refute Al-Muraisi’s opinions and verify the book. The book begins by introducing the author, Al-Marisi, and Ibn Al-Thalji, then addresses the introduction to the book and the manuscript, before moving to the second part, which contains an introduction and the reason for writing the book. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the author emphasizes the importance of memorizing the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet, and considers memorizing these books to be the preservation of the religion. This book shows the author's interest in the Islamic faith and responding to the opinions of opponents.
descriptions.2805: This book, “Refuting the words of the slanderers against the Hanbali Salafis,” by the writer Ahmed bin Hajar Al-Botami, is part of the classification of doctrine. The book contains a table of contents covering multiple topics, including responding to the theologians’ slander against the Hanbalis, explaining the Salaf’s doctrine of the attributes of God, and refuting the allegations attributed to Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and his followers. The book begins by discussing the issue of the creation of the Qur’an, discusses the Hanbali position on this issue, and responds to the Mu’tazilites’ transmissional and rational suspicions. It appears from the excerpt at the beginning of the book that the book aims to clarify the Hanbali doctrine and explain their position on matters of doctrine. The author believes that there are many slanders against the Hanbalis by theologians, and he aims to refute these slanders.
descriptions.2806: This book, “These are our concepts,” by author Saleh Al-Sheikh, is part of the classification of faith. The book contains multiple chapters that address various topics such as supplication, unification of divinity and divinity, intercession, atonement, blessing, and the circumstances of Muhammad al-Maliki. The book begins with a definition of the author and a statement of the values ​​in which he believes, then moves on to address the temptations that threaten society in this time, especially the temptation against fulfilling the meaning of the two testimonies. The book aims to guide readers towards understanding the straight path and truly realizing the meaning of the two testimonies.
descriptions.2807: This is a brief message and necessary advice regarding the necessity of resorting to God’s law, and a warning against resorting to anything other than it. It was written by the author Ibn Baz, in which he dealt with the subject of referring to God and His Messenger, and contrasted between the readers the necessity of resorting to God’s law and rejecting what contradicts it. He mentioned the importance of resorting to God in this worldly life and the hereafter, and placed among the readers between good and evil. He promised success and prosperity to those who follow God’s law, and promised torment and loss to those who refuse. God's law.
descriptions.2808: This book is a doctoral dissertation in the Islamic faith. It examines the concept of moderation among the Sunnis and the community and explains its linguistic and legal meaning. It explains what is meant by the term “Sunnahs,” its origin and the date of its launch, detailing the position of the various sects such as the Shiites, Mu’tazilites, and Ash’aris regarding this title, and explaining the names and titles of the Sunnis.
descriptions.2809: This book, “The Effect of Differences in Texts and Asnads on the Differences of Jurists,” written by Dr. Maher Yassin Al-Fahl, is considered one of the most important references in the science of Hadith and Islamic jurisprudence. The book deals with the issue of disagreement in texts and chains of transmission and its effects on disagreement among jurists. The book begins with an introductory chapter to explain the nature of disagreement, then moves to several chapters that deal with various types of disagreement, from disagreement in the chain of transmission to disagreement in the text, and explaining the reasons for this disagreement and its effects on the disagreement among jurists. This book is an important source for jurists and investigators in Hadith and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2810: This book, “Introducing the Science of Reasons,” by Hisham Al-Hallaf, is part of a series of books that aim to introduce readers to the Islamic sciences, especially the science of causes, which is considered one of the most important sciences in Hadith science. The author begins by defining the problem in the language, where he states that the problem means repetition or repetition, an obstacle that hinders, or a weakness in something. Then he moves to the definition of the reason in the terminology of the hadith scholars, where the term reason is used in the sense of a hidden reason that discredits the validity of the hadith. The author points out that the reason in the terminology of hadith scholars is used in two ways: general and specific, as the general reason is a hidden reason that discredits the validity of the hadith, while the specific reason is a hidden reason that discredits the validity of the hadith. This book is considered one of the important sources for introducing readers to modern science, especially the science of causes, which is considered one of the most important sciences in this field.
descriptions.2811: This book deals with the investigation of weak and fabricated hadiths related to the hadith “Whoever prays two rak’ahs after Fajr will have the reward of Umrah and Hajj,” where the author Ahmed Shehata Al-Iskandari explains the methods of narrating the hadith and the chains of transmission of its narrators, and reviews the reasons for each method and its narrator, confirming the weakness of the hadith and explaining the reasons for its weakness. The book is a type of book that is concerned with the science of reasons in hadith and falls under the classification of reasons and questions.
descriptions.2812: This book, “Al-Nafila fi Weak and False Hadiths,” by the author Abu Ishaq Al-Huwaini, is classified under the causes and questions. It deals with the subject of weak and false hadiths, and aims to investigate and analyze these different hadiths in their meaning and objectives. The book is a collection of different hadiths, the author presents an investigation of them, and attempts to prove the validity or weakness of these hadiths.
descriptions.2813: This book, “Abu Zar’ah al-Razi and His Efforts in the Prophetic Sunnah,” is considered one of the most important sources in understanding the role of Abu Zar’ah al-Razi in promoting the Prophetic Sunnah and laying the foundations for investigating it. The book shows that Abu Zar'ah al-Razi was one of the first scholars to exert great effort in collecting and verifying the Sunnah of the Prophet, especially with regard to narrators and weak ones. The book provides a comprehensive overview of the life of Abu Zar'ah al-Razi, from his upbringing to his death, and also includes a detailed analysis of his approach to fulfilling the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book also highlights the importance of the Prophetic Sunnah in Islam, highlighting the role of Abu Zar’ah al-Razi in promoting it.
descriptions.2814: This book deals with fabricated hadiths compiled by Al-Jurqani and Ibn Al-Jawzi, and Al-Dhahabi analyzes and criticizes them. The author focuses on showing the weakness of its evidence and the disbelief of its narrators, relying in this on his extensive knowledge of narration and investigation. The book is of the type of reasons and questions, as Al-Dhahabi explains the reasons for the weakness of these hadiths and reveals their defects.
descriptions.2815: This book, “Illegal Hadiths that Appear to be Authentic,” by Muqbil bin Hadi Al-Wadaei, deals with the study of hadiths that appear to be authentic on the surface but contain defects in reality. Al-Wada'i focuses on analyzing these hadiths and explaining the reasons for their weakness despite their apparent authenticity, while providing examples and benefits in this field. The book contains references from recent companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and aims to clarify the issue of the reasons in the Prophetic hadiths and the ways to weigh them.
descriptions.2816: This book, “The Parts of Strangeness and Individuals,” by Ibn al-Qaysrani, is classified under causes and questions. The book is a collection of Prophetic hadiths collected through a series of narrators, and the author shows his efforts in collecting and recording these hadiths. The book begins with the author introducing himself and explaining the reason for presenting the book in an out of order, then follows it with some prophetic hadiths collected through a series of narrators. The book shows the author's interest in the Prophet's hadith and his work on collecting and recording the Prophet's hadiths through a series of narrators.
descriptions.2817: Abu Abdullah Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Abi Bakr bin Ayyub bin Saad bin Hariz al-Zar’i al-Dimashqi al-Hanbali (691 - 751 AH / 1292 - 1350 AD), known as Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah or also Ibn al-Qayyim is a jurist, hadith scholar, commentator, and diligent Muslim scholar, and one of the most prominent imams of the Hanbali school of thought in the first half of the eighth century AH. …
descriptions.2818: This book, “Al-Athar Al-Marfu’ fi Al-Akhbar Al-Mawdoo’,” by Al-Laknawi author Abu Al-Hasanat, is part of the classification of causes and questions. The book contains a content index that shows that its main content relates to prayer and religious etiquette, with topics such as daily prayers, prayer on specific days of the year, and related virtues and etiquette. The book seems to aim to provide information about prayer and religious etiquette, while also covering some stories and topics related to them.
descriptions.2819: Falsehoods, Munkars, Sahihs, and Al-Mashhur is one of the books of hadith, written by Al-Hafiz Al-Jurqani. In his book, the author collected the fabricated hadiths that were false against the Messenger of God and demonstrated their falsity. He arranged them in the books and made sections underneath them, where he cites the hadiths with their chains of transmission and then judges them clearly and details the reason for his ruling and the sayings of the scholars regarding the descriptions of the narrators and the Sunnahs. The book included seven hundred and forty-one hadiths, some of which were fabricated and some of which were authentic.
descriptions.2820: This book, “Al-Asrar Al-Marfu’ fi Al-Akhbar Al-Mawdoo’,” by Mullah Ali Al-Qari, is classified under the category of reasons and questions. The book contains a table of contents that shows its structure, in addition to an excerpt from the beginning of the book that shows the author’s way of dealing with the Prophetic hadiths and identifying their sources. It seems that the book aims to study the Prophetic hadiths, identify their sources, determine between authentic and weak hadiths, and place them in their historical and social context.
descriptions.2821: The book “Al-Tammiz” by Muslim deals with the issue of the reasons for narrating and performing hadiths, and reviews errors and illusions in transmitting and preserving hadiths, indicating the differences between authentic and weak ones. The author focuses on the importance of investigation and distinction in narrating a hadith, discusses the reasons for errors in transmitting chains of transmission and texts, and presents examples of hadiths in which errors and errors occurred.
descriptions.2822: This book, “Al-Jami’ fi Al-Il’l and Ma’rifat Al-Rijal” by the author Ahmad ibn Hanbal, is considered one of the most important sources in the science of hadith and biographies. The book is concerned with defining men and causes, as it contains information about the biographies of hadith imams and narrators, and also includes opinions and rulings about the authenticity of hadith and narrators. This book is considered an essential source for researchers in hadith and translations, and is considered one of the most important sources in this field.
descriptions.2823: A book on the science of hadith. Its author selects from the book “Itqan Ma Hasan min narrations circulating on tongues” by his grandfather, Najm al-Din al-Ghazi al-Amiri, the two sections related to what was reported in the hadith and what is a lie and fabricated on the Prophet ﷺ, to show what was not reported from him, peace and blessings be upon him, from the hadiths circulating on tongues. The author has arranged his material according to the letters of the dictionary, from hamza to yā’, to be of assistance in distinguishing fabricated and false hadiths from those that have a basis in the Sunnah, even if they are weak.
descriptions.2824: This book is the first part of “Gharar Al-Fawaid Al-Majmu’ah” by Al-Rashid Al-Attar, and it deals with the hadiths that were mentioned in Sahih Muslim and which some considered to be without chains of transmission. Al-Attar aims to correct these hadiths and explain the aspects of their connection, reviewing fourteen of them, relying on what Imam Al-Mazari mentioned in his book “Al-Mualim” and reviewing the opinions of previous hadith scholars on this subject. The book focuses on clarifying the authenticity of these hadiths and correcting any suspected breaks in the chain of transmission.
descriptions.2825: The book “The Great Weak” by Al-Uqaili is a work on the science of wounds and modifications, and falls under the classification of causes and questions. The book aims to explain the conditions of the narrators from whom the hadith was transmitted and whose companionship is not proven, by mentioning their names in alphabetical order, while commenting on their hadiths and explaining what they contain of illusion, denial, or ignorance. The author begins his book by presenting the sayings of the imams of hadith regarding the necessity of clarifying the matter of those who are accused of memorizing the hadith or not memorizing it, based on the fact that this knowledge is a religion.
descriptions.2826: The book “Al-Illal Al-Saghir” by Al-Tirmidhi Muhammad bin Issa is considered an important reference in the field of reasons and questions, as it is concerned with studying and analyzing the reasons in the hadiths of the Prophet and men. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as supporting the statements of some prominent scholars, the sources of mentioning reasons in hadiths and men, and the opinions of jurists on some issues. The book shows an interest in analyzing and evaluating the chain of transmission of hadiths, with an emphasis on the importance of understanding the reasons in evaluating the authenticity of hadiths. The book provides a comprehensive overview of the field of causes and questions, and shows the extent of interaction and discussion among scholars in this field.
descriptions.2827: This book is by Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, and it is one of the books that is concerned with studying the reasons for weak and weak hadiths. In this work, the work deals with a critical review of multiple hadiths, indicating their causes and shortcomings, and reviewing various topics of belief, monotheism, jurisprudence, and the provisions of Sharia. The book aims to distinguish authentic hadiths from weak ones through careful investigation of their narrators and chains of transmission.
descriptions.2828: The book “The Reasons Contained in the Prophetic Hadiths” by Imam Al-Daraqutni is one of the best works in the science of the reasons for the hadith, and it is an art that searches for the hidden reasons that undermine the authenticity of the hadith despite the soundness of its apparent meaning. The book includes a large collection of prophetic hadiths that Al-Daraqutni was asked about, explaining the reasons for them in terms of chain of transmission and text, relying on a precise approach in criticism and distinguishing between the authentic and the incorrect. This book was compiled by his student Al-Barqani, and Abu Mansur Ibn Al-Karkhi added to it, to be a comprehensive reference on this art, which received great praise from scholars.
descriptions.2829: This is the book “Al-Ilal Ibn Abi Hatim” by the author Al-Razi, Ibn Abi Hatim, and it follows the classification of ills and questions. The book contains an extensive content index that covers a range of topics related to the Prophet’s hadith, including purity, the call to prayer, forgetfulness, prostration of the Qur’an, Friday prayers, zakat, conquest, sales, marriage, divorce, number, vows, oaths, limits, blood money, rulings, pre-emption, dress, food, drink, sacrifices, sacrifices, hunting, aqeeqah, religious duties, the Qur’an, interpretation of the Qur’an, asceticism, and faith. The book begins with greeting God Almighty and thanking His blessings, then moving on to talk about the Prophet of Islam Muhammad ﷺ, praising him and considering him the best of creation. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the science of hadith reasons, which is concerned with analyzing and interpreting the noble Prophetic hadiths.
descriptions.2830: This book is an investigation and conclusion of the book “Illnesses and Knowledge of Men” by Ahmed bin Hanbal, a narration by his son Abdullah. The book covers an introductory introduction that includes knowledge of men, al-Jarh, and al-Ta'deel, and then moves on to a brief translation of Imam Ahmad and a description of the book. The book contains seven parts that include studying the causes, analyzing hadith narrations, and knowing men from a critical perspective.
descriptions.2831: This is the book “Al-Ilal” by the author Ali bin Al-Madini, and it falls within the category of “Ilal” and Questions. The book contains a table of contents that explains the importance of the book and the hadith narrators cited in the book. The book begins with “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,” and then the author explains how he derived the hadith from different narrators, such as Zaid ibn Thabit, Qays ibn Abi Hazim, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and others. It appears that the book focuses on studying the reasons and narrators cited in the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.2832: This book, “Al-Firdaws Bi Ma’thur Al-Khattab” by Al-Dailami, is a collection of hadiths, sermons, and prophetic and wise sayings arranged according to the alphabet. The book addresses multiple topics related to morals, worship, and transactions, using the alphabetical arrangement technique to facilitate research and reference to the various topics.
descriptions.2833: The book “The Fabricated Benefits of Fabricated Hadiths” by Mar’i Al-Karmi, which is classified in the section on reasons and questions, deals with the issue of judging hadiths as fabricated, and shows the difficulty of doing so for later scholars due to their lack of collection of methods and frequent investigation, with reference to the scholars’ criticism of Ibn al-Jawzi’s expansion in his book “Al-Mawdoo’at” in ruling fabricated hadiths that are not of that merit, and a warning against imitating him in that without scrutiny.
descriptions.2834: This book, “Al-Qisas and Remembrancers” by the scholar Ibn al-Jawzi, is considered one of the most important books in the category of reasons and questions. The book deals with two main factions: the retaliators and the remembrancers. The book begins by mentioning the biographies of the chapters of the book, then moves to a chapter on the virtues of preaching from the perspective of meaning, followed by chapters mentioning the imams of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), then it moves to mentioning the imams of the schools of jurisprudence. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the science of causes and questions, as it contains separate chapters that address various topics in this field.
descriptions.2835: This book, “Pearls Made in Fabricated Hadiths” by Al-Suyuti, deals with the subject of fabricated hadiths attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author aims to revise the hadiths he wrote and separate them from the authentic ones, using multiple sources to document what he mentions. The book deals with various topics from faith and worship to transactions and literature, relying on the evidence of hadiths and examining their authenticity.
descriptions.2836: This book, “Pearls studded with no basis or fabricated origin,” by Al-Qasqaji, deals with the subject of fabricated and abnormal hadiths in Islam, and aims to warn against their publication and promotion among people. The book is classified according to the letters of the alphabet, and in each letter it presents a group of hadiths attributed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that are claimed to be fabricated or fabricated. The author emphasizes the seriousness of attributing it to the Prophet and conveys the opinions of scholars regarding the ruling on publishing and promoting it.
descriptions.2837: This book, “Made in Knowledge of the Fabricated Hadith,” by Mullah Ali Al-Qari, is classified under the causes and questions. The book is considered one of the most important works in the science of hadith, as it aims to clarify the origins of objective hadith and methods for determining it. The book begins by defining the objective hadith and explaining the importance of knowing it, then moving on to address the letters of the Arabic dictionary, where Al-Qari explains the importance of each letter in defining the objective hadith. The book shows the author's familiarity with the branches of hadith science and his interest in clarifying its origins. This book is an important source for researchers in Hadith and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2838: The book “Al-Mawdoo’at” by Ibn Al-Jawzi is a work of hadith science, which falls under the category of “Reasons and Questions”, and is specialized in collecting false and fabricated hadiths about the Prophet ﷺ. The book begins with an introduction about the importance of the Prophetic Sunnah and an explanation of the danger of lying to the Messenger of God. Then, it lists the hadiths arranged in various jurisprudential sections, including monotheism, faith, acts of worship, transactions, and others, with the aim of purifying the Prophetic Sunnah from any similar fabrication or fabrication.
descriptions.2839: This book, “The Brilliant Elite in the False Hadiths on Khair al-Bariyah,” was written by Prince Al-Maliki. It deals with the false hadiths that spread among the public and for which there is no authentic basis in the approved books of the Sunnah. Through it, the author aims to differentiate between authentic and false hadiths, and serve the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the Islamic nation. He collected four hundred false hadiths, and arranged them alphabetically in the dictionary to facilitate access to them, while neglecting their chains of transmission due to the lack of an authentic origin.
descriptions.2840: Warning the elite against the lies of retaliation, a book by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti.
descriptions.2841: This is the book “Tadhkirat al-Huffaz” by Ibn al-Qaysrani, which is a book about reasons and questions that contains the excerpts of the hadiths from the book “Al-Majrouhin” by Ibn Hibban. The book focuses on determining the credibility of the hadiths and narratives that people invoke in debates and protests. The book begins with the chapter Alif and continues with the rest of the letters of the alphabet. It contains hadiths circulated among people, analyzing them and determining their credibility. The book is considered an important source for researchers in modern causes, questions, and analysis.
descriptions.2842: This book, “Tadhkirat al-Mawdoo’at” by Al-Fatni, deals with fabricated and weak hadith topics, and aims to carefully investigate the status or weakness of the hadith, while differentiating between what is agreed upon and what is a matter of disagreement among scholars. The author focuses on the necessity of verifying the authenticity of the hadith and not being certain about its status based on one opinion, while warning against exaggeration and negligence in judging the hadiths. It also points out the spread of false topics in countries and discusses the issue of excluding the weak from authentic hadiths that may be unfairly judged to be false.
descriptions.2843: This book is a commentary and investigation by Ibn Abd al-Hadi on the book “Al-Ilal” by Ibn Abi Hatim, and it falls within the classification of “Ilāl and Questions” in Hadith science. The book deals with the study of the chains of transmission of the Prophet’s hadiths and their criticism, by tracing the paths of the narrators and explaining the differences in the chains of transmission and texts, while discussing the rulings of critical imams such as Abu Zur’ah and al-Tirmidhi on the authenticity of the hadiths or their reasons.
descriptions.2844: This is a book on the science of causes and questions, compiled by the author Muhammad Amr bin Abdul Latif, and it specializes in studying hadiths and narrations whose authenticity has not been proven to be attributed to the Prophet ﷺ nor attributed to the Companions or those after them. The book aims to purify the well-known narratives from those whose chain of transmission is not valid, whether it is a chain of transmission or a stop. The author included in its first section a group of hadiths that became clear to him that they were not proven after research and examination of the chain of transmission.
descriptions.2845: This book is a summary of Ibn al-Jawzi's book "Al-Mawdoo'at", in which Al-Dhahabi focuses on examining fabricated and false hadiths on various religious and causal topics. The author deals with supposed hadiths about monotheism, faith, and virtues, in addition to fabricated hadiths about the virtues of the Companions and Ahl al-Bayt, and other hadiths about beliefs and legal rulings. The book aims to distinguish between authentic and fabricated hadiths to ensure correct understanding and practice of Islamic law.
descriptions.2846: This book, “The Purification of the Revealed Sharia over Fabricated Heinous News,” by Sheikh Ibn Iraq, is considered an important book in classifying causes and questions. The book aims to identify alleged and abrogated hadiths about Islamic law, and to provide evidence of the authenticity or incorrectness of these hadiths. The book contains a comprehensive table of contents covering all letters from A to Z, and provides an excerpt from the beginning of the book explaining the importance of knowing alleged hadiths and determining their authenticity. This book is a valuable resource for researchers and investigators of Islamic sciences, and helps in determining the facts and reality regarding alleged hadiths.
descriptions.2847: This book deals with the issues and narrations of Ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of his sheikhs, as he mentions what he heard from them and what he narrated from them. It focuses on transmitting hadiths and historical stories related to famous scholars and imams, while providing personal assessments about the reliability of these sheikhs and their respective reputations in the field of science and jurisprudence. The book is classified as reasons and questions, which indicates his interest in studying the chains of transmission of hadiths and the authenticity of their transmission.
descriptions.2848: The book “The History of Preservation from Al-Kamil by Ibn Adi” is considered one of the important books in the science of the Prophet’s hadith, as it combines an index of words and a classification of hadiths. The author Ibn al-Qaysrani is considered one of the most famous scholars in this field. He translated and verified the hadiths found in the book “Al-Kamil” by Ibn Adi. The book contains a comprehensive table of contents that covers all the hadiths in the book, and it shows that the book focuses on hadiths that contain different reasons and classifications. The book seems to aim to facilitate access to authentic hadiths circulating in Islamic society, and provides an important source for researchers in this field.
descriptions.2849: This book deals with the questions of Imam Abu Bakr al-Barqani addressed to Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni in the field of wound science and modification. It focuses on examining men and determining the authenticity of their hadith, as this science is considered one of the most important sciences in the field of the noble Prophet’s hadith. The book is one of the important books in this field, as it reflects a scientific dialogue between prominent hadith scholars, and it aims to clarify the criteria for jarh and tadil and the conditions for jarh and tadil.
descriptions.2850: The book “Abu Dawud’s Questions to Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal” is one of the books of reasons and questions, and it collects Abu Dawud al-Sijistani’s questions to Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal about hadith narrators and the reasons for hadiths. The book deals with the conditions of narrators in terms of documentation and refutation, organized into sections according to countries and classes, such as the trustworthy people of Medina, Mecca, Yemen, the Levant, Iraq, and others, with a mention of the weak people of Medina in an appendix. It appears from the excerpts that the book is concerned with discussing the chains of transmission of hadiths and explaining the differences in the narrations and the narrators’ revisions of their sayings.
descriptions.2851: This book, “Ibn al-Junaid’s Questions to Abu Zakaria Yahya bin Ma’in,” ​​is part of the classification of reasons and questions, as it contains questions and answers about the credibility of some historical figures. The book features Yahya bin Ma'in's account of his questions about the reliability of some narrators, demonstrating his interest in Islamic history and narrators. This book is considered an important source for historical and narrative study of Islam.
descriptions.2852: The book “Al-Barqani’s Questions by Al-Daraqutni, Al-Karaji’s Narration from Him” is one of the books on the science of ills and questions in jarh and ta’deel. It collects Al-Barqani’s questions to Imam Al-Daraqutni about the conditions of the narrators and the extent of their trustworthiness or weakness. This book falls within the early scientific efforts that sought to distinguish authentic hadiths from weak ones by tracking the conditions of the hadith narrators. In its introduction, the book addresses the importance of the science of chain of transmission and the emergence of the science of jarh and modification, and refers to the development of books of questions as a basis for this science.
descriptions.2853: A book that examines the science of the causes of hadith through Imam al-Tirmidhi’s questions to Imam al-Bukhari about hadiths contained in Jami’ al-Tirmidhi. It includes a study of the importance of this science, the definition of the cause, its types, and how to recognize it. The book includes a comprehensive translation of Imam al-Tirmidhi and a summary of Imam al-Bukhari, with a focus on the question-and-answer approach to hadith criticism.
descriptions.2854: This book is Hafiz Khamis Al-Hawzi’s questions about the scholars and imams of hadith, where he asks the Salafi hafiz about their sheikhs, professors, and their scientific and historical status. The book covers information about scholars such as Omar bin Ali al-Maymouni, Abu Muhammad al-Ghandjani, Abu al-Barakat Ahmad bin Uthman bin Nafis, and Abu Abdullah al-Alawi, indicating the sayings of al-Hafiz Khamis al-Hawzi regarding those they heard from and the knowledge and foundations of hadith that reached them. The book focuses on the reasons and questions in the field of hadith and narration.
descriptions.2855: This is the book “Questions of Al-Hakim Al-Naysaburi by Al-Daraqutni”, which is a book about reasons and questions. It contains the questions of Al-Hakim Al-Naysaburi by Al-Daraqutni. The book presents questions and comments about the names of sheikhs from the people of Iraq. The book also includes questions about their conditions in jarh and ta’deel. The book is an important source for historical and heritage studies, as it provides information about the names of sheikhs and their conditions at that time.
descriptions.2856: The book “Questions of Al-Sulami by Al-Daraqutni” is one of the books of reasons and questions in the science of hadith, in which Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Sulami collected questions that he addressed to Imam Al-Daraqutni about hadiths and narrations, and he answered them. The author arranged these questions and answers in the order of the letters of the dictionary (Chapter Alif, Ba, and so on) to facilitate research. The book aims to explain the reasons for the hadiths and distinguish the authentic ones from the incorrect ones by directing specific questions to one of the imams of this art.
descriptions.2857: Hamza bin Yusuf Al-Sahmi’s Questions to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Daraqutni, one of the books of Al-Jarh wal-Ta’deel, written by Al-Hafiz Hamza Al-Sahmi.
descriptions.2858: The Questions of Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah by Ali bin Al-Madini is one of the books of jarh and ta’deel, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Jaafar bin Abi Shaybah (210 AH - 297 AH). The books of questions are what students transmit from the sheikhs of questions about jarh and ta’deel. They are mostly attributed to the one who asked them, and often go back to one imam. These questions were transmitted by Abu Jaafar bin Abi Shaybah from his sheikh, Ali bin Urban.
descriptions.2859: This book is the Questions of Masoud bin Ali Al-Sijzi with the Questions of the Baghdadis, and it is written by Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah. The book deals with Masoud bin Ali Al-Sijzi’s questions addressed to famous scholars and jurists, as it focuses on discussing the fairness and honesty of these scholars in transmitting hadith and its narrators. The book falls within the classification of reasons and questions, and aims to investigate the facts about the sources of hadiths and document them, relying on narrating information about the lives of scholars, their hearings, and their scientific reputation.
descriptions.2860: This is a book on the science of causes and questions, pertaining to the Sahih of Imam Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, by its author, Ibn Ammar the Martyr. The book studies and criticizes some of the hadiths contained in the Sahih, indicating any additions or defects in the chains of transmission and texts, by tracking the various narrations and judging them.
descriptions.2861: Illal al-Tirmidhi al-Kabir is one of the books of hadith, written by Abu Issa Muhammad al-Tirmidhi (209 AH - 279 AH). The book is a collection of several hadiths narrated by Imam al-Tirmidhi with his chains of transmission, then he follows them with a ruling on each hadith, either with his own words or with the words of the sheikhs whom he mentions. He says after the hadith: I asked so-and-so about him, and he said: such-and-such, and the greater share of the ruling on these hadiths went to Imam al-Bukhari, who issues the author’s narration. His words by saying: I asked Muhammad about him, and he sometimes says: I asked Muhammad bin Ismail about him, and the texts of this book reached 484 chained texts.
descriptions.2862: This book, “Rules of Causes and Evidence of Preference,” by author Adel Al-Zarqi, is considered within the classification of causes and questions. The book presents the principles of the science of reasons, and the author considers it one of the most important legal sciences. The book deals with the rules of practical reasons and weighting evidence, and combines what was mentioned in the books on reasons and histories. The book is a useful resource for researchers in Hadith and Sharia sciences.
descriptions.2863: This book, “Ma’rifat al-Tdhikrah fi al-Mawdoo’ah Hadiths,” by Ibn al-Qaysrani, deals with the false and weak hadiths promoted by some slanderers and those who are hesitant about the hadith. It classifies hadiths according to the alphabetical order of the dictionary, and mentions the author of each hadith and the reason for its weakness or falsehood, with the aim of warning against its spread among people and its use in religious discussions and debates.
descriptions.2864: This is the book “From the Questions of Abu Bakr Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Hani” by the author Ahmed bin Hanbal, and it falls within the classification of reasons and questions. The book contains questions and answers about hadith issues, and the index indicates that the book begins with In the Name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful, and includes the last part of the book. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book contains a series of questions and answers presented by Ahmad ibn Hanbal, where he presents questions and answers about hadith issues, such as hadith narrators and their hadiths, and indicates that some narrators were advanced in memorizing hadith.
descriptions.2865: The book “From the Words of Abu Zakaria Yahya bin Ma’in fi Al-Rijal” is a collection of the sayings of Imam Yahya bin Ma’in on the science of jarh and ta’deel, as it includes audio texts from him that address the conditions of hadith narrators and their degrees of confidence and weakness. The book falls within the category of “Reasons and Questions,” and presents its narrations with chains of transmission connected to Ibn Ma’in, including his critical rulings on a number of hadith scholars such as Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Ma’shar, and others.
descriptions.2866: This book is a collection of reasons and questions collected by Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It contains various issues about men and narrators, and it also includes some footnotes and comments on these questions. The book seems to focus on determining the credibility of narrators and narratives, and also includes some information about the lives and works of some narrators. This book is considered an important source for historical and heritage studies in Islam, and is considered part of the important Islamic heritage.
descriptions.2867: The book “Al-I`timad fi Naza’ir al-dha’ and al-dha’” by Ibn Malik is a linguistic dictionary that specializes in differentiating between words that are written and pronounced with the two similar letters (tha’ and dha’) in order to control correct pronunciation and writing. The book is organized into sections arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. For each letter, it mentions a pair of words that are similar in pronunciation but different in meaning according to the letter, with an explanation of the meaning of each word, citing the Holy Qur’an, the Prophet’s hadith, Arabic poetry, and the sayings of linguists. Through this book, the author aims to clarify the subtle differences between words that may confuse the speaker or writer, which makes it an important reference in linguistics and jurisprudence.
descriptions.2868: Al-'Abab Al-Zakher and Al-Lubab Al-Fakher, or in short Al-'Abab Al-Zakher, is one of the language books and its dictionaries, written by Imam Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Saghani (577 AH - 650 AH). This book is considered one of the rare dictionaries of the Arabic language composed in the seventh century AH. It was classified into twenty-eight parts, distributed according to the number of letters of the Arabic language, but they vary in the number of their pages. Because the number of items in each chapter varies. …
descriptions.2869: Al-Muhit in the language is one of the most famous dictionaries of the Arabic language in the fourth century AH. Its author, Al-Sahib bin Abbad, followed the example of Al-Khalil in Al-Ain in its arrangement and division of its chapters.
descriptions.2870: This is the book “Masculine and Feminine” by the author Ibn al-Tastari, the writer, and is classified among the strange, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book provides a table of contents that includes a chapter for each letter of the Arabic letter, covering the topics of the variables between masculine and feminine in the Arabic language. The book begins by stating that there is no consistent analogy between masculine and feminine, and indicates the presence of feminine signs such as the ha, the extended alif, and the shortened alif, which appear in feminine nouns. The book also analyzes the names of the human body, defining masculine and feminine parts of the body, and provides examples. The book also covers multiple topics, such as things that are found by ear to be feminine, such as salt, fire, bucket, and others. The book is a useful resource for researchers in the Arabic language and jurisprudence.
descriptions.2871: This is the book “The Creation of Man” by the author Al-Asma’i, and it is classified among the strange, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. This book is considered one of the main sources in Arabic linguistics and Islamic heritage. The book contains a table of contents that shows the variety of topics covered by the author, from women’s pregnancy and childbirth to the fluctuations of human conditions. The book begins by mentioning the meanings of words such as “fever,” “labor pain,” and “merciful,” and then addresses the parts of the human body from the head to the penis. The author demonstrates superior linguistic skills in describing concepts and meanings of words, making the book a valuable resource for study and benefit.
descriptions.2872: Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinauri's Treatise on Calligraphy and the Pen is a linguistic and cultural study that deals with the origins and aspects of the use of writing tools in the golden age of Islamic civilization. The author focuses on defining the terms writing, pen, ink, paper, and others, reviewing their uses and development over time. He also refers to some practical applications such as sharpening and cutting, relying on the linguistic and interpretive sources available in his time.
descriptions.2873: This is the book “Selected from Sihah Al-Jawhari” by the author Abu Nasr Al-Jawhari. It is considered a book of the traditional Arabic language, and it is classified as strange, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book contains selected materials from Al-Sihah by Al-Jawhari, arranged according to the first words. It also contains an index of contents that makes it easier for the reader to access various topics. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book covers a wide range of topics, including vocabulary and linguistic structures, and also shows that the book contains diverse material, including poetry, stories, and linguistic definitions.
descriptions.2874: Anecdotes by Abu Mishal is a book that deals with the language of the Arabs and their terminology in various areas of their daily lives, covering terms in milking, herding, hunting, trade, and others. The book focuses on presenting anecdotes, sayings, and proverbs from Lisan al-Arab, based on the narration of Abu Mishal al-Arabi and arranged in an objective way that allows understanding the vocabulary of the ancient Arabic language and its connotations.
descriptions.2875: This book deals with the issue of linguistic borrowing in Arabic military vocabulary, reviewing how legal guidance affected the linguistic significance of these borrowed vocabulary. The author focuses on analyzing how words from other languages ​​enter the Arabic linguistic dictionary, whether they are Arabized or foreign, and how they adapt to Arabic phonetic laws. It also sheds light on the historical circumstances that led to the spread of this vocabulary, such as contact with other cultures through trade, wars, and invasions.
descriptions.2876: The Basis of Rhetoric is a book written by Abu al-Qasim Mahmoud bin Amr bin Ahmed, Al-Zamakhshari (deceased: 538 AH). The book is considered one of the most important ancient linguistic dictionaries concerned with Arabic words and their rhetoric. The work mentioned linguistic metaphors, literary features, and expressions of rhetoricians, and arranged the book’s materials in alphabetical order according to the letters of the dictionary. The way the author presents the book is that he explains the word in Arabic, supplementing the explanation with the Qur’an and the Prophet’s hadiths, and with Arabic poetry and proverbs, and then mentions the metaphorical uses of the explained word.
descriptions.2877: This is the book “Anays al-Fuqaha fi Definitions of Frequently Used Words” by the author Qasim bin Abdullah al-Qunawi. It is classified under Gharib, Dictionaries, and the Language of Jurisprudence. The book is considered one of the sources that explains the terminology of jurists in books, and provides definitions of terms used among them. The book contains a content index that shows its organization and arrangement, and deals with topics related to Islamic jurisprudence, such as purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, and marriage. The book begins with definitions of common terms in jurisprudence, then moves on to explaining issues of Islamic jurisprudence. The book shows the author's interest in interpreting and defining the words of jurists, and explaining their meanings and terminology.
descriptions.2878: This is a book on the science of speech triangulation, which is an art that studies Arabic words whose meanings differ depending on their three vowels (fathah, dhammah, and kasra). The author Ibn Malik divided it into two main sections: the first for the triangle with similar meanings, the second for the triangle with different meanings, and the second was arranged into sections according to the first letter of the word. The book aims to collect the fragments of this art and complement what other authors have missed, while explaining its benefits in distinguishing similar meanings and making them accessible to the student.
descriptions.2879: The book “The Agreement of Buildings and the Divergence of Meanings” by Al-Daqiqi deals with a linguistic and jurisprudential field, as it examines the relationships between linguistic and jurisprudential concepts, and reviews the different definitions and uses of terms in the Arabic language, with a focus on the subtle differences between meanings and concepts. The book shows the importance of understanding and controlling the Arabic language in understanding jurisprudential and religious texts, and shows the complexity of the Arabic language and the richness of its vocabulary. The book is considered a valuable resource for those interested in the Arabic language and Islamic jurisprudence, as it provides a comprehensive vision of the relationship between language and jurisprudential concepts.
descriptions.2880: This book deals with the topic of times and naming their parts, talking about the sun, moon, stars, moon phases, and the hours of day and night, mentioning the pre-Islamic times and the names of the months and years. Author Qatrab focuses on addressing the linguistic and jurisprudential elements related to time and the sky, reviewing the opinions of scholars and grammarians in this field.
descriptions.2881: Different words with similar meanings Author: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Malik Al-Tai Al-Jiyani Abu Abdullah Publisher: Dar Al-Jeel - Beirut First Edition, 1411 Edited by: Dr. Muhammad Hassan Awad Number of parts: 1
descriptions.2882: This is the book “Following and Pairing” by the author Ibn Faris. It is classified under the classification of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book provides a catalog of content that covers a range of Arabic letters, with topics such as taqbiyyah and pairing, and also includes examples from the Arabic language and works by poets such as Al-A'sha and Al-Asma'i. The book shows an interest in the study of the Arabic language and its organization, addressing concepts such as obsequiousness and pairing, and indicates that the book provides a comprehensive overview of linguistic usages in the Arabic language.
descriptions.2883: Al-Manawi’s book “Al-Taqeef Ala Mahamat Al-Definitions” deals with the concepts and meanings of strange and lexical words in the language of Islamic jurisprudence. The book divides the letters of the dictionary and explains the meanings of words that begin with each letter, providing a valuable tool for understanding specialized jurisprudential and linguistic terms. The book aims to clarify the meanings of words used in hadiths, fatwas, and jurisprudential books, which contributes to deepening the understanding of legal texts and their linguistic accuracy.
descriptions.2884: The book “Germs” by Ibn Qutaybah Al-Dinauri is a linguistic dictionary specializing in the names of human organs and their innate and moral characteristics, in addition to terms related to the creation of man and his development in the womb. The book falls within the classification of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. It begins with an introduction to the division of worlds and creatures, then deals in detail with the parts of the body from head to foot, mentioning their various epithets and descriptions, citing Arab sayings and poetry.
descriptions.2885: This book is a linguistic dictionary that deals with the letters of the dictionary in detail, as each chapter focuses on a specific letter and explores the meanings of words and strange letters that begin with it. In this book, Abu Amr Al-Shaibani deals with interpretations and explanations of a group of strange words and rare meanings that begin with letters of the alphabet, relying on the Arab linguistic and cultural heritage. The book aims to provide a useful linguistic reference for researchers and intellectuals interested in the Arabic language and its sciences.
descriptions.2886: Elegant Borders and Precise Definitions Author: Zakaria bin Muhammad bin Zakaria Al-Ansari Abu Yahya Publisher: Dar Al-Fikr Al-Mu’asim - Beirut First Edition, 1411 Edited by: Dr. Mazen Al-Mubarak Number of parts: 1
descriptions.2887: The book “Al-Dala’il fi Ghareeb Al-Hadith” by Qasim Al-Sarqusti is a linguistic interpretation of strange and rare terms mentioned in the hadiths of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The book focuses on clarifying the meanings of ambiguous words and rare vocabulary that appear in the Prophet’s hadiths and authentic hadiths, explaining their meanings and explanations in detail. The book deals with various topics from the language of jurisprudence and hadith, and reviews strange terms through the texts of hadiths arranged according to the companions.
descriptions.2888: This book, “Al-Ramouz Ali Al-Sihah,” by Muhammad bin Al-Sayyid Hassan, is considered a jurisprudential and linguistic book that deals with multiple topics in the Arabic language and jurisprudence. The book begins with two chapters, the first dealing with Arabic dictionaries and the pronunciation of the dictionary, while the second chapter deals with linguistic study, as it deals with dialects and their definition, and also deals with topics such as the substitution between soft sounds and spelling. The book shows an interest in the Arabic language and Islamic jurisprudence, and is a useful resource for specialists in these fields.
descriptions.2889: This book, “Al-Zahir fi Ghareeb Al-Falaza Al-Shafi’i,” by the author Al-Azhari, is classified under the classification of strange words, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. This book is considered one of the important sources for understanding and interpreting Al-Shafi’i’s words, as it contains an extensive content index covering multiple topics of Islamic jurisprudence, including purification, intention, ghusl, menstruation, prayer, zakat, fasting, rituals, sales, mortgage, transfer, partnership, anger, and pre-emption. The author begins with an introduction in which he explains the importance of the book and the author’s goal, then moves on to an interpretation of the strange words of Al-Shafi’i, where he uses sources and references to clarify the meanings and data. The book shows the author's interest in the Arabic language and Islamic jurisprudence, and focuses on clarifying and interpreting Al-Shafi'i's words in a clear and useful way.
descriptions.2890: This book, “Al-Zahir fi Meanings of People’s Words” by the scholar Ibn al-Anbari, deals with the interpretation of the meanings of expressions and words common among people in the areas of daily life and worship. The author focuses on clarifying the goals of praises, supplications, and remembrances used in prayer and other Islamic acts of worship, while explaining the meanings of sentences and words used among people in various situations. The book is concerned with studying the Arabic language and its sciences, and provides linguistic and jurisprudential explanations for a group of phrases and words used in the religious and worldly life of Muslims.
descriptions.2891: This is the book “The Weapon” by the author Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam, and it is classified under the category of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book covers multiple weapon-related topics, including swords, spears, spears, shields, and more. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the author focuses on naming and defining various types of weapons, giving names and descriptions. The book is considered a useful source of knowledge about the language of jurisprudence and foreign language, and can be useful to researchers and professionals in this field.
descriptions.2892: The book “Al-Shaa” by Imam Al-Asma’i deals with the science of the strange and linguistic dictionaries through the study of the sheep, its specifications and characteristics. The book focuses on explaining the conditions of the sheep during pregnancy and childbirth, the names of its children, its defects and diseases, and also addresses its physiological and behavioral characteristics. The book aims to provide valuable information in the field of linguistics and Islamic jurisprudence related to the sheep.
descriptions.2893: This book, “Al-Shawarid,” by Al-Saghani, is a linguistic dictionary that deals with irregular and strange words in Qur’anic readings and the sayings of scholars. It focuses on the words that were unique to some language imams and reciters, indicating the uniqueness and anomalies in them, while mentioning the different readings. The book deals with the letters of the alphabet in detail, explaining each letter with irregular words associated with it.
descriptions.2894: Al-Sihah” is an important linguistic book written by Imam Al-Jawhari. It is considered the first correct and easy-to-read Arabic dictionary. The book contains an extensive table of contents covering various branches of the Arabic language, including foreign languages, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book begins with “In the Name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful,” then comes the introduction to Al-Sihah by King Fahd bin Abdulaziz, which is considered a new innovative study in the history of Arabic dictionaries. This is followed by the introduction to the third and second editions, then the author’s introduction, which explains the approach and classification of Al-Sihah. The book contains: Chapter on Alif Mahmuza, which covers the various branches of the Arabic language, including Alif, Ba, Ta, and Tha’. Al-Sihah is an important source for study and research in the Arabic language, and is considered one of the most important books in this field.
descriptions.2895: This is the book “Dozens in Strange Language” written by Ghulam Thalab, and it is classified among the books of strange things, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book collects linguistic terms in the form of chapters. In each chapter, it presents a group of words that share a certain meter or form, and explains their meanings based on accounts by Thalab and other linguists. The book begins with a funny story about the reason for its writing, then goes on to list linguistic chapters such as the chapter on “al-Taris,” the chapter on “al-jinan,” and the chapter on “blood,” explaining the meanings of the different words.
descriptions.2896: Al-Gharib Al-Musannaf or Musannaf Al-Gharib is a topical dictionary written by Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam, in which he lists everything related to the names and descriptions of things and creatures according to subject and meaning, as Abu Ubaid was keen to classify linguistic vocabulary into objective semantic fields, and it is considered the oldest known Arabic topical dictionary. The book was appreciated by ancient linguists to the extent that they wrote explanations and criticisms of it, such as the books “Explanation of the Gharib al-Musannaf” by Ibn Sayyidah al-Andalusi and “The Response to the Gharib al-Musannaf” by Abu Naim al-Isfahani. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaid that he said while talking about his book Al-Gharib Al-Musannaf:
descriptions.2897: This book, “The Excellence in Strange Hadith and Athar” by Al-Zamakhshari, deals with the language and words of the Prophet’s Hadith, explaining what is strange and surprising about it. The book deals with strange words and rare vocabulary in the hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the hadiths of others, and explains their meanings and linguistic implications. The book is divided according to the alphabet, and aims to clarify the precise meanings and specialized vocabulary in the field of hadith and hadith.
descriptions.2898: This book, “The Difference,” by the Islamic scholar Al-Sijistani, is a unique book that deals with the differences between humans and other animals in terms of language and body. The book begins by defining the mouth and its differences in language, then expands on explaining human body parts such as lips, labia, and jaws. The book shows an interest in language and the human body, and reflects artistic and linguistic thought in the field of Arabic language and jurisprudence.
descriptions.2899: Differences in Language, a book on language vocabulary compiled by Abu Hilal Al-Hasan bin Abdullah bin Sahl bin Saeed bin Yahya bin Mahran Al-Askari. It is considered a reference among the dictionaries and references of the Arabic language according to linguists. It contains a lot of linguistic information regarding the meanings of words. He said in the introduction to the book: He devoted it to explaining words that are close in meaning and explaining the many differences between them, such as: the difference between grace and mercy, benevolence and cattle, between forbearance and respite, patience and endurance, dignity and steadfastness. For example: the difference between preservation, care, guarding, and protection. For example: the difference between books and copies, between a publication and a book, and between a book, a notebook, and a newspaper.
descriptions.2900: The surrounding dictionary by the linguist Majd al-Din Abi Tahir Muhammad bin Yaqoub bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Omar al-Shirazi al-Fayrouzabadi, who died in the year (817 AH). The full name of the book is (Al-Qamoos Al-Muheet, Al-Qaboos Al-Wasit, Al-Qamoos Al-Wasit, Al-Qamoos Al-Muhit, Al-Qamoos Al-Wasit, Al-Qamoos Al-Muhit, Al-Qamoos Al-Wasit, Al-Qamoos Al-Qamoos Al-Wasat). It is the most famous dictionary of the Arabic language ever, as its fame was such that many people after it began to use the word dictionary synonymous with the word dictionary.
descriptions.2901: The book, The Dictionary of Jurisprudence in Language and Terminology, by the author Saadi Abu Habib, provides a comprehensive dictionary that deals with jurisprudential terms from a linguistic and terminological perspective. The book aims to link the linguistic meaning of the word to its jurisprudential meaning, showing the lineages between them. It also includes legal and jurisprudential definitions of words, based on Qur’anic verses and noble hadiths to clarify their meanings. Through this work, the author aims to clarify the language of legislation and detail its jurisprudential meanings for readers, explaining how Islam has changed the face of the Arabic language and given it new meanings.
descriptions.2902: This book, “Al-Kulliyat” by the writer Abu Al-Baqa Al-Kafawi, is considered one of the most important terms and linguistic differences in the Arabic language. The book covers multiple topics related to words and linguistic differences, and provides detailed information about these topics. The book seems to be concerned with clarifying the linguistic differences between different words, and providing information about the languages ​​of the Galilean systems. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book is considered one of the most important sources in the Arabic language, and provides rich and in-depth information about the topics it covers.
descriptions.2903: This book, “The Linguistic Treasure in the Arabic Language,” by Ibn al-Sakit, deals with various linguistic topics related to foreign words and dictionaries, with a focus on the rules of inversion and substitution between letters. It contains detailed studies of cases of changing letters in Arabic words, based on narrations and hadiths from various cultural and literary sources. The book aims to provide rich and diverse linguistic material, including explanations of the meanings of words and their applications in poetry and speech.
descriptions.2904: This book, “Al-Latif fi Al-Lughah” by Al-Labbabidi, is considered an important book in the field of the Arabic language and linguistic heritage. The book deals with the topic of synonymy in the Arabic language, as it defines synonymy and explains its causes, addresses the importance of synonymy in the Arabic language, and talks about the reasons for the large number of synonyms in the Arabic language. The book is a valuable resource for researchers in the field of the Arabic language and linguistic heritage.
descriptions.2905: Al-Muhkam and Al-Muhit Al-Azam is an Arabic dictionary written by Ibn Sayyidah, arranged according to phonetic levels.
descriptions.2906: Al-Mukhāsās is a huge book by the son of his master Al-Mursi. One of the treasures of Arabic knowledge, arranged according to its meanings. Ibn Sayyidah included the materials of his dictionary called: (Al-Muhkam). There is only a unique copy of it in the world's libraries, which is the ancient Moroccan copy, which was in the Egyptian princely library, and which Al-Shanqeeti adopted in his edition. (The Princely Press in Egypt, 1901 AD, in five volumes). He said in his appreciation of the book: (The best collection of collections in the Arabic language, and the book most deserving of being sought after by those who want to excel in excellence. Enough of its author is this beautiful deed that time has not permitted and does not permit to be equaled... as he collected in it what the Arabs spoke in every sublime and precise manner......
descriptions.2907: Al-Misbah Al-Munir fi Ghareeb Al-Sharh Al-Kabir, written by Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Ali Al-Fayoumi Al-Muqri, who died 770 AH/1368 AD. In his writing, the writer relied on about 70 works, including: Tahtheeb Al-Azhari Majmal, Ibn Faris, Islah Al-Log, by Ibn Al-Sakit. Diwan al-Adab, by Al-Farabi. Al-Sihah, by Abu Nasr Ismail bin Hammad Al-Jawhari. Eloquent, Grammar Fox. The Basis of Rhetoric, by Al-Zamakhshari.
descriptions.2908: The book “Al-Mut`la’ Ala Al-Muqni’” by Al-Bali Shams Al-Din deals with the interpretation of the words of the book “Al-Muqni” in Hanbali jurisprudence by Ibn Qudamah Al-Maqdisi, explaining their meanings and linguistic and jurisprudential implications. The book covers multiple jurisprudential topics, including purity, prayer, and others, and is distinguished by its precise explanation of the terms al-Muqni’ and its detailing of their meanings, which makes it an important reference for students of knowledge and jurists in the Hanbali school of thought and other schools of thought.
descriptions.2909: This book, “The Intermediate Dictionary,” is a linguistic dictionary that covers a group of Arabic vocabulary. It is considered part of the classification of linguistic dictionaries. It contains a content index divided into parts related to the vowels of the Arabic language, such as Bab al-Hamza, Bab al-Ba, all the way to Bab al-Ya. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book covers topics related to the Arabic language, such as grammar and morphology, and also includes information on Arabic vocabulary, trees, and plants. This book is a useful resource for researchers and thinkers in the field of the Arabic language and Islamic heritage.
descriptions.2910: This book deals with the study of Arabized Arabic words and their classification according to the alphabet, with a focus on their arrangement and correcting them from distortion and corruption. In its various chapters, the author deals with the hamza with the other letters successively, then moves on to study the ba with the letters as well, as part of an attempt to refine and organize jurisprudential terminology to facilitate understanding and use.
descriptions.2911: Al-Nihayah fi Ghareeb al-Hadith wa al-Athar is a book written by Majd al-Din al-Mubarak bin Muhammad bin Abdul Karim al-Shaybani al-Jazari, known as Ibn al-Atheer, to explain the strange words mentioned in hadiths, especially after the non-Arabs entered Islam. In it, he combined two previous books in this field, and added to them.
descriptions.2912: This is the book “The Sufficient and Healing Guidance to Explain the Truths of the Imam” by the author Al-Rassa’, and it is classified under the category of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book contains a comprehensive table of contents that shows the book's topics, which include the explanation of the limits of Ibn Arafa, the Book of Purity, the Book of Prayer, and others. The book begins with an introduction that introduces the author and shows his interest in interpretation and explanation. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows the author's interest in interpretation and explanation, and talks about the importance of explanation in stating facts. The book shows an interest in the Arabic language and Islamic jurisprudence, and points out the importance of explanation in understanding and interpreting religious texts.
descriptions.2913: Taj Al-Arous is one of the jewels of the dictionary, a dictionary in Arabic, by the scholar Al-Murtada Al-Zubaidi, in which he explains the dictionary of “Al-Qamoos Al-Muhit” by Al-Fayrouzabadi. They said in Al-Warraq Library when they presented it to him: “The largest dictionary of the Arabic language, ancient and modern, and it began to be printed in 1965, and volume (21) of it was printed in 1984, and in its introduction is an introduction to what is under printing from it, and all of them (35) volumes, and Mustafa Hijazi edited three volumes of it and participated in six, and the Arab Heritage Revival House in Beirut issued a bulletin of it, and on all There is a constant typographical error in his volumes, which is that the book (verified by Ibrahim al-Tarazi) is not authentic, but only the tenth part of it has been verified, and there is another edition of it with Mustafa’s verification...
descriptions.2914: This book is an edit of the words of Al-Nawawi’s book Al-Tanbih, where the author deals with the language of the book and the control of its words, showing what is objectionable in its words and what is eloquent. He also deals with common words and their meanings, and the linguistic rules related to morphology, singular and group, pointing out the differences between synonyms and explaining what the reader may use in it. The book aims to clarify and refine complex jurisprudential terms to help students and mentors better understand jurisprudential texts.
descriptions.2915: This book, by Al-Safadi, deals with the topic of revisionism and change in linguistic and scientific transmission. It focuses on clarifying the errors that can occur in translating words and phrases, especially when starting with the letter hamza along with other letters. The author mentions examples of corrections that occurred even by prominent scholars, indicating the importance of investigating and scrutinizing transmission to avoid such errors. The book falls into the categories of foreign language, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence, which indicates his interest in the grammar of the Arabic language and its scientific applications.
descriptions.2916: The book “Correction of Lisan al-Arab” by Ahmed Taymur Pasha is a linguistic work that falls under the classification of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. It specializes in alerting readers to the errors that occurred in the printed version of the “Lisan al-Arab” dictionary by Ibn Manzur. The author collected his notes that he had previously published in newspapers and magazines, and added to them what he had not published before, intending to restore the book to authenticity without claiming infallibility. The book includes warnings about errors in the printed version, along with correction of misconceptions that occurred in the author’s introduction and translation, such as an error in the date of his birth and death, and a statement that his dictionary is based on five sources, not six.
descriptions.2917: This book is an explanation of the strange and thorny vocabulary contained in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, where the author, Ibn Abi Nasr al-Humaydi, deals with the vocabulary of the Musnad one after the other, explaining what is strange in the hadiths of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The book aims to clarify the ambiguous meanings and rare vocabulary that the reader may encounter while studying the two Sahihs, which helps him understand the texts in a deeper and more accurate way.
descriptions.2918: “Tahdheeb al-Lughah” is a book written by Al-Azhari, and it is considered one of the most important books in the field of the Arabic language and the language of jurisprudence. The book is concerned with refining and defining the Arabic language, specifically in the field of jurisprudence and language. The book contains an extensive table of contents that covers various sections of the Arabic language, including words, vocabulary, and morphemes. The book begins by defining the author himself and explaining the reasons for writing the book, and then moves on to identifying the imams of the language whom he relied upon in writing the book. “Tahdheeb al-Lughah” is an important source for learning The study is in the field of the Arabic language and the jurisprudential language, and it is considered one of the most important books in this field.
descriptions.2919: The book Al-Jumhara on Language was written by Abu Bakr bin Duraid, who died in the year 321 AH, who was the chief linguist of his time, and whose students included Abu Ali Al-Qali, Ibn Khalawayh, and Abu Faraj Al-Isfahani. Al-Azhari stated that he only mentioned words in his dictionary that were correct to hear, so he called it Tahdheeb al-Lughah. Ibn Duraid said in the introduction to his book, explaining the reason for calling it Al-Jumahrah, “And we loaned it this name because we chose for it the common ones from the speech of the Arabs and we postponed it to be brutal and reprehensible.” Ibn Duraid mentioned in his dictionary the common pronunciation and not the strange, rare one, as Ibn Duraid devoted separate sections to the rare expressions at the end of Al-Jumahrah, as his purpose was very similar. What is the essential purpose of purifying the language of impurities and excluding some of its words? …
descriptions.2920: This book is a linguistic dictionary that deals with Arabic words that begin with the letter T. It combines the terms of jurisprudence and language and explains their meanings and terminology, introducing some strange words and synonyms. The author focuses on analyzing words letter by letter, starting from the hamza to the yaa, with a special focus on the letter thaa, which contains twenty words. The book takes a systematic approach to presenting words, referring to the sources from which the author quotes word definitions.
descriptions.2921: The best speech in investigating the mistakes of the common people Author: Ali bin Bali Al-Qastanini Publisher: Al-Resala Foundation - Beirut Second Edition, 1983 Edited by: Dr. Hatem Saleh Al-Damen Number of parts: 1
descriptions.2922: Dastur al-Ulama or Jami’ al-Ulum fi Terminology of the Arts is a book by Abd Rab al-Nabi ibn Abd Rab al-Rasul al-Ahmad Nakri on definitions divided into four parts, dealing with jurisprudence, language, literature, poetry, medicine, pharmacy, history, principles, Sunnah, anecdote, story, astronomy, space, stars, philosophy, and horoscopes.
descriptions.2923: This is the book “Students of Students” by Al-Nasafi author, Abu Hafs, and is classified under the category of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book is considered one of the important sources in the field of Islamic jurisprudence, as it contains a collection of books that cover various aspects of Islamic life, from purity to zakat, fasting, rituals, marriage, breastfeeding, divorce, real estate, loyalty, oaths, limits, theft, conduct, approval, investigation, capture, retention, lost, usurpation, deposit, nakedness, partnership, hunting, sacrifices, and sacrifices. The book begins with an introduction that explains the importance of jurisprudential terminology, then moves to the Book of Purity, where it explains the concept of purity and its controls. The book shows the author's interest in interpretation and explanation, as he explains the verses of the Holy Quran and the prophetic traditions in relation to Islamic jurisprudence. This book is an important resource for jurists and commentators, as it contains detailed information on various aspects of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2924: The book “Gharib al-Hadith” by Ibn al-Jawzi is a work of linguistics and the meanings of the words of the Prophet’s Hadith. It falls under the category of strange words, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The author aims to explain the strange and mysterious words that occurred in the words of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, which became unknown to many people due to the mixing of Arabs with foreigners and the spread of melody. Ibn al-Jawzi built his book on the method of arranging words alphabetically according to letters, beginning with the book Alif and then Ba, relying in his introduction on an explanation of people’s need for this knowledge, and pointing to the efforts of the scholars who preceded him in this field, such as Abu Ubaid al-Qasim bin Salam, al-Khattabi, and Ibn Qutaybah.
descriptions.2925: This book, “The Error of Weak Jurists,” by Ibn Bari, is considered one of the books that dealt with the subject of linguistic error in Islamic jurisprudence. The book shows that the author has combined grammar and jurisprudence, as he explains the linguistic errors committed by some jurists, and provides definitions and data to clarify what is correct. The book seems to aim to teach jurists and improve their linguistic skills, making it a useful book for researchers and investigators in the field of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2926: This is a linguistic book that falls under the classification of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. Its author, Al-Kawkabani, wrote it as an introduction to Al-Qamoos Al-Muhit by Al-Fayrouzabadi, in which he explains the morphological and linguistic conventions that the reader needs in the dictionary and other language books. The book is organized into an introduction, two objectives, and a conclusion. The introduction deals with the basis of the dictionary, the translation of its author, and the history of the emergence and development of the Arabic language, while the objectives address morphological topics such as the weights of nouns, infinitives, and derivatives.
descriptions.2927: This is a book on the science of Arabization, and it is a footnote by Ibn Bari to Al-Jawaliqi’s book “What Arabs Arabized of Non-Arab Speech.” The book examines foreign words that entered the Arabic language, and how the Arabs dealt with them through Arabization and substitution of letters. The author mentions which letters are prohibited to be replaced in extraneous words and which are not, citing examples from the Holy Qur’an and the speech of the Arabs.
descriptions.2928: This book, written by Ibn al-Qattaa al-Siqilli, is considered one of the important books in the field of foreign words, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book includes a study of the linguistic uses of the verb in the Arabic language, with a focus on threefold, fourfold, doubled, and doubled verbs. The book shows a high quality of charity, although there is no precise arrangement or statement. The Book of Verses is an important resource for learning the Arabic language, especially for learning their true meanings, and it can help in understanding the Holy Quran and Arabic poetry.
descriptions.2929: The Book of Definitions by Al-Jurjani (d. 816 AH) is a dictionary that includes defining the meanings of terms used in science, philosophy, logic, language, arts, and jurisprudence during his era.
