It is one of the first dictionaries to have an alphabetical order. In the manner of a glossary. Its owner is Al-Jurjani Ali bin Muhammad bin Ali Al-Sharif Al-Husseini, known as Sayyid Mir Sharif, who is an astronomer, jurist, musician, philosopher, and linguist.
descriptions.2930: The Al-Ain dictionary is the first coordinated dictionary of the Arabic language. It was written by Al-Khalil bin Ahmed Al-Farahidi and completed and arranged by Al-Layth bin Al-Muzaffar Al-Laithi Al-Kanani. Its arrangement is based on the origins of the letters from the deepest point in the throat, through the movements of the tongue, to the tips of the lips. Thus, its first letter is Al-Ain and the last is the meem, then they are followed by the subterranean vowels (w, y, a).
descriptions.2931: This is the book “Jamal Al-Gharaib” by Al-Naysaburi, which is an important book in the science of modern Gharib, and is considered one of the most important works in this art. The author is Muhammad Ajmal Al-Islahi, and the book deals with the subject of strange hadith science, and it is considered one of the most important sciences that arose to serve the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ. This book is one of the works that originated in the second century AH at the hands of linguists, and was then undertaken by scholars who, in addition to their mastery of the language, were involved in the science of hadith and jurisprudence. The book “Jamal al-Gharaib” by Bayan al-Haqq Mahmoud bin Abi al-Hasan bin al-Hussein al-Naysaburi is considered one of the most important works in the science of strange hadiths, as the author derived his material from many sources that he stated in his introduction, including the books of the early scholars that were lost in the lost heritage of Islam. This book is considered one of the most important works in modern Gharib science, as it is considered one of the most important works in this art.
descriptions.2932: The book “Kifayat al-Mutahzaf wa Nihayat al-Mutalafiq” by Ibn al-Ajdabi is a linguistic dictionary specialized in Arabic words, collecting the language’s vocabulary according to an objective classification. The book is organized into chapters and sections covering the characteristics of men and women, the names of husbands and women’s adornments, the life stages of humans, camels and horses, parts of swords and spears, types of wild animals, plants, flowers, milk, and other topics. Through it, the author aims to provide the reader with the vocabulary of the classical Arabic language in various fields, while briefly explaining its meanings, making it a useful reference in the study of foreign language and the language of jurisprudence.
descriptions.2933: Lisan al-Arab is an Arabic linguistic dictionary compiled by Ibn Manzur al-Ansari (d. 711 AH). Al-Zirakli said in describing the dictionary that its author “collected in it the most important books of the language, so he almost dispensed with them all.” Al-Baalbaki said: It is considered the most famous Arabic dictionary without dispute, due to the vastness of its material, and because it includes a large group of authentic evidence that it derived from the Holy Qur’an, the noble Prophet’s hadith, and Arab proverbs and poetry. Ibn Manzur finished writing it in the year 690 AH.
descriptions.2934: This book, “What came on I did and I did in one sense,” by the author Ibn al-Jawaliqi, is considered within the classification of strangers, dictionaries, and the language of jurisprudence. The book contains a table of contents that shows a careful organization of the first part of the book, which covers topics related to the verb and the present tense, with concepts such as ba, ta, tha, and ji. The book begins with an introduction to the author, then moves on to address the topics of verbs and the present tense, with directions for using vocabulary in different contexts. The book shows an interest in the Arabic language and Islamic jurisprudence, while addressing concepts related to the verb and the present tense in different contexts.
descriptions.2935: This is the book “Majmal al-Lughah” by Ibn Faris, which is a linguistic book that is considered one of the most important sources in Arabic linguistics. The book is concerned with collecting and analyzing Arabic words, and includes a content index that shows the organization of the book around Arabic letters. The book begins with the author introducing the importance of the Arabic language and the necessity of collecting words in one book that makes it easier for the reader to access the meanings. The excerpt presented from the book shows that the author relied on the book “Al-Ain” by Khalil bin Ahmed and the book “Al-Jumhara” by Abu Bakr bin Duraid, but he sought succinctness in speech and easy access to meanings. This book is an important source for Arabic linguistic studies.
descriptions.2936: Mukhtar al-Sihah was written by Muhammad bin Abi Bakr bin Abdul Qadir al-Razi. He had shortened it from Taj al-Lughah and Sihah al-Arabiya, leaving the arrangement of its entries according to the traditional order, that is, starting with the letters of the last words. Mukhtar Al-Sahhah's dictionary was distinguished by its frequent reference to weak, bad, and Arabized words, mentioning rare words and opposites, and its attention to aspects of morphology such as derivation, substitution, and causation. Mukhtar Al-Sahhah’s dictionary was first published in two volumes by the Egyptian Boulaq Press in 1865, and the second edition was published in 1957, edited by Ahmed Abdel Ghafour Attar. …
descriptions.2937: The book “Mashariq Al-Anwar Ala Sihah Al-Athar” by Judge Ayyad is a linguistic dictionary specialized in explaining the strange words of the Prophet’s hadith contained in the books of Sihah. It is concerned with controlling the words, clarifying their meanings, and correcting any illusions or distortions that may occur in the narrations. The book is organized according to the letters of the dictionary, and deals with strange and problematic words in the hadiths, with special chapters included to point out areas of disagreement and illusion among the narrators.
descriptions.2938: Differences in Language, a book on language vocabulary compiled by Abu Hilal Al-Hasan bin Abdullah bin Sahl bin Saeed bin Yahya bin Mahran Al-Askari. It is considered a reference among the dictionaries and references of the Arabic language according to linguists. It contains a lot of linguistic information regarding the meanings of words. He said in the introduction to the book: He devoted it to explaining words that are close in meaning and explaining the many differences between them, such as: the difference between grace and mercy, benevolence and cattle, between forbearance and respite, patience and endurance, dignity and steadfastness. For example: the difference between preservation, care, guarding, and protection. For example: the difference between books and copies, between a publication and a book, and between a book, a notebook, and a newspaper.
descriptions.2939: Diwan al-Adab by Abu Ibrahim Ishaq bin Ibrahim al-Farabi (died: 350 AH). It is considered one of the first linguistic dictionaries created by its author for writers. This linguistic dictionary is one of the dictionaries written by non-specialists. It did not gain as much fame as it was written by others, and it is the first Arabic dictionary arranged according to structure.
descriptions.2940: This is a dictionary of the language of jurists, in which author Muhammad Qalaji collected the terms of jurisprudence through a journey that lasted more than twenty-five years. This dictionary is intended for Arab researchers and advocates, as it combines Arabic and English terms. The author aims to define jurisprudential terms and determine their linguistic origins, then prove their linguistic definition, then prove their equivalent in the English language. This dictionary is a first step in defining Islamic jurisprudence in comparative legal studies, and contributes to restoring the bygone glory of the Islamic nation.
descriptions.2941: The book “Dictionary of the Reins of Science in Borders and Drawings” by Al-Suyuti is a comprehensive terminological dictionary that aims to introduce the reader to the terms used in various sciences and arts, explaining the subtle differences between their meanings according to each group of scholars. The book is organized into twenty-one chapters, covering various fields, including interpretation, hadith, jurisprudence and its origins, theology and dialectics, and Arabic language sciences such as grammar, morphology, rhetoric, and prosody, in addition to logic, wisdom, form, geometry, arithmetic, music, astrology, medicine, ethics, and mysticism.
descriptions.2942: Keys to Science is an encyclopedic book written by the Muslim scholar Muhammad bin Ahmed Al-Khwarizmi, in which he provided an answer to many of the outstanding questions among the Arabs, especially regarding the term during the ninth century AD. The book mentioned in its introduction two articles: one on the sciences of Sharia and the Arabic sciences associated with it, and the second on the sciences of the Persians and other nations that preceded it.
descriptions.2943: This is a research book that studies the approach of Imam Majd al-Din Ibn al-Atheer in his book “Al-Nihayah fi Ghareeb al-Hadith wal-Athar.” It is divided into five sections that deal with the movement of writing in Ghareeb al-Hadith, introducing Ibn al-Atheer, analyzing his approach in his book, and explaining the importance of “Al-Nihayah,” while mentioning some of the criticisms against it. The research aims to highlight the position of this work in serving the Prophet’s Hadith by explaining its strange words, within a scientific framework that clarifies the features of the author’s approach and aspects of his care for the strange.
descriptions.2944: This book, “The Encyclopedia of Birds and Animals in the Prophetic Hadith,” by Abdul Latif Ashour, is considered a comprehensive encyclopedia in the field of animals and birds in Islam, as it combines language, nature, and noble hadiths. The book begins with an analysis of the hadiths related to animals, then moves on to studying each animal separately, from the camel, the rabbit, the wild animal, and the lion, and discusses their natures and characteristics, while directing attention to the noble hadiths related to them. The book highlights the importance of kindness to animals and compassion for them, and indicates that Islam preceded modern science in studying animals and directing attention to their observation. The book is considered an important source for researchers and students in the field of animals and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2945: This book, “Economic Fatwas,” brings together a group of decisions and fatwas issued by the Islamic Fiqh Academy in the field of economics and zakat. The book covers various topics such as zakat on debts, zakat on real estate and leased lands, and insurance and reinsurance. It appears from the contents of the book that the Fiqh Academy has considered various aspects of Islamic economics, and has established controls and fatwas to regulate these areas. The book is a useful resource on economic issues and zakat in Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2946: This book is an archive copy of the content of the Arabic section of the “Islam Question and Answer” website under the supervision of Sheikh Muhammad Saleh Al-Munajjid. It includes a huge collection of automatically numbered legal fatwas, in addition to books and articles. The website aims to provide authentic scientific answers to questions related to Islam in its various aspects, relying on the approach of the Sunnis and the community, evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah, and the words of scholars. The book deals with various topics, including faith, worship, transactions, and intellectual and social issues, while avoiding engaging in sterile controversy.
descriptions.2947: This book, “Letters and Fatwas of Abdul Aziz Al Sheikh,” by author Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al Sheikh, is classified under the category of automatically numbered fatwas. The book contains a collection of letters and fatwas presented by the author, covering various topics such as education, worship, Sharia laws, and social issues. The book begins with an introduction to the author and an explanation of some useful methods for teaching, such as giving proverbs and stories, having students initiate questions, and students taking the initiative to do what raises their questions. The book shows the author's interest in providing advice and reminders to benefit from in education in a way that pleases God Almighty.
descriptions.2948: This book, “Fatwas of Sheikh Ibn Jibreen,” is a collection of fatwas written by Sheikh Ibn Jibreen in the field of Islamic jurisprudence. The book covers a wide range of topics, including wiping over the socks, the principles of jurisprudence, the call to prayer, etiquette, foods, oaths and vows, selling, interpretation, Hajj, punishments, breastfeeding, testimonies, prayer, fasting, divorce, purity, number, belief, religious duties, dress and adornment, the disabled and the senseless, expenses, marriage, Ramadan fatwas, and evidence on the obligation of Zakat, the money on which zakat is due, offering and delaying zakat, the ruling on denying the obligation of zakat and the ruling on preventing it out of stinginess or ingratitude, the wisdom of legislating zakat, and the zakat on crops and fruits that come out of the land. The book is an important source of Islamic fatwas, and reflects Sheikh Ibn Jibreen's interest in jurisprudence and fatwas.
descriptions.2949: This book is an archive of the fatwas posted on Sheikh Hussam al-Din Afana’s website until October 2010, and it contains his responses to multiple questions in various legal fields. Fatwas address topics related to faith, hadiths, demonstrations, dealing with jinn, Shiites, mockery of prayer, and many other issues that concern Muslims in their daily lives. The book is automatically numbered and aims to spread Islamic jurisprudence and understanding among Muslims via the Internet.
descriptions.2950: This book, “Fatwas Noor Ala al-Darb” by author Ibn Uthaymeen, is classified within the category of automatic numbered fatwas. The book is considered one of the main sources in the field of Islamic belief, as it covers multiple topics such as monotheism, Islamic belief, faith and Islam, worship, and divine monotheism. The book contains a detailed content index that shows the variety of topics covered. The book seems to aim to provide comprehensive and clear answers to questions related to the Islamic religion, making it a useful resource for Muslims and Muslims.
descriptions.2951: This book contains fatwas and advice from the Islam Today website, classified according to jurisprudential classification. It deals with various topics from the Holy Qur’an and its sciences, dealing with verses that have caused problems for commentators and questioners, and also includes fatwas on various legal rulings. The book is distinguished by its exegetical and jurisprudential style, as it combines the interpretation of Qur’anic texts and an explanation of the provisions of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.2952: This book of Sheikh Ibn Baz’s fatwas deals with legal and political topics from a legal perspective, focusing on the prohibition of hijacking aircraft and the necessity of resorting to the Qur’an and Sunnah in solving security and political problems. The author stresses the necessity of rejecting man-made laws and the arbitration of Islamic Sharia in all cases, considering that ruling by any system that contradicts Sharia is the rule of ignorance. The book calls for efforts to prevent global crimes and protect lives and nations through adherence to Islamic law and its arbitration in all cases.
descriptions.2953: Al-Hawi li-Fatawa is one of the books of jurisprudence written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911). It is also considered one of the books of Shafi’i jurisprudence that discusses jurisprudential fatwas, issues and rulings, as the author mentioned his fatwas in all of the issues presented to him. The book included benefits in the sciences of jurisprudence, interpretation, hadith, grammar, parsing, and other arts. Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti says, explaining the reason for writing his book containing fatwas:
descriptions.2954: This book, “Pearls of Sunnah in Najdi Answers,” is a collection of authors, and is classified within the category of fatwas. It contains a table of contents that includes four volumes, covering various topics, including beliefs, monotheism, names, attributes, and acts of worship. The book begins with an introduction and notes by Najd scholars, emphasizing the importance of this collection and the effort the author made in collecting these letters and answers. This book is an important source for scholars and thinkers in the field of fatwas and the Islamic religion.
descriptions.2955: This book is “Al-Aqwad Al-Durriyya fi Taqnih Al-Fatawa Al-Hamidiyyah” by Ibn Abidin, and it is a collection of fatwas related to matters of religion and Islamic law, distributed into multiple sections that deal with elements of a Muslim’s daily life and the obligatory and voluntary prayers, with a focus on the jurisprudential rules and etiquette related to performing fatwas.
descriptions.2956: This book, “Hadith Fatwas” by Ibn Hajar Al-Haytami, is classified within the category of fatwas. The book is a collection of hadith fatwas that address various issues, and includes an index of contents. The book begins with the author introducing and thanking God, then moves on to address various issues, including reciting {Say: He is God, One} one hundred times, its reward, and its effects in Islam. The book shows the author's interest in the Prophet's hadith and jurisprudential fatwas, and includes sayings and hadiths from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.2957: This book presents various fatwas on financial transactions related to the buying and selling of gold, with a focus on the ruling on usury and its prohibition in financial transactions. The author, Ibn Uthaymeen, addresses a set of frequently asked questions about these transactions and provides legal answers to them, based on Qur’anic and Hadith texts and the sayings of scholars. The book aims to clarify the jurisprudential rulings related to gold and precious metals and explain what financial transactions are permissible and what are not permissible.
descriptions.2958: This book, “The Great Jurisprudential Fatwas” by Ibn Hajar Al-Haytami, is considered one of the most important jurisprudential sources in Islam. The book covers a wide range of jurisprudential topics, including purity, prayer, fasting, Hajj, and commandments. The book shows the author's mastery in the field of Islamic jurisprudence, and reflects his wide influence in the field of jurisprudence and fatwas. The book is considered a valuable resource for scholars and commentators, and contributes to the understanding and application of Islamic law.
descriptions.2959: This book deals with fatwas in the field of Islamic jurisprudence, focusing on the rules and rulings related to purity and impurity. The book is divided into sections detailing the obligations and Sunnahs of ablution, washing, and tayammum, based on the prevailing schools of jurisprudence at the time. It aims to provide clear and accessible fatwas to jurists and muftis, with a focus on clarifying correct practices and avoiding heresies and whims in understanding and application.
descriptions.2960: This book, “The Prohibition of Spreading Spread on Earth” by author Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al Sheikh, is classified within the category of fatwas. The book contains the fatwa of His Eminence Sheikh Imam Abdul Aziz bin Baz (may Allah have mercy on him) about the bombing incident in Mecca in 1409 AH, in addition to the decisions of the Council of Senior Scholars about the bombing incidents in Riyadh and Al-Khobar. The book focuses on the prohibition of corruption on earth and considers bombing in Mecca a great crime and a heinous abomination, and warns against violating the sanctity of the Sacred Land. The book aims to clarify the Islamic prohibition of spreading corruption on earth and the necessity of respecting the sanctity of the Sacred Land.
descriptions.2961: The book Letters and Fatwas of Sheikh Hamad bin Nasser Al Muammar contains in-depth jurisprudential discussions on issues of ijtihad and imitation. It focuses on the obligation of obedience to God and His Messenger, and discusses whether beginners are required to know the evidence in every issue, or can rely on imitating scholars. The book also addresses the ruling on imitating the four imams, and reviews their opinions on this subject, noting that these imams have forbidden imitating them in everything they say.
descriptions.2962: This book, “Messages and Fatwas of Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Hassan bin Muhammad Abdul Wahhab,” is a collection of letters and fatwas written by Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Hassan Al Sheikh. The book deals with various religious and legal topics, including obedience and disobedience, faith and polytheism, imamate and teaching, and the meaning of there is no god but God and its conditions. The book shows Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Hassan’s interest in reminding people of religion and advising him regarding goodness and blessings, and reflects an in-depth religious thought in understanding legal texts and dealing with religious matters.
descriptions.2963: The book “Messages and Fatwas of Allama Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Aba Butin” includes a group of letters and fatwas dealing with various jurisprudential and doctrinal topics, including the doctrine of the Sunnis regarding the word of God Almighty, the ruling on some financial transactions, and fatwas regarding fasting on the Day of Doubt, selling mortgages, and conditions for peace. The author focuses on clarifying the different schools of jurisprudence and explaining the doctrine of the Sunnis and the community on disputed issues, relying on the Qur’an and Sunnah to prove his opinions.
descriptions.2964: This book is a collection of jurisprudential treatises by Sheikh Hamad bin Nasser Al Muammar, dealing with various issues in jurisprudence and fatwas, most notably the rulings on divorce and its suspension, conditions in the marriage contract, issues in the sacrifice and will, acts of worship, and other branches of jurisprudence. The author presents the opinions of scholars on these issues with reasoning and weighting, which makes him a reference in the jurisprudential issues at hand.
descriptions.2965: The book “The Eyes of Messages and Answers to Issues” by Abdul Latif Al Sheikh is a work in the section on fatwas, and it is presented in two main sections: The first is a study of the author's era and life, and the second is a study of the book itself. The first section deals with details of the author’s life, including his lineage, upbringing, elders, and works, while the second section is devoted to introducing the book and studying the author’s approach and sources. The book aims to provide a rigorous scientific study of the author’s jurisprudential messages and answers.
descriptions.2966: A book that collects the fatwas of Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen on the pillars of Islam, and begins with the fatwas of the creed that address the definition of monotheism and its types, issues of faith, the names and attributes of God, ruqyah and amulets, and other doctrinal topics. These fatwas were collected and selected from the collection of his fatwas based on the desire of some brothers to publish them in Arabic and translate them, relying on the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of scholars.
descriptions.2967: The book “Islamic Fatwas” includes fatwas and answers to various questions in various sections of Islamic jurisprudence and doctrine, presented by prominent scholars such as Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz, Sheikh Muhammad bin Uthaymeen, and Sheikh Abdullah bin Jibreen. The book addresses topics related to worship, transactions, ethics, and doctrine, with a focus on clarification and guidance in complex legal issues. The fatwas were collected and arranged by Muhammad bin Abdulaziz Al-Musnad, and the book aims to provide a correct and documented legal fatwa to Muslims in various parts of the world.
descriptions.2968: Fatwas al-Ramli by Imam Jurist Shihab al-Din Ahmad bin Hamza al-Ansari al-Ramli al-Shafi’i (d. 957 AH) is a collection of fatwas compiled by his son Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Abi al-Abbas Ahmad bin Hamza Shihab al-Din al-Ramli (d. 1004 AH). It is considered one of the most important books of jurisprudence in the Shafi’i school of thought and one of the most important books of general fatwas.
descriptions.2969: The book “Fatawa al-Subki” includes legal fatwas and answers written by Imam Taqi al-Din al-Subki, one of the prominent scholars of the Ottoman era, and covers multiple areas of jurisprudence, doctrine, and interpretation. The book deals with the interpretation of various Qur’anic verses and answers various questions related to Islamic law, providing a deep and comprehensive jurisprudential vision.
descriptions.2970: A book that collects fatwas related to the provisions of purity and prayer for the sick, based on the texts of Sharia. It is organized into detailed sections that begin with issues of tayammum for a patient and how to perform it, then move on to the provisions of ablution and washing in cases of disability or the presence of wounds and medical devices, all the way to issues of examining patients and dissecting corpses. The book aims to facilitate worship for the sick in accordance with Sharia controls, in response to people's need to know the provisions of their religion in cases of necessity.
descriptions.2971: “Fatwas of the Permanent Committee - First Group” is a book that deals with topics of the Islamic faith, and includes a group of fatwas issued by the Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwa. The book covers topics such as the unification of divinity, divinity, and names and attributes, and deals with the three types of monotheism: monotheism of divinity, monotheism of divinity, and unification of names and attributes. The book contains excerpts from the beginning of the book, and includes topics such as unification of divinity, unification of divinity, and unification of names and attributes, and it also deals with topics such as Creation, livelihood, revival, death, worship, monotheism, management and management. The book is considered an important source of Islamic fatwas, and deals with important topics in the Islamic faith.
descriptions.2972: This book, “Fatwas of the Permanent Committee - Second Group,” is a collection of important and fundamental fatwas that dealt with various topics of belief, jurisprudence, and monotheism, and was collected from questions and letters sent to the Fatwa House in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The book contains an introduction by the Grand Mufti of the Kingdom, followed by a group of various fatwas, covering topics such as the unification of divinity, the unification of worship, and what is meant by the principles of religion. They were prepared by the Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwa. This book is an important source for scholars and researchers in the field of faith and jurisprudence, and it contributes to providing answers to people’s questions and fulfilling their scientific needs.
descriptions.2973: This book deals with fatwas related to the rulings of Hajj, Umrah, and visiting, where Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz answers multiple questions about these acts of worship, explaining the legal rulings related to them and explaining some common practices. The book focuses on providing clear jurisprudential guidance to help Muslims perform their rituals correctly, with an emphasis on general jurisprudential rules and their practical applications.
descriptions.2974: This book deals with legal fatwas addressed to health professionals, doctors, and nurses, related to their practical issues in hospitals. It focuses on various issues such as the rulings on prayer for the patient and the doctor, controls on dealing between the sexes in a health work environment, and other fatwas related to various medical conditions and religious sermons. The book is written by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz and aims to provide practical legal guidance to users of health services.
descriptions.2975: A book that collects the fatwas of the scholar Ibn Baz on the issues of Hajj and Umrah, and answers various questions that begin with an explanation of the three rituals (alone, tamattu, and qiran) and how to practice them and which are best. Then, it deals with the rulings on timings and ihram and what is necessary to bypass it, the prescription of ihram for men and women, the issues of tawaf, sa’i, and standing at Arafat, Muzdalifah, and Mina, the rulings on sacrificing, ransom, and exiting ihram, and other things that the Hajj and Umrah pilgrim needs.
descriptions.2976: This book deals with the fatwas and messages of Sheikh Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Sheikh, the Grand Mufti of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Chief Justice. The book focuses on the areas of jurisprudence and doctrine, as the first part includes fatwas on Islamic beliefs, while the second part deals with the principles of jurisprudence and issues of purity and prayer. The book aims to provide legal answers to various issues facing Muslims, based on the knowledge and understanding of the Sheikh in religious and jurisprudential affairs.
descriptions.2977: This book, “Fatwas and Issues,” written by Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, is considered part of his works, and is classified within the category of fatwas. The book contains a group of questions answered by Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and it deals with topics related to good deeds and intentions, and is divided into different types, such as the good deeds that people do seeking the face of God, the good deeds that people do seeking people’s hypocrisy, and the good deeds that people do seeking money. This book is considered one of the important sources in understanding the thought of Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab and his views on good deeds and intention.
descriptions.2978: This book, “Fath al-Ali al-Malik fi al-Fatwa on the Doctrine of Imam Malik,” is a collection of fatwas on various sections of Islamic doctrine and jurisprudence, in which the author confined himself to the Maliki doctrine. The book deals with various topics of the Islamic faith and issues of jurisprudence, and aims to clarify the legal rulings according to the Maliki school of thought, while presenting various fundamental and jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.2979: This is the book “The Collection of Fatwas of Allama Abdul-Aziz Ibn Baz (may Allah have mercy on him)”, which is a collection of fatwas, letters and lectures by Allama Abdul-Aziz Ibn Baz, covering various topics in doctrine, jurisprudence, monotheism, polytheism, worship, seeking help, and celebrating the Prophet’s birthday. The book contains an introduction and an introduction that explains the importance of compiling the fatwas of Allama Ibn Baz, and an introduction to the life, knowledge, and scientific work of Allama Ibn Baz. The book begins with a discussion of the correct doctrine and what opposes it, then addresses topics such as monotheism and its types, polytheism and its types, the worship for which the heavy ones were created, and the necessity of ruling on God’s law and rejecting what contradicts it. The book also contains messages and fatwas dealing with topics such as seeking help from jinn and devils, celebrating the Prophet’s birthdays, and worshiping heretical and polytheistic rituals.
descriptions.2980: The Collection of Fatwas by His Eminence Sheikh Saleh Al-Fawzan presents fatwas in multiple areas of the Islamic faith, including monotheism, disbelief, and polytheism, and also discusses practices such as supplication, astrology, and magic, with a focus on nullifying deviant and heretical practices. The book also addresses issues such as immigration to Islamic countries and its place in religion, and falls within the classification of fatwas that aim to clarify legal positions on religious and social issues.
descriptions.2981: This is the book “The Collection of Fatwas and Messages of His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen”, which is a collection of fatwas and messages collected by the author from the fatwas of Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen, one of the sincere scholars of the twentieth century. The book contains a group of topics related to doctrine, monotheism, faith, Islam, worship, divinity, and the Shahada, and also addresses some jurisprudential and methodological issues. The book is an important resource for scholars and believers seeking an accurate understanding of the Islamic religion.
descriptions.2982: The collection of Najdi letters and issues consists of letters and fatwas by prominent Najd scholars, and includes guidance and answers on various jurisprudential and scientific issues that were posed to them. This collection shows the efforts made by Najdi Dawa scholars to spread the Salafist doctrine and Islamic law, and refute the suspicions promoted by the enemies of the Sunnah. It also highlights the importance that student students attach to documenting their writings and sciences, with the aim of preserving rare scientific benefits and making them available to researchers in the future.
descriptions.2983: This fourth part of the “Collection of Najdi Messages and Issues” includes a collection of letters and fatwas by Najd scholars, and is classified as books of fatwas. The book deals with doctrinal and jurisprudential issues, and its introduction highlights the discussion of the issue of supplication to other than God and the response to those who claim that disbelief is not attributed to the one who does it, detailing the types of supplication and the ruling on each type. It also includes messages in response to the graves, the purification of self and attributes, issues in monotheism, covenant, and security, and various fatwas on reading and responding to opponents.
descriptions.2984: This is a book that collects a number of letters and jurisprudential and doctrinal issues by Abdul Latif Al Sheikh, and is classified under the Fatwa section. The letters deal with various topics, most notably the issues of takfir and denunciation of those who declare Muslims to be unbelievers in ways other than what the jurists have agreed upon, the ruling on traveling to the lands of the polytheists, emigration and residence among them, in addition to the issues of temptations, the community, the commandment to adhere to the Qur’an and the Sunnah, and responding to some dissenting letters and articles.
descriptions.2985: This book is a collection of letters, issues, and fatwas by Muhammad bin Nasser Al Muammar, one of the scholars of the thirteenth century AH. The book deals with various jurisprudential and doctrinal topics, including responding to those who do not rule according to the Sunnah and the Qur’an, research into the imitation of the four imams, and fatwas on various jurisprudential issues. The book aims to provide a pure source of knowledge for those interested in Islamic heritage and Sharia sciences.
descriptions.2986: This book is “A Collection of Letters and Fatwas on Important Issues that Touch the Need of the Age.” It is a book of fatwas that combines letters and fatwas from various authors, covering a group of important issues that touch the need of the era. The book begins with a message about following and prohibiting extremism in religion, where the authors explain the importance of sincerity in worshiping God and following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The book deals with the concept of temptation and trial, defines sincerity and follow-up, and stresses the importance of working for God and following the apostolic command. The book is considered an important source of fatwas and messages on important issues that affect the needs of the times, and is considered a valuable source for learning and benefiting.
descriptions.2987: This book contains fatwas and jurisprudential and fundamental issues related to Islamic jurisprudence and monotheism, as Sheikh Abdul Rahman bin Hassan Al Sheikh addresses various topics related to worship, transactions, and doctrine, with a focus on responding to the innovators, the Rafidites, and the Jahmiyas. It also contains advice and sermons for rulers and scholars, and fatwas on various issues, including women going out, wearing silk, and divorce. The book focuses on clarifying issues of jurisprudence and principles in a way that is consistent with the Salafi doctrine, noting the importance of adhering to legal texts and understanding them in the correct way.
descriptions.2988: This book, “The Methodology of Da’wah and Hisbah between the Sunnis and the People of Heresy” by the author Saleh bin Ghosun, is considered within the classification of fatwas. The book contains a fatwa on demonstrations, assassinations, and marches, and clarification of the legal treatment of those who call for these actions. The book shows the author's interest in advocacy and guidance, clarifying the truth, and being patient, and relies on the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet in his interpretation of what is called “the method of advocacy and hisbah” between the Sunnis and the heretics.
descriptions.2989: This book deals with fatwas on the jurisprudence of jihad and Sharia politics, with a focus on the necessity of justice and the prohibition of injustice against all people. In this work, Sheikh Saleh Al-Luhaidan discusses the Islamic ruling on the events that occurred after September 11, and emphasizes that such crimes are among the most dangerous and vile crimes according to Islamic law. He also stresses that Islam prohibits injustice and forbids the indiscriminate killing of civilians, explaining that Islamic law provides more prevention than treatment for these acts.
descriptions.2990: This book, “Akhbar Abu al-Qasim al-Zajjaji,” is considered one of the most important sources in the science of grammar and morphology, as it contains an explanation of various grammatical and morphological issues. The book begins by explaining the grammatical issue and then explains it in detail, and relies on the sayings of scholars and poets in this regard. The content shows that the book covers a wide range of grammatical and morphological topics, including nouns, verbs, morphology and structure. The book also appears to contain verses from Arab poets, which shows the author's interest in poetry and the Arabic language.
descriptions.2991: This book is an explanation of poetic verses from the book Al-Jamal in the field of grammar and morphology. In this work, Al-Batalyusi deals with the interpretation of the meanings of sentence verses and their parsing, reviewing the names of their speakers. The author aims to provide clarifications that show the speaker’s purpose and style in poetry, relying on reviewing and developing previous explanations by others. The book is numbered automatically and contains explanations of some poetic verses, along with mentioning some of the historical stories associated with them.
descriptions.2992: This book is “Al-Durrat Al-Bahiyya Nazm Al-Ajrumiyah” by Al-Amriti, which is a book on grammar and morphology that aims to organize and explain the principles of Arabic grammar. The book begins by mentioning praise to God, thanks for knowledge, and trust in God, then it moves on to explaining the principles of speech and pronunciation, and explaining that speech is divided into three parts: a noun, a verb, and a vowel. The book also explains the principles of syntax and morphology, explains the signs of syntax and morphology, explains verbs, nominatives, nouns, and other grammatical principles. The book is considered one of the main sources in Arabic grammar and morphology, and is considered an important source for researchers and interpreters.
descriptions.2993: Hastening the Dew with an Explanation of Qatr al-Nada is a simplified explanation of the book Qatr al-Nada by Al-Ansari. It deals with topics of grammar and parsing in an easy and useful way for beginner students. Author Abdullah Al-Fawzan focuses on simplifying explanation and parsing examples, while avoiding unnecessary grammatical differences, and follows an approach that aims to simplify the academic material and bring it closer to the student. The book contains various chapters that deal with the rules of grammar and parsing based on Matn al-Qatar and other grammatical books. It is the result of the author’s efforts in teaching Matn al-Qatar to his students at the university.
descriptions.2994: A book on grammar and morphology, which brings together various topics on grammatical analogy, objects, infinitives, plurals, forms of exaggeration, the verbal and nominal sentences, derivation, and other morphological and grammatical issues. The author reviews the opinions of grammarians on these topics, addressing the issue of using poetry as evidence and the eloquent scholars who use it as evidence, relying on an analytical approach in studying linguistic phenomena.
descriptions.2995: This book, “Bride’s Decorations from Taraf and Al-Nafa’is fi Takhrej” by Imam Ibn al-Mubarrad, deals with topics in grammar and morphology, arranged in the form of linguistic rules and principles. The author focuses on clarifying linguistic and grammatical issues based on Qur’anic verses and Prophetic hadiths, and reviews the branches of linguistic rules and their applications in Islamic jurisprudence. The book is divided into several rules. Each rule includes an explanation of the meaning of the word or sentence, along with examples and linguistic details according to the grammarians’ approach.
descriptions.2996: This is an explanation of Al-Ajrumiyah Grammar and Morphology, which is a book that explains the principles of Arabic grammar and morphology by explaining the introduction to Al-Ajrumiyah, which is a brief and concise introduction that has received great attention from scholars. The book aims to teach the importance of learning the Arabic language and grammatical sciences, and to introduce the reader to the relationship between grammar science, the Islamic religion, and Islamic law. The book begins by defining the importance of grammar, the integrity of tongues, the integrity of the speaker’s speech, and the integrity of the two tongues. The book is considered an important reference for learning and studying in the field of Arabic grammar and morphology.
descriptions.2997: This book is an explanation of the text of “Al-Ajurumiyyah” in the science of grammar. It begins with an introduction to the virtue of the Arabic language and the importance of learning it for understanding Sharia law. Then it explains the basic chapters of grammar, beginning with the definition of speech, and moving on to the nominatives, accusatives, and declinables of nouns, with details in the subjects of the subject, subject, predicate, adjective, conjunction, emphasis, substitution, object, infinitive, adverb, distinction, exception, vocative, and others.
descriptions.2998: The book “Mammatamim al-Ajrumiyya” by Al-Hattab al-Ra’ini is a summary of grammar that aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to most grammar sections in a short time. The book covers multiple topics in grammar and morphology, such as parsing and construction, the subject and predicate, the object, and other basic grammatical rules. The book is characterized by accuracy of expressions and breadth of vision in explaining grammatical rules, while staying away from minor disputes and mostly following the opinion of Ibn Malik.
descriptions.2999: Letters of Meanings and Attributes: A book written by Abu Al-Qasim Abdul Rahman Al-Zajjaji. Meanings of Letters (by Al-Farahidi): A book attributed to Al-Farahidi. Meanings of Letters (by Al-Rummani): A book written by Al-Rummani.
descriptions.3000: This book, “The Parsing Joke” by the author Jamal al-Din Ibn Hisham, is considered one of the pioneering books in the field of grammar and morphology. It deals with important topics in the science of parsing, such as sentences that have a place of parsing, and sentences that have no place of parsing, and it relies on an easy and clear approach to facilitate understanding of the material for students and those with understanding. This book is a useful resource for researchers and lecturers in the field of grammar and morphology.
descriptions.3001: Alfiyyah Ibn Malik, also called “Al-Khalasa,” is a poetic text compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Malik al-Ta’i al-Jiyani. It is one of the most important grammatical and linguistic systems, because it received the attention of scholars and writers who were keen to comment on it, with explanations and footnotes, and a shortened text from his major system, “Al-Kafiya al-Shafi’a,” in which he collected a summary of the sciences of grammar and morphology, in a nice summary, with reference. To the doctrines of scholars, and to explain the opinions he chooses, sometimes. …
descriptions.3002: The clearest paths to Alfiyyah Ibn Malik is a book on the science of grammar, written by Ibn Hisham Al Ansari. The book is an explanation of “Alfiyyah Grammar” by Imam Ibn Malik.
descriptions.3003: The book “Isfar al-Fusih” is one of the important grammatical and morphological works by the Harawi author Abu Sahl. The book deals with studying the life of its author and analyzing its scientific content, as it focuses on Abu Sahl’s methodology in his explanation of the book Al-Fusih and his presentation of Arabic issues. The book also studies the sources and evidence used, compares Abu Sahl's explanation with some other explanations, and provides an evaluation of the book's scientific value. The book is divided into parts and chapters that deal with a section of the Arabic language in each of them, thus providing a valuable reference in the field of linguistic and grammatical studies.
descriptions.3004: This is a book on grammar and parsing, which specializes in studying the parsing of the sentence “There is no god but God” and verifying a manuscript attributed to Ibn Hisham Al-Ansari on this subject. In his introduction, the author presents the manuscripts that dealt with the parsing of this word, and points out the benefits and grammatical guidance that distinguished this letter. The book aims to establish the text, evaluate the expressions, and explain the different aspects of the parsing of linguistic evidence.
descriptions.3005: This book, “The Parsing of Lamiya al-Shanfari,” by the Al-Akbari author, Abu Al-Baqa, is considered within the category of grammar and morphology. The book contains an explanation and interpretation of Lamiya al-Shanfari, in which the author provides an accurate and detailed interpretation of the meanings of words and sentences in the poem. The book shows the author's skill in interpreting grammar and morphology, and provides a deep understanding of the meanings of the Arabic language.
descriptions.3006: This book deals with the topic of parsing in the words of the Prophet’s Hadith, focusing on clarifying the meanings of sentences and words that may shape their understanding. The author begins by studying the Musnads of men, arranged according to the letters of the alphabet, in which he reviews examples from the hadiths of the Companions, with an analysis of some famous sentences such as “what touched the woman” and “where is peace in your land”, showing the different aspects of parsing and the validity of each of them. The book is a type of grammatical and morphological book specialized in analyzing hadith words.
descriptions.3007: This book, “A Brief Definition in the Science of Morphology,” by Ibn Malik, falls within the classification of grammar and morphology. The book contains an introduction and two sections, the first section being the “study,” which includes a study of the author and a study of the book. The book is considered one of the works that deals with the science of morphology, and it includes discussions about the author’s life, his qualities and scholarly status, his sheikhs and students, his scholarly influences, establishing his name and documenting his lineage, the subject of the book and its approach, the salient features of the book, its sources and evidence, and its impact on those who disagreed.
descriptions.3008: This book, “Ithaf al-Fadil, with a passive verb in the passive participle,” by the scholar Ibn Allan, deals with the subject of the passive verb in Arabic grammar, and divides its study according to the letters of the alphabet. The author aims to enhance the reader's understanding of the concept of passive verbs and its applications, while adding new information to a previous book on this topic. The book is intended for advanced grammar students and those interested in this aspect of Arabic linguistics.
descriptions.3009: This is a book on grammar and morphology, written by Jamal al-Din Ibn Hisham, and it deals with a delicate grammatical issue, which is “the objection of a condition to a condition.” In this chapter, the author explains the permissibility of two or more conditions for one answer in a sentence, and distinguishes between the forms that grammarians call this term and what some of them mistakenly think of it. He mentions five main issues related to this rule, and discusses the disagreement between grammarians and commentators regarding its guidance and permissibility.
descriptions.3010: The Fundamentals of Grammar is a book on Arabic grammar, by Abu Bakr Ibn al-Siraj, who died in the year (316 AH). This book has a special status among grammarians, and its opinions are of great importance in the science of grammar. Its author collected in it the chapters on grammar and morphology, and arranged the issues of Sibawayh in the best order. He summarized the principles of Arabic and collected its standards until it was said: “Grammar was still crazy until Ibn al-Siraj made sense of its principles.” It was verified by Abdul Hussein Al-Fatli, and printed by Al-Resala Foundation in Beirut four times in three parts. Its indexes were collected by Mahmoud Al-Tanahi in a separate booklet, then edited by Muhammad Othman in 2009.
descriptions.3011: This book is “The Grammatical Puzzles” or “The Style in Puzzles” by the author Al-Suyuti. It is classified under the category of grammar and morphology. The book contains a set of grammatical puzzles, which are divided into two parts: a section asking for an interpretation of the meaning and a section asking for an interpretation of the parsing. The book shows the author's skill in using the grammatical puzzle as a teaching tool to explain grammatical concepts, and includes a group of puzzles that are used to clarify different grammatical concepts.
descriptions.3012: This book by Ibn Jinni deals with the marginalized words used in the Arabic language, classifying them according to the letters of the dictionary. The author focuses on common words and avoids rare, strange words. He explains their meanings and ways of using them in sentences and verbs, thus providing a useful reference for grammarians and intellectuals interested in the Arabic language and its grammar.
descriptions.3013: This book, “Fairness in Issues of Disagreement between Basra and Kufan ​​Grammarians,” by the author Abu al-Barakat al-Anbari, is considered an important book in the science of grammar and morphology, as it deals with the disagreements between the grammarians of Basra and Kufa on various issues. The book contains a group of controversial issues, such as the parsing of the six nouns, the feminine plural of nouns, the nominative of the subject, the nominative of the predicate, the precedence of the predicate over the subject, the factor in the nominative noun after lula, and others. The book is an important source for grammarians and researchers in Arabic science, as it provides a comprehensive overview of the issues of disagreement between the grammarians of Basra and Kufa.
descriptions.3014: This book, “The Election to Reveal Syntactic Verses,” written by Ali bin Adloun, deals with the topics of grammar and morphology through the study of syntactic poetic verses. In this book, the author deals with the Arabic alphabet from Alif to Ya, and studies the poetic verses that include these letters from a precise grammatical perspective. The book aims to clarify the rules of parsing and their applications in Arabic poetry, and to help researchers understand the subtleties of the Arabic language and protect it from distortion and change over time.
descriptions.3015: This is a brief book on grammar and morphology, examining the differences between the masculine and feminine in the Arabic language. The author explains that the masculine is the original, and divides it into the real and the unreal, just as he divides the feminine into the real and the unreal, and shows the verbal and discretionary signs of feminization, citing examples from the Holy Qur’an and Arabic poetry.
descriptions.3016: This book, “Application of Grammar,” by Abdo Al-Rajhi, is a book in the field of grammar and morphology. It aims to apply the principles of grammar to examples and questions, which makes it useful for students and scholars in this field. The book contains successive chapters that address various topics in grammar, such as parsing, construction, nominal and verbal sentences, and stylistics, while including examples and warnings for correcting common errors in contemporary usage. The author shows great effort in revising and editing the book, making it a valuable resource for learning and benefiting.
descriptions.3017: This book deals with the topic of the exclamation of the direct object, which is one of the topics that Arabic scholars and critics have been interested in throughout history. The author reviews previous scientific debates between scholars such as Abu Jaafar al-Nahhas and Abu al-Abbas ibn Welad, and reviews their different opinions on the permissibility of using direct exclamatory forms such as (what I do) and (I do) when an active reaction occurs. The book focuses on the grammatical differences related to this topic, and the conditions for the permissibility of using different exclamatory forms, noting that exclamations using (what is more difficult) or (more strongly) are accepted by agreement if they do not lead to ambiguity.
descriptions.3018: “Al-Jamal fi Grammar” may mean the following: The book Al-Jamal fi Grammar by Al-Farahidi is a book attributed to Al-Khalil bin Ahmed Al-Farahidi. Book of sentences in grammar by Al-Zajjaji
descriptions.3019: The proximal genie fi the letters of meanings is a book on linguistics and grammar written by the jurist and scholar of linguists and literature, Abu Muhammad al-Hasan bin Qasim bin Abdullah bin Ali al-Muradi al-Masri al-Marakshi (? - 749), known as Badr al-Din al-Muradi. He wrote a poetic system that included the meanings of letters, then wrote a book explaining his system, then decided to shorten the book and add other linguistic benefits, so he collected al-Mafraq in the precious books of this meaning. It is considered the primary source in this field to this day
descriptions.3020: The book “The Limits in the Science of Grammar” by Al-Shihab Al-Abdhi is considered one of the most important sources in the science of grammar, as it includes a large number of grammatical terms and definitions with their explanation, interpretation, and clarification. The book is considered very useful and has many benefits, despite its small size. The author, Al-Shihab Al-Abdhi, shows skill in describing the book's topics and general scope, which makes the book a valuable resource for grammar researchers.
descriptions.3021: The Book of Characteristics is one of the most famous books on philology and philosophy, and the secrets and facts of the Arabic language. It was written by Ibn Jinni, and he said in the introduction to his book about it: “A book that I have always been in a state of disarray, and the passage of time, noticing it, contemplating it, drawing opinion and insight into it, and I would find something neglectful by which I could dismiss it, or a flaw in which I would improve with its work, and time would increase with its passing. It is narrow, and it does not approach the beginning in a way. This is despite my veneration for it, my disobedience to the reasons entrusted to it, and my belief in it that it is one of the most honorable things written in Arab science, and I take it along the path of analogy and theory... and I gather it as evidence for what this honorable language has deposited...” The book is considered the most important of Ibn Jinni's books, as he completely invented the Arabic language in it. …
descriptions.3022: The book "The Link and Its Impact on Structures in Arabic" provides a comprehensive overview of the concept of the link in the Arabic language and how to use it in constructing various sentences. The author, Hamza Al-Nashrati, focuses on the types of verbal and moral connections and their role in linking parts of sentences and determining their meanings, while reviewing examples from the Holy Qur’an and the Prophet’s Hadith to clarify the concept of linking and its applications. The book also addresses grammatical discussions about the use of certain connectives such as “al” and its relationship to the pronoun, as well as its analysis of compound conjunctions that combine different connectives in one sentence.
descriptions.3023: This is a book on the science of morphology, written by Ibn al-Hajib, and it includes the text of “Al-Shafiyya” along with its verses called “Al-Wafiyya.” The book begins by defining morphology as a science that identifies the conditions of word structures that are not grammatical. Then, it discusses in detail the types of structures for nouns and verbs, morphological scale, spatial reversal, and the correct and ill-defined sections. It extends to include multiple morphological topics such as diminutive, relative, plural, and stopping.
descriptions.3024: This book, “Poetic Necessity and its Concept among Grammarians, A Study” by the author Ibrahim bin Saleh Al-Handoud, is considered one of the grammatical studies that dealt with the concept of poetic necessity and its impact on the construction of words and the formulation of phrases in poetry. In the introduction to the book, the author shows his interest in the Arabic language and its service, and talks about the importance of preserving its language and its purity. He points out that the previous view of the arts of poetry and prose was the same, but Arabic scholars noticed the disparity between them in the construction of words and the formulation of phrases. The author highlights that poetic necessity was not specifically defined in the books of grammarians, but rather an expression that led to its meaning without declaring its wording was sufficient. The book shows interest in the grammatical and analytical study of Arabic poetry, and deals with the concept of poetic necessity and its impact on the construction of words and phrasing in poetry.
descriptions.3025: This book, “Al-Umda fi Parsing Al-Burda,” is considered one of the most important sources in grammar and morphology, as it contains a comprehensive study of Al-Busiri’s poem “Al-Burda,” which is considered one of the most famous Arabic poems. The book begins with an introduction to the manuscript, then moves on to a detailed study and analysis of the poem Burdah, including its elements, prophetic praises, and the influence of its parsing. The book contains an index of topics, including aspects of parsing, an index of morphology, an index of holy verses, an index of poetry, an index of notables, an index of places and countries, and sources and references. It appears from the excerpt at the beginning of the book that the author has created this rare manuscript, and it reflects his interest in the Arab and Islamic heritage, and this work is considered part of the heritage revival movement in the lives of nations and peoples.
descriptions.3026: The book “The Amazing Benefits of Parsing Strange Words” by Ibn Abidin is a book on grammar and morphology, which deals with explanation and parsing of a group of words and phrases commonly used among scholars, whose parsing or meaning may be hidden. The book aims to clarify the linguistic problems in these constructions, such as “so on,” “oh God, except that it be,” and “it must be such and such,” relying on the statements of grammarians and linguists to guide them.
descriptions.3027: This is the book "Part One" of the book of Sibawayh, the distinguished author in the science of grammar and morphology. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the science of Arabic linguistics, as it contains multiple branches of grammar, such as the science of speech, the final syllables of words, the predicate and the predicate to it, pronunciation of meanings, correctness of speech and referral, and others. The book shows Sibawayh's contributions to understanding and interpreting the Arabic language, and his influence on grammar and linguists in the Middle Ages is clear. This book is considered an essential source for study and research in grammar and morphology, and it forms part of the Arab cultural heritage.
descriptions.3028: The book deals with revealing the identity of the author of the book “Al-Basit” on grammar, a book mentioned in the works of many grammar scholars without revealing its author. The author aims to clarify the mystery surrounding this book and its author, relying in doing so on a study of the books attributed to the author of Al-Basit and criticizing the delusions of contemporary investigators. The book also discusses the grammatical approach of Sahib Al-Basit and his grammatical views, with a review of the authors who quoted from him.
descriptions.3029: This is a brief book on grammar and morphology. Its author devoted it to studying the letter Lām and investigating its types and locations in Arab speech and in the Holy Qur’an. The author begins by enumerating thirty-one lamas, explaining their meanings and actions, and arguing for each of their locations, while mentioning the disagreement that may arise over some of them among scholars. The book then goes on to detail these types, chapter by chapter, beginning with the original lam that occurs in nouns, verbs, and letters.
descriptions.3030: This book, “Al-Lubab fi Illal al-Basna wa al-Parsing,” by Al-Akbari author Abu Al-Baqa, is considered one of the most important sources in the field of grammar and morphology. The book is considered one of the main sources for understanding and applying the rules of grammar and morphology in the Arabic language. The book contains in-depth chapters on the reasons for construction and parsing, where the author explains the principles of grammar and morphology and presents clear examples of how to apply these principles in the Arabic language. The book is a useful resource for researchers and investigators in the field of the Arabic language and Islamic heritage.
descriptions.3031: The book “Al-Lahma fi Sharh Al-Malha” is a grammatical explanation of Al-Hariri’s “Malha” system of parsing, written by Muhammad bin Al-Hassan Al-Sayegh. The book falls within the science of grammar and morphology, and its author took care to clarify the rules of parsing and grammatical issues by explaining the verses of the system. The book includes a comprehensive study of the author and his method of explanation, in addition to the verified text that begins with the chapter on speech and extends to include the chapters on the noun, verb, letter, and parsing.
descriptions.3032: The book: “Al-Lam’ in Arabic” by Abu Al-Fath Uthman Ibn Jinni is one of the books on grammar and morphology, in which he collected a set of grammar rules and linguistic sciences. This book became famous, in addition to the fame of its author, as the book brings together the rules of grammar and some rules of morphology in brief. Scientists were interested in this book, and many of them explained it.
descriptions.3033: This is a scientific thesis written by Jamal al-Din Ibn Hisham, concerned with studying and analyzing the concepts of grammar and morphology, especially with regard to the conditional. The book begins by defining issues related to the conditional and other conditional nouns, then moves on to analyzing and interpreting these concepts through logical inferences and explanation of meanings. It appears from the aforementioned passages that the book deals with topics such as the significance of nouns and vowels on meaning in the self and others, the analysis of conditional nouns, and the study of the introduction and arrangement of sentences. This book is one of the important sources in the field of grammar and morphology, and reflects the author's interest in investigating and explaining these areas.
descriptions.3034: The book provides a comprehensive study of the main Arabic grammar schools, with a focus on the Basra school as the first to establish the foundations of grammar. The author deals with the history of the development of grammar in Basra and Kufa, and refers to prominent grammatical figures such as Al-Khalil bin Ahmed and Ibn Al-Sarraj, while analyzing their contributions and their impact on the development of grammar science. The book aims to provide a comprehensive vision of the overall efforts made to establish and develop the science of grammar throughout history.
descriptions.3035: Travel Issues is a treatise written by Ibn Hisham Al-Ansari in which he explains the parsing of verses from the Qur’an that he was asked about while he was traveling, and he answered that.
descriptions.3036: This book, “Al-Mughni fi Conjugation of Verbs” by the author Muhammad Abdel-Khaleq Adima, is considered one of the most important books in the field of grammar and morphology. The book contains a table of contents that explains the content of the book, and includes an introduction to the third edition that explains the importance of the book and its impact on grammar and morphology. The book begins by mentioning the value of Sibawayh’s book and its impact on grammar and morphology, then it talks about the authors who devoted independent writing to morphology. The book also explains the importance of the conjugations of Al-Mazini and Al-Mansif by Ibn Jinni. The book contains an excerpt from the beginning of the book that explains the style of the book and the author's purpose in writing it. It appears throughout the book that the author has read many grammatical and morphological books, and relied on the method of the Holy Qur’an in emphasizing verbs. The book is considered one of the most important sources in the field of grammar and morphology, and is considered an important source for researchers and lecturers in this field.
descriptions.3037: The Key to Morphology is a book on morphology, written by the linguist Abdul Qahir al-Jurjani. It is a key to the science of morphology, as it is a brief book that includes the principles in the science of morphology, without elaboration, and it rarely cites Qur’anic or poetic evidence or sayings. It is more like abbreviations or summary books such as: Al-Maluki fi Al-Tasrif by Ibn Jinni, Nuzhat Al-Tarf fi Ilm Al-Marf by Al-Maydani, and Shafiya Ibn Al-Hajib. Its author said in the introduction to the book: “This is a book with little elaboration, many meanings, easy to memorize, and easy to understand. I named it “The Key” in the hope that I would mention it in favor of the supplications of the believers.” Then he began to define morphology, then the structures of nouns, then the structures of verbs...etc.
descriptions.3038: Al-Mufassal fi Sanat al-Arab is a book that discusses the science of grammar and parsing. The importance of this book is due to the importance of its author, Al-Zamakhshari, who is a distinguished imam in this field.
descriptions.3039: Al-Muqtadsib is an Arabic grammar book. It is considered the second grammatical encyclopedia after the book of Sibawayh. It was written by Al-Mubarrad, who died in the year 285 AH. The book Al-Muqtadsib was distinguished by its clarity and ease of expression, due to the literary skill that characterized its author Al-Muqtadsib. Al-Muqtadsib did not gain fame and attention due to grammarians’ preoccupation with Sibawayh’s book. Abu Al-Barakat Al-Anbari said in Al-Mubarrad, “He wrote many books, the largest of which is Al-Muqtadsib. It is valuable, but it is rarely used.”
descriptions.3040: Al-Mumti’ Al-Kabir fi Al-Tasrif is a book on the science of morphology. Ibn Asfour compiled this book briefly, and presented it to Prince Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Abi Al-Asbagh, the ruler of Seville. Then he added many additions to it, which made Abu Hayyan call it “Al-Mumti’ Al-Kabir.” Ibn Malik, the author of the Millennium, commented on it with many coins, to which Abu Hayyan added more, then he summarized it in a book called “The Creator’s Summary from the Fun” and it was published in Kuwait in 1982 AD, edited by Abd al-Hamid Sayyid Talab. …
descriptions.3041: This book is an explanation of the book Al-Tasrif by Abu Othman Al-Mazni, prepared by Ibn Jinni to strengthen its principles and refine its chapters. The book deals with the interpretation of morphology in the Arabic language, providing examples and analogues to enhance understanding, and aims to make the book stand alone and distinct in its field. The explanation includes explaining linguistic problems and difficulties in morphology, while providing clarifications of some errors and ambiguities that the reader may encounter.
descriptions.3042: This book deals with a specific linguistic topic, which is focused on approximation in grammar and morphology, and reviews it from two different perspectives, namely the Kufic and Basri schools. The author begins by defining the approximation and its conditions according to the Kufans, then moves on to discuss their opinions regarding its rulings and sections, and compares it with the case and the final. Then he moves on to study the opinion of the Basrans on this term and their opinions on its rulings, and reviews the opinions of their scholars such as Sibawayh and Thalab. The book aims to clarify the differences between the two schools in this linguistic field and explain the reasons for their differences in it.
descriptions.3043: This book, “Al-Mansub Ala Naza’ al-Khafid in the Qur’an,” by Ibrahim bin Sulaiman Al-Baimi, is considered a grammatical and morphological research in the field of grammar and morphology. The book aims to study and apply the removal of the Khadif in the Holy Qur’an, while addressing the definition of the term, its provisions, its analogy, and the difference between the removal of the Khadif and the inclusion. The book shows interest in the Holy Qur’an and its grammatical and morphological applications, and indicates that there are hidden secrets in Qur’anic readings that need to be highlighted. This book is considered a useful resource for researchers in the field of grammar and morphology, especially those who focus on the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.3044: This book, “The Inhabited Manhole in the Passive Voice” by Abu al-Khair Muhammad bin Dhahirah, is a work on grammar and morphology, dealing with Arabic verbs whose subject is not named, known as “the passive voice.” The author studies the types of these verbs and their rules, and reviews his scientific effects and poetry in the introduction to the book. The book aims to clarify the rules for constructing verbs whose actor is not known, and it constitutes the first independent work on this subject, paving the way for subsequent studies in this field.
descriptions.3045: This is the book “The Summary of Arabic Grammar” by Saeed Al-Afghani. This book is considered one of the most important sources in the field of grammar and morphology, as the author presents the principles and rules of the Arabic language in a clear and easy way. This book is an important resource for students and researchers in the field of the Arabic language, as the author provides them with a deep understanding of the language’s rules and applications.
descriptions.3046: The book “Refined Grammar” by author Muhammad Eid presents a contemporary view of the science of grammar, trying to simplify it and rid it of the unnecessary fillers and branches that have spread in traditional books. The book focuses on the basics of grammar and its original principles, seeking to make it more understandable and easy for students of the Arabic language. The book reviews various topics from parsing and construction to nominal and verbal sentences, relying on a scientific approach that aims to distinguish between what is necessary in grammar and what is superfluous and not useful.
descriptions.3047: This book, “Clear Grammar in Arabic Grammar,” by Ali Al-Jarim, is considered one of the important sources in the field of grammar and morphology. The book contains in-depth chapters on dividing a word into a noun, a verb, and a letter, classifying a verb based on its tense, and exercises on that. The book also covers other topics such as the useful sentence, parts of the sentence, the verbal sentence and the nominal sentence, the accusative and accusative of the present tense verb, the nominative of the present tense verb, as well as the genitive noun and adjective. The book is a useful resource for teachers and students in understanding and applying Arabic grammar.
descriptions.3048: This is the book “Al-Nahm Al-Wafi” on grammar and morphology, written by Abbas Hassan. The book deals with the basics of grammar and its importance in understanding Arab and Islamic sciences, explaining its role as a support for the Arabic language and its grammar. The book includes multiple problems on word classes, syntax, construction, nouns, verbs, pronouns, and other grammatical rules. Through this book, the author aims to provide a comprehensive and useful reference for studying grammar and understanding it more deeply.
descriptions.3049: This research is concerned with studying the afāl form in the Arabic language, specifically among grammarians and linguists, and analyzing its uses in the Arabic language. The author, Mustafa Ahmad Al-Namas, begins by defining the form of “af’l” and its history in the Arabic language, then moves on to analyze the opinions of scholars regarding “af’l” and “af’l” in one meaning, and refers to Ibn Qutaybah’s opinion on this topic. The author also shows how the form I do is used in various constructions, such as the exclamatory and the superlative, and points out some verbs that have served a special function for it. The research aims to collect the rulings on hearing, analogy, anomaly, nadur, and similar linguistic rulings for the form of afāl, and analyze their uses in the Arabic language.
descriptions.3050: This book, “The Interpenetration of Linguistic Principles and Its Impact on Building the Dictionary,” written by Abd al-Razzaq bin Farraj al-Sa’idi, is considered one of the most important and difficult areas of linguistic activity, and requires special specifications in its pioneers. The book shows that the field of lexicographic work requires precision, patience, and patience. It also shows that Arabic language scholars have left behind a rich lexical heritage, and have provided this important matter with reasons for maturity and success. The book also shows that the field of fertile linguistic studies on sounds, structures, structures, and semantics still needs more studies. The book also shows that words in the Arabic language are linked to their origins and meanings in a very precise system, and shows that every word and what is derived from it has only one origin, but there are origins that overlap, which leads to overlap with its true origin.
descriptions.3051: The book “Explanation of Objectives and Paths with an Explanation of Alfiyyah Ibn Malik” by Al-Muradi, known as Ibn Umm Qasim, provides a detailed explanation of Ibn Malik’s Alfiyyah in grammar and morphology, stating in it the opinions and doctrines of grammarians in a clear and precise manner. The author focuses on clarifying the purpose of the millennium and bringing it closer to the reader, which made his explanation an important reference for researchers in this field. The book consists of two parts: the first deals with a historical and scientific study of the subject of the explanation, and the second contains the explanation itself.
descriptions.3052: The Collection of Arabic Lessons is a book specialized in grammar, written by Sheikh Mustafa Al-Ghalayini. This book is considered one of the most prominent references in Arabic grammar thanks to its clarity and ease of presentation, which makes it accessible to everyone. Its author was also proficient in the sciences of the Arabic language, which enabled him to present abundant scientific material. This book derives its content from major traditional books, which relieves the reader of the need to read lengthy works on grammar.
descriptions.3053: Hashiyat al-Ajrumiyya is a book on grammar and morphology, written by the author Abd al-Rahman bin Qasim. The book is considered a footnote to the book Al-Ajrumiyah, which is a book on grammar that is considered one of the most important Arabic grammar books. The book contains multiple chapters that address various topics in grammar and morphology, such as parsing, signs, verbs, subject, object, predicate, agents, emphasis, substitution, accusative, object, infinitive, time and place, adverb, distinction, exception, non-negative of gender, vocative, object for its sake, object with it, and declinables of nouns. The book is considered an important source for learning and studying in the field of Arabic grammar and morphology.
descriptions.3054: This book is Al-Sabban’s commentary on Al-Ashmouni’s explanation of Alfiyyah Ibn Malik. It is a book on grammar and morphology that is considered one of the most important sources in this field. The author Al-Sabban is considered one of the most famous scholars of grammar and morphology in the modern era. He wrote this footnote to Al-Ashmouni’s explanation of Alfiyyah Ibn Malik, which is considered one of the most famous books on grammar and morphology. The book contains a detailed table of contents from which it appears that the book deals with many topics in grammar and morphology, such as speech and what it consists of, the inflected and the constructed, the indefinite article and the knowing, the demonstrative noun, the relative, the definite article with the definite article, the beginning, was and its sisters, an introduction, a chapter on what and not and that the mutabals are not, verbs of convergence, if and its sisters, the subject, the substitute for the subject, the operator’s occupation of the subject, the transitivity of the verb and its immanence, conflict in the action, the absolute object, the direct object. him.
descriptions.3055: This book, “The Movement of Present Letters,” by Abdullah Al-Qarni, is considered part of the field of grammar and morphology.
