The book provides a content index that shows its division into sections and notes, covering topics such as the definition of selling, the legality of selling and its ruling, forbidden items, selling dead bodies, selling blood, and selling human and animal waste. The excerpt from the beginning of the book shows that the book is an academic research aimed at providing a better understanding of Islamic law regarding prohibited sales, defining its limits, and clarifying its provisions.
descriptions.3184: This research deals with the ruling on insurance after Al-Fatihah in prayer, its description and time. It reviews the meaning of insurance, its virtue and its formula, then explains its legitimacy for the imam, the person praying behind him, and the individual, and details the nature and time of insurance for each of them. It also addresses the issue of correcting insurance and its repetition.
descriptions.3185: This book, “Adornment and the Danger of Women Participating with Men in the Field of Their Work,” written by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz, is concerned with warning against women displaying their adornment and not covering themselves with men. This book is considered part of the classification of research and issues, as it examines the importance of hijab and the prohibition of adornment, and presents the dire consequences of women going out to work, the prohibition of mingling, and the prohibition of all means leading to it, in addition to the recognition by men of the West and East of the harms and evils of mingling. The book is considered one of the Islamic sources that highlight the importance of the hijab and warn against women’s adornment, and it is considered an important source for Muslims who are looking to understand Islam and deal with it in daily life.
descriptions.3186: The book “Protection from the Devils’ Cunning” is a study of issues related to the jinn, magic, the evil eye, and envy, and explains the terms associated with them, such as touch, seeking help, divination, and astrology. The author aims to explain the legal rulings on these matters and clarify the difference between what is legitimate and what is invalid in terms of practices, with a focus on the legal means of immunization.
descriptions.3187: Investigation and clarification of many issues of Hajj, Umrah, and visiting in the light of the Qur’an and Sunnah. It is a book written by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz, the Mufti of Saudi Arabia, as a summary of the issues of Hajj, Umrah, and visiting the Prophet’s Mosque ﷺ in Medina. The book was printed for the first time in 1363 AH, and it underwent a number of amendments by the same author after that year, simplifying some of its issues and increasing the investigations. He wrote in the introduction:
descriptions.3188: This book, “Tarawih for More than a Thousand Years in the Prophet’s Mosque,” ​​by author Attiya Salem, is classified under the category of “Research and Issues.” The book presents historical research on the subject of Tarawih, starting from the Prophet’s era and continuing through the ages until the Saudi era. The author shows the progression and development in the legality of Tarawih, from absolute encouragement to progressive development in later eras. The book aims to give Tarawih its due and analyze it through Islamic texts, and opens the way for readers to participate in discussion and research on this sensitive topic.
descriptions.3189: This book, “Social Solidarity in Comparative Islamic Jurisprudence,” by author Abdullah Al-Tayyar, is an encyclopedic research in the field of social solidarity in Islamic jurisprudence, as it compares the system of social solidarity in Islam with the system of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The book begins by defining social solidarity and the history of its origin and development, then moves on to a detailed analysis of the Islamic system of social cooperation, including its foundations and the patterns it follows. The author shows that social solidarity in Islam is a comprehensive system that covers all aspects of social life, from raising an individual to family planning and financial dealings. This book is a valuable source for study and research in the field of social solidarity in Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.3190: This book deals with the subject of astrology and its rule in Islam, and reviews the sections of astrology and its development throughout history. The author shows that God Almighty is the only one who creates and manages, and that astrology contradicts monotheism. The book also addresses the ruling on learning astronomy, the ruling on working with astrology, and believing what astrologers tell them, and reviews the evidence of the corruption of the astrologers’ industry. The book aims to distance the prophets from astrology and explain its ruling in Islamic law.
descriptions.3191: The book “Al-Jami fi Al-Khatim” by Al-Bayhaqi is a jurisprudential and hadith study specializing in the rulings on rings in Islam. The book collects a number of issues related to sealing, such as the ruling on wearing a silver ring on the right or left, the permissibility of the ring to the imam, engraving the ring, sealing books with it, and the danger of the gold ring. The author relies on the narration of the Prophetic hadiths and the hadiths mentioned in the chapter, while discussing their chains of transmission and explaining what is preserved from them and what is anomalous, as appears from his introduction in which he begins by mentioning the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ sealing himself with a silver ring in his right hand.
descriptions.3192: This book, “Hajj Arafa,” by author Muhammad Aman al-Jami, is classified under the “Research and Issues” category. The book covers topics related to Hajj, including the limits of stopping, the names of Mount Al-Rahma, prayer on the mountain, advice for pilgrims, the time to stop, and jurisprudential rulings. The book begins by defining the Hajj of Arafat and describing its worship, then moving on to describing the boundaries of the situation on the day of Arafat, where it identifies the eastern, southern, northern and western sides of the spot in which the pilgrim resides. The book shows an attention to detail and accurate description of the conditions and surroundings of the Hajj, making it a useful source of knowledge on the subject.
descriptions.3193: This is a comprehensive book that deals with the rulings of Hajj, Umrah, and visiting the Prophet’s Mosque. In it, the author collected the virtues, rulings, rituals, and etiquette related to these acts of worship, in addition to warnings about common errors and violations, and important fatwas. The book aims to provide a comprehensive reference that meets the needs of Hajj and Umrah pilgrims, benefiting from previous literature in this field.
descriptions.3194: This book deals with in-depth research into the subject of punishments and ta’zirat according to Imam Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, reviewing his opinions and rulings in this field through an analysis of the contents of his various books. The author, Bakr Abu Zaid, focuses on studying the legislative and jurisprudential dimensions of these issues, relying on the discussions of Ibn al-Qayyim presented in several of his books. The book aims to provide a comprehensive and analytical view of Ibn al-Qayyim’s position on punishments and discretionary punishments, with a focus on the differences between them and other legal punishments.
descriptions.3195: The book “Beware of Magic” is written by Dr. Khaled Al-Jarisi wrote a book focusing on the subject of magic and spiritual sciences. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as the verse on magic, the hadith on magic, and an explanation of the meaning of magic and terms related to it. It also contains a chapter that explains the types of magic and their relationship to what are called (spiritual sciences). The book aims to make readers aware of the danger posed by magic, and to explain the importance of being cautious of it.
descriptions.3196: The book deals with the ruling on amputating a thief’s hand in Islamic law, reviewing its provisions and wisdom from a jurisprudential perspective. The author focuses on the wisdom of determining punishment, presenting evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah, and reviews the views of jurists on the permissibility of dropping this punishment or replacing it with another. It also shows that the assessment of severe penalties for serious crimes is entrusted to God Almighty, to ensure the achievement of justice and deterrence without compromising on the limits specified by Sharia law.
descriptions.3197: The book “Al-Hail” by Muhammad Al-Masoudi is a jurisprudential research that deals with issues of tricks in Islamic jurisprudence, and sheds light on their types and rulings. The author aims to clarify the ambiguity of these issues and reveal their facts, dividing the topic into an introduction, preface, and seven chapters, relying on inferences from the Qur’an and Sunnah and providing examples to facilitate understanding.
descriptions.3198: This book, “The Wicked or the Wicked,” by Sheikh Abdel Fattah Ashmawi, is considered one of the books of Islamic jurisprudence, research, and issues. The book deals with the issue of the prohibition of alcohol and its effect on humans, and addresses various aspects of this topic, including the most important types of alcohol that have been developed, their effect on the body, the ruling on medication with alcohol, and the punishment for drinking alcohol. The book shows a progression in the prohibition of alcohol, from the predominant meaning of abandonment to a categorical prohibition during prayer. This book is a useful resource for Muslims who wish to understand various aspects of Islamic jurisprudence and the prohibitions found in the religion.
descriptions.3199: The book “Al-Tharaj and the Writing Industry” by Al-Baghdadi writer Qudamah bin Jaafar deals with various topics related to financial management and government functions in the Abbasid era. It focuses on the tax system and its details, and includes multiple chapters that deal with the various state debtors and their functions, in addition to discussing some other administrative and financial issues. The book reflects the author's interest in state issues, administrative and financial sciences, and also demonstrates his extensive experience in the fields of government writing and blogging.
descriptions.3200: This book, “Al-Kharaj” by Abu Yusuf Al-Qadi, deals with the issue of the annual tax imposed on agricultural lands in the Islamic State, and reviews the history of imposing the kharaj from the era of the Prophet until the era of Caliph Harun Al-Rashid. The author focuses on the legal rulings related to the imposition and division of tax, and discusses various issues related to agricultural tax and tribute and how they are applied in various Islamic lands.
descriptions.3201: This is an introductory summary of the book: The book is titled “Alcohol and its Effect on the Eyes,” and the author is written by Dr. Fikri Al-Sayyed Awad, an ophthalmologist at the university. The book focuses on the effect of bad alcohol on the eyes, and addresses the effect of alcohol on the optic nerve, the muscles that move the eyes, and the blood vessels that nourish the eye. The book begins with an introductory introduction to wine and alcohol, then moves on to the effect of alcohol on the body and the eye, and discusses the effect of ethyl and methyl alcohol on the eye. The book is a type of research and issues in the field of medicine and ophthalmology.
descriptions.3202: Al-Durr al-Mandūd fi Blessings and Peace be upon the Owner of the Praiseworthy Maqām by Imam Ibn Hajar al-Haytami al-Makki (d. 974 AH) is a book that deals with the topic of praying for the Prophet Muhammad, and its virtues.
descriptions.3203: This book deals with brief religious instructions for general Muslims, divided into sequential lessons that begin with Surah Al-Fatihah and short surahs, then move on to the pillars of Islam and faith, and the sections of monotheism and polytheism, with an explanation of basic concepts such as testimony to monotheism and its conditions, the pillars of prayer, Muslim etiquette and things that invalidate ablution, and preparing the dead and his prayers. The book aims to simplify the main Islamic doctrines and acts of worship to make them easier to understand and apply in the daily lives of ordinary Muslims.
descriptions.3204: This is a book in defense of the great companion Abu Bakra (may Allah be pleased with him) and his narrations, especially his famous hadith, “A people will never succeed if their affairs are governed by a woman,” in response to an article by Sheikh Muhammad Al-Ashqar in which he criticized Abu Bakra and Sahih Al-Bukhari. The author explains the virtue of Abu Bakra and the scholars’ praise of him, frees his narrations from criticism, and discusses the contradictions in the aforementioned article about women’s guardianship over men.
descriptions.3205: This book, “Blood Money” by Sheikh Ibn Abi Asim, is considered one of the most important sources in the science of hadith and Islamic jurisprudence, as it focuses on topics related to blood money, killing, retaliation, and seeking recovery. It deals with the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ on these topics, and includes multiple branches such as glorifying the killing of those who professed Islam, faith is subject to lethality, killing in whatever form it is, punishment, retaliation for beatings, and others. The book is an important source for jurists and researchers in this field, as it contains multiple narrations from the Companions and followers, and it forms an essential part of the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.3206: The book “Sacrifices in Hajj Rites, Their Sources and Expenses” by Dr. Ahmed Ali Taha Rayan deals with the topic of sacrifices offered in Hajj rites and their importance in drawing closer to God and social solidarity among Muslims. The author focuses on the legal reasons for offering these sacrifices and their impact on the life of Islamic society, reviewing evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book is a type of research and religious issues that aims to gain a deeper understanding of authentic rituals and their purposes.
descriptions.3207: This is a book on Islamic jurisprudence, which falls within the research of controversial issues between sects. The book is organized into multiple sections related to the provisions of jihad and spoils, such as dividing spoils, taking weapons, horse shares, selling captives, establishing borders in the land of war, land tax, and other jurisprudential issues related to travel and battles. It appears from the beginning of the book that its author presents the opinions of Imam Abu Hanifa and responds with them to the opinions of Imam Al-Awza’i on these issues, based on the hadiths of the Prophet and the events of his biography.
descriptions.3208: The book “Bribery” by His Eminence Sheikh Attiya Salem Al-Qadi deals with a detailed study of the concept of bribery from a linguistic and terminological perspective, reviewing the sayings of scholars and commentators regarding its definition and synonymous words. The book also addresses the negative effects of bribery on the individual and society, and discusses the factors behind its spread and ways to combat it, relying on Qur’anic and Prophetic texts to explain its ruling and explain the difference between it and a gift.
descriptions.3209: This book is an investigation into the subject of slavery. It begins by defining it linguistically, terminologically, and its historical origin among ancient nations. Then it deals with the situation of slavery in pre-Islamic times, and devotes the largest part to explaining Islam’s position on slavery. It explains its reality in Sharia law, discusses whether Islam approved slavery or called for its liberation, and concludes by explaining the impact of the slavery system on Islamic civilization.
descriptions.3210: Al-Zahr al-Nadr fi Hal al-Khidr is a book on faith, in which its author, Imam Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (773 AH - 852 AH), discusses the issue of the prophecy of al-Khidr, his lineage, what was mentioned in his development, and whether he was deceased or not. Ibn Hajar reported from the books that preceded him on this subject, such as the book “Ibn al-Munadi.” Ibn Hajar reviewed it and transferred it to his book after adding to its material many things that he found after a long follow-up, detailing the statement regarding He had summed it up when talking about Al-Khidr in his book “Al-Isabah fi Taymiz Al-Sahaba.”
descriptions.3211: A book that deals with the provisions of marriage in Islam, its goals and rulings, with guidance on choosing a life partner according to the standards of religion, morals, beauty, and others. The author explains the provisions and etiquette of engagement and the conditions of the marriage contract, based on what he sees as the causes of family problems resulting from ignorance of the legal rules and the psychological characteristics of each spouse.
descriptions.3212: This book, “Marriage,” by Ibn Uthaymeen, is classified under the “Research and Issues” category. The book provides a table of contents that includes the most important chapters and questions that will be addressed in the book, including chapters related to the meaning of marriage, the ruling on marriage, the conditions of marriage, the quality of the woman who should be married, the prohibitions of marriage, the permissible number of marriages, the wisdom of marriage, the consequences of marriage, the ruling on divorce and what should be taken into account, and the consequences of divorce. The book begins with an introduction that provides some information about a lecture given by the author at the Colleges of Sharia and Arabic Language in Qassim, and addresses some issues related to Islamic preaching in our time.
descriptions.3213: This book is a message by Imam Al-Sakhawi in which he discusses the difference between praiseworthy money and reprehensible money in the light of Sharia texts. He explains when money is praised and when it is reprehensible, along with an explanation of its rulings and the ranks of people in it. It also includes an investigation of the issue and a collection of hadiths that may give the illusion of conflict in this matter, such as the hadith of Anas praying for an abundance of money and children.
descriptions.3214: This is a brief book on the rulings and etiquette of travel derived from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It begins by defining travel and the traveler and explaining its types, then moves on to detailing the recommended etiquette and duties that the traveler should observe, with a focus on the rulings on shortening prayers, combining them, and travel concessions, benefiting from the reports of his sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz.
descriptions.3215: This book deals with the issue of Palestine from the perspective of the Salafists, and reviews the opinions of Salafist scholars on guerrilla operations and their fatwas related to the Palestinian conflict. It also contains a criticism and interpretation of Sheikh Al-Albani's fatwa regarding the expulsion of the people of Palestine. The book aims to present a Salafist vision for dealing with the Palestinian issue and analyze the fatwas related to it.
descriptions.3216: The book “The Sun at Midnight” by Dr. Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali presents a field study of the polar lands, examining their climatic and geographical conditions, with a focus on the phenomenon of the sun not setting there for long periods. The author also discusses how this phenomenon affects Islamic prayer times, and reviews his trip to those areas and his observations there. The book falls under the category of research and issues, and contains specialized research on the Arctic lands and the challenges of worship there.
descriptions.3217: The book, “Prayer: A Detailed Description of Prayer with Its Introductions,” by author Abdullah Al-Tayyar, deals with in-depth research into the provisions of prayer, its pillars, and conditions, citing the Qur’an and Sunnah as evidence. It focuses on the importance of prayer in Islam and its great status, and reviews the provisions of ablution and washing and how to perform them, explaining their virtues, conditions, and contradictions. The book also deals with the etiquette, sunnahs and duties of prayer, indicating the utmost importance for a Muslim to understand the provisions and conditions of prayer in order to perform worship correctly.
descriptions.3218: This book, “Fasting is Paradise,” written by Dr. Khaled Al-Jarisi, deals with the topic of fasting from its various aspects, explaining its rulings, virtues, and secrets, and reviewing the types of fasting, its conditions, and jurisprudential issues. The book also discusses the virtues of fasting during the month of Ramadan and Laylat al-Qadr, relying on legal evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.3219: This book is written by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and deals with the topic of purity in Islamic law from its various aspects. The book includes research and issues related to the rulings on water, cleansing, the obligations and characteristics of ablution, and other issues related to the purity of objects and deeds. The book aims to explain the provisions of purity and show how to regulate it in the daily life of a Muslim, relying on Sharia texts and jurisprudential sayings.
descriptions.3220: The book “The Lesson in the Month of Fasting” by Sheikh Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad deals with topics related to worship and trials in this world, with a focus on the virtue of the month of Ramadan and the seasonality of fasting in the life of a Muslim. The author presents lessons and sermons on the meaning of the religious test and renews the call to piety and getting closer to God through fasting and other obedience. The book is a type of religious book that aims to remind Muslims of the importance of worship and its activation in their daily lives, while providing an overview of the provisions of fasting and its spiritual and worldly benefits.
descriptions.3221: This is a book that collects hadiths and prophetic traditions related to the temptations that agitate Iraq, and studies the connection between that and the contemporary temptations that have ravaged the region. The author begins by explaining that temptations emerge from the East in general and Iraq in particular. Then he discusses in detail the methods and evidence of the hadiths mentioned in that, and responds to a slander attributed to some texts. The book devotes chapters to studying temptations, their types and times, and focuses on the phenomenon of the Kharijites and their relationship with Iraq, tracing its extension to contemporary temptations such as the temptation of Juhayman in the Great Mosque of Mecca, the temptation of Hama, and the temptation of Algeria, with a discussion of the fatwas of scholars on those events.
descriptions.3222: This is a book on the science of religious duties, which is the science of inheritance derived from the Holy Qur’an, written by Al-Suhaili to explain the wisdom and secrets inherent in the verses about wills and inheritances. The author explains the meanings of the Qur’anic terms in the verses on inheritance, and deduces the rulings related to the share of heirs such as children, parents, spouses, and brothers, while explaining the meanings of kaalalah and blocking. The book aims to demonstrate divine wisdom and justice in distributing estates, based on the rulings contained in the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.3223: The book “The Obligations” by its author, Abdul Karim Al-Lahim, provides detailed research on the science of inheritance, covering the definition of the science of inheritance, its importance, and its main topics, which include the rights related to inheritance, the pillars, conditions, and causes of inheritance, the types of heirs, men and women, the duties determined in the Qur’an, and special provisions regarding grandmothers, agnates, and veils. The book focuses on clarifying the wisdom of differentiation between males and females in inheritance, while responding to those who question the fairness of these rulings.
descriptions.3224: This book, “Real and Aspirational Art - Stories of Male and Female Artists’ Repentance,” is written by Dr. Khaled Al-Jarisi is a research book that addresses the subject of representational art and its effects on young people, while addressing the importance of education and consolidation of Islamic concepts in society. The book shows the author's interest in the negative effects of representational art on young people, and focuses on the importance of awareness and education in order to preserve the Islamic faith. The book contains multiple chapters that address topics such as representational art and women, representational art and consolidating concepts, and the role of the media in promoting art. This book is a useful source of knowledge about the impact of representational art on society, and helps understand the importance of educating and consolidating Islamic concepts in daily life.
descriptions.3225: This book, “Al-Fawaid Al-Jaliya fi Al-Faridah Investigations” by Ibn Baz, deals with the subject of the science of religious duties in the Hanbali school of thought. The book focuses on studying the rulings and rules of inheritance, relying on Sharia texts and the sayings of scholars. The book includes various research and issues on the causes and aspects of inheritance, while providing scientific comments and benefits in this field.
descriptions.3226: This book is an investigation into the major jurisprudential rule, “No harm, no harm,” where the author begins by summarizing the Prophetic hadith on which this rule is based, and presents its various methods and chains of transmission with a discussion of their authenticity. The book then moves on to apply this rule to a number of jurisprudential issues and practical rulings, such as the rulings on wills, custody, the rights of spouses, and sales issues such as tawarruq and ‘inah, and an explanation of the controls for using rights and not harming others.
descriptions.3227: The book, “The Most Praiseworthy Saying about Rulings Concerning the Sanctity of the Mosque,” ​​deals with legal rulings related to preserving the sanctity of the mosque and preserving it from everything that is incompatible with its holiness. The author, Abdullah Al-Sahli, focuses on preventing the entry of those whose condition is not compatible with the sanctity of the mosque, such as hadiths, menstruating women, and polytheists. He also discusses the rulings on the entry of boys, the insane, and menstruating women, with an emphasis on maintaining the cleanliness of the mosque and glorifying its status.
descriptions.3228: The book “The Clear Speech Concerning the Mistakes of Worshipers” by the writer Mashhour Al Salman is a study of issues of worship that focuses on the mistakes that worshipers make in their clothing, the place and character of their prayer, based on a detailed index that includes chapters on errors related to clothing, the positions of prayer, and the performance of the pillars. It aims to alert the reader to violations of the Sunnah and duties related to prayer and to highlight their importance in Islam.
descriptions.3229: The book “Al-Qawl fi Ilm al-Astrology” by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi is a book of research and issues that deals with astronomy from an Islamic perspective, as it distinguishes between what is permissible in terms of knowing the names of the planets and their locations and what is prohibited in terms of using them in astrology. The author explains the contents of astrology, including the names of the planets, their constellations, locations, prayer times, and the direction of the Qiblah, based on the texts of the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of scholars. It aims to clarify the permissible benefits of this science and clarify what is desirable and what is disliked in dealing with it.
descriptions.3230: The book “The Wonderful Saying in Praying for the Beloved” by Sayyid Al-Shams Al-Din Al-Sakhawi is a scientific research that deals with the wording of the prayer for the beloved Prophet from linguistic, legal, and doctrinal aspects. The author reviews the definition of prayer from the linguistic and terminological aspects, and analyzes its rulings and details from vows to singling them out, clarifying the differences between the Prophet and the Messenger and the reasons for adding prayer to God and His angels. It includes detailed chapters on verifying the terms, mentioning the names of the Prophet, his wives, his descendants, and his family, with the parsing of the blessing in his words, which makes it an extensive reference in the field of research and issues related to praying for the Beloved.
descriptions.3231: The book “The Wonderful Saying about Praying for the Beloved Intercessor” by Al-Sakhawi covers various researches and issues about praying for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author focuses on defining the concept of prayer linguistically and terminologically, discusses its ruling and obligation, studies the merits of praying upon the Prophet, discusses the differences between the Prophet and the Messenger, reviews the reasons for wisdom in praying upon him, and explains some of the words used in praying upon him, such as the words “O God” and “ﷺ.” The book aims to provide a deep understanding of praying for the Prophet by discussing multiple jurisprudential and fundamental issues.
descriptions.3232: The book “The Great Sins” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab is a book in the category of research and issues. It includes an introductory introduction and then the text of the main book that deals with the topic of major sins in Islamic law according to the author’s vision. It is printed within the collection of the Sheikh’s works and is considered a reference that contributes to clarifying the concept of major sins and clarifying their rulings in accordance with the Salafi approach. The text aims to provide an accurate scientific study that helps researchers understand the Sheikh’s call and its objectives in this field.
descriptions.3233: The book “The Qur’an and the Sunnah, Their Impact, Status, and Necessity” by the writer Rabi’ bin Hadi Al-Madkhali is a study in the field of research and issues that sheds light on the role of the Qur’an and the Sunnah in establishing education within schools. The book deals with the influence of the Qur’an on the minds of Arabs and believers, and reviews the status of the Sunnah and its place in the souls of the nation, based on Qur’anic texts and prophetic hadiths. The author aims to show the importance of science in Islam and link this to the importance of applying religious values ​​in education curricula.
descriptions.3234: Al-Luma’a in Performing the Rak’ah to Perform the Friday Prayer by Suyuti is a jurisprudential study that deals with the issue of performing the Friday prayer when the second imam bows, and reviews the opinions of the three sheikhs of the Shafi’i school of thought regarding the continuation of prayer after the imam’s greeting. The book includes asking the question and formulating the answer, while clarifying the differences between jurists regarding the ruling on adding or difference before the greeting. The text focuses on clarifying the concept of awareness and explaining the necessary procedures for the person praying in that situation.
descriptions.3235: The book “Al-Lum’a fi the Characteristics of Friday” by Imam Al-Suyuti is a brief treatise that explores the characteristics and virtues that are specific to Friday and not any other day. The author begins by enumerating the particularities mentioned by Ibn al-Qayyim, then follows them up to collect them into one hundred particularities, reviewing their evidence from the Prophet’s hadiths and traces. The book falls within the research of jurisprudential and hadith issues, as it deals with rulings such as the dislike of singling out Friday for fasting, the virtue of washing and arriving early, reciting certain surahs in the morning, and other rulings and etiquette.
descriptions.3236: This book is brief on the rulings on acts of worship such as purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj. It extracts the most important rulings from approved books of jurisprudence and presents them in easy, accessible language. The book deals with jurisprudential issues related to worship in a question-and-answer style, and contains more than one thousand five hundred issues, designed to be a pocket size that is easy to carry and read.
descriptions.3237: The book “Debt” by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen is a jurisprudential study of the rulings on financial transactions, explaining the types of debt (selling the absent person for what is due or vice versa) and its divisions. The book begins by explaining the ruling on purchasing a commodity for a later period at a price in excess of its present price, whether for personal use or for trade, and states that this is permissible. It also discusses the ruling on taking current dirhams in exchange for something owed on a deferred basis, which is permissible peace, and discusses the methods used by people in debt.
descriptions.3238: The book “The Prophet’s Medina, Its Virtue, the Virtue of Its Residents, and Its Visit” by Abu Bakr Al-Jaza’iri is a research work that deals with the virtues of the Holy City and its position among the holy cities, with a focus on the merits of its people and residents, including immigrants and Ansar. The content is divided into chapters concerned with the merit and honor of the people of Medina, based on the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ in the text. The author aims to clarify the importance of respecting and appreciating the city and its inhabitants and to highlight its role in Islamic history.
descriptions.3239: This book deals with the topic of joking from a legal and social perspective, explaining its rulings and rulings, and what is permissible and what is not permissible in it. The author focuses on the need to be wise and moderate in joking, while warning against excessive amounts of it or exposure to sensitive or taboo issues. The book combines hadiths, jurisprudential sayings, wisdom, and proverbs to support his point of view on this topic.
descriptions.3240: The book “The Nine Issues” by the writer Hamid Mirza Al-Farghani is concerned with studying and settling nine jurisprudential and procedural issues through verifying hadiths and clarifying the legal rulings. It deals with topics such as wiping the socks and socks, proving the Sunnah of the Friday prayer, raising the hands when bowing, straightening the rows, using the rosary for those who remember, and other issues related to worship and etiquette. The book falls within the classification of research and issues, which shows its analytical and research nature in Islamic jurisprudence. The author aims to provide arguments based on Sharia texts to clarify rulings and clarify what is permissible and what is not permissible in these topics.
descriptions.3241: Jurisprudential Issues” by Ibn Qaddah is a reference that combines fatwas and jurisprudential issues based on the Maliki school of thought, and is concerned with detailing issues related to prayer, purity, fasting, zakat, sacrifices, marriage, sales, and other various topics. The book shows an analytical approach that raises jurisprudential questions and is based on the opinions of major jurists, while documenting legal positions according to reliable sources. It aims to guide the reader to the correct understanding of Sharia rulings and their application in various daily situations.
descriptions.3242: Important Issues: What a Contracting Contractor Needs When Engaging with Pampering is a research work in Islamic jurisprudence, written by Muhammad bin Ahmed al-Maqdisi, and is classified under research and issues. The book focuses on the fundamental issues that the contracter faces in the issue of pampered engagements, and includes an introduction and an investigation section that deals with the translation sources of the work. Through this investigation, the author aims to show the scientific wealth of the jurisprudential heritage and present it to the beneficiary reader.
descriptions.3243: Intoxicants and drugs is a jurisprudential research that sheds light on the position of Islamic law on intoxicating drinks and drugs, based on the principle of preserving reason and preventing harm. It deals with the prohibition of alcohol and the progression of legislation related to it, reviewing the prophetic evidence and the health and social effects of intoxicants. It also devotes chapters to drugs and scientists’ positions on them.
descriptions.3244: The book “What is permissible and what is forbidden in the mosque” by Sheikh Faleh bin Muhammad Al-Sagheer is a study of legal issues related to the behavior of worship and activities inside the mosque, and reviews what is permissible, desirable, and forbidden in prayers, sermons, seclusion, and teaching the Qur’an, in addition to the role of the mosque as a headquarters for fatwa and consultation and a shelter for the needy. The book also covers the provisions of mosque architecture, from choosing the land to the type of construction and accessories, with instructions for its maintenance and cleaning. This work is classified under research and issues, and its content is based on legal inferences and passages from religious texts.
descriptions.3245: This book deals with the subject of handshakes from a legal and social perspective, reviewing its ruling and special provisions for shaking hands with foreign women, the sick, and those in a state of impurity. It also studies the effect of shaking hands on ablution and its appropriate times, based on legal evidence and the wisdom behind these actions. The book aims to clarify the rulings on shaking hands and explain its ruling in various cases, with a focus on its importance in promoting Islamic morals and etiquette in society.
descriptions.3246: A book that collects fatwas and legal rulings related to the call to prayer and the muezzin, divided into seven sections covering the conditions for the call to prayer, its words, the description of the muezzin, the provisions for answering the call to prayer, and its invalidations and dislikes, with the last section devoted to explaining the violations and mistakes common among the muezzins. In preparing it, the author relied on realistic questions that he presented to Sheikh Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Jibreen, who presented the book and praised this effort.
descriptions.3247: This book is by Imam Al-Harith Al-Muhasibi, and it deals with various topics in Islamic jurisprudence and ethics, including permissible and forbidden gains, piety in transactions and behavior, and doubts in actions and etiquette. The author focuses on explaining the doctrines of the predecessors on these topics, and refers to God’s ruling in prohibiting some gains and the necessity of piety in transactions, while emphasizing the importance of adhering to what is permissible and staying away from what is forbidden. The book aims to guide Muslims towards correct behavior in their professional and financial lives, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and Qur’anic verses.
descriptions.3248: Al-Manasik by Ibn Abi Orouba is a book about the rituals of Hajj in the form of a question and answer, located in one part (158 questions in 114 pages)
descriptions.3249: The book “Verbal Prohibitions” by Ibn Uthaymeen specializes in clarifying words and terms prohibited in Islam, and explaining the ruling on their use and their effects on religious belief and practices. The book addresses various issues related to specific names, specific sayings and expressions, and discusses the ruling on their use from the perspective of Islamic law, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the words used in the Sunnah of the Prophet and avoiding what contradicts the correct doctrine.
descriptions.3250: The book deals with fatwas about the jurisprudence of jihad and Sharia politics, as it focuses on explaining the truth about jihad and its controls through the opinions of prominent scholars. Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Baz explains the ruling on attacking foreigners in Islamic countries, and stresses that it is absolutely not permissible to attack them, while Sheikh Saleh Al-Fawzan calls for the rejection of assassinations and bombings as a jihadi method, warning of their negative effects on Muslims.
descriptions.3251: The Curriculum for those Who Want to Umrah and Hajj by Ibn Uthaymeen is a book from the category of research and issues that specializes in explaining the methods of Hajj and Umrah in terms of etiquette and legal controls. In its chapters, the book deals with travel etiquette, women’s travel, the traveler’s prayer, timings, types of rituals, and conditions for the ihram and the sacrifice. It also explains the description of Umrah, the prescription of Hajj, and visiting the Prophet’s Mosque and its benefits. The author aims to guide the reader to sincerity in worship and adherence to the Sunnah of the Prophet by knowing the details of the rituals and controls related to them.
descriptions.3252: The book provides an extensive study of money in the Holy Qur’an from a legal and social perspective, based on the texts of the Qur’an and their interpretations. His book deals with multiple topics, including the rights of the poor, zakat, usury, good loans, women’s testimony, sources of earning, women’s work and the nation, and topics related to inheritance and justice in the distribution of wealth. It highlights the concept of money as a means owned by God and used by man in accordance with the teachings of Islam, with an emphasis on balancing individual and collective interests.
descriptions.3253: The book deals with specialized research on the man’s guardianship over the woman, its concept and wisdom, and discusses the concept of the wife’s righteousness and its impact on the lives of the spouses. The book also studies the concept of the wife's disobedience and how to treat it through gradual means such as preaching, abandonment, and beating, while addressing the role of arbitrators in resolving marital disputes and urging reconciliation between spouses as it is better than disagreement.
descriptions.3254: The book, “Al-Waraqat Concerning What Men and Women Differ,” written by Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Omari, is classified as research and jurisprudential issues. It sheds light on the differences between the sexes in the rulings on financial transactions, wills, guardianship, and other legal issues. His book deals with various topics, such as the signs of puberty, the ruling on paying money to a young man and a female slave, the spouses’ disposal of money, and the procedures for gifts and wills between children and spouses. The work aims to clarify the jurisprudential differences between men and women to strengthen religious understanding and clarify the relevant legal rulings.
descriptions.3255: The book “Guardianship in Marriage” by Awad bin Raja Al-Awfi is a jurisprudential research that deals with the concept of guardianship and a comparison of the legality of marriage in various cases, from the free woman in charge to the young, the insane, the foolish, and the slaves. In its chapters, the author presents detailed definitions and discussions about guardianship provisions in marriage, based on sectarian evidence and jurisprudential discussions. The book falls within the classification of research and issues, and targets researchers and scholars in the field of Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.3256: The book “Research on Contemporary Jurisprudential Issues” by Judge Muhammad Taqi Al-Othmani brings together a group of jurisprudential research that dealt with modern issues in Islamic law, as it addresses the provisions of installment sales, sale by contract and rental, futures contracts in goods, the provisions of banknotes and changes in the value of the currency, in addition to the topics of real estate financing, bank deposits, slaughter, imported meat, and other contemporary issues. The author aims to show how to derive jurisprudential rulings on new developments in light of Sharia principles.
descriptions.3257: The book “Researches and Fatwas on Wiping Over the Socks” by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen is concerned with studying the jurisprudential issues related to wiping over the socks, reviewing the opinions of scholars and their differences regarding the conditions for wiping, its types, duration, and the change in the condition of the person praying. The content is divided into three main sections: research on wiping over the socks, jurisprudential issues, and fatwas covering wiping over the socks, turbans, and splints. The book aims to clarify the legal rulings and provide practical guidance to Muslims in implementing this obligation.
descriptions.3258: This is a book by Imam Al-Suyuti explaining the ruling on starting a new row before completing the row before it in prayer, and he answered in it that this action is disliked and does not achieve the virtue of congregational prayer. In his fatwa, the author relies on the sayings of jurists and hadith scholars, and states that every bad thing in a group nullifies its virtue, while distinguishing between the virtue of weakening and the origin of the group’s blessing.
descriptions.3259: This book, “The Purpose of the Voluntary Prayer in Voluntary Prayer,” by Muhammad bin Omar Bazmoul, deals with the rulings on voluntary prayers and performing them according to the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book focuses on defining voluntary prayers, their types, and their virtues, relying on authentic hadiths and their explanations. It also explains the types of regular Sunnahs and their rulings, and deals with the night prayer, Witr, and other miscellaneous prayers. The book aims to bring closer the understanding of voluntary prayers for readers and facilitate access to their rulings by collecting them in one brief reference.
descriptions.3260: This book deals with the issue of divorce from a modern jurisprudential perspective, attempting to reconsider some of the jurisprudential issues related to it. The author focuses on the importance of studying this topic in depth due to its serious implications for Islamic society. The book also addresses the role of the Sunnah in clarifying the rulings on divorce, and points out the importance of multiple jurisprudential opinions in this field rather than being limited to one opinion. The book aims to provide a new understanding of the jurisprudential rules related to divorce, taking into account legal traditions and contemporary challenges.
descriptions.3261: The book “Insight of Those with Minds about the Heresy of Dividing Religion into Peel and Core” aims to respond to the idea of ​​dividing religion into peel and core, and shows that this division is heresy and misguidance. The book shows that adhering to the guidance of the Messenger of God - ﷺ - ​​is the correct guidance, and that paying attention to the apparent and hidden aspects of religion is an integral part of the Prophet’s guidance. The book warns of the danger of some Muslims being deceived by this division, and shows that the term “peel and peel” may seem compassionate on the surface, but it contains torment on the inside. The book presents a comprehensive vision of the concept of Prophetic guidance and adherence to it, and defends the importance of following the Sunnah of the Prophet in all aspects of life.
descriptions.3262: This book, written by Abdul Rahman bin Qasim, falls under the classification of research and issues, and deals with the subject of the ruling on shaving the beard in Islam. The book presents evidence from the Sunnah of the Prophet on the necessity of growing a beard and the prohibition of shaving or shortening it, citing the statements of a number of scholars on the issue. It also includes a chapter on the ruling on someone who intentionally shaves his beard in the belief that this is a solution, and concludes with fatwas related to the issue of shaving the beard.
descriptions.3263: This book, “Tuhfat al-Amin fi Man Whose Speech is Accepted Without an Oath,” by Al-Balqini, deals with multiple legal and judicial topics, including zakat, sale, mortgage, endowment, certificates, and other jurisprudential issues. The author focuses on the conditions for accepting a person’s testimony or confession without resorting to an oath, relying in doing so on legal evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book contains detailed research on various jurisprudential issues, and aims to provide a deep understanding of the jurisprudential rules related to legal transactions and rights.
descriptions.3264: A book that collects important answers to questions related to the five pillars of Islam, with a focus on issues of belief and monotheism. It explains the polytheistic and heretical violations that the public may fall into, such as those related to graves, swearing, vows, and supplication. Then it deals with the rulings on prayer and related jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.3265: An investigation of the preponderance of fasting on the day of doubt in Ramadan by the scholar Maree Al-Karmi is a research work in jurisprudence that specializes in the issue of fasting on the day of doubt in the month of Ramadan. It presents the opinions of the four imams and the sayings of the companions and is based on the evidence of the Hanbalis and other Islamic sources. The book deals with quoting the sayings of the Companions and the precautions required, then it reviews the clear evidence that governs fasting on this day, while providing answers to the various objections. The author aims to clarify jurisprudential rulings in a simplified and organized manner, based on traditional sources and references.
descriptions.3266: A book concerned with studying the times for which prayer is prohibited from a jurisprudential perspective, detailing the number of these times and their locations, and evaluating their rulings in terms of validity or nonexistence. It also addresses the issue of making up for missed prayers and obligatory prayers, funeral prayers, and the greeting of the mosque, in addition to the pillars of Ihram, circumambulation, and ablution, and reviews the times of eclipses and rainwater. It is based on Sharia texts and Islamic sources to provide a balancing vision that contributes to clarifying what prayers are permissible and what are not permissible in prayers during forbidden times.
descriptions.3267: Greetings to the Mosque by the writer Muhammad Zia al-Rahman al-Azami is a study in Islamic jurisprudence that deals with the issue of the obligation or recommendation of two rak’ahs before sitting in the mosque based on hadiths of the Prophet. The book sheds light on the different opinions of jurists and hadith scholars on the form of imperative and obligation, based on hadith sources from Al-Muwatta and Al-Jami’. The work aims to clarify the legal rulings related to this practice and show the evidence that supports it.
descriptions.3268: This reminder is concerned with the virtues of fasting and praying and details their rulings according to a research approach based on Salafi scientific sources. The book includes chapters that address the reality of fasting, its obligation, its virtues, and the characteristics of the month of Ramadan, in addition to the rulings on fasting in cases of travel, illness, and women, and what breaks the fasting person and what does not break his fast. It also sheds light on the virtue of night prayers, Ramadan prayers, and Laylat al-Qadr. The second part also deals with the provisions of Zakat al-Fitr, from its definition to its legitimacy and purposes. The author, Abdullah bin Saleh Al-Qaseer, presents what he collected from his sheikhs in a brief format aimed at benefit and guidance.
descriptions.3269: “Facilitating the Obligations” provides the reader with an opportunity to learn the provisions and rules of inheritance through its treatment of the entire jurisprudential rules related to the duties and inheritance. The book focuses on explaining the principles of the science of religious duties and detailing its branches, with reference to the reasons and contraindications for inheritance and the rules for dividing estates. The author aims to clarify God’s ruling on inheritance and demonstrate the validity of the rules stated in Islamic law in this field, while emphasizing the importance of following them and not violating them.
descriptions.3270: A book that explains the rulings of Hajj and Umrah in a simple manner, drawn from the books of ancient and contemporary scholars. It begins with an introduction to the virtues of the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, then addresses the obligation of Hajj and its virtues, the temporal and spatial timings, and the actions of Ihram and Umrah, then details the actions of Hajj from the day of Arafat to the days of Tashreeq, and concludes with a visit to the Prophet’s city.
descriptions.3271: This book, “Female Education and Upbringing,” by Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali, is considered one of the Islamic books that dealt with the subject of women’s education and upbringing under Islam. The book is divided into three different schools of thought regarding female education and upbringing, and the writer attempts to prove the validity of the first school of thought, which rejects teaching women to write and read, and considers them an excuse for corruption and disloyalty. The book is considered one of the books that dealt with the subject of women’s education and upbringing under Islam, and reflects the writer’s views on the importance of preserving women’s chastity and educating them according to the Islamic method.
descriptions.3272: The book Teaching Prayer by Abdullah Al-Zaid is a brief educational treatise that falls within research and issues of worship, aiming to explain the five pillars of Islam with a focus on prayer and its provisions. The book begins by explaining the meaning of the two testimonies and the importance of prayer, then goes on to detail the various types of purity rulings, the prescription for obligatory prayer, and the rulings for congregational, Friday, and traveler prayers, and concludes by mentioning the Sunnah remembrances and the obligatory Sunnahs.
descriptions.3273: “Dressing Back on Lively Issues” is a book by Saleh Bin Humaid that falls under the category of research and issues. It deals with a group of contemporary questions posed by religious and cultural institutions on topics such as equality, freedom, slavery, women, the application of Sharia, and other jurisprudential and social issues. The book relies on a review of Islamic sources and text-based answers to clarify Islamic positions in the face of criticism and allegations. It aims to provide scholarly responses to what the author considers intellectual attacks on Islam.
descriptions.3274: This book is brief on the science of religious duties. It aims to teach the division of inheritance according to Islamic law in an easy manner with illustrative examples. It begins by defining the obligations, their benefits, and their ruling, then moves on to explaining the rights related to the inheritance and its arrangement, the reasons for inheritance, its conditions, and its prohibitions. It reviews in detail the owners of the obligations and the amounts of their shares, in addition to the provisions of agnates, blocking, restitution, and relatives.
descriptions.3275: This book, “Tanwir al-Ghabash fi the Virtue of Sudan and Ethiopia,” by Sheikh Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, deals with the study of the virtues of the people of Sudan and Ethiopia from a religious and social perspective. The book is divided into twenty-eight chapters, each chapter dealing with a different topic related to the people of these regions, from their lineage and characteristics to the reasons for their dark colors. The book aims to clarify that virtues and good morals are the true measure of human value, not skin color or external appearance.
descriptions.3276: This is a book on the jurisprudence of hunting and its rulings, written by Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Ahmed Al-Tayyar, and falls within the framework of research and jurisprudential issues. The author aims to provide guidance and cautions to fishing enthusiasts, responding to questions posed to him at a fishing session. The book is divided into eight sections, dealing with basic rules, the definition of hunting and its ruling, rulings on the hunter and the hunted, hunting etiquette, and issues specific to lizard hunting and hunting with raptors, in addition to other important issues related to hunting.
descriptions.3277: The book “Three Treatises on Prayer” by the scholar Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz collects three treatises on the jurisprudence of prayer, the first on explaining how the Prophet ﷺ prayed in accordance with his command, “Pray as you have seen me pray,” the second on the obligation of performing prayer in congregation, and the third on the issue of placing the hands after rising from bowing. The book falls within the research and issues of worship, and in detailing the rulings it is based on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.3278: In his book “A Tour of the Books of Songs and the Yamani Sword,” Sheikh Muhammad Al-Majzoub presents an in-depth critical research on the book “Al-Aghani” by the expert Abu Al-Faraj Al-Isfahani, examining the facts and fabrications contained in the book. Al-Majzoub focuses on revealing the malicious methodology followed by the songwriter, and discusses his impact on shaping the historical image of the Abbasid era and beyond. The book also addresses the contradictions of the songs and its accusations against prominent historical figures, and also reviews the school of criticism that arose around this book.
descriptions.3279: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah deals with the rulings on the obligatory dress during prayer for both men and women, based on Sharia evidence that requires men to cover their shoulders during prayer, and not just cover the private parts. The author criticizes the neglect of many worshipers about this duty, and explains that God is more deserving of the servant beautifying himself in his prayers.
descriptions.3280: This book deals with the rulings and etiquette of women according to what is stated in the Qur’an and the Sunnah, explaining the good sayings revealed by the laws and commanded by women, and the bad actions that the Qur’an and Sunnah forbid. The author focuses on the hadiths and verses that are specific to women, while touching on the rulings common to men and women. The book aims to clarify the roles and responsibilities that women must carry out according to Islamic law, while providing explanations of some verses and hadiths related to women.
descriptions.3281: This book is a message explaining the right of the neighbor in Islam, in which the author collected the Prophetic hadiths contained in the virtue of being kind to the neighbor and honoring him, and prohibiting harming him. The book falls within the general classification of research and issues, and reviews multiple texts from the Sunnah of the Prophet revolving around this topic, mentioning the methods and chains of transmission of the narration.
descriptions.3282: This book examines the status of animal welfare in Islamic law, and establishes it as a legal principle and worship, comparing this to man-made laws that were established late on purely moral foundations. The book reviews jurisprudential rulings that define animal rights, and warns against abuse of rights such as slaughter, riding, and loading, considering animal abuse a sin.
descriptions.3283: The book “The Truth about Impeachment: An Applied Theoretical Study” by Dr. Abdullah bin Abdul Wahed Al-Khamis deals with the issue of impeachment from a theoretical and applied jurisprudential perspective. The book aims to clarify the truth about dismissal, its conditions and pillars, while addressing the different forms and types of dismissal. The research also addresses the jurisprudential adaptation of dismissal and discusses the differences between jurists in this regard. Through this work, the author aims to provide a comprehensive and objective study of the impeachment, away from a brief sectarian approach, with a focus on the practical aspects of the issue.
descriptions.3284: A book of research and issues that presents the concept of jihad in Islam and is based on the texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah to clarify the obligation of jihad and determine who should wage jihad and how to call and fight. It also addresses the prohibition of departing from the Muslim ruler and presents arguments in this regard, while clarifying an alternative to takfir groups. The author concludes with a comprehensive analysis of the topic in a conclusion that summarizes the above.
descriptions.3285: This book is a brief study into the reality of magic and its ruling in Islam. It aims to explain the danger of resorting to charlatans and sorcerers, and to root the issue in the Qur’an and Sunnah. It begins by defining magic linguistically and legally and explaining its types. Then it discusses its reality and whether it has a real effect or is it just imagination, reviewing the sayings of the Sunnis and the Mu’tazilites on that matter. It also explains the ruling on learning, teaching, and working with magic, the punishment of the magician in this world and the hereafter, and the conditions for his repentance, and concludes with an explanation of the ruling on treating magic (al-Nashra) and its legal description.
descriptions.3286: This book examines the issue of paying Zakat al-Fitr in cash instead of in kind, which is a contemporary jurisprudential issue common in many Islamic countries. The research reviews the concept of value in Zakat al-Fitr, the ruling on this obligation, the wisdom behind its legislation and its amount, then it details the doctrines of jurists regarding the ruling on paying it in cash, relying on legal evidence and a descriptive, inductive approach.
descriptions.3287: This is a jurisprudential book that addresses the issue of representation as a contemporary issue. It reviews its reality, history, types, and purposes. Then, it explains the jurisprudential understanding of its legal ruling, and responds to the suspicions of those who permit it, relying on the texts and rules of the Sharia, and pointing to the positions of scholars regarding it from the past centuries.
descriptions.3288: This book is a study into the ruling on magic and divination and what is related to them. It shows the danger of these practices to Islam and Muslims, and clarifies the difference between legitimate treatment for ordinary reasons and going to priests and sorcerers. The author also addresses issues such as the wife’s magic against the husband, the ruling on asking witches, and treatment by a popular doctor who uses the jinn, with an explanation of the legitimate treatment for witchcraft, and clarification of the right for the jinn to enter into humans.
descriptions.3289: The book “The Ruling on Reciting the Qur’an for the Dead” by Al-Shuqayri is an investigation into a legal issue related to the reward for reciting the Qur’an reaching the dead. The author reviews the sayings of the commentators, imams of hadith, the four schools of thought, and scholars of fundamentals on this issue, relying on evidence from the Sunnah of the Prophet to explain what the deceased benefits from after his death. The book concludes that what is prescribed in visiting graves is to pray and ask forgiveness for the dead, and not to recite the Qur’an to them.
descriptions.3290: This is a book explaining the ruling on building polytheistic churches and temples in Muslim countries. Its author collected evidence from the Prophet’s hadiths, antiquities, and texts of the four schools of thought, declaring the prohibition of that and the necessity of demolishing what was created, while singling out the Arabian Peninsula for a more severe ruling. The book concluded with two letters by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim, and comes in response to what was published in some newspapers regarding the permissibility of establishing churches in Islamic countries.
descriptions.3291: This is a book on a major jurisprudential issue, which is the ruling on one who neglects prayer, and the author has classified it as research and issues. It begins with an introduction in which he explains the importance of the issue and the large amount of disagreement regarding it among scholars, ancient and modern. Then the book is divided into two chapters: the first on the ruling on one who abandons prayer, and the second on what results from apostasy by abandoning prayer or otherwise. In the first chapter, the author reviews the sayings of the four imams on the issue, then refers the disagreement to the Qur’an and Sunnah to explain the most correct ruling according to him.
descriptions.3292: This book is a jurisprudential research that addresses the issue of repeatedly holding congregational prayers in one mosque, and reviews the opinions of jurists in cases of permissibility and prohibition, detailing the rulings related to mosques that have regular imams and those that do not, based on the statements of the various jurisprudential schools of thought.
descriptions.3293: This book is a study into the ruling on smoking tobacco from a legal perspective, explaining its prohibition based on Qur’anic and Prophetic evidence that forbids evil things and forbids harm. It also addresses the issue of the imamate of someone who openly smokes during prayer, and the validity of his imamate with other sinners. The book concludes with an important report on the topic of smoking.
descriptions.3294: This book examines the characteristics and components of the Islamic economy compared to positive economic systems, especially the socialist system. The author begins by criticizing the material foundations of the socialist economy based on class conflict and the denial of individual ownership, then moves on to explain the Islamic approach based on moderation and justice in production and spending. It also discusses Islam's view of money and its uses, and concludes by stating the advantage of Islamic economics over other systems.
descriptions.3295: This modest research is about the Friday sermon in the Qur’an and Sunnah. It was written based on a commission from the Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Endowments, Da’wah and Guidance to participate in the first forum for imams and preachers. The book begins with an introduction to the status of the Friday sermon in Islam. Then, in its five chapters, it deals with the types of sermons, the Friday sermon in the Holy Qur’an, the recipe for the Prophet’s sermon ﷺ and examples of it, and jurisprudential issues related to the sermon, such as listening to it, crossing necks, and sleeping during it, and it concludes with whispers and warnings to the Friday preacher.
descriptions.3296: This is a jurisprudential book that discusses the provisions of the Friday sermon, based on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It begins by defining the sermon and the Friday prayer and its ruling, then discusses in detail the conditions of the sermon such as the intention, time, standing, speaking loudly, and loyalty, leading to an explanation of its pillars such as praise, blessings upon the Prophet, the sermon, and reading the Qur’an. The author aims to clarify what should be included in the sermon according to the approach of the Salaf, with a focus on the practical and preaching aspects.
descriptions.3297: This book examines the topic of the Friday sermon as an effective means of advocacy and education. It reviews its basic components, such as the sermon being short and including verses, hadiths, proverbs, and stories, with an emphasis on the necessity of defining the topic and preparing it well, and adopting the good method that avoids defamation, exaggeration, exaggeration, and despair. It also highlights the importance of preaching and urging piety in the sermon, based on the fact that sermon is a tool for change and influence in souls since the time of the prophets, noting that its success is not achieved simply by ascending the pulpit, but rather requires practice, preparation, and knowledge.
descriptions.3298: This is a research book that deals with the subject of empowerment on earth, based on verse 41 of Surat Al-Hajj, and reviews the four pillars upon which the Muslim state is based, which are establishing prayer, paying zakat, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. The author moves from an explanatory study of the Noble Verse, the reasons for its revelation, and the commentators’ sayings about it, to detailing the nature of each pillar and its importance. Then, he links this to the application of these pillars in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia since the era of its first founder, King Abdul Aziz, with an explanation of the fruits of this application.
descriptions.3299: The book “Defending Islamic Punishments” is a legal study that aims to explain the wisdom of punishments in Islamic law and respond to the criticisms directed at it. The author begins by defining crime linguistically and terminologically, then reviews Islam’s view of it, emphasizes that punishment is a social necessity, and explains the wisdom behind it, to finally answer the question of whether Islamic punishments are harsh, in the context of comparing them to man-made laws.
descriptions.3300: The book “Defending Sin in the Issue of Recitation” by Al-Suyuti is a jurisprudential research that addresses the issue of the supplications mentioned when rising from bowing in prayer, as it explains the Shafi’i doctrine of the desirability of combining the sayings “God hears those who praise Him” and “Our Lord, praise be to You” for the imam, the one praying behind him, and the one praying alone, and it presents the opinions of other schools of thought such as Abu Hanifa, Malik, and Ahmad on this issue. The book is organized into nine sections in which the author presents evidence and jurisprudential discussions about the arguments based on the Prophetic hadiths, such as the hadiths of Abu Hurairah and Aisha, to clarify the most correct opinion on this issue of worship.
descriptions.3301: This book deals with the provisions of Hajj and Umrah and visiting the Prophet’s Mosque ﷺ, and provides detailed guidance on how to perform them correctly while pointing out common mistakes that must be avoided. It focuses on the importance of religious awareness and practical guidance for pilgrims and Umrah performers to ensure the performance of their duties in the manner commanded, while providing practical advice and important commandments for those who intend to perform these acts of worship.
descriptions.3302: This research deals in detail with the permission to break the fast when traveling during the month of Ramadan, reviewing its linguistic and legal meaning, explaining the amount of distance permitted for it, the jurisprudential disagreement over whether it is a permission or an intention, and the preference of fasting or breaking the fast for the able traveler. It also examines the implications of adopting this permission, such as how to make up for it, the rule of successiveness in it, and the ruling on someone who neglects to make up until another Ramadan catches up with him or he dies, within the framework of the rule of removing hardship and tolerance in Islamic law.
descriptions.3303: This book is the first collection of the letters of Imam Ibn Hazm Al-Andalusi, and it includes four main treatises: “The Dove’s Ring on Familiarity and Thousands,” which deals with love, its conditions and motives, a treatise on healing souls, a treatise on the rule of entertaining singing, and a treatise on the soul’s knowledge of others and its ignorance of itself. These letters represent a summary of Ibn Hazm’s intellectual and life experiences, and vary between personal philosophy, jurisprudential issues, and intellectual dialogue. They gained wide fame, especially the letter “Tawq al-Hamamah,” which was translated into multiple languages.
descriptions.3304: This is a message explaining the legal ruling on the hijab for Muslim women, written by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen. The author reviews the evidence of the obligation of hijab from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and analogy, then presents the evidence of those who permitted uncovering the face and responds to it, with the aim of removing doubt about the ruling on covering the face and showing that it is a legal obligation and not just a habit.
descriptions.3305: This is a brief message explaining the natural bleeding that affects women, namely menstruation, istihaadah, and postpartum, and its legal rulings. The author explains the meaning of each type, its wisdom, and its duration, then explains the rulings on menstruation related to prayer, fasting, circumambulation, intercourse, and others. Then he discusses istihaadah and its rulings, post-partum bleeding, its duration and rulings, and concludes with an explanation of the ruling on using something that prevents menstruation or brings it on, or prevents or aborts pregnancy, relying in this on the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.3306: This is a message explaining the ruling on zakat on permissible jewellery, in which the author presents the disagreement among scholars on the issue based on five opinions, then he prefers the opinion that zakat is obligatory on it if it reaches the quorum every year, citing the Qur’an, Sunnah and narrations.
descriptions.3307: This is a brief message on the rulings on prostration of forgetfulness in prayer, aiming to correct the common mistakes made by many worshipers and imams regarding the places and causes of prostration of forgetfulness. The author explains that there are three reasons for prostration of forgetfulness: excess, deficiency, and doubt, and explains the ruling for each case in detail, explaining the special rulings that result from the prayer being prayed in prayer.
descriptions.3308: This book collects two letters by Ibn Baz related to the rulings on prayer. The first is entitled “How to Pray the Prophet ﷺ”, and explains the nature of the Prophet’s prayer from ablution to submission based on the Sunnah. As for the second message, its subject is the obligation to perform prayer in congregation, and an explanation of its legal ruling. The book falls within the research and issues of practical worship.
descriptions.3309: A book that collects seventy prophetic hadiths on the virtue of jihad for the sake of God and its rulings, divided into chapters that include affirming the obligation of jihad, explaining the status of the martyr, the virtue of sincere intentions in it, and spending, bonding, and guarding for the sake of God. The author aims to bring together the legal texts related to this topic, relying on the hadiths narrated from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the virtue of early morning and soul for the sake of God, the guarantee of Paradise for the mujahid, and an explanation that martyrdom is not limited to killing in battle.
descriptions.3310: This book examines the issue of intoxicants and drugs from the perspective of Islamic advocacy. It provides a definition of them and an explanation of their types, then reviews their legal ruling based on the Sunnah of the Prophet, the general rules of Sharia, and the consensus of jurists. The book also discusses the wisdom of prohibiting it, and explains the approach followed by the Islamic call to prevent it, by deepening respect for God’s command, instilling a sense of its ugliness, social control, and applying legal punishments.
descriptions.3311: This book is an investigation and study of the explanation of “The Important Chapters on the Inheritance of the Ummah” by the tribe of al-Mardini. It is a book on the science of religious duties (inheritance), which is considered one of the most important legal sciences. The work consists of two parts: a study section that deals with the life of the author and the original author (Ibn al-Haym), a description of the manuscripts, and the approach to the book, and a second section is the text of the edited book itself, which begins with a statement of the rights related to the estate. The book aims to revive this important jurisprudential body in the provisions of inheritance according to Islamic law.
descriptions.3312: This book addresses the issue of the legitimacy of transactions conducted by contemporary Islamic banks, and discusses the fundamental differences between the Islamic bank and the usurious bank in terms of purpose and method. The author focuses on criticizing some of the practical practices in these banks, especially with regard to Murabaha sales, specifying the conditions for its dissolution and prohibition, and indicating the aspects of fraud that may be involved in it. The book aims to evaluate the progress of Islamic banks to comply with the provisions of Sharia in earning and investing.
descriptions.3313: This book is a brief treatise on the jurisprudence of prayer, in which the author explains the nine conditions of prayer, its fourteen pillars, and its eight duties, based on evidence from the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book falls within the research and issues of worship, and explains the provisions of purity and ablution and the conditions and obligations related to them.
descriptions.3314: This book is a scientific research into the issue of traveling to visit the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, and it falls within the scope of research and jurisprudential issues. The author presents his opinion on the ruling on this issue, and discusses what he sees as errors in opposing opinions, relying on Sharia evidence and discussing the issue through several main topics.
descriptions.3315: The book “Ramadan Pages” by Abdul Karim bin Sunaitan Al-Omari, which is one of the books that deals with the topic of the blessed month of Ramadan. Through it, the author aims to remind Muslims of what they should be like in this month, combining advice and guidance derived from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and the words of the Salaf. The book covers a number of issues and virtues related to Ramadan, such as the virtues of fasting and praying, the etiquette of suhoor and iftar, and the rulings on zakat and Umrah, while noting some common violations such as extravagance and smoking.
descriptions.3316: This book is a jurisprudential research specializing in Tarawih prayer. It begins by defining it linguistically and explaining the encouragement to perform prayers in Ramadan. Then it deals with the ruling on Tarawih prayer in congregation, reviews the hadith of Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), and studies in detail the number of its rak’ahs, with a focus on studying the narrations narrated on the authority of Omar ibn Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) in this regard.
descriptions.3317: This book is a specialized jurisprudential study that deals with the prayer of repentance and the rulings related to it in Islamic jurisprudence. It begins with a preface about God’s mercy through repentance and not requiring the killing of oneself to be accepted, as was the case in previous nations.
