The book is indispensable for any researcher or amateur of gemstones. He also wrote about metals, specifically: mercury, gold and its metals, silver, copper, iron, isrba, and others.
descriptions.3454: This is a book on logic, written by the author to set the rules and rulings of logic in brief sentences. The book begins by defining the meaning of the word (conformity, inclusion, and commitment), and then deals with the division of words into singular and compound, total and partial, genus, type, and separation, and specific and general presentation. The book aims to present basic logic issues in a focused manner.
descriptions.3455: This is a book on logic by Abu Al-Walid Ibn Rushd. It examines analogy, its types and forms, beginning with the definition of the premise and its divisions in terms of quantity and quality, then moving on to detailing the statement about the reflection of the premises and the combination of analogy in its three forms, with a study of the mixing of necessary, existential and possible premisses. The book aims to achieve the goal of the science of analogy, which is to reach proof and obtain demonstrative knowledge of existing beings.
descriptions.3456: This is a brief book on logic, written by Sheikh Muhammad bin Arafa al-Tunisi. Through it, the author aims to collect the rules of logic in a concise manner, in response to his students’ need to understand the logical terms that later scholars mixed with their speech in other sciences, especially in matters of jurisprudence. The book begins by defining science and its sections of perception and belief, analyzing and discussing the opinions of scientists on these basic concepts.
descriptions.3457: This is a manuscript on the interpretation of dreams and interpretation of visions, written by Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Ghannam al-Hanbali al-Mu’bar, and arranged in the alphabetical order of the dictionary to facilitate research for the reader. The book begins with an introduction that includes fourteen articles on the nature of the dream, the etiquette of the dreamer and the sleeper, and the sections and times of the dream. Then it begins to explain what the sleeper sees, arranged according to the letter with which the viewer begins or the word spoken in the dream.
descriptions.3458: This book is a summary of the art of rhetoric according to the method of Aristotle, in which the author explains the relationship of rhetoric and argumentation and that they are two rhetorical art directed at others, and a person does not use them with himself as proof. The book makes it clear that this industry requires constant skill and knowledge of the causes of actions to achieve mastery. It deals with statements that anticipate rhetorical confirmation, such as pronouns, with detail in their topics such as praise, blame, complaint, and apology, and the conditions of those being addressed, such as the morals of young people and the elderly.
descriptions.3459: Hayy Bin Yaqzan is a novel that tells the story of a person called Hayy Bin Yaqzan who grew up on an island alone. It symbolizes man and his relationship with the universe and religion. It contained philosophical contents, and was co-authored by several Arab and Muslim writers. The first author of the story of Hayy Bin Yaqzan was the philosopher Ibn Sina. He wrote it during his imprisonment, then it was reconstructed by Sheikh Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi, after which it was rewritten by the Andalusian philosopher Ibn Tufayl, and then it was the last novel. The story was written by Ibn al-Nafis, who noticed some of the original contents of Ibn Sina’s narration, which did not agree with his doctrine, so he reformulated it to be Hayy bin Yaqzan’s narration on the authority of Salih bin Kamil. The most famous author among these four to whose name the story is attached is Ibn Tufayl. …
descriptions.3460: This book collects a number of philosophical treatises by Ibn Bajjah, dealing with various topics in philosophy and science, such as the nature of natural longing, the dispositional soul, unity and oneness, in addition to discussions in the science of form and astronomy, and criticism of the opinions of some scholars such as Al-Zarqala and Ibn Al-Haytham. The book also includes correspondence and articles on music and proof, which reflects the author's interest in the various fields of knowledge of his time.
descriptions.3461: This is a treatise on psychology by the Andalusian philosopher Ibn Rushd Al-Hafid, aiming to present the opinions of commentators on this science in accordance with the principles of Aristotle and naturalism. The author begins with an account of the material principles upon which the study of the soul is based, such as the structure of matter and form, and the nature of simple bodies and the spheres. Then he moves on to detail the psychic powers, starting with the nourishing and sensitive powers and the five senses, all the way to the speaking and inclining powers, addressing the topics of the physical and intelligible forms.
descriptions.3462: This book, “Zij al-Sabi,” by Al-Battani, deals with advanced astronomical and mathematical topics, focusing on astronomical calculations and the movement of the planets and stars. The book deals with the division of the astronomical circle and knowing its chords, as well as the inclination of the zodiac and its effect on astronomical calculations. The book also studies the properties of parallel lines, the height of the pole, and the increase in daylight, while presenting mathematical methods to understand these astronomical phenomena. The book aims to present astronomy in an organized and accurate manner, while correcting some errors found in previous astronomy books.
descriptions.3463: Explanation of the Anatomy of the Law by Ibn Sina A manuscript explaining the science of anatomy in the book The Canon of Medicine by Ibn Sina, written by the Arab physician Ibn al-Nafis in the thirteenth century. The manuscript was discovered in 1924 in the archives of the Prussian State Library in Berlin, Germany. Contains the earliest descriptions of the coronary circulation and the pulmonary circulatory system.
descriptions.3464: A book that combines philosophical and spiritual reflections on the nature of dreams and their relationship to the material and spiritual life of man. It begins with a theoretical introduction to the concept of man as a small circle in the larger universe, then moves to a section for questions and responses about what a dream is and how to interpret it. The book includes a dictionary of dream terms arranged alphabetically, starting with the letter Alif, to include symbolic interpretations of various visions, people, and things that may occur in a dream.
descriptions.3465: This is a book in which its author summarized the essence of the words of the ancient and later sages in mentioning precious gems with their types and qualities, addressing their known minerals, their value and properties. The book is divided into sections that include talking about rubies in their colors and ranks, balkhash, pajadi, diamonds, pearls, emeralds, aquamarines, turquoise, crystals, dahans, jasper, fazhar, and kharut, mentioning the characteristics and defects of each gem.
descriptions.3466: The book “The Seasons in the Seasons of the Arabs” by Ibn Qutaybah Al-Dinouri is a book on the science of the seasons, which is an ancient science that links the phases of the moon, the seasons of the Arabs, and weather conditions. The book explains the names of the twenty-eight phases of the moon and their forms, the meaning of the storm, how the stars rise and set, and the Arabs’ relationship with the percentage of rain to them. It also deals with the four seasons of the year among the Arabs, and mentions the famous zodiac signs and planets such as the daughters of the coffin and the two eagles, which makes it a reference in popular astronomy and traditional meteorology.
descriptions.3467: A book on the science of interpreting visions and dreams. Its author aims to establish this science legally and explain its legitimacy. The book is organized into sections and chapters that deal with seeing the Divine Self, the Throne, and the Throne, then seeing the angels, the heavens, the spheres, the planets, night, and day, all the way to the vision of the Resurrection and its signs, Heaven, and Hell. In his material, the author relies on the books of the predecessors and the sayings of the respected sheikhs in this field.
descriptions.3468: Signs and Warnings is one of Ibn Sina's last books, written in Arabic.
descriptions.3469: Approximation to the definition of logic and the introduction to it with colloquial words and jurisprudential examples is a book on logic written by Imam Ibn Hazm Al-Andalusi (d. 456 AH). It is considered one of the most important contributions of Muslim scholars to writing logic in the Arabic language, as the author Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali preceded it in linking logic and the principles of jurisprudence. His student Al-Humaidi said: “The same applies to the Book of Approximation to the Limits of Logic, which is introduced to it with colloquial words and jurisprudential examples. In its clarification, the removal of misconceptions about it, and the disbelief of those who disagree with it, it followed a method that no one had followed before it, as far as we have learned.”
descriptions.3470: Al-Hawi on Medicine is considered one of the most important books of Abu Bakr al-Razi. It has been described as a great encyclopedia of medicine that contains many summaries from Greek and Indian authors, in addition to his precise observations and his own experiences. Al-Hawi was translated from Arabic into Latin and printed for the first time in Brescia in northern Italy in 1486. It was reprinted several times in Venice in the sixteenth century AD. Al-Razi’s skill is evident in this huge work. Al-Razi’s historians almost agree that the book was not written by himself, but by his students. who completed it.
descriptions.3471: This book is a huge medical encyclopedia written by Ibn al-Nafis, dealing with the medical industry and dealing with medicines and foods. The book includes multiple parts, some of which exist and some of which are still missing. Each part is devoted to an independent topic and is linked to the rest of the parts. The existing content begins with a study of individual drugs arranged in alphabetical order, devoting articles and chapters to each drug that discuss its nature, nature, and actions in various organs of the body.
descriptions.3472: The book “Food and Nutrition” by Abdul Rahman Musaiqer is a scientific work that falls within university medical textbooks, and aims to provide basic knowledge in the science of nutrition and its relationship to health and development. The book covers various topics, including the structure of the human body, digestive systems, and food components such as carbohydrates, proteins, and vitamins, in addition to balanced nutrition and meal planning. This book was published as part of efforts to Arabize medical and health sciences, to be an educational reference in the Arabic language for students and teachers in educational institutions.
descriptions.3473: The Canon of Medicine is a medical encyclopedia divided into five volumes written by the Muslim scholar, physician, and philosopher Ibn Sina, published in 1020 AD. The book is considered one of the influential and authoritative works in the field of medicine in the world, as it was adopted as a basic reference for teaching medicine in many universities until the eighteenth century. …
descriptions.3474: This is a book on the history of modern philosophy. It begins by presenting the stage of transition from the Middle Ages to the modern era, addressing the intellectual currents of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Then it moves on to detailing the mothers of philosophical schools of thought in the seventeenth century by studying their figures such as Bacon, Descartes, and Spinoza, and concludes with an analysis of philosophy in the eighteenth century in England, France, and Germany, all the way to the philosophy of Immanuel Kant.
descriptions.3475: A book on the interpretation of visions and dreams. Its author arranged it alphabetically in the dictionary to facilitate research in it, and made it extensive after seeing a brief book on this topic by Ibn Ghannam. It begins with an introduction to the importance of good vision and its relationship to revelation, then proceeds to explain the images and things that the sleeper sees, arranged alphabetically from A to Z, with a conclusion to the book.
descriptions.3476: A book on the interpretation of dreams attributed to Ibn Sirin, and classified among other sciences. It begins with an introduction to dividing visions into what is from God and what is from Satan, based on the Prophet’s hadith. Through its many chapters, the book deals with the interpretation of the servant’s vision of his Lord, the angels, and the Companions, and extends to include the interpretation of the vision of the surahs of the Qur’an, acts of worship such as prayer and fasting, and conditions of the afterlife such as Resurrection, Paradise, and Hell, in addition to visions of man and his organs, animals, kings, craftsmen, and other various topics.
descriptions.3477: This is a book on Aristotelian logic, examining sophistical fallacies that give the illusion that they are valid proofs, but in reality they are misleading. The author explains the difference between true analogy and fallacious analogy, and details the reasons that lead to this confusion, the most important of which is what exposes meanings through words.
descriptions.3478: The Incoherence of Philosophers is a book by Imam Al-Ghazali. Some considered this book a blow to what some described as the arrogance of philosophers and their claim to reach the truth in unseen matters with their minds. Al-Ghazali declared in his book The Incoherence of the Philosophers the failure of philosophy to find an answer to the nature of the Creator, and declared that the topics of philosophy’s interests must remain in measurable and observable issues such as medicine, mathematics, and astronomy. Al-Ghazali considered the attempt of philosophers to perceive something that cannot be perceived by human senses to be fundamentally inconsistent with the concept of philosophy. …
descriptions.3479: This is a book on the interpretation of visions and dreams, compiled by its author from the books of previous scholars and arranged into sections and chapters. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue and importance of visions, then deals with the interpretation of seeing God Almighty, the throne, the chair, the tablet, and the pen, followed by the interpretation of seeing angels, prophets, and companions, then seeing the Resurrection and its signs, heaven and hell, seeing the sky, sun, moon, and stars, and other topics related to the interpretation of dreams.
descriptions.3480: This book is an Arabic translation of the book “Principles of Philosophy” by the philosopher René Descartes, by Othman Amin. The book provides an organized presentation of the principles of Cartesian philosophy in the form of claims and results. Descartes wrote it in response to the campaign launched against him by supporters of traditional scholastic philosophy. The first part of the book includes discussions on the principles of human knowledge, along with letters and dedications from the author and translator.
descriptions.3481: The book “Developmental Psychology from the Fetus to Old Age” by Adel Al-Ashwal is a foundational study in the field of developmental psychology, dealing with the development of human behavior across the different stages of life. The book begins with a historical and theoretical introduction that introduces the psychology of development and its importance, then reviews the determinants of behavior such as maturity, learning, and heredity, and moves on to a detailed explanation of the stages of development, starting from pre-birth until old age. The book also provides an analysis of the most prominent influential theories in this field, such as the theories of Piaget, Kohlberg, Freud, and Erikson, in addition to the research methods and tools used in studying development.
descriptions.3482: The book “Psychology of Development” by author Hassan Mustafa Abdel Moati is a work in the field of psychology, which studies and analyzes the subject of human growth from its various aspects. In its first part, the book presents the foundations and theories of growth, beginning with an explanation of the nature of human growth, its laws and principles, then it delves into the issue of the interaction between heredity and environment and their influence on shaping behavior, and concludes by presenting the research approaches and methods used in this field.
descriptions.3483: The chapter on the connection between wisdom and Sharia is an Islamic philosophical essay written by the Andalusian Muslim and philosopher Ibn Rushd (1126–1198), in which he "examines the alleged tension between philosophy and religion" and concludes that in fact philosophy (in particular, Aristotle's philosophy) is not opposed to but in fact works alongside Islamic philosophy. In the essay, Ibn Rushd argues that some Muslims are obligated to study philosophy, and that this subject should be considered an Islamic science. The essay also contains several other unique insights, including Ibn Rushd's assertion "that the Qur'an must sometimes be read non-literally." …
descriptions.3484: This is a book on the science of dream interpretation, compiled by its author in response to a request from a group of people, and he arranged it into an introduction to the rules of this science that includes fourteen chapters, then into sections that deal with mentioning what the sleeper sees in the sky, earth, animals, and other things, with an explanation of their meanings and interpretations.
descriptions.3485: The Touchstone of Consideration is a book on logic written by Imam Al-Ghazali (died: 505 AH). Imam Al-Ghazali’s book Touchstone of Consideration is distinguished in that it is considered a turning point that followed the standard of science, establishing this complete digestion of logic and transforming it into Eastern Islamic meanings in a complete Arabic language. The book's research revolves around traditional logic topics: limit, proposition, and analogy. The book “The Touchstone of Consideration” differs from Al-Ghazali’s previous books, such as “The Objectives of the Philosophers” and “The Criterion of Science.” In it, the Imam took a different approach to the traditional terminology of logic and delved deeper into the Islamic contents and Arabic, jurisprudential, and theological terminology. The study of the limit in the test is divided into two main topics that fall within the two sections of the book. …
descriptions.3486: The book “A Summary of Medicine, Treatment with Food and Herbs” by Abd al-Malik ibn Habib is a work on prophetic medicine and treatment. It combines the hadiths contained in urging treatment and prescriptions for herbs and foods. The book covers various topics, such as cupping, its places and times, and the treatment of diseases such as fever, headaches, and leprosy, with an explanation of what medicines are permissible and forbidden. The book includes chapters on ensuring the doctor and healing wounds, based on traces narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ and the imams of the predecessors.
descriptions.3487: The standard of science in the art of logic by Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali
descriptions.3488: A book on the methodology of scientific research in political science. It begins by presenting the major philosophical schools and the development of the concept of philosophy from ancient times until the modern era, passing through the Islamic research method and the Ibn Khaldun method. Then it deals with the liberal concept of research approaches and methods, touching on historical, economic and social approaches, and analyzing political phenomena such as power and decision-making. It concludes by presenting the Marxist concept of research methods, to constitute a foundational reference in the origins of political research.
descriptions.3489: The book "Human Development from the Fetal Stage to the Elderly Stage" is a study in developmental psychology, tracing the human journey from formation to old age. In classifying the stages of growth, the author relies on the Qur’anic division of life into two stages of weakness separated by a stage of strength, moving away from the traditional division. The book reviews the general foundations of human development, and examines the origins of this science in Western culture, while presenting an Islamic point of view based on the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the heritage of Muslim scholars.
descriptions.3490: A book on the science of hadith grading and the study of chains of transmission. It explains the concept of grading linguistically and terminologically, explains the types of attribution, original and secondary books, and details the methods of grading prophetic hadiths, such as looking at the chain of transmission, knowing the companions, and seeking help from chains of narration, dictionaries, excerpts, and indexes. It also deals with the sections of the hadith in terms of acceptance and response, ruling on the hadith and the text, and the benefits of the science of graduation and its ranks, with advice for students of knowledge in this field.
descriptions.3491: A book on Hadith terminology, compiled by its author from the books of the Imams of Hadith to be a curriculum for second-year students at the Islamic University in Sadiqabad, Pakistan. The book is organized into chapters that cover the etiquette of the student of hadith, the titles of the text and narrators, the types of acceptable hadith, what is rejected and what is wrong, the forms of tolerance and performance, the reasons for distortion and modification, the rules of documentation, and the types of hadith books. Its material has been formulated in an easy and clear manner with brief phrases sufficient to meet the needs of the student in his primary stage regarding the tasks and terminology of this noble science.
descriptions.3492: This book is an explanation of the Al-Bayquniyya system in hadith terminology. The author delivered it in scientific gatherings, then it was collected and written. The book explains the different types of Prophetic hadith, such as authentic, hasan, weak, marfo’, suspended, and others, following the approach of the early ones and the edits of the later ones on the issues. The explanation aims to provide the student with a foundation in terminology, while editing and clarifying the issues.
descriptions.3493: The book “Hadith Research” by Maher Al-Fahal is a collection of critical studies in the sciences of hadith, examining and investigating a number of noble prophetic hadiths, such as the hadith on the praying person’s jacket, the hadith on putting on a ring, the hadith on there is no ablution except from sound or wind, and others. The book aims to study these hadiths in terms of their chains of transmission and texts, while explaining the impact of the jurists’ differences in understanding them, in a scientific manner that relies on the hadith scholars’ rules of criticism and weighting.
descriptions.3494: The book “Researches in Terminology” by Maher Al-Fahl is a specialized study in the sciences of hadith, dealing with methodological issues such as difference, disorder, inversion, and inclusion in narrations, with an analysis of their causes and examples. The book aims to clarify how to deal with conflicting chains of transmission and texts, and to explain the impact of this on accepting or rejecting a hadith, reviewing applied models from the hadith heritage.
descriptions.3495: This book is an explanation of the “Alfiyyat al-Iraqi” system in Hadith sciences, delivered by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair in closed lessons. The explanation begins with an introduction about the importance of the science of hadith and its rules, which are known as the case of the narrator and the narrated. Then, it gradually addresses the explanation of the millennium verses, touching on the topics of the hadith such as the authentic, the good, the weak, the mursal, the interrupted, the fraudulent, the abnormal, and other terms of the science of hadith.
descriptions.3496: This book is an explanation and commentary on the book “Uum al-Hadith” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Katheer, which in turn is an abbreviation of the book “Ulum al-Hadith” known by Ibn al-Salah. The work falls within the field of hadith sciences and terminology, as it deals with explanation and explanation of the different types of hadith that Ibn al-Salah classified and arranged, starting with the authentic, good, and weak hadith, and passing through other types such as the musnad, the raised, the suspended, and the mursal, all the way to the topics of jarh and modification, and the methods of carrying and narrating the hadith.
descriptions.3497: This book is an explanation of the system “The Hidden Pearls in the Cases of Asanid and Matūn” organized by Hafez Al-Hakami, and it consists of sixteen lessons drawn from the lessons of Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair. The explanation deals with the subject of Hadith sciences, focusing on explaining the conditions of the chains of transmission and texts, and opening with a discussion of the virtue of Islamic knowledge and the importance of sincerity in seeking it.
descriptions.3498: This book is an explanation of the Al-Bayquniyya system in the science of hadith terminology, delivered by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair in four lessons. The explanation aims to explain the rules and controls of Hadith science by which the authenticity and weakness of Prophetic hadiths are known, in preparation for distinguishing acceptable ones from those that are rejected. The author begins by emphasizing the importance of the Prophet’s Sunnah as a second source of legislation, and the necessity of knowing what is proven from it through the rules of this science.
descriptions.3499: This book is an explanation of Imam Abu Dawud al-Sijistani’s letter to the people of Mecca, in which he explained his approach in his book “Al-Sunan,” his conditions for it, and his method for classifying it. The commentator explains that many of the authoritative imams did not declare their conditions in their books, and that these conditions are often deduced from examining and examining their books, which may lead to scholars disagreeing in defining them. The book falls within the sciences of hadith, and is divided into four lessons.
descriptions.3500: This book is an explanation of the introduction to Sahih Imam Muslim, delivered by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair in three lessons. The explanation begins by talking about praise and blessings upon his family and companions, then addresses the meaning of “as for after,” the sections of the hadith, and the narration of authentic hadiths, and concludes by talking about the classes of men. The explanation aims to clarify Imam Muslim’s approach in his book, and to explain his conditions for selecting hadiths, with an emphasis on the importance of distinguishing between authentic and incorrect narrations.
descriptions.3501: This book is an explanation of the text “Nukhbat al-Fikr” by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani on the science of hadith terminology, delivered by Sheikh Abdul Karim al-Khudair in a series of recorded lessons. The explanation begins with an introduction to the books on terminology and the importance of the text of the elite and its explanations and footnotes. Then it deals in detail with the ten principles of science, and explains the division of news into mutawatir and hadiths, with an explanation of the definition of news, the ruling on mutawatir, and what it benefits.
descriptions.3502: A book that criticizes the contemporary hasty approach in judging the levels of soundness and weakness of hadiths, considering it similar to naive mathematical equations that may lead to correcting the weak or weakening the true. The book reviews examples of the narrators of “Taqrib al-Tahdheeb” by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, focusing on the fifth and sixth levels of narrators, criticizing some of the rulings issued against them.
descriptions.3503: The book “Fragments” by the author Ahmed Shehata Al-Iskandari is a work in the sciences of hadith, in which he criticizes the contemporary hasty approach in judging the levels of health and weakness of hadiths, considering it similar to naive mathematical equations that may lead to abnormal results, such as violating the rulings of previous imams. The book is based on studying the rulings of Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani in “Taqrib Al-Tahdheeb” to explain the ranks of narrators, focusing on examples of narrators of the fifth and sixth ranks and discussing their conditions.
descriptions.3504: A book that examines how the student of knowledge can benefit from the books of the Prophet’s Sunnah, and clarifies the status of the Sunnah as a second source of legislation after the Holy Qur’an, and its clarification for him. In two lessons, the book deals with the issue of writing down the Prophet’s hadith, the wisdom behind forbidding it in the first place, and the difference between the memorization and writing stage.
descriptions.3505: The book “Lectures on Hadith Sciences” by Maher Al-Fahl is an educational work on hadith terminology, providing a systematic explanation of the basic concepts of hadith classification. The book begins by defining the authentic hadith and its five conditions (contact, justice, precision, denial of abnormality, and denial of defect), then it discusses in detail the sections of the hadith in terms of acceptance and rejection, such as authentic, good, and weak, with an explanation of the types of weak, methods of grading the hadith, and judging the chains of transmission.
descriptions.3506: This book is a summary of lessons by Sheikh Abd al-Karim al-Khudair, in which he deals with a comparison between the explanations of the six books of the Sunnah, which are Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawud, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, and Sunan al-Nasa’i, with an explanation of the disagreement regarding the definition of the sixth book. The book reviews the most famous commentaries on each of these books, such as Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar, Umdat al-Qari by al-Aini in Sharh al-Bukhari, al-Minhaj by al-Nawawi in Sharh Muslim, and Maalim al-Sunan by al-Khattabi in Sharh Sunan Abi Dawud, in a comparative framework that clarifies the characteristics of each commentary and its author’s approach.
descriptions.3507: The book “Symposium on Hadith Sciences, Sciences and Horizons” deals with various topics in the field of Hadith sciences, focusing on the historical development of these sciences and the challenges of understanding and teaching them in the modern era. The book deals with the efforts of revival and renewal in this field, and discusses the difficulties faced by students and professors in teaching and learning the sciences of hadith, with an emphasis on the necessity of benefiting from the efforts of advanced and backward scholars. The book also addresses the approaches of the ancients in dealing with the authentic and weak Sunnah, and calls for the necessity of correcting the defect occurring in learning and serving the sciences of hadith.
descriptions.3508: This book is an academic treatise on Hadith sciences, examining the impact of the reasons for the Prophet’s Hadith on the differences of jurists. It begins by defining the reason in language and terminology, and reviews its causes and types. Then, it deals in detail with the reasons for the chain of transmission, such as interruption, transmission, and deception, while providing applied examples of reasoned hadiths and explaining the impact of this on different jurisprudential rulings, such as the ruling on singing, Friday prayers, and the zakat on a child’s money.
descriptions.3509: The Literature of Dictation and Dictation is a book about the dictator and the dictator, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Saad Al-Sama’ani (506 AH - 562 AH).
descriptions.3510: Al-Suyuti’s Alfiya fi Ilm al-Hadith, Terminology, or Al-Alfiya al-Athar, also called Nazm al-Durar fi Ilm al-Athar by Imam al-Suyuti, is a poetic system consisting of 970 verses explaining the science of hadith and its sections.
descriptions.3511: This book is a poetic text on the sciences of hadith, organized by Al-Hafiz Zain al-Din al-Iraqi, and made it in the form of an alfiyah to facilitate its memorization and control of the rules of terminology. The book is organized into multiple sections that begin by defining the categories of hadith, such as authentic, hasan, and weak. Then it moves on to its types, including the nominative, suspended, and mutqat, and deals with issues such as deception, abnormality, objectionable, and reasoned, and other basic topics in the science of hadith terminology.
descriptions.3512: This is a book on the sciences of hadith. It examines the issue of requiring knowledge of hearing in the hadith that is disputed among contemporaries. Its author claims the consensus of hadith scholars on not requiring that, discussing the evidence of those who say it is required, and relying on the texts of imams such as Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others, and on conveying the consensus from a group of scholars.
descriptions.3513: A book on Hadith sciences, examining the issue of abrogated and abrogated in the Prophetic hadiths. The author has classified it under the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Purity. The book presents the hadiths contained in each issue, then mentions other hadiths that contradict them, and discusses the issue of abrogation among them, as appears from its introduction, which dealt with the issue of standing urine and the differences in the hadiths regarding it.
descriptions.3514: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, compiled by Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Qaysrani to explain the names of the companions whose sons narrated about them in the Prophet’s hadiths without their names being explicitly mentioned in the narration, which makes it difficult for the non-specialist to know them. The author has separated these names into chapters arranged according to kinship, such as the chapter on the grandmother, father, paternal uncle, and paternal uncle, only mentioning the names without narrating the hadiths or using them as evidence, in order to make it easier for the seeker of knowledge.
descriptions.3515: This book is an abbreviation of the book “Ulum al-Hadith” by Ibn al-Salah, compiled by al-Hafiz Ibn Katheer, and is also known as “Al-Ba’id al-Hathith ila Akhtar Ulum al-Hadith.” The book falls within the classification of hadith sciences, and deals with the types of prophetic hadith in terms of acceptance and rejection, starting with the authentic hadith, then the good, then the weak, mentioning their definitions, sections, and the most famous works in it, in a brief manner.
descriptions.3516: This is a book in the sciences of hadith that studies the phenomenon of differing opinions of critics regarding narrators whose rulings differed between jarah and ta'deel, with a focus on studying this phenomenon according to Imam Yahya bin Ma'in. The book deals with works on different narrators, and presents examples of the critics’ differing opinions regarding one narrator, and the positions of some scholars regarding the different sayings of Ibn Ma’in.
descriptions.3517: A book on the sciences of hadith, focusing on the necessity of accompanying knowledge with work and warning against neglecting it. It includes chapters that deal with harsh treatment of those who abandon work with their knowledge, and condemnation of seeking knowledge for the sake of showing off, showing off, or achieving worldly goals, while emphasizing that work is the fruit of knowledge and an increase in the afterlife, and urging seizing leisure and youth before obstacles.
descriptions.3518: This is a book on Hadith sciences, examining the bad effects of placing false hadiths on the Prophet ﷺ. In this part, the author focuses on the religious effects of the situation, showing how this phenomenon has left negative effects on the nation, and is still suffering from its remnants in the modern era, especially with the weakness of religious culture and the spread of superstitions and deviant doctrines.
descriptions.3519: A book on the sciences of hadith, in which its author collected hadiths in which the names of some men and women were mentioned vaguely, that is, not explicitly mentioned, and then followed each hadith with another comprehensive hadith that clarifies and reveals that ambiguous name. The author has arranged these hadiths in the alphabetical order of the dictionary, beginning with the chapter Alif, so that the book will be a reference in knowing the ambiguous names mentioned in the prophetic narrations.
descriptions.3520: A book on the sciences of hadith, which deals with the rules of strengthening weak hadiths with evidence and follow-ups, and explains the concept of “regard” and its importance in the science of hadith. The author explains the foundations on which this section is based, warning against leniency or excess in its application, while citing the approach of critical imams in dealing with narratives.
descriptions.3521: The book “Obligations and Tracing” by Imam Al-Daraqutni is a work of Hadith sciences, in which he criticizes the approach of Sheikhs Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs. The author mentions hadiths narrated by one or both of the two sheikhs on the authority of a narrator from among the Successors, then he explains that this narrator or his counterpart has other famous preserved hadiths that they did not narrate, considering that narrating them is obligatory according to their conditions and doctrine in grading. The book aims to trace back what the two sheikhs missed of hadiths that meet their conditions of authenticity, to complete what they overlooked.
descriptions.3522: Gaining knowledge of the origins of the narration and restricting listening. A book on the sciences of hadith written by Judge Ayyad after the book (Al-Kifaya fi Ilm Al-Rawaa’) and (Al-Jami’ Li Al-Khulaq Al-Narwi wa Al-Adha Al-Hearer) by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi. In the book, the author explained the principles of narrating hadiths and restricting hearing. The author says: Its first chapter is knowing the etiquette of asking, taking, and listening, then knowing the science of that and its aspects and from whom it is taken, then mastery and restriction, then memorization and awareness, then discrimination and criticism by knowing what is correct, incorrect, good, acceptable, abandoned, fabricated, and so on.
descriptions.3523: This book is a specialized scientific study in the sciences of hadith, dealing with the life of Imam Abu Al-Hasan Al-Daraqutni and his scientific status, with a focus on his approach in his book “Al-Sunan”. The research makes it clear that Al-Daraqutni’s purpose in his book was not to collect authentic hadiths to use as evidence, like the rest of the Sunan books, but rather to collect invalid hadiths and their narrations, excluding the authentic ones except for scientific necessity such as a comparison or correction. The book also reviews aspects of Al-Daraqutni’s biography, such as his pursuit of knowledge, his travels, his sheikhs, and his qualities such as piety and intelligence.
descriptions.3524: This book is written by Sheikh Abdul Mohsen Al-Abad, and it is in the field of Hadith sciences, and deals with the biography of Imam Al-Bukhari and his book “Al-Jami’ Al-Sahih.” The book begins by mentioning Imam al-Bukhari’s lineage, birth, and upbringing, then deals with his journeys in seeking knowledge and his qualities, such as the strength of his memorization and the praise of scholars for him. The author also devotes a section to talking about Sahih al-Bukhari, explaining its name, the reason for its composition, its content, its conditions, the number of its hadiths, the scholars’ praise of it, the reasons for its preference over Sahih Muslim, and the scholars’ interest in it.
descriptions.3525: The book “Imam Muslim and his Sahih” by Abd al-Muhsin al-Abbad is a study in the sciences of hadith. It deals with the biography of Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi, and the details of his life and journeys in seeking knowledge, his sheikhs, and his students. Then, it moves on to talking about his Sahih, explaining the reason for its composition, its status among the books of the Sunnah, its condition, the number of its hadiths, the scholars’ interest in it, and the issue of criticizing some of the hadiths in it and answering them.
descriptions.3526: A book on Hadith sciences, examining the issue of the abrogated and abrogated from the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ, and explains the reality of abrogation, its conditions and signs. The author presents the different approaches to identifying the abrogated from the abrogated, based on what his knowledge of the narrations has concluded, indicating the difficulty and ambiguity of this science, and the differences of the Companions regarding the transmitted rulings.
descriptions.3527: The suggestion in explaining the terminology and what was added to it from the hadiths that are counted from the Sahih books, a book on the science of hadith written by Taqi al-Din Ibn Daqiq al-Eid, in which he collected the terminology of the hadith and the levels of narration and narrators in short and conciseness. Its author intended it to be an introduction to the expansion of this art and he arranged it into sections.
descriptions.3528: This is a book on the sciences of hadith that studies the historical aspect of the hadith scholar Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, and reviews his approach in his book “History” and its branches such as Al-Maghazi, Al-Futuh, and biographies of notables. The research demonstrates the importance of hadith sources in the study of early Islamic history, and sheds light on the historical narratives unique to Ibn Abi Shaybah that may have been lost from other sources.
descriptions.3529: The book “Al-Tadlis wal-Mudallisoon” by Sheikh Hammad Al-Ansari is a book on the sciences of hadith, in which the author collects one hundred and sixty-one narrators from the mudlisun, divided between agreed upon and disputed ones. The book begins by defining fraud in language and terminology, then explains its three sections: fraud in the chain of transmission, fraud in the sheikhs, and fraud in the settlement, with an explanation of the rulings of each section and the differences between scholars in it. The book aims to make this art easier for students of hadith at a time when those working in it were at a premium.
descriptions.3530: The book “Al-Tadhkirah fi Ulum al-Hadith” by Ibn al-Mulqin is a summary of the science of hadith, which the author extracted from his larger book, “Al-Muqni’.” The book aims to present the principles of this science to beginners, with benefit to those who have completed it. It begins by defining the three types of hadith: authentic, good, and weak. Then it begins enumerating the more than eighty types of hadith sciences, such as the musnad, the continuous, the nominative, the suspended, and the mutqat, explaining each type briefly.
descriptions.3531: The book “Al-Tarif fi Al-Tashfir” by Imam Al-Suyuti is a book on the sciences of hadith, specializing in collecting the Prophetic hadiths in which there was a distortion or distortion in their wording or setting, with an explanation of what is correct in them. The book begins with the chains of narrators, and deals with the hadiths of the Companions arranged according to their chains of transmission. It mentions the various narrations and judges them as authentic or misprinted, based on the statements of major critics such as Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar and Al-Qadi Ayyad.
descriptions.3532: Approximation and facilitation of knowledge of Sunan al-Bashir al-Nadhir fi Usul al-Hadith by Abu Zakaria Muhyi al-Din Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi (died: 676 AH), which is an abbreviation of the book of Hadith Sciences by Ibn al-Salah, and was explained by al-Suyuti in Training the Narrator. As Al-Sakhawi explained it in Sharh Al-Taqreeb.
descriptions.3533: A book on the sciences of hadith. It explains the Al-Bayquni system that Al-Bayquni organized in the terminology of hadith, and explains the sections of hadith and its sciences, such as the authentic, the good, and the weak, and what is related to the chain of transmission and the text in terms of acceptance and rejection.
descriptions.3534: Restriction and clarification. It is also called Nukat al-Iraqi, a book compiled by al-Hafiz Zain al-Din Abu al-Fadl Abd al-Rahim al-Iraqi, and it is an explanation of the book Introduction by Ibn al-Salah. He said in the introduction to the book: The best book on knowledge of terminology is the book “Ulum al-Hadith” by Ibn al-Salah, in which he collected the murmurs of the benefits, so he became conscious, and he called for him to groups of strays, and they responded willingly. However, there are places where it has been violated and other places that need to be restricted and warned. So I wanted to compile jokes about him that would restrict the absolute and open the closed. More than one of the latecomers reported information that was not correct, so I thought I would mention the correction of the Sheikh’s words and his preference so that those who do not know the terminology of the people would not relate to them.
descriptions.3535: The book of torture by Al-Muallami, “Punishment, including the false rebukes of Al-Kawthari” by Abd al-Rahman Al-Muallimi (d. 1386 AH), is one of the books of refutations among scholars in the fourteenth century AH, as many specialists see it. It is in its origin a scholarly response to the book “Reprimanding the Khatib for the Lies He Made in Abu Hanifa’s Translation” by Muhammad Zahid Al-Kawthari. Regarding its importance, Muhammad Nasir al-Din Al-Albani says: “He explained it with conclusive evidence.” And the bright evidence...
descriptions.3536: The most brilliant clarification of Ibn al-Mulqin’s remembrance in the science of archeology. A book compiled by Shams al-Din al-Sakhawi, Sharh Kitab al-Tadhkirah fi Ulum al-Hadith, by Ibn al-Mulqin. It is a nice commentary in which he refers to many types of hadith sciences, as mentioned in the introduction to the book.
descriptions.3537: It combines the morals of the narrator and the morals of the listener. A book on the sciences of hadith written by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi, in which he explained the morals of the narrator and the etiquette of the listener, and what is obligatory, desirable and disliked for them, since there is no need for any of the scholars of hadith to know that. In this book, Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi has fully mentioned the etiquette and duties required by the hadith scholar and the student of hadith. Rather, he expanded on it, and collected and comprehended it, and there was nothing left to add, and the unquestionable truth is that the book satisfies - in its subject matter - everyone who wants the end in this research, and access to the depths of this topic.
descriptions.3538: A book on Hadith sciences, examining the meaning of the Sunnah and explaining its status in religion and its being a revelation and clarification of the Holy Qur’an. It then reviews the roles of the Prophet’s Sunnah throughout history, starting from the era of the Prophet ﷺ, through the time of the Rightly Guided Caliphate, and up to the second century AH, discussing the approach of the Companions and followers in preserving, narrating and writing down hadith, and their efforts to confront lies and fabrication.
descriptions.3539: This is a brief book on the science of hadith terminology, aiming to introduce the student of knowledge to the origins of this science and its basic terminology. The book begins by defining the text, the hadith, the chain of transmission, and the chain of transmission. Then it moves on to explaining the sections of the hadith in terms of acceptance and rejection, such as the authentic, the good, and the weak. It reviews other types, such as the mutawatir, the ahad, the musnad, the raised, the mursal, and others, to be a comprehensive of the most important chapters of this art.
descriptions.3540: A book on the sciences of hadith that responds to the claims of the orientalists Gold Zsher and Joseph Schacht and those who supported them among the Westernizers, who challenged the Sunnah of the Prophet and claimed that the Prophetic hadith is fabricated and fabricated, and that the method of criticism of the hadith scholars is unscientific. The book deals with criticizing these opinions and responding to them with evidence, stressing that the methodology of hadith scholars in criticizing the chain of transmission and the text is a correct and comprehensive scientific methodology.
descriptions.3541: The book “The Narrators Who Knew Abu Zur’ah” is a work in the sciences of hadith, specializing in the art of knowing nicknames and names. The author aims to collect and document the names of narrators who became famous by the nickname “Abu Zar’ah,” tracing them in printed and manuscript books of nicknames. This is preceded by an introduction that deals with the types of nicknames and the most important works on them, with a distinction between the most famous people who used this nickname, namely Abu Zar’ah al-Razi and Abu Zar’ah al-Dimashqi.
descriptions.3542: A book on the science of hadith, examining the issue of the spacing between the deaths of two narrators from one sheikh. It mentions the narrators in alphabetical order, and explains the time difference between the deaths of each narrator. This work falls within the arts of hadith sciences, which are concerned with the classes of narrators and their deaths. Al-Hafiz al-Khatib al-Baghdadi classified it as a reference in this type of hadith investigations.
descriptions.3543: This book on Hadith sciences examines the status of the Prophet’s Sunnah as the second source of Islamic legislation after the Holy Qur’an. It is organized into four main sections that deal with the authority of the Sunnah and its evidence from the Qur’an, Hadith, consensus, and reason, then its rank as a source subsequent to the Qur’an, its role in clarifying the legislative provisions of confirmation, specification, restriction, and abrogation, and finally its status in terms of implementation before and after the mission.
descriptions.3544: This book examines the subject of the Prophetic Sunnah and explains that it is a revelation from God Almighty that is preserved like memorizing the Holy Qur’an, in the context of responding to the suspicions and challenges to which the Sunnah is exposed from some sects and intellectual trends. The book is organized into sections that address the infallibility of the prophets and their diligence, then presents evidence that the Sunnah is a divine revelation like the Qur’an, based on the approach of the Sunnis in defending the authenticity and sanctity of the Sunnah.
descriptions.3545: This book examines the status of the Prophetic Sunnah as a revelation from God, reviewing evidence from the Holy Qur’an, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and the sayings of the Companions on that. It also addresses the efforts of the Companions, the Successors, and the followers of the Successors in preserving, codifying, and disseminating the Sunnah of the Prophet, starting from the era of the Prophet ﷺ until the later stages of codification.
descriptions.3546: This is a book on Hadith sciences, examining the subject of the Prophet’s Sunnah being a revelation from God Almighty. The author reviews the evidence for this from the Holy Qur’an, the Sunnah of the Prophet, evidence of prophecy, and scientific miracles, differentiating between the revelation of the Holy Qur’an and the revelation of the Noble Prophet’s Sunnah.
descriptions.3547: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, written by the hadith jurist Ibn Rashid al-Sabti, and he compiled it for his son. The book deals with topics related to the classes of narrators and methods of carrying knowledge, with special attention to the issue of the authenticity of the chains of transmission and the absence of any breaks in them or damage to their transmitters. It also indicates the conditions for the validity of carrying knowledge by writing and transmitting it.
descriptions.3548: This book is an explanation and refinement of the book “Sciences of Hadith” by Ibn al-Salah. It is in one volume and is classified under the Sciences of Hadith. The author explains the different types of hadith developed by Ibn al-Salah, starting with the authentic, hasan, and weak, and passing through the types of chain of transmission such as the musnad, continuous, and mursal, arriving at topics related to the etiquette of the hadith narrator, the student of hadith, and methods of transmission and narration.
descriptions.3549: A book on Hadith sciences, examining the methods of hadith scholars in receiving, narrating, and criticizing the Sunnah of the Prophet, starting from the era of the Prophet and continuing through the era of the Companions. It studies and analyzes the issues of the authenticity of the Sunnah and its relationship to the Qur’an, and the position of the Companions regarding narration and verification, with a focus on discussing the suspicions raised about some narrators such as Abu Hurairah.
descriptions.3550: This is a book criticizing Orientalist studies, focusing on revealing the methodological flaws in the writings of the Orientalist Joseph Schacht related to the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book begins by defining Schacht and his most important views on the Sunnah, then details six major methodological flaws into which he fell, such as racial bias, selectivity in sources, unsystematic skepticism, and neglect of counter-evidence. The research aims to prove that these flaws make Schacht's results unacceptable according to the principles of the scientific method, even among non-Muslims.
descriptions.3551: Al-Ghawi fi Sharh al-Hidaya fi the science of narration is one of the books of hadith and terminology, written by Al-Hafiz Shams al-Din al-Sakhawi (831 AH - 902 AH). The book is considered one of the most important books of terminology and hadith. In it, al-Sakhawi explained the words and mysteries that were mentioned by the scholar Ibn al-Jazari in his system Al-Guidance in the Science of Narration. Al-Sakhawi explained this system in an average way.
descriptions.3552: The book “Al-Fasl li’l-Wasl al-Madarou fi al-Naql” by Al-Hafiz Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi is a book on the science of hadith, specializing in the art of insertion into narration, which is for the narrator to include in the hadith what is not from him, whether it is from his own words or from the words of others. The book includes sections that classify the types of insertion, such as inserting the words of narrators into the texts of hadiths, inserting the sayings of the followers into hadiths that are raised, connecting the mursal with the traceable, and mixing different texts into one narration. This book is considered one of the primary sources in its field, as it is concerned with revealing this delicate critical phenomenon in the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.3553: A book on the sciences of hadith that discusses the issue of the mursal hadith, which is what the Tabi’i narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ without mentioning the companion. The book presents the doctrines of scholars in accepting this type of hadith and acting on it or rejecting it, with an explanation of the meaning of transmission in language and terminology, and a mention of the narrators of the hadiths and the balance between them.
descriptions.3554: A book on the sciences of hadith, in which its author, Abu Musa al-Madini, collected nice types of narration science that only critical memorizers can be guided to. The book begins with a special chapter on the narration of two men, each of them on the authority of the other, with the union of the sheikh who narrated on his authority. It begins with examples from the honorable companions, such as Omar’s narration on the authority of Abu Bakr and vice versa, and then extends to include the classes of narrators. The workbook aims to bring this art closer to its students, relying on an oral dictation that he dictated in a scientific council.
descriptions.3555: The book “Theologians fi Rijal” by Al-Hafiz Shams al-Din al-Sakhawi is a part of the science of hadith concerned with mentioning the critics of hadith narrators across the ages, starting with the Companions and the Followers and then onwards. The author lists the names of the imams who are famous for speaking about wounds and amendments on this matter, relying in its original on a part by Al-Dhahabi. Al-Sakhawi included this chapter in his books “The Announcement of Rebuke” and “Fath al-Mughith.” The book aims to introduce those whose words are relied upon to criticize men, without a comprehensive investigation, but rather by mentioning those who have come to mind from the early and late scholars.
descriptions.3556: A book on the sciences of hadith, documenting a lecture the author gave in defense of the Sunnah of the Prophet, after attending another lecture in Sudan in which he saw camouflage and misleading of the attendees. The book begins with an introduction in which the author recounts the circumstances of his visit to Sudan and how he attended that lecture, which prompted him to participate in discussing it and responding to it.
descriptions.3557: This is a brief book on the science of hadith, written by Al-Kafiji to be a facilitating introduction for students of this science, after he saw their lack of interest in lengthy books. The book begins with an introduction defining the science of hadith and its subject, then it is divided into two chapters and a conclusion, to include what the student of this art needs in terms of rules and principles.
descriptions.3558: A book on the science of hadith, which specializes in collecting the names of narrators from whom only one narrator, or a very limited number of narrators, narrated, with a mention of those who alone narrated from them. In arranging it, the author follows an alphabetical approach based on the letters of the dictionary, starting with the chapter Alif, mentioning the name of the Companion or Tabi’i, then describing the state of his narration by saying, “We do not remember that anyone narrated from him except so-and-so,” or “So-and-so alone narrated from him,” along with listing some of the hadiths that were narrated by these unique people with their chains of transmission.
descriptions.3559: This book deals with the topics of Al-Madbaj and Narration of Al-Azra in Hadith Sciences, and reviews the definition and examples of each of them. It also studies the relationship between them and their benefits in hadith science. The author focuses on the importance of chain of transmission in transmitting hadith and preserving it from distortion and falsity, showing the virtue of this nation in preserving chain of transmission and the care of its scholars about them.
descriptions.3560: A book on the sciences of hadith, which is included in the works of Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah Al-Naysaburi, and is concerned with explaining the method of classification in authentic hadith and distinguishing it from others. The author begins his book by citing prophetic hadiths and commandments, including the hadith of Al-Irbad ibn Sariya regarding the commandment to piety, hearing, obedience, and adhering to the Sunnah, which indicates that the book deals with the rules of hadith criticism and controls on authenticity by citing texts.
descriptions.3561: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, written by Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, and it is concerned with explaining the types of authentic hadith and the levels of authentication and modification, as it divided those who are authenticated into ten classes. Through it, the author aims to provide the student with knowledge of the conditions of Sharia law, the ranks of the Companions, and the chains of narrations that are considered a way to reach the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.3562: This is a book on the sciences of hadith. Al-Suyuti compiled it and made it a nice, brief part of the book “Taqrīb al-Mahjīb bi Tiḥār al-Mudārī” by Ibn Hajar, while limiting it to mentioning “Madarūj al-Matn” and not “Madraj al-Isnad,” and adding important additions to it from the Mudrajat al-Mutūn. The book aims to distinguish the words of the narrators included in the text of the Prophet’s hadith from the words of the prophecy itself, based on what hadith critics have written in their works.
descriptions.3563: A book on the sciences of hadith. It specializes in studying one of the types of hadith sciences, which is the disturbed hadith. It defines it linguistically and terminologically, explains the types of disturbance and its rulings, and clarifies the rules of disturbance in the chain of transmission and the text together or in each of them separately. Then, it devotes a second section to narrators described as disturbed.
descriptions.3564: A book on Hadith sciences, classified by the author as a summary and refinement of Ibn al-Salah’s book, with important additions and benefits. He begins by defining the authentic hadith and its sections, then deals successively with the different types of hadith sciences such as the musnad, the mursal, the interrupted, the problematic, the irregular, the illah, and other types, which reached sixteen types in his index.
descriptions.3565: The Al-Bayquniyya system is a text on the term Hadith by Omar bin Muhammad bin Futuh Al-Bayquni Al-Dimashqi Al-Shafi’i, who died around 1080 AH. It is a system from Bahr Al-Rajz and is in 34 verses.
descriptions.3566: A book that studies the history of the emergence of hadith sciences and the development of its term, tracing the stages of its development from the era of the Prophet ﷺ until later times, while explaining the impact of rational sciences such as doctrines of doctrine and the principles of jurisprudence in shaping this term. The author presents a theoretical approach to understanding the term hadith, discusses the invalidity of what contradicts it, then reviews books on hadith sciences and their various approaches, and concludes with practical steps for understanding the term.
descriptions.3567: This is a brief book on the sciences of the Prophet’s Hadith. It aims to introduce the student of knowledge to the origins of this art, its divisions, and its terminology. The book begins with an introduction to the honor of the science of hadith, then deals in detail with the discussion of the text, its sections, and types, beginning with the authentic and weak, and passing through thirty types of the text, such as the mutqat’, the mursal, the interrupted, the irregular, the fabricated, and others. The author also devotes the second part of the book to talking about chain of transmission and its related types, with an explanation of basic terms such as text, chain of transmission, chain of transmission, hadith, and news.
descriptions.3568: This book is an applied study on the project of creating a comprehensive hadith encyclopedia, located in the field of hadith sciences. The author reviews the practical visions for implementing this project, starting with the stages of verifying the written origins of hadith works, all the way to determining the tasks of the teams working on it, including researchers, modernists, and scientific committees. It also discusses the various paths of the proposed encyclopedia, such as the landmark of the Prophet’s guidance and the blog of hadiths of rulings, while presenting the necessary research for the success of this great scientific work.
descriptions.3569: This is a book on hadith sciences. It deals with the issue of encyclopedic compilation of the Sunnah of the Prophet, and reviews the efforts made in this field by the ancients and contemporaries, with a focus on computerized hadith projects. The author aims to provide a critical and analytical vision of the encyclopedic reality, and to put forward practical proposals for developing encyclopedic work in the service of the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.3570: The book “Al-Mawqaza fi Ilm al-Hadith Terminology” by Imam Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi, which is a book on the sciences of hadith, deals with defining the types of Prophetic hadith and explaining their ranks, starting with the authentic, the good, and the weak, and passing through other types such as the mursal, the interrupted, the suspended, and the raised, and focusing on issues related to deception, wording, performance, and etiquette of the hadith.
descriptions.3571: Loyal jokes including the explanation of the millennium is a book explaining the millennium of Imam Abd al-Rahim al-Iraqi in the science of hadith, written by Imam Burhan al-Din al-Biqa’i (809-885). The book is a collection of benefits and reliable and rare investigations of the millennium of Iraq, but Burhan al-Din did not complete it, but rather stopped at half of it. Imam Burhan al-Din al-Buqa’i said in the introduction to his book: The most important features and features of the approach that Imam Burhan al-Din al-Buqa’i followed. Explanation of it: The book included objections to some poetic verses from Imam Abd al-Rahim al-Iraqi’s Alfiyyah, presenting what he saw as more appropriate in composition, more complete in benefit, and more comprehensive. …
descriptions.3572: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. It is concerned with comments and jokes on Ibn Al-Salah’s book on the sciences of hadith, with a discussion of the approaches of a number of hadith scholars such as Ibn Al-Salah and Al-Iraqi. The book includes an investigation of its name and its attribution to its author, and it includes a study of the different types of hadith such as authentic, good, weak, mursal, interrupted, and others, which makes it a specialized work in consolidating and criticizing the rules of this art.
descriptions.3573: The book “Jokes on the Introduction to Ibn al-Salah” is a book on the sciences of hadith, which organizes an explanation and commentary on the famous book “The Introduction to Ibn al-Salah” in this art. The compiler aims to explain the difficult to understand names, lineages, and languages, and solve the issues that are difficult to understand, while adding jokes and benefits to the different types of hadith that Ibn al-Salah dealt with, such as knowing the authentic, the good, the weak, the chain of transmission, the continuous, the mursal, and others.
descriptions.3574: A book on the sciences of Hadith and its terminology. Its author provides a comprehensive introduction to the science of the Noble Prophet’s Hadith, covering the history of narration and codification from the time of the Prophet ﷺ until later times, with an explanation of the hadith scholars’ approaches to composing, the narrator’s conditions, and methods of endurance and performance.
descriptions.3575: The book “Standing on the Mounded on Sahih Muslim” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani is a work in the sciences of hadith, which collects suspended and cut off hadiths that were included in the text of Sahih Muslim, and which are not evaluated by the fabricated hadiths. The author selects these narrations from various sections of jurisprudence, such as purity, prayer, zakat, Hajj, and others, relying on independent sayings and actions attributed to the Companions and followers.
descriptions.3576: This is a book on hadith sciences, in which the author explains “Nukhbat al-Fikr” by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, and it is a famous text on hadith terminology. The book begins with an introduction explaining the Basmala and Al-Hamdala, then deals with the definition of hadith science, narration and knowledge, and explains the sections of the narration such as the Mutawatir, with a lengthy translation of Ibn Hajar that includes his name, lineage, sheikhs, and his writings.
descriptions.3577: The book “Researches in the History of the Noble Sunnah” by the author Akram Al-Omari, which is one of the books of hadith sciences, deals with study and analysis of the issue of the situation in the Prophet’s hadith. It reviews its beginnings and its causes, such as political and verbal disputes and the role of heretics and storytellers. Then it moves to the efforts of scholars to resist this situation through writing in the science of men, and studies the types of works in it, such as the books on the knowledge of the Companions, classes, and al-Jarh and al-Ta’deel until the end of the fifth century AH.
descriptions.3578: In the language of the Arabs in the term Athar al-Habib is a book compiled by Sheikh Abi al-Fayd Muhammad Murtada al-Zubaidi, the author of the book Taj al-Arous from Jawahir al-Qamoos. He is a landmark in the noble hadith, the Arabic language, and genealogy and one of the great compilers of his time. He was born in 1145 AH/1732 AD, in Belgram, a town in India, and grew up in Zabid in Yemen. He traveled to the Hijaz and resided in Egypt. He was originally from the city of Wasit in Iraq. He died of an illness. Plague in Egypt, 1205 AH/1790 AD. The book is one of the Islamic books that deals with the subject of the term Prophetic Hadith.
descriptions.3579: A book that discusses the concept of scientific miracles in the Sunnah of the Prophet, and reviews the aspects of miracles in the Holy Qur’an and the Noble Sunnah, while setting controls and rules for claiming miracles. The author presents his experience in writing his previous book on this topic, and explains his approach to applying these controls to what he wrote.
descriptions.3580: This book, written by Abdul Aziz Al-Othaim, falls in the field of hadith sciences, and deals with the issue of acting on weak hadith. The author begins by emphasizing the importance of distinguishing the authentic hadith from the weak one, then he defines the weak hadith and reviews its types, and moves on to discuss the ruling on narrating it and acting upon it. The book presents the opinions of different scholars on this issue, detailing the conditions stipulated by those who permitted acting on a weak hadith. The author gives weight to his opinion, supported by evidence and arguments.
descriptions.3581: A book on the sciences of hadith that discusses the issue of defining a companion, methods of proving companionship, determining the justice of the companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and responding to those who challenge them based on invalid hadiths, with separate sections allocated to each of these issues.
descriptions.3582: Training the Narrator is a book by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, one of the most important books on the science of hadith terminology. It is an explanation of the book al-Taqrib wa al-Taysir by Imam al-Nawawi, and “Taqrib” is a summary of the book “Al-Irshad” by Imam al-Nawawi, which is a summary of the introduction to Ibn al-Salah by Imam Abu Amr Uthman bin Abdul Rahman al-Shahrazuri, known as Ibn al-Salah. The book consists of two volumes, edited by: Tariq Awadallah, and Tariq Awadallah added a third volume to it, which is: “The Summary Containing Tasks for Training the Storyteller” in order to be a summary of the Book of Approximation.
descriptions.3583: This book deals with the subject of codifying the Prophetic Sunnah during the second and third centuries AH, with reference to the fourth century, within the framework of a historical and methodological study. The author begins by defining basic terms such as writing, recording, and classification, then reviews the stages of development of the process of codifying the Sunnah in those periods, highlighting the scientific efforts made by hadith scholars in serving the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book aims to highlight the methodological, critical, doctrinal, and jurisprudential dimensions included in the codification process, considering it a gateway to understanding the general pattern of the work of the hadith scholars.
descriptions.3584: This is a book on Hadith sciences, which deals with the historical study of the origins of the codification of the Prophet’s Sunnah and its development over the centuries, starting from the first century AH until the end of the ninth century. The author reviews the status of the Sunnah in Islam, the attention of the predecessors to it, and the efforts of the Companions and followers in codifying it. Then he traces the stages of development in codification during the second and third centuries AH, with a focus on examples of hadith works such as the Musnads and the Six Books.
descriptions.3585: A book that deals with the subject of the Prophet’s Sunnah in terms of its definition and an explanation of its status and position as a source of legislation, with a focus on it being a revelation from God Almighty and an explanation of the Holy Qur’an. The book reviews the history of the codification of the Prophetic Sunnah and its various stages, starting from the era of the Prophet ﷺ, passing through the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and the Successors, all the way to the era of general codification, with a discussion of the issue of prohibition and permissibility in writing hadith.
descriptions.3586: A book on the sciences of hadith, compiled by Al-Suyuti from the book Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi, deals with the phenomenon of the narrator forgetting the hadith he narrated. It mentions examples and accounts of narrators who narrated hadiths and then forgot them or denied them after that, along with listing the chains of transmission and narrations that document these cases.
descriptions.3587: This is a book on the sciences of hadith. It studies the issue of correcting and improving hadiths according to Imam Ibn al-Salah, and deals with critical analysis of his opinion on preventing later scholars from correcting. The book presents Ibn al-Salah’s text and analyzes it, then discusses the developments of the era and their impact on knowing what is authentic and hasan, and focuses on the concept of “juz’” and the chains of transmission of later scholars. It also reviews the positions of the most prominent opponents of Ibn al-Salah’s opinion, such as al-Nawawi, al-Iraqi, Ibn Hajar, and al-Suyuti, and discusses them in an objective manner supported by scientific and historical reality.
descriptions.3588: This is a book on Hadith sciences that aims to evaluate scientific works that dealt with the scientific and medical miracles in the Sunnah of the Prophet. It begins with an introduction to scientists’ attention to scientific miracles in the modern era. Then, in its chapters, it addresses definitions of miracles and methods of studying them, and evaluates various works and efforts in this field, with a presentation of some relevant university projects and theses.
descriptions.3589: Restricting Knowledge is a book written by Imam Abu Bakr al-Khatib al-Baghdadi (d. 463 AH), in which he collected everything related to the issue of restricting knowledge - which is writing it and copying it in newspapers. It is an old issue due to the prohibition against writing, which is why some scholars argued against restricting the hadith, then after a while they immersed themselves in writing the hadith and there was no scholar who did not have a book on the hadith...
descriptions.3590: The book “Documenting the Sunnah in the Second Century AH, Its Foundations and Directions” by the author Rifaat bin Fawzi Abdul Muttalib, which is one of the books of Hadith Sciences, studies the scientific efforts made by the imams of the second century AH in documenting the Prophet’s Sunnah and laying the methodological foundations to preserve it from distortion and fabrication. The book examines the issues of documenting the chain of narrators and narrators, methods of receiving and performing hadith, studies the authority of mutawatir and hadiths, and sheds light on the role of major hadith scholars and jurists in confronting the challenges that targeted the Sunnis in that era.
descriptions.3591: A book on the sciences of hadith. It aims to establish the foundations of the science of hadith and explain its origins. It examines the meaning of the Prophet’s hadith and its parts, the reason for its collection and codification, and methods for distinguishing what is proven from what is not. The book also deals with the sections of the hadith, such as mutawatir and ahad, and details the authentic hadith, with important benefits for reading hadith, biographies, and news books.
descriptions.3592: Clarifying ideas for the meanings of refinement of eyes. A book on the science of hadith in two parts, compiled by Muhammad bin Ismail al-San’ani, and it is an explanation of the book “Naqih al-Ansar” written by al-Hafiz Muhammad bin Ibrahim al-Wazir. The author said in the introduction to the book: This is an explanation written by the scholar Al-Nazar on “Tanqih Al-Anzar” written by Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al-Wazir. May God make him dwell in gardens beneath which rivers flow, for he collected the precious things of the investigations of the imams of antiquities, and added to it from his insights what is a light for insights and visions. For the second, he asked to write down its wording and highlight it in the face...
descriptions.3593: A book on the science of hadith terminology, which aims to present the rules and controls of this science in a simple manner and with a clear educational approach. The author begins with a historical overview of the emergence of terminology and the most famous works therein, then deals in detail with the division of the hadith in terms of its reach to us, its strength and its weakness, touching on the types of hadith such as the frequent, single, well-known, dear, and strange hadith, in addition to the sacred, raised, suspended, and mutqat hadith.
descriptions.3594: A book on the sciences of hadith, examining the issues of criticism and modification related to the heretical narrations, and explaining the categories of heresy and the consequences of accepting or rejecting the narration. The author discusses, through analysis and discussion, issues such as the definition of justice, the difference between testimony and narration, and the ruling on the narration of an infidel and corrupt innovator, relying on Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar’s explanation of the elite of thought.
descriptions.3595: This is a book on Hadith sciences, examining the efforts of hadith scholars to reveal the hidden reasons that undermine the authenticity of the Prophet’s hadiths. It begins by defining the science of ills linguistically and terminologically, and explains its importance and honor. Then it reviews the most prominent imams of this art and their works in it, and concludes with applied examples that illustrate the accuracy of critics in explaining hadiths.
descriptions.3596: This book is a scientific treatise by Imam al-Hafiz Abd al-Azim al-Mundhiri, which he wrote in response to questions he received from one of the scholars of his time, relating to precise issues in the science of jarh, modification, and criticism of narrators.
