The thesis addresses topics such as the levels of jarh and ta’dil words, and the differences of hadith scholars in accepting the innovator’s narration, and in stipulating the number of the purifier and the jarh, with applied examples on some narrators such as Ibn Ishaq and Shababah ibn Siwar. The message, despite its small size, is distinguished by its great benefits and original answers that will help those working in the sciences of hadith.
descriptions.3597: This book is concerned with explaining the authority of the Prophet’s Sunnah and its place in Islamic legislation, as it begins by defining the Sunnah linguistically and terminologically, then moves on to detailing its status as a second principle of legislation after the Holy Qur’an. The author reviews the efforts of scholars from the Companions and Successors and those after them to memorize and maintain the Sunnah, while mentioning examples of the biographies of its men who served this great field.
descriptions.3598: A book that examines the validity of the Prophet’s Sunnah and the necessity of acting upon it, and responds to the suspicions raised by those who deny its use as evidence. The author reviews the consensus of the majority of Muslims and their scholars throughout the ages that the Sunnah is a binding argument like the Holy Qur’an, and discusses the organized campaigns that have emerged in the modern era to undermine the status of the Sunnah with the aim of demolishing Islamic legislation.
descriptions.3599: This book examines the issue of the validity of single narrations in Islamic law, whether in the field of beliefs or practical rulings. It begins by defining the news of singles and its origin, then reviews the efforts of scholars in writing and defending its authority, and lists the evidence for the necessity of acting on it while responding to those who almost deny it. The book also discusses the emergence of the phenomenon of questioning the validity of single narrations and its causes, and elaborates on the issue of the benefit of single narrations for knowledge or suspicion, and ends with an examination of the emergence of the distinction between beliefs and rulings in using it as evidence.
descriptions.3600: The book “A Dialogue about the Methodology of the Hadith scholars in Criticizing Narrations in the Sanad and the Text” by Abdullah Al-Ruhaili is a work in the sciences of hadith. It presents a dialogue that took place between the author and one of those interested in the method of criticism among the hadith scholars, in which he addresses the relationship between the criticism of the chain of transmission and the criticism of the text, and the extent of their integration in distinguishing authentic narrations from their invalid ones. The book also includes two appendices on the importance of verification in the narration and reflections on the features of the hadith scholars’ approach, relying on rational critical questions within faith controls.
descriptions.3601: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, which specializes in studying the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and is considered a major source and a close reference for hadith scholars. In it, the author mentions how he heard the Musnad and the way he narrated it from his sheikhs, discussing some of the characteristics of this great book.
descriptions.3602: This is a brief book on the science of wounds and modifications, one of the branches of Hadith sciences. It aims to present the rules of this science and its basic issues in a concise manner. The book begins by defining the main terms such as jarah and tadil linguistically and terminologically, then deals with the terms of modifier and jarah, and elaborates on the definition of justice and an explanation of its conditions. The book is based on lectures given in Mecca, then edited to be like brief scientific texts that help the student of knowledge understand this art.
descriptions.3603: The book “Studies in the Sunnah of the Prophet” by Muhammad Dhia al-Rahman al-Azami is a book on hadith sciences. It begins by defining the word “Sunnah” in the Arabic language, reviewing its multiple meanings such as method, biography, face, and photography, citing Arab poetry and its uses. Then he links these linguistic meanings to the Qur’anic usage and the Prophet’s hadith, showing their application to the concept of the Prophet’s Sunnah through the verses and hadiths that mention the word “Sunnah” or refer to its meaning.
descriptions.3604: This book is a specialized scientific study in the sciences of hadith. It deals with the words of Al-Hafiz Abu Zar’ah Al-Razi in Sunan Ibn Majah, and examines the status of this book among the six books of hadith. The author presents the number of books of Sunan, their chapters, and hadiths, then he cites the sayings of scholars in response to Abu Zur’ah’s statement, and he specifically mentions the responses of Imam Ibn al-Rashid and al-Hafiz Ibn al-Mulqin. The book also studies the narrators from whom Ibn Majah alone narrated, along with other authors of the Sunan, and who were considered weak by Abu Zur’ah, within the framework of a critical evaluation of the issue of using Ibn Majah’s Sunan as evidence.
descriptions.3605: This is a letter from Imam Abu Dawud al-Sijistani to the people of Mecca and others, in which he describes his approach in his book “Al-Sunan.” In it, he explains the criteria for his selection of hadiths, and explains the authentic and good hadiths in his book, while mentioning his position on weak, mursal, and fabricated hadiths. He also explains the reason for the scarcity of hadiths in some chapters, his method of repeating the hadith to increase the benefit, and confirms that the hadiths of his book are the foundations of jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.3606: This is a brief treatise on the foundations of hadith, collecting its rules and terminology, and organized into an introduction and objectives. It begins by defining the text, the chain of transmission, and the hadith, then moves on to explaining the categories of hadith, including authentic, hasan, and weak, and deals with the chapters on jarh and modification, the interpretation of the hadith, and the names of men. The thesis aims to present a comprehensive summary of knowledge of the science of hadith, based on the sayings of imams on this matter, such as Ibn al-Salah, Ibn al-Jawzi, and Imam Ahmad.
descriptions.3607: This is a treatise on the sciences of hadith by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Mandah. It deals with an explanation of the virtue of prophetic news and an explanation of the doctrines of the scholars of hadith in receiving and correcting narrations. The author begins the book with praise and praise, then addresses topics that include the conditions of the imams in accepting the hadith, the classes of hadith scholars and transmitters of hadiths from the era of the Companions and the Successors and those after them, along with the order of the narrators in terms of acceptance and refutation, and mentioning those famous for creating chains of transmission and texts.
descriptions.3608: The book “The Modernization Fees in the Sciences of Hadith” by Al-Jaabari is a nice summary of the science of hadith terminology, in which its author summarized the book “The Sciences of Hadith” by Ibn Al-Salah, and added to it jurisprudential revisions and fundamental interpretations. The book begins with an introduction to the definition of news and prophetic hadith, then explains and details the main types of hadith, such as authentic, hasan, and weak, and extends to include other types such as the musnad, continuous, nominative, suspended, interrupted, and mursal, mentioning the meanings of each type and its rulings.
descriptions.3609: This is a book on Hadith sciences that studies the narrations and copies of Al-Jami’ Al-Sahih by Imam Al-Bukhari, and examines the differences between them. The book begins by introducing Imam Al-Bukhari and his interest in his works, then it discusses the Sahih narrations and their narrators, and its most famous editions and its manuscript and printed copies. It also details the types of differences between narratives, such as illusions and distortions that occurred in the chains of transmission, relying on what hadith scholars reported in their works.
descriptions.3610: The book “Doubts About the Sunnah” by Abd al-Razzaq Afifi is a work in hadith sciences that aims to respond to the doubts raised about the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author begins by confirming the status of the Sunnah as a divine revelation and a counterpart to the Qur’an in legislation, then addresses in detail various doubts, such as the claim of restricting oneself to the Qur’an and denying the Sunnah, rejecting hadiths because they contradict reason, and the issue of codifying the Sunnah, and provides answers to them, explaining in detail the ruling on rejecting the Sunnah.
descriptions.3611: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, and it is an explanation of the “insight and reminder” system known as “Al-Alifiyah al-Iraqi.” The book is considered an encyclopedia in the terminology of hadith, as it includes studies, corrections, and additions to the book “Introduction to Ibn al-Salah,” in which it clarifies what is hidden from it and explains what deserves explanation. The book included two sections: a study section that dealt with the biography of the author and Ibn al-Salah and the method of explanation, and an investigation section for the book.
descriptions.3612: This book is an explanation of the Al-Bayquniyya system in the terminology of hadith. It was written by Ibn Uthaymeen and is located in the classification of hadith sciences. He begins with the body of the system and then explains it in verses, covering the definitions of the main categories of hadith such as authentic, hasan, and weak, and the types of musnad, continuous, mursal, and other hadith terms, with an explanation of the conditions and controls for each type.
descriptions.3613: This is a book on the science of ills compiled by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali, and it is an explanation of the book “Al-Ilal al-Saghir” by Imam al-Tirmidhi. The book falls into two main sections, the first of which deals with the definition of the term “Illah” in hadith, its field, and the most famous scholars who worked with it, then the definition of the origin of the book, the author’s approach to it, and its sources. The second section includes an analytical study of the causes of the problem and how to detect it through Ibn Rajab’s explanation, with a study of the terminology of hadith drawn from the book itself.
descriptions.3614: This book is an encyclopedic explanation of the text “Nukhbat al-Fikr fi Terminology of the People of Athar” by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, compiled by Mullah Ali al-Qari to explain the rules of hadith science and its terminology. The author begins with an introduction to the virtue of knowledge and the importance of the Basmalah, then addresses the definitions of narration, hadith, and traces, and explains the divisions of narration in terms of its multiple methods, such as frequent and single, and in terms of acceptance and rejection, such as authentic, good, and weak. It also addresses critical issues such as the most correct chains of transmission, the comparison between the two Sahihs, and discussion of the hadiths criticized by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, so that the book becomes a reference in the principles of authentication and weakness.
descriptions.3615: The book “The Honor of the Companions of Hadith” by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi is a book on the sciences of hadith, which aims to explain the virtue of the Companions of Hadith and their position in Islam, and to respond to those who criticize them from among the innovators. The book reviews a number of Prophetic hadiths and hadiths that praise the bearers of the Sunnah, describing them as successors to the Messenger in conveying the message, trustees of the religion, inheritors of knowledge, and protectors of the Sharia. The author also discusses the virtues of seeking hadith and the journey in its path, and defends the Sunnis against the accusations of those who disagree with them.
descriptions.3616: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, written by Ibn al-Salah under the title “Preserving Sahih Muslim from breach and error and protecting it.” It is dedicated to studying Sahih Muslim and explaining any breach, error or omission that may occur in it, with an explanation of its meanings and control of its wording. The author aims to alert students of hadith to the areas of omission and error in the book, and to protect them from them, noting that its usefulness extends to include Sahih al-Bukhari and other books of hadith.
descriptions.3617: A book on Hadith sciences, examining the methodology of compiling the Prophet’s hadiths by relying on the highest narrator, i.e. the companion to whom the chain of transmission ended. It begins by defining the methods and graduation, then it details the method of graduation from the method of the Musnads, from the method of knowing the Companions and writing their names, and from the method of the parties arranged according to the highest narrator, with an introduction to the most famous sources in each chapter and an explanation of how to reach the hadith in them.
descriptions.3618: This is a book on the sciences of hadith that examines the science of generating the Prophet’s hadith and its role in serving the Sunnah of the Prophet. It reviews the methods of graduating the hadith, studying the chain of transmission, and judging the hadith, with an explanation of the books that help the researcher to uncover the men of the chain of transmission.
descriptions.3619: This is a book on the science of graduation of the Prophet’s Hadith. It examines the concept of graduation, its importance and benefits, and its origin and development throughout the ages. It reviews the efforts of scholars in translating hadiths, whether through specific books or in general, and explains the various methods and means of translating hadiths based on the features of the chain of transmission and the text, including computer methods. It also deals with the study of the chains of transmission, references, and evidence, and shows the practical steps for studying them and books that help in knowing the conditions of the narrators.
descriptions.3620: A book on the sciences of hadith, examining the science of analysis and modification that arose to preserve the Sunnah of the Prophet and distinguish authentic narrations from invalid ones. The author explains the importance of the Sunnah as a second source of legislation, and reviews the rulings on wounding and justice, and the position of scholars towards narrators, while explaining the reasons for not wounding the Companions, the command to wound the weak, and the warning against lying to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.3621: This is a book on the science of men, examining the origins of this science and its development over the centuries, from the first century AH until the end of the ninth century. The author presents a systematic study of the different types of men's books, such as books on classes, knowledge of the Companions, al-Jarh wa al-Ta'deel, local histories, books on names and nicknames, and others, with an introduction to each type and the most famous works in it.
descriptions.3622: This is a book on the science of the reasons for hadith. It aims to explain the concept of the reason in the Prophet’s hadith, its parts, causes, and places, while highlighting the importance of this science in preserving the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author provides applied examples of the reasons in light of the conditions of authenticity, explaining how the reason lies in the narrators in terms of justice, control, communication, and anomaly.
descriptions.3623: This book, written by Saleh bin Hamid Al-Rifai, is a study in Hadith sciences that deals with two basic aspects of memorizing the Sunnah of the Prophet. The first chapter examines the scholars’ attention to chain of transmission, explaining its definition, its importance, its being one of the characteristics of the Islamic nation, and its impact on memorizing the Sunnah. The second chapter deals with the science of jarh and modification, touching on its definition, the reasons for its appearance, the attention of scholars to it, and its impact in distinguishing authentic narrations from invalid ones.
descriptions.3624: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, in which the author explains the millennium of hadith by Imam al-Iraqi, detailing the sections of hadith from authentic, hasan, and weak, and their levels and conditions, and talking about the most famous books of hadith, such as the two Sahihs, the Sunans, and the Musnads, with an explanation of the terms of the nominative, the musnad, the connected, the suspended, and the mutqat, in a manner that combines scientific investigation and clarification of symbols and problems.
descriptions.3625: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, compiled by the author Abu al-Qasim al-Issaradi to explain the virtues of “Al-Jami’” by Imam Abu Issa al-Tirmidhi. The book mentions the position of this compilation among the five books of hadith that have received acceptance, and describes Al-Tirmidhi’s approach to it in terms of its inclusion of the jurisprudence of hadith, its reasons, and an explanation of the conditions of the narrators. The book also includes a mention of the circumstances of the narrators of Al-Jami’ and the methods of narrating it, while allocating sections to narrators from specific sheikhs such as Al-Jarahi and Al-Karukhi.
descriptions.3626: This book is a treatise on the science of wounding and modification, in which the author discusses the rule of prioritizing wounding over modification, and shows that this rule is not absolute. Rather, an exception is made from it for those whose Imamate and justice are proven, whose praise is many, and who are rarely hurtful by him, with evidence indicating the fanaticism of the wounder, so he should not pay attention to wounding against him. In this regard, the author relies on the statements of previous scholars, such as Ibn Abd al-Barr, and discusses the issue of scholars speaking to one another, specifying a criterion for distinguishing between acceptable criticism and others.
descriptions.3627: This is a treatise on the science of history and the method of historical criticism, placed by the author Taj al-Din al-Subki within the classification of Hadith sciences. In it, he explains that historians may fall into slander or non-objective modification due to fanaticism, ignorance, or reliance on unreliable transmission, and he states that fanaticism is greater among historians than among those who criticize and modify. Then he imposes four conditions regarding what the historian transmits, and four others regarding what he translates on his own, so that his transmission and translation are acceptable and considered.
descriptions.3628: A book on the sciences of hadith, in which the author summarizes the rules of this art and its terminology, reviewing the types of hadith in terms of acceptance and rejection, such as authentic, good, and weak, and in terms of methods of interpretation and performance, levels of chain of transmission, and conditions of narrators in terms of wounding and modification. The book is considered a comprehensive summary of the most important sections of the term, basing its approach on what was recorded by the major imams of hadith such as Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi and Ibn Al-Salah.
descriptions.3629: Rules of modernization from the arts of modern terminology. It is a book on the sciences of hadith written by Imam Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi, based on the term books written before it. It has clarity in the expression and contains innovative additional issues that benefit the student of knowledge, a contemporary of the author, Sheikh Taher al-Jazairi.
descriptions.3630: This book is a scientific study in the sciences of hadith. It deals with the issue of writing the Prophet’s hadith in the Prophet’s era, and examines the hadiths that were mentioned prohibiting writing and the hadiths that were mentioned permitting it. The author aims to reconcile these apparently conflicting hadiths, through the method of reasoning and eliminating the contradiction, while explaining the fact that the Companions wrote the hadith in the hands of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.3631: This is a book on hadith sciences that examines the issue of writing down the Prophet’s hadith. It reviews the evidence forbidding writing and the evidence for permitting it, then presents the scholars’ position on these hadiths and ways to combine them. The book begins by defining writing linguistically and terminologically and its references in Sharia law. Then it deals with the Arabs’ relationship with writing at the time of the mission, and the virtue of writing and its impact on preserving knowledge, before detailing the hadiths mentioned in the chapter and understanding them in the light of the scholars’ sayings.
descriptions.3632: This book is classified as Hadith Sciences, and deals with the subject of writing the Prophet’s Hadith during the era of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, and explaining its impact on preserving the pure Sunnah. The author aims to clarify the features of this important period in the codification of the Sunnah, and to respond to the suspicions raised by some researchers about it, by studying what the Companions wrote and what the Prophet ﷺ authorized some of them to write.
descriptions.3633: This book is written by Ahmed Omar Hashem, and is located in the field of Hadith sciences. It deals with the subject of writing and recording the Sunnah of the Prophet in the era of the Prophet and the Companions, and explaining the impact of this early writing in preserving and preserving the Sunnah. It also presents the status of the Sunnah in religion and the approach of the Companions in narration, and includes a response to some of the suspicions and appeals directed against the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.3634: This book is written by Rifaat bin Fawzi Abdul Muttalib, and is located in the field of Hadith sciences. The research aims to prove that much of the Prophetic Sunnah was written during the era of the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions, in response to those who claim that the Sunnah was not written until the end of the first century AH, which makes it vulnerable to forgetfulness and distortion. The book presents examples and evidence from newspapers and writings in the eras of the Prophet and the Companions, to show that the Sunnah was preserved in writing, in addition to being preserved in the chests.
descriptions.3635: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Ibn Asakir, in which he collects the virtues of the book “Al-Muwatta’” by Imam Malik bin Anas. The book falls within the Hadith classification, and it appears from its opening that it narrates with continuous chains of transmission some of what was mentioned about the virtues of Al-Muwatta and its people, beginning with a dream vision that indicates the status of this book among the predecessors.
descriptions.3636: A book that examines ways to benefit from the six main hadith books, which are Sahih Al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawud, Sunan Al-Nasa’i, Jami’ Al-Tirmidhi, and Sunan Ibn Majah. The author provides simple overviews of how to benefit from these books, beginning with an explanation of the virtue of the blessing of the Prophet’s mission ﷺ and the virtue of the Companions in receiving and performing hadith. Then he refers to the stage of codification of the Sunnah and the emergence of these six books as the most important works in this field.
descriptions.3637: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, examining the forms of performance that are attributed to the Prophet ﷺ from the sayings and actions of the Companions, such as their saying: “We used to say such-and-such,” or “He ordered us to do so,” or “from the Sunnah such-and-such.” The author explains the different levels of transmission of the Sunnah by the Companions, and details the ruling on each formula, and whether it is considered a marfoo’ hadith or a suspended hadith, with a focus on what there is no room for opinion, and the Companions’ interpretation of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3638: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, devoted to studying the “serial hadith” by definition, sections, and benefits. It has been divided into an introduction to the chain of transmission and four sections: the first on the definition of the serial hadith and the efforts of scholars in it, the second on its sections according to the chain of transmission in case or description, the third on its benefit and some of what is wrong with it, and the fourth on the types of complete and incomplete serials.
descriptions.3639: This book is a collection of Imam Al-Nisa’i’s letters on the sciences of hadith. The first deals with naming the jurists of the regions from the Companions and the Successors and those after them, arranged according to the countries such as Medina, Mecca, Kufa, Basra, the Levant, Egypt, and Khorasan. The second message classifies the narrators into graded classes, and the third specializes in mentioning those from whom only one narrator narrated. The book collects scientific material on knowledge of the classes of narrators and jurists of the regions, making it a reference in the science of men and classes.
descriptions.3640: This is a book on hadith sciences, studying the history of the hadith school in Egypt from the Islamic conquest until the end of the tenth century AH. Its author divides it into sections, the first of which deals with prominent Egyptian hadith scholars throughout the ages, the second of which deals with their approaches to narration, blogging, and classification, and the third of which is the most prominent hadith blogs that were written in Egypt, such as books of rulings and books of encouragement and intimidation.
descriptions.3641: This book introduces the Medina Research and Studies Center, and reviews its role in serving the Prophet’s biography, addressing its organizational structure, departments, and achievements. It begins with a historical introduction to Medina and its importance, then explains the motives for establishing the center and its goals in collecting and studying the vast cultural heritage related to it.
descriptions.3642: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, written by Ibn al-Qaysrani, and it discusses the issue of ascending and descending in the chain of transmission. The author explains the signs of ascension in the hadith and how the beginner distinguishes between ascension and descent, with a brief explanation and establishing evidence that leads to knowing this. The book falls within the general classification of hadith sciences, and its material is based on the authorizations and chain of narrations mentioned in the introduction.
descriptions.3643: This book is “The Sheikhs of Al-Qazwini” by Imam Siraj Al-Din Omar bin Ali Al-Qazwini, and it is one of the books of Hadith sciences that combines narration and chain of transmission. The book includes a collection of hadiths and narrations that the author heard and narrated from his sheikhs, while taking care to explain the types of hadith sciences such as authentic, good, weak, mursal, uninterrupted, and others. The book begins with the author's introduction in which he explains the reason for writing the novel and his condition for the novel, emphasizing the importance of verification and honesty in transmitting the hadith.
descriptions.3644: A book on the science of hadith terminology, aiming to establish rules for distinguishing what is accepted from what is rejected in what is attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. The author explains the sections of the report in terms of the methods of transmitting it (such as mutawatir and ahad), and addresses the definitions of authentic and hasan, and the reasons for the hadith such as interruption, fraud, and insertion, in addition to the topic of jarh and modification. It also examines the sections of the news, considering who is added to it, and the methods of carrying the hadith, performing it, writing it, and codifying it.
descriptions.3645: This is a book on hadith sciences, written by Ibn al-Salah, and is also known as “Ibn al-Salah’s Introduction.” It is considered one of the most important works in this art, in which the author collected the types of hadith sciences and explained them, beginning with the book’s sermon, which included praise and praise to God and blessings upon the Prophet, emphasizing the status of the Prophet’s Sunnah and its relationship to the Holy Qur’an, and the importance of chain of transmission in preserving the religion. The book deals with a comprehensive study of the types of hadith and its rules. The verified copy included a study of the author’s biography, his approach to the book, and its sources.
descriptions.3646: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, compiled by Ibn al-Salah to be a comprehensive introduction to the types and origins of this science. The author begins by praising God and praising the science of hadith, then sequentially lists the types of hadith sciences, beginning with knowledge of the authentic, the good, and the weak, and passing through the types of chains of transmission such as the musnad, the continuous, the raised, and the suspended, all the way to the methods of endurance, hearing, and authorization. The book aims to establish the rules of hadith criticism and explain its terminology, making it an essential reference in this art.
descriptions.3647: The book “The Key to Paradise in Invoking the Sunnah” by Al-Suyuti is a book on the sciences of hadith, which aims to defend the authority of the Prophet’s Sunnah and respond to those of the heretics and Shiites who deny invoking it, stressing that it is a revelation from God and a basic source of legislation alongside the Holy Qur’an. The author begins his book by explaining the status of the Sunnah and the necessity of adhering to it, then responds to the suspicions raised about it, relying on transmissional and rational evidence.
descriptions.3648: This book deals with the definition of hadith and its types in the science of hadith, going over the basic terms such as the nominative, suspended, and mutqat, and explaining the differences between them and the hadith and the report. It also studies the concept of the chain of transmission and the text and their symptoms, and reviews different types of hadiths, such as the mu’allaq, the mutqat’, the mursal, and the interrupted, with an explanation of the ruling on each of them. The book aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to the terminology and principles of Hadith science.
descriptions.3649: This scientific system in the science of hadith, written by Muhammad Adam al-Athibi, specializes in explaining the fabricated hadith and the types of fabricated hadiths. The system begins with an introduction to the honor of the science of hadith and the importance of knowing the subject, then it details the truth of the subject, its signs and rulings, reviewing signs that indicate the status of the hadith and ways to distinguish it.
descriptions.3650: A book on Hadith sciences, which studies the methods of hadith scholars from the first century AH until the present era, with a focus on the place of the Prophet’s Sunnah in Islamic legislation and responding to those who deny it, past and present. The book deals with the manifestations of the Companions’ interest in the Sunnah, the writing of the Hadith during the Prophet’s era, and the Companions’ methods in narrating it, with a detail of the role of a number of the many Companions and Mothers of the Believers in serving the Noble Hadith.
descriptions.3651: This is a book on the sciences of hadith that studies the approach of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in criticizing hadiths and judging them based on reason, by following his sayings in the books on reasons and issues. The author reviews the sources that recorded Imam Ahmad’s approach to explanations, such as the Book of Reasons according to the narration of his son Abdullah and other narrations, then he details the types of explanations by criticizing the narrators, such as ignorance or what violates justice. The book aims to reveal the rules and controls that Imam Ahmad adopted in distinguishing authentic hadiths from weak ones.
descriptions.3652: This is a book on the sciences of hadith, which studies Imam Bukhari’s approach to correcting hadiths and explaining them. In its first chapters, the author reviews the development of hadith sciences and hadith criticism until the era of Al-Bukhari, then presents a comprehensive translation of Imam Al-Bukhari and his scientific works, focusing on his approach in his book “Al-Jami’ Al-Sahih” and the jurisprudential purposes he intended from it.
descriptions.3653: The book “Method of Criticism in Hadith Sciences” by Nour al-Din Attar is a work in the field of Hadith sciences, aiming to present an organized, systematic study of the rules of this science and its history. The book presents an innovative classification of the types of hadith sciences, separating what is related to the text and the chain of transmission, and studies the roles in the development of this science throughout the ages, with a focus on providing illustrative examples for each of its types.
descriptions.3654: This is a book on Hadith sciences, which studies the sources relied upon by Imam Al-Bayhaqi in writing his book “Al-Sunan Al-Kubra.” The author divides these resources into sections that include books on the sciences of the Qur’an, Hadith, jurisprudence, histories, al-Jarh, al-Ta’deel, and others, and then presents a critical study of al-Bayhaqi’s approach to using these sources. The work aims to explain the nature of the resources from which Al-Bayhaqi derived his scientific material, the extent of their value, and how he dealt with them in terms of adoption or criticism.
descriptions.3655: A book on the sciences of hadith, in which the author explains the misconceptions that occurred regarding the issue of combining and separating the names of narrators, their surnames, and their genealogies, as narratives differ in naming a single narrator or separating those united by a name. The author devoted the first part to explaining Imam Bukhari’s delusions in this section, tracing a number of delusions that occurred in various narrations, explaining the truth of each name and its lineage in order to correct the path in knowing the narrators.
descriptions.3656: A book that discusses the issue of the requirement of meeting and hearing between contemporary narrators in the chain of narrators, and the position of Imams Al-Bukhari and Muslim on this condition. The author reviews the roots of the issue historically, and details the means of proving the encounter according to Al-Bukhari, and the effect of not proving the encounter on the validity of the hadith according to him, while explaining his critical approach in his texts related to this issue.
descriptions.3657: A book on Hadith sciences, which examines the hadiths of abrogation and abrogation in the Sunnah of the Prophet, and collects the hadiths in which an earlier ruling was abrogated by a later ruling. The author begins by explaining the concept of abrogating a hadith, citing the sayings of the Companions and Followers, then moves on to apply that to the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Purity, presenting the abrogated hadiths, then the hadiths that abrogate them, addressing issues such as ablution from what has touched fire, washing, ablution for every prayer, and other rulings.
descriptions.3658: This is a book on Hadith terminology, which studies the text of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani’s “Nukhbat al-Fikr” in terms of its author’s approach to it. The book deals with the innovative approach taken by Ibn Hajar in writing “Nukhbat al-Fikr”, his satisfaction with this text, the scholars’ praise of it, and the efforts made to serve it. The work aims to shed light on the importance of this text in Hadith science, and to demonstrate the scholars’ interest in it as a tool for preserving the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.3659: This is a brief book on the science of hadith terminology. Its author wrote it in response to a request from some of the Brotherhood, to summarize for them the important rules of this art. It begins by dividing the narration in terms of the number of its ways into the frequent, the famous, the dear, and the strange. Then it moves on to explain the types of hadith in terms of acceptance and rejection, addressing the reasons for challenging narrators such as omissions, illusion, ignorance, and poor memorization. It concludes with chapters on forms of performance, knowledge of nicknames, and other topics in the science of attribution and narrators.
descriptions.3660: The book “The Journey of the Listeners in the Narrations of the Companions on the authority of the Successors” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani is a work in the sciences of hadith, in which the author summarized what Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi collected from the narrations of the Companions about the Successors, and arranged them according to the letters of the dictionary in the names of the Successors. The book aims to collect and document hadiths and hadiths narrated by the Companions about the Tabi’in class, with the author adding comments on them.
descriptions.3661: A book on the sciences of hadith, in which its author explains the text of “Nokhbat al-Fikr,” which he himself wrote, covering the types of reports in terms of frequency and single ones, and explaining the categories of authentic, good, and weak hadith, and what is related to the sciences of narration and knowledge such as serial, abnormal, munkar, follow-up, and consideration, while mentioning the reasons for challenging narrators, such as lying and fraud.
descriptions.3662: A book on the sciences of hadith, which provides methodological advice to the student of the Prophet’s Sunnah, and reviews the characteristics and advantages of the science of hadith, with a focus on the importance of good faith and acting according to the hadith, methods of memorizing and studying it, and the method of reading and learning books on hadith and terminology.
descriptions.3663: The book “Advice to the People of Hadith” by Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi is a treatise on the sciences of hadith, written by the author as an advice to the student of hadith in particular and to others in general, urging him to distinguish himself from the people of ignorance and to strive diligently in seeking knowledge. The book directs the student of hadith to the necessity of understanding the sciences of hadith and knowing its rulings before he ascends to leadership, citing traditions from the predecessors urging him to seek knowledge at an early age.
descriptions.3664: The book “Secrets of Statement in Quranic Expression” by author Fadel Saleh Al-Samarrai, which is one of the books on the sciences of the Qur’an, deals with study and analysis of multiple aspects of Quranic expression, such as introduction and delay, mention and deletion, emphasis, similarities and differences between verses, the characteristics of verse breaks, and the expressive characteristic of context. The book aims to show the accuracy of the Qur’anic expression and its artistic precision by balancing the verses and examining them linguistically and rhetorically, while applying this to Qur’anic stories such as the story of our master Adam and Moses, peace be upon them.
descriptions.3665: This book deals with the topic of rational consideration in the Holy Qur’an and Islamic thought, and examines its origins and evidence. The author reviews the relationship between religiosity and philosophizing, and compares the emergence of philosophy in Greece and the development of theological thought in the Jewish and Christian religions, pointing to the impact of Islamic civilization on the emergence of Jewish philosophers. It also discusses the evidence proving the existence of God according to thinkers such as Augustine and Anselm, within the framework of a comparative historical study of religious and philosophical thought.
descriptions.3666: A book that examines aspects of the scientific miracle in the Holy Qur’an through the verse “And He knows what is in the wombs,” where the author links the Qur’anic text with scientific facts related to the stages of fetal formation, starting with the journey of the sperm “gametes” all the way to its attachment to the womb and its development in three darknesses. The book explains and analyzes the accuracy of the Qur’anic description of the process of creation, with a comparison between what is stated in the text and what modern science has revealed. It also addresses jurisprudential rulings related to the fetus, such as lineage, inheritance, and expenses.
descriptions.3667: This is a book concerned with extracting grammatical issues from Tafsir Al-Bahr Al-Muhit by Abu Hayyan Al-Andalusi, and arranging them on the surahs of the Holy Qur’an, starting from Al-Fatihah to Surat Al-Ankabut. The author provides a detailed parsing of the verses with a discussion of the grammatical and linguistic aspects, based on the sayings of the grammarians Kisbawayh, al-Kisa’i, al-Farra’, and al-Zamakhshari, with a focus on guiding readings and interpreting the compositions.
descriptions.3668: This is a book that studies Imam Al-Buqa’i’s approach to interpreting the eloquence of the Holy Qur’an, and divides it into two parts: the first deals with his struggle in seeking and teaching knowledge, the struggle of his pen, and the position of scholars on its interpretation, and the second explains his approach in interpreting the eloquence of the Qur’anic text through the Qur’anic proportionality on its structural and ordinal levels, with a detailed analysis of the construction of the surahs, verses, and the Qur’anic word.
descriptions.3669: This book is an introduction to the Holy Qur’an, shows its virtue and status, and confirms that it is the word of God revealed to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the primary source of Islamic legislation. He stresses the necessity of reading it with contemplation and awareness, describing it as a miraculous, precise book to which falsehood does not come, a guide to what is most upright, and one that is protected from distortion.
descriptions.3670: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that presents an approach to understanding the Qur’anic meaning through studying the context of the Surah. It deals with the jurisprudence of the position of the Surah in the overall Qur’anic context, the unity of the context of the Surah and its greatest purpose, dividing it into comprehensive complexes, and then graphic analysis. The author aims to establish the concept of contemplation and explain the stages of the path to the jurisprudence of Quranic meaning, relying on the methods of rhetoric and interpretation scholars in explaining the proportionality and interconnectedness of the surahs.
descriptions.3671: A book that examines the Holy Qur’an as an integrated approach to reforming society. It addresses the general goal of its revelation, man’s relationship with his Lord, and his relationship with his society. The author reviews the state of the world before the prophetic mission of darkness and error, then shows how the Qur’an brought guidance and comprehensive change, emphasizing its miraculousness and the fact that it is an enduring and preserved miracle that addresses all aspects of life.
descriptions.3672: This book is concerned with the knowledge of Meccan and Medinan verses in the Holy Qur’an. It reviews its origins and various definitions, and explains the reasons for the difference in the designation of Meccan and Medinan surahs and the benefits of knowing that. He also mentions the works on this art, lists the narrations that define the surahs, and explains the rules and regulations by which the Meccan and Medinan ones are known, while clarifying the most correct opinion regarding the disputed surahs.
descriptions.3673: This book is a comprehensive study in the field of Qur’anic sciences. It deals with the subject of electronic publishing of translations of the meanings of the Holy Qur’an and its importance in serving the Islamic call. The author reviews the concept of electronic publishing, its characteristics and advantages, with a focus on its role in publishing translations of the meanings of the Qur’an via the World Wide Web, in a historical context of translating the meanings of the Holy Qur’an. The research aims to shed light on the necessity of investing in modern technologies in serving the Book of God, especially in light of the contemporary information explosion.
descriptions.3674: A book on the science of Tajweed of the Holy Qur’an, explaining the rulings on its recitation from the origins of the letters and their attributes, and the rulings on the noun saukah, tanween, meem saukah, length and shortening, amplification and thinning, stopping and beginning, and other topics related to improving reading. The book begins by defining Tajweed linguistically and terminologically, and explaining its ruling and virtue, based on evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus.
descriptions.3675: This is a book on the sciences of the Holy Qur’an. It begins by defining the Qur’an and explaining that it is the word of God Almighty revealed to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, then it deals with the subject of revelation, its truth and method, and the ways of God’s communication to His messengers. The book also presents the issue of preserving the Holy Qur’an and its safety from distortion. It mentions the aspects of its preservation during the era of the Prophet and the Companions, and addresses its revelation as an astrologer. Then it explains the principles of interpreting the Qur’an using the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the Companions and Followers, and concludes by talking about abrogating previous laws in the Qur’an.
descriptions.3676: This book deals with the history of the development of writing and printing the Noble Qur’an, starting from the first stages of its writing during the era of the Prophet ﷺ and its compilation during the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, through the development of Arabic calligraphy, the dots of the Qur’an, its intonation and decoration, all the way to the era of modern printing. The author also devotes extensive space to talking about the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s care for the Holy Qur’an, especially through the King Fahd Complex for the Printing of the Noble Qur’an, explaining the method of work in writing and printing the complex’s Qur’an copies, in addition to recording recitations, translations, and Qur’anic studies.
descriptions.3677: This is a research book in the field of Qur’anic sciences, aiming to evaluate the methods used in teaching the Holy Qur’an in the stages of general education and university education. The book begins with a theoretical framework that reviews different teaching methods, such as exemplary, combined, and individual reading. Then it moves to field procedures that include the research sample and tools, and presents the results related to the pre-learning test, formative evaluation, and the use of educational methods.
descriptions.3678: The book “Nuggets of Gold: A Study in Qur’anic Rhetoric” by Mahmoud Tawfiq Muhammad Saad is a study in the field of Qur’anic sciences, focusing on Arabic jurisprudence in explaining the Qur’anic revelation. The book deals with various rhetorical topics, such as context, Qur’anic readings, Qur’anic vocabulary, and the rhetoric of vocative and interrogative methods, shortening, and conditionals, through analyzing verses from the Holy Qur’an. The author aims to show that the Arabic study of the Qur’an must derive its curriculum from the reality of the statement of the Arabs in the era of revelation, away from foreign curricula.
descriptions.3679: This book is an explanation of the introduction to interpretation included by Imam Al-Suyuti in his book “Al-Niqaya”, presented by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair in a series of lessons. The explanation addresses basic topics in the sciences of the Qur’an, such as the definition of the Qur’an and the surah, its types, and issues of reading and interpreting it, in addition to discussions on the reasons for revelation, abrogation, abrogation, and other issues related to interpretation. The work aims to guide the student towards caring for and understanding the Book of God, with an emphasis on the importance of interpretation and Qur’anic sciences in the school curricula.
descriptions.3680: This book is an explanation of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah’s introduction to the principles of interpretation, delivered by Sheikh Saleh bin Abdul Aziz Al Sheikh in the form of serial lessons. The explanation begins with an introductory lecture on the schools of interpretation, then covers in detail the rules and foundations laid down by Ibn Taymiyyah for understanding and interpreting the Book of God, with special attention to the approach of the righteous predecessors in that. The book aims to open the doors of the science of interpretation and explain its complexes and rules to the seeker of knowledge.
descriptions.3681: The book “Fath al-Karim al-Mannan fi Etiquette of Carriers of the Qur’an” by Ali al-Dabaa’ is a nice overview of the etiquette of the reader, writer, teacher, and learner of the Qur’an, extracted from the books of respected imams. The book falls under the section on the sciences of the Qur’an, and deals in detail with the etiquette of the reader, such as sincerity and purity, the etiquette of touching, carrying, and writing the Qur’an, in addition to the etiquette of the teacher and the learner, and the etiquette of the people and listeners of the Qur’an gatherings.
descriptions.3682: This is a book on Qur’anic sciences that deals with the study of the technical structure of the Qur’anic surah, and focuses on the unity of the text and the connection of its verses to each other. The author discusses the artistic styles and intellectual structures to which the surahs are subject, and highlights the shortcomings of ancient and modern studies in treating this aspect comprehensively for all the surahs.
descriptions.3683: The book “They Said About the Qur’an” by Imad al-Din Khalil collects testimonies and testimonies from a number of orientalists, Western and non-Muslim thinkers about the Holy Qur’an, highlighting their recognition of its miracle, eloquence, and precedence for modern science. The book falls within the classification of Qur’anic sciences, and begins with excerpts presenting the opinions of figures such as Khalil Ahmed, who was a missionary priest and then converted to Islam, and Thomas Arnold, the British Orientalist, to reveal the fascination of non-Muslims with multiple aspects of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3684: A book that brings together a group of articles and essays on the verses of the Holy Qur’an, dealing with various topics such as the creation of Eve, the martyrdom of women, the meanings of the command in the Qur’an, and the relationship of the legal ruling to its source. The author criticizes some calls for renewal that lack depth in understanding the Arabic language and the principles of interpretation, relying on the Sunnah of the Prophet and Al-Qurtubi to guide the meanings of the verses.
descriptions.3685: The book on the languages ​​of the tribes mentioned in the Qur’an. Its author is: Abu Ubaid al-Qasim bin Salam. Abu Ubaid sought knowledge, heard hadith, studied literature, and studied jurisprudence. He resided in Baghdad for a period, then Patrosus became the judge, and after that he went to Mecca, where he lived there until he died. Among his books are: Ghareeb al-Hadith, Book of Money, and Proverbs. He died in the year 224 AH. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said about him: “He was one of the imams in the religion and one of the most prominent scholars of the Muslims.” Al-Dhahabi said about him: “One of the scholars of Baghdad, grammatical hadith scholars according to the doctrine of the Kufans, narrators of the language and strangers, on the authority of the Basrans, the Kufans, scholars of readings, and those who collected types of knowledge and compiled books in every art of science and literature and more.” …
descriptions.3686: A book that studies the secrets of Qur’anic expression and graphic touches in texts from the revelation, through analysis of the choice of words and methods of rhetorical formulation in multiple surahs such as Al-Fatihah, Al-Kahf, Al-Hadid, and others. The author addresses topics such as deletion from the verb, masculinization or feminization of the verb, introduction and delay, and the Qur’anic comma, showing that the miracle of the Qur’an is multi-faceted and includes legislative, linguistic, and scientific fields.
descriptions.3687: This book is a dictionary that deals with terms related to the Holy Qur’an, defining its concepts, rulings, and readings. Includes introduction to the names of surahs, stopping marks, readings, and parts and parts of the Qur’an. It also explains technical terms such as slanting and tilting, explaining how to parse them and their sign. The book aims to provide a comprehensive reference for the terminology of Qur’anic sciences and its readings.
descriptions.3688: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an that studies the connotations of the words that express the two parts of the day in the Holy Quran, such as morning, evening, evening, and early, and reveals the reasons for the diversity in their use and the secret of their coming in different forms of definition, indefiniteness, and contrast. The author aims to clarify the rhetorical secrets behind the selection of these times over others, and to demonstrate the impact of this diversity on the Qur’anic system of systems.
descriptions.3689: This book is an encyclopedia of scientific miracles in the Qur’an and Sunnah, combining correct transmission, clear reason, common sense, and objective reality. It begins with foundational introductions about monotheism, worship, and the causal system in the universe, and then addresses in detail multiple aspects of human creation, its body, and its systems, such as balance in creation, the biological clock, human fingerprints, and the relationship between the soul and health. It also examines topics in Islamic psychology, such as despair, hypocrisy, and the effects of joy and sadness, and moves on to verses about sleep and its health benefits, linking scientific facts with Sharia texts.
descriptions.3690: This is a research book that presents Imam Al-Shawkani’s position on the science of occasions in the Holy Qur’an, through studying his words in the introduction to his interpretation of “Fath Al-Qadeer,” in which he called for abandoning this science and claimed that it is of no benefit. Then he moves on to monitor its practical contradiction by mentioning many aspects of occasions within the folds of his interpretation itself. The research provides comprehensive and detailed responses to the most important issues raised by Al-Shawkani in his talk about occasions, highlighting the importance of this science in understanding meanings and weighing opinions.
descriptions.3691: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which examines verbally similar verses in the Holy Qur’an, and explains how to distinguish between them. The author devotes the fifth section of the book to talking about a type of similarity that is consistent at the beginning of the verses and differs at the end, with an introduction and a conclusion.
descriptions.3692: This book deals with the study of the personality of Imam Abu Bakr Al-Baqalani and his concept of the Qur’anic miracle, as it sheds light on his biography in terms of his name, upbringing, sheikhs, disciples, and influences, with a focus on his prominent role in theology and Maliki jurisprudence. The book highlights the importance of its author, “The Miracle of the Qur’an,” as the first work by a Salaf scholar to respond to opponents, and reviews his distinguished scholarly position in supporting the Ash’ari school of thought and crystallizing its opinions.
descriptions.3693: The Book of Ahkam Al-Qur’an by Al-Tahawi Abu Jaafar Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Salama bin Abdul-Malik Al-Azdi Al-Tahawi, the Hanafi jurist; The leadership of Abu Hanifa's companions ended with him. The interpretation of the verses of the rulings received a level of liberation and refinement that was not the case for other chapters, and it is no secret that its reason is the details of the practical laws that are based on it. However, Al-Tahawi takes the issues he mentioned to highlight the Hanafi school of thought to which he belongs. Rather, the matter may go beyond looking down upon the opponents and extending undue lengths upon them. …
descriptions.3694: Ahkam al-Qur’an by al-Shafi’i is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, after he collected the sayings and interpretations of al-Shafi’i found in his books or the books of others, and included them in the book Ahkam al-Qur’an by al-Shafi’i.
descriptions.3695: Ahkam al-Qur’an (Ibn al-Arabi): A book written by: Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi. Ahkam Al-Qur’an (Al-Jassas): A book written by: Abu Bakr Al-Jassas. Minor Provisions of the Qur’an: A book written by Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi. Ahkam al-Qur’an (Al-Harasi): A book of jurisprudential interpretation of the Holy Qur’an according to the Shafi’i school of thought, written by Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Ali al-Tabari. Ahkam Al-Qur’an by Al-Shafi’i: A book of jurisprudential interpretation of the Holy Qur’an according to the Shafi’i school of thought, written by Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi. Ahkam al-Qur’an (Al-Tahawi): A book written by: Al-Tahawi. Ahkam Al-Qur’an (Al-Jahdhami): A book written by: Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Qadi.
descriptions.3696: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, explaining the etiquette and morals that should be possessed by those who possess the Holy Qur’an, whether those who learn it or those who teach it. It deals with the virtues of reciting and teaching the Qur’an, and mentions the good morals of its people, warning at the same time against the morals of those who recite it for other than the sake of God. It also devotes sections to the etiquette of the reciter and listener, and the good voice and etiquette that should be taken into account during recitation.
descriptions.3697: Questions and answers about the parsing of the Qur’an, a book written by Abdullah bin Yusuf bin Hisham, who died in the year 761 AH,
descriptions.3698: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It examines the reasons for the revelation of Quranic verses and surahs, arranged according to the order of the surahs of the Noble Qur’an, beginning with an explanation of the first and the last of the Qur’an that was revealed, then mentioning the reasons for the revelation of each surah of the Mighty Book.
descriptions.3699: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, specializing in the study of similar verses that are repeated in the Holy Qur’an with verbal differences between them, such as addition, subtraction, precedence, delay, and substitution of letters. The author aims to explain the reasons and rulings behind this repetition, and the difference between the verse and its counterpart, while clarifying what is suitable for one in place of the other. He devoted it to explaining the similarities after he devoted the interpretation of the verses in another book of his, following the approach of the imams who preceded him, while adding an explanation of the aspects of the difference and their reasons.
descriptions.3700: The harmony of pearls in the proportionality of the surahs by Imam Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911 AH) is a nice book, in which his author dealt with the sciences of the Qur’an, namely the arrangement of the surahs, their harmony, and their appropriateness, and the clarification of the miracle, clarification, and purposes of that. It was also printed under the name: Secrets of the Arrangement of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3701: This is a book on the principles of interpretation, which explains the rules and foundations upon which one relies in understanding and interpreting the words of God Almighty. The author begins by explaining the revelation of the Noble Qur’an, the first thing that was revealed from it, the reasons for the revelation, the Meccan and the Medinan, then moves on to talk about the interpretation itself, an explanation of what is required of a Muslim regarding it, the approved references in interpreting the Qur’an, the types of disagreement in the interpretation of the hadiths, and the ruling on translating the Qur’an, with brief biographies of the most famous interpreters of the Companions and Followers.
descriptions.3702: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, highlighting the eloquence and miracles of the Holy Qur’an. The author begins by defining the Qur’an linguistically and terminologically, reviews its names and attributes, then addresses the issue of the Qur’anic miracle and its origin, conveying the opinions of scholars such as Al-Jahiz in this section.
descriptions.3703: A great example of questions and answers about the strange things of the verse of revelation: by Muhammad bin Abi Bakr al-Razi. This book is considered one of the fruits of study among friends about the Holy Qur’an, and it is an approach that few scholars of the present era follow. It is one of the important books in studying the problematic verses of the Qur’an. Its author wrote it in a precise, scientific style characterized by knowledge of the Book of God, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the sayings of the Companions and Followers, as well as knowledge of the words of the Arabs with which the Holy Qur’an was revealed. It is also a unique model for interpreting the Qur’an with the Qur’an, and what is problematic in its verses must be returned to its decisive verses, as well as interpreting the Qur’an according to the Sunnah of the Prophet, and according to the sayings of the Companions and Followers, or interpreting the Qur’an in accordance with the words of the Arabs. …
descriptions.3704: The book Izraz al-Ma'ani is considered one of the first explanations of (Harz al-Amani) by al-Shatibiyyah. Its author is Abu Shamah Abd al-Rahman bin Ismail al-Maqdisi, and one of the reasons for writing it was: the many benefits that he found in the text of al-Harz, and he did not find anyone before him who had mentioned them. He took care to mention the issues of parsing and language in addition to the readings, and he said about his book (a treasure filled with knowledge). This book has a high status; When a group of scholars praised him, Al-Dhahabi said about him: “He wrote an exquisite commentary on Al-Shatibiyyah,” and Ibn Al-Jazari said about him: “He wrote and composed, and he was the only one of his time to compose many types of sciences. He explained Al-Shatibiyyah at length and did not complete it, then he shortened it, and it is the famous explanation.”
descriptions.3705: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that specializes in the science of Qur’anic recitations. It collects the fourteen famous recitations, their narrations, and methods, and explains their rulings, such as assimilation, extension, shortening, tilting, and stopping, with attention to mentioning the reasons for the recitations and their guidance. The book includes detailed chapters on the rulings on the Nūn Sakinah, Tanween, Hā’, Kannaya, Hamzat, and other issues of this art, with explanatory comments on some of what the reader may wonder.
descriptions.3706: This book examines the effective educational methods that the teacher should follow in teaching the Holy Qur’an, focusing on four main axes: teaching recitation, teaching understanding, memorization, and working with the Qur’an. The study included a field survey to measure the effectiveness of these methods in charitable organizations’ seminars for teaching and memorizing the Holy Qur’an, with a presentation of the results and recommendations.
descriptions.3707: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, in which the author presents interpretive and rhetorical views on verses from Surahs Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah, relying on a rational approach and fine rhetorical taste to highlight the aspects of the Qur’anic miracle. The book deals with the interpretation of verses in a precise analytical manner, revealing the deep verbal and rhetorical meanings that reveal penetrating insight into the Book of God Almighty.
descriptions.3708: The Miracle of the Qur’an by Al-Baqalani The miracle of the Qur’an continues until the Day of Resurrection, and its break with tradition in its style and eloquence, and its telling of the unseen. Not a single era passes without something appearing in it of what it was told would happen, indicating the validity of his claim. Scholars have written extensively on the aspects of the Qur’an’s miracles, and some of them have limited the aspects of its miracles to eighty, and it is most likely that there is no end to the aspects of its miracles.
descriptions.3709: The Miracle of the Qur’an and the Prophetic Rhetoric is the second part of the book “The History of Arab Etiquette” by the author Mustafa Sadiq Al-Rafi’i. Its first edition was published under the name The Miracle of the Qur’an and the Prophetic Rhetoric in 1928 AD.
descriptions.3710: The book “The Parsing of the Great Qur’an” by Zakaria Al-Ansari is a work in the sciences of the Qur’an that specializes in parsing the words of the Holy Qur’an and explaining their grammatical and linguistic aspects. The book begins with the parsing of Surat Al-Fatihah, detailing its words and verses. Then it moves to Surat Al-Baqarah, covering the parsing of its vocabulary and structures, while mentioning some readings and grammatical directions. The author relies on the question and answer method to explain some grammatical issues, which clarifies the grammatical and morphological rulings of the verses.
descriptions.3711: This is a book on the parsing of the Holy Qur’an, written by a group of authors. It aims to present the parsing of Qur’anic verses in a concise and concise manner, avoiding elaboration on aspects of interpretation, rhetoric, and language. The authors relied on the method of brevity in grammatical phrases, deleting some details such as grammatical movements or naming some grammatical elements, depending on the reader’s initial information, while choosing the easiest aspect when there are multiple grammatical aspects. The book begins with an introduction explaining their approach to parsing, then proceeds to parse Surah Al-Fatihah as Surah Al-Baqarah, verse by verse.
descriptions.3712: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. Its subject is parsing the words of the Holy Qur’an and explaining their grammatical rulings. Its author arranged it into ninety chapters, in which he dealt with various issues such as the incorporation of sentences, the deletion of the genitive, the addition of letters, the juxtaposition of nouns, and other topics related to parsing and language in revelation. The book is incorrectly attributed to Al-Zajjaj, while its real author is Abu Al-Hasan Al-Baquli.
descriptions.3713: The Parsing of the Qur’an by Al-Nahhas is a book by Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas, and it is one of the books that took interpretation in a special direction, which is paying attention to the linguistic and grammatical aspects of the words and phrases of the Qur’an, and trying to understand the Qur’anic text through that. It follows the school of linguistic interpretations, and linguistic interpretation is: explaining the meanings of the Qur’an as stated in the Arabic language.
descriptions.3714: This book falls within the sciences of the Qur’an. It deals with the issue of denying the existence of the jinn as it is one of the extremes that some commentators have fallen into in the modern era. It focuses on proving the existence of the jinn based on the texts of the Qur’an and the authentic Sunnah. It discusses the position of some scholars who denied this unseen world influenced by material civilization.
descriptions.3715: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which studies interpretation trends in the fourteenth century AH, and is divided into several volumes. The book begins with an introduction, then deals in the first chapter with the doctrinal trend in interpretation, dividing it into chapters that deal with the approach of the Sunnis and the community in interpretation, the approach of the Shiites, and the approach of the Ibadi, with an introduction to each sect, its beliefs, and examples of their interpretations.
descriptions.3716: Extracting controversy from the Holy Qur’an is a book about debate and argument in the Holy Qur’an, written by Nasih al-Din ibn al-Hanbali (554 - 634 AH = 1159 - 1236 AD). The author talks about debate and argument, and is the first to enact debate and disagreement, and the debate of the prophets (peace be upon them), while mentioning evidence of the oneness of the Almighty Creator, and the prophecy of Muhammad. The book contains eight chapters, which are as follows: On mentioning the controversy in the Holy Book, its praiseworthy and its reprehensible ones. The first to initiate controversy. The debate of the prophets, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them and the nations. Mention the evidence and its types for the existence of the Creator, Glory be to Him. Citing evidence that it is one. Mention the evidence of the resurrection. Mention the evidence of Muhammad’s message from the Holy Qur’an. In questions, answers, and jokes about arguments. …
descriptions.3717: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an by Abu Amr al-Dani. It deals with the subject of the seven letters with which the Holy Qur’an was revealed. The book explains the meaning of these letters, the wisdom behind the Qur’an being revealed to them, and shows the differences between them and the origin of the differences in readings. It also discusses important issues such as whether all seven letters are correct, and that they do not come together in one narration or reading, while explaining what should be believed in the letters, readings, and the history of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3718: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. Its approach is based on two principles: a linguistic origin and a religious origin, from which its name “The Two Principles” is derived. The author reviews a wide range of topics related to the Holy Qur’an, such as the places and times of revelation, the decisive and the similar, abrogation, readings, the collection of the Qur’an, interpretation and interpreters, the miracle of the Qur’an, Quranic rhetoric, and other topics that are considered introductions to interpreting the Qur’an and understanding its meanings.
descriptions.3719: A book that studies the Qur’anic proverbs that God Almighty has set for faith in Him. It is divided into two volumes, the first devoted to fundamental introductions about the concept of the proverb in the Qur’an and the definition of faith linguistically and legally, while the second volume deals with an applied study of specific Qur’anic proverbs, such as the proverb set for God’s light in the hearts of believers, by analyzing its context and its rhetorical and analogical form.
descriptions.3720: Explaining the Meanings of Recitations is a book written by Makki bin Abi Talib about the meanings of recitations and their benefits and mentioning the strange meanings of them, as well as an explanation of the hadith: “The Qur’an was revealed in seven letters.” The importance of the book also lies in that it is connected to his book “Revealing the Faces of Recitations.” The book Al-Ibanah by Abu Muhammad Makki Al-Qaisi was distinguished by several features that indicated its importance, including: the fact that the author of the book was one of the advanced scholars, as he died in the fifth century AH, as well as the praise of a number of scholars for the author of the book, and it is also one of the approved books for specialists in recitations, and a number of recitation scholars have quoted from him, such as: Badr Al-Din Al-Zarkashi in his book Al-Burhan fi Ulum Al-Qur’an, and Ibn Al-Jazari, from whom Al-Suyuti transmitted in his book Al-Itqan. …
descriptions.3721: Perfection in the Sciences of the Qur’an is a book written by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (who died in the year 911 AH). The book is considered one of the most famous works written in the sciences of the Qur’an, ancient and modern, and the most useful, and the most extensive in material.
descriptions.3722: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It examines the Israelites and topics that have entered the books of interpretation, explains their meaning and the sections of interpretation, and sheds light on the interpreters of the Companions and Followers and the various schools of interpretation, while explaining the coloration of the books of interpretation according to the culture of their authors. It aims to purify the interpretation of the Qur’an from the falsehoods and myths attached to it.
descriptions.3723: A book that examines the concept of chain of transmission and its importance in the science of Qur’anic readings, and explains its position among Muslim scholars in general and among Qur’anic scholars in particular, with a focus on the requirement of the chain of transmission and its authenticity for the reading to be accepted, and an explanation of the scholars’ efforts in distinguishing correct chains of transmission from weak and anomalous ones, and their journeys in seeking connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.3724: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It studies the issue of the graphic miracle of the Holy Qur’an through an inductive and analytical approach. In its first part, it deals with the concept of the miracle and the controversy surrounding the Qur’anic challenge, the aspects of the graphic miracle, and studies the openings of the surahs and the connotations of words and methods. The second part is devoted to studying the issues of Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq, which are Qur’anic terms that Ibn al-Azraq asked about and were interpreted by Ibn Abbas. The author presents them in text and study.
descriptions.3725: The Book of Persuasion in the Seven Recitations, by Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Khalaf al-Ansari al-Gharnati, known as Ibn al-Badash, a scholar of recitations. He was the preacher of Granada. Al-Dhahabi said about him: “He was a skilled reciter, skilled, knowledgeable of the language, a conversant, knowledgeable of names, and of religion and goodness. People wrote about him a lot.” The book is about the science of recitations, which is: “knowledge of how the words of the Qur’an are performed and their differences, attributed to its transmitter. With this definition, science emerged: language, grammar, and interpretation, or it is a doctrine followed by one of the imams, differing from others in pronouncing the Holy Qur’an, with the narrations agreeing on it. It is a difference in dialects, pronunciation, and methods of performance.” …
descriptions.3726: Al-Ikleel fi Istinbat al-Tanzeel is a book written by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, one of the books related to the Holy Qur’an, in which the author mentions everything that was deduced from the Qur’an or inferred from it from a matter of jurisprudence, origin, or belief, coupled with an interpretation of the verse where the understanding of inference depends on it, while attributing the statement to its speaker. His method is that he selects specific verses from each surah and mentions what was said in them, or some of what was said in them in terms of deduction, interpretation, inference, funny joke, or nice benefit. The book is of great importance, as it contains many legal and linguistic issues and rules and other various issues. …
descriptions.3727: This book is written by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is a work on the sciences of the Qur’an. It deals with the issue of similarity and interpretation, and focuses on the interpretation of the verses that relate to Satan’s casting of the wish of the prophets. At the beginning, the author explains the division of hearts into three categories: the cruel, the sick, and the hidden believers, explaining the relationship of knowledge to faith and the position of those who are firmly rooted in knowledge regarding similarities.
descriptions.3728: The book “Victory for the Qur’an” by Al-Baqalani is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, aiming to defend the Holy Qur’an and respond to the suspicions of those who challenge it. The book addresses important issues such as the authenticity of the Qur’an’s transmission, composition, and arrangement, the virtue of the Companions in memorizing it, explaining the meaning of the seven readings and the abrogated verses, and responds to allegations of distortion and distortion in the Qur’anic text.
descriptions.3729: The book “Axioms in the Holy Qur’an” by author Fahd Al-Rumi falls within the classification of Qur’anic sciences, and deals with the study of Qur’anic verses that are characterized by the closeness of their meaning and the clarity of their significance to the point that they are not hidden from anyone, and they are self-evident matters that a person immediately realizes. The book reviews the types of these axioms, such as the arithmetic, linguistic, and ordinary axioms, and links them to rhetorical sciences such as redundancy and emphasis, shedding light on the wisdom of these clear meanings in the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.3730: The Book of Al-Badur Al-Zahira fi Al-Ten Mutawatir Recitations is a book by Abd al-Fattah bin Abd al-Ghani bin Muhammad al-Qadi (d. 1403 AH) on the science of recitations. It is a book that talks about the ten recitations of the Holy Qur’an from the paths of al-Durrah and al-Shatibiyyah, which are two texts with systems of recitations, al-Shatibiyyah by al-Qasim ibn Firah al-Shatibiyyah, and al-Durra by Ibn al-Jazari. The author spoke about the general topic of the book and said: “When I saw the urgent need of the students of the first stage of the Qira’at Institute for a book that collects the recitations in Al-Shatibiyyah and Al-Durra, I wrote this book, and included in it the ten recitations from the two paths of Taysir and Al-Tahbir, and Al-Shatibiyyah and Al-Durrah.”
descriptions.3731: The book of proof in the proportionality of the surahs of the Qur’an, its author: Ahmad bin Ibrahim bin Al-Zubayr bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Al-Zubair, Abu Jaafar, Al-Thaqafi Al-Gharnati, born in the year (627 AH). He recited the seven to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Shari and heard from him and from Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Tusi. He died in the year (708 AH). Ibn Hajar said about him: “He devoted himself to reading the Book of God Almighty, listening to hadith, teaching Arabic, and teaching jurisprudence, devoting to that all his day, persevering in benefiting and disseminating knowledge.
