He was the only one to do that, and the journey to him became one of the people of Tajweed and proficiency, knowledgeable of recitations, memorizer of hadith, distinguishing authentic from incorrect, remembering its men and their histories, and extensively narrating it for me greatly.” …
descriptions.3732: The book of proof in the sciences of the Qur’an. It is a book written by Imam Al-Zarkashi, Abu Abdullah, Badr Al-Din, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bahadur bin Abdullah Al-Zarkashi Al-Masry, born in Cairo in the year 745 AH and died in the year 794 AH, scholar, jurist, fundamentalist, hadith scholar, interpreter, author, author, methodologist, Shafi’i school of thought, Turkish origin. The book Al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Qur’an, which is unique in its subject matter, is very famous and very useful.
descriptions.3733: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It specializes in the issue of counting the verses of the Holy Qur’an. It mentions the number of verses of each surah according to the different schools of thought (the first Medinan and the last, the Meccan, the Kufi, the Basri, and the Levant), with an explanation of the areas of agreement and disagreement between the imams of the regions. The book also deals with knowing the words and letters of the Qur’an, its khams and tithes, and distinguishing Mecca from Medina, based on the Sunnahs and the traditions mentioned in this regard from the predecessors.
descriptions.3734: Al-Tibyan fi Etiquette of Bearers of the Qur’an is a book that contains the etiquette required of the bearer of the Holy Qur’an, the descriptions of its memorizers and students, the etiquette of the teacher of the Qur’an, the virtue of reciting it, and the honor that God has prepared for the people of the Qur’an. The author of the book is Imam Al-Nawawi, and the book consists of ten chapters.
descriptions.3735: Al-Tibyan fi Parsing the Qur’an, by Abu Al-Baqa Al-Akbari, is one of the most famous books on parsing the Qur’an, and perhaps the best of them. Because of its specialization, comprehensiveness, and comprehensiveness of the subject, in addition to clarity in approach, accuracy in research, and correct opinion, it includes a general parsing of the words of the Qur’an, except for a few words that have not been parsed. Due to its clarity, and beginners’ knowledge of its parsing. Its topics: parsing the surahs of the Qur’an, the readings contained therein, and explaining the languages ​​contained therein.
descriptions.3736: Al-Tibyan fi Tafsir Ghareeb Al-Qur’an is one of the books on interpretation of the Holy Quran, written by Ibn Al-Haim (d. 815 AH).
descriptions.3737: The book “Al-Tasarif li-Tafsir Al-Qur’an, Menu whose Names Are Ambiguous” by Yahya bin Salam is one of the early books in the science of faces and Qur’anic analogies, which is a science that investigates the Qur’anic words that are repeated in the Holy Qur’an with different meanings. The book aims to explain the multiple meanings of a single Qur’anic word according to its different contexts, which helps to understand the purposes of the Qur’an and the secrets of its explanation. This work was completed as part of a research plan that sheds light on the Tunisian Africa’s contribution to the service of the Qur’an and its sciences, and it is considered one of the first books to appear in this field, alongside the book by Muqatil bin Sulaiman.
descriptions.3738: A book that deals with the study of the artistic and aesthetic aspects of the Holy Qur’an, focusing on the style of artistic photography, sensory imagination, and anthropomorphism in Quranic expression. The author examines the characteristics of the Qur’anic story, its religious and artistic purposes, how to draw characters and the harmony of images, while analyzing the emotional logic that characterizes the Qur’anic style.
descriptions.3739: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that examines the style of Qur’anic depiction and an explanation of its rhetorical and miraculous aesthetics, with a focus on how moral and legislative values ​​are embodied through this depiction. The author reviews the aspects of the Qur’anic miracle, the reality of graphic depiction, and the characteristics of Qur’anic literature of majesty, sweetness, and beauty. Then he moves on to practical applications of Qur’anic depiction in the stories of the prophets and previous nations, models of hypocrisy, and other topics that highlight the cohesion of music, meanings, and values ​​in the Qur’anic text.
descriptions.3740: This book, written by Dr. Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Zahrani, aims to provide an objective interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, as it focuses on studying verses that address a single topic or a common goal, regardless of their different wording and multiple locations. The book deals with various topics of Islamic beliefs, acts of worship, and legislation, and uses the reasons for revelation, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and the sayings of the predecessors in its interpretation. This method aims to achieve a more comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an by linking verses related to one topic, and highlighting its greatness and multiple laws.
descriptions.3741: The book “Tafsir and Interpreters” by Muhammad Hussein Al-Dhahabi is a fundamental study in the sciences of the Qur’an, dealing with the origins of the science of interpretation and its development through three main historical stages: the stage of the Companions, the stage of the Followers, and the stage of codification. The author examines the meaning of interpretation and interpretation and the difference between them, and reviews the different schools of interpretation, detailing the approaches to interpretation based on tradition and interpretation based on opinion, and the position of Islamic sects such as the Shiites, Zaidis, and Imamis regarding the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.3742: Introduction to the Science of Tajweed, is a book by Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Ali bin Yusuf, Abi Al-Khair Ibn Al-Jazari, and the book is on the science of Tajweed, which is the science that investigates Quranic words, in terms of giving the letters their right and due, and the right of the letter is: its outlet and attributes that do not separate from it, such as whispering and loudness. What it deserves are the qualities with which the letter is sometimes described, and sometimes separated from it, such as amplification and thinning in relation to the rā’. The author mentioned ten chapters in which he covered the topics of intonation. The book began by mentioning the readers and what is learned by refining words, and concluded it with supplications for concluding the Qur’an. Among the topics he addressed in his book were: distinguishing the dha from the dha, stopping and beginning, and the titles of letters and their causes. …
descriptions.3743: The Book of Tayseer in the Seven Recitations is a book on the science of recitations. Its author was Abu Amr Othman bin Saeed al-Dani, who died (444 AH), and he was a proficient memorizer and researcher, as Al-Dhahabi described it. His book, Al-Tayseer, is a brief book in which he collected the authentic Quranic recitations, and limited it to two narrations for each reciter, and a path for each narrator, with authentic and proven chains of transmission in these seven recitations. Therefore, it was an approved book among recitation scholars, for its brevity and distinction. …
descriptions.3744: The book “The Table in the Parsing of the Holy Qur’an” by Mahmoud Safi is a work in the sciences of the Qur’an, concerned with the parsing of verses of the Holy Qur’an and their morphological and rhetorical analysis. The book begins with Surah Al-Fatihah, dealing with each verse separately, providing a detailed parsing of its words, then explaining the morphological aspects of the words, and following them with rhetorical hints and explanatory benefits, similar to what was mentioned in the explanation of the Basmala. The index covers Surahs Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah, indicating that the book aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the Qur’an in a systematic tabular manner.
descriptions.3745: The book “Al-Durrah Al-Mudhiyya fi Al-Qira’at Al-Qira’at Al-Three Supplementary to the Ten” is a poetic system in the science of Qur’anic readings, written by Ibn Al-Jazari. The book aims to record the three readings that complement the seven famous readings, which are the reading of Abu Jaafar, Ya’qub, and Khalaf, thus completing the number of ten readings. The book is organized into sequential chapters that begin with the introduction, then the chapter on the Basmala and Umm al-Qur’an. It deals with the provisions of Tajweed and various readings such as assimilation, extension, shortening, hamzat, and inclination, and concludes with the chapter on the brushing of letters, which covers the surahs of the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.3746: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that calls for adherence to the Book of God Almighty, and shows the impact of this on the individual and collective life of a Muslim. The author starts from noticing that many Muslims have turned away from working with the Qur’an despite showing reverence for it, so he seeks to bring together the subject and highlight its features through legal texts.
descriptions.3747: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an that studies the subject of the question in the Holy Qur’an from an educational perspective. The author explains the place of the question in the Qur’an and its importance in learning and teaching, and reviews the etiquette that learners and teachers should adhere to when asking, while explaining the educational characteristics of the question and answer in light of the Qur’anic educational approach.
descriptions.3748: This book studies the alleged suspicions about the Holy Qur’an as mentioned in two international encyclopedias, the Islamic Encyclopedia and the British Encyclopedia, and analyzes and criticizes them. The author begins by defining encyclopedias and their importance, then reviews the Orientalist approach to studying the Qur’an according to what is stated in these two encyclopedias. He then moves on to detail the suspicions contained in them and respond to them, focusing on issues such as the origin of the word and its synonyms, the principle of the universality of Islam, and the position of the Qur’an on freedom of human will. The book aims to correct the wrong image of the Holy Qur’an that may result from these encyclopedias.
descriptions.3749: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which specializes in collecting authentic and chain of transmission hadiths related to the reasons for the revelation of Qur’anic verses, arranged according to the order of the surahs of the Holy Qur’an. His author took care to graduate the hadiths and explain what was authentic and what was weak, relying on fundamental rules for correcting and weakening, and in his fourth edition he added some additions and modifications to what had come before.
descriptions.3750: A book written by the Islamic thinker Malek Bennabi. Its first edition was published in French in 1946, translated by Abdel Sabour Shaheen. Its first Arabic edition was published in 1958 and the second in 1961. A new edition was issued by Dar Al-Fikr in Damascus, and the pages of the book exceed three hundred pages.
descriptions.3751: The Book of Wonders in the Statement of Reasons, is a book on the reasons for the revelation of verses of the Holy Qur’an, written by Abu al-Fadl Ahmad bin Ali bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Hajar al-Asqalani (died: 852 AH). The book talks about an important topic among the topics related to the Holy Qur’an, which is the science of the reasons for the revelation, and this knowledge shows us the temporal and spatial circumstances of the revelation of the verse.
descriptions.3752: This is a brief research into the sciences of the Qur’an, aiming to explain the care that the Holy Qur’an received during the noble Prophet’s era from the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. The research falls into two chapters: The first deals with general topics about the Qur’an, such as its definition, virtues, and the virtue of reciting and memorizing it, while mentioning its most prominent writers and reciters among the Companions. As for the second chapter, it focuses on the Prophet ﷺ’s special care for the Qur’an, such as his keenness to receive and memorize it, his guidance to the Companions to make a commitment to it, his command to improve one’s voice in it, and the prohibition of speaking about it without knowledge.
descriptions.3753: A book that examines the efforts of Muslims in serving the Holy Qur’an and its sciences, and reviews the most prominent scholars and authors in the fields of teaching the Qur’an, readings, and writing in them, from the beginning of the fourth century AH until the modern era. The book is divided into two main chapters, the first of which is devoted to introducing the most famous scholars of the Qur’an and recitations throughout the centuries, and the second to the most important classified works in the sciences of the Qur’an and recitations during the same period.
descriptions.3754: The title of The Seven Readings is a book by its author, Abu al-Tahir Ismail bin Khalaf bin Saeed bin Imran al-Ansari, the Andalusian reciter and grammarian of Al-Saraqusti, who died in the year 455 AH. Al-Saraqusti mentioned the reason for writing the book by saying: “For I will mention in this book - God willing - what the seven famous reciters of the imams of the regions differed about, briefly and concisely, in order to approach those who are cautious and interested in this matter rather than the novices and young people, since I have made my book What is translated as “sufficiency” is sufficient for the finite and the beginner, so I extended it in a simple way that does not constitute a single meaning, so I made this summary as the title and translation of it, for those who practice this matter and are concerned with interpreting a verse in their service; If readers disagree over two translations regarding the letter, I will mention the translation...
descriptions.3755: This book studies and analyzes the proselytizing campaigns directed against the Holy Qur’an, and aims to reveal their motives, methods and history, while refuting the suspicions and allegations they raise about the authenticity of the Qur’an and it being the revealed word of God. The book falls within the framework of the sciences of the Qur’an and responding to suspicions. It begins with an introduction that frames the contemporary civilizational and religious conflict, then reviews the concept of Christianization and its dangers, studies the history of the Christian controversy against the Qur’an from early times until the modern era, and ends by refuting the claims of the skeptics and invalidating their arguments.
descriptions.3756: The book “Al-Fara’id Al-Hassan fi Counting Verses of the Qur’an” by Abdel Fattah Al-Qadi is a poetic collection of verse counting, and it is one of the branches of Qur’anic sciences that specializes in clarifying the number of verses of each surah according to the different schools of thought of the readers. The book explains the disagreement among numerology scholars regarding the verse, such as the Meccan, the Medinan, the Kufi, the Basri, and the Levant, relying on systems to facilitate memorization and control. The author begins with Surah Al-Fatihah and then continues to mention the surahs, explaining for each surah what the readers agreed upon or disagreed about regarding the number of verses.
descriptions.3757: The book “Chapter and Connection in the Holy Qur’an” written by Munir Sultan, is one of the books specialized in the sciences of the Qur’an and Arabic rhetoric. The book deals with the study of the concepts of separation and connection in the Holy Qur’an, tracing the development of this study among the rhetoricians before, after, and after Abdul Qahir al-Jurjani, with a focus on the efforts of Al-Zamakhshari, Al-Sakaki, Al-Qazwini, and Al-Subki. The author aims to overcome the shortcomings of the traditional rhetorical rules for these two concepts, and to provide a new taste of them in the context of the Holy Qur’an, seeking an approach that combines rooting and innovation in the rhetorical lesson.
descriptions.3758: Al-Fawz Al-Kabir fi Usul Al-Tafsir, by Wali Allah Al-Dahlawi, mentioned in it rules that help in understanding and contemplating the Holy Qur’an, and divided it into five chapters, in which he mentioned the approaches of the commentators, the interpretation of strange things, knowledge of the reasons for the revelation, and other things. The book received attention from specialists, and some scholars praised it. It was also decided to teach it in some Islamic schools, and it was explained by one of the Indian scholars. The book was translated from Persian to Arabic and published by some publishing houses.
descriptions.3759: This book studies the personality of Judge Ayyad and his approach to understanding the Qur’anic miracle, reviewing his scientific biography, his journeys in seeking knowledge, and his most prominent teachers and works, with a focus on his book “Al-Shifa bi Definition of the Rights of the Chosen One” as a focus for analyzing his concept of the miracle.
descriptions.3760: A book that deals with the subject of the scientific miracle in the Holy Qur’an, through which the author seeks to prove that the Qur’an is an eternal miracle in which God’s scientific power is revealed. The book reviews universal verses that refer to scientific facts that were not known at the time the Qur’an was revealed, to reveal, with the advancement of science, the accuracy and magnificence of these verses. The work aims to strengthen belief in the greatness and sanctity of the Qur’an, and to emphasize that it is a book preserved from any alteration or change.
descriptions.3761: A book that combines contemplation of verses in the Holy Qur’an and the study of earth sciences. It reviews cosmic and natural phenomena such as stars, planets, the atmosphere, land, water, and energy, from a Qur’anic perspective that aims to link science with belief and contemplate creation.
descriptions.3762: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an that responds to the objections raised by some monks and Christians about the Holy Qur’an, and focuses on refuting the geographical and historical suspicions mentioned by the priest Abdullah Al-Fadi in his book. The author relies on the method of scientific criticism and objective analysis, using the statements of commentators and scholars, to demonstrate the integrity of the Qur’an from contradiction and error, and to demonstrate the greatness of its miracle and its freedom from distortion.
descriptions.3763: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, dealing with an aspect of the Qur’anic miracle, which is the challenge that the Qur’an addressed to humans to produce a surah like it. The author reviews the verses that included this challenge, and explains their linguistic and graphic implications, showing the inability of the polytheists to oppose the Qur’an despite their challenge, in the context of proving the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ and that the Qur’an is the word of God.
descriptions.3764: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an. Its author sets out a set of methodological rules and principles that help in understanding and interpreting the Book of God, based on the connotations of words and the methods of the Qur’an in determining beliefs and rulings. It aims to open the doors of interpretation to the reader and train him to extract meanings through applied examples, focusing on the purposes of the surahs and verses and the methods of pilgrims and argumentation.
descriptions.3765: Rules and References in the Principles of Readings is a book by Ahmed bin Omar bin Muhammad al-Hamawi al-Shafi’i, known as (Ahmed bin Abi al-Rida). The author talked about the issue of preferring some parts of the Qur’an over others, the meaning of the Hadith of the Seven Letters, and the compilation of the Qur’an during the reign of Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him). He also talked about thirty-two origins.
descriptions.3766: The book “The Truest Saying” by Ali Al-Dabaa is an explanation of a system organized by Sheikh Muhammad Al-Mutawali, in which he explains the areas of disagreement between the narration of Abu Bakr Al-Isbahani and the narration of Abu Yaqoub Al-Azraq in Qur’anic readings, through the methods of “Taybat Al-Nashr” and “Al-Shatibiyyah.” The book is organized into successive chapters covering the provisions of recitation, such as the basmalah, the madd and qasr, the euphemism, the hamzat, the adjectives and assimilations, the inclinations, the ra’as and lamas, the ya’s of additions and extras, with a conclusion to the book.
descriptions.3767: The Book of Languages ​​in the Qur’an, written by Abdullah bin Al-Hussein bin Hasnoun Abu Ahmed Al-Samari, is one of the books written in explaining what is in the Qur’an regarding the languages ​​of the Arab tribes and the languages ​​of other non-Arab nations. The book is arranged according to the surahs and verses of the Qur’an. It mentions the word and explains the language of the tribe that spoke it. The book is considered one of the oldest written in explaining the languages ​​of other tribes and nations in the Qur’an. It sheds light on the languages ​​of the tribes before Islam, and determines the proportion of each tribe’s language in the Qur’an. The book was printed and edited by Salah al-Din al-Munajjid and published by Al-Resala Press in Cairo.
descriptions.3768: The book “Al-Mujtaba from the Problem of Parsing the Qur’an” by Ahmed Al-Kharrat is a work in the sciences of the Qur’an that specializes in the science of parsing, and aims to clarify Qur’anic verses whose parsing is ambiguous or difficult to understand. The author selects the problematic verses from the Holy Qur’an, arranging them according to the order of the surahs in the Qur’an, relying on the efforts of previous scholars in this field, and focusing on explaining the parsing of vocabulary, sentences, and semi-sentences.
descriptions.3769: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, specializing in explaining the aspects of abnormal readings and protesting against them, and clarifying their linguistic, grammatical and morphological meanings, based on the origins of Arabic and aspects of usage. The author begins with an introduction to the emergence of readings and the classes of readers, then proceeds to interpret Qur’anic verses, chapter by chapter, mentioning the readings that differ from the well-known ones and showing their linguistic aspect.
descriptions.3770: The Book of Al-Muhkam fi Al-Muhkam fi Al-Qur’an Books is a book by Othman bin Saeed Abi Amr Al-Dani (d. 444 AH). It is a book on the Al-Muhkam fi Al-Qur’an letters and the method of placing marks on them, and it is considered one of the largest and most extensive books in this section. The author mentioned the subject of the book and said: “This is a book that teaches the Qur’an notations and how they are based on the forms of recitation and the doctrines of reading in what they agreed upon and what they differed on, and on what was practiced by the past and used by the copyists, and what is necessitated by Arabic analogy and its verification by the method of language, explaining that with its origins and branches, showing its reasons and aspects, with mentioning of the Sunnahs reported from the past predecessors and the earlier Imams in the points, who started with it first, who among them disliked it, and who gave it concessions, etc. This is what is added to it and is connected to it from the mention of drawing the openings of the surahs and the visions...
descriptions.3771: The Brief Guide to Sciences Related to the Mighty Book, written by Abu Shamah Al-Maqdisi. He wrote it for the people of the Qur’an who are interested in recitations. It mentions some of the sciences related to the Holy Qur’an, especially explaining the meaning of the recitations and their controls, talking about the hadith of the Qur’an being revealed in seven letters, and explaining what it means in detail. The book is considered one of the most important and comprehensive books in explaining the meaning of readings and talking about the hadith of the revelation of the Qur’an in seven letters. The book has been printed in two editions.
descriptions.3772: A book that studies the manuscripts of the Qur’an preserved in the Holy Qur’an Library of the King Abdul Aziz Library in Medina, which dates back to the eleventh century AH. The research addresses the numerical and qualitative trends of these Qur’an manuscripts in terms of types of calligraphy, papers, gilding, and binding. It also sheds light on the efforts of copyists and transcribers and their contributions to preserving these manuscripts. The work aims to provide a scientific vision about the characteristics of these Qur’anic copies and their importance in Qur’anic and historical studies.
descriptions.3773: The Book of the Four Terms in the Qur’an is a treatise written by Professor Abu al-A’la Maududi in the year 1360 AH, corresponding to 1941. He published its chapters successively in his monthly magazine, Tarjuman al-Qur’an, then collected and published it in a treatise called The Four Terms in the Qur’an. What Maududi himself wrote in his introduction to this treatise:
descriptions.3774: Al-Musfi with the most knowledgeable people of Al-Rusukh from the knowledge of abrogated and abrogated, by its author: Abu Al-Faraj, Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Al-Jawzi Al-Hanbali Al-Baghdadi. He summarized it from a book of his on the subject called “Umdat Al-Rasikh” and exaggerated its abbreviation to urge those who wish to memorize it, and he suffices with it in comparison to other works in this field. The author presented important rules regarding the matter of abrogation, such as the possibility of its occurrence, that it concerns commands and prohibitions and not news, and the importance of knowing it for those who work with interpreting the Qur’an. Then he mentioned the related verses in the order of their occurrence in the Qur’an. The book is of interest to those who want to review the verses in which abrogation occurred, for the sake of knowing them and what was said in them briefly, or for the purpose of remembering them.
descriptions.3775: A book that studies a specialized type of classification in the sciences of the Qur’an, which is indexed dictionaries of the words of the Holy Qur’an. The author reviews the origins and development of this type of composition, introduces his most prominent works, and discusses the methods used in arranging them, such as radical and pronunciation order, while balancing them. The book aims to provide a critical, original study of these dictionaries, with a proposal for a project to compose an indexed dictionary that meets the needs of researchers.
descriptions.3776: A book that examines the issue of the Qur’anic miracle, and its author divides it into two main parts: the first deals with the revelation of the Qur’an, its collection, its arrangement, and its readings, and the second devotes it to explaining the aspects of the Qur’anic miracle, focusing on the rhetorical miracle and the characteristics of the Qur’anic style and its words.
descriptions.3777: This is an encyclopedic dictionary specialized in the words of the Holy Qur’an and its readings. It aims to fill a gap in previous lexicographic works that dealt with the Qur’anic text. In his introduction, the author reviews the previous types of Qur’anic dictionaries, such as strange dictionaries, word dictionaries, and indexed dictionaries, indicating the aspects that each of them focuses on, then presenting a new lexical approach that combines the study of words and linking them to Qur’anic readings.
descriptions.3778: Al-Mufradat fi Gharib al-Qur’an is a book written by Al-Raghib Al-Isfahani (who died in 502 AH). The nation’s scholars and notables are almost unanimous in saying that the book “Al-Mufradat fi Gharib Al-Qur’an” by Al-Raghib Al-Isfahani comes first among the many books written on this subject.
descriptions.3779: This is a brief book on the science of stopping and starting in the Holy Qur’an, summarized by its author from the book “The Guide to Stopping and Starting” by the scholar Al-Omani, with the addition of an explanation of the place of revelation of the surahs and other additions. The book aims to summarize the objectives of the art, and explain the positions of stopping that the readers have stipulated, taking into account the meanings and meanings in determining the good and perfect stopping and other things.
descriptions.3780: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an specializing in drawing the Qur’an and controlling its letters. In it, its author collected what he narrated from his sheikhs regarding the decree of the scripts of the Qur’an of the people of the cities (Medina, Mecca, Kufa, Basra, and the Levant) and what they disagreed upon or agreed upon, arranging that in sections and chapters that deal with the deletion and confirmation of the alif, yay, waw, and hamza, and the rulings on cutting, connecting, and feminizing ha’s, with mentioning the news and Sunnahs related to the compilation and writing of the Qur’an. The Qur’an.
descriptions.3781: This book examines the qualities and components necessary for a teacher of the Holy Qur’an, dividing them into three types: subjective, related to belief, intention, and character, scientific, which includes qualifications in the Islamic sciences and familiarity with specialized sciences, and educational, related to teaching methods such as gradualism, gentleness, patience, and consideration of individual differences. The author emphasizes that the teacher is the active element in the educational process, and that these components are necessary to qualify him to carry out his role in teaching the Book of God, basing this on the importance of reception and oral communication in learning the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.3782: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an that specializes in explaining the rulings on stopping and starting when reciting the Book of God. Its author collected it from the sayings of commentators and the books of reciters and grammarians. The book begins with a theoretical introduction explaining the types of endowments (complete, sufficient, good, and ugly) and their rulings. Then, it moves on to applying these rulings to the surahs of the Holy Qur’an in order from Surat Al-Fatihah to the end of the Qur’an, mentioning the interpretation, meaning, and parsing related to each position. The author intended to be brief and concise in order to make it easy to read and to be of general benefit to both the beginner and the advanced.
descriptions.3783: Al-Muhadhdhab regarding the Arabized words that occurred in the Qur’an is a book written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911). He compiled it to show the Arabized words in the Qur’an, which have their origin in another language and then entered the Arabic language and became used in it. The author spoke about the occurrence of these words in the Qur’an, and chose that they are present in it, and that this is part of the perfection of the Qur’an and its encompassing of all other sciences. The author listed the aforementioned words in order according to the letters of the dictionary, and explained the origin of each word, conveying the words of the commentators and linguists before him, then he concluded that with Ibn al-Subki’s systems for the Arabized words, and Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, who commented on al-Subki, organized them, then what the author explained about both of them and organized that as well.
descriptions.3784: This book is an encyclopedia of Qur’anic sciences. It deals with the characteristics of Qur’anic surahs through study and analysis, through topics that include the objectives of each surah, the interconnectedness of its verses, the secrets of its arrangement, the language of its revelation, and its linguistic and metaphorical meanings. Its material has been collected from the main books of the Islamic heritage and modern works on the sciences of the Qur’an, to be a comprehensive reference to help understand the meaning of the Wise Qur’an.
descriptions.3785: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that specializes in the science of Qur’anic recitations. It presents the differences in reading verses according to fourteen approved narrations, starting with Surah Al-Fatihah and Surah Al-Baqarah. For each verse, the book mentions the different readings and the names of the readers who narrated it, along with an explanation of how to pronounce some letters, such as isham, sukka, and madd, indicating that some readers agree with others in some ways.
descriptions.3786: The abrogated and abrogated in the Book of God, by its author, Qatada bin Du’amah Al-Sadoosi, who was a student of Ibn Al-Musayyab and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and was a miracle in memorization, and knowledgeable in interpretation, genealogy, Arabic, language, and the days of the Arabs. Ibn Salamah mentioned the book of Qatada among the sources from which he derived his book, and Al-Zarkashi mentioned Qatada at the head of those who wrote about the abrogated and abrogated, and al-Nahhas and Makki also transmitted many sayings from Qatada, and they are stated in the book, except that this opinion may be far-fetched. Because the classification did not begin in the middle of the second century AH, and because he was blind, rather what is meant is that he collected this topic in his mind, and dictated it to his students and in his lessons. …
descriptions.3787: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which aims to explain the aspects of the Qur’an’s graphic, linguistic and mental miracles, with a focus on proving that the Qur’an is the word of God and not created by humans. The author moves from defining the meaning of the Qur’an to researching its source, through multiple stages that include studying the circumstances of the revelation and the essence of the Qur’an itself, leading to an analysis of its declarative characteristics and the purposes of its surah.
descriptions.3788: “Taybat al-Nashr fi al-Qira’at al-Ten” is Ibn al-Jazari’s Alfiyyah collection of the ten major recitations in which Imam Ibn al-Jazari collected what the reciters differed on and what was reported from them among the most correct methods that he chose. The number of its verses is (1014) verses., on Bahr al-Rajaz (mustaf’ilun six times), and it was called that due to the closeness of its parts and the scarcity of its letters. Ibn Sayyidah Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Ismail, d. 458 AH, said: “Rajaz: poetry whose parts begin with: two rhymes, then ‘watad’, which is a meter that is easy to hear and resonates with the soul.”
descriptions.3789: This book, written by Abu Amr al-Dani, is about the sciences of the Qur’an. It is concerned with explaining the origins of the points of the Qur’an and setting them according to the terms of recitation and the doctrines of reading. The author begins by mentioning the disagreement regarding those among the Followers who began to dot the Qur’an, those who disliked it, and those who permitted it. Then he moves on to detailing the rulings on vowels, signs of sukun and stress, the rulings on the silent noon, assimilation, and appearance, and other issues of control and parsing related to drawing the Qur’an.
descriptions.3790: This is the book “Al-Nukat al-Iladān fi al-‘Ulum al-Ahkam” by Abu Ahmad al-Qassab, in which he deals with verses from the Holy Qur’an, explaining their meanings and implications in various Islamic sciences and laws. The author focuses on clarifying the purposes and benefits of the verses, using precise jokes about the sublime and mysterious verses, the apparent and the difficult, with the aim of showing the legal facts and refuting the attempts of opponents and innovators in interpreting the texts. The book aims to reveal verses that may affect the reader, and explain what may be hidden in their meanings, relying on noble verses from different surahs of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3791: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It presents exegetic, linguistic, and syntactic collections of verses from the Holy Qur’an, arranged according to the surahs from Al-Fatihah to Surat Al-A’raf. The author begins by explaining the Meccan and Medinan surahs, then explains and analyzes linguistic, grammatical, and rhetorical issues in selected verses, with special attention to the meanings of words, forms of parsing, and reading guidance.
descriptions.3792: A book that discusses the ruling on learning Tajweed and its application in reading the Holy Qur’an, reviewing its definition linguistically and terminologically, its origin, the nation’s interest in it, how to receive it, the ruling on adopting it, and melody in reading. The author aims to explain the necessity of Tajweed and to respond to those who separate the Qur’an from Tajweed, relying on the sayings of the imams of Iqra and those with high chains of transmission.
descriptions.3793: The book, Basa’ir Dhu’l-Tamim, was written by Muhammad bin Yaqoub al-Fayrouzabadi, who died in the year 817 AH. The author dealt with a number of sciences, such as: the interpretation of the Great Qur’an, the science of the Prophet’s hadith and its implications, the sciences of knowledge and facts, jurisprudence and its foundations, as well as the science of dialectics, language, industries, and others, through fifty-six objectives mentioned by the author in the beginning of his book. The author of the book was one of the imams of language and literature, a judge, who was the authority of his time in language, hadith, and interpretation. He moved to Shiraz and learned from its scholars. He continued in Zabid for twenty years, and during this period he came to Mecca repeatedly and visited Medina and Taif. He died in Zabid in the year 817 AH. Among his works: Tanweer Al-Miqbas fi Tafsir Ibn Abbas. …
descriptions.3794: The book “Bayan al-Ma’ani” by Mulla Huwaish is an interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, whose chapters and verses are arranged according to the order of revelation, and not according to the order found in the circulating Qur’an. The book begins with a lengthy introduction that includes fundamental topics in the sciences of the Qur’an, such as the principles that the interpreter needs, the conditions of the interpreters, the abrogated and abrogated, readings, and how to compile and arrange the Qur’an. Then he begins to interpret the Meccan surahs, beginning with Surah Al-Alaq, explaining the meanings of the verses and the reasons for their revelation, seeking to achieve the purpose of Imam Ali bin Abi Talib in revealing the history of the revelation and its purposes.
descriptions.3795: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It deals with the issue of metaphor in the Holy Qur’an by studying the position of Imam Ibn Taymiyyah and his students towards it. It presents their opinions between denial and approval, and discusses the evidence of both groups. The author devotes chapters to the most prominent figures on this issue, such as Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, and Sheikh al-Shanqeeti, while citing the sayings of previous imams on the subject.
descriptions.3796: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, written by Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinouri to ward off the suspicions and appeals raised by atheists about the Holy Qur’an, explaining and clarifying the aspects of the problem in it. The author begins by explaining what God has bestowed upon the Arabs in terms of clarification and the breadth of metaphor, then responds to those who challenge the aspects of the readings, and refutes the claims of melody, contradiction, and difference in the Qur’an. He devotes chapters to explaining metaphor, metaphor, the inverted, deletion, abbreviation, repetition of speech, metonymy, exposition, and the apparent contradiction of the word to its meaning, such as using the word “command” when it is threatening or permissible, and the generality of the word with the intention of specificity.
descriptions.3797: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It examines the history of the Holy Qur’an, its compilation, writing, the arrangement of its verses and surahs, its control and correction, with a focus on the drawing of the Uthmani Qur’an, its rules and oddities, whether it was drawn by a Tawqifi or not, and the ruling on following it, in addition to discussions on the points of the Qur’an, its shape, and its writing, ancient and modern.
descriptions.3798: The book “Tahbir al-Taysir fi al-Qira’at al-Ten” by Ibn al-Jazari is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It aims to explain and expand the book “Al-Taysir” by Abu Amr al-Dani in the Seven Qira’at, while adding the other three readings to complete the ten readings. The author begins by mentioning his lineage and status, then addresses the names of the reciters and those who transmitted them, and details the provisions of intonation and recitation, such as seeking refuge, naming, assimilation, extending and shortening, hamzat, tilting, and pausing, in order to correct the misconceptions about limiting the correct readings to what was stated in the books of Al-Taysir and Al-Shatibiyyah only.
descriptions.3799: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It deals with the issue of the prohibition of writing the Holy Qur’an in non-Arabic letters, whether foreign or Latin. In reporting this ruling, the author relies on evidence from the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Companions. Then he quotes the sayings of the four imams, jurists, and hadith scholars, and presents the opinions of contemporary committees, councils, and fatwa bodies on the issue.
descriptions.3800: This book is a poetic collection on the science of reciting the Qur’an, written by Sheikh Suleiman Al-Jamzouri, and is located in the section on the sciences of the Qur’an. The nazim explains the basic rulings of recitation, starting with the rulings on the noon sakinah and tanween, then moving on to the rulings on the stressed nun and meem, the sakinah meem, the definite lam and the verb lam, and the attributes of letters such as the mathlin and the contiguous, and he concludes with the sections and rulings of the madd. The systems were formulated in an easy-to-learn style, with brief explanations aimed at resolving whatever meanings might be confusing to the student.
descriptions.3801: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that deals with the issue of translating the meanings of the Holy Qur’an. The author emphasizes in his introduction that this topic is not new, but rather as old as Islamic jurisprudence, and reviews the importance of addressing it clearly and realistically in light of Islamic law, which is characterized by comprehensiveness and flexibility to accommodate every new reality.
descriptions.3802: This book is written by Ibrahim Abdel Hamid Salama, and it falls in the field of Qur’anic sciences. It deals with the subject of the Qur’anic verses that describe the Qur’an as confirming the previous heavenly books, and aims to explain the correct meaning of this approval and dominance, in response to the suspicions of orientalists and missionaries who claimed that this means that the previous books are safe from distortion and that it is necessary to act upon them. The book reviews the aspects of the Qur’an’s dominance over the heavenly books and the relationship of this dominance to ratification.
descriptions.3803: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that aims to correct misunderstandings of some verses, and explains the necessity of contemplating the Qur’an and making it easy for understanding, while warning against saying its meanings without knowledge. The book presents examples of corrections by the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions to some misunderstood Quranic concepts, such as clarifying the meanings of the two threads, injustice, easy reckoning, and other verses.
descriptions.3804: This is a book on the interpretation of verses of rulings from the Holy Qur’an. It aims to extract legal and jurisprudential rulings from the verses they cover, relying on an approach that combines interpretation by tradition and interpretation by opinion. The book begins with an introduction to the science of interpretation and its types, then begins the interpretation of Surat Al-Fatihah and Surat Al-Baqarah, covering with explanation and analysis the verses of the rulings related to prayer, abrogation, usury, and others, with an explanation of the rulings taken from them.
descriptions.3805: A book that examines the truth of the interpretation attributed to the Sufi Ibn Arabi, and reveals the danger of its publication and circulation. The author begins with a historical foundation of the emergence and development of Sufism, distinguishes between theoretical and philosophical Sufi interpretation and indicative Sufi interpretation, then devotes the largest section to explaining Ibn Arabi’s position on these two types, and concludes with a critical evaluation of his article and determining the truth of the interpretation attributed to him, warning of the doctrinal harms resulting from its circulation among general readers.
descriptions.3806: A book that examines the evaluation of methods of teaching the Holy Qur’an and its sciences through various media, such as the mosque, school, radio, television, and the Internet. The author reviews the general foundations for evaluating the teaching method derived from the Qur’an, such as dialogue, stories, and proverbs, and then moves on to evaluating practical methods for memorizing and encouraging it, while devoting a section to Internet programs and translating the meanings of the Qur’an. The book aims to evaluate these educational methods in light of the Qur’anic curriculum, with reference to the efforts of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in printing and publishing the Qur’an.
descriptions.3807: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that aims to evaluate the methods of teaching memorization of the Holy Qur’an in the circles of Qur’an memorization associations, reviewing the virtues of learning and teaching the Qur’an, the goals of the Qur’an circles, and the methods used in education, pointing out the common errors in them, and proposing the optimal method for achieving quality in education.
descriptions.3808: A book that aims to evaluate the methods of teaching the Holy Qur’an and its sciences in memorization schools, reviewing the virtues of the Qur’an, the etiquette of its recitation, and the goals of teaching it, with a focus on evaluating the methods of memorizing the Qur’an, recitation, intonation, readings, interpretation, and the sciences of the Qur’an. The book is organized into two chapters, preceded by an introduction, and ends with a conclusion and recommendation, to be an educational reference in the field of teaching the Qur’an.
descriptions.3809: Alerting the heedless and guiding the ignorant about the mistakes that happen to them when they recite the clear Book of God, by its author, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad Al-Saffaksi Al-Nouri, the owner of a private school concerned with the Qur’an in terms of correct performance, and his dedication to this aspect was great, as he founded a school concerned with this in Sfax, influenced in that regard by his Sheikh Ibn Al-Nasser, who founded his famous zawiya in Morocco that concerned with the Sunnah. He touched on most of the rulings of recitation, such as the chapter on exits and attributes, seeking refuge and basmalah, and the rulings on the noon sakinah and tanween, and he separated the chapter on letters, mentioning each letter separately, and explaining everything that distinguishes each letter from the other, while explaining the mistakes that readers make with these letters, and how to avoid them.
descriptions.3810: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, in which the author collected Qur’anic words that had multiple readings in three grammatical forms (nominative, accusative, and genitive), and arranged them according to the letters of the dictionary to facilitate researchers. The book begins with an introduction in which he explains his approach, then deals with each letter of the alphabet, mentioning the verses in which the Trinity is mentioned, and explaining the grammatical aspects of each reading.
descriptions.3811: The book “Tuhfat Al-Azra fi what was recited in triliteral form from the letters of the Qur’an” by the author Al-Ra’ini Abi Jaafar. It is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It collects the Qur’anic words that were mentioned in three different readings (in triangulation) with an explanation of their parsing and orientation. The author arranged his material according to the letters of the dictionary to make it easier for the viewer, starting with the letter hamza, and following that with jokes and jokes that he included throughout the book.
descriptions.3812: This is a book on the interpretation of the noble verse: {Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world, and the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope}. It discusses the reason for its revelation and the differences of the interpreters in what is meant by the enduring good deeds. Then the author prefers one of the sayings, and mentions the hadiths contained in the virtue of praising God, praising God, glorifying God, and glorifying Him, and explains the secret of the virtue of these four words, with the addition of Al-Hawqala to them.
descriptions.3813: The Beauty of the Qur’an is a book by its author, Ilm al-Din Ali bin Muhammad al-Sakhawi, one of the compilers of the sciences of the Qur’an. It shows its importance in its connection to the Holy Qur’an. Its author divided it into seven sciences, which are: scattering pearls in mentioning verses and surahs, concise disclosure in clarifying the miraculous, the stages of reverence and glorification in the virtues of the Great Qur’an, fragmentation of the Qur’an, the strongest number in knowing the number, mentioning the abnormal, and the firm foundation in the abrogated and abrogated. A group of scholars of the sciences of the Qur’an benefited from his book, including: Abu Shama, as he quoted from it in many places, and Al-Suyuti was most proficient in the sciences of the Qur’an from narrating from it, as in Mecca and Medina, urban and travel, day and night, and others.
descriptions.3814: A book that examines the history of collecting, preserving, and writing the Holy Qur’an, reviewing the stages of caring for it from its revelation until its recording in the Qur’an. He begins by defining the meaning of the collection of the Qur’an linguistically and terminologically, then addresses its memorization in heaven and on its way to earth and on earth, and details its writing during the era of the Prophet ﷺ and its tools and writers of revelation. It also covers the collection of the Qur’an during the era of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Uthman bin Affan (may Allah be pleased with them both), explaining the reasons for each collection, its methods, and its characteristics.
descriptions.3815: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, examining an important stage in the history of the codification of the Holy Qur’an, which was its compilation during the reign of the two caliphs Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with them both). The book is organized into detailed sections that review the motives, means, and results of the combination in each era, while explaining the differences between the two combinations and their relationship to the seven letters. Through this research, the author aims to highlight the interest of the early Muslims in preserving the Book of God and transmitting it reliably.
descriptions.3816: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, examining the stage of compiling the Holy Qur’an during the caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with them both). The book explains the motivations and reasons for collecting in each era, how to implement it, the methods adopted in it, and its results and benefits. He also draws a comparison between the two collections, and addresses the issue of the seven letters and their consideration in each of them.
descriptions.3817: Jewels of the Qur’an and Its Pearls, a book by Imam Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali, in which he explains the secrets and purposes of the Qur’an. The book is not considered an interpretation of the Qur’an, but rather it is an explanation of the sciences of the Qur’an, a statement of the preference of some verses of the Qur’an over others, a narration of what Al-Ghazali called the jewels of the Qur’an, then a narration of what he called the pearls of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3818: This is a footnote to the introduction to the interpretation of the Qur’an, written by the author Abdul Rahman bin Qasim to explain and clarify the meanings of the original introduction and clarify its objectives. The book is organized into topics on the sciences of the Qur’an. It deals with the revelation of the Qur’an and its being the word of God, the places of its revelation, the seven letters, the collection of the Qur’an, the reason for the revelation, the abrogated and abrogated, the decisive and the similar, the miracle of the Qur’an, methods of interpretation, and a mention of the best interpretations, with a response to the people of innovation and a warning against interpretation by opinion.
descriptions.3819: The book of Hujjat al-Qira’at, the science of Qira’at is an important science that deals with the readings mentioned by the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ in the Holy Qur’an. They are aspects of reading some words of the Qur’an or in the method of writing from Rum or Ishmaam. The multiplicity of readings does not mean making each of them a Qur’an that changes a ruling or changes its content. Attaining this knowledge is not an easy matter, so the student attains it without effort or fatigue. …
descriptions.3820: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, written by Imam Muwaffaq al-Din al-Maqdisi, and it contains a debate that took place between him and some heretics about the nature of the Holy Qur’an. The author explains at the beginning that he did not want to write the debate as a story for fear of addition or subtraction, but rather he intended to mention the areas of disagreement between him and them, as he believes that the Qur’an is the word of God and that it is these surahs and verses that are recited, heard and written, while his opponents see that these surahs are not the Qur’an but rather an expression of it and a story of it, and that they were created.
descriptions.3821: A book that deals with an aspect of the scientific miracles in the Holy Qur’an, and focuses on specific examples such as honey and dates, reviewing their components and medical benefits as mentioned in the Qur’anic text. The author aims to show the compatibility of some modern scientific facts with what is stated in the Qur’an, emphasizing the comprehensiveness of the Qur’anic miracle in various fields of knowledge.
descriptions.3822: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an and rhetoric, and it was originally a scientific research discussed to obtain a doctorate degree. The book studies the characteristics of Qur’anic expression and its rhetorical features, examining in its first chapters the function of linguistic expression and its development, and the elements of language and linguistic meaning. Then it moves to the value of rhetorical aspects in the beauty of expression across different eras, with a focus on the connection of rhetoric to major issues of criticism.
descriptions.3823: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that responds to the claims of Orientalists who deny the divine revelation of the Holy Qur’an and claim that it is from the Prophet ﷺ. The author begins by defining Orientalism and explaining the sayings of the Orientalists, then proceeds to refute these claims with arguments and proofs, based on the texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah, and showing that the hostility of the Orientalists to the messengers and prophets is an extension of the hostility of the human devils and the jinn to the truth and its people.
descriptions.3824: This is a book on the sciences of the Holy Qur’an. It aims to provide a comprehensive study of this science, beginning with defining it linguistically and terminologically, and explaining the differences between the Qur’an and the sacred hadiths, and its names and attributes. The book reviews the emergence of Qur’anic sciences and their development throughout the ages, starting from the era of the Prophet ﷺ, through the era of the Companions and Followers, with a focus on the prominent scholarly schools in Mecca, Medina, and Kufa.
descriptions.3825: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It examines a number of basic topics related to the Holy Qur’an, beginning with the definition of the sciences of the Qur’an, their origin and development, then it deals with the names of the Qur’an and the difference between it and the holy and prophetic hadith. It moves on to the study of the revelations of the Qur’an and its astrology, the first and last revelations, and the destinations of revelation. Then it examines the Meccan and Medinan sciences, their controls and purposes, and concludes with a study of the verses of the Qur’an and its surahs, their order and number, and the revelation of the Qur’an in seven letters.
descriptions.3826: Durrat al-Tanzeel wa Ghurat al-Interpretation, deals with the topic of directing Qur’anic verses that are similar in pronunciation, that are repeated in multiple places with identical or different words, about which a problem may arise, or that may be subject to consideration for some reason. The author mentioned the reason for writing the book in the introduction to the book; He said: “I was called by strong motives, prompted by consideration and consideration, at the repeated verses, with the words that agree, the different ones, and their similar, related, and deviant letters, searching for signs that would remove the ambiguity of their ambiguities, and single out the word with its verses, not its forms. So I resolved upon it after I contemplated most of the books of the ancients and those of the later ones, and searched for the secrets of the meanings of the clear-eyed, verified interpreters, and I did not find anyone among its people who had attained the ultimate meaning of its essence. How? …
descriptions.3827: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It is a scientific thesis for which its author obtained a doctorate degree. It studies the claims of those who challenge the Holy Qur’an during the fourteenth century AH. The book begins with an introduction that defines the objection in the Qur’an and the terms that are synonymous with it, then it is divided into two parts: the first is theoretical, examining the origins of the challenge, its causes, and how to confront it, and the second is practical, presenting the overall responses to the objections and studying the position of the challengers regarding the verses of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3828: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which aims to prevent the illusion of contradiction and confusion between the verses of the Holy Qur’an, by combining verses in which there may be an illusion of difference, and showing the aspects of reconciliation between them. The author arranged his material according to the order of the surahs, beginning with Surah Al-Baqarah, to show that the verses of the book are all truth and justice, with no contradiction in them.
descriptions.3829: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, explaining the “Mawrid al-Thirst” system in the techniques of Qur’anic drawing and control. It begins with an introduction to the origins of Qur’anic readings and the controls for their authenticity, then deals in detail with the rules of drawing and controlling the Qur’an, such as deletion and affirmation, foreign names, adding and deleting letters, separation and connection, and other sections of Qur’anic drawing.
descriptions.3830: This book examines the issue of the drawing of the Uthmani Qur’an and its relationship to the differences in Qur’anic readings, by responding to the opinions of the orientalist Ignaz Goldziher, who claimed that the absence of dots and shapes in the Arabic script was the reason for the emergence of these differences. The author relies on historical and narrational evidence to show the connection of the readings with the Prophet’s chain of transmission, and studies the position of grammarians and ancient readers regarding the drawing of the Qur’an, addressing the issues of choice in the readings and rhetoric in the differences, with appendices that remove suspicions and clarify the major facts in this field.
descriptions.3831: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an that examines the issue of drawing and controlling the Qur’an, and the extent of its connection to the Prophet’s suspension or whether it is an ijtihad term. The author reviews the history of compilation of the Qur’an during the reign of Abu Bakr and Uthman, the nature of the writing of the Ottoman Qur’an, the phenomena of Ottoman drawing and the position of scholars towards it, while discussing the decisions of the jurisprudence councils in this regard, and ends with an explanation of the modern control rules and their relationship to ancient drawing.
descriptions.3832: Masterpieces of Al-Bayan, Interpretation of Verses of Rulings from the Qur’an, a book on the science of interpretation, specialized in explaining Qur’anic verses containing legal rulings. Its author: Muhammad Ali Al-Sabouni. The book focuses on interpretation, mentioning the vocabulary of the language, and summarizing the rulings taken from the verses. It mentions the sayings of the interpreting scholars, the sayings of linguists, and scholars of schools of jurisprudence, and hadith. The book is considered a scientific reference, and is distinguished by its clear style of presentation.
descriptions.3833: The Spirit of Meanings in the Interpretation of the Great Qur’an and the Seven Mathanis is an interpretation of the Qur’an by Abu Al-Thana’ Al-Alusi. Al-Alusi's book is considered one of the important books of interpretation, and his method in doing so is researching how to pronounce the words of the Holy Qur’an, their meanings, their individual and syntactic rulings, their meanings that carry the state of composition, and the sequels to that, such as knowing the abrogation, the reason for the revelation, a story that explains what is obscure in the Qur’an, and so on. He finished writing the interpretation in 1267 AH.
descriptions.3834: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an that studies Surah Al-Waqi’ah in terms of its approach to determining Islamic beliefs. It deals with the topics of the Surah, such as the rational inevitability of resurrection, the destinies of people on the Day of Resurrection, the bliss of Paradise and the torment of Hell, while linking that to philosophical and scientific discussions about the annihilation of the world.
descriptions.3835: This book examines one aspect of the Qur’anic miracle, focusing on the miracle of Islamic law contained in the Holy Qur’an. The author moves from talking about the nature of previous miracles to explaining why the miracle of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was a moral one, namely the Qur’an, to suit the immortality and generality of the message. The book then reviews examples of Sharia rulings, such as zakat, marriage, divorce, inheritance, and freedoms, showing their distinction and justice, to prove that their legislative system itself represents evidence of the miraculous nature of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3836: The book Pages in the Sciences of Recitations, written by Abdul Qayyum bin Abdul Ghafour Al-Sindhi. This book falls under the classification of Qur’anic Sciences or Sciences of Recitations. The first edition was in the year 1415 AH, corresponding to 1995 AD, in Arabic, and has now reached the seventh edition in 2015. It was translated in 2015 into the Urdu language. It is printed by Al-Imdiya Scientific Library, which was previously called Al-Imdiya Library. Some faculty members in the Reading Department at Umm Al-Qura University also adopt it as a basic reference for male and female students.
descriptions.3837: This is an audio book specialized in the sciences of the Qur’an, which studies the phenomenon of the occasional tide of calm through an applied experimental approach. The research is based on accurately measuring the time period of this tide using audio laboratory devices, in the reading of four contemporary reciters of Surah Hud, according to the narration of Hafs on the authority of Asim. The book aims to determine the precise time average of the occasional elongation of sukun, comparing it to the opinions of reading scholars who estimated its duration as two, four, or six movements.
descriptions.3838: This book defends the infallibility of the Holy Qur’an and responds to the suspicions raised by missionaries, detailing the linguistic and content objections they raise to the Qur’anic text. The author criticizes the attacks on Islam and the Qur’an from different religious backgrounds, and analyzes some linguistic suspicions, such as the use of certain formulas or the presence of foreign words, considering them to be foolish things that do not affect the sanctity and eloquence of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3839: This book, written by Muhammad Al-Sayyid Radhi Jibril, is located in the field of Qur’anic sciences, and deals with the subject of the miraculous nature of the Holy Qur’an. The author begins by defining the miraculous and explaining its importance, then reviews the opinions of scholars regarding the miraculous, and dedicates a chapter to give a historical rooting of the issue. The book devotes the main sections to detailing the various aspects of miracles, covering rhetorical and systemic miracles, information about the unseen, information about previous nations, and psychological, legislative, and scientific miracles.
descriptions.3840: This book is a study concerned with demonstrating the close correlation between the sciences of the Qur’an and the sciences of the Arabic language, and confirming that serving the Holy Qur’an was the greatest motivation for the emergence and development of Arabic sciences. The author explains that it is impossible to separate these two sciences in terms of origin, history, and composition, and that each of them cannot do without the other.
descriptions.3841: This book is concerned with studying the role of the Islamic Endowment in serving the Holy Qur’an throughout the ages, tracing the development of the institutions concerned with it, such as mosques, libraries, and Quranic schools. The author reviews the legitimacy of the endowment and the goals of the endowments, highlighting historical examples of endowments dedicated to teaching, reciting, and printing the Qur’an, with appendices documenting some Quranic schools in Damascus and Cairo.
descriptions.3842: This book presents the efforts of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in serving the Holy Qur’an, focusing on two main aspects: interpreting the Holy Qur’an and translating its meanings into other languages. The author reviews the programs and projects implemented by various government agencies to achieve this concern, such as establishing Qur’an memorization schools, holding local and international competitions, establishing a specialized radio station, and printing the Holy Qur’an and its translations. The book aims to highlight the Kingdom’s pioneering role in spreading and teaching the Book of God inside and outside the country.
descriptions.3843: This book is the title of the guide from the Decrees of the Tanzeel Line by Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakshi. It deals with the study of the Qur’an’s script and the details of its letters and signs, compared to the Anam script, to explain the differences between them and explain their reasons. It focuses on analyzing the letters hamza, alif, waw, and yaa, dealing with the extension and contraction of the ta’at, and also discusses the rules of connection and reservation in reading the Qur’an. The book aims to guide the reader to a more accurate understanding of the script of the Qur’an and the mechanisms of translating written letters into audible sounds.
descriptions.3844: A book on the science of reciting the Holy Qur’an. It aims to teach the reader of the Qur’an the rules and etiquette of correct recitation, reviewing the virtue of reciting the Qur’an and the importance of learning and teaching it. The book covers a historical overview of the science of Tajweed and recitations, and explains the meaning and purpose of Tajweed, with a detail of its practical and theoretical sections, and an explanation of the pillars of correct recitation and their levels, in addition to the definition of melody and its sections.
descriptions.3845: The book “The Stranger of the Qur’an, called Nuzhat al-Qulub,” was written by Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Uzair al-Sijistani, and it is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. The book aims to explain the strange words mentioned in the Holy Qur’an. The author has arranged it according to the letters of the dictionary (the alphabet) to facilitate its reading and memorization, as each chapter is divided into chapters according to the movement of the first letter of the word. The book begins with an introduction to the disjointed letters at the beginning of the surahs, then proceeds to explain the strange Qur’anic vocabulary chapter by chapter.
descriptions.3846: The Stranger of the Qur’an in Arab Poetry is a book attributed to Abdullah bin Abbas, from the narration of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim. The book contains Ibn Abbas’s answers in response to issues that troubled Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq (Al-Kharji), and he came to ask Abdullah bin Abbas about them.
descriptions.3847: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that explains the strange words mentioned in the Holy Qur’an, and clarifies their linguistic meanings, with special attention to the derivation of God’s names and attributes and the interpretation of letters that occur frequently in the Holy Book. The author begins his interpretation of Surah Al-Fatihah, proceeding through the surahs and verses, explaining the obscure words according to a linguistic approach.
descriptions.3848: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, explaining the meanings of strange words mentioned in the Holy Qur’an, beginning with mentioning the Most Beautiful Names and Attributes of God and their derivation, then moving on to interpreting the words that are frequently repeated in the book, following the order of the surahs from Al-Fatihah to Surat Al-Shu’ara’. The author aims at brevity and clarification, drawing his material from the books of commentators and linguists, avoiding lengthy grammar, hadith, and chains of transmission, and rejecting objectionable interpretation and fabricated interpretation.
descriptions.3849: The book “Fath al-Rahman Bi Revealing What is Ambiguous in the Qur’an” by Zakaria al-Ansari is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, aiming to clarify the areas of problem and confusion that may pose a problem to the reader in the verses of the Holy Qur’an. The book begins with an interpretation of Surat Al-Fatihah, then deals with the Qur’anic surahs in turn, up to Surat Al-Qasas, revealing the problematic meanings in them. This work falls within the efforts of scholars to serve interpretation and clarify the details of the Qur’anic text.
descriptions.3850: The book “Fath Rab al-Bariyah Explanation of the Introduction to Tajweed Al-Jazariyya” is an explanation of the famous “Introduction to Al-Jazariyya” text in the science of Tajweed of the Holy Qur’an. The book is organized into chapters that cover basic topics of Tajweed science, such as the characteristics of letters and their origins, the rulings on the noon sakunah and tanween, the duration, stopping and beginning, and other topics. The second edition of the book was distinguished by the addition of some important sections, such as seeking refuge and the basmalah, and a section on stress and Qur’anic approval, along with reviewing and correcting errors.
descriptions.3851: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, in which its author, Abu Ubaid al-Qasim bin Salam, collected a number of hadiths and traces related to the merits of the Holy Qur’an, its learning and teaching, and an explanation of the etiquette of its recitation and carrying it. The book deals with various topics, including the virtue of reading and listening to the Qur’an, the virtue and priority of its people, rulings related to reciting it, such as chanting and improving one’s voice with it, and issues regarding concluding it and reciting it regularly, with an explanation of the etiquette and glorification that should be given to the bearer of the Qur’an, and a warning against forgetting it or relying on it.
descriptions.3852: The book “The Virtues of the Qur’an” by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It collects hadiths and traces related to the merits of reciting, learning and teaching the Qur’an. It explains the status of the people of the Qur’an and the necessity of understanding it, while warning against turning away from it, arguing about it, or speaking about it without knowledge.
descriptions.3853: The virtues of the Qur’an are very many, countless. For Muslims, the Holy Qur’an is the book that God Almighty revealed to Muhammad ﷺ, as guidance and mercy for all people. It is the eternal book of God, and His ultimate proof, and it will endure until life on earth ends. Reading the Qur’an has great virtue. Through it, a Muslim attains good deeds and receives a great reward. In this regard, the Prophet ﷺ says: “Whoever reads a letter from the Book of God will have a good deed for it, and a good deed is multiplied ten times as much. I do not say (Alif) is a letter, but Alif is a letter, Laam is a letter, and Meem is a letter,” and the memorizer of the Qur’an has a great reward from God. The Qur’an will intercede for its companion on the Day of Resurrection, and will raise his status and rank in Paradise. So he will be with the angels, the honorable and the righteous. …
descriptions.3854: The Virtues of the Qur’an is a book by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ayyub bin Yahya bin Dharis Al-Bajli Al-Razi, (200 AH - 294 AH). The book is about observing the virtues of the Holy Qur’an. The author mentioned topics related to the Holy Qur’an, and we can consider his book to be divided into two parts. The first section was devoted to mentioning topics related to the sciences of the Qur’an, including: seeking refuge from a verse in which there is an exorcism, asking for mercy at a mercy verse, the hatred of tithes, the virtue of one who learns and teaches the Qur’an, how the Qur’an was revealed and in how many times it was revealed? The second section relates to mentioning the virtues of the surahs and verses, so he mentioned the virtue. Al-Fatihah, Surat Al-Baqarah, Surat Al-Kahf, Surat Al-Sajdah, Surat Al-Hashr, and Surat Al-Ikhlas. …
descriptions.3855: The Virtues of the Qur’an is a book on the virtues of the Holy Qur’an, written by Ahmed bin Ali bin Shuaib bin Ali bin Sinan bin Bahr Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Nasa’i. Its content is that in order to monitor the virtues of the Holy Qur’an, the author mentioned in it topics related to the Holy Qur’an, and we can consider his book to be two parts. The first section was devoted to mentioning topics related to the sciences of the Qur’an, including: the revelation of the Qur’an, Gabriel’s presentation of the Qur’an, mentioning reading the Qur’an, and writing the Qur’an, and the second section is related to mentioning The virtues of the surahs and verses, and he mentioned the virtues of Al-Fatihah, Ayat Al-Kursi, Al-Kahf, Al-Zalzalah, and Al-Mu’awwidhatayn. He mentioned 126 hadiths in his book. …
descriptions.3856: Arts of Art in the Eyes of the Sciences of the Qur’an is a book on the sciences and explanation of the contents of the Holy Qur’an, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn al-Jawzi (508 AH - 597 AH). The book is considered one of the oldest books devoted to the sciences of the Qur’an. In his book, the author talks about the virtues of the Holy Qur’an, and that it is not created, and about the seven letters, and the writing of the Qur’an, and the number of surahs, verses, letters, points, and parts, and about everything that is Meccan surahs and Medinan surahs, and the languages in the Qur’an. The Noble One, about the etiquette of stopping and starting, about the problematic and the similar, substitution, addition and subtraction, and the difference between interpretation and interpretation.
descriptions.3857: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that examines understanding and interpreting the meanings of the Qur’an, with a focus on issues of God’s purity, attributes, and names, and responding to theological sects such as the Jahmiya, Mu’tazila, Mushhabi, and Hashiya. The book also deals with the subject of the mind and its function in receiving Sharia, and details issues of abrogation, the creation of the Qur’an, and promise and threat, with attention to linguistic methods such as introduction, delay, implication, separation, and connection.
descriptions.3858: Fayd al-Mu’in on collecting the forty in the virtue of the clear Qur’an was written by: Ali bin Sultan al-Harawi al-Qari, known as Mulla Ali al-Qari, a Hanafi jurist. He was born in Herat, lived in Mecca, and died there in the year 1014 AH - 1606 AD. He wrote many books. Topics of the book: The book talks about the virtues of the Qur’an, and the virtues of those who read the Qur’an, and he referred to that in his book. One of the features of this book is that it extracts hadiths from their original sources with the wording that matches the source, and does not alter them. It makes judgments on the hadith when necessary, and explains some issues by way of brevity.
descriptions.3859: Necklaces of Coral in the Statement of the Abrogated and Abrogated from the Qur’an is a book written by Mar’i bin Yusuf Al-Karmi, one of the scholars of the eleventh century AH. He was born in Tulkarm and died in Cairo in the year 1033 AH. In this book, the author addressed abrogated and abrogated verses in the Qur’an. He began with a nice mention in which he alerted to the importance of abrogated and abrogated and condemned ignorance of them. Then he spoke about the meanings of abrogation in language and terminology. Then he mentioned the divisions of abrogated and abrogated in the Holy Qur’an. Then he spoke about what may be abrogated and abrogated. Then he mentioned the surahs that the abrogated and abrogated included, which are twenty-five. Then he mentioned some controls and rules in abrogation, then he discussed the abrogated. The surahs of the Holy Qur’an are abrogated according to their order in the Qur’an.
descriptions.3860: A book on the science of recitation of the Holy Qur’an. It specializes in the narration of Hafs on the authority of Asim, and collects a summary of what is in ancient works in a manner suitable for students.
