It begins with a historical introduction to Tajweed and recitations, then deals in detail with the origins of the letters and their characteristics, and the rulings on the noun sakinah, tanween, meem sakinah, madd, shortening, and haa of metonymy, with applied exercises. The author aims to approximate the rules of this art, relying on eloquent Arabic taste, while emphasizing the importance of the practical application of correct pronunciation.
descriptions.3861: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, specializing in mentioning the seven famous Qur’anic recitations and their imams. The author begins by explaining people's differences in recitation as well as their differences in rulings, and describes the positions of those who memorize the Qur'an and their degrees in knowledge and mastery. Then the book is devoted to mentioning the imams of reciters in the cities (Medina, Mecca, Kufa, Basra, and the Levant), their lineages, teachers, and students, along with listing the chains of transmission that were quoted from them.
descriptions.3862: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, specializing in explaining the seven frequent recitations, their origins and their interpretations, based on the methods of Tayseer and Shatibiyyah, with the addition of authentic benefits. It begins with an introduction to the virtue of recitation, then addresses the details of the recitation of each of the seven imams, beginning with Nafi’s recitation, and includes sections on the rulings on recitation such as seeking refuge, basmalah, madd, shortening, assimilation, tilting, and stopping.
descriptions.3863: A book that deals with the status and great status of the Holy Qur’an, and shows that it is the dominant book over the heavenly books that preceded it. The author reviews the aspects of the miraculous nature of the Qur’an, the virtue of reciting and memorizing it, and the etiquette that must be observed by its reader, while explaining the amount of it that must be memorized.
descriptions.3864: The Book of the Qur’an is a book about the collection of the Holy Qur’an, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud. In his book, the author deals with many issues related to the Holy Qur’an, its writing, the date of its compilation, the names of the writers of the revelation, the compilation of the Qur’an after the death of the Prophet, and talk about the Uthmani Qur’an, the Imam’s Qur’an, and the Qur’an of the Companions. The author followed his method in writing the book as follows: The compiler divided the book into sections, and gave each section a title that carries a brief reference to the content of the texts he will mention in it. The door. …
descriptions.3865: The book “Arguments of the Qur’an” by Al-Razi Ibn Al-Mukhtar is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, aiming to extract arguments and proofs from the Holy Qur’an for various Islamic sects. The book begins with a sermon by the author in which he explains the virtue of contemplating God’s verses. Then, in its many chapters, he deals with doctrinal topics such as will and will, guidance and misguidance, predestination, the actions of servants, and those who commit major sins, citing Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths in discussing the opinions of sects such as the Jabriyah, the Qadariyah, the Murji’ah, and others.
descriptions.3866: The book “Kashf al-Ma’ani fi al-Mutabhab Min al-Mathani” by Ibn Jama’ah, Badr al-Din, is an author on the sciences of the Qur’an. He explains and analyzes similar verses in the Holy Qur’an, beginning with Surat al-Fatihah and continuing by presenting issues related to word structures and their connotations, such as explaining the benefit of introducing the name “The Most Merciful” to “The Most Merciful” and the wisdom of repeating the basmalah. The book aims to reveal the precise meanings and respond to the problems related to the verbal similarities between surahs and verses.
descriptions.3867: A book that examines the subject of memorizing the Holy Qur’an, reviews its virtues and the morals of its followers, while explaining the concept of memorization and the factors necessary for it, such as personal preparation, time management, and receiving from a reciter. The book presents practical Islamic methods for memorization, including general steps and the role of the reciter and student, in addition to programs and auxiliary means such as recordings and competitions, within a systematic framework aimed at facilitating the memorization of the Book of God.
descriptions.3868: Lubab al-Naqul fi Asbab al-Nazul is a book written by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849 AH/1445 AD - 911 AH/1505 AD), in the chapter on the reasons for the revelation of verses of the Qur’an. This book is considered one of the most important books written in the chapter on the causes of revelation, and it is distinguished from Al-Wahidi’s book “The Causes of Revelation” by its brevity, additions to it, attributing each hadith to those who narrated it among the authors of respected books, distinguishing the authentic from others, and what is accepted from what is rejected, combining multiple narrations, and setting aside what is not among the causes of revelation.
descriptions.3869: The book “Graphic Touches in Texts from the Revelation” is a study in the sciences of the Qur’an. Its author aims to highlight the secrets of Qur’anic expression and artistic touches in selected texts from multiple surahs, such as the surahs of Al-Fatihah, Al-Ma’idah, and Stories of the Prophets. The book reviews aspects of the accuracy of the choice of words and expression in the revelation, considering it a step towards understanding the Quranic miracle, not a comprehensive statement of it, and emphasizing the multiplicity of aspects of the miracle that require various specializations.
descriptions.3870: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an by its author, Mahmoud Shukri Al-Alusi, which deals with research and reasoning with the verses mentioned in the Holy Qur’an that refer to the rules of the new structure, such as the movement of the Earth and its rotation around the sun, and its being one of the moving planets. The author reviews the Qur’anic verses in the order of the surahs, showing their agreement with clear reason and correct transmission, and stressing that the Sharia did not attempt to absorb the rules of mathematical sciences as much as it referred to them among its higher purposes.
descriptions.3871: This book is written by Muhammad Taqi al-Din al-Hilali, and it falls in the field of Qur’anic sciences. It deals with the topic of words that are said to have appeared in the Holy Qur’an from other than the Arabic language, and discusses the issue of the overlap of languages ​​and the occurrence of foreign words in the Qur’anic text. The author begins with a theoretical introduction to the phenomenon of languages ​​borrowing from each other, then moves on to list specific examples of Qur’anic words that have been controversial, such as “jugs” and “Istabraq,” to investigate their linguistic origins.
descriptions.3872: This book examines the science of objective interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, addressing its definition, origins, development, colors, and importance, while explaining the research methods in it, whether through a specific topic or a single surah. The author also devotes a section to the relationship of this type of interpretation to the science of occasions, explaining the types of occasions in a single surah and between surahs, while providing fundamental introductions on the issues of divinity, nature, and monotheism in the Qur’an.
descriptions.3873: The book “Investigations in the Sciences of the Qur’an” by Subhi Al-Saleh is an academic study in the sciences of the Qur’an, divided into four main sections. The first chapter deals with the topics of the Qur’an and revelation, while the second chapter examines the history of the compilation and writing of the Qur’an and the Seven Letters. The third chapter is devoted to presenting the various sciences of the Qur’an, such as the causes of revelation, the Meccan and the Medinan, the readings, the abrogated and the abrogated, while the fourth chapter concludes with a study of the Qur’anic interpretation and miracle. The book was originally written as university lectures aimed at simplifying these sciences and bringing them closer to students and researchers in a clear scientific manner.
descriptions.3874: The text of Al-Shatibiyyah, called Harz Al-Amani and Waja Al-Tahani fi Al-Saba’ Al-Qira’at, is a collection by Imam Al-Qasim bin Firah bin Khalaf Al-Shatibi Al-Ra’ini in the science of readings. Its original name is Harz Al-Amani and Waja Al-Tahaniyya, but it is known as Al-Shatibiyyah, named after its nazim. The number of its verses reached 1,173, in which Al-Shatibi organized the seven frequent recitations from the imams Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amer, Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i. …
descriptions.3875: Metaphor of the Qur’an. A book on the meanings of the Qur’an and its declarative methods, compiled by Abu Ubaidah Muammar bin Al-Muthanna Al-Taymi Al-Basri. It is considered the first author in linguistic sciences, and Al-Tabari benefited from it in his interpretation.
descriptions.3876: This is a dictionary book specialized in the terminology of the science of Quranic recitations, in which the author collected the terms and arranged them according to the letters of the dictionary from A to Z, relying in defining them on the custom of Quranic scholars only, and excluding what is not specific to this science except what is frequently used in its sources. He was careful to define the term accurately and clearly without prolonging it, while mentioning its multiple meanings when the context of its use differs, arranged according to popularity and usage.
descriptions.3877: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which summarizes the rules of interpretation and its origins, divided into objectives that cover the topics of the revelation of the Qur’an, its reasons and place of revelation, the readings, and the arrangement of verses and surahs. Then it moves on to the linguistic and graphic rules of interpretation, such as manifestation, implication, deletion, introduction, and delay, and the tools that the interpreter needs, in addition to the chapters on names, conjunctions, emphasis, synonyms, commands, prohibitions, negations, and interrogations, and the general and specific, the absolute, the restricted, the spoken, and the understood.
descriptions.3878: The book “The Orientalists’ Claims About the Holy Qur’an” by Muhammad Mehr Ali, which is one of the books on the sciences of the Qur’an, presents and discusses a number of suspicions and allegations raised by the Orientalists about the Holy Qur’an, focusing on contemporary examples such as Wansborough, Judas De Nevo, and Bellamy. The author begins with an introduction explaining that the position of the Orientalists is not new, but rather an extension of the position of the polytheists of Mecca who claimed that the Qur’an was created by humans. Then he shows how the Qur’an responded to these claims in multiple ways.
descriptions.3879: The Problem of Parsing the Qur’an is a book written by Makki bin Abi Talib Al-Qaisi. The importance of the book is evident by looking at the biography of its author and the number of his works, which indicates the breadth of his knowledge. One of his approaches to the book is to parse the problematic verses. He lists all the acceptable aspects of parsing, and is concerned with guiding the readings. He did not intend to write the book for beginners in parsing. Among the drawbacks in criticizing the book are the confusion in attributing statements to their authors, not attributing statements to their authors, repeating the parsing of apparent issues, and parsing unproblematic issues. …
descriptions.3880: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that examines the science of proportion, which studies the interconnection and cohesion of the verses and surahs of the Holy Qur’an. It reviews basic introductions in the definition of surah and verse and the difference between the science of proportion and objective interpretation. Then it deals with the history of this science and its most prominent figures such as Al-Razi, Al-Buqa’i, Al-Farahi, and Sayyid Qutb. It classifies the types of occasions between verses, within a single surah, and between surahs, with applied models that illustrate this interconnection and Qur’anic miracle.
descriptions.3881: This is a book that studies aspects of the sciences of the Holy Qur’an and its interpretation according to Imam Abu Ishaq Al-Shatibi. It presents his biography, his sheikhs, his students, and his scientific effects, and then deals with his opinions on multiple topics such as the reasons for revelation, indicative and scientific interpretation, the ruling on translating the Qur’an, interpreting the Qur’an according to the Qur’an and the Sunnah, issues of grammar, rhetoric, readings, and verses of doctrine and rulings.
descriptions.3882: A book that studies the emergence and development of dictionaries of the meaning of the Holy Qur’an, and reviews the most prominent works in this field with a critical methodology to distinguish what actually falls under this classification. It begins with an introduction and introduction, then deals in its five sections with the difference between linguistic and Qur’anic dictionaries, the relationship of the Qur’anic dictionary to the emergence of the Arabic dictionary, the development of the need for its interpretation, and the methodological differences in its composition, and concludes with a chronological glossary of strange dictionaries arranged according to the deaths of their authors.
descriptions.3883: A book that studies the dictionaries of the Holy Qur’an’s vocabulary by balancing them, with a focus on the book “The Vocabulary of the Words of the Qur’an” by Al-Ragheb Al-Isfahani as a prominent teacher in this field. The author reviews a historical overview of the composition in the meanings of the Qur’an and its strange things, then analyzes the features of Al-Raghib’s vocabulary and its complements, and compares it to four other Qur’anic dictionaries: Umdat al-Huffaz, Basa’ir Dhu’l-Taymiz, Mufradat al-Qur’an by al-Farahi al-Hindi, and the Dictionary of the Words of the Qur’an by the Arabic Language Academy. The book concludes with critical remarks and suggestions for developing this type of dictionary.
descriptions.3884: Meanings of the Qur’an may mean: Meanings of the Qur’an by Al-Akhfash: a book. The meanings of the Qur’an for fur. The meanings of the Qur’an for copper: a book by Abu Jaafar al-Nahhas. Meanings of the Qur’an and its parsing (Glass)
descriptions.3885: The book “The Meanings of Recitations” by Al-Azhari is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, concerned with explaining the meanings and aspects of the various Qur’anic recitations. The book begins with an introduction to the work in which it discusses God’s facilitation of memorizing the Qur’an, then provides the evidence for the readings of the seven reciters, such as Ibn Kathir, Asim, and Hamza, followed by an interpretation of the meanings of the Qur’anic verses, surah by surah, beginning with Al-Fatihah and then Al-Baqarah, with a focus on explaining the words and structures in which multiple readings occur.
descriptions.3886: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which examines the aspects of the miracle of the Holy Qur’an, reviewing them in detail and analysis, beginning with an explanation that the miracle of this nation is rational, then it deals with multiple aspects such as saj’, the opening of surahs and their endings, ambiguous verses, the abrogated and abrogated, the decisive and the ambiguous, the introduction and delay of words, the generality of verses and their particulars, informing of the unseen, and other topics related to the miracle of the Qur’an.
descriptions.3887: A book that deals with the scientific miracle in the Holy Qur’an, reviewing a number of cosmic and natural phenomena referred to in the Qur’anic verses, such as the origin and expansion of the universe, duality in creatures, and internal and surface waves. The author presents a Qur’anic interpretation of the verses and then follows it with a modern scientific explanation that shows the compatibility of the Qur’anic text with scientific discoveries, citing verses from the Qur’an and hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.3888: The book “The Miracle of the Qur’an” by Sheikh Muhammad Metwally Al-Shaarawi, and is located in the classification of Qur’anic sciences. The book deals with the topic of the Qur’anic miracle as an eternal miracle that will remain until the Day of Resurrection, explaining that the Qur’an is not a book of science in the direct sense, but it contains a miracle for all ages. The author reviews aspects of the miracle of the Qur’an in revealing the veils of the unseen, past, present, and future, and in its scientific references, such as the sphericity of the Earth and embryology, challenging humanity to do the same as what it brought.
descriptions.3889: The book “Dictionary of Qur’anic Verses” is a detailed index of verses of the Holy Qur’an, arranged alphabetically, aiming to facilitate reference to Qur’anic verses for researchers and students. The book falls within the classification of Qur’anic sciences, and its author emphasizes in its introduction the importance of indexes as a first step in precise, systematic scientific research to study the Qur’an from its many aspects.
descriptions.3890: A book that studies four main Qur’anic dictionaries: “The Indexed Dictionary of the Words of the Holy Qur’an,” “The Dictionary of Tools and Pronouns in the Holy Qur’an,” “The Dictionary of Meanings in the Holy Qur’an,” and “Studies of the Style of the Holy Qur’an,” and analyzes them in terms of their approach and usefulness in investigating grammatical and morphological issues in the Holy Qur’an. The author aims to fill the need of researchers to trace verses that contain certain grammatical devices and pronouns, thus facilitating the study of Qur’anic methods.
descriptions.3891: This book, “The Tajweed Teacher,” written by Dr. Khaled Al-Jarisi, deals with the science of Tajweed comprehensively, presenting the concept of the Qur’an, its virtues, and the pillars of correct recitation, while introducing the terms of this science and explaining them in detail. The book also deals with the various provisions of Tajweed, stressed letters, stopping and starting, and other rules related to the recitation of the Holy Qur’an, providing valuable scientific material for students of Tajweed and imams of mosques.
descriptions.3892: Mufhamat Al-Azra fi Al-Muhbamat Al-Qur’an is one of the books of interpretation of the Holy Quran, written by Jalal Al-Din Al-Suyuti.
descriptions.3893: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It aims to liberate the basic concepts related to interpretation, interpretation, deduction, and contemplation, while discussing the terms “interpretation by tradition” and “interpretation by opinion” and correcting the course in them. The author presents and analyzes scholars' definitions of interpretation, and shows the differences between interpretation and other information that comes after it, with a practical application to Surat Al-Kawthar. The book also addresses contemporary issues such as scientific and numerical miracles, criticizing some uncontrolled claims in this field.
descriptions.3894: Introduction to the Principles of Interpretation A brief book on the Principles of Interpretation, written by Ibn Taymiyyah, which includes the rules that interpreters must rely on in their interpretation and understanding of the Qur’an. The subject of the book is a mention of the rules and principles upon which understanding the Qur’an is based, meaning that whoever is aware of these rules will find it easier for him to understand the Qur’an.
descriptions.3895: A book on the sciences of the Qur’an that deals with the presentation and description of plants as mentioned in the Qur’anic texts, and reviews the verses that talk about the creation of plants, their diversity, and their role in life, while contemplating their implications for the Creator’s power and wisdom.
descriptions.3896: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, which studies and analyzes some Qur’anic verses whose parsing is problematic for grammarians or whose expressions depart from the rules of rhetoricians. At the beginning, the author presents two of these problems, one grammatical and the other rhetorical, and reviews the opinions of commentators and grammarians regarding their direction, indicating the problematic areas in them and the differences in interpretations that have been made regarding their parsing and meaning.
descriptions.3897: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It deals with the issue of the occasions of verses and surahs, and examines the extent to which they relate to the arrangement of verses and surahs in the Qur’an, and whether this arrangement is arbitrary or ijtihad. The book presents the opinions of different scholars on occasions, and discusses the four main trends in them, citing the sayings of a number of imams such as Al-Shawkani and Al-Izz bin Abdul Salam, with a focus on evidence regarding the order of the verses in their surahs.
descriptions.3898: The book “The Ways of Knowledge in the Sciences of the Qur’an” by its author, Muhammad Abd al-Azim al-Zarqani, is a comprehensive encyclopedia in the field of Qur’anic sciences. It aims to explain the meaning of these sciences and the history of their codification, with a focus on basic topics such as the truth and manner of the revelation of the Qur’an. The author presents his material in a manner that combines scientific investigation with ease of expression, seeking to make the book an accessible reference for science students and intellectuals alike.
descriptions.3899: Upholsterer of reciters and guide of seekers, is a book by Ibn al-Jazari on the science of recitations. The book began by defining the science of recitations, and mentioned rulings and etiquette for the reader and the reciter. It then went back to the conditions of reading that scholars considered correct reading, as well as the reading that scholars considered abnormal reading. It was distinguished by translating a number of those who read the ten recitations and mentioned some of their conditions.
descriptions.3900: This poetic system by Imam Ibn al-Jazari in the science of Tajweed, and it is a brief introduction that the reader of the Qur’an must know before starting to read. The book is organized into sequential chapters that begin with the origins of the letters and their attributes, then move on to the rules of intonation such as the sukoon noun, tanween, and mudd, and it deals with stopping, beginning, mutqal, connected, and other rules necessary for reciting the Qur’an in the most eloquent languages.
descriptions.3901: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, written by the scholar Muhammad Al-Amin Al-Shanqeeti, in which he discusses the issue of the occurrence of metaphor in the Holy Qur’an, and sees that the Qur’an is all truths and does not contain metaphor, warning against the use of metaphor because it entails a denial of the attributes of God Almighty established in the Qur’an and Sunnah. The author arranged his thesis into an introduction, four chapters, and a conclusion, in which he discussed the evidence of those who advocate metaphors and answered the verses that they claimed were metaphors, while investigating the status of verses about attributes.
descriptions.3902: This book is a poetic text composed by Imam Ibn al-Jazari in the science of Qur’anic recitations, and it is considered one of the most important and widely circulated texts in this art. The book is organized into sections and chapters that cover the principles of the ten major recitations, starting with the introduction and the chapter on seeking refuge and the basmalah, then it deals with rulings such as assimilation, extension, shortening, hamza, tilting, and pausing, all the way to the chapter on brushing the letters, which explains the differences between the readers in the verses. The author formulated his material in easy-to-memorize poetic verses, collecting in it the rules of readings and their rulings according to the doctrine of the ten reciters.
descriptions.3903: This book is the text of “Tayyab al-Nashr” in the Ten Recitations, written by Ibn al-Jazari, and it is classified within the sciences of the Qur’an. The book is organized into sections and chapters that cover topics of Qur’anic recitations, such as seeking refuge, basmalah, assimilation, long and short periods, stopping, tilting, and other rules of recitation. The author opened it with a poetic introduction in which he talked about the virtue and honor of the bearers of the Qur’an, then he proceeded to organize the rules of the ten recitations for the sake of brevity and precision.
descriptions.3904: The book “Masa’id al-Nazr to Supervise the Objectives of the Surahs” was written by Burhan al-Din al-Baqa’i, and it is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. The book aims to explain the purposes of the surahs of the Holy Qur’an, and to reveal the proportionality of its parts, with a focus on matching the name of each surah to its content. The book includes an introduction and comments from a number of scholars, then it begins to talk about Surat Al-Fatihah, the regulations of Mecca and Medina, and the virtues of the Qur’an, to be a reference in understanding the purposes of the surah.
descriptions.3905: The book “Elevators of Consideration for Supervising the Objectives of the Surahs” by Burhan al-Din al-Baqa’i is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It aims to explain the purposes of the surahs of the Holy Qur’an and link their names to their meanings. The book includes an introduction and reports from a number of scholars, then deals with various topics such as the virtue of the Qur’an, how the revelation was revealed, and the criterion of Meccan and Medinan, with a focus on the purpose of each surah, starting with Surat Al-Fatiha.
descriptions.3906: The transcriber and abrogator of the Mighty Qur’an: Ibn al-Barazi, Hibat Allah ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Hamawi, the mufti and judge of the Levant and the imamate came to him during his time. He died in the year seven hundred and thirty-eight. This book is distinguished by the fact that the number of abrogated places in it is two hundred and forty-nine places, and with this large number it exceeds its predecessors and successors, and it also mentioned abrogated places that no one else referred to. Another of the author’s merits in this book is his drawing of the method in the introduction to his book, saying: “We will mention all the abrogated places in the order of the surahs, and we mention with each abrogated one what it abrogated, and we specify the name of the surah in which the abrogated one is, if it is not from the abrogated surah.” He adhered to this except in five places.
descriptions.3907: This is a book on Quranic sciences that aims to lay methodological foundations for building a historical dictionary of Quranic terms. It explains the concept of the historical dictionary and the concept of Quranic terminology, and explains the objectives of this dictionary, its sources, and the method of its arrangement. The book is based on the idea that Qur’anic words possess a semantic specificity that requires studying them terminologically throughout the history of their use, and it presents an applied model for a class of terminology.
descriptions.3908: This book is an investigation into the subject of the revelation of the Holy Qur’an. It begins by establishing the meaning of revelation linguistically and terminologically, and distinguishes between revelation and revelation. It reviews the opinions of scholars regarding the revelations of the Holy Qur’an and the stages of its revelation, discussing the evidence and weighing between them. The research deals with the time, place, duration, and amount of revelation, within the framework of caring for the Holy Qur’an and its sciences.
descriptions.3909: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an. It examines how the Holy Qur’an was revealed. It deals with its descent as a whole from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, the wisdom behind its revelation in parts, and the issue of its revelation in seven letters. Then the book moves on to explain the care for the Qur’an during the era of the Prophet ﷺ, showing the manifestations of this care through its memorization, writing, and practical application.
descriptions.3910: This is a book on the sciences of the Qur’an, dealing with the subject of the revelation of the Holy Qur’an from its many aspects. It begins by defining the Qur’an and explaining its miracles, then moves on to talk about the beginning of the revelation and its duration, how the Prophet ﷺ received the revelation, and the wisdom behind the revelation of the Qur’an in general and in detail. It also discusses important issues such as the revelation of seven letters, the reasons for the revelation, the first thing that was revealed from the Qur’an and the last thing that was revealed, mentioning the benefits and rulings resulting from that.
descriptions.3911: The book “Nail al-Maram min Interpretation of Verses of Rulings” by author Siddiq Hassan Khan is an interpretation of verses of the Holy Qur’an that contain legal rulings, and it falls in the field of Qur’anic sciences. The book begins with an introduction to the author's life, then deals with the interpretation of selected verses from Surahs Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa and what follows them, with a focus on deriving jurisprudential rulings from these verses.
descriptions.3912: A book on the science of Tajweed of the Holy Qur’an. It explains the provisions of recitation and the principles of performance based on the narration of Hafs on the authority of Asim, beginning with an introduction to the narrator and the imam. Then it deals with the principles of the science of Tajweed and the levels of recitation, detailing the origins of the letters and their characteristics, the topics of amplification and thinning, and the difference between the dād and the dā’.
descriptions.3913: Guidance of the doubtful and the purpose of preservation and students in clarifying the ambiguous book, written by Alam al-Din al-Sakhawi, the reciter. The book in which the author organizes the verbal ambiguous in the Holy Qur’an, and mentions the ambiguous in its various types, such as substitution, addition and subtraction, or advancement and delay, and so on. The author mentioned his approach to arranging words in the system. He arranged them in the order of the letters of the dictionary. He lists problematic or similar words in verses of the Qur’an, organizes their wording and differences, and places every disagreement in its section, that is, in the first letter of the word. He also explained his method of identifying the section of problem and the fact that the word is an addition to its origin. …
descriptions.3914: The book “A Pause with Some English Translations of the Meanings of the Holy Qur’an” by the author Wajih Hamad Abdul Rahman, is a book in the field of Qur’anic sciences. It studies and criticizes the various English translations of the meanings of the Holy Qur’an, and divides them into Orientalist, Islamic, and Qadiani translations. Then, it presents some of the problems that obstruct the translation process, such as semantic and grammatical errors, with the aim of evaluating these translations and pointing out their shortcomings.
descriptions.3915: The Ruby of Sirat in the Interpretation of Strange Words in the Qur’an is a book written by Abu Omar al-Zahid: Muhammad bin Abdul Wahid, known as Ghulam Tha’lab (261 AH - 345 AH = 875-957 AD), in which he mentions the interpretation of strange words in the Holy Qur’an, starting from Surah Al-Fatihah to the end of the Qur’an, where he mentions the word and then its interpretation, and sometimes he mentions some evidence from the Qur’an, Hadith, or Arab poetry. The book is considered one of the most important books on Gharib al-Qur’an, due to the time of its writing, and because it contains important texts about people of the language who were older than the author’s time and his contemporaries. The book was printed in the Library of Science and Governance in Medina, edited by Muhammad Yaqoub al-Turkestani.
descriptions.3916: This book is an explanation of the text of “The Shortest Abbreviations” in Hanbali jurisprudence. It begins with an introduction to the importance of jurisprudence in religion and its definition, then deals with explanation and explanation of the issues of the Book of Purity, beginning with the sections on water and the rulings on utensils and cleansing, all the way to the rulings on ablution and wiping over the socks and what contradicts it, with a brief translation of the imams of the sects and the author of the text.
descriptions.3917: This book is an explanation of the text of “Zad al-Mustaqni’” in Hanbali jurisprudence, delivered by Sheikh Abdul Karim al-Khudair in audio lessons, which were then completed and organized in this volume. The explanation begins with the Book of Fasting, addressing its definition, ruling, virtues, and the wisdom behind its legality. Then it moves to the Book of Rites to include the chapters on timings, Ihram, its prohibitions, ransom, and the penalty for hunting. The explanation aims to facilitate the study of the text for students of knowledge, while directing them to the importance of agreeing on the doctrine of the scholars, while paying attention to the origin of the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.3918: This book is an expanded explanation of the text of “Zad al-Mustaqni’” in Hanbali jurisprudence, presented by Sheikh Hamad bin Abdullah al-Hamad in a series of lessons. The explanation begins with the Book of Purity and deals successively with the various sections of jurisprudence, such as prayer, zakat, fasting, rituals, sales, jihad, religious duties, marriage, divorce, felonies, punishments, and others, according to the order of the chapters of the original text.
descriptions.3919: This book is an explanation of the book on fasting from the text of “Umdat Al-Fiqh” by Ibn Qudamah Al-Maqdisi, presented by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair in three detailed lessons. The work falls within Hanbali jurisprudence, and deals with explaining the provisions of obligatory and voluntary fasting, with an explanation of the virtue of voluntary fasts and their role in completing the obligatory prayers, based on Sharia texts.
descriptions.3920: This book is an explanation of the text of “Mukhtasar Al-Kharqi” in jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, delivered by Sheikh Abdul Karim Al-Khudair in recorded lessons, and it begins with the Book of Purity. The commentator addresses in detail and explanation the issues of Hanbali jurisprudence based on the text of the summary, relying on an educational method that aims to bring jurisprudential expressions closer to students. The book includes seventy-three lessons, numbered automatically, and is concerned with explaining the provisions of purity such as water, utensils, ablution, washing, and tayammum.
descriptions.3921: This is a jurisprudential book based on the Hanbali school of thought, compiled by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and it includes sections on practical acts of worship such as prayer with its rulings and etiquette, zakat of all kinds, and fasting and what invalidates it. The book begins with a chapter on the etiquette of walking to prayer, mentioning what is recommended to do and say when going out to prayer, such as purity, serenity, and well-known supplications.
descriptions.3922: The book “Etiquette of Walking to Prayer” by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab is a book on Hanbali jurisprudence, dealing with the etiquette and rulings related to going out to prayer and performing it. The book begins by explaining the Sunnahs of going out to the mosque with humility and purity, and the permissible supplications when leaving and entering, then it goes on to detail the nature of prayer and its rulings, such as reciting the takbir aloud, praying to a sutrah, prostration of forgetfulness, and voluntary prayers, with a focus on the duties that are omitted by mistake and the easy work in prayer.
descriptions.3923: Akhtar al-Mukhtasarat () is one of the approved texts in the Hanbali school of thought, written by Ibn Balban al-Dimashqi al-Hanbali (1006-1083 AH / 1598-1672 AD). He summarized it from his book Kafi al-Mubtadi. Ibn Balban did not declare the date of the beginning of his writing of the shortest abbreviations, but it was mentioned in his oldest copy that the date of its completion was on Wednesday, Ramadan 16, 1054 AH, that is, twenty-nine years before his death. He stated in the introduction to the book that the reason for writing “The Shortest Acronyms” was to shorten his book “Kafi Al-Mubtadi” so that it would be easier for beginners to memorize. He stated the name of the book in his introduction and called it “The Shortest Acronyms.” …
descriptions.3924: A jurisprudential book based on the Hanbali doctrine, written in a question-and-answer style to facilitate review and memorization. It begins by defining jurisprudence and Sharia rulings, then discusses in detail the Book of Purity and its chapters, such as water, utensils, and cleansing, citing Sharia evidence for each issue.
descriptions.3925: Persuasion in the jurisprudence of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It is called “Al-Iqna’” for short, a jurisprudential book written by the jurist Sharaf al-Din Abu al-Najah Musa ibn Ahmad al-Hijjawi al-Maqdisi al-Salhi (d. 968 AH), and it is a book based on the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The book is considered a collection of the Hanbali doctrine, as Al-Hijjawi compiled a text that combines the book Al-Furu’ by Ibn Muflih and the virtues of the corrections of Alaa Al-Din Al-Mardawi. He wrote the book Al-Iqna’, in which he collected the most correct sayings of the early and late ones. The book was edited by Abdul Latif Muhammad Musa Al-Sabki.
descriptions.3926: Fairness in knowing what is more correct than the disagreement is one of the books of Hanbali jurisprudence, written by Alaa al-Din al-Mardawi. The book is considered one of the books of comparative jurisprudence within the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, in which the author mentions all the narrations contained in every jurisprudential issue on the authority of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and mentions what is relied upon in the doctrine on the authority of the imam by analogy based on its rules, principles, and texts, and he often places warnings regarding the benefit of the dispute.
descriptions.3927: This is a jurisprudential book based on the Hanbali school of thought, and it is an explanation of the summary of “Zad al-Mustaqni’” in jurisprudence, explaining its issues and rulings. The book begins with an introduction to praise and praise, then deals with the sections on purity with its sections, such as water, utensils, cleansing, ablution, washing, and tayammum. Then it moves to the book of prayer and what is related to it, including the call to prayer, conditions, prescriptions, pillars, prostration of forgetfulness, voluntary prayer, congregational prayer, rulings on imamate, those who have excuses, and the traveler’s shortening of prayer.
descriptions.3928: This book is an expanded explanation of the text of “Al-Muqni” in jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, compiled by its author based on the book “Al-Mughni” and other jurisprudential sources. The explanation begins with the Book of Purity, detailing the issues of water, its divisions and rulings, and vessels, reviewing the various narrations and jurisprudential aspects of the school of thought.
descriptions.3929: The book Al-Mumti’ Explanation on Zad Al-Mustaqni’, written by Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen, an explanation of the book Zad Al-Mustaqni’, which is a text that summarizes Ibn Qudamah’s book Al-Muqni’ in Hanbali jurisprudence. Its basis is mosque lessons collected and then revised in one book.
descriptions.3930: The book “Al-Iddah Sharh Al-Umda” is a brief explanation of the book “Al-Umda” in jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, written by Bahaa Al-Din Al-Maqdisi. The explanation aims to bring clarity to jurisprudential issues and clarify them, based on authentic hadiths. It begins with the Book of Purity, covering the rulings on water, ablution, and washing, then moves to the Book of Prayer and its various chapters, all the way to the Book of Zakat.
descriptions.3931: A book on jurisprudence based on the Hanbali doctrine, written by Muwaffaq al-Din al-Maqdisi, combining an explanation of the legal rulings and their evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah, relying on the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The author averred between length and brevity, and attributed the hadiths to their sources from the books of the imams of the regions, so that it would be sufficient in his chapter. The book begins with a sermon and then deals with the book of purity and the provisions related to water, impurities, ablution, washing, and tayammum.
descriptions.3932: The book “The Creator in Sharh al-Muqni” is an extensive explanation of jurisprudence based on the Hanbali school of thought, written by Burhan al-Din Ibn Muflih to explain the rulings on purity and acts of worship according to the school’s approach. The book begins with the author’s introduction, which includes praise of God and prayers upon the Prophet. Then he begins to detail issues of jurisprudence, beginning with the book on purity, covering the sections on water, utensils, cleansing, the siwak, and ablution, relying on the text of “Al-Muqni” by Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Qudamah.
descriptions.3933: This is a book on jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Its author has summarized it, refined it, and arranged it so that it contains the most basic principles of the issues, free of reasons and evidence, with brevity in pronunciation to facilitate students of its memorization. The book begins with the chapter on purity and the rulings on water, ablution, washing, and tayammum, then moves on to the book of prayer and the related times, the call to prayer, and the prescription and rulings of prayer.
descriptions.3934: A book on jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, explaining the rulings on purity and water and the detailed jurisprudential issues related to them, based on Sharia evidence. The author begins his book with an introduction to the virtue of science and jurisprudence, then goes on to detail the rulings on water, its types, and the extent of its suitability for purification, addressing delicate issues such as used water, impure water, and how to purify it.
descriptions.3935: The book “Summary of Jurisprudence” is a book on jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought. It provides a summary of the rulings on purity and prayer and what is related to them, based on their evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. This summary was composed at the request of listeners after it was delivered on radio episodes, and it was reviewed and arranged for printing, relying for its scientific material on the explanation of the book “Al-Rawd al-Murabba’” and its footnote. The book aims to facilitate legal knowledge and provide useful jurisprudence coupled with evidence.
descriptions.3936: This book is an explanation and commentary on the book “The Editor” by Majd al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah. It organizes the sections of Hanbali jurisprudence, and is concerned with clarifying problematic issues therein and editing the sayings, aspects, and jurisprudential conclusions. The book begins with issues of purity, and discusses the rulings on impure water and methods of purifying it, reviewing the opinions of the companions and balancing them.
descriptions.3937: The book “Guidance on the Doctrine of Imam Abu Abdullah Ahmad” by Al-Kaludhani is a work on Hanbali jurisprudence, aiming to present the issues of the Hanbali doctrine according to an organized approach. The book begins with the author’s sermon and then addresses the chapters of jurisprudence, starting with the Book of Purity, including chapters such as water, utensils, ablution, and wiping over the socks. This book is considered one of the important references in the jurisprudence of the Hanbali school of thought, and researchers have been concerned with controlling its text and extracting its verses and hadiths.
descriptions.3938: This is a book on Hanbali jurisprudence, which collects the issues of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to endowments and dismounting. It includes chapters that prove the legality of endowments, respond to those who challenge it, and detail its provisions in terms of its conditions, management, and disposal, and what relates to endowments for oneself, family, or mosques, with an explanation of what is disliked and what is permitted.
descriptions.3939: The Beginning of the Abid and the Sufficiency of the Ascetic is a book on the jurisprudence of worship written by Abd al-Rahman al-Baali (1110 - 1192 AH / 1698 - 1778 AD).
descriptions.3940: This book deals with Hanbali jurisprudence issues, deriving most of them from the sayings of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It focuses on issues of worship and obligations, relying on the Prophet’s hadiths and jurisprudential narrations. The book also addresses some jurisprudential rulings related to fasting, Hajj, prayers, and other important jurisprudential topics in the Hanbali school of thought.
descriptions.3941: This book is a footnote to the explanation of “Al-Rawd Al-Murabba’” to the text of “Zad Al-Mustaqni’” in jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, compiled by the author Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad bin Qasim. The book begins with a translation of the life of the author and his sheikhs, then deals with the principles and rules of jurisprudence, and begins to detail the rulings on worship, beginning with the Book of Purity, where it examines the types and conditions of water, utensils, cleansing, sunnahs of ablution, and other jurisprudential issues related to purity according to the Hanbali school of thought.
descriptions.3942: Minutes of Uli al-Nuha to explain al-Muntaha, known as Sharh Muntaha al-Iradat, is an explanation of “Muntaha al-Iradat” that al-Bahuti wrote after explaining al-Iqna’ and followed his method, and he summarized it and Ibn al-Najjar’s explanation called “Ma’onat Uli al-Nuha.” He intended his explanation to be short and easy, and he believes that the author went on at length in his explanation in some places while leaving others without evidence or explanation, so his explanation was not satisfactory. Ibn Dahish defended Ibn al-Najjar on this claim in the introduction to his investigation of the book. …
descriptions.3943: A student’s guide to achieving demands. The book is a text on Hanbali jurisprudence, written by Mar’i Al-Karmi (d. 1033 AH / 1624 AD). The author based it on one opinion, which is the most correct opinion in the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The investigators mentioned that Al-Karmi relied in writing his book on the book Muntaha Al-Iradat by Ibn Al-Najjar Al-Futuhi, and they disagreed on two opinions: The first described the book Al-Dalil as a summary of Muntaha Al-Iradat, including Saleh Al-Bahuti. The second described Al-Dalil as a summary of Muntaha Al-Iradat and was not limited to it only, but rather added to it from the book Al-Iqna’. Among those who held this opinion were Ahmad bin Awad and Ibn Bishr Al-Najdi. The author stated in the introduction to his book:
descriptions.3944: The book Zad al-Mustaqni’ fi Ikhtir al-Muqni’ is a very brief text on jurisprudence based on the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Written by the scholar, Hanbali Mufti Sharaf al-Din Abu al-Naja Musa bin Ahmed bin Musa al-Hijjawi al-Maqdisi al-Salhi. (d. 968 AH - 1560 AD)
descriptions.3945: This book is an expanded explanation of Al-Kharqi’s summary of Hanbali jurisprudence, written by Shams al-Din al-Zarkashi. The author begins with a verbal and semantic analysis of the title “The Book of Purity,” then moves on to defining purity linguistically and terminologically according to jurists, reviewing its detailed issues such as the rulings on water, utensils, ablution, and cleansing. The explanation aims to clarify jurisprudential texts and edit their meanings according to the Hanbali doctrine.
descriptions.3946: This book is an explanation of the message of Sheikh al-Islam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab regarding the conditions, pillars, and duties of prayer. It is one of the books of Hanbali jurisprudence. The author explains the nine conditions of prayer, the fourteen pillars, and the eight obligations, detailing the conditions of purity, the obligations of ablution, and its contradictions. The author also explains Surah Al-Fatihah and the words of the opening prayer and the tashahhud in the context of his explanation of the pillars of prayer.
descriptions.3947: This book is an explanation of the book “Etiquette of Walking to Prayer” by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab. It falls into three main sections: prayer, zakat, and fasting. It was compiled by Sheikh Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al Sheikh from his scientific reports. The explanation aims to explain the rulings of these acts of worship according to the Hanbali school of thought, relying on evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah and consensus, and devoid of what the author described of the uninitiated or controversial matters. This manual is an example of research into worship, and is useful for beginners, intermediates, and imams of mosques.
descriptions.3948: The book “Umdat al-Fiqh” is a summary of jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, compiled by the author Muwaffaq al-Din al-Maqdisi, in which he limited himself to one saying to serve as a guide for his reader, far from the differences in faces and narrations. The book begins with the chapter on purity, the rulings on water and utensils, ablution, and washing, then moves to the book of prayer and the conditions, pillars, and obligations related to it, prostration of forgetfulness, voluntary prayer, congregational prayer, Friday prayers, and two Eids, followed by the book on funerals and the book on zakat. The author has deposited authentic hadiths in the book based on them, dispensing with attributing them to their meanings.
descriptions.3949: A book on the jurisprudence of worship according to the Hanbali school of thought, explaining the rulings on purity and prayer according to this school of thought. Its author compiled it from lessons she received from her sheikh and from the famous books of Hanbali jurisprudence, with evidence of the rulings based on verses and hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.3950: The Book of Al-Furu’, along with the Correction of Al-Furu’, is a jurisprudential encyclopedia based on the Hanbali school of thought, compiled by the author Ibn Muflih. It included an extensive jurisprudential text in the sections on acts of worship such as purity and ablution, with comments and corrections from Alaa al-Din al-Mardawi on the original text. The book aims to edit jurisprudential issues, correct doctrine, and give weight to opinions, relying on a wide collection of sayings and issues.
descriptions.3951: Kashshaf al-Qinaa’ about the text of Persuasion is the unique explanation of the text “Al-Iqna’” written by Mansour Al-Bahuti. He followed the path of Ibn al-Najjar in his explanation of “Al-Muntaha.” He mixed the text with the explanation until they became like one thing, and no one could differentiate between them except one with insight or foresight, and he strove to reveal the truths of its meanings by investigating its origins, which Al-Hajjawi relied upon in composing the text. Such as Al-Muqni’, Al-Muharrir, Al-Furoo’, Al-Mustasim, in addition to the explanations of those books, in particular: Al-Sharh Al-Kabir, Al-Mubdi’, in addition to Al-Insaaf, which is considered a book of correction of the books of the doctrine. …
descriptions.3952: This is a book on Hanbali jurisprudence, and it is an explanation of the book “Akhsar al-Mukhtasarat” by Ibn Balban al-Hanbali, compiled by Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah al-Baali. The commentator aims to uncover the ambiguity in the text and clarify its issues in a way that is neither long, boring, nor short, beginning with the book on purity, then prayer, funerals, zakat, fasting, and Hajj, all the way to books on transactions such as sales, marriage, divorce, felonies, punishments, judiciary, and testimonies.
descriptions.3953: This is a brief book on jurisprudence according to the Hanbali school of thought, compiled by the author Al-Kharqi to be close to learners. The book begins with the chapter on purity and the rulings on water and impurities, then moves to the book of prayer and the related times, the call to prayer, leading prayers, the rulings on travel, Friday prayers, the two Eids, and others, and concludes with the book on funerals.
descriptions.3954: This book is a summary of Hanbali jurisprudence, compiled by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab from the books “Al-Insaaf” and “Al-Sharh Al-Kabeer” to facilitate benefiting from them. The book is organized into the well-known sections of jurisprudence, starting with purity, then prayer, then funerals, relying on evidence and referring to the Qur’an and Sunnah. The author intended this summary to bring jurisprudential issues closer to the Hanbali school of thought, especially at a time when he saw the need for this.
descriptions.3955: This book is a collection of jurisprudential issues that Imam Ahmed bin Hanbal was asked about, and narrated by his son Abdullah. The book falls within the classification of Hanbali jurisprudence, and deals mainly with the rulings on purity, beginning with the chapters on water and its rulings in terms of change by impurity and purity therein, then moving on to the rulings on ablution, washing, tayammum, menstruation, and istihaadah. Its material is based on the question-and-answer format, as it presents questions asked by Imam Ahmad and documents his answers to them.
descriptions.3956: This book is a collection of jurisprudential issues narrated by Abu al-Fadl Salih ibn Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal on the authority of his father, and it is classified within the jurisprudence of the Hanbali school of thought. The book deals with various rulings in acts of worship, such as fasting, zakat, and Hajj, in addition to issues regarding divorce, oaths, and purity, in the form of direct questions and answers between the son and his father, the imam.
descriptions.3957: The book “Issues of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh” was written by Ishaq ibn Mansur al-Kawsaj, and it is one of the books of Hanbali jurisprudence that collects various jurisprudential issues. The book includes questions directed by the author to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and then he often directed the same questions to Imam Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, while sometimes presenting the words of Sufyan al-Thawri on the issue. The book is distinguished by its large number of issues, which amount to about three thousand and six hundred issues, and by the scholarly and trustworthy status of its author, as he presented the issues to Imam Ahmad and he approved them for him, which added additional documentation to them.
descriptions.3958: A book containing jurisprudential issues narrated by Abu Dawud al-Sijistani on the authority of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and it is classified within Hanbali jurisprudence. The book deals with the provisions of purity, such as facing the Qiblah and the impurity of water, and details the issues of prayer, such as timings, reading, leading, qunoot, and praying, in addition to the provisions of congregational prayer, the Qiblah, and mosques. The scientific material is taken from direct questions and answers between the student and his sheikh, which gives a picture of Imam Ahmad’s approach to reasoning and fatwa.
descriptions.3959: Matalib Uli al-Nuha fi Sharh Ghayat al-Muntaha, which is the only complete explanation of the text of al-Ghaya, was written by Mustafa al-Suyuti al-Ruhaybani, and he combined in his explanation what Mansour al-Bahuti said in his explanation of “Al-Muntaha” and “Al-Iqna’,” adhering to that for the most part, and was not limited to that only. But he also had good investigations, research, and sayings on “refinement,” “persuasion,” and “ultimacy.” Pointing out what Mar’i, the author of Al-Ghaya, did not point out about the dispute between “persuasion” and “ultimate”, and also correcting some of that. As for Mar’i’s trends, his solution to many of them is clear consideration, and Al-Shatti has tracked him down.
descriptions.3960: The book “Manar Al-Sabil fi Sharh Al-Dalil” is an encyclopedic commentary on “The Student’s Guide to Attaining the Demands” in Hanbali jurisprudence. Through it, the author aims to present legal evidence and jurisprudential explanations for the issues with brevity, while adding some necessary issues and mentioning narrations or other aspects when their evidence is strong. The explanation is based on well-regarded Hanbali jurisprudential sources, such as the book “Al-Kafi” and “Al-Muqni’,” the branches of Ibn Muflih, and the rules of Ibn Rajab, and covers the chapters of worship, starting with purity and prayer.
descriptions.3961: A jurisprudential book that specializes in presenting the rulings on acts of worship according to the Hanafi school of thought, and its subject matter is limited to the section on acts of worship only. The author aims to present jurisprudential issues in a contemporary manner based on division, numbering, and labeling, while documenting the information and attributing it to its original references. The book begins with an introduction about Imam Abu Hanifa and the Hanafi school of thought, then discusses in detail the Book of Purity and the Book of Prayer within sequential sections and chapters.
descriptions.3962: The book “Al-Asl known as Al-Mabsut” by Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Shaybani is a jurisprudential encyclopedia in the Hanafi school of thought, which deals with the provisions of worship and transactions in detail. The book begins with the chapter on ablution and the rulings on purity, then moves on to detailing the rulings on prayer in terms of how to enter it, its timing, what interrupts it, the rulings on leading the prayer, congregational prayer, naked prayer, and other jurisprudential issues based on the sayings of Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and the author himself.
descriptions.3963: The book “Al-Ikhtiyar li’lil Al-Mukhtar” is a summary of jurisprudence based on the doctrine of Imam Abu Hanifa. It was compiled by the author in response to a request from those who had to answer it, and he limited it to the doctrine of the Imam and issued a fatwa based on it. The book begins with an introduction by the author, then deals with the book of purity, including the provisions of ablution, washing, tayammum, wiping over the socks, menstruation, and impurity, followed by the book of prayer, which includes the definition of prayer, its times, the call to prayer, the iqama, the actions of prayer, and the Witr prayer.
descriptions.3964: The book “Al-Bahr Al-Ra’iq Sharh Kanz Al-Daqa’iqa’” is an encyclopedic explanation of the summary “Kanz Al-Daqa’iqa’” in Hanafi jurisprudence. It aims to clarify the meaning of the texts and their meaning while returning the branches of fatwas and explanations to them. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue of the science of jurisprudence, then deals with the book of purity comprehensively, explaining the provisions of ablution, washing, water, and purification with tanning and animal hair, with extensive branches and edits.
descriptions.3965: This book is an expanded explanation of the text of “Guidance” in Hanafi jurisprudence. It begins with an introduction to the etiquette of opening books with the basmalah and hamdala. Then it deals in detail with the Book of Purifications, explaining the provisions of ablution, including its definition, duties, sunnahs, and contradictions, relying on the approach of Hanafi jurisprudence in reasoning and weighting.
descriptions.3966: This is a book on Hanafi jurisprudence, and it is an explanation of the text of “Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir” compiled by Muhammad bin Al-Hasan from forty jurisprudential books, and it is considered one of the most important issues that no one who holds the position of judge and fatwa should be without memorizing. The explanation begins with the Book of Prayer and its chapters related to ablution, impurity, leading, reading, etc., then moves to the Book of Zakat and the related chapters of tithes and tax.
descriptions.3967: The book “The Bright Jewel” is a brief explanation of the text of “Mukhtasar Al-Qadouri” in jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. The author compiled it with brief words and clear phrases to make it easy to understand. The book begins with an introduction, then deals with the book of purity in a comprehensive manner, touching on its Sunnahs, the requirements for washing, tayammum, wiping over the socks, and the rulings on menstruation and impurities. Then it moves to the book of prayer, detailing the rulings on the call to prayer, the conditions and characteristics of prayer, making up for prayers, voluntary prayers, prostration of forgetfulness, Friday prayers, the two Eids, and the eclipse.
descriptions.3968: The book “The Proof on the People of Medina” by Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Shaybani is a jurisprudential work based on the Hanafi school of thought, presenting the opinions of the jurists of Kufa and responding to the opinions of the jurists of Medina on matters of worship. The book begins with a discussion of the time of dawn prayer, then deals in detail with the chapters of purity and prayer, such as ablution, tayammum, and wiping over the socks, leading to the rulings on forgetfulness and forgetfulness in prayer.
descriptions.3969: This is a book on Hanafi jurisprudence by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani. It deals with the rulings on jihad and conduct, and includes various sections that include the etiquette of invasion, the division of spoils and the fifth, the rulings on captives and captives, reconciliation and farewell with the people of war, the rulings on trustworthy persons and trade in the land of war, in addition to issues of apostasy and felonies. The book begins by mentioning hadiths and traces of the Prophet ﷺ regarding the etiquette of invasion and directing armies.
descriptions.3970: Al-Inaya Sharh al-Hidaya is a book of jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought, in which its author, Akmal al-Din al-Babarti (d. 786 AH), explained the book al-Hidaya, an explanation of the beginning of al-Mubtadi in the branches of Hanafi jurisprudence, by Imam Sheikh al-Islam Burhan al-Din al-Marghinani (d. 593 AH). He called it: al-Inaya Sharh al-Hidaya. He abbreviated it from the book al-Nihayah Sharh al-Hidaya by his sheikh Hussam al-Din al-Saghnaqi (d. 710 AH), and he brought it revised. He is polite. He mentions the evidence and arranges it in a jurisprudential order in books and chapters. He mentions the opinions of scholars of his school of thought and explains the most correct ones. He also mentions the opinions of scholars of other schools of thought, and he explains some words linguistically to clarify the intended meaning.
descriptions.3971: The book “Al-Gharrah al-Munifah fi Taqihqi some Issues of Imam Abu Hanifa” by Siraj al-Din al-Ghaznawi is a work of jurisprudence based on the Hanafi school of thought, which he wrote in response to the request of a great prince, in which he translated a Persian book into Arabic and added to it evidence and discussions attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa. The book is organized into sequential jurisprudential sections that begin with purity and end with emancipation, and presents controversial issues with reasoning for them, as appears from its introduction, which indicates his approach in presenting arguments and responses.
descriptions.3972: This book is an explanation of “The Book of Earning” by Imam Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Shaybani. It falls within the chapter of completion in Hanafi jurisprudence. It deals with the subject of earning in terms of its linguistic and legal definition, and an explanation of its rulings and legitimate causes, relying on the effects and jurisprudential issues that have been classified in this section. The author aims to clarify the path of perception in matters of earning, and to urge students of knowledge to participate in lawful work and earning.
descriptions.3973: The book “Al-Lubab fi Al-Baytun Al-Sunnah wal-Qur’an” by Al-Khazraji Al-Manbaji is a work on Hanafi jurisprudence, aiming to show the Hanafi school of thought’s submission to the Quran and Sunnah and to respond to those who attribute work by analogy without effect. The book begins with the chapter on purity, and deals with precise jurisprudential issues such as mixing water with purified things, exfoliation of pussy, ablution with wine, impurity with semen and urine, cleansing the skin of a dead body with tanning, and other rulings, while collecting evidence from the Prophet’s hadiths and explaining what is strange about them.
descriptions.3974: This is the book “Al-Lubab fi Sharh Al-Kitab” by Abdul-Ghani Al-Maidani, and it is an explanation of Al-Qadouri’s summary of jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam Abu Hanifa. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue and importance of jurisprudence, then deals with the chapters of worship, beginning with the book on purification, tayammum, and wiping over the socks, then the book on prayer and its various rulings, such as the call to prayer, its conditions and characteristics, making up for prayers, voluntary prayers, prostration of forgetfulness, Friday prayers, the two Eids, and funerals, all the way to the book of zakat. The explanation aims to bring jurisprudential issues closer to beginner students while clarifying the areas of disagreement between schools of thought when needed.
descriptions.3975: Al-Mabsut is a book on jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought, written by Shams al-Imam al-Sarkhasi (d. 483 AH). Imam al-Sarkhasi dictated it to his students from memory while he was imprisoned in the well (in a well) in Uzjand (Ferghana). The reason for his imprisonment was a word advised by the Khaqan. This book is considered a comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedia in comparative jurisprudence between the doctrines of the two Imams Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i, in addition to them sometimes the doctrine of Imam Malik, in the controversial issues between them, discussing them and commenting on them, in addition to being one of the most important books of Hanafi jurisprudence approved in fatwas. …
descriptions.3976: The book “Al-Muhit Al-Burhani fi Al-No’mani Jurisprudence” is a jurisprudential encyclopedia based on the doctrine of Imam Abu Hanifa, written by Mahmoud bin Mazza Al-Bukhari. The book begins with an introduction by the author in which he explains the virtue of knowledge and jurisprudence, then he begins the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Purifications, which deals with the provisions of ablution, washing, tayammum, wiping over the socks, impurities, menstruation, and postpartum, followed by the Book of Prayer, which details the timings, obligatory duties, sunnahs, how to pray, and the rulings on reading and leading the prayer. The book combines the presentation of jurisprudential issues and the editing of their evidence according to the Hanafi doctrine.
descriptions.3977: This book is an abbreviation of the book “Mushkil al-Athar” by Imam al-Tahawi, compiled by Jamal al-Din al-Malati, and arranged it according to the chapters of Hanafi jurisprudence to facilitate access to its issues. The author aims to collect problematic hadiths that have caused problems for people, explain their meanings, and extract jurisprudential rulings from them, after finding the original book long and scattered in its arrangement. The book begins with an introduction to the Prophet ﷺ and his names and characteristics, then moves to the sections on acts of worship such as ablution and prayer.
descriptions.3978: The book “Al-Natf fi al-Fatawa” by Al-Sogdi is a work of jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. Its author begins with the book of worship, covering the rulings on water, its types, and details of purity. The book presents precise jurisprudential issues, such as wiping over the socks and socks, based on presenting the opinions of jurists and their differences in assessments and rulings, which makes it a reference for comparative jurisprudential fatwas within the school of thought.
descriptions.3979: The book “Al-Hidaya fi Sharh Bidayat al-Mubtadi” by Al-Marginani is an extensive explanation of jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. Its author aims to combine narration and knowledge while avoiding redundancy. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue of knowledge, then addresses the chapters on purity and prayer in detail, explaining the rulings on ablution, washing, tayammum, wiping over the socks, and menstruation, as well as the times, conditions, and characteristics of prayer, leading the prayer, and what invalidates it.
descriptions.3980: Bada'i' al-Sana'i fi Tahrani al-Shar'i' is one of the books concerned with the branches of Hanafi jurisprudence. It is a comprehensive book covering the chapters of Islamic jurisprudence according to the four schools of thought. It was written by Imam Alaa al-Din al-Kassani al-Hanafi, who died in the year 587 AH. It is an explanation of the book of his sheikh Alaa al-Din al-Samarqandi al-Hanafi, called (Tuhfat al-Fuqaha), which is an explanation of (Mukhtasar al-Qadduri). The compiler arranged the issues in this explanation in the industrial order that the craftsmen are satisfied with. Judgmental composition with evidence. …
descriptions.3981: This is a book on Hanafi jurisprudence, and it is an explanation of the summary “Treasure of Minutes” with Al-Shalabi’s footnote to it. It begins with an introduction to praise and praise, then deals with the Book of Purity, detailing the rulings on ablution, washing, tayammum, wiping over the socks, menstruation, and postpartum, explaining the words of the text, explaining its rulings, and adding some appropriate branches.
descriptions.3982: The book “Tuhfat al-Fuqaha” is a book on jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought, written by Alaa al-Din al-Samarqandi to provide an explanation, addition, and detail on al-Qadduri’s summary, mentioning the evidence and dividing the issues. The book begins with the Book of Purity, dealing with the rulings on impurity, impurities, and tayammum. Then it moves to the Book of Prayer, detailing its times and rulings, from the call to prayer and the iqama to congregational prayer, making up for prayers, and the prostration of recitation, all the way to the Book of Funerals.
descriptions.3983: Tuhfat al-Muluk fi Jurisprudence of the Doctrine of Imam Abu Hanifa is a brief book on acts of worship according to the doctrine of Imam Abu Hanifa al-Numan, by Imam Zain al-Din al-Razi, the author of (Mukhtar al-Sihah), who died a year later (666 AH = 1268 AD). What is striking about this book is that no library in the world is empty without finding a copy of it, and if this indicates anything, it only indicates the interest of the predecessors in this book despite its small size. …
descriptions.3984: This footnote is a nice entry and commentary on the book “Maraqi Al-Falah Sharh Nour Al-Idah” in jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. In it, the author explains the text of “Nour al-Idah,” beginning with the sermon of the book and the rulings on the basmalah, then he discusses in detail the chapters of purity, such as the rulings on suwar, ablution, washing, and tayammum, all the way to the book of prayer, its disliked times, and the call to prayer, relying on previous explanations and other benefits.
descriptions.3985: Durar Al-Hikam, Explanation of Gharar Al-Ahkam, a book on Hanafi jurisprudence, by its author: Muhammad ibn Framarz ibn Ali, known as Mullah - or Manla, or the Master - Khusraw (died: 885 AH) Publisher: Dar Ihya al-Kutub al-Arabiyah Edition: Unprinted and undated Subject: Hanafi jurisprudence
descriptions.3986: Hashiyat Ibn Abidin (The Response of the Confused to al-Durr al-Mukhtar) is a book that is a footnote and a comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedia on the jurisprudence of Imam Abu Hanifa al-Numan, and it is based on the explanation of the scholar Alaa al-Din al-Hasakfi on the book Tanwir al-Absar by Sheikh Shams al-Din al-Tamirashi al-Ghazi al-Hanafi. Ibn Abidin explained it comprehensively, in which he addressed the explanation of linguistic vocabulary, and provided legal evidence from Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths and a chapter on The opinions and sayings of the people of the school of thought, and what is relied upon in the school of thought and what is apparent in it. It also sometimes includes the opinions of the remaining schools of thought, with an investigation of the area of disagreement and the editing of the issues. Therefore, this footnote is considered one of the best written by the later scholars in the branches of the Hanafi school of thought. …
descriptions.3987: This book is an explanation of the book “Al-Nukat” by Imam Al-Sarkhasi, which falls within the section of jurisprudence of the Hanafi school of thought. The author deals with precise jurisprudential issues related to divorce, emancipation, inheritance, sale, and prayer, relying on the method of commentary and analysis of the jurisprudential issues mentioned in the original. The book begins with the chapter on divorce in the Sunnah, discussing the rulings on agency and granting divorce, and explaining the differences between granting divorce and suspending it.
descriptions.3988: This book is a footnote to “Rad al-Muhtar” by Ibn Abidin, and it is a continuation of the explanation of “Al-Durr al-Mukhtar” in Hanafi jurisprudence. The book deals with various jurisprudential topics related to drinking, hunting, mortgages, felonies, blood money, wills, obligations, and certificates, and aims to clarify and supplement the jurisprudential rulings in the Hanafi schools of thought.
descriptions.3989: A book on Hanafi jurisprudence, compiled by its author when he was afflicted with the judiciary, to be a brief guide for the rulers in detailing cases and rulings. He arranged it into thirty chapters, in which he dealt with a number of sections of jurisprudence, such as judicial ethics, lawsuits and evidence, testimonies, power of attorney, marriage, sales, felonies and punishments, and others, selecting these from the books of the imams of the school of thought.
descriptions.3990: This book is a brief text on jurisprudence based on the doctrine of Imam Abu Hanifa, compiled by the author Al-Marghinani to be a basis for beginners in studying jurisprudential rulings. The book begins with the chapter on purity, and explains the obligations of ablution, its Sunnahs, and what contradicts it. Then it moves to the rulings on washing and impurities, after which it deals with chapters on prayer, zakat, fasting, marriage, divorce, and other sections of Hanafi jurisprudence.
descriptions.3991: The Journal of Judicial Rulings is a legislative and jurisprudential collection based on the Hanafi school of thought. It was issued in the Ottoman era to codify civil judicial rulings. It consists of sixteen books beginning with the Book of Sales and ending with the Book of Judiciary. The book includes an introduction that includes a definition of the science of jurisprudence and its division, and a statement of the general rules of jurisprudence, then it deals in detail with the provisions of sales, their pillars and conditions, and issues of delivery and delivery. This code had a wide legal impact, as it formed the basis for personal status and penal laws in many Arab countries.
descriptions.3992: The book “Majma’ Al-Anhar fi Sharh Multaqa Al-Abhr” is an explanation of the text of “Multaqa Al-Abhr” in jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. It was compiled by its author to bring together the issues of the approved books of jurisprudence such as Al-Qadduri, Al-Mukhtar, Al-Kanz and Al-Waqiya, with the addition of issues from Al-Majma’ and Al-Hidaya. The book aims to present the issues in easy terms, clarify the disagreement between the imams, and give preference to the strongest and most correct fatwa. It begins with the book’s sermon and then addresses the chapters of jurisprudence, starting with the Book of Purity.
descriptions.3993: A jurisprudential book based on the Hanafi school of thought. Its author devoted it to explaining the provisions of guarantees in financial transactions, with a focus on issues related to zakat, Hajj, sacrifice, and emancipation, then detailing the provisions of guarantees for the tenant and the employee in various professions and crafts such as shepherding, porterage, tailoring, dyeing, and others. The author aims to collect issues related to guarantees from approved fatwa books, given their importance in resolving disputes and the necessity of knowing them for everyone who undertakes the judiciary or issuing fatwas, and even for every Muslim who is wary of wasting the rights of people.
descriptions.3994: This book is an explanation of the text “Nour al-Idah” in jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought, compiled by its author to be of assistance to students in correcting the five acts of worship, relying on evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus. The book begins with the chapter on purity, covering the rulings on water and its types, then moves on to the chapters of ablution, washing, tayammum, and wiping over the socks, arriving at the chapter on menstruation, post-partum bleeding, and istihaadah, thus covering a number of jurisprudential issues related to purity.
descriptions.3995: The Light of Clarification and the Salvation of Souls is a book written by Imam Al-Sharnabulali (d. 1069 AH) and is considered one of the most famous and important texts of Hanafi jurisprudence. Because it includes a comprehensive and accurate summary of matters of worship. This text has become widespread and famous since the lifetime of its author, so the author returned to it a second time, explained it, then shortened his explanation, and called it: “Maraqi al-Falah,” and one of the scholars made a footnote on it, known as the footnote of al-Tahtawi. These three books: the text, the explanation, and the footnote are still the destination of the people of knowledge and their dependents, and they benefit from them and are beneficial. The book discusses the following topics: purity, prayer, fasting, zakat, and Hajj.
descriptions.3996: A book on Shafi’i jurisprudence, explaining the rulings on worship according to the doctrine. It begins with an introduction about the life of Imam Shafi’i and his scholarly status, then addresses the chapters on purity, water, and utensils.
