In its fifth edition, the author took care to review the jurisprudential material, amend some rulings, and add illustrations to the Hajj book, while extracting hadiths from their modern sources.
descriptions.3997: Asna Al-Matalib Sharh Rawdat al-Talib by Imam Jurist Zakaria al-Ansari al-Shafi’i (823-926 AH) is an encyclopedic book in jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, and it is an explanation of the book “Rawdat al-Talib” by Ibn al-Muqri (d. 837 AH), which is a summary of the book “Rawdat al-Talibin” by Imam al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH). The book Asna al-Matalib has great importance among the Shafi’is, to the point that some of them said: He who has not read Asna al-Matalib is not a Shafi’i. Shihab al-Din al-Ramli (d. 957 AH) included a footnote to this book. …
descriptions.3998: The book “Helping the Seekers to Solve the Words of Fath al-Mu’in” is a footnote in Shafi’i jurisprudence, which the author placed on the explanation of “Fath al-Mu’in” by Zain al-Din al-Mulibari, which in turn is an explanation of the text of “Qurat al-Ain bi Mahmat al-Din.” The author collected these footnotes, which he commented while reading the explanation in a scientific forum, in response to the request of some students, relying in his statement on the most important books of the doctrine, such as Al-Tuhfa, Al-Nihayah, and Sharh Al-Manhaj. The book covers the sections of jurisprudence from prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj, passing through transactions such as sale, agency, and leasing, and ending with crimes, punishments, jihad, judiciary, and emancipation.
descriptions.3999: Kitab al-Umm by Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi’i (150-204 AH), a book on jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam al-Shafi’i, the author of the book. It was compiled by Yusuf bin Yahya al-Buwaiti (d. 231 AH), the companion of Imam al-Shafi’i, and his name was not mentioned. It was attributed to al-Rabi’ bin Suleiman al-Muradi, as he compiled the book and attributed it to him rather than to the one who wrote it, as he did not mention himself in it, nor attribute it to himself, as Imam al-Ghazali said in al-Ihya. He said in Al-Mahmat: It is about fifteen average volumes. Ibn Hajar said in (Manaqibah): The number of books of the Imam: one hundred and forty books.
descriptions.4000: This is a brief book on jurisprudence based on the doctrine of Imam al-Shafi’i, compiled by its author roughly for the sake of knowledge of the doctrine and to facilitate its learning, to be a reminder to the world and insight to the learner. The book begins with the chapter on purity and the rulings on water and ablution, then deals with a number of jurisprudential chapters such as the rulings on ihram, peace, agency, pre-emption, marriage to polytheistic women, and the aqeeqah.
descriptions.4001: Persuasion in the Solution of Abu Shuja’a’s Words is a book on jurisprudence by Sheikh Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Muhammad al-Khatib al-Shirbini (d. 977 AH), in which he explains the text of the purpose and approximation known as “the text of Abu Shuja’.” It is considered one of the most important and famous books of Shafi’i jurisprudence, and it is one of the approved books for teaching at Al-Azhar Mosque and other Islamic legal institutes and schools.
descriptions.4002: Al-Bayan by Imam Jurist Abu Al-Khair Yahya Al-Omrani Al-Yamani Al-Shafi’i (489-558 AH), is an encyclopedic book in Shafi’i jurisprudence, and it is an explanation of the book Al-Muhadhdhab by Abu Ishaq Al-Shirazi (who died in the year 467 AH). Imam Al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH) also explained the book Al-Muhadhdhab and called it “Al-Majmu’ Sharh Al-Muhadhdhab.” Al-Nawawi’s explanation was more famous than Al-Omrani’s explanation. However, The book Al-Bayan is of great importance. It is one of the books of comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedias in the Shafi’i school of thought and other schools of thought, and it is one of the rich sources that contains valuable sayings and many branches, to the point where it was said: (He was not woven in his style, and time has not brought an example of him). …
descriptions.4003: This is a jurisprudential footnote on the explanation of the curriculum in the branches of the Shafi’i school of thought, compiled by the author from what he wrote on both copies of the explanation of the curriculum and Al-Shabramlsi’s footnote to it, along with what he benefited from the reports of his sheikhs in the lessons. The book begins with a sermon, then deals with the chapters of jurisprudence, such as purity and prayer, and the provisions related to them, such as juveniles, ablution, washing, tayammum, and impurity. Then it moves on to detailing the rulings on prayer, its times and conditions, prostration of forgetfulness, recitation, congregational prayer, and the traveler.
descriptions.4004: A book on jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought. It begins with an introduction to monotheism and the foundations of belief, then it begins with the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the book on purity, detailing the rulings on water, ablution, washing, tayammum, and menstruation. Then it moves to the book of prayer to explain its conditions, pillars, sunnahs, invalidations, prostration of forgetfulness, and times of prohibition.
descriptions.4005: The book “Al-Tanbih fi Al-Shafi’i Jurisprudence” by Abu Ishaq Al-Shirazi is a brief text on the jurisprudence of the Shafi’i school of thought. It begins with the book of purity, covering the rulings on water, utensils, the siwak, ablution, washing, and tayammum. Then it moves to the book of prayer to include its times, the rulings on the call to prayer, the description of prayer, its obligations, its sunnahs, and what is related to it, such as prostration of forgetfulness, recitation, and congregational prayer. The book presents jurisprudential issues in a concise manner, mentioning the differences and preferences within the school of thought, making it an educational reference for beginners in the study of Shafi’i jurisprudence.
descriptions.4006: Al-Hawi Al-Kabir fi Jurisprudence of the Imam Shafi’i Doctrine by Imam Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Habib Al-Mawardi Al-Basri (364 - 450 AH). He is one of the most important books of jurisprudence in the Shafi’i school of thought, and one of the most important and famous Shafi’i books. It is an explanation of the summary of Al-Muzani (d. 264 AH). This book is considered a comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedia that contains the sayings of many scholars of the school of thought and others. Haji Khalifa says in his book “Kashf al-Dhunoun”: “Al-Hawi al-Kabir fi al-Furoo’,” by Judge Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad al-Mawardi al-Basri al-Shafi’i, who died in the year four hundred and fifty. It is a great book, in ten volumes, and it is said that it is thirty volumes. Nothing like it has been written in the doctrine.
descriptions.4007: This book is a poetic collection of jurisprudence based on the Shafi’i school of thought, organized by its author to be concise and easy to memorize, covering the chapters of jurisprudence from purity and prayer to zakat and transactions such as mortgages, stones, and partnerships. The book begins with an introduction to the foundations of faith, monotheism, and the importance of intention and sincerity, then moves to the jurisprudential rulings arranged in chapters.
descriptions.4008: This book is a nice explanation of the text of “Al-Minhaj” by Imam Al-Nawawi in jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, written by Muhammad Al-Ghamrawi in response to a request to facilitate understanding of the text adopted by the imams of the school of thought. The author aims to clarify hidden expressions and reveal the mysteries of issues in a concise and easy manner, making use of the previous explanations so that they are inherent in the text and easy to benefit from. The book covers multiple jurisprudential sections, such as purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, sales, religious duties, and other rulings.
descriptions.4009: The magnificent Gharar fi Sharh al-Bahja al-Wardiyya system by Imam jurist Zakaria al-Ansari al-Shafi’i (823-926 AH) is a comprehensive encyclopedic book in jurisprudence based on the Shafi’i doctrine. It is an explanation of the al-Bahja al-Wardiyya system by Ibn al-Wardi (d. 749 AH), in which the book al-Hawi al-Saghir by al-Qazwini (d. 665 AH) was composed. The Shafi'is paid great attention to this book, explaining, studying, and teaching, and they included a group of footnotes on it, the most important of which is: Footnote by Ibn Qasim al-Abadi (d. 944 AH). Hashiyat al-Sherbini (d. 1326 AH). …
descriptions.4010: The book “Al-Lubab fi Shafi’i Jurisprudence” is a book on jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, compiled by its author to include various sections of jurisprudence such as purity, prayer, zakat, Hajj, sales, and others. The book is considered one of the advanced jurisprudential sources relied upon by the jurists of the doctrine, and it contains jurisprudential issues, rules, controls, and jurisprudential differences.
descriptions.4011: Al-Majmu’ Sharh al-Muhadhdhab was written by Imam Muhyiddin al-Nawawi, in which he explained the book: “Al-Muhadhdhab in Shafi’i Jurisprudence” by Sheikh Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi, the well-known fundamentalist jurist. Al-Suyuti said in “Al-Hawi”: He composed it in the style of “Al-Mughni” by Ibn Qudamah Al-Hanbali, and it has been said: If the author of Al-Mughni and the author of Al-Majmu’ agree on an issue, then it is the truth whose correctness is most likely. Al-Nawawi was one of the imams of hadith scholars, so he preserved his book from fabricated hadiths, and pointed out the weakness of weak hadiths.
descriptions.4012: The Hadhrami introduction to the jurisprudence of the Shafi’i masters, called Mukhtasar Ba Fadl, or Al-Mukhtasar Al-Kabir, or Education Issues, a comprehensive summary book on Shafi’i jurisprudence, authored by the jurist Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Ba ​​Fadl Al-Hadrami (850 - 981 AH). It is a well-known book among students of Shafi’i jurisprudence, and it is widely circulated. Despite its brevity, scholars’ explanations of it and their printed and manuscript footnotes abound, and it has been published in books all over the world. This text, which became famous and benefited from far and near, was distinguished by the clarity of its style, with scrutiny and investigation of its issues. Therefore, it was accepted and spread in most countries. It is considered one of the most important abbreviations in Shafi’i jurisprudence because of the jurisprudential controls it contains. …
descriptions.4013: This book is an explanation of the text of the “Hadrami Introduction” to jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought. It begins with introductions in the translation of the text by the author and its commentator, then deals with the provisions of purity in detail, beginning with chapters on water, utensils, ablution, and washing, arriving at the chapter on impurity and tayammum.
descriptions.4014: The book “Al-Muhadhdhab fi Jurisprudence of Imam Al-Shafi’i” by Abu Ishaq Al-Shirazi is a work of jurisprudence based on the Shafi’i school of thought. Its author aims to mention the principles of the school of thought with their evidence, while explaining the issues emanating from it and their reasons. The book begins with an introduction and then covers the book of purity comprehensively, examining the types of water and their rulings, utensils, ablution, washing, ablution, menstruation, and removing impurity. Then it moves to the book of prayer to discuss its timings and rulings.
descriptions.4015: Al-Waseet is a book written by Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (d. 505 AH), on the jurisprudence of Imam al-Shafi’i (d. 204 AH).
descriptions.4016: This is a footnote by Al-Bujayrami on Al-Khatib’s explanation of the text of Abu Shuja’ in jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, in which the author collected precise jokes and edits from the approved footnotes, in response to the request of his sheikh and students of knowledge. The book begins with introductory discussions on the principles of jurisprudence and language, then begins detailing the rulings on purity and the issues related to it, such as ablution, washing, cleansing, and the siwak.
descriptions.4017: This book is an expanded explanation of the text of “Al-Minhaj” in jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought. It begins with an introduction on praise and praise, then deals with the provisions of purity and prayer and the conditions, pillars, sunnahs and invalidations related to them, with details on the issues of congregation, shortening prayers, and travel. The book also includes footnotes by Al-Shirwani and Al-Abadi that follow up on the explanation and increase its clarification.
descriptions.4018: A jurisprudential book based on the Shafi’i school of thought, which aims to present the rulings on contracts, transactions, and the judiciary, with special attention to what judges, notaries, and witnesses need. It begins with an introduction to the virtue of knowledge, then deals in detail with jurisprudential sections such as acknowledgment, sales, peace, mortgage, interdiction, and reconciliation, reviewing jurisprudential issues and the differences therein.
descriptions.4019: This book is two footnotes to Imam al-Jalal al-Mahli’s explanation of Imam al-Nawawi’s Minhaj al-Talibin in Shafi’i jurisprudence, in which the authors al-Qalyubi and Amira al-Mu’tamid collected jurisprudential issues, clarifying hidden expressions and rejecting objections. The book begins with the chapter on purity and the provisions of water, cleansing, ablution, washing, tayammum, and menstruation, then moves to the book of prayer, its provisions, and the conditions for its obligation.
descriptions.4020: The book “Hilyat al-Ulama fi Ma’rifat al-Mazhab al-Fuqaha’” by Abu Bakr al-Shashi is a jurisprudential encyclopedia based on the Shafi’i school of thought, in which the author collected the sayings of scholars and their differences in matters of jurisprudence, beginning with the chapters of purity such as water, ablution, ablution, wiping over the socks, menstruation, and postpartum. The book aims to present the doctrine of every diligent person and his method of ijtihad, while mentioning the two sayings and narrations of Al-Shafi’i and others, to be a comprehensive reference for the schools of jurisprudence.
descriptions.4021: The book “The Secrets of the Corners” by Badr al-Din al-Zarkashi is a work on Shafi’i jurisprudence, in which he collected the jurisprudential issues mentioned by Imams al-Rafi’i and al-Nawawi in their books (Sharh al-Wajiz and Rawdat al-Talibin) in places other than their usual chapters. The author traced these issues and returned them to their original places and appropriate chapters, and he gave it this name in reference to their concealment in the corners of the two books.
descriptions.4022: The book “Daqaeq Al-Minhaj” by Imam Al-Nawawi is a precise explanation of the wording of the book “Al-Minhaj” in Shafi’i jurisprudence, with an explanation of the differences between it and the wording of the book “Al-Muharrir” by Al-Rafi’i. The book begins with an introduction explaining the legal and linguistic terms mentioned in the sermon, then it addresses the well-known sections of jurisprudence such as purity, prayer, zakat, sale, marriage, and wounds. The work aims to clarify the precise meanings of jurisprudential terms and edit them, making it a specialized linguistic and jurisprudential work.
descriptions.4023: Rawdat al-Talibin wa Umdat al-Muftin is a book written by Imam al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH), on Shafi’i jurisprudence. In it, Al-Nawawi summarized the book Fath Al-Aziz with Sharh Al-Wajez by Al-Rafi’i, which (i.e. Al-Rafi’i’s book) is an explanation of the book Al-Wajez in the Jurisprudence of Imam Al-Shafi’i by Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali.
descriptions.4024: This book is an explanation of the “Al-Zabad” system in jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, organized by Sheikh Ahmed bin Raslan. The commentator aims to solve the words of the text, highlight its subtleties, and edit its issues, while adding the benefits of new developments. The commentator begins with an introduction explaining the Basmala linguistically and terminologically, then proceeds to explain the verses of the system, paragraph by paragraph.
descriptions.4025: A book on Shafi’i jurisprudence, in which the author collected jurisprudential issues and rulings in the form of fatwas, with special attention to explaining the conditions, descriptions and rulings of the mufti, and the manner and etiquette of fatwa and fatwa. The book includes multiple sections on acts of worship, such as zakat and fasting, and transactions such as usury, peace, mortgage, partnership, and other various jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.4026: Fath al-Mu'in bi Sharh Qurrat al-Ain bi-Mahat al-Din is a book on jurisprudence by Imam Ahmad Zain al-Din bin Abdul-Aziz al-Ma'bari al-Mulaibari al-Fannani al-Shafi'i (d. 987 AH/1579 AD), in which he explained his book called “Qurat al-Ain bi Mahat al-Din,” and it is considered one of the most important and famous Shafi’i books. It is taught in India, and is popular among students of Shafi’i jurisprudence in Egypt, the Levant, and the Arabian Peninsula, from Hijaz, Yemen, and Hadhramaut, as well as in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. The author says in the introduction to the book:
descriptions.4027: This book is an explanation of the text of “Minhaj al-Talibeen,” which the author summarized from “Minhaj al-Talibeen” by Imam al-Nawawi in the jurisprudence of the Shafi’i school of thought. The explanation aims to solve the words of the text, clarify its meaning, and complete its benefit. The author opened it by thanking God who guided him to this writing. The book falls within the books of Shafi’i jurisprudence, and in its first volume it deals with the topics of purity, prayer, and funerals in detail.
descriptions.4028: The book “Al-Wahhab’s Conquests by Clarifying the Explanation of the Student Method” is a footnote by the author Al-Jamal on the explanation of the method in Shafi’i jurisprudence. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue of the science of jurisprudence and praise for the explanation of the method. Then it deals in detail with the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Purity and its rulings such as minor ritual impurities, ablution, washing, and tayammum, all the way to the Book of Prayer and its rulings such as the times, the call to prayer, the congregational prayer, and shortening the prayer.
descriptions.4029: This book is a brief explanation of jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, aiming to facilitate understanding of the legal rulings in acts of worship such as purity and prayer, beginning with an explanation of the virtue of jurisprudence and the importance of sincere intention in seeking knowledge.
descriptions.4030: This book is a summary of jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam al-Shafi’i. Its author wrote it to be accessible to learners and easy to memorize for beginners. It is organized into the well-known chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with purity and prayer, moving on to zakat, fasting, and Hajj, then transactions, religious duties, and marriage, then felonies, punishments, and jihad, and concluding with hunting, oaths, decrees, and emancipation. The book is distinguished by its abundance of divisions, limited characteristics, and details of jurisprudential rulings in a concise manner.
descriptions.4031: This book is a summary of jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought. The author collected it from the knowledge of Imam al-Shafi’i to bring it closer to those who wanted it, while informing him of his prohibition against imitating him and imitating others. The book begins with the chapter on purity, covering the rulings on water, utensils, ablution, washing, and tayammum. Then it moves to the book of prayer, explaining its times, the call to prayer, its characteristics, and the rulings related to forgetfulness, congregational prayer, and the qiblah.
descriptions.4032: Mughni, who needs to know the meanings of the words of the curriculum, is a book on jurisprudence by Sheikh Shams al-Din Muhammad bin al-Khatib al-Shirbini (d. 977 AH), in which he explains the book Minhaj al-Talibeen by Imam al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH). It is one of the most important and famous Shafi’i books, and the one most widely discussed by students of jurisprudence of all sects. It is a comprehensive book of the rulings on acts of worship and transactions, distinguished by its precision of expression, smoothness of style, and good arrangement.
descriptions.4033: Minhaj al-Talibin wa Umdat al-Muftin is a book for the works of Imam al-Nawawi. It is the main source of muftis and the destination for those who ask questions according to the Shafi’i school of thought. This is due to the strength of its expression, the abundance of its material, and the completeness of its usefulness. In deriving its material, his compiler relied on the reliable one, as he said: “Our companions [(may Allah have mercy on them)] have extensively classified the simple and abbreviated ones, and he perfected the summary of ‘al-Muharrir’ by Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Rafi’i, the author of investigations, and it has many benefits, and it is intended for fulfilling the doctrine. It is approved for the mufti and other first-time desires.” Then he said: “I saw it shortened to about half its size; So that it will be easy to preserve it, along with the new precious things I will add to it, God willing.
descriptions.4034: A book on jurisprudence based on the doctrine of Imam al-Shafi’i, explaining the rulings of worship, starting with purity and the divisions of water and their rulings, passing through the chapters of ablution, washing, and tayammum, then detailing the rulings on prayer of its types, zakat, fasting, and seclusion. The author presents jurisprudential issues in a concise manner, relying on linguistic and terminological definitions, while mentioning jurisprudential rulings such as prohibition, detestation, and permissibility.
descriptions.4035: This is a book on jurisprudence according to the Shafi’i school of thought, and it is an explanation of the book “The Joy of the Eye with the Missions of Religion.” The author aims to facilitate jurisprudential issues for beginners, and in it he relied on the main books of the Shafi’i school of thought, such as “Nihayat al-Muhtaj” and “Tuhfat al-Muhtaj.” The book is organized into chapters on acts of worship, such as prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj. Then, it addresses some chapters on transactions, such as selling, with special attention to the branches of prayer, its rulings, and details of its Sunnahs and those that corrupt them.
descriptions.4036: Nihayat al-Muhtaj li Sharh al-Minhaj by Imam Jurist Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Abi al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Hamza ibn Shihab al-Din al-Ramli al-Manufi al-Masri al-Ansari, famous for al-Shafi’i al-Saghir, who died in the year 1004 AH. He is one of the mothers of jurisprudence books in the Shafi’i school of thought, and he is one of the two most important commentaries on the book al-Minhaj by Imam al-Nawawi. The other is Tuhfat al-Muhtaj by Ibn Hajar al-Haytami. …
descriptions.4037: Nihayat al-Muttalib fi Diriyah al-Madhab is the largest printed book on Shafi’i jurisprudence. It was written by Abu al-Ma’ali al-Juwayni Abd al-Malik ibn Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad al-Juwayni Rukn al-Din, nicknamed the Imam of the Two Holy Mosques, who died in the year 478 AH. It is an explanation of the summary of al-Muzani, in which its author collected the content of the Shafi’i doctrine, by way of investigating it. It is considered one of the most important books of the doctrine, and Shafi’i jurists have adopted it, taken from it, and provided abbreviations and explanations for it.
descriptions.4038: The book “The Full Moon with Authentic Evidence of Rulings” written by Nasser bin Saeed Al-Saif, is a book on general jurisprudence, in which the author collected authentic hadiths related to the rulings on worship, relying on what was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, or one of them. The book begins with an introduction that explains the importance of the Prophet’s Sunnah in understanding the Qur’an. Then it is organized into jurisprudential chapters that begin with the Book of Purity and include the rulings on water, ablution, washing, and tayammum. Then it is followed by the Book of Prayer and its related times, the call to prayer, conditions, prescription, prostration, congregational prayer, Friday prayers, two Eids, and others.
descriptions.4039: This book is a series of monthly meetings by Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Uthaymeen, in which he answers various questions in general jurisprudence, and provides lessons and guidance on various religious topics. The book begins by talking about the importance of useful knowledge and good deeds, then deals with jurisprudential issues such as the rulings on prayer, fasting, and buying and selling, in addition to contemplative pauses on the biography of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4040: A book that collects Ramadan sessions given by the author over a period of six years, dealing with the virtues of the month of Ramadan and urging it to be used for good deeds and obedience. The book is organized into topics that include the rulings on fasting, praying, intention, and suhoor, and details jurisprudential issues such as things that break the fast and what results from mistakes and forgetfulness, with answers to practical questions related to the fasting person.
descriptions.4041: This book is a collection of lessons and fatwas delivered by Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen in the Prophet’s Mosque during the year 1416 AH, and combines interpretation and jurisprudential issues. The book begins with an interpretation of Surat Al-Tariq, addressing the meanings of its verses and proof of the vision of God Almighty, then it moves on to answering various questions in jurisprudence, such as the rulings on prayer, funerals, marriage, and photography, in addition to general advice.
descriptions.4042: This book is an explanation of the book “Bulugh Al-Maram” by Abu Al-Aza’im Atiya Salem, and it is related to the topics of Islamic jurisprudence, especially in the chapter on purity. The explanation covers the hadiths of the book with detailed explanations about the rulings on impure and pure water, and also includes an explanation of Imam Ibn Hajar’s terminology in this book. The book is numbered automatically and deals with topics such as the ruling on dead amphibians and dead sea animals, and the conditions for impurity and purification of water.
descriptions.4043: This book is an explanation of the book “Umdat al-Ahkam” by Imam Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi, located in the field of general jurisprudence. In it, the author deals with the explanation of the prophetic hadiths contained in the rulings on purity and ablution and other jurisprudential issues, opening with an explanation of the hadith “Actions are but by intentions” and an explanation of the requirement of intention for purity, relying on the authentic hadiths from the Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
descriptions.4044: This book is an encyclopedia of the jurisprudence of financial transactions, and deals in detail with the provisions of sale in terms of its definition, evidence of its legitimacy, and its various divisions. The book explains the characteristics of the contracting parties, the terms of the sale and the price, and discusses the issues of formula, pricing, increase and deduction, relying on evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah, consensus and what is reasonable.
descriptions.4045: This book is an excerpt from Sheikh Abdul Aziz Al-Tarifi’s explanation of the book “Bulugh Al-Maram” in general jurisprudence, and its index has been automatically numbered. The commentator begins with an introduction to the importance of the Prophetic Sunnah and its being a revelation from God. He then proceeds to explain the hadiths about purity, water, and impurities, addressing rulings such as the purity of water, the impurity of a dog, ablution thanks to a woman, and other jurisprudential issues related to purity.
descriptions.4046: The book “The Open Door Meeting” is a collection of various jurisprudential questions and answers, collected from open meetings with Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen. The book covers issues of worship such as ablution, prayer, zakat, and fasting, in addition to contemporary issues such as the ruling on television and video, the rulings on dealing with people of innovation, and issues in sales and sacrifices. The book's style is characterized by ease and clarity, as it presents the question and is followed by a detailed answer supported by Sharia evidence.
descriptions.4047: This is a comprehensive encyclopedia of jurisprudence, prepared by a group of authors. It begins with a definition of jurisprudence linguistically and terminologically in the first book and among the fundamentalists, then it deals with jurisprudential sources, legislation, diligence, doctrines, and codification of jurisprudence. The book includes jurisprudential sections arranged in alphabetical order, beginning with the letter hamza, and dealing with various rulings such as the father, the instrument, the utensil, the father and his guardianship in marriage, the gift, the will, and emancipation.
descriptions.4048: This book is a poetic composition in which the author collected the jurisprudential choices of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and arranged them according to the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the book of purity, then prayer, then fasting, then inheritance. The systems aim to bring together the issues that Ibn Taymiyyah distinguished from other schools of thought, relying on evidence and weighting. The systems are preceded by a brief translation of the life of Nazim Suleiman bin Sahman, including his upbringing, his sheikhs, his students, and his works.
descriptions.4049: This is a book of poetic composition in which its author collected jurisprudential issues that were unique to Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah on the authority of the four imams, and arranged them in the form of verses to make them easier to memorize. The book falls within the general classification of jurisprudence, and deals with various issues such as shortening prayers while traveling and others, which sparked controversy in its time.
descriptions.4050: This is a book on general jurisprudence, written by Abd al-Rahman al-Saadi in an innovative style based on the question-and-answer format, to include important ruling issues in easy words and clear meanings. The book is organized into the chapters of worship, starting with purity, then prayer, then zakat, then fasting, then Hajj and Umrah, relying for rulings on the well-known doctrine of Imam Ahmad, with preference to what the author deems more correct, continuing with similarities, analogues, and differences between issues.
descriptions.4051: The book “The Differences of Imams and Scholars” by Ibn Hubayra is considered one of the most important books of comparative jurisprudence that a Muslim cannot do without in the present and the future. It is one of the most prominent books that presented a new and unique narrative of its kind, as it shed light on the difference between imams and scholars in the chapters of jurisprudence, and showed us that this difference is a mercy, and discussed the intended difference here and the difference between it and other differences. The book includes legal rulings related to matters of worship, transactions, etc., and the differing opinions of scholars regarding these matters. The first to write down jurisprudence was: Abu Hanifa al-Numan, and after him Imam Malik. Then came Imam al-Shafi’i and after him Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, so the issues of the Sunnis and the community were confined to them. …
descriptions.4052: This is a book on general jurisprudence. It presents the opinions of jurists and their differences on various jurisprudential issues, beginning with the chapters of purity, such as rinsing the mouth and nose, and what invalidates ablution, then moving on to the Book of Prayer and the related rulings on congregational prayer, leading the prayer, and the prescription of prayer. The author aims to document the areas of disagreement among scholars on these issues, based on hadiths and narrations, to be a reference in the jurisprudence of disagreement.
descriptions.4053: The book “The Great Legal Rulings” by Abd al-Haqq al-Ashbili is a comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedia. Its compilation begins with the Book of Faith, covering its chapters and issues in detail, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and narrations. The book falls within the general classification of jurisprudence, and is concerned with explaining the major legal rulings that include the foundations of religion and its branches, starting with the definition of Islam and faith and explaining the people of faith and the virtues of deeds.
descriptions.4054: This is a book on general jurisprudence, providing an explanation and commentary on the text of “The Beautiful Pearls in Jurisprudential Issues” by Imam Al-Shawkani, with a focus on abstracting the jurisprudential issues indicated by the correct evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The author aims to present Islamic jurisprudence in an accessible manner, adding explanations, comments, and corrections based on the manuscript, to serve as a study reference in religious institutes. The book deals with the chapters of jurisprudence, starting with the Book of Purity, divided into detailed chapters and sections that include the rulings on water, impurities, ablution, ghusl, tayammum, and menstruation.
descriptions.4055: Al-Awsat fi Sunan, Consensus, and Differences is a jurisprudential book, written by Imam Ibn al-Mundhir al-Naysaburi (241 AH - 318 AH). The book is considered a summary of another book by the author, which is Al-Sunan Al-Mabsoot. The author divided the book into jurisprudential books, as is the custom of those who write about the science of jurisprudence, but he did not classify the issues within one book. Rather, he mentioned titles and listed under them the issues that he wanted to talk about. He would begin by mentioning the jurisprudential issue, then mention the evidence from the Book of God, then add the hadiths. The book is considered an important reference for those who want to learn about the doctrines of scholars in matters of jurisprudence, and the number of texts contained in the book has reached 3345 texts, varying between hadiths with chain of transmission and traceable hadiths attributed to the Companions and followers.
descriptions.4056: A book that collects what the Mother of the Believers Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) understood about a number of the Companions on jurisprudential issues and narrations, indicating the areas in which they disagreed with her or returned to her words. The author begins with a brief translation of Aisha and her characteristics, then devotes chapters to her explanations of the major companions such as Omar, Ali, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah and others, mentioning the evidence and news that reached him regarding that.
descriptions.4057: The book “Al-Ijma’” by Ibn Al-Mundhir is a work on general jurisprudence, collecting issues on which there has been consensus among scholars according to the author’s approach. The book begins with a study of the life of Ibn al-Mundhir and his works, then deals with sequential jurisprudential chapters that begin with the Book of Ablution and end with the Book of Marriage, with a focus on mentioning what the jurists have unanimously agreed upon in each chapter.
descriptions.4058: The book “Al-Iqna’” by Ibn Al-Mundhir is a work of general jurisprudence. It begins with the Book of Purity, detailing the provisions of ablution, washing, tayammum, and impurities. Then it moves to the Book of Prayer, covering its timings and the rulings on the call to prayer, leading the prayer, Friday prayer, the two Eids, fear, the eclipse, and rain. The author relies on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths with his jurisprudential sayings in explaining what requires ablution and washing and what nullifies purity, combining narration and knowledge in jurisprudential issues.
descriptions.4059: The book “Al-Darari Al-Madiya Sharh Al-Durar Al-Bahiyya” by Imam Al-Shawkani is an extensive explanation of general jurisprudence, covering the rulings on purity and prayer in detail. The book begins with the chapter on the rulings on water, where the jurisprudential rule states that water is pure and purified, and nothing changes it from this characteristic unless one of its three descriptions (smell, color, or taste) changes due to impurity, citing evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus. The explanation aims to clarify jurisprudential issues and edit evidence, while discussing different opinions and giving preference to the stronger ones.
descriptions.4060: The book “Al-Rawdah Al-Nadiyah Sharh Al-Durar Al-Bahiyya” is an explanation of a summary of jurisprudence by the author Muhammad Al-Shawkani, compiled by Siddiq Hasan Khan to explain the jurisprudential issues whose evidence is based on the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book is organized into the well-known sections of jurisprudence, beginning with purity and prayer, then zakat and funerals, relying on the approach of investigation and following the evidence without adhering to the well-known schools of thought.
descriptions.4061: A jurisprudential book based on the method of reasoning with legal arguments and evidence, far from pure imitation. Sheikh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani paid attention to it with his comments, which included explaining the strange, grading and criticism, discussing issues and weighing them, and explaining hadith terminology and terminological rules. The book includes the text “The Beautiful Pearls in Jurisprudential Issues” and begins with the book “Purity and then Prayer.” It is one of the useful jurisprudential books whose author followed the method of the hadith scholars.
descriptions.4062: The overwhelming torrent flowing over the flower gardens is a book written by Muhammad bin Ali bin Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Shawkani and published by Ibn Hazm in the year 1425 AH, corresponding to the year 2004 AD.
descriptions.4063: The book “Simplified Jurisprudence in the Light of the Qur’an and Sunnah” is a general jurisprudential work prepared by an elite group of scholars, aiming to present legal rulings in a simple manner based on the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book begins with an introduction that emphasizes the importance of jurisprudence in religion. Then, in its first parts, it deals with the provisions of purity in detail in multiple sections, including water and utensils, etiquette for relieving oneself, the siwak, and the Sunnahs of common sense.
descriptions.4064: “Fiqh according to the four schools of thought” may mean the following: Jurisprudence according to the four schools of thought (book): Wikimedia clarification page. Jurisprudence on the Four Doctrines (Book, Abd al-Rahman al-Jaziri): A book written by Abd al-Rahman al-Jaziri. Jurisprudence on the Four Doctrines (Book, Egyptian Ministry of Endowments): Book.
descriptions.4065: Al-Muhalla fi Sharh al-Majali, with arguments and narrations, by Imam Ali Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi, the publisher of the Zahiri school of thought. Al-Muhalla’s book is considered one of the most important books of Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi. He was famous for it and was considered the publisher of the Zahiri school of thought, which takes the apparent meaning of the text and its verbal and moral meaning, and is diligent. He does not consider analogy in meanings at all, and considers verbal analogy to be the denotation of the word or the meaning of the word. Rather, the disagreement between the people of the principles of jurisprudence is in words, and does not consider the reason or meaning. It is ruled only by the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Companions, and the book is a jurisprudential wealth and a comprehensive encyclopedia in comparative jurisprudence containing the equivalent of 2,312 issues, which the author began with doctrines and ended with issues of discretion, during which Ibn Hazm reviewed the opinions of jurists...
descriptions.4066: The book “Al-Muntaqa Min Fareed Al-Fawa’id” is a collection of jurisprudential and doctrinal issues selected from the works of major scholars, collected by the author and selected from a notebook in which he recorded the benefits. The book includes benefits extracted from the books of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, such as “The Book of Faith” and “Explanation of the Doctrine of Al-Isfahani,” and from “Bada’i’ al-Fawa’id” and “Al-Huda” by Ibn al-Qayyim, in addition to benefits from the interpretation of Sheikh Muhammad al-Amin al-Shanqeeti and from the book “Al-Munaqalah Bi-Waqf.” The book deals with various topics in general jurisprudence, with special attention to issues of faith, Islam and its distinction.
descriptions.4067: The Kuwaiti Jurisprudence Encyclopedia is a comprehensive jurisprudential work prepared by a group of authors. It is divided into forty-five parts and covers the sections of general Islamic jurisprudence. The book opens with an introductory introduction that addresses the concept of jurisprudence linguistically and terminologically, the terms related to it, and the historical stages that Islamic jurisprudence passed through from the era of prophecy until the development of ijtihad, with an explanation of the classes of diligent scholars, the schools of jurisprudence, and the sources of ijtihad.
descriptions.4068: A book on general jurisprudence, in which its author collected what Mrs. Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) taught about a number of major companions, such as Abu Bakr, Omar, Ali, and Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them). The book begins with a translation of Mrs. Aisha and mentions her characteristics, then moves on to list those jurisprudential and hadith corrections in which she saw a contradiction to what those companions believed.
descriptions.4069: The book “The Answer to Report What Aisha Reflected on the Companions” by Imam Badr al-Din al-Zarkashi, which is a book on general jurisprudence, in which the author collects what has been authentically reported from Mrs. Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) from comments on a number of major companions, such as Abu Bakr, Omar, Ali, and Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them). The book begins with a translation of Mrs. Aisha and an explanation of her characteristics, then moves on to list those corrections in sections and chapters, thus demonstrating the breadth of her knowledge and the accuracy of her understanding.
descriptions.4070: The book “Bustan Al-Ahbar Mukhtasar Nil Al-Awtar” is a summary of the explanation of “Nil Al-Awtar” by Imam Al-Shawkani based on the book “Muntaqa Al-Akhbar” by Ibn Taymiyyah, and it falls in the field of general jurisprudence. The author aims to bring Sharia rulings closer by condensing the explanation and limiting it to what indicates translation, while mentioning disagreement when necessary, so that it will be the most useful and delicious book of rulings for the viewer and listener. The book begins with the chapter on purity and water, covering the rulings on impurities and purification according to the hadiths of the Prophet.
descriptions.4071: This book combines three works in one volume, aiming to correct the doctrine and clarify Islamic jurisprudence. It begins with the book “Purifying the Heavens and the Pillars from the Defilements of Polytheism and Unbelief,” which criticizes the heresies and misguidance associated with worshiping graves and seeking saints, and stresses the importance of pure monotheism. Then follows the “Four Rules,” which explain the principles of distinguishing monotheism of worship from polytheism, citing the conditions of the polytheists, ancient and modern. The book concludes with “The Approach of the Travelers and Clarification of Jurisprudence in Religion,” which is a summary of general jurisprudence that deals with the rulings on purity and prayer and the duties, sunnahs, and invalidations related to them.
descriptions.4072: The book “Tahdhib al-Athar” by Imam al-Tabari is a work on general jurisprudence, and this missing part of it deals with the continuation of the Musnad of the companion Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with him). The book is concerned with collecting the Prophetic hadiths reported by the Companions and explaining their methods, with a focus on verifying the chains of transmission and discussing the differences in the narrations. It also addresses jurisprudential issues such as the rulings on swearing an oath in Islam and pre-Islamic times, and the rulings on forgetfulness in prayer, reviewing the opinions of the Companions and followers in that regard.
descriptions.4073: Tahdheeb al-Athar is a book of hadith, written by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (224 AH - 310 AH). The book has two editions, the first under the name: Tahdheeb al-Athar, while the second: Detailing what is proven from the Messenger of God from the narrations. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari’s approach in the book is summarized as follows: al-Tabari mentioned in the book what was authentic to him from what the Companions attributed on the authority of the Messenger, so he began with the Musnad of the Ten, Ahl al-Bayt, the Mawali, and some of the Musnad of Ibn Abbas, and he died before completing it. The author spoke about the hadiths, criticizing and modifying them, correcting them and weakening them, explaining the methods of the hadiths and their reasons. He spoke about the jurisprudence of hadiths, the differences of scholars and their arguments. He spoke about the meanings and the strange, explaining this with Arab words and poetry.
descriptions.4074: The book, Hujjatullah al-Baghiha, is one of the most prominent Islamic works written by the scholar Shah Waliullah Dehlawi in the eighteenth century, and it brilliantly combines sociology and Islamic doctrine. This book is widely viewed as the jewel of Dehlawi's work, as it represents a unique work that combines history, philosophy, jurisprudence, theology, and psychology. The book seeks to clarify the intentions and objectives behind Islamic laws, rituals and traditions by integrating spiritual, rational and textual approaches. …
descriptions.4075: The book “Khulasat Al-Kalam Sharh Umdat Al-Ahkam” is a book on general jurisprudence, in which the author explains the book “Umdat Al-Ahkam” based on the hadiths of Al-Ahkam. The book begins with a comprehensive translation of the life of the author, his sheikhs, and his students, then deals with the sections of jurisprudence, starting with the Book of Purity and passing through the Book of Prayer and the times it contains, the call to prayer, leading the prayer, and the prescription and rulings of prayer, all the way to the Friday prayer, the two Eids, and the eclipse.
descriptions.4076: This is a book on easy jurisprudence, which falls under the classification of general jurisprudence, and begins with an introduction that explains the status of the jurisprudential heritage and its importance in the life of a Muslim. The book aims to facilitate legal knowledge based on the Qur’an and Sunnah. It was originally prepared as part of the curricula of the Institute of Imams and Preachers, then reprinted to be a course in the courses of the Mosque Care Program. The first section of the book deals with acts of worship, explaining the pillars of Islam, starting with purity, passing through prayer and its rulings, all the way to zakat and fasting in Ramadan.
descriptions.4077: The book “Umdat al-Ahkam min Kalam Khair al-Anam ﷺ” is a book on general jurisprudence, compiled by Al-Hafiz Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi, and he selected its hadiths from what Imams al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed upon in their Sahihs, in response to a request to shorten a number of hadiths on ahkam. The book includes about four hundred and more hadiths, arranged under the sections of jurisprudence, such as purity, prayer, and Friday prayers, which makes it a foundation for the study of Islamic jurisprudence in the manner of the scholars of hadith and narration.
descriptions.4078: The book Fiqh al-Sunnah is a book that deals with issues of Islamic jurisprudence coupled with evidence from the clear Qur’an and authentic Sunnah, written by a former master. The first part of the book was published in the mid-forties of the twentieth century AD, corresponding to the year 1365 AH, and it is a small treatise, of small pieces, and it was on (the jurisprudence of purity). It was issued with an introduction from the general guide of the Muslim Brotherhood, Sheikh Imam Hassan Al-Banna, praising the sheikh’s approach to writing, his good way of presenting jurisprudence, and his endearment to the people. The Sheikh continued to write about jurisprudence after that, and every period he published a small part until fourteen parts were completed, and then it was published in three large parts. …
descriptions.4079: The book “Jurisprudence of Calamities” by Bakr Abu Zaid is a jurisprudential work that addresses emerging issues and contemporary issues, and includes within it five independent treatises. The first thesis deals with the topic of “codification and binding” and discusses the obligation of judges to adhere to a specific doctrine or codified law, while the second examines “conformity in terminology” and the effect of changing legal terminology. The other three letters discuss modern calamities such as the bank guarantee letter, the life support device, the sign of death, and modern reproductive methods such as in vitro fertilization, within the framework of studying the legal rulings on these new facts.
descriptions.4080: This book is a collection of Prophetic hadiths arranged under the headings of jurisprudence, compiled by Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab. The book begins with the Book of Purity, covering the rulings on water, ablution, tayammum, and impurities. Then it moves to the Book of Prayer to include the chapters on the call to prayer, timings, the prescription of prayer, the congregational prayer, the imamate, and Friday prayer. The author relies on narrating the chain of transmission of hadiths and extracting them from well-known Sunnah sources, to be a modern jurisprudential reference that includes practical rulings.
descriptions.4081: This is a book on general jurisprudence, summarizing the issues of disagreement among scholars, and it begins with issues of purity such as water mixed with impurity, what dies in a well, the content of various animals, the purity of impurities, and the recipes for ablution. The book presents the opinions of jurists of different sects, such as Abu Hanifa, Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Al-Awza’i and others, with evidence and comments on them.
descriptions.4082: This book is brief on general jurisprudence. It focuses on the issues in which the dispute occurred between the two Imams Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa, based on the news and reports contained therein. The book begins with issues of purity, presenting the opinions of both groups with their evidence and discussions, such as the ruling on removing impurity with anything other than water, and the purity of a garment stained with blood. The summary presents a comparative jurisprudential approach based on tracing the hadiths and narrations contained in each issue.
descriptions.4083: A book on general jurisprudence in which the author collected issues on which scholarly consensus was valid, and separated them from issues on which disagreement occurred, to be a reference that facilitates memorizing and requesting rulings. Consensus has been divided into two parts: necessary consensus regarding what is agreed upon as being obligatory or forbidden, and figurative consensus regarding what is agreed upon that the doer has performed what he owes. The book includes sections on acts of worship, such as purity, prayer, zakat, and Hajj, as well as transactions such as settlements, sales, marriage, and divorce, with a mention of the beliefs related to that.
descriptions.4084: The book “Mazyid al-Nimah to collect the sayings of the imams” is a jurisprudential summary that comprehensively covers the most important issues of worship, in which its author, Hussein bin Muhammad al-Mahli al-Shafi’i, compared the sayings of the imams who hold the four famous schools of thought. The book is organized into jurisprudential sections that begin with the Book of Purity and end with the Book of Hajj and Umrah, thus covering the practical pillars of Islam. This edition was issued with a study section dealing with the life of the author and a study on the methodology of his book, followed by an investigation section containing the jurisprudential text.
descriptions.4085: Manhaj al-Saliken wa Clarification of Jurisprudence in Religion is a book on jurisprudence written by Sheikh Abu Abdullah, Abdul Rahman bin Nasser bin Abdullah bin Nasser bin Hamad Al Saadi (deceased: 1376 AH).
descriptions.4086: This book, “Guiding the Traveler to the Most Ashraf of Paths,” is a text of Maliki jurisprudence that deals with the rulings on purity, prayer, and other main branches of jurisprudence. The book is distinguished by its collection of a large number of jurisprudential rulings in its brief form, with the addition of a footnote that clarifies some ambiguous issues. The book deals with the opinions of Maliki jurists in Iraq, which may sometimes differ from the opinions of Maliki jurists in other countries, with a discussion of the strength and weakness of these opinions.
descriptions.4087: The book “Irshad al-Salik ila Ashraf al-Masalik” is a brief text on jurisprudence according to the doctrine of Imam Malik. It aims to collect jurisprudential rulings in a concise manner while accommodating many issues that are only found in lengthy books. In this book, the author follows the method of the Malikis of Iraq, which makes it include jurisprudential opinions that may contradict what is known among other Malikis in other countries, whether these opinions are strong and supported by evidence or weak and have no support. The book begins with the Book of Purity, covering the obligations and invalidations of ablution, washing, tayammum, and menstruation. Then it moves to the Book of Prayer to include the call to prayer, the pillars of prayer, the congregational prayer, the prostration of forgetfulness, and the prostration of recitation.
descriptions.4088: This is a book on Maliki jurisprudence, compiled by its author and making it an explanation, guidance and justification for what was stated in the issues of the Attibiya, starting with the book of ablution and the related rulings on purity, water and impurities, covering in detail and analysis multiple branches of jurisprudence, according to the Maliki method of reasoning and weighting.
descriptions.4089: This is a book on Maliki jurisprudence, and it is an explanation of Khalil’s summary. Its author aims to extract texts from the books of the doctrine to address the issues of the summary, to be a witness to its transmission and an aid to its understanding. The book begins with the commentator’s sermon, then deals with the Book of Purity with its various sections and chapters, such as the rulings on water, impurities, ablution, washing, and tayammum. Then it moves to the Book of Prayer and what is related to its times, the call to prayer, and the conditions for its validity.
descriptions.4090: A book on Maliki jurisprudence, explaining the rulings on purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, and funerals, beginning with an explanation of the types of purity from impurity, its divisions, and its obligatory, sunnah, and virtuous rulings, with details of the conditions and pillars of ablution.
descriptions.4091: This is a jurisprudential book according to the Maliki school of thought, in which the author summarized Sahnoun’s “Madwana Al-Kubra” and arranged its issues in well-known jurisprudential chapters such as purity, prayer, zakat, Hajj, marriage, and others. The book was distinguished by its shortness and conciseness, with correct pronunciation and accuracy of style. It was based on a narration with a continuous chain of transmission from Sahnoun. The verified copy included an introductory introduction to the work and the book’s scientific value, in addition to a message introducing Malik’s companions.
descriptions.4092: The book “Al-Thamar Al-Dani Sharh Risala Ibn Abi Zaid Al-Qayrawani” is an expanded explanation of the text of the jurisprudential treatise by Imam Ibn Abi Zayd Al-Qayrawani, and it falls within the chapter of Maliki jurisprudence. The author begins by explaining the Basmala and the Hamdala, then deals in detail with issues of faith according to the doctrine of the Salaf, followed by the chapters on acts of worship such as purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj, all the way to the rulings on jihad and sacrifices. The book aims to clarify the words of the text and explain its jurisprudential rulings and evidence.
descriptions.4093: A book on Maliki jurisprudence, presenting issues of worship in an educational manner that combines questions and answers, with summaries of each chapter to facilitate memorization and understanding. The book begins with the chapter on purity and what is related to it, such as ablution, washing, tayammum, and wiping over the socks and splints, detailing its rulings, duties, sunnahs, dislikes, and nullifiers. In editing the issues, the author relied on the most important books of the Maliki school of thought, with an expansion in explaining the problems to be suitable for beginners.
descriptions.4094: The book “Al-Dhakhira” by Al-Qarafi is an innovative work in Maliki jurisprudence, combining the branches of the doctrine and its origins, and is considered one of the most important jurisprudential works of the seventh century AH. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue of knowledge and its etiquette, then deals with topics of the principles of jurisprudence, such as limits, connotations, truth, metaphor, and specification, in addition to chapters on the meanings of letters and the opposition of the requirements of words. Through this work, the author aims to provide fertile theoretical content and vivid diligent evidence, far from the excessive abbreviations that prevailed in his time.
descriptions.4095: The book “Al-Fawakih Al-Dawani on the Risala of Ibn Abi Zaid Al-Qayrawani” is an expanded explanation by the scholar Al-Nafrawi on the text of “Al-Risala” by Imam Ibn Abi Zayd Al-Qayrawani, and it is one of the approved books in Maliki jurisprudence. The explanation begins with an introduction to the doctrine and principles of religion, then deals in detail with the provisions of purity, such as ablution, washing, and tayammum, leading to an explanation of the rulings on prayer, its times and characteristics, and the Sunnahs and dislikes related to it.
descriptions.4096: Jurisprudential Laws is a book compiled by its compiler, Ibn Jazi al-Kalbi, on the laws of legal rulings and issues of jurisprudential branches, according to the doctrine of the Imam of Medina, Abu Abdullah Malik ibn Anas. He added to that a warning about much of the agreement and disagreement between Imam Malik ibn Anas and the rest of the Hanafi, Shafi’i, and Hanbali schools of thought, in order to thus complete the benefit and maximize the benefit.
descriptions.4097: Al-Kafi fi jurisprudence of the people of Medina Al-Maliki is a book of brief Maliki jurisprudence, written by Al-Hafiz Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul-Barr Al-Nimri Al-Qurtubi Abu Omar (368 AH - 463 AH). It is one of the most prominent books of jurisprudence and therefore it is widely circulated among students of knowledge, as it is an important source in the jurisprudence of the people of Medina Al-Maliki. The author collects in Al-Kafi the issues that are foundations and mothers of the branches and proofs on which he builds on the benefits of rulings and the knowledge of what is permissible and what is forbidden. It is comprehensive, polite, adequate, close, concise, and classified by which one can recall when busy and boredom. It suffices for lengthy writings and serves as a place for study when not studying. …
descriptions.4098: The book “Al-Madkhal” by Ibn Al-Hajj is a work on Maliki jurisprudence, focusing on correcting intentions and directing a Muslim’s daily actions to return them to what is obligatory or recommended. The book begins with an exhortation to bring intention into all actions, then deals in detail with the etiquette of acts of worship such as ablution and prayer, and moves on to the etiquette of the scholar and the learned in gatherings of knowledge, warning against heresies, backbiting, and lying. Through it, the author aims to teach people the purposes of their legitimate actions, in response to his sheikh’s desire to direct acts of worship and behavior in accordance with the requirements of Sharia.
descriptions.4099: The book “Al-Mudawwana” by Imam Malik bin Anas is a comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedia in the Maliki school of thought, which deals with the provisions of purity, ablution, and washing in detail, based on the sayings of Imam Malik and the narrations of his students, such as Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb. The book begins with issues of ablution in terms of the number of washings and timing, citing prophetic influences on how to perform ablution. Then it moves on to the rulings on impurities and wiping over splints, the garments of animals, and those who are in a state of ritual impurity, thus including a number of practical jurisprudential issues related to worship.
descriptions.4100: The book “Introductions to Introductions” by Ibn Rushd Al-Jadd is a book on Maliki jurisprudence, which aims to provide fundamental and doctrinal introductions that pave the way for the study of issues of the jurisprudential code. The book begins with chapters on the fundamentals of religion, such as monotheism and the names of God, then moves to the fundamentals of jurisprudence, such as ruling by analogy, before detailing the rulings on purity, prayer, and other chapters of worship, combining an explanation of the legal rulings and linking them to their evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.4101: Bidayat al-Mujtahid is a jurisprudential book that contains comparative jurisprudence. It was written by the Maliki philosopher Ibn Rushd al-Hafid. It is considered one of the best books that included an explanation of the reasons for disagreement between scholars on every issue. Ibn Rushd said in the introduction to the book:
descriptions.4102: In the language of the traveler, according to the closest path, it is a book on Maliki jurisprudence by Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Sawi Al-Maliki (died: 1241 AH). The book is also known as Hashiyat Al-Sawi on Al-Sharh Al-Saghir. The small explanation is Sheikh Ahmad Al-Dardir’s explanation of his book called The Closest Paths to the Doctrine of Imam Malik.
descriptions.4103: Jami' al-Umma is a book on Maliki jurisprudence by Ibn al-Hajib. In writing it, the author intended to collect the aforementioned issues of jurisprudence and its branches, summarized from the sayings of the scholars of the Maliki school of thought and their famous books, and in this he says: When I was busy writing my book, I used to collect the mothers, then collect what those mothers included in a brief statement, then put it in the book until it was completed. Some scholars who have an interest in the book mention that Ibn al-Hajib condensed his book into sixty collections, and that it contained sixty-six thousand issues. …
descriptions.4104: This is a jurisprudential book according to the Maliki school of thought, which includes a footnote by Sheikh Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Dasouki on “Al-Sharh Al-Kabir” by Sheikh Ahmad Al-Dardir, which is an explanation of the summary of Sheikh Khalil bin Ishaq. The footnote begins with a chapter on the provisions of purity and the conditions related to ablution, its obligations, sunnahs, and things that nullify it. Then it moves to the requirements for washing and tayammum, mentioning the provisions for wiping the socks and the etiquette of relieving oneself.
descriptions.4105: This is a footnote by the scholar Ali al-Saidi al-Adawi on the explanation of “Kifayat al-Talib al-Rabbani” to Ibn Abi Zaid al-Qayrawani’s treatise on Maliki jurisprudence. In it, the author collected his observations and comments that appeared to him while studying with the Brotherhood, explaining the words of the text and explaining the provisions of purity and prayer and the conditions and duties related to them according to the Maliki school of thought.
descriptions.4106: This book is a footnote by Ali Al-Saidi Al-Adawi to Al-Kharshi’s explanation of Khalil’s summary of Maliki jurisprudence. The book deals with the chapters of jurisprudence, starting with purity and prayer, detailing its provisions, conditions, duties, and Sunnahs according to the Maliki school of thought. The book includes in its introduction a brief translation of the authors Al-Kharshi and Al-Adawi, and then begins to explain jurisprudential issues in a commentative and analytical manner.
descriptions.4107: This is a simplified book on the jurisprudence of worship according to the Maliki school of thought. It aims to present jurisprudential rulings in a practical, contemporary manner, based on their evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book covers the topics of purity, prayer, zakat, and fasting. Its material was collected from sources of the Maliki school of thought and reviewed to ensure scientific accuracy.
descriptions.4108: Al-Akhdari’s text on worship according to the doctrine of Imam Malik. It is a brief book on Islamic jurisprudence based on the doctrine of Malik ibn Anas, written by Imam Abd al-Rahman al-Akhdari (920-953 AH).
descriptions.4109: This book is a comprehensive text on Maliki jurisprudence, compiled by the author to include the foundations of the faith and the provisions of worship such as purity, prayer, fasting, zakat, and Hajj, in addition to chapters on jihad, sacrifices, and others. The book begins by stating the duties of faith and what must be believed in God’s essence, attributes, and actions. Then it moves on to detailing the practical jurisprudential rulings, reviewing their conditions, pillars, duties, and Sunnahs.
descriptions.4110: This is a brief book on jurisprudence according to the Maliki school of thought, compiled by its author in response to the request of a group of students of knowledge, in order to explain what the fatwa in the school of thought is. The book begins with the section on worship, dealing with the provisions of purity and prayer and the conditions and Sunnahs related to them, recommended and disliked matters, relying in presenting the issues on symbols and references to the main books of the doctrine such as the Mudawwanah and the choices of the great jurists.
descriptions.4111: The book “Manah al-Jalil Sharh Mukhtasar Khalil” is an expanded explanation of the text of “Mukhtasar Khalil” in Maliki jurisprudence. It begins with the introduction to the Mukhtasar and then addresses the chapters of purity and prayer in detail, explaining the words of the text and its jurisprudential issues in an analytical manner based on language and principles.
descriptions.4112: The book “The Talents of the Galilee in Sharh Mukhtasar Khalil” is an expanded explanation of the text of “Mukhtasar Khalil” in Maliki jurisprudence. It begins with an introduction to the virtue of knowledge and a statement of the doctrine’s support, then deals with fundamental and jurisprudential issues such as imitation and fatwa, before proceeding to detail the rulings on purity and acts of worship according to the Maliki doctrine.
descriptions.4113: The book “Tuhfat al-Majalis fi Commentaries on the Index of Indexes” is a work on the science of narration and chain of transmission, compiled by the author as a commentary on the book “The Index of Indexes” by al-Kattani, at the request of his sheikh, Muhammad Yassin al-Fadani. The book includes corrections and clarifications to some of what was mentioned in the original book, such as correcting the names and dates of some of the memorizers and correcting their lineage to the centuries in which they lived. Through these comments, the author aims to serve those working in the science of narration and attribution.
descriptions.4114: The book “A List of the Printed Works of Sheikh al-Islam” by Abd al-Salam al-Husayn is an alphabetical index that includes the titles of the printed works of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. The book aims to facilitate access to these writings and limit them, noting in its introduction the importance of writing for the Sheikh of Islam and the large number of his works that he wrote to meet people’s needs and current issues.
descriptions.4115: A book that guides the student of Islamic knowledge on how to build his personal library, reviewing the beginnings of codification and classification in the Islamic heritage, and Muslims’ care for public and individual libraries. The author provides examples of the basic books that should be acquired in various sciences, with a focus on books of interpretation and the sciences of the Qur’an, as part of a series of detailed lessons.
descriptions.4116: This book is a comprehensive index of the works of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, aiming to limit and classify his writings, letters, and fatwas in the fields of doctrine, jurisprudence, interpretation, and hadith. The book demonstrates the diversity of the sheikh’s forms of writing, including books, letters, and speeches, and reflects the impact of the reformist call in enriching the Arab library. It also includes indexes of the explanations written on his works and some sources of his translation.
descriptions.4117: Abjad al-Ulum is an encyclopedia to introduce the sciences and arts, especially Islamic ones, history, and biographies. It was compiled by Muhammad Siddiq Khan, the Emir of Bhopal, and his classification was based on the book Statistics of Sciences by Al-Farabi, Keys to Science by Al-Khwarizmi, The Key to Happiness by Tata Shukbarizadeh, and Revealing Suspicions by Haji Khalifa.
descriptions.4118: This book is an index of the names of books, written by the author to complement the book “Kashf al-Dunun” in listing the titles of works. It begins with an introduction in which it lists the circumstances of its writing, then lists the names of the books in alphabetical order from A to Z, mentioning their authors and some details about them and their works. The book falls within the classification of indexes of books and guides, and is concerned with collecting the names of works in various sciences and arts.
descriptions.4119: This is a book concerned with studying the curriculum of Ibn Malik’s Alfiyyah and its explanations. It is one of the books of indexes and evidence known for the famous grammatical system and its author. The book begins with a brief translation of Ibn Malik, discussing his upbringing, scientific journeys, and writings, with a focus on the most prominent of them, which is “the compendium,” known as the Alfiyya. He describes it as a scientific educational system that was summarized from “Al-Kafiyya al-Shafi’a” and in which a summary of grammar and most of the topics of morphology were collected.
descriptions.4120: This book is an explanation that Al-Suyuti wrote in his pamphlet called “Al-Naqāya,” which includes a summary of fourteen religious sciences. In this explanation, the author aims to clarify the meanings and subtleties that he has deposited in the fold of the words of purity, so that the benefit may be widespread and the student can dispense with them from other great books. The book begins with an explanation of the fundamentals of religion, then deals with interpretation and hadith, and follows the method of brevity while covering the basic topics in each science.
descriptions.4121: Ismail Pasha bin Muhammad Amin bin Mir Salim al-Babani al-Baghdadi (1839-1920 AD / 1339 AH). He is a writer and historian who lived in the late era of the Ottoman Empire and died a few years before its fall. Khair al-Din al-Zirikli mentioned in his translation of it that he resided in their time in Makari Kuy near Istanbul.
descriptions.4122: The book “Being content with what is printed” is an index and directory of books, concerned with studying the interest of the Franks in the Arabic language and its literature. In its first chapters, the book reviews the branches of the Semitic tongue, the history of the Arabic language and its spread, and the efforts of the Orientalists in compiling its dictionaries and studying its grammar and morphology, in addition to their collection of proverbs and colloquial tales. The second chapter also deals with transmitted Arabic literature, such as pre-Islamic poetry, mu’allaqat, and collections of poets, to serve as a bibliographic reference documenting the Arabic works printed by the Franks.
descriptions.4123: The book “Proof in the Manuscripts of the Imams” by Ali bin Abdul Aziz Al-Shibl is a work in indexes of books and evidence, aiming to indicate and guide the writings of three imams of Islam: Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, the scholar Ibn Al-Qayyim, and Al-Hafiz Ibn Rajab. The author collected the names of their manuscripts from the manuscript indexes and shelves, indicating the name of each book, a description of the number of its pages, the year of its publication, the place of preservation, and its number. He arranged the manuscripts for each imam separately. The book begins with an introduction and preface explaining the approach followed, then moves to the manuscripts of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, including a translation of him from the footer of The History of Islam by al-Dhahabi, and presents an index of his works arranged alphabetically.
descriptions.4124: This is a book that presents and analyzes the writings that dealt with the Prophet’s biography in the English language, and divides it into two main parts: the writings of Muslims, and the writings of non-Muslims from among the English and English speakers. The book reviews the beginnings of writing in this field in the modern era, influenced by the spread of the English language in the Indian subcontinent, and focuses on the motivations for writing among Muslims, such as responding to the suspicions of Orientalists. It also analyzes prominent examples of Orientalist biographical writings, such as the works of Muir, Margoliouth, and Watt.
descriptions.4125: This is a bibliographic book concerned with inventorying and classifying works related to the biography of the Prophet written in the Bengali language, with their presentation and analysis. The author divides the biography books into sections that include primary works, original works, and translated works, in addition to non-Muslim works in this field, and ends with a review of modern trends in writing the biography of the Prophet in the Bengali language.
descriptions.4126: The book “Interest in the Prophet’s Biography in the Russian Language” by Elmir bin Rafael Kuliyev is a work in book indexes and guides, providing a guide to the literature that dealt with the Prophet’s biography in the Russian language. The book begins with an introduction that emphasizes the importance of studying the Prophet’s biography for understanding Islam, then deals with the works of Russian orientalists in this field, and concludes with a list of sources and references.
descriptions.4127: This book addresses the issue of interest in the Sunnah of the Prophet in Hausa countries through teaching it and translating it into the local language. The author focuses on the efforts made in scientific circles and educational institutions to enhance understanding of the Sunnah among members of the Hausawi community. He also analyzes the importance of translating hadith books into their language and its role in spreading the true religion and correcting wrong practices.
descriptions.4128: This is a book that presents and analyzes the interest in the Prophet’s biography in French-language writings, dividing it into Muslim and Orientalist writings, with chapters devoted to academic studies, encyclopedias, and translations. The book falls within the classification of indexes of books and evidence, and begins with an introduction that emphasizes the importance of introducing the Prophet’s biography in languages ​​other than Arabic to achieve the universality of the Islamic message.
descriptions.4129: A book that examines the efforts of scholars of the fifth century AH in classifying the Sunnah of the Prophet and its sciences, and reviews the types of modern works of that era. The author divides his research into sections covering classification in the sciences of hadith, the hadith of the Prophet, hopes and councils, histories and biographies, in addition to the general works of hadith scholars. The work aims to highlight the abundance of literature in this century and introduce its scholars, relying on a descriptive and analytical approach.
descriptions.4130: The book “Al-Hittah fi Dhikr al-Sihah al-Sittah” is a book on the science of hadith, which aims to provide a comprehensive study on the six approved books in the Prophet’s Hadith (the Sihah al-Sittah) and their authors. The book begins with an introductory sermon that addresses the virtue of knowledge and scholars, and the honor of the science of hadith. It then expands into multiple chapters covering the history of hadith collection and classification, the different types of hadith books such as Musnads, dictionaries, and parts, and the branches of hadith science such as narration, knowledge, jarh, modification, and reasons for hadith. The book also deals with biographies of hadith narrations and its narrators, and collects scientific benefits needed by the student of the Prophetic Sunnah, whether he is a beginner or an advanced student.
descriptions.4131: The book “The Guide to Scientific Texts” by Abdul Aziz bin Ibrahim bin Qasim is a work in indexes of books and evidence, aiming to introduce the student of legal knowledge to the basic texts in each art, with an explanation of their explanations, footnotes, and books related to them, arranged according to the gradation in the request. The book begins with an introductory chapter that deals with definitions of knowledge, progression, memorization, and the text, then moves to the first chapter devoted to Sharia sciences, including chapters on interpretation, monotheism, the term Hadith, jurisprudence, its origins, and obligations, with sections allocated to the four schools of jurisprudence.
descriptions.4132: This book is an academic research that deals with the personal letters of Sheikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and focuses on the importance of these letters in understanding his personality and the circumstances surrounding his mission. The research begins by discussing the issue of the authenticity of the texts and the importance of verifying them before drawing conclusions.
