Then, it reviews the historical and religious circumstances in Najd when the call appeared, its style, and the position of those who opposed it from the desert, the scholars of Al-Ahsa, and the nobles. The author aims to shed light on an aspect not detailed in previous studies about the Sheikh’s life and his mission.
descriptions.4133: The Extreme Message of a Famous Statement The compiled books of the Sunnah by Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Jaafar ibn Idris ibn al-Ta’i al-Kattani al-Hasani al-Idrisi al-Fasi. In this book, the compiler collected the famous books of the Sunnah, attributed them to their authors and mentioned the years of their death. He began with the first ones who were classified in al-Awtar, then went on at length to talk about the books of hadith and its arts, such as Sihahs, Sunans, serials, and mursalas. Hadith, parts, and hadith hopes, and the works of hadith sciences of all kinds, and the multiplicity of their arts, and perhaps only a few things differed from this book, which included most of what is related to this noble art, and this book is considered a comprehensive index of the collections of...
descriptions.4134: This is a book in the indexes of books and evidence, studying the relationship between the Prophet’s biography and the books of interpretation. It reviews the Qur’anic verses related to the biography, then deals with how books of interpretation, such as the interpretation of al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Kathir, deal with the biography of the Prophet, and concludes with a comparison between the books of biography and books of interpretation from the documentary, objective, and historical aspects.
descriptions.4135: The Index is a book written by the writer and biographer Al-Nadim, in which he collected all the Arabic books and articles published in his time, books on religions, jurisprudence, and law, and about famous kings, poets, scholars, and thinkers. He stated in his translation of Al-Marzbani that he was working on composing it in the year 377 AH, and he died in the year 385 AH, and he left in it a lot of writings, which the Moroccan vizier completed in the year (418 AH), but the vizier’s completion did not reach us, compared to what Yaqut reported from it. It seems that people quoted from it the accounts of some of Ibn al-Nadim’s contemporaries, such as Ibn Nubatah, who died a year later (400 AH), and Ibn Jinni in (392). In it, he divided the humanities into ten branches, the chapters of which captured the outcome of the Arab culture of his time. …
descriptions.4136: A bibliographic book concerned with listing Turkish works on the Prophet’s hadith and its sciences during the Republican era in Turkey, divided into three time periods starting from 1924 until 2003. It provides a comprehensive index of academic and other works, classified according to their topics, such as the authority of the Sunnah, the sciences of the hadith, its explanation, and its criticism, in addition to research on the Prophet and the Companions.
descriptions.4137: A book that studies the art of prophetic praise in Arabic poetry from its inception until the end of the royal era, tracing the drivers of its prosperity and spread from political, social, and religious reasons. The book deals with the emergence of this art and its limits throughout the various Islamic eras, analyzes the content of the Prophet’s praise and its poetic style, and then concludes by explaining the impact of these praises on society.
descriptions.4138: This is a book that studies the poetry of prophetic praise in the sixth and seventh centuries AH, with a focus on the era that witnessed the Crusades. The author presents an analytical study of the artistic value of this poetry, and presents selected examples of the poems of a number of poets of that era, such as Ibn Bint Al-Azz, Ibn Daqiq Al-Eid, and Ibn Al-Saati. The book aims to show how prophetic praise was a means of expressing pain, hope, and turning to God and His Messenger in times of adversity and adversity that passed through the Islamic world.
descriptions.4139: The book “The Indexed Dictionary or Abstracting the References of Famous Books” is a work on book indexes and evidence, compiled by its author in response to a request from some of the Brotherhood to abstract the chains of transmission of famous books and scattered parts. The author arranged his material into sections, starting with classified and lengthy books, then Musnads, then Hadith Arts, then Dictionaries, Shaykhs, Forties, and other Hadith classifications. The book aims to facilitate access to the chains of transmission of books and narrations, while explaining how the author compiled them through listening, reading, or taking a leave of absence.
descriptions.4140: The book “The Islamic Library” by Imad Ali Jumaa is a bibliographic work that falls within the indexes of books and guides, and aims to present an organized picture of Islamic sources in various branches of heritage. The book begins with an introduction that presents Islam’s interest in science, tolerance, and the era of codification. Then, in its first chapters, it deals with the science of bibliography and Muslims’ interest in it, and classifies Islamic sources according to multiple rules such as topics and names of authors and publications. The book devotes detailed sections to sources related to the Holy Qur’an and its sciences, and the Noble Hadith and its sciences, arranging them according to the date of their creation to trace the development of the authorship movement in each art.
descriptions.4141: This is a brief guide book that aims to introduce graduate students to the most prominent references in translations, countries, and works in the Arab heritage, while mentioning books on science definitions and terminology. In his introduction, the author reviews the motives for writing the book, addressing the issues of questioning heritage and the importance of arming yourself with knowledge of original sources. The book provides a detailed index of references to biographies of scholars in various disciplines such as hadith scholars, jurists, and linguists, in addition to books from countries and bibliographic references.
descriptions.4142: This book is a specialized bibliography concerned with inventorying and documenting the literature and writings published in the English language about the Prophet’s hadith and the Sunnah. The work is based mostly on two previous sources published in 1980 and 1981, with the addition of newer publications after their date. The author collected his material from several libraries and scientific institutions in different countries. The book is included in the indexes of books and guides, and aims to provide a comprehensive reference for researchers in this field.
descriptions.4143: The book “The Sewerage Programme” is a scientific index written by Abu Abdullah Al-Majari, and falls within the classification of indexes of books and guides. The book includes the author’s authorization of his program to Abu al-Qasim al-Bayad and his two sons, in addition to the author’s introduction in which he mentions his sheikhs from whom he took knowledge. The work aims to record the names of the sheikhs and document the knowledge the author received from them, to serve as a guide to narrating and authorizing knowledge.
descriptions.4144: This book is a scientific index written by its author, Al-Wadi Ashi, and it is classified among the indexes of books and evidence. He aims to record the names of the sheikhs he met in Tunisia and during his travels, mentioning the narrations and authorizations he took from them, whether from those he met or from those who authorized him from the East and West. The author arranged his material into two parts, the first of which was devoted to the names of the sheikhs, their lineages, and deaths, and the second to the knowledge and narrations taken from them.
descriptions.4145: The book “Verifying and Publishing Texts” by Abdel Salam Haroun is a work in the field of book indexes and evidence. It deals with research and study the journey of Arab culture since its inception, and how it reached us through the ages. The book explains the stages of development of the written text, the origins of manuscripts, and the methods of verifying and publishing them, with a focus on the rules for examining copies and confirming texts. Through it, the author aims to emphasize the importance of Arab and Islamic heritage and the necessity of caring for and disseminating it.
descriptions.4146: This is a book that studies the development of writing the Prophet’s biography throughout the ages, and is classified among the indexes of books and evidence. In its various chapters, the book deals with the development of the concept of biography linguistically and terminologically, and reviews the independent, brief, and integrated works in history and class books, in addition to the independent classification of aspects of biography such as birth, characteristics, meanings, and characteristics. The work aims to provide a systematic study of the scope of the Prophet’s biography and its formation through various historical sources.
descriptions.4147: This book is “proven” from the classification of indexes and evidence, compiled by Abu Jaafar Al-Balawi, and it contains the names of his sheikhs from whom he received knowledge, mentioning their chains of transmission and narrations. The author begins by mentioning his first sheikh in Granada, the scholar Al-Qalasadi. Then he addresses the Al-Qalasadi sheikhs themselves, lists a number of scholarly approvals and handshakes, and includes examples of the narrations of major hadith scholars such as Al-Muwatta and the Sahihs of Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
descriptions.4148: The book “The Efforts of Russian Orientalism in the Field of Sunnah and Biography” is a bibliographic study that traces the scientific effects of Russian Orientalism in the field of the Prophet’s Sunnah and biography, and monitors the books, articles, and published research produced in this field. The book is divided into two chapters, the first deals with the emergence and roots of Russian Orientalism, and reviews printed sources related to the Sunnah and biography, while the second is devoted to hadith manuscripts preserved in Russian treasures, mentioning the most important places of preservation and examples of them.
descriptions.4149: This is a bibliographic book concerned with monitoring and classifying what was written in the biography of the Prophet during the eighth and ninth centuries AH. The author follows a descriptive approach to review the stages of development of biography writing, then divides the works according to their topics into books on general biography, characteristics and characteristics, birth and death, and finally systems and praises. The research aims to provide an accurate perception of the scientific movement in that period, and open the way for researchers to benefit from that heritage.
descriptions.4150: This book is an investigation into the concept and definition of educational poetry. It deals with its origins and development among ancient nations such as the Greeks, Indians, and Arabs, reviewing the fields in which this poetic form was employed, such as morals, beliefs, history, and sciences, with an explanation of its artistic value.
descriptions.4151: This is a book in the indexes of books and evidence. It studies and criticizes Spanish writings on the Prophet’s biography, and reviews the interests of Spanish researchers in it throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, with a focus on the practical applications of the biography in the West. The author aims to correct the misconceptions that Spaniards have about Islam and Muslims by presenting an objective study of the Prophet’s biography.
descriptions.4152: This is a bibliographic guide prepared by the author’s son, which includes a comprehensive list of the works of the scholar Muhammad al-Mukhtar al-Susi and his manuscripts, both published and unpublished, with a brief introduction to each work. The book is located in one volume, and is classified among the indexes of books and guides. It aims to provide a general idea of ​​the scientific and literary heritage left by the author, covering multiple aspects of his works, such as encyclopedias, poetry collections, letters, and licenses.
descriptions.4153: This book is a critical bibliographic guide that aims to provide a careful and comprehensive reading of a large number of books related to women and the family, within the “The World of Women and the Family” series. The first part includes indexes of titles beginning with the letters alif and b, dealing with various topics such as rulings on women, marriage, hijab, raising a child, and breastfeeding, with a focus on studying these books from a jurisprudential and educational perspective.
descriptions.4154: A book that aims to monitor and document the efforts of scholars of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in serving the Prophet’s Sunnah and biography, with a focus on their role in adhering to it and calling for it. The book deals with the biographies of the most prominent of these scholars, and reviews the means of their various efforts, such as education, writing, investigation, speeches, and lectures, leading to an evaluation of these efforts and their impact.
descriptions.4155: A book that examines the efforts of the scholars of Mecca during the fourteenth century AH in serving the Prophet’s Sunnah and biography, through teaching and writing. The book reviews scientific life in Mecca during that period, and the role of the circles of the Grand Mosque and educational institutions in spreading these sciences. It also highlights the impact of these efforts on other Islamic countries to which scholars have moved or to which students of knowledge have returned.
descriptions.4156: A book that presents a statistical approach to studying dictionaries of Islamic translations in the Middle Ages, with its application to the biographies of hadith narrators in Nishapur, based on the books of Al-Hakim Al-Naysaburi and Abd al-Ghafir Al-Farsi. The researcher uses quantitative methods to extract results about the average age of scholars, the movement of transport and trade, and the impact of political events on economic activity in the region, using graphs and comparing the results with general historical information.
descriptions.4157: The book “Index of Ibn Khair al-Ishbili” is a comprehensive index of the narrations of the sheikhs and their compositions, compiled by the author Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Khair bin Omar bin Khalifa, and arranged them into sections that include the various arts of science. The book begins by mentioning the Muwatta’at and the Musnad compilations, then it deals with the books of Hadith, Sunans, and Musnads, and extends to include books of jurisprudence according to Malik’s doctrine, books of asceticism and subtleties, literature and languages, and other classifications. The author opened his book with an introduction in which he mentioned his chain of transmission in a hadith about knowledge, stressing the importance of knowledge that is beneficial to the heart.
descriptions.4158: The book “Index of Ibn Atiyya” is a work in the field of indexes of books and evidence. It includes a list of the names of the sheikhs of the author Ibn Atiyya whom he met and narrated from, mentioning the knowledge and narrations that he learned from them. The book begins by presenting the author's lineage and his scientific career, then lists the names of the sheikhs from whom he learned in Andalusia and the Levant, such as Abu Othman Saeed bin Khalaf Al-Kalabi and Abu Al-Rabi' Suleiman bin Al-Rabi' Al-Qaisi, with reference to the books he examined and read to them, such as Al-Muwatta' and Al-Mudawwanah.
descriptions.4159: This is a book on indexes and chains of transmission, compiled by the author Al-Lubli in response to the desire of a group of students of knowledge, to be a collection in which he mentions his sheikhs from whom he took it in the Eastern and Western countries, and explains the ways in which he acquired the compilations from them through reading, listening, handling, and approval. The book begins by mentioning the translation of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ash'ari and his works, then returns to the translation of some of his sheikhs, such as Khosrowshahi, with a description of their conditions and an explanation of their connected chains of transmission in the science of theology and the principles of jurisprudence.
descriptions.4160: This book is an index by Ali bin Khalifa Al-Maskani, and it falls within the classification of indexes of books and evidence. The author begins his book by praising and praising God, and blessings upon the Prophet. Then he states that the reason for writing this work is the request of some students of knowledge from him to connect them with his fathers in the religion who inherited knowledge and passed it on, in the hope of obtaining their favor and blessing. The book includes an apologetic conclusion, and it seems to focus on proving the chain of transmission and scientific communication between the author and the scholars who preceded him.
descriptions.4161: The book “Qataf al-Thamar fi Raising the Attestations of Works in Arts and Athar” by the author Al-Fulani is a work in the indexes of books and evidence, aiming to raise the chains of transmission of hadith works and explain the methods of narrating them. The book begins by mentioning a series of the most prominent books of the Prophet’s hadith, such as Al-Muwatta’, the two Sahihs, Al-Sunan, and Al-Musnad, then deals with their explanations and abbreviations, with a focus on attributing these works to their authors. It appears from the excerpt that the author presents his work as a means of scientific communication with the heritage of the hadith scholars, opening his book with praise and praise for God and His Messenger, and explaining his approach to tracking the chains of transmission.
descriptions.4162: This book is a study in the science of “strange Qur’an”, which is one of the branches of linguistic science that arose around the Holy Qur’an, as it specializes in explaining strange Qur’anic words that need clarification. The author reviews the beginnings of this science, addressing the oldest person to whom a book in this field is attributed, namely Abdullah bin Abbas, with a discussion of the narrations related to that. The book aims to provide an index of books, literature, and studies that have dealt with this topic, making it a reference in its section.
descriptions.4163: Revealing suspicions about the names of books and arts is a huge glossary of Arabic, Persian, and Turkish books, compiled by Haji Khalifa, a scholar of the eleventh century AH (seventeenth century AD). The book included the names of thousands of books in addition to the names of their authors. Therefore, it is considered one of the main references for those searching for the works of authors in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4164: The book “The Al-Ajlan Snapshot of What Man Needs to Know” by Siddiq Hassan Khan is a book in the indexes of books and evidence, dealing with the subject of history from its broadest aspects. The author begins with a sermon defining history and its importance to humans, then moves on to narrate the histories of nations and creation, starting with creation and the flood, passing through the history of ancient nations such as the Persians, India, and Britain, all the way to Hijri history. The book also includes chapters on solar and lunar days and weeks, and mentions countries and nations and the differences in their generations and lineages, with reference to epics and Jafar, based on Qur’anic and archaeological texts.
descriptions.4165: A book that examines the emergence and development of libraries throughout Islamic and global history, with an introduction to the most famous ancient and modern libraries in the Arab and Islamic world. It also provides methodological guidance on scientific research methods, sources and references, and ways to organize catalogs and benefit from libraries, with a focus on Islamic and Arabic sciences.
descriptions.4166: The book “Sources for Receiving the Prophet’s Biography” by Muhammad Anwar al-Bakri is a work in indexes of books and evidence, examining the basic sources on which the study of the Prophet’s biography depends. The book reviews the most important of these sources, such as the Holy Qur’an, books of Hadith, Shama’il, proofs, characteristics, and mysteries. It also deals with the most famous types of biography during the first three centuries, with a focus on the classes of the Companions, the Successors, and those after them.
descriptions.4167: This is an index book concerned with collecting the names of the most important printed biographical books, ancient and modern, and arranging them according to the letters of the dictionary for easy access. Through it, the author aims to facilitate knowledge of these works, distinguish between what has been verified and what has not been verified, while pointing out their close connection to the science of history. The book begins with an introduction that emphasizes the importance of biographical books and their scientific, historical, and preaching value.
descriptions.4168: The book “Dictionary of Books” by Ibn al-Mubarrad is a comprehensive index of the works of a number of notables of the Hanbali school of thought. It begins with the works of Ibn al-Jawzi, Ibn Qudamah, and Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and then mentions issues narrated on the authority of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, narrated by his students such as al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, and others, with brief biographies of the narrators and a statement of their deaths.
descriptions.4169: An index book concerned with inventorying and classifying fundamentalist works that have been classified according to the Shafi’i school of thought. This includes Hanafi fundamentalist texts explained by Shafi’i scholars. The work aims to facilitate access to these works and demonstrate their diversity, within the framework of serving the Islamic scientific heritage in the field of jurisprudence.
descriptions.4170: This book is a dictionary specialized in indexing fundamentalist works according to the Malikis, and it falls into two main sections: The first is devoted to Maliki fundamentalist works, and the second to Hanafi fundamentalist texts explained by Maliki scholars. The book aims to limit and document these works on the science of jurisprudence, which is considered one of the machine sciences necessary for understanding Sharia law, in the context of talking about God’s preservation of His religion and sciences throughout the ages.
descriptions.4171: Dictionary of Arabic and Arabized Publications, a dictionary compiled by Youssef Elian Sarkis. It includes the names of books printed in Eastern and Western countries, mentioning the names of their authors and a glimpse of their translation, from the day of the appearance of printing until the end of the year 1339 AH - 1919 AD.
descriptions.4172: This is a book that combines the principles of scientific research and the methods of heritage investigation, providing an integrated vision for the researcher on how to deal with Islamic and heritage sources. In its three chapters, the book introduces the Islamic library, its history, and its most famous libraries, ancient and modern. It then reviews the most important sources and references in various Islamic sciences, such as interpretation, hadith, jurisprudence, and language, and concludes with the methodology for verifying and publishing manuscripts.
descriptions.4173: This book addresses the writing methods of Arab and Muslim scholars in the field of literature, tracing the emergence of the scientific and historical movement and blogging since the dawn of the Arab intellectual movement. The author reviews the development of writing and composition as a tool for authorship, then moves on to study the pioneers of non-specialized literary composition in the second century AH, all the way to specialized, systematic literary composition. The book aims to present an intermediate approach that describes the process of literary composition and its early stages, away from complexity.
descriptions.4174: This book was written by Muhammad Montaser Al-Kattani, and is classified among the indexes of books and guides. It deals with the subject of encyclopedias of Islamic jurisprudence and jurisprudential dictionaries, highlighting the efforts to codify jurisprudence across the various schools of thought from the era of the Companions until the first five centuries. The author mentions that the Andalusians were pioneers in this field, and specifically mentions Imam Ibn Hazm Al-Andalusi and his book “Al-Isal,” which he considers to be the first comprehensive jurisprudential encyclopedia, with a description of its content and importance.
descriptions.4175: A book that examines the history of the emergence and development of the science of Arabic grammar, starting with the reasons for its development, time and place, passing through its four stages: development and formation, emergence and growth, maturity and perfection, all the way to mentioning the famous Basra and Kufic grammarians and their classes. The book includes indexes of the most important references relied upon by the author, arranged chronologically according to the deaths of their authors, with excerpts from grammatical debates between the Basra and Kufic schools.
descriptions.4176: The book “Anecdotes of Manuscripts” by Abdul Salam Haroun is a work in the field of book indexes and evidence, which includes a group of verified heritage texts. The book begins with “The Egyptian Message” by Abu al-Salt Umayyah ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Andalusi, in which the author describes his trip to Egypt and the events he encountered there, discussing his biography and his relationship with al-Wazir al-Afdal. The book also includes other texts, such as “The Book of Synonyms from Quraysh” and “The Father’s Masterpiece regarding those whose lineage is related to someone other than his father,” in addition to “The Book of the Sermon of Wasil Ibn Ata,” which presents aspects of Wasil Ibn Ata’s life and the characteristics of his sermon.
descriptions.4177: The book “The Gift of Those Who Know the Names of Authors and Effects of Compilers” by Al-Babani is a dictionary of biographies and indexes of authors and compilers throughout the Islamic era, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. The book begins with Chapter Alif, and it translates many famous figures, such as Abu Al-Hasan Adam bin Abi Iyas Al-Asqalani and Sayyid Khawaja Adam Al-Hindi Al-Banuri, mentioning their names, deaths, and works. This work falls within the classification of indexes of books and guides, to be a reference for introducing authors and their scientific works.
descriptions.4178: This book deals with the efforts of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in caring for the Holy Qur’an, and reviews the manifestations of this care since the era of King Abdul Aziz, through the early stages of printing the Holy Qur’an, all the way to the establishment of the King Fahd Complex for the Printing of the Holy Qur’an, its goals, and its work method. It also highlights the recording of recitations of the Holy Qur’an and the translation and dissemination of its meanings, relying on historical documents and practical observations that confirm the status of the Qur’an as a way of life in the Kingdom.
descriptions.4179: This book examines the issue of electronic terrorism from an Islamic perspective, explaining its meaning and danger, then reviewing its various methods, such as e-mail, creating and destroying websites. It also addresses ways to combat it by rationalizing access to the Internet and protection systems, and presents efforts to confront it at the local and international levels, based on the principle that Islamic law includes everything that benefits humanity.
descriptions.4180: This book deals with the topic of human development from an Islamic perspective, with a focus on the stage of higher education students. The author explains the concept of growth in language and terminology, and reviews its importance, stages, and factors affecting it, in addition to the various aspects of growth among students at this stage. The book aims to provide appropriate Islamic guidance that helps control aspects of growth and employ them in a manner consistent with human nature and formation, based on education policy and the objectives of academic courses in this field.
descriptions.4181: This book examines the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's efforts to serve Islam and Muslims, with a focus on its actions in the West. The author reviews multiple forms of this service, such as establishing mosques and Islamic centers, establishing institutes for the study of Islamic and Arab sciences, providing scholarships and cultural aid, in addition to popular and private efforts. The book also explains the general foundations on which these services are based, within the framework of cultural communication and acquaintance between peoples.
descriptions.4182: This book deals with the subject of hisbah in Islam, and reviews its historical applications in the Saudi state from its early inception until the modern era in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The author begins by defining the hisba and explaining its legitimacy and legal rule, then provides an overview of the religious and social situation in the Arabian Peninsula before the establishment of the first Saudi state, with a focus on the prevalence of evil and corruption. The book devotes successive chapters to studying the role of the Hisbah in each stage of the Saudi state, explaining its approach to enjoining good and forbidding evil.
descriptions.4183: This book documents the efforts of the General Administration of Curricula in the Saudi Ministry of Education in caring for and preserving the Book of God Almighty, by reviewing study plans and courses for reciting, memorizing and interpreting the Holy Qur’an in the stages of general education. It also addresses the curricula of schools for memorizing the Holy Qur’an in the primary, middle, and secondary stages, in addition to the subject of Tajweed, teaching methods, and evaluation methods in this field.
descriptions.4184: This book documents the efforts of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Fahd bin Abdulaziz, in supporting Muslim minorities around the world, reviewing his biography and the path of giving and giving in the service of Islam and Muslims. The book discusses the concept of Muslim minorities and their geographical distribution in Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas, and then analyzes the problems and challenges they face. It also details areas of Saudi support for these minorities, including material and relief aspects, building mosques and Islamic centers, spreading science and education, and serving the Holy Qur’an and the Two Holy Mosques.
descriptions.4185: This book is a research presented to the University’s Mission Conference, which deals with the Saudi University’s mission towards the Arabic language and Islamic culture. The author begins by explaining the virtue of the Holy Qur’an in preserving the entity of the Arabs and their language, and examines the impact of the language on the destinies of nations, and the characteristics of Arabic that made it the language of Islam. It also addresses the challenges that Arabic faces from its enemies, the role of universities in serving the Arabic statement, and ways to correct the path of education and literature to serve this language.
descriptions.4186: A book that deals with the issue of security and stability as a great blessing that must be preserved, and reviews a number of legal, national and social requirements necessary for that. The book is organized into fifteen demands that cover multiple aspects, such as adherence to Sharia law, listening and obedience to the ruler, moderation, advice, and the role of the citizen, family, and scholars in enhancing security, in addition to giving thanks for blessings and fighting intellectual invasion. The book begins with an introduction that highlights the importance of security, citing historical experiences of its loss in the Arabian Peninsula before its unification.
descriptions.4187: This book deals with the study of King Abdulaziz Al Saud’s approach to governance and administration, reviewing the origins of this approach derived from the monotheism of God Almighty, the establishment of Islamic law, and the achievement of unity. The book also analyzes the originality of King Abdulaziz’s political thought and its sources, such as Shura and the public interest, while discussing the problems that obstruct the application of the approach and the importance of continuing with it. The book includes important documents in its appendices, such as the Basic Law of Governance and statements from historical conferences.
descriptions.4188: A book that collects hadiths and hadiths related to money in Islam, explaining the rulings on taking it from its rightful place, the virtue of permissible money, and ways to reform and manage it, with guidance on gentle living, professionalism, trade, being intentional about food and clothing, inheritances, and explaining the reality of poverty and wealth.
descriptions.4189: Enjoining good and forbidding evil. A book compiled by Imam Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, in which he collected prophetic hadiths, the works of the predecessors, and their poems, which speak about enjoining good and forbidding evil. It is a valuable book and a valuable reference among the books of Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4190: The book “Al-Ahwal” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book of revelations and exhortations, dealing with the horrors and evils of the Day of Resurrection. The book includes sequential chapters that begin with a mention of the approaching Day of Resurrection, then the images, the changing of the earth, the resurrection and resurrection, the reckoning and presentation, the situation, and the resurrection. The author relies on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and hadiths with their chains of transmission to describe these scenes and warn against them.
descriptions.4191: Saints. A book written by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya. Its talk revolves around the virtue of saints, what they have in this world and the hereafter, and what are their basic characteristics, and that they are hidden, pious, and characterized by all beautiful things. Then he mentioned some of the stories of the righteous and righteous, and the stories of ascetics, and the news and dignity he has, and what happened to some of the saints from that.
descriptions.4192: Sincerity and intention. A book compiled by Imam Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, which includes a number of Prophetic hadiths and traces of the predecessors that speak about intention and sincerity. Although it is small in size, it is valuable and contains many benefits. It is a reference for Islamic heritage books.
descriptions.4193: The book “The Brotherhood” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and prophetic hadiths collected by the author on the subject of brotherhood and love in God. The book deals with the virtue of those who love one another for the sake of God, the encouragement to seek brotherhood, and the etiquette of companionship and affection, such as visiting, shaking hands, hugging, giving, and feeding. The book aims to explain the status of brothers in religion and the importance of harmony among Muslims.
descriptions.4194: The book “Supervision in the Houses of Nobles” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths, antiquities, historical narratives, and news, collected by the author under a title that refers to the virtues of the nobles and their positions. The book includes various narrations about the Companions and followers, including stories, sermons, and poems, with a focus on the biographies of some prominent figures such as Omar bin Al-Khattab, Othman bin Affan, and Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with them).
descriptions.4195: The book “Consideration and the Aftermath of Pleasure and Sorrows” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a preaching and reminder book that collects hadiths and hadiths related to the fluctuations of the conditions of the world, and a statement that every joy is followed by relief, that happiness does not last, and that calamities and temptations are inherent in life. The book aims to remind the reader of the reality of the mortal world, and to urge him to be patient and considerate, by narrating stories and news about kings, caliphs, and others, to show that the outcome belongs to God alone.
descriptions.4196: The book “Humility and Idleness” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on Islamic virtues and etiquette. It collects prophetic hadiths and traditions from the predecessors regarding the virtue of idleness and the necessity of humility, and warnings against fame, arrogance, and arrogance. The book is organized into multiple chapters that address these meanings, beginning with the chapter on idleness, then the chapter on fame, then the chapter on modesty in dress and good manners, concluding with the chapters on arrogance and arrogance.
descriptions.4197: The book “Hunger” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of prophetic hadiths and narrated narrations from the Companions, followers, and righteous people. It deals with the topic of the virtue of hunger and frugality in food, and the warning against filling the stomach, citing the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ and the experiences of the predecessors in asceticism and austerity.
descriptions.4198: The book “The Dream” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a work on Islamic ethics and etiquette. It collects prophetic hadiths, sayings of the predecessors, wisdom, and poetry that urge the virtue of forbearance and patience, and explain the honor of the patient in the sight of God and his reward in the afterlife. The book deals with various topics, such as patience in the face of calamity, the virtue of remaining silent over fools, and the commandments of Luqman and the sages regarding being forbearing, while providing evidence that dreaming is one’s adornment and a reason for elevation and sovereignty.
descriptions.4199: A book that collects hadiths and hadiths related to the virtue of contentment with God’s will and destiny, and explains the condition of the believer who submits to God’s command and is patient in His trials, mentioning the status of those who are satisfied in this world and the hereafter, and explaining that contentment is one of the most beloved deeds to God and the highest degree of faith.
descriptions.4200: A book that collects hadiths and narrations about crying out of fear of God, His reward, His grace, its causes, and its causes, such as prayer, reading the Qur’an, and purification, with mentioning the news of the prophets, angels, and righteous people who cried.
descriptions.4201: The book “Asceticism” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a work of purification and subtleties, collecting prophetic hadiths and traditions from the predecessors denouncing the world and urging asceticism in it. The book includes connected narrations that begin with an explanation of the humiliation of the world before God, describing it as a prison for the believer and a paradise for the infidel, and enumerating the disadvantages of its love and its fleeting pleasures. Through these texts, the author aims to remind the reader of the shortness of hope and preparation for the afterlife, relying on the hadiths of the Prophet and the sayings of the companions and followers.
descriptions.4202: The book “Al-Shukur” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of prophetic hadiths and narrations from the predecessors, which the author collects under the topic of gratitude for divine blessings. The book deals with the virtue and importance of gratitude, and explains that gratitude is a limitation of blessings and a reason for increasing them, while warning against ungratefulness in blessings and not appreciating them. The book includes various narrations that encourage goodness in the presence of blessings, link gratitude and abandonment of sin, and mention that God loves to see the effect of His grace on His servant.
descriptions.4203: The book “Patience and the Reward for It” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on softening and admonition, collecting prophetic hadiths and traces of companions and followers related to the virtue of patience and its reward. The book explains the types of patience, such as patience in obedience to God, in disobeying Him, and in calamities, and it cites sayings that patience is the best gift given to a servant, and that it is one of the treasures of goodness that can only be given to a servant who is generous to God.
descriptions.4204: This is a book on Islamic etiquette, in which its author collected sections related to guarding the tongue and the virtue of silence, and condemning loose speech, backbiting, gossiping, hypocrisy, quarrels, and lying, while explaining what a Muslim should have of honesty, fulfillment of promises, and keeping secrets, all of which is supported by hadiths and narrations.
descriptions.4205: This is a book by Imam Al-Hafiz Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, in which it collects hadiths, narrations, and wisdom that urge isolation, isolation, and avoiding mixing with people, while mentioning the sayings of scholars who support and reject it. The book reviews the benefits of isolation, such as devoting time to worship and being safe from the sins that result from contact. It includes the commandments and wishes of a number of companions and followers in this section.
descriptions.4206: The book “The Mind and Its Virtue” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on the virtue of the mind and its place in Islam. It collects hadiths and hadiths that deal with the qualities and reward of the mind, and the relationship of the mind with faith, work, and reward in the afterlife. The book is organized into multiple sections that highlight that reason is one of God’s greatest blessings after faith, and that people excel in it, and that the rational person is the one whose dream overcomes his ignorance and understands the command of his Lord.
descriptions.4207: The book “Punishments” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and monuments that deal with the subject of divine punishments, their causes and types, reviewing stories from the Holy Qur’an about previous nations such as the people of Noah, Ad, Thamud, and Lot, in addition to news of the Children of Israel and others. The book aims to explain the consequences of disobedience and injustice, and to remind that God does not hasten the punishment, but rather gives time until the excuse is achieved.
descriptions.4208: A book that collects hadiths and hadiths related to longevity and good deeds, gray hair in Islam, and what has been reported of the virtue of a young man in obeying God, with some mention of what is related to pigmentation and the conditions of old age.
descriptions.4209: This book, “The Children” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, deals with the topic of spending on children and their rights. It contains hadiths and fatwas related to caring for boys and girls and how to raise and educate them, in addition to talking about spending on wives and the importance of justice between children. The book also focuses on being kind to sons and daughters and raising them to pray and memorize the Qur’an, mentioning the virtues of being kind to one’s children and God’s reward for that.
descriptions.4210: Relief after Distress is a book written by Judge Al-Tanukhi, in which he included a lot of news and stories and divided it into 14 chapters. Al-Tanukhi’s book is not the only book that bears this name, as its author indicated in the introduction, where he mentioned that the first person to name a book with this title was Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madaini, then Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, then Al-Qadi Abu Hussein. He said: “I found that Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and the judge Abu Al-Hussein did not mention that Al-Madaini had a book with this meaning. If they did not know this, then it is funny, and if they deliberately left out mentioning it out of misuse of their books and covering up the man’s book, then it is funnier...”
descriptions.4211: A book that collects hadiths and hadiths related to graves and the conditions of the dead, and the sermons and lessons received when visiting them. It includes chapters on funeral sermons and consideration of them, on resurrection, a comprehensive mention of graves, and what is read from the book on graves, which falls within the books of revelations and preaching in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4212: The book “Contentment and Chastity” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on gentleness and asceticism. It collects prophetic hadiths and narrations from the Companions and predecessors urging people to abandon the affairs of people and do without them, and explaining the virtue of chastity and contentment with one’s livelihood, while mentioning the rulings and sermons received regarding trust in God and contentment with the division.
descriptions.4213: The book “Al-Mutaminin” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and narrations that narrate the hopes and wishes of the Companions and others, based on Sharia texts. The book deals with scenes of wishing to die, return to this world, or transform into other forms, as an expression of fear of the afterlife or the desire to escape its horrors. It falls within the books of Al-Raqif and Asceticism, as it reflects deep psychological and religious states towards death and judgment.
descriptions.4214: The Dying Ones is a book written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Abi Al-Dunya. In it, he collected the conditions of those who were subjected to death, in which he mentioned the hadiths and narrations from the Companions and Followers that were mentioned in that regard.
descriptions.4215: The book “Sickness and Expiations” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of prophetic hadiths and hadiths that deal with the subject of being afflicted with illness and pain, and an explanation of the consequent expiation of sins and raising of ranks. The book includes hadiths regarding the severity of the affliction of the prophets and the righteous, and the virtue of fever and pain in erasing sins, with mention of some prophetic supplications and incantations related to illness.
descriptions.4216: This is a book compiled by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, in which he collects hadiths and traces related to weather phenomena. He arranged it into sections that include rain, thunder, lightning, and wind. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, and deals with what was reported from the Prophet’s guidance in dealing with these phenomena, such as his appearance of rain and his description of the clouds and the distance between the sky and the earth.
descriptions.4217: The book “Dreams” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and narrations that deal with the conditions of the dead and the barzakh, and the relationship of the living with them. The book focuses on topics such as presenting the deeds of the living to the dead, knowing the dead person who washes him and visits him, and the condition of the soul after its departure, citing news and dreams of the righteous. In this work, the work collects supported narrations that aim to remind the reader of the afterlife and the conditions of the graves, making it one of the books of enlightenment and preaching in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4218: The book “Worry and Sadness” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and hadiths that deal with the topic of worry and sadness in the life of a believer, reviewing their virtues and their impact in expiating sins and raising ranks. The book includes various chapters that examine God’s relationship with the sad heart, and images of the sorrows of the prophets and the righteous, with an emphasis on the fact that sadness is an inherent characteristic of the believer in this world. The author relies on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and the sayings of the righteous predecessors to explain the meanings of sadness and its importance in faith.
descriptions.4219: The book “Fear and Trust in Action” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and hadiths that deal with the topics of fear of God and hope in His mercy, with an emphasis on the importance of good deeds as evidence of the sincerity of faith. The book includes sections such as “Hope and Fear,” “Good Thought Means Good Action,” “Intimidation,” and “Diligence in Work,” where it is shown through the texts that good belief in God is not valid except through good deeds, and that true fear pushes the servant to be diligent and diligent in obedience.
descriptions.4220: The book “Al-Wara” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on Islamic education and behavior, collecting prophetic hadiths and narrations from the Companions and followers on the virtues of piety and piety. The book deals with the topic of piety in various aspects of life, such as sight, hearing, tongue, stomach, private parts, endeavors, buying and selling, and provides news of the pious and their reward, urging them to avoid forbidden things and abstain from sins.
descriptions.4221: The book “Al-Yaqin” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths, prophetic narrations, and sayings of the predecessors, collected by the author under the topic of certainty in God and its importance in religion. The book discusses the virtues of certainty and its relationship to asceticism, piety, and true wealth, warning of the weakness of certainty and its effect on faith. The book includes multiple chapters that present famous sayings from the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and the Companions regarding the meaning of certainty and its fruits, with an emphasis on the fact that certainty is one of the greatest things a servant can be given after recovery.
descriptions.4222: A book that collects prophetic hadiths and narrations from the Companions and Followers, revolving around the virtue of having good faith in God Almighty, and explaining that it is good worship, and that God is up to His servant’s thoughts of Him, with stories and news that encourage this character and show its effect in forgiveness and mercy.
descriptions.4223: The book “Dumming Transgression” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a work on ethics, preaching, and Islamic education. It collects prophetic hadiths and traces from the Companions and Followers, and focuses on warning against creating transgression, injustice, and violating people’s rights, and explaining its bad consequences in this world and the hereafter. The book deals with various topics, such as the punishment of those who break ties with one another and a prostitute, and describes transgression as a disease of nations. It includes sermons and stories about the people of transgression, with prophetic instructions to be humble and avoid reprehensible characteristics.
descriptions.4224: The book “Dumming the World” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on asceticism and gentleness. It collects prophetic hadiths and narrations from the Companions and Followers warning of the world and abstaining from it, and explaining its contempt for God Almighty, citing examples from the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ and the words of the predecessors.
descriptions.4225: A book that collects hadiths and hadiths denouncing the evils of the tongue, such as backbiting, gossiping, hypocrisy, and quarrels. It explains what speech is permissible and what is forbidden, while mentioning the virtue of defying a Muslim’s honor and the expiation for backbiting.
descriptions.4226: This book is part of the book “Silence and Etiquette of the Tongue” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, which the investigator devoted to a separate section entitled “Denunciation of Lying and Its People.” The author collects prophetic hadiths and narrations from the companions and followers that condemn lying and warn against it, show that it leads to immorality and hellfire, and describe the scourge of lying as a sign of hypocrisy. The book falls within the categories of warnings, preaching, and reminders of the afflictions of the tongue.
descriptions.4227: A book that describes Paradise, its bliss, and what God has prepared for His righteous servants, collecting hadiths and traces contained in the description of Paradise, its gates, palaces, its people, their food, drink, clothing, and jewelry, and the beautiful beautiful women in it, servants, singing, strolling, and visiting. The book begins with an invitation to roll up your hair and prepare for Paradise, then it lists the doors successively, describing its trees, its blessedness, its levels, its king, and its market.
descriptions.4228: A book in which the author narrates hadiths and traditions related to the nature of fire and its horrors, beginning with seeking refuge in God from it. The book deals with a description of Hell, its gates and its vastness, its mountains and valleys, and the oppressions, chains, and shackles in it, in addition to the food and drink of the people of Hell, including boils and pus, and the bites they suffer from snakes and scorpions, and the blistering of their faces by fire, concluding with a mention of the colors of torment and the crying of the people of Hell.
descriptions.4229: The book “The Virtues of Ramadan” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book that deals with the virtues of the blessed month of Ramadan and its rulings, as it includes hadiths and narrations related to remembering the month and its virtues, praying during it, and suhoor. The book falls within the classification of Ibn Abi al-Dunya’s books, and its material is presented through continuous chains of narration that begin with an attributional introduction that mentions the narrators of the hadith.
descriptions.4230: The book “Guest Villages” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths, prophetic narrations, and traditions of the predecessors, united by the theme of honoring the guest and hospitality. The book lists the virtues of providing food and receiving guests well, citing stories of the prophets and righteous people in giving and generosity, while explaining the etiquette of hospitality and its legal limits.
descriptions.4231: The book “The Palace of Hope” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a work of revelations and preaching, collecting hadiths and hadiths that urge shortening hope in this world and preparing for the afterlife. The book addresses topics such as taking the initiative to do good deeds, condemning procrastination and postponement, and forbidding extravagance in construction and attachment to the world. The book begins with a prophetic commandment by Abdullah bin Omar calling for living life as a stranger or a passerby, and not exhausting oneself with long hopes.
descriptions.4232: The book “Making Needs” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book urging people to do good and meet people’s needs, and it includes chapters that address the virtue of meeting needs, asking for it from people with good faces, and giving thanks for a good deed. The book falls within the classification of Ibn Abi al-Dunya’s books, and is based on the narration of hadiths and traces in this field.
descriptions.4233: A book that collects hadiths, hadiths, and sermons about repentance and returning to God. It deals with topics such as the danger of sins, both small and large, the insinuations of Satan, the virtue of remorse, and the breadth of God’s mercy, while mentioning stories and commandments of the predecessors in this section.
descriptions.4234: The book “The Condemnation of Intoxicants” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a book on warning against alcohol and every intoxicant, in which the author collects prophetic hadiths and traces from the Companions and Followers clarifying the prohibition of alcohol and that it is the mother of all evils and the key to major sins. The book deals with the definition of intoxicants and their types, and emphasizes that every intoxicant is alcohol and forbidden, while telling stories and expressing the bad consequences of drinking them.
descriptions.4235: This book was written by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, and it collects a number of news and narrations that talk about incidents in which people lived after their death, or showed signs of life after their death. The book falls within the general classification of Ibn Abi Al-Dunya’s works, and deals with topics related to the miracles and wonders in the stories of the dead, based on hadiths and narrations from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.4236: A book that collects hadiths and traditions related to the passage of night and day, and the sermons and lessons they contain for the believer. The author urges the listener to seize the time and prepare to meet God, warning against heedlessness and reminding that the days are quickly moving towards the end. The book includes narrations from the Prophet ﷺ and from the Companions and Followers urging remembrance and repentance during the hours of the day and night.
descriptions.4237: The book “Trust in God” is one of the works of Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, and it collects prophetic hadiths and traces from the righteous predecessors about the virtue and truth of trust in God. The book deals with the meanings of trusting God and relying on Him for livelihood and all matters, citing famous sayings about being content with His judgment and seeking His help. This work falls within the books on gentleness, asceticism, and Islamic education, which are concerned with refining souls and strengthening faith.
descriptions.4238: The book “Politeness of People” by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya is a work of Islamic literature, collecting hadiths and traces related to the art of dealing with people. The book deals with various topics, such as patience with people’s harm, being courteous to them, good relations with good manners, and condemning bad manners. It also devotes sections to a man being kind to his wife and a woman being kind to her husband, avoiding evil and its people, and reconciliation between people.
descriptions.4239: This is a book that narrates the details of the killing of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib (peace be upon him), written by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya. The book includes his virtues, his will, the recipe for his washing, shrouding, and burial, and deals with the story of his killer, Ibn Muljim, and his elegies, and mentions his children. The book begins by mentioning his lineage, the date of his death, and his pledge of allegiance to the caliphate.
descriptions.4240: A book that collects hadiths and hadiths related to the world of the jinn and Satan, the ways of his machinations and whisperings, and what protects the believer from them. It deals with the types of jinn, their formation, and their dwellings, and details the characteristics of Satan and his offspring, and the most beloved plots against him, with an explanation of what protects against Satan, such as the Throne Verse and the remembrance of God.
descriptions.4241: A book that collects prophetic hadiths and traces about the virtues and good deeds of morals. It begins with a chapter on honesty and the condemnation of lying, then deals with multiple topics such as maintaining ties of kinship, honesty, censuring one’s friend and neighbor, and rewarding good deeds and generosity, based on narrations attributed to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4242: The book “Hawatif al-Jinan” by Ibn Abi al-Dunya is a collection of hadiths and narrations narrated with their chains of transmission, united by one topic, which is hearing unseen voices or “telephones.” The author divides his material into sections, and deals with what was reported about telephones related to graves, others related to supplication, and a third related to the jinn, beginning his book with prophetic hadiths about seeing King Gabriel and hearing his voice.
descriptions.4243: Rulings of the People of the Dhimmah is a book of jurisprudence and legal policy, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 1349). The book deals with the rulings of the People of the Dhimmah of the Jews and Christians, with an introduction to the types of infidels. In his research, the author focuses on issues of the relationship of Muslims with the People of the Book in their holidays, marriage, allegiance, inheritance, and intercourse. The book contains 279 chapters, beginning with The tribute and ends with a chapter on cursing the Prophet and his companions. The book is considered one of the major books and books, as it contains 1748 pages. The book is considered one of the largest and best Islamic books specialized in the rulings of the people of Dhimmah. …
descriptions.4244: Notable Signatories on the authority of the Lord of the Worlds is a book written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah in which he combined jurisprudence and its principles, the objectives of Sharia law, the history of legislation and Sharia policy, drawing on the first that was taken and received from the Messenger of God ﷺ, and from those from whom jurisprudence and religion spread. Then he spoke about ijtihad and analogy in a lengthy study, which he brought to the end of the second volume, with lengthy examples. Then he dealt with a detailed study of a large group of fatwas on important issues in matters of judiciary, belief, worship, transactions, marriage, divorce, and usury, and some fatwas about necessities that permit prohibited things and other things. He cited well and was thoughtful in his weighting.
descriptions.4245: Relief to the Anxious in the Ruling on Divorce of Anger is a book or jurisprudential treatise, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 1349). The book is an answer to the question of the ruling on divorce in anger, whether it takes place or not. The author’s work contains citations of the Holy Qur’an, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and many of the sayings of the people of the Salaf. He classified anger into types, and mentioned the differences in ruling according to the type of anger. He also referred in this letter to other issues regarding divorce and other issues. Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi said about it: (It is a valuable book, which greatly benefits the nation in the aforementioned issue... and my father (may Allah have mercy on him) always read it and rejoiced in it).
descriptions.4246: Relief to the Anxious from the Traps of Satan is a book written by Abu Abdullah Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zari al-Dimashqi, known as Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, (691-751 AH). He arranged it into thirteen chapters, in which he presented diseases of the human soul and their treatment, and the machinations of Satan that he plots against man. It contains chapters of great benefit, and scholars have attested to his precedence in serving science and introducing religion to Muslims.
descriptions.4247: The meeting of the Islamic armies on the invasion of the Mu’ta’ilah and the Jahmiyyah is a book by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya. The book spoke about two sects and schools of theology, and in it its author responded to those whom he called the Mu’ta’ilah and the Jahmiyyah from the people of theology, through the interpretation of some of the verses about the attributes, and the sayings of the scholars and interpreters of the Companions, the Successors, and those who came after them. The issue of ascendancy over the throne is one of the most important issues addressed in the book.
descriptions.4248: Proverbs in the Qur’an is a book extracted from the famous signatories of Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, on the proverbs contained in the Holy Qur’an. There are (43) examples in the Holy Qur’an. Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah dealt with the proverbs of the Qur’an and explained them and explained them. The book contains nineteen chapters, all of which contain proverbs.
descriptions.4249: Al-Tibyan fi the Sections of the Qur’an or Al-Tibyan fi the Faiths of the Qur’an is a book written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 AH 1349). The book deals with all the places in which the oath was mentioned explicitly or implicitly in the Holy Qur’an, beginning with the verses and presenting them from the end of the Qur’an to the beginning, discussing and clarifying the interpretation of the verses in the short surahs that begin with the oath until their end, and explaining the relationship of the oath in the surah to the one it is sworn to. The answer to the oath, and the relationship of the oath to the Surah itself and the meanings contained in it. …
descriptions.4250: The sufficient answer for those who asked about the cure or the disease and the cure is a book written by Imam Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyyah (691 AH - 751 AH). In its chapters, it deals with the topic of reforming, correcting, and refining the soul according to the Islamic perspective, as the reader moves between its chapters, passing through advice and rebuke. The book deals with the ills of the soul that leads to evil, showing its faults and mistakes, showing the power of desires over it, and warning against the machinations of Satan and his tricks to cause the soul to commit transgressions and sins, and to rely on worldly life and its adornments. It is an Islamic book that deals with Islamic psychology with rational and textual evidence. …
descriptions.4251: Al-Risalah al-Tabukiyya, is a book by Muhammad bin Abi Bakr Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (d. 751 AH). The book includes important topics that Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah began by explaining the Almighty’s saying: “And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression.” [Al-Ma’idah: 2], and he mentioned the types of cooperation, and that the greatest and most important type of cooperation in righteousness and piety is cooperation on the journey of migration to God and His Messenger with the hand, tongue and heart, and he touched on the subject of happiness and its perfection, as he explained verses (24-30) of Surat Al-Dhariyat.
descriptions.4252: The book “Prayer and the Rulings on One Who Does Not Pray” by Ibn al-Qayyim is a jurisprudential treatise that addresses ten main issues related to the ruling on one who deliberately abandons prayer, and begins by stating that the sin of neglecting prayer is greater than murder and adultery. The book deals with the issue of killing the one who neglects prayer and how to do it, the ruling on the invalidation of deeds by abandoning them, the validity of solo prayer with the ability to pray in congregation, the requirement of the congregation and the mosque, the ruling on those who decided to pray, and the amount of the Prophet’s prayer ﷺ. The book falls within the works of Ibn al-Qayyim, which combine an explanation of the ruling and legal evidence.
descriptions.4253: The book “The Thunderbolts sent in Response to the Jahmiyyah and the Muta’ilah” by Ibn al-Qayyim is a work on the Islamic faith, in which the author responds to the two sects of the Jahmiyyah and the Muta’ilah, which deny the attributes of God Almighty or interpret the texts of revelation. The book begins by explaining the truth of interpretation linguistically and terminologically, and differentiates between correct and false interpretation, then addresses in detail the reasons that lead to corrupt interpretation, and refutes the suspicions of opponents that they have made tyrants rely on, such as saying that verbal texts do not benefit certainty, or prioritizing reason over revelation in the event of conflict.
descriptions.4254: This book is part of the encyclopedia "Zad al-Ma'ad fi Huda Khair al-Ibad", which the author has designated in the classification to explain the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in medicine and treatment. The book combines treatment with natural medicines, cupping, and honey, and spiritual treatment, based on the Prophet’s hadiths in treating diseases such as fever, plague, epilepsy, and headaches. The author aims to show that Islamic law included guidance for the body and soul, and that the Prophet ﷺ was given medical knowledge in addition to his message of faith.
descriptions.4255: Judicial Methods in Sharia Policy is a book on Sharia judiciary, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH - 751 AH / 1292 AD - 1349 AD). The book deals with the origins of Sharia judiciary, and achieving its methods that suit the nations’ policy of justice. The reason for writing it is: to answer questions that came to him called: “Al-Tarabulsiyyat,” and this is similar to his other books that were answers to questions that came to him, such as: “The Disease and the Drug,” “Al-Manar Al-Munif,” “Matala’ Al-Saad bi Kashf Al-Hamd,” and “Discourse on the Issue of Hearing.” …
descriptions.4256: Equestrian Muhammadiyah. A book by the scholar, Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abi Bakr bin Ayyub Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, which he wrote after he was tested by some of the scholars of his time because of what he used to issue fatwas not stipulating that what is permissible in the race and struggle, so he showed approval to the public in order to quell and ward off strife. So he wrote this book and mentioned in it the issue of stipulating the permissible condition in the race, and included the evidence of both groups, then he pointed out those who denied this opinion and the fatwa based on it, and that the reason for that was reliance on imitation, then he mentioned the provisions of mortgage in many issues related to shooting and racing.
descriptions.4257: Benefits. It is a book written by Sheikh Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, who was one of the scholars of the eighth century AH. He was born in Damascus in the year 1292 AD, and died in the year 1350 AD, and studied under Ibn Taymiyyah. The book included various nice benefits and many benefits from various rare scientific issues in which it delved into the meanings of divine truths, and clarification of the wisdom of Sharia law in multiple topics related to the Qur’an, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and Islamic jurisprudence.
descriptions.4258: Al-Manar Al-Munif in the Sahih and the Weak, or Criticism of the Transmitted and the Critique of Distinction between the Rejected and the Accepted, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyyah.
descriptions.4259: The Righteous Barrage of Good Words is a book by Sheikh Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah in which he explains the hadiths about supplications and supplications that were mentioned in the book The Good Words, which was written by his teacher Ibn Taymiyyah. Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyyah presented his book with introductions on the virtue of dhikr and its importance, then he included seventy-five chapters on supplications and recitations: which a Muslim should not abandon, supplications for sleep and waking up from them, the call to prayer, entering graves, rain falling, seeing the crescent moon, grief, one who has lost something, eclipses and solar eclipses, marriage and congratulations, and many others.
descriptions.4260: The book Bada’i’ al-Fawaid by Sheikh Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah. The book is dominated by linguistic investigations and contains precise knowledge in the interpretation of the Book of God to explain the approach of the Qur’anic method in the statement. Within the scope of doctrine, he clarifies and resolves the position in many problems. In jurisprudence, he presents many detailed and lengthy rulings, such as clarifying the hypothesis of Hajj and resolving the matter in multiple fundamental issues.
descriptions.4261: Tuhfat al-Mawdud Bi Ahkam al-Mawlid is a book by Sheikh Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, who died in 751 AH.
descriptions.4262: The book “Jalaa’ al-Afham fi the Virtue of Praying and Peace be upon Muhammad, the Best of Humans” by Ibn al-Qayyim, which is a book that is unique in its meaning, examining the virtue of prayer and peace upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The author explains the hadiths contained in this matter, distinguishes the authentic ones from the good ones and the negative ones, then deals with the secrets and honor of this supplication and the rulings and benefits it contains, in addition to explaining the reasons for praying for him and the amount of it that is obligatory.
descriptions.4263: This book was written by Ibn al-Qayyim, and it is one of the books that deals with issues of praise and its formulas. The book begins with a discussion of the hadith, “Praise be to God, praise be to Him that will repay His blessings and reward more,” where the author explains the ruling on this hadith in terms of authenticity and reliability, and mentions that it is not in the Two Sahihs or in the approved books of hadith. The book also addresses jurisprudential issues related to the formulas of praise, such as the ruling on swearing praise in the mosques of Muhammad, and reviews some of the formulas transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ regarding praise and praise.
descriptions.4264: The Guide of Souls to the Land of Joy is a book written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, in which he describes Paradise in a way that will be enjoyable for its reader and interesting for the one who looks at it. He describes its people, their food and drink, their brides from among the beautiful houris, and their characteristics. He also mentioned the many gates of Paradise, the widening of its gates, the degrees of Paradise, and the descriptions of the people of this nation who preceded it, and he mentioned the types of the people of Paradise that were guaranteed to them to the exclusion of others, along with a description of the soil of Paradise, its light, its palaces, its trees, the drink of its people, their food, and their clothing. And their tents, and their beds, and their servants and their servants, and as he mentioned the women of the people of Paradise, their types, their beauty, and their apparent and hidden beauty, and the greatest chapter of the Book is the mention of the people of Paradise looking at their Lord openly, basing everything he mentions on the Holy Qur’an and the Prophetic hadiths, and he divided…
descriptions.4265: This is a letter from Imam Ibn al-Qayyim to one of his brothers, containing advice and advice on spiritual education and reform. In it, the author focuses on the importance of seizing time and beingware of the company of those who waste time and corrupt the heart, indicating that wasting time and corrupting the heart are the root of every evil that befalls the servant. It also links neglect of the remembrance of God and following one’s desires, and explains that the corruption of people’s conditions arises from these two principles.
descriptions.4266: The Garden of Lovers and the Excursion of the Missing is a book written by Sheikh Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah.
descriptions.4267: Zad al-Ma'ad fi Huda Khair al-Ibad is a book written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah in five volumes. It deals with jurisprudence, its principles, biography, and history. It mentions the biography of the Messenger ﷺ in his conquests and life, and explains his guidance in his livelihood, worship, and treatment of his companions and enemies. He wrote these books while traveling, and he did not have any sources from which to transmit the hadiths, sayings, and opinions he needed related to the topics of the book. However, his book included prophetic hadiths from the Sahihs, Sunans, dictionaries, and biographies, and he confirmed each hadith on the topic that concerned it. Knowing that Ibn al-Qayyim memorized the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, which includes more than thirty thousand hadiths. …
descriptions.4268: Healing the Ailing Person in Issues of Predestination, Predestination, Wisdom, and Reasoning is a book of the Islamic faith, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 1349). The book deals with one of the most important and most dangerous issues of faith and the fundamentals of religion, which is the issue of belief in predestination and destiny. In his book, the author explains the approach of the Sunnis and the community on this issue, supporting his opinion with evidence from the Holy Qur’an, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and the sayings of the righteous predecessors among the Companions and Followers. Then after that, he responded to those who disagreed with them, explaining their statements and the absurdity of their minds. Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah wrote two complete chapters in his book, one to respond to fatalism and the other to respond to fatalism, in addition to responding to it and others in the chapters of his book.
descriptions.4269: The book “Characteristics of Hypocrites” by Ibn al-Qayyim deals with the topic of hypocrisy as a dangerous internal disease, and explains that it is divided into two types: greater hypocrisy, which requires eternity in Hell, and lesser hypocrisy. The book reviews the characteristics of hypocrites and their secrets revealed by the Qur’an, and focuses on the danger of their temptation to Islam and Muslims, citing the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, which devotes thirteen verses to talking about them due to their abundance and the severity of the nation’s affliction with them.
descriptions.4270: The Path of the Two Migrations and the Chapter on the Two Happinesses is a book by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, about faith and belief, and he saw it represented in two paths: the first: migration to God through servitude, trust, repentance, submission, fear, and hope. The second: migration to the Messenger of God - ﷺ -, as he is a good example for Muslims and their ideal.
descriptions.4271: The Kit of the Patient and the Treasure of the Thankful is a book about the virtue of patience and gratitude, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 1349). The book deals with sayings from the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, noble prophetic hadiths attributed to their meanings, Salafi traditions attributed to their authors, jurisprudential issues established with evidence, and behavioral details along the same path. Knowing this is not hidden from anyone who thinks. And bring his mind.
descriptions.4272: This book, written by Ibn al-Qayyim, deals with the rules of the beautiful names and their origins, explaining their meanings and considerations, the difference between telling about them and naming them, the levels of counting them, and the types of atheism in them. The author aims to establish a scientific foundation that regulates the understanding of God’s names and attributes according to the rules of a universal college, based on the approach of the Salaf in the chapter on names and attributes.
descriptions.4273: This book is a long poem composed by Ibn al-Qayyim, known as “Al-Nuniya” or “Al-Kafiyyah Al-Shafi’ah.” He devoted it to talking about the issue of the word of God Almighty and His attributes, and responding to the groups that disagree with that, such as the Jahmiyah, Mu’tazila, and philosophers. The book is organized into multiple chapters that discuss the evidence of the various sects about the Qur’an and the description of speech, with a focus on proving the supremacy of God above His throne and explaining the approach of the Sunnis in the legal texts.
descriptions.4274: This book is a summary of the words of Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, in which he responds to the Jahmiyyah and Mu`talilah sects who denied the attributes of God Almighty or gave them an interpretation that contradicted the apparent meaning of the texts.
