The author explains the reality of interpretation linguistically and terminologically, and details the statement on the verses about the attributes, and commits those who disagree with what they escaped from, stressing that interpretation is worse than obstruction. It also addresses the issue of prioritizing reason over transmission, and invalidates the suspicions of those who claim that they contradict each other, while proving the transcendence and supremacy of God and denying his anthropomorphism.
descriptions.4275: The Paths of the Travelers between the Houses of You we worship and You we seek help, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 1349 AH), and it is an explanation of the book of the Sheikh of Islam Imam Abu Ismail al-Harawi called The Homes of the Walkers to the Lord of the Worlds. Ibn al-Qayyim began his author by speaking on the opening of the book, Surah al-Fatihah, and spoke about slavery. As for the book, it consists of many chapters and stages of slavery. Ibn al-Qayyim says in the introduction to his book:
descriptions.4276: The Key to the House of Happiness and the Publication of the Guardianship of Knowledge and Will is a book on happiness in knowledge, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (691 AH 751 AH - 1292 1349). In his book, the author dealt with will and knowledge and made them a key to everything that is useful in life and a tool that opens the door to happiness, reveals the greatness of the Creator and the wonderfulness of his work, and points to the path of truth and goodness. …
descriptions.4277: Guidance of the Perplexed in Answers to the Jews and Christians, written by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, in which he presents what he called the aspects of distortion in Christianity and Judaism, citing everything he believes in texts from Christian and Jewish books, and in which he responds to their criticism of the Messenger of Islam, defending him, and explaining his argument with the good news of the Torah and the Gospel of the Prophet Muhammad.
descriptions.4278: This book deals with hadiths and hadiths narrated by Al-Qasas on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, and some of them on the authority of God Almighty, and Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah presents them in this work by presenting his jurisprudential opinion on them, where he shows the validity or weakness of those hadiths, and clarifies whether they are from the Israelites or from what is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ. The book focuses on clarifying the spiritual and moral meanings of hadiths, while emphasizing the importance of faith and good deeds in a Muslim’s life.
descriptions.4279: This book is written by Ibn al-Qayyim, and it is an index of the works of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, where he mentions the names of the treatises and works that he saw or learned about, arranged according to Qur’anic surahs in interpretation, then according to jurisprudential and doctrinal topics, and others. The book aims to limit and document Ibn Taymiyyah’s scientific heritage, making it an important reference for researchers of his writings.
descriptions.4280: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah deals with the topic of heart diseases and their healing from an Islamic perspective, based on Quranic verses that mention heart disease, its hypocrisy, and its cruelty. The author explains the concept of heart disease by analogy with body disease, showing how corruption of perception and normal movement leads to deviations in understanding facts and following what is harmful.
descriptions.4281: The necessity of the straight path to differ from the people of hell is a book by Ibn Taymiyyah in which he spoke about the issues of imitating the Jews and Christians and their holidays. It is an explanation of the hadith of the Messenger ﷺ: “Whoever imitates a people is one of them.” One thousand books before the year 715 AH.. in which the author dealt with the phenomenon of Muslims resembling others, and explained the rulings related to that. …
descriptions.4282: A book on enjoining good and forbidding evil by Ibn Taymiyyah, which explains that this ritual is one of the foundations of religion, as God’s message is based on command, prohibition, and permissibility. The book deals with the levels of enjoining good and forbidding evil, the obligatory conditions for enjoining and forbidding, linking sins and calamities, dividing sins and lives, and addressing the condemnation of stinginess and cowardice, patience in the face of calamities, and the types of people in courage and enjoining good. It also details the status of sincerity and correctness, and confirms that submitting one’s face to God and benevolence are the foundations of Sharia law.
descriptions.4283: The book “Integrity” by Ibn Taymiyyah is a book on the fundamentals of religion, jurisprudence, and Sufism. It focuses on the necessity of uprightness, moderation, and following the Qur’an and Sunnah, and discusses issues related to God’s names, attributes, and monotheism. The book deals with analysis and criticism of modern opinions in principles and branches, such as modern speech and modern opinion in jurisprudence, and modern worship such as Sufism, and shows that religion has been perfected and does not need additions. It also presents topics such as drunkenness, its causes and rulings, the love of beauty, jealousy, pleasure and pleasure, and enjoining good and forbidding evil, with an emphasis on the fact that division and misguidance only occurred by abandoning some of the truth and following innovations.
descriptions.4284: The Iraqi Masterpiece is a book written by Ibn Taymiyyah. He wrote it at the request of a friend of his who asked him for an explanation about the ruling on heartfelt actions.
descriptions.4285: This book is written by Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is a message in investigating the issue of proving the divine names and attributes according to the doctrine of the Salaf, while explaining the truth of combining destiny and Sharia. The author begins by preaching the book and then explains the reason for writing it, which is the need to achieve the principles of monotheism and attributes, law and destiny, due to the abundance of confusion in them. The book addresses the unification of divinity and attributes from the point of view of the narrative between denial and affirmation, and the unification of law and destiny from the point of view of demand and will, and discusses the doctrines of opponents such as the Batiniyya, the Mu'tazilites, and Ibn Sina.
descriptions.4286: “The Correct Answer to Whoever Changes the Religion of Christ” is a book by Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is one of the most famous books in responding to Christians, and according to what is stated in the book, it contains evidence and arguments for distorting the Gospel, as he put it. The writer says at the conclusion of his book that the religion of all the prophets is the same throughout the ages, and they are brothers and call for the monotheism of God and give good tidings to the Prophet Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and he says that this good news is found in the Bible. …
descriptions.4287: This is a book about the Hisbah system in Islam. It was written by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and it discusses the concept of Islamic guardianship and the responsibility of the hisba in enjoining good and forbidding evil. The book addresses topics such as fraud and deception in transactions, legal penalties, financial discretion, and a statement of reward and punishment, within the framework of explaining that the purpose of the Islamic mandates is to establish religion for God Almighty.
descriptions.4288: The book “The Good and the Bad” by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah is a treatise that deals with the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: {Whatever good befalls you is from God, and whatever evil befalls you is from your own soul}, and explains the great wisdom contained in this verse. The book falls within the works of Ibn Taymiyyah. It begins with a rhetorical introduction and then moves on to interpreting the verse in the context of the command to wage jihad and condemnation of those who disobey it.
descriptions.4289: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah is a response to some of what was mentioned in the parties of the Shadhiliyya order and what was classified in the etiquette of the road, where the author criticizes what he sees as evils and legal violations in those parties, focusing on the issues of trust, supplication, and infallibility. The book begins by discussing the phrase “And your knowledge is sufficient for me” and explaining what he sees as its contradiction to the Sunnah, then he analyzes and criticizes other concepts such as infallibility from sins and doubts, and the beliefs of some of those affiliated with the Shadhiliyya in Al-Qutb and Al-Ghawth, indicating what he sees as misguidance in understanding worship, intercession, and supplication.
descriptions.4290: Response to logicians. A book by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah that examines what they took as a basis for human thought since the earliest times before Islam and its developments in the era of Islam until the age of the author. It shows the deep impact and great authority of that basis in Islamic ideas and legal sciences, then reveals the corruption and crookedness within it with careful investigation, penetrating insight, and rare audacity. He distinguishes between truth and falsehood, distinguishes between true and corrupt, guides to a straight path, and hurls truth at falsehood, destroys it, and then it is lost. The author of the book confronted a dense army of suspicious suspicions, false suspicions, misleading heresies, and embellished innovations, so he carried out truthful campaigns against him, armed with an unbreakable weapon and adorned with a shield.
descriptions.4291: Responding to those who say that Paradise and Hell will annihilate, a book written by Ibn Taymiyyah.
descriptions.4292: The Complete Message Concerning the Attributes of Perfection That God Must Have. Author: Taqi al-Din Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abd al-Halim ibn Abd al-Salam ibn Abdullah ibn Abi al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Ibn Taymiyyah al-Harrani al-Hanbali al-Dimashqi (died: 728 AH). This treatise is a detailed answer to a question about the attributes of God, Glory be to Him, and it included a summary of the common opinions regarding His attributes, Glory be to Him, and what must be confirmed of them and what must not, as well as what must be denied about Him, Glory be to Him. Because it is an attribute of deficiency, this includes all attributes, whether experiential, actual, existential, psychological, or cognitive.
descriptions.4293: This is a letter by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, which he wrote to one of his students, in which he dealt with the issue of metaphor and truth in the attributes of God Almighty, confirming what he said in it according to the doctrine of the Salaf. The message falls within the topics of the Islamic faith, specifically in the chapter on names and attributes, where the author explains the approach of the Sunnis in proving the divine attributes in reality without interpretation or representation.
descriptions.4294: This book, written by Ibn Taymiyyah, brings together topics on asceticism, piety, and worship according to the Sunni approach. Its chapters address topics such as the straight path in worship, self-purification, the meaning of certainty, beautiful patience, contentment, determination and determination. The author aims to show that adhering to the Sunnah is the path preserved from the evil of the soul and Satan, warning against following desires and heresies that he associates with error and error.
descriptions.4295: The strict one who curses the Messenger, a book by Ibn Taymiyyah, about those who insult the Messenger and the ruling on insulting the Messenger ﷺ, after the incident of Assaf Al-Nasrani in the year 693 AH / 1294 AD.
descriptions.4296: Al-Safadiyya is a book written by Ibn Taymiyyah in which he answered a fatwa he received from one of the questioners. Ibn Abdul Hadi said about it: Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned in his book:
descriptions.4297: Slavery or the Message of Slavery is one of the books of the Hanbali jurist Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. It is a small message that is an answer to questions directed to him, in which he was asked about worship: What is it? What are its branches? Is the total debt included in it or not? What is the truth about slavery? Is it the highest position in this world and the hereafter, or is there any position above it? In it, Ibn Taymiyyah discussed the actions of the heart, and explained the true meaning of servitude, and the danger of the heart’s attachment to the fleeting symptoms of this world. …
descriptions.4298: A book on the Islamic faith, explaining the belief of the Sunnis and the community in the foundations of faith and its six pillars, with a focus on belief in God Almighty and His names and attributes. The author explains the moderate approach in proving the divine attributes as mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah, while denying distortion, disruption, conditioning, and representation, and emphasizes proving the transcendence of God, His equality upon His throne, and His closeness to His creation.
descriptions.4299: The Great Fatwas is a book by Ibn Taymiyyah. The book includes hundreds of fatwas that Ibn Taymiyyah was asked about and answered, and the book is arranged according to jurisprudential topics.
descriptions.4300: The Great Hamwi Fatwa, the Hamwi Creed, or the Hamwi Fatwa, is a book on the Islamic faith written by Ibn Taymiyyah.
descriptions.4301: A book that examines the distinction between God’s friends and Satan’s friends, based on evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. It explains the characteristics of God’s faithful, pious saints, and differentiates between them and those who claim guardianship and are of the kind of soothsayers, sorcerers, or hypocrites. The book deals with the topics of faith and piety, love for God and hatred for Him, and a statement that God’s guardianship is only through faith and good deeds, and that there is no path to God other than Islam.
descriptions.4302: This book is a poem by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, which he composed in response to questions he received about the issue of predestination and predestination, and related to invoking predestination against sin. The book begins with a poetic question from a questioner who is confused about reconciling God’s will for disbelief with His prohibition of it and His punishment for it. Then the Sheikh responds with a long poem in which he explains the principles of the Sunnis on this issue, and responds to the suspicions of fatalism, stressing that God’s will is effective in everything, and that wisdom and mercy are linked to His actions, and that delving into the justification for God’s actions is the root of the misguidance of the sects.
descriptions.4303: Al-Qawa'id al-Nuraniyyah is a book on the rules of jurisprudence, written by Ibn Taymiyyah, in which he mentioned some jurisprudential rules and arranged them in a jurisprudential order. The book was divided into several chapters, each chapter specializing in a specific jurisprudential topic.
descriptions.4304: This book is a supplement to the collection of fatwas of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. It collects additional fatwas and messages that were not included in the original collection. The book deals with various topics in belief and monotheism, and focuses on issues of monotheism of divinity, warning against heresies and innovations such as building mosques on graves and traveling to them, swearing by other than God, and other issues related to faith and polytheism. The work aims to complete the fatwas issued by the Sheikh of Islam and collect them in one methodological context.
descriptions.4305: A book that collects selections from the works of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, arranged by author Alawi al-Saqqaf into sections beginning with the section on monotheism and belief. The book deals with issues of God’s names and attributes, faith and disbelief, and responding to sects such as the Murji’ah and Kharijites, in addition to topics such as visiting graves, jinn, and devils.
descriptions.4306: The book “Prophecies” by Ibn Taymiyyah is a book on the science of Islamic doctrine, dealing with the subject of prophecy and the message from its many aspects. The book examines the truth of prophecy and the wisdom behind sending the messengers and their functions, detailing the sayings about the miracles of the prophets and their proofs, and discussing the sayings of different sects, such as the Ash’aris, in defining and proving a miracle. The work aims to establish belief in the prophets as a pillar of faith, and to explain that Islam is the religion of all prophets, while responding to those who disagree on issues of love and wisdom and explaining God’s actions.
descriptions.4307: This book is written by Ibn Taymiyyah, and it responds and criticizes the beliefs of the Nusayri sect (Alawites) as stated in a question directed to him. The book describes their alleged beliefs in the permissibility of alcohol, the transmigration of souls, the antiquity of the world, the denial of resurrection, their interpretation of acts of worship such as prayer and fasting in the names of people, and their claim to the divinity of Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). The book also discusses their concept of the name and meaning in the roles of the prophets, basing its criticism on what it sees as a distortion of the Islamic faith.
descriptions.4308: The mediator between truth and creation. A small book by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah on belief and monotheism, in which he talked about the types of mediation, supplication, monotheism, polytheism, and other important issues of belief.
descriptions.4309: The book “Bughiyat al-Murtadd fi refutation ala al-Mustafasilafah wa Qaramitah” by Ibn Taymiyyah is a book in response to sects and sects that contradict the Islamic faith. The book begins with a discussion of well-known prophetic hadiths about the virtue of the mind and its character, and shows their weakness and status. Then it expands in criticizing what was built on them, including the articles of those who believe in the unity of existence and the sayings of philosophers, Qarmatians, and mystics, with a clarification of truth from falsehood.
descriptions.4310: Explaining the confusion of the Jahmiyas in establishing their theological heresies or nullifying the establishment is a book by Ibn Taymiyyah in which he responded to the book Establishing Sanctification by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, and he edited many of the issues in it. His student, Al-Najib Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyyah, praising the book in its Nounin, said:
descriptions.4311: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah investigates the issue of applying the description “the Word of God” to Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him), and the relationship of that to the issue of the Qur’an being the word of God and its being uncreated. The author responds to the suspicions of Christians and Jahmiyas who use as evidence the use of the word “the Word” on Jesus to claim the creation of the Qur’an, showing the corruption of this argument by clarifying the verbal co-existence and liberalization of what is meant by “the Word of God” in the legal texts. The book also addresses the response to the Christian beliefs in divinity and hypostases, and the influence of some Islamic sects by the articles of the Jews and Christians.
descriptions.4312: This book is a collection of letters by Ibn Taymiyyah, beginning with a treatise on “Qunoot of all things to God Almighty,” in which he deals with the interpretation of the meanings of Qunoot, Islam, prostration, and praise as mentioned in the Holy Qur’an, and shows that they are general attributes that include all creatures of God Almighty.
descriptions.4313: The book Jami’ al-Mas’a’il by Ibn Taymiyyah, in nine volumes, contains numerous letters and fatwas by Ahmad Ibn Taymiyyah (died: 728 AH), compiled by Muhammad Uzair Shams. It is something that has never been published before, and was printed within the project of the works of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. It is a variety of treatises on different sciences, such as interpretation, hadith, jurisprudence, principles, beliefs, and other things. The manuscript originals were collected from the world’s libraries, for the benefit of specialists in the legal sciences and all researchers in Islamic knowledge. The book contains many letters, some of which are brief, some of which are long, some of which are chapters on specific issues, and some of which are fatwas on questions asked by the author. The approach of these letters is not a unified approach.
descriptions.4314: This book by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah addresses two main issues in the Islamic faith. The first is the ruling on swearing by someone other than God, as he explains the prohibition of that contained in the Prophetic hadiths, and the second is the ruling on praying to graves. The book also contains a separate chapter that deals with the issue of seeking help, within the framework of explaining the legal rulings related to monotheism and the prohibition of polytheism.
descriptions.4315: This book, written by Ibn Taymiyyah, deals with the subject of the rights of the Prophet’s family, and explains their concept and characteristics, while emphasizing the obligation of love and affection for them based on Sharia texts. The book also discusses issues related to the intellectual conflict around this issue, distinguishes between types of love (psychological, mental, and heart), and warns against heresies and misguidance associated with the position of some sects such as the Shiites, while emphasizing the prohibition of insulting the Companions against the Prophet’s family and others.
descriptions.4316: Preventing the conflict of reason and transmission, or “the agreement of the authentic transmitted with the clear and reasonable” or “combining reason and transmission”: is the name of a book that is considered one of the most valuable books of Ibn Taymiyyah, as stated by most of those who translated it. Its subject: as its title indicates, it is to refute the contradiction established by theologians and philosophers between reason and transmission - that is, the Qur’an and the Sunnah - so Ibn Taymiyyah confirms the auditory evidence, and proves its benefit with certainty and certainty. He says: “As for this book of ours, it is in explaining the absence of the rational opponent and invalidating the statement of those who claim to provide rational evidence absolutely.” …
descriptions.4317: The book “Details of the Comprehensive Interpretation of Ibn Taymiyyah’s Interpretation” is a collection of fatwas and interpretive issues selected from Ibn Taymiyyah’s words, combining Qur’anic interpretation, jurisprudence, and doctrine. The book deals with various topics, such as the interpretation of verses related to patience and prayer, the position of nations towards the messengers, and the response to Christians regarding Christ, in addition to jurisprudential issues such as atonement for swearing an oath and the punishment of warriors. The book aims to explain the meanings of the Holy Qur’an and link them to the origins of religion and its branches, with a focus on responding to suspicions and establishing monotheism.
descriptions.4318: This book is a letter by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, in which he answers a question related to the head of Hussein bin Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both), and is it true that it was moved and buried in a specific place? The book falls within the general classification of Ibn Taymiyyah’s works, and deals with the issue from a historical legal perspective, as it provides the answer based on the texts and news reported in this regard.
descriptions.4319: This is a letter by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah on the fundamentals of religion. It begins with the issue of the permissibility of delving into fundamental issues in which there is no text from the Prophet ﷺ. The author responds to this question by stating that what is called the fundamentals of religion cannot be devoid of the Prophet’s explanation of it, and that the claim of non-transmission leads to false assumptions. He explains that whoever thinks so is ignorant of the truth of what the Messenger brought or what people understand, or both.
descriptions.4320: Lifting blame from eminent imams. A book compiled by Ibn Taymiyyah, whose title indicates its content. He removed the blame from the eminent imams, in which he mentioned the reasons for the disagreement of the nation’s eminent people in some branches of issues of Islamic jurisprudence, and that this does not detract from their value and worth, and was not a whim in their souls. The instigator behind writing this book was the blame that some people were giving to some of the nation’s notables for contradicting some of the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ. The goal of this book was to remove that blame from them and justify their position. It was necessary to clarify the matter to the people, and that this blame was false. Here, Ibn Taymiyyah specializes in the nation’s notable figures, and not any student of knowledge may make a mistake and repeat the mistake on his own. …
descriptions.4321: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah deals with the issue of visiting graves and seeking help from the graves, and answers questions related to the ruling on requesting supplication from the dead, seeking their help, making vows to them, and wiping their graves. In his response, the author explains the legal controls for visiting, and distinguishes between what is permissible in it and what is reprehensible and polytheistic, addressing in detail the issues of supplication, the reality of the pole and relief, and the story of Al-Khidr (peace be upon him).
descriptions.4322: Prostration of recitation, its meanings and rulings, a book written by Ibn Taymiyyah in which he mentioned what is related to prostration of recitation, what is specific to it and its ruling, and whether it is permissible without purity or not.
descriptions.4323: This book is a fatwa by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah on the issue of prayer after the first call to prayer on Friday, where he examines the ruling on this prayer and whether it was reported from the Prophet ﷺ or the Companions or the Imams. The author reviews the evidence from the Sunnah, the sayings of the Companions, and the schools of jurisprudence, and discusses the inference of the hadith “between every two calls to prayer,” and the extent of its generality or specificity to Friday. The author concludes that the majority of imams agree that there is no temporary year estimated before Friday, while mentioning the opinions of those who disagree and discussing their evidence.
descriptions.4324: Explanation of the Hadith of Revelation is a letter written by Ibn Taymiyyah after a fatwa he received and asked him to answer by clarifying the truth of the Hadith of Revelation and its meaning
descriptions.4325: This book is an explanation of the book “Umdat al-Fiqh,” starting with the book on prayer, in which the author explains the definition of prayer linguistically and legally, and reviews the evidence of its obligation from the Qur’an and Sunnah, then deals with the provisions of the call to prayer and the iqama and the conditions of prayer such as purity, time, covering the private parts, facing the qiblah, and intention, in addition to the etiquette of walking to prayer.
descriptions.4326: This book is an explanation of the book “Umdat al-Fiqh” by Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi, written by Ibn Taymiyyah, and it covers two main sections: the Book of Purity and the Book of Hajj. The explanation aims to explain the issues of the book, outline its evidence, and branch out its rules, intermediate between brevity and redundancy. The author begins with issues of purity, detailing the rulings on water, impurities, and utensils, following a comparative jurisprudential approach based on Sharia evidence.
descriptions.4327: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah deals with the subject of the virtue of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), and is concerned with explaining his virtues and characteristics that were unique to him from other companions, with a comparison between his virtues and the virtues of Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). The author relies on the Prophetic hadiths to show that Abu Bakr is the best of the nation after the Messenger of God ﷺ, criticizing what he sees as incorrect or not explicit hadiths in preferring others over him.
descriptions.4328: This book collects a fatwa by Ibn Taymiyyah describing the types of clothing that the Prophet ﷺ used to wear, and the weapons he used for war and the animals for riding. The author aims to bring the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ closer to these practical aspects of life, based on the hadiths contained therein, while extracting the jurisprudential benefits related to the sections on clothing, food, and war machines.
descriptions.4329: This is a book on monotheism and the Islamic faith, written by Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is concerned with explaining the meaning of the monotheism of God and sincerity in worship and work for Him alone. The book explains the servant’s lack of God in everything, and explains the meanings of Qur’anic verses related to the unification of divinity and divinity, seeking God’s help, and pure worship of Him.
descriptions.4330: A Great Rule for Tawassul and Wasila is a book written by Ibn Taymiyyah in which he talks about tawassul and its rulings from the perspective of the Sunnis and the community.
descriptions.4331: This is a book by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah that discusses in detail the meanings of the four supplications: Tasbih, Praise, Tahlil, and Takbir, which are known as “the lasting good deeds.” The author explains the monotheistic meanings of these words, explains their connection to each other, and responds to some errors in understanding their meaning, based on Sharia texts.
descriptions.4332: This book by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah deals with the fundamental differences between the worship of the people of Islam, which are based on monotheism and following the Sharia, and the worship of the people of polytheism and hypocrisy. The author shows that correct worship is built on two principles: sincerity of worship to God alone, and following what God has legislated through the words of His messengers. The book reviews the positions of the Companions and followers, and warns against heresies and polytheism such as using graves as mosques, stressing the importance of following the Messenger ﷺ in all acts of worship.
descriptions.4333: This book by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah deals with a delicate jurisprudential issue related to the rulings on jihad, which is the ruling on a Muslim immersing himself in the ranks of the enemy when there is a strong suspicion that he will be killed, and discusses the legality of that and its evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book falls within the classification of jihadi jurisprudence, as it presents images of the issue and reviews the legal evidence supporting it, with a focus on the controls of legitimate jihad.
descriptions.4334: This is a message by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah that deals with the topic of patience, which is one of the greatest good qualities encouraged by the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author reviews in twenty different aspects the aspects of this virtue, based on Sharia texts that show the status and importance of patience in the life of the believer.
descriptions.4335: This book by Imam Ibn Taymiyyah deals with the topic of love from a legal and ideological perspective, explaining that it is the origin of every action and movement in the world, and detailing the difference between praiseworthy and blameworthy love. The book criticizes the opinions of philosophers and theologians on issues of love, will, and pleasure, and affirms that love of God is the origin of practical monotheism, and that associating others with love is the origin of polytheism in God. The book also discusses issues of love and some sects’ interpretations of love, and links love and religion as a basis for worship and obedience.
descriptions.4336: This is a brief message by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah that deals with the topic of the obligation of obeying God, His Messenger, and those in charge of affairs, and explains the approach of the Sunnis and the community in dealing with those in charge, which is based on following and adhering to influence, not innovation and opinion. The author begins his message with a number of narrations narrated from the righteous predecessors, such as Ibn Masoud, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and Al-Awza’i, emphasizing the necessity of the Sunnah and confining ourselves to what the early predecessors were upon, and leaving out innovations and innovations.
descriptions.4337: Majmoo’ al-Fatawa is a book that collects the fatwas of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. It contains many books on doctrine and monotheism, jurisprudence and principles, hadith and interpretation, and other sciences. It was written in (37) original volumes and printed in (20) volumes.
descriptions.4338: The collection of letters and issues by Ibn Taymiyyah includes letters and fatwas in various fields of Islamic sciences, including interpretation, hadith, principles, beliefs, etiquette, rulings, and Sufism. The book deals with various topics related to ethics, jurisprudence, and doctrine, with a focus on responding to the doctrines that the author deems contrary to the truth, and explaining the doctrine of the Salaf in controversial issues.
descriptions.4339: This book is a summary of the fatwas of Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah that he issued in Egypt. It was summarized by Badr al-Din al-Baali. The summary selects from these fatwas what is dominated by the jurisprudential side, which may be difficult for beginners to learn. The book includes various sections and chapters that include issues of intention, purity, sales, quarantine, reconciliation, guarantee, agency, approval, marriage, division, major sins, and other jurisprudential rulings.
descriptions.4340: This book is an abbreviation of the book “Minhaj al-Sunnah al-Nabawiyyah” by Ibn Taymiyyah, written by Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Ghunayman, and focuses on rebutting the claims of the Shiites and Qadariyya and responding to their claims. The book deals with topics such as the origins of religion according to the Imamis, their contradiction in the issue of the Imamate, and explaining some of the follies of the Shiites and the polytheism of some Sufis, while emphasizing the importance of knowing the truth about these sects at the present time.
descriptions.4341: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah deals with a jurisprudential issue comparing the virtue of stationing in the borders and the virtue of neighboring areas in Mecca, reviewing the legal evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah and the sayings of the predecessors on both matters. The author aims to explain which of the two is better and more rewarding, discussing the opinions of those who dislike close proximity and those who prefer it, and explaining the virtues of rabat in the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4342: This book is a fatwa by Ibn Taymiyyah regarding the rule of churches in Islamic countries, in which he was asked about the claim of the people of the Dhimmah that closing their churches in Cairo is unjust, and their request to open them on the basis of a pretext he presented from the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. The author answers this issue by clarifying the reality of those churches, the ruling on demolishing them in the land of force, and the age conditions to which they were bound, along with his response to the claim that the Muslims oppressed them, and a statement of the hostility of the Batini and the Rafidites to the Muslims.
descriptions.4343: This book by Ibn Taymiyyah addresses the issue of the servant having love for things that are good, right, and praiseworthy in themselves, such as benevolence, knowledge, and honesty, regardless of whether they are for God or for others. The author discusses the psychological motives for this love, and classifies the methods of knowledge into three: sight, hearing, and reason (the heart). The book falls within the classification of Ibn Taymiyyah’s books, and addresses a delicate topic in the science of behavior and human psychology from an Islamic perspective.
descriptions.4344: This book collects a number of questions and answers by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, dealing with various doctrinal and jurisprudential topics such as faith and disbelief, intercession, destiny, the provisions of purity and prayer, sacrifices, and others. The book also includes a collection of issues known as “Questions of the People of Al-Rahba,” in addition to “Selections of Sheikh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah” by his student Ibn Abdul-Hadi, and a translation of Sheikh Al-Islam written by Al-Dhahabi.
descriptions.4345: The Methodology of the Sunnah of the Prophet in refuting the words of the Shiites and the Qadariyyah is a huge book written by the Sunni jurist Ibn Taymiyyah. This book is considered one of his most famous books ever, and it includes a response to the Twelver Shiites and the Qadariyya sect. He originally wrote it in response to the book of the well-known Shiite jurist Ibn al-Mutahhar al-Hilli, Minhaj al-Karama.
descriptions.4346: Criticism of the Ranks of Consensus is a book written by Ibn Taymiyyah in which he commented on Ibn Hazm’s book Al-Ijma’ and made some corrections about it.
descriptions.4347: A book in which its author answers a question about the way to advance Muslims, stressing the necessity of providing attention to monotheism and correct doctrine as a basis for reform, in accordance with the approach of the prophets and messengers. The book clarifies that interest in monotheism does not mean neglecting the rest of the Sharia, but rather it is the basis on which worship, behavior and transactions are based, and it shows the need to make an effort in calling for the correct doctrine and raising people according to it.
descriptions.4348: This book is a summary that brings together the hadiths that Sheikh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani retracted in his rulings on them between authentication and weakness, with the addition of some corrections and warnings. The research has been divided into main sections that show hadiths whose rulings have moved from weak to sound or vice versa, in addition to a section for corrections and research related to these regressions. The work aims to present the Sheikh's final judgment on the hadiths in which he changed his opinion, based on his books and printed investigations.
descriptions.4349: This book is a “proven” comprehensive collection of the works of the hadith scholar Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani, compiled by Abdullah al-Shamrani. It includes a comprehensive list of his books, investigations, conclusions, responses, and articles, with an explanation of the characteristics of his books and his approach to classification. The book includes chapters on the Sheikh’s translation, documented works, articles, and books for those interested in his knowledge and method.
descriptions.4350: This is a book on the Prophet’s hadith, in which the author collected the hadiths contained in encouraging virtues and warning against vices, and arranged them under the sections of jurisprudence, beliefs, and behavior, with an explanation of which of them are authentic and which are weak, in accordance with his approach to correcting and weakening.
descriptions.4351: This book is Al-Albani’s investigation of the hadiths of Sunan Abu Dawud, in which he explains the degree of each hadith in terms of health and weakness. The book begins by mentioning the transmitted hadiths with the author’s ruling on them, such as “hasan sahih,” “authentic,” or “weak,” and covers various jurisprudential sections, such as the rulings on relieving oneself and purity. The work aims to distinguish authentic hadiths from weak ones in this important hadith source.
descriptions.4352: This book is an investigation and grading by Al-Albani of the hadiths of Sunan Ibn Majah, where he explains what is authentic and what is weak according to his approach to hadith criticism. The book includes hadiths in various jurisprudential sections, with comments on whether they are valid or weak based on evidence and evidence from other hadith books.
descriptions.4353: This book is an investigative work on Sunan al-Tirmidhi, in which the author summarizes his hadiths and explains their degree of validity and weakness according to his approach to hadith criticism. The book falls within the classification of Al-Albani’s books, and contains the texts of the Prophet’s hadiths with the author’s comments on them, where he mentions his ruling on each hadith (authentic, hasan, weak) with an indication of the authors of other Sunans who narrated it.
descriptions.4354: This book is Al-Albani’s investigation of the hadiths of Sunan al-Nasa’i. It aims to clarify the degree of authenticity or weakness of the hadiths based on his approach to authentication and weakness. The book includes attributed hadiths with the author’s ruling on them, such as “authentic” or “good,” with references to his other works such as Al-Sahihah and Al-Irwa’. The work falls within the author’s efforts to purify the Sunnah of the Prophet and classify the noble Prophet’s hadiths.
descriptions.4355: Weak persuasion and intimidation. A book written by the hadith sheikh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani, with the intention of clarifying the weak hadiths contained in the book al-Targhib wa al-Tarheeb by al-Hafiz al-Mundhiri. Sheikh Al-Albani was keen to extract the hadiths from the book and attribute them to their sources. In his approach to the book, he pointed out what Al-Mundhiri was accused of -(may Allah have mercy on him)- of matters and illusions that occurred to him in his hadiths. Sheikh Al-Albani -(may Allah have mercy on him)- ranked the hadiths of the book into five levels, which are: weak, very weak, fabricated, objectionable, and abnormal.
descriptions.4356: A book that explains the etiquette and Sunnahs of the Prophet related to the stage of marriage and consummation with the wife, based on established hadiths in the pure Sunnah. The author aims to remind Muslims of the etiquette prescribed by the Prophet ﷺ, such as courting the wife and praying for her, and the rulings on intercourse, washing, and feasting, while alerting to some matters that concern every married person.
descriptions.4357: The book “Ahkam al-Fanaaz” by the hadith scholar Nasir al-Din al-Albani, which is a book on the jurisprudence of funerals and the legal rulings related to them derived from the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The book begins with an explanation of what is required of the sick person and instructing the dying person, then moves on to the rulings on washing, shrouding, praying at the funeral, burial, and condolences, with a detail of funeral innovations that contradict the Sunnah of the Prophet. The author aims to establish servitude to God in treating the dead in the best possible way, and being kind to him and his family, in accordance with what is stated in the Qur’an and Sunnah.
descriptions.4358: This is a book explaining the description of the Prophet’s prayer ﷺ from the takbir to the salaam, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and explaining their methods and chains of transmission. The author aims to enable the Muslim to perform prayer in the manner in which the Prophet ﷺ prayed, in response to his command, “Pray as you have seen me pray.” The book includes discussions on the rulings on prayer, such as facing the qiblah, standing, the sutrah, and clothing, while refuting doubts that may get in the way of following the Sunnah.
descriptions.4359: The book “Irwa’ al-Ghaleel fi Graduation of the Hadiths of Manar al-Sabil” is a scholarly graduate work by its author, Nasser al-Din al-Albani. It aims to graduate the prophetic hadiths contained in the book “Manar al-Sabil” by Mar’i ibn Yusuf al-Karmi, which is a jurisprudential book according to the doctrine of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The book begins with introductions that include a translation by the author and the author of the text, then proceeds to summarize the hadiths, chapter by chapter, starting with the introduction to the book and moving on to the Book of Purity, mentioning the hadiths and indicating their degree of authenticity and weakness. The book is divided into several parts, and is characterized by an accurate scientific method in criticizing hadiths and explaining their sources.
descriptions.4360: A book that examines the investigation of the Prophet’s hadiths related to some jurisprudential and doctrinal issues, with a focus on grading them and indicating their degree of validity and weakness. The author deals with hadiths such as the hadith of Zamzam water when it is drunk for it, the hadiths about the purity of the water, and the hadith of the Black Stone, and classifies them between authentic and weak, while mentioning the explanations.
descriptions.4361: The book “The Clear Verses Concerning the Dead Not Hearing” by Ibn Al-Alusi, which is one of the books that discusses an unseen issue related to the world of the isthmus, which is whether the dead hear the living or not. In his research, the author relies on inferences from legal texts from the Qur’an and Sunnah, and reviews the opinions of the various schools of thought on the issue, with a focus on the Hanafi school of thought. He emphasizes that the ruling on this issue is not defined by opinions or analogies, but rather by its proven evidence from the text.
descriptions.4362: The book “Useful Answers to the Questions of the University Mosque Committee” by the author Nasser al-Din al-Albani, which is included in the classification of his books. The book deals with answering questions received from the University Mosque Committee, and it revolves around the rulings and innovations of Friday prayers. It begins with a discussion of the hadith of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)’s call to prayer and its various additions, to be a basis for responding to the issues raised.
descriptions.4363: This is a book about grading the hadiths of the Night Journey and Mi’raj and explaining the authentic ones from the incorrect ones. The author collected them from the narrations of the numerous companions such as Abu Hurairah, Anas bin Malik, Ibn Abbas and others. The compiler aims to distinguish the authentic hadiths contained in this great prophetic incident, while narrating them in a unique style. The author has left a mark on the symbols used to indicate the sources of hadiths from the books of the Sunnah, such as Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Ahmad.
descriptions.4364: This book is an investigation of the issues of faith by Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and his hadiths were compiled by Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani. The book deals with the definition of faith and an explanation of its branches and degrees, citing the authentic hadiths of the Prophet that explain the reality of Islam, faith, migration and jihad, and show the characteristics of the Muslim and the believer. The book falls within the doctrinal classification that explains the pillars of faith and the actions of the hearts and limbs.
descriptions.4365: Invoking Destiny is a book written by Ahmed Ibn Taymiyyah, in which he discusses the invocation of some people and sects by Destiny to commit sins, because God has decreed it for them. Ibn Taymiyyah began his book with the hadith that the author referred to at the beginning of his book, which is: On the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
descriptions.4366: The book “Al-Tahjil fi Takhrij of what has not been extracted from the hadiths” is a complementary work that aims to graduate the fabricated hadiths and the suspended reports that were mentioned in the book “Manar Al-Sabil Sharh Al-Dalil” by Ibn Dhuwayan, and which the scholar Al-Albani did not graduate in his book “Irwa’ Al-Ghaleel.” The author is committed to grading what Al-Albani overlooked or did not find out, while following the method of brevity in speaking about the narrators and mentioning the methods, excluding what was previously grading in the book “Al-Takmil.” The book covers topics of Islamic jurisprudence from purity to punishments, thus completing what was missed in the original source.
descriptions.4367: This book is Sheikh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani’s comments on Sahih Ibn Hibban, distinguishing between the authentic hadiths of his hadiths and those that were omitted or distorted, within the framework of Prince Ala al-Din Ali bin Balban al-Farsi’s arrangement of the Sahih. The book includes twelve parts, including introductions, comments, and a narration of the books and chapters. It deals with various topics such as faith, knowledge, righteousness, and charity, while pointing out some doctrinal violations in the original book without addressing them in detail.
descriptions.4368: This is a book on grading hadiths and narrations, written by Saleh Al-Sheikh to complete what he missed from the book “Irwa’ al-Ghaleel” by the scholar Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani. The book specializes in grading the hadiths that were mentioned in the book “Manar Al-Sabil Sharh Al-Dalil” by Sheikh Ibrahim bin Dhawayan, which Al-Albani did not stop at in his grading, or he said about them that he did not find a way out of them. The author confines himself to grading these hadiths without elaborating on the biographies of the narrators or the sayings of jarh and ta'deel. The book is arranged according to the sections of jurisprudence, beginning with the book on purity, prayer, funerals, and zakat.
descriptions.4369: A book that examines the concept of tawassul in Islam, distinguishing between its legitimate and innovative types according to the author’s approach. It begins by defining tawassul linguistically and legally, then defines the legitimate means such as tawassul with the names and attributes of God, good deeds, and the supplication of a righteous man, and responds to the doubts raised about this topic. The book is based on two lectures by the author, to which benefits from a previous message were added, making it a brief, comprehensive study of the rulings on supplication.
descriptions.4370: The book “Hadith is a proof by itself in beliefs and rulings” by the author Nasser al-Din al-Albani, and it is one of the books of doctrine and the principles of jurisprudence. The book addresses the issue of the necessity of referring to the Sunnah of the Prophet and seeking judgment from it in beliefs and rulings, and focuses on the invalidity of prioritizing analogy and other rules over the authentic hadith. The author also devotes a chapter to defending the validity of the Hadith of Ahadith in beliefs and rulings, explaining that it benefits knowledge and certainty, and discusses the issue of sectarian tradition and its effects.
descriptions.4371: This is a book by the scholar and hadith scholar Nasser al-Din al-Albani, and it is a response to those who disagreed with the scholars and became strict and obliged women to cover their faces and hands and made it obligatory, while the author believes that covering the face is a recommended Sunnah and not an obligation. The book begins with an introduction in which the author states his intention to reprint his book “The Hijab of the Muslim Woman” and add new benefits to it, while discussing contemporary views on the issue of covering women’s faces.
descriptions.4372: The Good Speech is a book in which Ibn Taymiyyah collected several prophetic hadiths about the supplications that a Muslim says on his day in various matters. The book began with an introduction about the encouragement to remember and its importance.
descriptions.4373: This book is an investigation and study of the issue of wiping over socks and sandals during ablution, written by the scholar Muhammad Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi. The author begins by rooting the issue legally, explaining that the rulings are due to the Holy Book, then he reviews the evidence of surveying from the Qur’an and Sunnah, conveying the opinions of the Companions and scholars on that matter. The book falls within the modern jurisprudential classification, and aims to give weight to the view that it is permissible to wipe over socks based on Sharia texts.
descriptions.4374: The book “The Beginning of the Spirit in Favoring the Messenger ﷺ” by the scholar Izz Al-Din bin Abdul Salam is a book on the virtues of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, his characteristics and miracles. The book includes a collection of authentic prophetic hadiths that prove his high status and dignity, such as the miracle of water springing from between his fingers and the trunk’s longing for him. It also discusses the great intercession that was unique to him above all other prophets, and an explanation of his superiority over the rest of creation.
descriptions.4375: Warning the prostrating person against taking graves as mosques is a book written by the hadith imam Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani, who died in the year 1420 AH. The book includes a warning against polytheism and taking graves as mosques, and it is considered one of the most important books on monotheism at the present time.
descriptions.4376: This is a book explaining the prohibition of singing and musical instruments, written by Nasir al-Din al-Albani in response to a fatwa that permitted music and singing under conditions, based on authentic prophetic hadiths and the sayings of the imams of the sects. The book includes chapters mentioning the hadiths indicating the prohibition, explaining the strange ones, and responding to those among the scholars who permitted them, such as Ibn Hazm, while discussing the suspicions of those who permitted them and explaining the wisdom of the prohibition, touching on the ruling on singing without an instrument, Sufi singing, and Islamic chants.
descriptions.4377: Graduation of the Hadiths of the Virtues of the Levant and Damascus is a book of hadith written by Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani. It was published in several editions by the Islamic Office in Beirut. In it, Al-Albani investigated the hadiths contained in the book The Virtues of the Levant and Damascus by its author, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rubi, and these hadiths about the virtue of the Levant in general and the virtue of the city of Damascus in particular.
descriptions.4378: This is a book on grading the Prophetic hadiths related to the subject of poverty, in which the author collected the hadiths contained in this section and explained their degree of validity and weakness, based on the hadith scholars’ approach in criticizing the chains of transmission and texts. The book aims to distinguish the correct from the incorrect in the hadiths that deal with the problem of poverty and ways to address it in Islam, which serves researchers in this field.
descriptions.4379: This book is a modern scientific and jurisprudential research by the hadith scholar Nasser al-Din al-Albani, which deals with the issue of breaking the fast in Ramadan before traveling after dawn. The author presents the hadith contained in this issue and defends its authenticity, citing evidence from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and Salafi traditions, and discusses dissenting opinions that deny the authenticity of the hadith out of sectarian fanaticism.
descriptions.4380: A book that summarizes the rulings on funerals and related legal rulings derived from the Sunnah of the Prophet, starting with the will for the dying, washing and shrouding the dead, passing through praying over him and burying him, and ending with condolences. The author aims to bring these provisions to general readers as a quick reference when needed, especially in cases of death.
descriptions.4381: The book “Tamam al-Manna fi Commentary on the Jurisprudence of the Sunnah” is a scientific work by the hadith scholar Nasser al-Din al-Albani. It falls within the classification of his books, and is specialized in criticizing and verifying the hadiths contained in the book “The Jurisprudence of the Sunnah.” The book includes a set of methodological rules in the science of hadith, such as rejecting abnormal, distorted, and distorted hadith, and explaining the weakness of some well-known hadiths, with an emphasis on the necessity of acting according to the authentic hadith and not relying on weak hadiths even regarding the virtues of deeds. The book includes extensive comments on parts of "Sunnah jurisprudence", with a summary of the hadiths and a statement of their degree of validity and weakness.
descriptions.4382: A book explaining the rulings on Muslim women’s robes according to what is stated in the Qur’an and Sunnah. It deals with the conditions that must be met in Muslim women’s clothing, based on Sharia evidence and Salafi traditions. In this new edition, the author presents important additions, including additional evidence that a woman’s face and hands are not private, and a discussion of the interpretation of some verses in this regard, in addition to other issues such as the danger of using infidel maids and the colors of a woman’s dress.
descriptions.4383: A book explaining the argument of the Prophet ﷺ as narrated by the companion Jabir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), relying on established prophetic hadiths. The book includes comments and benefits in explaining the rituals of Hajj, and concludes by mentioning a number of heresies that some pilgrims fall into from the beginning of their travel until their return, in addition to the heresies of visiting the Prophet’s Mosque and Al-Aqsa Mosque.
descriptions.4384: This is a book that combines an investigation of the Prophet’s hadiths and an explanation of women’s rights in Islam, with comments on the authenticity of the hadiths and their study. The book deals with topics related to the status of women and their share of the general Muhammadan reform, citing hadiths from the Prophet and traces of the Companions, while explaining their degrees of health and weakness.
descriptions.4385: This is a book explaining the ruling on one who neglects prayer. It begins with an introduction about the seriousness of the sin of intentionally abandoning the obligatory prayer, citing Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths warning against that. Then, it presents the differences of imams and scholars regarding the issue of declaring the one who intentionally abandons prayer to be an infidel.
descriptions.4386: This is a book that examines the sermon on the need that the Prophet ﷺ taught his companions, and the author presents it in one text after tracing its methods and wording from the books of the Sunnah. The book consists of two chapters and a conclusion, where the first chapter is devoted to the text of the sermon, and the second chapter to its conclusion, and in the conclusion it shows the work of the righteous predecessors by presenting it in their lessons and affairs.
descriptions.4387: This is a book about criticizing the hadith approach and scientific graduation, written by Sheikh Nasser al-Din al-Albani. It studies and analyzes the book “Jurisprudence of Biography” by Dr. Muhammad Saeed al-Bouti, where the author criticizes what he sees as a shortcomings in applying precise scientific rules in grading prophetic hadiths and reports related to biography, calling for the necessity of studying the chains of transmission and judging the hadiths as whether they are true or weak before relying on them in writing and teaching.
descriptions.4388: The book Riyadh al-Saliheen, from the words of the Master of the Messengers, was written by Imam Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi al-Dimashqi. In this book, he collects authentic hadiths narrated from the Prophet Muhammad bin Abdullah in all matters of faith and life, and presents them arranged in sections and chapters, so that they are topics that are easy for the reader to return to and benefit from. Al-Nawawi said:
descriptions.4389: A book on the science of hadith. It brings together the Prophetic hadiths authenticated by the author with an explanation of their jurisprudence and benefits. It is distinguished by graduating hadiths and studying them critically. This new edition of the first volume included new additions and investigations, and responses to some of the criticisms directed at the modern approach followed in the series.
descriptions.4390: An encyclopedic book that aims to collect weak and fabricated hadiths and explain their bad impact on the Islamic nation, relying on a critical approach in extracting hadiths and distinguishing the correct ones from the weak ones. The book includes fourteen volumes, and begins with an introduction by the author in which he explains his approach in this new edition and the hadith and jurisprudential benefits he has added, with an introduction known as weak and fabricated hadiths.
descriptions.4391: This book is “Sahih Abu Dawud - Al-Umm” by the hadith scholar Muhammad Nasir Al-Din Al-Albani. It is an expanded compilation of the hadiths of Sunan Abi Dawud. It includes discussion of its chains of transmission and its narrators in detail in terms of modifications, distortions, corrections, and weakening, according to the approach the author took in his “Sahih” and “Weak” series. The first part begins with the book on purity, covering multiple sections starting from the etiquette of relieving oneself and abandoning oneself, passing through the rulings on cleaning oneself and using the siwak, and other issues of jurisprudence and hadith.
descriptions.4392: This is the book “Sahih al-Adab al-Mufrad” by Imam al-Bukhari, and it is an abbreviation and refinement of his original book, “Al-Adab al-Mufrad,” in which he collected prophetic hadiths in Islamic etiquette and morals. The book is limited to authentic hadiths according to the specialist’s approach, and focuses on the topics of honoring one’s parents and maintaining family ties, beginning with an interpretation of the verses and hadiths contained in that.
descriptions.4393: This book is a graduation and verification of the hadiths contained in the book “Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir” by Al-Suyuti and its additions, where the author arranged the hadiths according to the letters of the dictionary, and explained their degree of soundness and weakness according to his method of correcting and weakening. The book includes various prophetic hadiths on beliefs, acts of worship, transactions, etiquette, and rituals, with reference to their original sources and degree of authenticity.
descriptions.4394: A book that collects what is authentic from the biography of the Prophet ﷺ, his days, his conquests, his expeditions, and the delegations to him, according to a critical approach based on deleting weak chains of transmission and paths and being satisfied with the correct narration while mentioning the name of the companion. The author aims to present documented biographical material limited to what has been proven from the news, while shortening some phrases to suit this methodological abbreviation.
descriptions.4395: A book that examines the etiquette of fatwas and the rulings of the mufti and the questioner, and reviews the responsibility of issuing legal fatwas and the danger of speaking against God without knowledge, relying on texts from the Prophet’s hadiths to explain the controls of fatwas and the importance of verifying them.
descriptions.4396: The Characteristics of the Prophet’s Prayer is a book by Sheikh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani. He arranged it according to the method of prayer, from its beginning with facing the Qiblah, standing, and saying “Allahu Akbar” to its end with the salutation and the obligation to greet, explaining the ruling on every characteristic of prayer, whether obligatory or recommended, with quoting the hadiths contained in that, mentioning the jurists whom he relies on in that issue, to strengthen his doctrine, indicating if he finds contradiction to it, and discussing his evidence. In this book, Sheikh Al-Albani demonstrated his absolute diligence in the science of hadith, as he did not work with hadiths in which he found weakness, while citing the early jurists in correcting, weakening, and deriving jurisprudential rulings, even if some jurists worked on them.
descriptions.4397: This is a book on the jurisprudence of Tarawih prayer. It begins with an introduction to the desirability of praying in congregation during it, based on three things: the Prophet’s acknowledgment of congregational prayer in it, his establishment of it, and his explanation of its virtue. The book presents the hadiths contained in this matter, such as the hadith of Tha’labah ibn Abi Malik al-Qurazi, the hadith of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, and the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, with their grading and an explanation of their degree of authenticity and goodness.
descriptions.4398: This book is a brief treatise by the hadith scholar Nasser al-Din al-Albani, in which he proves that the Sunnah of the Prophet regarding the two Eid prayers (Al-Fitr and Al-Adha) is to perform them in the prayer area outside the country, and not in the mosque. The author relies on the hadiths mentioned regarding the Prophet ﷺ’s perseverance in this, and responds to those who explained the reason for praying in the prayer place due to the narrowness of the mosque, explaining the wisdom of this Sunnah and dispelling the doubts surrounding it.
descriptions.4399: This book is “Weak Abu Dawud - Al-Umm” by the hadith scholar Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani, and it is a work specialized in examining the weak hadiths contained in Sunan Abu Dawud, and explaining their reasons and ruling on them. The book includes two volumes, beginning with the Book of Purity, in which the author adopted a detailed approach in studying the chains of transmission and the speech of the narrators, amending and criticizing him, similar to what he did in his two series, Al-Sahihah and Al-Da’eef.
descriptions.4400: This book is a summary of the hadiths contained in the book “Al-Adab Al-Mufrad” by Imam Al-Bukhari, with an explanation of the weaknesses in them according to the author’s approach to classification. The book includes multiple sections related to righteousness, connection, and Islamic etiquette, such as honoring one’s parents, maintaining family ties, and being good neighbors. It cites hadiths and classifies them in terms of strength and weakness.
descriptions.4401: A book that collects the weak and fabricated hadiths that were mentioned in the books “Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir” and “Ziyadah” by Al-Suyuti, with an explanation of the degree of weakness or fabrication of each hadith. The author arranged the hadiths according to the letters of the dictionary (Alif, Baa, Ta...) to facilitate searching in them, and mentioned for each hadith its ruling in terms of weakness, status, or severity. The book aims to purify the Prophet’s Sunnah from what is not proven about it, according to the hadith scholars’ approach to criticizing narratives.
descriptions.4402: Sahih Sunan al-Tirmidhi and Weak Sunan al-Tirmidhi is a book to verify Sunan al-Tirmidhi to distinguish authentic hadiths from weak ones. Edited by Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani.
descriptions.4403: The book “Ghayat al-Maram fi Tajharj al-Halaal and al-Haram” by the author Nasir al-Din al-Albani, which is a compilation of the hadiths of the Prophet related to the rulings on what is permissible and forbidden. The book begins by mentioning various prophetic hadiths, classified according to degrees of authenticity (authentic, good, weak), dealing with topics such as the source of legislation and the origins of what is permissible and forbidden, warning against innovation in religion, and explaining the meaning of worshiping rabbis and monks by following their analysis and prohibition.
descriptions.4404: The book “The Sedition of Takfir” by the hadith scholar Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani deals with the issue of takfir as a great, ancient sedition adopted by the Kharijite sect, and warns against falling into it due to shallow knowledge and lack of understanding of the legal rules. The book explains that departing from the path of the believers and following a method other than theirs is the reason for the misguidance of many sects, past and present, based on the Qur’anic verse that condemns those who oppose the Messenger and follow a path other than the believers. The book includes a report from Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz and a commentary from Sheikh Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Othaimeen.
descriptions.4405: A book on the virtue of praying upon the Prophet ﷺ, compiled by the author Imam Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Jahdhami, in which he collected the hadiths contained in this section, indicating their degree of authenticity and weakness. The book aims to explain the virtue of praying upon the Prophet and its great reward, based on the prophetic texts that show the double reward for whoever prays upon the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4406: A book that deals with the concept of "jurisprudence of reality" that was raised in the context of the temptations that divided the ranks of Muslims. The author explains that knowledge of reality is necessary for those responsible for guiding the nation, based on the rule of "judging something is separate from its perception." The book criticizes engaging in this term without knowledge, warning against speaking unjustly, and emphasizing that the truth is known by its light and evidence, not by its speaker.
descriptions.4407: A book that deals with the virtue of performing the month of Ramadan, how to perform it, and explaining the legitimacy of performing it in a group, with valuable research on i’tikaf. The author aims to revive the Sunnah of the Prophet in Tarawih prayer, and to respond to what he sees as innovations and violations that have spread in its performance, relying on hadiths and proven reports.
descriptions.4408: The book “The Word of Sincerity and Realization of its Meaning” by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali, which is one of the books specialized in explaining the meaning of the testimony of monotheism “There is no god but God” and explaining its truth and implications. The book examines the meaning of sincerity in this word, and focuses on the deeds and duties that result from it, while citing the Prophet’s hadiths in explaining its virtue and the conditions for its acceptance.
descriptions.4409: This is a small message that collected questions that were asked to Sheikh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani and their answers, related to issues in the interpretation and understanding of the Holy Qur’an, such as the authenticity of some hadiths attributed to the interpretation, the ruling on kissing the Qur’an, and the meaning of some verses. The message aims to clarify the principles and rules that should be followed to interpret the Qur’an in the correct way according to the approach of the Salaf, with an emphasis on the importance of adhering to the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4410: This book is a summary of the book “Al-Shama’il al-Muhammadiyah” by Imam al-Tirmidhi, and it collects the hadiths contained in the moral and moral qualities of the Prophet ﷺ, and what relates to his appearance, clothing, food, drink, walk, and speech. The summary is organized into sequential sections that begin with a description of his character, the seal of prophethood, and his hair, and continue with his clothes and weapons, all the way to the details of his daily living, such as his food, drink, and perfume. The book aims to bring the image of the Prophet ﷺ closer to the Muslim through selected authentic hadiths.
descriptions.4411: A book documenting a scientific debate between the two Imams Al-Izz bin Abdul Salam and Ibn Al-Salah about the ruling on the heretical prayer of desires. The researcher has extracted the hadiths contained in this debate and explained their degree of validity and weakness, relying on texts from the Sunnah of the Prophet in explaining the virtue of praying at home and the rulings on fasting and the innovative prayers.
descriptions.4412: The Misbah Al-Masabih is a book written by Muhammad Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi in which he collected the texts of the Prophet’s hadiths, then arranged them in the manner of mosque books, and added judgment on them (as to whether they are authentic, good, or otherwise), and it was influenced by Al-Baghawi’s book Misbah Al-Sunnah. But despite his admiration for the lamps, he saw that they needed to be rectified, so he wrote the Mishkat al-Masabah, compiled his hadiths, and mentioned the name of the companion who narrated the hadith. Because Al-Baghawi did not often mention this, and Al-Tabrizi said about the book Misbah Al-Sunnah:.
descriptions.4413: A book that provides a practical guide to the rituals of Hajj and Umrah, extracted from the Sunnah of the Prophet and the traditions of the predecessors, with a focus on the nature of Hajj as mentioned in the hadith of Jabir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him). The book begins with advice for the pilgrim before performing the rituals, then explains the steps of Hajj and Umrah in order from Ihram to the Farewell Tawaf, with a breakdown of the rulings and Sunnahs. The book concludes with a special chapter on innovations related to Hajj, Umrah, and visiting, warning against them and explaining what contradicts the Sunnah in every ritual.
descriptions.4414: A book that examines the status of the Prophet’s Sunnah in Islamic legislation, and its importance as the second source after the Holy Qur’an. The author relies on a lecture he gave during the month of Ramadan, in which he explains the function of the Sunnah in explaining the Qur’an and detailing its provisions, and stresses the necessity of adhering to it and not dispensing with it.
descriptions.4415: The book “Establishing catapults to destroy the story of the cranes” is a research treatise by the hadith scholar Nasser al-Din al-Albani, in which he aims to explain the falsity of the famous story of the cranes in some books of interpretation and hadith, which claim that Satan uttered on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ words praising the gods of the polytheists. The author relies on tracking the various narrations of the story and explaining its reasons in the chain of transmission and the text, then responds to those who supported it, such as Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, and cites the statements of other imams in invalidating it, relying on legal and rational evidence that confirms the infallibility of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4416: A book on al-Takhreej and al-Zawa’id, which collects hadiths about monotheism and its types extracted from the six books and Sahih al-Jami’, arranged into chapters that begin with an explanation of the meaning of monotheism and its parts, then move on to rulings related to polytheism and what contradicts it, such as ritual amulets, amulets, ruqyah, and slaughtering for other than God, with a mention of the virtues of the monotheists and the reward prepared for them.
descriptions.4417: This is a comprehensive book of the noble Prophetic hadiths. It includes three main works: “Collecting the Mosques” by Imam Al-Suyuti, “Al-Jami’ Al-Azhar” and “Treasures of Truths” by Al-Manawi, and “Al-Fath Al-Kabir” by Al-Nabhani. His hadiths were arranged alphabetically into two main sections: the Sayings section and the Actions section, with the exact texts and the grading of his hadiths. The book aims to complete the Prophetic hadiths and collect them to be a key to the doors of the upper Musnads.
descriptions.4418: A book that collects prophetic hadiths extracted from their sources, attributed to their context in the books of the Sunnah and its explanations, with a mention of judging their chains of transmission as sound, weak, or otherwise, basing many of its sources on the book “Fath al-Bari” by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani. It is included in the books of graduation and appendices. Its articles are arranged in automatic numbering, and it opens with a group of hadiths and narrations concerned with explaining the reasons for revelation, the virtue of intention, and the circumstances of revelation.
descriptions.4419: A book on Al-Takhreej and Al-Zawa’id, which collects hadiths and narrations narrated from the Companions and Followers that the author deems to be authentic, arranged and supported by their chains of transmission. It aims to present the authentically proven sayings of the predecessors, while judging them as authentic or good. It was published in two volumes, the first agreeing with the publication and the second not agreeing with it.
descriptions.4420: A book that collects the hadiths contained in “Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir and its Ziyada” by Imam Al-Suyuti, with an explanation of their ruling in terms of soundness and weakness according to the graduation method. It aims to distinguish authentic hadiths from weak ones in this large hadith collection, relying on extracting and judging the chains of transmission. It is included in the books of graduation and additions that are concerned with studying the chains of transmission of hadiths and their rulings.
descriptions.4421: The book “The Hadiths of Al-Muwatta’ and Mention of the Agreement of the Narrators on the authority of Malik” by Al-Daraqutni is a work in the science of graduation and additions, specializing in the study of the hadiths attributed to the Muwatta of Imam Malik ibn Anas. The author mentions the hadiths contained in Al-Muwatta in order according to the sheikhs of Malik, beginning with Al-Zuhri, while tracking the difference of narrators from Malik and their agreement, and the uniqueness of some of them in narrating from him. The book aims to document the chains of transmission of Al-Muwatta and explain its narrations by comparing the narrations of Malik’s various students.
descriptions.4422: This book is the first part of the series “Hadiths and Narrations on Al-Mizan”, and it is a graduate and critical study of the methods of the hadith “The Heart of the Qur’an Yaseen” and what is mentioned about its merit. The author intends to trace the general paths of the hadith, whether raised, suspended, or interrupted, then he details these paths one by one, quoting the sayings of the Companions and followers regarding that. The work aims to scrutinize the narratives and indicate their degree of validity and weakness according to the hadith scholars’ approach.
descriptions.4423: This is a book about graduation and additions. It studies one prophetic hadith known as “the Hadith of Fiyinah,” and traces its various methods and narrations. The author presents five main methods of hadith, including the path of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas and the path of Saeed bin Jubayr, with a discussion of the chains of transmission and texts. The book aims to scrutinize the narrations and point out whether they are true or weak according to the hadith scholars’ approach.
descriptions.4424: The book “Asna Al-Matalib fi Hadiths of Different Ranks” by the author Al-Hout is a workbook on the science of graduating hadith and distinguishing its grades. It collects various hadiths and narrations arranged according to the letters of the dictionary from hamza to yā’, with a conclusion on the reasons for establishing the hadith and its signs.
