The book aims to explain what is true, weak, or false in these hadiths, relying on the statements of critics such as Ibn al-Jawzi and others to judge each narration.
descriptions.4425: This is a research book concerned with studying the personality of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan, the narrator of Sahih Muslim, and explaining his narration of the Sahih and its importance, while tracking the additions he added to the text of the book and his comments on it. The book falls into four sections, starting with Ibn Sufyan’s translation, then moving on to studying his narration of Sahih Muslim and responding to the criticism directed at it, then detailing his additions, which amounted to thirteen, with their graduation and study, and finally his comments on the Sahih.
descriptions.4426: Ithaf Al-Khayra Al-Mahrah with the additions to the ten Musnads is one of the hadith books and hadith compilations, written by Al-Hafiz Shihab Al-Din Al-Busairi (762 AH - 839 AH). The importance of the book is due to highlighting the amount of hadiths, chains of transmission, and additional texts from the ten Musnads over the six books of hadith, and with some of them combined, it becomes a hadith encyclopedia.
descriptions.4427: The book “Ithaf Al-Mahra bi Al-Fawa’id Al-Mukhtari’ Min Al-Ashra” is a chain of transmission encyclopedia by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, in which he collected the extremities of hadiths from eleven sources from the books of the honorable Sunnah, including Al-Muwatta, Musnads, Sunans, extracts, and Al-Mustadrakat, in the manner of the art of the extremities, which aims to facilitate access to the outputs of hadiths. The author arranged these parts similar to the method of Al-Hafiz Al-Mazzi in arranging them, often listing the performance formulas in the chains of transmission, to be a reference for hadith scholars in tracking the hadiths contained in these sources.
descriptions.4428: The book “Itraf al-Musnad al-Mu’tali bi-Atraf al-Musnad al-Hanbali” is a book of graduations and additions, compiled by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani to arrange the hadiths of the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and the additions of his son Abdullah. The author arranged the names of the companions mentioned in the Musnad according to the letters of the dictionary, then arranged the narrators for each companion, mentioning the ends of the hadiths and indicating their places in the original, and merging the multiple methods of one hadith in one place.
descriptions.4429: The fortieth holy hadiths. A book written by the imam and hadith scholar Ali bin Muhammad, known as Mullah Ali Al-Qari. His letter included forty holy hadiths, most of which were selected from the authentic ones, but it was not devoid of weak ones, and two hadiths leaked into it. Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah went on to say that one of them is false, and that it is one of the Israelites, which is: God Almighty said: Whoever is not satisfied with My judgment, and is not patient with My affliction, let him seek a usury equal to Me. He said: Abu Ishaq Al-Huwaini: It is strange that the authentic sacred hadiths, despite their abundance, have been mentioned in this book by the author, despite his permissibility, eleven weak hadiths out of a total of forty, and this indicates the degree of his criticism, especially since he authenticated most of them, with the clarity of their reasons.
descriptions.4430: The book “Familiarity with Hadiths of Ahkam” by Ibn Daqiq al-Eid is a summary of hadith science, aiming to collect Prophetic hadiths related to jurisprudential rulings. In this book, the author is committed to citing the hadiths documented by the imams of al-Jarh and al-Ta'deel, relying on the method of preservation and jurists in correcting them. The book begins with a sermon and then addresses sequential jurisprudential topics such as purity, prayer, and zakat, citing the hadiths associated with each chapter.
descriptions.4431: The book “Al-Badr Al-Munir fi Takhrej Al-Hadith wal-Athār” by Ibn Al-Mulqin is a work on the science of hadith grading. It aims to trace the hadiths and narrations contained in the books of jurisprudence and rulings and attribute them to their original sources in the collections of the Sunnah. The author clarifies his approach to dealing with hadiths. He mentions whether the hadith is in the Two Sahihs or other books of the imams, such as Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i, relying on a wide range of hadith sources such as the books of the Companions, Al-Ilal, Al-Marsail, Al-Mawdoo’at, Parties, Ahkam, Al-Amali, in addition to books of explanations of Hadith, Al-Gharib, and jurisprudence. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue of the Prophet’s Sunnah and an explanation of its importance in explaining the Holy Qur’an, and the necessity for the hadith scholar and diligent scholar to know it in order to distinguish legal rulings.
descriptions.4432: A book on grading the hadiths that were used as evidence in controversial jurisprudential issues, in which the author mentions the Hanbali doctrine on the issue and the opposing doctrine, then shows the degree of soundness and weakness of the hadiths contained in each doctrine, relying on hadith criticism. The book aims to reveal the transmission evidence of the doctrines fairly, without bias or risk, so that the reader can know the correct one from the incorrect one in the evidence of the jurists.
descriptions.4433: The book “Encouragement and Intimidation” by the author Ismail Al-Asbahani is a book in the chapter on graduation and additions, in which his author collected hadiths and traditions that encourage good deeds and good words (encouragement) and warn against bad deeds and ugly words (intimidation), mentioning the reward and punishment mentioned in that. The author has arranged his chapters according to the letters of the dictionary (A, B, T, T) to make it easier for the student to find them, presenting in each chapter the encouragement mentioned, then the warning mentioned.
descriptions.4434: Summary of Al-Habir is a book on hadith, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani (773 AH - 852 AH). This book is one of the most honorable books and the best in its collection, classification, and arrangement. In it, its author collected the methods of hadith in one place, and spoke about them in the words of the knowledgeable, critical and insightful person, criticizing and altering them, correcting and explaining them, which indicates a broad mastery of the sciences of hadith and a comprehensive understanding of it. All of this is done with integrity and impartiality, which makes this book an essential reference for scholars of all sects, when there is a need to seek evidence.
descriptions.4435: This is a book that collects the agreed upon hadiths between the two Sahih books by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, while mentioning what is unique to each of them, arranged according to the chain of transmission of the Companions, starting with the ten who were promised Paradise and then after them. The author aims to bring the two Sahihs closer together and facilitate access to the established prophetic hadiths, limiting himself to what is authentic in their chain of transmission. The book falls within the books of graduation and additions that are concerned with collecting hadiths from their original sources.
descriptions.4436: The book “Al-Jawhar Al-Pure Ala Sunan Al-Bayhaqi” by Ibn Al-Turkmani is a book on graduation and additions, which includes comments and benefits on the book “Al-Sunan Al-Kubra” by Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi. These comments are mostly in the nature of objection, discussion, and discussion with Al-Bayhaqi in his hadiths and narrations, as the author presents some hadiths and discusses their chains of transmission and texts.
descriptions.4437: The book “Al-Dariyah fi Graduation of the Hadiths of Guidance” is a work in the science of Hadith graduation, specializing in the graduation of the Prophetic Hadiths contained in the book “Al-Hidaya” in Hanafi jurisprudence. The author begins with an introduction in which he explains his approach in summarizing the graduation of hadiths, then he begins to trace the hadiths of the jurisprudential chapters, starting with the Book of Purity and passing through the books of prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, and other books of transactions, punishments, and crimes, attributing each hadith to its original sources.
descriptions.4438: Scattered Pearls in the Famous Hadiths is one of the books of hadith, written by Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911). The book is considered an explanation of the status of some hadiths spread according to the general Sunnah and those who compared them among the jurists, and a statement of what has no basis in that and other things. Imam al-Zarkashi wrote a nice book about that, and al-Suyuti followed him with this book, so he revised what was in it, added to it, made jokes, and benefited. Al-Hafiz Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti says, explaining the reason for writing his book, Al-Durar Al-Mutanthira fi Al-Masharah Hadith:
descriptions.4439: This is a book by Imam al-Dhahabi in which he responds to al-Hafiz Ibn al-Qattan in his book “Bayan al-Whum wa al-Ihlam,” and it belongs to the books of al-Takhrij and al-Zawa’id. The book discusses a number of prophetic hadiths that were criticized by Ibn al-Qattan against al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad. Al-Dhahabi shows what is right and wrong in those criticisms, relying on the rules of criticism, modification, and criticism of narrators. It appears from the introduction that Al-Dhahabi acknowledges Ibn Al-Qattan’s erudition and intelligence, but objects to his strictness and stubbornness towards some narrators and hadiths.
descriptions.4440: The book “Al-Saarim Al-Manki fi Al-Rad Al-Subki” by Ibn Abd Al-Hadi is a book in the chapter on refuting innovators, and it falls in the classification of books of graduation and additions. The book criticizes Al-Subki’s opinions, which the author considered a victory for heresy and an attack on the Sunnah. It focuses on discussing the hadiths mentioned about visiting the grave of the Prophet ﷺ and explaining their weakness, while including benefits in the science of jarh, amendment, correcting hadiths and their weakness.
descriptions.4441: The book “Al-Fath al-Samawi bi Takhrej Al-Qadi Al-Baydawi” by Al-Manawi is a work in the science of hadith grading. Its author devoted it to grading the hadiths included in Al-Qadi Al-Baydawi’s interpretation, explaining what is in them - authentic, weak, fabricated, and unfounded. The book follows the order of the surahs of the Holy Qur’an, beginning with Surah Al-Fatihah, and presents the hadiths, mentioning their sources and chains of transmission.
descriptions.4442: This is a book of graduation and additions, compiled by Al-Suyuti as an appendix to his book “Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir”, in which it includes the Prophetic hadiths that he missed or recovered after writing it, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. The book begins by mentioning the hadiths mentioned in the letter hamza, following an approach in narrating the hadith while attributing it to its original sources such as Musnad Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others, noting the additions he added.
descriptions.4443: The book “Al-Fawa’id al-Majmu fi al-Hadith al-Mawdoo‘” by Al-Shawkani is a work of Hadith science, specializing in collecting false hadiths about the Prophet ﷺ. The author aims to distinguish the topic from the hadith, and alert scholars, preachers, and compilers to what should be avoided regarding false narratives. The book includes various jurisprudential sections, such as purity, prayer, and Hajj, in addition to books on virtues, virtues, and attributes. The author has collected in it what was included in the previous works on topics, including fabricated hadiths, while mentioning what is not correct to call the subject, but is very weak.
descriptions.4444: Al-Qawl Al-Musadd fi Al-Dhib on the authority of the Musnad of Imam Ahmad is a book by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. Al-Hafith Ibn Hajar investigated in this book the denial of fabrication in the hadiths of the Musnad, and it became clear from his research that most of them are horses, and that it is not possible to definitively fabricate any of them, or even to rule that any of them is fabricated, except for the rare individual with a strong possibility of denying that. Al-Suyuti said in the sermon of his book Al-Jami’ Al-Kabeer, the wording: Everything that is in Musnad Ahmad is acceptable, for the weak in it is close to the good.
descriptions.4445: The Book of Pearls and Coral, as agreed upon by the two Sheikhs, by Muhammad Fouad Abdel Baqi. It is one of the hadith books that collected the hadiths agreed upon in the Sahih. The size of the book is 700 pages and it was printed in three parts and then collected in one volume.
descriptions.4446: This is a brief book on the Prophetic hadiths related to legal rulings. Its author selected it from the books of famous imams, such as the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Sahihs of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, Al-Sunan, and others, and arranged it according to the chapters of jurisprudence, starting with the Book of Purity and ending with the Fear Prayer. The author took care to mention those who declared the hadith authentic or weak, and to speak about some of the narrators in terms of distortion or modification, while striving to shorten and edit terms.
descriptions.4447: A book that collects the Prophetic hadiths and their methods contained in a group of major hadith books, such as Al-Muwatta', Al-Muwatta', Al-Sunan, and Al-Sihah, arranged according to the chain of transmission of the Companions according to the letters of the dictionary. The work aims to facilitate access to the Prophetic hadiths from their original sources. The authors began with the Musnad of the Companions whose names begin with the letter Alif.
descriptions.4448: Al-Mutālib al-āliyya bi’l-Muṣānīd al-Muṣānīd al-‘Ālāya is a book of hadith books written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani (773-852), in which the author divided his work into forty-four books, then the content of each book is divided into chapters that fit the hadiths it contains, and the number of these chapters increases or decreases according to the scientific material collected. In each chapter, he presents the nominative form of the hadith, then the suspended hadith, then the interrupted ones, and so on. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani has an approach in the additions that takes precedence over other books of additions in Next: The hadith is mentioned in the extras if it was not narrated in the original. Or it was reported, but in another way. Or in the same way, but with a significant increase in the branch. …
descriptions.4449: This is a book on grading the hadiths from the book “Ihya’ Ulum al-Din” by Abu Hamid Al-Ghazali, compiled by the author, in which he summarizes the hadiths contained in Ihya’, limiting himself to mentioning the main parts of the hadith, its companions, its source, and an explanation of its degree of authenticity, goodness, or weakness, to make it easy to carry in travels. The book begins with a summary of the hadiths of the sermon and the book of knowledge, then it successively deals with books on the rules of beliefs, purity, the secrets of prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj, leading to the etiquette of reciting the Qur’an, remembrances, and supplications.
descriptions.4450: The book “Al-Maqasid Al-Hasanah fi Explaining Many of the Hadiths That Are Famous on the Languages” by Al-Hafiz Shams Al-Din Al-Sakhawi is a comprehensive work in the science of hadith grading. It aims to clarify the authenticity or weakness of hadiths spread among people, while taking care to mention the evidence, chains of transmission, and places of grading in approved books. The book is distinguished by its editing and mastery, and Ibn al-Imad al-Hanbali described it as the most comprehensive of al-Suyuti’s book “Al-Durar Al-Manthara” in this section, with the presence in each of them of what is not in the other.
descriptions.4451: The book “The True Criticism of the Objectionable Hadiths of Al-Misbah” by Al-Hafiz Salahuddin Al-Ala’i is a work in the science of hadith graduation and criticism. It deals with study and analysis of the hadiths that Imam Al-Baghawi cited in his book “Misbah Al-Sunnah” which were subject to objection and criticism by scholars. The book explains Al-Baghawi’s approach in collecting hadiths between authentic and hasan, then discusses the objections to some of those hadiths, and explains what should be judged on them in terms of authenticity, weakness, and status, based on the sayings of critics among the hadith scholars.
descriptions.4452: This is a book on the science of graduation and the study of chains of transmission, written by Ibn al-Qattan al-Fassi as a critic and corrector of the book “Al-Ahkam” by Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili. The work aims to explain the misconceptions and mistakes that the author of “Al-Ahkam” made in terms of additions and subtractions in the chains of transmission, or attributing hadiths to people other than their narrators, or raising the suspended and stopping the raised. The second section also addresses the explanation of the illusion, revealing hadiths that the author thought were disconnected while they were connected, or he attributed them with incorrect reasons, or authenticated them while they were weak, while pointing out what he overlooked regarding the conditions of the narrators and the additions to the chains of transmission.
descriptions.4453: This is a book on al-Takhreej and al-Zawa’id, annotated by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti on the book “Al-Athkar” by al-Nawawi, and picked up from al-Amali on it by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, with additions from others. The book examines the issue of acting on weak hadith regarding the virtues of deeds, encouragement, and intimidation, and mentions the conditions for that according to the hadith scholars, with a summary of the hadiths contained in dhikr and an explanation of their degree.
descriptions.4454: The book “Tuhfat Al-Ashraf Ma’rifat Al-Afara” by Al-Mazzi is a hadith encyclopedia concerned with collecting the excerpts of the hadiths contained in the six books (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami’ Al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Al-Nasa’i, and Sunan Ibn Majah) and some of their appendices, and the author arranged them according to the names of the companions who narrated those hadiths. The book aims to facilitate access to the Prophetic hadiths and to know their meanings in the original sources, while adding some additions and corrections to previous works in this art.
descriptions.4455: The book “Tuhfat al-Talib bi-Mirafa Ahadith Mukhtasar Ibn al-Hajib” is a work in the science of graduation, in which its author, Al-Hafiz Ibn Katheer, graduated the hadiths contained in the book “Mukhtasar Ibn al-Hajib” in the principles of jurisprudence. The book aims to explain the narrations of this important summary, which has received the attention of scholars, and highlights Ibn Kathir’s efforts in this art, with a study of the lives of the authors and the importance of graduation.
descriptions.4456: The book “Tuhfat al-Muhtaj ila Adalaat al-Minhaj” by Ibn al-Mulqin is a summary of hadiths on rulings, and is included in the books of graduation and additions. Its author is committed to mentioning only authentic or good hadiths, pointing out the weak ones when necessary and explaining their weakness, and attributing the hadiths to their sources such as the two Sahihs, Sunans, and Musnads. The book aims to present modern evidence for jurisprudential issues organized into the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Purity and then the Book of Prayer.
descriptions.4457: A book that aims to summarize the hadiths and hadiths contained in the interpretation of “In the Shadows of the Qur’an” by Sayyid Qutb, with an explanation of their sources and degree of authenticity. In its arrangement, the author follows the order of the surahs of the Holy Qur’an, starting with Surat Al-Fatihah, then Al-Baqarah, then Al-Imran, and so on. The introduction to the book included a response to two doubts related to the value of compiling a book that contains doctrinal errors, citing the work of previous scholars in compiling hadiths from famous books known to contain deviations.
descriptions.4458: The book “Graduation of Hadiths and Traditions of the Tafsir Al-Kashshaf” by the author Jamal Al-Din Al-Zayla’i, which is one of the books of Al-Takhrej and Al-Zayla’i. The book aims to summarize the hadiths and traces that were mentioned in Al-Kashshaf’s interpretation by Al-Zamakhshari, following them surah by surah from Surat Al-Fatihah until Surat An-Naml. The author begins by mentioning the hadith or hadith, then explains its degree and sources, criticizing some narrations and explaining what is correct in them.
descriptions.4459: This is a book on grading the hadiths and narrations contained in the book “Minhaj al-Usul” by Judge Nasser al-Din al-Baydawi. The author, Ibn al-Mulqin, compiled it for the sake of brevity, beginning by talking about the hadiths before the narrations. The book aims to explain the source of the hadiths mentioned in the curriculum and study them, relying on the scientific graduation method. The author has arranged it in the order of the hadiths mentioned in the original, starting with the first hadith.
descriptions.4460: The book “Taghleeq Al-Malqa’ ala Sahih Al-Bukhari” is a work in the science of hadith that falls within the books of graduation and additions, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. In this book, the author aims to connect the outstanding hadiths that Imam Al-Bukhari mentioned in his Sahih without a complete chain of transmission, by explaining their chain of transmission through other paths. The book covers multiple sections of Sahih al-Bukhari, starting with the Book of the Beginning of Revelation, the Book of Faith, the Book of Knowledge, and the Book of Purity, with a focus on verifying the hadiths and explaining their reasons and connections.
descriptions.4461: This book, “Alert the wise man to the invalidity of what has spread among people,” by Sheikh Muhammad Ahmad Abd al-Qadir al-Shanqeeti al-Madani, is part of the classification of graduate books and appendices. The book deals with the subject of the hadith attributed to Abd al-Razzaq’s work, which is called the Hadith of Light, and indicates that this hadith is considered a falsehood that has no basis in health. The book aims to prove the falsity of this hadith and determine the reasons for its falsity. It also addresses some of the most important characteristics of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, such as his many virtues and virtues.
descriptions.4462: The book “Alert the Reader to Strengthen What Al-Albani Weaked” by the author Abdullah Al-Dawish is a work in the field of graduation and additions, aiming to discuss some hadith rulings by the scholar Nasser Al-Din Al-Albani. The author provides warnings and corrections for errors that occurred in the rulings on authentication and weakness, dividing the hadiths he dealt with into three categories: hadiths that the author authenticated, hadiths whose chains of transmission were not found, and hadiths that Sheikh Al-Albani weakened in one place and authenticated in other places. The book explains the scholars’ approach to pointing out errors without compromising scientific respect, based on multiple methods and evidence to strengthen hadiths.
descriptions.4463: A book that aims to correct errors and distortions in the names of the men of chain of transmission within the book “Majma’ al-Zawa’id and Manba’ al-Fawa’id” by Al-Hafiz al-Haythami. The author relies on reviewing the origins of manuscripts and men’s books to show what is correct in the distorted names or the Qur’an, arranging his notes according to the letters of the dictionary. This work is considered a scientific service for controlling the texts of one of the most important collections of the Sunnah of the Prophet, which collects additions to the six books.
descriptions.4464: The book “Revision of Investigation into the Commentary Hadiths” is a book on the grading of hadiths, written by Ibn Abd al-Hadi, and it is a refinement and commentary on the book “The Investigation” by Ibn al-Jawzi on the Hadiths of Ahkam. The author aims to study the hadiths that jurists cite as evidence, while talking about them, correcting and weakening them, according to the approach of the earlier hadith scholars, and is characterized by fairness and distance from sectarian fanaticism. This book is considered one of the most important graduation books that helps the student of knowledge learn how to judge hadiths and study the chains of transmission practically.
descriptions.4465: A book on graduation and additions, which aims to trace the errors and misconceptions that occurred in some hadith books, with a focus on criticizing hadith rulings. The book includes scientific material collected by the author from his works and investigations, and presents examples of the delusions that occurred to Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, such as his claim that the hadith is according to the conditions of the two sheikhs even though it is not authentic, or his saying that they narrated it even though they did not narrate it.
descriptions.4466: The book “Alert Al-Hajid to What Happened from Considering the Books of the Majid” is a book on the science of graduation and additions, compiled by its author from his works, investigations, and graduations, to be an independent book in six volumes. The book deals with explaining the delusions that occurred in some books of hadith, such as Al-Hakim’s delusions in “Al-Mustadrak,” which the author enumerated in various types, such as claiming the condition of the two sheikhs or one of them in hadiths that are not according to their condition, or correcting incorrect hadiths. The author had previously published part of this book containing five hundred traces, then completed it and made it an independent book.
descriptions.4467: Jami` al-Usul fi the Hadiths of the Messenger is one of the books of the mosques, a major collection of hadiths, by its author, Majd al-Din Abu al-Saadat al-Mubarak ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Karim al-Shaybani al-Jazari ibn al-Atheer, in which he referred to the hadiths included in the five principles with Muwatta Malik that are approved by jurists and hadith scholars, and which contained most of what was authentic about the Prophet, so he collected them all in one work, after arranging them, refining them, and approximating their usefulness, and Imam Ibn al-Dayba` al-Shaybani summarized it in his book. Facilitating access to the comprehensive origins of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.4468: The book “Jami’ al-Musnad wa al-Sunan al-Guidance to the Most Righteous Sunan” by Ibn Katheer is a hadith encyclopedia of books of graduation and additions, in which its author collected the prophetic hadiths contained in the Musnad and Sunan, arranged according to the names of the companions who were narrators of the hadith, beginning with the letter alif. The book aims to bring the Prophet’s Sunnah closer together and facilitate access to it. It is distinguished by its arrangement methodology that combines the Musnads and Sunnahs in one work, with an introduction that the author opens with praise and praise to God and prayers upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
descriptions.4469: This book, “Collecting the benefits from Jami’ al-Usul and Majma’ al-Zawa’id,” is written by the scholar Muhammad bin Sulaiman al-Maghribi. It contains prophetic hadiths collected from the books of Jami’ al-Usul by Muhaddith al-Dailami, and Majma’ al-Zawa’id by al-Haythami, in addition to Razin’s additions. The author has graduated, corrected, and arranged the hadiths according to jurisprudential chapters, which makes him a useful reference in the field of hadith science and graduation.
descriptions.4470: The book “Khulasat al-Ahkam fi Mihmat al-Sunan wa al-Qa’id al-Islam” by Imam al-Nawawi is a book of graduation and additions, aiming to distinguish authentic hadiths from weak ones in the sections of Islamic jurisprudence and etiquette. The author begins with an introduction that emphasizes the necessity of following the authentic Sunnah and warning against acting on weak hadiths in rulings. Then he begins to mention the hadiths related to purity, ablution, wiping over the socks, and other acts of worship, detailing the sections and chapters and explaining what is authentic and what is weak.
descriptions.4471: This book is “Khulasat Al-Badr Al-Munir” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Al-Mulqin. It is a summary that aims to index the hadiths contained in his larger book, “Al-Badr Al-Munir,” which is concerned with compiling hadiths and talking about their reasons and the narrators of their chains of transmission. The book falls within the books of graduation and additions, and it is arranged in the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the book of purity and ending with the book of the eclipse prayer, with references to the places of hadiths in other graduation books.
descriptions.4472: This book is a follow-up to the book “Al-Qawl Al-Musadd fi Al-Dhab from Al-Musnad” by Imam Ahmad. It is included in the books of Al-Takhraj and Al-Zawa’id, and is written by Sibhatullah Al-Madrasi Al-Hindi. The author aims to trace the hadiths that Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani missed in his studies on Al-Hafiz Al-Iraqi, completing what he began by defending the hadiths contained in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal. The book begins by mentioning the hadiths that Al-Hafiz Al-Suyuti referred to in his book “Al-Nukat Al-Badi’at Ala Al-Mawdoo’at” and which Ibn Al-Jawzi claimed to have fabricated, so the author summarizes them and explains their condition.
descriptions.4473: This book is a graduate thesis by Imam Al-Dhahabi, in which he collected the methods of the hadith “Whoever I am his master, then Ali is his master” contained in the virtue of Imam Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). The book falls within the books of graduation and additions, as the author aims to trace the narrations of this hadith and its various chains of narration, indicating the strength or weakness in them, according to the hadith critical approach. The verified copy included an introduction prepared by the investigator, indicating that this work is part of a scientific heritage that was prepared after the death of the original investigator.
descriptions.4474: This is a scientific book that studies the additions of Abu Bakr al-Quta’i on the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, narrated by his son Abdullah, and he graduates and studies them. The book is divided into two main chapters, the first of which deals with a fundamental study to introduce Al-Qati’i and his additions, the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, and the narrators’ additions in general, while the second chapter is devoted to grading a number of hadiths that Al-Qati’i was unique in his narration of the Musnad.
descriptions.4475: The book “Ghayat al-Maqsad fi Zawa’id al-Musnad” by the author Nour al-Din al-Haythami is a book on the science of graduation and additions, in which the author collected the hadiths that were unique to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in his Musnad from the six books, with the addition of what his son Abdullah ibn Ahmad and al-Nasa’i added in his major Sunan. The author arranged these additions to the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Faith, and mentioned in his introduction his approach to citing the entire hadith or limiting himself to adding to it, with reference to what other hadith scholars narrated.
descriptions.4476: The book “Fath al-Ghaffar al-Jami` li-Ahkam al-Ahkam al-Sunnah of our Chosen Prophet” is a vast hadith encyclopedia of books of graduation and appendices. Its four-volume book collected between its two covers most of the hadiths that contain the focus of legal rulings, and it is considered one of the most extensive books classified in this section. The book aims to serve the hadiths of rulings in terms of collecting them, explaining their chains of transmission, and judging them as whether they are sound or weak. The number of its original hadiths reached (6529) hadiths, without additions and differences in wording.
descriptions.4477: The book “Revealing the Covers of the Additives of Al-Bazzar” by Al-Hafiz Nour Al-Din Al-Haythami is a book on the science of graduation and additions, in which the author collects the extra hadiths that were unique to Musnad Al-Bazzar from the six books and other principles of hadith. The book begins with the Book of Faith, covering various sections such as monotheism, the truth of faith, its characteristics, whispering, night journey, hypocrisy, polytheism, and other doctrinal and behavioral topics, extracting hadiths with their chains of transmission from Musnad al-Bazzar.
descriptions.4478: Revealing the hidden things and eliminating confusion about the famous hadiths on the tongues of the people is a book of hadiths, written by Imam Ismail Al-Ajlouni (1087-1162). The book is considered one of the most extensive and comprehensive books in explaining the famous hadiths. Its author benefited from the scholars who preceded him in classifying in this field, and added many hadiths from his own, and one of the most important sources on which he relied was the book Al-Maqasid Al-Hasanah by Al-Hafiz Al-Sakhawi. Imam Al-Ajlouni did not limit himself in his book to the famous hadiths. He presented hadiths that were not well-known, and concluded his book in which he invalidated the attribution of some works that were known to be falsely attributed to people, and he concluded by stating comprehensive controls on the topics. The book Kashf al-Khifa included approximately 3,281 hadiths. …
descriptions.4479: Revealing the hidden things and eliminating confusion about the famous hadiths on the tongues of the people is a book of hadiths, written by Imam Ismail Al-Ajlouni (1087-1162). The book is considered one of the most extensive and comprehensive books in explaining the famous hadiths. Its author benefited from the scholars who preceded him in classifying in this field, and added many hadiths from his own, and one of the most important sources on which he relied was the book Al-Maqasid Al-Hasanah by Al-Hafiz Al-Sakhawi. Imam Al-Ajlouni did not limit himself in his book to the famous hadiths. He presented hadiths that were not well-known, and concluded his book in which he invalidated the attribution of some works that were known to be falsely attributed to people, and he concluded by stating comprehensive controls on the topics. The book Kashf al-Khifa included approximately 3,281 hadiths. …
descriptions.4480: The book, Kanz Al-Ummal, whose full name is “Kanz Al-Ummal fi Sunan Al-Aqwal Al-A’wal”. It is a book on hadith. Written by Aladdin Ali Al-Muttaqi bin Hussam Al-Din Al-Hindi Al-Burhan Fawri, known as Al-Muttaqi Al-Hindi. Its author combined the two books, Al-Jami’ Al-Saghir and its appendices, and Al-Suyuti’s book Collecting Al-Jami’. Thus, he included about fifty thousand hadiths devoid of chains of transmission and attributed to the companion, the narrator of the hadith, or to someone who narrated the hadith in the books of the Sunnah. The author has arranged the hadiths in the book into jurisprudential sections. The author himself spoke about the reason for writing the book, saying:
descriptions.4481: Majma’ al-Zawa’id and Manba’ al-Fawa’id is one of the books of hadith, in which Al-Hafiz al-Haythami collected additions: Musnad Ahmad, Musnad al-Bazzar, Musnad Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili, and the three dictionaries of al-Tabarani. On the six books, he deleted their chains of transmission. Before writing Majma’ al-Zawa’id, he had classified the additions of each book separately, while keeping the chains of transmission and explaining them as follows: The Bahrain Council on the additions of the two dictionaries (the middle and small dictionaries). Al-Badr Al-Munir in the additions to the great dictionary by Al-Tabarani. Uncovering the curtains in the appendages of the seedbed. The most rational purpose in the additions to the Musnad of Imam Ahmad. The highest saying in the additions of Musnad Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili. His sheikh, Zain al-Din Abu al-Fadl Abd al-Rahim bin al-Iraqi, advised him and said to him:
descriptions.4482: Misbah al-Zajjah fi Zawa'id Ibn Majah is a book on the science of hadith and one of the books of hadith, written by Imam Shihab al-Din al-Busayri (762 AH - 839 AH). In his book, the author specializes in the additions mentioned in Sunan Ibn Majah and not mentioned in the remaining five Sahihs: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Abu Dawud, mentioning the extra hadith or the hadith with the extra places in it while mentioning its evidence, arranged according to Sunan Ibn Majah.
descriptions.4483: Raising the banner for the Hadiths of Guidance by Sheikh Imam Hadith Abdullah Al-Zayla’i, in which Imam Al-Zayla’i included the hadiths contained in the Book of Guidance, and the Book of Guidance is a book on Hanafi jurisprudence written by the scholar Burhan Al-Din Ali bin Abi Bakr Al-Marghinani Al-Hanafi, who died in the year 593 AH. Al-Zayla’i did not limit himself to grading the Hadiths of Guidance, but rather embellished it by clarifying the evidence of the opponents.
descriptions.4484: A book that examines the hadith “My companions are like the stars,” which is famous in the books of the principles of jurisprudence, and reviews six different narrations of this hadith, and discusses them in terms of the chain of transmission to show the extent of their authenticity, weakness, or status, relying on the sayings of the scholars who conveyed and compiled their sayings about it.
descriptions.4485: This is a book on the science of hadith, which specializes in collecting frequent hadiths and organizing them. Its author has arranged it according to the various chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the hadith, “Actions are but by intentions,” then dealing with the topics of knowledge, faith, purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, and other rulings, leading to the book The Beginning of Creation and the Virtues of the Qur’an. The book aims to highlight hadiths that have reached the degree of frequency in various sections of religion, making it a reference in this special type of hadith sciences.
descriptions.4486: The book “Nawader Al-Usul Fi Hadiths of the Messenger ﷺ” by Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi is one of the books of graduation and additions. It collects noble prophetic hadiths and arranges them under multiple principles. The book begins with an explanation of protection from a scorpion sting and the word for seeking refuge with complete words, covering various topics such as anger, the etiquette of wearing one’s clothes, the prohibition of disgust, and the influence of the believing eye. The author aims to explain the meanings of hadiths and explain the rulings and benefits they contain, while linking them to religious and practical principles.
descriptions.4487: This is a linguistic book that studies the tense system in the Arabic language through comparison with other languages. It divides tenses into simple and compound, and details their types such as the absolute past, the absolute present, and the absolute future, in addition to the restricted tenses such as the recent past, the fictional past, and the pending future. The author begins his book by explaining the importance of tenses and their relationship to action, pointing out that Arabic scholars did not devote a special section to each tense form as in other languages, attributing this to their lack of familiarity with foreign languages ​​that might raise the need for such details.
descriptions.4488: This is an educational study on the science of writing hamza words, organized by the author Mahmoud Abu Saree to be a basis for writing hamza. The book is organized into three sections: the primary hamza, the intermediate hamza, and the extreme hamza, mentioning the exceptions and arranging the movements in terms of strength to determine the form of the hamza.
descriptions.4489: This is a book organized into punctuation marks, explained by author Mahmoud Abu Saree in a poetic, educational style. The system aims to bring closer the rules of punctuation and its benefits to students, as it enumerates signs such as the comma, period, and question marks, and explains the places where they are used in writing. The book begins with an introduction to the virtue of punctuation and its importance in distinguishing parts of speech and clarifying meaning, and then moves on to explain each sign separately with examples.
descriptions.4490: This is a linguistic book concerned with the phenomenon of substitution in the Arabic language, as it studies words in which letters are replaced by others with similar or different meanings. The book is organized into multiple sections that classify words according to the letters they exchange, such as nun and lam, ba and meem, ayn and hamza, and other literal pairs. In his material, the author relies on narrations by linguists such as Al-Asma’i and Abu Amr Al-Shaibani, while citing ancient Arab poetry to demonstrate linguistic uses.
descriptions.4491: A book on teaching Arabic spelling rules. It aims to develop learners’ spelling skills and train them to draw words correctly. The book covers basic dictation topics such as madd, tanween, marbuta and fatha ta’, solar and lunar lam, in addition to the rules of hamza, wasl and qat’ hamzas, and punctuation marks, with applied examples for typical lessons.
descriptions.4492: This is a linguistic dictionary specialized in correcting common errors in the language of Arabic media in its broad sense, whether written, audio, or visual. The author relies in his approach on presenting consistent grammatical and morphological rules and prioritizing irregular usages, with the aim of preserving the unity of the Arabic language. The dictionary begins by addressing errors related to the letter hamza and then the letter b, correcting and correcting a number of words and phrases in which errors are common.
descriptions.4493: This is a book that studies the biography of Abu Turab, the linguist, and his lost book, “Al-Itqab,” and collects his texts scattered in ancient linguistic sources, such as “Tahdheeb Al-Lughah” by Al-Azhari. The research falls into two parts: the first deals with the author’s translation, his scientific life, the methodology of his book, its sources, and its scientific value, and the second includes the texts collected from the book arranged in chapters according to the letters of the dictionary.
descriptions.4494: The book “Akhbar Al-Mushafin” by Al-Hafiz Al-Askari is a book in the language. It collects news and narrations about corruption in the language, the Qur’an, and the Hadith. It cites sayings from the predecessors warning against taking from the Mushafs and journalists, while mentioning examples of corruption in names and narrations.
descriptions.4495: This is a book in the Arabic language that studies common linguistic errors in contemporary usage, especially among writers and radio broadcasters. It begins with an introduction and preface that explains the motivation for its writing and examples of errors. Then, in its chapters, it deals with phonological and pronunciation errors, such as confusion between voiced and whispered sounds, and morphological errors, such as errors of pluralism, pluralism, and attribution. The book aims to monitor and classify these errors with the aim of correcting the language and raising the level of classical language in the media and writing.
descriptions.4496: The book “Arabic Secrets” by Abu Al-Barakat Al-Anbari is a book on the science of Arabic grammar, organized into sequential chapters covering the rules of parsing and construction, the rulings on nouns and verbs, types of objects, infinitives, adverbs, distinctions, and other basic grammatical topics. The book aims to explain the subtleties of the Arabic language and its grammatical secrets in a systematic educational manner.
descriptions.4497: The book “Foundations of Linguistics” by Ahmed Mukhtar Omar is a foundational work in the field of linguistic studies, classified as language books. In its first section, the book presents basic issues in linguistics, addressing the differences between it and philology, the characteristics of the spoken language, and the various levels of linguistic analysis such as sounds, morphology, grammar, and semantics, in addition to the classification of languages ​​and their geographical distribution. The second section specializes in descriptive linguistics, explaining its basic terms such as phonemes, morphemes, and grammatical structure, according to the information available from the table of contents and the excerpt.
descriptions.4498: This book deals with the emergence and development of Arabic science in Medina, tracing the factors behind the emergence of the linguistic lesson there, such as the phenomenon of melody and the protection of the Qur’an. It sheds light on the most prominent founders of this science among the companions and followers, such as Ali bin Abi Talib and Abu Al-Aswad Al-Du’ali. It also presents the notables of the linguistic study in Medina and its various manifestations, including writings and grammatical and linguistic issues, in response to those who denied the existence of a linguistic or grammatical Imamate for the people of Medina.
descriptions.4499: Islah al-Logic by Ibn al-Sakit. This book is considered a linguistic dictionary, one of the oldest dictionaries that control the language using forms. It is one of the sources of the linguistic heritage that deals with what has occurred in the Arabic language in terms of melody and errors, and in it it collects words that agree in the same meter with a difference in meaning, or that differ in it with an agreement in meaning, and what is valid and what is valid, and what is sung and what is not sung, and other linguistic control chapters. It explains the word in Arabic, supporting the explanation with the Qur’an, the Prophet’s hadiths, and poetry. And Arabic proverbs, and this book makes a great effort to correct the linguistic errors that are common among people
descriptions.4500: The book “Clarification of the Evidence of Clarification” by Abu Ali Al-Qaisi is a linguistic explanation of the evidence of the book “Al-Idah” by Abu Ali Al-Farsi. It aims to clarify the positions of the witness in poetic verses, and explain their meanings and parsing, while attributing them to those who said them. The book is organized into language sections, explaining each poetic line in terms of language, meaning, and parsing, using proverbs and rare stories to complete its usefulness.
descriptions.4501: This book examines the educational implications of studying the Arabic language, reviewing its role in developing verbal flair, cognitive acquisition, and intellectual and moral education. The author starts from the importance of the Arabic language as the language of the Holy Qur’an and a vessel for knowledge and civilization, and focuses on educational care for its sciences and their impact on refining souls and educating minds.
descriptions.4502: This is a book in the Arabic language, in which the author collected words and phrases used in the arts of writing and expression, and arranged them into sections and demands that include exports, brotherhoods, congratulations, condolences, requests, and other matters. The book aims to provide a linguistic repertoire of eloquent words and consistent meanings, which helps the writer to formulate messages and texts in an eloquent manner.
descriptions.4503: This is a linguistic book that studies the phenomenon of phonetic substitution in the dialects of the Arabic Azd tribe, based on the method of modern linguistics. The author divides his study into two main chapters: the first deals with the substitution of consonants (consonants), whether in nicknamed languages ​​such as Istiṭānā and Tamānīyah, or in unnamed languages, such as replacing the ta with a dal or ha, and the second examines the substitution in vowels (consonants), such as the substitution between fatha and kasra in the present tense letters and the adjacent lam. The research aims to collect and analyze the differences between these linguistic phenomena in various heritage sources, shedding light on an important aspect of the dialects of this ancient Arab tribe.
descriptions.4504: The book “Al-Ittiba’” by Al-Suyuti is a linguistic work that examines the phenomenon of “Al-Itti’ab” in the Arabic language, which is when a word is followed by another word according to its weight or narration for emphasis and satisfaction, such as their saying “thirsty, thirsty.” The book begins with the definition of following, quoting Ibn Faris and Abu Ubaid, then discusses the difference between following and tandem, and mentions examples and evidence from the words of the Arabs and the Prophet’s hadith, while stating the opinions of scholars on this linguistic phenomenon.
descriptions.4505: This is a book on the rules of spelling and punctuation in Arabic writing. It presents the general controls for drawing letters in their different positions, covering the topics of the hamza, the soft alif, deleted and extra letters, and punctuation marks, with a section dedicated to talking about spelling in the educational field, its goals and types. The author aims to facilitate knowledge of the correct rules for drawing words for students, teachers, and writing workers, while pointing out the disagreement among scholars about some of the rules.
descriptions.4506: This is a book that deals with the history of linguistic studies among the Arabs from its early inception until the fifth century AH, when lexical trends were completed and the study of grammar, morphology, and phonetics reached its peak. The book includes three sections, the first of which is devoted to introductory studies on the sources of Arab linguists and linguistic studies among non-Arabs, the second of which deals with the stages of development of Arabic linguistic studies in sounds, grammar, morphology, and lexicon, and the third of which discusses the issue of influence and influence between Arabic and foreign linguistic efforts.
descriptions.4507: The book “Linguistics to the Origins of the Language” by Muhammad Siddiq Hassan Khan is a study in philology, aiming to explain the origins of the Arabic language and its topics. The book is divided into two parts, the first deals with topics of philology, while the second deals with other aspects of linguistic study. This edition was edited as part of an academic dissertation.
descriptions.4508: This is a book that studies the efforts of Al-Ragheb Al-Isfahani in the field of language, and reviews his opinions on linguistic issues such as synonymy and derivation, with a focus on highlighting his scientific standing, which the author believes has not received its due study. The book also addresses the problem of determining Al-Raghib’s era and the date of his death, trying to provide a preliminary picture of his life and his intellectual and linguistic efforts.
descriptions.4509: The book “Al-Sahibi in the jurisprudence of the Arabic language and its issues and the Sunnahs of the Arabs in its speech” by Ibn Faris is a book in the sciences of the Arabic language. It deals with the origins of the Arabic language and its origins, and details the saying about its characteristics and virtues, the levels of its speech, and its divisions of nouns, verbs, and letters. It examines issues of derivation, nouns, and how they apply to nouns, within sequential chapters that begin with introductions to languages, their eloquence, and Arabic script.
descriptions.4510: This book, “Al-Lubab fi Grammar and Literary Tools” by Al-Sarraj, deals with the sciences of the Arabic language such as grammar, morphology, rhetoric, prosody, language, and proverbs. The author aims to simplify these sciences and facilitate their understanding for students, by collecting them in one book and explaining them with examples, verses of poetry, and parsing, with a focus on their practical and applied aspects. The book is divided into three sections: the first on grammar and morphology, the second on rhetoric and prosody, and the third on language and proverbs.
descriptions.4511: A book on Arabic linguistics that combines the study of the phonetic, morphological, and grammatical systems of the language, with a focus on the relationship between meaning and structure. The author provides an analysis of the parts of speech, commentary clues, and contextual phenomena, based on a descriptive approach that aims to understand classical Arabic and renew its consideration.
descriptions.4512: This is a book on linguistics written by the British linguist John Lyons, and it is intended for intellectuals and specialists alike. The first part deals with five basic chapters in purely descriptive linguistics. It begins with the definition of language and its nature, then reviews the branches of linguistics and its methodology, moves on to the study of language sounds and its grammatical rules, and concludes with research in semantics.
descriptions.4513: The book "Language" by Joseph Vendrys is a comprehensive linguistic study that deals with language from its phonetic, grammatical, and lexical aspects, with research into its origin and development, the formation of dialects and lingua franca, in addition to the emergence and development of writing. The author aims to present a modern scientific vision of language as a social system influenced by and influencing society, calling for going beyond traditional approaches to the study of languages, especially Arabic, to keep pace with the modern era.
descriptions.4514: This is a book on linguistics and linguistic research methods. It begins with defining language and its importance, then studies the topics of the human voice and description of sounds, the emergence of human language according to multiple schools of thought, and the relationship of linguistics to society, the psyche, and linguistic geography. The book reviews three main approaches to linguistic research: the descriptive, historical, and comparative approaches, with special attention to applications of the comparative approach.
descriptions.4515: Al-Mizhar in the Sciences of Language and its Types, a book by the scholar Abd al-Rahman Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. He said: In the introduction to the book, this is an honorable science. I invented its arrangement, and its diversification and classification. This is in the sciences of language and its types, and the conditions for its performance and listening. I have imitated the sciences of hadith in its divisions and types, and brought in it wonderful wonders and curiosities of great creativity. Many of those who came forward were knowledgeable about things like this, and took care in explaining them by paving the way, but no one preceded me to this collection, nor did Tariq follow its path before me. He divided it into fifty types.
descriptions.4516: A book that collects research and articles in the sciences of the Arabic language, which the author previously published in scientific journals and presented at conferences, then revised and arranged them into sections and chapters. It covers various topics, including language sounds and structures, the origins of linguistic protest, the history of classical Arabic and its challenges, linguistic research methods, and the characteristics of ancient Arabic dialects and their extension into contemporary dialects.
descriptions.4517: The book “The Corrections of the Modernists” by Abu Ahmad Al-Askari is a specialized linguistic work that aims to address and correct errors that occur in controlling words, especially those related to the words of the Prophet’s Hadith and the names of narrators. The author explains the problematic names and words that are similar in handwriting, leading to misprints, and shows how to adjust them in shape and dots so that hadith narrators and news transmitters avoid them. The author extracted this book from his large book on misprints, and limited it to what hadith scholars need, arranging it into sections that include suspected names, along with their explanations and an explanation of the narrators who are famous for them.
descriptions.4518: This book is a lecture delivered by the author to a group of Al-Azhar professors, in which he studied and analyzed the subject of the Talmud from a linguistic and terminological standpoint. The author examines the origin of the word “Talmud” in the Hebrew language and its derivations, and explains the difference between the Jewish sects in belief in it, and also presents some of the provisions and beliefs contained in the Talmud.
descriptions.4519: The book “Studies on the Origins of the Arabic Languages” by Abdul Aziz Al-Qari is a linguistic research that deals with the subject of the origin of the Arabs and the origins and development of the Arabic language. The author begins by discussing the virtue of the Arabic language and God’s choice of the Arab nation to carry the message. Then he studies the origin of the Qahtani and Adnani Arab tribes and the stages of development of the Arabic language. The book aims to provide a comprehensive study of the roots of the Arabic language and the tribes that spoke it, relying on linguistic comparison and research into the origins of the tribes.
descriptions.4520: A book that brings together seven linguistic topics that address phonetic, morphological, and grammatical issues in the Arabic language. Some of them are derived from the heritage of ancient linguists, such as the study of the alif, waw, yā’, hamzat al-wasl, and sukun, and some are new, such as common errors in the sentence system among university students. In treating it, the author adopts an objective, descriptive approach based on analyzing linguistic reality without interpretation or assumption, combining care for the ancient and presenting it in light of the modern linguistic lesson.
descriptions.4521: This is a book on philology, examining the origins and development of this science among the Arabs, and its relationship to modern linguistics. The book deals with the characteristics of classical Arabic and its position among its Semitic sisters, with a study of its most important ancient and modern dialects. In its third edition, the author also presents the topic of formulas and meters, and the status of Arabic in the modern era, criticizing the suspicions raised around it.
descriptions.4522: This is a book in Arabic linguistic studies, which deals with research and analysis of three of the most important language books: “Al-Sahibi in the jurisprudence of language” by Ibn Faris, “Al-Khasa’is” by Ibn Jinni, and “Al-Mizhar.” The author begins with a fundamental introduction to the emergence and development of Arabic linguistic studies, explaining its ancient and modern concept, then moves on to study each of these books in a simplified, objective study.
descriptions.4523: Durrat al-Ghawwas fi Iwham al-Khawas is a book written by al-Hariri in linguistic interpretations. This book has several explanations and footnotes, which are full of warnings about al-Hariri’s delusions and fallacies, including: Tahdheeb al-Khawwas from Durrat al-Ghaws by Ibn Manzur, in response to al-Hariri The sequel and tail to Durrat al-Ghaws by al-Jawaliqi Footnotes on Durrat al-Ghaws by Ibn Bari and Ibn Dhafar Al-Saqali Al-Mulahin by Ibn Duraid Sharh Durrat Al-Ghawas fi Awham Al-Khawas by Al-Khafaji. The book was printed for the first time in Al-Jawa’ib Press in the year 1291 AH, and many editions followed that.
descriptions.4524: The book “The Secret of Syntax Industry” by Abu Al-Fath Othman bin Jinni is an author on the sciences of the Arabic language. His subject tends to study the language and its sounds more than he is interested in abstract grammatical rules. The author adopts an approach based on arranging the letters of the dictionary alphabetically. He analyzes each letter from multiple phonetic aspects, such as loudness and whispering, occlusion and openness, tightness and softness, describing the characteristics of each letter and the substitutions, deletions, or additions it contains. The book aims to reveal the causes and secrets behind the linguistic and phonetic phenomena in the structure of the Arabic word.
descriptions.4525: The book “The Arrow of Words in the Illusion of Words” by Ibn al-Hanbali is an appendix and commentary on the book “Durrat al-Ghaws fi Illusions al-Khawas” by al-Hariri, and is included among the language books. The author is concerned with tracking down the words in which linguistic errors and errors occur, whether specific or common, so he mentions the word and explains what is correct in it, dealing with a number of Arabized, extraneous, and incorrectly used words.
descriptions.4526: This is a specialized linguistic book that studies the form of “fa’lan” and the uses that stem from it in the Arabic language. It deals with it in the chapters on the infinitive, knowledge, and adjective, and looks at the rulings on its plural, morphological, and diminutive forms, citing examples of eloquent Arabic usage and colloquial dialects.
descriptions.4527: This is a book on Arabic linguistics, which aims to present the general foundations of historical and comparative research in the Arabic language, based on the general theory of modern linguistics and the Arabic linguistic heritage. The book addresses various topics, including the nature and function of language, branches of modern linguistics such as comparative, descriptive, and historical, in addition to linguistic sciences in the Arab heritage and the grammatical library.
descriptions.4528: The book “Linguistics: An Introduction to the Arab Reader” by Mahmoud Al-Saran is a foundational work in the field of linguistic studies, aiming to present this science to the Arab reader in a systematic manner. The book deals with the subject of linguistics and its essence. It examines the origins of language and its nature as a system of signs. It also devotes a separate chapter to linguistic phonology, including its history, the mechanism of pronunciation, and the classification of sounds. The author also reviews the relationship of linguistics with other sciences, such as psychology, and sheds light on the reality of linguistic studies in the literary East and the obstacles it faces.
descriptions.4529: Linguistics, linguistics, or linguistics is the scientific study of a language. Linguistics depends on the theoretical study as well as the descriptive study of a language, and is linked to the applied fields of language studies and learning, which entails the study of specific languages. Before the twentieth century, linguistics developed alongside literary study and did not use scientific methods. Modern linguistics is considered a science because it involves a comprehensive, systematic, objective, and precise analysis of all aspects of language, such as cognitive, social, cultural, psychological, environmental, biological, literary, grammatical, paleographic, and structural aspects. …
descriptions.4530: Philology and the secret of Arabic. A book written by Abd al-Malik bin Muhammad bin Ismail Abu Mansour al-Tha’alabi on the sciences of the Arabic language. It is considered one of his most famous works after his book “The Orphan of Time.”
descriptions.4531: The book “Research Methods in Language” by Tammam Hassan is a work in the field of linguistic studies, dealing with issues of methodology in the study of language. The book begins with a general introduction to the need for a linguistic approach, then moves on to detailing the approaches to studying linguistic sounds in terms of their forms and characteristics (phonics), and the approach to studying the phonetic and functional system of language (phonology), touching on concepts such as linguistic sound, phoneme, and syllable.
descriptions.4532: This is a linguistic book that studies the phenomenon of the death of words in classical Arabic. It deals with nouns and verbs whose use was abandoned in the eras of linguistic protest, and examines the reasons for their death, such as phonetic, semantic, and social factors. Then it looks at the possibility of reviving these dead words and the position of scholars and language academies on that.
descriptions.4533: The book “Minutes of Warning and Introducing the Errors and Corrections in the Selected Hadiths” is a work specialized in criticizing and verifying hadith texts, aiming to correct the errors and distortions that occurred in the first edition of the book “The Selected Hadiths” by Al-Hafiz Al-Dia’ Al-Maqdisi. The author mentions a number of repeated errors in the names of the narrators and their genealogies, along with an explanation of what is correct in them. The book begins with a brief translation by Imam Al-Dhia Al-Maqdisi.
descriptions.4534: This book collects one hundred hadiths with missing chains of transmission from all the circulating editions of Sunan al-Nasa’i. These hadiths were included in an old Moroccan copy, narrated by Hamza al-Kinani on the authority of al-Nasa’i, and they are distributed in various places in the book, such as purity and prayer. The work aims to prove these additions that have not been proven in publications, while mentioning the numbers of the hadiths and their original locations.
descriptions.4535: A book that collects hadiths narrated on the authority of Imam Abu Hanifa al-Numan, narrated by Al-Hasakfi, and is classified among the hadith texts. The book includes various sections that include faith, Islam, destiny, intercession, purity, prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, marriage, divorce, punishments, jihad, sales, and other jurisprudential rulings, etiquette, slavery, and virtues. The book begins with the chapter on faith and Islam, including a hadith about Gabriel’s question (peace be upon him) to the Prophet ﷺ about faith and Islam.
descriptions.4536: Musnad Ishaq bin Rahawayh is a book of Musnad in the Prophet’s hadith, and its author is Ishaq bin Rahawayh.
descriptions.4537: The book “The Hadiths of the Trustworthy Sheikhs of the Great Sheikhs” is a work on hadith texts, compiled by Qadi al-Maristan, and includes chains of transmission and narrations from a large number of trustworthy sheikhs, arranged in multiple parts. The book begins by mentioning the author’s sheikhdom and his narrations from his sheikhs, such as Abu Muhammad al-Jawhari and others, including prophetic hadiths supported by their continuous chains of transmission. The book aims to collect the hadiths that the author narrated from his sheikhs through authorization or hearing, which makes it an important source in the science of sheikhs and hadith parts.
descriptions.4538: The book “Akhbar Mecca in Ancient and Modern Times” by Al-Fakihi is a hadith compilation that collects hadiths and monuments related to Mecca, and specifically mentions the virtues of the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner and the rulings on receiving them, kissing them, and circumambulating the Kaaba. The book includes detailed sections on the virtue of the pillars, the obligatory prayer, and the supplication between the pillar and the place, with a mention of the chain of narrations related to that. The author begins by mentioning the virtue of the Black Corner and that it is one of the stones of Paradise, based on hadiths from Ibn Abbas and other companions.
descriptions.4539: News of Mecca and its antiquities were written by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Walid Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ahmad Al-Azraqi. He is one of the books on the history of Mecca and its antiquities. He provides detailed information about the plans of Mecca, the quarters and wells, and talks about the Noble Sanctuary, its surrounding areas, the rituals connected to it, and other holy places. The book contains historical narratives about the construction of the Kaaba from ancient times until the era of Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf Al-Thaqafi (d. 95 AH/713 AD), as well as the emergence of Mecca, the landing of tribes there, the expansion of urbanization, and the dispersion of nations. Al-Azraqi discussed the virtues of Mecca, many of its places, and the characteristics of some places, in addition to studying a group of verses and hadiths.
descriptions.4540: This part of the book “Amali Ibn Bishran” is a collection of hadith dictation councils, which includes various prophetic hadiths on etiquette, sermons, and virtues, such as the virtue of the group, the dignity of the martyr, honoring one’s parents, and the prohibition of backbiting and betrayal. The book falls within the classification of hadith texts, and presents narrations supported by chains of transmission from the Prophet ﷺ, with a diversity of topics between belief, behavior, and acts of worship.
descriptions.4541: The book “Amali Ibn Bishran” is a collection of hadith councils dictated by the author Abu al-Qasim Ibn Bishran, and it is classified among the hadith texts. The book includes multiple councils starting from the six hundred and thirty-eighth council and continuing until the six hundred and sixty-ninth council, and they were dictated in different months of the year. The book includes supported prophetic hadiths that the author narrates with his chain of transmission on the authority of the Companions, such as the hadith of Abu Ubaidah bin al-Jarrah about Paradise and Paradise, and the hadith of Ali bin Abi Talib about a prisoner who claimed that a king had captured him.
descriptions.4542: The book “Amali Ibn Samoun Al-Wa’iz” is a collection of hadith councils dictated by the author, and it is one of the books of hadith texts that collects prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission. The book includes twenty sessions, starting with the second session and ending with the twentieth session, and it includes supported hadiths narrated by Ibn Samoun on the authority of his sheikhs, such as the hadith “Ride these animals safely” and the hadith “Indeed, there are a hundred levels in Paradise.”
descriptions.4543: This is a book on the texts of hadith, compiled by Imam Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, which he devoted to proving the doctrine of the torment of the grave and the questioning of the two angels based on what was mentioned in the Sharia of Qur’anic verses, narrated narrations, and the sayings of the nation’s predecessors, with a clarification of the permissibility of this according to reason in the power of God Almighty. The book deals with various topics related to the causes of the torment of the grave, such as gossip, urine, deceit, and religion, and what is hoped for in safety, such as martyrdom for the sake of God, reading Surat Al-Mulk, and death on Friday night, in addition to the Prophet ﷺ seeking refuge from the torment of the grave and his command to do so, and praying for the believer to be steadfast after burial.
descriptions.4544: The book “Heart Disease” by Al-Kharaiti is a collection of hadith texts, collecting prophetic hadiths and traditions from the predecessors related to heart diseases and their treatment. It deals with various topics such as repentance, struggle with oneself, condemning passion and lust, warning against temptation with women and rebelliousness, lowering one’s gaze, love and chastity, and fulfilling one’s covenant. The book aims to refine souls and reform hearts in a way that removes their rust and directs them towards obedience to God.
descriptions.4545: The book “Al-Athar” by Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Shaybani is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting hadiths and narrations attributed to the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions, narrated by the author on the authority of his sheikhs such as Abu Hanifa. The book begins with the chapters on purity and ablution, detailing its provisions, such as washing, wiping, and tayammum. Then it moves to the chapters on prayer, its timing, and how to perform it. The book presents hadiths with jurisprudential comments by the author explaining the rulings he takes.
descriptions.4546: The book “Al-Athar” by Abu Yusuf Al-Qadi is a compilation of hadith texts. It collects hadiths and chain of transmission from the Prophet ﷺ and from the Companions and Followers, arranged under the chapters of jurisprudence. The book begins with the chapter on ablution, then addresses the chapters on purity, prayer, zakat, and Hajj, and extends to the chapters on divorce, waiting period, making up, obligatory prayers, and wills, relying in his narration on his sheikhs, such as Abu Hanifa.
descriptions.4547: The book “Al-Ahad wal-Mathani” by Ibn Abi Asim is a compilation of hadith texts. It collects hadiths and chain of transmission. It is distinguished by its focus on naming the Companions and mentioning their virtues and lineages, with special attention to mentioning the people of Badr, those promised Paradise, and the followers of the Prophet ﷺ. The book also begins by mentioning the friend Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and his lineage and description.
descriptions.4548: The book “Al-Adab” by Imam Al-Bayhaqi deals with a group of Prophetic hadiths and jurisprudential fatwas related to the principles of Islamic behavior and morals. The book focuses on various topics related to mercy and kindness to others, good manners, turning away from the honor of Muslims, enjoining good and forbidding evil, and social interactions between Muslims. The book aims to enhance moral and behavioral values ​​in Islamic society by presenting hadiths and sayings contained in this field.
descriptions.4549: The book “The Selected Hadiths” or “The Extracts from the Hadiths” is a collection of hadith texts, compiled by Al-Hafiz Diya’ al-Din al-Maqdisi, and he specializes in the hadiths that were not included by Imams al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs, with the exception of some outstanding hadiths or those with defects that the author explains. The book begins with hadiths narrated from Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), then deals with the narrations of a number of companions and followers, arranged according to the narrators of each companion.
descriptions.4550: This is a book on hadith texts, in which Imam al-Bukhari collected prophetic hadiths and narrations from the companions and followers, and arranged them into chapters that begin with a Qur’anic verse, to explain the virtues of good morals and Islamic etiquette. The first section focuses on honoring one’s parents and maintaining family ties. It mentions rulings, virtues, and punishments related to these duties, beginning with a chapter on the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying (And We have enjoined upon man to be good to his parents).
descriptions.4551: Al-Adab Al-Mufrad is a book written by Al-Bukhari. The book deals with the individual Islamic morals contained in the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book includes some sayings of the Companions and Followers. Ibn Hajar mentioned, “It includes hadiths in addition to what is in the Sahih, and it contains few authenticated reports, and it is very useful.” The book contains 1,322 hadiths distributed over 644 chapters, and the hadiths in the book are mostly authentic. The reason for not all of them being authentic is that Al-Bukhari does not adhere to the conditions in this book in the book Al-Sahih, because the hadiths are hadiths that contain etiquette and not rulings.
descriptions.4552: The book “Al-Adab” by Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah is a hadith compilation that falls within the hadith texts. It collects hadiths, prophetic traditions, and sayings from the companions and followers related to etiquette and daily transactions. The book covers various topics such as the etiquette of greeting and seeking permission, speech and nicknames, perfume and musk, asking for needs, advice, kissing the hand, and other desirable and disliked social and moral etiquettes, which makes it a reference in refining the soul and organizing relationships between people in accordance with the Prophet’s guidance.
descriptions.4553: Names and Attributes is a book on the Islamic faith written by Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi. It contains chain of transmission hadiths that include the names and attributes of God. Al-Bayhaqi called it (the book of the names of God, glory be to Him, and His attributes, the proof of which was indicated by the Book of God Almighty, or by the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ, or by the consensus of the predecessors of this nation before the occurrence of division and the emergence of heresies). …
descriptions.4554: The book “Al-Amali fi Athar al-Sahaba” by Al-Hafiz Abd al-Razzaq al-San’ani is a collection of hadiths and narrations narrated from the Companions and followers, collected by the author’s attribution to his sheikhs. The book deals with various topics, including the provisions of jurisprudence, such as divorce, waiting period, wills, retaliation, and food, in addition to the virtues of some of the Companions, the positions of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and doctrinal issues such as faith and caliphate.
descriptions.4555: A book on the texts of hadith, which collects narrations and sayings from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others on the issue of enjoining good and forbidding evil. The book deals with the provisions of this ritual and its obligation, and how to denounce evil with the hand, tongue, and heart, with details on the etiquette of kindness and denunciation of the ruler, relatives, and distant people. It also devotes chapters to practical issues, such as denouncing those who beat the drum or play chess, the ruling on breaking evil instruments, and explaining what a man should do when he sees evil from afar or in the homes of others.
descriptions.4556: The book “Money” by Ibn Zangwayh is a collection of hadith texts, collecting hadiths and narrations related to legal and financial policy in Islam. The book begins with a chapter that requires advice between the imam and the subjects, then deals in detail with the provisions of fayyah, jizyah, and tax, and details the conquests of lands and their rulings, whether by force or peace, all the way to the covenants and covenants written by the Prophet ﷺ and his companions for the people of peace.
descriptions.4557: This book is a refinement and arrangement of the book “Al-Taqaseem wal-Sawa’il” by Imam Ibn Hibban, which is considered one of the most comprehensive works on the Prophet’s narrations. The summary has brought the book closer together and made it easier for his students by placing each hadith in its appropriate section, and arranging its sections according to commands, prohibitions, permissible things, and the actions of the Prophet ﷺ. The book falls within the texts of the Hadith, and includes introductions to the author’s translation and its conditions in the Sahih, in addition to chapters on adherence to the Sunnah and revelation.
descriptions.4558: The book “Faith” by Ibn Mandah is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting hadiths and traces that show the truth of faith, its pillars and branches, opening with the famous hadith of Gabriel in teaching religion. The book deals in detail with the issues of belief in destiny, resurrection, heaven, and hell, and emphasizes that faith is a statement with the tongue, belief in the heart, and action in the pillars, while explaining the difference between believers in it, its increase, and its decrease.
