The book also presents the qualities that increase faith, the degrees of Islam and faith, and emphasizes that the origin and highest point of faith is the testimony that there is no god but God.
descriptions.4559: Belief and Guidance to the Path of Righteousness is a book by Imam Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi in explaining the belief of the Sunnis and the community according to the doctrine of the righteous predecessors, the people of Hadith, and the method of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ash’ari. The book contained a number of hadiths and narrations from the predecessors on various issues of faith. It began with the first thing that a servant must know and acknowledge, and dealt with some topics related to names and attributes, destiny and intercession, belief in the torment of the grave, proving the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, saying about the family of the Prophet and his companions, saying about the miracles of the saints, and other things. The book included a statement of what the obligated person must believe and acknowledge, with reference to the points. His evidence on the path to abbreviation, and what should be...
descriptions.4560: The book “Innovations and Prohibition of Them” by Ibn Waddah Al-Qurtubi is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting hadiths and narrations related to the subject of innovations in religion and warnings against them. The book deals with defining heresies and explaining their ruling, with a focus on the Prophetic hadiths that forbid initiating and following them. It also devotes sections to talking about changing heresies and the dislike of meeting with their followers. The book also includes various issues, such as the prohibition of sitting with people of innovation, an explanation of the ruling on repentance for the one who commits innovation, and archaeological stories such as the story of Sabigh al-Iraqi.
descriptions.4561: A book on hadith texts, in which the author, Al-Hussein bin Harb, collected hadiths and traces related to honoring one’s parents and maintaining family ties, and the rulings that stem from them, such as maintenance on family and children, the rights of the owned, sponsoring an orphan, and disobedience to one’s parents. The book includes multiple sections that begin with honoring one’s parents and ending with the rulings on maintaining family ties and breaking them, relying on narrations from Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak and others.
descriptions.4562: Resurrection and Resurrection is a book by Imam Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, in which he narrated a number of hadiths about the Day of Resurrection and what is in it, as well as the description of Paradise and Hell, and so on.
descriptions.4563: Encouraging the virtues of deeds and the reward for doing so is a book about mentioning what was mentioned in encouragement from the Prophetic hadiths, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Shaheen (297 AH - 385 AH). In his book, the author dealt with the issue of encouraging the virtues of deeds and urging them to perform them and mentioning the reward for those who do them. He divided his book into chapters and gave each chapter a title, then included under it what was appropriate of Qur’anic verses, hadiths traced back to the Prophet, and traces attributed to the Companions. The number of texts contained in the book reached five hundred and eighty-one texts.
descriptions.4564: This is a book that collects what was mentioned in “Sunan Saeed bin Mansour” of hadiths and traces related to the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, arranged on the surahs of the Qur’an from Al-Fatihah to Surat Al-Ra’ad. The book falls within the texts of hadith, and includes the virtues of the Qur’an and the interpretation of its verses according to the method of hadith scholars, with an introduction that includes a study of the author and his book Sunan.
descriptions.4565: This book is the interpretation section of Sunan Saeed bin Mansour, and it is classified in the texts of hadith. It collects hadiths and chain of transmission related to the interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, starting with its virtues and passing through the interpretation of Surat Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah and its verses. The book includes narrations from the Companions and followers regarding the meanings of the verses and the reasons for the revelation, relying on the evidence of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.4566: A book on hadith texts, in which its author collected a number of prophetic hadiths and traces related to knowing God Almighty by His names and attributes, and proving His oneness and purifying Him from what does not befit Him. The book begins by mentioning how God described Himself in terms of oneness and permanence, then it deals with the narration of the issues of the creation of the throne and Adam, the virtues of monotheism and the word sincerity, and lists a number of God’s most beautiful names and His highest attributes.
descriptions.4567: The book is “Al-Jami’ Al-Kabir” known as “Sunan Al-Tirmidhi”, written by Muhammad bin Isa Al-Tirmidhi, and is classified among the texts of the Prophet’s hadith. The book begins with the chapters on purity, examining its rulings in detail through the narration of the chain of transmission of hadiths, along with comments on their authenticity and goodness, in accordance with the approach for which the author is famous for combining narration and criticism.
descriptions.4568: The book “Al-Jami’ fi Al-Hadith” by Ibn Wahb is a hadith compilation that includes marfoo’ hadiths and narrations from the Companions and Followers, collected by the author Abdullah bin Wahb Al-Qurashi. The book deals with various topics, including lineages and names, righteousness and brotherhood in God, silence and isolation, in addition to issues of ruqyah, amulets, and rituals, which makes it a reference in Islamic rulings and etiquette derived from the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4569: This book is “Jami’ Muammar bin Rashid”, and it is one of the texts of the Prophet’s hadith, and it includes a collection of hadiths and traces narrated from the companions and followers. The book begins with the chapter on the necessity of asking for permission, discussing its rulings and etiquette, such as the number of times to ask for permission and how to greet one another, then it moves on to various other topics such as the rulings on rings, riding, piety, contagion, jealousy, and other legal etiquette and rulings.
descriptions.4570: The book “Al-Jami’” by Imam Abdullah bin Wahb Al-Masry is a hadith compilation that collects prophetic hadiths and narrations from the companions and followers, arranged into jurisprudential sections that include rulings such as prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, marriage, drinks, and blood money. The book begins with the introduction of the investigator and then cites hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, dealing with various jurisprudential issues such as impurities and forbidden sales, which makes it a reference in the Sunnah of the Prophet and the legal rulings.
descriptions.4571: The book “Jihad” by Ibn Abi Asim is a book of hadith texts, collecting prophetic hadiths related to the virtues and rulings of jihad. The book begins by mentioning the hadiths that encourage and desire jihad, such as the fact that jihad is the pinnacle of the hump of Islam, the fact that the mujahid is a guarantor of God, the virtue of morning and evening in the path of God, spending on it, and preparing the invader. The book deals with various topics, such as patience when meeting the enemy, the virtue of those whose feet are dusty in the path of God, the virtue of shooting an arrow, fasting in the path of God, wounds and speech, and the issue of martyrs and those who deserve the name of martyrdom.
descriptions.4572: The book “The Supplication” by Al-Tabarani is a hadith compilation of the Prophet’s supplications ﷺ, written by the author to deal with the spread of innovated, resonant supplications that have no basis in the Sunnah. The book begins by mentioning the virtues and etiquette of supplication, then arranges its chapters according to the circumstances in which the Prophet used to supplicate, including rulings such as the dislike of sajnah and aggression in supplication, and qualities such as raising the hands and assurance, and response times such as Friday.
descriptions.4573: The book “The Great Supplications” by Imam Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi is a compilation of hadith texts, in which its author collected what was reported from the information mentioned in the supplications that the Prophet ﷺ prayed with or taught to his companions, arranging them in chapters according to the order of Imam Ibn Khuzaymah in his summary, with additions of his own. The book includes supplications and supplications for different times and conditions, such as morning and evening, entering and leaving the mosque, prayer, distress, and others, supported by chains of transmission to explain their ranks and rewards.
descriptions.4574: The book “Replying to the Jahmiya” written by Othman bin Saeed Al-Darimi. He compiled the book to respond to the “Jahmiyyah” and “Mu’tallah” and mentioned in it important rules for responding to them.
descriptions.4575: The book “Al-Rawd Al-Dani Al-Mu’jam Al-Saghir” is one of the hadith books classified by Imam Al-Tabarani, and it falls within the classification of hadith texts. The book includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by the author on the authority of his sheikhs in the regions. He allocated one hadith to each sheikh, and arranged their names according to the letters of the dictionary to make it easier to search for them. The book begins with the chapter Alif, then proceeds through the letters of the alphabet, and contains various hadiths on different topics.
descriptions.4576: The book “Asceticism” by Abu Dawud al-Sijistani is a book on hadith texts, in which the author collects news and sayings about asceticism and piety narrated from a number of honorable companions, starting with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Omar ibn al-Khattab, and Uthman ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them), all the way to other predecessors. The book falls within the hadith works concerned with collecting hadiths and narrations on the subject of asceticism, beginning with excerpts from the words of Jesus Ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) and news from previous books.
descriptions.4577: A book on hadith texts, collecting prophetic hadiths and traditions from the predecessors on the subject of asceticism and gentleness. It includes various chapters urging obedience to God, and explaining the virtue of worship, sadness and crying, sincerity, intention, trust, humility, condemning hypocrisy and arrogance, remembering death, and belittling the world and its contempt for God.
descriptions.4578: The book “The Sunnah” by Ibn Abi Asim is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting prophetic hadiths related to condemning whims and innovations, urging adherence to the Sunnah and the community, and warning against newly invented matters and division. The book deals with doctrinal topics such as contentment with destiny, taking the covenant, creating the pen, and issues of the children of polytheists, based on narrations attributed to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4579: The book “Al-Sunan Al-Shafi’i,” compiled by Al-Muzani, is a book in the texts of hadith. It collects hadiths narrated from Imam Al-Shafi’i, supported by their chains of transmission. It deals with a number of jurisprudential rulings and acts of worship, such as prayer while traveling, combining two prayers, the eclipse prayer, and the fear prayer, in addition to chapters on fasting, zakat, sales, and other legal issues.
descriptions.4580: A book that collects the Prophetic hadiths related to temptations and the signs of the Hour, and the changes that will follow them and the corruption of religion, based on what was narrated by the Companions and followers. The author aims to present a set of Sunnahs contained in this section for the believer to follow and be disciplined, addressing topics such as seeking refuge from temptations, staying home when they occur, the virtue of working during a time of turmoil, and the minor and major signs of the Hour.
descriptions.4581: Sharia (book): A book written by: Al-Ajri. Sharia (ship) Islamic Sharia: Islamic law. Jewish law or halakhah: Jewish law. The Pali Canon: Buddhist Grammar Texts. The Code of Urnamu: a Sumerian code that is the oldest existing code today. The Code of Hammurabi: legislation and laws from Hammurabi.
descriptions.4582: This is a book on prophetic medicine compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Naeem Al-Asbahani, and it is one of the compilations of hadith texts that is concerned with hadiths and traces contained in medicine and medication. The book consists of seven articles, dealing with various topics such as the virtues of making medicine, body composition and health management, treatment of illnesses, knowledge of drugs, management of the sick, incantation and amulets, relying on the hadiths of the Prophet and the sayings of the predecessors in this section.
descriptions.4583: A book on the texts of hadith, in which Abu Ubaid al-Qasim bin Salam collected hadiths and traces related to the rulings on purity and water. The book begins by mentioning the virtues of purification and ablution, then deals in detail with the Sunnahs of ablution, the number of times it is performed, and the amounts of water in it. It goes over the rulings on water, its impurity, the prohibition of various animals, and the licenses and prohibitions related to that, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and narrations.
descriptions.4584: Al-Tairiyat is a book written by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Sadr Al-Din Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Salfa, selected from the originals of the books of his sheikh, Abu Al-Hussein bin Abdul-Jabbar Al-Tairy Al-Sayrafi. The book is known as “The Birds,” and this selection contains many and varied narrations, distinguished by the superiority of their chains of narration, and the humor of their topics, in addition to the interesting and strange things they contain, songs and stories.
descriptions.4585: The book “Al-Azma” by Abu Sheikh Al-Isbahani is a collection of hadith texts that collects hadiths and traces that encourage contemplation of God’s signs, His power, His sovereignty, His greatness, and His oneness. The book deals with various topics, including the glorification of the Lord, Blessed and Most High, the description of His throne, chair, and veils, the creation of angels and their greatness, the attributes of the heavens and the earth, and the wonders of creatures such as the sun, moon, stars, clouds, rain, and sea. The book aims to remind the reader of the greatness of the Creator through contemplation of His creatures, while adhering to the Prophetic hadiths and the effects mentioned in this section.
descriptions.4586: The book “Al-Fawa’id” by Tamam bin Muhammad Al-Dimashqi is a hadith collection within the classification of hadith texts. It collects chain of transmission of prophetic hadiths that the author narrates with his chain of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs. The book includes multiple copies, including the copy of Zain bin Shuaib Al-Iskandarani and the copy of Nafi bin Abi Naeem Al-Qari, in addition to the hadiths of Juma bin Thub Al-Rahbi. The topics of the hadiths vary between jurisprudence and acts of worship such as Hajj and Friday prayers.
descriptions.4587: A book on hadith texts, aiming to prove destiny and respond to those who deny it, based on verses of the Holy Qur’an, the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ, and the sayings of the Companions, followers, and Muslim imams. The author shows that all the actions of creation are destined and written by God, and that God’s eternal knowledge includes everything that was and what will be, while mentioning evidence that God determined all decrees before creating the heavens and the earth. The book includes sections on how to believe in destiny, and the prohibition of sitting with the Qadariyyah and approaching them.
descriptions.4588: Al-Kifaya fi Ilm al-Riwaa is a book on the science of hadith written by al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ali al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, who died in the year (1002 AD - 1071 AD), in which he completed research into the laws of narration, and explained its principles and general rules. In the introduction to the book, he spoke about many issues related to the science of hadith, and then he finished those issues. He spoke about the punishment for one who conceals knowledge, so he narrated the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “The most tormented person on the Day of Resurrection is a scholar whom God will not benefit from with his knowledge.” And the hadith of Abdullah: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom God has given wisdom, so he says it, and a man to whom God has given money, so he spends it in his right. …
descriptions.4589: The book “Al-Kunya wa Al-Asmaa” by Al-Dulabi is a work of Hadith science, specializing in collecting and arranging the names of the Companions and narrators and their nicknames. The book begins by mentioning the nickname of the Prophet ﷺ and the hadiths contained in the prohibition of combining his name with his nickname. Then it lists the names of the Companions in order according to their nicknames, beginning with the major companions such as the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and following that by mentioning those of the Companions of the Messenger of God known by the nickname ﷺ.
descriptions.4590: This is a book on the texts of hadith, compiled by the author Abu Bakr al-Dinouri, entitled “Sitting and the Jewels of Knowledge,” and it includes twenty-six parts that include hadiths and chain of transmission. The book's attribution to its author has sparked some controversy over its authentication, as the charge of fabricating the hadith came from Al-Daraqutni, while others defended it and considered it to be relied upon. Also, his narrations appeared in books such as Al-Mukhtara by Al-Diya' Al-Maqdisi, which is considered implicit documentation of it.
descriptions.4591: This book is a collection of hadith parts selected from the hadiths of Abu Tahir al-Mukhlis, and it is one of the compilations of hadith texts. The book includes several parts of “Al-Mukhlasiyat” that were selected by his students, such as Ibn Abi Al-Fawares and Ibn Al-Baqal, in addition to sessions from his Amaliyah and other parts selected from his hadith. The work aims to collect what was found from the Savior’s written works and verify them, to represent scientific material in the narration of the Prophet’s hadith.
descriptions.4592: This book is an introduction to “Al-Sunan Al-Kubra” by Imam Al-Bayhaqi, and is concerned with explaining the origins and rules of hadith science and methods of dealing with different narrations. The book addresses important topics such as the etiquette of seeking and teaching knowledge, the scholar’s ​​position on fatwas and similarities, and how to give weight to news when there is disagreement. The book includes multiple sections that talk about the virtue of knowledge, the hatred of preventing it, the importance of honesty in narration, and verification before issuing a fatwa, which makes it a reference in the methodology of dealing with the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4593: The book “Al-Maraseel” by Abu Dawud Al-Sijistani is a book on the texts of hadith. It collects the hadiths narrated by the followers on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ without mentioning the Companions. The compiler arranged them according to the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the book of purity, then prayer, then fasting, zakat, Hajj, and other rulings. The book includes hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, and is concerned with collecting correspondences that are a type of Prophetic hadith.
descriptions.4594: Al-Mustadrak on the Two Sahihs is one of the books of the Prophet’s hadith according to the Sunnis and the community. In it, its author, Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hakim Al-Naysaburi, collected the hadiths that he believed to be authentic and on the condition of the two sheikhs (Bukhari and Muslim) or on the condition of one of them, and the two sheikhs (Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate them in their Sahihs, but they extracted their narrations in their books, then he added some hadiths that his diligence led him to correct. Hadith scholars among the Sunnis and the community said that Al-Hakim was lenient in correcting, so many weak and fabricated hadiths fell into the book. Al-Hafiz Al-Dhahabi summarized the book and added some comments to it. …
descriptions.4595: This book is “Al-Musnad Al-Sahih Al-Mukhtasar, Translating Justice from Justice”, known as “Sahih Muslim”, by Imam Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, and it is one of the foundations of the Sunnah of the Prophet and the most important books of authentic hadith. The book falls under the category of “Hadith Texts,” and includes the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ that were narrated by Muslim with a trustworthy chain of transmission, arranged into books and chapters that begin with an introduction to the origins and etiquette of narration, then the Book of Faith, which explains the characteristics of faith and Islam and their pillars.
descriptions.4596: This is the book “Al-Musnad Al-Musnad Ala Sahih Muslim” compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Naeem Al-Asbahani, and it is one of the books of Hadith texts that is concerned with grading the hadiths contained in Sahih Muslim with methods and chains of transmission other than those cited by Imam Muslim. The author begins with an introduction in which he explains the importance of the Prophet’s Sunnah and the necessity of referring to it. Then he lists the hadiths in alphabetical order (Chapter Alif, Ba, and so on) to facilitate access to them.
descriptions.4597: The book “Al-Musnad” by Al-Shashi is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting hadiths narrated from the honorable companions, arranged according to the names of the companions who narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ. The book begins by mentioning the hadiths reported on the authority of Talha bin Ubaidullah, then moves to other companions such as Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, and Omar bin Al-Khattab, while tracing the different narrations about each companion through his students and narrators of the hadith about him.
descriptions.4598: The book “Al-Musannaf” by Abd al-Razzaq al-San’ani is one of the comprehensive collections of the Prophet’s hadith, and is classified among the hadith texts. The book begins with the chapters on purity, detailing the rulings on ablution, washing, and wiping the head and ears, and what relates to water and impurities, based on narrations narrated from the Companions and followers.
descriptions.4599: Al-Mu'jam Al-Awsat by Al-Tabarani is one of the most extensive books of hadith attributed to the Sunnis and the community. It was compiled by Imam Abu al-Qasim Suleiman bin Ahmad bin Ayyub al-Tabarani, and arranged it in the manner of dictionaries, that is, he arranged it according to the order of the names of his sheikhs from whom he narrated the texts based on the letters of the dictionary. Al-Tabarani said about him: “This book is spiritual,” because he worked hard on it. The book contains 9489 supported texts. Some of them are marfo’, suspended, or cut off. Al-Tabarani directed his attention in this book to a collection, just as he took great care in it to collect it in which he brings about each sheikh’s oddities, wonders, and benefits of the sheikhs. He did not stipulate authenticity, so the texts varied between authenticity and weakness. …
descriptions.4600: The Great Dictionary by Al-Tabarani is one of the books of hadith attributed to the Sunnis and the community. It was collected by Imam Abu al-Qasim Suleiman bin Ahmad bin Ayyub al-Tabarani, and he arranged it in the manner of dictionaries, that is, he arranged it according to the letters of the dictionary, but in the Great Dictionary it is according to the letters of the dictionary for the names of the Companions.
descriptions.4601: The book “The Dictionary by Ibn al-Muqri” is a compilation of hadith texts. It collects chained prophetic hadiths arranged according to the letters of the dictionary according to the names of the author’s sheikhs and narrators, starting with the chapter on the alif, with someone named Ahmad, then Ibrahim, and so on. The book includes narrations with connected chains of transmission, which the author opens with the hadith “Actions are but by intentions” and other hadiths, to serve as a reference in the narration of the Sunnah of the Prophet in lexical order.
descriptions.4602: The book “Al-Maqsad Al-Ali fi Zawa’id Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili” is a book on the texts of hadith, compiled by Nour Al-Din Al-Haythami from the Musnad of Imam Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili, extracting what is in it from hadiths in addition to what is in the six books, either by completing the hadith or adding to it. The author has arranged these additions to the chapters of jurisprudence, beginning with the Book of Faith and the Book of Knowledge, to make it easy to discover them and benefit from them.
descriptions.4603: This book, “The Selected from the Musnad of Abd ibn Humayd,” is a collection of selected hadiths of the Prophet from the Musnad of Abd ibn Humayd, and has been edited and selected from multiple copies to ensure the accuracy of the text. The book deals with hadiths related to the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and reviews the Musnads of each of the major imams such as Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, Omar bin Al-Khattab, Othman bin Affan and others. The second edition of the book was distinguished by revising the texts of the hadiths in several manuscripts, and adding more interpretations and sayings of the scholars, with some amendments to the rulings based on the development of jurisprudence and the emergence of the hadith reasons.
descriptions.4604: The book “Al-Muntaqa min al-Sunan al-Musnad” by Ibn al-Jaroud is a book on the texts of the Prophet’s hadith, which collects hadiths on rulings arranged according to the chapters of jurisprudence. The book begins with the Book of Purity, covering the obligations and contradictions of ablution, the recipe for ablution, wiping over the socks, the rulings on impurity and menstruation, and other issues of purity, based on the chain of transmission of hadiths.
descriptions.4605: A book on Hadith texts, in which its author collected wide sections of Prophetic hadiths and hadiths that urge good and noble morals, and desire to embody them. The book is organized into multiple sections that include urging good morals, the reward for good behavior, good character, refraining from harm, doing good deeds, being gentle in speech, keeping trustworthiness, fulfilling promises, maintaining family ties, honoring guests, modesty, forgiveness, reconciliation between people, and other virtues. The author opened his book by mentioning the hadith, “I was sent only to complete good morals,” to explain the basic purpose of the honorable prophetic mission.
descriptions.4606: The Great Dictionary by Al-Tabarani is one of the books of hadith attributed to the Sunnis and the community. It was collected by Imam Abu al-Qasim Suleiman bin Ahmad bin Ayyub al-Tabarani, and he arranged it in the manner of dictionaries, that is, he arranged it according to the letters of the dictionary, but in the Great Dictionary it is according to the letters of the dictionary for the names of the Companions.
descriptions.4607: The Great Dictionary by Al-Tabarani is one of the books of hadith attributed to the Sunnis and the community. It was collected by Imam Abu al-Qasim Suleiman bin Ahmad bin Ayyub al-Tabarani, and he arranged it in the manner of dictionaries, that is, he arranged it according to the letters of the dictionary, but in the Great Dictionary it is according to the letters of the dictionary for the names of the Companions.
descriptions.4608: This book is part of the “Great Dictionary” by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Suleiman bin Ahmed Al-Tabarani, and it is one of the most important books of the Prophet’s hadith. This twenty-first volume includes an excerpt from the Musnad of the companion Al-Numan bin Bashir (may Allah be pleased with him), which includes hadiths narrated by various narrators and followers. This work comes as part of the efforts to verify the manuscripts to complete the shortcomings that were in the previous edition of the book.
descriptions.4609: The book “Bahr al-Fawaid al-Mashhur bi Ma’ani al-Akhbar” is one of the works of Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi, and is classified among the texts of hadith. The book begins with an introduction of praise and praise, then the author presents the Prophetic hadiths with their connected chains of transmission, explaining their meanings and explaining their benefits.
descriptions.4610: This book is “The Program of Al-Tajibi” compiled by Al-Qasim bin Yusuf Al-Tajibi, and it falls in the field of hadith texts. The book includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by the author with his chain of transmission, and is considered one of the books that collects the narrator’s narrations and documents their chains of transmission. The excerpt also indicates that the author intended to collect what he had read or heard of hadiths and scientific methods.
descriptions.4611: The book “Baghiyat al-Muthith `an-Zawa’id Musnad al-Harith” is a book on the texts of hadith, compiled by al-Harith ibn Abi Usama, and it includes hadiths attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. The book begins with the Book of Faith, covering sections such as the virtue of the two testimonies, the sanctity of a Muslim’s blood and property, the qualities of faith, and major sins. Then it moves to the Book of Knowledge, which includes the virtue of scholars, seeking knowledge, and writing hadith. The book presents hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, as appears in the beginning excerpt, which cites hadiths from Omar ibn al-Khattab, Abdullah ibn Masoud, and others.
descriptions.4612: A book on Hadith texts, collecting narrations and news related to Medina during the era of the Prophet ﷺ and after. The book covers various topics, such as the provisions of the Prophet’s Mosque and the etiquette and rulings related to it, mentioning the mosques and places where the Prophet prayed, in addition to news of the graves, Al-Baqi’, and the graves of the Companions and their family. The book also includes hadiths and traces related to funerals, praying over them, and other places such as Bir Rumah and Naqi’.
descriptions.4613: This is a book that specializes in examining the chain of transmission of the chain of transmission of the hadiths mentioned in the book “Al-Tarikh Al-Kabir” by Imam Al-Bukhari, which is one of the books of hadith texts. It aims to collect the hadiths that Al-Bukhari attributed to the Prophet ﷺ in his historical work, with their chains of transmission and texts as they were originally reported. The book includes a range of Prophetic hadiths on various topics, such as biography, virtues, rulings, and etiquette.
descriptions.4614: The book “Arrangement of Al-Amali Al-Khamisiyah by Al-Shajri” is a compilation of hadith texts, compiled by Yahya bin Al-Hussein Al-Shajri and arranged its topics. The book includes multiple chapters that include prophetic hadiths about faith and monotheism, the virtue of knowledge and scholars, the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt, mentioning the killing of Hussein bin Ali, in addition to chapters on acts of worship such as fasting, Hajj, and zakat, and sermons on repentance, honoring one’s parents, and upholding family ties. The book begins with the chain of transmission of the hadith, “Actions are based on intentions,” and other chain of narrators.
descriptions.4615: A book on hadith texts, in which its author, Muhammad bin Nasr al-Marwazi, collected a number of hadiths, narrations, and stories that exalt the value of prayer and explain its superiority over all other deeds, and warn against neglecting it or abandoning it, and deals with rulings such as the dislike of sleeping before dinner and turning around in it, and explaining the place of consideration, and the virtue of completing the obligatory prayers with voluntary prayers, while mentioning the stories of the prophets such as David, Zechariah, Solomon, and Adam (peace be upon them) regarding prayer.
descriptions.4616: Jami' Bayan Bayan al-Ilm wa its Virtues is a book about the virtue of knowledge and its pursuit, written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Abd al-Barr (368 AH - 463 AH). The author mentions the meaning of knowledge and the virtue of seeking it and the praise of striving for it and taking care of it. He explains the corruption of saying about the religion of God without knowledge and the prohibition of ruling without proof or evidence. Ibn Abd al-Barr also spoke about the etiquette of learning and what the scholar and learner must adhere to and persevere in, citing many prophetic hadiths and traces on this subject.
descriptions.4617: This book is a part of a hadith in which the author narrates a group of noble prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ, and it includes various rulings and etiquette such as the prohibition of selling fruit before it is ripe, the encouragement of mercy and forgiveness, the virtue of patience in the face of the loss of children, the rulings on fasting and expiations, the characteristics of the Prophet ﷺ in his prayers and clothing, and other jurisprudential and behavioral topics.
descriptions.4618: This is a hadith book compiled by Imam al-Bukhari on the subject of the ruling on the person being led behind the imam in prayer. It includes detailed sections on the issues of reciting loudly and silently, reciting while the imam is silent, and the number of what is recited in the rak’ahs. The author begins the book by narrating hadiths from the Companions and Followers, including the hadith of Ali bin Abi Talib detailing the recitation in the silent and loud prayers, and the hadith of Ubadah bin al-Samit that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the opening of the book.”
descriptions.4619: The book “The Farewell Pilgrimage” by Ibn Hazm is a collection of hadith texts that collects the hadiths contained in describing the actions of the Prophet ﷺ in the Farewell Pilgrimage, which were reported in multiple ways with different wording. The workbook aims to coordinate these reports and link them together to remove any apparent conflict or problem in understanding them, while pointing out one place where it was difficult to determine the location of the noon prayer on the Day of Sacrifice.
descriptions.4620: This book is a collection of my hadiths that includes parts of the narrations of Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Thaqafi Al-Sarraj. It is one of the hadith texts that is concerned with narrating the Prophetic hadiths with their connected chains of transmission. The book begins by narrating the first hadith from the great companion Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) in the story of the birth of Asma bint Umays, to be an example of the narrated hadiths it contains.
descriptions.4621: This book is a collection of my hadiths in which Ali bin Hajar al-Saadi narrates on the authority of Ismail bin Jaafar al-Madani, and it includes hadiths narrated on the authority of a number of the sheikhs of Ismail bin Jaafar, such as Abdullah bin Dinar, Hamid al-Taweel, Muhammad bin Amr bin Alqamah, and others. The book falls within the classification of hadith texts, and contains prophetic hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, including those related to the provisions of Hajj, sales, and other legal rulings.
descriptions.4622: The book Creating the Actions of the People and the Response to the Jahmiyyah and the People of al-Ta’il, written by Imam Muhammad bin Ismail al-Bukhari, in which he collected hadiths and traces that indicate that the actions of the slaves were created, and which prove that the Qur’an is the word of God, not created, to respond to the sects of the Jahmiyyah and al-Mu’talil according to what he divided the topics of the book.
descriptions.4623: The book “Remembrance of peers and their narrations on the authority of each other” by Abu Sheikh Al-Isbahani is a book on hadith texts, which collects hadiths narrated by one narrator on the authority of another, then that other narrates on the authority of the first, in a phenomenon known as narration by peers. The book begins by mentioning examples of these narrations exchanged between the Successors and others, such as the narration of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr and the opposite, and the narration of Al-Amash on the authority of Abu Salih and the opposite, along with listing the chains of transmission and texts related to that.
descriptions.4624: A book on the science of wounds and amendments, in which its author explains the classes of critics whose statements are relied upon to authenticate narrators and weaken them, and divides them into sections according to their strictness, leniency, or moderation in judging narrators.
descriptions.4625: This is a comprehensive book in which its author collected the texts contained in the Book of God Almighty and the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ related to the vision of the Creator, the Majestic and Most High, and some matters of the afterlife. He is one of the books of hadith texts, which is concerned with compiling hadiths and their narrations. The book includes a number of hadiths narrated by the Companions, such as Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, Abu Hurairah, Jabir bin Abdullah, and Anas bin Malik, on the issue of seeing God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection, along with tracing their methods and chains of transmission.
descriptions.4626: Sunan Abu Dawud, known as Al-Sunan, is one of the six books of hadith and the four Sunnahs, which occupies an advanced position among the Sunnis. It is considered one of the most important sources of hadith among them. Where it comes in rank after the two Sahihs, (2) it was classified by Imam Abu Dawud Sulayman bin Al-Ash’ath bin Ishaq bin Bashir bin Shaddad bin Amr Al-Azdi Al-Sijistani (202 AH - 817 AD / 275 AH - 888 AD), in which Abu Dawud collected a number of hadiths, and his hadiths amounted to 5274 hadiths. He selected it from five hundred thousand hadiths. …
descriptions.4627: Sunan Ibn Majah is one of the books of the Prophetic hadiths, and it is the sixth of the six books that are the foundations of the honorable Sunnah of the Prophet, by its author, Ibn Majah Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid al-Qazwini. His author’s name is his father Yazid, and he is one of the most venerable, greatest, and most enduring of his books over time, and by which he is known and famous. He arranged the hadiths according to the books and chapters, and the scholars disagreed about his status among the books of the Sunnah. The Sunnahs of Ibn Majah include: the authentic, the good, the weak, and even the objectionable and the fabricated ones, although they are few. Whatever the case, the fabricated hadiths are few compared to the total number of hadiths in the book, which are more than 4,000 hadiths. He died in the year 273 AH
descriptions.4628: Jami` al-Tirmidhi, known as Sunan al-Tirmidhi, is one of the six books of hadith compiled by Imam al-Tirmidhi. Sunni scholars consider it the fifth of the six books of hadith. Sheikh Al-Albani divided it into Sahih al-Tirmidhi and Da’eef al-Tirmidhi.
descriptions.4629: Sunan Saeed bin Mansour is one of the books of the Prophet’s hadith according to the Sunnis and the community, compiled by Abu Othman Saeed bin Mansour Al-Khorasani. The number of hadiths in the book reached 2791 chained hadiths, and the book included a combination of hadiths attributed to the Messenger of God, Muhammad bin Abdullah ﷺ, and hadiths attributed to the Companions, and the author did not adhere to authenticity in his book. The author arranged the book into jurisprudential sections and placed under each section the appropriate hadiths. He did not comment on the hadiths except on rare occasions. Among the characteristics of the book: the book is distinguished by its high chain of transmission, which led scholars to extract from its path, including the authors of the six books and others. …
descriptions.4630: Explanation of the foundations of the belief of the Sunnis and the community from the Qur’an and the Sunnah and the consensus of the Companions and the Successors and those after them. It is a book on the Islamic faith written by Al-Lalikai (d. 418 AH). In it, Al-Lalikai divided the foundations of the belief according to the Sunnis and the community into monotheism, names and attributes, belief in the Prophet, and the meaning of faith is that it is words and deeds, belief in intercession, belief in the afterlife, Paradise, Hell, the sights of the Day of Resurrection, and the virtues of the Companions. Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyyah praised the book in his novel, saying:
descriptions.4631: “Explanation of the Sunnah” may mean: Explanation of the Sunnah by Al-Barbahari: a book written by Al-Barbahari. Explanation of the Sunnah by Al-Baghawi: A book written by Al-Baghawi. Explanation of the Sunnah by Al-Muzani: A book written by Ismail bin Yahya Al-Muzani.
descriptions.4632: This is a book on the texts of hadith, explaining the doctrines of the Sunnis and the community, and mentioning the virtues of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs and their unique virtues. It also includes sections on responding to the Jahmiya and Mu’tazilites and explaining their sayings, the virtue of reviving the Sunnahs, and the servant’s hope in the reward of God.
descriptions.4633: The book Explanation of Mushkil al-Athar by Imam al-Tahawi is considered a useful book in the hadiths of rulings and evidence of controversial issues. Its author classified it in the order of the books and chapters of jurisprudence, and in it he mentioned the narrations transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ in the rulings, some of which are thought to invalidate others, and he clarified the abrogated ones from the abrogated ones, and the ones who restricted them from the absolute ones, and what is obligatory to act upon and what is not obligatory, along with a list of the narrations that the people of disagreement cling to, and a statement of their support and text. And the sayings of the Companions, Imams and scholars about it. The book was explained by Badr al-Din Mahmoud bin Muhammad al-Aini (855 AH), and he paid attention to the names of its men, Zain al-Din, known as Ibn al-Hammam (661 AH), as Abu al-Hussein Muhammad al-Bahili (321 AH) explained it.
descriptions.4634: Explanation of the Meanings of Athars is a book on the hadiths of rulings and evidence of controversial jurisprudential issues, arranged according to the books and chapters of jurisprudence. In it, its compiler, Imam Abu Jaafar al-Tahawi, mentioned the hadiths transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ in the rulings, some of which he imagines to refute others, and the one who abrogates them and clarifies them from the absolute, and what is obligatory to act upon and what is not obligatory. The book Explanation of the Meanings of Athar is one of the respected sources of the Prophet’s hadith, and Al-Hafiz bin Hajar considered it in his book - Ithaf Al-Mahra - one of the hadith books that comes after the six books in terms of it being the source of authentic hadith. …
descriptions.4635: Sahih Ibn Hibban is one of the famous books of the Prophet’s hadith written by Al-Hafiz Muhammad ibn Hibban ibn Ahmad ibn Hibban ibn Muadh ibn Ma’bad, Al-Tamimi, Abu Hatim, Al-Darimi, Al-Busti (deceased: 354 AH)
descriptions.4636: Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah is one of the books of the Prophet’s hadith, one of the books of hadith considered by the Sunnis and the community, and it is considered, in addition to Sahih Ibn Hibban and Al-Mustadrak on the two Sahihs by Al-Hakim Al-Naysaburi, one of the most important books written in the Sahih Al-Majared after the two Sahihs by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The name of the original book is: (Mukhtasar al-Mukhtasar from the authentic Musnad on the authority of the Prophet, with the transmission of justice from justice, connected to it without interruption during the chain of transmission and without interruption in the transmitters of the news). It is clear to us from it that its author, Ibn Khuzaymah, stipulated that he should not produce in it except a hadith that is authentic in his opinion, its narrators are trustworthy and trustworthy, and its chain of transmission is continuous and uninterrupted.
descriptions.4637: The book “The Description of Paradise” by Abu Naeem Al-Isbahani is a book on hadith texts, in which the author collects hadiths and traces related to the description of Paradise and its bliss. The book begins by mentioning the Qur’anic verses calling for the abode of peace, then deals in detail with various topics such as the creation of Paradise, the number of its gates, the description of its soil and its construction, the longing of the beautiful houris for their wives, and the conversation of the angels with its inhabitants. The book aims to motivate believers to seek Paradise and remind them of the blessings God has prepared therein for the righteous.
descriptions.4638: This is a book on hadith texts, in which the author Al-Tabarani collected the methods of the hadith “Whoever deliberately lies about me” on the authority of a large number of companions, starting with the Rightly Guided Caliphs, then the ten promised Paradise, and the companions after them, where he cites each method by attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4639: The book “The Work of the Day and the Night” by Ibn al-Sunni is a compilation of hadith texts. It collects prophetic hadiths and traces related to the remembrances and actions of the day and the night, starting with waking up from sleep, putting on a garment, entering the toilet, and performing ablution, all the way to the conditions of prayer and the call to prayer. The book aims to guide the Muslim towards preserving his tongue and preoccupying himself with the remembrance of God Almighty, by narrating the sayings and deeds of the Prophet on various daily occasions.
descriptions.4640: The book “The Work of the Day and the Night” by Imam Al-Nasa’i is a collection of hadith classified within the texts of hadith, in which the author collects the prophetic hadiths related to the remembrances, supplications, and actions that are said and done at different times of the day and night. The book begins by mentioning what the Prophet ﷺ used to say in the morning, then deals with various topics such as the virtues of glorifying God and seeking forgiveness, the supplications related to ablution, entering and leaving the mosque, blessings upon the Prophet, what is said at the end of prayers, and other daily actions.
descriptions.4641: The book “The Virtues of Times” by Al-Bayhaqi is one of the books of hadith texts, in which the author collects hadiths and narrations related to the virtues of certain times and months in the year, such as the month of Rajab, Shaban, Ramadan, and the last ten days of it, and the days of Eid, the day of Arafah, and Ashura. The book aims to explain what has been reported regarding the encouragement of worship and diligence in these times, based on legal texts and narrations.
descriptions.4642: The book “The Virtues of the Four Caliphs and Others” by Abu Naim Al-Isbahani is a book in the texts of hadith, which collects the virtues of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs: Abu Bakr, Omar, Othman, and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them). In this book, the author presents hadiths and narrations that highlight the virtues of each caliph individually, focusing on the unique virtues that each one of them possesses and that no one else shares.
descriptions.4643: The Virtues of the Companions is a book written by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal on the virtues of the Companions of the Prophet Muhammad. The book contains (1963) texts with a chain of narration, some of which are traceable and some are less than that.
descriptions.4644: The book “The Benefits of Abu Muhammad Al-Fakihi” is a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Al-Fakihi. The book falls within the classification of hadith texts, and contains various hadiths on etiquette, morals, acts of worship, and transactions, such as the virtue of good manners, the rulings on Friday, zakat, and prayer, and a description of some of the characteristics of the people of Hell and the days of holidays. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, and includes hadiths about charity and spending on one’s family.
descriptions.4645: A book on the texts of hadith, in which Imam Al-Bukhari collected the hadiths and reports mentioned regarding raising the hands in prayer when pronouncing takbeer, bowing, and raising from it, in response to those who denied that. The book includes continuous narrations from the Prophet ﷺ and his companions and followers, indicating the legitimacy of raising the hands in specific places during prayer.
descriptions.4646: A book that collects the Prophetic hadiths that have become proverbs on people’s tongues. It mentions the hadith and then cites it with its chains of transmission. The author begins by mentioning the proverbs that were memorized from the Prophet ﷺ, then he cites the hadiths that took place in the course of the proverbs, such as his saying, “War is a deception,” “News is not the same as seeing,” and “The believer is not stung from the same hole twice,” while mentioning their ways and chains of transmission.
descriptions.4647: The book “The Imamate and the Response to the Rafidah” by Al-Asbahani is a compilation of hadith texts, aiming to establish the imamate and arrange the caliphate according to the perspective of the Sunnis. The book begins by mentioning the caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, then moves to the virtues of Omar ibn al-Khattab and the hadiths contained therein, leading to the succession of Ali ibn Abi Talib, while citing prophetic hadiths that support the order of succession and the preference for the companions.
descriptions.4648: A book on the texts of hadith, which aims to prove the monotheism of God Almighty and prove His attributes mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah. The book includes several chapters, including a chapter mentioning the evidence that acknowledging that God is in heaven is part of faith, chapters proving the attribute of God’s speech, and a chapter mentioning the position of the Throne before the creation of the heavens. The author begins his book by mentioning prophetic hadiths related to proving the attribute of the soul to God Almighty, citing continuous chains of transmission from the Companions.
descriptions.4649: This is a book on hadith texts, in which the author collected the prophetic hadiths related to condemning whims and innovations, urging adherence to the Sunnah and the community, and warning against division and controversy, while mentioning a number of hadiths about destiny, the pen, and intercession. The book also includes a summary of the hadiths it contains.
descriptions.4650: The Book of Trials by Naeem bin Hammad Al-Maruzi is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting hadiths and narrations related to the temptations and epics that will occur at the end of time, based on what the Prophet ﷺ and his companions told him. The book deals with various topics, such as the signs of the Hour, the signs of temptations, the mention of caliphs and kings, the attributes of the Mahdi and the Sufyani, and the major events that precede the rise of the Hour, relying on supported narrations.
descriptions.4651: The Book of Destiny by Al-Faryabi is a book on the texts of hadith, in which the author collects hadiths and traces related to the issue of predestination and destiny, and explains what was mentioned about the desires and the denial of the people of predestination. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission in which it narrates the story of the creation of the earth, the heavens, and Adam (peace be upon him), the bringing out of his offspring from his back, and Adam choosing the right hand of his Lord, which shows that its content revolves around determining issues of destiny, creation, and divine will according to what was stated in the texts.
descriptions.4652: This book is an excerpt from the book “Explanation of the Fundamentals of the Belief of the People of the Sunnah and the Community” by Al-Kā’i, and it brings together what was mentioned in the Holy Qur’an, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and the narrations of the Companions and Followers regarding the honors of the saints and the manifestation of extraordinary signs in them. The author begins by interpreting the verses that indicate miracles, such as the story of Mary, peace be upon her, then he cites hadiths and narrations related to the miracles of a number of companions and followers, such as Othman, Ali, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Aisha, and others (may Allah be pleased with them).
descriptions.4653: This book is a summary of Jami’ al-Tirmidhi, compiled by the author Ali bin Nasr al-Tusi and arranged in the jurisprudential chapters, beginning with the chapter on purity. The summary is limited to presenting the texts of the Prophet’s hadiths with their chains of transmission, without the comments or extensive jurisprudential rulings for which Jami’ al-Tirmidhi is famous. The book aims to present the texts of the Prophet’s hadith in a concise form to facilitate their memorization and circulation.
descriptions.4654: The book “Disadvantages and Reprehensible Morals” by Al-Kharaiti is a collection of hadith texts, collecting prophetic hadiths that condemn bad morals and warn against them. The book begins with a chapter on the hatred of bad character, then it deals with hatred and censure of a number of evils such as cursing, cursing, obscenity, lying, backbiting, gossip, disobedience to one’s parents, severing family ties, hypocrisy, anger, miserliness, bad neighbourliness, and other moral evils, with a mention of what was mentioned in the severity of some of them, such as adultery and sodomy.
descriptions.4655: It is one of the books of the Prophet’s hadith, and it has another name (Extract of Abu Awanah). The author (Abu Awanah Al-Isfarayini) extracted his hadiths from Sahih Muslim and mentioned in it many independent hadiths during the chapters, which Muslim did not extract in the Sahih. The author pointed out many of them, including the authentic, the good, the weak, and the suspended ones. The author divided his book into jurisprudential books, then divided the single book into chapters, and included in each chapter a set of hadiths; As is the custom of imams, the number of texts contained in the book reached more than seven thousand chain texts.
descriptions.4656: Musnad Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi is one of the books of hadith according to the Sunnis and the community. It was compiled by the hadith scholar Yunus bin Habib, who died in 267 AH. He narrated it on the authority of his sheikh, Imam Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and he also narrated a few hadiths on the authority of other than Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi. The book is compiled in the manner of Musnads, meaning that the hadiths are arranged according to their narration by the Companions, and each Musnad collects the hadiths narrated by a specific Companion. The author began the book with the support of the ten promised Paradise. He also started with the Musnads of the male Companions, and placed the Musnads of the Women Companions in the middle of the Musnads of the Men, and began the Musnads of the Women Companions with the Musnad of Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad. The total number of narrated hadiths amounted to about 2882 hadiths.
descriptions.4657: Musnad Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili: It is one of the books of hadith according to the Sunnis and the community, classified by Imam Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili. The book deals with the narrations of Imam Abu Ya’la and ranks above the chain of transmission of the Companions.
descriptions.4658: The book “Musnad of the Commander of the Faithful Abu Hafs Omar Ibn Al-Khattab” by Ibn Kathir is a compilation of hadith texts, collecting hadiths narrated on the authority of Caliph Omar Ibn Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). The book is organized into various jurisprudential sections that begin with purity and end with miracles and virtues. The author cites hadiths with their chains of transmission and mentions the different ways of narrating them. From the beginning of the book, it appears that Ibn Kathir relied on extracting hadiths from their sources, such as the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, with a comparison between the wording of the narrations.
descriptions.4659: Musnad Ishaq bin Rahawayh is a book of Musnad in the Prophet’s hadith, and its author is Ishaq bin Rahawayh.
descriptions.4660: The book “Musnad Ibn Abi Shaybah” is a compilation of the texts of the Prophet’s hadith. It collects hadiths narrated from the honorable companions with their chains of transmission. The book begins with the Musnad of the companion Abu Ayyub Khalid bin Zaid, then covers the Musnads of a number of Companions, such as Khuzaymah bin Thabit, Abu Darda’, Sahl bin Hanif, Rafi’ bin Khadij, Zaid bin Thabit, Abdullah bin Masoud, Ammar bin Yasser and others, leading to other hadiths of various companions. The book aims to present the Prophet’s hadiths arranged according to the narrators of the Companions, making it a reference in the science of hadith.
descriptions.4661: The book “Musnad Ibn al-Ja’d” is one of the books of hadith texts. It collects the narrations of Ali ibn al-Ja’d al-Jawhari on the authority of his sheikhs, and its index highlights a special focus on the narrations of Shu’bah ibn al-Hajjaj on the authority of a number of followers, such as Amr ibn Murrah and al-Hakam ibn Utaiba. The book begins with news related to Shu`bah and its translation, then lists the hadiths supported by their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4662: The Musnad of Imam Abu Hanifa, the narration of Abu Naim, is a book that deals with Abu Naim al-Isbahani’s narration of the Musnad of Abu Hanifa, where it mentions the hadiths of Abu Hanifa on the authority of the Companions and Followers, and classifies the narrations according to the first letters of the names of the narrators. The book includes talk about the biography of Abu Hanifa and his scientific travels, and includes his narrations about Hammad bin Abi Suleiman, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and other scholars.
descriptions.4663: Musnad Ahmad, known as Al-Musnad, is one of the most famous and extensive books of the Prophet’s hadith, which occupies an advanced position among the Sunnis. As it is considered one of the most important sources of hadith among them, and it is the most famous of the Musnads, the hadith scholars placed it in the third rank after the two Sahihs and the four Sunans. …
descriptions.4664: This book is “Musnad al-Imam al-Shafi’i,” narrated by al-Rabi’ ibn Sulaiman al-Muradi. It was arranged and revised by Abu Sa’id Sanjar ibn Abdullah al-Nasiri, known as al-Jawli. He reorganized the hadiths of the Musnad, which were repeated and scattered in various places, and arranged them in the chapters of jurisprudence to make it easier for the student of hadith to access them. The book begins with the chapter on purity, covering the rulings on water, impurities, ablution, and the siwak. It is one of the books of Hadith texts that collects the narrations of Imam al-Shafi’i.
descriptions.4665: This book is an arrangement of the Musnad of Imam al-Shafi’i, prepared by Sheikh Muhammad Abed al-Sindi, where he arranged his hadiths on the sections of jurisprudence to make it easy to benefit from them. The book includes hadiths narrated by Imam al-Shafi’i on the topics of faith, knowledge, and adhering to the Qur’an and Sunnah. It then discusses in detail the rulings on purity and prayer and the chapters and branches of jurisprudence related to them.
descriptions.4666: Musnad Al-Bazzar, published under the name Al-Bahr Al-Zakhkhar, is a book that collects hadiths of the Prophet, and it was written by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar, who died in the year 292 AH.
descriptions.4667: Musnad al-Humaydi is one of the books of hadith attributed to Imam al-Humaydi (d. 219 AH). The author began writing the book by mentioning the Musnads of the ten who were promised Paradise, then the Muhajireen and the Ansar, men and women. His hadiths reached 1,300 hadiths, and the author concluded his Musnad by explaining his belief.
descriptions.4668: Musnad Al-Ruyyani, Musnad of Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Harun Al-Ruyyani, who died in the year 370 AH, medium musnad
descriptions.4669: Musnad al-Siraj is one of the books of the Prophet’s Hadith compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq al-Siraj al-Nashabouri (died 313 AH).
descriptions.4670: The book “Musnad al-Shamiyyin” by Imam al-Tabarani is one of the books of hadith texts, and it collects the narrations of one narrator, Ibrahim bin Abi Abla. The book begins by mentioning his virtues and news, then lists the hadiths that he narrated on the authority of the Companions and followers, such as Anas bin Malik, Abu Umamah, Ubadah bin al-Samit, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and others. The book falls within the hadith works that focus on the narrations of a specific narrator from the people of the Levant, which makes it an important source for studying the chain of transmission and texts in that class.
descriptions.4671: Musnad Al-Shihab is one of the books of the Prophet’s hadith, written by Judge Abu Abdullah Al-Qadha’i.
descriptions.4672: This book is a dictionary written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in which he collected the names of his sheikhs from whom he heard the hadith in various regions, and those who authorized him to narrate it from the people of the regions and countries. The author arranged their names according to the order of the dictionary letters in their names and the names of their fathers and grandfathers, starting with the alif chapter. The book falls within the classification of hadith texts, and it represents an important source in the biographies of hadith narrators and its chains of transmission.
descriptions.4673: The book “Makarim Al-Akhlaq” by Al-Tabarani is a collection of hadith texts, in which its author collected chapters on the virtues of good morals by which a believer attains honor during his life and hopes for salvation after his death. The book includes prophetic hadiths arranged under various topics, such as the virtue of good morals, kindness and forbearance, patience and forgiveness, maintaining family ties, providing relief to the needy, caring for orphans and widows, doing good deeds, and supporting the oppressed. The author has shortened the methods and merely mentioned the texts to make it easier to benefit from them.
descriptions.4674: The book “The Noble Manners, Their Excellencies, and their Praiseworthy Ways” by Al-Kharaiti is a book of hadith texts, collecting prophetic hadiths and hadiths urging and desiring to have virtuous morals. The book is organized into multiple sections that cover broad aspects of good morals, such as urging charity and maintaining family ties, modesty, forgiveness, honoring the guest and neighbor, guarding the tongue, covering private parts, fairness, and reconciliation between people, which makes it a comprehensive reference for the virtues of Islamic etiquette and good conduct.
descriptions.4675: The book “From the Hadith of Khaythama bin Sulaiman al-Qurashi al-Atrabelsi” is a collection of the texts of the Prophet’s hadith, narrated by the author Khaythama bin Suleiman al-Atrabelsi with his chains of transmission. The book includes various chapters on the virtues of the Companions, their dignity, sermons and revelations, in addition to noble hadiths and anecdotes, making it a modern work that combines narration and encouragement.
descriptions.4676: The book “Mawarid al-Thirst to the Addendums of Ibn Hibban” by the author Nour al-Din al-Haythami is a book on hadith texts, in which the author collected the excess hadiths that were unique to Sahih Ibn Hibban over the Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and arranged them into jurisprudential chapters to facilitate access to them. The author committed himself to mentioning the hadith with its chain of transmission with the Companion as its narrator, relying on the authentication of Ibn Hibban, while pointing out what may be the subject of the words of some of the memorizers. The book begins with the Book of Faith, then the Book of Knowledge, and includes various sections that include rulings, etiquette, rqaq, interpretation, and others.
descriptions.4677: Al-Muwatta' is a book written by the founder of the Maliki school of thought, Imam Malik ibn Anas, written in the eighth century AD, and it is one of the oldest collections of hadith texts that deal with topics of Islamic law. The Abbasid Caliph Abu Jaafar al-Mansur (d. 158 AH) resorted to Imam Malik during the Hajj season, asking him to write a book on jurisprudence that would bring together the diaspora and organize the writing according to scientific standards that he had set for him, saying: “O Abu Abdullah, put down jurisprudence and write books from it and avoid the hardships of Abdullah bin Omar, and permit Abdullah bin Abbas and the strays of Abdullah bin Masoud, and aim for the middle of matters, and what the imams and companions agreed upon, so that the people can endure.” God willing, we will protect your work and your books, and we will broadcast them throughout the regions and entrust them not to violate them.” …
descriptions.4678: This book is one of the narrations of the Muwatta of Imam Malik ibn Anas, narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani, and it is classified among the texts of the Prophet’s hadith. The book includes jurisprudential chapters in an organized manner that begin with the chapters on prayer and purity, including the rulings on timing, ablution, washing, tayammum, etc., with jurisprudential comments from the narrator compared to the opinions of other jurists.
descriptions.4679: This book is a manuscript of hadiths that includes a collection of noble prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Al-Hasan Al-Jubri with continuous chains of transmission, and it deals with various topics including the rulings on alcohol and circumstances, fulfilling a vow, warning against the temptations of this world, urging charity, and remembrances and supplications, while including some narrations from the Successors in preference among scholars.
descriptions.4680: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Al-Hussein Al-Kilabi with its continuous chains of transmission. It appears from its index that it includes narrations from a number of hadith scholars such as Abu Zur’ah, Abdullah, and Ahmad bin Abi Al-Hawari. The manuscript begins by mentioning the chain of narrators that ends with the companion Abu Hurairah, and includes various hadiths on supplications, virtues, and other religious topics.
descriptions.4681: This book is a manuscript of hadiths that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Sheikh Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ahmed bin Ibrahim Al-Razi on the authority of his sheikhs, and transmitted by the narrations of a number of hadith scholars. The hadiths mentioned in its index address various topics, including the virtues of the Companions and the moral qualities of the Prophet ﷺ. The manuscript also includes in its introduction talk about the covenants that God has imposed on scholars and the necessity of revealing knowledge and not concealing it.
descriptions.4682: This book is part of a manuscript of my hadiths compiled by Al-Hafiz Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi, and it includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as asceticism in this world, the virtue of fasting and charity, the description of Muslim children in Paradise, the conditions of the Day of Resurrection, and other morals and sermons.
descriptions.4683: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Al-Sari bin Yahya on the authority of his sheikhs, with chains of transmission connected to the Companions, especially Jabir bin Abdullah. The hadiths deal with various topics in jurisprudence, etiquette, and religious matters, such as the rulings on sacrifice, ablution, prayer, Friday prayers, zakat, the virtues of good deeds, and the Prophet’s prohibition of certain practices such as marking the face and drinking from the mouth of a waterskin.
descriptions.4684: This book is a manuscript of my hadith that includes the second part of the hadiths of Abu Taher al-Salafi that he narrated on the authority of Sheikh Jaafar al-Sarraj, and it includes chain of transmissions connected to a number of narrators. The manuscript begins by mentioning a series of narrators, leading to narrations that include various topics such as faith, hunting, sacrifices, destiny, males, and marriage, which indicates that it is a collection of hadiths with diverse chapters.
descriptions.4685: This book is a manuscript of hadiths compiled by Imam Abd al-Mu’min ibn Khalaf al-Dumyati, and it includes a collection of hadiths narrated by him from his sheikhs with his chains of transmission, including types of sayings, approvals, novenas, handshakes, chants, and pieces. The compiler begins by mentioning noble prophetic hadiths on various topics such as morals, etiquette, and acts of worship, taking care to explain his narrations and their dates from his sheikhs.
descriptions.4686: This is a hadith manuscript that collects Awali hadiths, selected benefits, and chants, narrated by Sheikh Abu al-Qasim Ali bin Muhammad al-Kufi al-Naysaburi on the authority of his sheikhs. The book includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths on various topics, such as righteousness, fasting, charity, morals, and etiquette, with mention of the narration’s evidence and methods of tolerance, such as hearing and permission.
descriptions.4687: A book that collects narrated hadiths about the virtues of Alexandria and Ashkelon. It is included in the hadith manuscripts, and it contains texts related to the virtues of residence and Rabat in these two cities, and the reward and reward mentioned in that.
descriptions.4688: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of serial hadiths, which are hadiths in which the narrators of the hadith follow a specific quality or condition in the chain of transmission. The manuscript begins with a series of hadiths about good character, addressing topics such as sincerity and good character, through continuous chains of transmission that highlight the narrators’ care in transmitting the hadith and describing their conditions.
descriptions.4689: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of serial hadiths narrated by Ibn Naqa al-Kufi and al-Hanafi on the authority of his sheikhs, and it begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ. The book deals with various religious topics, including what is stated in its index about the prohibition of insulting Muslims and an explanation of the ruling on fighting them.
descriptions.4690: This is a manuscript of my hadith by Abu Naeem Al-Isbahani, which collects supported hadiths related to the chapters of the judiciary, and the author includes critical comments on their chains of transmission and narrations. It appears from the excerpt that the book includes hadiths about virtues and virtues, with the author commenting on some narrators and weakening some hadiths.
descriptions.4691: This book is a manuscript of hadiths that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet excerpted from the book “The Forty Series,” compiled by Imam Al-Hafiz Ali bin Al-Mufaddal Al-Maqdisi. The book begins with a hadith about the Prophet’s intercession for those who commit major sins from his nation, and includes various other hadiths on topics such as intercession, heaven, good character, and harm. The aforementioned hadiths are characterized by their being supported and connected in chain of transmission, with mention of their chains of transmission that include formulas for swearing an oath between narrators.
descriptions.4692: This manuscript is a collection of Prophetic hadiths narrated by Amali Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Dost Al-Alaf, a hadith scholar who died in the year 381 AH. The book includes supported hadiths narrated by the author on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission, and their topics vary between Islamic etiquette, temptations, remembrance, and supplication.
descriptions.4693: This manuscript is a collection of prophetic hadiths selected from the sheikhdom of Abu al-Qasim al-Hussein bin Hibat Allah bin Sasri al-Taghlabi al-Dimashqi, narrated by his student Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ismail bin al-Anmati. The book includes chain of transmission hadiths narrated by Ibn Sosri on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission, and includes narrations of interpretation, remembrances, and prophetic commandments.
descriptions.4694: This book is a manuscript of hadiths written by Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi. It collects selected prophetic hadiths that focus on the strange words in the words of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that people need to use and understand their meanings. The book includes hadiths on various topics, such as gifts, adultery, remembrance, i'tikaf, and complaint, with special attention to explaining the strange linguistic vocabulary contained therein.
descriptions.4695: This book is a manuscript of my hadith, in which Al-Hafiz Wali al-Din Abu Zar’ah Ahmad ibn al-Hafiz Abi al-Fadl Abd al-Rahim al-Iraqi collected hadiths and benefits selected from the hearings of Sheikh al-Musnad Abu al-Faraj Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mubarak al-Ghazi al-Shafi’i, known as Ibn al-Shafi’i. The book includes hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, which makes it one of the hadith works concerned with narrating good hadiths and the heard benefits.
descriptions.4696: This is a manuscript of my hadith that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and stories that Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi selected from the original books of Sheikh Abu Abdullah Al-Tabari in Mecca, and narrated their chain of transmission from him. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the hadith of honoring one’s parents, and its index includes titles of narrations from various sheikhs, such as Al-Nasawi, Al-Yazdi, Al-Qurashi, and Al-Sabouni, which indicates the diversity of his sources in the narration.
descriptions.4697: This hadith manuscript collects news and stories narrated from the sheikhs of Abu Ali Muhammad bin al-Qasim bin Marouf, narrated by his nephew Abd al-Rahman bin Uthman. The book includes prophetic hadiths and traces of companions and followers, in addition to stories from previous nations, such as what was reported about Moses (peace be upon him). The work falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting narratives supported by their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4698: This book is a modern manuscript that includes four sessions written by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ali bin Thabit Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi, which he dictated in the Damascus Mosque on Fridays in Shawwal and Muharram in the year four hundred and fifty-nine. It contains hadiths narrated with chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ, which makes it part of the hadith heritage heard and read in scholarly dictation councils.
descriptions.4699: This book is a hadith section in which its author collected forty hadiths, the chains of transmission of which are distinguished by being novena, meaning that the number of narrators of each hadith in it is less than nine people between him and the Prophet ﷺ. The author extracted these hadiths from his audio narrations, beginning by mentioning the chain of transmission for each hadith, and limiting himself to the text of the noble hadith without explanation or comment. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths with their high chains of transmission.
descriptions.4700: This manuscript is a collection of hadith compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Mufaddal Al-Maqdisi, which includes forty hadiths of the Prophet, in which he adhered to the approach of the hadith imams who preceded him in collecting the Forties, based on what was mentioned in the urging to memorize forty hadiths in the traditions of prophetic wisdom. The author begins his book by praising God and praying for the Prophet, then he begins to narrate the hadiths with their chains of transmission back to the Prophet ﷺ, mentioning the ways in which he narrated them from his sheikhs in Mecca, Alexandria, and elsewhere.
descriptions.4701: This hadith manuscript includes a selected collection of forty prophetic hadiths, extracted from the fourth part of the book “Al-Tibb” by Abu Naim Al-Asbahani, and selected by Abu Bakr bin Ali bin Abi Al-Haram Al-Saqili Al-Qalanisi, known as Ibn Al-Siraj. The hadiths mentioned in the manuscript revolve around various topics related to food, drink, and Prophetic medicine, such as the preference for meat and describing it as the master of eating, and the mention of rice and other foods, with chains of transmission that go back to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4702: This manuscript is the one hundred and twenty-first council of Amali Abu al-Fath al-Maqdisi, and it is part of a series of hadith councils narrated by Sheikh Nasr bin Ibrahim al-Maqdisi with his continuous chains of transmission. The manuscript includes noble prophetic hadiths, some of which relate to the etiquette of meeting needs and reconciliation between people, and some of them relate to the places of prostration in the Holy Qur’an.
descriptions.4703: This book is the one hundred and twenty-eighth council of Amali Abu al-Qasim al-Samarqandi, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet and chain of transmission that were dictated by Sheikh al-Hafiz to his students. The council deals with various topics, including those related to fasting on the day of Ashura and its virtues, narrations about Hajj and Umrah, in addition to some wisdom and sermons.
descriptions.4704: This book is part of the Amali Abu Bakr al-Najjad, which is a hadith manuscript that includes dictation sessions heard by his students, and includes various prophetic hadiths on various topics such as beliefs, acts of worship, etiquette, and temptations, such as seeking refuge from the torment of the grave, the rulings on prayer and selling, the description of the basin, and the prohibition of some evils.
descriptions.4705: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes dictation sessions delivered by Judge Abu Ya’la Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Farra to his students, and lists the Prophet’s hadiths with their chains of transmission connected to the Companions.
