The book deals with various topics of Sunnahs, virtues, and sermons, such as the virtue of fasting on Ashura and Arafah, the characteristics of a believer and a hypocrite, and the dignity of witnesses, based on narrations from major hadith scholars such as Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Baghawi.
descriptions.4706: This book is part of the hopes of Al-Hafiz Abu Zakaria Yahya bin Abdul-Wahhab bin Mandah Al-Asbahani, narrated by Sheikh Abu Abdul-Rahman Muhammad bin Hayyah Al-Habar. It is a hadith manuscript that includes dictation sessions that the author delivered to the ears of his students, and it contains attributed hadiths that he narrates with chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ, which makes it one of the sources of audio hadith narration.
descriptions.4707: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes dictation sessions by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Mandah, narrated by Sheikh Abi Al-Fadl Al-Mutahhar bin Abdul-Wahid Al-Bazani. The book includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as the virtue of the ten days, the virtue of some good deeds such as praising and glorifying God, issues of virtues, temptations, destiny, and other religious topics.
descriptions.4708: This book is a collection of hadiths and narrations about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, dealing with various topics related to Islamic worship and morals, with a focus on fasting in the month of Shaban and Ramadan. The book is considered one of the modern manuscripts that contain narrations from the sheikhs of Al-Jawhari, and it shows the importance of this period of the year in Islam and the fasting customs and traditions related to it.
descriptions.4709: A book that includes forty Prophetic hadiths, selected by the author from his narrations, and whose chains of transmission and texts are distinguished by contrast and differences. The book is included among the hadith manuscripts, and contains hadiths narrated by a number of companions, including Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Omar ibn al-Khattab, and Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them). The author opened it with an introduction to the virtue of the Prophet’s hadith and its importance in Islamic law.
descriptions.4710: This hadith manuscript collects a thousand prophetic hadiths, each of which is supported by a chain of narrators in which the number of narrators increases to seven between the author and the companion. It was compiled by Muhammad bin Kharqi al-Sahri al-Yamani from the originals of the audiobooks of Sheikh Zahir bin Taher al-Shahami. The manuscript includes separate parts of the book, all of which begin with a continuous chain of transmission to the companion Anas bin Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), and include various hadiths about the virtues of the companions, sermons, and acts of worship.
descriptions.4711: This book is a hadith part that includes one hundred hadiths collected from the narrations of Sheikh Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Shurayh al-Ansari, and narrated by his students with continuous chains of transmission. The book deals with various topics in Islamic etiquette, gentleness, and asceticism, such as the virtue of the Qur’an, charity, upholding ties of kinship, the morals of believers, signs of the Hour, and other prophetic hadiths that address religious and worldly affairs.
descriptions.4712: This book is a manuscript of hadiths in which the author collected forty hadiths from the narrations of Imams Al-Bukhari and Muslim, or one of them, and described them as “abdāl” and “enneagrams.” That is, it was mentioned by attributing the ninth number. The graduation aims to present corrected hadiths with high chain of transmission, mentioning the agreements he had with the imams of hadith such as Ahmad bin Shuaib and Al-Tirmidhi. The book begins with an introduction of praise and praise, then begins to narrate the hadiths with their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4713: This is a manuscript of my hadith compiled by Abu Nasr Muhammad bin Ali bin Wad’an, and it includes forty prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, in addition to one hundred wisdoms attributed to Ali bin Abi Talib, the Prophet’s will to him, and one thousand one hundred hadiths censuring this world and praising the afterlife. Some critics have pointed out the weakness of its hadiths and challenged its authorship, which makes the manuscript questionable in terms of its authenticity.
descriptions.4714: This hadith manuscript collects forty prophetic hadiths about the virtue of the poor and people of good character, narrated by the author Abu Taher al-Salafi with his chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, beginning with a hadith describing the garment of poverty that Gabriel dressed the Prophet ﷺ on the Night of the Night Journey. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts that are concerned with collecting hadiths on a specific topic, and its chains of transmission have been deleted as stated in its introduction, noting that the people of the Suffah were forty men.
descriptions.4715: This book is a manuscript of hadiths in which the author Abu al-Mahasin al-Tabsi collected forty hadiths, which he extracted from the books of al-Sihah, and designated them to be from the narrations of the narrators whose name was Muhammad, in a series with an unbroken chain of transmission back to the Prophet ﷺ. The book begins by mentioning the forty hadiths in order, the first of which is a hadith about the virtue of one whose name is Muhammad on the Day of Resurrection. The manuscript includes continuous chains of transmission narrated from sheikhs with the names of two Muhammads.
descriptions.4716: The book “The Forty Series of Divergent Chain of Transmissions” by Ibn al-Mubarrad is a manuscript that is classified as a hadith manuscript. The book contains a collection of noble Prophetic hadiths. It begins by identifying the chain of transmission of the hadith scholars who narrated the hadiths, and continues by mentioning the hadiths themselves. It appears from the beginning of the book that the author aims to collect these hadiths for the benefit of students and Muslims, praying to God to benefit them with them. The book seems to focus on collecting serial hadiths with varying chains of narration, which indicates the importance of chain of transmission and narration in hadith science.
descriptions.4717: A hadith book that includes forty prophetic hadiths, narrated by the author on the authority of forty companions, and grouped them into forty chapters on religion and the laws of Islam. He arranged the hadiths with their chains of transmission, beginning with the hadiths about the Commander of the Faithful Omar ibn al-Khattab, followed by the rest of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them).
descriptions.4718: This hadith manuscript was written by Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr ibn Ahmad al-Hanbali al-Qadri, known as Ibn al-Rassam. It contains forty prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of forty sheikhs of Islam, from whom the hadith was taken in Egypt and the Levant. Through this collection, the author aims to provide a guide to the student of the knowledge of the Noble Hadith, enriching him in the narration of these masters, and being convincing in exaggeration and guidance.
descriptions.4719: This manuscript is a collection of prophetic hadiths, hadiths, and poems that the author dictated from his memorization in a scholarly council after his lessons in the book “Al-Shama’il” by Al-Tirmidhi. He collected them in these papers out of his desire to revive the Sunnah and pay attention to the news before it disappears. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts, and begins with a continuous chain of transmission narrated by the author from his sheikhs, all the way to Al-Hafiz Al-Iraqi and other hadith scholars.
descriptions.4720: This book is the first part of a manuscript of my hadith entitled “The First of the Khula’iyat” by its author, Al-Khula’i, and it includes a group of selected, attributed benefits. The book includes prophetic hadiths and traces of companions and followers, dealing with various topics such as interpretation, the virtues of monotheism, and the testimony that there is no god but God, in addition to religious stories and wisdom, narrated with continuous chains of transmission from a number of narrators.
descriptions.4721: This book is a part of hadith in which Judge Ahmad bin Sulaiman bin Hudhalam narrates prophetic hadiths transmitted by his sheikhs, and it includes a group of diverse hadiths in the sections of jurisprudence, etiquette, chips, jihad, and others, which makes it a hadith manuscript that includes a number of prophetic narrations.
descriptions.4722: This book is the first part of the dictionary of the sheikhs of al-Hafiz al-Dumyati, and it is a manuscript on hadith science that is included in the books of hadith dictionaries. In it, the author lists the biographies of the sheikhs he met and heard from, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, beginning with the chapter Alif. He mentions for each sheikh something from the heard hadith, benefits, or poetry, with an explanation of their classes, deaths, and the height of their chains of transmission.
descriptions.4723: This is a recent manuscript that examines the differences between the narrations of the book “Al-Jami’ Al-Sahih” by Imam Al-Bukhari, and focuses on the discrepancy in the narration of Al-Farbari’s narrators from him, while mentioning other narrations from Ibrahim bin Maqil Al-Nasafi. The author begins by explaining the defects that appear in some copies of the Sahih, and provides examples of errors and corrections that occurred in the names of narrators or the texts of hadiths, correcting them based on the approved copies and the statements of critics.
descriptions.4724: This manuscript is the nineteenth part of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatahah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” and it is classified by Al-Khula’i in the field of hadith manuscripts. The book includes a collection of prophetic hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, and begins with an introduction that mentions the lineage of the narrators and the grading of the hadiths, which indicates that it is part of a hadith work that aims to collect authentic and strange hadiths.
descriptions.4725: This book is the nineteenth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and supported scientific benefits. The author narrates in it on the authority of his sheikhs with his continuous chain of transmission, including hadiths narrated by a number of hadith scholars such as Abu Fath al-Azdi, Abu Bakr al-Shafi’i, and Ibn Shaheen, in addition to poetic extracts and narrations from other sheikhs.
descriptions.4726: This manuscript is the ninth part of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan min Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib” by Al-Qadi Al-Khula’i. It is a hadith book that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, and it begins with an excerpt that deals with the topic of belief in destiny, its good and its evil.
descriptions.4727: This book is the ninth part of “The Baghdad Sheikhdom” by Abu Taher Al-Salafi, and it is a manuscript in the field of the Prophet’s Hadith and its sciences. It contains a collection of hadiths and transmitted hadiths narrated by the author on the authority of his sheikhs, such as Abu Muhammad al-Khallal al-Hafiz and Abu Ali bin Shazan, in addition to including some poems and literary hadiths. The book falls within the books of hadith parts, which collect the hadith’s narrations from his sheikhs with connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4728: This hadith part is the ninth of the series “The Benefits of Abu Othman Al-Buhairi,” and it includes a collection of hadiths and narratives narrated with connected chains of transmission, dealing with various topics that include urging contemplation, explaining the truth of faith, warning against stinginess, the virtue of learning poetry, and other sermons and wisdom.
descriptions.4729: This book is the ninth part of the dictionary of Sheikha Maryam, which is a hadith manuscript that includes biographies of a number of narrators and hadith scholars, mentioning their chains of transmission and narrations. The book begins with the translation of Fatima bint Abd al-Daim al-Maqdisi, and lists her speakers, sheikhs, and the date of her death. Then, it lists other names in the alphabetical order of the dictionary, with the chain of narrators that they narrated.
descriptions.4730: This book is the twenty-ninth part of “Al-Mashaykhat Al-Baghdadi” by Abu Taher Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits, narrated by Al-Salafi on the authority of his sheikhs in Baghdad. The book begins with an authorization from a Salafi from Alexandria, then includes hadith councils from a number of hadith scholars such as Abu Al-Hasan Al-Zaafarani, Abu Muhammad Al-Jawhari, and Al-Qadi Al-Tanukhi, with chains of transmission that go back to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4731: The book “Expansion on Family” by Zain al-Din al-Iraqi is a hadith manuscript that collects the Prophetic hadiths contained in the virtue of spending and expansion on family and dependents, and includes narrations from a number of companions such as Jabir, Ibn Masoud, Abu Hurairah, Abu Saeed al-Khudri, and Ibn Omar. The author begins with an introduction on praise and praise, then moves to a jurisprudential issue related to the ruling on eating chicken and grains on the day of Ashura, quoting a fatwa by Ibn Taymiyyah on the issue, then returning to the narration of the hadiths mentioned in the index.
descriptions.4732: This is a recent manuscript by Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi, in which it collects a number of hadiths and traces related to the virtues of trusting in God, asking Him, and relying on Him in hardship and prosperity, with mentioning the stories of the prophets and the righteous in this section. The book begins by attributing the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ to Ibn Abbas to protect God and trust in Him, then follows it with other news that reinforces the meaning of trust in God and certainty in Him.
descriptions.4733: This is the thirteenth part of the book “Al-Fawaid Al-Muntakatahah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” known as “Al-Khula’iyat” after its narrator, Judge Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as supplication, jihad, purity, prayer, funerals, wills, and other rulings and etiquette.
descriptions.4734: This is the thirteenth part of the Baghdadi Sheikhs, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and traces, narrated by Abu Taher al-Salafi with his chain of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs. The book deals with various topics, including asceticism and solitude, patience in the face of affliction, the virtue of dhikr, the condemnation of lying, and some jurisprudential rulings such as ablution and a concession in the blood of rabbis. The part begins with a talk about the advent of isolation and asceticism on the mountaintops one hundred and eighty years after the Hijra, then it is followed by traces of jurisprudence before isolation.
descriptions.4735: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, collected by Ibn al-Muqri in the thirteenth part of its benefits. The book covers various hadiths on etiquette, worship, temptations, and sermons, such as urging honesty in speaking about the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, the virtue of remembering God, people’s choice of their families, the rulings on purity, prayer, and ablution, and other topics. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, in which he narrates the hadith “Actions are but by intentions,” then follows it with other chained hadiths.
descriptions.4736: This book is the third part of a manuscript of my hadith entitled “The Selected Benefits of the Good and the Strange,” from the narration of Judge Abi Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i. It includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their connected chains of transmission, which falls under the section on comprehensive hadiths and selected benefits.
descriptions.4737: This book is the third part of the collection “The Selected Benefits” compiled by Abu Al-Hasan Al-Harbi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes prophetic hadiths narrated with chains of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs. The book includes a collection of hadiths on various topics, including rulings, virtues, etiquette, and subtleties, such as the rulings on prayer, selling, marriage, jihad, and the virtues of some tribes and deeds. The book begins with an introduction that mentions the series of narrations, then presents the hadiths, with their chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4738: This book is the third part of the collection “Fawaid Abu Uthman al-Buhairi.” It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission. It includes various rulings, virtues, and etiquette, such as the manner of prayer, ablution, dress, will, advice, and other religious topics.
descriptions.4739: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated by Imam Al-Daraqutni from the narration of Abu Omar Muhammad bin Al-Abbas bin Hayyat Al-Khazzaz on the authority of his sheikhs. The hadiths deal with various topics in jurisprudence, acts of worship, and etiquette, such as the witr on a camel, the timing for shaving the pubic and armpits, wiping over the socks and the turban, cupping for the fasting ihram, the virtue of repenting before gargling, the virtue of killing polytheists and killing the Kharijites, wiping the socks off for the traveler and the resident, and the angels’ prayers upon the Prophet and Ali bin Abi Talib.
descriptions.4740: This book is the third part of the Dictionary of Sheikha Maryam, and it is a hadith manuscript written by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. It collects the biographies of a number of narrators and hadith scholars arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, mentioning their chains of transmission and their attributed narrations. It begins with the translation of Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Tawzri Al-Qastalani and mentions his sheikhs and his death, then lists the rest of the names and the related authorizations and hadith narrations.
descriptions.4741: This is the third part of the Dictionary of the Sheikhs of Damietta, which is a hadith manuscript that includes the names of a number of the sheikhs the author met and heard from, along with listing the hadiths that he narrated from them with their chains of transmission. The book begins with the translation of Sheikh Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Lakhmi Al-Iskandari, then the rest of the sheikhs are mentioned in succession, assigning each hadith to its narrator.
descriptions.4742: This hadith part is the thirty-third of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi, and it includes a group of benefits and chain of transmission of hadiths that he narrated on the authority of his sheikhs, including narrations from a number of hadith scholars such as Abu Jaafar Al-Khalidi, Judge Abu Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Al-Wazir Al-Sahib bin Abbad, in addition to various benefits and one hadith about Al-Kiya’ Al-Tabari. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths and hadiths with their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4743: This is the twenty-third hadith part of Abu Tahir al-Salafi’s The Baghdadi Sheikh, and it is a collection of hadiths, benefits, and chain of transmission that the author collected on the authority of his sheikhs. It includes narrations on the authority of Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Shafi’i, and on the authority of a number of hadith scholars such as Abu Bakr al-Shafi’i and Abu Muhammad al-Khallal, in addition to poetic benefits and chain of narrations.
descriptions.4744: This book is the eighteenth part of the series “Al-Fawaid Al-Muntakatahah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths attributed with connected narrations to the Prophet ﷺ. The book begins with the chain of transmission of the first hadith on the authority of Anas bin Malik mentioning the torment in the grave, then the narration of the hadiths with their various chains of transmission continues, making it an example of the parts of the hadith narrated in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4745: This book is the eighteenth part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and chain of transmission of benefits that Al-Salafi narrated on the authority of his sheikhs, including narrations from a number of hadith scholars such as Abu Ali bin Al-Sawaf and Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi. The book falls within the books of hadith parts that collect narrated hadiths with connected chains of transmission, and it contains one story in addition to the narrated hadiths.
descriptions.4746: This eighth hadith part of the parts of Abu Ali bin Shazan includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics including guidance and righteous behavior, economy in worship, the rulings on Hajj and marriage, the virtue of learning the Qur’an, issues in prayer and purity, and mentioning some of the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Companions.
descriptions.4747: This book is the eighth part of the manuscript of my hadith entitled “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan min Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib”, directed by Ahmad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Hussein Al-Shirazi, and narrated by Judge Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Hussein Al-Faqih. The book includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as kindness and good manners, which makes it a model for hadith collections that select authentic and strange hadiths.
descriptions.4748: This book is the eighth part of the collection “Fawa’id Abu Uthman al-Buhairi,” and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as worship, etiquette, chips, temptations, signs of the Hour, and other chapters of the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4749: This book is the eighth part of the Dictionary of Sheikha Maryam, which is a hadith manuscript that includes biographies of a number of narrators and hadith scholars. It begins with a translation of Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Armawi, the Shafi’i Sufi, and mentions his sheikhs, speakers, birth and death, then follows it with other biographies by Ali bin Hassan Al-Tanukhi and others, mentioning their chains of transmission and narrations.
descriptions.4750: This book is the eighth part of the Dictionary of Sheikhs, authored by Abd al-Mu’min ibn Khalaf al-Damiyati, and it contains biographies of a number of scholars, jurists, and historians, most of whom bear the name Muhammad. The book deals with the biographies of these men and their scientific works, relying on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and moral stories that reflect the values ​​of justice and mercy. The book is a hadith manuscript and aims to preserve and document the chain of hadith narrators.
descriptions.4751: This hadith part is the twenty-eighth of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Abu Taher al-Salafi, and it includes a collection of hadiths narrated by the Prophet with their chains of transmission, including what is narrated on the authority of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi and other sheikhs. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with collecting hadiths and narrating them through the sheikhdom and authorisation.
descriptions.4752: This manuscript is the twelfth part of the book “Al-Fawaid Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan Al-Sahih wa Al-Gharaib,” known as “Al-Khula’iyat,” from Al-Khula’i’s classification. It is a hadith part that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, and begins with narrations from the companions Aisha and Abdullah bin Omar (may Allah be pleased with them), which indicates that it falls within the books of hadith collections that select authentic and gharaib hadiths.
descriptions.4753: This book is the twelfth part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths and chain of transmission of hadiths that Al-Salafi narrated on the authority of his sheikhs with his chain of transmission. The book includes selections from the narrations of a number of hadith scholars such as Ibn Bakir, Al-Barqani, and Al-Suri, in addition to the benefits of Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Al-Khallal and others, which makes it an important source in the hadith narration and scholarly approvals.
descriptions.4754: This book is a part of a hadith narrated by Sheikh Abu Ali Al-Hassan bin Ahmed bin Shazan, and it includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics in jurisprudence, etiquette, and sermons, such as the rulings on fasting, the Qiblah, jihad, trade, ablution, the Qur’an, and other rulings and sermons.
descriptions.4755: This book is the second part of Ibn al-Sawaf’s parts, and it is a hadith manuscript that collects prophetic hadiths and traces related to the stories of the prophets, especially the story of Adam (peace be upon him), starting with his creation and breathing the soul into him, and passing through the issue of his age and his giving of forty years to David, his conversation with the angels, his prostration, and his exit from Paradise. The book also includes hadiths about the virtue of Friday, about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his relationship with previous prophets, and his birth in the Year of the Elephant.
descriptions.4756: This book is the second part of Amali Abi Al-Hussein bin Bishran, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths that the author narrated on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission. The hadiths deal with various topics, including the rulings on purity, the signs of the Hour, the virtues of the Companions, and other legal issues, as part of a series of hadith dictates that he dictated to his students.
descriptions.4757: This is the second part of Amali Ibn al-Sammak, which is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of noble prophetic hadiths that the author dictated to his students. The narrated hadiths deal with various topics, including the virtues of ablution and prayer, the rulings on purity and Friday prayers, issues of zakat, divorce, and punishments, in addition to moral commandments and warnings against some sins and heresies. The book begins with the attribution of the first hadith on the authority of Abu Umamah, then the narration of the hadiths continues with their chain of transmission back to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4758: This part is from the manuscript of “Al-Farad” by Imam Al-Daraqutni, which is a hadith collection that specializes in hadiths that were narrated solely by one narrator on the authority of his sheikh. The book includes various prophetic hadiths on various topics such as funerals, charity, bond, commandments, etiquette, temptations, epics, and others, with special care being taken to point out the strangeness of each hadith and the uniqueness of its narrator.
descriptions.4759: This book is the second part of the manuscript of my hadith entitled “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hassan min Al-Sihah Al-Gharaib”, directed by Ahmad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Hussein Al-Shirazi, and narrated by Judge Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Faqih. The book includes prophetic hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, beginning with narrations from companions such as Safwan ibn Assal, and dealing with jurisprudential topics such as wiping the socks, which makes it among the books of hadith collections that narrate oddities and authentic ones.
descriptions.4760: This book is a manuscript of hadiths that includes a collection of selected benefits, narrated by Ibn al-Sammak on the authority of his sheikhs, and includes noble prophetic hadiths on various topics such as Hajj, prayer, zakat, morals, chips, temptations, and other sections of religion.
descriptions.4761: This book is the second part of the book “Al-Misbah fi Uyun al-Sihah,” which is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, and specializes in hadiths that were unique to Imam Muslim in his Sahih. The book begins with a sermon by the Prophet ﷺ in which he teaches the Companions the Sunnahs of Prayer, then includes hadiths on various topics such as purity, oaths and vows, food and drink, the Prophet’s attributes and names, and the stories of some of the Prophets.
descriptions.4762: This book is a manuscript of a hadith compiled by Al-Wakhshi, and it includes a collection of narrated prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as ruqyah, prophetic medicine, jurisprudential rulings such as sales and prayers, the virtues of deeds, and some prophetic stories. The book begins by mentioning multiple hadiths about the black seed and its cure for every disease except poisoning, with repeated narrations with different chains of narration.
descriptions.4763: This book is a hadith part that includes the second group of the narrations of Ali bin Harb al-Tai on the authority of his sheikh Sufyan bin Uyaynah. It contains various prophetic hadiths on topics including etiquette and morals, purity and prayer, marriage and divorce, food and drink, temptations and signs of the Hour, and other sections of jurisprudence and slavery, attributing their chains of transmission to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
descriptions.4764: This book is the second part of my hadith manuscript, which collects hadiths and narrations related to the virtues and virtues of Omar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). The book includes chained narrations that begin with their chains of transmission, and deal with positions and sayings of the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions, clarifying Omar’s position and status, such as the hadith “Abu Bakr, Omar and I were” describing him as one of the masters of the elderly people of Paradise. The work is classified among the hadith manuscripts concerned with collecting the virtues and characteristics of the Companions.
descriptions.4765: This is the second part of a collection of hadiths known as “Fawa’id Abu Uthman al-Buhairi,” compiled and compiled by his student Abu Saad al-Shabi from the audiobooks of his sheikh. The book contains narrated prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, which address various topics in worship, etiquette, and sermons, such as the rulings on prayer and Hajj, the virtue of the first-born, the Prophet’s intercession for those who commit major sins, the virtue of waiting for relief, and other attributed hadiths.
descriptions.4766: This book is the second part of the “Dictionary of Sheikha Maryam”, which is a hadith manuscript compiled by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. It includes chains of transmission and narrations from the sheikhs of hearing and authorization. The manuscript begins with a translation of one of the sheikhs, mentioning his sheikhs, his narrations, and the dates of their deaths, with a narration of the chains of transmission of heard and metaphorical hadiths. The book falls within the hadith works concerned with collecting the names of narrators and methods of reception and narration.
descriptions.4767: This is the second part of the dictionary of the sheikhs of Al-Hafiz Abd al-Mu’min bin Khalaf al-Dumyati. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a list of the names of the sheikhs he met and narrated from them, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary. The manuscript begins with the translation of its sheikh, Muhammad bin Ibrahim al-Tilmisani, and its chain of transmission goes to Imam Malik bin Anas, which indicates his care in narrating the hadith with its continuous chains of transmission. The book combines historical documentation of the names of the narrators and a statement of their classes, and represents an important source in the science of men and the knowledge of the sheikhs of the hadith scholars of his time.
descriptions.4768: This book is the thirty-second part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths, benefits, and chain of narrations, narrated by the author on the authority of his sheikhs, such as Abu Husayn Al-Wada’i, Abu Al-Hussein bin Al-Tayouri, Abu Bakr Al-Shafi’i, and others, with special attention to citing their chains of transmission and the methods of narrating them.
descriptions.4769: This part is the twenty-second of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Taher Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission from a number of sheikhs of Baghdad, such as Abu Ali Al-Maamari, Abu Bakr Al-Najjad and others, and it contains various hadith benefits.
descriptions.4770: This book is the thirtieth part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths and chain of transmission that was narrated by Al-Salafi on the authority of his sheikhs. The book includes the benefits of a number of narrators, such as Abu Omar bin Haywa, Ibn al-Fadl al-Qattan, al-Barjalani, and Hanad. It contains various narrations that include prophetic hadiths, news about the predecessors, and historical tales.
descriptions.4771: This book is the third part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a manuscript in the science of hadith that collects the chains of transmission and narrations of a number of Baghdad sheikhs. The book includes hadiths narrated from sheikhs such as Abu Al-Hasan bin Al-Khal, Abu Ali Al-Sawaf, Al-Lalikai, Al-Shafi’i, and others, with special attention to mentioning the methods of receiving and authorizing them. The manuscript begins by attributing the hadith of the Night Journey on the authority of Abu Hurairah, then lists the rest of the hadiths and the transmitted benefits.
descriptions.4772: This book is the third part of my hadith manuscript that includes a collection of chain of transmission from the Prophet, compiled by the author Abu Ali Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Sawaf, selected by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Hasan Al-Daraqutni, and narrated by Abu Naeem Al-Isfahani. The manuscript contains one hundred and sixty-eight hadiths, beginning with hadiths about temptations and the conditions of the grave and resurrection, and includes various topics in beliefs, etiquette, and sermons.
descriptions.4773: This book is the eighth part of the Baghdadi Sheikhdom, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths and chain of narrations collected by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission from a number of sheikhs, and includes various chapters such as the Hadith of Al-Adam and the Hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri, in addition to benefits and dreams narrated from some scholars.
descriptions.4774: This manuscript is the second part of the narrations of Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Omar Al-Harbi, and it is one of the books of hadith with chain of transmission that includes hadiths narrated with a chain of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ. The manuscript contains hadiths narrated by Al-Harbi on the authority of his sheikhs, with multiple speakers and narrations by later narrators, making it a model for the hadith parts that preserved narration methods in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4775: This part of “Al-Mashikhat Al-Baghdadi” by Abu Taher Al-Salafi is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted reports, collected by the author from his sheikhs through dictation and hearing sessions. The book begins with hadiths from Ibn Bishran and other hadith scholars, and includes separate chapters from the narrations of Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Ghailan, Al-Jawhari, Ibn Shaheen, and Ibn Al-Samarqandi, in addition to benefits and a serial hadith from the narration of Ibn Al-Siraj.
descriptions.4776: This manuscript is the second part of the hadiths of Abu Muhammad Hajib bin Ahmad al-Tusi, and it is a collection of chain of narrations that al-Tusi narrates on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission. The book includes noble prophetic hadiths and narrations about the Companions and followers, covering various topics such as morals, virtues, and acts of worship, in addition to some historical and attributional news.
descriptions.4777: This book is the fifth part of “Al-Mashikhat Al-Baghdadi” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths and transmitted hadiths that the author narrated on the authority of his sheikhs. The book includes chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ, in addition to benefits and narrations from a number of hadith scholars such as Abd al-Aziz al-Azji, Ibn al-Tuwayri, al-Harith bin Abi Usama and others, which makes it an important source in the science of hadith and narration of chain of transmission.
descriptions.4778: This manuscript is the fourth part of the book “Al-Fawa’id Al-Awali Al-Muntakafa,” known as “Al-Thaqafiyyat.” It is compiled by Al-Qasim bin Al-Fadl Al-Thaqafi, and is included in the manuscripts of the Prophet’s Hadith. It contains hadiths narrated with high chains of transmission, including what was narrated by his sheikhs, such as Abu al-Fath Hilal bin Muhammad and others. It appears from its introduction that it was heard and narrated by a number of narrators, such as Abu Taher al-Salafi and others, with care being taken to adjust the speakers and permissions.
descriptions.4779: This manuscript is the fourth part of the book “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Awali”, which is a collection of hadith selected by Al-Hafiz Omar bin Jaafar Al-Basri from the hadiths of Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Jaafar Al-Quta’i on the authority of his sheikhs. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating hadiths supported by high levels of chain of transmission. The copy included multiple speakers from narrators across different classes, which reflects the interest of hadith scholars in transmitting and narrating these hadiths.
descriptions.4780: This book is the fourth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhdom” by Abu Taher Al-Salafi, and it is a manuscript in the field of Prophetic Hadith. The book includes a group of hadiths and attested narrations that the author narrates from his sheikhs, including attributions connected to the Prophet ﷺ, as in the hadith mentioned at the beginning about the division of mercy. Its index contains titles of narrations from a number of hadith scholars, such as Ibn Hayyan, Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Hanbal, and Abu Bakr Al-Khatib, which makes it a model for books on sheikhs that collect parts of the author’s audiobooks.
descriptions.4781: This book is the fourth part of the series “The Quartet of the Followers” ​​by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Musa Al-Madini. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths that are narrated with quatrain chains of transmission, meaning that between its narrator and the Prophet ﷺ are only four men. The hadiths mentioned in his index deal with various topics, including the virtues of deeds such as Umrah in Ramadan, etiquette and morals such as good manners and kindness, the rulings on prayer such as congregational prayer and prostration, and jurisprudential issues such as the ruling on someone who finds his belongings with a bankrupt person.
descriptions.4782: This is the sixth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a group of hadiths and chain of transmission that the author heard or was approved by the sheikhs of Baghdad. The book begins with a hadith about raising the hands in prayer, and the table of contents includes chains of transmission from a number of hadith scholars, such as Abu al-Abbas al-Basir al-Razi, Ibn al-Tuwayri, and Abu Bakr al-Khatib, which makes it an example of dictionary or sheikh books that collect the narrations of a specific narrator from his sheikhs.
descriptions.4783: This book is the twentieth volume of the Baghdadi Sheikhs. It is a hadith manuscript that includes chains of transmission and narrations from a number of sheikhs. The author, Abu Taher al-Salafi, collected and selected them. The book begins with an authorization and hearing, then presents prophetic hadiths and narrations from the Companions with continuous chains of transmission, which makes it a model for books of hadith parts that are concerned with narrating narrations by attributing the author to his sheikhs.
descriptions.4784: This is a manuscript of a hadith by Muhammad al-Badiri al-Damiyati al-Shafi’i, in which the author collects a number of high-quality hadith chains that are characterized by their small number of narrators and their closeness to the Prophet ﷺ. He opened the book by praising God and praising Him, then he began to mention the chains of transmission that scholars paid attention to in the past, explaining the virtue of seeking the hadith and the high chain of transmission, and the efforts made by the hadith scholars in collecting and preserving it.
descriptions.4785: This book is the eleventh part of the manuscript of my hadith entitled “The Selected Benefits of Al-Hasan Al-Sihah and Al-Gharaib,” from the narration of Judge Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i. The book includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, and begins with a talk about Omar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)’s charity with his money from Khaybar. The manuscript combines authentic and strange hadiths in the context of hadith classification.
descriptions.4786: This book is the eleventh part of the “Baghdadi Sheikhdom” series compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and hadiths narrated with continuous chains of transmission from the sheikhs of Baghdad. The book begins with the Salafi authorizing his students, then lists hadiths narrated by narrators such as Al-Quta’i, Abu Othman Al-Sabouni, and Al-Daraqutni, including texts urging people to do without people and not to decorate mosques, in addition to some narrations from the Salaf.
descriptions.4787: This book is the eleventh part of the Dictionary of Sheikha Maryam. It is a hadith manuscript that includes biographies of a number of narrators and hadith scholars, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, mentioning their names, lineages, sheikhs, and dates of their deaths. It contains chains of transmission and narrations attributed to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4788: This book is the thirty-first part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes one hadith with a chain of transmission that the author narrates with his chain of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs. The book falls within the books of Hadith parts that deal with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths with their connected chains of transmission. The excerpt includes a hadith about seeing the Prophet ﷺ in the Farewell Pilgrimage and the story of the blessed boy.
descriptions.4789: This hadith part is the fifty-first of the Amali al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, and it includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission back to the Prophet ﷺ, mentioning the methods of narration and follow-ups. The content of the book is dominated by hadiths related to fasting and its virtues, such as fasting three days of every month and fasting on the white days, in addition to other hadiths on etiquette and worship.
descriptions.4790: This book is the twenty-first part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhdom” by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi, and it is a manuscript in the field of the noble Prophet’s hadith. The book includes a group of hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission from a number of sheikhs of Baghdad, such as Abu Bakr al-Jawhari and Abu al-Hussein bin Bishran, and begins with narrations from the companions such as Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, al-Baraa bin Azib, and Jabir bin Abdullah. This part falls within the books of hadith parts, which collect hadiths narrated through approval and hearing from specific sheikhs.
descriptions.4791: This book is the fifteenth part of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatahah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a group of attributed prophetic hadiths, and it begins with narrations related to the virtues of fasting Ramadan and praying for Laylat Al-Qadr. The work falls within the hadith heritage narrated with continuous chains of transmission, and is concerned with collecting authentic hadiths and selected strange ones.
descriptions.4792: This book is the fifteenth part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits. In this part, the author narrates hadiths from his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission, including narrations from a number of hadith scholars, such as Abu Bakr al-Shafi’i, al-Daraqutni, and Ibn al-Tuwayri. The topics of the hadiths vary between dhikr, legal ruqyah, and other religious issues.
descriptions.4793: This book is the fifth part of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hassan min Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib.” It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission. It includes hadiths on various topics such as seeking permission and consideration, inheritance between a Muslim and an infidel, the virtue of the Umrah of Ramadan, the virtue of companions such as Omar, Ali and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them), and other issues such as the prohibition of deserting and lying to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4794: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of selected prophetic hadiths, collected by Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni and narrated with his continuous chains of transmission. The selected hadiths address various topics of worship and etiquette, such as night prayer and Witr prayer, the virtue of the Companions, advising one’s neighbor, and warning against the torment of Hell. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting the Prophet’s hadiths with their chains of transmission.
descriptions.4795: This book is the fifth part of a manuscript of my hadiths compiled by Abu Ali Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Wakhshi, and selected from the hadiths of Abu Naim Al-Asbahani. The book includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics including Islamic morals and etiquette, encouragement and intimidation, softening, asceticism, characteristics of believers, conditions of the afterlife, and warnings against lying to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4796: This hadith part is the fifth of Ibn Haywayh al-Khazzaz’s Mashaykh, and it is a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs, and it was narrated by Imam al-Daraqutni. The book includes hadiths on various jurisprudential topics, such as the rulings on prayer, fasting, purity, and inheritance, in addition to hadiths on etiquette and prohibitions against lying to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4797: This book is the fifth part of the dictionary of Sheikha Maryam, which is a hadith manuscript that includes biographies of a number of narrators and hadith scholars, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, and begins with the rest of the letter ha. The book includes a list of the names of the narrators, their lineages, sheikhs, students, and dates of their deaths, along with examples of narrations and chains of transmission.
descriptions.4798: This is the fifth part of the Dictionary of the Sheikhs of Al-Hafiz Al-Dumyati, which is a modern manuscript that includes the biographies of thirty-six sheikhs whom he met and narrated from, whose names begin with Muhammad ibn Abd al-Azim and end with Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Andalusi. In each translation, the author mentions the name of the Sheikh, his lineage, his country, and his sect, then he cites with his chain of transmission some of the hadiths or authorizations he heard from him, mentioning the circumstances of the hearing and the date.
descriptions.4799: This book is the thirty-fifth part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhdom” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits that the author narrated from his sheikhs in Baghdad. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, and includes narrations from a number of hadith scholars such as Abd al-Aziz al-Azji, Hanad al-Nasafi, and Judge Abu al-Qasim al-Tanukhi, making it a source of hadith narration in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4800: This book is the twenty-fifth part of the series “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths and transmitted hadiths that Al-Salafi narrated on the authority of his sheikhs. The book contains narrations from a number of hadith scholars and jurists such as Abu al-Fadl al-Zuhri, Abu Bakr al-Shafi’i, Ibn Battah al-Akbari, and others, which makes it a source of hadith narration in the Islamic heritage.
descriptions.4801: This book is the fourteenth part of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib” compiled by Judge Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as the virtue of the call to prayer and the iqama, intercession, the basin, the attributes of the Prophet ﷺ, the virtues of some of the companions, and other Islamic rulings and etiquette.
descriptions.4802: This book is the fourteenth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhdom” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a manuscript in the field of the Prophet’s Hadith and includes a collection of hadiths and chain of transmission. In this part, the author narrates hadiths from his sheikhs, such as Abu Nasr ibn al-Banna and Abu al-Hasan al-Maqdisi, with chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ, touching on various topics, including the virtues of Quraysh and some prophetic events.
descriptions.4803: This book is the fourth part of my hadith manuscript entitled “The Selected Benefits of the Good from the Sahih and Ghareeb,” compiled by Al-Khula’i. It includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, selected from the sources of authentic and gharib hadith, and it begins with an introduction that mentions the chain of narrators and the path of hearing and authorization.
descriptions.4804: This book is the fourth part of the collection “Fawa’id Abu Uthman al-Buhairi,” and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission. The hadiths mentioned in its index deal with various topics, including the virtues of deeds, Islamic etiquette, rulings on acts of worship and transactions, softening, temptations, and other chapters of the Sunnah of the Prophet. The book begins with the chain of transmission of the hadith “Islam began as a strange thing,” then it is followed by other hadiths with continuous chains of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4805: This book is the fourth part of the “Dictionary of Sheikha Maryam” by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. It is a manuscript in the science of hadith and falls within the books of hadith dictionaries that arrange the names of narrators and sheikhs according to the letters of the dictionary. The book includes biographies of a number of hadith scholars and narrators, male and female, starting with those named “Asma,” “Aqush,” “Aydmar,” and others, along with a narration of their chains of transmission and attributed narrations, including what the author narrates with authority from his sheikhs.
descriptions.4806: This is the fourth part of the Dictionary of the Sheikhs of Damietta, which is a modern manuscript that includes the biographies of thirty-three of the author’s sheikhs, starting in order from Muhammad ibn Sanqar to Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz. The author lists the names of his sheikhs, their lineages, and their countries, then he cites with his chain of transmission the hadiths and narrations that he heard about them, following the method of the hadith scholars in presenting the chains of transmission and texts.
descriptions.4807: This book is the thirty-fourth part of the “Baghdadi Sheikhdom” series compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits. The book contains narrations from various sheikhs, including the benefits of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ateeqi and Abu Muhammad Al-Jawhari, in addition to hadiths from the narration of Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Hanbal on the authority of his father, and other hadith chains and narrations.
descriptions.4808: This book is the twenty-fourth part of the “Baghdadi Sheikhdom” series compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi, and it is a manuscript in the field of Prophetic Hadith. It contains a collection of hadiths and transmitted hadiths narrated by the Salafis on the authority of his sheikhs, such as Abu Muhammad al-Khallal, Abu Abdullah al-Souri, Abu al-Hussein bin Bishran, and others, in addition to some poetic verses and stories. The book falls within the books of hadith parts, which collect the narrations of one narrator from his sheikhs with connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4809: This is a manuscript of my hadith that collects the biographies of fourteen narrators of the Prophet’s hadith, who are famous for having “Abdullah” in their names, and they are from the class of sheikhs of Imam al-Bukhari or from his class. The author begins by mentioning their names, then gives each of them something from his narrations supported by his chains of transmission, beginning with Al-Qanabi and the famous hadith of intentions.
descriptions.4810: This book is a manuscript of hadiths compiled by Al-Hafiz Diya’ al-Din al-Maqdisi, and it specializes in mentioning the narrators who narrated on the authority of Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi, the author of al-Sahih. The author lists the names of these narrators, attributing to them the hadiths and narrations they received from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, beginning by mentioning his chains of transmission to each narrator.
descriptions.4811: This manuscript is the seventeenth part of the series “The Selected Benefits of Al-Hasan Al-Sihah and Al-Gharaib” compiled by Al-Khula’i. It is a hadith book that includes prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission. The part begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, and at the beginning it deals with the story of the man who asked for a fatwa regarding the punishment for adultery, which indicates that its content revolves around the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths in various rulings and sermons.
descriptions.4812: This book is the seventeenth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits, narrated by the author on the authority of his sheikhs with a continuous chain of transmission. The book begins with hadiths from Abu Zakaria al-Bukhari and other narrators, and includes passages from the hadiths of Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal, Abu Bakr al-Shafi’i, and a group of hadith scholars, making it a model for books of hadith parts that collect various narrations from multiple sheikhs.
descriptions.4813: This book is the seventh part of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan min Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib,” and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, and begins with excerpts related to the virtues and rewards of Hajj. The work falls within the hadith heritage, which is concerned with collecting authentic and strange hadiths and narrating them through continuous chain of transmission.
descriptions.4814: This book is a part of a narrated hadith, compiled by Abu Othman Al-Buhairi, and includes a collection of various Prophetic hadiths in different sections of jurisprudence, etiquette, and subtleties, such as the virtue of the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, the rulings on marriage, clothing, and purity, the virtue of the siwak, the prohibition of selling loyalty, and visiting graves. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ in a hadith about the Tree of Paradise, and then continues to narrate the hadiths with their chains of transmission.
descriptions.4815: This book is the seventh part of the Dictionary of Sheikha Maryam, and it is a hadith manuscript compiled by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. It includes biographies of a number of narrators and hadith scholars arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, and begins with the one named Abdul Aziz, with a mention of their chains of transmission and attributed narrations.
descriptions.4816: This is the seventh part of the Dictionary of the Sheikhs of Damietta, which is a modern manuscript that includes biographies of a number of the author’s sheikhs. It begins with the translation of Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Zaid and ends with the translation of Muhammad bin Al-Muzaffar bin Al-Munir, and they number thirty-one sheikhs. The book includes chains of transmission and narrations that the author heard about these sheikhs, mentioning the lineage of each sheikh and the method of receiving him, which makes it an important source in the science of attribution and narration.
descriptions.4817: This book is the twenty-seventh part of the “Baghdadi Sheikhdom” series compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits. In this part, the Salafi narrates, with his chain of transmission on the authority of Baghdadi sheikhs, such as Abu Muhammad al-Khallal and others, various hadiths, including those related to faith, vows, and other legal topics.
descriptions.4818: This book is the sixteenth part of the series “The Selected Benefits of Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wal-Gharaib” collected by Ahmed bin Al-Hasan Al-Shirazi, and narrated by Judge Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as prayer, funerals, religion, jihad, marriage, temptations, signs of the Hour, and other rulings and sermons.
descriptions.4819: This book is the sixteenth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission from the sheikhs of Baghdad. The book begins by mentioning the chains of transmission of the hadith from narrators such as Ibn al-Ghariq and al-Qadi Abu al-Hussein al-Hashimi, and includes hadiths on various topics such as the virtue of times and mention of temptations, which makes it a model for books of hadith parts that collect the narrations of a specific sheikh or a specific country.
descriptions.4820: This book is the sixth part of the manuscript of my hadith entitled “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan min Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib”, directed by Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Shirazi, and narrated by Judge Abi Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Faqih. The book includes a group of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission. It begins with an introduction that proves hearing the narrators and their narrations. Then it cites hadiths with chain of transmission from the Companions, including the hadith of seeing the Lord, Blessed and Most High.
descriptions.4821: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and narrated hadiths with their chains of transmission, collected by the author Abu Othman Al-Buhairi in the sixth part of its benefits. The hadiths deal with various topics, including interpretation, the virtues of deeds, temptations, and judicial rulings, such as the hadith explaining the verse about killing a believer, the hadith describing the antichrist, and the hadith about the virtue of Surah Blessed. The manuscript begins with the chain of transmission of the hadith of Ibn Abbas on the issue of the repentance of the intentional killer of a believer, then the narration of the chain of transmission of the hadiths continues.
descriptions.4822: This book is the sixth part of Ibn Hayyah al-Khazzaz’s Mashaykh, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs, and it was compiled by Imam al-Daraqutni. The hadiths deal with various topics, including the provisions of purity, prayer, zakat, jihad, and commandments, in addition to some linguistic interpretations of Qur’anic verses, through narrations with a connected chain of transmission.
descriptions.4823: This book is the sixth part of the dictionary of Sheikha Maryam, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes biographies of hadith narrators and students of knowledge, arranged according to the letters of the dictionary, beginning with the letter al-ayn. The author lists the biographies of the hadith scholars, with their names, lineages, sheikhs, and dates of their deaths, along with examples of the hadiths they narrated with their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4824: This is the sixth part of the Dictionary of the Sheikhs of Al-Hafiz Al-Dumyati, which is a modern manuscript that includes the biographies of thirty-two of his sheikhs. It begins with the translation of Muhammad bin Ali bin Mahmoud and follows it with the translation of Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Rustam. In each translation, the author mentions the names of the sheikhs, their lineages, and their countries, then he cites the hadiths he heard about them with their connected chains of transmission, beginning by mentioning his first sheikh and the way he heard him from him.
descriptions.4825: This book is the twenty-sixth part of the “Baghdadi Sheikhdom” series compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and transmitted benefits. The book contains narrations from a number of hadith sheikhs, such as Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami, Abu Hatim Al-Labban Al-Razi, and Hanad Al-Nasafi, in addition to individual stories and narrations. The manuscript begins with a long chain of transmission that narrates the Prophet’s sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage and his praise of the Companions.
descriptions.4826: This manuscript by Al-Maqrizi is a brief treatise devoted to studying the news of Tamim Al-Dari (may Allah be pleased with him), where the author begins with an introduction about the origin of humanity and the lineage of nations, agreeing with the Islamic consensus that all people are descendants of Adam and then Noah, peace be upon them, and exposing the opinions of other nations such as India and China regarding the story of the flood. The book is included among the modern manuscripts, and in its first chapters it deals with issues of lineage and tribal divisions of the Arabs, in preparation for arriving at the news of the great companions of Tamim al-Dari.
descriptions.4827: This book is the tenth part of “The Baghdadi Sheikhs” by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of hadiths from the Prophet and the transmitted benefits that Al-Salafi narrated from his sheikhs in Baghdad. The book includes hadiths narrated by a number of hadith scholars, such as Abu Muhammad al-Khallal, Ibn al-Tuwayri, and Abu Ahmad al-Yashkari, in addition to one audio anecdote. This part falls within the Sheikhs series, which is concerned with collecting the sheikh’s chains of transmission and his narrations from his sheikhs in a specific country.
descriptions.4828: This is the tenth part of the book “The Lamp in the Eyes of Al-Sihah”, which is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, taken from Sahih Muslim. The book begins with the chain of transmission of the hadith of Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad in the story of milk, then it lists various hadiths on various topics such as wills, faith, punishments, temptations, rulings on transactions, and other sections of religion.
descriptions.4829: This book is the tenth of Sheikha Maryam’s collections, and it is written by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani. The book covers the biographies and sayings of a number of scholars and jurists, providing information about their scientific and religious lives, relying on the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths and historical stories related to them. The book is a type of hadith manuscript, and it reviews the lives of scholars from various Islamic sects, with a focus on transmitting hadiths and sayings that they heard or narrated.
descriptions.4830: This hadith part is the twentieth of the series “Al-Fawa’id Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wa Al-Gharaib” compiled by Al-Khula’i. It includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various jurisprudential rulings such as purity, prayer, and zakat, in addition to etiquette and sermons.
descriptions.4831: This manuscript is classified by Ibn al-Jazari in the science of hadith, and deals with the topic of “Al-Awali,” that is, hadiths whose chain of transmission has a small number of narrators. The author begins the book with praise and praise for God, then explains the virtue of the high chain of transmission and its importance among the imams of hadith, quoting sayings from major hadith scholars such as Yahya ibn Ma’in and Ahmad ibn Hanbal urging seeking it and considering it a closeness to God.
descriptions.4832: This book is a manuscript of my hadiths compiled by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Ismail bin Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Isbahani, and it includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths whose chain of transmission was distinguished by its superiority and agreement with the sheikhs of Imam Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The author arranged his hadiths according to the letters of the dictionary, beginning with his name Ahmad, blessing him with the name of the Prophet ﷺ, intending to collect one hundred hadiths known as “The Hundred of Al-Muwafaqat Al-Awali.” The book deals with various topics of rulings, etiquette, tenderness, and temptations, which makes it a reference in the science of good deeds and approvals according to hadith scholars.
descriptions.4833: This book is a modern manuscript that includes dictation councils by two sheikhs, Nasr bin Abdul Aziz Al-Farisi and Abu Zakaria Abdul Samad bin Ahmed Al-Bukhari. It was collected and narrated by Abu Jaafar Ahmed bin Yahya bin Al-Jaroud. The book includes various prophetic hadiths on topics such as the virtue of fasting and remembrance, and an explanation of some rulings such as the prohibition of sexual intercourse with women, and the virtues of deeds such as taking a brother’s side, in addition to moral commandments such as modesty and seeking the truth.
descriptions.4834: This book is a manuscript of a hadith in which its author collected a group of attributed Prophetic hadiths, including various jurisprudential rulings such as purity, zakat, Hajj, and punishments, in addition to sermons and virtues for deeds. It appears from its index that it includes hadiths on various topics such as charity, honesty, ablution, wine, dogs, Hajj, and jihad, with special attention to the chains of transmission and methods of narration, as appears from its introduction.
descriptions.4835: This book is the first part of a collection of hadiths titled “The Benefits Extracted from the Principles of Abu Al-Hussein’s Speakers”, compiled by Abu Al-Hussein Ali bin Ghanaim Al-Maliki Al-Kharqi. The book contains prophetic hadiths narrated with continuous chains of transmission, including what was narrated on the authority of Imam al-Shafi’i, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and it includes comments and narrations from a number of hadith scholars and jurists. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with collecting high-quality chains of narrations and benefits heard from the sheikhs.
descriptions.4836: The book “Al-Fawaid Al-Muntakatah Al-Hasan Al-Sihah wal-Gharaib” is a hadith manuscript compiled by Abi Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i. It includes a collection of hadiths and narrated hadiths with their chains of transmission, with a graduation by Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Shirazi. The book deals with various topics, including the interpretation of some Qur’anic verses and narrations on virtues and sermons, which makes it one of the hadith sources concerned with transmitting authentic and strange hadiths.
descriptions.4837: This book is part of a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of selected prophetic hadiths that meet the conditions of authenticity according to Imams Bukhari and Muslim. The book begins with the hadith, “Actions are based on intentions,” supported by a series of narrators. The table of contents includes hadiths on various topics, such as supplication when seeing rain, warning against consuming a Muslim’s wealth by false oaths, explaining the ruling on intoxicants, and other hadiths that are attributed to the Prophet.
descriptions.4838: This hadith manuscript, entitled “The Selected Benefits and the Beautiful Strangeties Called the Sheikhdom of Mosul,” was produced by Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Fahm al-Abbasi al-Dimashqi. It includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and the transmitted benefits that the author narrated on the authority of his sheikhs, with special attention to mentioning their chains of transmission and the methods of narrating them. The book begins with narrations and authorizations transmitted by his students, then he cites the hadiths with continuous chains of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, making it a model for hadith sheikhs that collect the narrations of one narrator about his sheikhs in a specific country.
descriptions.4839: This is a manuscript of my hadith by Imam Abu Musa al-Madini, which deals with study and analysis of the hadith of lying down narrated on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, and examines its chain of transmission and text, with a focus on the narration reported by the companion Abu Sa`id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) and his position on the prohibition of the aforementioned lying position.
descriptions.4840: This is a manuscript of my hadith by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, devoted to speaking about the hadith “My wife does not reject the hand of someone who touches her.” He discusses the condition of the hadith and its ruling, mentions those who narrated it from the Sunan and Musnad narrators, gives the context of its text and its various narrations, and answers questions related to its meaning and the man and woman mentioned in it.
descriptions.4841: The book “Al-Marhamah Al-Ghaithiya with Al-Laythiya Translation” is a hadith manuscript written by Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, in which it collects brief news about Imam Al-Layth bin Saad, with some of his hadith stories. The author arranged the book into eight sections, including the translator’s lineage, birth, pursuit of knowledge, and scholars’ praise of him for his jurisprudence and memorization of hadith, then he concluded it with selected hadiths. The material came in response to a request from a group of brothers, to be a reminder of the era of Al-Laith bin Saad and an insight into his condition.
descriptions.4842: This is a hadith manuscript that includes a group of parts of hadith with chain of transmission, collected by Abu Tahir al-Salafi and narrated by his sheikhs in Baghdad. It contains about one thousand and six hundred hadiths with their chains of transmission, including those related to rulings, virtues, and gentleness. Its material is arranged in sequential parts starting from the second part and ending with the thirtieth part, with the first and seventh parts missing.
descriptions.4843: The book “The Lamp in the Eyes of the Prophet” is a hadith manuscript written by Abd al-Ghani ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Maqdisi, and it includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of the Companions, based on the sayings of Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj. The book deals with various topics, including the provisions of prayer, ablution, clothing, food, drink, signs of the Hour, temptations, and Islamic etiquette, based on a series of chain of narrations.
descriptions.4844: This manuscript is “Al-Mukhtab min Amali Ibn Hajar min Takhrij Mukhtasar Ibn Al-Hajib”, and it is classified by Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani in the field of Prophetic Hadith. The book is included among the hadith manuscripts, and contains a summary and commentary on Ibn al-Hajib’s summary, with chains of transmission and narrations connected to the Prophet ﷺ, as appears in its opening, which includes a series of sheikhs and sermons.
descriptions.4845: This is a manuscript of my hadith compiled by Al-Dhia Al-Maqdisi, and arranged according to the names of his sheikhs. It includes hadiths from the Prophet, including those related to fasting, washing on Fridays, prayer, travel, emancipation, and other rulings and etiquette. There was a mixing of the leaves of this manuscript with another manuscript in the same collection, which led to some suspicion that it was part of Ibn Hamkan’s Fawa’id, which is not the case.
descriptions.4846: This book is a modern manuscript in which its author collected a number of hadiths and reports related to the grace of praise to God Almighty, and what was stated regarding its legitimacy in opening matters of concern, in sermons, when sleeping and waking up, and when eating and drinking. The book includes marfoo’ hadiths and narrations from the Companions, including those related to the well-known formulas of praise and their virtues, along with their chains of transmission and ways of narrating them.
descriptions.4847: This hadith manuscript is entitled “In the Language of the Eager Student in Sahih Awali Al-Hadith” written by Muwaffaq Al-Din Ibn Qudamah Al-Maqdisi, and graduated by Al-Diya’ Al-Maqdisi, and it is a collection of authentic prophetic hadiths that are characterized by a high chain of transmission. The manuscript includes chains of transmission linked to the Prophet ﷺ, with a grading of some hadiths and an explanation of who among the authors of books considered Muslim to have produced them.
descriptions.4848: This book is the second part of my hadith manuscript, which includes a collection of authentic prophetic hadiths narrated by Imam Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi with high chains of transmission. In it, he collected various hadiths on rulings, etiquette, sermons, temptations, and others, which appear from the indexes of its topics. The book begins by mentioning the chains of transmission of the narration connected to the Prophet ﷺ, which indicates the author’s attention to the quality of the chain of transmission and the authenticity of the hadith.
descriptions.4849: This is a manuscript of my hadith by Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, which deals with the topic of delaying injustices and grievances until the Day of Resurrection, based on the Prophet’s hadiths and narrations. The book begins with the story of Tha'labah bin Hatib with the Prophet ﷺ, and what happened to him when he asked for money and the test of charity, which explains an aspect of the rulings of darkness and the consequences of denying rights.
descriptions.4850: The book “Nine Councils of Amali Tarrad bin Muhammad al-Zainabi” is a modern manuscript that includes a group of scholarly councils dictated by Sharif Abu al-Fawaris Tarad al-Zainabi, and it was directed by Sheikh Abu Ali al-Bardani. The book includes narrated prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, with references to those among the authors of the two Sahihs, such as Al-Bukhari and Muslim, who were the only ones to narrate them, making it a model for the hadith books that were presented in public assemblies.
descriptions.4851: Three sessions from the dictation of Abu al-Qasim bin Bishran, a manuscript of my hadith that includes dictation sessions that I heard from Sheikh Abu al-Qasim Abdul Malik bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bishran. They include narrated hadiths with their chains of transmission, including those related to the jurisprudence of fasting and others. The manuscript also includes a group of hadiths from the narrations of Abu Al-Faraj Al-Tanajiri on the authority of his sheikhs. These councils and narrations were collected in one part with the narration of Al-Mubarak bin Ali bin Abdul Baqi Al-Baghdadi.
descriptions.4852: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes three collections of dictation from al-Hafiz Abu Sa`id al-Naqqash, which his students heard from him. The book contains a collection of prophetic hadiths and narrated hadiths with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics that include acts of worship such as seclusion in Ramadan and praising God in prayer, etiquette such as urging gratitude for blessings and condemning haste, jurisprudential rulings such as amputating the hand of a thief and the dislike of fasting while traveling, and virtues such as the virtue of walking to mosques in the dark.
descriptions.4853: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes three sessions written by the Sufi Sheikh Abu Abdullah Al-Rawdhabari, which he dictated in Jami’ Sour, and he narrates it with a chain of transmission from Imam Ali bin Abi Talib on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ. The manuscript includes a collection of various prophetic hadiths on topics including the virtues of deeds, etiquette, and jurisprudential rulings such as sales, inheritance, and divorce, in addition to commandments and sermons.
