descriptions.4854: This is part of my hadith in which Adam bin Abi Iyas narrates chained prophetic hadiths, which include various topics such as the virtue of Surat Yasin, the blessing of the firstborn, the fulfillment of judgments by oath with a witness, the lack of inheritance of prophets, the virtue of praying at home, the prohibition of intoxicants, and the encouragement to learn the religious duties. The book includes hadiths narrated with continuous chains of transmission on the authority of the Companions, with special attention to narrating one hadith on the authority of Adam ibn Abi Iyas through several narrators.
descriptions.4855: This book is a part of hadith in which Muhammad bin Mukhlid Al-Attar narrates prophetic hadiths on the authority of his sheikhs. It includes a group of diverse hadiths on various topics such as fasting, zakat, Hajj, jihad, gentleness, and etiquette. It is distinguished by its continuous chain of transmission that begins with the author and ends with the companions.
descriptions.4856: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, compiled by Ibn Bakawayh. The hadiths deal with various topics, including beliefs, acts of worship, etiquette, morals, and temptations, such as denying contagion and temptation, urging fasting on the White Days, the virtue of the Companions, signs of the Hour, rulings on purity and menstruation, and other rulings and sermons. The manuscript begins with a chain of narration of the hadith “There is no contagiousness or tirah” on the authority of Abu Hurairah, then follows it with other chain of narrations.
descriptions.4857: This book is a manuscript of a hadith in which Ibn Tabarzad narrates a group of news and stories narrated with connected chains of transmission, including the story of Ja`far al-Sadiq with al-Mansur, issues and news about Ali bin Abi Talib and his wife Fatima, peace be upon them, the hadith of Umm Zur`, and news from the hadith of Yazid bin Ahmad al-Katib.
descriptions.4858: This book is a part of my hadith in which Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Omar bin Muhammad bin Al-Hasan bin Shazan Al-Sukkari Al-Harbi narrates a group of noble Prophetic hadiths with his chains of transmission connected to the Companions. The book includes hadiths on various topics, including the rulings on marriage and divorce, the commandment to pray and stand, the virtues of Medina and the People of the House, the signs of the Hour, and other Islamic rulings and etiquette.
descriptions.4859: This book is a hadith part in which Al-Qasim bin Musa Al-Asheeb narrates a group of Prophetic hadiths with his chains of transmission, including jurisprudential rulings, virtues, supplications, and morals, such as supplication between the two prostrations, fasting six days of Shawwal, the virtue of Surat Al-Fatihah, private parts issues, and other various topics that fall under the science of hadith and narrations.
descriptions.4860: This book is a part of a hadith in which Judge Abu al-Qasim al-Miyanji narrates prophetic hadiths with chain of transmission from the Companions. It includes a group of hadiths on various topics that include acts of worship such as ablution, prayer, and Hajj, etiquette such as modesty, advice, and family ties, rulings such as divorce, marriage, and endowment, temptations and signs of the Hour, and virtues such as the virtue of Zamzam water and the virtue of a group of the nation.
descriptions.4861: This book is a recent part of the selection of Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi, in which he collected hadiths narrated with chains of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs, including what he selected from the foundations of the books of Sheikh Abu Muhammad Jaafar bin Ahmed bin Al-Siraj Al-Lughi. The book includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths on various topics such as etiquette, commandments, and acts of worship, such as urging the pursuit of knowledge, the virtue of Hajj, the prohibition of lying to the Prophet, and other rulings and sermons. This part falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths with their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4862: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a council dictated by Sharif Abi Al-Fawares Tarad bin Muhammad Al-Zaynabi, and it contains prophetic hadiths supported by narrations connected to the chains of transmission, including the hadith of Anas bin Malik about the Prophet ﷺ opening the door of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
descriptions.4863: This hadith part, compiled by Hafiz Diya al-Din al-Maqdisi, includes a collection of hadiths of the Prophet with high chain of transmission, in addition to stories and poems. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating hadiths with continuous chains of transmission, and it includes hadiths on the virtues of the Companions, jihad, etiquette, and other topics.
descriptions.4864: This is a manuscript of my hadith that includes three serial hadiths, narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi and other sheikhs. Each narrator in the chain of transmission has committed himself to making the hadith he narrates be the first hadith he hears from his sheikh. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating serial hadiths, paying attention to the condition of updating and explaining how to listen and approve.
descriptions.4865: This manuscript includes seven sessions written by Amali Abu al-Qasim bin Bishran, and it is one of the books of the Prophet’s hadith that is narrated with continuous chains of transmission. The book contains a collection of Prophetic hadiths on various topics, including etiquette and morals, rulings on acts of worship such as prayer and Hajj, the virtues of the Qur’an, signs of the Hour, and other things mentioned in the excerpt from the table of contents.
descriptions.4866: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Imam Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Dhahli, and it includes hadiths on multiple topics such as worship, etiquette, and rulings. The book begins by mentioning the chain of narrators connected to its author, then presents the hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, making it a model for manuscript hadith works that were concerned with collecting narrations and transmitting them with connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4867: This book is a part of a hadith compiled by Imam Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Maqdisi, known as al-Bukhari. It includes a collection of prophetic hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as the virtue of remembrance and repentance, the warning against miserliness, a description of the condition of the people of Paradise and Hell, and the famous hadith regarding the weight of the word monotheism in the scale.
descriptions.4868: This book is a part of a hadith in which Abu Ishaq Al-Habal narrates a group of noble Prophetic hadiths with connected chains of transmission. The book includes hadiths on various topics, including the virtues of patience in this world, the importance of choosing good companions, the encouragement of mercy, and some jurisprudential rulings related to conditions in marriage.
descriptions.4869: This book is a part of a hadith in which Abu Bakr al-Najjad narrates noble prophetic hadiths with continuous chains of transmission. It includes a group of hadiths on various topics, including the rulings on purity, prayer, sales, divorce, temptations, sermons, and etiquette. It is included among the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths and collecting them, along with mentioning the methods of their chain of transmission.
descriptions.4870: This book is part of my hadith in which Abu Ali Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Sawaf narrates a group of noble Prophetic hadiths, attributing their chains of transmission to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him. The hadiths narrated in this part revolve around a number of Islamic virtues and etiquette, such as urging people to cover one’s private parts, fulfilling the needs of Muslims, the virtue of bringing joy to the household, and explaining some jurisprudential rulings and etiquette related to prayer, swearing an oath, and so on.
descriptions.4871: This book is a part of a manuscript of hadiths, which includes ten selected hadiths from the thirteenth part of the benefits selected from the foundations of the hadith of Judge Abu Tahir Al-Dhuhli, and they were selected by Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni. The selected hadiths deal with various topics from the Prophet’s biography, etiquette, and rulings, such as what happened in the Battle of Uhud, the ruling on boys, issues of purity and fasting, and some well-known supplications.
descriptions.4872: This manuscript contains prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Abu al-Hasan al-Na’ali through a series of narrators, and it deals with multiple topics related to worship, morals, and Islamic sermons. The book is based on a continuous narration from the author's grandfather to his son, and begins with the narration of a prophetic hadith about intention in actions, thus providing an overview of the nature of the hadith content of the text.
descriptions.4873: This book is a hadith part in which Abu Al-Hasan Khaythama bin Suleiman Al-Atrabelsi narrates prophetic hadiths from his sheikhs, including narrations on various topics such as acts of worship, transactions, virtues, and subtleties. It is included among the hadith manuscripts that are concerned with collecting the Prophet’s hadiths with their connected chains of transmission, and it contains hadiths about fasting, selling, ruqyah, jihad, and others.
descriptions.4874: A hadith book in which its author responds to a previous book by Abu al-Qasim bin Asakir, in which he accuses him of fanaticism towards the Ash’ari school of thought, and of collecting fabricated and fabricated hadiths denouncing those who oppose him. The author mentions that he saw these narrations in other books, then he came across Ibn Asakir’s book and decided to expose the suspicions in it, explaining that they are counterfeit dirhams that appear to be of good quality but within are corruption. The book includes chapters on condemning heresies, speech, and fanaticism towards heresy.
descriptions.4875: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission on the authority of Abu al-Hasan al-Sukkari. It includes various hadiths on rulings, etiquette, softening, and temptations, including those related to prayer, zakat, Hajj, sales, divorce, and clothing, in addition to some stories and news.
descriptions.4876: This book is part of a manuscript of hadiths, in which Abu Al-Hussein bin Al-Aali collected noble prophetic hadiths, selected by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Fadl Al-Jarudi. The book includes a collection of narrated hadiths with their chains of transmission, covering various topics such as commandments and sermons, the provisions of purity and prayer, Islamic etiquette, the virtues of deeds, and an explanation of some of the Prophet’s Sunnahs.
descriptions.4877: This book is a part of my hadith in which Abu Al-Hussein bin Al-Muzaffar Al-Hafiz narrates a group of noble Prophetic hadiths with continuous chains of transmission. It includes various narrations on rulings, etiquette, softening, and temptations, including those related to purity, prayer, Hajj, sales, and funerals. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission that tells the story of Ka’b bin Ujrah with the Prophet ﷺ in the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, and it contains hadiths on various topics such as the virtue of mosques, intercession, and hypocrisy.
descriptions.4878: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of noble prophetic hadiths, narrated by Abu Al-Qasim Ismail bin Al-Qasim Al-Halabi on the authority of his sheikhs, and it deals with various topics that include asceticism, Islamic etiquette, the virtues of the Companions, signs of the Hour, and other rulings and sermons.
descriptions.4879: This book is a part of a hadith in which Abu al-Qasim al-Kinani narrates a group of noble Prophetic hadiths with connected chains of transmission. It includes various narrations on various topics such as threats, punishment, etiquette, and virtues. It is included among the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting the Sunnah of the Prophet through a chain of narrators.
descriptions.4880: This manuscript is a part of a hadith compiled by the author Abu Bakr Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Muhandis, and includes his narrations from a number of his sheikhs, including Abu Al-Qasim Aafia bin Muhammad, Abu Bakr Al-Maliki, Abu Ya’la Al-Abbasi, and others. The manuscript includes supported hadiths narrated by the author on the authority of these sheikhs with their chains of transmission, and begins with an example of this, the hadith of Jabir regarding the description of Hajj and Umrah. The manuscript is classified among the hadith manuscripts, and it is an audio recording by Sahl bin Bishr al-Isfarayini.
descriptions.4881: This is a manuscript of my hadith that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ Al-Bahrani, and it includes hadiths on the rulings on bed, breastfeeding, intercession, temptations, signs of the Hour, and other topics, attributed with their chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4882: This book is part of a hadith in which Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Al-Haytham Al-Anbari Al-Bundar narrates a group of Prophetic hadiths with continuous chains of transmission. The book includes hadiths in various sections of jurisprudence, worship, and etiquette, such as the nature of prayer, purity, zakat, Hajj, foods, clothing, and other topics.
descriptions.4883: This book is a part of my hadith in which Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Anbari, known as Al-Bundar, narrates hadiths from his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission. The book includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths on various topics such as the rulings on prayer, wiping over the socks, modesty, pride, self-righteousness, and others, making it a modern manuscript that documents narrations from multiple methods.
descriptions.4884: This book is the second part of the narrations of Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Yusuf bin Khallad al-Nusabi. It is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with continuous chains of transmission from his sheikhs. The hadiths deal with various topics, including the rulings on purity, prayer, zakat, and fasting, as well as travel etiquette, charity, jihad, and issues of morality, preaching, and softening. It appears from the excerpt that the book is preserved with multiple narrations from a number of hadith scholars, which reflects the narrators’ care in transmitting this part of the hadith.
descriptions.4885: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, collected by Al-Hafiz Abu Jaafar Al-Tahawi. The topics of the mentioned hadiths range from rulings on prayer, fasting, and selling, to stories about the Companions, and an explanation of some of the virtues of deeds and legal etiquette. The manuscript begins with a continuous chain of transmission in which Al-Tahawi narrates hadiths on the authority of his sheikhs. It represents an example of the hadith books that focused on narrating the hadiths with chain of transmission.
descriptions.4886: This book is a part of a hadith in which Muhammad bin Zaid Al-Ansari narrates a group of Prophetic hadiths with connected chains of transmission, and it includes various topics that include the virtues of deeds, encouragement and intimidation, and legal etiquette, such as obedience in prayer, compassion between people, the rulings on cupping, and the signs of the Hour.
descriptions.4887: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths supported by connected narrations. It begins with narrations from the companions such as Abu Hurairah and Anas bin Malik, and deals with various topics such as urging people to work for the afterlife and the virtue of reading the Qur’an.
descriptions.4888: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabri on the authority of his sheikh Abdul Razzaq bin Hammam, through a series of connected narrators. The manuscript begins by mentioning the multiple chains of narration that reach al-Dabari, then cites the hadiths supported by their chains of narration, making it part of the hadith heritage narrated by hearing and authorization.
descriptions.4889: This book is part of the narrations of the Prophet’s hadith, compiled by Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Ahmed bin Rizqawayh. It narrates hadiths with chains of transmission to the Companions and followers. It includes excerpts from the sayings of the narrators and the virtues of some of the Companions. It is one of the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting news and chains of transmission.
descriptions.4890: This book is a part of a hadith that narrates a collection of noble Prophetic hadiths through a series of narrators beginning with Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Malaeb. The book includes hadiths on various topics, including those related to Friday prayers, hypocrisy, making up for prayers, reading, prayers, and holidays, in addition to some hadiths that contain commandments and sermons. This work falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting the Sunnah of the Prophet with its connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4891: This modern manuscript tells the story of a Bedouin from Banu Sulaym who hunted a lizard, then brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and addressed him harshly and accusingly, so that the Prophet ﷺ responded to him with a dream and called him to Islam. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts that include supported prophetic hadiths, and the author began it with a chain of narrators that reaches all the way back to the companion Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).
descriptions.4892: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Bishr ibn Matar al-Daqqaq, narrated on the authority of his two sheikhs, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Waki` ibn al-Jarrah. The book includes hadiths on various topics of jurisprudence, etiquette, and religious matters, such as rulings on funerals, purity, fasting, and Hajj, in addition to hadiths on asceticism and morals. The manuscript represents part of the hadith narrations with chain of transmission, which is concerned with transmitting the Sunnah of the Prophet with its connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4893: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths narrated by Khalid bin Mardas al-Siraj. It has reached us through a series of trustworthy narrators. The hadiths mentioned in its index deal with various topics of worship, etiquette and rulings, such as the nature of prayer and ablution, Friday etiquette and dress, the virtues of deeds, morals and dealings. This part is an example of hadith narrations that were circulated in dictation and hearing sessions in the advanced Islamic centuries.
descriptions.4894: This book is a hadith manuscript that collects some hadiths narrated from the learned Imam Dhul-Nun al-Misri, and includes a series of connected chains of transmission that narrate famous sayings about the Prophet ﷺ. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting news and attributed narrations, with a focus on hadiths related to remembrance and signs of God’s love and hatred.
descriptions.4895: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Imam Sufyan bin Uyaynah, through the narration of Al-Qadi Al-Khula’i. The book includes hadiths on various topics, including etiquette and morals, prophetic medicine, the provisions of prayer, zakat, inheritance, and other jurisprudential and doctrinal issues. The manuscript is part of the hadith of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and it was narrated with a chain of chain of transmission that begins with Al-Khula’i and ends with Ibn Uyaynah.
descriptions.4896: This is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, compiled by the author Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Najih al-Baghdadi al-Bazzaz, and narrated by his student Abu Ali ibn Shazan. The manuscript includes various hadiths on various topics, such as fasting, the Qur’an, and poetry, with the chain of narrators’ chains of transmission dating back to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4897: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated on the authority of Abbas bin Abdullah al-Tarqafi. It was narrated with continuous chains of transmission starting from a number of later narrators all the way up to al-Tarqafi. The hadiths address various topics, including acts of worship such as prayer and fasting, Islamic etiquette such as backbiting and modesty, and some jurisprudential rulings such as purity and wills, in addition to the virtues of good deeds and jihad.
descriptions.4898: This hadith manuscript collects three narrated hadiths: the hadith of Isa bin Maryam (peace be upon him), the hadith of the bird with Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, and the hadith of the lizard with the Prophet ﷺ, in addition to stories transferred from the book of Al-Samarkandi. The manuscript begins with the story of a blind temporal woman who has no hands, legs, or eyes. She tells Jesus (peace be upon him) the reason for her satisfaction with God’s judgment. Then the story concludes with her death after Jesus gave her the good news that she was a companion of the prophets in Paradise.
descriptions.4899: This book is a manuscript of my hadiths that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Muhammad bin Sulaiman al-Musaysi, known as Blawin. It includes various hadiths on topics such as the virtue of monotheism, the rulings on prayer, jihad, the prophetic commandments, and other issues of Islamic law and etiquette.
descriptions.4900: This is a manuscript of my hadith in which Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi narrates a group of stories and news about Imam Shu`bah ibn al-Hajjaj, including prophetic hadiths and narrations with chain of transmission from his sheikhs, while mentioning some of his lineage and loyalty. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting chains of transmission and information from earlier hadith scholars.
descriptions.4901: This is a manuscript of my hadith that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths collected by Jaafar bin Ibrahim Al-Makki from the originals of the speakers of Sheikh Abu Al-Hussein bin Al-Naqur, and he narrates them with a continuous chain of transmission. The book includes various hadiths on the virtues of deeds, sermons, and temptations, such as the virtue of fasting and praying at a funeral, the signs of the Hour, and the classes of the nation.
descriptions.4902: This book is a manuscript of a hadith in which the author collected hadiths and traces related to the ruling on reciting the Basmalah loudly during prayer. The book includes multiple narrations from the Companions and followers, including sayings and actions that differ between reciting the Basmalah out loud and silent, with quotations from hadiths attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. The book aims to present scientific material on this jurisprudential issue through supported narrations.
descriptions.4903: This is a manuscript of my hadiths that includes the biographies of the sheikhs of the author Abu al-Fadl Ibn al-Mahdi, mentioning their circumstances and dates of their death and selecting some of their hadiths. The author arranged his sheikhs according to their classes, starting with Banu Hashim, then the authentic witnesses, then the jurists, then the reciters, then the preachers and ascetics, then the sheikhs of hadith and memorizers, then the rest of the virtuous. The manuscript contains the chain of transmission of his narration through the author’s son, through his father, and through Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir Al-Salafi.
descriptions.4904: This is a manuscript of my hadith that collects narrations and news related to those to whom miracles and miracles appeared, and to those who spoke after death from the righteous and others. The book is organized into sections in which hadiths and hadiths are presented, supported by their chains of transmission, beginning with a long hadith about Tamim al-Dari describing the Angel of Death seizing the soul of the guardian.
descriptions.4905: This is a brief treatise on the science of hadith, in which the author collected chapters in which prophetic hadiths were mentioned, then showed that they were not authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ according to the major critics of hadith. The author moves through multiple sections, such as faith, destiny, the virtues of the Qur’an, and the virtues of the Companions, pointing out that the famous hadiths in them are not authentic, and that some of them are the words of the Companions and Followers or fabricated by the consensus of the hadith scholars.
descriptions.4906: This hadith part tells the story of the marriage of Abu Al-Aas bin Al-Rabi’ to Zainab, daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ, including details of their lineage and children, and the position of the Prophet ﷺ towards his son-in-law. The book reviews some hadiths and traces related to this incident, such as the Prophet ﷺ returning his daughter Zainab to Abu Al-Aas for the first marriage after his conversion to Islam.
descriptions.4907: This is a manuscript of my hadith in which the author collected the methods of the Prophet’s hadith, peace and blessings be upon him: “I am at the Basin and see who will respond to me,” and what it means from hadiths reported from a number of companions, such as Jabir bin Abdullah, Bilal, Abu Musa, Abdullah bin Amr, and others. The book aims to trace the chains of transmission of this hadith and its various narrations, while mentioning the hadith scholars who narrated it.
descriptions.4908: This is a hadith manuscript that collects hadiths, stories, and chain of transmission, written by Al-Hafiz Abu Musa Al-Madini Al-Asbahani. The book falls within the hadith books concerned with narrating lengthy narrations with their connected chains of transmission, and it appears from its introduction that it narrates on the authority of its sheikhs with a continuous chain of transmission to the Companions, such as the hadith of Qayla bint Makhramah.
descriptions.4909: This book is a hadith manuscript in which its author, Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, collected a collection of prophetic hadiths whose chain of transmission to him was linked to ten narrators between him and the Prophet ﷺ, and for this reason it was called “Ashariyat.” The hadiths mentioned in the table of contents revolve around various topics such as the virtue of fasting, modesty, gratitude, consideration, and other Islamic etiquette and virtues, which makes it a work concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths with their high chains of transmission.
descriptions.4910: This manuscript is part of the narrations of the Prophet’s hadith. It includes ten hadiths selected from the thirteenth part of Fawa’id Abu Tahir al-Dhuhli, and they were selected by al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni. The manuscript includes references and authorizations for hadith narrators through connected chains of transmission, which makes it a model for books of hadith parts that are concerned with transmitting hadiths with their chains of transmission.
descriptions.4911: This is a manuscript of my hadith collecting hadiths and narrations about the virtues of the companion Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him), compiled by Abu Al-Qasim Ubayd Allah Al-Saqati. The book includes supported narrations that address the virtues of Muawiyah, and some critics have pointed out the weakness of some of its chains of transmission and the strangeness of its contents. The manuscript falls within the hadith works dedicated to the virtues of the Companions.
descriptions.4912: This is a manuscript of my hadith in which the author Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti collected a number of hadiths and narrations contained in the virtue of the Alexandrian port, beginning with chains of transmission connected to the Companions, and focusing on what was reported of the encouragement to reside in it and bond in it.
descriptions.4913: This book is a manuscript of a hadith in which the author collected a number of narrated hadiths regarding the virtues of the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of Arafat, including what was reported regarding the reward of fasting on these two days and the virtues related to them. The book falls within the hadith classification, as it presents hadiths supported by their chains of transmission, beginning by mentioning the series of narrators on the authority of the Companions on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4914: This book is part of a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, compiled by Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Bishr al-Zubayri al-Ikri. The book begins by mentioning the chain of narrators all the way back to the Prophet ﷺ, and includes hadiths on various topics such as worship, etiquette, temptations, slavery, and jurisprudential rulings.
descriptions.4915: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, compiled by Abu Bakr bin Khallad al-Nusaybi. Hadiths address various topics in jurisprudence, acts of worship, and transactions, such as the provisions of zakat, blood money, prayer, inheritance, divorce, food and drink, in addition to commandments and legal etiquette. The manuscript begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, and contains hadiths supported by the narration of Al-Harith bin Muhammad bin Abi Usama on the authority of his sheikhs.
descriptions.4916: This book includes hadiths and benefits narrated by Abu Saad Al-Baghdadi on the authority of his sheikhs, and it was narrated on his authority with a continuous chain of transmission from his compiler to his scholars. The book deals with multiple Islamic topics through hadiths and stories, focusing on the lessons and sermons learned from the lives of the Prophet and his companions.
descriptions.4917: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that collects a number of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, dealing with the rulings on zakat and its quorum, the etiquette of Friday prayer and prayer, the virtues of deeds such as jihad and looking after the insolvent, issues of common sense and good character, and other jurisprudential and preaching topics. The book includes connected narrations about the Prophet ﷺ by a number of hadith sheikhs, and it is compiled by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl bin Nazif Al-Farra’ Al-Misri.
descriptions.4918: This book is a hadith manuscript that collects a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, and deals with various topics including the virtues of deeds and acts of worship, stories of the prophets, signs of the Hour, and the virtues of some of the companions and holy places. The book begins by mentioning the chain of narrators and moves on to narrate the chain of transmission of hadiths covering multiple aspects of belief, behavior, and sermons.
descriptions.4919: This book is a hadith manuscript that collects a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their chains of transmission, and it is known as “Fawa’id Abu Ali al-Mada’ini.” The book includes hadiths on various topics, such as acts of worship, such as prayer, fasting, and seclusion, etiquette, such as eating and being neighbourly, and rulings, such as pre-emption, trade, and loyalty, in addition to some hadiths on slavery and temptations. The book begins with the benefits and sayings of the imams of hadith in documenting narrators and the virtues of some books such as Al-Muwatta’.
descriptions.4920: This book is a part of Hadith that includes a group of attributed benefits narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ali Abd al-Rahman bin Muhammad bin Fadhalah al-Naysaburi, and it contains prophetic hadiths and various effects on topics of encouragement, intimidation, asceticism, and etiquette, such as the virtue of seeking knowledge, urging piety, and mentioning some foods and deeds.
descriptions.4921: This book is a hadith part that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths and related benefits, collected and published by Al-Hafiz Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Jama’at Al-Kanani. It is included among the hadith manuscripts, and includes texts of well-known hadiths about compassion and compassion, warning against lying to the Prophet ﷺ, and other benefits supported by continuous chains of transmission.
descriptions.4922: This book is a manuscript of hadiths in which the author collected hadiths narrated by Imam Al-Awza’i on the authority of his sheikhs, and arranged them according to their names. The book includes Al-Awza’i’s narrations on the authority of a number of followers, such as Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, Al-Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab, and Abu Al-Zubair. The hadiths vary between rulings, virtues, and prophetic etiquette.
descriptions.4923: This book is a manuscript of my hadith that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths selected from the narration of Abu Shuaib al-Harrani. It includes hadiths on various topics that include acts of worship such as prayer and ablution, transactions such as usury and charity, etiquette such as modesty and humility, and gentleness such as supplication and illness. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission that narrates hadiths about the Prophet ﷺ through a number of narrators, and in its paragraphs it deals with jurisprudential and moral issues derived from the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4924: A book on the science of hadith, compiled by the author Abu Musa al-Madini, and it is concerned with a special type of hadith narrations, which is known as “the narration of two men, each of them from the other,” in which he cites examples from the Companions, the Successors, and those after them, who each narrated on the authority of his companion, with the union of the sheikh who narrated on his authority. The book aims to highlight the subtleties of this art of Hadith sciences, which only skilled memorizers can be guided to.
descriptions.4925: This is a manuscript of my hadith compiled by Ibn al-Jawzi, collecting serial hadiths that he narrated with his chain of transmission on the authority of his sheikhs. The book begins by mentioning the first hadith the author heard from his sheikh, then follows it with a number of other series of what he heard, in response to a request from one of the students of hadith. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating hadiths related to the chain of transmission in particular.
descriptions.4926: This is a book on the science of hadith by Abu Amr al-Dani, in which he explains the methods of transmitting narrations and explains their types, including the musnad, the mursal, the suspended, and the mutqa’, along with details of the conditions of the mudalis, their classes, and their sects. The author aims to acquaint students of hadith with how to distinguish these types of traces contained in works, relying on abbreviations and examples for each type.
descriptions.4927: This is a manuscript of my hadith in which the author, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Khallal, narrates a number of prophetic hadiths related to the remembrance of the eternal and the karamat of the saints, based on a series of chains of transmission that reach the Companions on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ. The book includes narrations that deal with the characteristics of the Abdals, their numbers and locations, and the signs of the Hour mentioned about them, as part of the hadith scholars’ approach to collecting chain of narrations.
descriptions.4928: This book is a manuscript of my hadiths that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami in the dictation council in Nisapur. It includes various hadiths in the rulings of jurisprudence, etiquette, and preaching, such as the story of al-Jasassah, the prohibition of selling loyalty, the virtue of seeking knowledge, and Bilal’s command to call the call to prayer and sing the iqama.
descriptions.4929: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a council composed by the jurist Abu al-Fath al-Maqdisi, and it includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated with its chain of transmission, dealing with jurisprudential and devotional topics such as fasting, zakat, and glorifying the two Eids, and it begins with a hadith about determining the decrees before the creation of the heavens and the earth.
descriptions.4930: This manuscript is a part of a hadith containing two sets of dictation, the first of which is from the narrations of Sheikh Abu Bakr al-Shirazi in Naysaburi, and the second is from the hadiths of Sheikh al-Khatib Abu Bakr al-Naysaburi, and they were narrated by Judge Abu Bakr al-Shahzouri from them. The manuscript falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths with their connected chains of transmission, and it appears from its introduction that it was heard and dictated in scholarly councils in the fifth century AH.
descriptions.4931: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a collection of poems by Imam Abu Bakr al-Najjad, narrated from him by Abu Abdullah al-Mahamili. The Council contains a collection of Prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics including the virtues of deeds, legal etiquette, and jurisprudential rulings, such as urging suhoor, forbidding some types of clothing, and explaining the provisions of inheritance and succession.
descriptions.4932: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a council composed by Sheikh Abu Saad Al-Baghdadi, and it includes prophetic hadiths narrated with continuous chains of transmission, including those related to the conditions of the Day of Resurrection and the merits of the Qur’an. The work falls within the hadith heritage narrated through listening and dictation, and shows a pattern of scholarly dictation councils that hadith scholars used to hold for their students.
descriptions.4933: This book is a majlis written by Amali Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Mukhlid Al-Attar, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths that the author narrated on the authority of his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission. The aforementioned hadiths deal with various topics, including the rulings on transactions, such as the prohibition against the rich’s wealth, the virtue of spending for the sake of God, in addition to the etiquette of prayer and congregational prayer, and the condemnation of lying to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4934: This book is a collection of the hopes of Al-Hafiz Abu Musa Al-Madini, and it is a hadith manuscript that includes the narration of the Prophet’s hadiths with a series of connected chains of transmission. The text begins by mentioning the methods of narration and permissions related to Al-Hafiz Al-Madani, which makes it a model for the hadith books of Al-Amali that are concerned with transmitting the Sunnah of the Prophet through multiple chains of transmission.
descriptions.4935: This manuscript is part of the Amali al-Hafiz Ibn Mandah, which is one sitting that he dictated in the month of Ramadan in the year three hundred and eighty-eight AH, and it was narrated from him by his son Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman. The manuscript includes attributed prophetic hadiths narrated by Ibn Mandah with his chain of transmission to the Companions, and begins with a dictation council in which he mentions the series of narrations and authorization. This work falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths with their connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4936: This manuscript is part of the dictates of Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Batarqani, which is one sitting that he dictated to his students in the month of Ramadan in the year four hundred and fifty-eight. The book is included among the hadith manuscripts, in which the author narrates prophetic hadiths transmitted by his sheikhs with continuous chains of transmission, beginning with the hadith, “Actions are but by intentions.”
descriptions.4937: This manuscript is a collection of the dictations of Imam Abu Bakr al-Najjad, narrated by Abu al-Hussein Ibn Mukhlid al-Bazzar, and it includes a collection of transmitted prophetic hadiths that al-Najjad dictated to his students. The council includes hadiths on various topics, including those related to the Most Beautiful Names of God, eating etiquette as an answer to the invitation, and the story of the Prophet of God Solomon (peace be upon him), through multiple methods from the narration of Muhammad bin Sirin on the authority of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).
descriptions.4938: This is a hadith manuscript containing a majlis dictated by Abu al-Fawaris Tarad al-Zainabi, narrated by Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Tusi. The manuscript includes one hadith with a chain of transmission narrated by Ibn Masoud about the Prophet ﷺ entering Mecca and breaking the idols around the Kaaba, mentioning the chain of narrators up to the author. The manuscript falls within the hadith dictation councils that the hadith scholars used to dictate to their students.
descriptions.4939: This book is a hadith part that includes a dictation council delivered by the author on Friday the fourteenth of Shaban in the year four hundred and seventy-eight, and it includes a collection of transmitted prophetic hadiths that he narrated from his sheikhs. The hadiths mentioned in this council revolve around religious and educational topics, such as belief in destiny and the urge to work, the virtue of contentment with God and Islam, the Prophet’s commandment to be kind to the tongue and the house and to cry over sin, the virtue of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and the descent of God on the night of the middle of Shaban.
descriptions.4940: This hadith manuscript combines two verses from the narration of Abu Bakr al-Anbari, and includes a group of prophetic hadiths narrated with their chains of transmission, the topics of which vary between the rulings on alcohol and intoxicants, the virtue of seeking knowledge and carrying the forty hadiths, the virtues of Hajj, commandments regarding asceticism in this world, and an explanation of some jurisprudential rulings such as fraud, impurity, zakat, and other things included in the table of contents.
descriptions.4941: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes two sessions dictated by Sheikh Abu Saad al-Baghdadi in the Prophet’s Mosque ﷺ, and it includes supported prophetic hadiths that he narrates with continuous chains of transmission, including the hadith of asking the Prophet ﷺ about the best deeds. The manuscript contains connected narrations from the Companions, with mention of some hadiths related to virtues and etiquette.
descriptions.4942: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes two verses written by Abu Muhammad al-Hasan bin Ali al-Jawhari. It contains a collection of prophetic hadiths and chain of narrations that deal with various topics, including the virtues of the Companions, virtues, prophetic commandments, and some jurisprudential rulings such as usury and suhoor in Ramadan.
descriptions.4943: This book is a manuscript of a hadith containing two verses written by Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Yahya bin Muhammad bin Sa’id. It is a collection of narrated hadiths of the Prophet with their connected chains of transmission. The hadiths address various topics, including legal etiquette, the prohibition of some sins such as playing with dice, the rulings on sales and usury, the virtues of business and morals, signs of the Hour, and prophetic commandments in religious and worldly affairs.
descriptions.4944: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes two collections written by Sheikh Abu Muhammad al-Jawhari, published by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, in which he narrates prophetic hadiths with their connected chains of transmission. The narrated hadiths address various topics, such as legal etiquette, such as the prohibition on facing the Qiblah when relieving oneself, prophetic commandments regarding raising and teaching children, the virtue of keeping the Sunnah alive, and describing some of the scenes on the Day of Resurrection.
descriptions.4945: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes two sessions, written by Sheikh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan bin Muhammad al-Khallal. It contains narrated prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, dealing with various topics such as the virtue of reading the Qur’an, the description of the Prophet’s prayer ﷺ, the rulings on prayer and the danger of abandoning it, signs of nature, the prohibition against using graves as mosques, and other hadiths and sermons.
descriptions.4946: This hadith manuscript was compiled by Abu al-Qasim Ismail bin Muhammad bin al-Fadl al-Taymi, and it includes a group of serial hadiths for which he is famous, such as the serial hadith about cutting nails, the serial hadith about shaking hands, the serial hadith about taking the hand, and others. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating hadiths connected to the chain of transmission with special characteristics or forms. In it, the author recorded what he narrated on the authority of his sheikhs with connected chains of transmission.
descriptions.4947: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes a collection of audible prophetic hadiths on the authority of Sheikh Rizq Allah al-Tamimi al-Baghdadi al-Hanbali, attributing their chains of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ. The book deals with various topics of the virtues of deeds, such as the Night of Power, the dawn and evening prayers, commandments regarding good morals and salvation, and an explanation of God’s presence to His servants who draw near to Him through the obligatory and voluntary prayers.
descriptions.4948: This book is a hadith manuscript that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, collected by Abu Umayyah al-Tarsusi in his Musnad. The hadiths deal with various topics, including the rulings on marriage and divorce, fasting, prayer, zakat, jihad, slavery, and other Islamic rulings and etiquette. It appears from the table of contents that the book is concerned with collecting the Prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, with a focus on jurisprudential and educational rulings.
descriptions.4949: This book is a part of my hadith in which Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Omar Al-Harbi Al-Sukkari narrates the hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ on the authority of his sheikhs, supporting them with his continuous chains of transmission. The book includes a collection of Prophetic hadiths on various topics, including the rulings on purity, punishments, sales, marriage, and wills, in addition to the virtues of deeds, gentleness, and etiquette.
descriptions.4950: This book is a manuscript of my hadiths that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Judge Abu Al-Hasan Ahmad bin Sulaiman bin Hudhalam on the authority of his sheikhs. It contains hadiths on various topics such as purity, fasting, charity, temptations, the virtue of the Qur’an, and other legal rulings and etiquette.
descriptions.4951: This manuscript is “Daniyal’s Mashaykh” compiled by Daniyal ibn Mankali ibn Sarfa al-Karaki, and it is a hadith work that falls within the hadith manuscripts. The book includes a summary of his narrations and chains of transmission from his trustworthy sheikhs. The author began it with an introduction in which he describes the request of Judge Diya al-Din Abi al-Fadayl Daniel to produce a sheikh that includes the principles of his speakers and his narrations on the authority of the sheikhs. Then he cites the hadiths attributed with their chains of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4952: This manuscript is a hadith part that includes a group of hadiths narrated by Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Dahli Al-Naysaburi, and transmitted by the narration of Abu Ali Muhammad bin Ahmed bin Muhammad Al-Maidani Al-Maqili on his authority. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting the Sunnah of the Prophet through continuous chains of transmission, and it contains transcripts and authorizations for narrators later than their sheikhs, which highlights the interest of hadith scholars in narrating and preserving hadith.
descriptions.4953: This manuscript is a hadith part that includes a collection of prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ali bin Lal on the authority of his sheikhs, and it is classified among the hadith manuscripts. The book begins with a continuous chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, and includes hadiths on the virtues of the month of Ramadan and fasting, urging prayers upon the Prophet, honoring one’s parents, and other religious topics.
descriptions.4954: This manuscript is a hadith part that includes the narrations of Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Lahyani on the authority of his sheikhs, and it is narrated with chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ. The manuscript includes chain of transmission hadiths, including those related to prostration of forgetfulness and Al-Muzara’ah, making it a source of hadith narration from approximately the fourth century AH.
descriptions.4955: This manuscript is a part of a hadith in which Abu Muhammad Hibat Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, known as Ibn al-Akfani, narrates hadiths from his sheikhs with his chain of transmission, and in its introduction it includes audio recordings and narrations from a number of narrators from its author. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting prophetic hadiths with their connected chains of transmission, and it contains examples of hadiths with chain of transmission, such as the hadith of God’s satisfaction with the people of Paradise.
descriptions.4956: This manuscript is a hadith part that includes a collection of noble prophetic hadiths narrated by Abu Mansour Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Othman Al-Sawaq, on the authority of his sheikhs connected with their chains of transmission to the Companions. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting chain of narrations, and it includes hadiths on various topics such as mosque etiquette and the virtues of patience in the face of adversity.
descriptions.4957: This hadith manuscript collects hadiths narrated by the jurist Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Aziz bin Ali al-Shahrzuri al-Maliki on the authority of his sheikhs, and it was narrated on his authority by his students. The manuscript includes chains of transmission connected to the Prophet ﷺ, with mentioning of the methods of hearing and approval among narrators, which makes it a model for books of hadith parts that are concerned with the narration of hadiths with chain of transmission.
descriptions.4958: This manuscript is a hadith part that includes a collection of hadiths narrated on the authority of Imam Malik bin Anas, collected and narrated by Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Ali bin Sakhr Al-Azdi on the authority of his sheikhs. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with transmitting the Prophetic hadiths with their connected chains of transmission, and it appears from its introduction that it was narrated through a series of later narrators.
descriptions.4959: This manuscript is part of “Awali Musnad Abd ibn Hamid”, which is a collection of Prophetic hadiths that the author selected from his Musnad and is distinguished by its high chain of transmission. The manuscript includes narrations with a chain of transmission traceable back to Abd ibn Hamid, with a mention of the methods of hearing and approval by which these hadiths reached the narrators of the manuscript. This work falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating hadiths with high levels of chain of narration.
descriptions.4960: This manuscript is part of "Fawa'id Abu al-Qasim Ibn Ali", which is a collection of hadiths narrated by Abu al-Qasim Ali bin Abdul Rahman bin al-Hussein bin Alik al-Naysaburi on the authority of his sheikhs, and it includes prophetic hadiths supported by their chains of transmission. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths and collecting them through hearing and authorization, and it appears from its beginning that it is narrated in several ways from connected narrators.
descriptions.4961: This manuscript is a part of a hadith that includes the dictation sessions of Abu Sa`id al-Naqqash, narrated from him by Abu Muti` al-Sahhaf, and it includes hadiths attributed with their chains of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ, including those related to the reason for the revelation of some verses. The book falls within the hadith manuscripts concerned with narrating the Prophet’s hadiths through hearing and dictation sessions.
descriptions.4962: A hadith book that collects a number of hadiths and traces contained in the virtues and merits of the great companion Jaafar bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and is concerned with narrating them with the chains of transmission of the author to the Prophet ﷺ or to the Companions. The book includes hadiths that refer to Jafar’s high status in Paradise, describing him as “the one with two wings,” and other situations from his life with the Prophet ﷺ.
descriptions.4963: This book is a modern part that includes a selection of the narrations of Yunus bin Ubaid, collected by Al-Hafiz Abu Naim Al-Isbahani. It contains a collection of various prophetic hadiths on rulings, etiquette, and sermons, such as the rulings on sales, punishments, purity, and prayer, and narrated them with chains of transmission connected to the Companions.
descriptions.4964: This book is part of a hadith manuscript that includes a selection of hadiths narrated by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Mukhlid al-Attar. It contains a collection of diverse prophetic hadiths on various topics such as worship, transactions, etiquette, and temptations, including those related to Hajj, ablution, prayer, dowry, and food and drink. They were narrated with continuous chains of transmission starting from the author and ending with the Companions.
descriptions.4965: This book is a selection of the twenty hadith volumes known as “Al-Khula’iyyat”, compiled and narrated by Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Khula’i Al-Shafi’i on the authority of his sheikhs. Its narrations include noble prophetic hadiths about the virtues of the Companions and their positions, commandments and sermons, with special attention to the issue of guardianship and disavowal.
descriptions.4966: This book is a part of my hadith that includes a selection of hadiths from Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Al-Haytham Al-Anbari, narrated by Abdul Haq bin Abdul Khaleq on the authority of Abu Ghaleb Al-Baghal. The book includes a collection of various prophetic hadiths on various topics, such as the rulings on sales and usury, etiquette of prayer, commandments, chips, and other sections of the Sunnah of the Prophet.
descriptions.4967: This manuscript is “Selected from the Hadith of Al-Jassas and Al-Hana’i” by Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad bin Abdul-Daim Al-Maqdisi. It is a collection of hadiths that selects hadiths from the narrations of the two sheikhs, Abu Yusuf Yaqoub bin Ahmad Al-Jassas and Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Hana’i, on the authority of their sheikhs. The manuscript includes various prophetic hadiths with their chains of transmission, including those related to worship, etiquette, and preaching, such as a hadith about cupping for the fasting person in ihram and a hadith forbidding insulting the companions.
descriptions.4968: This book is a manuscript of a hadith by Imam Al-Dhahabi. It studies and criticizes the hadiths that Al-Hakim mentioned in his Mustadrak, and explains the weak or weak ones in them. The author begins by mentioning hadiths related to the virtues of Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), then moves on to hadiths about judiciary and guardianship, while following each hadith by stating the status of its narrators and his ruling on it. He acknowledges the authenticity of some of them and declares the status of others.
descriptions.4969: This book is a manuscript of a hadith that includes the copy of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, which is a collection of hadiths of the Prophet narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik, dealing with various topics including the rulings on Friday, ablution, fasting, suhoor, retaliation, and Islamic etiquette, in addition to the interpretation of some Qur’anic verses. The manuscript falls within the hadith heritage, which is concerned with transmitting the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ and his actions through continuous chains of transmission.
